segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Islam began as something strange, and it will return to being strange, so glad tidings to the strangers."
It was asked, "Who are the strangers?" He said, "Those who have withdrawn from their tribes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, he said:
"To it ends whatever ascends from the earth, and whatever descends from above."

He said: Then Allah gave him there three things that He had not given to any prophet before him: the prayers were made obligatory upon him as five, he was given the closing verses of Sūrat al-Baqarah, and his Ummah was forgiven the grave sins, so long as they did not associate anything with Allah.
Ibn Masʿūd said regarding:
"when there covered the Lote Tree that which covered [it]" (53:16), he said: The Lote Tree is in the sixth heaven.

Sufyān said: [It was] a covering of gold, and Sufyān gestured with his hand and made it tremble. Someone other than Mālik ibn Mighwal added: To it the knowledge of creation ends; they have no knowledge of what lies beyond that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: "For those who do good is the best [reward] and more" (10:26), and said:

"When the people of Paradise have entered Paradise and the people of the Fire have entered the Fire, a caller will call out: O people of Paradise, you have a promise with Allah that He wishes to fulfil for you."

"They will say: What is it? Has He not made our scales heavy, made our faces bright, admitted us into Paradise and saved us from the Fire? Then the veil will be lifted and they will look at Him. By Allah, Allah will not have given them anything more beloved to them than looking at Him, nor anything more delightful to their eyes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When it was revealed:
"And warn your closest kinsmen" (26:214), the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered Quraysh, addressing particular groups and then all together, and said:

"O company of Quraysh, save yourselves from the Fire, for I cannot avail you anything against Allah, neither harm nor benefit. O company of Banū ʿAbd Manāf, save yourselves from the Fire, for I cannot avail you anything against Allah, neither harm nor benefit. O company of Banū Quṣayy, save yourselves from the Fire, for I cannot avail you anything, neither harm nor benefit. O company of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, save yourselves from the Fire, for I cannot avail you anything, neither harm nor benefit. O Fāṭimah daughter of Muḥammad, save yourself from the Fire, for I cannot avail you anything, neither harm nor benefit. You have a bond of kinship, and I will keep it moist by maintaining it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:
"The five prayers, and from one Friday prayer to the next, and from Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what is between them, so long as the major sins are avoided."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you performs ablution, let him draw water into his nostrils and then blow it out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Prophet ﷺ after he had performed ablution, leaving on his feet a spot the size of a fingernail unwashed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Go back and perform your ablution well."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you urinates, let him not touch his private part with his right hand, and let him not clean himself with his right hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr, all from Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar,
Ibn Ayyūb said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us: al-ʿAlāʾ informed me, from his father,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If the believer knew what punishment Allah has, no one would have hope of His Paradise; and if the disbeliever knew what mercy Allah has, no one would despair of His Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I stayed for a year wanting to ask
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb about a verse,

but I could not do so out of awe of him, until he went out for Hajj and I went out with him. When he returned, and we were on part of the road, he turned aside toward an arāk tree for a need of his. I waited for him until he finished, then I walked with him and said, "O Commander of the Faithful, who were the two women among the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who supported one another against him?" He said, "They were Ḥafṣah and ʿĀʾishah."
I said to him, "By Allah, I have wanted to ask you about this for a year, but I could not out of awe of you."

He said, "Do not do that. Whenever you think I have any knowledge, ask me about it, and if I know it, I will tell you." He said: And ʿUmar said, "By Allah, in the Time of Ignorance we did not count women as having any standing, until Allah the Exalted revealed concerning them what He revealed and apportioned for them what He apportioned. One day, while I was considering a matter, my wife said to me, 'If only you would do such and such.' I said to her, 'What business is it of yours, and what concern do you have with a matter that I intend?' She said to me, 'How strange of you, son of al-Khaṭṭāb! You do not want to be answered back, while your daughter answers back the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he spends his whole day angry!'"
ʿUmar said: "So I took my cloak and went out right then until I entered upon Ḥafṣah and said to her, 'My daughter, do you answer back the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he spends his whole day angry?'"
Ḥafṣah said, "By Allah, we do answer him back."

I said, "Know that I warn you of the punishment of Allah and the anger of His Messenger. My daughter, do not be deceived by that one, who is pleased with her own beauty and the love of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for her."

Then I went out until I entered upon Umm Salamah because of my kinship with her, and I spoke to her. Umm Salamah said to me, "How strange of you, son of al-Khaṭṭāb! You have entered into everything, until you want to enter between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his wives."

He said: She took hold of me in a way that broke down some of what I had felt, so I left her. I had a companion from the Anṣār: when I was absent he would bring me the news, and when he was absent I would bring him the news. At that time we were fearing a king of the Ghassān, who had been mentioned to us as intending to march against us, and our hearts were filled with fear of him. Then my Anṣārī companion came knocking at the door and said, "Open! Open!"
I said, "Has the Ghassānī come?" He said, "It is worse than that: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has withdrawn from his wives."
I said, "May the noses of Ḥafṣah and ʿĀʾishah be rubbed in the dust."

Then I took my garment and went out until I came, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in an upper room of his, which one climbed to by a ladder-like step, and a black servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at the top of the steps. I said, "This is ʿUmar." So he permitted me to enter.

ʿUmar said: I related this account to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when I reached the account of Umm Salamah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled. He was lying on a mat with nothing between him and it, and under his head was a leather pillow stuffed with palm fibre. At his feet was a heap of qaraẓ leaves, and at his head hung tanned hides. I saw the mark of the mat on the side of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I wept. He said, "What makes you weep?"
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, Chosroes and Caesar are in what they are in, while you are the Messenger of Allah!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Are you not pleased that for them is this world and for you is the Hereafter?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I wanted to ask

ʿUmar about the two women who supported one another against each other in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I waited a year without finding an opportunity, until I accompanied him to Makkah. When we were at Marr al-Ẓahrān, he went to relieve himself and said, "Bring me a container of water." I brought it to him, and when he had finished and returned, I began pouring water over him, and I remembered, so I said to him, "O Commander of the Faithful, who were the two women?" I had not finished my words before he said, "ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no owner of camels who does not fulfil their due, but that they will come on the Day of Resurrection more numerous than they ever were, and he will be seated for them in a broad, level plain, and they will trample him with their hooves and feet. And there is no owner of cattle who does not fulfil their due, but that they will come on the Day of Resurrection more numerous than they ever were, and he will be seated for them in a broad, level plain, and they will gore him with their horns and trample him with their hooves. And there is no owner of sheep and goats who does not fulfil their due, but that they will come on the Day of Resurrection more numerous than they ever were, and he will be seated for them in a broad, level plain, and they will gore him with their horns and trample him with their cloven hooves; none among them will be hornless or have a broken horn. And there is no owner of treasure who does not fulfil its due, but that his treasure will come on the Day of Resurrection as a bald-headed serpent, following him with its mouth open. When it reaches him, he flees from it, and it calls out to him: 'Take your treasure that you hid, for I have no need of it.' When he sees that there is no escape from it, he puts his hand into its mouth, and it crushes it as a stallion crushes [its food]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The earth will vomit up the pieces of its liver, like pillars of gold and silver." He said: "Then the thief will come and say, 'For the like of this my hand was cut off.' The murderer will come and say, 'For this I killed.' The one who severed [ties] will come and say, 'For this I severed my ties of kinship.' Then they will leave it, and they will not take anything from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"O people, Allah is Pure and accepts only what is pure. Allah has commanded the believers with what He commanded the Messengers, for He said: {O Messengers, eat from the good things and do righteous deeds; indeed, I know well what you do.} And He said: {O you who believe, eat from the good things We have provided for you.}"

Then he mentioned a man who travels far, disheveled and dusty, stretching out his hands to the sky, [saying,] "O Lord! O Lord!" while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished by the unlawful. So how can [his prayer] be answered?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"O son of Adam, if you give away what is surplus, it is better for you, and if you withhold it, it is worse for you. You will not be blamed for [keeping] what is sufficient. Begin with those you support, and the upper hand is better than the lower hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not be persistent in asking. For by Allah, none of you asks me for something and has his request drawn out of me while I dislike it, and yet is blessed in what I give him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever asks people for their wealth in order to accumulate more is only asking for embers of Hell. So let him ask for little or for much."
label: machine translation

segments_en: For one of you to go out in the morning, gather firewood and carry it on his back, give charity from it and be independent of people, is better for him than asking a man, whether he gives to him or refuses him. For the upper hand is better than the lower hand, and begin with those you support."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ mentioned a people who would be among his community, who would emerge as a group among the people, whose mark is shaving [their heads]. He said:
"They are the worst of creation," or "among the worst of creation. The one of the two parties closer to the truth will kill them."
He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ gave an example for them, or he said something like this:
"A man shoots an arrow, or he said, at a target, and he looks at the arrowhead and sees no trace [of blood], and he looks at the shaft and sees no trace, and he looks at the notch and sees no trace."
He said: Abū Saʿīd said, "And you [people of Iraq] are the ones who killed them, O people of Iraq."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"After me from my community, or there will be after me from my community, a people who recite the Qurʾān but it does not go beyond their throats. They will pass out of the religion as the arrow passes through the game, and then they will not return to it. They are the worst of creation and of beings."

Ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit said: I met Rāfiʿ ibn ʿAmr al-Ghifārī, the brother of al-Ḥakam al-Ghifārī, and said, "What is this report I heard from Abū Dharr, such and such?" and I mentioned this hadith to him. He said, "And I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to kiss me while he was fasting. And which of you can control his desire as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ controlled his desire?
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When any of you is invited to a wedding feast, let him attend it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hannād said: Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib said, and Sulaymān reported from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib,

"The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to do seven things and forbade us from seven. He commanded us to visit the sick, to say "may Allah have mercy on you" to one who sneezes, to help someone fulfil an oath, to support the oppressed, to spread the greeting of peace, to answer the one who invites, and to follow funeral processions. And he forbade us from gold rings, from silver vessels, from silk saddle-cloths (mayāthir), from qasiyy garments, and from brocade (istabraq), silk (ḥarīr) and dībāj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: During the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ we used to avoid speaking freely and being relaxed with our wives, for fear that something of the Qurʾān would be revealed about us. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, we spoke.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Eleven women sat down and made a pledge and covenant that they would not conceal anything about their husbands. The first said: "My husband is the meat of a lean camel on top of a rugged mountain: neither easy to climb, nor fat enough to be carried down."
The second said: "My husband: I will not spread his news, for I fear I could not finish it. If I mention him, I mention all his faults, outward and hidden."
The third said: "My husband is the tall one. If I speak, I am divorced; if I stay silent, I am left hanging."
The fourth said: "My husband is like the night of Tihāmah: neither hot nor cold, with no fear and no weariness."
The fifth said: "My husband, when he enters, is a leopard; when he goes out, a lion; and he does not ask about what he has left behind."
The sixth said: "My husband, if he eats, he eats everything up; if he drinks, he drains it all; if he lies down, he wraps himself up alone, and he does not put his hand in to know my grief."
The seventh said: "My husband is hopelessly inept and dull. Every ailment is found in him: he may split your head, or wound you, or do both to you."
The eighth said: "My husband: his touch is the touch of a rabbit, and his scent is the scent of zarnab."
The ninth said: "My husband has a lofty pillar, a long sword-belt, abundant ashes, and a house close to the gathering place."

The tenth said: "My husband is Mālik, and what is Mālik? Mālik is better than all that. He has many camels, kept mostly at the watering places and seldom sent out to pasture. When they hear the sound of the lute, they are certain they will be slaughtered."

The eleventh said: "My husband is Abū Zarʿ, and what is Abū Zarʿ? He hung ornaments on my ears, filled my upper arms with fat, and pleased me so that I became pleased with myself. He found me among a family of sheep-herders in poor circumstances and brought me to a family with horses and camels, with threshers and winnowers. With him I speak and am not rebuked; I sleep until morning; and I drink until I am satisfied."
"The mother of Abū Zarʿ, and what is the mother of Abū Zarʿ? Her storage bags are full and her house is spacious."
"The son of Abū Zarʿ, and what is the son of Abū Zarʿ? His bed is like a drawn sword, and a lamb's foreleg satisfies him."
"The daughter of Abū Zarʿ, and what is the daughter of Abū Zarʿ? She obeys her father and her mother, her garment is well filled, and she is the envy of her co-wife."

"The maidservant of Abū Zarʿ, and what is the maidservant of Abū Zarʿ? She does not spread our talk about, she does not waste our provisions, and she does not leave our house filled with rubbish like a nest."

She said: "Abū Zarʿ went out while the milk-skins were being churned and met a woman with two sons of hers like two leopards, playing beneath her waist with two pomegranates. So he divorced me and married her. Afterwards I married a noble man who rode a swift horse and carried a spear. He gave me plentiful livestock and gave me a pair of every kind of animal."
He said: "Eat, Umm Zarʿ, and give provisions to your family." But if I gathered everything he gave me, it would not fill the smallest vessel of Abū Zarʿ.
ʿĀʾishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"I was to you as Abū Zarʿ was to Umm Zarʿ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ—and he mentioned several hadith, among them—the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A woman must not fast while her husband is present except with his permission, and she must not permit anyone into his house while he is present except with his permission. And whatever she spends from his earnings without his instruction, half of its reward is for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I stood at the gate of Paradise, and most of those who entered it were the poor,
while the people of wealth were held back,
except that the people of the Fire had been ordered to the Fire.
And I stood at the gate of the Fire, and most of those who entered it were women."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The blood of a Muslim who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah is not lawful except in one of three cases: a man who commits adultery after being married, for he is stoned; a man who goes out waging war against Allah and His Messenger, for he is killed, or crucified, or banished from the land; or a man who kills a person, for he is killed in retaliation for that person."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If a slave runs away to the land of polytheism, he has no protection.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was leading a blind man, and we came to ʿIkrimah, who began to narrate to us. He said: Ibn ʿAbbās told me that there was a blind man in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who had a concubine who had borne him two sons. She would often slander the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and revile him. He would rebuke her but she would not stop, and he would forbid her but she would not desist. Then one night she mentioned the Prophet ﷺ and slandered him, and I could not bear it: I got up, took a dagger, placed it on her belly and leaned on it until I killed her. In the morning she was found dead, and this was reported to the Prophet ﷺ. He gathered the people and said:
"I adjure by Allah the man who did this, and to whom I have a right, to stand up."

The blind man came forward, stumbling, and said: O Messenger of Allah, I am the one. She was my concubine and was kind and gentle to me, and I have two sons by her like two pearls. But she often slandered you and insulted you. I forbade her but she would not desist, and I rebuked her but she would not stop. Last night she mentioned you and slandered you, so I got up, took the dagger, placed it on her belly and leaned on it until I killed her.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Bear witness that her blood is without penalty."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq when he became angry with one of the Muslims, and his anger against him grew very intense. When I saw that, I said: O Successor of the Messenger of Allah, shall I strike his neck? But when I mentioned killing, he turned away from that talk and turned to other matters. When we dispersed, he sent for me and said: O Abū Barzah, what did you say? I had forgotten what I said. I replied: Remind me.
He said: Do you not remember what you said? I said: No, by Allah.

He said: Do you remember when you saw me angry with a man and you said, "Shall I strike his neck, O Successor of the Messenger of Allah?" Would you have done that? I said: Yes, by Allah, and even now, if you ordered me, I would do it.
He said: By Allah, that is not for anyone after Muhammad ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cut off the hands of those who had stolen his milch camels and gouged out their eyes with fire, Allah the Exalted rebuked him for that and revealed: {The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon the earth to cause corruption is none but that they be killed or crucified...} the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Pardon one another in matters of the prescribed punishments before they reach me, for once a prescribed punishment comes to me, it becomes obligatory."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman

went out in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intending to pray, and a man met her, overpowered her, and satisfied his need with her. She cried out and he left. A man passed by her and she said: That man did such and such to me.
She also passed by a group of the Emigrants and said: That man did such and such to me.
They went and seized the man she thought had assaulted her, and brought him to her. She said: Yes, this is him.

They brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when he ordered that he be stoned, the man who had actually assaulted her stood up and said: O Messenger of Allah, I am the one who did it. So he said to her:
"Go, for Allah has forgiven you."
And he spoke kindly to the man [who was accused], and about the man who had assaulted her he said: "Stone him." And he said:
"He has repented with a repentance that, if the people of Medina repented with it, it would be accepted from them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of people

from the Kalāʿiyyīn had some goods stolen from them, and they accused some weavers. They went to al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ, who imprisoned them for some days and then released them. They came to al-Nuʿmān and said: You released them without beating them or interrogating them.
Al-Nuʿmān said: What do you want? If you wish, I will beat them; if your goods come out, well and good, and if not, I will take from your backs the like of what I took from theirs.
They said: Is this your ruling? He said: This is the ruling of Allah and the ruling of His Messenger ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ mentioned something and said:
"That will be at the time when knowledge disappears."

I said, "O Messenger of Allah, how will knowledge disappear when we recite the Qur'an, and we teach it to our children, and our children will teach it to their children until the Day of Resurrection?" He said:

"May your mother be bereaved of you, Ziyād! I used to consider you one of the most understanding men in Madinah. Do not these Jews and Christians read the Torah and the Gospel, yet they do not act upon anything of what is in them?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Islam will wear away just as the embroidery of a garment wears away, until no one knows what fasting is, nor prayer, nor rites of worship, nor charity. And the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will be taken away in one night, so that not a single verse of it remains on the earth. Groups of people will remain, the old man and the old woman, saying: 'We found our fathers upon this saying, there is no god but Allah, so we say it.'"

Ṣilah said to him, "What will 'there is no god but Allah' avail them, when they do not know what prayer is, nor fasting, nor rites of worship, nor charity?" Ḥudhayfah turned away from him. Then he repeated it to him three times, and each time Ḥudhayfah turned away from him. Then in the third time he turned to him and said, "O Ṣilah, it will save them from the Fire," three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wants to destroy a servant, He removes modesty from him. When modesty is removed from him, you will meet him only as hateful and hated. When you meet him only as hateful and hated, trustworthiness is removed from him. When trustworthiness is removed from him, you will meet him only as a traitor and distrusted. When you meet him only as a traitor and distrusted, mercy is removed from him. When mercy is removed from him, you will meet him only as accursed and cast out. When you meet him only as accursed and cast out, the bond of Islam is removed from his neck."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The signs come after the two hundred."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My Ummah is of five generations. For forty years they will be people of righteousness and piety. Then those who follow them, up to one hundred and twenty years, will be people of mutual compassion and good family ties. Then those who follow them, up to one hundred and sixty years, will be people of turning away from one another and severing ties. Then comes chaos, chaos! Escape, escape!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took me to a place in the desert near Makkah, and there was dry ground surrounded by sand. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Beast will come out from this place."
Then there was a gap of a handspan.
Ibn Buraydah said: Some years after that I performed Hajj, and he showed us his staff, and it was about the size of this staff of mine, such and such.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Toward the west, before the setting of the sun, there is an open door, its width being seventy years. That door will remain open for repentance until the sun rises from its direction. When it rises from there, no soul will benefit from its faith, if it had not believed before or earned some good through its faith."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I bear witness that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the land is Allah's land and the servants are Allah's servants, and whoever revives dead land has the greater right to it. This came to us from the Prophet ﷺ through those who brought us the prayers from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever builds a wall around a piece of land, it is his."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hishām said: The unjust root is when a man plants in another person's land and thereby claims it as his own.
Mālik said: The unjust root is anything taken, dug, or planted without right.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went on the expedition to Tabūk with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When he came to Wādī al-Qurā, there was a woman in her garden. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions, "Estimate [its yield]."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ estimated ten wasqs, and he said to the woman, "
Keep count of what it yields."

Then we came to Tabūk, and the king of Aylah gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a white mule as a gift, clothed him with a cloak, and wrote to him—meaning—[confirming his authority] over his coastal region.
He said: When we came back to Wādī al-Qurā, he said to the woman, "
How much was in your garden?"
She said, "Ten wasqs, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ estimated."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
I am hurrying to Medina, so whoever of you wishes to hurry with me, let him hurry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She used to delouse the head of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while the wife of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān and some of the Emigrant women were with him. They were complaining about their houses, that they were becoming cramped for them and they were being made to leave them. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that the houses of the Emigrants be inherited by the women. Then ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd died, and his wife inherited a house in Medina.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever ties the jizyah around his neck has disowned what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stands upon.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "

Whoever takes land with its jizyah has asked to be released from his emigration, and whoever removes the humiliation of a disbeliever from his neck and puts it on his own neck has turned his back on Islam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said, "
On buried treasure is the fifth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Buried treasure (rikāz) is ancient treasure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When we went out with him to Ṭāʾif, we passed by a grave, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "

This is the grave of Abū Righāl. He was in this Sanctuary, and was protected by it. When he left, the punishment that struck his people at this place struck him, and he was buried here. A sign of this is that a branch of gold was buried with him; if you dig him up, you will find it with him."
So the people rushed to it and dug out the branch.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the people of Syria, called Abū Manṭūr, from his paternal uncle,
who said: My uncle narrated to me,
from ʿĀmir ar-Rām,

the brother of al-Khiḍr—Abū Dāwūd said: an-Nufaylī said it was al-Khiḍr, but this is how he said it—He said: I was in our land when banners and flags were raised before us. I said, "What is this?" They said, "This is the banner of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." So I came to him while he was under a tree, with a cloak spread for him, sitting on it, with his Companions gathered around him. I sat with them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned illnesses and said, "

When a believer is afflicted with illness and then Allah relieves him of it, it is an expiation for his past sins and an admonition for him regarding the future. And when a hypocrite becomes ill and then is relieved, he is like a camel whose family tied it up and then released it; it does not know why they tied it nor why they released it."
A man among those around him said, "O Messenger of Allah, what are illnesses? By Allah, I have never been ill."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Get up and leave us, for you are not one of us."

While we were with him, a man came wearing a cloak, with something wrapped up in his hand. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, when I saw you I was coming toward you, and I passed a thicket of trees and heard the voices of chicks of a bird. I took them and put them in my cloak. Their mother came and circled above my head. I uncovered them for her, and she fell upon them with them, so I wrapped them in my cloak, and here they are with me." He said, "Put them down."
So I put them down, but their mother refused anything except to stay with them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions, "
Are you amazed at the mother of the chicks' mercy for her chicks?"
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said, "

By the One who sent me with the truth, Allah is more merciful to His servants than the mother of chicks is to her chicks. Go back with them until you put them down where you took them from, with their mother alongside them." So he went back with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Love Allah for the blessings with which He nourishes you, love me out of love for Allah, and love the people of my household out of love for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"What an excellent man is Abū Bakr; what an excellent man is ʿUmar; what an excellent man is Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ; what an excellent man is Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr; what an excellent man is Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās; what an excellent man is Muʿādh ibn Jabal; what an excellent man is Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Paradise longs for three: ʿAlī, ʿAmmār, and Salmān."
This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith; we do not know it except from the narration of al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When death came to Muʿādh ibn Jabal, it was said to him: "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, give us advice." He said: "Sit me up."

Then he said: "Knowledge and faith have their places; whoever seeks them will find them," saying that three times. "Seek knowledge from four men: from ʿUwaymir Abū al-Dardāʾ, from Salmān al-Fārisī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, and from ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām, who was a Jew and then embraced Islam. For I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'He is the tenth of ten in Paradise.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Follow the two who come after me from among my Companions, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; be guided by the guidance of ʿAmmār; and hold fast to the covenant of Ibn Masʿūd."
This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith from this route, from the narration of Ibn Masʿūd; we do not know it except from the narration of Yaḥyā ibn Salamah ibn Kuhayl.

Yaḥyā ibn Salamah is considered weak in hadith. Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ is named ʿAbdullāh ibn Hāniʾ. The Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ from whom Shuʿbah, al-Thawrī and Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated is named ʿAmr ibn ʿAmr; he is the son of the brother of Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, the companion of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Madinah and asked Allah to grant me a righteous companion to sit with. He granted me Abū Hurayrah, so I sat with him and said to him: "I asked Allah to grant me a righteous companion to sit with, and I was guided to you."
He said to me: "Where are you from?" I said: "From the people of Kufa; I have come seeking goodness and pursuing it."

He said: "Do you not have among you Saʿd ibn Mālik, whose supplication is answered; Ibn Masʿūd, the keeper of the purification water and sandals of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; Ḥudhayfah, the keeper of the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; ʿAmmār, whom Allah protected from the Devil upon the tongue of His Prophet; and Salmān, the possessor of the two Books?"
Qatādah said: The two Books are the Injīl and the Qurʾān.
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb hadith.
Khaythamah is the son of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Sabrah; he is attributed to his grandfather.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would appoint a successor." He said:
"If I appointed a successor over you and you disobeyed him, you would be punished. But whatever Ḥudhayfah tells you, believe it, and whatever ʿAbdullāh teaches you to recite, recite it."
ʿAbdullāh said: I said to Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā: "They say this is from Abū Wāʾil."
He said: "No, it is from Zādhān, if Allah wills."
This is a ḥasan hadith, and it is the hadith of Sharīk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He assigned Usāmah ibn Zayd a stipend of three thousand five hundred, and assigned ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar three thousand. ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said to his father: "Why did you favor Usāmah over me? By Allah, he never preceded me to any battle."

He said: "Because Zayd was more beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than your father, and Usāmah was more beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than you; so I preferred the love of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over my own love."
This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The brother of Zayd said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, send my brother Zayd with me." He said: "Here he is." Then he said:
"If he goes with you, I will not prevent him."
Zayd said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I choose no one over you."
He said: I saw that my brother's opinion was better than mine.
This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith; we do not know it except from the narration of Ibn al-Rūmī from ʿAlī ibn Mushir.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became gravely ill, I came down, and the people came down to Madinah. I went in to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and my speech had been cut off, so I could not speak. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to place his hands on me and raise them, and I knew that he was making supplication for me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Badr, when the Prophet ﷺ took ransom, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has become dominant in the land" up to His saying: "you would have been touched by a great punishment for what you took", meaning the ransom. Then Allah made the spoils of war lawful for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ set the ransom of the people of the Jāhiliyyah on the day of Badr at four hundred.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the people of Makkah sent to ransom their captives, Zaynab sent money to ransom Abū al-ʿĀṣ, and she sent with it a necklace of hers that had belonged to Khadījah, who had given it to her when she took her to Abū al-ʿĀṣ [in marriage].
She said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw it, he was moved with deep compassion for her, and he said:
"If you see fit to release her captive for her and return to her what is hers [then do so]." They said: Yes.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had taken from him a pledge, or he had promised him, that he would let Zaynab go to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Zayd ibn Ḥārithah and a man from the Anṣār, and said:
"Stay in the valley of Yājaj until Zaynab passes by you, then accompany her until you bring her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He separated a slave girl from her child, so the Prophet ﷺ forbade him from that and annulled the sale.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A slave of Ibn ʿUmar
ran away to the enemy. The Muslims then overcame them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned him to Ibn ʿUmar and did not distribute him [as spoils].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two slaves went out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, meaning on the day of Ḥudaybiyah, before the treaty. Their masters wrote to him, saying: "O Muḥammad, by Allah, they did not come out to you out of desire for your religion; they only came out to flee from slavery." Some people said: "They speak the truth, O Messenger of Allah; return them to them."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry and said:
"I do not see you ceasing, O assembly of Quraysh, until Allah sends against you someone who will strike your necks over this."
And he refused to return them, and said:
"They are those freed by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: An army
took as spoils food and honey in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the fifth was not taken from them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samurah in Kabul, and the people obtained spoils and plundered them. He stood up to give a speech and said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid plundering.
So they returned what they had taken, and he distributed it among them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: Did you take the fifth, meaning of food, in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: We obtained food on the day of Khaybar, and a man would come and take from it as much as sufficed him, then leave.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from the Anṣār said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and the people were afflicted with severe need and hardship. They got some sheep and plundered them, while our pots were boiling. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, walking on his bow, and overturned our pots with his bow. Then he began to cover the meat with dust, and then said:
"Plundered goods are no more lawful than carrion," or:
"Carrion is no more lawful than plundered goods."
The doubt is from Hannād.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Companion of the Prophet ﷺ said: We used to eat carrots on campaign and not distribute them, so much so that we would return to our saddles and our bags were full of them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were stationed at the frontier at the city of Qinnasrīn with Shuraḥbīl ibn al-Simṭ. When he conquered it, he obtained sheep and cattle there; he distributed a portion of them among us and placed the rest in the common spoils. I met Muʿādh ibn Jabal and told him, and Muʿādh said: We went on a campaign with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Khaybar and obtained sheep there; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ distributed a portion among us and placed the rest in the common spoils.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Dāwūd said: And I am more precise in his narration,
more precise. Both said: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us,
from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq,
from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb,
from Abū Marzūq,
the freed slave of Tujīb, from Ḥanash al-Ṣanʿānī,
from Ruwayfiʿ ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī,
that the Prophet ﷺ said:

"Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should not ride an animal from the spoils of the Muslims until, when he has made it lean, he returns it to it; and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should not wear a garment from the spoils of the Muslims until, when he has worn it out, he returns it to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jaʿfar, from Nāfiʿ, from Ṣafiyyah, from Ḥafṣah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, that he would pray the two units of prayer of the dawn prayer, making them two brief units.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said concerning the two units of prayer at the break of dawn:
"They are more beloved to me than the whole world."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, many a time,

what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would recite in the two units of the dawn prayer was: {We believe in Allah and what has been sent down to us} — this verse. He said: This was in the first unit; and in the last unit: {We believe in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah: "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite a whole sūrah in a single unit of prayer?" She said: "The Mufaṣṣal [sūrahs]."
He said: I said, "Did he pray sitting?" She said: "When the people had worn him down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd,
from al-Muṭṭalib ibn Abī Wadāʿah al-Sahmī, from Ḥafṣah,

that she said: "I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray his voluntary prayer sitting, until a year before his death; then he would pray his voluntary prayer sitting, and he would recite a sūrah and recite it so slowly and distinctly that it became longer than one that was longer than it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A man's prayer while sitting is half the prayer."

He said: Then I came to him and found him praying sitting down, so I placed my hand on his head. He said, "What is the matter with you, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr?" I said, "I was told, O Messenger of Allah, that you said:
'A man's prayer while sitting is half the prayer,'
and yet you pray sitting?" He said:
"Yes, but I am not like any of you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray thirteen units of prayer at night, of which he would pray five as the Witr,
not sitting in any of the five until he sat in the last one, and then he would give the salām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked ʿĀʾishah about the prayer of

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at night. She said: "He would pray thirteen units: nine units standing, in which he would pray the Witr, and two units sitting. When he wished to bow, he would stand up, then bow and prostrate. He would do that after the Witr. Then when he heard the call of the dawn, he would stand and pray two brief units."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to Jābir, meaning Ibn ʿAbdullāh, and he said: I travelled with the Prophet ﷺ on a campaign. He stood to pray, and I was wearing a cloak. I tried to cross its two ends over one another, but it was not long enough for me, and it had tassels, so I turned it upside down. Then I crossed its two ends and held them with my chin so that it would not fall. Then I came and stood at the left of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He took me by my hand and turned me around until he made me stand at his right. Then Ibn Ṣakhr came and stood at his left, and he took both of us by the hands until he made us stand behind him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to watch me without my noticing. Then I realized it, and he signalled to me to wrap it around my waist as a waist-wrapper. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished, he said: "O Jābir."
He said: I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"If it is wide, cross its two ends over one another, and if it is narrow, tie it around your waist."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, or he said that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

"If one of you has two garments, let him pray in both of them. If he has only one garment, let him wrap it around his waist as a waist-wrapper, and let him not wrap himself in it the way the Jews do."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbaydullāh al-ʿAtakī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Buraydah, from his father,
said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade praying in a blanket that one does not wrap over the shoulders, and the other [prohibition was] praying in trousers while having no cloak on.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever lets his lower garment hang down in his prayer out of arrogance has no standing with Allah, in what is permitted or what is forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While a man was praying with his lower garment hanging down, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Go and perform ablution."
So he went and performed ablution, then came back. Then he said: "Go and perform ablution."
So he went and performed ablution, then came back. A man said to him: O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with you that you ordered him to perform ablution? He said:
"He was praying with his lower garment hanging down, and Allah, the Exalted, does not accept the prayer of a man whose lower garment hangs down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She asked Umm Salamah: In what garments may a woman pray? She said: She may pray in a head-covering and a full-length garment that covers the tops of her feet.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿĀʾishah

stayed with Ṣafiyyah, the mother of Ṭalḥah al-Ṭalaḥāt, and saw some daughters of hers. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered while there was a young girl in my room, and he threw me his waist-wrapper and said:

"Tear it into two pieces, and give half to this girl and half to the girl who is with Umm Salamah, for I think she has surely reached puberty," or, "I think that both of them have surely reached puberty."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade letting the garment hang down loosely in prayer, and a man covering his mouth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Most of the time that I saw ʿAṭāʾ, he would pray with his garment hanging down loosely.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was leading his Companions in prayer, he took off his sandals and placed them on his left. When the people saw that, they threw off their sandals. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer, he said:
"What made you throw off your sandals?"
They said: We saw you throw off your sandals, so we threw off ours.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Jibrīl, peace be upon him, came to me and told me that there was filth on them." And he said:
"When one of you comes to the mosque, let him look. If he sees filth or harm on his sandals, let him wipe it off and pray in them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, with this [report], he said: "filth" was on them.
He said "filth" in both places.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Be different from the Jews, for they do not pray in their sandals or their leather socks."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When one of you prays, let him not put his sandals on his right or on his left, for then they would be on the right of someone else, unless there is nobody on his left. Let him put them between his feet."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you prays and takes off his sandals, let him not harm anyone with them. Let him put them between his feet, or let him pray in them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to visit Umm Sulaym, and the time of prayer would sometimes come upon him, and he would pray on a mat of ours, which was a woven mat that we sprinkled with water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray on a mat and on a tanned sheepskin.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Abū Hurayrah], may Allah be pleased with him, said: When people saw the first fruit of the season, they would bring it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it, he would say: "

O Allah, bless us in our fruits, bless us in our city, and bless us in our ṣāʿ and our mudd. O Allah, Ibrahim is Your servant, Your intimate friend, and Your prophet, and I am Your servant and Your prophet. He called upon You for Makkah, and I call upon You for Madinah with the like of what he called upon You for Makkah, and the like of it along with it."
Then he would call the youngest child he saw and give him that fruit.
He said: This is a good and sound hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the first fruit was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would say: "
O Allah, bless us in our city, in our fruits, in our mudd and in our ṣāʿ, blessing upon blessing."
Then he would hand it to the youngest of the children present with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Qaṭan ibn Wahb ibn ʿUwaymir ibn
al-Ajdaʿ, from Yuḥannas,
the freed slave of az-Zubayr, who informed him that he
was sitting with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar during the time of the trial, when a freed slave woman of his came to greet him and said: I want to leave, O Abū ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān; the times have become hard on us.
ʿAbdullāh said to her: Stay put, you foolish woman, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
No one will be patient through its hardship and severity except that I will be a witness or an intercessor for him on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A prayer in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the last of the prophets and his mosque is the last of the mosques.

Abū Salamah and Abū ʿAbdullāh said: We had no doubt that Abū Hurayrah was relating this from the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but that prevented us from asking Abū Hurayrah to confirm that hadith. When Abū Hurayrah died, we discussed it and blamed one another for not having spoken to Abū Hurayrah about it so that he would trace it back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, if he had heard it from him. While we were in that state, we sat with ʿAbdullāh ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Qāriẓ and mentioned that hadith and our failure regarding Abū Hurayrah's explicit statement of it. ʿAbdullāh ibn Ibrāhīm said to us: I bear witness that I heard Abū Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
I am the last of the prophets and my mosque is the last of the mosques."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that his father

took part with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the conquest of Makkah. He said: We stayed there fifteen days—thirty, counting nights and days—and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted us temporary marriage with women. So I and a man from my people went out; I had the advantage over him in looks, while he was close to being unattractive. Each of us had a cloak: my cloak was worn out, while my cousin's cloak was new and fresh. When we were at the lower or upper part of Makkah, we met a young woman, tall and slender like a young she-camel. We said: Would you be willing for one of us to have temporary marriage with you? She said: What will you give? So each of us spread out his cloak, and she began looking at the two men, while my companion saw her looking at his side. He said: This one's cloak is worn out, and my cloak is new and fresh.
She would say: This one's cloak is not bad,
three times or twice. Then I had temporary marriage with her, and I did not leave until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Farewell Hajj, and they said: O Messenger of Allah, being unmarried has become very hard on us. He said: "
Then have temporary marriage with these women."
So we went to them, but they refused to marry us unless we set a fixed term between us and them. They mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "
Set a term between you and them."
So I went out with a cousin of mine. He had a cloak and I had a cloak, and his cloak was better than mine, while I was younger than he. We came to a woman, and she said: A cloak like a cloak.
So I married her and stayed with her that night. Then in the morning I went out, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing between the Corner and the door, saying: "

O people, I had permitted you temporary marriage, but now Allah has forbidden it until the Day of Resurrection. So whoever has any of these women with him, let him let her go, and do not take back anything of what you have given them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Who do you count as the childless one (al-raqūb) among you?"
We said: "The one who has no children born to him." He said:
"That is not the raqūb, rather he is the man who has not sent ahead any of his children." He said:
"And who do you count as the strong wrestler among you?"
We said: "The one whom men cannot throw down." He said:
"That is not so, rather he is the one who controls himself when angry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should say: 'My soul has become wicked.'
Rather let him say: 'My soul has become troubled.'"
This is the narration of Abū Kurayb. Abū Bakr said: from the Prophet ﷺ, and he did not mention "rather."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Zaynab
had been named Barrah, so it was said that she was declaring herself pure.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named her Zaynab.
The wording of the hadith is that of these narrators, not Ibn Bashshār.
And Ibn Abī Shaybah said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us from Shuʿbah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When there are three, two should not converse privately to the exclusion of the third."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed, I will precede you to the Pool, and I will take pride in your numbers before the other nations, so do not fight one another after me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That she wanted to buy
Barīrah, but her owners stipulated that the walāʾ would be theirs. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Buy her, for walāʾ belongs only to the one who pays the price," or "to the one who bestows the favor."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not give preference among the prophets."
And in the narration of Ibn Numayr: ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā, my father narrated to me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he entered upon al-Ḥajjāj, who said: "O Ibn al-Akwaʿ, have you turned back on your heels and become a Bedouin again?" He said: "No, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted me to live in the desert."
And from Yazīd ibn Abī ʿUbayd, who said: When ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān was killed, Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ went out to al-Rabadhah,
and he married a woman there, and she bore him children,
and he stayed there until a few nights before he died, when he came down to Medina.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave and from the trial of the Dajjāl. He said, and he ﷺ said:
"You will be tested in your graves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever completes the ablution as Allah the Exalted commanded him, then the obligatory prayers are expiations for what is between them."
This is the narration of Ibn Muʿādh. In the narration of Ghundar there is no mention of the governorship of Bishr, nor of the obligatory prayers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I was listening,
and the wording is his, from Ibn Wahb,
from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from Bukayr,
that Abū al-Sāʾib informed him that he
heard Abū Hurayrah
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should bathe in standing water while in a state of janābah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān used to begin the recitation with "Al-ḥamdu lillāhi rabbil-ʿālamīn." Abū ʿĪsā said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.

The practice according to this among the people of knowledge from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, the Successors and those after them was that they would begin the recitation with "Al-ḥamdu lillāhi rabbil-ʿālamīn."

Al-Shāfiʿī said: The meaning of this hadith is that the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān used to begin the recitation with "Al-ḥamdu lillāhi rabbil-ʿālamīn," meaning that they would begin by reciting the Opening of the Book before the sūrah. It does not mean that they did not recite "Bismillāh ir-Raḥmān ir-Raḥīm."
Al-Shāfiʿī held that one should begin with "Bismillāh ir-Raḥmān ir-Raḥīm" and recite it aloud when reciting aloud.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Misʿar,
and al-Bakhtarī ibn al-Mukhtār,
heard it from Abū Bakr ibn ʿUmārah ibn Ruʾaybah, from his father,
who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"No one who prays before the rising of the sun and before its setting will ever enter the Fire."
He meant the Fajr and ʿAṣr prayers.
A man from the people of Basra said to him: "Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Yes."
The man said: "And I bear witness that I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; my two ears heard it and my heart retained it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When revelation came down upon the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, it would distress him and his face would darken. He said: One day it was revealed to him and he experienced the same; and when it was lifted from him, he said:

"Take it from me. Allah has made a way for them: the previously married with the previously married, and the unmarried with the unmarried. For the previously married, one hundred lashes and then stoning with stones; and for the unmarried, one hundred lashes and then banishment for a year."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar passed by some youths of Quraysh who had set up a bird as a target and were shooting at it, having agreed that the owner of the bird would get every arrow of theirs that missed. When they saw Ibn ʿUmar, they scattered. Ibn ʿUmar said: "Who did this? May Allah curse whoever did this. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed whoever takes a living thing as a target."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿīd, the freed slave of ʿĀmir ibn Kurayz, from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do not envy one another, do not artificially bid up prices against one another, do not hate one another, do not turn away from one another, and do not undercut one another in a sale; and be servants of Allah, brothers.
The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not wrong him, does not forsake him, and does not despise him.
Piety is right here."
And he pointed to his chest three times. [Then he said:]
"It is enough evil for a person to despise his Muslim brother. Every Muslim is sacred to every Muslim: his blood, his wealth, and his honor."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And she was
married to the son of Abū Qatādah, when Abū Qatādah came in to see her.

She said: I poured out water for his ablution. She said: Then a cat came to drink, and he tilted the vessel for it until it drank. Kabshah said: He saw me looking at him and said, "Are you surprised, my niece?" I said, "Yes."
He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not impure. It is one of those who go around among you, male or female."

This is the view of most of the scholars among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, the Successors, and those after them, such as al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad and Isḥāq: they saw no harm in the leftover water of a cat.
And this is the best thing reported on this subject.
Mālik transmitted this hadith excellently from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, and no one brought it more completely than Mālik.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he prostrated, place his knees before his hands, and when he rose, raise his hands before his knees.
He said: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī added in his narration: Yazīd ibn Hārūn said, "Sharīk did not narrate from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb anything except this hadith."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my father is a very old man who cannot perform Hajj, ʿUmrah, or travel." He said:
"Perform Hajj and ʿUmrah on behalf of your father."
Abū ʿĪsā said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
ʿUmrah is mentioned from the Prophet ﷺ in this hadith only [to show] that a man may perform ʿUmrah on behalf of another.
And Abū Razīn al-ʿUqaylī's name is Laqīṭ ibn ʿĀmir.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Muḥammad,
the two sons of Abū Bakr, from their father,
from Abū al-Baddāḥ ibn ʿAdī, from his father,
that the Prophet ﷺ gave permission to the shepherds to throw [the pebbles] on one day and leave off the next.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAwn, Salamah ibn ʿAlqamah, and Hishām ibn Ḥassān – the narrations of some of them merge into others – from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn,
Salamah said, from Ibn Sīrīn:
I was informed from Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ,
and the others said, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn,
from Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ,

who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: Beware! Do not inflate women's dowries, for if it were an honor in this world or piety in the sight of Allah, the most deserving of you of it would be the Prophet ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not give any of his wives a dowry, nor was any of his daughters given one, of more than twelve ūqiyahs. A man may inflate his wife's dowry until it becomes enmity toward her in his heart, and he says, "I went through the burden of the water-skin strap for you." I was an Arab-born boy of mixed origin, and I did not know what "the water-skin strap" meant. He said: And there is another thing you say about one who is killed in your campaigns or dies: "So-and-so was killed a martyr," or "So-and-so died a martyr," when perhaps he had loaded the back of his mount or the saddle of his riding animal with gold or silver, seeking trade. So do not say that, but say as the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever is killed in the cause of Allah, or dies, will be in Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And the wording:

The hadith of Maʿmar, from the narration of ʿAbd and Ibn Rāfiʿ—Yūnus and Maʿmar both said—from al-Zuhrī: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqāṣ and ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd informed me, from the hadith of ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, when the people of the slander said about her what they said, and Allah cleared her of what they said. Each of them related to me a portion of her account, and some of them were better at retaining her account and more precise in relating it; and I retained from each one of them the account he told me, and some of their accounts confirm others. They mentioned that ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to set out on a journey, he would draw lots among his wives, and whichever of them her lot came out, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would take her with him. ʿĀʾishah said: He drew lots among us for a military expedition he undertook, and my lot came out, so I set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. That was after the hijāb had been revealed. I was carried in my howdah and set down in it during our journey. Then, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished his expedition and returned, and we drew near Medina, he gave notice one night to march on. I got up when they gave notice to march and walked until I had passed the army. When I had relieved myself, I came back to my mount and touched my chest, and behold, my necklace of Ẓafār beads had broken. So I went back and searched for my necklace, and the search for it detained me. The group who used to saddle my camel for me came and lifted my howdah and placed it on my camel which I used to ride, thinking that I was in it. She said: Women in those days were light; they were not heavy and flesh had not covered them, for they ate only a little food. So the people did not find the weight of the howdah strange when they lifted it and raised it. And I was a young girl. They set the camel moving and went on. I found my necklace after the army had gone. I came to their camp, and there was no one calling and no one answering. So I made for the place where I had been, thinking that they would miss me and return to me. While I was sitting in my place, sleep overcame me and I slept. Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal al-Sulamī, then al-Dhakwānī, had stopped to rest behind the army for the night and then travelled before dawn, and in the morning he reached my place. He saw the figure of a sleeping person and came to me, and he recognised me when he saw me, for he used to see me before the hijāb was imposed on me. I woke up at his saying “Innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rājiʿūn” when he recognised me, and I covered my face with my cloak. By Allah, he did not say a word to me, and I heard no word from him other than his saying “innā lillāh,” until he made his camel kneel and stepped on its foreleg, and I mounted it. Then he set off leading the camel with me on it until we reached the army, after they had halted at the height of noon in the scorching heat. Then those who were destined to perish perished concerning my affair, and the one who took the greatest part in it was ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl. We reached Medina, and I was ill for a month after we reached Medina, while the people spread the words of the people of the slander, and I knew nothing of that. What made me doubtful during my illness was that I did not find from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the kindness I used to see from him when I was ill. He would only enter, give the greeting of peace, and then say: “How is that one?”

That made me doubtful, but I was unaware of the evil, until I went out after I had begun to recover, and Umm Misṭaḥ went out with me toward al-Manāṣiʿ, which was where we relieved ourselves, and we would not go out except from night to night. That was before we had built latrines near our houses; our custom was that of the early Arabs in going out to open places, and we found it distasteful to have latrines near our houses. So Umm Misṭaḥ and I set out—she was the daughter of Abū Ruhm ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manāf, and her mother was the daughter of Ṣakhr ibn ʿĀmir, the maternal aunt of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, and her son was Misṭaḥ ibn Uthāthah ibn ʿAbbād ibn al-Muṭṭalib. I and the daughter of Abū Ruhm were returning to my house when we had finished our business, and Umm Misṭaḥ tripped over her wrap and said: “May Misṭaḥ be ruined!”
I said to her: “What an evil thing you have said! Do you curse a man who took part in Badr?”

She said: “O you naive one, have you not heard what he said?” I said: “And what did he say?” She said: Then she told me what the people of the slander were saying, and my illness increased upon my illness. When I returned to my house, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me, greeted me, and then said: “How is that one?”
I said: “Will you permit me to go to my parents?” She said: I wanted at that time to confirm the news from them.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me permission, so I went to my parents and said to my mother: “O Mother, what are the people talking about?” She said: “My dear daughter, take it easy, for by Allah, rarely has there been a beautiful woman with a husband who loves her and who has co-wives, but that they make much of it against her.” I said: “Glory be to Allah! Are the people really talking about this?” She said: So I wept that night until morning, my tears would not cease and I had no sleep. Then morning came and I was still weeping. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Usāmah ibn Zayd, when the revelation was delayed, to consult them about parting from his wife. She said: As for Usāmah ibn Zayd, he advised the Messenger of Allah ﷺ according to what he knew of his wife's innocence and what he knew in himself of affection for them. He said: “O Messenger of Allah, they are your family, and we know only good.”

As for ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: “Allah has not placed a restriction on you, and there are many women besides her; and if you ask the slave girl, she will tell you the truth.” She said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Barīrah and said:
“O Barīrah, have you seen anything that makes you doubt about ʿĀʾishah?”

Barīrah said to him: “By the One who sent you with the truth, I have never seen anything in her that I would hold against her, other than that she is a young girl who sleeps through her family's dough, and then the domestic animal comes and eats it.” She said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up on the pulpit and asked for support against ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said while on the pulpit:

“O company of Muslims, who will excuse me regarding a man whose harm has reached my family? By Allah, I know nothing about my family except good, and they have mentioned a man about whom I know nothing but good, and he never entered upon my family except with me.”

Saʿd ibn Muʿādh al-Anṣārī stood up and said: “I will excuse you from him, O Messenger of Allah. If he is from the Aws, we will strike his neck, and if he is from our brothers the Khazraj, you command us and we will carry out your command.” She said: Then Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah stood up, and he was the chief of the Khazraj; he had been a righteous man, but tribal zeal carried him away. He said to Saʿd ibn Muʿādh: “You have lied, by the everlasting life of Allah! You will not kill him, and you are not able to kill him.”

Then Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr, who was the cousin of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, stood up and said to Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah: “You have lied, by the everlasting life of Allah! We will surely kill him, for you are a hypocrite, arguing on behalf of the hypocrites.” The two tribes, the Aws and the Khazraj, rose up until they were about to fight one another, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing on the pulpit. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept calming them until they fell silent, and he fell silent. She said: I wept that day of mine, my tears would not cease and I had no sleep; then I wept the following night, my tears would not cease and I had no sleep, and my parents thought that the weeping would split my liver. While they were sitting with me and I was weeping, a woman of the Anṣār asked permission to enter, so I let her in, and she sat weeping. She said: While we were in that state, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to us, greeted us, and sat down. She said: He had not sat with me since what was said about me was said, and he had stayed a month without any revelation coming to him concerning my matter. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the testimony of faith when he sat, and then said:

“To proceed: O ʿĀʾishah, it has reached me about you such and such. If you are innocent, Allah will soon declare your innocence; and if you have committed a sin, then seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him, for when a servant confesses a sin and then repents, Allah accepts his repentance.”

She said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished his speech, my tears dried up until I felt not a drop of them. I said to my father: “Answer the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on my behalf concerning what he said.”

He said: “By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” Then I said to my mother: “Answer the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on my behalf.” She said: “By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” So I said, and I was a young girl who had not read much of the Qur'an: “By Allah, I know that you have heard this until it settled in your souls and you believed it. So if I tell you that I am innocent, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will not believe me in that; and if I confess to you a matter, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will believe me. By Allah, I find no likeness for myself and you except what the father of Yūsuf said: ‘So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe.’”

She said: Then I turned away and lay down on my bed. She said: By Allah, I knew at that time that I was innocent and that Allah would declare my innocence; but by Allah, I did not think that a revelation that would be recited would be sent down about my affair. My own affair was too insignificant in my own eyes for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to speak about me in a matter that would be recited. But I hoped that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would see a dream in his sleep by which Allah would clear me. She said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not left his seat, and no one of the household had gone out, when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down revelation upon His Prophet ﷺ, and there came over him the distress that used to come over him at the time of revelation, so that drops of sweat like pearls would run down from him on a wintry day because of the weight of the word that was being revealed to him. She said: When it was lifted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he was smiling, and the first word he spoke was:
“Rejoice, O ʿĀʾishah! As for Allah, He has declared you innocent.”

My mother said to me: “Get up and go to him.” I said: “By Allah, I will not get up to him, and I will praise none but Allah; He is the One who sent down my innocence.” She said: Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you}—ten verses. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down these verses declaring my innocence. She said: Abū Bakr, who used to spend on Misṭaḥ because of his kinship to him and his poverty, said: “By Allah, I will never spend anything on him again after what he said about ʿĀʾishah.”

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin}, up to His saying: {Would you not love that Allah should forgive you?} Ḥabbān ibn Mūsā said: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak said: This is the most hope-inspiring verse in the Book of Allah.
Abū Bakr said: “By Allah, I certainly love that Allah forgive me.”
So he restored to Misṭaḥ the spending that he used to spend on him, and said: “I will never take it away from him.”
ʿĀʾishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had asked Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, about my affair:
“What do you know, or what have you seen?”
She said: “O Messenger of Allah, I protect my hearing and my sight. By Allah, I know nothing but good.”

ʿĀʾishah said: She was the one among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ who used to compete with me, but Allah protected her through her piety. Her sister Ḥamnah bint Jaḥsh went on fighting on her behalf, and she perished among those who perished.
Al-Zuhrī said: This is what has reached us about the affair of these group of men.
And in the hadith of Yūnus he said: “Tribal zeal carried him away.”
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ghumayṣāʾ,

or ar-Rumayṣāʾ, came to the Prophet ﷺ complaining about her husband, that he did not have relations with her. Before long her husband came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, she is lying. He does have relations with her, but she wants to return to her first husband."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not so, until you taste his sweetness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to him and said, "I have made my wife forbidden to me."

He said, "You have lied. She is not forbidden to you." Then he recited this verse: {O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?} "The severest expiation is upon you: freeing a slave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My wife and I were both slaves,

and I divorced her with two divorces. Then we were both freed. I asked Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said, "If you take her back, she will be with you with one [divorce remaining]." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled thus. Maʿmar disagreed with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qurayẓah: that they were presented to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Qurayẓah. Whoever had reached puberty or had grown pubic hair was killed, and whoever had not reached puberty or had not grown pubic hair was left alone.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a Persian neighbor who made good broth. One day he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while ʿĀʾishah was with him. He gestured with his hand to invite him to come, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gestured toward ʿĀʾishah, meaning, "And this one too?" The other gestured with his hand like this, meaning no, twice or three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We discussed the month in his presence, and some of us said, "Thirty."
And some of us said, "Twenty-nine."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man made ẓihār from his wife, then had relations with her before making expiation. This was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"What made you do that?"
He said, "May Allah have mercy on you, O Messenger of Allah, I saw her anklet," or her shins, "in the moonlight."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Keep away from her until you do what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"Women who seek to be released from their marriages and women who seek khulʿ are the hypocrites."
Al-Ḥasan said, "I did not hear it from anyone other than Abū Hurayrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had al-ʿAjlānī and his wife carry out liʿān, and she was pregnant.
label: machine translation
