The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only forbade the muṣfarah, the mustaʾṣalah, the bakhqāʾ, the mushayyiʿah and the kasrāʾ. The muṣfarah is the one whose ear is cut off so that its ear-hole shows; the mustaʾṣalah is the one whose horn is cut off from its root; the bakhqāʾ is the one whose eye is put out; the mushayyiʿah is the one that cannot follow the sheep because of leanness and weakness; and the kasrāʾ is the one with a broken leg."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, "What is the aʿḍab?" He said, "Half or more of the horn [broken off]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: {So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned} and {do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned} — this was abrogated, and an exception was made from it, for He said: {And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade eating the food of the muʿāqarah of the Bedouins.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] from Banū Ḥārithah was grazing a milch she-camel in one of the mountain paths of Uḥud when death overtook her. He found nothing with which to slaughter her, so he took a peg and stabbed her in the throat until her blood flowed. Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of that, and he commanded him to eat it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sharīṭah of the devil.
Ibn ʿĪsā added in his narration: It is the animal that is slaughtered, the skin is cut but the jugular veins are not severed, and then it is left until it dies.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us [to give] one sheep for every fifty sheep.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Leave the birds in their nesting places."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were on a journey with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I was on a water-carrying camel that was at the very back of the people. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck it, or he said: he prodded it, I think he said, with something that he had with him. After that it began to go ahead of the people, pulling against me so that I had to hold it back. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Will you sell it to me for such and such [a price]? And may Allah forgive you."
He said: I said, "It is yours, O Prophet of Allah." He said:
"Will you sell it to me for such and such [a price]? And may Allah forgive you."
He said: I said, "It is yours, O Prophet of Allah."
He said: And he said to me:
"Have you married after your father [died]?" I said, "Yes." He said:
"A previously married woman or a virgin?"
He said: I said, "A previously married woman." He said:
"Why did you not marry a virgin, so that you could laugh with her and she with you, and you could play with her and she with you?"
Abū Naḍrah said: This became a saying that the Muslims would use:
"Do such and such, and may Allah forgive you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ash-Shaʿbī said, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾishah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave his wives the choice, and that did not count as a divorce.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Marwān sent for Fāṭimah and asked her, and she told him that she had been married to Abū Ḥafṣ, and that the Prophet ﷺ had appointed ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, meaning over part of Yemen, and her husband went out with him. He sent her the remaining divorce pronouncement that was left to her, and he ordered ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah and al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām to spend on her. They said, "By Allah, she has no maintenance unless she is pregnant."
So she came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"You have no maintenance unless you are pregnant."
She asked his permission to move, and he permitted her. She said, "Where should I move, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"To Ibn Umm Maktūm."

He was blind; she would take off her garments in his presence and he could not see her. She remained there until her waiting period was over, and then the Prophet ﷺ married her to Usāmah. Qabīṣah returned to Marwān and told him of that. Marwān said, "We have not heard this ḥadīth except from a woman, so we will hold to the safeguard that we found the people following." When that reached Fāṭimah, she said, "Between me and you is the Book of Allah. Allah the Exalted said: {Divorce them for their waiting period} up to {You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some new matter}." She said, "What new matter could come about after the third [divorce]?" Abū Dāwūd said: Yūnus also narrated it like this from az-Zuhrī. As for az-Zubaydī, he narrated both ḥadīths: the ḥadīth of ʿUbaydullāh with a meaning like Maʿmar's, and the ḥadīth of Abū Salamah with a meaning like ʿUqayl's. Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated it from az-Zuhrī, that Qabīṣah ibn Dhuʾayb related it to him, with a meaning indicating the report of ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh when he said: Qabīṣah returned to Marwān and told him of that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Ḥuṣayn and Mughīrah,
and Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind,
and Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, and he mentioned
others, from ash-Shaʿbī,
who said: I visited Fāṭimah bint Qays and asked her about the ruling

of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning her. She said: Her husband divorced her irrevocably, and she took her dispute with him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding housing and maintenance. She said: He did not grant me housing or maintenance, and he ordered me to spend my waiting period in the house of Ibn Umm Maktūm.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Her husband divorced her three times, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not grant her housing or maintenance. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"When you become lawful [to marry], let me know."
So I informed him. Muʿāwiyah, Abū Jahm and Usāmah ibn Zayd proposed to her.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"As for Muʿāwiyah, he is a poor man who has no wealth. As for Abū Jahm, he is a man who strikes women. But Usāmah ibn Zayd..."
She gestured with her hand like this, saying, "Usāmah, Usāmah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"Obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger is better for you."
She said: So I married him, and I was envied.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My maternal aunt was divorced, and she wanted to harvest her dates, but a man rebuked her for going out to do so. She went to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Yes, harvest your dates, for perhaps you will give charity or do a good deed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿUwaymir al-Anṣārī,
of Banū al-ʿAjlān, came to ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī.

And he narrated the ḥadīth like the ḥadīth of Mālik, and inserted into the ḥadīth the statement: And his separation from her, after a year, was [the practice] for those who undergo mutual imprecation.
And he added in it: Sahl said: She was pregnant, and her son used to be called by his mother's name.
Then the practice continued that he inherits from her and she inherits from him what Allah prescribed for her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿĀʾishah and said to her, "Will you not tell me about the illness of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" She said, "Yes. The Prophet ﷺ became heavy [with illness] and said, 'Have the people prayed?'
We said, 'No, they are waiting for you, O Messenger of Allah.' He said,
'Put water for me in the basin.'
We did so, and he washed, then went to get up but fainted. Then he recovered and said, 'Have the people prayed?'
We said, 'No, they are waiting for you, O Messenger of Allah.' He said,
'Put water for me in the basin.'
We did so, and he washed, then went to get up but fainted. Then he recovered and said, 'Have the people prayed?'
We said, 'No, they are waiting for you, O Messenger of Allah.' He said,
'Put water for me in the basin.'
We did so, and he washed, then went to get up but fainted. Then he recovered and said, 'Have the people prayed?'
We said, 'No, they are waiting for you, O Messenger of Allah.'

She said: The people were gathered in the mosque, waiting for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the late evening prayer. She said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent word to Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer. The messenger came to him and said, 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commands you to lead the people in prayer.'
Abū Bakr, who was a tender-hearted man, said, 'ʿUmar, lead the people in prayer.'
ʿUmar said, 'You are more deserving of that.'

She said: So Abū Bakr led them in prayer during those days. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ felt some relief in himself and came out between two men, one of whom was al-ʿAbbās, for the Ẓuhr prayer, while Abū Bakr was leading the people. When Abū Bakr saw him, he went to step back, but the Prophet ﷺ signaled to him not to step back, and said to the two men,
'Seat me beside him.'

So they seated him beside Abū Bakr. Abū Bakr was praying standing, following the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ, and the people were praying following the prayer of Abū Bakr, while the Prophet ﷺ was sitting.
ʿUbaydullāh said: I went to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās and said to him, 'Shall I not present to you what ʿĀʾishah told me about the illness of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?' He said, 'Go ahead.'
So I presented her narration to him, and he did not reject any of it, except that he said, 'Did she name for you the man who was with al-ʿAbbās?' I said, 'No.'
He said, 'It was ʿAlī.'
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Allah hears whoever praises Him,"
none of us would bend his back until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had gone down in prostration; then we would go down in prostration after him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would keep the prayer brief yet complete.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn,
from Abū Hurayrah,

that the Prophet ﷺ finished [the prayer] after two [rakʿahs], and Dhū al-Yadayn said to him, "Has the prayer been shortened, or have you forgotten, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Is Dhū al-Yadayn right?"
The people said, "Yes."

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and prayed two more rakʿahs, then gave the salām, then said the takbīr and prostrated like his [usual] prostration or longer, then said the takbīr and raised his head, then prostrated like his [usual] prostration or longer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned his face to us when he stood for prayer, before saying the takbīr, and said,
"Straighten your rows and press close together, for I see you from behind my back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ one night and stood on his left.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of my head from behind,
and placed me on his right.
He prayed and then slept, and the muʾadhdhin came to him,
so he got up and prayed without performing ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt, "Did the Prophet ﷺ recite in the Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr prayers?" He said, "Yes."
He said: I said, "By what did you know his recitation?" He said, "By the movement of his beard."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"O Abū Dharr, I see that you are weak, and I love for you what I love for myself. Never take charge over two people, and never take charge of the wealth of an orphan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ on the pulpit addressing the people, and he said:

"After me there will be troubles and troubles. Whoever you see has separated from the community, or wants to divide the affair of the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, whoever he may be, kill him. For the hand of Allah is over the community, and Satan runs with the one who separates from the community."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd,
from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Qatādah, from his father,

who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think: if I am killed in the cause of Allah, patient, seeking reward, advancing and not retreating, will Allah expiate my sins for me?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Yes."
When the man turned away, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him, or ordered that he be called, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "What did you say?"
So he repeated his words to him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Yes, except for debt. Jibrīl, peace be upon him, told me that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We asked ʿAbdullāh about this verse:
{Do not think of those who were killed in the cause of Allah as dead; rather they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.} He said: We asked about that, and he said:

"Their souls are inside green birds that have lanterns hanging from the Throne. They roam in Paradise wherever they wish, then take shelter in those lanterns. Their Lord looked upon them and said, 'Do you desire anything?' They said, 'What could we desire when we roam in Paradise wherever we wish?' He did that to them three times. When they saw that they would not be left without being asked, they said, 'O Lord, we want our souls to be returned to our bodies so that we may be killed in Your cause once more.'
When He saw that they had no need, they were left alone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my mount has been exhausted, so provide me with a mount." He said:
"I do not have anything to carry you on, but go to so-and-so; perhaps he will provide you with a mount."
So he went to him and he provided him with a mount. Then he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever guides to good will have a reward like that of the one who does it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sanctity of the wives of those who go out to fight is, for those who stay behind, like the sanctity of their own mothers. There is no man among those who stay behind who takes care of the family of one of the fighters, but that he will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said, 'O so-and-so, this is so-and-so, so take from his good deeds whatever you wish.'"
Then the Prophet ﷺ turned to his Companions and said:
"What do you think? Do you think he will leave anything of his good deeds for him?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When you travel in times of plenty, give the camels their share of the land. When you travel in a year of drought, hasten to get them through while they still have some marrow. And when you stop for the night, avoid the road, for it is the path of animals and the dwelling place of vermin at night."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If you shoot game and find it after three nights with your arrow in it, eat it so long as it has not rotted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was admitted into Paradise, and on it he was sent down from it. On it there is an hour in which no Muslim servant happens to be praying and asks Allah for something, except that He gives it to him."
Abū Hurayrah said: Then I met ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām and mentioned this hadith to him, and he said: I know that hour best.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabbān, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade fasting on two days: the day of al-Aḍḥā and the day of al-Fiṭr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
all of them from Ibn
ʿUyaynah. Abū Bakr said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us,
Ayyūb ibn Mūsā narrated to us,
from Nubayh ibn Wahb,

who said: We set out with Abān ibn ʿUthmān, and when we were at Malal, ʿUmar ibn ʿUbaydillāh complained of his eyes. When we were at al-Rawḥāʾ, his pain became severe, so he sent to Abān ibn ʿUthmān to ask him. Abān sent back to him: Bandage them with aloe, for ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a man who complains of his eyes while in a state of iḥrām: bandage them with aloe.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās and Muʿāwiyah, who would touch every corner of the House he passed. Ibn ʿAbbās said to him: The Prophet ﷺ used to touch only the Black Stone and the Yemeni Corner.
Muʿāwiyah said: No part of the House is to be abandoned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥārith ibn Miskīn, [narrating] by recitation to him while I listened,
in his narration from Sufyān,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥumayd,
from al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd,
from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī,
who said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The emigrant may stay in Makkah for three days after completing his rites."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr, from ʿAbd
al-Malik ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father,
that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Umm Salamah and she spent the morning with him, he said to her:
"You are not held in contempt by your family. If you wish, I will stay seven nights with you, and if you wish, I will stay three and then rotate [among my wives]." She said: Three.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever dies without having fought and without having resolved within himself to do so dies upon a branch of hypocrisy."
Ibn Sahm said: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak said: We think that this was during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: The Prophet ﷺ went out one morning wearing a black woolen cloak with patterns of camel saddles. Then al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī came, and he brought him in under it. Then al-Ḥusayn came and entered with him. Then Fāṭimah came, and he brought her in. Then ʿAlī came, and he brought him in. Then he said: {Allah only intends to remove impurity from you, O people of the household, and to purify you thoroughly.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿUbaydullāh ibn Saʿīd,
and Muḥammad ibn Bashshār, they said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us,
from ʿUbaydullāh, who said: Nāfiʿ informed me,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed the name ʿĀṣiyah and said: "You are Jamīlah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never struck anything with his hand, neither a woman nor a servant, except when fighting in the cause of Allah. And he never took revenge on anyone for something done against him, unless one of the sacred limits of Allah was violated, in which case he would take revenge for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, Allah is gentle and loves gentleness. He gives for gentleness what He does not give for harshness, and what He does not give for anything else."
label: machine translation

segments_en: the brother of Banū Fihr, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"By Allah, this world compared to the Hereafter is only like what one of you gets when he puts this finger of his—and Yaḥyā pointed with the index finger—into the sea; let him see what it returns with."
In the narration of all of them, other than Yaḥyā, [it says]: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say that.
In the narration of Abū Usāmah, from al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddād, the brother of Banū Fihr, and also in his narration he said: and Ismāʿīl pointed with the thumb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ashʿath bought some slaves from the slaves of the fifth (khumus) from ʿAbdullāh for twenty thousand. ʿAbdullāh sent a message to him asking for their price, and he said: "I only took them for ten thousand."
ʿAbdullāh said: "Then choose a man to judge between you and me."
Al-Ashʿath said: "You are the judge between me and yourself."
ʿAbdullāh said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'When the two parties to a sale disagree and there is no proof between them, then the statement of the owner of the goods is accepted, or they cancel the transaction.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When land has been divided and its boundaries set, there is no right of pre-emption (shufʿah) in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"The neighbor has more right to what is next to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever finds an animal that its owners are unable to feed and have set loose, and he takes it and revives it, then it is his."
In the narration of Abān, ʿUbaydullāh said: I asked: "From whom [is this reported]?" He said: "From more than one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Among the servants of Allah there are people who are neither prophets nor martyrs, yet the prophets and martyrs will envy them on the Day of Resurrection because of their position with Allah, the Exalted."
They said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us who they are." He said:

"They are people who love one another through the spirit of Allah, without any ties of kinship between them and without wealth that they exchange. By Allah, their faces will be light, and they will be upon light. They will have no fear when people fear, and they will not grieve when people grieve."
And he recited this verse: {Indeed, the friends of Allah have no fear, nor will they grieve.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"The likeness of one who takes back what he gave is like a dog that vomits and then eats its vomit. So when the giver takes it back, he should be made to stand, and it should be made known what he took back; then what he gave should be handed over to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"Whoever intercedes for his brother with an intercession, and he gives him a gift for it and he accepts it, has come to a great door of the doors of usury (ribā)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "The ʿumrā (a gift for the lifetime of the recipient) is permissible."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled in the case of a woman of the Ansar to whom her son had given a garden of date palms. She died, and her son said: "I only gave it to her for her lifetime." He had brothers.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is hers, in her life and in her death."
He said: "I had given it to her as charity." He said:
"That is even further from you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The ʿumrā is when a man says to another: "It is yours for as long as you live." When he says that, it belongs to him and to his heirs. The ruqbā is when a person says to another: "It is for whichever of us outlives the other."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ borrowed some coats of mail from him on the day of Hunayn. He said: "Are you seizing them, O Muhammad?" He said:
"No, rather a loan that is guaranteed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the family of ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣafwān: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Ṣafwān, do you have any weapons?"
He said: "A loan or a seizure?" He said:
"No, a loan."

So he lent him between thirty and forty coats of mail. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on the expedition to Hunayn, and when the polytheists were defeated, Ṣafwān's coats of mail were gathered and some of them were found missing. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Ṣafwān:
"We have lost some of your coats of mail. Shall we compensate you?"
He said: "No, O Messenger of Allah, because today there is in my heart what was not there that day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the family of Ṣafwān, who said: The Prophet ﷺ borrowed—then he mentioned something similar in meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has given everyone with a right his right, so there is no bequest for an heir, and a woman must not spend anything from her husband's house except with his permission."
It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, not even food?" He said:
"That is the best of our property." Then he said:
"A loan must be returned, a gifted animal for milk must be given back, a debt must be paid, and the guarantor is liable."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"When my messengers come to you, give them thirty coats of mail and thirty camels."
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it a guaranteed loan or a loan to be returned?" He said: "Rather, one to be returned."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "I have never seen anyone prepare food like Ṣafiyyah. She prepared food for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and sent it, and I was seized by a trembling, so I broke the vessel. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the expiation for what I did?' He said:
'A vessel like the vessel and food like the food.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"Whoever seeks the office of judge among the Muslims until he obtains it, and then his justice outweighs his injustice, will have Paradise; and whoever's injustice outweighs his justice will have the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we reached Dhāt al-Riqāʿ. He said: Whenever we came upon a shady tree, we would leave it for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: Then a man from among the polytheists came, while the sword of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was hanging from a tree. He took the sword of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and drew it, and said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "Do you fear me?" He said, "No."
He said, "Then who will protect you from me?" He said, "
Allah will protect me from you."

He said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ threatened him, so he sheathed the sword and hung it back up. He said: Then the call to prayer was made, and he led one group in two rakʿahs, then they withdrew, and he led the other group in two rakʿahs. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed four rakʿahs, while the people prayed two.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We entered upon ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and Ḥassān ibn Thābit was with her, reciting poetry to her,
composing amorous verses of his own, and he said:
"A chaste, dignified woman, who is not suspected of any wrongdoing, and who wakes up hungry rather than eat the flesh of heedless women." ʿĀʾishah said to him, "But you are not like that."
Masrūq said: I said to her, "Why do you allow him to enter upon you,
when Allah the Exalted has said: {And as for him among them who took upon himself the greater part of it, for him is a great punishment}?"
She said, "And what punishment is worse than blindness?"
She said to him, "He used to defend the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or to answer satire with satire on his behalf."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah we were one thousand four hundred, and the Prophet ﷺ said to us, "
Today you are the best of the people of the earth."
Jābir said: If I could see, I would show you the location of the tree.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I did see the tree,
then I came to it afterwards and did not recognize it.
Maḥmūd said: Then I was made to forget it afterwards.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I set out for Hajj and passed by some people who were praying. I said, "What is this mosque?" They said, "This is the tree,
where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the Pledge of Riḍwān."
So I went to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and told him. Saʿīd said: My father told me that he was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ under the tree.
He said: When we went out the following year, we had forgotten it,
and we were not able to find it.
Saʿīd said: The Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ did not know it, yet you came to know it? Then you must know better!
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was travelling on one of his journeys,
and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was travelling with him at night.
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb asked him about something, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not answer him. Then he asked him again, and he did not answer him,
then he asked him again, and he did not answer him. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said, "May your mother lose you, ʿUmar!
You pressed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ three times,
and each time he did not answer you."
ʿUmar said: So I urged my camel on and went ahead of the Muslims,
fearing that a Qurʾān revelation would come down concerning me.
Before long I heard someone calling out to me. He said: I said, "I feared that a Qurʾān revelation had come down concerning me."
Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and greeted him with salām, and he said, "
Tonight a sūrah has been revealed to me that is more beloved to me than everything the sun has risen upon."
Then he recited: {Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting behind ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz when he said to the people, "What do you say about al-qasāmah?" ʿAnbasah said, "Anas ibn Mālik narrated to us such and such." I said, "Anas narrated to me: Some people came to the Prophet ﷺ."
And he related the hadith like the hadith of Ayyūb and Ḥajjāj.

Abū Qilābah said: When I had finished, ʿAnbasah said, "Glory be to Allah!" Abū Qilābah said: I said, "Do you accuse me, ʿAnbasah?" He said, "No, this is how Anas ibn Mālik narrated to us. You people of Syria will not cease to be well as long as this man, or the like of him, is among you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"All of my Ummah will enter Paradise,
except those who refuse."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, who would refuse?" He said:
"Whoever obeys me will enter Paradise,
and whoever disobeys me has refused."
label: machine translation

segments_en: O company of Qur'an reciters, stay upright, for you have taken a far lead. If you take to the right or to the left,
you will have gone far astray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with ʿUmar, and he said, "We have been forbidden from over-burdening ourselves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb asked about a woman's miscarriage, [that is, the woman whose belly is struck so that she drops her fetus]. He said, "Which of you heard anything about it from the Prophet ﷺ?" I said, "I did."
He said, "What is it?" I said, "I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
'The compensation is a slave, male or female.'"
He said, "Do not leave until you bring me someone to support what you say." So I went out and found Muḥammad ibn Maslamah and brought him,
and he testified with me that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
'The compensation is a slave, male or female.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Idrīs and Ibn Abī Ghaniyyah, from Abū Ḥayyān, from ash-Shaʿbī,
from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I heard ʿUmar
on the pulpit of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He addressed us on the pulpit of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: This washtub used to be set down for me and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we would both dip into it together.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Medina and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām met me. He said to me, "Come to the house, and I will give you a drink from a cup the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank from,
and you can pray in a place of prayer where the Prophet ﷺ prayed." So I went with him. He gave me sawīq to drink and fed me dates,
and I prayed in his place of prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman asked the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He mentioned Kaʿb al-Aḥbār and said, "Even if he was among the most truthful of those narrators who report from the People of the Book,
we nevertheless found falsehood in what he said."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAṭāʾ said: Jābir said
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed the people, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said:
"What do you advise me concerning people who slander my family? I have never known anything bad about them."
ʿUrwah said: When ʿĀʾishah was informed of the matter, she said, "O Messenger of Allah, will you permit me to go to my family?"
He permitted her and sent the servant boy with her.
A man from the Anṣār said, "Glory be to You! It is not for us to speak of this.
Glory be to You! This is a great slander."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever tells you that Muḥammad ﷺ saw his Lord has lied, for Allah says: {Vision does not perceive Him}. And whoever tells you that he knew the unseen has lied,
for Allah says: None knows the unseen except Allah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying, "I send out my trained dogs." He said:
"When you send out your trained dogs and mention the name of Allah, and they catch [the game], then eat.
And when you throw the miʿrāḍ and it pierces [the game], then eat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿĀʾishah [reported]
that Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, kissed the Prophet ﷺ after he had died.
He said: ʿĀʾishah said, "We forced medicine into his mouth during his illness,
and he began to gesture to us
not to force medicine into his mouth.
So we said, 'It is the patient's dislike of medicine.'
When he recovered, he said,
'Did I not forbid you to force medicine into my mouth?'
We said, 'It is the patient's dislike of medicine.' He said,
'No one will remain in the house without having medicine forced into his mouth while I look on, except al-ʿAbbās, for he did not witness you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: "And those of you who die and leave wives behind..." He said: This waiting period, which she observed at the house of her husband's family, was obligatory,

so Allah revealed: "And those of you who die and leave wives behind, [let them make] a bequest for their wives of provision for a year without turning them out. But if they leave, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves of what is right." He said: Allah gave her a full year, seven months and twenty nights, as a bequest;
if she wished, she could stay in her bequeathed residence,
and if she wished, she could leave,
and that is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "without turning them out. But if they leave, there is no blame upon you." So the waiting period remains obligatory upon her as it was.
He claimed that [this was] from Mujāhid.
And ʿAṭāʾ said: Ibn ʿAbbās said, This verse abrogated her waiting period at her husband's family's home,
so she observes her waiting period wherever she wishes,
and that is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "without turning them out."
ʿAṭāʾ said: If she wished, she observed the waiting period at his family's home and stayed in her bequeathed residence,
and if she wished, she left, because of the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "there is no blame upon you for what they do."
ʿAṭāʾ said: Then inheritance came and abrogated the right to residence, so she observes her waiting period wherever she wishes,
and she has no right to residence.
And from Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf: Waraqāʾ narrated to us from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, with this [report].
And from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: This verse abrogated her waiting period at her husband's family's home,
so she observes her waiting period wherever she wishes, because of the saying of Allah: "without turning them out," similar to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say: "We used to call Zayd ibn Ḥārithah only 'Zayd ibn Muḥammad,' until the Qurʾān was revealed: 'Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah.'" The Shaykh Abū Aḥmad Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā said: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Sarrāj and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf al-Duwayrī informed us, both saying: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us this hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: "On the Day We will say to Hell, 'Have you been filled?' and it will say, 'Are there any more?'" We were informed from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from Anas ibn Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:

"Hell will continue to be thrown into while it says, 'Are there any more?' until the Lord of Might places His foot in it, and its parts draw together, and it says, 'Enough, enough, by Your might and generosity.'
And there will remain surplus room in Paradise until Allah creates a [new] creation for it and settles them in the surplus of Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I grieved over those who were killed at al-Ḥarrah, so Zayd ibn Arqam wrote to me, after my intense grief had reached him, mentioning that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"O Allah, forgive the Anṣār and the children of the Anṣār."
Ibn al-Faḍl was unsure about "the children of the children of the Anṣār." Then some of those present asked Anas, and he said, "He is the one about whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'This is the one for whom Allah fulfilled [His promise] through his ear.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The best charity is that which leaves one self-sufficient,
and the upper hand is better than the lower hand,
and begin with those whom you support."
The wife says, "Either feed me or divorce me."
The servant says, "Feed me and make use of my work."
The son says, "Feed me,
to whom are you leaving me?" They said, "O Abū Hurayrah, did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?"
He said, "No, this is from Abū Hurayrah's own pocket."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar would not eat until a poor person was brought to eat with him,
so I brought in a man to eat with him, and he ate a great deal. [Ibn ʿUmar] said, "O Nāfiʿ, do not bring this man in to me. I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
'The believer eats in one intestine, and the disbeliever eats in seven intestines.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to love sweets and honey.
This is a good, sound, and unfamiliar (gharīb) hadith.
ʿAlī ibn Mus-hir also narrated it from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, and in the hadith there is more discussion than this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Zayd ibn ʿAbd Allāh,
from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq,
from Umm Salamah,
the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The one who drinks from vessels of silver is only gulping the Fire of Hell into his belly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Ḥamzah ibn ʿAmr al-Aslamī
asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a man who fasts continuously.
Should I fast while travelling?" He said:
"Fast if you wish, and break your fast if you wish."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on a journey when he saw a man around whom people had gathered and who was being shaded. He said, "What is the matter with him?"
They said, "He is a man who is fasting."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not righteousness to fast while travelling."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father,
from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar, from his father,
who said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"When the night comes from here and the day departs from there," Musaddad added:
"and the sun has set, then the fasting person has broken his fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr. Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said, "He informed us," and the others said,
"Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Dīnār,
that he heard Ibn
ʿUmar say: A man mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he was being deceived in transactions, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whomever you deal with, say: 'There is no deception.'"
So whenever he made a transaction, he would say, "No deception."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"People will not cease to attack this House until an army attacks it; when they are in the desert, or in a desert of the earth, the earth will swallow up the first of them and the last of them, and the middle of them will not escape."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what about those among them who were unwilling?" He said:
"Allah will raise them up according to what is in their own hearts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Mālik: "Did Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn narrate to you,
from Abū Sufyān,
the freed slave of Ibn Abī Aḥmad, from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted the sale of ʿarāyā by estimation, for less than five awsuq or for five awsuq?" (Dāwūd was unsure whether he said five or less than five.) He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever sells a date palm that has been pollinated, its fruit belongs to the seller, unless the buyer stipulates [otherwise]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Mūsā said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and with me were two men of the Ashʿarīs, one on my right and the other on my left. Both of them asked for a position of work, while the Prophet ﷺ was silent. Then he said:
"What do you say, O Abū Mūsā?" or:
"O ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays?"
I said, "By the One who sent you with the truth, they did not let me know what was in their hearts, and I did not realize that they were seeking a position."
He said: It is as though I can see his tooth-stick beneath his lip, which had drawn up. He said:
"We will not appoint—or: we do not appoint—to our work anyone who desires it. But go, you, O Abū Mūsā," or "O ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays."
So he sent him to Yemen, and then followed him with Muʿādh ibn Jabal. He said: When Muʿādh came to him, he said, "Dismount."
And he laid a cushion for him. Suddenly there was a man with him who was bound. He said, "What is this?" He said, "This man was a Jew who accepted Islam, then returned to his evil religion."
He said, "I will not sit until he is killed; this is the judgment of Allah and His Messenger."
He said, "Sit down, yes."
He said, "I will not sit until he is killed; this is the judgment of Allah and His Messenger."

Three times. So he ordered it, and he was killed. Then the two of them discussed the night prayer. One of them, Muʿādh ibn Jabal, said, "As for me, I sleep and I stand in prayer—or I stand in prayer and I sleep—and I hope for reward in my sleep as I hope for it in my standing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I attended the prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of ʿĪd. He began with the prayer before the sermon, without adhān or iqāmah. When he had finished the prayer, he stood leaning on Bilāl, praised Allah and extolled Him, admonished the people, reminded them, and urged them to obey Him. Then he turned and went to the women, with Bilāl accompanying him, and he commanded them to fear Allah, admonished them, reminded them, praised Allah and extolled Him, and urged them to obey Him. Then he said:
"Give charity, for most of you are fuel for Hell."
A woman from the lower class of women, dark-cheeked, said, "Why, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"You complain a great deal and you are ungrateful to your husbands."
So they began to take off their necklaces, earrings, and rings, throwing them into Bilāl's garment as charity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The day of ʿArafah, the day of sacrifice, and the days of Tashrīq are our festival, us people of Islam, and they are days of eating and drinking."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was asked which prayer is best after the obligatory prayer, and which fasting is best after the month of Ramadan. He said:
"The best prayer after the obligatory prayer is the prayer in the middle of the night, and the best fasting after the month of Ramadan is fasting the month of Allah, Muharram."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"This is the ʿUmrah that we have enjoyed. Whoever does not have the sacrificial animal with him should leave the state of iḥrām completely, for the ʿUmrah has entered into the Hajj until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the price of a dog, and [he said that] if someone comes seeking the price of a dog, fill his palm with dust.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, used to anoint himself with oil.

I mentioned that to Ibrāhīm, and he said, "What will you do with his saying? Al-Aswad narrated to me from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: 'It is as if I can see the gleam of perfume in the parting of the hair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in iḥrām.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I have been given five things that no one before me was given: Every prophet was sent only to his own people, but I have been sent to every red and black person; the spoils of war have been made lawful for me and were not lawful for anyone before me; the earth has been made for me pure, clean, and a place of prostration, so whichever man of my nation is overtaken by the time of prayer may pray wherever he is; I have been supported with awe [cast into the enemy] at a distance of a month's journey; and I have been given the intercession."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed in a woollen garment that had markings on it,
and he glanced at its markings once.
When he finished, he said:
"Take this garment of mine to Abū Jahm and bring me the plain woollen garment of Abū Jahm,
for it distracted me just now from my prayer."
And Hishām ibn ʿUrwah said, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"I was looking at its markings while I was in prayer, and I feared that it would distract me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lying on his back in the mosque,
with one of his legs placed over the other.
And from Ibn Shihāb, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who said: ʿUmar and ʿUthmān used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray Ẓuhr when the sun had passed its zenith, and he used to pray ʿAṣr between these two prayers of yours, and he used to pray Maghrib when the sun had set, and he used to pray ʿIshāʾ when the twilight had disappeared—then he said right after—and he used to pray Fajr until the sight could spread [with light].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "Lead your people in prayer."
He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I find something in myself [about that]." He said, "Come closer."
He sat me down in front of him, then placed his palm on my chest between my breasts, then said, "Turn around."
Then he placed it on my back between my shoulder blades, then said:

"Lead your people in prayer. Whoever leads a people in prayer should make it light, for among them are the elderly, the sick, the weak, and those with needs. And when one of you prays alone, let him pray as he wishes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have been commanded to prostrate on seven [parts], and not to gather up the hair or the clothing."
Ibn Ṭāwūs said: My father used to say, "[They are] the hands, the knees, and the feet," and he used to count the forehead and the nose as one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"This is a day of festival,
which Allah has made for the Muslims.
So whoever comes to the Friday prayer, let him bathe.
And if he has perfume, let him apply some of it. And you should use the siwāk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He
asked Zayd ibn Thābit about recitation
behind the imām, and he said, "There is no recitation behind the imām in anything."
And he claimed that he recited to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ {By the star when it descends}, and he did not prostrate.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The caliphate in my Ummah will last thirty years, then there will be kingship after that."
Then Safīnah said to me: "Count the caliphate of Abū Bakr, the caliphate of ʿUmar, and the caliphate of ʿUthmān."
Then he said to me: "Count the caliphate of ʿAlī."
He said: So we found it to be thirty years.
Saʿīd said: I said to him, "The Banū Umayyah claim that the caliphate is among them."
He said: "They lie, the sons of the blue-eyed woman! Rather, they are kings, and among the worst of kings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people from Rabīʿah were with ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, and a man from Bakr ibn Wāʾil said: "Quraysh must stop, or Allah will place this authority in the mass of the Arabs other than them."
ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: "You have lied. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Quraysh are the rulers of the people in good and in evil until the Day of Resurrection.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We feared that something might happen
after our Prophet, so we asked the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Indeed, in my Ummah there will be the Mahdī. He will emerge and live five, or seven, or nine years." Zayd was the one in doubt.
He said: We said, "What is that?" He said: "Years." He said:
"A man will come to him and say, 'O Mahdī, give me, give me!'" He said:
"So he will scoop for him into his garment as much as he is able to carry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The conquest of Constantinople will be along with the coming of the Hour.
He said: This hadith is gharīb.
Constantinople is the city of the Romans; it will be conquered when the Dajjāl emerges. Constantinople was [also] conquered in the time of some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, who said: I heard my uncle,
Mujammiʿ ibn Jāriyah al-Anṣārī, say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The son of Maryam will kill the Dajjāl at the gate of Ludd."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The father and mother of the Dajjāl will remain thirty years without having a child. Then a one-eyed boy will be born to them, the most harmful and least beneficial of things; his eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ described his parents to us, saying:
"His father will be tall and thin, with a nose like a beak, and his mother will be a broad-bodied woman with long hands."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do not curse the wind. If you see what you dislike, then say: 'O Allah, we ask You for the good of this wind, the good of what is in it, and the good of what it has been commanded to do; and we seek refuge in You from the evil of this wind, the evil of what is in it, and the evil of what it has been commanded to do.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ ascended the pulpit and smiled, and said:

"Tamīm ad-Dārī told me a story that pleased me, so I wanted to relate it to you. He told me that some people from the people of Palestine boarded a ship at sea, and it tossed them about until it cast them onto an island among the islands of the sea. Suddenly they met a beast, thickly covered, with its hair spread out. They said, 'What are you?' It said, 'I am the Jassāsah.' They said, 'Then tell us.'
It said, 'I will not tell you, nor ask you; but go to the farthest part of the village, for there is someone who will tell you and ask you.'
So we came to the farthest part of the village, and there was a man bound in a chain. He said, 'Tell me about the spring of Zughar.'
We said, 'It is full and overflowing.'
He said, 'Tell me about the lake.' We said, 'It is full and overflowing.'
He said, 'Tell me about the palm trees of Baysān, between Jordan and Palestine: have they borne fruit?' We said, 'Yes.'
He said, 'Tell me about the Prophet: has he been sent?' We said, 'Yes.'
He said, 'Tell me how the people are towards him.' We said, 'They hasten to him.'
He said: Then he leapt up so violently that he almost broke free.
We said, 'Then who are you?' He said, 'I am the Dajjāl, and I will enter all the cities except Ṭaybah.' And Ṭaybah is Madīnah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: You will be given victory, you will attain [success], and [lands] will be opened for you. Whoever among you lives to see that, let him fear Allah, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. And whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A time will come upon the people when the one among them who is patient in his religion will be like one holding a burning coal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When my Ummah walks with arrogant strutting, and the sons of kings, the sons of Persia and Rome, serve them, the worst of them will be given power over the best of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood by some people who were sitting and said:
"Shall I not tell you who is best among you and who is worst?"
He said: They remained silent. He said that three times. Then a man said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, tell us who is best among us and who is worst." He said:
"The best of you is the one from whom good is hoped for and from whose evil people are safe, and the worst of you is the one from whom good is not hoped for and from whose evil people are not safe."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was asked about the Hajj of tamattuʿ (combining ʿUmrah and Hajj).
He said: The Muhājirūn, the Anṣār, and the wives of the Prophet ﷺ entered into iḥrām during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and we also entered into iḥrām.
When we arrived in Makkah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Make your intention for Hajj into an ʿUmrah, except for the one who has garlanded his sacrificial animal."
So we circled the House and walked between Aṣ-Ṣafā and Al-Marwah, and we came to our wives,
and we put on our [regular] clothes. And he said:
"Whoever has garlanded his sacrificial animal is not permitted to leave iḥrām until the sacrificial animal reaches its place of sacrifice."
Then on the evening of the Day of Tarwiyah he commanded us to enter iḥrām for Hajj.
When we had finished the rites, we came and circled the House and walked between Aṣ-Ṣafā and Al-Marwah, and our Hajj was complete,

and we owed a sacrificial animal, as Allah the Exalted said: {then whatever sacrificial animal is easily available; and whoever cannot find one, then fasting three days during the Hajj and seven when you return} to your home cities. A sheep suffices.
So they combined two acts of worship in one year, Hajj and ʿUmrah,
for Allah the Exalted revealed it in His Book, and His Prophet ﷺ established it as a Sunnah, and permitted it for the people other than the people of Makkah.
Allah said: {That is for the one whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque.} And the months of Hajj that Allah the Exalted mentioned are Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and Dhū al-Ḥijjah.
Whoever performs tamattuʿ in these months owes a sacrificial offering or fasting. Rafath is sexual intercourse, fusūq is acts of disobedience, and jidāl is disputing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The House will surely be visited for Hajj and ʿUmrah after the emergence of Yājūj and Mājūj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Shaybah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is as though I can see him: a black man, bowlegged,
pulling it down stone by stone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And whoever avoids any part of the House.
Muʿāwiyah used to touch all the corners,
so Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) said to him: These two corners are not touched.
He said: No part of the House is to be abandoned.
And Ibn az-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them both) used to touch all of them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ibn Hishām prevented women from circling the House with the men, [ʿAṭāʾ] said: How can he prevent them, when the wives of the Prophet ﷺ circled with the men?
I said: Was it after the veil [was prescribed] or before? He said: Yes, by my life, I witnessed it after the veil.
I said: How did they mix with the men? He said: They did not mix. ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) used to circle apart from the men, not mixing with them,
and a woman said: Let us go, Mother of the Believers, so we may touch [the Black Stone].
She said: Go on without me. And she refused.
They used to go out disguised at night,
and circle with the men,
but when they wished to enter the House, they would stand until they entered and the men were sent out.
I used to visit ʿĀʾishah along with ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, while she was staying in seclusion in the midst of Thabīr.
I said: What was her screen? He said: She was in a Turkish tent with a covering,
and there was nothing between us and her other than that,
and I saw her wearing a rose-colored chemise.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to Makkah,
and he circled [the House] and walked between Aṣ-Ṣafā and Al-Marwah,
and he did not approach the Kaʿbah after his circling of it until he returned from ʿArafah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people
circled the House after the dawn prayer,
then sat down with a preacher,
until, when the sun rose, they stood up to pray. So ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: They sat until the time at which prayer is disliked, then they stood up to pray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw ʿAbdullāh ibn az-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them both) circling the House after dawn and praying two rakʿahs.
ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: And I saw ʿAbdullāh ibn az-Zubayr praying two rakʿahs after the ʿAṣr prayer,
and he reported that ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) told him that the Prophet ﷺ never entered her house without praying them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to the drinking place and asked for a drink.
Al-ʿAbbās said: Fadl, go to your mother,
and bring the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a drink from her. But he said: "Give me a drink."
He said: Messenger of Allah, they put their hands in it. He said: "Give me a drink." So he drank from it,
then he went to Zamzam,
where they were drawing water and working at it. He said: "Keep working,
for you are doing a righteous deed." Then he said: "Were it not that you would be overwhelmed, I would get down and place the rope on this."
—meaning his shoulder—and he pointed to his shoulder.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met Anas.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf,

in the year he came down against Ibn az-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them both), asked ʿAbdullāh (may Allah be pleased with him): What do you do at the standing place on the day of ʿArafah? Sālim said: If you want the Sunnah, then pray early on the day of ʿArafah.
ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: He has spoken the truth.
They used to combine the Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr prayers in accordance with the Sunnah.
I said to Sālim: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do that? Sālim said: And do you follow anything in that matter other than his Sunnah?
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was looking for a camel of mine.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥuṣayn said to me: "I am going to narrate to you a hadith by which Allah may perhaps benefit you after today. Know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a group of his family perform ʿUmrah during the ten days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not forbid it, and no verse was revealed abrogating it. [But] afterwards a man said about it whatever he wished to say, according to his own opinion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ declared the intention for Hajj, and he arrived on the fourth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. He prayed the dawn prayer, and when he had finished the dawn prayer he said:
"Whoever wishes to make it an ʿUmrah, let him make it an ʿUmrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man asked Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both: "May I circumambulate the House when I have entered ihram for Hajj?" He said: "What prevents you?" The man said: "I saw that the son of so-and-so dislikes it, and you are dearer to us than he is. We have seen that the world has tempted him."

He said: "And which of us has not been tempted by the world?" Then he said: "We saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ enter ihram for Hajj, circumambulate the House, and walk between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. So the way of Allah and the way of His Messenger ﷺ is more deserving of being followed than the way of so-and-so, if you are truthful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw ʿUmar kiss the Stone and embrace it, and he said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being very gracious to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was
riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, [and reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the people on the evening of ʿArafah and the morning of Jamʿ, when they set out: "Keep calm and tranquil."
He was holding back his camel, until when he entered Muḥassir, which is part of Minā, he said:
"Take the small pebbles, of the kind that are thrown."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ continued to say the Talbiyah until he threw the Jamrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Anas on the morning of ʿArafah: "What do you say about the Talbiyah on this day?" He said: "I made this journey with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions. Among them were those who said the Talbiyah and those who said the Takbīr, and none of them criticized the other."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥabībah said: "We used to do that in the time of the Prophet ﷺ: we would set out in the darkness before dawn from Jamʿ to Minā."
And in the narration of an-Nāqid: "We would set out in the darkness before dawn from Muzdalifah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had thrown the Jamrah, sacrificed his offering, and was to have his head shaved, he handed the barber the right side [of his head], and he shaved it. Then he called Abū Ṭalḥah al-Anṣārī and gave it to him. Then he handed [the barber] the left side and said: "Shave."
So he shaved it, and he gave it to Abū Ṭalḥah and said:
"Distribute it among the people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to garland the sheep and send them [to Makkah], while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in a state of being unrestricted, and nothing was forbidden to him because of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I set out with Sinān ibn Salamah,

both of us intending ʿUmrah. He said: Sinān set out with a camel for sacrifice which he was driving, but it became exhausted on the road, and he was at a loss about what to do with it if it broke down, [and how] he should bring it.
He said: "If I reach the town, I will certainly ask about that."
He said: So I reached the morning. When we stopped at al-Baṭḥāʾ, he said: "Go with me to Ibn ʿAbbās so that we can talk to him."
He said: So he mentioned to him the matter of his camel.

He said: "You have come upon one who knows. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent sixteen sacrificial camels with a man and gave him instructions about them." He said: "He went on, then came back and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what should I do with those of them that break down on me?' He said:
'Slaughter it, then dip its two sandal-garlands in its blood, then put it on its side, and do not eat from it, neither you nor anyone of your travelling companions.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us and said:
"O people, Allah has made Hajj obligatory upon you, so perform Hajj."
A man said: "Every year, O Messenger of Allah?" He remained silent until the man had said it three times. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Had I said yes, it would have become obligatory, and you would not have been able [to do it]." Then he said: "Leave me as I have left you, for those before you were destroyed only by their many questions and their disagreeing with their prophets. So when I command you to do something, do of it what you are able, and when I forbid you from something, leave it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar used to give the zakāh of Ramadan by the mudd of the Prophet ﷺ, the first mudd,
and for the expiation of an oath, by the mudd of the Prophet ﷺ.
Abū Qutaybah said: Mālik said to us, "Our mudd is greater than your mudd, but we see the virtue only in the mudd of the Prophet ﷺ."

And Mālik said to me: "If a ruler came to you and struck a mudd smaller than the mudd of the Prophet ﷺ, by what would you give?" I said: "We would give by the mudd of the Prophet ﷺ." He said: "Then do you not see that the matter returns to the mudd of the Prophet ﷺ?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah
and al-ʿAbbās, may peace be upon them both, came to Abū Bakr seeking their inheritance from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and at that time they were asking for their land at Fadak,
and their share of Khaybar.
Abū Bakr said to them: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'We are not inherited from;
what we leave is charity (ṣadaqah).
The family of Muḥammad only eat from this wealth.'"
Abū Bakr said: "By Allah, I will not abandon any matter that I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ doing with it, except that I will do it."
He said: Fāṭimah then withdrew from him,
and did not speak to him until she died.
label: machine translation

Then Sulaymān said: "He ruled among us."

and we would rise to him with our hands, our sandals, and our cloaks [to strike him],
until the last part of ʿUmar's rule, when he gave forty lashes,
until, when they became arrogant and defiant, he gave eighty lashes.

segments_en: A man
in the time of the Prophet ﷺ whose name was ʿAbdullāh
and who was nicknamed "Donkey"
used to make the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh.
The Prophet ﷺ had lashed him for drinking.
One day he was brought in, and [the Prophet ﷺ] ordered that he be lashed, and he was lashed.
A man among the people said: "O Allah, curse him! How often he is brought in!" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not curse him,
for by Allah, I know only that he loves Allah and His Messenger."

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh [said]:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said during the Farewell Hajj: "
Which month do you know to be the most sacred?"
They said: "This month of ours." He said: "
Which city do you know to be the most sacred?"
They said: "This city of ours." He said: "
Which day do you know to be the most sacred?"
They said: "This day of ours." He said: "
Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made your blood, your wealth, and your honor sacred, except by right,
like the sacredness of this day of yours,
in this city of yours,
in this month of yours.
Have I conveyed [the message]?"
[He said it] three times, and each time they answered him, "Yes." He said: "
Woe to you! Do not return to disbelief after me,
with some of you striking the necks of others."

segments_en: When Māʿiz ibn Mālik came to the Prophet ﷺ, he said to him: "
Perhaps you only kissed, or touched, or looked."
He said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Did you have intercourse with her?" [He said it] without euphemism.
He said: At that point he ordered that he be stoned.

He separated them, and her husband said: "I would have lied about her if I kept her."
He said: I memorized this from az-Zuhrī: "
If she gives birth to such-and-such, then he is [his],
and if she gives birth to such-and-such, resembling a wiḥrah, then he is [the other's]."

is the shedding of forbidden blood without right.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of the Conquest, the conquest of Makkah:
"There is no [more] emigration, but [there is] jihad and intention, and when you are called to march out, then march out."
And he said on the day of the Conquest, the conquest of Makkah:

"Indeed, this city Allah made sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not permitted to anyone before me, and it was permitted to me only for an hour of a day. So it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorny trees may not be cut down, its game may not be startled, and its lost property may not be picked up except by one who will announce it, and its fresh grass may not be cut."
Al-ʿAbbās said, "O Messenger of Allah, except the idhkhir, for it is for their blacksmiths and for their houses." So he said, "Except the idhkhir."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah,
where will you stay in your house in Makkah?" He said:
"And has ʿAqīl left any houses or dwellings?"
ʿAqīl had inherited from Abū Ṭālib, he and Ṭālib, while neither Jaʿfar nor ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both, inherited anything, because they were both Muslims,
while ʿAqīl and Ṭālib were disbelievers.
So ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say, "The believer does not inherit from the disbeliever."

Ibn Shihāb said: They used to interpret the saying of Allah, the Exalted: {Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and those who gave shelter and aid, those are allies of one another} — the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The one with two small shins from Abyssinia will destroy the House of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with them both: The people of

the Pre-Islamic Era used to fast on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims fasted it before Ramadan was made obligatory. When Ramadan was made obligatory, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"ʿĀshūrāʾ is one of the days of Allah, so whoever wishes may fast it, and whoever wishes may leave it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he came to Makkah, touch the Black Corner when he first performed the circumambulation upon arriving, and he would walk briskly for three of the seven circuits.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿUbaydullāh ibn Saʿīd,
all from Yaḥyā,
al-Qaṭṭān. Ibn al-Muthannā said: Yaḥyā narrated to us,
from ʿUbaydullāh, who said: Nāfiʿ narrated to me,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
who said: I have not stopped touching these two corners, the Yemeni one and the Stone, since I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ touching them, in hardship or ease.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ circumambulated the House,
while he was on a camel,
and whenever he came to the Corner, he pointed to it with something in his hand and said "Allahu akbar."

or something else,
so the Prophet ﷺ cut it with his own hand, then said, "Lead him by his hand."

segments_en: Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq sent me, in the Hajj for which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had appointed him as leader before the Farewell Hajj, with a group to announce to the people on the Day of Sacrifice: "After this year no polytheist may perform Hajj, and no one may circumambulate the House naked."
Ibn Shihāb said: Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān used to say, "The Day of Sacrifice is the Day of the Greater Hajj."
This is because of the hadith of Abū Hurayrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh,
and Sālim ibn ʿAbdillāh,

spoke to ʿAbdullāh when al-Ḥajjāj came down to fight Ibn az-Zubayr. They said, "It will not harm you not to perform Hajj this year, for we fear there may be fighting among the people that would come between you and the House." He said, "If I am prevented from it, I will do as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did, and I was with him, when the disbelievers of Quraysh came between him and the House. I make you witness that I have made ʿUmrah obligatory upon myself."

Then he set out until he came to Dhū al-Ḥulayfah and called out the talbiyah for ʿUmrah. Then he said, "If the way is cleared for me, I will complete my ʿUmrah, and if I am prevented, I will do as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did, and I was with him."

Then he recited: {Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example.} Then he travelled on until, when he was on the open plain of al-Baydāʾ, he said, "The matter of the two is the same. If I am prevented from ʿUmrah, I am prevented from Hajj. I make you witness that I have made Hajj obligatory together with ʿUmrah."

Then he set out until he bought a sacrificial animal at Qudayd, then performed one circumambulation of the House for both of them, and between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and did not leave the state of iḥrām for either of them until he left it for both on the Day of Sacrifice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, teach me the sunnah of the adhān."
He said: Then he wiped the front of my head and said:

"You say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, raising your voice with it. Then you say: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, lowering your voice with it. Then you raise your voice with the testimony: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Come to prayer, come to prayer; come to success, come to success. If it is the dawn prayer, you say: Prayer is better than sleep, prayer is better than sleep. Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; there is no god but Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, similar to this report, and in it:
"Prayer is better than sleep, prayer is better than sleep," in the first call of the dawn prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Prayer passed through three stages. He said: Our companions told us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"It pleased me that the prayer of the Muslims, or he said the believers, be one, so much so that I considered sending men out among the houses to call the people to the time of prayer, and I even considered ordering men to stand on the high structures to call the Muslims to the time of prayer, until they nearly rang the bell, or were about to ring the bell."

He said: Then a man of the Anṣār came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, when I returned, because of what I saw of your concern, I saw a man wearing two green garments standing on the mosque, and he called the adhān. Then he sat for a moment, then stood and said the like of it, except that he said, 'The prayer has begun.' And if people were not to say, Ibn al-Muthannā said: if you were not to say, I would say that I was awake, not asleep."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, and Ibn al-Muthannā said:
"Allah has shown you good."
But ʿAmr did not say:
"Allah has shown you good. So instruct Bilāl to call the adhān."
He said: Then ʿUmar said, "I had seen the same as what he saw, but when he beat me to it, I felt shy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Prayer passed through three stages, and fasting passed through three stages. Naṣr related the hadith at length, and Ibn al-Muthannā recounted from it only the story of their praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis. He said: The third stage was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Medina and prayed, meaning toward Bayt al-Maqdis, for thirteen months. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse: {We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Ḥarām. And wherever you [believers] may be, turn your faces toward it.} So Allah, the Exalted, directed him toward the Kaʿbah.

His report is complete, and Naṣr named the man who had the dream. He said: Then ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd, a man of the Anṣār, came, and he said in it: He faced the qiblah and said: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah; I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; come to prayer, twice; come to success, twice; Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; there is no god but Allah. Then he waited a short while, then stood and said the like of it, except that after he said:
"Come to success,"
he added: The prayer has begun, the prayer has begun.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Teach it to Bilāl."

So Bilāl called the adhān with it. And he said regarding fasting: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast three days of every month and to fast the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed: {Fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you} up to His saying {the feeding of a poor person}. So whoever wished to fast fasted, and whoever wished to break the fast and feed a poor person each day, that sufficed him. This was one stage. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed: {The month of Ramaḍān in which the Qurʾān was revealed} up to {other days}. So fasting was made firm for whoever witnesses the month, and the traveler must make up the days, and feeding remained for the very old man and old woman who are unable to fast. Then Ṣirmah came, having worked his day, and he related the hadith.
label: machine translation
