"You make people stingy, cowardly and ignorant, and yet you are among the sweet-scented blessings of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has three daughters, or three sisters, or two daughters, or two sisters, and treats them well and fears Allah regarding them, for him is Paradise."
He said: This is a gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever supports two girls, he and I will enter Paradise like these two," and he gestured with his two fingers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever takes an orphan from among the Muslims into his care, to his own food and drink, Allah will certainly admit him to Paradise, unless he commits a sin that is not forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One above the heavens will be merciful to you. The womb is a branch from the Most Merciful; whoever maintains it, Allah will maintain him, and whoever severs it, Allah will sever him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Each of you is a mirror of his brother. If he sees any harm in him, let him remove it from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever defends his brother's honor, Allah will turn the Fire away from his face on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Cursed is the one who harms a believer or deceives him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of companions in the sight of Allah are those who are best to their companion, and the best of neighbors in the sight of Allah are those who are best to their neighbor."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"They are your brothers; Allah has placed them under your hands. So whoever has his brother under his hand, let him feed him from his own food, clothe him from his own clothing, and not burden him with what overwhelms him. If he does burden him with what overwhelms him, let him help him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you strikes his servant and he mentions Allah, then lift your hands."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"For a man to discipline his child is better than for him to give a ṣāʿ in charity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No father gives his child a gift better than good manners."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Your smiling in your brother's face is charity for you; your enjoining good and forbidding evil is charity; your guiding a man in a land of misguidance is charity for you; your assisting a man of poor sight is charity for you; your removing a stone, a thorn or a bone from the road is charity for you; and your pouring from your bucket into your brother's bucket is charity for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever gives a gift of a milk-animal, or of silver, or guides someone along a path, will have the reward equal to freeing a slave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"The generous person is near to Allah, near to Paradise, near to the people, and far from the Fire. The miser is far from Allah, far from Paradise, far from the people, and near to the Fire. And an ignorant person who is generous is more beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, than a worshipper who is miserly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Two traits do not come together in a believer: miserliness and bad character."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Neither the deceitful, nor the one who reminds others of his favors, nor the miser will enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn Hārūn al-Ghassānī, "Did ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Rawwād narrate to you, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
that the Prophet ﷺ said:
'When a servant lies, the angel moves away from him a mile because of the stench of what he has brought.'"
Yaḥyā said: ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn Hārūn acknowledged it and said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to set out to the land of the Negus. He then mentioned his story, and said: The Negus said, "I bear witness that he is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that he is the one of whom ʿĪsā ibn Maryam gave glad tidings. Were it not for the kingship that I am in, I would come to him until I carried his sandals."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn died, his funeral was carried out and he was buried. The Prophet ﷺ commanded a man to bring him a stone, but the man was unable to carry it. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up and went to it, and bared his forearms. Kathīr said: al-Muṭṭalib said: The one who informed me of this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: It is as though I can see the whiteness of the forearms of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he bared them. Then he carried it and placed it by his head, and said:
"I am marking with it the grave of my brother, so that I may bury beside him those of my family who die."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī, al-Faḍl and Usāmah ibn Zayd washed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they were the ones who lowered him into his grave. He said: Marḥab, or Ibn Abī Marḥab, told me that they also had ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf go down with them. When ʿAlī had finished, he said: "Only a man's own family take charge of him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf
went down into the grave of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: It is as though I can see them, four [of them].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥārith left instructions that
ʿAbdullāh ibn Yazīd should pray over him. So he prayed over him, then put him into the grave from the side of the foot of the grave, and said: This is from the Sunnah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿĀʾishah and said: O Mother, uncover for me the grave of the Prophet ﷺ and his two Companions, may Allah be pleased with them both. So she uncovered for me three graves, neither raised high nor level with the ground, covered with the red pebbles of the open yard. Abū ʿAlī said: It is said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is in front, Abū Bakr is at his head, and ʿUmar is at the feet of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ had finished burying the dead, he would stand over the grave and say:
"Ask forgiveness for your brother, and ask that he be made steadfast, for he is being questioned right now."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no slaughtering at the grave in Islam."
ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: They used to slaughter a cow or a sheep at the grave.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "What is your name?" He said: Zaḥm. He said:
"Rather, you are Bashīr."
He said: While I was walking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he passed by the graves of the polytheists and said:
"These have missed out on much good."
[He said it] three times. Then he passed by the graves of the Muslims and said:
"These have attained much good."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ happened to glance and saw a man walking among the graves wearing sandals, and he said:
"O wearer of the two sibtī sandals, woe to you! Take off your sandals!"
The man looked, and when he recognized the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he took them off and threw them away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man was buried with my father, and I felt some concern about that in myself. So I took him out after six months, and I found nothing objectionable in him except a few hairs of his beard that had been touching the ground.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man was brought to the Prophet ﷺ whose mount had thrown him and broken his neck, so he died while in the state of iḥrām. He said:
"Shroud him in his two garments and wash him with water and lotus leaves, and do not cover his head, for Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection reciting the talbiyah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever swears a binding oath falsely, let him take his seat in the Fire, facing it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

from Kindah and a man from Ḥaḍramawt brought a dispute before the Prophet ﷺ over land in Yemen. The Ḥaḍramī said: O Messenger of Allah, my land was seized from me by this man's father, and it is in his possession. He said:
"Do you have proof?"
He said: No, but make him swear by Allah that he does not know that it is my land which his father seized from me. So the Kindī got ready to swear, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No one takes property by an oath except that he will meet Allah with his hand cut off."
Then the Kindī said: It is his land.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The hadith of the story of the Bedouin. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"By his father, he will succeed if he is truthful. By his father, he will enter Paradise if he is truthful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever swears by trust is not one of us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning idle talk in oaths, he said: ʿĀʾishah said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is a man's speech in his house: 'No, by Allah,' and 'Yes, by Allah.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: O Allah, You know that there is no one whom I would love more to fight for Your sake than a people who denied Your Messenger ﷺ and drove him out.
O Allah, I think that You have brought the war between us and them to an end.
And Abān ibn Yazīd said: Hishām narrated to us, from his father: ʿĀʾishah informed me: [there is none I would rather fight] than a people who denied Your Prophet and drove him out from Quraysh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with Ibn ʿAbbās by the Kaʿbah when a Bedouin came to him and said, "Why is it that I see your cousins giving people honey and milk to drink, while you give nabīdh to drink? Is it out of need or out of stinginess?" Ibn ʿAbbās said, "Praise be to Allah, it is neither need nor stinginess. The Prophet ﷺ came on his mount with Usāmah behind him and asked for a drink. We brought him a vessel of nabīdh, and he drank, then gave the remainder to Usāmah to drink, and said:
"You have done well and you have done beautifully. Do likewise."
So we do not wish to change what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
they said: Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us,
from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī,
with this chain of narration, like it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Muʿādh ibn Hishām informed us,
who said: My father informed me, both of them,
from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid,
from Ibn Abī
Laylā, from ʿAlī,
from the Prophet ﷺ; but in their narration there is no mention of the wage of the butcher.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ﷺ said: "So when we left the state of iḥrām, he commanded us to offer a sacrificial animal, and a group of us would share in one offering." That was when he commanded them to leave the state of iḥrām from
their Hajj, in this hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah says: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sacrificed on behalf of his wives.
And in the narration of Ibn Bakr, from ʿĀʾishah: a cow, during his Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ. (Transition to another chain.)
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas. (Transition to another chain.)
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent eighteen camels for sacrifice with a man.
Then he mentioned [the rest] like the hadith of ʿAbd al-Wārith, but he did not mention the beginning of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās when Zayd ibn Thābit said, "Are you giving the ruling that a menstruating woman may depart
before her last act is at the House?"

Ibn ʿAbbās said to him, "If you will not accept it, then ask such-and-such woman of the Anṣār whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded her to do that." Then Zayd ibn Thābit returned to Ibn ʿAbbās laughing and saying, "I see only that you have spoken the truth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered the Kaʿbah, which had six pillars. He stood by a pillar and made supplication, but he did not pray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Did the Prophet ﷺ enter the House during his ʿUmrah?" He said, "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Were it not that your people have only recently left the time of ignorance"—or he said, "of disbelief"—"I would have spent the treasure of the Kaʿbah in the cause of Allah, made its door level with the ground, and included the Ḥijr within it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"O ʿĀʾishah, were it not that your people have only recently left polytheism, I would have demolished the Kaʿbah and made it level with the ground, and I would have made two doors for it, an eastern door and a western door, and added to it six cubits from the Ḥijr, for Quraysh shortened it when they built the Kaʿbah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUbayd: Al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbdullāh came as a delegate to ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān during his caliphate. ʿAbd al-Malik said, "I do not think Abū Khubayb," meaning Ibn al-Zubayr, "heard from ʿĀʾishah what he claimed to have heard from her."
Al-Ḥārith said, "Yes, I heard it from her."
He said, "What did you hear her say?" He said, "She said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

'Your people fell short in building the House, and were it not for their recent exit from polytheism, I would restore what they left out of it. If it occurs to your people after me to rebuild it, then come, and I will show you what they left out of it.'"
And he showed her about seven cubits.
This is the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUbayd, and al-Walīd ibn ʿAṭāʾ added to it that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"'And I would have made two doors for it, set level with the ground, one eastern and one western. Do you know why your people raised its door?'"
She said, "I said, 'No.'" He said:
"'To be arrogant, so that only those whom they wished would enter it. When a man wished to enter, they would let him climb up, and when he was about to enter, they would push him and he would fall.'"
ʿAbd al-Malik said to al-Ḥārith, "Did you yourself hear her say this?" He said, "Yes."
He said: He tapped the ground with his staff for a while, then said, "I wish I had left it as it was and what it carried."
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said, "Would I then say about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what I did not hear?" He said: I heard him say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not undertake a journey except to three mosques: this mosque of mine, the Sacred Mosque, and the farthest mosque." And I heard him say:
"A woman must not travel for two days at any time unless she has with her a mahram relative or her husband."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Dharr used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The roof of my house was opened while I was in Makkah, and Jibrīl (peace be upon him) descended and opened my chest. Then he washed it with Zamzam water. Then he brought a golden basin filled with wisdom and faith, and poured it into my chest. Then he closed it. Then he took me by the hand and ascended with me to the heaven. When we reached the lowest heaven, Jibrīl (peace be upon him) said to the keeper of the lowest heaven, 'Open.'
He said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'This is Jibrīl.'
He said, 'Is there anyone with you?' He said, 'Yes, Muhammad ﷺ is with me.'

He said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.' So it was opened. He said: When we went up into the lowest heaven, there was a man, with dark shapes on his right and dark shapes on his left. He said: When he looked to his right he laughed, and when he looked to his left he wept. He said: He said, 'Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous son.' He said: I said, 'O Jibrīl, who is this?' He said, 'This is Ādam (peace be upon him), and these dark shapes on his right and on his left are the souls of his descendants. The people on the right are the people of Paradise, and the shapes on his left are the people of the Fire. So when he looks to his right he laughs, and when he looks to his left he weeps.' He said: Then Jibrīl ascended with me until he came to the second heaven.
He said to its keeper, 'Open.' He said: Its keeper said to him the same as the keeper of the lowest heaven had said, and it was opened."

Anas ibn Mālik said: He mentioned that he found in the heavens Ādam, Idrīs, ʿĪsā, Mūsā and Ibrāhīm (the blessings of Allah be upon them all), and he did not establish how their positions were, except that he mentioned that he found Ādam (peace be upon him) in the lowest heaven and Ibrāhīm in the sixth heaven. He said:

"When Jibrīl and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by Idrīs (the blessings of Allah be upon him), he said, 'Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous brother.' He said: Then he passed on, and I said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'This is Idrīs.' He said: Then I passed by Mūsā (peace be upon him), and he said, 'Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous brother.' He said: I said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'This is Mūsā.' He said: Then I passed by ʿĪsā, and he said, 'Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous brother.'

I said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'ʿĪsā ibn Maryam.' He said: Then I passed by Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him), and he said, 'Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous son.' He said: I said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'This is Ibrāhīm.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and he said:
"O Mughīrah, take the water container."

So I took it and went out with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on until he was hidden from me, and he relieved himself. Then he came back wearing a Syrian cloak with narrow sleeves. He tried to bring his hand out through its sleeve, but it was too tight for him, so he brought his hand out from underneath it. I poured water for him, and he performed ablution as for prayer. Then he wiped over his leather socks, and then he prayed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Kaaba was being built, the Prophet ﷺ and ʿAbbās went to carry stones. Al-ʿAbbās said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Put your lower garment on your shoulder to protect you from the stones."
He did so, but he fell to the ground, and his eyes were fixed on the sky. Then he stood up and said, "My garment! My garment!"
So his lower garment was tied firmly on him.
Ibn Rāfiʿ said in his narration: on your neck.
And he did not say: on your shoulder.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a red leather tent,
and I saw Bilāl take the water left from the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I saw the people rushing to that ablution water,
so whoever got some of it rubbed himself with it,
and whoever did not get any of it took from the moisture of his companion's hand.
Then I saw Bilāl take a short spear and plant it in the ground,
and the Prophet ﷺ came out in a red garment, with his garment tucked up,
and he led the people in prayer, two rakʿahs, facing the spear,
and I saw the people and the animals passing in front of the spear.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read in the original book of Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh — Ibn ʿAwf said: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from his father,
who said: Ḍamḍam ibn Zurʿah narrated to me,
from Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd,
who said: Jubayr ibn Nufayr gave me a ruling about washing
after sexual impurity, that Thawbān narrated to them that they
asked the Prophet ﷺ about that, and he said:

"As for the man, let him spread out his hair and wash it until the water reaches the roots of the hair. As for the woman, there is no harm if she does not undo it; let her scoop three handfuls of water onto her head with her palms."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Banū Sawāʾah ibn ʿĀmir, from ʿĀʾishah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to wash his head with marshmallow (khiṭmī) while in a state of sexual impurity, being content with that and not pouring water over it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Banū Sawāʾah ibn ʿĀmir, from ʿĀʾishah,

regarding the fluid that flows between a man and a woman, she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would take a handful of water and pour it over the fluid, then take another handful of water and pour it over it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If he has relations with her at the beginning of the blood, [he gives] a dinar, and if he has relations with her when the blood has stopped, half a dinar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That she

asked ʿĀʾishah, saying: One of us menstruates, and she and her husband have only one bed. She said: I will tell you what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did. He came in one night while I was menstruating and went to his place of prayer — Abū Dāwūd said: she means the prayer place in his house — and he did not come back until sleep overcame me, and the cold pained him. He said: "Come close to me."
I said: I am menstruating. He said:
"Even so, uncover your thighs."
So I uncovered my thighs, and he laid his cheek and chest upon my thighs, and I bent over him until he became warm and slept.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When I menstruated, I would come down from the bed onto the mat, and we would not go near the Messenger of Allah ﷺ nor come close to him until we were pure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ [said] that when the Prophet ﷺ wanted something from a menstruating woman, he would throw a garment over her private part.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command us, at the height of our menstruation, to put on a waist wrapper, and then he would be intimate with us. And which of you can control his desire as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ controlled his desire?
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Anṣār, that a woman
used to have a flow of blood; then he mentioned the meaning of the hadith of al-Layth. He said:
"Then when she has left them behind and the time of prayer arrives, let her wash."
And he related the hadith with its meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this account, he said in it:
"She leaves the prayer, and washes for the rest of the time, binds herself with a cloth, and prays."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That she instructed Asmāʾ — or Asmāʾ narrated to me that she
was instructed by Fāṭimah bint Abī Ḥubaysh — to ask
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he instructed her to remain [apart from prayer] for the days she used to remain, then to wash.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Her menstruation became disordered and she bled [continuously]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to instruct her: let her consider the amount [of days] she used to menstruate each month while her cycle was regular, and let her count that number of days, then leave the prayer during them or for their duration, then let her wash, then bind herself with a cloth, then pray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Sahlah bint Suhayl

suffered from irregular bleeding, so she came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he instructed her to wash for every prayer. When that became hard on her, he instructed her to combine Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr with one washing, Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ with one washing, and to wash for the morning prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: O Messenger of Allah, Fāṭimah bint Abī Ḥubaysh has had irregular bleeding for such and such a time, and she has not prayed.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Glory be to Allah! This is from Satan. Let her sit in a tub, and when she sees yellowness above the water, let her wash once for Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, once for Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ, and once for Fajr, and let her perform ablution in between."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the woman with irregular bleeding: she washes — meaning once — then performs ablution until the days of her [regular] periods.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That al-Qaʿqāʿ
and Zayd ibn Aslam

sent him to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab to ask how the woman with irregular bleeding should wash. He said: She washes from one Ẓuhr to the next, and performs ablution for every prayer; and if the blood overcomes her, she binds herself with a cloth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The woman with irregular bleeding, when her menstruation has ended, washes every day and uses a piece of wool containing clarified butter or oil.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he asked al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad about the woman with irregular bleeding,
and he said: She leaves the prayer during the days of her periods, then washes and prays, then washes [again] during the [following] days.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Umm Ḥabībah bint Jaḥsh
suffered from irregular bleeding, so the Prophet ﷺ instructed her to wait for the days of her periods, then wash and pray; and if she saw anything of that, she would perform ablution and pray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whenever the people suffered drought, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) would ask for rain through al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. He would say, "O Allah, we used to seek a means to You through our Prophet, and You would send us rain; now we seek a means to You through the uncle of our Prophet, so send us rain." He said: And they would be given rain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for rain and turned his cloak inside out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
complained to the Prophet ﷺ about the destruction of wealth and the hardship of the families,
so he supplicated to Allah, asking for rain,
and he did not mention that he turned his cloak over or that he faced the qiblah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yazīd al-Anṣārī went out, and with him went al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib and Zayd ibn Arqam (may Allah be pleased with them), and he prayed for rain.
He stood with them on his feet, without a minbar, and asked forgiveness,
then he prayed two rakʿahs, reciting aloud, without an adhān and without an iqāmah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin man from the desert people came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on Friday and said, "O Messenger of Allah,
the livestock have perished, the families have perished, the people have perished."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands, supplicating,
and the people raised their hands with him, supplicating.
He said: We had not even left the mosque before we were rained upon,
and we continued to be rained upon until the following Friday.
Then the man came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the traveler is in hardship and the road is blocked."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The keys of the unseen are five that none knows except Allah:
none knows what the wombs diminish except Allah;
none knows what will be tomorrow except Allah;
none knows when the rain will come except Allah;
no soul knows in what land it will die except Allah;
and none knows when the Hour will come except Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I memorized from the Prophet ﷺ ten rakʿahs: two rakʿahs before Ẓuhr and two after it,
two rakʿahs after Maghrib in his house,
two rakʿahs after ʿIshāʾ in his house,
and two rakʿahs before the Ṣubḥ prayer.
That was a time when no one would enter upon the Prophet ﷺ. Ḥafṣah told me
that when the muʾadhdhin called the adhān and the dawn had broken, he would pray two rakʿahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir al-Juhanī and said, "Shall I not amaze you with Abū Tamīm, who prays two rakʿahs before the Maghrib prayer?"
ʿUqbah said, "We used to do that in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
I said, "Then what prevents you now?" He said, "Being busy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ﷺ, and he had fought twelve battles alongside the Prophet ﷺ. [Transition to another chain.]
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) would not pray the Ḍuḥā prayer except on two days: the day he arrived in Makkah,
for he used to arrive there in the forenoon, and he would circumambulate the House,
then pray two rakʿahs behind the Station [of Ibrāhīm];
and the day he came to the Mosque of Qubāʾ,
for he used to come to it every Saturday,
and when he entered the mosque he disliked leaving it until he had prayed in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Four things I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—or he said, he narrated them from the Prophet ﷺ—which pleased me and impressed me: "
That a woman should not travel a distance of two days without her husband or a mahram;
no fasting on two days, al-Fiṭr and al-Aḍḥā;
no prayer after two prayers: after ʿAṣr until the sun sets,
and after Ṣubḥ until the sun rises;
and that journeys are not to be undertaken except to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, my mosque, and the Aqṣā Mosque."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were in al-Ahwāz fighting the Ḥarūriyyah [Khawārij],
and while I was on the bank of a river, there was a man praying,
and the reins of his mount were in his hand, and the animal kept pulling against him,
and he kept following it. Shuʿbah said: He was Abū Barzah al-Aslamī. A man from the Khawārij began saying, "O Allah, do such-and-such to this old man."
When the old man finished, he said, "I heard what you said,
and I fought with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in six, seven, or eight battles, and I witnessed his ease [in religion],
and truly, going back and forth with my animal is dearer to me than leaving it to return to its stable, which would be hard on me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw phlegm on the qiblah wall of the mosque,
and he was angry at the people of the mosque and said: "
Allah is in front of any one of you,
so when he is in his prayer,
let him not spit—or he said, let him not clear phlegm."
Then he came down and scraped it off with his hand.
Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: When one of you spits, let him spit to his left
label: machine translation

segments_en: during prayer.
Hishām and Abū Hilāl said, from Ibn Sīrīn,
from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed me over aṭ-Ṭāʾif, something began to come over me in my prayer until I did not know what I was praying. When I saw that, I travelled to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ?"
I said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"What brought you?"
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, something came over me in my prayer until I did not know what I was praying." He said:
"That is the devil. Come closer."
So I came close to him and sat on the tops of my feet.
He said: Then he struck my chest with his hand, spat into my mouth, and said:
"Get out, enemy of Allah!"
He did that three times, then said, "Go back to your work."
He said: ʿUthmān said, "By my life, I do not think it has come near me since."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when a Bedouin came to him and said, "I have a brother who is ailing." He said:
"What is wrong with your brother?"
He said, "He has a touch of madness." He said:
"Go and bring him to me."

He said: So he went and brought him, and made him sit before him. Then I heard him [the Prophet ﷺ] seek refuge for him with Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, four verses from the beginning of al-Baqarah, two verses from its middle, {And your god is one God}, Āyat al-Kursī, three verses from its end, a verse from Āl ʿImrān — I think he said {Allah witnesses that there is no god but He} — a verse from al-Aʿrāf {Indeed your Lord is Allah, who created} to the end of the verse, a verse from al-Muʾminūn {And whoever invokes besides Allah another god, for which he has no proof}, a verse from al-Jinn {And that exalted is the majesty of our Lord; He has taken neither a wife nor a son}, ten verses from the beginning of aṣ-Ṣāffāt, three verses from the end of al-Ḥashr, {Say, He is Allah, the One}, and the two sūrahs of refuge.
Then the Bedouin stood up, cured, with nothing wrong with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed in a single wrapping cloth which he had knotted around himself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ insult anyone, nor did he have a garment folded away for himself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw ʿUmar wearing a white shirt and said:
"Is this garment of yours washed or new?"
He said, "No, it is washed." He said:
"Wear new clothes, live praiseworthy, and die a martyr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marking sheep on their ears, and I saw him wearing a cloak as a waist wrapper.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best thing with which you can visit Allah in your graves and your mosques is white."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Sufyān ibn Sahl, do not let your garment hang down, for Allah does not love those who let their garments hang down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to wear a shirt with short sleeves and short length.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to Fāṭimah or to Umm Salamah, "Your hem is a cubit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said regarding the hems of women's garments, "A handspan."
ʿĀʾishah said, "Then their legs would be exposed." He said, "Then a cubit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade brocade, silk, and heavy silk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade wearing silk and gold, and he said:
"It is for them in this world, and for us in the Hereafter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Ibn ʿUmar buy a turban with a decorated border. He called for a pair of shears and cut it off. Then I went in to Asmāʾ and mentioned that to her. She said, "What misery for ʿAbdullāh! Girl, bring the cloak of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
So she brought a cloak whose two sleeves, collar opening, and two slits were trimmed with brocade.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A garment was given as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, trimmed with silk, either in its warp or its weft, and he sent it to me. I came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, what should I do with it? Should I wear it?" He said:
"No, but turn it into head coverings for the Fāṭimahs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the muffadam.
Yazīd said: I asked al-Ḥasan, "What is the muffadam?" He said, "That which is heavily dyed with safflower."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me — and I do not say he forbade you — from wearing garments dyed with safflower.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the family of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, and the women gathered, weeping over him. ʿUmar stood up, forbidding them and driving them away, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Leave them, ʿUmar, for the eye is tearful, the heart is afflicted, and the loss is recent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ commanded that those slain at Uḥud be returned to the places where they had fallen,
after they had been carried to Madinah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The soul of the believer is but a bird in the trees of Paradise, until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sends it back to its body on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said to Ḥudhayfah, "At what time did you eat the pre-dawn meal with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "It was day, except that the sun had not yet risen."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
asked ʿĀʾishah about fasting,
and she said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast the whole of Shaʿbān, and he would make a point of fasting on Mondays and Thursdays."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every deed of the son of Adam is multiplied: a good deed is rewarded ten times its like, up to seven hundred fold.
Allah, Glorified is He, said: 'Except fasting, for it is for Me and I will reward it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ called for milk to give him to drink, and Muṭarrif said, "I am fasting." ʿUthmān said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Fasting is a shield, like the shield of one of you in battle.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is not righteousness to fast while traveling. Hold to the concession of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and accept it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is said: Fasting while traveling is like breaking the fast while resident.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ:
"Has any of you eaten today?" We said,
"Some of us have eaten and some have not." He said:
"Complete the rest of your day,
those who have eaten and those who have not.
And send word to the people of al-ʿArūḍ, so that they complete the rest of their day."
He said, meaning the people of al-ʿArūḍ around Madinah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to give the charity of breaking the fast before zakāh was revealed. When zakāh was revealed, he neither commanded us nor forbade us, and we continued to do it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Eat, drink, give charity, and dress, so long as it is not mixed with extravagance or arrogance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The one who fights in the cause of Allah, the one performing Hajj, and the one performing ʿUmrah are the delegation of Allah: He called them and they answered Him, and they asked Him and He gave them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If he cannot find a waist-wrapper, let him wear trousers; and if he cannot find sandals, let him wear leather socks and cut them off below the ankles."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad, Abū Muʿāwiyah and Abū Usāmah, from ʿUbaydullāh,
from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀʾishah,
who said: I perfumed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for his state of iḥrām when he entered it, and for his release from it when he left it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Part of the talbiyah of the Prophet ﷺ was:
"Here I am, O God of Truth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among some people with me, he said: The Prophet ﷺ arrived in Makkah on the morning of the fourth day of Dhū al-Ḥijjah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Shaybah said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ running between Ṣafā and Marwah, and he was saying:
"The valley of al-Abṭaḥ is not crossed except at a run."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me on the morning of al-ʿAqabah, while he was on his mount:
"Pick up pebbles for me."
So I picked up for him some pebbles, of the size of those used for flicking. When I placed them in his hand, he said, "Like these,
and beware of excess in religion, for those before you were destroyed only by excess in religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not gather dust in the cause of Allah and the smoke of Hell in the belly of a Muslim, and Allah does not gather faith in Allah and miserliness together in the heart of a Muslim.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A young woman
came to her and said, "My father married me to his brother's son to raise his own lowly status through me, and I dislike it."

She said, "Sit until the Prophet ﷺ comes." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and I told him, so he sent for her father and called him, and he gave the matter to her. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, I permit what my father has done, but I wanted to know whether women have any say in the matter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib married a woman from Banū Jusham, and it was said to him, "May there be harmony and sons."
He said, "Say as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'May Allah bless you and bless you [both].'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man called Nahīk ibn Sinān came to ʿAbdullāh.

[He narrated] like the hadith of Wakīʿ, except that he said: ʿAlqamah came to enter upon him, so we said to him, "Ask him about the comparable surahs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in a single rakʿah." So he went in to him and asked him, then came out to us and said, "Twenty surahs from the Mufaṣṣal, in the arrangement of ʿAbdullāh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was reciting {Say: He is Allah, the One}, repeating it.
When morning came, he went to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him,
and the man seemed to regard it as little. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose Hand is my soul, it is equal to a third of the Qur'an."
Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar added, from Mālik,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father,
from Abū Saʿīd: My brother informed me,
Qatādah ibn al-Nuʿmān, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She was the wife of Abū Ayyūb, [narrating] from Abū Ayyūb,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Is any of you unable to recite a third of the Qur'an in a night? Whoever recites 'Allah is the One, the Eternal Refuge' has recited a third of the Qur'an."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ went to his bed each night, he would join his palms together, blow into them, and recite into them:
{Say: He is Allah, the One} and
{Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak} and

{Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind}. Then he would wipe over as much of his body as he could with them, beginning with his head and face and the front of his body. He would do that three times.
He said: This is a good, strange (gharīb), authentic hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Three men came to the houses of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ asking about the worship of the Prophet ﷺ. When they were told, it was as though they considered it little, and they said, "Where are we compared to the Prophet ﷺ? Allah has forgiven him his earlier and later sins."
One of them said, "As for me, I will pray all night, always."
Another said, "I will fast continuously and never break my fast."
Another said, "I will keep away from women and never marry."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and said:
"You are the ones who said such and such. By Allah, I am the one among you who fears Allah most and is most mindful of Him,
yet I fast and I break my fast,
I pray and I sleep, and I marry women.
So whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We attended with Ibn ʿAbbās the funeral of Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, at Sarif. Ibn ʿAbbās said, "This is the wife of the Prophet ﷺ. When you lift her bier, do not jolt it or shake it, and be gentle, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had nine wives; he would give a share of his time to eight and not give a share to one."
ʿAṭāʾ said: The one to whom he did not give a share was Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him. He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, why do you seek out [spouses] among Quraysh and leave us?" He said, "Do you have someone?"
I said, "Yes, the daughter of Ḥamzah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"She is not lawful for me; she is the daughter of my brother through breastfeeding."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, marry my sister, the daughter of Abū Sufyān." He said, "Do you like that?" I said, "Yes,
I am not alone with you [as your only wife],
and I love for my sister to share with me in good." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"That is not lawful for me."
I said, "But we have been told that you want to marry the daughter of Abū Salamah." He said:
"The daughter of Umm Salamah?" I said, "Yes." He said:
"Even if she were not my stepdaughter in my care, she would not be lawful for me. She is the daughter of my brother through breastfeeding;
Thuwaybah nursed me and Abū Salamah. So do not offer me your daughters or your sisters."

ʿUrwah said: Thuwaybah was a freed slave woman of Abū Lahab. Abū Lahab had freed her, and she nursed the Prophet ﷺ. When Abū Lahab died, one of his family saw him in a terrible state and asked him, "What have you met with?" Abū Lahab said, "I have met no ease after you, except that I am given a drink in this [small hollow] because I freed Thuwaybah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with Anas ibn Mālik, and a daughter of his was with him. Anas said: A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ and offered herself to him.
She said, "O Messenger of Allah, do you have any need of me?" Anas's daughter said, "How little modesty she has!"
He said, "She is better than you. She desired the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and offered herself to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man must not sell over the sale of his brother, nor bid against the bid of his brother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Ibn] ʿUmar [narrated] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever buys food, let him not sell it until he has taken full possession of it."
He said: We used to buy food from caravans by estimation without measuring, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us to sell it until we had moved it from its place.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade selling a heap of dates whose measure is unknown in exchange for a specified measure of dates.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade muzābanah: selling the fruit of the palm trees for dried dates by measure, selling grapes for raisins by measure, and selling standing crops for wheat by measure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he forbade mukhābarah, muzābanah and muḥāqalah, and [forbade] selling fruit until its good condition is apparent, and that it be sold only for dinars and dirhams; and he permitted the ʿarāyā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While he was sitting with ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, [narrating] from Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh:

that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade muḥāqalah, muzābanah and mukhābarah, and that one buy palm trees [fruit] until it shows color—and showing color means that it turns red or yellow or something of it is eaten. Muḥāqalah is selling a field for a known measure of food; muzābanah is selling palm trees [fruit] for wasqs of dried dates; and mukhābarah is [farming for] a third or a quarter and the like.
Zayd said: I said to ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ: Did you hear Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh mention this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: Yes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar

used to rent out his land until he was told that Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj al-Anṣārī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to forbid renting out land. ʿAbdullāh met him and said: O Ibn Khadīj, what do you narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about renting land? Rāfiʿ said to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar: I heard my two uncles—who had both been at Badr—telling the people of the house that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade renting out land.
ʿAbdullāh said: By Allah, I knew during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that land was rented out.
Then ʿAbdullāh feared that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ might have introduced something new regarding it of which he had no knowledge, so he gave up renting out land.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Rabīʿah ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
from Ḥanẓalah ibn Qays,
that he asked Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj about renting land,
and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade renting out land. [Ḥanẓalah] said: I said: Even for gold and silver? He said: As for gold and silver, there is no harm in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj about renting land

for gold and silver. He said: There is no harm in it. People used to lease land during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in return for what grew along the watercourses and the heads of the streams, and certain portions of the crop; so this one's [portion] would be destroyed and that one's would be safe, or this one's would be safe and that one's destroyed. People had no other form of renting except this, so that is why it was prohibited. But as for something guaranteed and known, there is no harm in it.
The narration of Ibrāhīm is more complete, and Qutaybah said: from Ḥanẓalah, from Rāfiʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That she asked ʿĀʾishah, "Should a menstruating woman make up the prayers?" ʿĀʾishah said, "Are you a Ḥarūrī? The wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to menstruate; did he command them to make [them] up?" Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar said: She means, "to make them up."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah, saying, "Why does a menstruating woman make up the fasting but not make up the prayer?" She said, "Are you a Ḥarūrī?" I said, "I am not a Ḥarūrī, but I am [merely] asking."
She said, "That used to happen to us, and we were commanded to make up the fasting, but we were not commanded to make up the prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ablution is [required] after [eating] what the fire has touched."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
entered upon Umm Ḥabībah, and she gave him a cup of barley meal to drink. He called for water and rinsed his mouth. She said, "O son of my sister, will you not perform ablution? The Prophet ﷺ said:
'Perform ablution after [eating] what the fire has changed.'"
Or he said, "what the fire has touched."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her, she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to remember Allah at all times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The call to prayer was taught to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by himself, and he said:

"Say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah; I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah"—twice each. Then he said: "Then go back and raise your voice: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah; I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; come to prayer, come to prayer; come to success, come to success; Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; there is no god but Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Ḥaywah,
and Saʿīd ibn Abī Ayyūb,
from Kaʿb ibn ʿAlqamah,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ,
that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say:

"When you hear the muezzin, say the same as he says. Then send blessings upon me, for whoever sends one blessing upon me, Allah will send ten blessings upon him for it. Then ask Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to grant me the wasīlah, for it is a station in Paradise that is fitting for only one of the servants of Allah, the Exalted, and I hope that I will be that one. Whoever asks Allah to grant me the wasīlah, intercession will be due for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pass his hand over our shoulders in prayer and say:
"Stand straight and do not differ, for your hearts will differ. Let those of you who are mature and possess understanding stand closest to me, then those who come next, then those who come next."
Abū Masʿūd said: Today you are more divided than ever.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw some of his Companions hanging back, so he said to them:
"Come forward and follow me, and let those after you follow you. People will keep hanging back until Allah causes them to be held back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to estimate the standing of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Zuhr and ʿAṣr prayers. We estimated his standing in the first two rakʿahs of Zuhr to be about the length of reciting Alif Lām Mīm Tanzīl, [Sūrat] as-Sajdah; and we estimated his standing in the last two to be about half of that. We estimated his standing in the first two rakʿahs of ʿAṣr to be equal to his standing in the last two of Zuhr, and in the last two of ʿAṣr to be half of that.
Abū Bakr did not mention "Alif Lām Mīm Tanzīl" in his narration, and said: about thirty verses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ lifted the curtain, with his head bandaged, during his illness in which he died, and said:

"O Allah, have I conveyed [the message]?"—three times. "Nothing remains of the glad tidings of prophethood except the good dream, which a servant sees or which is seen for him. Indeed, I have been forbidden to recite [the Qurʾān] while bowing or prostrating. So when you bow, glorify your Lord, and when you prostrate, strive earnestly in supplication, for it is likely to be answered for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met Thawbān, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said, "Direct me to a deed that will benefit me or that will admit me to Paradise." He was silent for a while, then turned to me and said, "You should prostrate, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'There is no servant who prostrates to Allah once but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, raises him one degree for it and removes one sin from him for it.'"
Maʿdān said: Then I met Abū ad-Dardāʾ and asked him about what I had asked Thawbān. He said to me, "You should prostrate, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'There is no servant who prostrates to Allah once but Allah raises him one degree for it and removes one sin from him for it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, and he used to recite in the Fajr prayer; it is as though I can still hear his recitation: "So I swear by the retreating stars, those that run their course and set."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "I am unable to learn anything of the Qur'an, so teach me something that will suffice me in its place." He said:
"Say: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, and there is no power and no strength except with Allah."
The man said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; what is there for me?" He said:
"Say: O Allah, have mercy on me, provide for me, grant me well-being, and guide me."
When the man stood up, he gestured like this with his hand, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"As for this man, he has filled his hand with good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you prostrates, let him not kneel down like a camel kneels; let him place his hands before his knees."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī, Abū Masʿūd, and said to him, "Tell us about the prayer of

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He stood before us in the mosque and said the takbīr. When he bowed, he placed his hands on his knees with his fingers below them, and kept his elbows apart from his sides until every part of him was settled. Then he said, "Allah hears whoever praises Him," and stood until every part of him was settled. Then he said the takbīr and prostrated, placing his palms on the ground and keeping his elbows apart from his sides until every part of him was settled. Then he raised his head and sat until every part of him was settled. He did the same again. Then he prayed four rakʿahs like this rakʿah and completed his prayer. Then he said, "This is how we saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When {So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great} was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:
"Make it part of your bowing."
And when {Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High} was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:
"Make it part of your prostration."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I stood in prayer with the Prophet ﷺ. He began by using the tooth-stick and performing ablution, then stood and prayed. He began by opening with Sūrat al-Baqarah. He did not pass a verse of mercy without stopping and asking, and he did not pass a verse of punishment without stopping and seeking refuge. Then he bowed and remained bowing for about as long as he had stood, saying in his bowing:
"Glory be to the Possessor of might, sovereignty, majesty, and greatness."
Then he prostrated for about as long as his bowing, saying in his prostration:
"Glory be to the Possessor of might, sovereignty, majesty, and greatness."
Then he recited Āl ʿImrān, then another sūrah, then another sūrah, doing the same each time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a man of Banū ʿAbs, from Ḥudhayfah:
that he saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying at night, and he would say:
"Allah is the Greatest" three times, "Possessor of sovereignty, might, majesty, and greatness."
Then he began the prayer and recited Sūrat al-Baqarah. Then he bowed, and his bowing was about as long as his standing, and he would say in his bowing:
"Glory be to my Lord, the Most Great; glory be to my Lord, the Most Great."
Then he raised his head from bowing, and his standing was about as long as his bowing, saying, "To my Lord belongs all praise."
Then he prostrated, and his prostration was about as long as his standing, and he would say in his prostration:
"Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."
Then he raised his head from prostration and sat between the two prostrations for about as long as his prostration, and he would say:
"My Lord, forgive me; my Lord, forgive me."
He prayed four rakʿahs in which he recited al-Baqarah, Āl ʿImrān, an-Nisāʾ, and al-Māʾidah or al-Anʿām; Shuʿbah was unsure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed beside the Prophet ﷺ while he was praying voluntary prayer at night. He passed a verse of punishment and said:
"I seek refuge in Allah from the Fire, and woe to the people of the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I have not prayed behind anyone after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whose prayer resembled the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ more than this young man, meaning ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.
He said: We estimated that in his bowing there were ten glorifications, and in his prostration ten glorifications.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed the hands prostrate just as the face prostrates. So when one of you places his face, let him place his hands, and when he raises it, let him raise them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib described to us: he placed his hands, leaned on his knees, and raised his posterior, and said, "This is how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to prostrate."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ complained to the Prophet ﷺ of the hardship of prostrating when they spread their limbs apart, so he said, "Seek help by using the knees."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥarām was killed on the day of Uḥud, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met me and said:
"O Jābir, shall I not tell you what Allah said to your father?"
And Yaḥyā said in his narration: He said:
"O Jābir, why do I see you broken-hearted?"
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, my father was martyred and left behind dependents and a debt." He said:
"Shall I not give you glad tidings of how Allah met your father?"
He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"Allah has never spoken to anyone except from behind a veil, but He spoke to your father face to face.
He said: 'O My servant, ask Me and I will give you.'
He said: 'O my Lord, bring me back to life so that I may be killed in Your cause a second time.'
The Lord, glorified be He, said: 'It has already been decreed by Me that they will not return to it.'
He said: 'O my Lord, then convey [this] to those I left behind.'
So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: {Do not think of those who were killed in the cause of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the Day of Resurrection, the slain person will come bringing his killer, holding the killer's forelock and head in his hand, with his own jugular veins gushing blood, saying: 'O my Lord, this one killed me,' until he brings him close to the Throne."
He said: They mentioned repentance to Ibn ʿAbbās, so he recited this verse:
{Whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell}. He said: "This verse has not been abrogated or changed, so how could there be repentance for him?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was camped between Ḍajnān and ʿUsfān, with the polytheists besieged. The polytheists said: "These people have a prayer that is dearer to them than their sons and their firstborn. Gather your resolve, then charge at them in a single assault." So Jibrīl, peace be upon him, came and commanded him to divide his Companions into two halves, leading one group in prayer while the other group faced their enemy, taking their precautions and their weapons. He would lead them in one rakʿah, then these would withdraw and those would advance, and he would lead them in one rakʿah. Thus each would have one rakʿah each with the Prophet ﷺ, while the Prophet ﷺ would have two rakʿahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] was asking forgiveness for his parents while they were both polytheists, so I said:
"Do you ask forgiveness for them when they are polytheists?" He said: "Did Ibrāhīm not ask forgiveness for his father?"
So I went to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and [the verse] was revealed: {Ibrāhīm's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, where was our Lord before He created His creation?" He said:
"He was in a cloud, with no air beneath it and no air above it, and He created His Throne upon the water."
Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn said: "al-ʿAmāʾ means that nothing was with Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Allah did not reveal in the Torah or in the Gospel anything like Umm al-Qurʾān. It is the Seven Oft-Repeated [verses], and it is divided between Me and My servant, and My servant will have what he asks for."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and others,

—the meaning is the same, and the wording is that of Ibn Bashshār—they said: Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us: Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū Rāfiʿ, from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding the barrier [of Gog and Magog]. He said:

"They dig at it every day, until when they are almost through it, the one in charge of them says: 'Go back, you will break through it tomorrow.' Then Allah restores it to what it was before. Until, when their time is complete and Allah wishes to send them out against the people, the one in charge of them says: 'Go back, you will break through it tomorrow, if Allah wills,' making an exception.

He said: So they return and find it as it was when they left it, and they break through it. They come out upon the people, drinking up the waters, and the people flee from them. They shoot their arrows into the sky, and the arrows return stained with blood, and they say: 'We have conquered those on earth and have overcome those in the sky,' out of harshness and arrogance.

Then Allah sends upon them a worm in their necks, and they perish. He said: By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, the beasts of the earth will grow fat, become sleek, and thrive abundantly on their flesh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Allah gathers the people on the Day of Resurrection, a day about which there is no doubt, a caller will call out: 'Whoever associated anyone with Allah in a deed he did for Allah, let him seek his reward from other than Allah, for Allah is the most self-sufficient of partners, needing no association.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ was driven out of Makkah, Abū Bakr said: "They have driven out their Prophet; they will surely be destroyed." Then Allah revealed:
{Permission [to fight] is given to those who are being fought, because they have been wronged, and indeed Allah is able to give them victory}—the verse.
Abū Bakr said: "I knew that there would be fighting."
He said: This is a ḥasan hadith.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī and others also narrated it from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr as a mursal report, without [mention of] Ibn ʿAbbās.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Ibn ʿUmar], may Allah be pleased with them both, [reported] that the Prophet ﷺ met Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl at the bottom of Baldaḥ,
before revelation came down upon the Prophet ﷺ. A tablecloth of food was presented to the Prophet ﷺ,
and he refused to eat from it. Then Zayd said, "I do not eat from what you slaughter for your stone idols,
and I eat only that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned."
Zayd ibn ʿAmr used to criticize the Quraysh for their slaughtered animals,
and he would say, "The sheep: Allah created it,
and sent down water for it from the sky,
and made vegetation grow for it from the earth,
and then you slaughter it without the name of Allah," objecting to that and regarding it as a grave matter.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl went out to Syria,
asking about the religion so that he might follow it. He met a scholar of the Jews,
and asked him about their religion,
and said, "Perhaps I will adopt your religion, so tell me about it."
He said, "You will not be on our religion until you take your share of the anger of Allah."
Zayd said, "I flee only from the anger of Allah,
and I will never bear any of the anger of Allah,
and I am able to avoid it. Can you guide me to something other than this?" He said, "I know of nothing except that he be a ḥanīf."
Zayd said, "What is a ḥanīf?" He said, "The religion of Ibrāhīm, who was neither a Jew nor a Christian, and worshipped none but Allah."
So Zayd left and met a scholar of the Christians, and mentioned the same to him,
and he said, "You will not be on our religion until you take your share of the curse of Allah."
He said, "I flee only from the curse of Allah,
and I will never bear any of the curse of Allah nor of His anger,
and I am able to avoid it. Can you guide me to something other than this?" He said, "I know of nothing except that he be a ḥanīf."
He said, "What is a ḥanīf?" He said, "The religion of Ibrāhīm, who was neither a Jew nor a Christian, and worshipped none but Allah."
When Zayd saw what they said about Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, he left,
and when he came out into the open, he raised his hands and said, "O Allah, I bear witness that I am on the religion of Ibrāhīm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl standing with his back resting against the Kaʿbah, saying, "O people of Quraysh,
by Allah, none of you is on the religion of Ibrāhīm except me."
He used to save the baby girls who were to be buried alive,
saying to a man who wanted to kill his daughter, "Do not kill her,
I will take care of her upkeep for you."
So he would take her, and when she grew older, he would say to her father, "If you wish, I will hand her over to you,
and if you wish, I will take care of her upkeep for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿUbaydullāh ibn Abī Yazīd,
both said: In the time of the Prophet ﷺ there was no wall around the House;
people used to pray around the House,
until the time of ʿUmar,
who built a wall around it. ʿUbaydullāh said: Its wall was short,
and Ibn al-Zubayr then built it up.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr used to say: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather,
who said: A flood came in the Jāhiliyyah and covered what lies between the two mountains.
Sufyān said: He would say, "This hadith is indeed one of great significance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr entered upon a woman of Aḥmas called Zaynab,
and saw that she did not speak,
so he said, "What is wrong with her that she does not speak?" They said, "She has performed Hajj in silence."
He said to her, "Speak,
for this is not permissible;
this is from the practice of the Jāhiliyyah." So she spoke,
and said, "Who are you?" He said, "A man of the Muhājirūn."
She said, "Which of the Muhājirūn?" He said, "From Quraysh."
She said, "Which of Quraysh are you?" He said, "You ask a lot! I am Abū Bakr."
She said, "How long will we remain upon this good order that Allah brought after the Jāhiliyyah?" He said, "You will remain upon it as long as your leaders remain upright with you."
She said, "And who are the leaders?" He said, "Did your people not have chiefs and nobles who would command them and whom they would obey?" She said, "Yes."
He said, "Then they are those over the people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Qāsim used to walk in front of the funeral procession and would not stand for it,
and he reported from ʿĀʾishah that she said: The people of the Jāhiliyyah used to stand for it,
and when they saw it they would say, "You were among your family, what are you [now]?" [They said it] twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Abū Usāmah, "Did Yaḥyā ibn al-Muhallab narrate to you, [saying] Ḥuṣayn narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah,
regarding {and a cup full to the brim}, he said: [It means] filled, one after another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the Jāhiliyyah [they would say], "Give us a cup full to the brim to drink."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr had a slave who would pay him a regular payment from his earnings,
and Abū Bakr used to eat from his earnings.

One day he came with something and Abū Bakr ate from it. The slave said to him, "Do you know what this is?" Abū Bakr said, "What is it?" He said, "In the Jāhiliyyah I practiced soothsaying for a man, and I was not good at soothsaying,
but I deceived him.
Then he met me and gave me this for it,
and this is what you have eaten from."
So Abū Bakr put his hand [in his throat] and vomited everything in his stomach.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Running in the bottom of the valley between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah is not a sunnah.
Rather, the people of the Jāhiliyyah used to run it and say, "We will not cross the valley bed except at a run."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he disliked a man being married to both a paternal aunt and a maternal aunt of the same woman, or to two maternal aunts, or two paternal aunts [at the same time].
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this report, he said: So ʿAlī remained silent about that marriage.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and we discussed the temporary marriage of women. A man called Rabīʿ ibn Sabrah said to him: I bear witness that my father narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it during the Farewell Pilgrimage.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ made the temporary marriage of women forbidden.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-ʿAbbās

married his daughter to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥakam, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān married his daughter to him, and they had made that the dowry. Muʿāwiyah wrote to Marwān ordering him to separate them, and he said in his letter: This is the shighār that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: We saw that it was ʿAlī, peace be upon him, [who narrated] from the Prophet ﷺ with similar meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ said:
"If a slave marries without the permission of his master, his marriage is invalid."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you proposes to a woman, if he is able to look at what would encourage him to marry her, let him do so."
He said: So I proposed to a girl and I used to hide so as to see her, until I saw of her what encouraged me to marry her, and I married her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had a sister who was being asked for in marriage. A cousin of mine came to me and I married her to him. Then he divorced her with a revocable divorce, and left her until her waiting period ended. When she was again being asked for in marriage, he came to propose to her, and I said: No, by Allah, I will never marry her to you.
He said: This verse was revealed about me: "And when you divorce women and they reach the end of their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands..." [al-Baqarah 2:232] the verse.
He said: So I made expiation for my oath and married her to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will, nor to constrain them so that you may take away part of what you gave them, unless they commit a clear immorality." [al-Nisāʾ 4:19] That was because a man would inherit the wife of a relative and would constrain her until she died or returned to him her dowry. So Allah put a firm end to that and forbade it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Consult women regarding their daughters."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with my father on the pilgrimage of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. My father approached him while he was on a she-camel of his, and he stopped for him and listened to him. He had with him a whip like the whip of a schoolteacher. I heard the Bedouins and the people saying: "Al-Ṭabṭabiyyah, al-Ṭabṭabiyyah, al-Ṭabṭabiyyah!" My father drew near to him and took hold of his foot, and he allowed him, stopped by him and listened to him. He said: I was present at the army of ʿUthrān — Ibn al-Muthannā said: the army of Ghuthrān — and Ṭāriq ibn al-Murarraʿ said: Who will give me a spear in return for its reward? I said: What is its reward? He said: I will marry to him the first daughter born to me.
So I gave him my spear, then I was away from him until I learned that a daughter had been born to him and had reached maturity. Then I came to him and said: Send my wife to me.

But he swore that he would not do so unless I gave him a new dowry, different from what had been between him and me, and I swore that I would not give any dowry other than what I had given. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"And of which generation of women is she today?"
He said: She has seen grey hair [i.e., she is of advanced age]. He said:
"I think you should leave her."
He said: That alarmed me, and I looked at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When he saw that in me, he said:
"You will not be sinful, nor will your companion be sinful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She was one who was given a dowry, a woman of truthfulness. She said: While my father was on a military expedition in the Jāhiliyyah, they were scorched by the heat of the ground, and a man said: Who will give me his sandals, and I will marry to him the first daughter born to me? So my father took off his sandals and threw them to him. Then a daughter was born to him and she reached maturity. And he mentioned something similar, but did not mention the story of the grey hair.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Najāshī
married Umm Ḥabībah bint Abī Sufyān to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a dowry of four thousand dirhams, and he wrote about that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who accepted.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever gives as a woman's dowry a double handful of barley meal or dates has made [her] lawful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Something like this story, without mentioning the waist-wrapper and the ring. He said:
"What do you know of the Qurʾān?"
He said: Sūrat al-Baqarah or the one after it. He said:
"Then get up and teach her twenty verses, and she is your wife."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Something like the report of Sahl. He said: Makḥūl used to say: That is not for anyone after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you pass by the gardens of Paradise, graze in them."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what are the gardens of Paradise?" He said, "The mosques."
I said, "And what is grazing, O Messenger of Allah?" He said,
"Subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, and Allāhu akbar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you pass by the gardens of Paradise, graze in them."
He said, "And what are the gardens of Paradise?" He said, "The circles of remembrance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When any of you is struck by a calamity, let him say:
'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we shall return. O Allah, with You I seek reward for my calamity, so reward me for it and replace it for me with something better.'"
When Abū Salamah was dying, he said, "O Allah, leave in my family someone better than me." When he passed away, Umm Salamah said:
"Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we shall return. With Allah I seek reward for my calamity, so reward me for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, teach me something that I may ask Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for." He said,
"Ask Allah for well-being."
I waited for some days, then came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, teach me something that I may ask Allah for." He said to me,
"O ʿAbbās, O uncle of the Messenger of Allah, ask Allah for well-being in this world and the Hereafter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever among you has the door of supplication opened for him, the doors of mercy are opened for him. And Allah is not asked for anything He loves more than that He be asked for well-being."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Supplication benefits against what has descended and what has not descended. So hold fast to supplication, servants of Allah."
He said: This is a gharīb hadith.
We do not know it except from the narration of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr al-Qurashī, who is al-Makkī al-Mulaykī, and he is weak in hadith; some scholars graded him weak because of his memory.
Isrāʾīl narrated
this hadith from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr,
from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"Allah is not asked for anything He loves more than well-being."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ, when he intended to do something, would say:
"O Allah, choose what is best for me and select for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
