"Glorification [tasbīḥ] is half the scale, and 'al-ḥamdu lillāh' fills it. And 'lā ilāha illā Allāh' has no veil between it and Allah until it reaches Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Banū Sulaym, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ counted them on my hand or on his hand:
"Glorification is half the scale, praise fills it, and 'Allāhu akbar' fills what is between the heavens and the earth. Fasting is half of patience, and purification is half of faith."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was
from Banū Asad, from al-Aghar ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ,
from Khalīfah ibn Ḥuṣayn,
from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib,
who said: Most of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ supplicated with on the evening of ʿArafah, while standing at the place of standing, was:

"O Allah, to You is praise, as You say and better than what we say. O Allah, to You belong my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying; to You is my return, and to You, my Lord, is my inheritance. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, the whisperings of the heart, and the scattering of affairs. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what the wind brings."
He said: This is a gharīb hadith from this route, and its chain is not strong.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a long supplication of which we did not memorize anything. We said, "O Messenger of Allah, you made a long supplication of which we did not memorize anything." He said,

"Shall I not direct you to what encompasses all of that? You say: O Allah, we ask You for the good that Your Prophet Muḥammad asked You for, and we seek refuge in You from the evil that Your Prophet Muḥammad sought refuge from. You are the One whose help is sought, upon You is the delivery of the message, and there is no power and no strength except with Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"People will be lined up in rows on the Day of Resurrection" – and Ibn Numayr said: "the people of Paradise" – "and a man from the people of the Fire will pass by a man [of them] and say, 'O so-and-so, do you not remember the day you asked for water and I gave you a drink?' So he will intercede for him. And another man will pass by and say, 'Do you not remember the day I handed you water for ablution?' So he will intercede for him."
Ibn Numayr said:
"And he will say, 'O so-and-so, do you not remember the day you sent me on such and such an errand and I went for you?' So he will intercede for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about stray camels that come to my water troughs, which I have plastered for my own camels: will I have a reward if I give them water? He said:
"Yes. In every creature with a living liver there is a reward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"They are your brothers, whom Allah has placed under your hands. So feed them from what you eat and clothe them from what you wear, and do not burden them with what overpowers them. And if you do burden them, then help them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Our Prophet ﷺ commanded us to spread the greeting of peace.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I am riding to the Jews tomorrow, so do not initiate the greeting of peace with them. And if they greet you with peace, then say: 'And upon you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, may one of us bow to another?" He said, "No."
We said, "May one of us embrace another?" He said:
"No, but shake hands."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We kissed the hand of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Ghundar,
and Abū Usāmah, from Shuʿbah,
from ʿAmr ibn Murrah,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Salamah,
from Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl: that some people
of the Jews kissed the hand and the feet of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is the greeting of peace, but what is seeking permission (istiʾnās)?" He said:
"The man says 'Subḥān Allāh,' 'Allāhu akbar,' and 'Al-ḥamdu lillāh,' and clears his throat, and makes the people of the house aware."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "How are you this morning, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Better than a man who has not woken up fasting and has not visited a sick person."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon the family of al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and said, "Peace be upon you."
They said, "And upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah and His blessings." He said, "How have you spent the morning?"
They said, "Well, praise be to Allah. And how have you spent the morning, O Messenger of Allah, our father and mother?" He said:
"I have spent the morning well, praising Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the noble one of a people comes to you, honor him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever apologizes to his brother with an excuse and he does not accept it, will bear a sin like that of a tax collector."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr went out on a trading journey to Buṣrā a year before the death of the Prophet ﷺ, and with him were Nuʿaymān and Suwaybiṭ ibn Ḥarmalah, both of whom had been present at Badr. Nuʿaymān was in charge of the provisions, and Suwaybiṭ was a man fond of joking. He said to Nuʿaymān, "Feed me."
He said, "Not until Abū Bakr comes." He said, "Then I will surely make you angry."
He said: They passed by some people, and Suwaybiṭ said to them, "Will you buy from me a slave of mine?" They said, "Yes."
He said, "He is a slave who talks, and he will tell you, 'I am free.'
If, when he says this to you, you will leave him alone, then do not spoil my slave for me."
They said, "No, we will buy him from you."
So they bought him from him for ten young she-camels. Then they came to him and put a turban or a rope around his neck.
Nuʿaymān said, "This man is making fun of you, and I am free; I am not a slave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade sitting between the shade and the sun.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ found me sleeping on my stomach in the mosque, and he nudged me with his foot and said:
"What is the matter with you and this way of sleeping? This is a way of sleeping that Allah dislikes," or he said, "that Allah hates."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by me while I was lying on my stomach, and he nudged me with his foot and said:
"O Junayb, this is only the way the people of the Fire lie down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a man sleeping in the mosque, lying face down, and he struck him with his foot and said:
"Get up and sit, for this is the sleep of Hell."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If I live, Allah willing, I will forbid the names Rabāḥ, Najīḥ, Aflaḥ, Nāfiʿ, and Yasār."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAlqamah,
both said: We came to ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd in his house, and he said: Have those people prayed behind you? We said: No.
He said: Then stand and pray.

He did not command us to give the adhān or the iqāmah. He said: We went to stand behind him, but he took us by our hands and placed one of us on his right and the other on his left. He said: When he bowed, we placed our hands on our knees. He said: So he struck our hands, pressed his palms together, and then put them between his thighs. He said: When he had finished the prayer, he said: There will be rulers over you who delay the prayer beyond its proper time and stifle it until the time of the dying sun. When you see that they have done so, pray the prayer at its proper time, and make your prayer with them a voluntary one. If you are three, pray together; and if you are more than that, let one of you lead you. When one of you bows, let him spread his forearms over his thighs, bend, and press his palms together. It is as though I can see the spreading of the fingers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he showed them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb

delivered a sermon on Friday. He mentioned the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and mentioned Abū Bakr. He said: I saw as if a rooster pecked me three times, and I think that this is nothing but the approach of my death. Some people are telling me to appoint a successor, but Allah will not let His religion be lost, nor His caliphate, nor that with which He sent His Prophet ﷺ. If my end comes quickly, then the caliphate is to be decided by consultation among these six, with whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pleased when he died. I know that some people will find fault with this matter; I struck them with this hand of mine for the sake of Islam. If they do so, they are the enemies of Allah, the disbelievers, the misguided. Then, I leave behind nothing more important to me than kalālah. I never asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about anything as much as I asked him about kalālah, and he never was as stern with me about anything as he was about it, until he poked me in the chest with his finger and said:
O ʿUmar, is the verse of the summer, at the end of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, not sufficient for you?

If I live, I will judge in it with a ruling by which those who recite the Qurʾān and those who do not recite it will judge. Then he said: O Allah, I call You to witness against the governors of the regions. I only sent them to them so that they would be just toward them, teach the people their religion and the Sunnah of their Prophet ﷺ, distribute among them their fayʾ, and refer to me whatever is unclear to them of their affairs. Then, O people, you eat two plants which I consider nothing but foul: this onion and garlic. I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he found the smell of them on a man in the mosque, order that he be taken out to al-Baqīʿ. So whoever eats them, let him kill their smell by cooking.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū ʿAmr said: Transfer. And Dāwūd ibn Rashīd narrated to us: Al-Walīd narrated to us,
and this is his wording, from al-Awzāʿī, from al-Zuhrī,
from Abū Salamah,
from Abū Hurayrah: The prayer
would be called for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the people would take their places before the Prophet ﷺ took his.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to us, and there was no one but me, my mother, and Umm Ḥarām, my maternal aunt. He said:
Get up, so that I may lead you in prayer.
It was not at a time of obligatory prayer, and he prayed with us.
A man said to Thābit: Where did he place Anas in relation to him? He said: He placed him on his right.
Then he made supplication for us, the people of the house, for every good of this world and the Hereafter. My mother said: O Messenger of Allah, your little servant, pray to Allah for him.
He said: So he made supplication for me for every good, and among the last things he asked for me was that he said:
O Allah, increase his wealth and his children, and bless him in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered the land of the Romans with Maslamah, and a man who had stolen from the spoils was brought. He asked Sālim about him, and he said: I heard my father narrate from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "
If you find a man who has stolen from the spoils, burn his belongings and beat him."
He said: We found a copy of the Qurʾān among his belongings, so he asked Sālim about it, and he said: Sell it and give its price in charity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yaḥyā [narrated] that a man
from the polytheists joined the Prophet ﷺ in order to fight alongside him, and he said: "Go back."
Then they came to an agreement, and he said: "
We do not seek the help of a polytheist."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Badr with a sword and said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah has healed my chest today of the enemy, so grant me this sword. He said: "
This sword is neither mine nor yours."
So I left, saying: It will be given today to someone who has not been tried as I have been.
While I was in that state, the messenger came to me and said: Respond to the call.
I thought that something had been revealed about me because of my words. So I came, and the Prophet ﷺ said to me: "

You asked me for this sword, and it was neither mine nor yours, but Allah has now made it mine, so it is yours." Then he recited: {They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger} to the end of the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I set out with al-Ashtar

to ʿAlī, peace be upon him, and we said: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entrust you with anything that he did not entrust to the people in general? He said: No, except what is in this book of mine. Musaddad said: He brought out a book; and Aḥmad said: a book from the sheath of his sword. In it was: "

The believers are equal in their blood, and they are one hand against others, and the least of them may extend their protection. Beware: a believer is not to be killed for a disbeliever, nor one under a covenant during his covenant. Whoever introduces an innovation, it is upon himself; and whoever introduces an innovation or gives shelter to one who introduces an innovation, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people."
Musaddad said, from Ibn Abī ʿArūbah: He brought out a book.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a treaty between Muʿāwiyah and the Romans, and he used to travel through their lands. When the treaty expired, he raided them. Then there was a man on a mount, or on a horse, saying: Allah is the Greatest! Fulfilment, not treachery!
It was ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah. Muʿāwiyah asked him about that, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
Whoever has a treaty with a people must not loosen it or tighten it until its term has run out, or he openly renounces it to them on equal terms."
He said: So Muʿāwiyah returned with the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Whoever kills a person under a treaty without just cause, Allah has forbidden Paradise to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Makḥūl and Ibn Abī Zakariyyā went to Khālid ibn Maʿdān, and I went with them. He narrated to us from Jubayr ibn Nufayr about the truce.
Jubayr said: Come with us to Dhū Mikhbar, a man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. So we went to him, and Jubayr asked him about the truce. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "

You will make a secure peace with the Romans, then you and they will fight an enemy behind you. You will be given victory, take spoils, and be safe. Then you will return until you camp in a meadow with hillocks. A man from the Christians will raise the cross and say: The cross has prevailed. A man from the Muslims will become angry and smash it. At that, the Romans will act treacherously and gather for the great battle."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a man: "
I have been commanded to observe the Day of Aḍḥā as a festival, which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has made for this nation."
The man said: What if I find only a female milk-animal that was lent to me; should I sacrifice it? He said: "
No. Rather, take some of your hair, trim your nails, clip your moustache, and shave your pubic hair. That is the completion of your sacrifice with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of sacrifice the Prophet ﷺ sacrificed two horned rams, mostly white, with testicles removed. When he turned them to face [the qiblah], he said: "

Indeed I have turned my face to Him who created the heavens and the earth, upright in the faith of Abraham, and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner. This I have been commanded, and I am of the Muslims. O Allah, from You and for You, on behalf of Muhammad and his nation. In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest." Then he sacrificed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever visits a sick person whose appointed time has not yet come and says by him seven times: I ask Allah the Mighty, Lord of the Mighty Throne, to heal you, Allah will cure him of that illness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hannād and Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd al-Muḥāribī — the meaning is the same — said: ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Ḥarb al-Mulāʾī narrated to us,
from Abū Khālid al-Dālānī, from Qatādah,
from Abū al-ʿĀliyah,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
that he saw the Prophet ﷺ fall asleep while prostrating until he breathed heavily or snored, and then he got up to pray.
So I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have slept!" He said:
"Ablution is only obligatory for the one who sleeps lying on his side, for when he lies down, his joints relax."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and I was with him, and he entered the house of a woman of the Anṣār. She slaughtered a sheep for him and he ate, and she brought him a tray of fresh dates and he ate from it. Then he performed ablution for the Ẓuhr prayer and prayed. Then he left, and she brought him some of the leftover meat of the sheep, and he ate. Then he prayed the ʿAṣr prayer without performing ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Jarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh perform ablution and wipe over his leather socks. He said: I asked him about that, and he said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ perform ablution and wipe over his leather socks.
So I said to him: Was that before the revelation of Sūrat al-Māʾidah or after it? He said: I only accepted Islam after [the revelation of] al-Māʾidah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh about wiping
over the leather socks, and he said: It is the Sunnah, O son of my brother.
He said: And I asked him about wiping
over the turban, and he said: Wipe the hair with water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sometimes the Prophet ﷺ would bathe after sexual impurity, then come and seek warmth with me, and I would embrace him to myself without having bathed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When I was menstruating, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would command me to wear a waist wrapper, and then he would have physical contact with me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If it is red blood, [the expiation is] one dinar, and if it is yellow blood, half a dinar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was asked about tayammum,
and he said: Allah said in His Book when He mentioned ablution:
"Wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows,"
and He said about tayammum:
"Wipe your faces and your hands," and He said:
"As for the male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands." The Sunnah regarding cutting is [that it is at] the palms.
It is only the face and the palms, meaning tayammum.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have us recite the Qur'an in every state, as long as he was not in a state of sexual impurity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Similar to this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Prayer has a beginning and an end. The beginning of the time of the Ẓuhr prayer is when the sun passes its zenith, and the end of its time is when the time of ʿAṣr enters. The beginning of the time of ʿAṣr is when its time enters, and the end of its time is when the sun turns yellow. The beginning of the time of Maghrib is when the sun sets, and the end of its time is when the twilight disappears. The beginning of the time of the last ʿIshāʾ prayer is when the twilight disappears, and the end of its time is when half of the night has passed. The beginning of the time of Fajr is when dawn breaks, and the end of its time is when the sun rises."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Pray Fajr when it is bright, for that is greater in reward."
He said: Shuʿbah and al-Thawrī also narrated this hadith from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq.
He said: And Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān also narrated it from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatādah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw anyone hasten the Ẓuhr prayer more than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor Abū Bakr, nor ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would hasten the Ẓuhr prayer more than you do, and you hasten the ʿAṣr prayer more than he did.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to converse at night with Abū Bakr about a matter of the affairs of the Muslims, and I was with them both.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The first time of the prayer is the pleasure of Allah, and the last time is the pardon of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never prayed a prayer at the end of its time twice, until Allah took his soul.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever combines two prayers without an excuse has come to one of the doors of the major sins."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When morning came, we went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I told him about the dream, and he said:
"This is a true dream. Stand with Bilāl, for he has a more beautiful and farther-reaching voice than you. Teach him what was said to you, and let him call it out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The call to prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in pairs, in pairs, in both the adhān and the iqāmah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Bilāl:

"O Bilāl, when you call the adhān, be measured in your adhān, and when you call the iqāmah, be quick. And make between your adhān and your iqāmah a interval long enough for the one eating to finish his food, the one drinking to finish his drink, and the one who has entered to relieve himself to finish his need. And do not stand until you see me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She was asked, "Did the Prophet ﷺ ever recite lines of poetry?" She said, "He would recite the poetry of Ibn Rawāḥah, and he would recite and say:
'And he will bring you news, one whom you did not provide with supplies.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I sat with the Prophet ﷺ more than a hundred times. His Companions would recite poetry to one another and recall matters from the Jāhiliyyah (the pre-Islamic era), while he remained silent, and at times he would smile along with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a man to sleep on a roof that has no barrier around it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah has given a parable: a straight path, with a wall on each side of the path, in which are open doors, and over the doors hang curtains. A caller calls at the head of the path, and another caller calls from above it:

'And Allah invites to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path.' The doors on either side of the path are the limits set by Allah, so no one falls into the limits of Allah until the curtain is lifted. And the one who calls from above it is the admonisher from his Lord [within every believer]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us one day and said:
"I saw in a dream that Jibrīl was at my head and Mīkāʾīl at my feet, and one of them said to the other, 'Give him a parable.'

He said, 'Listen, may your ear hear, and understand, may your heart understand. Your likeness and the likeness of your nation is that of a king who took a residence, then built a house in it, then placed a table in it, then sent a messenger to invite people to his food. Some of them answered the messenger and some of them left him. So Allah is the King, the residence is Islam, the house is Paradise, and you, Muḥammad, are the messenger. Whoever answers you enters Islam, whoever enters Islam enters Paradise, and whoever enters Paradise eats what is in it.'"
This hadith has been narrated through more than one route from the Prophet ﷺ, with a chain that is more authentic than this one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer, then left, took ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd by the hand and went out with him to the valley of Makkah. He made him sit, then drew a line around him, then said:
"Do not leave your line, for men will come up to you, and do not speak to them, for they will not speak to you."

He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went where he wished. While I was sitting inside my line, men came to me who looked like the Zuṭṭ, in their hair and bodies; I saw no nakedness and no [outer] covering. They would come up to me but not go past the line, and then turn back toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then, when it was the end of the night, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me while I was sitting, and he said:
"I have been watching me [i.e., looking for me] since the beginning of the night."

Then he came in to me inside my line, rested his head on my thigh, and slept. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ slept, he would breathe heavily. While I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ resting his head on my thigh, suddenly there were men wearing white garments; Allah knows how beautiful they were. They came up to me, and one group of them sat at the head of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and a group at his feet. Then they said among themselves, "We have never seen a servant given what this Prophet has been given: his eyes sleep while his heart is awake. Give him a parable: a lord who built a palace, then prepared a banquet and invited people to his food and drink. Whoever answers him eats of his food and drinks of his drink, and whoever does not answer him, he punishes," or he said, "he torments." Then they rose up, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke at that moment and said:
"Did you hear what these said? And do you know who these are?"
I said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"They are the angels. Do you know what the parable is that they gave?"
I said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:

"The parable they gave: the Most Merciful, Blessed and Exalted, built Paradise and invited His servants to it. Whoever answers Him enters Paradise, and whoever does not answer Him, He punishes or torments."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The likeness of my nation is that of rain: it is not known whether its beginning is better or its end."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do you know what this is and what this is?" and he threw down two pebbles.
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"That is hope, and that is the appointed term [of death]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He accompanied
Yazīd ibn Abī Kabshah on a journey,
and Yazīd used to fast while travelling. Abū Burdah said to him: I heard Abū Mūsā say many times that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When a servant falls ill or travels,
there is recorded for him the same [reward] as what he used to do when resident and healthy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Badr, prisoners were brought,
and al-ʿAbbās was brought, and he had no garment on him.
The Prophet ﷺ looked for a shirt for him, and they found that the shirt of ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy would fit him,
so the Prophet ﷺ clothed him with it.
For that reason the Prophet ﷺ took off his own shirt that he had put on him.
Ibn ʿUyaynah said: He had done the Prophet ﷺ a favour, so he wanted to repay him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the children: ʿAmr used to narrate to us from Ibn Shihāb,
from the Prophet ﷺ, and then we heard it from az-Zuhrī,
who said: ʿUbaydullāh informed me,
from Ibn ʿAbbās, from aṣ-Ṣaʿb, who said: "They are from them."
And he did not say as ʿAmr said:
"They are from their fathers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh, may Allah be pleased with him, said to me: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Will you not relieve me of Dhū al-Khalaṣah?"
It was a house of Khathʿam called the Yemeni Kaʿbah,
so I set out with one hundred and fifty of Aḥmas,
and they were horsemen.
I told the Prophet ﷺ that I could not stay firm on horses,
so he struck my chest until I saw the mark of his fingers on my chest, and he said:
"O Allah, make him firm, and make him a guide, rightly guided."
So he went to it, broke it down and burned it,
then he sent a messenger to the Prophet ﷺ to give him the good news. Jarīr's messenger said: O Messenger of Allah,
by the One who sent you with the truth,
I did not come to you until I had left it like a mangy camel.
So he blessed the horses of Aḥmas and their men five times.
Musaddad said: A house in Khathʿam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In Sūrat al-Muzzammil, {Stand [in prayer] at night, except for a little — half of it}, was abrogated by the verse in which [Allah says]: {He knows that you will not be able to keep count of it, so He has turned to you in forgiveness; so recite what is easy of the Qur'an}. "Nāshi'at al-layl" means the early part of the night, and their prayer used to be at the beginning of the night. He says: this is more fitting for you to keep count of what Allah made obligatory upon you of standing in the night prayer, because when a person sleeps, he does not know when he will wake up. As for His saying {more suitable for speech}, it means more fitting for understanding the Qur'an. And His saying {Indeed, you have by day a long occupation} means long free time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the beginning of Sūrat al-Muzzammil was revealed, they used to stand in prayer about as much as they did in the month of Ramadan, until the end of it was revealed. Between its beginning and its end was a year.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah may Allah be pleased with her said: Do not abandon the night prayer, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never abandoned it, and when he was ill or feeling sluggish, he would pray sitting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would be woken by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, during the night, and the pre-dawn time would not arrive until he had finished his portion [of prayer].
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I said to her: At what time would he pray? She said: When he heard the crying out [of the rooster], he would get up and pray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whenever something distressed the Prophet ﷺ, he would pray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning this verse: {Their sides forsake their beds,
they call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and spend from what We have provided them}, he said:
They would stay awake between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ, praying.
And al-Ḥasan used to say: It is the night prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: {They used to sleep but little of the night}, he said:
They used to pray between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ.
In the narration of Yaḥyā he added:
And likewise {Their sides forsake [their beds]}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The recitation of the Prophet ﷺ, while he was in the house, was at a level that those in the room could hear.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The recitation of the Prophet ﷺ at night was such that he would raise his voice at times and lower it at times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ with this account, without mentioning [the earlier part], he said to Abū Bakr: "
Raise your voice a little," and to ʿUmar: "Lower it a little." He added: "
And I heard you, Bilāl, reciting from this sūrah and from that sūrah." He said:
[Bilāl said:] Good words, which Allah the Exalted joins together one with another. The Prophet ﷺ said: "
All of you have done right."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her: A man
stood [in prayer] during the night and recited, raising his voice with the Qur'an.
When morning came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
May Allah have mercy on so-and-so,
how many a verse he reminded me of last night that I had omitted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in spiritual retreat in the mosque, and he heard them reciting aloud.
He drew back the curtain and said: "
Indeed, every one of you is conversing privately with his Lord, so let none of you disturb another,
and let none of you raise his voice over another in recitation." Or he said: "in prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah,
may Allah be pleased with her, was asked about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the depths of the night, and she said:
He would pray the ʿIshāʾ prayer in congregation,
then return to his family and pray four rakʿahs,
then retire to his bed and sleep, with his water for ablution covered by his head
and his siwāk placed [ready], until Allah woke him at the time of the night He woke him.
He would use the siwāk and perform ablution thoroughly,
then stand at his place of prayer and pray eight rakʿahs, reciting in them Umm al-Kitāb, a sūrah of the Qur'an, and whatever Allah willed,
without sitting in any of them until he sat in the eighth, and he would not give the salām.
He would recite in the ninth,
then sit and supplicate with whatever Allah willed that he supplicate,
asking Him and turning to Him in longing, and he would give one salām, a forceful one,
so strong that it almost woke the people of the house,
then he would recite Umm al-Kitāb while sitting,
and bow while sitting,
then recite in the second [rakʿah], bow and prostrate while sitting,
then supplicate as much as Allah willed that he supplicate,
then give the salām and depart.
That continued to be the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he grew heavy [in age], and he reduced two from the nine,
making it six or seven rakʿahs, and the two rakʿahs while sitting, until he was taken [in death] in that state, ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ consulted [the people] when news reached him of the approach of Abū Sufyān. [The narrator] said: Abū Bakr spoke, but he turned away from him. Then ʿUmar spoke, but he turned away from him. Then Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah stood up and said: "Is it us you mean, O Messenger of Allah? By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you ordered us to plunge our horses into the sea, we would plunge them in, and if you ordered us to strike their livers [urging them on] as far as Barkal-Ghimād, we would do it." He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called the people, and they set out until they camped at Badr. The water-carriers of Quraysh came to them, and among them was a black boy belonging to the Banū al-Ḥajjāj. They seized him, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began asking him about Abū Sufyān and his companions.
He would say: "I have no knowledge of Abū Sufyān, but here are Abū Jahl, ʿUtbah, Shaybah and Umayyah ibn Khalaf."
When he said that, they beat him, and he said: "Yes, I will tell you. This is Abū Sufyān."
Then when they left him and asked him again, he said: "I have no knowledge of Abū Sufyān, but here are Abū Jahl, ʿUtbah and Umayyah ibn Khalaf among the people."
When he said this too, they beat him, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing in prayer. When he saw that, he finished [his prayer] and said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, you beat him when he tells you the truth, and you leave him when he lies to you."
He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"This is the place where so-and-so will fall."
He said: And he placed his hand on the ground, [saying] "here and here." He said: And not one of them [the enemy] strayed from the place where the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sons of Kaʿb ibn Mālik [narrated] that Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ

said: On the day of Khaybar, my brother fought fiercely alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but his sword rebounded on him and killed him. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke about that and doubted [his status]: a man who died by his own weapon. Salamah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from Khaybar, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you permit me to recite verses of rajaz for you?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted him. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Know what you say." So I said: "By Allah, were it not for Allah we would not have been guided, nor given charity, nor prayed." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You have spoken the truth."
"So send down tranquility upon us, and make our feet firm if we meet [the enemy]. The polytheists have transgressed against us." When I finished my verses, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Who said this?" I said: "My brother."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "May Allah have mercy on him."
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, some people are hesitant to pray over him, saying: a man who died by his own weapon."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He died striving, a fighter in the cause of Allah."
Ibn Shihāb said: Then I asked a son of Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ, and he narrated to me from his father the like of that, except that he said, when I said that some people were hesitant to pray over him,
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"They are wrong. He died striving, a fighter in the cause of Allah, so his reward is twofold." And he gestured with his two fingers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went on seven military expeditions with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I would stay behind in their camps, make food for them, treat the wounded, and attend to the sick.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered with my father upon the Prophet ﷺ, and I heard him say:
"This matter will not come to an end until twelve caliphs have passed among them."
He said: Then he said something that I could not hear well. He said: So I asked my father, "What did he say?" He said:
"All of them are from Quraysh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Numayr and Abū Bakr [narrated], attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ, and in the narration of Zuhayr he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Those who act justly will be with Allah on pulpits of light, on the right of the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic, and both His hands are right hands: those who are just in their judgment, in their families, and in whatever they are put in charge of."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O people, whoever among you we appoint to a task and he conceals from us even a needle or more, that is misappropriation, and he will bring it on the Day of Resurrection."
A dark-skinned man of the Anṣār stood up, as if I can see him now, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, take back your assignment from me." He said: "What is that?"
He said: "I heard you say such and such." He said:
"And I say it now: whoever we appoint to a task, let him bring [all of it], little and much. Whatever he is given from it, he may take, and whatever he is forbidden from, he must refrain from."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to Ibn ʿUmar
and asked him about ʿUthmān.
He mentioned some of his good deeds.
[Ibn ʿUmar] said, "Perhaps that upsets you." He said, "Yes."
He said, "May Allah rub your nose in the dust!"
Then he asked him about ʿAlī.
He mentioned some of his good deeds, and [Ibn ʿUmar] said, "That is he,
his house is in the middle of the houses of the Prophet ﷺ."
Then he said, "Perhaps that upsets you." He said, "Indeed."
He said, "May Allah rub your nose in the dust!
Go and do your utmost against me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Judge as you used to judge,
for I dislike disagreement, until the people are united,
or I die as my Companions died.
Ibn Sīrīn used to think that most of what was reported from ʿAlī was falsehood.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people used to say,
"Abū Hurayrah narrates too much."
But I used to stay close to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the sake of filling my stomach,
so that I would not eat leavened bread,
nor wear fine silk,
nor would this man or that woman serve me.
I used to press my belly against the pebbles because of hunger,
and I would ask a man to recite a verse to me, though I knew it, so that he would take me with him and feed me.
The best of people to the poor was Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib;
he would take us home and feed us whatever was in his house,
even to the point that he would bring out to us the empty fat-skin,
and we would split it open and lick what was in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whenever Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, greeted the son of Jaʿfar, he would say, "Peace be upon you, O son of the one with two wings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah, peace be upon her, sent a message to Abū Bakr asking for her inheritance from the Prophet ﷺ, from what Allah had granted as spoils to His Messenger ﷺ,
seeking the charity of the Prophet ﷺ in Medina and Fadak and what remained of the fifth of Khaybar.
Abū Bakr said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'We are not inherited from;
whatever we leave is charity.
The family of Muḥammad eat from this wealth,' meaning the wealth of Allah, 'but they may not take more than their food.'"
"By Allah, I will not change anything of the charity of the Prophet ﷺ from the condition it was in during the time of the Prophet ﷺ,
and I will act regarding it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted." Then ʿAlī recited the testimony of faith,
and said, "We recognize, O Abū Bakr, your virtue."
And he mentioned their kinship to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and their right.
Then Abū Bakr spoke and said, "By Him in whose hand is my soul,
the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are dearer to me to keep ties with than my own relatives."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr said, "Watch over Muḥammad ﷺ in his family."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Fāṭimah is a part of me;
whoever angers her angers me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān suffered a severe nosebleed in the year known as the Year of the Nosebleed,
so that it kept him from Hajj, and he made a will.
A man from Quraysh came to him and said, "Appoint a successor."
He said, "Are they saying that?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "Who?" The man was silent.
Then another man came to him, I think it was al-Ḥārith, and said, "Appoint a successor."
ʿUthmān said, "Are they saying that?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "Who is he?" He was silent. [ʿUthmān] said, "Perhaps they said al-Zubayr." He said, "Yes."
He said, "By Him in whose hand is my soul, he is the best of them as far as I know,
and he was the dearest of them to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with ʿUthmān
when a man came to him and said, "Appoint a successor."
He said, "Is that being said?" He said, "Yes, al-Zubayr."
He said, "By Allah, you know that he is the best of you." [He said it] three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Companions of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to al-Zubayr on the day of Yarmūk, "Will you not charge so that we may charge with you?" He said, "If I charge, you will not follow."
They said, "We will."
So he charged at them until he broke through their lines,
and passed beyond them with no one with him,
then he returned, and they seized his bridle
and struck him two blows on his shoulder, between which was a blow he had received on the day of Badr.
ʿUrwah said, "I used to put my fingers into those wounds, playing, when I was young."
ʿUrwah said, "ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr was with him that day, and he was ten years old,
so he put him on a horse and assigned a man to look after him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day, while in the mosque, Ibn ʿUmar looked at a man dragging his garments in a corner of the mosque and said, "Look who this is. I wish he were with me."
A man said to him, "Do you not know him, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān? This is Muḥammad ibn Usāmah."
Ibn ʿUmar lowered his head
and tapped the ground with his hands,
then said, "If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seen him, he would have loved him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One night, when he had finished his prayer, [he said]:

"O Allah, I ask You for a mercy from You by which You guide my heart, gather my affairs, mend my disarray, set right what is absent from me, raise up what is present with me, purify my deeds, inspire me with right guidance, restore my familiar affairs, and protect me from every evil. O Allah, grant me faith and certainty after which there is no disbelief, and a mercy by which I attain the honor of Your generosity in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, I ask You for success in what You give, and [it is also reported:] in what You decree, for the lodging of the martyrs, the life of the blessed, and victory over the enemies. O Allah, I present my need to You, though my judgment falls short and my deeds are weak; I am in need of Your mercy. So I ask You, O Decreer of affairs and O Healer of hearts, just as You grant safe passage between the seas, to grant me safety from the punishment of the blazing Fire, from the cry of destruction, and from the trial of the graves. O Allah, whatever good my judgment has fallen short of, my intention has not reached, and my request has not attained, of any good You have promised to any of Your creation or any good You will give to any of Your servants, I desire it from You and ask You for it by Your mercy, O Lord of the worlds. O Allah, Possessor of the firm cord and of the sound command, I ask You for security on the Day of the Warning and for Paradise on the Day of Eternity, with those brought near, the witnesses, those who bow and prostrate, who fulfill their covenants. You are Merciful and Loving, and You do what You will. O Allah, make us guides who are rightly guided, neither astray nor leading others astray, at peace with Your friends and hostile to Your enemies. We love, by Your love, whoever loves You, and we oppose, by Your enmity, whoever opposes You. O Allah, this is the supplication, and the response is up to You; this is the effort, and reliance is upon You. O Allah, place light for me in my grave, light in my heart, light before me, light behind me, light on my right, light on my left, light above me, light beneath me, light in my hearing, light in my sight, light in my hair, light in my skin, light in my flesh, light in my blood, and light in my bones. O Allah, make light great for me, give me light, and make light for me. Glory be to Him who is clothed in might and is described by it. Glory be to Him who is robed in majesty and is generous through it. Glory be to Him to whom alone glorification is due. Glory be to the Possessor of grace and blessings. Glory be to the Possessor of majesty and generosity. Glory be to the Possessor of glory and honor."
label: machine translation

segments_en: His name is Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Hamdānī. Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad narrated to us,
who said: Ibn Jurayj said: Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah informed me,
from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever sits in a gathering in which there is much idle talk, and before getting up from that gathering says: 'Glory and praise be to You, O Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You,'
he will be forgiven for whatever occurred in that gathering."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a matter distressed the Prophet ﷺ, he would raise his head to the sky and say:
"Glory be to Allah, the Almighty."
And when he exerted himself in supplication, he would say:
"O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I intend to travel, so give me provisions. He said:
"May Allah provide you with piety." He said: Give me more. He said: "And may He forgive your sin."
He said: Give me more, may my father and mother be your ransom. He said:
"And may He make good easy for you wherever you are."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her. She said: When the Prophet ﷺ saw the wind, he would say:

"O Allah, I ask You for its good, the good of what is in it, and the good of what it was sent with; and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil of what is in it, and the evil of what it was sent with."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard the sound of thunder and thunderbolts, he would say:
"O Allah, do not kill us with Your wrath, and do not destroy us with Your punishment, and grant us well-being before that."
He said: This hadith is gharīb; we do not know it except through this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ saw the new moon, he would say:
"O Allah, bring it over us with blessing and faith, with safety and Islam. My Lord and your Lord is Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And that is because I asked him, "What do you think of the withdrawal of al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays? What was it?" He said: I heard al-Aḥnaf say: I came to Madinah while on Hajj, and while we were in our lodgings putting down our saddles, someone came and said, "The people have gathered in the mosque." I went out to look, and there were the people gathered, and in their midst a group sitting, and among them were ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, al-Zubayr, Ṭalḥah and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may Allah's mercy be upon them. When I stood over them, it was said, "This is ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, he has come." He said: He came wearing a yellow cloak. I said to my companion, "Stay where you are until I see what has brought him."
ʿUthmān said, "Is ʿAlī here? Is al-Zubayr here? Is Ṭalḥah here? Is Saʿd here?" They said, "Yes."
He said, "Then I ask you by Allah, other than Whom there is no god: do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Whoever buys the mirbad of the family of so-and-so, Allah will forgive him'?"
So I bought it, then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "I have bought the mirbad of the family of so-and-so." He said:
"Then make it part of our mosque, and the reward is yours." They said, "Yes."
He said, "Then I ask you by Allah, other than Whom there is no god: do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Whoever buys the well of Rūmah, Allah will forgive him'?"
So I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "I have bought the well of Rūmah." He said:
"Then make it a source of drinking water for the Muslims, and the reward is yours." They said, "Yes."
He said, "Then I ask you by Allah, other than Whom there is no god: do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Whoever equips the army of hardship, Allah will forgive him'?"
So I equipped them until they lacked not even a hobbling rope or a bridle. They said, "Yes."
He said, "O Allah, bear witness! O Allah, bear witness! O Allah, bear witness!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met Abū Dharr and said, "Narrate to me."
He said: Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no Muslim servant who spends a pair from every kind of his wealth in the cause of Allah, except that the gatekeepers of Paradise will meet him, every one of them calling him to what he has."
I said, "How is that?" He said:
"If they are camels, then two camels; if they are cattle, then two cows."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He entered with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon a deceased person, and the women wept. Jabr said, "Do you weep while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is sitting?" He said:
"Let them weep as long as he is among them. But when it has become obligatory, let no weeping woman weep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade celibacy (tabattul).
label: machine translation

segments_en: He entered upon the Mother of the Believers, ʿĀʾishah, and said, "I want to ask you about celibacy (tabattul); what is your view of it?" She said, "Do not do it. Have you not heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, say: {And We certainly sent messengers before you and gave them wives and offspring}? So do not practice celibacy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, proposed to Fāṭimah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "She is young."
Then ʿAlī proposed to her, and he married her to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married and went in to his wife. Anas said: My mother, Umm Sulaym, made ḥays (a dish of dates, cheese and ghee), put it in a bowl, and said, "Anas, take this to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and say: 'My mother sent this to you, and she sends you greetings of peace and says: This is a small gift from us to you, O Messenger of Allah.'" So I took it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "My mother sends you greetings of peace and says: This is a small gift from us to you, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"Put it down." Then he said, "Go and invite for me so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so, and whomever you meet."
And he named several men. Anas said: So I invited those he had named and whomever I met.
[The narrator] said: I asked Anas, "How many were they?" He said, "About three hundred."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me,
"Anas, bring the bowl."
He said: They came in until the Ṣuffah and the room were full. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Let them sit in circles of ten, and let each person eat from what is in front of him."
He said: So they ate until they were satisfied. A group went out and another group came in, until all of them had eaten. Then he said to me,
"Anas, lift it up."

He said: So I lifted it, and I do not know whether there was more when I set it down or when I lifted it. Some groups of them stayed on, talking in the house of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting there and his wife was facing the wall. They became a burden on the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and greeted his wives with peace, then returned. When they saw that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had returned, they thought they had burdened him. He said: So they hurried to the door and all of them left. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and let down the curtain and went in, while I was sitting in the room. He stayed only a short while before coming out to me.

And this verse was revealed, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and recited it to the people: {O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet except when you are permitted to a meal, not waiting for its readiness. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse, without seeking to remain for conversation. Indeed, that used to harm the Prophet...} to the end of the verse.
Al-Jaʿd said: Anas ibn Mālik said, "I am the most recent of people in knowledge of these verses, and the wives of the Prophet ﷺ were veiled [from view]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"A woman must not fast while her husband is present, except with his permission, other than in Ramadan; and she must not permit anyone into his house while he is present, except with his permission."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with them both: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned Ramadan, and he struck his hands together and said,

"The month is like this, and like this, and like this" — then he folded his thumb on the third time — "so fast when you see it [the crescent] and break the fast when you see it, and if it is overcast for you, then calculate it as thirty [days]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We slaughtered a horse during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and we ate it.
And Qutaybah said in his narration: So we ate its meat.
ʿAbdah ibn Sulaymān differed with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about eating the dabb (spiny-tailed lizard), and he said,
"I do not eat it, and I do not declare it forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to al-Aswad, "Did you ask the Mother of the Believers about the containers in which it is disliked to prepare nabīdh?" He said, "Yes."
I said, "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade preparing nabīdh in."
She said, "He forbade us, the People of the House, from preparing nabīdh in gourds and in pitch-coated containers."
He said: I said to him, "Did you not mention the ḥantam and the jarr?" He said, "I only narrate to you what I heard. Should I narrate to you what I did not hear?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAṭāʾ said to me: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Do not combine fresh dates and unripe dates, nor raisins and dates, together in nabīdh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to breathe three times while drinking from the vessel, and he claimed that Anas said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to breathe three times while drinking from the vessel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ḥibbān ibn ʿAṭiyyah disputed, and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said to Ḥibbān: "I know what emboldened your companion"—meaning ʿAlī—"to shed blood."
He said: "What is it, may you have no father?" He said: "Something I heard him say."
He said: "What is it?" He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, al-Zubayr, and Abū Marthad, and each of us was a horseman, and he said:

'Go until you reach Rawḍat Ḥājj'—Abū Salamah said: this is how Abū ʿAwānah said it, 'Ḥājj'—'for there is a woman there carrying a letter from Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah to the polytheists. Bring it to me.'
So we set off on our horses until we overtook her at the very place the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had told us, riding on a camel of hers.
He had written to the people of Makkah about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marching against them.
We said: 'Where is the letter you have with you?' She said: 'I have no letter.'
So we made her camel kneel,
and we searched her saddle but found nothing.
My companion said: 'We do not see a letter with her.'
He said: I said: 'We know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not lie.' Then ʿAlī swore by the One by whom oaths are sworn: 'You will bring out the letter, or I will strip you.'
She reached for her waist-wrap, for she had it tied with a cloak, and brought out the letter.
They brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and ʿUmar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, he has betrayed Allah, His Messenger, and the believers.
Let me strike off his neck.'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'O Ḥāṭib, what made you do what you did?'
He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, why would I not be a believer in Allah and His Messenger?
But I wanted to have some favor with the people,
by which Allah would protect my family and my property,
and there is none of your Companions except that he has someone from his people there through whom Allah protects his family and property.' He said: 'He has spoken the truth,
so say nothing to him except good.'
He said: ʿUmar repeated and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, he has betrayed Allah, His Messenger, and the believers,
let me strike off his neck.' He said:
'Is he not one of the people of Badr?
How do you know? Perhaps Allah looked upon them and said: Do what you wish, for I have made Paradise obligatory for you.'
ʿUmar's eyes filled with tears, and he said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.'
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī, peace be upon him,
burned some people who had apostatized from Islam. That reached Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "I would not have burned them with fire, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Do not punish with the punishment of Allah.'
I would have killed them according to the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Whoever changes his religion, kill him.'"
That reached ʿAlī, peace be upon him, and he said: "Woe to Ibn ʿAbbās!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah, peace be upon them both, complained of what she suffered in her hand from the grinding mill,
so she went to the Prophet ﷺ to ask him for a servant, but did not find him,
so she mentioned that to ʿĀʾishah,
and when he came, she told him.
[ʿAlī] said: He came to us after we had taken to our beds,
and I started to get up, but he said: "Stay where you are."
He sat between us until I felt the coolness of his feet on my chest. Then he said:
"Shall I not guide you to something better for you than a servant?
When you go to your bed,
or take to your beds,
say 'Allāhu akbar' thirty-three times,
say 'Subḥān Allāh' thirty-three times,
and say 'Al-ḥamdu lillāh' thirty-three times.
This is better for you than a servant."
And from Shuʿbah, from Khālid, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: The tasbīḥ is thirty-four.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A skin of fat was lowered on the day of Khaybar. He said: I went to it and clung to it. He said: Then I said, "I will not give anyone any of this today." He said: I turned around, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiling at me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sulayk al-Ghaṭafānī came on Friday while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting on the pulpit, and Sulayk sat down before praying. The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "Did you pray two rakʿahs?" He said, "No." He said, "Stand up and pray them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ two rakʿahs before the Ẓuhr prayer,
and two rakʿahs after the Ẓuhr prayer,
and two rakʿahs after the Maghrib prayer,
and two rakʿahs after the ʿIshāʾ prayer,
and two rakʿahs after the Friday prayer.
As for Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ, [he prayed them] in his house.
Ibn Abī az-Zinād said, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from Nāfiʿ: after ʿIshāʾ, [he prayed] with his family.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I attended the ʿĪd prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with them, and all of them used to pray before the sermon.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Yūnus,
and ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith,
that Ibn Shihāb
informed them, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah,

who said: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray eleven rakʿahs between finishing the ʿIshāʾ prayer and Fajr, giving the salām after every two rakʿahs and praying Witr with one. He would prostrate a prostration about as long as it takes one of you to recite fifty verses, then raise his head. When the muʾadhdhin fell silent after the call to the Fajr prayer and dawn had become clear to him, he prayed two light rakʿahs, then lay down on his right side until the muʾadhdhin came to him for the iqāmah, and he went out with him. Some of them add to others in the narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said:
"The sun and the moon do not eclipse because of anyone's death or life, but they are two signs among the signs of Allah. So when you see them, pray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Medina to Mecca, and he used to pray two rakʿahs until we returned to Medina. We said, "Did you stay there for any time?" He said, "We stayed there ten days."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to travel a journey of three days or more unless her father, or her son, or her husband, or her brother, or a mahram relative of hers is with her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed Ẓuhr with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Medina, four rakʿahs, and I prayed ʿAṣr with him at Dhū l-Ḥulayfah, two rakʿahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Maʿmar once [reported] from ʿImrān,
who said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ about the prayer of a man while sitting, and he said:
"Whoever prays standing, it is better;
and whoever prays sitting, he will have half the reward of the one standing;
and whoever prays lying down, he will have half the reward of the one sitting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Yazīd and Abū n-Naḍr,
from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾishah,

that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray sitting, reciting while sitting. When about thirty or forty verses of his recitation remained, he would stand and recite while standing, then bow, then prostrate. Then he would do the same in the second rakʿah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ said:

"The most beloved fasting to Allah is the fasting of Dāwūd; he used to fast half of the time. And the most beloved prayer to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the prayer of Dāwūd, peace be upon him; he used to sleep half of the night, then stand [in prayer], then sleep the last part of it, standing for a third of the night after its half."
He said: I said to ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, "Did ʿAmr ibn Aws say, 'He would stand a third of the night after its half'?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Devil ties three knots with a rope at the back of the head of each of you when he sleeps at night. If he wakes up and remembers Allah, one knot is undone; when he gets up and performs ablution, another knot is undone; and when he stands for prayer, all the knots are undone. He then starts the morning energetic and in good spirits, having gained good. If he does not do so, he starts the morning lazy and in bad spirits, having gained no good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Agharr,
and from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and says: Who calls upon Me, that I may answer him? Who asks Me, that I may give him? Who seeks My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: "He it is who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are clear—they are the foundation of the Book—and others that are ambiguous. As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow what is ambiguous in it, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation. And none knows its interpretation except Allah. And those firmly grounded in knowledge say: 'We believe in it; all is from our Lord.' And none takes heed except those of understanding." She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you see those who follow what is ambiguous in it, they are the ones whom Allah has named, so beware of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed ʿUwaymir
came to ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī, who was the chief of the Banū ʿAjlān, and said: "What do you say about a man who finds another man with his wife?
Should he kill him, and then you would kill him? Or what should he do? Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this for me." So ʿĀṣim came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah,"
but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked such questions.
Then ʿUwaymir asked him [about it], and he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked such questions and condemned them."
ʿUwaymir said: "By Allah, I will not stop until I ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it." So ʿUwaymir came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, a man finds another man with his wife.
Should he kill him, and then you would kill him? Or what should he do?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah has revealed Qur'an concerning you and your wife."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the two to carry out the mutual invocation of curses (liʿān) as Allah has described in His Book.
So he invoked the curse against her, and then said: "O Messenger of Allah,
if I keep her, then I have wronged her." So he divorced her.
This became the established practice for those after them among couples who exchange the oath of liʿān.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Watch: if she gives birth to a child who is very dark, with large black eyes, large buttocks and thick legs, then I do not think but that ʿUwaymir has told the truth about her,
and if she gives birth to a child who is ruddy, like a small lizard (waḥarah), then I do not think but that ʿUwaymir
has lied about her."
Then she gave birth to a child with the description by which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had described, confirming ʿUwaymir's account.
So afterwards he used to be attributed to his mother.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abzā instructed me to ask Ibn ʿAbbās
about these two verses:
"And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein." So I asked him, and he said: "Nothing has abrogated it."

And [I asked] about this verse: "And those who do not call upon another god along with Allah, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden [to kill] except by right." He said: "It was revealed concerning the polytheists."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yaʿlā [reported] that Saʿīd ibn Jubayr informed him from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that some people
from among the polytheists had killed a great deal and committed adultery a great deal,
and they came to Muḥammad ﷺ and said: "What you say and call to is indeed good, if only you would tell us that there is expiation for what we have done."

Then it was revealed: "And those who do not call upon another god along with Allah, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden [to kill] except by right, and do not commit adultery," and it was revealed: "Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of you—or the most excellent of you—is the one who learns the Qur'an and teaches it."
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.

Likewise, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī and more than one [narrator] reported from Sufyān al-Thawrī, from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿUthmān, from the Prophet ﷺ; and Sufyān does not mention in it Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah.
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān also narrated
this hadith from Sufyān and Shuʿbah,
from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad,
from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah,
from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿUthmān, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I married a woman, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Have you married?" I said: "Yes." He said:
"A virgin or a previously married woman?" I said: "Previously married." He said:
"Where are you from the young virgins and their play?"
Shuʿbah said: I mentioned it to ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, and he said: "I heard it from Jābir, and he only said:
'Why not a young girl, so you could play with her and she with you?'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr performed Hajj with us, and I heard him say: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "
Allah does not take away knowledge by snatching it from the people after having given it to them,
but He takes it away by taking away the scholars along with their knowledge,
so that there remain ignorant people who are asked for rulings and give rulings by their own opinion, so they go astray and lead others astray."

I related this to ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ. Then ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr performed Hajj again afterward, and she said: "O my nephew, go to ʿAbdullāh and confirm for me what he told you from him."
So I came to him and asked him, and he related it to me just as he had related it before.
Then I went to ʿĀʾishah and told her, and she was amazed and said: "By Allah, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr has indeed memorized well."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Abū Shurayḥ said] to ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, as he was sending expeditions to Makkah: "Permit me, O Commander, to tell you a statement which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up and delivered on the day after the conquest. My ears heard it, my heart retained it, and my eyes saw him when he spoke it. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "

'Makkah was made sacred by Allah; the people did not make it sacred. It is not lawful for anyone who believes in Allah and the Last Day to shed blood in it or to cut down a tree in it. If anyone seeks a concession on the basis of the fighting of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in it, then say to him: Allah permitted His Messenger ﷺ but did not permit you. He permitted me only for an hour of a day, and its sanctity has returned today just as it was sanctified yesterday. Let those present convey this to those absent.'"

Abū Shurayḥ was asked: "What did ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd say to you?" He said: "He said: 'I know that better than you, O Abū Shurayḥ. The Sanctuary does not give protection to a disobedient person, nor to one fleeing after shedding blood, nor to one fleeing after committing a grave crime.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him: "Do you have anything that is not in the Qurʾān?" And once he said: "anything that the people do not have?" He said: "By the One who split the grain and created the soul, we have nothing except what is in the Qurʾān,
except the understanding that a man is given of His Book,
and what is in this sheet."
I said: "And what is in the sheet?" He said: "The blood-money, the ransoming of captives,
and that a Muslim is not to be killed for a disbeliever."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the ʿIshāʾ prayer one night near the end of his life. When he finished the prayer, he stood up and said: "
Do you see this night of yours? At the end of one hundred years from it, no one who is on the face of the earth today will remain."

Ibn ʿUmar said: The people were mistaken about that statement of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in what they were saying in these reports about one hundred years. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said: "No one who is on the face of the earth today will remain,"
meaning by that that that generation would come to an end.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It reached me that Jarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh
said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Make the people be silent and listen." Then he said: "
Do not return to disbelief after me, striking one another's necks."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Sulaym bint Milḥān came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah is not shy of the truth. Is a bath required of a woman," meaning a full bath, "if she sees in her sleep what a man sees?" He said: "
Yes, if she sees the fluid, she should bathe."
Umm Salamah said: I said to her: "You have disgraced the women, O Umm Sulaym!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
all of them from Ibn ʿUyaynah,
Yaḥyā said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father,
may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked what a person in iḥrām may wear. He said: "

A person in iḥrām should not wear a shirt, a turban, a hooded cloak, or trousers, nor any garment touched by wars or saffron, nor leather socks, unless he cannot find sandals, in which case let him cut them off until they are below the ankles."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When one of you drinks, he should not breathe into the vessel,
and when one of you urinates, he should not touch his private part with his right hand,
and when one of you cleans himself, he should not wipe with his right hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Meat was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day, and the foreleg was handed to him, which he liked. He took a bite from it and said:

"I am the master of mankind on the Day of Resurrection. Do you know why? Allah will gather the first and the last on a single plain, so that the caller can make them all hear and the eye can take them all in. The sun will draw near, and the people will reach a degree of distress and anguish that they cannot bear or endure. Some of the people will say to others, 'Do you not see the state you are in? Do you not see what has befallen you? Will you not look for someone who can intercede for you with your Lord?' Some of the people will say to others, 'Go to Adam.'

So they will go to Adam and say, 'O Adam, you are the father of mankind. Allah created you with His own hand, breathed into you of His spirit, and commanded the angels, and they prostrated to you. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the state we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us?' Adam will say, 'Indeed my Lord is angry today as He has never been angry before and will never be angry again like it. He forbade me from the tree and I disobeyed Him. Myself, myself! Go to someone else. Go to Noah.'

So they will go to Noah and say, 'O Noah, you were the first of the messengers to the earth, and Allah named you a grateful servant. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the state we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us?' He will say to them, 'Indeed my Lord is angry today as He has never been angry before and will never be angry again like it. I had one supplication which I made against my people. Myself, myself! Go to Abraham, peace be upon him.'

So they will go to Abraham and say, 'You are the Prophet of Allah and His close friend from among the people of the earth. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the state we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us?' Abraham will say to them, 'Indeed my Lord is angry today as He has never been angry before and will never be angry again like it.'
And he will mention his untruthful statements. 'Myself, myself! Go to someone else. Go to Moses.'

So they will go to Moses, peace be upon him, and say, 'O Moses, you are the Messenger of Allah; Allah favored you above people with His messages and by speaking to you. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the state we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us?' Moses, peace be upon him, will say to them, 'Indeed my Lord is angry today as He has never been angry before and will never be angry again like it. I killed a soul that I had not been commanded to kill. Myself, myself! Go to Jesus, peace be upon him.'

So they will go to Jesus and say, 'O Jesus, you are the Messenger of Allah, you spoke to people in the cradle, and you are His word which He cast to Mary and a spirit from Him. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the state we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us?' Jesus, peace be upon him, will say to them, 'Indeed my Lord is angry today as He has never been angry before and will never be angry again like it' (and he will not mention any sin of his), 'Myself, myself! Go to someone else. Go to Muhammad ﷺ.' So they will come to me and say, 'O Muhammad, you are the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets, and Allah has forgiven you your past and future sins. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see the state we are in? Do you not see what has befallen us?' So I will set out and come beneath the Throne and fall down in prostration to my Lord. Then Allah will open to me and inspire me with some of His praises and beautiful glorification such as He has not opened to anyone before me. Then it will be said, 'O Muhammad, raise your head. Ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted.'
So I will raise my head and say, 'My Lord, my Ummah! My Ummah!'
