segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If only one day of this world remained, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would lengthen it until a man from my family rules the mountain of ad-Daylam and Constantinople."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Qur'an will come on the Day of Resurrection and say, 'O Lord, adorn him.' So he will be clothed with the crown of honor. Then it will say, 'O Lord, give him more.' So he will be clothed with the garment of honor. Then it will say, 'O Lord, be pleased with him.' So He will be pleased with him. Then it will be said to him, 'Recite and ascend,' and for every verse a good deed will be added for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He passed by a reciter who was reciting, and then he asked [people for something]. He said, "Truly to Allah we belong and to Him we return," and then said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever recites the Qur'an should ask Allah by it, for there will come people who recite the Qur'an and ask people by it.'"

Mahmūd said: This is Khaythamah al-Baṣrī, from whom Jābir al-Juʿfī narrated, and he is not Khaythamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. This Khaythamah is a Basran shaykh whose patronymic is Abū Naṣr. He narrated several hadith from Anas ibn Mālik, and Jābir al-Juʿfī also narrated several hadith from this Khaythamah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The one who treats as lawful what the Qur'an has forbidden has not believed in the Qur'an."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: The Prophet ﷺ would not sleep until he had recited Sūrat Banī Isrāʾīl and Sūrat al-Zumar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever says three times in the morning, 'I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan,' and recites the last three verses of Sūrat al-Ḥashr, Allah will appoint seventy thousand angels over him who will pray for him until evening. If he dies that day, he dies a martyr. And whoever says it in the evening will have the same status."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Whoever is kept busy by the Qur'an from remembering Me and asking of Me, I will give him better than what I give to those who ask.' And the superiority of the speech of Allah over all other speech is like the superiority of Allah over His creation."
This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would recite with pauses between verses. He would recite, "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds," then pause; then "the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful," then pause; and he would recite it, "Master of the Day of Judgment." Abū ʿĪsā said: This is a gharīb hadith, and Abū ʿUbayd recites accordingly and prefers it. Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī and others narrated it thus from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from Umm Salamah, but its chain is not continuous, because al-Layth ibn Saʿd narrated this hadith from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from Yaʿlā ibn Mamlak, from Umm Salamah, that she described the recitation of the Prophet ﷺ letter by letter. The hadith of al-Layth is more authentic, and in the hadith of al-Layth there is no mention that he would recite "Master of the Day of Judgment."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ recited, "A life for a life, and an eye for an eye." Suwayd ibn Naṣr narrated to us, saying:
ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us,
from Yūnus ibn Yazīd,
with this chain, similarly.
Abū ʿAlī ibn Yazīd is the brother of Yūnus ibn Yazīd. This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
Muḥammad said: Ibn al-Mubārak was alone in narrating this hadith from Yūnus ibn Yazīd. Abū ʿUbayd likewise recited "and the eye for the eye," following this hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ recited, "Is your Lord able..." This is a gharīb hadith that we know only from the narration of Rishdīn, and its chain is not strong.
Rishdīn ibn Saʿd and al-Ifrīqī are considered weak in hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Badr, the Romans prevailed over the Persians, and this pleased the believers, so the following was revealed:
"Alif, Lām, Mīm. The Romans have been defeated," up to His saying:
"...the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah." He said: So the believers rejoiced at the Romans' victory over the Persians.
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith from this route. Thus Naṣr ibn ʿAlī recited: "The Romans have been defeated."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ used to recite, "[For him is] rest, fragrance, and a Garden of bliss."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ recited:
"And you will see the people intoxicated, though they are not intoxicated."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ met Jibrīl and said:
"O Jibrīl, I have been sent to an unlettered nation, among whom are the old woman, the very old man, the boy, the girl, and the man who has never read a book."
He said, "O Muḥammad, the Qur'an was revealed in seven modes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this chain of transmission.
with a similar meaning, and both added: from Shuʿbah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aṣbahānī, who said: I heard Abū Ḥāzim narrating from Abū Hurayrah, who said:
"Three who have not reached the age of puberty..."
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Our homes were far from the mosque,
so we wanted to sell
our houses and move close to the mosque. But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us and said:
"For every step you take there is a degree [of reward]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever purifies himself in his house, then walks to one of the houses of Allah to fulfil one of the obligations of Allah, his steps will be such that one erases a sin and the other raises a degree."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The most beloved of places to Allah are its mosques, and the most hated of places to Allah are its markets."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Qilābah said to me: Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayrith Abū Sulaymān narrated to us,
saying: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with some people, and we were young men of about the same age.
And both of them related the hadith similar to the hadith of Ibn ʿUlayyah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr. Ibn Ayyūb said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
he said: Muḥammad informed me,
who is the son of ʿAmr, from Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥarmalah,
from al-Ḥārith ibn Khufāf,
that he said: Khufāf ibn Īmāʾ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed, then raised his head and said:
"Ghifār, may Allah forgive them; Aslam, may Allah keep them safe; and ʿUṣayyah, who disobeyed Allah and His Messenger. O Allah, curse Banū Liḥyān, and curse Riʿl and Dhakwān."
Then he went down in prostration.
Khufāf said: So because of that, I made cursing the disbelievers [part of my prayer].
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and we travelled by night until, at the end of the night just before dawn, we lay down to rest, the kind of rest than which nothing is sweeter to a traveller. Nothing woke us except the heat of the sun.
And he related the hadith similar to the hadith of Salm ibn Zarīr, with some additions and omissions.

And he said in the hadith: When ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb woke up and saw what had befallen the people, and he was a man of strong, powerful voice, he said "Allahu akbar" and raised his voice with the takbīr until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke up because of the loudness of his takbīr. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke up, they complained to him about what had befallen them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no harm. Set out." And he related the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on a journey and stopped to rest at night, he would lie on his right side; and when he stopped to rest shortly before dawn, he would prop up his arm and rest his head on his palm.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed two rakʿahs at Minā, as did Abū Bakr after him, and ʿUmar after Abū Bakr, and ʿUthmān during the early part of his caliphate. Then later ʿUthmān prayed four.
So when Ibn ʿUmar prayed with the imam, he would pray four, and when he prayed alone, he would pray two.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed at Minā the prayer of a traveller, as did Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān for eight years, or he said six years.
Ḥafṣ said: Ibn ʿUmar used to pray two rakʿahs at Minā, then go to his bed.
So I said: Uncle, if only you would pray two rakʿahs after it.
He said: If I did that, I would be completing the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He called the call to prayer on a cold, windy and rainy night, and at the end of his call he said: Pray in your dwellings! Pray in your dwellings!
Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command the muʾadhdhin, on a cold or rainy night during a journey, to say: Pray in your dwellings.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās
commanded his muʾadhdhin, in the hadith of Maʿmar, on a Friday on a rainy day.
similar to their hadith. And in the hadith of Maʿmar it is mentioned: One better than me did this, meaning the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās gave us a sermon one day after the ʿAṣr prayer until the sun set and the stars appeared, and the people began saying, "The prayer! The prayer!" He said: Then a man from Banū Tamīm came to him, not letting up and not turning away, saying, "The prayer! The prayer!"
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Are you teaching me the Sunnah, you rascal?
Then he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ combine Ẓuhr with ʿAṣr, and Maghrib with ʿIshāʾ.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq said: Something about that stirred doubt in my chest, so I went to Abū Hurayrah and asked him, and he confirmed what [Ibn ʿAbbās] had said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
was with the Prophet ﷺ when another man passed by him. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I truly love this man."
The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "Have you told him?"
He said, "No." He said, "Tell him."
So he caught up with him and said, "I love you for the sake of Allah."
He replied, "May He for whose sake you love me love you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, a man loves a people but cannot do deeds like theirs." He said,
"You, Abū Dharr, are with those whom you love."
He said, "I love Allah and His Messenger." He said,
"Then you are with those whom you love."
He said: Abū Dharr repeated it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ repeated it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rejoice at something; I had never seen them rejoice at anything more. A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, a man loves another man for the good deeds he does, but he cannot do the like of them." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"A person is with the one whom he loves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "The one who is consulted is trusted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Your love of a thing makes you blind and deaf [to its faults]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī was the governor of the Prophet ﷺ over Bahrain, and whenever he wrote to him, he began with himself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He wrote to the Prophet ﷺ and began with his own name.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, to whom should I show devotion?" He said,
"Your mother, then your mother, then your mother, then your father, then the next closest and the next closest."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"No man asks his dependent for some surplus that he has, and he withholds it from him, except that on the Day of Resurrection the surplus he withheld will be summoned for him as a bald-headed serpent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, to whom should I show devotion?" He said,
"Your mother, your father, your sister, your brother, and then your closest dependent after that: an obligatory right and a bond of kinship to be maintained."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ distributing meat at al-Jiʿrānah. Abū al-Ṭufayl said: I was a boy at that time, carrying the bone of a slaughtered camel. Then a woman approached until she came near the Prophet ﷺ, and he spread out his cloak for her, and she sat on it. I said, "Who is she?" They said, "This is his mother who nursed him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It reached him

that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting one day when his foster father came, so he spread part of his garment for him and he sat on it. Then his foster mother came, and he spread the other side of his garment for her and she sat on it. Then his foster brother came, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up for him and seated him in front of him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever has a daughter and does not bury her alive, does not humiliate her, and does not prefer his sons over her—meaning males—Allah will admit him to Paradise."
And ʿUthmān did not mention "meaning males."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever supports three daughters, teaches them good manners, marries them off, and treats them well, will have Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"I and a woman with darkened cheeks will be like these two on the Day of Resurrection."
And Yazīd gestured with the middle and index fingers:
"A woman who lost her husband, who has status and beauty, and who devoted herself to her orphans until they grew up and became independent or died."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ complaining about his neighbor. He said, "Go and be patient."
He came to him two or three times, and he said,
"Go and throw your belongings out on the road."

So he threw his belongings on the road, and people began asking him, and he told them his story. The people began to curse the neighbor, saying, "May Allah do such and such to him." Then his neighbor came to him and said, "Go back; you will not see from me anything you dislike."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Whoever among your slaves is compatible with you, feed him from what you eat and clothe him from what you wear. Whoever is not compatible with you, sell him, and do not torment the creation of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And
Rāfiʿ, of Juhaynah, had been present at al-Ḥudaybiyah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said,
"Good treatment of those under one's authority brings growth, and bad character brings misfortune."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever corrupts a man's wife or his slave is not one of us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"If the eye has entered, there is no permission [to be sought]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah
and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās
said: When the illness of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became severe, he began to throw a woollen cloak of his over his face,
and when he became distressed by it, he uncovered his face.
While he was in that state, he said:
"The curse of Allah be upon the Jews and the Christians: they took the graves of their prophets as places of worship."
He was warning against what they had done.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, one of you is in prayer as long as the prayer detains him,
and the angels say: O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy on him,
as long as he does not get up from his prayer place or break his wudūʾ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day at the door of my room,
while the Abyssinians were playing in the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was screening me with his cloak
so that I could watch their play.
Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir added: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Yūnus informed me,
from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah,
who said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ while the Abyssinians were playing with their spears.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the year of the Conquest, the Prophet ﷺ came, riding with Usāmah behind him on al-Qaṣwāʾ.
With him were Bilāl and ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥah, until he made the camel kneel by the House.
Then he said to ʿUthmān: "Bring us the key."
So he brought him the key and opened the door for him.
The Prophet ﷺ entered, together with Usāmah, Bilāl and ʿUthmān,
and then they closed the door behind them.
He stayed for a long part of the day, then came out,
and the people hurried to enter.
I got ahead of them and found Bilāl standing behind the door. I said to him: Where did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray? He said: He prayed between those two front pillars.
The House was on six pillars, in two rows.
He prayed between the two pillars of the front row,
placing the door of the House at his back,
and facing the direction that is in front of you as you enter the House, with the wall between him and it.
He said: I forgot to ask him how many [rakʿahs] he prayed. And at the place where he prayed there was a piece of red marble.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A man's prayer in congregation exceeds his prayer in his home and his prayer in his marketplace by twenty-some degrees. That is because when one of them performs wudūʾ and does it well, then comes to the mosque, moved only by the prayer, wanting nothing but the prayer, he does not take a step except that a degree is raised for him by it and a sin is removed from him by it, until he enters the mosque. Then, once he enters the mosque, he is in prayer as long as the prayer is what detains him. And the angels send blessings upon any of you as long as he remains in his place where he prayed, saying: O Allah, have mercy on him; O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, accept his repentance, so long as he does not harm anyone there and so long as he does not break his wudūʾ there."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to stop at Dhū Ṭuwā and spend the night there until he prayed the dawn prayer, when he came to Makkah. The place where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed was on a thick hillock, not in the mosque that was built there, but lower than that, on a rough, thick hillock.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us at midday in the heat,
and wudūʾ water was brought, so he performed wudūʾ and led us in the Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr prayers, with a short spear planted in front of him,
while women and donkeys passed by beyond it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Between the wall of the mosque on the side of the qiblah and the minbar there was enough space for a sheep to pass.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to come to the place of the voluntary Ḍuḥā prayer and make for the pillar beside the copy of the Qurʾān and pray near it. I would say to him: Will you not pray here? and I would point to some other part of the mosque. He would say: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seeking out this place.
label: machine translation

segments_en: What a terrible comparison you have made, equating us with a donkey and a dog! I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying while I was lying across in front of him. When he wanted to prostrate, he would nudge my leg, and I would draw it in; then he would prostrate.
label: machine translation

segments_en: This house, and he pointed to the house of ʿAbdullāh, said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Which deeds are most beloved to Allah? He said:
"Prayer at its proper time."
I said: Then which? He said:
"Then kindness to parents."
I said: Then which? He said:
"Then striving in the cause of Allah."
He said: He told me these, and had I asked for more, he would have given me more.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When we prayed the Ẓuhr prayers behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we would prostrate on our garments to protect ourselves from the heat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We prayed Ẓuhr with ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, then we went out until we came to Anas ibn Mālik and found him praying ʿAṣr. I said: Uncle, what is this prayer you have prayed? He said: ʿAṣr, and this is the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which we used to pray with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had flogged for drinking wine with palm branches and sandals, and Abū Bakr flogged forty. When ʿUmar took charge, he summoned the people and said to them, "The people have come close to the countryside" — and Musaddad said, "to the villages and the countryside" — "so what do you think about the prescribed punishment for wine?" ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said to him, "We think you should make it like the lightest of the prescribed punishments."
So he flogged eighty for it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān when al-Walīd was brought to him; he had prayed the dawn prayer with two rakʿahs and then said, "Shall I give you more?" Two men testified against him. One of them, Ḥumrān, testified that he had drunk wine, and the other testified that he had seen him vomit. ʿUthmān said, "He would not have vomited unless he had drunk it." Then he said, "ʿAlī, get up and flog him."
ʿAlī said, "Get up, Ḥasan, and flog him."
Al-Ḥasan said, "Let the one who enjoys its comfort bear its burden," as if he was upset with him. So [ʿUthmān] said, "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, get up and flog him."
So he flogged him while ʿAlī counted, until he reached forty, and [ʿAlī] said, "Stop."
Then he said, "The Prophet ﷺ flogged forty, Abū Bakr flogged forty, and ʿUmar eighty, and each is a sunnah, but this one is dearer to me."
ʿAlī ibn Ḥujr added in his narration: Ismāʿīl said, "I also heard the hadith of al-Dānāj from him, but I did not memorize it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were on a journey with the Prophet ﷺ, a man came on a mount of his. He began to turn his gaze right and left, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has an extra mount should give it to someone who has no mount, and whoever has surplus provisions should give them to someone who has no provisions."
He said: He mentioned various kinds of property, as many as he mentioned, until we thought that none of us had any right to anything surplus.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I fought with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ against Hawāzin. He said: While we were eating our morning meal, most of us on foot and some weak ones among us, a man came on a red camel. He pulled a leather rope from the camel's waist and tied up his camel with it. Then he came to eat the morning meal with the people. When he saw how weak they were and how poor their mounts were, he went off running to his camel, untied it, made it kneel, sat on it, and set off urging it on. A man from Aslam followed him on a grey she-camel, which was the best mount of the people. He said: I went out running and caught up with him, with the head of the she-camel at the hindquarters of the camel, and I was at the hindquarters of the she-camel. Then I went ahead until I was at the hindquarters of the camel, then ahead again until I took hold of the camel's halter and made it kneel. When it put its knee on the ground, I drew my sword and struck his head, and it flew off. Then I came leading his mount with what was on it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met me among the people, coming forward, and said:
"Who killed the man?"
They said, "Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ." He said:
"All of his spoils belong to him."
Hārūn said: This is the wording of Hāshim.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned several hadith, among them that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any town you come to and stay in, your share is in it. And any town that disobeys Allah and His Messenger, its fifth belongs to Allah and His Messenger, then the rest is for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When it was the day of Badr — and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, and the wording is his: ʿUmar ibn Yūnus al-Ḥanafī narrated to us, ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmār narrated to us, Abū Zumayl, who is Simāk al-Ḥanafī, narrated to me, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrated to me, he said: On the day of Badr, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at the polytheists, who were a thousand, while his Companions were three hundred and nineteen men. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ faced the qiblah, then stretched out his hands and began to call upon his Lord:
"O Allah, fulfill for me what You promised me. O Allah, bring about what You promised me. O Allah, if this band of the people of Islam is destroyed, You will not be worshipped on earth."

He kept calling upon his Lord, with his hands stretched out, facing the qiblah, until his cloak fell from his shoulders. Abū Bakr came to him, took his cloak, put it on his shoulders, and then embraced him from behind.

He said, "O Prophet of Allah, this pleading with your Lord is enough, for He will fulfill for you what He promised you." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {When you were seeking help from your Lord, and He answered you: I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another.} So Allah reinforced him with the angels.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote, before his death, to Khosrow, to Caesar, to the Negus, and to every tyrant, calling them to Allah. This was not the Negus for whom the Prophet ﷺ prayed the funeral prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he used to go to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb when he was a boy, wearing two garments dyed with safflower. He said: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ told them:

"A servant among the servants of Allah said: 'My Lord, to You belongs all praise, as befits the majesty of Your Face and the greatness of Your authority.' The two angels were overwhelmed and did not know how to record it, so they ascended to the heaven and said: 'Our Lord, Your servant has said a statement that we do not know how to write down.'

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said, though He knows best what His servant said: 'What did My servant say?' They said: 'My Lord, he said: My Lord, to You belongs all praise, as befits the majesty of Your Face and the greatness of Your authority.'
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to them: 'Write it down as My servant said it, until he meets Me, and then I will reward him for it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, and a man said: "Praise be to Allah, abundant, good and blessed praise."
When the Prophet ﷺ had finished the prayer, he said:
"Who is the one who said this?"
The man said: "I did, and I intended nothing but good." Then he said:
"The gates of the heaven were opened for it, and nothing held it back until it reached the Throne."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafiyyah bint Shaybah, from ʿĀʾishah,
who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw something he liked, he would say:
"Praise be to Allah, by whose favour good deeds are completed."
And when he saw something he disliked, he would say:
"Praise be to Allah in every circumstance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ used to say:
"Praise be to Allah in every circumstance. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the state of the people of the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah does not bestow a blessing on a servant and he says, 'Praise be to Allah,'
except that what he has been given is better than what he has taken."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by him while he was planting a plant, and said:
"Abū Hurayrah, what is it that you are planting?"
I said: "A plant of mine." He said:
"Shall I not guide you to a planting better for you than this?"
He said: "Yes, Messenger of Allah." He said:
"Say: 'Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest.' For each one, a tree will be planted for you in Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Among the things by which you glorify Allah's majesty are saying 'Glory be to Allah,' 'There is no god but Allah,' and 'Praise be to Allah.' They turn around the Throne with a humming like the humming of bees, mentioning the one who said them. Would one of you not love to have someone, or to always have someone, who mentions him?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Messenger of Allah, direct me to a deed, for I have grown old, weak and heavy." He said:

"Say 'Allah is the Greatest' a hundred times, 'Praise be to Allah' a hundred times, and 'Glory be to Allah' a hundred times. That is better than a hundred bridled and saddled horses in the cause of Allah, better than a hundred sacrificial camels, and better than freeing a hundred slaves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Hold to 'Glory be to Allah,' 'Praise be to Allah,' 'There is no god but Allah,' and 'Allah is the Greatest,' for they shed sins just as a tree sheds its leaves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had a sharp tongue against my family, though it did not go beyond them to others. I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Where are you with regard to seeking forgiveness? Seek forgiveness from Allah seventy times a day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Glad tidings to the one who finds in his record much seeking of forgiveness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ used to say:
"O Allah, make me among those who, when they do good, rejoice, and when they do wrong, seek forgiveness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever does not call upon Allah, Glorified is He, He is angry with him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whenever he sat in a gathering for remembrance, he would say: "Allah is the Judge, the Just; the doubters have perished." One day Muʿādh ibn Jabal said: "Ahead of you lie trials in which wealth will abound and the Qurʾān will be opened [to people], until the believer and the hypocrite, the man and the woman, the young and the old, the slave and the free will all take it up. Soon someone will say: 'What is wrong with the people? They do not follow me, though I have recited the Qurʾān! They will not follow me until I invent something else for them.' So beware of what he invents, for what is invented is misguidance. And I warn you against the slip of the wise man, for Satan may speak a word of misguidance through the tongue of a wise man, and the hypocrite may speak a word of truth."

He said: I said to Muʿādh: "May Allah have mercy on you, how would I know that the wise man may speak a word of misguidance and that the hypocrite may speak a word of truth?" He said: "Indeed. Avoid those well-known sayings of the wise man about which it is said, 'What is this?' But do not let that turn you away from him, for perhaps he will retract. And accept the truth when you hear it, for the truth has a light upon it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: For by Allah's permission it is a protection for you. Then know that people have never invented an innovation except that, before it, there had already passed something that is evidence against it or a lesson concerning it. For the Sunnah was only established by one who knew what lies in opposing it. Ibn Kathīr did not say "who knew".

of error, slipping, foolishness, and excessive probing. So be content for yourself with what the people [of the earlier generations] were content with for themselves, for they stopped with knowledge and held back with penetrating insight. They were stronger at uncovering matters, and more deserving of any merit that was in them. If the guidance is what you are following, then you have outstripped them to it. And if you say, "It only arose after them,"

then none introduced it except one who followed a path other than theirs and turned away from them in preference for himself, for they were the forerunners. They spoke about it with what suffices and described of it what heals. So there is none below them who falls short, and none above them who goes beyond. A people fell short of them and so were harsh, and others aspired beyond them and so were excessive, while they were between these two, upon straight guidance. You wrote asking about affirming the decree (qadar); you have fallen upon one well-informed, by Allah's permission. I know of no novelty that people have introduced, nor any innovation they have invented, whose trace is clearer or whose matter is more firmly established than the affirmation of the decree. It was mentioned even in the Days of Ignorance; they spoke of it in their speech and in their poetry, consoling themselves with it over what they had missed. Then Islam added nothing to it except strength. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned it in more than one or two hadith, and the Muslims heard it from him and spoke of it during his life and after his death, in certainty and submission to their Lord, and in acknowledgment of their own weakness, [believing] that anything could exist that His knowledge had not encompassed, His Book had not enumerated, and His decree had not carried out. Moreover, it is in the firmly established verses of His Book; from it they took it and from it they learned it. And if you say, "Why did Allah reveal such-and-such verse, and why did He say such-and-such?"

they recited of it what you recite, and they knew of its interpretation what you do not know. After all that they said: it is by a Book and a decree; wretchedness has been written; whatever is decreed will be; what Allah wills is, and what He does not will is not; and we possess for ourselves neither harm nor benefit. Then after that they strove in hope and in fear.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar had a friend from the people of Syria who used to write to him. ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar wrote to him: "It has reached me that you have spoken about something concerning the divine decree. So beware of writing to me, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'There will be in my nation people who deny the divine decree.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to al-Ḥasan: "O Abū Saʿīd, tell me about Ādam,
was he created for the heaven or for the earth?" He said: "No, for the earth."
I said: "What if he had held fast and not eaten from the tree?" He said: "He could not have avoided it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding the saying of the Exalted, {and for that He created them}, he said: These were created for this, and those for that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked al-Ḥasan about {You cannot tempt [anyone] away from Him, except him who is to burn in Hell}. He said: Except one for whom Allah the Exalted has made it binding that he will burn in Hell.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥasan used to say: "To fall from the sky to the earth is dearer to him than to say, 'The matter is in my hand.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥasan came to us in Makkah, and the jurists of Makkah spoke to me to ask him to sit for them one day to admonish them. He said: "Yes."

They gathered and he addressed them, and I never saw anyone more eloquent than him. A man said: "O Abū Saʿīd, who created Satan?" He said: "Glory be to Allah! Is there any creator other than Allah? Allah created Satan, and He created good and He created evil."
The man said: "May Allah fight them! How they lie about this shaykh!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAṭāʾ said: A Friday and the day of Fiṭr fell together in the time of Ibn al-Zubayr. He said, "Two festivals have coincided on one day." So he combined them and prayed two rakʿahs for both early in the morning, and he did not add anything to them until he prayed the ʿAṣr prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb found a silk brocade garment being sold in the market, so he took it and brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "Buy this and adorn yourself with it for the festival and for receiving delegations."
Then he narrated the rest of the hadith, and the first version is more complete.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ became heavy in body, Tamīm al-Dārī said to him, "Shall I not make you a pulpit, O Messenger of Allah, that would support—or carry—your bones?" He said, "Yes."
So he made a pulpit for him with two steps.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he disliked prayer at midday except on Friday, and he said:
"Hell is stoked [every day] except on Friday."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took his place [on the pulpit] on Friday, he said, "Sit down."
Ibn Masʿūd heard that and sat down at the door of the mosque. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him and said,
"Come, ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to deliver two sermons. When he ascended the pulpit he would sit until [the caller to prayer] had finished—I think he said, the muʾadhdhin—then he would stand and deliver the sermon, then sit without speaking, then stand and deliver [the second] sermon.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I sat with a man who had been a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, called al-Ḥakam ibn Ḥazn al-Kulafī, and he began to narrate to us. He said: I came as part of a delegation to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as the seventh of seven or the ninth of nine. We entered upon him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we have visited you, so supplicate Allah for good for us." He ordered for us some dates—and the situation then was modest. We stayed there for some days, during which we attended the Friday prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He stood leaning on a staff or a bow, praised Allah and glorified Him with brief, good, blessed words. Then he said:
"O people, you will never be able—or you will never do—everything you are commanded, but be steadfast and rejoice in good news."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the tashahhud [in his sermon], he would say:

"All praise is for Allah; we seek His help and ask His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leads astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger, whom He sent with the truth as a bearer of good news and a warner before the Hour. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been rightly guided, and whoever disobeys them harms only himself, and he does not harm Allah in anything."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked Ibn Shihāb about the tashahhud
of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on Friday, and he mentioned something similar, saying:
"And whoever disobeys them has gone astray."
And we ask Allah, our Lord, to make us among those who obey Him and obey His Messenger, who follow His good pleasure and avoid His anger, for we are by Him and for Him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raise his hands in supplication on his pulpit or on anything else, but I saw him do like this—and he pointed with the index finger and closed the middle finger with the thumb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to keep the sermons short.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not lengthen the exhortation on Friday; it was only a few brief words.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I found in my father's book in his own handwriting, though I did not hear it from him: Qatādah said, from Yaḥyā ibn Mālik, from Samurah ibn Jundab, that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"Attend the remembrance [the sermon] and draw near to the imam, for a man keeps distancing himself until he is put back in Paradise, even if he enters it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with Muʿāwiyah at Bayt al-Maqdis, and he led us in the Friday prayer. I looked, and most of those in the mosque were Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and I saw them sitting with their arms wrapped around their knees while the imam was delivering the sermon.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"Three kinds of people attend the Friday prayer: a man who attends it and talks idly, and that is his share of it; a man who attends it and supplicates, so he is a man who asks Allah, the Mighty and Majestic—if He wills He gives him, and if He wills He withholds; and a man who attends it with attentiveness and silence, does not step over the necks of any Muslim and does not harm anyone—it is an expiation for the period until the next Friday and an additional three days, because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: {Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times the like thereof.}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed in his room, and the people followed him in prayer from behind the room.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the narration of Hammām: A group of people from ʿUraynah came to the Prophet ﷺ; and in the narration of Saʿīd: from ʿUkl and ʿUraynah. [The rest is] like their narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakrah said, from his father: When that day came, the Prophet ﷺ sat on a camel, and a man was holding its rein—or he said, its halter. Then he mentioned [the hadith] like the narration of Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
[It is] like the narration of ʿUqayl from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd and Abū Salamah, from Abū Hurayrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿīd [said] that a man
from Aslam, called Māʿiz ibn Mālik, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I have committed an indecency, so carry out [the punishment] upon me."

The Prophet ﷺ sent him away several times. He said: Then he asked his people, and they said: "We know nothing wrong with him, except that he committed something for which he thinks nothing will cleanse him except that the prescribed punishment be carried out for it." He said: So he returned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he commanded us to stone him. He said: We took him to Baqīʿ al-Gharqad. He said: We did not bind him and did not dig a pit for him. He said: We threw bones, clods of earth, and pieces of pottery at him. He said: He ran, and we ran after him until he reached the side of the lava field, where he stood facing us, and we threw the stones of the lava field at him—meaning rocks—until he fell silent. He said: Then in the evening the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up to give a speech and said:

"Whenever we set out on a campaign in the cause of Allah, a man stays behind among our families, bleating like the bleating of a male goat! I swear that if a man who has done that is brought to me, I will surely make an example of him."
He said: He did not ask forgiveness for him, nor did he revile him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Māʿiz ibn Mālik came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, purify me." He said:
"Woe to you! Go back, seek Allah's forgiveness, and repent to Him."
He said: So he went back not far, then came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, purify me."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Woe to you! Go back, seek Allah's forgiveness, and repent to Him."
He said: So he went back not far, then came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, purify me."
The Prophet ﷺ said the same, until, when it was the fourth time, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "From what shall I purify you?"
He said: "From adultery."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked: "Is there madness in him?"
He was informed that he was not mad. Then he said: "Has he drunk wine?"
A man stood up and smelled his breath, but did not find the smell of wine on him.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Have you committed adultery?" He said: "Yes."

So he ordered that he be stoned, and he was stoned. The people were divided about him into two groups: one saying, "He is ruined; his sin has surrounded him," and another saying, "No repentance is better than the repentance of Māʿiz, for he came to the Prophet ﷺ, put his hand in his hand, and said: Kill me with stones." He said: They stayed like that for two or three days. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to them while they were sitting, greeted them with salām, sat down, and said:
"Ask forgiveness for Māʿiz ibn Mālik."
He said: They said: "May Allah forgive Māʿiz ibn Mālik."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He has repented with a repentance that, if it were divided among a nation, it would suffice them."
He said: Then a woman from Ghāmid, of the Azd, came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, purify me." He said:
"Woe to you! Go back, seek Allah's forgiveness, and repent to Him."
She said: "I see that you want to send me back as you sent back Māʿiz ibn Mālik." He said: "And what is that?"
She said that she was pregnant from adultery. He said: "You?" She said: "Yes." He said to her:
"[Not] until you give birth to what is in your womb."
He said: A man of the Anṣār took responsibility for her until she gave birth. He said: Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "The Ghāmidī woman has given birth." He said:
"Then we will not stone her and leave her child small with no one to nurse him."
A man of the Anṣār stood up and said: "His nursing is my responsibility, O Prophet of Allah." He said: Then he stoned her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no verse in the Qur'an more beloved to me than this verse:
"Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills." He said: This hadith is hasan gharīb.
Abū Fākhitah's name is Saʿīd ibn ʿIlāqah, and Thuwayr is called Abū Jahm; he was a man of Kūfah from among the Tābiʿīn, and he heard from Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn al-Zubayr.
Ibn Mahdī used to criticize him slightly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when this verse was revealed to him:
"Whoever does a wrong will be recompensed for it, and will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Abū Bakr, shall I not recite to you a verse that was revealed to me?"
I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah.
He said: So he recited it to me, and I knew nothing except that I felt a breaking in my back, and I stretched myself because of it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What is the matter with you, O Abū Bakr?"
I said: O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be ransomed for you, which of us has not done wrong, and are we to be recompensed for what we have done? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"As for you, O Abū Bakr, and the believers, you will be recompensed for that in this world, until you meet Allah with no sins upon you. As for the others, that is gathered up for them until they are recompensed for it on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sawdah feared that the Prophet ﷺ would divorce her,
so she said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Do not divorce me; keep me, and make my day for ʿĀʾishah." He did so, and it was revealed:
"There is no blame upon them if they make settlement between themselves, and settlement is best."
So whatever they agree upon is permissible. It seems to be from the words of Ibn ʿAbbās.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās recited:

"This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion." A Jewish man was with him and said: If this had been revealed to us, we would have taken that day as a festival.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: It was revealed on a day of festival, on a Friday, and the day of ʿArafah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to be guarded until this verse was revealed:
"And Allah will protect you from the people." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put his head out of the tent and said to them:
"O people, go away, for Allah has protected me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, when I eat meat, I become aroused for women and my desire seizes me, so I have forbidden meat to myself. Then Allah revealed:

"O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful to you and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors. And eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good." He said: This hadith is hasan gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning this verse:

"O you who have believed, testimony among you when death approaches one of you..." [Tamīm al-Dārī] said: People are free of blame regarding it except me and ʿAdī ibn Baddāʾ. They were two Christians who used to travel to Syria before Islam. They came to Syria for their trade, and a freed slave of Banū Sahm called Budayl ibn Abī Maryam came to them with merchandise, with a silver cup that he intended for the king, and it was the greatest part of his merchandise. He fell ill and made a bequest to the two of them, telling them to deliver what he left to his family. Tamīm said: When he died, we took that cup and sold it for a thousand dirhams, then ʿAdī ibn Baddāʾ and I divided it. When we came to his family, we gave them what we had with us, but they missed the cup and asked us about it. We said: He left nothing but this, and nothing else was handed to us. Tamīm said: When I became Muslim after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, I felt guilty about that. So I went to his family, told them the matter, and paid them five hundred dirhams, and told them that my companion had the same amount. They went with him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who asked them for proof, but they had none. So he commanded them to make him swear by what is held great by the people of his religion, and he swore. Then Allah revealed:
"O you who have believed, testimony among you when death approaches one of you..." up to His saying:
"...or they fear that oaths will be refuted after their oaths."
Then ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and another man stood up and swore, and the five hundred dirhams were taken from ʿAdī ibn Baddāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The table was sent down from heaven with bread and meat, and they were commanded not to be dishonest and not to store up for the next day. But they were dishonest, stored up, and put aside for the next day, so they were transformed into monkeys and pigs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a man
from the desert Arabs came to the Prophet ﷺ, believed in him and followed him, and then said, "I will emigrate with you."

So the Prophet ﷺ entrusted him to some of his Companions. When there was a battle, the Prophet ﷺ took some captives and distributed them, and he allotted a share to the man as well. He gave his Companions the share that had been allotted to him, and the man used to tend their riding animals. When he came back, they handed it over to him. He said, "What is this?" They said, "It is a share that the Prophet ﷺ apportioned for you."
So he took it and brought it to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "What is this?" He said, "I apportioned it for you."
The man said, "It was not for this that I followed you. Rather, I followed you so that I might be struck here"—and he pointed to his throat—"by an arrow, and die, and enter Paradise." He said,
"If you are truthful with Allah, He will be truthful with you."

They waited a little while, then rose to fight the enemy. He was brought to the Prophet ﷺ being carried, having been struck by an arrow exactly where he had pointed. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Is it he?" They said, "Yes." He said,
"He was truthful with Allah, so Allah was truthful with him."
Then the Prophet ﷺ shrouded him in the Prophet's own cloak, placed him forward and prayed over him. Among what could be heard of his prayer was:
"O Allah, this is Your servant. He went out as an emigrant in Your cause and was killed as a martyr, and I am a witness to that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A poor woman in al-ʿAwālī became ill, and the Prophet ﷺ used to ask about her. He said,
"If she dies, do not bury her until I have prayed over her."

She passed away, and they brought her to Madinah after the late evening. They found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asleep and disliked to wake him, so they prayed over her and buried her in Baqīʿ al-Gharqad. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose in the morning, they came and he asked them about her. They said, "She has been buried, O Messenger of Allah. We came to you but found you sleeping and disliked to wake you." He said, "Then let us go."
He set out walking and they walked with him until they showed him her grave. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, and they formed rows behind him, and he prayed over her and said the takbīr four times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sunnah in the funeral prayer is to recite Umm al-Qurʾān (al-Fātiḥah) silently after the first takbīr, then to say the takbīr three more times, with the salutation of peace after the last.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was reported] in similar terms.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū al-Malīḥ led us in prayer over a funeral, and we thought he had already said the takbīr. He turned his face to us and said, "Straighten your rows, and let your intercession be good." Abū al-Malīḥ said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Salīṭ narrated to me, from one of the Mothers of the Believers, Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: The Prophet ﷺ told me, saying,
"There is no deceased person over whom a group of people pray, except that their intercession for him is accepted."
I asked Abū al-Malīḥ about the group, and he said, "Forty."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about those killed at Uḥud: "Wrap them in their blood,
for there is no wound inflicted in the cause of Allah except that it will come on the Day of Resurrection bleeding,
its color the color of blood and its scent the scent of musk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He, who was called ʿUbaydullāh ibn Muʿiyyah, said:
Two Muslim men were struck down on the day of Ṭāʾif,
and they were carried to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who ordered that they be buried where they had fallen.
Ibn Muʿiyyah had been born during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That they went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day,
and he saw a new grave and said, "What is this?" They said,
"This is so-and-so, the freed woman of the family of so-and-so,"
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ knew her. [They said,] "She died at midday while you were asleep, taking your midday rest,
and we did not like to wake you for her."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, the people formed rows behind him, and he said the takbīr four times over her. Then he said:
"No one among you will die, as long as I am among you, without you informing me of it,
for my prayer for him is a mercy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade plastering graves,
or building over them,
or anyone sitting on them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade plastering graves.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, [what about] the cooking pots of the polytheists, may we cook in them?" He said:
"Do not cook in them."
I said, "But if we need them and have no alternative?" He said:
"Then wash them thoroughly, then cook and eat [in them]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said, "War is deception."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said, "War is deception."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I fought a man in single combat and killed him, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted me his spoils as an extra reward.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted him as an extra reward the spoils of a man he had killed on the day of Ḥunayn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever kills [an enemy], he shall have the spoils."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went on a campaign against Hawāzin with Abū Bakr, in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. We reached a watering place of Banū Fazārah and made camp for the night. When it was dawn, we launched a raid upon them. We came upon the people of the water and attacked them by night and killed them, in nine or seven households.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went on a campaign with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and passed by a slain woman around whom people had gathered. They made way for him, and he said, "This woman was not among those who fought."
Then he said to a man, "Go to Khālid ibn al-Walīd and tell him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commands you, saying: Do not kill any children or hired laborers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Ḥunayn, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer beside a camel from the shares of the spoils. Then he took something from the camel, a tuft, meaning a piece of wool, placed it between his two fingers, and said:

"O people, this is from your spoils. Return the thread and the needle, and whatever is more than that or less than that. For stealing from the spoils is a disgrace for its perpetrator on the Day of Resurrection, and a shame and a fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ gave as an extra reward a quarter on the outward journey and a third on the return.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no extra reward after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; the Muslims share it back, the strong among them to the weak.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Alqamah ibn Mujazziz on an expedition, and I was among them. When he reached the end of his campaign, or was part of the way along the road, a group from the army asked his permission [to leave], and he permitted them and appointed ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥudhāfah ibn Qays as-Sahmī over them. I was among those who went out with him. When they were part of the way along the road, the people kindled a fire to warm themselves or to cook something on it. ʿAbdullāh, who had a sense of humor, said, "Do I not have a right to your hearing and obedience?" They said, "Yes."
He said, "Then I do not command you to do anything but that you do it?" They said, "Yes."
He said, "Then I order you to leap into this fire."
Some people stood up and began to prepare themselves. When he thought they would leap, he said, "Hold back, for I was only joking with you."
When we returned, they mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever among them commands you to disobey Allah, do not obey him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"After me, your affairs will be taken over by men who extinguish the Sunnah, act upon innovation, and delay the prayer from its proper times."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, if I live to see them, what should I do?" He said:
"You ask me, O son of Umm ʿAbd, what you should do? There is no obedience to one who disobeys Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Children of Israel were led by their prophets; whenever one prophet died, another succeeded him. But there will be no prophet after me among you."
They said, "Then what will there be, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"There will be caliphs, and they will be many."
They said, "What should we do?" He said:
"Fulfil the pledge of allegiance to the first, then the first. Give them their due, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will question them about what they were responsible for."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They said, "O Messenger of Allah, is Hajj every year?" He said:
"If I said yes, it would become obligatory, and if it became obligatory, you would not carry it out, and if you did not carry it out, you would be punished."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ performed Hajj on a worn-out saddle with a velvet cloth worth four dirhams or not even that, and then he said:
"O Allah, [make this] a Hajj without showing off or seeking fame."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"Those performing Hajj and ʿUmrah are the delegation of Allah. If they call upon Him, He answers them, and if they seek His forgiveness, He forgives them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, is jihad obligatory upon women?" He said:
"Yes, upon them is a jihad in which there is no fighting: Hajj and ʿUmrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "...and what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women, to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, while you desire to marry them."
She said: This concerns the orphan girl who is in the care of a man,
who may perhaps be a partner with him in his wealth,
and he is the one with the closest claim over her,
so he wishes to marry her, and he prevents her from marrying others because of her wealth,
and no one else marries her,
out of dislike that anyone should share with him in her wealth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ash-Shaybānī said: Abū al-Ḥasan as-Suwāʾī mentioned it, and I think he mentioned it only from Ibn ʿAbbās:

"O you who believe, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will, nor should you constrain them so that you may take away part of what you have given them." He said: When a man died, his guardians had a greater right over his wife:
if some of them wished, he would marry her,
and if they wished, they would marry her off to someone else,
and if they wished, they would not marry her off at all;
so they had a greater right over her than her own family.
So this verse was revealed concerning that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh said: We used to go on military expeditions with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and we had nothing [with us]. So we said, "Should we not castrate ourselves?" He forbade us from that, and then permitted us to marry a woman for a garment.
Then he recited to us: "O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They asked Anas ibn Mālik about faḍīkh [date liquor].

He said: We had no wine other than this faḍīkh of yours, which you call faḍīkh. I was standing, serving it to Abū Ṭalḥah, Abū Ayyūb, and some men from among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in our house, when a man came and said, "Has the news reached you?" We said, "No." He said, "Wine has been prohibited." Then [Abū Ṭalḥah] said, "O Anas, pour out these jars." He said: They did not return to it, nor did they ask about it after the man's report.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he was delivering a sermon on the pulpit of Madīnah and said: O people, indeed the prohibition of wine was revealed on the day it was revealed, and it is made from five things: grapes, dates, honey, wheat, and barley. And wine is whatever clouds the intellect.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this verse was revealed, "Say: He is the One Who is able to send upon you punishment from above you," the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "I seek refuge in Your Face."
[The verse continues:] "or from beneath your feet," and he said, "I seek refuge in Your Face."
[Then:] "or to confuse you into factions and make some of you taste the violence of others." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "This is easier," or "This is lighter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding His saying, "Take what is easy [to forgive]" he said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ was commanded to accept the easy and forgiving side of people's character.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Jahl said: O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.

Then it was revealed: "But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness. And why should Allah not punish them while they bar [people] from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām..." to the end of the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "If there are twenty steadfast among you, they will overcome two hundred." So it was prescribed for them that one should not flee from ten. Sufyān said more than once: that twenty should not flee from two hundred. Then it was revealed: "Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you..." the verse,
and so it was prescribed that one hundred should not flee from two hundred. Sufyān added once: [It was revealed:] "Urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty steadfast among you..."
Sufyān said: Ibn Shubrumah said, "And I consider enjoining good and forbidding evil to be like this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, he invited the people; they ate, and then sat talking. He said: He began as if preparing to get up, but they did not get up. When he saw that, he stood up, and when he stood, those who stood from among the people stood.

ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā added in their narrations: Three remained seated. The Prophet ﷺ came to enter, and the people were still sitting; then they got up and left. He said: I came and informed the Prophet ﷺ that they had left. He said: So he came and entered; I went to enter, but he drew the curtain between me and him. He said: And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission for a meal, without waiting for its preparation..." up to His saying, "...indeed that would be an enormity in the sight of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "And the sun runs to a resting place for it." He said:
"Its resting place is beneath the Throne."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq came to my father in his house and bought a saddle from him. He said to ʿĀzib, "Send your son with me to carry it with me to my house." My father said to me, "Carry it."

So I carried it, and my father went out with him to check the payment. My father said to him, "O Abū Bakr, tell me what you two did on the night you travelled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said, "Yes. We travelled all that night until the midday hour arrived and the road was empty, with no one passing along it. Then a long rock appeared to us, with shade that the sun had not yet reached, so we stopped beside it. I went to the rock and levelled with my hand a place for the Prophet ﷺ to sleep in its shade, then spread a fur cloak over it. Then I said, 'Sleep, O Messenger of Allah, and I will watch over your surroundings.' So he slept, and I went out to look around him. Suddenly I came upon a shepherd driving his sheep toward the rock, wanting from it what we had wanted. I met him and said, 'To whom do you belong, boy?' He said, 'To a man of the people of Madinah.' I said, 'Is there milk in your sheep?' He said, 'Yes.'
I said, 'Will you milk for me?' He said, 'Yes.'

He took a sheep, and I said to him, 'Wipe the udder clean of hair, dust, and dirt.'" (The narrator said: I saw al-Barāʾ strike one hand against the other, showing the wiping.) "He milked for me into a wooden bowl he had, a small quantity of milk. He said: I had with me a water-skin from which I used to carry water for the Prophet ﷺ to drink and perform ablution. I went to the Prophet ﷺ, and I disliked waking him from his sleep, but I found that he had woken up. So I poured some water onto the milk until its lower part cooled. I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, drink this milk.' He drank until I was pleased. Then he said,
'Has the time not yet come for setting out?' I said, 'Yes, it has.'
He said: So we set out after the sun had passed its zenith, and Surāqah ibn Mālik followed us. He said: We were on hard ground. I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we have been overtaken!' He said,
'Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us.'

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ supplicated against him, and his horse sank up to its belly, as I saw. He said, 'I know that you two have supplicated against me, so pray for me. By Allah, I will turn back the pursuit from you.'

So he prayed to Allah and he was freed. He went back, and did not meet anyone without saying, 'I have spared you what is here,' and he turned back everyone he met. He said: And he kept his word to us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a man who was a Christian and then accepted Islam, and he recited al-Baqarah and Āl ʿImrān.
He used to write for the Prophet ﷺ.
Then he returned to Christianity, and he would say, "Muhammad knows nothing except what I wrote for him."
Then Allah caused him to die, and they buried him.
In the morning the earth had cast him out. They said, "This is the doing of Muhammad and his Companions.
Because he fled from them, they dug up our companion."
So they threw him down and dug a grave for him, making it deep.
In the morning the earth had cast him out again.
They said, "This is the doing of Muhammad and his Companions; they dug up our companion because he fled from them."
So they threw him down and dug a grave for him,
making it as deep in the earth as they could.
In the morning the earth had cast him out again.
Then they knew that it was not from people, so they left him thrown down.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Musaylimah the Liar came during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and began to say, "If Muhammad makes me his successor after him, I will follow him."
He had come with a great number of his people.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ approached him, accompanied by Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās,
and in the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was a piece of palm branch. He stood before Musaylimah among his companions and said,
"If you were to ask me for this piece, I would not give it to you, and you will never go beyond Allah's decree concerning you.
If you turn away, Allah will surely destroy you.
And I see that you are the one I was shown in what I was shown.
And this is Thābit; he will answer you on my behalf."
Then he turned away from him.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: I asked about the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
"I see that you are the one I was shown in what I was shown."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ called his daughter Fāṭimah during the illness in which he passed away,
and he whispered something to her, and she wept. Then he called her and whispered to her, and she laughed.
She said: I asked her about that.
She said, "The Prophet ﷺ whispered to me and informed me that he would be taken in the illness in which he died, so I wept.
Then he whispered to me and informed me that I would be the first of his family to follow him, so I laughed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in the mosque. Misʿar said: I think he said, "in the forenoon." He said, "Pray two rakʿahs."
He owed me a debt, so he repaid me and gave me more.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿAmr, "O Abū Muḥammad, did you hear Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh
say: A man passed through the mosque carrying arrows, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, 'Hold them by their heads (arrowheads)'?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to stop at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah when he performed ʿUmrah,
and during his Hajj when he performed Hajj,
beneath a samurah tree at the place of the mosque in Dhū al-Ḥulayfah.
And when he returned from a military expedition by that route, or from Hajj or ʿUmrah, he would descend into the bottom of a valley,
and when he came up out of the valley he would make his camel kneel on the sandy ground at the eastern edge of the valley,
and he would stop there for the rest of the night until morning,
not at the mosque built of stones,
nor on the hillock on which the mosque stands.
There was a channel there where ʿAbdullāh used to pray,
in the midst of which were sand dunes where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray there.
Then the flood washed over it with sand until it buried that place where ʿAbdullāh used to pray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is al-Muhallabī, and Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUlayyah, both from ʿAwf,
from Sayyār ibn Salāmah,
who is Abū al-Minhāl ar-Riyāḥī, from Abū Barzah,
who said: The Prophet ﷺ disliked sleeping before the ʿIshāʾ prayer and talking after it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The prayer in congregation is superior to a man's prayer alone by twenty-five degrees." He said, "
And the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the Fajr prayer."
Abū Hurayrah said: Recite, if you wish: {And the recitation of the dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the dawn is ever witnessed.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the recitation in the Fajr prayer, he would say the takbīr and raise his head, saying: "
Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You belongs all praise."
Then he would say, while standing: "

O Allah, save al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd, Salamah ibn Hishām, ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah, and the oppressed believers. O Allah, press down Your severity upon Muḍar and make it upon them years like the years of Yūsuf. O Allah, curse Liḥyān, Riʿl, Dhakwān, and ʿUṣayyah, who disobeyed Allah and His Messenger."
Then it reached us that he abandoned that when it was revealed: {You have no say in the matter, whether He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: The Prophet ﷺ said, "
Permit women to go to the mosques at night."
A son of his said, "By Allah, we will not permit them, for they would use it as a pretext for mischief. By Allah, we will not permit them."
He said: So he rebuked him and was angry, and said, "I say the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, 'Permit them,'
and you say, 'We will not permit them'?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
entered the mosque on Friday while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was delivering the sermon, and he said, "Pray two rakʿahs."
Then he came the second Friday while the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the sermon, and he said, "Pray two rakʿahs."
Then he came the third Friday, and he said, "Pray two rakʿahs." Then he said, "Give charity."
So they gave charity, and he gave him two garments. Then he said, "Give charity."
So the man threw down one of his two garments, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Do you not see this man? He entered the mosque in a shabby state, and I hoped that you would notice him and give him charity, but you did not, so I said, 'Give charity.'
So you gave charity, and I gave him two garments. Then I said, 'Give charity,'
and he threw down one of his two garments. Take your garment." And he rebuked him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is al-Baṭīn, who is Ibn ʿImrān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, not even jihad in the cause of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Not even jihad in the cause of Allah, except for a man who goes out with his self and his wealth and returns with nothing of that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raising his hands until I saw the whiteness of his armpits, saying: "
Beware! No mother's offense is to be charged against her child. Beware! No mother's offense is to be charged against her child."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say: "By Allah, besides whom there is no god, I used to press my liver against the ground from hunger,
and I used to tie a stone to my belly from hunger.
One day I sat down on the path they used to come out by.
Abū Bakr passed by,
and I asked him about a verse from the Book of Allah.
I only asked him so that he would feed me,
but he passed by and did not do so.
Then ʿUmar passed by me, and I asked him about a verse from the Book of Allah.
I only asked him so that he would feed me,
but he passed by and did not do so.
Then Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ passed by me, and he smiled when he saw me, and he knew
what was in my soul and on my face. Then he said: "Abū Hirr."
I said: "At your service, Messenger of Allah." He said: "Follow me." He went on and I followed him. He entered and asked permission, and I was given permission,
and he went in and found milk in a cup. He said:
"Where is this milk from?"
They said: "So-and-so, a man or a woman, gave it as a gift to you." He said: "Abū Hirr."
I said: "At your service, Messenger of Allah." He said:
"Go to the People of the Ṣuffah and invite them to me."
He said: The People of the Ṣuffah were the guests of Islam;
they had no family to shelter with, nor wealth,
nor anyone [to turn to].
When charity came to him, he sent it to them
and did not take any of it for himself,
and when a gift came to him, he sent for them
and took some of it and shared it with them.
That distressed me, and I said: "What is this milk among the People of the Ṣuffah? I had more right to get a drink of this milk to strengthen myself with.
Then when they come, he will order me, and I will be the one to give it to them,
and what would reach me of this milk?"
Yet there was no way out of obeying Allah and obeying His Messenger ﷺ.
So I went to them and invited them, and they came,
and they asked permission, and they were given permission,
and they took their places in the house. He said:
"Abū Hirr."
I said: "At your service, Messenger of Allah." He said: "Take it and give it to them."
He said: So I took the cup and began giving it to a man, and he would drink until he was satisfied,
then he would return the cup to me,
and I would give it to another man, and he would drink until he was satisfied,
then he would return the cup to me, and he would drink until he was satisfied,
then he would return the cup to me,
until I reached the Prophet ﷺ, and all the people had been satisfied.
He took the cup and put it on his hand, looked at me, smiled, and said: "Abū Hirr."
I said: "At your service, Messenger of Allah." He said:
"There remain only you and I."
I said: "You have spoken the truth, Messenger of Allah." He said: "Sit down and drink." So I sat and drank. He said: "Drink." So I drank,
and he kept saying: "Drink,"
until I said: "No, by the One who sent you with the truth,
I can find no room for it." He said: "Then show me."
So I gave him the cup, and he praised Allah, said the name of Allah, and drank the remainder.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Anas ibn Mālik: "Was there handshaking among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Yes."
label: machine translation
