segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he forbade a man to be made to rise from his seat so that another may sit in it,
but [he said]: "Make room and spread out."
And Ibn ʿUmar disliked that a man should rise from his seat
and then another sit in his place.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ confided a secret to me, and I have not told anyone about it since.
Umm Sulaym asked me about it, and I did not tell her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw myself with the Prophet ﷺ building a house with my own hand,
that would shelter me from the rain
and shade me from the sun,
and none of Allah's creation helped me with it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I spent a night at my maternal aunt Maymūnah's. The Prophet ﷺ got up during the night, went to relieve himself, then washed his face and hands, and slept again. Then he got up, went to the water-skin, untied its string, and performed ablution, one between the two [extremes], neither using too much nor falling short of thoroughness. Then he stood and prayed. I got up and stretched, disliking that he should see that I had been watching him, and I performed ablution. He stood and prayed, and I stood on his left; he took my hand and turned me around to his right. So the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was completed at thirteen rakʿahs. Then he lay down and slept until he breathed heavily, and whenever he slept he would breathe heavily. Then Bilāl came to him and informed him of the prayer, and he got up and prayed without performing ablution. Among his supplications was:

"O Allah, place light in my heart, light in my sight, light in my hearing, light on my right, light on my left, light above me, light below me, light in front of me, light behind me, and make light great for me."

Kurayb said: "And seven are in the chest." Then I met some of the descendants of al-ʿAbbās, and he told me of them, mentioning my nerves, my flesh, my blood, my hair, and my skin, and he mentioned two other things.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We witnessed Khaybar with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about a man who was with us and who claimed to be a Muslim: "
This one is of the people of the Fire."
When the fighting began, the man fought with the greatest ferocity,
and he was covered with wounds and was left incapacitated.

Then a man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, do you see the one you said was of the people of the Fire? He has fought in the cause of Allah with the greatest ferocity,
and he has received many wounds." The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Indeed, he is of the people of the Fire."
Some of the Muslims almost fell into doubt. While matters stood thus, the man felt the pain of his wounds, so he reached with his hand to his quiver,
pulled an arrow out of it, and killed himself with it.
Some of the Muslims hurried to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, Allah has made your statement true.
So-and-so has killed himself; he has taken his own life."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
O Bilāl, get up and call out:
None will enter Paradise except a believer,
and Allah will support this religion even through a wicked man."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a written note that he showed me in comparison, then he read it to me; he said: Ḥanẓalah ibn Abī Sufyān informed us: Saʿīd ibn Mīnāʾ narrated to us, saying: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh say: When the trench was being dug, I saw that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in severe hunger, so I turned back to my wife and said to her, "Do you have anything? For I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in severe hunger."

She brought out a bag for me containing a ṣāʿ of barley, and we had a tame young goat. He said: I slaughtered it, and she ground the barley. When I had finished, I cut it up into pieces in her cooking pot. Then I turned to go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said, "Do not disgrace me before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and those with him." He said: I came to him and spoke to him privately, saying, "O Messenger of Allah, we have slaughtered a young goat of ours and ground a ṣāʿ of barley that we had, so come, you and a small group with you."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called out loudly and said: "
O people of the trench, Jābir has prepared a feast for you, so come quickly!"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also said: "
Do not take your pot off the fire and do not bake your dough until I come."
So I came, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, leading the people, until I reached my wife, and she said, "This is on you, and on you!"
I said, "I have done just what you told me."
Then she brought out our dough for him, and he spat in it and blessed it. Then he went to our pot, spat in it, and blessed it. Then he said: "
Call a woman baker to bake with you, and ladle out from your pot, but do not take it off the fire."
They were a thousand. I swear by Allah, they ate until they left it and turned away, and our pot was still bubbling as it was, and our dough—or as aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk said—was still being baked as it was.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us one day and mentioned misappropriation of war booty. He declared it a grave matter and stressed its seriousness. Then he said: "
Let me not find any of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with a camel on his neck, groaning, saying, 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!'
And I will say, 'I have no power to help you at all; I conveyed the message to you.'
Let me not find any of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with a horse on his neck, neighing, saying, 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!'
And I will say, 'I have no power to help you at all; I conveyed the message to you.'
Let me not find any of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with a sheep on his neck, bleating, saying, 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!'
And I will say, 'I have no power to help you at all; I conveyed the message to you.'
Let me not find any of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with a soul on his neck, crying out, saying, 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!'
And I will say, 'I have no power to help you at all; I conveyed the message to you.'
Let me not find any of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with pieces of cloth on his neck, fluttering, saying, 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!'
And I will say, 'I have no power to help you at all; I conveyed the message to you.'

Let me not find any of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with gold and silver on his neck, saying, 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' And I will say, 'I have no power to help you at all; I conveyed the message to you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man called Karkarah was in charge of the baggage of the Prophet ﷺ.
He died, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "
He is in the Fire."
So they went to look, and they found on him a cloak or a robe that he had stolen from the war booty.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar said to Ibn az-Zubayr, "Do you remember when we met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, you, I, and Ibn ʿAbbās?" He said, "Yes. He carried us and left you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"O Abū Dharr."
I said, "At your service, O Messenger of Allah, and at your pleasure."
Then he mentioned the hadith, in which he said:
"How will you be when death afflicts the people, such that a house [will be sold] for a slave?"
I said, "Allah and His Messenger know best," or he said, "Whatever Allah and His Messenger choose for me." He said, "You must be patient," or he said, "Be patient."
Then he said to me:
"O Abū Dharr."
I said, "At your service and pleasure." He said:
"How will you be when you see the Aḥjār al-Zayt submerged in blood?"
I said, "Whatever Allah and His Messenger choose for me." He said:
"Stay with those whom you belong to."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, should I not take my sword and place it on my shoulder?" He said:
"Then you would be joining the people [in the strife]."
I said, "Then what do you command me?" He said, "Stay in your house."
I said, "What if someone enters my house?" He said:
"If you fear that the gleam of the sword will dazzle you, then throw your garment over your face; he will bear your sin and his own sin."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Ahead of you are trials like pieces of the dark night, in which a man will be a believer in the morning and a disbeliever in the evening, and a believer in the evening and a disbeliever in the morning. In them, the one sitting is better than the one standing, the one standing is better than the one walking, and the one walking is better than the one running."
They said, "Then what do you command us?" He said:
"Be [like] the saddle-cloths of your houses."
label: machine translation

segments_en: By Allah, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"Truly, fortunate is the one who is kept away from trials; truly, fortunate is the one who is kept away from trials; truly, fortunate is the one who is kept away from trials; and [fortunate is] the one who is tested and is patient. How excellent [is he]!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Khālid ibn Abī ʿImrān said, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Baylamānī,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hurmuz,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There will be a trial, deaf, dumb and blind. Whoever looks toward it, it will look toward him, and [using] the tongue in it is like the falling of the sword."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ziyād Saymīn Kūsh
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were on the expedition to Constantinople, at Dhulqiyyah, when a man from the people of Palestine came forward, one of their nobles and best, whom they recognized as such, called Hāniʾ ibn Kulthūm ibn Sharīk al-Kinānī. He greeted ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Zakariyyā, whose right he recognized. Khālid said to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Zakariyyā narrated to us, saying: I heard Umm al-Dardāʾ say: I heard Abū al-Dardāʾ say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Every sin, Allah may forgive, except for one who dies a polytheist, or a believer who deliberately kills a believer."
Then Hāniʾ ibn Kulthūm said: I heard Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ narrating from ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit that he heard him narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said:
"Whoever kills a believer and rejoices in his killing, Allah will not accept from him any obligatory or voluntary [deed]."
Khālid said to us: Then Ibn Abī Zakariyyā narrated to me from Umm al-Dardāʾ, from Abū al-Dardāʾ, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The believer remains sound and in a state of ease so long as he has not shed forbidden blood; but when he sheds forbidden blood, he is exhausted."
And Hāniʾ ibn Kulthūm narrated from Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ, from ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, exactly the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Khālid ibn Dihqān said: I asked Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā al-Ghassānī about the phrase "iʿtabaṭa bi-qatlihi" [rejoiced in his killing].
He said: They are those who fight in a time of trial, and one of them is killed, and he thinks that he is on guidance, [so] he does not seek Allah's forgiveness for that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding His words, {And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell}, he said: It is his recompense, but if Allah wills to pardon him, He does so.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ when he mentioned a trial and emphasized its seriousness. We said, or they said, "O Messenger of Allah, if this reaches us, it will destroy us."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No! Being killed is enough for you."
Saʿīd said: And I saw my brothers killed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"This nation of mine is a nation shown mercy. It will have no punishment in the Hereafter; its punishment is in this world: trials, earthquakes, and killing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If only a single day of time remained, Allah would raise a man from my family who would fill it with justice as it had been filled with injustice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The first to speak about divine decree (qadar) in Basra was Maʿbad al-Juhanī. So Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥimyarī and I set out, performing Hajj or ʿUmrah, and we said: "If only we could meet one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask him about what these people say regarding divine decree." Then ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb happened to be entering the mosque, so my companion and I flanked him, one of us on his right and the other on his left. I thought that my companion would leave the speaking to me, so I said: "Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, some people have appeared in our region who recite the Qurʾān and pursue knowledge" and he mentioned something of their affairs, "and they claim that there is no divine decree, and that the matter is entirely new [i.e., Allah only knows things as they occur]."

He said: "When you meet those people, tell them that I am free of them and that they are free of me. By the One by whom ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar swears, if one of them had gold equal to Mount Uḥud and spent it, Allah would not accept it from him until he believes in divine decree." Then he said: "My father, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, narrated to me: While we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day, a man appeared before us whose clothes were intensely white and whose hair was intensely black. No sign of travel could be seen on him, and none of us knew him. He sat down before the Prophet ﷺ, rested his knees against his knees, placed his palms on his thighs, and said: 'Muḥammad, tell me about Islam.'"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Islam is that you bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, that you establish prayer, give zakāh, fast Ramadan, and perform Hajj to the House if you are able to make the journey." He said: "You have spoken truly."
He said: "We were amazed at him: he asks him and then confirms that he is right."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were forbidden in the Qurʾān from asking the Prophet ﷺ about things, so we liked it when an intelligent man from the desert people would come and ask him. A man from the desert people came and said: "Muhammad, your messenger came to us and told us that you claim Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent you." He said: "He spoke truly."
He said: "Who created the heavens?" He said: "Allah."
He said: "Who created the earth?" He said: "Allah."
He said: "Who set up the mountains in it?" He said: "Allah."
He said: "Who placed benefits in it?" He said: "Allah."
He said: "Then by the One who created the heavens and the earth, set up the mountains, and placed benefits in it, did Allah send you?" He said: "Yes."
He said: "Your messenger claims that we must pray five prayers every day and night." He said: "He spoke truly."
He said: "Then by the One who sent you, did Allah command you with this?" He said: "Yes."
He said: "Your messenger claims that we must pay zakāh on our wealth." He said: "He spoke truly."
He said: "Then by the One who sent you, did Allah command you with this?" He said: "Yes."
He said: "Your messenger claims that we must fast the month of Ramadan every year." He said: "He spoke truly."
He said: "Then by the One who sent you, did Allah command you with this?" He said: "Yes."
He said: "Your messenger claims that we must perform Hajj if we are able to make the journey." He said: "He spoke truly."
He said: "Then by the One who sent you, did Allah command you with this?" He said: "Yes."
He said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, I will not add anything to these, nor will I subtract from them."
When he turned to leave, the Prophet ﷺ said:
"If he is true, he will enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ under the tree, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever swears a false oath by a religion other than Islam is as he said. Whoever kills himself with something will be punished with it on the Day of Resurrection. And a man has no vow concerning something he does not own."
label: machine translation

segments_en: No man takes the right of a Muslim by his oath except that Allah forbids Paradise to him and makes the Fire obligatory for him."
A man among the people said: "Messenger of Allah, even if it is something small?" He said:
"Even if it is a twig of the arāk tree."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered the mosque and found ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ sitting in the shade of the Kaʿbah with people gathered around him. I went to them and sat beside him. He said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and we stopped at a resting place. Some of us were mending their tents, some were practising archery, and some were with their grazing animals, when the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ announced: "Prayer is about to be held in congregation!"
So we gathered around the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:

"There was no prophet before me but that it was his duty to guide his nation to the best that he knew for them, and to warn them against the worst that he knew for them. This nation of yours has had its well-being placed in its beginning, and the last of it will be struck by trials and by matters that you will disapprove of. Then a trial will come that makes the previous one seem light, and a trial will come, and the believer will say: 'This is my destruction.'
Then it will clear away, and another trial will come, and the believer will say: 'This is it, this is it.'

Whoever wishes to be removed from the Fire and admitted to Paradise, let death come to him while he believes in Allah and the Last Day, and let him treat people as he would like to be treated. And whoever pledges allegiance to a leader, giving him the clasp of his hand and the fruit of his heart, let him obey him if he is able. If another comes to contest his authority, strike the neck of the other."

I drew close to him and said: I ask you by Allah, did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He pointed with his hands to his ears and his heart and said: My two ears heard it and my heart retained it.

I said to him: This cousin of yours, Muʿāwiyah, orders us to consume our wealth among ourselves unjustly and to kill ourselves, while Allah says: {O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, but only through trade by mutual consent among you, and do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you.} He said: He was silent for a while, then said: Obey him in obedience to Allah, and disobey him in disobedience to Allah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse from the pulpit:
"And prepare against them whatever you are able of power." Then he said:
"Indeed, power is archery," three times. "Indeed, Allah will open the earth to you, and you will be spared the burden of provision. So let none of you be too lax to play with his arrows."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nabīdh used to be prepared for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a waterskin. When they could not find a waterskin, it was prepared for him in a stone vessel. Some of the people said, while I was listening, to Abū al-Zubayr: From a stone pot? He said: From a stone pot.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to prepare nabīdh for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a waterskin. We would take a handful of dates or a handful of raisins and put it in, then pour water over it. We would prepare it in the morning and he would drink it in the evening, and we would prepare it in the evening and he would drink it in the morning.
Abū Muʿāwiyah said: in the daytime and he would drink it at night, or at night and he would drink it in the daytime.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd,
Allāh ibn Ḥunayn, from his father,
from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade wearing qassī garments and garments dyed with safflower, wearing gold rings, and reciting the Qurʾān while bowing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The most beloved words to Allah are four: Subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, and Allāhu akbar.
It does not harm you with which of them you begin.
And do not name your slave boy Yasār, Rabāḥ, Najīḥ, or Aflaḥ, for you will ask, 'Is he there?' and he will not be, and the answer will be, 'No.'"
These are four, so do not add more to me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

began praising ʿUthmān. Al-Miqdād went over and knelt on his knees, and he was a heavily built man, and began throwing pebbles in the man's face. ʿUthmān said to him: What is the matter with you? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you see those who excessively praise, throw dust in their faces."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He set out for Hajj or ʿUmrah with people accompanying him, and he was leading them in prayer. One day he called the iqāmah for the dawn prayer, then said: Let one of you step forward to lead.
And he went to relieve himself, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"When one of you wants to relieve himself and the prayer has been called, let him begin with relieving himself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw ʿAlī perform ablution. He washed his hands until he had cleaned them, then rinsed his mouth three times, sniffed water into his nose three times, washed his face three times and his forearms three times, and wiped his head once. Then he washed his feet up to the ankles. Then he stood, took the remainder of his ablution water, and drank it while standing. Then he said: I wanted to show you how the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us on the Day of Sacrifice and said:
"None of you should slaughter until he has prayed."
He said: My maternal uncle said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is a day on which meat is disliked [to be lacking]."
Then he narrated the rest with a meaning similar to the hadith of Hushaym.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade eating the meat of the sacrificial animals after three days.
Sālim said: Ibn ʿUmar would not eat the meat of the sacrificial animals beyond three days.
And Ibn Abī ʿUmar said: "after three days."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every intoxicant is forbidden, and every intoxicant is khamr."
Al-Husayn said: Aḥmad said, "This hadith is sound."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me four things: wearing a garment dyed with safflower, wearing a gold ring, wearing qasiyyah garments, and reciting the Qur'an while bowing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A donkey that had been branded on its face passed by the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Has it not reached you that I have cursed whoever brands an animal on its face or strikes it on its face?"
So he forbade that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her. She said: Children would be brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he would supplicate for blessing for them. Yūsuf added: and he would perform taḥnīk for them. He did not mention blessing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas ibn Mālik said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"O my son, when you enter upon your family, give the greeting of peace; it will be a blessing upon you and upon the people of your household."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū al-Muʿtamir said: I think that Anas ibn Mālik
narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a prayer that does not benefit."
And he mentioned another supplication.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He added in it: "and distress."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque and found a man of the Anṣār called Abū Umāmah, and he said:
"O Abū Umāmah, why do I see you sitting in the mosque at a time that is not a time of prayer?"
He said: Worries and debts have overwhelmed me, O Messenger of Allah. He said:
"Shall I not teach you words which, if you say them, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will remove your worry and settle your debt?"
He said: I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said:

"Say, when you rise in the morning and when you enter the evening: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, and I seek refuge in You from incapacity and laziness, and I seek refuge in You from cowardice and miserliness, and I seek refuge in You from being overcome by debt and the domination of men."
He said: I did that, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removed my worry and settled my debt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr said: Its right is the payment of zakāh. And he said: a hobbling cord.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wasq is sixty ṣāʿ, sealed by the measure of al-Ḥajjājī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said to ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn: O Abū Nujayd, you narrate to us reports for which we find no basis in the Qur'an.

ʿImrān became angry and said to the man: Have you found in the Qur'an that on every forty dirhams there is one dirham, and on every such-and-such number of sheep one sheep, and on every such-and-such number of camels such-and-such? Have you found this in the Qur'an? He said: No.
label: machine translation

segments_en: To proceed: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command us to give charity from what we prepare for sale.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to wear anklets of gold, so I said: O Messenger of Allah, is it a hoarded treasure? He said:
"Whatever reaches the amount on which zakāh is due and you pay its zakāh, is not a hoarded treasure."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We entered upon ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me and saw large silver rings on my hand, and he said:
"What is this, O ʿĀʾishah?"
I said: I made them to adorn myself for you, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Do you pay zakāh on them?"
I said: No, or as Allah wills. He said:
"It is enough for you from the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: This is a copy of the document of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which he wrote concerning charity, and it is with the family of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. Ibn Shihāb said: Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar had me read it, and I memorized it exactly as it is, and it is the one that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz copied from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar. Then he mentioned the hadith and said:

"When it reaches one hundred and twenty-one, then three bint labūn are due, until it reaches one hundred and twenty-nine. When it is one hundred and thirty, then two bint labūn and one ḥiqqah, until it reaches one hundred and thirty-nine. When it is one hundred and forty, then two ḥiqqahs and one bint labūn, until it reaches one hundred and forty-nine. When it is one hundred and fifty, then three ḥiqqahs, until it reaches one hundred and fifty-nine. When it is one hundred and sixty, then four bint labūn, until it reaches one hundred and sixty-nine. When it is one hundred and seventy, then three bint labūn and one ḥiqqah, until it reaches one hundred and seventy-nine. When it is one hundred and eighty, then two ḥiqqahs and two bint labūn, until it reaches one hundred and eighty-nine. When it is one hundred and ninety, then three ḥiqqahs and one bint labūn, until it reaches one hundred and ninety-nine. When it is two hundred, then four ḥiqqahs or five bint labūn, whichever age you find you take; and for grazing sheep..."
Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn, and in it:
"No old animal, no defective animal, and no billy goat is to be taken in charity, unless the collector wishes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mālik said: The statement of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, "What is separate is not to be combined, and what is combined is not to be separated,"
means that each man has forty sheep, and when the collector comes upon them they combine them so that only one sheep is due on them. And "what is combined is not to be separated" means:

that two partners, when each of them has one hundred and one sheep, owe three sheep between them; but when the collector comes upon them they separate their flocks, so that only one sheep is due from each. This is what I heard about that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think about a cousin of mine whom I go to and ask, but he does not give me or maintain ties with me? Then he becomes in need of me and comes to me and asks me, though I have sworn that I will not give him or maintain ties with him." So he ordered me to do what is better and to expiate for my oath.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He said, meaning the Prophet ﷺ:
"There is no vow for the son of Adam concerning what he does not own, nor in disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
ʿAlī ibn Zayd differed from him, and narrated it from al-Ḥasan, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samurah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The lodging brought ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit and Muʿāwiyah together, and ʿUbādah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us to sell gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, and dates for dates—one of them said: and salt for salt, while the other did not say it—except like for like, equal for equal. One of them said: Whoever gives more or takes more has engaged in usury, while the other did not say it. And he commanded us to sell gold for silver and silver for gold, wheat for barley and barley for wheat, hand to hand, as we wish. This hadith reached Muʿāwiyah, so he stood up and said: What is the matter with men who narrate hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when we accompanied him and did not hear it from him?
That reached ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, so he stood up and repeated the hadith, and said: We will certainly narrate what we heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, even if Muʿāwiyah is displeased.
Qatādah differed from him, narrating it from Muslim ibn Yasār, from Abū al-Ashʿath, from ʿUbādah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people from Banū Thaʿlabah attacked a man from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and a man from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "O Messenger of Allah, these are Banū Thaʿlabah who killed so-and-so."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No soul is to bear the offense of another."
Shuʿbah said: That is, no one is to be taken for [the wrong of] another. And Allah the Exalted knows best.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A thief's hand is cut off for [stealing] the price of a shield. And the price of a shield in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was one dinar or ten dirhams.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb saw a silk-striped garment and said, "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would buy this garment for the delegations and for Friday."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Only one who has no share in the Hereafter wears this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded them, he would command them [to do] deeds they were able to bear. They said, "We are not like you, O Messenger of Allah,
for Allah has forgiven you your earlier and later sins."
He would become angry until the anger could be seen in his face, then he would say:
"I am the most God-fearing of you and the most knowledgeable of you about Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"I was shown the Fire, and most of its inhabitants were women, because they are ungrateful."
It was asked, "Are they ungrateful to Allah?" He said, "They are ungrateful to their husbands and ungrateful for kindness.
If you were good to one of them for a lifetime, then she saw something [she disliked] from you, she would say: I have never seen any good from you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw him wearing a cloak and his servant wearing a cloak, so I said, "If you took this one and wore it, it would be a full set,
and you could give him another garment."
He said: There was an exchange of words between me and a man,
and his mother was non-Arab,
so I disparaged her. He mentioned me to the Prophet ﷺ, who said to me, "Did you insult so-and-so?" I said, "Yes." He said:
"Did you disparage his mother?" I said, "Yes." He said:
"You are a man who still has some ignorance [of the pre-Islamic days] in you."
I said, "Even now, at this time of my life, in my old age?" He said, "Yes. They are your brothers,
whom Allah has placed under your hands.
So whoever has his brother placed under his hand by Allah, let him feed him from what he eats
and clothe him from what he wears,
and not burden him with work that overwhelms him.
If he does burden him with what overwhelms him, let him help him with it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out to support this man,
and Abū Bakrah met me and said, "Where are you heading?" I said, "To support this man."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted:

"Alif, Lām, Mīm. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land..." He said: They were defeated and then they defeated. The polytheists liked the people of Persia to prevail over the Romans, because they and the Persians were people of idols, while the Muslims liked the Romans to prevail over the Persians, because they were People of the Book. They mentioned this to Abū Bakr, and Abū Bakr mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said:
"Indeed, they will be victorious."

Abū Bakr told them that, and they said: "Set a term between us and you. If we prevail, we will have such and such, and if you prevail, you will have such and such." So he set a term of five years, but the Romans did not prevail. They mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Why did you not make it less than—" he said: I think he meant ten.
Saʿīd said: The biḍʿ is what is less than ten. He said: Then the Romans prevailed afterward.
He said: That is the saying of Allah, the Exalted:
"Alif, Lām, Mīm. The Romans have been defeated" up to His saying:
"the believers will rejoice, in the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills." Sufyān said: I heard that they prevailed over them on the day of Badr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this was revealed:

"Alif, Lām, Mīm. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land; but after their defeat they will be victorious, within a few years," the Persians on the day this verse was revealed were overpowering the Romans, and the Muslims liked the Romans to prevail over them, because they and the Romans were People of the Book. Concerning that is the saying of Allah, the Exalted:

"On that day the believers will rejoice, in the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful." The Quraysh liked the Persians to prevail, because they and the Persians were not People of the Book and did not believe in resurrection. When Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse, Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, went out crying in the outskirts of Makkah:

"Alif, Lām, Mīm. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land; but after their defeat they will be victorious, within a few years." Some people of the Quraysh said to Abū Bakr: "Then this is between us and you. Your companion claims that the Romans will defeat the Persians within a few years. Shall we not wager you on that?" He said: "Yes."

That was before wagering was prohibited. So Abū Bakr and the polytheists made a wager and agreed upon its terms. They said to Abū Bakr: "How long do you make the biḍʿ? It is from three years to nine years. Name a middle term between us and you, at which it ends."

He said: So they named six years between them. He said: The six years passed before the Romans prevailed, so the polytheists took Abū Bakr's stake. When the seventh year began, the Romans prevailed over the Persians. The Muslims faulted Abū Bakr for naming six years, because Allah, the Exalted, said:
"within a few years." He said: Many people accepted Islam at that time.
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb hadith from the narration of Niyār ibn Mukram. We do not know it except from the narration of ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abī az-Zinād.
label: machine translation

segments_en: This verse: "They forsake
their beds,
" was revealed concerning waiting for this prayer which is called al-ʿAtamah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "What do you think of the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:

'Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body.' What was meant by that?" He said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ stood one day to pray, and a thought crossed his mind. The hypocrites who were praying with him said: "Do you not see that he has two hearts, one heart with you and one heart with them?" So Allah revealed:
"Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿĪsā,
the two sons of Ṭalḥah, from their father,
Ṭalḥah, that the Companions of

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to an ignorant Bedouin: "Ask him about the one who has fulfilled his vow—who is he?" They did not dare to ask him, out of respect and awe for him. So the Bedouin asked him, but he turned away from him. Then he asked him, and he turned away from him. Then he asked him, and he turned away from him. Then I appeared from the door of the mosque, wearing green garments. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me, he said:
"Where is the one who asked about the one who has fulfilled his vow?"
The Bedouin said: "I am, O Messenger of Allah."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"This man is one of those who have fulfilled their vow."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith. We do not know it except from the narration of Yūnus ibn Bukayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: "
The master supplication for forgiveness is to say: O Allah, You are my Lord;
there is no god but You;
You created me and I am Your servant;
and I am upon Your covenant and Your promise as far as I am able.
I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done;
I acknowledge Your favor upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me,
for no one forgives sins except You." He said: "
Whoever says it during the day, firmly believing in it,
and dies on that same day before evening comes,
he is among the people of Paradise;
and whoever says it during the night, firmly believing in it,
and dies before morning comes,
he is among the people of Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ took to his bed at night, he would place his hand under his cheek and then say: "
O Allah, in Your name I die and I live."
And when he woke up, he would say: "
Praise be to Allah, who gave us life after having made us die, and to Him is the resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

When one of you gets up from his bed and then returns to it, let him shake it out three times with the edge of his lower garment, for he does not know what has come onto it after he left. Then when he lies down, let him say: In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and by You I raise it. If You take my soul, have mercy on it, and if You release it, protect it with that by which You protect Your righteous servants.
And when he wakes, let him say: Praise be to Allah, who granted me well-being in my body, returned my soul to me, and permitted me to remember Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Let none of you say: O Allah, forgive me if You wish;
have mercy on me if You wish;
provide for me if You wish. Rather, let him be firm in his request,
for He does whatever He wills,
and no one can compel Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him,
and whoever dislikes meeting Allah, Allah dislikes meeting him."
ʿĀʾishah, or one of his wives, said: "We dislike death." He said: "That is not it,
rather, when death comes to the believer, he is given the good news of Allah's pleasure and honor,
so nothing is dearer to him than what lies ahead of him,
so he loves to meet Allah, and Allah loves to meet him.
And when death comes to the disbeliever, he is given the news of Allah's punishment and retribution,
so nothing is more hateful to him than what lies ahead of him,
he dislikes meeting Allah, and Allah dislikes meeting him."
Abū Dāwūd and ʿAmr abridged it from Shuʿbah.
And Saʿīd said, from Qatādah, from Zurārah, from Saʿd, from ʿĀʾishah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was read to al-Ḥārith ibn Miskīn while I was present:
Ibn Wahb informed you,
he said: Mālik informed me,
from Abū al-Zinād,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hurmuz,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
A vow does not bring the son of Adam anything that I had not decreed for him,
but the vow meets with the decree that I have decreed, drawing [something] out of the miser, so that he gives what he would not have given before."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Most often the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would swear with this oath: "No, by the Turner of hearts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Divide the wealth among the people of the prescribed shares according to the Book of Allah, and whatever the prescribed shares leave over goes to the nearest male relative."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hurayrah [said] that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled concerning the fetus of a woman of Banū Laḥyān who miscarried it dead, that a ghurrah, a male or female slave, be given. Then the woman against whom the ghurrah had been ruled died, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that her inheritance goes to her sons and her husband, and that the blood-money is on her paternal relatives.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ said: "
A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, and a disbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ [said]: "The child belongs to the bed, and for the adulterer is the stone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿUmar,

meaning Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, delivered a sermon and said: Allah sent Muḥammad ﷺ with the truth and revealed the Book to him, and among what was revealed to him was the verse of stoning. We recited it and understood it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ carried out stoning and we carried it out after him. I fear that, as time passes, someone will say: We do not find the verse of stoning in the Book of Allah, and so they will go astray by abandoning an obligation that Allah, the Exalted, revealed. Stoning is a right upon whoever commits unlawful intercourse, men and women, when he is married, when the proof is established, or there is pregnancy, or confession. By Allah, were it not that people would say, "ʿUmar added to the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic," I would have written it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you has prayed the two rakʿahs before the dawn prayer, let him lie down on his right side."
Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam said to him, "Is it not enough for one of us to walk to the mosque, without having to lie down on his right side?" ʿUbayd Allāh said in his narration: He replied, "No."
He said: That reached Ibn ʿUmar, who said, "Abū Hurayrah has narrated too much on his own account."
He said: Ibn ʿUmar was asked, "Do you deny anything of what he says?" He said, "No, but he was bold and we were timid."
He said: That reached Abū Hurayrah, who said, "What is my fault if I memorized and they forgot?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ. (Transmission switches:) And al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ narrated to us:
Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us:
Ḥammād ibn Salamah informed us,
from Thābit al-Bunānī,
from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabāḥ,
from Abū Qatādah:

That the Prophet ﷺ went out one night and found Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, praying with a low voice. He said: And he passed by ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who was praying with a raised voice. He said: When the two were together with the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Abū Bakr, I passed by you while you were praying with your voice lowered." He said:
"I made the One I was whispering to hear me, Messenger of Allah."
He said: And he said to ʿUmar:
"I passed by you while you were praying with your voice raised." He said: ʿUmar said:
"Messenger of Allah, I was waking the drowsy and driving away Satan."
Al-Ḥasan added in his narration: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Abū Bakr, raise your voice a little." And he said to ʿUmar:
"Lower your voice a little."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Madinah and entered upon ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her. She said, "Who are you?" I said, "I am Saʿd ibn Hishām ibn ʿĀmir."
She said, "May Allah have mercy on your father."
I said, "Tell me about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
She said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to be such and such." I said, "Yes."

She said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray the ʿIshāʾ prayer at night, then retire to his bed and sleep. When it was the middle of the night, he would get up to attend to his need and to his purification, perform ablution, then enter the mosque and pray eight rakʿahs. It seemed to me that he made them equal in recitation, bowing and prostration. He would pray Witr with one rakʿah, then pray two rakʿahs sitting, then lay down on his side. Often Bilāl would come and call him to prayer before he had dozed off, and often he would doze; at times I doubted whether he had dozed or not, until Bilāl called him to prayer. That was the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he grew old and heavy (and she mentioned his weight as Allah willed). She said: And the Prophet ﷺ would lead the people in ʿIshāʾ, then retire to his bed. When it was the middle of the night, he would get up to his purification and his need, perform ablution, then enter the mosque and pray six rakʿahs. It seemed to me that he made them equal in recitation, bowing and prostration. Then he would pray Witr with one rakʿah, then pray two rakʿahs sitting, then lay down on his side. Often Bilāl would come and call him to prayer before he had dozed off, and often he would doze; at times I doubted whether he had dozed or not, until he called him to prayer." She said: "That continued to be the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās how the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was. He said:
I spent a night with him while he was at Maymūnah's,
He slept until, when a third of the night or half of it had passed, he woke up, went to a water skin containing water, and performed ablution, and I performed ablution with him,
Then he stood and I stood at his side, on his left, and he placed me on his right,
Then he put his hand on my head as if touching my ear, as if to rouse me, and prayed two light rakʿahs. I said:
"Did he recite Umm al-Qurʾān (al-Fātiḥah) in each rakʿah?" Then he gave the salām, then prayed until he had prayed eleven rakʿahs including Witr,
Then he slept, and Bilāl came to him and said:
"The prayer, Messenger of Allah."
So he got up and prayed two rakʿahs,
Then he led the people in prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked the Prophet ﷺ in how many days the Qurʾān should be recited. He said:
"In forty days." Then he said, "In a month." Then he said, "In twenty." Then he said:
"In fifteen." Then he said, "In ten." Then he said, "In seven."
He did not go lower than seven.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed one day and then ascended the pulpit, which he had never ascended before that except on Friday. That was hard on the people, some standing and some sitting, so he gestured to them with his hand: "Sit down.

By Allah, I have not stood in this place of mine for something that benefits you, whether out of hope or out of fear. Rather, Tamīm ad-Dārī came to me and told me news that kept me from taking my midday rest, out of joy and delight, so I wanted to spread your Prophet's joy among you. Tamīm ad-Dārī told me that a cousin of his told him that the wind drove them to an island they did not know, so they sat in the small boats of the ship and went out in them. Then they came upon a creature, hairy and black. They said to it, 'What are you?' It said, 'I am the Jassāsah.' They said, 'Tell us.'

It said, 'I will not tell you anything, nor will I ask you anything. But this monastery, you have caught sight of it, so go to it, for in it is a man who is eager to tell you and to be told by you.' So they went to it and entered upon him, and there was an old man, bound tightly in chains, showing grief and complaining bitterly. He said to them, 'Where are you from?' They said, 'From Syria.'

He said, 'What have the Arabs done?' They said, 'We are a people of the Arabs; what are you asking about?' He said, 'What has this man who has appeared among you done?' They said, 'Well: he fought a people and Allah gave him victory over them, and today their command is united, their god is one and their religion is one.' He said, 'What has become of the spring of Zughar?' They said, 'Well: they water their crops from it and draw water from it for drinking.' He said, 'What has become of the palm trees between ʿUmān and Baysān?' They said, 'They bear fruit every year.'
He said, 'What has become of the Lake of Tiberias?' They said, 'Its banks overflow with the abundance of water.'

Then he sighed three times and said, 'If I were freed from these chains of mine, I would leave no land without treading it with these two feet of mine, except Ṭaybah; I have no way into it.' The Prophet ﷺ said:

"This is where my joy ends. This is Ṭaybah. By the One in whose hand is my soul, there is no road in it, narrow or wide, no plain and no mountain, but that over it is an angel with his sword drawn until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Muslims will burn the bows of Gog and Magog, their arrows and their shields, as fuel for seven years."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us, and most of what he said in his sermon was what he told us about the Antichrist (ad-Dajjāl) and warned us about. Among his words was this:

"There has been no trial on earth, since Allah scattered the offspring of Adam, greater than the trial of the Antichrist. Allah did not send any prophet without warning his nation about the Antichrist. I am the last of the prophets and you are the last of the nations, and he will surely emerge among you. If he emerges while I am among you, I will argue against him on behalf of every Muslim; and if he emerges after me, then each person must argue for himself, and Allah is my successor over every Muslim. He will emerge from a tract between Syria and Iraq, and he will spread corruption to the right and to the left.

O servants of Allah, O people, hold firm! For I will describe him to you with a description that no prophet before me described. He will begin by saying, 'I am a prophet,' and there is no prophet after me. Then he will repeat and say, 'I am your Lord.'

But you will not see your Lord until you die. He is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed. Between his eyes is written 'Disbeliever,' which every believer will read, whether literate or not. Among his trials is that he has with him a paradise and a fire; his fire is a paradise and his paradise is a fire. Whoever is tested by his fire, let him seek help from Allah and recite the opening verses of Sūrat al-Kahf, and it will be cool and safe for him, as the fire was for Abraham. Among his trials is that he will say to a Bedouin, 'Do you think that if I raise your father and mother for you, you will testify that I am your Lord?' He will say, 'Yes.'
Then two devils will take the form of his father and mother, and they will say, 'O my son, follow him, for he is your Lord.'

Among his trials is that he will be given power over one person; he will kill him and saw him with a saw until he falls in two pieces. Then he will say, 'Look at this servant of mine; I will now raise him up,' and then he will claim that he has a lord other than me.

Then Allah will raise him up, and the Antichrist will say to him, 'Who is your Lord, you wretch?' He will say, 'My Lord is Allah, and you are the enemy of Allah. You are the Antichrist. By Allah, I have never had more insight into you than I have today.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was read to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, on the authority of Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from ʿAlqamah ibn Abī ʿAlqamah, from his mother,
that she heard ʿĀʾishah say:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up one night, put on his clothes, and went out. She said: I told my maidservant Barīrah to follow him, so she followed him until he came to al-Baqīʿ.
He stood at its nearest edge for as long as Allah willed him to stand,
then he turned back. Barīrah got ahead of him and told me,
but I did not mention anything to him until morning.
Then I mentioned that to him, and he said: "
I was sent to the people of al-Baqīʿ to pray for them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was walking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he passed by the graves of the Muslims and said: "
These have preceded [us] with much evil."
Then he passed by the graves of the polytheists and said: "
These have preceded [us] with much good."
Then he happened to glance around and saw a man walking among the graves in his sandals, and he said: "
O wearer of the two sibtī sandals, throw them off!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with the believers that they are tested in their graves, except the martyr?" He said: "
The flash of swords above his head is trial enough."
label: machine translation

segments_en: This is the one for whom the Throne shook, for whom the gates of heaven were opened, and whom seventy thousand angels attended. Yet he was squeezed once, and then it was eased for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jewish woman came to her and asked her for something, so ʿĀʾishah gave her something. She said, "May Allah protect you from the punishment of the grave."
ʿĀʾishah said: That weighed on my mind until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, and I mentioned it to him. He said: "
They are indeed punished in their graves with a punishment that the animals hear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. The first of creation to be clothed will be Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him." Then he recited: {Just as We began the first creation, We will repeat it.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The truthful one, to whom the truth was confirmed ﷺ, narrated to me: "

People will be gathered in three groups: a group riding, well fed, and clothed; a group the angels will drag on their faces and the Fire will gather; and a group walking and hurrying. Allah will cast calamity upon the mounts so that none remains, to the point that a man will have a garden which he would give away for a saddled camel, yet he will not be able to get one."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood to give an admonition and said: "
O people, you will be gathered to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, naked."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ sat, a group of his Companions would sit with him. Among them was a man who had a young son who would come to him from behind his back, and the man would sit him in front of him. Then the boy died, and the man held back from attending the gathering because he remembered his son and grieved for him. The Prophet ﷺ missed him and said: "
What is the matter that I do not see so-and-so?"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, his son whom you saw has died."
The Prophet ﷺ met him and asked him about his son, and he told him that he had died. He consoled him about it and then said: "

O so-and-so, which would you prefer: that you enjoy him for your whole life, or that you never come tomorrow to any of the gates of Paradise without finding that he has gotten there before you, opening it for you?"
He said, "O Prophet of Allah, rather that he go ahead of me to the gate of Paradise and open it for me is dearer to me." He said: "Then that is yours."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not curse with any curse that is worth mentioning. And when he was near the time of meeting Jibrīl, peace be upon him, who would review [the Qurʾān] with him, he was more generous in doing good than the blowing wind.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We visited ʿUtbah ibn Farqad and began to discuss the month of Ramadan. He said, "What are you discussing?" We said, "The month of Ramadan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in a house in which ʿUtbah ibn Farqad was, and I wanted to narrate a hadith. A man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ was there who seemed more entitled to narrate than I, so that man narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "

In Ramadan the gates of heaven are opened, the gates of the Fire are closed, and every rebellious devil is chained. And a caller calls out every night: O seeker of good, come forward! And O seeker of evil, hold back!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mursal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mursal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He addressed the people on the day about which there was doubt and said: Indeed, I sat with the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and questioned them, and they told me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

Fast when you see it [the crescent], break the fast when you see it, and perform the rites for it. If it is overcast for you, complete thirty days. If two witnesses testify, then fast and break the fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From one of the Ansār, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a funeral, and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the grave instructing the gravedigger:
"Widen it at the side of his feet, widen it at the side of his head."

When he returned, the messenger of a woman met him with an invitation, so he went, and food was brought. He put his hand [in it], then the people put [their hands in] and ate. Our fathers saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ chewing a morsel in his mouth, then he said:
"I find the meat of a sheep that was taken without its owners' permission."

So the woman sent word and said: O Messenger of Allah, I sent someone to al-Baqīʿ to buy a sheep for me but he did not find one. So I sent to a neighbor of mine who had bought a sheep, asking him to send it to me for its price, but he was not there. So I sent to his wife, and she sent it to me.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Feed it to the prisoners."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say during the Farewell Pilgrimage:
"Beware! Every form of ribā of the Jāhiliyyah is abolished for you. You have your capital: do not wrong, and you will not be wronged.
Beware! Every [claim of] blood from the Jāhiliyyah is abolished, and the first blood of theirs that I abolish is the blood of al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib."
He had been placed for nursing among Banū Layth, and Hudhayl killed him. He said:
"O Allah, have I conveyed [the message]?" They said: Yes. [He said it] three times. He said: "O Allah, bear witness," three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Makkah, before he emigrated, with this hadith, and he did not mention "weighing for payment."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said to Shuʿbah: Sufyān disagrees with you. He said: You have crushed me.
And it has reached me from Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn that he said: Whoever disagrees with Sufyān, the saying is that of Sufyān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sufyān had a better memory than I.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From his father,
from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"Indeed, among the greatest of sins with Allah with which a servant can meet Him, after the major sins that Allah has forbidden, is that a man dies owing a debt and leaves nothing to pay it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ with this report, with some additions and omissions, and he added: He said: "When these categories differ, then sell as you wish, provided it is hand to hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the year of Khaybar, a necklace containing gold and beads was brought to the Prophet ﷺ. Abū Bakr and Ibn Manīʿ said: It had beads strung with gold. A man had bought it for nine or seven dinars, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"No, not until you separate one from the other."
He said: I only wanted the stones. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"No, not until you separate them."
He said: So he returned it until he separated them.
Ibn ʿĪsā said: I wanted trade.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered him to equip an army, but the camels ran out, so he ordered him to take young camels from the charity (ṣadaqah) camels. So he would take one camel in exchange for two, [payable] from the charity camels.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ bought one slave in exchange for two slaves.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of fresh dates for dried dates on credit.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The ʿariyyah is when a man gives another man a palm tree [for its fruit], or a man excepts one or two palm trees from his property to eat from, and then he sells it for dried dates.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The ʿarāyā are when a man gives,
another man some palm trees, and it is burdensome for him to attend to them, so he sells them for the equivalent of their estimated yield.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a man of Banū Tamīm, who said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib addressed us, or he said: ʿAlī said. Ibn ʿĪsā said: This is how Hushaym narrated it to us,

He said: "A time of harshness will come upon the people, when the wealthy will cling tightly to what is in his hands, though he was not commanded to do so. Allah the Exalted said: {And do not forget graciousness between yourselves.} And people in desperate need will be made to sell, though the Prophet ﷺ forbade the sale of one under compulsion, the sale involving uncertainty, and the sale of fruit before it ripens."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed Allah says: I am the third of two partners,
as long as neither of them betrays his companion. If one betrays the other, I depart from between them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this report, though its wording differs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a man of the people of Madinah, from Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām,

that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him with a dinar to buy a sacrificial animal for him. He bought it for a dinar and sold it for two dinars. Then he returned and bought a sacrificial animal for him for a dinar, and brought a dinar to the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ gave it in charity and supplicated for him that his trade be blessed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ibn Muslim said: I heard a man

from Muzaynah, one of those who pursue knowledge and retain it—then the two narrators agreed—while we were with Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, and he narrated to us from Abū Hurayrah (this is the wording of Maʿmar, and it is more complete): A man and a woman from the Jews committed adultery. Some of them said to others, "Take us to this Prophet, for he is a prophet sent with leniency. If he gives us a ruling short of stoning, we will accept it and use it as an argument before Allah, saying: it is the ruling of one of Your prophets." So they came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was sitting in the mosque among his Companions, and said, "O Abū al-Qāsim, what do you say about a man and a woman who committed adultery?" He did not say a word to them until he came to their house of study. He stood at the door and said:
"I adjure you by Allah, who sent down the Torah to Moses, what do you find in the Torah as the punishment for one who commits adultery when he is married?"

They said, "His face is blackened, he is mounted [backwards], and he is flogged." (The tajbiyah is that the two adulterers are placed on a donkey with their backs facing each other and are paraded around.) He said: A young man among them stayed silent. When the Prophet ﷺ saw him silent, he pressed him with the oath. So he said, "O Allah, since you have adjured us, we do find stoning in the Torah." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Then what was the first thing by which you relaxed the command of Allah?"

He said: A relative of one of our kings committed adultery, and the king postponed the stoning for him. Later a man from an ordinary family committed adultery and he wanted to stone him, but his people stood in the way and said, "Our man will not be stoned until you bring your man and stone him." So they agreed on this punishment among themselves. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Then I judge by what is in the Torah."
He ordered that the two be stoned, and they were stoned.

Az-Zuhrī said: It has reached us that this verse was revealed concerning them: {Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light; the prophets who submitted [to Allah] judged by it} and the Prophet ﷺ was among them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī,

may Allah be pleased with him, passed through Babylon while traveling, and the muʾadhdhin came to him to call the adhān for the ʿAsr prayer. When he had left it behind, he ordered the muʾadhdhin, who then called the iqāmah for the prayer. When he finished, he said: My beloved ﷺ forbade me to pray in the cemetery, and he forbade me to pray in the land of Babylon, for it is cursed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the meaning of [the report of] Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd. He said: "When he went out."
[This is] in place of "When he had left it behind."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We entered upon him, and he said to his wife, "When should a boy pray?" She said: A man among us used to relate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he was asked about that, and he said:
"When he knows his right hand from his left, order him to pray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: …from the Anṣār said: The Prophet ﷺ was concerned about how to gather the people for prayer. It was said to him, "Raise a flag when the prayer time comes, and when they see it, they will inform one another." He did not like that. Then the qunʿ was mentioned to him—meaning the horn—and Ziyād said: the horn of the Jews. He did not like that, and said:
"That is from the practice of the Jews."
He said: Then the bell was mentioned to him, and he said:
"That is from the practice of the Christians."

Then ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih went away, concerned because of the concern of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was shown the adhān in his sleep. He said: He went early to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him, saying, "O Messenger of Allah, I was between sleep and wakefulness when someone came to me and showed me the adhān."
He said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, had seen it before that and had kept it secret for twenty days. Then he informed the Prophet ﷺ, who said to him:
"What prevented you from telling me?"
He said, "ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd preceded me, and I felt shy." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Bilāl, get up and see what ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd commands you, and do it."
He said: So Bilāl called the adhān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on an errand, then came in, and I had hung up a curtain with winged horses on it. [She said:] When he saw it, he said, "Take it down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jibrīl, peace be upon him, asked permission to enter upon the Prophet ﷺ, and he said, "Come in."

He said, "How can I enter when in your house there is a curtain with images on it? Either cut off their heads or make it into a carpet to be trodden on, for we, the company of angels, do not enter a house in which there are images."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Say: O Allah, guide me aright and keep me on the right course."
And he forbade me from sitting on the mayāthir. The mayāthir were saddles of silk that women used to make for their husbands to put on the riding saddle, like velvet cloths of crimson.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people from the Ashʿarites came to me and said, "Go with us to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for we have a need."
So I went with them, and they said, "O Messenger of Allah, employ us in your service."
Abū Mūsā said: I excused myself from what they had said and told him that I did not know what their need was, so he believed me and accepted my excuse. Then he said:
"We do not employ in our work anyone who asks us for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Prophet of Allah, my father is a very old man who cannot perform Hajj, and if I carry him he cannot hold on firmly. Shall I perform Hajj on his behalf?" He said:
"Perform Hajj on behalf of your father."
label: machine translation

segments_en: People pressed ʿAbdullāh with questions one day, and ʿAbdullāh said: "There was a time when we did not judge and were not in a position to do so. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, decreed that we reached what you see. So whoever among you is faced with a case for judgment after today, let him judge by what is in the Book of Allah. If a matter comes that is not in the Book of Allah, let him judge by what His Prophet ﷺ judged. If a matter comes that is not in the Book of Allah and was not judged by His Prophet ﷺ, let him judge by what the righteous judged. If a matter comes that is not in the Book of Allah, was not judged by His Prophet ﷺ, and was not judged by the righteous, let him exercise his own judgment, and not say, 'I fear, and I fear.' For the lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters, so leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He wrote to ʿUmar asking him, and [ʿUmar] wrote back to him: "Judge by what is in the Book of Allah. If it is not in the Book of Allah, then by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. If it is not in the Book of Allah nor in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then judge by what the righteous judged. If it is not in the Book of Allah, nor in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the righteous did not judge by it, then if you wish, go forward, and if you wish, hold back; and I see holding back as nothing but better for you. And peace be upon you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to prostrate, sleep, and breathe heavily, then get up and pray without performing ablution.
[Ibn ʿAbbās] said: I said to him, "You prayed without performing ablution, although you had slept." He said:
"Ablution is only required of one who sleeps lying on his side."
ʿUthmān and Hannād added:
"For when he lies on his side, his joints relax."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If one of you passes wind during prayer, let him leave, perform ablution, and repeat the prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: To al-Miqdād... and he mentioned something similar to this. He said: Al-Miqdād asked him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let him wash his private part and his testicles."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to al-Miqdād... and he mentioned its meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about what makes a full bath obligatory, and about the fluid that comes after the [first] fluid. He said:
"That is prostatic fluid (madhy), and every male discharges it. So wash your private part and your testicles because of it, and perform ablution as you do for prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: What is lawful for me with my wife while she is menstruating? He said:
"What is above the waist-wrapper is yours."
And he also mentioned eating with a menstruating woman, and related the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about what is lawful for a man with his wife while she is menstruating. He said:
"What is above the waist-wrapper, and refraining from that is better."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ gave a concession to a person in a state of major impurity, when he wanted to eat, drink, or sleep, to perform ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿĀʾishah: Tell me, did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bathe after sexual impurity at the beginning of the night or at its end? She said: Sometimes he bathed at the beginning of the night, and sometimes at its end.
I said: Allah is the Greatest! Praise be to Allah, who has made room in the matter.
I said: Tell me, did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray the Witr at the beginning of the night or at its end? She said: Sometimes he prayed Witr at the beginning of the night, and sometimes at its end.
I said: Allah is the Greatest! Praise be to Allah, who has made room in the matter.
I said: Tell me, did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite the Qurʾān aloud or quietly? She said: Sometimes he recited aloud, and sometimes quietly.
I said: Allah is the Greatest! Praise be to Allah, who has made room in the matter.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came while the doors of the houses of his Companions opened onto the mosque, and he said:
"Turn these houses away from the mosque."
Then the Prophet ﷺ went in, but the people did nothing, hoping that a concession would be revealed for them. Afterwards he came out to them and said:
"Turn these houses away from the mosque, for I do not make the mosque lawful for a menstruating woman or for one in a state of major impurity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered with my mother and my maternal aunt upon ʿĀʾishah, and one of them asked her: How did you act when bathing? ʿĀʾishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would perform ablution as for prayer, then pour water over his head three times, while we would pour water over our heads five times because of the braids.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to bathe after sexual impurity, he would begin by washing his hands, then wash his groins and pour water over himself. When he had cleaned them, he would rub his hands on a wall, then perform ablution fully and pour water over his head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: If you wish, I will show you the mark of the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the wall, where he used to bathe after sexual impurity.

segments_en: When Ibn ʿAbbās bathed after sexual impurity, he would pour with his right hand over his left hand seven times, then wash his private part. Once he forgot how many times he had poured, and asked me, "How many times did I pour?" I said, "I do not know."

He said, "May you have no mother! What prevents you from knowing?" Then he performed ablution as for prayer, then poured water over his skin, and said: This is how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to purify himself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Prayer was fifty [prayers], bathing after sexual impurity was seven times, and washing urine from a garment was seven times. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept asking until prayer was made five, bathing after sexual impurity once, and washing urine from a garment once.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of us was in a state of major impurity, she would take three handfuls like this, meaning with both palms, and pour them over her head. Then she would take [water] with one hand and pour it over this side, and with the other over the other side.

I call Allah to witness against you: the people of Khaybar steep a drink from such-and-such and call it such-and-such, and it is khamr; and the people of Fadak steep a drink from such-and-such and call it such-and-such, and it is khamr," until he had counted four drinks, one of which was honey.

And she forbade me from the gourd, the naqīr, the pitch-coated vessel, and the ḥantam.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays, when they came to him, from the gourd, the naqīr, the pitch-coated vessel, and the cut-off waterskin, and he said:
"Steep [your drink] in your waterskin, tie its mouth, and drink it while it is sweet."
Some of them said, "O Messenger of Allah, allow me [something] like this." He said:
"Then you would make it like this."
And he indicated with his hand, describing it.

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was traveling, he stopped by a people and heard noisy talk from them, and he said:
"What is this sound?"
They said, "O Prophet of Allah, they have a drink that they are drinking."
He sent for the people and called them, and said:
"In what do you steep [your drinks]?"
They said, "We steep in the naqīr and gourds, and we have no [other] containers." He said:
"Do not drink except from what you have tied shut."
He said: He stayed so for as long as Allah willed, then he returned to them, and they had been struck by illness and had turned yellow. He said:
"Why do I see that you have been ruined?"
They said, "O Prophet of Allah, our land is plague-ridden, and [containers] were forbidden to us except those we tie shut." He said:
"Drink, but every intoxicant is forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: (may Allah be pleased with him) that he used to say, "I do not care whether I drank khamr or worshipped this pillar instead of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
