When the woman saw that he had not decided anything about her, she sat down. Then a man from among his Companions stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, if you have no need of her, then marry her to me." He said,
"Do you have anything?"
He said, "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"Go to your family and see whether you can find anything."
So he went, then returned and said, "No, by Allah, I did not find anything."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Look, even if it is an iron ring."
So he went, then returned.
He said, "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, not even an iron ring.
But this is my waist-wrapper"—Sahl said: he had no cloak—"and she may have half of it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"What will you do with your waist-wrapper? If you wear it, none of it will be on her, and if she wears it, none of it will be on you."
So the man sat down, and when he had sat for a long time he got up. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him walking away and ordered that he be called. When he came, he said,
"How much of the Qur'an do you know?"
He said, "I know such-and-such a sūrah and such-and-such a sūrah," and he counted them. He said,
"Can you recite them from memory?" He said, "Yes." He said,
"Go, for I have given her to you in marriage for what you know of the Qur'an."
This is the narration of Ibn Abī Ḥāzim, and the narration of Yaʿqūb is close to it in wording.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Saʿīd ibn Jubayr about a man who performs Hajj and stipulates a condition.

He said, "The stipulation is [a matter] among people." So I told him the narration of ʿIkrimah, and he related to me from Ibn ʿAbbās that Ḍubāʿah bint al-Zubayr ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I want to perform Hajj, so what should I say?" He said,
"Say: Labbayk, Allāhumma labbayk (Here I am, O Allah, here I am), and my place of release is wherever You detain me, for you will have with your Lord what you stipulated."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman is married for four reasons: for her wealth, her lineage, her beauty, and her religion.
So seek the one who is religious, may your hands be rubbed with dust."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
—and the wording is Muḥammad's—from Ibn al-Qāsim, from Mālik,
from Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl,
from Anas ibn Mālik,
that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf
came to the Prophet ﷺ with a trace of yellow [perfume] on him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him, and he told him that he had married a woman from the Anṣār. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"How much did you give her as dowry?"
He said, "The weight of a date-stone in gold."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Hold a wedding feast, even if with a single sheep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar. He said: I said, "A man divorced his wife while she was menstruating."
He said, "Do you know ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar?" I said, "Yes."
He said, "ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar divorced his wife while she was menstruating.
So ʿUmar came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him, and he said,
"Order him to take her back, then let him divorce her at the beginning of her waiting period."
I said, "Is that counted as a divorce?" He said, "What else? Do you think that if he were incapable and acted foolishly [it would not count]?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a Jewish man attacked a girl,
took the silver ornaments she was wearing and crushed her head.
Her family brought her to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while she was at her last breath and had lost the ability to speak.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her,
"Who struck you? So-and-so?"
[He named someone] other than the one who had struck her,
and she gestured with her head, meaning no.
He said: Then he named another man, other than the one who had struck her,
and she gestured no. Then he said, "Then so-and-so?"
[naming] the one who had struck her, and she gestured yes.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that his head be crushed between two stones.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Quraysh sent me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Islam was cast into my heart. So I said, "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I will never return to them." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I do not break a covenant, and I do not detain envoys. But return; and if what is in your heart now is what is in your heart, then return."
He said: So I went back, then I came to the Prophet ﷺ and accepted Islam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said] to the two of them when he read the letter of Musaylimah:
"What do the two of you say?"
They said, "We say as he said." He said:
"By Allah, were it not that envoys are not killed, I would have struck off your necks."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to ʿAbdullāh and said, "I have no grudge against anyone among the Arabs, but I passed by a mosque of Banū Ḥanīfah, and they were affirming belief in Musaylimah."
So ʿAbdullāh sent for them and they were brought, and he asked them to repent, except Ibn al-Nawwāḥah, to whom he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Were it not that you are an envoy, I would have struck off your neck."

"But today you are not an envoy." So he ordered Qaraẓah ibn Kaʿb, and his neck was struck in the marketplace. Then he said, "Whoever wishes to see Ibn al-Nawwāḥah killed, [let him look] in the marketplace."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She gave protection to a man from among the polytheists on the day of the conquest [of Makkah]. Then she came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him about that, and he said:
"We have given protection to whomever you have protected, and we have granted safety to whomever you have granted safety."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman could give protection on behalf of the believers, and it was permitted.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That

when the sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he performed ablution and gave an order, and it was announced that the prayer was being gathered for. He stood and made his standing in prayer long.
ʿĀʾishah said: I estimated that he recited Sūrat al-Baqarah. Then he bowed and made the bowing long. Then he said:
"Allah hears the one who praises Him."

Then he stood as long as he had stood before, and he did not prostrate. Then he bowed and then prostrated. Then he stood and did the same as he had done: two bowings and one prostration. Then he sat, and the sun cleared.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood for prayer, and those with him stood. He stood for a long time. Then he bowed and made the bowing long. Then he raised his head and prostrated and made the prostration long. Then he raised his head and sat and made the sitting long. Then he prostrated and made the prostration long. Then he raised his head and stood, and in the second rakʿah he did the same as he had done in the first rakʿah of standing, bowing, prostrating and sitting. At the end of his prostration in the second rakʿah he began to blow, and he wept and said:
"Did You not promise me this while I am among them? Did You not promise me this while we are seeking Your forgiveness?"
Then he raised his head, and the sun cleared. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and addressed the people. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said:

"The sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So when you see an eclipse of either of them, hasten to the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, Paradise was brought near to me until, had I stretched out my hand, I could have taken some of its clusters. And the Fire was brought near to me until I began to shield myself from it, fearing that it would envelop you. I even saw in it a woman of Ḥimyar being punished on account of a cat that she had tied up; she neither let it eat from the creatures of the earth, nor did she feed it or give it water, until it died. I saw it clawing at her when she came forward, and when she turned away it clawed at her rear. I also saw in it the man with the two cloaks, the brother of Banū ad-Daʿdāʿ, pushing himself along in the Fire with a two-pronged staff. And I saw in it the owner of the curved staff, who used to steal from the pilgrims with his curved staff, leaning on his staff in the Fire and saying: 'I am the thief of the curved staff.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed when the sun was eclipsed like our prayer, bowing and prostrating.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed two rakʿahs like this prayer of yours, and he mentioned the eclipse of the sun.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he asked az-Zuhrī about the Sunnah
of the eclipse prayer. He said: ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr informed me, from ʿĀʾishah,

who said: The sun was eclipsed, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded a man, who called out that the prayer was being gathered for. The people gathered, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led them in prayer. He said the takbīr, then recited at length. Then he said the takbīr and bowed for a long time, as long as his standing or longer. Then he raised his head and said:
"Allah hears the one who praises Him."
Then he recited at length, though less than the first recitation. Then he said the takbīr and bowed for a long time, though less than the first bowing. Then he raised his head and said:
"Allah hears the one who praises Him."

Then he said the takbīr and prostrated for a long time, as long as his bowing or longer. Then he said the takbīr and raised his head, then said the takbīr and prostrated. Then he said the takbīr and stood and recited at length, less than the first. Then he said the takbīr and bowed for a long time, less than the first bowing. Then he raised his head and said:
"Allah hears the one who praises Him."

Then he recited at length, less than the first recitation in the second standing. Then he said the takbīr and bowed for a long time, shorter than the first bowing. Then he said the takbīr and raised his head and said:
"Allah hears the one who praises Him."
Then he said the takbīr and prostrated, less than his first prostration. Then he recited the tashahhud, then gave the salām. Then he stood before them, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said:

"Indeed the sun and the moon are not eclipsed for the death of anyone nor for his life, but they are two signs among the signs of Allah. So whichever of them is eclipsed, or if either is, then turn in fear to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with the remembrance of prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed during the eclipse. He stood and made the standing long. Then he bowed and made the bowing long. Then he rose and made the standing long. Then he bowed and made the bowing long. Then he rose. Then he prostrated and made the prostration long. Then he rose. Then he prostrated and made the prostration long. Then he stood and made the standing long. Then he bowed and made the bowing long. Then he rose and made the standing long. Then he bowed and made the bowing long. Then he rose. Then he prostrated and made the prostration long. Then he rose. Then he prostrated and made the prostration long. Then he rose and then finished.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

from among the Muslims saw in a dream that he met a man from the People of the Book, who said: "What excellent people you would be, were it not that you commit shirk, saying: 'What Allah wills and Muhammad wills.'"
He mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "
By Allah, I have indeed been aware of this about you. Say: 'What Allah wills, and then what Muhammad wills.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I made a vow during the Jāhiliyyah, and after I became Muslim I asked the Prophet ﷺ about it, and he commanded me to fulfil my vow.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have vowed to sacrifice a camel at Buwānah." He said: "
Is there anything of the matter of the Jāhiliyyah in your mind?" He said: "No." He said: "Fulfil your vow."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Her father
met the Prophet ﷺ while she was riding behind him, and said: "I have vowed to sacrifice a camel at Buwānah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Is there an idol there?" He said: "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "My mother has died owing a vow of fasting; she died before she could fulfil it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Let her guardian fast on her behalf."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man has not earned any earning better than the work of his own hand, and whatever a man spends on himself, his family, his child, and his servant is charity (ṣadaqah)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The trustworthy, truthful, Muslim merchant will be with the martyrs on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting in a gathering when the Prophet ﷺ came with traces of water on his head. One of us said to him: "We see you in good spirits today." He said: "
Yes, and praise be to Allah."
Then the people began to speak about wealth, and he said: "
There is nothing wrong with wealth for the one who fears Allah, but good health is better than wealth for the one who fears Allah, and good spirits are among the blessings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Be moderate in seeking worldly gain, for everyone is made ready for that for which he was created."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The people with the greatest concern are the believers who are concerned about the affairs of their worldly life and the affairs of their Hereafter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

O people, fear Allah and be moderate in seeking [provision], for no soul will die until it has received its provision in full, even if it is slow in coming to it. So fear Allah and be moderate in seeking: take what is lawful and leave what is forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Whoever attains something [of provision], let him stick to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to prepare goods for Syria and Egypt, then I prepared goods for Iraq. So I went to ʿĀʾishah, Mother of the Believers, and said to her: "O Mother of the Believers, I used to prepare goods for Syria, then I prepared goods for Iraq."
She said: "Do not do that. What is the matter with you and your trade route? For I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
When Allah makes a means of provision available to one of you through a certain way, he should not abandon it until it changes for him or turns against him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Zakariyyā was a carpenter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The most untruthful of people are the dyers and the goldsmiths."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The one who brings goods to market is provided for, and the hoarder is cursed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever hoards the food of the Muslims, Allah will strike him with leprosy and bankruptcy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I taught a man the Qur'an and he gave me a bow as a gift. I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "
If you take it, you are taking a bow of fire." So I returned it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had himself cupped and he paid the cupper his wage.
Ibn Mājah said: Ibn Abī ʿUmar alone narrated this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade selling singing girls, buying them, their earnings, and consuming their price.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade najsh [bidding up the price without intending to buy].
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Do not engage in najsh [bidding up prices deceptively]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bought a load of khabṭ [leaves] from a man of the desert Arabs. When the sale was concluded, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Choose."
The Bedouin said: "May Allah grant you long life as a seller!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah: Did you hear al-Zuhrī
relate from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī,
from Abū Ayyūb,
that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"When you go to relieve yourselves, do not face the qiblah and do not turn your backs to it for urine or stool, but face east or west."
Abū Ayyūb said: Then we came to Syria and found latrines that had been built facing the qiblah, so we would turn away from it and seek Allah's forgiveness. He said: Yes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led the prayer. Ibrāhīm said: I do not know whether he added or reduced. When he had given the salām, it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, has something new occurred in the prayer?" He said: "What is that?"
They said: You prayed such and such.
So he folded his leg, faced the qiblah, and performed two prostrations with them, then gave the salām. When he turned away, he turned his face to us ﷺ and said:
"Had something new occurred in the prayer, I would have informed you of it. But I am only a human being; I forget as you forget. So when I forget, remind me." And he said:
"When one of you is in doubt about his prayer, let him seek what is correct and complete his prayer accordingly, then give the salām, then perform two prostrations."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw spittle on the wall of the qiblah and scraped it off. Then he turned to the people and said:
"When one of you is praying, he should not spit in front of him, for Allah is in front of him when he prays."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw phlegm on the qiblah wall of the mosque and scraped it off with a pebble.
Then he forbade a man to spit in front of him or to his right,
but rather to his left or under his left foot.
And from al-Zuhrī, who heard Ḥumayd, from Abū Saʿīd, something similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah,
he stayed in the upper part of Madinah among a tribe called Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf. He said: He stayed among them for fourteen nights,
then he sent for the chiefs of Banū al-Najjār. He said: They came with their swords slung on.
He said: It is as though I can see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on his riding camel,
with Abū Bakr riding behind him,
and the chiefs of Banū al-Najjār around him, until he dismounted in the courtyard of Abū Ayyūb.
He said: He would pray wherever the prayer found him,
and he would pray in sheepfolds.
He said: Then he ordered the building of the mosque,
so he sent for the chiefs of Banū al-Najjār, and they came. He said:
"O Banū al-Najjār,
name me a price for this garden of yours." They said: No,
by Allah, we do not seek its price except from Allah.
He said: There was in it what I tell you: there were graves of the polytheists,
there were ruins,
and there were date palms.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that the graves of the polytheists be dug up, the ruins be leveled, and the palm trees be cut down.
He said: They lined up the palm trunks as the qiblah of the mosque. He said: And they made the doorposts of stone.
He said: They began carrying those stones while reciting rajaz verses,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with them, as they said: O Allah, there is no good except the good of the Hereafter, so help the Ansār and the Muhājirah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"May Allah curse the Jews and the Christians: they took the graves of their prophets as places of worship."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of people

came to Sahl ibn Saʿd, having disputed about the pulpit, from what wood it was made. He said: By Allah, I know exactly from what wood it was made and who made it, and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the first day he sat on it. He said: I said to him: O Abū ʿAbbās, then tell us.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent word to a woman. Abū Ḥāzim said: He did name her at that time. [He said:]
"Look to your carpenter slave to make me some wooden steps on which I can address the people."
So he made these three steps, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that they be placed in this spot. It is from tamarisk wood of the forest.

And I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stand on it and say the takbīr, and the people said the takbīr behind him while he was on the pulpit. Then he raised his head and went down backwards until he prostrated at the base of the pulpit, then went back up until he finished his prayer. Then he turned to the people and said:
"O people, I did this so that you would follow me and learn my prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) used to combine the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers at Jamʿ [Muzdalifah],
except that he would pass by the mountain path that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had taken, and he would enter it, relieve himself, and perform ablution,
and he would not pray until he prayed at Jamʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He set off with the Prophet ﷺ on the day of ʿArafah, and the Prophet ﷺ heard behind him a loud shouting, striking, and the sound of camels. So he gestured to them with his whip and said:
"O people, [keep to] calmness,
for righteousness does not lie in hurrying." ʿAwḍaʿū means: they hurried.
Khilālakum is from takhallul, meaning 'among you'; and "We caused rivers to gush forth within them (khilālahumā)" means: between the two.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh (may Allah be pleased with him) performed Hajj, and we came to Muzdalifah at the time of the call to the ʿIshāʾ prayer,
or close to that time.
He ordered a man, who gave the adhān and the iqāmah,
then he prayed Maghrib,
and prayed two rakʿahs after it,
then he called for his supper and ate,
then he ordered a man (I think) who gave the adhān and the iqāmah (ʿAmr said: I do not know the doubt to be from anyone but Zuhayr), then he prayed ʿIshāʾ, two rakʿahs.
When dawn broke, he said: The Prophet ﷺ did not pray at this hour except this prayer,
in this place,
on this day.
ʿAbdullāh said: These are two prayers that were shifted from their [usual] times: the Maghrib prayer, after the people arrive at Muzdalifah,
and the Fajr prayer, when dawn breaks.
He said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ do it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with ʿAbdullāh (may Allah be pleased with him) to Mecca,
then we came to Jamʿ, and he prayed the two prayers,
each prayer by itself with an adhān and an iqāmah, with supper between them,
then he prayed Fajr as soon as dawn broke,
with one saying, "Dawn has broken,"
and another saying, "Dawn has not broken."
Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"These two prayers were shifted from their time in this place: Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ.
So the people should not arrive at Jamʿ until it is dark,
and the Fajr prayer is [prayed] at this hour."
Then he stood [there] until it grew bright,
then he said: If the Commander of the Faithful were to depart now, he would have followed the Sunnah.
I do not know whether his statement was faster or the departure of ʿUthmān (may Allah be pleased with him). He kept reciting the talbiyah until he threw the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah on the Day of Sacrifice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ offered a hundred camels as sacrificial animals,
and he ordered me to [distribute] their meat, so I distributed it,
then he ordered me [to distribute] their covers, so I distributed them,
then their hides, so I distributed them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh (may Allah be pleased with him) used to slaughter at the place of slaughter.
ʿUbaydullāh said: The place of slaughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) used to send his sacrificial animals from Jamʿ in the last part of the night,
until they entered the place of slaughter of the Prophet ﷺ with pilgrims among whom were free people and slaves.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāfiʿ: Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ shaved his head during his Hajj.
label: machine translation

label: machine translation

then he slept for a short while at al-Muḥaṣṣab,
then he rode to the House and circumambulated it.

segments_en: The people of Medina
asked Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) about a woman
who had performed the circumambulation and then got her menstrual period.
He said to them: She may depart.
They said: We will not accept your statement and leave the statement of Zayd.
He said: When you reach Medina, ask.
So they reached Medina and asked,
and among those they asked was Umm Sulaym,
and she mentioned the hadith of Ṣafiyyah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbaydullāh was asked about al-Muḥaṣṣab,
so ʿUbaydullāh narrated to us from Nāfiʿ:
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ʿUmar, and Ibn ʿUmar stayed there.
And from Nāfiʿ: Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) used to pray there, meaning al-Muḥaṣṣab, Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, and I think he said also Maghrib.
Khālid said: I have no doubt about ʿIshāʾ. And he would sleep for a short while,
and he would relate that from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Shaʿbī of Hamdān: he asked Fāṭimah bint Qays, the sister of al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays, who was one of the earliest emigrant women, "Narrate to me a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and do not attribute it to anyone other than him." She said, "If you wish, I will do so." He said to her, "Yes, narrate to me."

She said: I married Ibn al-Mughīrah, who was one of the best of the young men of Quraysh at that time, and he was struck down in the first of the jihad with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When I became a widow, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf proposed to me among a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed me for his freed slave Usāmah ibn Zayd. I had been told that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said:
"Whoever loves me, let him love Usāmah."
So when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke to me, I said, "My affair is in your hands, so marry me to whomever you wish." He said:
"Move to Umm Sharīk."
Umm Sharīk was a wealthy woman from the Anṣār who spent greatly in the cause of Allah, and guests would stay with her. I said, "I will do so." He said:

"Do not do so. Umm Sharīk is a woman who has many guests, and I dislike that your head covering might fall off you or the garment might uncover your shins, and the people would see of you something you dislike. Rather, move to your cousin ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Umm Maktūm."

— he was a man from Banū Fihr, Fihr of Quraysh, from the same clan as hers — so I moved to him. When my waiting period ended, I heard the call of the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ announcing, "The prayer is being gathered."

So I went out to the mosque and prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I was in the row of the women that was nearest the backs of the men. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer, he sat on the minbar, smiling, and said:
"Let every person remain in his place of prayer." Then he said:
"Do you know why I gathered you?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:

"By Allah, I have not gathered you out of desire or out of fear, but I gathered you because Tamīm al-Dārī was a Christian man; he came, pledged allegiance, and accepted Islam, and he told me a story that agreed with what I used to tell you about the Antichrist, the Messiah. He told me that he sailed in a sea vessel with thirty men from Lakhm and Judhām, and the waves played with them for a month in the sea. Then they were brought to shore at an island in the sea at sunset, and they sat in the small boats of the ship and entered the island. There a beast met them, thick-haired, so covered in hair that they could not tell its front from its back because of the abundance of hair. They said, 'Woe to you, what are you?' It said, 'I am the Jassāsah.'
They said, 'And what is the Jassāsah?' It said, 'O people, go to this man in the monastery, for he is eager to hear news of you.'

He said: When it named a man for us, we feared it might be a female devil. He said: So we went quickly until we entered the monastery, and in it was the largest human being we had ever seen in build and the most tightly bound, his hands fastened to his neck, and between his knees and his ankles were iron shackles. We said, 'Woe to you, what are you?' He said, 'You have been able to learn of my news, so tell me, who are you?' They said, 'We are people from the Arabs. We sailed in a sea vessel and found the sea when it was raging, and the waves played with us for a month, then brought us to this island of yours. We sat in its small boats and entered the island, and a beast met us, thick-haired, so covered in hair that it could not be told its front from its back. We said, "Woe to you, what are you?" It said, "I am the Jassāsah."

We said, "And what is the Jassāsah?" It said, "Make for this man in the monastery, for he is eager to hear news of you." So we came to you quickly, frightened of it, and we were not sure it was not a female devil.' He said, 'Tell me about the date palms of Baysān.' We said, 'About what aspect of them do you ask?' He said, 'I ask you about its palms: do they bear fruit?' We said to him, 'Yes.'
He said, 'Soon they will not bear fruit.' He said, 'Tell me about the Lake of Tiberias.'
We said, 'About what aspect of it do you ask?' He said, 'Is there water in it?' They said, 'It has abundant water.'
He said, 'Soon its water will go away.'
He said, 'Tell me about the spring of Zughar.'

They said, 'About what aspect of it do you ask?' He said, 'Is there water in the spring, and do its people irrigate their farmland with the water of the spring?' We said to him, 'Yes, it has abundant water, and its people farm with its water.'
He said, 'Tell me about the Prophet of the unlettered people, what has he done?' They said, 'He has left Makkah and settled in Yathrib.'
He said, 'Do the Arabs fight him?' We said, 'Yes.'
He said, 'How did he deal with them?' So we told him that he had prevailed over those of the Arabs near him and they had obeyed him. He said to them, 'Has that happened?' We said, 'Yes.'

He said, 'It is better for them that they obey him. And I will tell you about myself: I am the Messiah, and I am about to be given permission to emerge, so I will go out and travel through the land, and I will not leave a single town without descending upon it within forty nights, except Makkah and Ṭaybah, for both are forbidden to me. Every time I wish to enter one of the two, an angel meets me with a drawn sword in his hand, turning me away from it, and at every pass leading to it are angels guarding it.'" She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, striking the minbar with his staff:
"This is Ṭaybah, this is Ṭaybah, this is Ṭaybah" — meaning Madīnah. "
Did I not tell you that?"
The people said, "Yes." "

I was pleased with the account of Tamīm, that it agreed with what I used to tell you about him, and about Madīnah and Makkah. But he is in the Sea of Shām or the Sea of Yemen — no, rather from the direction of the east; he is from the direction of the east; he is from the direction of the east."
And he gestured with his hand toward the east.
She said: So I memorized this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mukram al-ʿAmmī and Abū Bakr ibn Nāfiʿ — ʿUqbah said: Ghundar narrated to us; and Abū Bakr said: Ghundar informed us — Shuʿbah narrated to us,
He said: I heard Khālid
narrating from Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan, from his mother,
from Umm Salamah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAmmār:
"You will be killed by the rebellious group."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with a group of men, toward Ibn Ṣayyād, until they found him playing with the boys by the fortress of Banū Maghālah. Ibn Ṣayyād was close to puberty at that time. He did not notice until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck his back with his hand. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Ibn Ṣayyād:
"Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of Allah?"
Ibn Ṣayyād looked at him and said: I bear witness that you are the messenger of the unlettered people.
Then Ibn Ṣayyād said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Do you bear witness that I am the messenger of Allah? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rejected that and said:
"I believe in Allah and in His messengers."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "What do you see?"
Ibn Ṣayyād said: A truthful one and a liar come to me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"The matter has been confused for you."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"I have concealed something in my mind for you."
Ibn Ṣayyād said: "It is the dukh."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Be gone! You will never go beyond your limit."
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: Let me strike his neck, O Messenger of Allah.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"If he is the one, you will not be given power over him; and if he is not, there is no good for you in killing him."
Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar

say: After that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb al-Anṣārī set out to the palm grove where Ibn Ṣayyād was. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the palm grove, he began to take cover behind the trunks of the palm trees, trying to stealthily hear something from Ibn Ṣayyād before Ibn Ṣayyād could see him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him lying on a bed, wrapped in a velvet cloth of his, murmuring. Ibn Ṣayyād's mother saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as he was taking cover behind the palm trunks, and she said to Ibn Ṣayyād: O Ṣāf — which was Ibn Ṣayyād's name — here is Muḥammad!
So Ibn Ṣayyād jumped up.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If she had left him alone, he would have made things clear."
Sālim said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among the people, praised Allah as He deserves, then mentioned the Dajjāl and said:

"I warn you about him. There was no prophet but that his people were warned of him. Nūḥ warned his people. But I will tell you something about him that no prophet told his people: know that he is one-eyed, and that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is not one-eyed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Matters will only grow harder, the world will only turn away, people will only grow more miserly, and the Hour will only come upon the worst of people. And there is no Mahdī except ʿĪsā, son of Maryam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed through the market, entering from some part of the upper area of Madinah, with people on both sides of him. He passed by a dead kid with small ears, took hold of it by the ear, and then said:
"Which of you would like to have this for a dirham?"
They said: We would not like to have it for anything. What would we do with it? He said:
"Would you like to have it?"
They said: By Allah, even if it were alive it would be defective, because its ears are tiny; how much more so when it is dead! Then he said:
"By Allah, the world is more insignificant to Allah than this is to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was asleep, wearing a white garment. Then I came to him again and he was still asleep. Then I came to him once more, and he had woken up, so I sat with him. He said:
"There is no servant who says, 'There is no god but Allah,' and then dies upon that, except that he enters Paradise."
I said, "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said:
"Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals."
I said, "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said:
"Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals."
[He said this] three times, then on the fourth he said:
"Despite the nose of Abū Dharr [being rubbed in the dust]."
He said: Abū Dharr went out saying, "Even if it is against the will of Abū Dharr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar's letter came to us while we were in Azerbaijan with ʿUtbah ibn Farqad, or in Syria: "To proceed: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade silk, except for this much," [indicating] two fingers.
Abū ʿUthmān said: We did not doubt that he meant the decorative borders.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was of medium height,
and I saw him in a red garment; I have never seen anything more beautiful than him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Umm Salamah.
He said: She brought out to me some hair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, dyed with henna and katam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"One night I was shown myself at the Kaʿbah, and I saw a man of brown complexion, as handsome as the best you could see among brown-complexioned men. He had hair reaching his earlobes, as beautiful as the best you could see of such hair, combed, and dripping water, leaning on two men—or on the shoulders of two men—circling the House. I asked, 'Who is this?' It was said, 'This is the Messiah, son of Mary.'
Then I saw a man with very curly hair, blind in the right eye, as if it were a floating grape. I asked, 'Who is this?' It was said, 'This is the Messiah, the Antichrist (ad-Dajjāl).'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah has cursed women who tattoo and women who have themselves tattooed,
women who pluck their eyebrows, and women who file their teeth for beauty,
those who change the creation of Allah, the Exalted.
Why should I not curse those whom the Prophet ﷺ cursed, when it is in the Book of Allah: {Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it}?
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman who had tattooed was brought to ʿUmar. He stood up and said, "I ask you by Allah, who heard anything from the Prophet ﷺ about tattooing?" Abū Hurayrah said: I stood up and said, "O Commander of the Faithful, I heard [it]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would not leave anything in his house bearing crosses without breaking it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from a journey, and I had hung over my door a curtain of soft fabric with images of winged horses. He ordered me, so I took it down.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, who is most deserving of my good companionship?" He said, "Your mother."
He said, "Then who?" He said, "Your mother."
He said, "Then who?" He said, "Your mother."
He said, "Then who?" He said, "Then your father."
Ibn Shubrumah and Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb said: Abū Zurʿah narrated to us the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah said: I am the Most Merciful (ar-Raḥmān), and this is the womb (ar-raḥim). I have derived for it a name from My name. Whoever maintains it, I will maintain him, and whoever severs it, I will sever him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some captives were brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and among them was a woman who, whenever she found a child among the captives, would take him, press him to her belly, and nurse him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:
"Do you think this woman would throw her child into the Fire?"
We said, "No, by Allah, not if she is able not to throw him."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah made mercy one hundred parts,
and He kept ninety-nine parts with Him,
and sent down one part to the earth.
It is from that one part that creatures show mercy to one another,
so much so that a horse lifts its hoof away from its foal for fear of harming it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The likeness of the believers in their mutual love, mercy, and compassion is that of a body: when one part of it complains, the rest of the body responds with sleeplessness and fever."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some Jews
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "as-Sāmu ʿalayka (death be upon you)." He said, "And upon you."
ʿĀʾishah said, "Death be upon you,
and may Allah curse you and be angry with you."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Gently, O ʿĀʾishah! Hold to gentleness,
and beware of harshness and coarse speech."
She said, "Did you not hear what they said?" He said:
"Did you not hear what I said? I returned it to them,
and my prayer against them is answered,
but their prayer against me is not answered."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that a bell be made to be struck to gather the people for prayer, a man carrying a bell in his hand passed by me while I was asleep. I said, "Servant of Allah, will you sell the bell?" He said, "What will you do with it?" I said, "We will call to prayer with it."
He said, "Shall I not guide you to something better than that?" I said to him, "Yes."

He said, "Say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh; ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh, ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh; ḥayya ʿala aṣ-ṣalāh, ḥayya ʿala aṣ-ṣalāh; ḥayya ʿala al-falāḥ, ḥayya ʿala al-falāḥ; Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; lā ilāha illā Allāh." Then he moved back from me, not far, and said, "And when you begin the iqāmah of the prayer, say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh; ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh; ḥayya ʿala aṣ-ṣalāh; ḥayya ʿala al-falāḥ; qad qāmat aṣ-ṣalāh, qad qāmat aṣ-ṣalāh; Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; lā ilāha illā Allāh." When morning came, I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him what I had seen. He said:
"It is a true vision, Allah willing. Get up with Bilāl and relate to him what you saw, so that he may call the adhān with it, for his voice is more far-reaching than yours."

So I got up with Bilāl and began to relate it to him while he called the adhān with it. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb heard that while he was in his house, and he went out dragging his cloak and saying, "By the One who sent you with the truth, Messenger of Allah, I saw the same as what he saw."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "So to Allah belongs all praise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught him the adhān as nineteen phrases and the iqāmah as seventeen phrases. The adhān:

"Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh; ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh, ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh; ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh; ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh, ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh; ḥayya ʿala aṣ-ṣalāh, ḥayya ʿala aṣ-ṣalāh; ḥayya ʿala al-falāḥ, ḥayya ʿala al-falāḥ; Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; lā ilāha illā Allāh." And the iqāmah: "Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh; ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh, ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh; ḥayya ʿala aṣ-ṣalāh, ḥayya ʿala aṣ-ṣalāh; ḥayya ʿala al-falāḥ, ḥayya ʿala al-falāḥ; qad qāmat aṣ-ṣalāh, qad qāmat aṣ-ṣalāh; Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; lā ilāha illā Allāh."
So it is in his book, in the hadith of Abū Maḥdhūrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The muʾadhdhin of the mosque of al-ʿUryān, from Abū al-Muthannā,
the muʾadhdhin of the Jāmiʿ Mosque, who said: I asked Ibn ʿUmar about the adhān,

and he said: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the adhān was in pairs and the iqāmah was once each, except that when you said "qad qāmat aṣ-ṣalāh," you said it twice. When we heard "qad qāmat aṣ-ṣalāh," we performed ablution and then went out to prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The imam is a guarantor and the muʾadhdhin is entrusted. O Allah, guide the imams and forgive the muʾadhdhins."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me; he said:
"Say: O Allah, this is the coming of Your night, the departing of Your day, the voices of those who call to You, and the presence of Your prayers; I ask You to forgive me."
He said: This hadith is gharīb; we know it only through this route.
And Ḥafṣah bint Abī Kathīr, we do not know her or her father.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: Mūsā said elsewhere that ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ said, "Messenger of Allah, make me the imam of my people." He said:
"You are their imam. Follow the weakest of them, and appoint a muʾadhdhin who does not take payment for his adhān."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked the Prophet ﷺ and said, "Messenger of Allah, I am a man who is blind, my house is far away, and I have a guide who is not suitable for me. Is there a concession for me to pray in my house?" He said:
"Do you hear the call?" He said, "Yes." He said:
"I find no concession for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Messenger of Allah, Madinah has many vermin and wild beasts." He said:
"Do you hear 'Come to prayer, come to success'?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Then come!"
And he did not grant him a concession.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Which is better: prayer in my house or prayer in the mosque?" He said:
"Do you not see how close my house is to the mosque? Even so, that I pray in my house is more beloved to me than that I pray in the mosque, except for an obligatory prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When it is the night of the middle of Shaʿbān, stand in prayer during its night and fast during its day.

For at sunset on that night Allah descends to the lowest heaven and says: 'Is there anyone seeking forgiveness, that I may forgive him? Is there anyone seeking provision, that I may provide for him? Is there anyone afflicted, that I may grant him well-being? Is there anyone such-and-such? Is there anyone such-and-such?' [This continues] until the dawn rises."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, Allah looks upon [His creation] on the night of the middle of Shaʿbān and forgives all of His creation, except for a polytheist or one who harbors hatred [toward his brother]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, on the day he was given the good news of the head of Abū Jahl, prayed two rakʿahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Allah accepted his repentance, he fell down in prostration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Your Prophet ﷺ was commanded with fifty prayers, and he kept petitioning your Lord until He made them five prayers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A freed woman of the Prophet ﷺ said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, give us a ruling about Bayt al-Maqdis.' He said:
'It is the land of the gathering and the resurrection. Go to it and pray in it, for one prayer in it is like a thousand prayers elsewhere.'
I said: 'What if I am unable to travel to it?' He said:
'Then send it oil to be burned in its lamps. Whoever does that is like one who has come to it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A man's prayer in his house is [worth] one prayer; his prayer in the mosque of the tribes is [worth] twenty-five prayers; his prayer in the mosque where the congregation gathers [for Friday prayer] is [worth] five hundred prayers; a prayer in al-Aqṣā Mosque is [worth] fifty thousand prayers; a prayer in my mosque is [worth] fifty thousand prayers; and a prayer in the Sacred Mosque is [worth] one hundred thousand prayers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray facing a palm trunk when the mosque was [only] a shelter of branches, and he used to deliver the sermon beside that trunk. A man among his Companions said: "Would you like us to make something for you to stand on on Friday, so that the people can see you and hear your sermon?" He said: "Yes."

So he made for him three steps, which are those of the pulpit. When the pulpit was made, they placed it in the place where it stands. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to go to the pulpit, he passed by the trunk he used to deliver the sermon beside. When he passed the trunk, it cried out until it split and cracked. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came down when he heard the sound of the trunk and stroked it with his hand until it became quiet. Then he returned to the pulpit. When he prayed, he would pray facing it. When the mosque was demolished and altered, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb took that trunk and kept it in his house until it decayed, was eaten by termites, and turned to dust.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no servant who prostrates to Allah in a single prostration except that Allah records for him one good deed because of it, erases from him one sin because of it, and raises him one degree because of it. So perform many prostrations."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Keep your sandals on your feet.
If you take them off, place them between your feet.
Do not place them on your right,
nor on the right of your companion, nor behind you,
for you would harm the one behind you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Muslim has four duties toward a Muslim: to say 'May Allah have mercy on you' when he sneezes, to answer him when he calls him, to attend his funeral when he dies, and to visit him when he is ill."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abū Bakr visited me on foot while I was among Banū Salimah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would not visit a sick person until after three days.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ visited a man and said to him: "What do you desire?"
He said: "I desire wheat bread." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever has wheat bread should send it to his brother."
Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"When one of your sick desires something, let him be fed it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered upon a sick person to visit him and said:
"Do you desire anything? Do you desire cake?" He said: "Yes." So they sought it for him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to me:
"When you enter upon a sick person, ask him to pray for you, for his supplication is like the supplication of the angels."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and my name was not ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named me ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām.

segments_en: Saʿdā al-Murriyyah said: ʿUmar passed by Ṭalḥah after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Why do you look so gloomy? Did the rule of your cousin displease you?" He said: "No, but I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'I know a statement that no one says at the time of his death except that it will be a light for his record, and his body and soul will find relief in it at death.'
I did not ask him about it until he died."
[ʿUmar] said: "I know it. It is the one that he wanted his uncle to say; and had he known of anything that would save him more, he would have commanded him with it."

"There is no reserving of arāk trees."
He said, "[But] there is an arāk tree within my enclosures." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "
"There is no reserving of arāk trees."
Faraj said: By "my enclosures" he meant the land containing crops that is fenced in.

segments_en: Ṣakhr [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ campaigned against Thaqīf. When Ṣakhr heard of that, he rode out with cavalry to reinforce the Prophet ﷺ, but he found that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ had already withdrawn without conquering [it]. So Ṣakhr that day made a covenant with Allah and pledged under His protection that he would not leave that fortress until they surrendered to the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He did not leave them until they surrendered to the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then Ṣakhr wrote to him: "To proceed: Thaqīf has surrendered to your judgment, O Messenger of Allah, and I am on my way to them, with cavalry."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the call for the congregational prayer, and he made ten supplications for Aḥmas: "
"O Allah, bless Aḥmas in its cavalry and its men."

The people came to him, and al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah spoke and said: "O Prophet of Allah, Ṣakhr has taken my paternal aunt, [though] she had entered into what the Muslims have entered." So he summoned him and said: "
"O Ṣakhr, when a people accept Islam they secure their lives and their property. So hand over his aunt to al-Mughīrah."
So he handed her over to him. Then he asked the Prophet of Allah ﷺ for a water source belonging to Banū Sulaym, who had fled from Islam and abandoned that water.
He said: "O Prophet of Allah, settle me and my people there." He said: "Yes."

So he settled him there, and [then] they—meaning the Sulamīs—accepted Islam. They came to Ṣakhr and asked him to hand the water over to them, but he refused. So they came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Prophet of Allah, we have accepted Islam and came to Ṣakhr so that he would hand over our water to us, but he refused us." So he came to him and said: "
"O Ṣakhr, when a people accept Islam they secure their property and their lives. So hand over their water to them."
He said: "Yes, O Prophet of Allah."
Then I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ change at that, turning red out of shame at his having taken the girl and taken the water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stopped at the site of the mosque under a doum palm and stayed three days, then set out for Tabūk. The tribe of Juhaynah caught up with him at al-Raḥbah, and he said to them: "
"Who are the people of Dhū al-Marwah?"
They said: "Banū Rifāʿah of Juhaynah." He said: "
"I have granted it to Banū Rifāʿah."

So they divided it among themselves; some of them sold [their share] and some kept it and worked it. Then I asked his father ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz about this hadith, and he told me part of it but did not tell me all of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafiyyah and Duḥaybah, the two daughters of ʿUlaybah—who were the stepdaughters of Qaylah bint Makhramah, who was the grandmother of their father—[reported] that she told them. She said:

We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: My companion went ahead—meaning Ḥurayth ibn Ḥassān, the delegate of Bakr ibn Wāʾil—and pledged allegiance to him upon Islam, for himself and his people. Then he said: "O Messenger of Allah, write for us, between us and Banū Tamīm, [a boundary at] al-Dahnāʾ, so that none of them may cross it to us except a traveler or a neighbor." He said: "
"Write for him, boy, [the grant of] al-Dahnāʾ."

When I saw that he had ordered it to be given to him, I was alarmed, for it was my homeland and my home. So I said: "O Messenger of Allah, he did not ask you for a fair share of the land when he asked you. This al-Dahnāʾ is [only] the hobbling place of your camel and the pasture of the sheep, and the women and children of Banū Tamīm are beyond that." He said: "
"Hold, boy. The poor woman has spoken truly. A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim; water and trees suffice for both of them, and they help each other against the troublemaker."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ granted al-Zubayr [land as far as] the running of his horse. So he ran his horse until it stopped, then threw his whip, and [the Prophet ﷺ] said: "

segments_en: Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr said that one night he was reciting in his storage-yard (mirbad) when his horse began to shy and circle. He recited, then it circled again, so he recited, then it circled once more. Usayd said: "I feared it would trample Yaḥyā, so I got up and went to it, and there above my head was something like a canopy with lamps like [lights] in it, rising into the air until I could no longer see it." He said: "In the morning I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, last night, in the depth of the night, I was reciting in my yard when my horse began to circle.'"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Keep reciting, O Ibn Ḥuḍayr."
He said: "So I recited, then it circled again."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Keep reciting, O Ibn Ḥuḍayr."
He said: "So I recited, then it circled again."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Keep reciting, O Ibn Ḥuḍayr." He said: "So I stopped."
"Yaḥyā was close to it and I feared it would trample him. Then I saw something like a canopy with lamps in it, rising into the air until I could no longer see it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Those were the angels, listening to you. Had you kept reciting, by morning the people would have seen them; they would not have been hidden from them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Keep up your hold on this Qur'an, for by the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, it escapes more quickly than camels from their hobbles."

segments_en: My father married me to a woman of good lineage, and he would look in on his daughter-in-law and ask her about her husband. She would say: "What an excellent man! He has not laid down in our bed nor looked into our private affairs since we came to him." When this went on for a long time, [my father] mentioned it to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Bring him to meet me."
So I met him afterwards, and he said: "How do you fast?"
I said: "Every day." He said: "And how often do you complete the Qur'an?"
I said: "Every night." He said:
"Fast three days in every month and recite the Qur'an [to completion] once a month."
I said: "I am able to do more than that." He said:
"Fast three days in the week."
I said: "I am able to do more than that." He said:
"Break the fast for two days and fast one day."
I said: "I am able to do more than that." He said:
"Fast the best fasting, the fasting of Dāwūd: fast one day and break the fast the next, and recite [the whole Qur'an] once every seven nights."

I wish I had accepted the concession of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for I have grown old and weak. He used to recite a seventh of the Qur'an to some of his family during the day, [that is,] what he would recite he would review in the daytime so that it would be lighter for him at night. When he wanted to gain strength, he would break the fast for some days, counting them, and then fast the same number, disliking to abandon something he had parted from the Prophet ﷺ while doing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Recite the Qur'an as long as your hearts are united upon it,
but when you differ, then get up and leave it."
Yazīd ibn Hārūn said, from Hārūn al-Aʿwar:
Abū ʿImrān narrated to us, from Jundab, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a young man and I fear hardship for myself, and I do not have the means to marry women." He remained silent toward me.
Then I said the same again,
and he remained silent toward me. Then I said the same again,
and he remained silent toward me. Then I said the same again, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"O Abū Hurayrah, the pen has dried over what you will meet.
So either have yourself castrated for that, or leave it."

segments_en: Jābir said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a military expedition. When we were returning, I hurried ahead on a slow camel of mine. A rider caught up with me from behind and prodded my camel with a short spear he had, and my camel set off like the finest camel you could see. I turned around, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:
"What makes you hurry, O Jābir?"
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have only recently married." He said:
"Did you marry a virgin or a previously married woman?"
I said: "A previously married woman." He said:
"Why not a young girl, so you could play with her and she with you?"
He said: When we reached Madinah, we went to go in [to our homes], and he said:

"Wait until we enter at night," meaning in the evening, "so that the woman with unkempt hair may comb it and the one whose husband has been away may shave her private hair." He said, and he also said:
"When you arrive, then be wise, be wise [seek children]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Medina and met ʿItbān and said, "A hadith has reached me from you." He said, "Something afflicted my eyesight, so I sent word to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'I would like you to come and pray in my house so that I may take it as a place of prayer.'" He said: The Prophet ﷺ came with whomever Allah willed of his Companions. He entered while he was praying in my house, and his Companions were talking among themselves. Then they attributed the greater part of that matter to Mālik ibn Dukhshum. They said, "They wished that he would invoke against him so that he would perish, and they wished that some evil would befall him."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer and said:
"Does he not testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah?"
They said, "He says that, but it is not in his heart." He said:
"No one testifies that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah and then enters the Fire, or [the Fire] consumes him."
Anas said: This hadith pleased me, so I said to my son, "Write it down," and he wrote it down.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is my uncle. He sent for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "Come and mark out a place of prayer for me."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There was no prophet whom Allah sent to a nation before me but he had among his nation disciples and companions who followed his way and obeyed his command. Then there came after them successors who said what they did not do, and did what they were not commanded. Whoever strives against them with his hand is a believer; whoever strives against them with his tongue is a believer; and whoever strives against them with his heart is a believer. Beyond that there is not even a mustard seed of faith."

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the Farewell Hajj, while he was standing at ʿArafah. A Bedouin came to him, took hold of the edge of his cloak, and asked him for it. He gave it to him and the man left. It was then that begging was made prohibited. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Begging is not permissible for a rich person, nor for one who is strong and sound, except for one in severe poverty or one burdened with crushing debt. Whoever begs from people in order to increase his wealth, it will be scratches on his face on the Day of Resurrection and hot stones from Hell that he eats. So whoever wishes, let him ask little, and whoever wishes, let him ask much."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah accepts charity and takes it with His right hand, and He nurtures it for one of you just as one of you raises his foal, until a single morsel becomes like Mount Uhud."

And the confirmation of that is in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "And He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants" and takes the charities; "Allah destroys usury and nurtures charities."

"You will find people to be like mines: the best of them in the Jāhiliyyah are the best of them in Islam, if they gain understanding. And you will find among the best of people in this matter those who most dislike it before they fall into it. And you will find among the worst of people the two-faced one, who comes to these with one face and to those with another face."

"People follow Quraysh in this matter [of leadership],
their Muslims following their Muslims,
and their disbelievers following their disbelievers." "And people are like mines;
the best of them in the Jāhiliyyah are the best of them in Islam, if they gain understanding.
You will find among the best of people those who most dislike this matter, until they fall into it."

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about this verse:
"Say: I ask of you no reward for it except affection for [my] near relatives." Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "The relatives of Muḥammad ﷺ."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Do you know that there was no clan of Quraysh with whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not have a kinship tie? So he said: [Rather,] that you maintain the ties of kinship that are between me and you."

segments_en: Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān came to ʿUthmān, having been fighting alongside the people of Syria in the conquest of Armenia and Azerbaijan together with the people of Iraq. Their differences in recitation alarmed Ḥudhayfah, so Ḥudhayfah said to ʿUthmān: "O Commander of the Faithful, take hold of this nation before they differ about the Book as the Jews and Christians differed." So ʿUthmān sent to Ḥafṣah: "Send us the manuscripts so that we may copy them into copies [of the Quran], then we will return them to you." Ḥafṣah sent them to ʿUthmān, and he ordered Zayd ibn Thābit, ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr, Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, and they copied them into copies. ʿUthmān said to the three Qurashī men: "If you and Zayd ibn Thābit differ about anything of the Quran, write it in the dialect of Quraysh, for it was revealed in their tongue." They did so, until, when they had copied the manuscripts into copies, ʿUthmān returned the manuscripts to Ḥafṣah and sent to every region a copy of what they had copied, and he ordered that everything else of the Quran, in any sheet or copy, be burned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"The Hour will not come until a man from Qaḥṭān emerges, driving the people with his staff."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥassān ibn Thābit asked permission from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to satirize the polytheists, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What about my lineage?"
Ḥassān said: "I will draw you out from among them as a hair is drawn out from dough."
And from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, who said: I went to revile Ḥassān in the presence of ʿĀʾishah, but she said: "Do not revile him, for he used to defend the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He said:
"Look how Allah turns away from me the insults of Quraysh and their cursing. They insult Mudhammam and curse Mudhammam, while I am Muḥammad."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He mentioned several hadith, among them: Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ said:

"My likeness and the likeness of the prophets before me is that of a man who built houses and made them excellent, beautiful, and complete, except for the place of one brick in one of the corners. People would go around and admire the building, and say: 'If only you had placed a brick here, your building would be complete.'" Muḥammad ﷺ said:
"So I am that brick."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the most handsome of people in face and the best of them in character;
he was neither conspicuously tall nor short.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked him whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to dye his hair. He said: "It did not reach that; there was only a little [white] at his temples."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a man of Banū ʿAbs, from Ḥudhayfah:
that he prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night, and he heard him, when he said the takbīr, say:
"Allah is the Greatest, Possessor of power, sovereignty, majesty, and grandeur."
And in his bowing he would say:
"Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty."
And when he raised his head from bowing, he said:
"For my Lord is all praise, for my Lord is all praise." And in his prostration:
"Glory be to my Lord, the Most High." And between the two prostrations:
"My Lord, forgive me; my Lord, forgive me."
His standing and his bowing,
and when he raised his head from bowing, and his prostration, and what was between the two prostrations, were nearly equal [in length].
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he mentioned,
another [narrator] before him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hurmuz al-Aʿraj,
from Muḥammad ibn Maslamah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he stood in the night to pray voluntary prayer, would say when he prostrated:

"O Allah, to You I have prostrated, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. O Allah, You are my Lord. My face has prostrated to the One who created it, fashioned it, and opened its hearing and its sight. Blessed is Allah, the Best of creators."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿAlī ibn Yaḥyā ibn Khallād ibn Mālik ibn Rāfiʿ ibn Mālik
narrated to him from his father, from his uncle,

Rifāʿah ibn Rāfiʿ, who said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting and we were around him, a man entered, went toward the qiblah, and prayed. When he finished his prayer, he came and greeted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the people. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"And upon you. Go back and pray, for you have not prayed."

So he went and prayed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept watching his prayer without knowing what was wrong with it. When he finished his prayer, he came and greeted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the people. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"And upon you. Go back and pray, for you have not prayed."
He repeated it two or three times. Then the man said: O Messenger of Allah, what fault have you found in my prayer? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The prayer of any one of you is not complete until he performs ablution fully as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded him: he washes his face and his hands up to the elbows, wipes his head, and [washes] his feet up to the ankles; then he declares the greatness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, praises Him, and glorifies Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I do not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ever recited the whole Qur'an in a night, or stood in prayer a whole night until morning, or fasted a complete month, other than Ramadan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade building over a grave,
adding to it, or plastering it.
Sulaymān ibn Mūsā added:
or writing on it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about his fasting, and he became angry. ʿUmar said: We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muḥammad as Messenger.
And he was asked about one who fasts perpetually, and he said:
"He neither fasted nor broke his fast," or he said, "He did not fast and did not break the fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: O Prophet of Allah, I did not come to you until I had sworn more times than the number of these—[pointing] to the fingers of his hands—that I would not come to you and would not follow your religion. I am a man who understands nothing except what Allah and His Messenger have taught me. I ask you by the Face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: with what has your Lord sent you to us? He said: "With Islam."
He said: I said: What are the signs of Islam? He said:

"That you say: I have submitted my face to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and I have turned away [from all else]; that you establish prayer and give zakāh. Every Muslim is sacred to [every other] Muslim, brothers and supporters of one another. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will not accept any deed from a polytheist after he has embraced Islam until he separates from the polytheists [and joins] the Muslims."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade tabattul [renouncing marriage].
Zayd ibn Akhzam added: And Qatādah recited: {And We certainly sent messengers before you and made for them wives and offspring.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day Saʿd gave his judgment concerning Banū Qurayẓah, I was a boy. They doubted me and did not find that I had grown [pubic hair], so I was spared. And here I am among you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were discussing some matter, and I was new

to the Jāhiliyyah, and I swore by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: What an evil thing you said. Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and tell him, for we think you have surely committed disbelief. So I came to him and told him, and he said to me:
"Say: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, three times; seek refuge with Allah from the Devil three times; spit lightly to your left three times; and do not repeat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

The person with the lightest punishment among the people of the Fire will be a man who has two sandals and two straps of fire, from which his brain boils as a cauldron boils. He will not think that anyone suffers a worse punishment than he does, though he is the one with the lightest punishment among them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The extent of my Basin is like the distance between Aylah and Sanaa in Yemen,
and in it are drinking vessels as many as the stars of the sky."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, are the people of Paradise known from the people of the Fire?" He said, "Yes."
The man said, "Then why do the doers act?" He said, "Everyone acts for that which he was created for," or, "for that which is made easy for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us in a place and left nothing that would occur from that standing until the Hour is established except that he told us about it. Those who remembered it remembered it, and those who forgot it forgot it. These companions of mine know it. Indeed, something of it may occur that I had forgotten, and when I see it I recall it, as a man recalls the face of another man who has been absent from him, and then recognizes him when he sees him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I have seen nothing more similar to the minor sins (lamam) than what Abū Hurayrah reported from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "

Allah has decreed for the son of Ādam his share of adultery, which he will inevitably encounter. The adultery of the eyes is looking, the adultery of the tongue is speaking, the soul wishes and desires, and the private part either confirms that or denies it."
ʿAbd said in his narration: Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās [say]
label: machine translation

segments_en: The major sins are associating partners with Allah and disobedience to parents," or he said, "the false oath." Shuʿbah was unsure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Prophet ﷺ was delivering a sermon, he saw a man standing in the sun. He asked about him, and they said:
This is Abū Isrāʾīl. He has vowed to stand and not sit,
not to seek shade, not to speak, and to fast. He said: "
Order him to speak, to seek shade, and to sit, and to complete his fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever frees a believing slave, Allah will free from the Fire a limb of his for every limb of the slave, even his private part for the slave's private part."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah,

that she said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ wanted to send ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān to Abū Bakr to ask him for their inheritance from the Prophet ﷺ. ʿĀʾishah said to them, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not say: "
We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity"?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ — and Ādam narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him — that the Prophet ﷺ struck [the drinker] for wine with palm branches and sandals,
and Abū Bakr flogged forty.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The hand of a thief was not cut in the time of the Prophet ﷺ for less than the price of a shield,
a buckler or a small shield,
and each of them had value.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the mosque and we were sitting with him, a man came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed an offense deserving a prescribed punishment, so carry it out on me."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent toward him. Then he repeated, "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed an offense deserving a prescribed punishment, so carry it out on me."

He remained silent toward him, and the prayer was called. When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ finished, Abū Umāmah said: The man followed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as he left, and I followed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to see what answer he would give the man. The man caught up with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed an offense deserving a prescribed punishment, so carry it out on me." Abū Umāmah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "
Did you not, when you left your house, perform ablution and do it well?"
He said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "
Then you attended the prayer with us?"
He said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "
Then indeed Allah has forgiven your offense," or he said, "your sin."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him, along with Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān, during the days of Tashrīq, and he called out: "
None shall enter Paradise except a believer.
And the days of Minā are days of eating and drinking."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me one day: "
O ʿĀʾishah, do you have anything [to eat]?"
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, we have nothing." He said: "Then I am fasting."

She said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out, and a gift was given to us—or visitors came to us. She said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned, I said, "O Messenger of Allah, a gift was given to us—or visitors came to us—and I have kept something aside for you." He said, "What is it?" I said, "Ḥays." He said, "Bring it."
So I brought it, and he ate. Then he said: "
I had begun the morning fasting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me one day and said: "
Do you have anything?" I said, "No." He said, "Then I am fasting."

Then he passed by me after that day, when ḥays had been given to me as a gift, so I kept some aside for him—and he loved ḥays. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, we were given ḥays as a gift, and I kept some aside for you." He said: "
Bring it near. Indeed, I began the morning fasting."
Then he ate some of it, and then he said: "
The example of the voluntary fast is only like a man who takes out charity (ṣadaqah) from his wealth: if he wishes, he gives it out, and if he wishes, he keeps it back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Saʿīd ibn Jubayr about fasting
in Rajab—and we were in Rajab at that time. He said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would fast until we said, "He does not break his fast,"
