Then she went to a shepherd who used to take shelter by his hermitage and let him have her, and he lay with her and she became pregnant. When she gave birth, she said, 'It is from Jurayj.'

They came to him, made him come down, demolished his hermitage, and began to beat him. He said, 'What is the matter with you?' They said, 'You committed fornication with this prostitute and she bore a child from you.'

He said, 'Where is the child?' They brought him, and he said, 'Let me pray.' So he prayed, and when he finished he came to the child, poked him in the belly, and said, 'O boy, who is your father?' He said, 'So-and-so the shepherd.' He said: Then they turned to Jurayj, kissing him and wiping themselves against him, and said, 'We will build your hermitage for you out of gold.'
He said, 'No. Rebuild it from clay as it was.' And they did so.
And [the second one is] a baby who was nursing from his mother when a man passed by riding a fine mount and of handsome appearance. His mother said, 'O Allah, make my son like this man.'
The baby let go of the breast, turned to him, looked at him, and said, 'O Allah, do not make me like him.'
Then he turned back to his mother's breast and resumed nursing.
[Abū Hurayrah] said: It is as though I am looking at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as he imitated the baby's nursing, with his index finger in his mouth, sucking on it.
He said: And they passed by a slave girl whom they were beating, saying, 'You committed fornication! You stole!'
And she was saying, 'Allah is sufficient for me, and what an excellent Disposer of affairs.'
Her mother said, 'O Allah, do not make my son like her.'
The baby left nursing, looked at her, and said, 'O Allah, make me like her.'
Then the two of them exchanged words, and she said, 'Throat-cut! A man of fine appearance passed by and I said, "O Allah, make my son like him,"
and you said, "O Allah, do not make me like him."
And they passed by this slave girl while beating her and saying, "You committed fornication! You stole!"
and I said, "O Allah, do not make my son like her,"
and you said, "O Allah, make me like her."' He said, 'That man was a tyrant, so I said, "O Allah, do not make me like him."
And as for this girl, they say of her, "You committed fornication,"
when she did not commit fornication, and "You stole," when she did not steal, so I said, "O Allah, make me like her."'
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw a man from the people of Khurasan ask ash-Shaʿbī. He said, "O Abū ʿAmr, the people of Khurasan where we come from say about a man who frees his slave woman and then marries her that he is like one who rides his own sacrificial camel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"How will you be when the son of Maryam descends among you, and your leader is from among you?"
I said to Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, "Al-Awzāʿī narrated to us from az-Zuhrī, from Nāfiʿ, from Abū Hurayrah: 'and your imam is from among you.'"
Ibn Abī Dhiʾb said, "Do you know what 'your leader is from among you' means?" I said, "Tell me."
He said, "He will lead you by the Book of your Lord, Blessed and Exalted, and the Sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Thābit ibn Thawbān, from Ḥassān ibn ʿAṭiyyah,
from Abū Kabshah as-Salūlī,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Convey from me, even if it is a single verse, and narrate from the Children of Israel, for there is no blame in that. And whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey,
and the muʾadhdhin wanted to call the adhān for the Ẓuhr prayer. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Wait until it cools down."
Then he wanted to call the adhān again, and he said to him, "Wait until it cools down,"
until we saw the shade of the dunes. Then the Prophet ﷺ said,
"The intensity of the heat is from the blazing of Hell.
So when the heat becomes intense, delay the prayer until it cools down."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: "tatafayyaʾu" means "it inclines."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We memorized it from az-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"When the heat becomes intense, delay the prayer until it cools down,
for the intensity of the heat is from the blazing of Hell."
"The Fire complained to its Lord and said, 'My Lord, parts of me have consumed other parts.'
So He permitted it two breaths: one breath in the winter
and one breath in the summer.
That is the most intense heat that you feel,
and the most intense cold that you feel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He said, "It is as if I am hearing you right now." He said: I heard my father asking him about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said, "He did not mind delaying it somewhat" — meaning the ʿIshāʾ prayer — "until half the night, and he did not like sleeping before it or talking after it."

Shuʿbah said: Then I met him afterwards and asked him, and he said, "He used to pray Ẓuhr when the sun had passed its zenith, and ʿAṣr [at a time when] a man could go to the farthest part of Madinah and the sun was still alive." He said, "As for Maghrib, I do not know what time he mentioned."

He said: Then I met him afterwards and asked him, and he said, "He used to pray the Fajr prayer, and a man would leave and look at the face of his companion sitting beside him, whom he knew, and recognize him."
He said, "And he used to recite in it from sixty to one hundred verses."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed in Madinah seven and eight [rakʿahs]: Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ.
Ayyūb said, "Perhaps it was on a rainy night." He said, "Perhaps."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣuhayb, the freed slave of Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj, said: I heard Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj
say: We used to pray Maghrib with the Prophet ﷺ, and when one of us left, he could still see where his arrows fell.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When al-Ḥajjāj came to Madinah, we asked Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray Ẓuhr at midday, ʿAṣr while the sun was still clear, Maghrib when the sun had set, and ʿIshāʾ sometimes he would delay and sometimes he would hasten it: when he saw that the people had gathered, he would hasten it, and when he saw that they were slow, he would delay it. And Fajr, they used to — or he said — the Prophet ﷺ used to pray it in the darkness before dawn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They asked Anas about the ring of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer one night until about the middle of the night, or until nearly half the night had passed. Then he came and said:
"The people have prayed and gone to sleep, but you remain in prayer as long as you are waiting for the prayer."
Anas said: It is as if I can see the gleam of his silver ring. And he raised his left hand with the little finger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We ate the pre-dawn meal with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then we got up for the prayer.
I said, "[Qatādah] claims that Anas is the one who said it: How long was it between the two?" He said, "The time it takes a man to recite fifty verses."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Masrūq,
both said: We bear witness about ʿĀʾishah that she said: Whenever it was his day with me, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never failed to pray them in my house.
She meant the two rakʿahs after ʿAṣr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb,

on the day of the Trench, after the sun had set, began to curse the disbelievers of Quraysh and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I was barely able to pray until the sun was about to set." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By Allah, I have not prayed it."

So we went down with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Buṭḥān. He performed ablution for the prayer and we performed ablution for it, and he prayed ʿAṣr after the sun had set, and then after it he prayed Maghrib.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Abū Wāʾil, "Were you present at Ṣiffīn?" He said, "Yes."
And I heard Sahl ibn Ḥunayf
saying—[Another chain:] Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash,
from Abū Wāʾil,
who said: Sahl ibn Ḥunayf said, "O people, doubt your own opinion regarding your religion.
I saw myself on the day of Abū Jandal, and had I been able to reject the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would have rejected it.
Whenever we placed our swords on our shoulders for an affair that alarmed us, it would be made easy for us, leading to something we recognized—other than this affair."
He said: And Abū Wāʾil said, "I was present at Ṣiffīn—and how wretched was Ṣiffīn!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sahl ibn Ḥunayf stood up on the day of Ṣiffīn and said, "O people, doubt yourselves. We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah, and had we seen [a need for] fighting, we would have fought. That was during the treaty between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the polytheists. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, are we not in the right and they in the wrong?' He said, 'Indeed.'
He said, 'Are not our dead in Paradise and their dead in the Fire?' He said, 'Indeed.'
He said, 'Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion and go back, while Allah has not yet judged between us and them?' He said,
'O son of al-Khaṭṭāb, I am the Messenger of Allah, and Allah will never let me be lost.'
He said: So ʿUmar went off, unable to be patient, furious, and came to Abū Bakr and said, 'O Abū Bakr, are we not in the right and they in the wrong?' He said, 'Indeed.'
He said, 'Are not our dead in Paradise and their dead in the Fire?' He said, 'Indeed.'

He said, 'Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion and go back, while Allah has not yet judged between us and them?' He said, 'O son of al-Khaṭṭāb, he is the Messenger of Allah, and Allah will never let him be lost.'

He said: Then the Qur'an was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning the victory, so he sent for ʿUmar and recited it to him. ʿUmar said, 'O Messenger of Allah, is it a victory?' He said, 'Yes.'
So his heart was put at ease and he returned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ was prevented from reaching the House, the people of Makkah made a treaty with him that he would enter it and stay there three days, and that he would not enter except with the sheathed weapons—the sword and its scabbard.
And that he would not take out anyone of its people with him, and would not prevent anyone of those with him from staying there. He said to ʿAlī,
"Write the terms between us: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed upon."
The polytheists said to him, "If we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would follow you. But write: Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullāh."
So he ordered ʿAlī to erase it, but ʿAlī said, "No, by Allah, I will not erase it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Show me its place."
So he showed him its place, and he erased it and wrote,
"Ibn ʿAbdullāh."
So he stayed there three days. When the third day came, they said to ʿAlī, "This is the last day of your companion's term, so order him to leave."
He informed him of that, and he said, "Yes." Then he left.
Ibn Jannāb said in his narration, in place of "we would follow you," "we would pledge allegiance to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was prostrating, with some of the polytheists of Quraysh around him, ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ came with the entrails of a slaughtered camel,
and threw it onto the back of the Prophet ﷺ. He did not raise his head until Fāṭimah, peace be upon her, came and removed it from his back,
and she invoked [Allah's punishment] against the one who did that. Then the Prophet ﷺ said,
"O Allah, take care of the chiefs of Quraysh;
O Allah, take care of Abū Jahl ibn Hishām,
and ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah,
and Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah,
and ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ,
and Umayyah ibn Khalaf—or Ubayy ibn Khalaf."
I certainly saw them killed on the day of Badr,
and thrown into a well,
except Umayyah or Ubayy,
for he was a heavyset man,
and when they dragged him, his limbs came apart before he was thrown into the well.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Allah said: The son of Adam has denied Me, though he had no right to do so,
and he has insulted Me, though he had no right to do so.
As for his denying Me, it is his saying that I will not bring him back as I originated him.
As for his insulting Me, it is his saying that Allah has taken a child,
while I am the Self-Sufficient, Who has not begotten and has not been begotten, and there is none comparable to Me."
{He neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him}. Kufuʾan, kafīʾan, and kifāʾan are the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Barīrah made a contract of emancipation (mukātabah) for herself for nine ūqiyahs, to be paid one ūqiyah each year. She came to ʿĀʾishah asking for her help. ʿĀʾishah said, "No, unless they are willing for me to pay it to them in one lump sum and the walāʾ [right of patronage] be mine."

So Barīrah went and spoke to her people about that, but they refused unless the walāʾ be theirs. She came back to ʿĀʾishah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived at that moment. She told ʿĀʾishah what her people had said, and ʿĀʾishah said, "By Allah, no, unless the walāʾ is mine."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "What is this?"

She said, "O Messenger of Allah, Barīrah came to me asking for my help with her contract, and I said, 'No, unless they are willing for me to pay it to them in one lump sum and the walāʾ be mine.' I mentioned that to her people, but they refused unless the walāʾ be theirs."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Buy her and stipulate the walāʾ for them, for the walāʾ belongs to the one who sets free."
Then he stood up and addressed the people. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said,

"What is the matter with people who make stipulations that are not in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? They say, 'Free so-and-so and the walāʾ is mine.' The Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has greater right, and the condition of Allah is more binding. Every condition that is not in the Book of Allah is invalid, even if it be a hundred conditions."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then gave her the choice regarding her husband, who was a slave, and she chose herself.
ʿUrwah said: Had he been a free man, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not have given her the choice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Between every two calls [the adhān and the iqāmah] there is a prayer; between every two calls there is a prayer." Then he said the third time, "for whoever wishes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and he led us in the last evening prayer (ʿishāʾ), reciting in one of the two rakʿahs "By the fig and the olive."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Sumayy,
from Abū Ṣāliḥ,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"When the imam says, 'Allah hears whoever praises Him,'
then say, 'O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs all praise.'
For whoever's words coincide with the words of the angels will have his previous sins forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about wiping away the pebbles during prayer, and he said,
"If you must do it, then only once."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he mentioned,
to her that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar
says: "The dead person is punished because of the weeping of the living."
ʿĀʾishah said, "May Allah forgive Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. He did not lie, but he forgot or made a mistake. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only passed by a Jewish woman who was being wept over, and he said,
'They are weeping over her while she is being punished in her grave.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A funeral procession passed by and was praised well, so the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said,
"It is obligatory, it is obligatory, it is obligatory."
Another funeral procession passed by and was spoken of badly, so the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said,
"It is obligatory, it is obligatory, it is obligatory."
ʿUmar said, "May my father and mother be ransomed for you! A funeral passed by and was praised well, and you said, 'It is obligatory, it is obligatory, it is obligatory.'
Another funeral passed by and was spoken of badly, and you said, 'It is obligatory, it is obligatory, it is obligatory.'" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Whoever you praise well, Paradise becomes obligatory for him, and whoever you speak of badly, the Fire becomes obligatory for him. You are the witnesses of Allah on earth; you are the witnesses of Allah on earth; you are the witnesses of Allah on earth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik ibn Anas, from ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā al-Māzinī, from his father,
who said: I heard Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"There is no charity (zakāh) due on fewer than five camels, nor on less than five ūqiyahs, nor on less than five awsāq."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Yemen and commanded me to take a tenth from what the sky waters or what is watered by natural moisture (baʿl), and a half of a tenth from what is watered by water-wheels.
Yaḥyā ibn Ādam said: The baʿl, the ʿathariyy and the ʿadhy are what is watered by rain.
The ʿathariyy is what is planted for the clouds and the rain alone, receiving nothing but rainwater.
The baʿl is that of the vineyards whose roots have gone down into the earth to reach water, so they do not need irrigation for five or six years and can bear going without it. This is baʿl.
The sayl is the water of the valley when it flows.
The ghayl is a flow smaller than a sayl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Five are wrongdoers [fawāsiq] that may be killed in the sanctuary and outside it: the kite, the crow, the mouse, the scorpion, and the rabid dog."
ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Some of our companions mentioned that Maʿmar used to narrate it from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father, and from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah, that the Prophet ﷺ
label: machine translation

segments_en: may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Prophet ﷺ forbade eating any predatory animal with a fang.
Al-Zuhrī said: I did not hear this until I came to Syria.
And al-Layth added: Yūnus narrated to me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
who said: I asked him whether we may perform ablution with, or drink, the milk of donkeys, the bile of predatory animals, or the urine of camels.
He said: The Muslims used to treat themselves with these,
and they saw no harm in that.
As for the milk of donkeys, it has reached us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade their meat,
but no command or prohibition has reached us concerning their milk.

As for the bile of predatory animals, Ibn Shihāb said: Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī informed me that Abū Thaʿlabah al-Khushanī informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade eating any predatory animal with a fang.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Woe to you—or: Alas for you—" (Shuʿbah said: he was unsure which) "do not go back to disbelief after me,
striking one another's necks."
And al-Naḍr said, from Shuʿbah: "Alas for you."
And ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad said, from his father: "Woe to you" or "Alas for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When a judge rules, exerting his effort, and is correct, he has two rewards; and when he rules, exerting his effort, and is mistaken, he has one reward."
I narrated this to Abū Bakr ibn Ḥazm, and he said: This is how Abū Salamah narrated it to me, from Abū Hurayrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Samurah ibn Jundab said: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ I was a boy, and I used to memorize from him. Nothing prevents me from speaking except that there are men here who are older than I am. I prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over a woman who had died in childbirth, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood in the middle of her [body] for the prayer.
In the narration of Ibn al-Muthannā: ʿAbdullāh ibn Buraydah narrated to me, saying: He stood over her for the prayer, in the middle of her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: I entered the mosque while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting among the people. He said: So I sat down, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What prevented you from praying two rakʿahs before sitting?"
He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I saw you sitting and the people sitting." He said:
"When one of you enters the mosque, let him not sit until he has prayed two rakʿahs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Read] to him while I listened,
—and the wording is his—from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Dīnār,
from Sulaymān ibn Yasār,
from ʿIrāk ibn Mālik,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A Muslim owes no charity (ṣadaqah) on his slave or on his horse."
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ. [Another chain:] And Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm informed us,
who said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us,
who said: Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd and Abū
Salamah, from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"The injury caused by an animal is without liability, the well is without liability, the mine is without liability, and on buried treasure one-fifth is due."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Abū Bakr ibn
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the price of a dog, the earnings of a prostitute, and the fee of a soothsayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The most deserving of conditions to be fulfilled are those by which you have made private relations lawful."
This is the wording of the hadith of Abū Bakr and Ibn al-Muthannā.
Except that Ibn al-Muthannā said, "the conditions."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave us a choice, and we chose him. Was that a divorce?
Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us,
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash,
from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾishah, similarly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
all from Sufyān,
—Abū Bakr said: Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us—from al-Zuhrī,
from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

"Five are part of the natural disposition (fiṭrah)—or: five things belong to the fiṭrah—circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, trimming the nails, plucking the armpit hair, and trimming the moustache."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people raided the camels of the Prophet ﷺ and drove them off, and they apostatized from Islam and killed the herdsman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was a believer. So he sent [men] after them, and they were captured. He had their hands and feet cut off and their eyes gouged out.
He said: And the verse concerning those who wage war [against Allah and His Messenger] was revealed about them, and they are the ones about whom Anas ibn Mālik informed al-Hajjāj when he asked him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: in his house; I asked him,
about Sālim Abū an-Naḍr,
then he went on with the hadith, saying: or Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿUbaydullāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Let me not find any one of you reclining on his couch, when a matter comes to him from what I have commanded or forbidden, and he says: 'I do not know; whatever we find in the Book of Allah, we follow.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: He claimed that he was sitting in al-Baṭḥāʾ among a group, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting among them, when a cloud passed over them. They looked at it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you know what this is called?"
They said: Yes, this is the sahāb (cloud).
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "And the muzn." They said: And the muzn.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "And the ʿanān." They said: And the ʿanān.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them:
"Do you know how far apart the heaven and the earth are?"
They said: No, by Allah, we do not know. He said:
"The distance between them is either seventy-one, seventy-two, or seventy-three years, and the heaven above it is likewise."
He counted them until he had counted seven heavens in the same way. Then he said:

"Above the seventh heaven is a sea, the distance between its top and its bottom being like that from one heaven to the next. Above that are eight mountain goats, the distance between their hooves and their knees being like that from one heaven to the next. Then above their backs is the Throne, the distance between its bottom and its top being like that from one heaven to the next. And Allah is above that."
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd said: I heard Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn say: Does ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Saʿd not want to perform Hajj so that we may hear this hadith from him?
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was in the mosque of Ḥimṣ when a man passed by him. They said: This is one who served the Prophet ﷺ. So he stood up to him and said: Narrate to me a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with no men passing it between you and him. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"Whoever says, when he rises in the morning and when he enters the evening: 'We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger,' it is a right upon Allah that He will please him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ delivered a sermon on his she-camel while I was beneath her neck, and she was chewing her cud, and her saliva was running between my shoulders. I heard him say:

"Indeed Allah has given everyone who has a right his right, and there is no bequest for an heir. The child belongs to the marriage bed, and for the adulterer is the stone. Whoever claims to be the son of someone other than his father, or attaches himself to someone other than his masters, out of aversion to them, upon him is the curse of Allah; Allah will accept from him neither an obligatory nor a voluntary act."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution washing each part once, and said:
"This is the ablution without which Allah does not accept prayer."
Then he performed ablution washing each part twice, and said:
"This is the ablution of moderate measure."
And he performed ablution washing each part three times, and said:

"This is the most complete ablution, and it is my ablution and the ablution of the Intimate Friend of Allah, Ibrāhīm. Whoever performs ablution like this, then says upon finishing: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger,' the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter by whichever he wishes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Zuhayr,
and Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh and Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, who said:
I asked Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl about wiping

over the leather socks. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command us, when we were travelling, to wipe over our leather socks and not take them off for three days, whether for defecation, urination, or sleep, except for janābah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I have not sung, nor wished for anything vain, nor touched my private part with my right hand since I pledged allegiance with it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you cleans himself after relieving himself, let him not clean himself with his right hand; let him clean himself with his left."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was the first
to hear the Prophet ﷺ say:
"None of you should urinate facing the qiblah."
And I was the first to relate that to the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me to drink while standing and to urinate facing the qiblah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his lavatory facing the qiblah.

ʿĪsā said: I mentioned that to ash-Shaʿbī, and he said: Ibn ʿUmar spoke the truth, and Abū Hurayrah spoke the truth. As for Abū Hurayrah's statement, he said: In the open desert, one should neither face the qiblah nor turn his back to it. As for Ibn ʿUmar's statement, a lavatory has no qiblah, so face whichever direction you wish in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: People were mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who disliked facing the qiblah with their private parts, so he said:
"Have they really done that? Turn my seat to face the qiblah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you urinates, let him shake out his private part three times."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿādh ibn Jabal used to relate things that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not heard, and to remain silent about things they had heard. What he was relating reached ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: By Allah, I did not hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say this, and Muʿādh is about to put you to trial concerning the toilet.

That reached Muʿādh, so he met him and said: O ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, denying a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is hypocrisy, and its sin is only on the one who said it. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Beware of the three cursed acts: relieving oneself at watering places, in shade, and on the middle of the road."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Beware of camping for the night on the main roads and of praying on them, for they are the dwelling place of snakes and wild beasts, and relieving oneself on them, for that is among the cursed acts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade praying on the middle of the road, or setting up a place to relieve oneself on it, or urinating on it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not go to relieve himself until he was out of sight and could not be seen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and he wanted to relieve himself, so he said to me:
"Go to those two small palm trees."
Wakīʿ said: meaning small date palms.
Abū Bakr al-Qaṣṣār said: "
Tell them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ orders you to come together."
So they came together, and he screened himself with them and relieved himself. Then he said to me:
"Go to them and tell them that each of you should return to its place."
I told them, and they returned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The thing the Prophet ﷺ most liked to screen himself with when relieving himself was a high mound or a cluster of palm trees.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned aside to a mountain pass and urinated, until I felt pity for him, seeing his thighs spread apart as he urinated.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Two people must not converse while relieving themselves, each looking at the private parts of his companion, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, hates that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Most of the punishment of the grave is because of urine."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by two graves and said:
"They are both being punished, and not for something major. As for one of them, he is punished for urine; and as for the other, he is punished for backbiting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was performing ablution and greeted him with salām, but he did not return my greeting. When he finished his ablution, he said:
"Nothing prevented me from returning your greeting except that I was not in a state of ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ come out from relieving himself without touching water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah bint Masʿūd ibn al-Aswad, from her father, who said:

When that woman stole the velvet cloth from the house of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we considered the matter grave, for she was a woman from Quraysh. So we came to the Prophet ﷺ to speak to him, and we said, "We will ransom her with forty ūqiyyah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Her being purified is better for her."
When we heard the gentleness of the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we went to Usāmah and said, "Speak to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw that, he stood up to give a sermon and said:

"Why do you press me so much concerning one of the prescribed punishments of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that has befallen one of the female servants of Allah? By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, if Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah, had committed what this woman committed, Muhammad would cut off her hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man who had had intercourse with his wife's slave girl was brought before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he did not apply the prescribed punishment to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stoned two Jews, and I was among those who stoned them. I saw him [the man] shielding her [the woman] from the stones.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stoned a Jewish man and a Jewish woman.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If I were to stone anyone without proof, I would stone so-and-so, for suspicion has become evident in her speech, her appearance, and in those who enter upon her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the one who does the deed of the people of Lūṭ, the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Stone the one above and the one below; stone them both."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has intercourse with a close female relative [whom he cannot marry], kill him; and whoever has intercourse with an animal, kill him and kill the animal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If a man says to another man, 'O effeminate one,' flog him twenty lashes; and if a man says to another man, 'O Lūṭī,' flog him twenty lashes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among our houses there was a weak, deformed man. We were suddenly startled to find him with one of the female slaves of the household, committing immorality with her. Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah brought his case to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:
"Flog him with one hundred lashes."
They said, "O Prophet of Allah, he is weaker than that; if we flogged him one hundred lashes he would die." He said:
"Then take for him a palm stalk with one hundred small branches and strike him with it once."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr ibn Samurah ibn Ḥabīb ibn ʿAbd Shams
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I stole a camel belonging to the family of so-and-so, so purify me."
The Prophet ﷺ sent word to them, and they said, "We did lose a camel of ours." So the Prophet ﷺ gave the order, and his hand was cut off.
Thaʿlabah said: I was looking at him when his hand fell, and he was saying, "Praise be to Allah, Who has purified me of you. You wanted to bring my body into the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A slave
from among the slaves of the khumus stole from the khumus. The matter was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he did not cut off his hand, and he said:
"The wealth of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; some of it has stolen from other parts of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The hand is not cut off for the one who betrays a trust, nor for the one who plunders openly, nor for the one who snatches."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not give discretionary punishment of more than ten lashes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever among you commits an offence carrying a prescribed punishment and is punished for it promptly, that is his expiation; otherwise his matter is up to Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the verse on the prescribed punishments was revealed, Abū Thābit Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah, who was a very jealous man, was asked, "What do you think: if you found a man with Umm Thābit, what would you do?" He said, "I would strike both of them with the sword. Should I wait until I bring four witnesses? By then he would have fulfilled his need and gone away.
Or should I say, 'I saw such and such,' and then you would strike me with the prescribed punishment and never accept my testimony again?"
He said: That was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"The sword is sufficient as a witness." Then he said:
"No, but I fear that drunkards and jealous men would rush into doing that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever claims to belong to someone other than his father will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, though its fragrance can be found from a distance of five hundred years' travel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My maternal uncle passed by me—Hushaym, in his narration, named him al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr—and the Prophet ﷺ had tied a banner for him. I said to him, "Where are you heading?" He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to a man who married his father's wife after him, and he ordered me to strike off his neck."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a man,

called ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥunayn, had relations with the slave girl of his wife. The case was brought to al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, who was the governor of Kūfah. He said, "I will judge in your case by the ruling of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: if she had made her lawful for you, I will flog you a hundred lashes, and if she had not made her lawful for you, I will stone you with stones."
They found that she had made her lawful for him, so he flogged him a hundred lashes.
Qatādah said: I wrote to Ḥabīb ibn Sālim, and he wrote back to me with this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man was killed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The killer was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, who handed him over to the guardian of the slain man. The killer said, "O Messenger of Allah, no, by Allah, I did not intend to kill him."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the guardian of the slain man:
"If he is telling the truth and you then kill him, you will enter the Fire." So he let him go.
He said: He had been bound with a leather strap, so he went out dragging his strap, and he was called Dhū al-Nisʿah (the man of the strap).
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever kills his slave, we will kill him; whoever cuts off his nose, we will cut off his nose; and whoever castrates him, we will castrate him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"For the blood money for accidental killing: twenty ḥiqqah camels, twenty jadhaʿah camels, twenty bint makhāḍ camels, twenty bint labūn camels, and twenty male ibn makhāḍ camels."
And this is also the statement of ʿAbdullāh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There are two qualities that no Muslim man will keep up without entering Paradise. They are easy, yet few act upon them: to glorify Allah after every prayer ten times, to praise Him ten times, and to declare His greatness ten times."
He said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ counting them on his hand. He said:

"That is one hundred and fifty on the tongue and one thousand five hundred on the Scale. And when you take to your bed, you glorify Him, declare His greatness, and praise Him a hundred times; that is a hundred on the tongue and a thousand on the Scale. So which of you commits two thousand five hundred bad deeds in a day and night?"
They said: "And how is it that one does not keep up with them?" He said:
"Satan comes to one of you while he is in his prayer and says, 'Remember this, remember that,'
until he finishes, and perhaps he does not do it. And he comes to him while he is in his bed and keeps putting him to sleep until he sleeps."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
Shuʿbah and al-Thawrī also narrated this hadith from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib.
And al-Aʿmash narrated this hadith from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib in abbreviated form.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ never left my house without raising his gaze to the sky and saying:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from going astray or being led astray, from slipping or being made to slip, from wronging or being wronged, from acting ignorantly or having ignorance directed at me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah,
that al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām
asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "How does the revelation come to you?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest on me; then it departs from me, and I have retained what was said. And sometimes the angel appears to me as a man and speaks to me, and I retain what he says."
ʿĀʾishah said: I certainly saw it descend upon him on a very cold day, then depart from him, while his forehead was dripping with sweat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ. Transfer of chains: And Ādam narrated to us,
who said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Anas,
who said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"None of you truly believes until I am more beloved to him than his father, his child, and all people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet; he said, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"When a Muslim spends on his family, seeking reward from Allah for it,
it counts as charity (ṣadaqah) for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, "Why is it that I do not hear you narrating from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as I hear Ibn Masʿūd and so-and-so and so-and-so?" He said, "Indeed, I have not been apart from him since I accepted Islam, but I heard one statement from him; he said:
'Whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: [She] — may Allah be pleased with her — mentioned the women of the Ansār, praised them, and said good things about them. She said: "When Sūrat an-Nūr was revealed, they went to their waist-wrappers (or: their wrappers — Abū Kāmil was unsure), tore them, and made them into head coverings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When [the verse] "…let them draw their cloaks over themselves" was revealed, the women of the Anṣār came out as though there were crows on their heads, because of the cloaks [they wore].
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah] — may Allah be pleased with her — [reported] that Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr
entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wearing thin garments, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from her and said:
"O Asmāʾ, when a woman reaches the age of menstruation, it is not appropriate that anything of her be seen except this and this."
And he pointed to his face and his hands.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to Fāṭimah with a slave whom he had given to her. [The narrator] said: Fāṭimah — may Allah be pleased with her — was wearing a garment such that when she covered her head with it, it did not reach her feet, and when she covered her feet with it, it did not reach her head. When the Prophet ﷺ saw the difficulty she was facing, he said:
"There is no harm for you; he is only your father and your servant."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In this account: It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, he will die of hunger then!" So he permitted him to enter twice each week, to ask [for food], and then return.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "And tell the believing women to lower their gaze…" — the verse. This was abrogated, and an exception was made from it: "And women of old age who have no hope of marriage…" — the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"When one of you marries his slave man to his slave woman, he should not look at her private parts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"When one of you marries his servant — his slave or his hired worker — [to his female slave], he should not look at what is below the navel and above the knee."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered upon her while she was putting on her head covering, and he said:
"[Wrap it] one turn, not two."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fine Egyptian cloths were brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he gave me one of them and said:
"Split it into two pieces; cut one of them as a shirt, and give the other to your wife to use as a head covering."
When he turned away, he said:
"And tell your wife to put another garment beneath it so that it does not show the shape [of her body]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Maʿmar said: Az-Zuhrī used to reject tanning and say, "It may be used in any case."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, during the expedition of Tabūk, came to a house where a water-skin was hanging. He asked for water, and they said, "O Messenger of Allah, it is from a dead animal." He said: "Its tanning is its purification."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not ride on silk saddle-cloths, nor on leopard-skin saddle covers."
He said: Muʿāwiyah was not accused [of untruthfulness] in narrating from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Abū Saʿīd said to us: Abū Dāwūd said to us: Abū al-Muʿtamir's name is Yazīd ibn Ṭahmān; he used to live in al-Ḥīrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is from the Sunnah, when a man sits, that he take off his sandals and place them by his side.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw a group of travelers from the people of Yemen whose saddles were made of leather, and he said: "Whoever would like to see the group most resembling the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, let him look at these."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ ordered ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — may Allah be pleased with him — at the time of the Conquest, while he was at al-Baṭḥāʾ, to go to the Kaʿbah and erase every image in it. The Prophet ﷺ did not enter it until every image in it had been erased.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ travelled to Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd while he was in Egypt, and came to him and said: "I have not come to you as a visitor, but you and I heard a ḥadīth from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I hoped you would have knowledge of it."
He said, "What is it?" He said, "Such and such." He said, "Why do I see you disheveled when you are the governor of the land?" He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to forbid us from much luxury."
He said, "Why do I not see any shoes on you?" He said, "The Prophet ﷺ used to command us to go barefoot at times."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had a container of perfume from which he would apply fragrance.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has hair, let him honor it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman

came to ʿĀʾishah — may Allah be pleased with her — and asked her about dyeing with henna. She said, "There is no harm in it, but I dislike it; my beloved, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, disliked its smell."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah] — may Allah be pleased with her — [said] that Hind bint ʿUtbah
said, "O Prophet of Allah, take my pledge." He said:
"I will not take your pledge until you change your hands, as if they were the paws of a predator."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sister of ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan said: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a son of mine who had not yet eaten food, and he urinated on him. So he called for water and sprinkled it over [the spot].
She said: And I entered upon him with a son of mine whose throat I had treated by pressing on it because of the uvula ailment, and he said:

"Why do you torment your children by pressing on their throats like this? Use this Indian aloeswood, for in it are seven cures, among them [the cure for] pleurisy. It is taken through the nose for the uvula ailment, and it is administered at the side of the mouth for pleurisy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh, may Allah be pleased with them both, visited al-Muqannaʿ and then said: I will not leave until you have been cupped, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Indeed, in it is a cure."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no ruqyah [treatment] except for the evil eye or a poisonous sting.
I mentioned this to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and he said: Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The nations were shown to me.
A prophet passed by with a small group of followers, and another prophet passed by with one or two,
and another prophet had no one with him,
until a great multitude was shown to me.
I said: What is this? Is this my nation? It was said: This is Moses and his people.
Then it was said: Look at the horizon.
And there was a multitude filling the horizon.

Then it was said to me: Look here and there, in the regions of the sky. And there was a multitude that had filled the horizon. It was said: This is your nation, and seventy thousand of them will enter Paradise without reckoning."
Then he went inside and did not explain it to them, so the people began to discuss it and said: We are the ones who believed in Allah and followed His Messenger,
so we are they, or else our children who were born in Islam, for we were born in the time of ignorance.
When this reached the Prophet ﷺ, he came out and said: "They are those who do not seek ruqyah, do not believe in bad omens,
and do not cauterize, and who put their trust in their Lord."
ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan said: Am I one of them, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "Yes."
Then another man stood up and said: Am I one of them? He said: "ʿUkkāshah has beaten you to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAbd
al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās,
that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
set out for Syria, and when he reached Sargh, the commanders of the armies, Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ and his companions, met him and informed him that the plague had broken out in Syria.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: ʿUmar said, "Call for me the earliest Emigrants."

So I called them, and he consulted them and informed them that the plague had broken out in Syria. They differed: some of them said, "You have set out for a purpose, and we do not think you should turn back from it."
Others said, "You have with you the rest of the people and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we do not think you should bring them into this plague."
He said, "Leave me."
Then he said, "Call for me the Helpers." So I called them for him, and he consulted them, and they followed the path of the Emigrants and differed just as they had differed.
He said, "Leave me."
Then he said, "Call for me whoever is here of the elders of Quraysh, from those who emigrated at the time of the Conquest."
So I called them, and not two of them differed with him. They said, "We think you should return with the people and not bring them into this plague."
So ʿUmar announced to the people, "I am leaving in the morning on my mount, so be ready in the morning to do likewise."

Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ said, "Are you fleeing from the decree of Allah?" ʿUmar said, "If only someone other than you had said it, O Abū ʿUbaydah!" — and ʿUmar disliked disagreeing with him — "Yes, we flee from the decree of Allah to the decree of Allah. Do you not see that if you had camels and went down into a valley with two sides, one fertile and the other barren, would it not be that if you grazed them on the fertile side you would graze them by the decree of Allah, and if you grazed them on the barren side you would graze them by the decree of Allah?" He said: Then ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf came, having been absent attending to some need of his, and he said, "I have some knowledge about this. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'If you hear of it in a land, do not go to it; and if it breaks out in a land while you are in it, do not leave in flight from it.'"
He said: So ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb praised Allah and then departed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ came upon one of the Arab tribes, and the tribe did not extend hospitality to them.
While they were like that, the chief of that tribe was stung, and they said, "Do you have any medicine or anyone who can perform ruqyah?" [The Companions] said, "You did not extend hospitality to us,
and we will not do it unless you set a reward for us."
So they set a flock of sheep for them.
Then one of them began reciting Umm al-Qurʾān [al-Fātiḥah], gathering his saliva and spitting, and [the man] recovered. They brought the sheep,
but they said, "We will not take them until we ask the Prophet ﷺ." So they asked him, and he laughed and said:
"How did you know that it is a ruqyah? Take them,
and set aside a share for me with you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered his place of prayer and saw some people who seemed to be laughing excessively. He said:

"If you had remembered more often the destroyer of pleasures, it would have distracted you from what I see. So remember often the destroyer of pleasures: death. For no day passes over the grave except that it speaks, saying: 'I am the house of exile, I am the house of loneliness, I am the house of dust, and I am the house of worms.'

When a believing servant is buried, the grave says to him: 'Welcome, and greetings! Of all those who walked upon my back, you were the dearest to me. Now that I have been given charge of you today and you have come to me, you will see how I treat you.'
He said: It widens for him as far as his eyes can see, and a door to Paradise is opened for him.

And when a wicked servant or a disbeliever is buried, the grave says to him: 'No welcome and no greetings! Of all those who walked upon my back, you were the most hateful to me. Now that I have been given charge of you today and you have come to me, you will see how I treat you.'
He said: It closes in on him until it presses together over him and his ribs become interlaced."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ demonstrated with his fingers, putting some of them inside others. He said:

"And Allah appoints over him seventy serpents; if just one of them were to breathe upon the earth, it would never grow anything for as long as the world lasts. They bite him and claw him until he is brought to the Reckoning."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The grave is only one of the gardens of Paradise or one of the pits of the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever asks Allah for Paradise three times, Paradise says: 'O Allah, admit him into Paradise.'
And whoever seeks refuge from the Fire three times, the Fire says: 'O Allah, protect him from the Fire.'"

He said: Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq narrated this hadith in this way from Abū Isḥāq, from Burayd ibn Abī Maryam, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, similarly. It has also been narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from Burayd ibn Abī Maryam, from Anas ibn Mālik as his own statement (mawqūf).
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl al-Murādī, and he said to me: "What brings you?" I said: "The pursuit of knowledge."
He said: "It has reached me that the angels lower their wings for the seeker of knowledge, pleased with what he does."

I said: "Something has been troubling my mind, concerning wiping over the leather socks. Have you memorized anything from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it?" He said: "Yes. When we were on a journey, or travelling, he commanded us not to take off our socks for three days, except because of major impurity, but not because of defecation, urination, or sleep."

I said: "Have you memorized anything from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about love?" He said: "Yes. We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on one of his journeys, when a man at the back of the group called out to him in a loud voice, a coarse, rough Bedouin, saying: 'O Muhammad! O Muhammad!'
The people said to him: 'Be quiet! You have been forbidden from this.'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ answered him in a voice like his own: 'Here I am!' The man said: 'A man loves a people but has not yet joined them.'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'A person is with those whom he loves.'"

Zirr said: He kept on narrating to me until he told me that Allah has made in the west a door, whose width is a journey of seventy years, for repentance; it is not closed until the sun rises from its direction. That is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
"On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith..." the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They did not count [the years] from the sending of the Prophet ﷺ, nor from his death;
they counted only from his arrival in Medina.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They are the People of the Book. They divided it into parts,
believing in some of it and disbelieving in some of it.
He meant the saying of Allah, the Exalted: {Those who have broken the Qur'an into parts.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: It passed through the hands of more than ten owners, from one master to another.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I am from Rāmhurmuz.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The interval between ʿĪsā and Muḥammad ﷺ was six hundred years.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in any expedition he undertook, except the expedition of Tabūk,
though I did stay behind from the expedition of Badr,
and no one who stayed behind from it was rebuked.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had only set out seeking the caravan of Quraysh,
until Allah brought them and their enemy together without a prior appointment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I witnessed [a scene] of al-Miqdād. (Another chain:) Ḥamdān ibn ʿUmar narrated to me: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us: al-Ashjaʿī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Mukhāriq, from Ṭāriq, from ʿAbdullāh, who said: Al-Miqdād said on the day of Badr: "O Messenger of Allah, we will not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Mūsā: {So go, you and your Lord, and fight; we are sitting right here.} Rather, go forward, and we are with you."
It was as though [worry] was lifted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar and I were considered too young on the day of Badr.
The Emigrants on the day of Badr numbered a little over sixty,
and the Anṣār a little over two hundred and forty.
label: machine translation

segments_en: At Badr.
He means the hadith of the two sons of ʿAfrāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: This verse was revealed about us: {These are two opponents who disputed concerning their Lord.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man asked al-Barāʾ while I was listening,
"Did ʿAlī take part in Badr?" He said: He fought in single combat and provided support.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Zubayr had three sword wounds,
one of them on his shoulder.
He said: I used to put my fingers into them.
He said: Two were struck at Badr,
and one on the day of Yarmūk.
ʿUrwah said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān said to me when ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr was killed: O ʿUrwah,
do you recognize the sword of al-Zubayr? I said: Yes.
He said: What is [notable] in it? I said: It has a notch which it got on the day of Badr. He said: You have spoken truly.
"Their swords have notches from striking the battalions." Then he returned it to ʿUrwah.
Hishām said: We valued it among us at three thousand, and one of us took it,
and I wish I had been the one to take it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sword of al-Zubayr was decorated with silver.
Hishām said: And the sword of ʿUrwah was decorated with silver.
label: machine translation

segments_en: By Allah, they are the disbelievers of Quraysh.
ʿAmr said: They are Quraysh, and Muḥammad ﷺ is the blessing of Allah. {And they led their people to the home of destruction.} He said: The Fire, on the day of Badr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said: I was in the ranks on the day of Badr when I looked around,
and there, on my right and on my left, were two young lads,
and I felt unsure of being safe with them beside me,
when one of them said to me secretly, without his companion hearing: O uncle, show me Abū Jahl.
I said: O son of my brother,
what will you do with him? He said: I have promised Allah that if I see him, I will kill him or die trying.
Then the other said the same to me secretly, without his companion hearing. He said: I was never so pleased to be between two other men.
So I pointed him out to them,
and they attacked him like two falcons until they struck him down,
and they were the two sons of ʿAfrāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was mentioned to Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, who had fought at Badr, fell ill on a Friday. He rode to him after the day had advanced and the Friday prayer was near, and he left the Friday prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And
Rifāʿah was one of the people of Badr,
and Rāfiʿ was one of the people of ʿAqabah.
Rāfiʿ used to say to his son: It would not please me to have witnessed Badr instead of ʿAqabah. He said: Jibrīl asked the Prophet ﷺ about this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: An angel asked the Prophet ﷺ. And from Yaḥyā:
Yazīd ibn al-Hād informed him that he was with him on the day Muʿādh told him this hadith,
and Yazīd said: Muʿādh said: The questioner was Jibrīl, peace be upon him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said on the day of Badr:
"This is Jibrīl, holding the head of his horse, equipped with the gear of war."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Zayd died without leaving any offspring, and he had fought at Badr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Zubayr said: On the day of Badr I met ʿUbaydah ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, fully armored so that nothing of him could be seen but his eyes,
and he was known as Abū Dhāt al-Karsh.
He said: I am Abū Dhāt al-Karsh.
So I charged at him with a short spear,
and thrust it into his eye, and he died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn al-Aṣbahānī passed it on to us, having heard it from Ibn Maʿqil,
that ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said the takbīr over Sahl ibn Ḥunayf and said: He fought at Badr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The people should be led in prayer by the one who is most versed in the Book of Allah. If they are equal in recitation, then by the one most knowledgeable about the Sunnah. If they are equal in the Sunnah, then by the one who emigrated earliest. If they are equal in emigration, then by the eldest in age. A man must not lead another in prayer in the latter's domain of authority, nor sit in his house on his place of honor, except with his permission."
Maḥmūd ibn Ghaylān said: Ibn Numayr said in his narration: "the earliest of them in age."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I accompanied Ibn ʿUmar on the road to Makkah. He said: He led us in the Zuhr prayer, two rak'ahs, then he turned and we turned with him until he came to his lodging and sat down, and we sat with him. He happened to glance toward where he had prayed and saw some people standing. He said: "What are these people doing?" I said: "They are praying voluntary prayers."

He said: "Had I been going to pray voluntary prayers, I would have completed my prayer, O son of my brother. I accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on journeys and he did not add to two rak'ahs until Allah took him. I accompanied Abū Bakr and he did not add to two rak'ahs until Allah took him. I accompanied ʿUmar and he did not add to two rak'ahs until Allah took him. Then I accompanied ʿUthmān and he did not add to two rak'ahs until Allah took him. And Allah has said: 'There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined Zuhr with ʿAṣr and Maghrib with ʿIshāʾ in Madinah, without there being fear or rain.
In the narration of Wakīʿ, [the narrator] said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "Why did he do that?" He said: "So that he would not cause hardship to his Ummah."
And in the narration of Abū Muʿāwiyah: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked: "What did he intend by that?" He said: "He intended not to cause hardship to his Ummah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man entered the mosque while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the dawn prayer. He prayed two rak'ahs at the side of the mosque, then joined the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he said:
"O so-and-so, which of the two prayers do you count as yours: your prayer alone, or your prayer with us?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When one of you enters the mosque, let him send greetings of peace upon the Prophet ﷺ and say: 'O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.' And when he leaves, let him send greetings of peace upon the Prophet and say: 'O Allah, protect me from the accursed Satan.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, on Friday there is an hour in which a servant asks Allah for nothing except that Allah gives it to him."
They said: "O Messenger of Allah, which hour is it?" He said:
"From when the prayer is begun until it is finished."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever performs ablution and does it well,
then comes to the Friday prayer,
draws near, remains silent, and listens,
he will be forgiven what is between that Friday and the next Friday,
and three additional days.
But whoever touches the pebbles has engaged in idle talk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to pray the prayers with the Prophet ﷺ, and his prayer was moderate and his sermon was moderate.
And in the narration of Abū Bakr, from Zakariyyāʾ, from Simāk:
label: machine translation

segments_en: Marwān appointed Abū Hurayrah as deputy over Madinah and set out for Makkah. Abū Hurayrah led us in the Friday prayer and, after Sūrat al-Jumuʿah, recited in the second rak'ah: "When the hypocrites come to you." He said: I met Abū Hurayrah as he finished and said to him: "You recited two sūrahs that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib used to recite in Kūfah."
Abū Hurayrah said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite them on Friday."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he prayed during an eclipse; he recited, then bowed, then recited, then bowed, then recited, then bowed, then recited, then bowed, then prostrated.
He said: And the other [rak'ah] was like it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over a funeral, and I memorized from his supplication that he said:

"O Allah, forgive him, have mercy on him, grant him well-being, and pardon him. Honor his place of arrival, make his entrance spacious, and wash him with water, snow, and hail. Cleanse him of sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt. Give him an abode better than his abode, a family better than his family, and a spouse better than his spouse. Admit him into Paradise and protect him from the punishment of the grave" or "from the punishment of the Fire."
He said: So much so that I wished I were that deceased person.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Hayyāj al-Asadī said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said to me: "Shall I not send you on the mission on which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me? Do not leave any statue without effacing it, nor any raised grave without leveling it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people
of the Anṣār said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when Allah granted to His Messenger ﷺ the spoils of Hawāzin what He granted,
and he began giving a hundred camels to men of Quraysh, they said, "May Allah forgive the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he gives to Quraysh and leaves us,
while our swords are still dripping with their blood." Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was told of what they had said,
so he sent for the Anṣār
and gathered them in a leather tent,
and he did not call anyone else with them.
When they had gathered, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to them and said:
"What is this report that has reached me from you?"
Their men of understanding said to him, "As for our people of sound judgment, O Messenger of Allah, they said nothing.
But some of our young men said, 'May Allah forgive the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he gives to Quraysh and leaves the Anṣār,
while our swords are still dripping with their blood.'"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I give to men who have only recently left disbelief.
Are you not pleased that the people take away the wealth, while you return to your homes with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
By Allah, what you take back is better than what they take back."
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, we are pleased." He said to them:
"You will see after me severe favoritism,
so be patient until you meet Allah and His Messenger ﷺ at the Cistern."
Anas said: But we were not patient.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Az-Zubayr married me,
and he had no wealth on earth, no slave,
and nothing at all except a water-carrying camel and his horse.
I would feed his horse, draw water,
stitch his bucket and knead dough,
but I did not bake well.
Some neighbor women of mine from the Anṣār used to bake for me, and they were women of honesty.
I used to carry date stones on my head from az-Zubayr's land, which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had granted him,
and it was about two-thirds of a farsakh from me.
One day I came with the date stones on my head and met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a group of the Anṣār. He called me, then said, "Ikh! Ikh!" to make me ride behind him.
But I was shy to travel with the men,
and I remembered az-Zubayr and his jealous protectiveness,
and he was the most protective of people.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ realized that I was shy, so he went on.
I came to az-Zubayr and said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ met me while I had the date stones on my head,
with a group of his Companions. He made his camel kneel for me to ride,
but I was shy before him and I knew your protectiveness."
He said, "By Allah, your carrying the date stones was harder on me than your riding with him."
She said: Until after that Abū Bakr sent me a servant who relieved me of looking after the horse, and it was as if he had set me free.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar

ibn al-Khaṭṭāb expelled the Jews and Christians from the land of the Hijaz. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gained victory over Khaybar, he wished to expel the Jews from it. When he conquered it, the land belonged to Allah, His Messenger and the Muslims, so he wished to expel the Jews from it. The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to let them remain there on condition that they would work it, and they would have half of the fruit. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them:
"We will let you remain on that basis for as long as we wish."
So they remained there until ʿUmar expelled them to Taymāʾ and Jericho.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the expedition of Tabūk while he was in a tent of leather. I sat in the courtyard of the tent, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Enter, O ʿAwf."
I said, "All of me, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "All of you." Then he said:
"O ʿAwf, remember six things before the Hour: the first of them is my death."
He said: I was struck with intense grief at that. Then he said:

"Say: one. Then the conquest of Jerusalem; then a disease that will spread among you, by which Allah will make martyrs of your children and yourselves and purify your wealth; then wealth will be so abundant among you that a man will be given a hundred dinars and still remain angry; then a tribulation among you that will not leave a single Muslim house without entering it; then there will be a truce between you and the Banū al-Aṣfar, but they will betray you and march against you under eighty banners, under each banner twelve thousand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And she was
a Companion who had kept company with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"When a servant has been granted a rank by Allah that he has not reached through his deeds, Allah afflicts him in his body, or in his wealth, or in his children."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say, not once or twice:
"When a servant used to do righteous deeds and illness or travel keeps him from them, there is recorded for him the like of the righteous deeds he used to do while healthy and resident."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited me while I was ill and said:
"Rejoice, Umm al-ʿAlāʾ! For the illness of a Muslim removes his sins by Allah, just as the fire removes the impurities of gold and silver."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: O Messenger of Allah, I know the most severe verse in the Qurʾān. He said:
"Which verse, which verse, ʿĀʾishah?"
She said: The words of Allah, the Exalted: {Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it}. He said:
"Do you not know, ʿĀʾishah, that when a believer is struck by a misfortune or a thorn, he is repaid for his worst deeds? And whoever is called to account is punished."
She said: Does Allah not say: {Then he will be given an easy reckoning}? He said:
"That is the presentation [of deeds], ʿĀʾishah. Whoever is questioned closely in the reckoning is punished."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to visit ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy in the illness in which he died. When he entered upon him, he recognized death in him and said:
"I used to forbid you from loving the Jews."
He said: Asʿad ibn Zurārah hated them, and what came of it? When he died, his son came and said: O Messenger of Allah, ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy has died, so give me your shirt to shroud him in it.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took off his shirt and gave it to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever performs ablution and does it well, then visits his Muslim brother seeking reward from Allah, will be distanced from Hell by a journey of seventy autumns."
I said: O Abū Ḥamzah, what is an autumn? He said: A year.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no man who visits a sick person in the evening except that seventy thousand angels go out with him, asking forgiveness for him until morning, and he will have an autumn's [journey] in Paradise. And whoever visits him in the morning, seventy thousand angels go out with him, asking forgiveness for him until evening, and he will have an autumn's [journey] in Paradise.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāfiʿ was a servant of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī. He said: Abū Mūsā came to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī to visit him in his illness.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited me because of a pain I had in my eye.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"When a man comes to visit a sick person, let him say: O Allah, heal Your servant, that he may strike an enemy for You or walk to a funeral for You."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sudden death is a seizure of regret."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He was] an ally of Banū Zuhrah, and one of the companions of Abū Hurayrah, [narrating] from Abū Hurayrah, who said:

The sons of al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir ibn Nawfal bought Khubayb, for Khubayb had killed al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir on the day of Badr. Khubayb remained with them as a captive until they agreed to kill him. He borrowed a razor from the daughter of al-Ḥārith to shave with, and she lent it to him. A young son of hers crawled to him while she was unaware, until she came and found him seated on his thigh with the razor in his hand. She was terrified, and he noticed her terror. He said: Are you afraid that I will kill him? I would never do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When death came to him, he called for new clothes and put them on. Then he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The dead person will be resurrected in the clothes in which he dies."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever's last words are 'There is no god but Allah' will enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When any of you is struck by a calamity, let him say: {Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return.} O Allah, with You I seek reward for my calamity, so reward me for it and replace it for me with something better."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us from wailing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the woman who wails and the woman who listens to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He was] an official of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz at al-Rabadhah. Usayd ibn Abī Usayd narrated to me, from a woman,

of those who gave the pledge, who said: Among the good things in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a pledge from us, that we would not disobey him in them, was that we would not scratch our faces, nor call out for destruction, nor tear our garments, nor let our hair loose.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said. And Ādam ibn Abī Iyās narrated to us: Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah narrated to us: Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl al-ʿAdawī narrated to us: Abū Ṣāliḥ as-Sammān narrated to us: I saw Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī on a Friday praying toward something that screened him from the people,
and a young man from the Banū Abī Muʿayṭ wanted to pass in front of him, so Abū Saʿīd pushed him in the chest.
The young man looked and found no way through except in front of him,
so he went back to pass, and Abū Saʿīd pushed him harder than the first time.
The young man then spoke ill of Abū Saʿīd,
and he went in to Marwān and complained to him about what he had met with from Abū Saʿīd.
Abū Saʿīd followed him in to Marwān, who said: What is the matter between you and your nephew, Abū Saʿīd? He said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
"When one of you prays toward something that screens him from the people,
and someone wants to pass in front of him, let him push him away.
If he refuses, let him fight him,
for he is only a devil."
