{ḥaṣab} means firewood in Abyssinian.
Another said: {aḥissū} means expect it, from aḥsastu; {khāmidīn} means extinguished, lifeless.
Ḥaṣīd means utterly uprooted; it is used for one, two, or many.
{lā yastaḥsirūn} means they do not grow weary; from it comes ḥasīr, and one says ḥasartu baʿīrī [I exhausted my camel]. ʿAmīq means far away. {Nukisū} means they were turned back.
{The craft of garments (labūs)} means coats of armor.
{They fragmented their affair} means they differed.
Al-ḥasīs, al-ḥiss, al-jaras, and al-hams are the same,
and it is from faint sound. {Ādhannāka} means We informed you; {ādhantukum}: when you inform someone, you and he are on equal footing, and you have not betrayed [him].
Mujāhid said: {perhaps you will be asked} means you will understand; {irtaḍā} means He was pleased; {at-tamāthīl} means the idols; as-sijill means the scroll.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the pre-Islamic period we used to say, when a clan became numerous: the sons of so-and-so have become powerful.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with them both, said: On the Day of Resurrection people will kneel on their knees,
every community following its prophet,
saying: O so-and-so, intercede!
until intercession reaches the Prophet ﷺ. That is the day on which Allah will raise him to the Praiseworthy Station.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and Fāṭimah at night and said: "Will you not pray?"
{Conjecturing about the unseen} means it was not clear.
{Furuṭan} means regret; {its enclosure (surādiq)} is like a surādiq,
and the walled enclosure that surrounds tents.
{Yuḥāwiruhu} is from muḥāwarah [conversation]; {But as for me, He is Allah, my Lord}, meaning: but I—He is Allah, my Lord; then the alif was dropped and one nūn was merged into the other.
{Zalaqan} means [ground] on which no foot stays firm.
{There, the authority (walāyah)} is the verbal noun of walī.
{ʿUqban}, ʿāqibah, ʿuqbā, and ʿuqbah are the same, and it means the Hereafter. Qubulan, qibalan, and qubulan mean anew. {Liyudḥiḍū} means to remove; ad-daḥḍ means slipperiness.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked my father: {Say, shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?}—are they the Ḥarūriyyah? He said: No,
they are the Jews and the Christians.
As for the Jews, they denied Muḥammad ﷺ; and as for the Christians, they disbelieved in Paradise and said there is no food or drink in it.
The Ḥarūriyyah are those who break Allah's covenant after its confirmation,
and Saʿd used to call them the defiantly disobedient.
label: machine translation

segments_en: {And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge}: he said, a man would come to Madinah,
and if his wife bore a boy
and his mares foaled, he would say, this is a good religion.
But if his wife did not bear and his mares did not foal, he would say, this is a bad religion.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah,

what if a man finds another man with his wife; should he kill him, so that you would kill him [in retaliation]? Or what should he do? Then Allah revealed about them what is mentioned in the Qurʾān regarding mutual cursing (liʿān).
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"A ruling has been made concerning you and your wife." He said: So they performed liʿān,
and I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He separated from her, and it became the established practice that the two who perform liʿān are separated. She was pregnant,
and he denied her pregnancy, and her son used to be called by her name.
Then the practice continued regarding inheritance: that he inherits from her,
and she inherits from him what Allah has prescribed for her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿĀʾishah was accused, she fell down unconscious.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She would recite: {when you received it with your tongues}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Shortly before her death, Ibn ʿAbbās asked permission to see ʿĀʾishah,
while she was overcome [by illness]. She said: I fear he will praise me.
It was said: He is the cousin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and one of the prominent Muslims.
She said: Let him enter.
He said: How do you find yourself? She said: Well, if I have been God-fearing.
He said: You are well, Allah willing. You are the wife of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he married no other virgin besides you,
and your innocence was revealed from heaven.
Ibn al-Zubayr entered after him, and she said: Ibn ʿAbbās came in and praised me, and I wish I were something forgotten and discarded.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, will see his father on the Day of Resurrection with dust and darkness upon him."
Al-ghabarah is the same as al-qatarah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibrāhīm will meet his father and say: My Lord, You promised me that You would not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected. Allah will say: I have forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: {He will surely return you to a place of return}: he said, to Mecca.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I said, O Messenger of Allah,
both the righteous and the wicked enter upon you,
so if only you would order the Mothers of the Believers to observe the veil.
Then Allah revealed the verse of the veil.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hilāl ibn Umayyah, one of the three whose repentance Allah accepted, came in the evening from his land and found a man with his wife. He saw with his own eyes and heard with his own ears, but he did not provoke him until morning. Then he went early to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I came to my family in the evening and found a man with them. I saw with my own eyes and heard with my own ears." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked what he had brought, and it weighed heavily upon him. Then it was revealed: {And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them...} both verses. Then the distress was lifted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said,
"Glad tidings, O Hilāl! Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made for you a relief and a way out."
Hilāl said, "I was hoping for that from my Lord."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Send for her."

So she came, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the verses to them both, reminded them, and told them that the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe than the punishment of this world. Hilāl said, "By Allah, I have told the truth about her." She said, "He has lied."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Let them swear the oaths of condemnation (liʿān) between them."
So Hilāl was told, "Testify."

He testified four times by Allah that he was among the truthful. When it came to the fifth, he was told, "O Hilāl, fear Allah, for the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter, and this is the one that makes the punishment obligatory upon you."
He said, "By Allah, Allah will not punish me for it, just as He did not have me flogged for it."
So he testified the fifth time that the curse of Allah be upon him if he were among the liars. Then she was told, "Testify."

She testified four times by Allah that he was among the liars. When it came to the fifth, she was told, "Fear Allah, for the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter, and this is the one that makes the punishment obligatory upon you."

She hesitated for a while, then said, "By Allah, I will not disgrace my people." So she testified the fifth time that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he were among the truthful. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them, and ruled that her child would not be attributed to a father, that she would not be accused, and that her child would not be accused; and whoever accused her or her child would be liable for the prescribed punishment. He also ruled that she would have no housing or maintenance from him, because they were separated without a divorce and she was not a widow. And he said,

"If she gives birth to him reddish-fair, with thin hips and slender calves, then he belongs to Hilāl. But if she gives birth to him dark-skinned, curly-haired, handsome, with full calves and large buttocks, then he belongs to the one she was accused with." She gave birth to him dark-skinned, curly-haired, handsome, with full calves and large buttocks. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Were it not for the oaths, I would have had a matter to settle with her."
ʿIkrimah said: After that he became a governor over Muḍar, and he was not attributed to any father.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zayd ibn Ḥārithah went out to Makkah and came back with the daughter of Ḥamzah. Jaʿfar said, "I will take her. I have more right to her; she is my cousin's daughter, and her maternal aunt is with me, and the maternal aunt is a mother."
ʿAlī said, "I have more right to her; she is my cousin's daughter, and the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is with me, and she has more right to her."
Zayd said, "I have more right to her. I went out for her, travelled, and brought her back."
Then the Prophet ﷺ came out, and he mentioned a hadith. He said,
"As for the girl, I judge that she go to Jaʿfar, to be with her maternal aunt, for the maternal aunt is a mother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this report, though not in full, he said: He ruled that she go to Jaʿfar, and he said,
"Her maternal aunt is with him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When we left Makkah, the daughter of Ḥamzah followed us, calling, "O uncle! O uncle!"
ʿAlī took her, held her by the hand, and said, "Take your cousin's daughter."
So I carried her. Then he related the report. He said: Jaʿfar said, "She is my cousin's daughter, and her maternal aunt is my wife."
The Prophet ﷺ ruled that she go to her maternal aunt, and he said,
"The maternal aunt is in the position of the mother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She was divorced during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and there was no waiting period (ʿiddah) for a divorced woman. So when Asmāʾ was divorced, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the waiting period for divorce, and she was the first for whom the waiting period for divorced women was revealed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah was asked, "Have you not seen what Fāṭimah said?" She said, "There is no good for her in mentioning that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning Fāṭimah's leaving [her house], she said: "That was only due to bad character."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Madinah and was brought to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab. I said, "Fāṭimah bint Qays was divorced and left her house." Saʿīd said, "That is a woman who tempted people. She had a sharp tongue, so she was placed with Ibn Umm Maktūm, the blind man."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz

once delayed the prayer, so ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr came in to see him and told him that al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah once delayed the prayer while he was in Kūfah, so Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī came in to see him and said, "What is this, Mughīrah? Do you not know that Jibrīl came down and prayed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed; then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed; then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed; then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed; then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed; then he said, 'I was commanded with this'?"

ʿUmar said to ʿUrwah, "Be careful about what you report, ʿUrwah! Was it Jibrīl, peace be upon him, who established the time of prayer for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" ʿUrwah said, "That is how Bashīr ibn Abī Masʿūd used to narrate from his father."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Anas ibn Mālik in Damascus and he was weeping. I said, "What makes you weep?" He said, "I do not recognize anything of what I knew except this prayer,
and this prayer has been neglected."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came out when the sun had passed its zenith and prayed the Ẓuhr prayer. When he had given the salām, he stood on the pulpit and mentioned the Hour,
and mentioned that there would be momentous events before it. Then he said:
"Whoever would like to ask about anything, let him ask about it,
for by Allah, you will not ask me about anything but that I will inform you of it,
as long as I am in this place of mine."
Anas said: The people wept greatly,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept on saying, "Ask me."
Anas said: A man stood up to him and said, "Where will my entrance be, Messenger of Allah?" He said, "The Fire."
Then ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah stood up and said, "Who is my father, Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Your father is Ḥudhāfah."
He said: Then he kept on saying, "Ask me, ask me."
Then ʿUmar knelt on his knees and said, "We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muḥammad ﷺ as Messenger."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell silent when ʿUmar said that,
then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, Paradise and the Fire were just now shown to me across the breadth of this wall while I was praying,
and I have never seen the like of today in good and evil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father and I entered
upon Abū Barzah al-Aslamī, and my father said to him, "Tell us how

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the obligatory prayers." He said, "He used to pray the Hajīr, which you call the first prayer, when the sun had declined. He used to pray the ʿAṣr, and then one of us would return to his dwelling at the farthest part of Madinah while the sun was still bright." He said: I forgot what he said about the Maghrib. He said: "He preferred to delay the ʿIshāʾ prayer, which you call the ʿAtamah." He said: "He disliked sleeping before it and talking after it. He would finish the dawn prayer when a man could recognize the one sitting beside him, and he used to recite between sixty and one hundred verses."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Your time span compared to that of the nations that came before you is only from the ʿAṣr prayer until sunset.

Your likeness and the likeness of the Jews and Christians is that of a man who hired workers and said, 'Who will work for me until midday for one qīrāṭ each?' The Jews worked until midday for one qīrāṭ each.
Then he said, 'Who will work for me from midday until the ʿAṣr prayer for one qīrāṭ each?' The Christians worked from midday until the ʿAṣr prayer
for one qīrāṭ each.
Then he said, 'Who will work for me from the ʿAṣr prayer until sunset for two qīrāṭs each?' Indeed, you are those who work from the ʿAṣr prayer until sunset for two qīrāṭs each.
Indeed, yours is the reward twice over.
The Jews and Christians became angry
and said, 'We did more work and received less.'
Allah said, 'Did I wrong you of anything of your right?' They said, 'No.'
He said, 'Then it is My bounty; I give it to whom I will.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this report, he said in it: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him to remove it completely and to wash two or three times. And he related the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman in the state of iḥrām must not wear the face veil, nor wear gloves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāfiʿ, the freed slave of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, narrated to me from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid women, while in iḥrām, from wearing gloves and the face veil, and from wearing garments touched by wars or saffron. After that, she may wear whatever colors of garments she likes: safflower-dyed clothing, silk, jewelry, trousers, a shirt, or leather socks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He felt the cold and said: "Throw a garment over me, Nāfiʿ."
So I threw a burnous over him, and he said: "You throw this over me, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the person in iḥrām to wear it?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to set out with the Prophet ﷺ to Makkah, and we would apply perfumed musk to our foreheads at the time of iḥrām. When one of us sweated, it ran down her face, and the Prophet ﷺ would see it and not forbid her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I mentioned it to Ibn Shihāb, and he said: Sālim ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated to me,
that ʿAbdullāh,

meaning Ibn ʿUmar, used to do that, meaning he would cut the leather socks for a woman in iḥrām. Then Ṣafiyyah bint Abī ʿUbayd narrated to him that ʿĀʾishah narrated to her that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had permitted women to wear leather socks, so he abandoned that practice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made peace with the people of al-Ḥudaybiyah, he made peace with them on the condition that they would not enter it [Makkah] except with the julubbān of weapons. I asked him what the julubbān of weapons was, and he said: "The sheath with what is in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Riders used to pass by us while we were in iḥrām with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they came level with us, one of us would let her outer garment hang down from her head over her face, and when they had passed us, we would uncover it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had himself cupped while he was in iḥrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married me while we were both out of iḥrām, at Sarif.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās was mistaken about the marriage to Maymūnah while he was in iḥrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And al-Ḥārith

was ʿUthmān's deputy over aṭ-Ṭāʾif. He prepared food for ʿUthmān that included partridge, yaʿāqīb, and wild game meat. He said: He sent for ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and the messenger came to him while he was knocking leaves down for his camels. He came shaking the leaves off his hands, and they said to him: Eat.
He said: Feed it to people who are not in iḥrām, for we are in iḥrām.

Then ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I ask you by Allah, is there anyone here from Ashjaʿ? Do you know that a man gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a wild donkey as a gift while he was in iḥrām, and he refused to eat it? They said: Yes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Locusts are from the game of the sea."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came upon a swarm of locusts, and one of our men was striking them with his whip while he was in iḥrām. He was told that this was not proper, so it was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"It is only from the game of the sea."
I heard Abū Dāwūd say: Abū al-Muhazzim is weak, and both hadith are mistaken.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He had suffered an injury to his head, so he shaved it, and the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to offer a sacrificial animal, a cow.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In this account he added:
"Whichever of those you do will suffice for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever has a broken bone, or goes lame, or falls ill." Then he mentioned the same meaning.
Salamah ibn Shabīb said: Maʿmar told us
label: machine translation

segments_en: I set out for ʿUmrah in the year the people of Syria besieged Ibn az-Zubayr in Makkah. Some men of my people sent a sacrificial animal with me. When we reached the Syrians, they prevented us from entering the Sacred Precinct, so I slaughtered the sacrificial animal where I was, then came out of iḥrām and returned. The following year I set out to make up my ʿUmrah, and I went to Ibn ʿAbbās and asked him. He said: Replace the sacrificial animal, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded his Companions to replace the sacrificial animals they had slaughtered in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyah, in the makeup ʿUmrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to leave by the road of ash-Shajarah and enter by the road of al-Muʿarras.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and entered Makkah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the Black Stone and touched it, then circumambulated the House. Then he came to aṣ-Ṣafā and climbed it to where he could see the House, and he raised his hands and began to remember Allah as much as he wished and to supplicate Him. He said: And the Anṣār were below him. Hāshim said: So he supplicated, praised Allah, and prayed for whatever he wished to pray for.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the jizyah from the Zoroastrians of Bahrain, ʿUmar took it from Persia, and ʿUthmān took it from the Persians.
I asked Muhammad about this, and he said: It is [reported by] Mālik, from az-Zuhrī, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, we pass by a people who neither host us nor give us the right that is due to us from them, and we do not take from them."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If they refuse except that you take it by force, then take it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and the swift ones among the people went ahead and hurried to take some of the spoils and cooked [them], while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at the rear of the people. He passed by the cooking pots and ordered that they be overturned. Then he distributed [the spoils] among them, treating one camel as equal to ten sheep.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [This is] like the hadith of Abū Muʿāwiyah, but he did not mention in it "from Jarīr." And this is more authentic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah came to Abū Bakr and said: "Who will inherit from you?" He said: "My family and my children."
She said: "Then why do I not inherit from my father?" Abū Bakr said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'We [prophets] are not inherited from.'
But I will support whomever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to support, and spend on whomever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to spend on."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed Fāṭimah
came to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, asking for her inheritance from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They said: "We heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'I am not inherited from.'"
She said: "By Allah, I will never speak to you two again."
And she died without speaking to them.
ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā said: The meaning of "I will never speak to you two" is: regarding this inheritance, never—[meaning] "You two are truthful."
And this hadith has been narrated through more than one chain from Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, az-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ entered upon him. Then ʿAlī and al-ʿAbbās came, disputing with one another. ʿUmar said to them: "I ask you by Allah, by whose permission the heavens and the earth stand, do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'We are not inherited from; what we leave behind is charity'?" They said: "Yes."
ʿUmar said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, Abū Bakr said: 'I am the guardian of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.'

Then you and this man came to Abū Bakr; you were asking for your inheritance from your nephew, and this man was asking for his wife's inheritance from her father. Abū Bakr said: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"We are not inherited from; what we leave behind is charity."'
And Allah knows that he was truthful, righteous, rightly guided, and a follower of the truth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ on the day of the conquest of Makkah say:
"This [city] will not be raided after today until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I fought alongside the Prophet ﷺ. When dawn broke he would hold back until the sun rose, and when it rose he would fight. When it was midday he would hold back until the sun passed its zenith, and when the sun had passed its zenith he would fight until the afternoon. Then he would hold back until he had prayed the afternoon prayer, then he would fight.
He said: It used to be said that at that time the winds of victory stir, and the believers pray for their armies in their prayers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ went out for some need, he would be pleased to hear "O Rāshid! O Najīḥ!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, meaning:

"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: The one who strives in the cause of Allah is under My guarantee: if I take his soul, I will make him inherit Paradise, and if I return him, I will return him with a reward or spoils."
He said: It is authentic and gharīb through this chain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever fasts a day in the cause of Allah, Allah will place between him and the Fire a trench like the distance between the heaven and the earth."
This hadith is gharīb from the narration of Abū Umāmah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which charity is best. He said:
"The service of a servant in the cause of Allah, or the shade of a tent, or a mature male camel [given] in the cause of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever grows a gray hair in the cause of Allah, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever shoots an arrow in the cause of Allah, it is for him equal to freeing a slave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two eyes the Fire will not touch: an eye that wept from fear of Allah, and an eye that spent the night guarding in the cause of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He is not one of us who incites a woman against her husband, or a slave against his master."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked Ibn ʿUmar, "How many times did you divorce your wife?" He said, "Once."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he

sought a ruling from Ibn ʿAbbās about a slave who was married to a slave woman and divorced her twice, then both were later set free: is it permissible for him to propose to her again? He said, "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled thus."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said in this report, adding:
"And there is no vow except in what is intended for the sake of Allah, the Exalted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd Yazīd, the father of Rukānah and his brothers, divorced Umm Rukānah and married a woman from Muzaynah. She came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "He is of no more use to me than this hair is,"
a hair she took from her head. "So separate me from him." The Prophet ﷺ was seized by zeal, so he called for Rukānah and his brothers, then said to those sitting with him:
"Do you see that so-and-so resembles ʿAbd Yazīd in such and such, and so-and-so resembles him in such and such?" They said, "Yes."
The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAbd Yazīd, "Divorce her."
He did so. Then he said:
"Take back your wife, the mother of Rukānah and his brothers."
He said, "I divorced her three times, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"I know. Take her back."
And he recited: {O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed period.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās when a man came and said that he had divorced his wife three times.
He said: He was silent until I thought he would return her to him.

Then he said, "One of you goes off and commits folly, then says, 'O Ibn ʿAbbās, O Ibn ʿAbbās!' Yet Allah said: {Whoever fears Allah, He will make a way out for him}, and you did not fear Allah, so I find no way out for you. You disobeyed your Lord, and your wife is irrevocably separated from you. And Allah said: {O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them} at the start of their prescribed period."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū
Hurayrah and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ were asked about a virgin
whose husband divorced her three times. All of them said, "She is not lawful for him until she marries another husband."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

called Abū al-Ṣahbāʾ used to ask Ibn ʿAbbās many questions. He said, "Do you not know that when a man divorced his wife three times before consummating the marriage, they counted it as one in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, and the early part of ʿUmar's rule?" Ibn ʿAbbās said, "Yes. When a man divorced his wife three times before consummating the marriage, they counted it as one in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, and the early part of ʿUmar's rule. But when he saw people making a habit of it, he said, 'Enforce it upon them.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was told of that, and he [Rukānah] said, "By Allah, I intended only one."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By Allah, you intended only one?"
Rukānah said, "By Allah, I intended only one."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned her to him. Then he divorced her a second time in the time of ʿUmar, and a third time in the time of ʿUthmān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Khālid al-Ṭaḥḥān,
with the same meaning, all from Khālid,
from Abū Tamīmah al-Hujaymī, that a man
said to his wife, "O my sister."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Is she your sister?"
He disliked that and forbade it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My husband Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit made ẓihār against me, so I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to complain to him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was disputing with me about it, saying:
"Fear Allah, for he is your cousin."
I did not leave until the Qur'an was revealed: {Allah has heard the speech of the one who disputes with you concerning her husband} up to the obligation. He said, "Let him free a slave."
She said, "He cannot afford it." He said:
"Then let him fast two consecutive months."
She said, "O Messenger of Allah, he is an old man; he cannot fast." He said:
"Then let him feed sixty poor people."
She said, "He has nothing to give in charity." She said: Just then a basket of dates was brought. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I will help him with another basket." He said:
"You have done well. Go and feed sixty poor people with it on his behalf, and return to your cousin."
He said: The basket is sixty ṣāʿs. Abū Dāwūd said: In this [report] she made expiation on his behalf without consulting him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: By al-ʿaraq he means a large basket holding fifteen ṣāʿs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell ill, Jibrīl would perform ruqyah for him, saying: "In the name of Allah, may He cure you, and heal you from every disease, and from the evil of an envier when he envies, and from the evil of every evil eye."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was bewitched.
Abū Kurayb narrated the hadith with its story, similar to the hadith of Ibn Numayr, and in it he said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the well and looked at it, and it had palm trees around it.
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, take it out."
He did not say, "Why did you not burn it?" and he did not mention [the words]:
"So I ordered that it be buried, and it was buried."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jewish woman
put poison in meat and then brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, similar to the hadith of Khālid.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ granted the family of Ḥazm a concession to perform ruqyah for snakebite, and he said to Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays:
"Why do I see the bodies of my brother's children so thin? Is it because they are in need?"
She said: No, but the evil eye is quick to affect them. He said: "Perform ruqyah for them."
She said: I presented [the words] to him, and he said: "Perform ruqyah for them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-ʿAlāʾ [reported] that ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, the devil has come between me and my prayer and my recitation, confusing it for me.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"That is a devil called Khinzab. When you sense him, seek refuge in Allah from him and spit lightly to your left three times."
He said: I did that, and Allah removed him from me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"For every disease there is a cure. If the cure for the disease is found, it is healed by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father was struck on the day of al-Aḥzāb in the main vein of his arm, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cauterized it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were in Madinah when word reached me that plague had broken out in Kufa. ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār and others told me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If you are in a land and it breaks out there, do not leave it; and if you hear that it is in a land, do not enter it."
He said: I asked, "From whom did they report it?" They said, "From ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, who narrates it."

He said: I went to him, but they said he was away. So I met his brother Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd and asked him, and he said: I was present when Usāmah was narrating to Saʿd; he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"This pestilence is a punishment, or a remnant of a punishment, with which some people before you were punished. So if it is in a land while you are in it, do not leave it; and if you hear that it is in a land, do not enter it."
Ḥabīb said: I asked Ibrāhīm, "Did you hear Usāmah narrating to Saʿd, while he did not deny it?" He said: Yes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Usāmah ibn Zayd and Saʿd were sitting conversing, and they said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, similar to their hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no contagion." Then a Bedouin stood up.
Then he mentioned [the hadith] like the hadith of Yūnus and Ṣāliḥ.
And from Shuʿayb, from al-Zuhrī, who said: As-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, the son of Namir's sister, narrated to me that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"There is no contagion, no ṣafar, and no hāmah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no contagion, no ṣafar, and no ghūl."
I heard Abū az-Zubayr mention that Jābir explained to them the saying, "and no ṣafar."
Abū az-Zubayr said: Ṣafar is the belly.
Jābir was asked, "How so?" He said: It used to be said [to mean] the creatures of the belly.
He said: He did not explain ghūl.
Abū az-Zubayr said: This is the ghūl that leads people astray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: O Messenger of Allah, there are things we used to do in the Time of Ignorance; we used to go to soothsayers. He said:
"Do not go to soothsayers."
I said: We used to take omens from birds. He said:
"That is something one of you finds within himself, so do not let it turn you back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ [reported] from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:
"Whoever goes to a diviner and asks him about anything, his prayer will not be accepted for forty nights."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Lubābah
spoke to Ibn ʿUmar so that he might open a door for him in his house to bring him closer to the mosque. The boys found the skin of a snake. ʿAbdullāh said: Look for it and kill it.
Abū Lubābah said: Do not kill it, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade killing the snakes that live in houses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Lubābah passed by Ibn ʿUmar while he was at the fortress near the house of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, watching for a snake, similar to the hadith of al-Layth ibn Saʿd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered a person in iḥrām to kill a snake at Minā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A man from my Ummah will be called out before all of creation on the Day of Resurrection, and ninety-nine scrolls will be spread out for him, each scroll as far as the eye can see. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'Do you deny anything of this?' He will say: 'No, my Lord.' He will say: 'Have My recording scribes wronged you?' Then He will say: 'Do you have an excuse? Do you have a good deed?' The man will be afraid and say: 'No.'

He will say: 'Yes, you have good deeds with Us, and no injustice will be done to you today.' Then a card will be brought out for him on which is: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His slave and Messenger.' He will say: 'My Lord, what is this card compared to these scrolls?' He will say: 'You will not be wronged.'
Then the scrolls will be placed in one pan of the scale and the card in the other, and the scrolls will rise up and the card will weigh heavy."
Muhammad ibn Yaḥyā said: The biṭāqah is a small piece of paper, and the people of Egypt call a small piece of paper a biṭāqah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"Men will come to you from the direction of the East seeking knowledge. When they come to you, then treat them well."
He said: Whenever Abū Saʿīd saw us, he would say: "Welcome to the bequest of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said: We know this hadith only from the narration of Abū Hārūn from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"Do not seek knowledge in order to boast before the scholars, or to argue with the foolish, or to turn people's faces toward you. Whoever does that, he is in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"Whoever learns knowledge for other than Allah, or intends by it other than Allah, let him take his seat in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"May Allah make radiant a person who hears something from us and conveys it as he heard it, for perhaps the one to whom it is conveyed understands better than the one who heard it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"Whoever narrates a hadith from me while thinking that it is a lie, he is one of the liars."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The time is near when a man reclining on his couch will be told a hadith from my sayings, and he will say: 'Between us and you is the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. What we find in it to be lawful we take as lawful, and what we find in it to be forbidden we treat as forbidden.'
Indeed, what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has forbidden is like what Allah has forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith: "Know!"
He said: "What should I know, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Know, O Bilāl!"
He said: "What should I know, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:

"Whoever revives a Sunnah of mine that has been abandoned after me will have a reward like that of those who act upon it, without that diminishing their rewards in the least. And whoever introduces an innovation of misguidance, with which Allah and His Messenger are not pleased, will bear a sin like the sins of those who act upon it, without that diminishing the burdens of the people in the least."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"One person of deep understanding in religion is harder on Satan than a thousand worshippers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The word of wisdom is the lost property of the believer; wherever he finds it, he has the most right to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And the wording
is the wording of Yazīd, and the meaning is the same, from Shuʿbah,
from ʿAmr ibn Murrah,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Salamah,
from Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl al-Murādī: Two Jews,

one of them said to his companion: "Take us to this prophet so we may ask him." The other said: "Do not call him a prophet, for if he hears us say 'prophet,' he will have four eyes." So they came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do not associate anything with Allah; do not commit adultery; do not kill the soul that Allah has forbidden except by right; do not steal; do not practice sorcery; do not take an innocent person to a ruler so that he kills him; do not consume usury; do not slander a chaste woman; and do not flee from the battlefield" (Shuʿbah was unsure) "and especially for you Jews: do not transgress on the Sabbath."
They kissed his hands and feet and said: "We bear witness that you are a prophet." He said:
"Then what prevents you from accepting Islam?"
They said: "Dāwūd prayed to Allah that there would always be a prophet among his descendants, and we fear that if we accept Islam, the Jews will kill us."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever does not trim his moustache is not one of us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A man must not lead another in prayer in the latter's domain of authority, nor sit in his home on his place of honor, except with his permission."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
I was taken up to the Sidrah tree, and there were four rivers: two outward and two inward.
As for the two outward ones, they are the Nile and the Euphrates.
As for the two inward ones, they are two rivers in Paradise. Then I was brought three cups:
a cup containing milk,
a cup containing honey,
and a cup containing wine.
I took the one containing milk and drank, and it was said to me: 'You have chosen the natural way (fiṭrah), you and your nation.'"
Hishām, Saʿīd and Hammām reported from Qatādah, from Anas ibn Mālik, from Mālik ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the rivers, something similar,
but they did not mention the three cups.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Extinguish the lamps at night when you go to sleep, close the doors, tie up the water-skins,
and cover the food and drink."
Hammām said: I think he said: "even if by laying a stick across it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿIkrimah said to us: Shall I not tell you some short things
that Abū Hurayrah narrated to us?
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade drinking from the mouth of a water-skin or waterbag,
and [he forbade] a man to prevent his neighbor from fixing his beam into his wall.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the cup of the Prophet ﷺ with Anas ibn Mālik.
It had cracked, so he had bound it with silver. He said: It is a fine, wide cup made of nuḍār wood.
He said: Anas said: I gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drink from this cup more times than such and such.

He said: Ibn Sīrīn said: There was an iron ring on it, and Anas wanted to replace it with a ring of gold or silver, but Abū Ṭalḥah said to him: Do not change anything that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made. So he left it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah said: 'When I afflict My servant through his two beloved ones and he is patient, I will compensate him for them with Paradise.'" He means his two eyes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A boy,
who was Jewish, used to serve the Prophet ﷺ, and he fell ill.
The Prophet ﷺ came to visit him and said: "Accept Islam." So he accepted Islam.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said, from his father:
When Abū Ṭālib was dying, the Prophet ﷺ came to him
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: Oh, my head!
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
If that were to happen while I am alive,
I would ask forgiveness for you and pray for you."
ʿĀʾishah said: Oh, what a bereavement!
By Allah, I think you love for me to die,
and if that happened, you would spend the rest of your day spending the night with one of your wives. The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Rather, it is I who say, oh, my head! I had intended, or wanted, to send for Abū Bakr and his son
and make a designation, lest the sayers say or the wishers wish.
Then I said: Allah refuses, and the believers will repel [it],
or: Allah will repel, and the believers refuse."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She used to order talbīnah [barley broth] and say: It is the disliked yet beneficial thing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was read to Ayyūb from the books of Abū Qilābah,
some of which he had narrated and some of which was read to him,
and this was in the book, from Anas: that Abū Ṭalḥah and Anas ibn al-Naḍr cauterized him,
and Abū Ṭalḥah cauterized him with his own hand.
ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr said, from Ayyūb,
from Abū Qilābah,
from Anas ibn Mālik,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted a household of the Anṣār to perform ruqyah for poisonous stings and for the ear.
Anas said: I was cauterized for pleurisy while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was alive,
and Abū Ṭalḥah, Anas ibn al-Naḍr and Zayd ibn Thābit were present with me,
and Abū Ṭalḥah was the one who cauterized me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "The one who dies of an abdominal disease is a martyr, and the one who dies of plague is a martyr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group

of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ passed by a watering place where there was a person who had been stung or bitten. A man from the people of the water came to them and said: Is there any one of you who can perform ruqyah? There is a man at the water who has been stung or bitten.
So one of them went and recited the Opening of the Book over a flock of sheep, and the man recovered.
He brought the sheep to his companions, but they disliked that and said: You took payment for the Book of Allah!
When they reached Medina, they said: O Messenger of Allah, he took payment for the Book of Allah!
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The most deserving thing for which you may take payment is the Book of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to his bed, he would blow into his palms after reciting Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad and the two Muʿawwidhatayn together,
then wipe his face with them
and whatever his hands could reach of his body.
ʿĀʾishah said: When he fell ill, he would order me to do that for him.
Yūnus said: I used to see Ibn Shihāb do that when he went to his bed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I wrote to Jābir ibn Samurah, through my servant Nāfiʿ, asking him to inform me of something he had heard from
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He wrote back to me: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a Friday, the evening on which the man from Aslam was stoned, saying:
"This religion will continue to stand until the Hour is established, or until there have been twelve caliphs over you, all of them from Quraysh." And I heard him say:
"A small group of the Muslims will conquer the White House, the house of Khosrow or the family of Khosrow." And I heard him say:
"Before the Hour there will be great liars, so beware of them." And I heard him say:
"When Allah gives one of you some good, let him begin with himself and his family." And I heard him say:
"I will be your forerunner at the Pond."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he sent a message to Ibn Samurah al-ʿAdawī: Narrate to us what you heard from
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ḥātim.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was as though I were carrying a mountain on my right hand until I returned and went in to him. He asked me about the condition of the people, and I told him. He said: Then I said to him: I heard people saying something, and I resolved to tell it to you. They claim that you are not appointing a successor, and that if you had a shepherd of camels or sheep who then came to you and left them, you would consider that he had neglected them, so taking care of the people is more serious. He said: My words agreed with his thinking. He lowered his head for a while, then raised it to me and said: Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, protects His religion. If I do not appoint a successor, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not appoint one; and if I do appoint one, then Abū Bakr appointed one.

He said: By Allah, as soon as he mentioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abū Bakr, I knew that he would not put anyone on a par with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that he would not appoint a successor.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: O Messenger of Allah, will you not appoint me to a post? He said: He struck my shoulder with his hand and then said:
"O Abū Dharr, you are weak, and it is a trust, and on the Day of Resurrection it is disgrace and regret, except for one who takes it with its right and fulfills what is required of him in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to ʿĀʾishah to ask her about something,
and she said: Where are you from? I said: A man from the people of Egypt.

She said: How was your governor to you in this expedition of yours? He said: We held nothing against him. If a man among us had a camel die, he would give him a camel; if a slave died, he would give him a slave; and if he needed provisions, he would give him provisions. She said: What he did to my brother Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr will not stop me from telling you what I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say in this house of mine:
"O Allah, whoever takes charge of any matter of my nation and is harsh on them, be harsh on him; and whoever takes charge of any matter of my nation and is gentle with them, be gentle with him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Like the hadith of al-Layth from Nāfiʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (a transition to another chain)
label: machine translation

segments_en: He named him; and ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from Bukayr,
from Busr ibn Saʿīd,
who narrated to him from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,
from the Prophet ﷺ, with this meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿĀʾidh ibn ʿAmr
—who was one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—entered upon ʿUbaydullāh ibn Ziyād and said: My son, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The worst of shepherds is the harsh oppressor, so beware of being one of them."
He said to him: Sit down, for you are only from the chaff of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ.
He said: Did they have any chaff? The chaff came only after them and among others than them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned misappropriation of war booty and declared it a grave matter.
And he related the hadith. Ḥammād said: Then after that I heard Yaḥyā narrating it, and he narrated to us something like what Ayyūb narrated to us from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (a transition to another chain)
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ giving a sermon during the Farewell Hajj, saying:
"Even if a slave were appointed over you and he leads you by the Book of Allah, listen to him and obey."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿUmar and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUbādah ibn al-Walīd,
with this chain, the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Anas ibn Mālik about Aṣ-Ṣafā and Al-Marwah,
and he said: They were among the rites of the Jāhiliyyah, so when Islam came we held back from them, and Allah revealed:

"Indeed, Aṣ-Ṣafā and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever performs Hajj to the House or performs ʿUmrah, there is no blame upon him for walking between them." He said: They are voluntary: "and whoever volunteers good, then indeed Allah is Appreciative and Knowing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Abū an-Naḍr, from ʿUmayr,
the freed slave of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās, from Umm al-Faḍl bint al-Ḥārith, that some people
disputed in her presence on the Day of ʿArafah about the fasting of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Some of them said, "He is fasting," and some said, "He is not fasting."
So she sent him a cup of milk while he was standing on his camel at ʿArafah, and he drank it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I rode behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from ʿArafāt. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached the left-hand mountain path before Muzdalifah, he made his camel kneel and urinated. Then he came and I poured water for ablution over him, and he performed a light ablution. Then I said, "Prayer, O Messenger of Allah!" He said, "The prayer is ahead of you."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mounted and went until he reached Muzdalifah, and he prayed. Then al-Faḍl rode behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the morning of Jamʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And its meaning,
he said: with a single iqāmah for each prayer; no call was made for the first one, and he did not offer voluntary prayer after either of them.
Makhlad said: No call was made for either of them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
entered upon Umm Ḥabībah, and she informed him that the Prophet ﷺ sent her from Jamʿ by night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I remember twisting the garlands for the sacrificial animals of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from sheep. Then he would send it, and afterward he would stay among us, free of the restrictions of iḥrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ five nights before the end of Dhū al-Qaʿdah,
thinking of nothing but Hajj.

When we drew near Makkah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded whoever did not have a sacrificial animal with him, once he had circled the House and walked between Aṣ-Ṣafā and Al-Marwah, to leave iḥrām.
ʿĀʾishah said: On the Day of Sacrifice, beef was brought to us, and I said, "What is this?" He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sacrificed on behalf of his wives."
Yaḥyā said: I mentioned this ḥadīth to al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, and he said, "By Allah, she has brought you the ḥadīth exactly as it was."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, come upon a man
who had made his camel kneel and was about to slaughter it.
He said, "Send it standing, with its leg tied; that is the Sunnah of Muḥammad ﷺ."
And Shuʿbah said, from Yūnus: Ziyād informed me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd threw the pebbles at Jamrat al-ʿAqabah from the bottom of the valley, seven pebbles, saying the takbīr with each pebble.
He said: It was said to him, "Some people throw at it from above it."
ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said, "By the One besides whom there is no god, this is the place of the one upon whom Sūrat al-Baqarah was revealed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ said: I perfumed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with my own hand for his iḥrām when he entered iḥrām, and for his release when he left iḥrām, before he circled the House.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Stopping at al-Muḥaṣṣab is nothing [of the rites]; it was only a place where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ camped.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ wanted to depart, and he saw Ṣafiyyah at the door of her tent, gloomy and sad because she had begun her menses. He said,
"ʿAqrā ḥalqā" (in the dialect of Quraysh), "you are going to detain us!" Then he said,
"Did you perform the ṭawāf of ifāḍah on the Day of Sacrifice?"
meaning the circling. She said, "Yes." He said, "Then depart."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was at al-Jiʿrānah. The man wore a cloak with khalūq perfume on it, or he said a trace of yellow. He said, "How do you command me to perform my ʿUmrah?" Revelation came down upon the Prophet ﷺ, and he was screened with a cloth. Yaʿlā used to say, "I wished I could see the Prophet ﷺ when revelation came to him." He said: ʿUmar said, "Would it please you to look at the Prophet ﷺ while revelation is being sent down to him?" He said: ʿUmar lifted the edge of the cloth and I looked at him; he was snoring, and I think he said, like the snoring of a young camel. He said: When it was lifted from him, he said,
"Where is the one who asked about ʿUmrah? Wash off the trace of yellow, or he said the trace of khalūq, take off your cloak, and do in your ʿUmrah what you do in your Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some men among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to see dreams during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and would relate them to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say about them whatever Allah willed.
I was a young man, and my home was the mosque, before I married.
So I said to myself, "If there were any good in you, you would see [dreams] like those that these men see."
So when I lay down one night, I said, "O Allah, if You know any good in me, then show me a dream."
While I was in that state, two angels came to me, each of them holding an iron mace,
and they were bringing me toward Hell,
and I was between them, supplicating Allah: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from Hell."
Then I saw that an angel met me, in whose hand was an iron mace, and he said, "Do not be afraid.
What an excellent man you would be if only you would pray more."
So they took me until they made me stand at the edge of Hell, and behold, it was lined [with stone] like the lining of a well,
with horns like the horns of a well,
and between every two horns was an angel with an iron mace in his hand,
and I saw in it men hanging by chains, their heads downward,
and I recognized among them men of Quraysh,
then they turned me away to the right.
I told it to Hafsah, and Hafsah told it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Indeed ʿAbdullāh is a righteous man."
Nāfiʿ said: After that he never ceased to pray much.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh said: I asked ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, about the dream
of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he mentioned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ [said] this, and he said: "Every man was wrapping his head in his garment, weeping."
And he said, "I seek refuge with Allah from the evil of trials."
Or he said, "I seek refuge in Allah from the evil of trials."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with Abū Masʿūd, Abū Mūsā and ʿAmmār. Abū Masʿūd said, "There is none of your companions about whom I could not say something, if I wished, other than you,
and since you accompanied the Prophet ﷺ I have not seen anything in you more blameworthy in my view than your haste in this matter."

ʿAmmār said, "O Abū Masʿūd, and since you and this companion of yours accompanied the Prophet ﷺ, I have not seen anything in you or in him more blameworthy in my view than your slowness in this matter."
Abū Masʿūd, who was well-off, said, "O boy, bring two garments."
He gave one to Abū Mūsā and the other to ʿAmmār and said, "Go out in them to the Friday [prayer]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And I met him
in Kufa. Ibn Shubrumah came to me and said, "Bring me in to ʿĪsā so that I may admonish him."
It was as if Ibn Shubrumah feared for him, so he did not do it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr said: I saw Harmalah, who said: Usāmah sent me to ʿAlī and said, "He will soon ask you, 'What kept your companion behind?' So say to him: He says to you, 'Even if you were in the jaws of a lion, I would love to be with you in it,
but this is a matter that I do not see [as right].'"
But he gave me nothing,
so I went to Hasan, Husayn and Ibn Jaʿfar, and they loaded my riding animal [with provisions].
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ibn Ziyād and Marwān were in Syria,
Ibn al-Zubayr rose up in Mecca,
and the Qurrāʾ rose up in Basra,
I went with my father to Abū Barzah al-Aslamī until we entered upon him in his house while he was sitting in the shade of an upper room of his made of cane.

We sat with him, and my father began asking him to speak, saying, "O Abū Barzah, do you not see what the people have fallen into?" The first thing I heard him say was: "I reckon with Allah that I have woken up angry at the clans of Quraysh.
You, O assembly of Arabs, were in the state you know of humiliation, fewness and misguidance,
and Allah rescued you through Islam and through Muhammad ﷺ until [things] reached you as you see,
and it is this world that has corrupted [relations] among you.
That man in Syria, by Allah, is fighting only for the sake of this world."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Today the hypocrites are worse than they were in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. In those days they concealed [it], and today they are open [about it].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hypocrisy existed only in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. As for today, it is only disbelief after faith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ: "
Is there no man who will lend a household a she-camel that gives a large bowl of milk in the morning and a large bowl in the evening? Indeed, his reward is great."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he forbade [certain things], and he mentioned several qualities, and said: "
Whoever lends a milch animal, it goes out in the morning as charity and returns in the evening as charity, [through] its morning milk and its evening milk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ
label: machine translation

segments_en: Numayr and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb, both from Ḥafṣ,
ibn Ghiyāth. Ibn Numayr said: Ḥafṣ narrated to us,
from Muḥammad ibn Zayd, from ʿUmayr,
the freed slave of Abū al-Laḥm, who said: I was a slave, so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: May I give in charity from the wealth of my masters? He said: "
Yes, and the reward is split equally between the two of you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and al-Ḥasan al-Ḥulwānī,
and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd,
they said: Yaʿqūb narrated to us,
who is the son of Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd: My father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ,
Transfer [of chain]: and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us: ʿAbd
ar-Razzāq narrated to us: Maʿmar informed us,
both of them from az-Zuhrī,
with the chain of Yūnus and the meaning of his hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Who among you is fasting today?"
Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I am. He said: "
And who among you has followed a funeral procession today?"
Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I have. He said: "
And who among you has fed a poor person today?"
Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I have. He said: "
And who among you has visited a sick person today?"
Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I have.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
These [deeds] are not found together in a person except that he enters Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Khubayb ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān,
from Ḥafṣ ibn ʿĀṣim,
from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī,
or from Abū Hurayrah,
that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
[and he narrated] like the hadith of ʿUbayd Allah. And he said: "
and a man whose heart is attached to the mosque, when he leaves it until he returns to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Beware of [narrating] hadith, except a hadith that was [known] in the time of ʿUmar, for ʿUmar used to make people fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: "
Whoever Allah wants good for, He gives him understanding of the religion."
And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
I am only a treasurer. So whoever I give with a good heart, he will be blessed in it; and whoever I give because of begging and greed, he is like one who eats and is never satisfied."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī sent for the reciters of the people of Basra, and three hundred men who had recited the Qurʾān came to him. He said: You are the best of the people of Basra and their reciters, so recite it, and do not let the time grow long for you so that your hearts become hard, as the hearts of those before you became hard. We used to recite a sura that we likened in length and severity to Barāʾah, but I was made to forget it, except that I have memorized from it: "If the son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would seek a third valley, and nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam except dust."

And we used to recite a sura that we likened to one of the Musabbiḥāt, but I was made to forget it, except that I have memorized from it: "O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?" — so it is recorded as a testimony on your necks, and you will be questioned about it on the Day of Resurrection.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
He has succeeded who has submitted [to Islam], been provided with sufficient sustenance, and whom Allah has made content with what He has given him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a distribution, and I said: By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, others than these were more deserving of it than they. He said: "
They gave me the choice between asking me in an unseemly manner or regarding me as stingy, and I am not stingy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Eat and drink, and do not let the rising bright column [of light] hinder you. Eat and drink until the red [dawn] spreads across the horizon before you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to break his fast with fresh dates before praying. If there were no fresh dates, then with [dried] dates, and if there were no dates, he would take a few sips of water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cleaning his teeth with the siwāk while he was fasting.
Musaddad added: [He did so] more times than I can count or number.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
asked the Prophet ﷺ about physical intimacy for the one who is fasting, and he permitted it for him. Then another man came and asked him, and he forbade it to him.
The one to whom he gave permission was an old man, and the one whom he forbade was a young man.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let none of you say, 'I fasted the whole of Ramadan and stood in prayer through all of it.'"
I do not know whether he disliked self-praise, or whether he said, 'There must be some sleep or rest.'
label: machine translation

segments_en: The most beloved of months to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in which to fast was Shaʿbān; indeed, he would join it to Ramadan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked, or the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked, about fasting perpetually, and he said:
"Your family has a right over you. Fast Ramadan and the month that follows it, and every Wednesday and Thursday; then you will have fasted perpetually and also broken your fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast nine days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and three days of every month: the first Monday of the month and two Thursdays.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Abū Hurayrah in his house and asked him about fasting on the day of ʿArafah at ʿArafāt. He said:
Abū Hurayrah [said]: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade fasting on the day of ʿArafah at ʿArafāt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon the Mother of the Believers and heard her say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast three days of every month: the first Monday of the month, then Thursday, then the Thursday that follows it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:

"Every dead person's deeds are sealed, except the one who dies while stationed on guard in the cause of Allah; his deeds continue to grow for him until the Day of Resurrection, and he is safe from the trial of the grave."
And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The one who strives is the one who strives against his own self."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Strive against the polytheists with your wealth, your selves, and your tongues."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were in the city of the Romans when they brought out against us a great rank of the Romans, and an equal number of Muslims or more went out to face them. ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir was over the people of Egypt, and Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd was over the whole army. A man from the Muslims charged at the Roman line until he entered into them. The people cried out, saying, "Glory be to Allah! He is throwing himself into destruction with his own hands!" Then Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī stood up and said: "O people, you interpret this verse in this way, but it was only revealed about us, the company of the Anṣār. When Allah gave strength to Islam and its supporters became many, some of us said to others in secret, without the knowledge of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'Our wealth has been lost, and Allah has given strength to Islam and its supporters have become many. If only we stayed with our wealth and restored what was lost of it.'
So Allah revealed to His Prophet ﷺ, replying to what we had said:

'And spend in the cause of Allah, and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction.' Thus the destruction was staying with our wealth and tending to it, and abandoning fighting." Abū Ayyūb continued to go forth in the cause of Allah until he was buried in the land of the Romans.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"Military expeditions are of two kinds. As for the one who seeks the face of Allah, obeys the leader, spends the best of his wealth, is easy with his companion, and avoids corruption,
then his sleeping and his waking are all rewarded. But as for the one who fights out of boasting, showing off, and seeking reputation, and disobeys the leader,
and spreads corruption in the earth,
he will not return even with [what is] enough [i.e., breaking even]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was

one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. From ʿUbayd ibn Khālid as-Sulamī: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made two men brothers [in faith]. One of them was killed, and the other died after him. We prayed over him, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "What did you say?"
They said: "We supplicated for him: O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy on him; O Allah, join him with his companion." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Then where is his prayer compared to his [companion's] prayer, and where is his deed compared to his deed? Between the two is as far as the heavens are from the earth."
ʿAmr ibn Maymūn said: It impressed me, because he traced it back [to the Prophet ﷺ] for me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was a man who had been given a strength for intercourse with women that no one else had been given. When Ramadan came, I made a ẓihār declaration against my wife until Ramadan was over, fearing that I might approach her during my night and then continue until daylight caught me while I was unable to restrain myself. Then one night, while she was serving me, part of her was uncovered to me, and I leapt upon her. When morning came, I went to my people and told them what had happened to me. I said, "Come with me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that I can tell him my affair."

They said, "No, by Allah, we will not do so. We fear that a Qur'anic verse may be revealed about us, or that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will say something about us whose shame will remain with us. But you go and do whatever you see fit."
He said: So I went out and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him what had happened to me. He said, "You are the one who did that?"
I said, "I am the one who did that." He said, "You are the one who did that?"
I said, "I am the one who did that." He said, "You are the one who did that?"
I said, "I am the one who did that, and here I am, so carry out Allah's ruling upon me, for I am patient with it." He said, "Free a slave."
He said: So I struck the side of my neck with my hand and said, "No, by the One who sent you with the truth, I own nothing but this one." He said, "Fast two months."
I said, "Messenger of Allah, did anything befall me except through fasting?" He said,
"Then feed sixty poor people."
I said, "By the One who sent you with the truth, we spent this night of ours hungry, with no supper." He said,
"Go to the collector of the charity of Banū Zurayq and tell him to hand it over to you. Then feed sixty poor people from it with a wasq, and use the rest for yourself and your family."

He said: So I returned to my people and said, "I found narrowness and poor judgment with you, and I found ease and blessing with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He has ordered that your charity be given to me, so hand it over to me." So they handed it over to me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and said, "Prophet of Allah, he made a ẓihār declaration against his wife and then had intercourse with her before doing what was required of him." He said,
"What made you do that?"
He said, "Prophet of Allah, I saw the whiteness of her shanks in the moonlight."
The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said,
"Keep away from her until you have fulfilled what is required of you."
Isḥāq said in his narration,
"Keep away from her until you have fulfilled what is required of you." The wording is that of Muḥammad.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without a valid reason, the scent of Paradise is forbidden to her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned his daughter Zaynab to Abū al-ʿĀṣ on the basis of the first marriage; he did not do anything new.
Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr said in his narration, "after six years," and al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī said, "after two years."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "Messenger of Allah, I have accepted Islam and I have two sisters as wives." He said,
"Choose whichever of them you wish."
This hadith is ḥasan.
Abū Wahb al-Jayshānī's name is al-Daylam ibn Hawshaʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the verse of mutual imprecation (liʿān) was revealed, [he said],

"Any woman who brings into a people someone who is not of them has nothing to do with Allah, and Allah will not admit her into His Paradise. And any man who denies his child while he is looking at him, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will veil Himself from him and expose him before the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said,

"A woman must not observe mourning for more than three days, except for a husband, for whom she mourns four months and ten days. She should not wear dyed clothing, except ʿaṣb cloth, nor apply kohl, nor touch perfume, except a little when she becomes pure from her menses, a piece of qusṭ or aẓfār."
Yaʿqūb said, in place of "ʿaṣb," "except washed [clothing]." And Yaʿqūb added, "and she should not apply henna."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we fasted twenty-nine days more often than we fasted thirty.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ḥumayd, Abū Usayd, Sahl ibn Saʿd and Muḥammad ibn Maslamah gathered, and he mentioned this hadith, but he did not mention raising the hands when standing up after two [rakʿahs], nor the sitting. He said: until he had finished; then he sat, spread out his left foot, and turned the front of his right foot toward the direction of prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We did not know what to say when we sat in prayer, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had taught [us]. Then he mentioned something similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlqamah took me by my hand and told me that ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd took him by his hand, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took ʿAbdullāh by the hand and taught him the tashahhud in prayer. Then he mentioned the supplication like the hadith of al-Aʿmash:
"When you have said this, or finished this, you have completed your prayer. If you wish to stand, then stand, and if you wish to sit, then sit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: To proceed: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us that, when in the middle of the prayer or at its conclusion, we should begin before the salutation of peace and say:
"All greetings, good things, prayers and sovereignty belong to Allah." Then give the salām to the right, then give the salām to your reciter and to yourselves.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said, or they said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have commanded us to send blessings upon you and to greet you with peace. As for the greeting of peace, we have come to know it, but how should we send blessings upon you?" He said:

"Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrāhīm, and grant blessings to Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You granted blessings to the family of Ibrāhīm. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this report he said:
"Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad, the unlettered Prophet, and upon the family of Muḥammad."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbaydullāh ibn Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh ibn Kurayz: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Hāshimī narrated to me, from al-Mujmir,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

"Whoever would be pleased to be measured with the fullest measure when he sends blessings upon us, the people of the household, let him say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad the Prophet, his wives, the mothers of the believers, his offspring and the people of his household, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrāhīm. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade—Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said—a man to sit in prayer while leaning on his hand.
Ibn Shabawayh said: He forbade a man to lean on his hand in prayer.
Ibn Rāfiʿ said: He forbade a man to pray while leaning on his hand.
And he mentioned it in the chapter on rising from prostration.
Ibn ʿAbd al-Malik said: He forbade a man to lean on his hands when rising in prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was praying with his fingers interlaced. Ibn ʿUmar said: That is the prayer of those who earned [Allah's] anger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he saw a man leaning on his left hand while sitting in prayer—and Hārūn ibn Zayd said: falling over onto his left side; then they agreed—so he said to him: "Do not sit like this, for this is how those who are being punished sit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ commanded us to return the greeting to the imām, to love one another, and to give the salām to one another.
label: machine translation

segments_en: An imām of ours, who was called Abū Rimthah, led us in prayer and said: I prayed this prayer, or the like of this prayer, with the Prophet ﷺ.

He said: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar used to stand in the front row to his right, and there was a man who had witnessed the first takbīr of the prayer.
