"Leave him, ʿUmar, for it is swifter against them than the shooting of arrows."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was coming along with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he heard a man reciting: {Say: He is Allah, [who is] One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born. Nor is there to Him any equivalent.} The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is obligatory."
I asked him: What, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever recites the Qur'an and memorizes it, treating as lawful what it makes lawful and as unlawful what it makes unlawful, Allah will admit him to Paradise because of it and will grant his intercession for ten of his family, all of whom had been destined for the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "If only you would take the Station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer," and then it was revealed:
{And take the Station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was revealed about us, the group of the Anṣār. We were owners of date palms, and each man would bring from his palms according to how much or how little he had. A man would bring one cluster or two and hang it in the mosque. The People of the Ṣuffah had no food, so when one of them was hungry he would come to a cluster and strike it with his stick, and unripe and ripe dates would fall, and he would eat. There were some people who had no desire for good, who would bring a cluster of poor, withered dates, or a broken cluster, and hang it. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed:

{O you who believe, spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have brought forth for you from the earth, and do not aim toward the bad of it, spending [from that], while you would not take it yourselves except with closed eyes.} They said: If one of you were given a gift like what he gave, he would not take it except with closed eyes and shame. He said: So after that, each of us would bring the best of what he had.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Umāmah saw heads displayed on the steps of the mosque of Damascus, and Abū Umāmah said:
"Dogs of the Fire! The worst of those killed beneath the canopy of the sky; the best of those killed are those whom they killed." Then he recited:

{On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black} to the end of the verse. I said to Abū Umāmah: Did you hear it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: If I had not heard it except once, or twice, or three times, or four times, until he counted up to seven, I would not have narrated it to you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day and found him sitting with his Companions, speaking to them, with a bandage tied around his stomach—Usāmah said, "and I am unsure"—over a stone. I said to one of his Companions, "Why has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ tied his stomach with a bandage?" They said, "Because of hunger."

So I went to Abū Ṭalḥah, who was the husband of Umm Sulaym bint Milḥān, and said, "O father, I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a bandage tied around his stomach, so I asked some of his Companions and they said, 'Because of hunger.'"

Abū Ṭalḥah then went in to my mother and said, "Is there anything?" She said, "Yes, I have some pieces of bread and a few dates. If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ comes to us alone, we can satisfy him, but if someone else comes with him, it will not be enough for them."
Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith with its story.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some dates were brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ began to distribute them while sitting on his haunches, eating from them quickly.
And in the narration of Zuhayr: eating hurriedly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"A household that has dates will not go hungry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"In the ʿajwah dates of al-ʿĀliyah there is a cure," or, "they are an antidote at the start of the morning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took me by the hand one day to his house, and a piece of bread was brought out to him. He said:
"Is there no condiment?"
They said, "No, only some vinegar." He said:
"Vinegar is an excellent condiment."
Jābir said, "I have loved vinegar ever since I heard that from the Prophet of Allah ﷺ."
And Ṭalḥah said, "I have loved vinegar ever since I heard it from Jābir."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took him by the hand to his house.
Similar to the hadith of Ibn ʿUlayyah up to his words:
"What an excellent condiment vinegar is."
And he did not mention what comes after it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting in my house when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me and gestured to me, so I stood up to him. He took me by the hand and we went until he came to one of the rooms of his wives. He entered, then gave me permission, and I entered the room behind the curtain. He said:
"Is there any lunch?" They said, "Yes."

Three loaves were brought and placed on a plate. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took one loaf and placed it in front of him, took another loaf and placed it in front of me, then took the third and broke it in two, putting half in front of him and half in front of me. Then he said:
"Is there any condiment?" They said, "No,
only some vinegar." He said:
"Bring it, for it is an excellent condiment."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this chain of narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stayed with him, so the Prophet ﷺ stayed in the lower floor while Abū Ayyūb was on the upper floor. He said: Abū Ayyūb woke one night and said, "We are walking above the head of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!"
So they moved away and spent the night in a corner. Then he told the Prophet ﷺ about it, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "The lower floor is more convenient."
He said, "I will not be above a roof that you are beneath."

So the Prophet ﷺ moved to the upper floor and Abū Ayyūb to the lower floor. He used to prepare food for the Prophet ﷺ, and when it was returned to him, he would ask where his fingers had touched and follow the marks of his fingers. Once he prepared food containing garlic, and when it was returned to him, he asked where the fingers of the Prophet ﷺ had touched, and was told, "He did not eat it."
He was alarmed and went up to him and said, "Is it forbidden?" The Prophet ﷺ said:
"No, but I dislike it."
He said, "Then I dislike what you dislike," or, "what you have disliked."
He said: And the Prophet ﷺ used to be brought [revelation].
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib and heard him say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to do seven things and forbade us seven things. He commanded us to visit the sick, to follow funeral processions, to respond to one who sneezes, to fulfil oaths, or [to help] the one who swears an oath to fulfil it, to help the oppressed, to answer the one who invites, and to spread the greeting of peace.

And he forbade us from rings, or from wearing a ring, of gold, from drinking from silver vessels, from saddle cushions of silk (maythar), from qassī garments, and from wearing silk, brocade, and dībāj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ borrowed a young camel, and then camels from the charity (ṣadaqah) came to him.
Abū Rāfiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered me to repay the man his young camel.
I said: I find among the camels only a select, four-year-old camel.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Give it to him, for the best of people are those who are best in repaying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever sincerely asks Allah for martyrdom, Allah will bring him to the ranks of the martyrs, even if he dies in his bed."
Abū al-Ṭāhir did not mention "sincerely" in his narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade, meaning on the day of Khaybar, domestic donkeys, the meat of mules, every beast of prey with a fang, and every bird with a talon.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Indeed Allah has prescribed excellence in everything. So when you kill, kill well, and when you slaughter, slaughter well. Let one of you sharpen his blade and let him spare his slaughtered animal suffering."
He said: This is a good and sound hadith.
Abū al-Ashʿath al-Ṣanʿānī's name is Sharāḥīl ibn Adah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has a sacrificial animal to slaughter, then once the crescent of Dhū al-Ḥijjah appears, let him not take anything from his hair or his nails until he has offered the sacrifice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Wine comes from these two trees: the grapevine and the date palm."
In the narration of Abū Kurayb: "the grapevine and the palm trees."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ made a ring of silver, with an Abyssinian stone set in it, and engraved on it: Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Ibn Abī ʿUmar,
the wording being that of Ibn Abī ʿUmar, said: Sufyān narrated to us,
from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
the freed slave of the family of Ṭalḥah, from Kurayb,
from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Juwayriyah,
that the Prophet ﷺ left her early in the morning when he had prayed the Fajr prayer while she was in her place of prayer. Then he returned after the forenoon had come, and she was sitting. He said:
"Have you remained in the same state in which I left you?" She said: Yes. The Prophet ﷺ said:

"After I left you I said four words, three times, which if weighed against what you have said since today, would outweigh them: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, as many as the number of His creation, as much as pleases Him, as much as the weight of His Throne, and as much as the ink of His words."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Insulting a Muslim is wickedness, and fighting him is disbelief."
Zubayd said: I said to Abū Wāʾil: Did you hear it from ʿAbdullāh, narrating it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: Yes.
And in the narration of Shuʿbah there is no mention of Zubayd's statement to Abū Wāʾil.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about a stray sheep, and he said: "Take it,
for it is either for you, or for your brother, or for the wolf."
And he was asked about a stray camel,
and he became angry, his cheeks turned red, and he said:
"What do you have to do with it?
It has its hooves and its water-skin; it drinks water and eats from the trees,
until its owner finds it."
And he was asked about a lost item that is found, and he said:
"Know its tie and its container, and announce it for a year,
and if someone comes who recognizes it, [give it to him],
otherwise mix it with your own wealth."

Sufyān said: I met Rabīʿah ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. Sufyān said: I did not memorize anything else from him besides this. I said: What do you think of the hadith of Yazīd, the freed slave of al-Munbaʿith, about the matter of the stray animal; is it from Zayd ibn Khālid?
He said: Yes.
Yaḥyā said: Rabīʿah says, from Yazīd, the freed slave of al-Munbaʿith, from Zayd ibn Khālid.
Sufyān said: I met Rabīʿah and said to him:
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father mentioned it from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr,
from al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to wipe over his leather socks.
And someone other than Muḥammad said: over the upper part of the leather socks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bathed after sexual impurity, Sulaymān said: he would begin by pouring from his right hand onto his left.
And Musaddad said: he washed his hands, pouring the vessel over his right hand. Then they agreed: then he would wash his private parts.

Musaddad said: He would pour onto his left hand, and at times I was away from the private parts. Then he would perform his ablution as for prayer, then put his hands into the vessel and run them through his hair, until, when he saw that he had reached the skin, or had cleansed the skin, he would pour water over his head three times. Then, if some water remained, he would pour it over himself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafiyyah bint Shaybah, from Asmāʾ bint Abū Bakr,

said: One day the Prophet ﷺ was alarmed—she meant the day the sun was eclipsed—so he took up a cloak [by mistake] until he caught up with his own mantle. Then he stood for the people in a long standing. Had a person come in, he would not have known that the Prophet ﷺ had bowed, because of how long he stood, and he would not have thought that he had bowed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and he was alarmed and mistakenly took up a cloak, until afterwards he caught up with his mantle. She said: I took care of my need, then came and entered the mosque, and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing, so I stood with him. He prolonged the standing until I saw myself wanting to sit; then I would glance at a frail woman and say, "She is weaker than I am."
So I stood. Then he bowed and prolonged the bowing, then raised his head and prolonged the standing, so that if a man had come, it would have seemed to him that he had not bowed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr, all of them from Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar,
Ibn Ayyūb said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
Saʿd ibn Saʿīd informed me,
from ʿUmar ibn Kathīr ibn Aflaḥ, from Ibn
Safīnah, from Umm Salamah,
that she said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"There is no Muslim who is struck by a calamity and says what Allah commanded: 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we shall return. O Allah, reward me in my calamity and replace it for me with something better,'
except that Allah replaces it for him with something better."
She said: When Abū Salamah died, I said, "Which Muslim is better than Abū Salamah, the first household to emigrate to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?"
Then I said it [the supplication], and Allah replaced him for me with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah to propose to me on his behalf. I said, "I have a daughter, and I am jealous." He said:
"As for her daughter, we will pray to Allah to make her independent of her, and I will pray to Allah to remove the jealousy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Have you not seen that when a person dies, his eyes stay fixed open?" They said, "Yes." He said:
"That is when his sight follows his soul."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Namīr and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, all of them from Ibn
ʿUyaynah—Ibn Namīr said: Sufyān narrated to us—
from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from his father,
from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr,
who said: Umm Salamah said: When Abū Salamah died, I said, "A stranger, and in a foreign land! I will surely weep for him with weeping that will be spoken of."
I had prepared myself to weep for him when a woman from the highlands came, wanting to help me [mourn]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ met her and said:
"Do you want to bring Satan into a house from which Allah has driven him out?"
[He said it] twice, so I held back from weeping and did not weep.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a man from the Anṣār came to him and greeted him with salām. Then the Anṣārī turned to leave, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O brother of the Anṣār, how is my brother Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah?" He said, "He is well."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Which of you will visit him?"

He stood and we stood with him, about ten and some of us, with no sandals, no leather socks, no caps and no shirts, walking over that salty ground until we came to him. His people drew back from around him until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions who were with him came near.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿUmar was wounded, Ṣuhayb came from his house and entered upon ʿUmar, and stood in front of him weeping. ʿUmar said, "Why do you weep? Do you weep for me?" He said, "Yes, by Allah, I weep for you, O Commander of the Faithful."
He said: By Allah, you certainly know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The one who is wept over is punished."
[The narrator] said: I mentioned that to Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, who said: ʿĀʾishah used to say that those [referred to] were the Jews.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb,
when he was stabbed, Ḥafṣah wailed over him. He said, "O Ḥafṣah, did you not hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'The one who is wailed over is punished'?"
And Ṣuhayb wailed over him, so ʿUmar said, "O Ṣuhayb, did you not know
that the one who is wailed over is punished?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were at the funeral of Umm Abān bint ʿUthmān—and he related the hadith, but he did not state explicitly that it was traced back from ʿUmar to the Prophet ﷺ, as Ayyūb and Ibn Jurayj did explicitly; and their narration is more complete than the narration of ʿAmr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A gift of food was given to me and Ḥafṣah while we were both fasting, so we broke our fast. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in, and we said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, we were given a gift and we desired it, so we broke our fast." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no harm on you both. Fast another day in its place."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ while we were with him, and she said, "O Messenger of Allah, my husband Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal beats me when I pray, makes me break my fast when I fast, and does not pray the dawn prayer until the sun has risen."
He said: Ṣafwān was with him.

He said: So he asked him about what she had said, and he replied, "O Messenger of Allah, as for her saying that I beat her when she prays, she recites two surahs, and I have forbidden her." He said: So he said:
"If it were one surah, it would suffice the people."
"As for her saying that I make her break her fast, she goes off and fasts, and I am a young man and cannot hold back."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on that occasion:
"A woman must not fast except with her husband's permission."
"As for her saying that I do not pray until the sun rises, we are a household known for that; we hardly ever wake up until the sun has risen." He said:
"Then when you wake up, pray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would pass by a sick person while he was in seclusion (iʿtikāf), and he would pass on as he was, without turning aside to ask about him.
And Ibn ʿĪsā said: She said, "The Prophet ﷺ would visit the sick while he was in seclusion (iʿtikāf)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Sunnah for one in seclusion (iʿtikāf) is that he does not visit the sick, does not attend a funeral, does not touch a woman or have intimate contact with her, and does not go out for a need except for what is unavoidable; and there is no iʿtikāf without fasting, and no iʿtikāf except in a congregational mosque.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar,

may Allah be pleased with him, had made it binding upon himself during the Jāhiliyyah to spend a night or a day in seclusion at the Kaʿbah, so he asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he said, "Observe seclusion and fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah about living in the desert,

and she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would go out to these tracts of low ground. Once he wanted to go out to the desert, so he sent me a she-camel that had never been ridden, from the camels of charity (ṣadaqah), and he said to me:
"O ʿĀʾishah, be gentle, for gentleness is not in anything except that it adorns it, and it is not removed from anything except that it disgraces it."
Ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ said in his narration: "Never ridden" means it had not been ridden.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hijrah will not cease until repentance ceases, and repentance will not cease until the sun rises from its place of setting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr while people were with him, until he sat beside him, and said, "Tell me something you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There will be a hijrah after a hijrah, and the best of the people of the earth will be those who hold most closely to the place of Ibrāhīm's migration. There will remain on the earth the worst of its people; their lands will cast them out, Allah's soul will loathe them, and the Fire will gather them together with the apes and the pigs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Matters will come to the point that you will be mobilized armies: an army in Syria, an army in Yemen, and an army in Iraq."
Ibn Ḥawālah said, "Choose for me, O Messenger of Allah, should I live to see that." He said:

"Go to Syria, for it is Allah's chosen land of His earth; He gathers to it His chosen ones among His servants. But if you refuse, then go to your Yemen and drink from your pools, for Allah has guaranteed Syria and its people for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
said, "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to go wandering." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The wandering of my Ummah is jihad in the cause of Allah, the Exalted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "The return is like the expedition."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman called Umm Khallād came to the Prophet ﷺ, veiled, asking about her son, who had been killed. One of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said to her, "You have come asking about your son while you are veiled?" She said, "If I have been afflicted with the loss of my son, I will not be afflicted with the loss of my modesty."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Your son will have the reward of two martyrs."
She said, "Why is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Because the People of the Book killed him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None should travel by sea except one performing Hajj, or ʿUmrah, or fighting in the cause of Allah, for beneath the sea is fire, and beneath the fire is a sea."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ slept and then woke up while she was washing her head. He woke up laughing, and she said, "O Messenger of Allah, are you laughing at my head?" He said, "No."
And he related this report with additions and omissions.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I acquired a piece of land from the land of Khaybar, so I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "I have acquired land; I have never acquired any wealth that I love more or that is more precious to me than it."
And he narrated the hadith like theirs, without mentioning "So I narrated it to Muhammad" and what follows.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Thursday! And what a Thursday!"
Then his tears began to flow until I saw them on his cheeks like strings of pearls.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Bring me the shoulder blade and the inkwell—or the tablet and the inkwell—so that I may write for you a document after which you will never go astray."
They said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is raving."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik; and Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us,
and ʿAmr al-Nāqid and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ibn ʿUyaynah,
and Ḥarmalah ibn Yaḥyā narrated to me,
Ibn Wahb informed us; Yūnus informed me,
and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us,
and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd,
both said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us; Maʿmar informed us,
and ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us,
ʿAbdah ibn Sulaymān narrated to us,
from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah,
from Bakr ibn Wāʾil,
all of them from al-Zuhrī,
with the chain of al-Layth and the meaning of his hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
they said: Sufyān narrated to us,
ibn ʿUyaynah, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father,
who said: The Prophet ﷺ heard ʿUmar swearing by his father.
Like the narration of Yūnus and Maʿmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Like this account from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were on foot, so we came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ asking him to provide us with mounts.
Similar to the hadith of Jarīr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A beggar came to ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim and asked him for money toward the price of a servant, or part of the price of a servant.
He said, "I have nothing to give you except my coat of mail and my helmet, so I will write to my family to give them to you."

He said: The man was not satisfied, so ʿAdī became angry and said, "By Allah, I will not give you anything!" Then the man was satisfied, and he said, "By Allah, were it not that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever swears an oath and then sees something more God-fearing than it, let him do what is more God-fearing,'
I would not have broken my oath."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And
a man came to him asking him for a hundred dirhams.
He said, "You ask me for a hundred dirhams while I am the son of Ḥātim? By Allah, I will not give you."
Then he said, "Were it not that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, let him do what is better.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ returned from Ḥunayn, ʿUmar asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a vow he had made in the Time of Ignorance to spend a day in devotional retreat (iʿtikāf).
Then he mentioned it with the meaning of the hadith of Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The ʿUmrah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from al-Jiʿrānah was mentioned in the presence of Ibn ʿUmar, and he said, "He did not perform ʿUmrah from there." He said: And ʿUmar had vowed to spend a night in devotional retreat (iʿtikāf) in the Time of Ignorance.
Then he mentioned it similar to the hadith of Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim and Maʿmar from Ayyūb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of Shuʿbah and Abū ʿAwānah. As for the hadith of Ibn Mahdī, he mentioned in it:
"a prescribed punishment he had not committed."
And in the hadith of Wakīʿ:
"Whoever slaps his slave."
And he did not mention the prescribed punishment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to sell cloth in the house of Suwayd ibn Muqarrin, the brother of al-Nuʿmān ibn Muqarrin. A slave girl came out and said a word to one of our men, and he slapped her, so Suwayd became angry.
Then he mentioned it similar to the hadith of Ibn Idrīs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir said to me, "What is your name?" I said, "Shuʿbah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he was beating his slave, who began to say, "I seek refuge in Allah." He said: But he kept beating him, so the slave said, "I seek refuge in the Messenger of Allah."
So he let him go, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By Allah, Allah has more power over you than you have over him." He said: So he set him free.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"The slave is owed his food and clothing, and he is not to be burdened with work except what he can bear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a man

freed six slaves of his at the time of his death, and he had no wealth other than them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned them, divided them into three groups, then cast lots among them, and freed two and kept four in slavery. And he spoke harshly to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sale of the mudabbar (a slave to be freed upon his master's death).
All of these said, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the meaning of the hadith of Ḥammād and Ibn ʿUyaynah from ʿAmr from Jābir.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of people from ʿUraynah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, accepted Islam and pledged allegiance to him, and the mūm—which is birsām (pleurisy)—had broken out in Madinah. Then he mentioned it similar to their hadith and added: and with him were young men of the Anṣār, about twenty horsemen, so he sent them after them and sent with them a tracker to follow their trail.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a household among us called the Banū Ubayriq: Bishr, Bushayr, and Mubashshir. Bushayr was a hypocrite who composed poetry satirizing the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then attributed it to some of the Arabs, saying, "So-and-so said such and such; so-and-so said such and such." When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard that poetry, they would say, "By Allah, no one says this poetry except that wretch," or words to that effect, and they said, "Ibn al-Ubayriq said it." He said: They were a household of need and poverty in the Jāhiliyyah and in Islam. The people's food in Madinah was only dates and barley. When a man was well off and a caravan of traders arrived from Syria with fine white flour, he would buy some of it and keep it for himself, while his family's food was only dates and barley. A caravan arrived from Syria, and my uncle Rifāʿah ibn Zayd bought a load of fine flour and put it in a storeroom of his. In the storeroom were weapons, a coat of mail, and a sword. It was raided from beneath the house: the storeroom was tunneled into, and the food and weapons were taken. When morning came, my uncle Rifāʿah came to me and said, "My nephew, we were raided this night; our storeroom was broken into and our food and weapons were taken."
He said: So we searched around the house and asked, and we were told, "We saw the Banū Ubayriq light a fire this night, and we think it was only on some of your food."

He said: The Banū Ubayriq had said, while we were asking around the house, "By Allah, we think the culprit can only be Labīd ibn Sahl," a man among us known for his righteousness and Islam. When Labīd heard this, he drew his sword and said, "Me, steal? By Allah, this sword will mix with you [in combat] unless you make this theft clear!"
They said, "Keep away from this, man! You are not the one who did it."
We kept asking around the house until we had no doubt that they were the culprits. Then my uncle said to me, "My nephew, if only you would go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mention this to him."

Qatādah said: So I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "A household among us, people of rudeness, set upon my uncle Rifāʿah ibn Zayd, tunneled into a storeroom of his, and took his weapons and food. Let them return our weapons; as for the food, we have no need of it." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"I will look into the matter."

When the Banū Ubayriq heard of this, they went to a man of theirs called Usayr ibn ʿUrwah and spoke to him about it. Some people from the household gathered around this, and they said, "Messenger of Allah, Qatādah ibn al-Nuʿmān and his uncle have set upon a household of ours, people of Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without proof or evidence."
Qatādah said: I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke to him, and he said:
"You have set upon a household of whom Islam and righteousness have been mentioned, accusing them of theft without evidence or proof."

He said: So I returned, wishing that I had lost some of my wealth and had not spoken to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this. Then my uncle Rifāʿah came to me and said, "My nephew, what did you do?" I told him what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said to me. He said, "Allah is the One whose help is sought." Not long after, the Qur'an was revealed:
"Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous," meaning the Banū Ubayriq:
"And seek forgiveness of Allah," that is, for what you said to Qatādah:

"Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not like one who is treacherous and sinful. They conceal [their evil] from the people and do not conceal it from Allah," up to His saying:
"Forgiving, Merciful," that is, had they sought forgiveness from Allah, He would have forgiven them:
"And whoever earns a sin only earns it against himself," up to His saying:
"a manifest sin," referring to their statement about Labīd:
"And if it were not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy," up to His saying:

"We will give him a great reward." When the Qur'an was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought the weapons and returned them to Rifāʿah. Qatādah said: When I brought the weapons to my uncle, he was an old man who had gone dim-sighted or blind in the Jāhiliyyah, and I had thought his Islam was flawed. But when I brought him the weapons, he said, "My nephew, it is in the cause of Allah." So I knew that his Islam was sound. When the Qur'an was revealed, Bushayr joined the polytheists and stayed with Sulāfah bint Saʿd ibn Sumayyah. Then Allah revealed:

"And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers, We will turn him to what he has chosen and burn him in Hell, and what an evil destination. Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray." When he stayed with Sulāfah, Ḥassān ibn Thābit attacked her with verses of his poetry. She took his baggage, put it on her head, went out, and threw it down in the Abṭaḥ, then said, "You brought me Ḥassān's poetry! You brought me nothing good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Thaʿlabah, from the Prophet ﷺ. (Transfer of chain) And Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā an-Naysābūrī narrated to us:
Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us; Hammām narrated to us,
from Bakr al-Kūfī.
Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā said: He is Bakr ibn Wāʾil ibn Dāwūd, that az-Zuhrī
narrated to them from ʿAbdullāh ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Ṣuʿayr, from his father, who said:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood to deliver a sermon, and he commanded the charity of Fiṭr: one ṣāʿ of dates or one ṣāʿ of barley per person. ʿAlī added in his narration: or one ṣāʿ of wheat between two people. Then they both agreed: on behalf of the young and the old, the free and the slave.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Shihāb said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Thaʿlabah said, and Ibn Ṣāliḥ said, al-ʿAdawī said, but it is actually al-ʿUdhrī: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed the people two days before al-Fiṭr, similar in meaning to the narration of al-Muqriʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn and al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis came to the Messenger of Allah and asked him, so he ordered that they be given what they asked for, and he ordered Muʿāwiyah, who wrote for them what they asked. As for al-Aqraʿ, he took his document, wrapped it in his turban and left. As for ʿUyaynah, he took his document and came to the Prophet ﷺ right away and said: O Muḥammad, do you think I will carry to my people a document whose contents I do not know, like the document of al-Mutalammis?
Muʿāwiyah informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of his words, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever asks while he has what suffices him is only seeking to increase [his share] of the Fire."
And an-Nufaylī said in another place:
"[He is seeking to increase] the embers of Hell."
They said: O Messenger of Allah, what is it that suffices him? And an-Nufaylī said in another place: What is the wealth with which asking is no longer proper? He said:
"The amount that provides him lunch and dinner."
And an-Nufaylī said in another place:
"That he has enough to be full for a day and a night, or a night and a day."
He had narrated it to us in abridged form with these words that I have mentioned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and pledged allegiance to him. Then he mentioned a long hadith, saying: A man came to him and said: Give me some of the charity.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:

"Allah, the Exalted, was not pleased with the ruling of a prophet or anyone else concerning charities until He Himself ruled on them. He divided them into eight parts. If you are among those parts, I will give you your due."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿUmar,
and Abū Kāmil, the meaning being the same, said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us; Maʿmar narrated to us, from az-Zuhrī,
from Abū Salamah,
from Abū Hurayrah, who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said something similar. He said:
"But the poor person is the one who abstains from asking."
Musaddad added in his narration:
"He does not have what makes him self-sufficient, yet he does not ask, and his need is not known so that charity could be given to him; that is the deprived one."
And Musaddad did not mention:
"the one who abstains, who does not ask."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Charity is not permissible for a rich person, except [one who is] in the cause of Allah, or a traveler, or a poor neighbor who is given charity and then gives you a gift or invites you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Thawbān, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever guarantees to me that he will not ask people for anything, I will guarantee Paradise for him."
Thawbān said: I will.
So he never asked anyone for anything.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Hands are of three kinds: the hand of Allah is the uppermost; the hand of the giver is next to it; and the hand of the one who asks is the lowest. So give from what is surplus, and do not be incapable of providing for yourself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would pass by a stray date, and nothing prevented him from taking it except the fear that it might be charity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father sent me to the Prophet ﷺ with camels that he had given him from the charity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we used to count al-māʿūn as lending a bucket and a cooking pot.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [say] something like this account. He said to him, meaning to Abū Hurayrah: What is the right owed on camels? He said: Giving the best of them, lending out the milk-rich female, letting the back be used, letting the stud male cover, and giving milk to drink.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū az-Zubayr said: I heard ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr
say: A man said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the right owed on camels? Then he mentioned something similar, adding: "and lending out its bucket."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ commanded that from every [tree yielding] ten wasqs of dates, a cluster be hung in the mosque for the poor.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Khalīfah said to me: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah,
from Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, that he reported to them that the people of Makkah asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to show them a sign,
so he showed them the splitting of the moon.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat on the pulpit and said:
"A servant was given a choice by Allah between being given the splendor of this world and what is with Him, and he chose what is with Him."
Abū Bakr wept, and he wept, and said: "May we ransom you with our fathers and mothers."
[The narrator] said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the one who was given the choice, and Abū Bakr was the most knowledgeable of us about him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed, the person who has been most generous to me with his wealth and his companionship is Abū Bakr. If I were to take a close friend (khalīl), I would take Abū Bakr as a close friend, but [there is] the brotherhood of Islam. Let no small door remain in the mosque except the door of Abū Bakr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I have not heard the Prophet ﷺ say of anyone walking on the earth that he is of the people of Paradise,
except of ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām. He said: And it was regarding him that this verse was revealed: {And a witness from the Children of Israel bore witness}, the verse.
He said: I do not know whether Mālik said "the verse" or whether it was in the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Masrūq: Who informed the Prophet ﷺ about the jinn on the night they listened to the Qurʾān? He said: Your father, meaning Ibn Masʿūd, narrated to me that a tree informed him about them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Khadījah died three years before the Prophet ﷺ left for Madīnah.
He stayed [in Makkah] for two years or about that,
and he married ʿĀʾishah when she was six years old,
then he consummated the marriage with her when she was nine years old.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the time of al-Ḥudaybiyah. His Companions entered the state of iḥrām, but I did not. Then I saw a donkey, so I attacked it and hunted it. I mentioned the matter to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I mentioned that I had not been in iḥrām and that I had hunted it only for you. So the Prophet ﷺ ordered his Companions and they ate, but he did not eat from it when I told him that I had hunted it for him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of the Tree were one thousand three hundred, and Aslam made up one-eighth of the Muhājirūn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went to aṭ-Ṭūr and met Kaʿb there. I stayed with him for a day, telling him about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he told me about the Torah. I said to him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was brought down to earth, on it his repentance was accepted, on it he died, and on it the Hour will come. There is no creature on earth that does not wait attentively on Friday morning until the sun rises, in fear of the Hour, except jinn and mankind. And on it there is an hour which a believer does not happen to meet while he is praying and asking Allah for something, except that He gives it to him."
Kaʿb said: That is one day in every year.
I said: Rather, it is every Friday.
Kaʿb read the Torah and then said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke the truth; it is on every Friday.
Then I went out and met Baṣrah ibn Abī Baṣrah al-Ghifārī, who said: Where have you come from? I said: From aṭ-Ṭūr.
He said: If I had met you before you went there, you would not have gone.
I asked him: Why? He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
Saddle animals are not to be set out except for three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, my mosque, and the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis."

Then I met ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām and said: If only you had seen me. I went out to aṭ-Ṭūr and met Kaʿb, and I stayed with him for a day, telling him about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he told me about the Torah. I said to him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was brought down to earth, on it his repentance was accepted, on it he died, and on it the Hour will come. There is no creature on earth that does not wait attentively on Friday morning until the sun rises, in fear of the Hour, except jinn and mankind. And on it there is an hour which a believing servant does not happen to meet while he is praying and asking Allah for something, except that He gives it to him."
Kaʿb said: That is one day in every year.
ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām said: Kaʿb lied.
I said: Then Kaʿb read [the Torah] and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke the truth; it is on every Friday.
ʿAbdullāh said: Kaʿb is right. I know that hour. I said: My brother, tell me about it.
He said: It is the last hour of Friday before the sun sets. I said: Did I not hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
A believer does not happen to meet it while he is praying"?
But that hour is not a time of prayer. He said: Did you not hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
Whoever prays and then sits waiting for the prayer remains in prayer until the prayer comes to him that he is waiting for"? I said: Yes.
He said: Then it is just so.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever leaves the Friday prayer without an excuse should give a dinar in charity, and if he cannot find one, then half a dinar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "
Two Eids have come together on this day of yours. Whoever wishes, it suffices him in place of the Friday prayer, but we will hold the Friday prayer."
ʿUmar said, from Shuʿbah:
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr,
that Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī
narrated to him that Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabbān narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
It would not harm any of you if he were able" or: "
It would not harm any of you, if you were able, to take two garments for Friday besides the two garments of his work clothes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The call to prayer used to be made in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he sat on the pulpit on Friday, at the door of the mosque, and also in the time of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
Then he related it similarly to the hadith of Yūnus.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
If any of you breaks wind during his prayer, let him hold his nose and then leave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sulayk al-Ghaṭafānī came while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was delivering the sermon, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "
Did you pray two rakʿahs before you came?" He said: No. He said: "
Then pray two rakʿahs and keep them brief."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If any of you feels drowsy while he is in the mosque, let him move from his seat to another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would come down from the pulpit, and a man would approach him and speak to him, and the Prophet ﷺ would stand with him until he had finished his need. Then he would go forward to his place of prayer and pray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to sleep while in a state of major impurity, he would perform ablution as for prayer before sleeping.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār,
from Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he became in need of a purifying bath during the night, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Perform ablution, wash your private part, then sleep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, coinciding with the crescent of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. When we were at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, he said:
"Whoever wishes to assume ihram for Hajj, let him do so, and whoever wishes to assume ihram for ʿUmrah, let him do so for ʿUmrah."
Mūsā said in the narration of Wuhayb:
"Had I not brought sacrificial animals, I would have assumed ihram for ʿUmrah."
And he said in the narration of Ḥammād ibn Salamah:
"As for me, I assume ihram for Hajj, for I have the sacrificial animals with me."

Then they agreed [on the rest]: I was among those who assumed ihram for ʿUmrah. When we were part of the way, I began to menstruate. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me while I was weeping and said, "What makes you weep?"
I said, "I wish I had not gone out this year." He said:
"Give up your ʿUmrah, undo your hair, and comb it." Mūsā said: "and assume ihram for Hajj." And Sulaymān said:
"and do what the Muslims do in their Hajj."
When it was the night of departure, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and he took her to al-Tanʿīm.
Mūsā added: She assumed ihram for an ʿUmrah in place of her [earlier] ʿUmrah and circled the House, and Allah thereby completed her ʿUmrah and her Hajj.
Hishām said: In none of that was there a sacrificial animal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr and some people to look for a necklace of ʿĀʾishah that she had forgotten at a place where they had camped. The time for prayer came while they were not in a state of ablution and could not find water, so they prayed without ablution. They mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed the verse of tayammum. Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr said, "May Allah reward you with good! By Allah, no matter ever befell you that you disliked, except that Allah made good come from it for you and for the Muslims."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥah,
from Anas ibn Mālik, that his grandmother
Mulaykah invited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to a meal she had prepared. He ate from it, then said:
"Get up, so that I may lead you in prayer."

Anas ibn Mālik said: I got up and went to a mat of ours that had turned black from long use, and sprinkled it with water. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood on it, and the orphan and I formed a row behind him, with the old woman behind us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed two rakʿahs with us, then departed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He demanded repayment from Ibn Abī Ḥadrad of a debt that he owed him, in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the mosque. Their voices rose until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard them while he was in his house. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to them, lifting the curtain of his room, and called Kaʿb ibn Mālik, saying, "O Kaʿb!"
He said, "At your service, O Messenger of Allah."
He gestured to him with his hand, [signaling] to remit half of his debt.
Kaʿb said, "I have done so, O Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Get up and pay him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the verses of Sūrat al-Baqarah concerning usury were revealed,
the Prophet ﷺ went out to the mosque,
and recited them to the people,
then he prohibited the trade in wine.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Are you not [now] in as much food and drink as you wish? I saw your Prophet ﷺ, and he could not find even bad dates to fill his belly.
He said: This is a sound hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ lay down on a mat, and it left marks on his skin. I said, "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah! If only you had permitted us, we would have spread something over it for you to protect you from it."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What have I to do with this world? I am in this world only like a rider who takes shade under a tree, then goes on his way and leaves it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The son of Adam has never filled a vessel worse than his belly. It is enough for the son of Adam to have a few morsels to keep his back upright. But if it must be so, then a third for his food, a third for his drink, and a third for his breath."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Seek refuge with Allah from the Pit of Sorrow."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the Pit of Sorrow?" He said:
"A valley in Hell from which Hell itself seeks refuge four hundred times every day."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, who will enter it?" He said:
"It has been prepared for the reciters who show off with their deeds. And among the most hated of reciters to Allah are those who visit the rulers."
Al-Muḥāribī said: al-jawrah [meaning, those who visit the rulers].”
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, a man does a deed in secret and it pleases him, but when it becomes known it pleases him [too]." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He has two rewards: the reward of secrecy and the reward of openness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which people are most severely tested?" He said:

"The prophets, then the next best and the next best. A servant is tested according to his religion. If he is firm in his religion, his trial is severe, and if there is softness in his religion, he is tested according to his religion. Trials will keep afflicting a servant until they leave him walking on the earth with no sin upon him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, tell me of something I may hold fast to." He said:
"Say, 'My Lord is Allah,' then stay upright."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you fear most for me?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of his own tongue and then said, "This."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A wife of the Prophet ﷺ reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:
"All the speech of the son of Adam is against him, not for him, except enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong, or remembering Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"People will be presented [before Allah] on the Day of Resurrection in three presentations. As for two presentations, they will be disputation and excuses. As for the third presentation, at that time the records will fly into the hands: one will take his in his right hand and another will take his in his left."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My Lord, glorified is He, promised me that He would admit into Paradise seventy thousand of my Ummah without reckoning or punishment, and with every thousand seventy thousand more, and three handfuls from the handfuls of my Lord, Mighty and Majestic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"One came to me from my Lord and gave me the choice between half of my Ummah entering Paradise and intercession, so I chose intercession. It is for whoever dies without associating anything with Allah."
It has also been narrated from Abū al-Malīḥ, from another man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, from the Prophet ﷺ, without mentioning ʿAwf ibn Mālik. The hadith has a long story.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz sent for me, and I came to him by post-horse. When I arrived, he said, "We have put you to hardship in your travel, O Abū Sallām."
He said, "Indeed, by Allah, O Commander of the Faithful."

He said, "By Allah, I did not intend hardship for you, but a hadith has reached me that you narrate from Thawbān, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, about the Pond, and I wished you to tell it to me directly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was
among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A servant does not reach the rank of the God-fearing until he leaves what is not harmful out of caution against what is harmful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The people of Paradise will be one hundred and twenty rows: eighty of them from this Ummah and forty from all the other nations."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he was asked about a man
who had two slave girls; one of them nursed a girl and the other nursed a boy. Is it lawful for the boy to marry the girl? He said: No, the milk is one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the husband of

Barīrah was a black slave belonging to the Banū al-Mughīrah on the day Barīrah was freed. By Allah, it is as if I can see him in the roads of Madīnah and its outskirts, with tears running down his beard, begging her to choose him, but she did not.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When a man calls his wife for his need, let her come to him, even if she is at the oven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, one of us may be in the open desert and some wind passes from him, and there is little water. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you passes wind, let him perform ablution, and do not approach women through their backsides, for Allah is not shy of the truth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah will not look at a man who approaches a man or a woman in the rear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you passes wind, let him perform ablution, and do not approach women through their backsides."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And she was
a servant of the Prophet ﷺ. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The likeness of the woman who trails along in adornment among people who are not her family is like the darkness on the Day of Resurrection, having no light."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Do not enter upon women whose husbands are away, for Satan runs through one of you like blood."
We said: And through you? He said:
"And through me, but Allah helped me against him, so he submitted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Woman is ʿawrah; when she goes out, Satan looks eagerly at her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Women who seek khulʿ without cause are the hypocrites."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every divorce is valid except the divorce of the feeble-minded person whose reason is overcome."
label: machine translation

segments_en: People used to be such that a man could divorce his wife as many times as he wished, and she remained his wife if he took her back while she was in her waiting period, even if he divorced her a hundred times or more, until a man said to his wife: By Allah, I will not divorce you so that you become separated from me, and I will never shelter you.
She said: How is that? He said: I divorce you, and whenever your waiting period is about to end, I take you back.
The woman went and entered upon ʿĀʾishah and told her. ʿĀʾishah remained silent until the Prophet ﷺ came, and she told him. The Prophet ﷺ remained silent until the Qurʾān was revealed:
"Divorce is twice, then either retention in a proper manner or release with kindness." ʿĀʾishah said: So people began divorce anew from then on, whether they had previously divorced or not.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Salamah ibn Ṣakhr al-Anṣārī,

one of the Banū Bayāḍah, declared his wife to be to him like his mother's back until Ramadan passed. When half of Ramadan had passed, he had relations with her at night. He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Free a slave."
He said: I do not find one. He said:
"Then fast two consecutive months."
He said: I am not able to. He said:
"Feed sixty poor people."
He said: I do not have the means.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Farwah ibn ʿAmr:
"Give him that basket."
It was a large basket holding fifteen or sixteen ṣāʿ. Then he said:
"Feed sixty poor people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the people of the measure and the scale:
"You have been put in charge of two matters in which the nations before you perished."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sold a saddle blanket and a drinking bowl, and he said:
"Who will buy this blanket and bowl?"
A man said: I will take them for one dirham. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Who will offer more than one dirham? Who will offer more than one dirham?"
A man gave him two dirhams, so he sold them to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He said: And on this topic there are narrations from Anas, ʿĀʾishah, Abū Hurayrah, Ibn ʿAbbās, Jābir, Abū Saʿīd and Zayd ibn Thābit.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Gold for gold, like for like; silver for silver, like for like; dates for dates, like for like; wheat for wheat, like for like; salt for salt, like for like; barley for barley, like for like. Whoever gives more or asks for more has engaged in usury. Sell gold for silver however you wish, hand to hand; sell wheat for dates however you wish, hand to hand; and sell barley for dates however you wish, hand to hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two parties to a sale must not part except by mutual consent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ gave a Bedouin the option after the sale.
This is a ḥasan gharīb ḥadīth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he sold a camel to the Prophet ﷺ and stipulated that he could ride it back to his family.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah used to say: "Among the blessings Allah bestowed upon me is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died in my house, on my day,
resting between my chest and my throat,
and that Allah brought together my saliva and his saliva at the time of his death.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān came in to me with a tooth-stick in his hand, while I was supporting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I saw him looking at it.
I knew that he liked the tooth-stick, so I said, 'Shall I take it for you?' He nodded his head, meaning yes.
So I took it, but it was too hard for him, and I said, 'Shall I soften it for you?' He nodded his head, meaning yes. So I softened it.
In front of him was a small container of water or a bowl—ʿUmar was unsure which—
and he began putting his hands into the water and wiping his face with them, saying:
'There is no god but Allah.
Indeed, death has its agonies.'
Then he raised his hand and began saying:
'With the Highest Companion.'
until he passed away and his hand dropped."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The cup of the Prophet ﷺ was broken,
so he mended the crack with a chain of silver.
ʿĀṣim said: I saw the cup and I drank from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, were to have mentioned ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, he would have mentioned him on the day some people came to him and complained about ʿUthmān's collectors.
ʿAlī said to me, "Go to ʿUthmān and tell him that this is the charity of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
so order your collectors to act upon it."
So I brought it to him, and he said, "Put it away from us."
Then I brought it to ʿAlī and told him, and he said, "Put it back where you took it from."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father sent me, saying:
"Take this letter and go with it to ʿUthmān,
for in it is the command of the Prophet ﷺ concerning charity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, there are men who wrongfully dip into the wealth of Allah,
and for them is the Fire on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"War spoils have been made lawful for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
- and the wording is his - from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Nuʿaym ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Mujmir,
that Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd al-Anṣārī,
- and ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd is the one who was shown the call to prayer [in a dream] - informed him from Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī,

that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us in the gathering of Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah, and Bashīr ibn Saʿd said to him: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded us to send blessings upon you, O Messenger of Allah, so how should we send blessings upon you? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent until we wished that he had not asked him. Then he said:

"Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad and upon the family of Muḥammad, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrāhīm, and bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrāhīm, in all the worlds. Truly, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. And the greeting of peace is as you have been taught."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell ill, so we prayed behind him while he was sitting, and Abū Bakr was calling out the takbīr so that the people could hear his takbīr. He turned to us and saw us standing, so he gestured to us and we sat, and we prayed following his prayer, sitting. When he finished the prayer with the salām, he said:

"You were just now about to do what the Persians and the Romans do, standing over their kings while they are seated. Do not do so. Follow your imams: if he prays standing, pray standing, and if he prays sitting, pray sitting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed the dawn prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and in one of the two rakʿahs he recited: {And the tall palm trees with their layered spathes}. Shuʿbah said: I met him in the marketplace in the crowd, and he said: {Qāf}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Alqamah led us in the Ẓuhr prayer [and prayed] five [rakʿahs]. When he finished with the salām, the people said: O Abū Shibl, you prayed five.
He said: No, I did not do that.
They said: Yes. [The narrator] said: I was at the edge of the people, and I was a youth, and I said: Yes, you prayed five.
He said to me: And you too, O one-eyed one, say that? I said: Yes.

He then turned, performed two prostrations, then ended with the salām, and then said: ʿAbdullāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer [and prayed] five. When he turned, the people whispered among themselves, and he said: "What is the matter with you?"
They said: O Messenger of Allah, has something been added to the prayer? He said: "No."
They said: But you have prayed five.
So he turned, then performed two prostrations, then ended with the salām, and then said:
"I am only a human being like you; I forget just as you forget."
And Ibn Numayr added in his narration:
"So when any of you forgets, let him perform two prostrations."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The heaviest prayers upon the hypocrites are the ʿIshāʾ prayer and the Fajr prayer. If they knew what is in them, they would come to them even if crawling. I have indeed considered ordering that the prayer be established, then ordering a man to lead the people in prayer, and then going out with men who carry bundles of firewood to a people who do not attend the prayer, and burning their houses down upon them with fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
- and the wording is his - from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Abū az-Zubayr al-Makkī,
from Abū aṭ-Ṭufayl,
ʿĀmir ibn Wāthilah, that Muʿādh ibn Jabal informed him that they

went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year of Tabūk, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would combine the Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr prayers, and the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers. One day he delayed the prayer, then came out and prayed Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr together, then went in, then came out and prayed Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ [together].
label: machine translation

segments_en: When we prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we liked to be on his right, so that he would turn to us with his face. [The narrator] said: I heard him say:
"My Lord, protect me from Your punishment on the day You resurrect - or gather - Your servants."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Pray the Witr before the morning comes."
Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā said: In this hadith is evidence that the hadith of ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān is weak.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr saw me standing at a funeral while he was sitting, waiting for the bier to be put down. He said to me: What keeps you standing? I said: I am waiting for the bier to be put down, because of what Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrates.
Nāfiʿ said: Masʿūd ibn al-Ḥakam narrated to me from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, then he sat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he had a cluster of date palms in the orchard of a man from the Anṣār. He said: The man had his family with him. Samurah would go in to his palm tree, and the man was harmed and troubled by it. So he asked him to sell it, but he refused; he asked him to exchange it, but he refused. Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him. The Prophet ﷺ asked him to sell it, but he refused; he asked him to exchange it, but he refused. He said:
"Then give it to him, and you will have such and such,"
a matter he made him desire, but he refused. So he said, "You are causing harm."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Anṣārī:
"Go and uproot his palm tree."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men brought a dispute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the boundary area of a palm tree. In the report of one of them: He ordered that it be measured, and it was found to be seven cubits. In the report of the other: It was found to be five cubits. So he ruled accordingly.
ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: He ordered that one of its palm branches be used, and it was measured.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met Shabīb ibn Shaybah and he narrated it to me,
from ʿUthmān ibn Abī Sawdah,
from Abū al-Dardāʾ,
meaning from the Prophet ﷺ, with similar meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That while he was sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a man from the Jews was with him, a funeral procession passed by. He said, "O Muhammad, does this corpse speak?" The Prophet ﷺ said, "Allah knows best."
The Jew said, "It does speak."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whatever the People of the Book tell you, do not believe them and do not disbelieve them, but say: 'We believe in Allah and His messengers.' For if it is false, you will not have believed it, and if it is true, you will not have denied it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to write down everything I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, wanting to memorize it. But Quraysh forbade me and said, "Do you write down everything you hear, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is a human being who speaks in anger and in contentment?" So I stopped writing. I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he pointed with his finger to his mouth and said:
"Write! By the One in whose hand is my soul, nothing comes out of it except the truth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zayd ibn Thābit entered upon Muʿāwiyah, who asked him about a hadith,
and he ordered a person to write it down. Zayd said to him, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us not to write anything of his sayings," so he erased it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We did not write anything except the tashahhud and the Qurʾān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Abū ʿAmr, "What did they write?" He said, "The sermon that he heard from him on that day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A servant] of the Prophet ﷺ [reported] that the Prophet ﷺ, when he said something, would repeat it three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ forbade difficult questions meant to confound.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Whoever gives a legal opinion..."

Transfer of isnād: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb narrated to me, from Bakr ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAmr ibn Abī Nuʿaymah, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Ṭunbudhī, the foster brother of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān, who said: I heard Abū Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is given a legal opinion without knowledge, its sin is upon the one who gave it."
Sulaymān al-Mahrī added in his narration:
"And whoever advises his brother on a matter while knowing that the right course lies elsewhere has betrayed him."
And this is the wording of Sulaymān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You hear and are heard from, and those who heard from you will be heard from."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no blame."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ would narrate to us about the Children of Israel until morning, not getting up except for the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from among the Ansār was on the verge of death, and he said: "I will narrate to you a hadith that I narrate only seeking reward from Allah. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "

"When one of you performs ablution and does it well, then goes out to prayer, he does not raise his right foot except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, records a good deed for him, and he does not put down his left foot except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, erases a sin from him. So let one of you live near or far. If he comes to the mosque and prays in congregation, he is forgiven. If he comes to the mosque and they have prayed part of the prayer and part remains, he prays what he catches and completes what remains, and it is the same for him. And if he comes to the mosque and they have already prayed, and he completes the prayer, it is the same for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman's prayer in her house is better than her prayer in her courtyard, and her prayer in her inner chamber is better than her prayer in her house."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man praying alone, and he said: "
Is there no man who will give charity to this man by praying with him?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: What prevented you two from praying with us?"
They said: "We already prayed in our camping places." He said: "
Do not do that. If one of you has prayed in his dwelling and then reaches the imam who has not yet prayed, let him pray with him, for it will be a voluntary prayer for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came while the Prophet ﷺ was in prayer, so I sat and did not join them in the prayer. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to us, saw Yazīd sitting, and said: "
Have you not become Muslim, Yazīd?"
He said: "Yes, Messenger of Allah, I have become Muslim." He said: "
Then what prevented you from joining the people in their prayer?"
He said: "I had already prayed in my house, and I thought that you had already prayed." He said: "
When you come to the prayer and find people praying, pray with them, even if you have already prayed. It will be a voluntary prayer for you, and this one the obligatory."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Ibn Wahb, who said: ʿAmr informed me, from Bukayr,
that he heard ʿAfīf ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Musayyib
say: A man narrated to me,

from Banū Asad ibn Khuzaymah, that he asked Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī, saying: "One of us prays the prayer in his house, then comes to the mosque and the prayer is being established, so I pray with them, but I feel some uneasiness about that."
Abū Ayyūb said: "We asked the Prophet ﷺ about that, and he said: "
That one has the share of one who prayed in congregation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

The people are to be led in prayer by the one who recites the Book of Allah best, and who was earliest in reciting. If they are equal in recitation, then the one who emigrated earliest should lead them. If they are equal in emigration, then the eldest in age should lead them. A man must not lead another in his own house or in his domain of authority, and he must not sit on his special seat except with his permission."
Shuʿbah said: I said to Ismāʿīl, "What is his takrimah?" He said: "His bedding."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were living by a watering place that people passed by when they went to the Prophet ﷺ. When they returned they would pass by us and tell us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said such and such. I was a boy with a good memory, so I memorized much of the Qurʾān from that. Then my father went as part of a delegation to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a group of his people, and he taught them the prayer and said: "The one who recites the most among you should lead you."

I was the one who recited the most, because of what I had memorized, so they put me forward and I led them in prayer, wearing a small yellow cloak of mine. When I prostrated, it would ride up and expose me, and one of the women said: "Cover from us the private parts of your reciter."
So they bought me an Omani shirt, and I never felt joy at anything after Islam like my joy in it. I used to lead them in prayer when I was seven or eight years old.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this report he said: I used to lead them wearing a cloak that had been patched together and had a tear in it, so when I prostrated, my backside would show.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They came as a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ, and when they wanted to leave, they said: "Messenger of Allah, who should lead us in prayer?" He said: "
The one among you who has collected the most of the Qurʾān," or he said: "who has taken the most of the Qurʾān."

He said: None of the people had collected as much as I had. He said: So they put me forward while I was a boy, wearing a small wrapper of mine. I never attended a gathering of Jarm without being their imam, and I prayed over their dead until this day of mine.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ:
that he drew a square line, and a line in the middle of the square, and lines beside the line that was in the middle of the square, and a line extending outside the square. Then he said: "
Do you know what this is?" They said:
"Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "

This is the human being—the middle line—and these lines beside him are the afflictions that gnaw at him from every side; if he escapes this one, that one strikes him. The square is the encompassing appointed term, and the line extending outside is hope."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a man praying on a rock. He went to the side of Makkah and stayed for a good while, then returned and found the man still praying in the same state. So he stood, brought his hands together, and said: "
O people, keep to moderation," three times, "
for Allah does not grow weary until you grow weary."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "
O ʿĀʾishah, beware of deeds that are belittled, for they have a seeker from Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

When a believer commits a sin, a black spot appears on his heart. If he repents, gives it up, and seeks forgiveness, his heart is polished clean. But if he increases [in sin], it increases. That is the rust (rān) which Allah mentioned in His Book: {No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts like rust.}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "

I surely know of people from my nation who will come on the Day of Resurrection with good deeds like the white mountains of Tihāmah, but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will make them scattered dust." Thawbān said:
"O Messenger of Allah, describe them to us, make them clear to us, so that we do not become of them without knowing it." He said: "
They are your brothers, of your own kind, and they take from the night as you take. But they are people who, when alone with what Allah has forbidden, violate it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If you were to commit sins until your sins reached the sky, and then you repented, He would accept your repentance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
