Allah is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than a man who loses his mount in a barren desert and searches for it until, when he is exhausted, he covers himself with his garment. While he is like that, he hears the thud of the mount where he had lost it, so he uncovers his face and finds his mount there."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered with my father upon ʿAbdullāh and heard him say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Regret is repentance."
My father said to him:
"Did you hear the Prophet ﷺ say: 'Regret is repentance'?" He said: "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a man from the Anṣār came to him and greeted the Prophet ﷺ, then said:
"O Messenger of Allah, which of the believers is best?" He said: "The best of them in character."
He said: "Which of the believers is the most astute?" He said: "
Those who remember death the most and prepare best for what comes after it. Those are the astute."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The angels attend the dying person. If the man is righteous, they say:

'Come out, O good soul, that was in a good body. Come out praised, and receive glad tidings of comfort and fragrance and a Lord who is not angry.' It continues to be said to it until it comes out. Then it is raised to the heaven and [the gate] is opened for it, and it is asked:
'Who is this?' They say: 'So-and-so.' Then it is said:
'Welcome to the good soul,
that was in a good body. Enter, praised,
and receive glad tidings of comfort and fragrance and a Lord who is not angry.'

It continues to be said to it until it reaches the heaven in which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is. But if the man is evil, [the angel] says: 'Come out, O wicked soul, that was in a wicked body. Come out, blameworthy, and receive tidings of scalding water and foul discharge,
and other torments of similar kind, in pairs.'
It continues to be said to it until it comes out. Then it is raised to the heaven, but [the gate] is not opened for it, and it is asked:
'Who is this?' It is said: 'So-and-so.' Then it is said:

'No welcome to the wicked soul that was in a wicked body. Go back, blameworthy, for the gates of heaven will not be opened for you.' Then it is sent down from the heaven, and then it goes to the grave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the appointed time of one of you is in a land, need drives him to it. Then when he reaches the farthest point of his footsteps, Allah, Glorified is He, takes him. Then on the Day of Resurrection the earth says:
'My Lord, this is what You entrusted to me.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Hudhayfah in al-Madāʾin. Hudhayfah asked for a drink, and a village chief came to him with a drink in a silver vessel. He threw it at him and said, "I am telling you that I had ordered him not to give me a drink in it, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Do not drink from vessels of gold and silver, and do not wear brocade and silk, for they belong to them in this world, and they will be yours in the Hereafter on the Day of Resurrection.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present when Hudhayfah asked for a drink in al-Madāʾin, and a man brought him a silver vessel.
Then he mentioned it with the same meaning as the hadith of Ibn ʿUkaym from Hudhayfah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Asmāʾ sent me to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and said, "It has reached me that you forbid three things: a decorative border on a garment, red saddle cloths, and fasting the whole of Rajab."

ʿAbd Allāh said to me, "As for what you mentioned about Rajab, what then of the one who fasts perpetually? As for what you mentioned about the border on a garment, I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Only one who has no share [in the Hereafter] wears silk.'
So I feared that the border was part of it. As for the red saddle cloth, this is ʿAbd Allāh's saddle cloth, and it is red."
I returned to Asmāʾ and told her, and she said, "This is the cloak of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

Then she brought out to me a Kisrawānī cloak of heavy wool with a brocade collar, and with its two side openings trimmed with brocade. She said, "This was with ʿĀʾishah until she died, and when she died I took it. The Prophet ﷺ used to wear it, and we wash it for the sick, seeking healing through it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw me wearing two garments dyed with safflower, and he said:
"Did your mother order you to do this?" I said, "I will wash them." He said, "Rather, burn them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, and Zayd,
ibn Aslam, all of them reporting from Ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah will not look at one who drags his garment out of arrogance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while my lower garment was hanging low, and he said:
"O ʿAbd Allāh, raise your lower garment."
So I raised it. Then he said, "More."
So I raised it more, and I have been careful about it ever since.
Some of the people asked, "To where?" He said, "To the middle of the shins."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, similar to this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a gold ring on a man's hand, so he removed it and threw it away, and said:
"One of you goes to a live coal from the Fire and puts it on his hand."
After the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had left, the man was told, "Take your ring and benefit from it."
He said, "No, by Allah, I will never take it, since the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has thrown it away."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a gold ring made, and when he wore it he would place its stone on the inside of his palm, so the people made [rings] too. Then he sat on the pulpit and removed it, and said:
"I used to wear this ring and place its stone on the inside."
Then he threw it away and said:
"By Allah, I will never wear it."
So the people discarded their rings.
The wording of the hadith is that of Yaḥyā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, with this [report], but he did not mention "Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah" in the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He forbade me, meaning the Prophet ﷺ, to put my ring on this finger or the one next to it (ʿĀṣim did not know which of the two), and he forbade me to wear qassī garments and to sit on maythara cushions.

He said: As for the qassī, they are garments with ribbed stripes brought from Egypt and Syria, having something like this in them. As for the mayāthir, they were something women would make for their husbands on the saddle, like red velvet cloths.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, with this meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a man to eat with his left hand, or to walk in a single sandal, or to wrap himself in a garment so as to cover his arms (ishtimāl aṣ-ṣammāʾ), or to sit hugging his knees in a single garment while exposing his private parts.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Do not walk in a single sandal, do not sit hugging your knees in a single lower garment, do not eat with your left hand, do not wrap yourself in a garment so as to cover your arms, and do not place one of your legs over the other when you lie on your back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Quḥāfah was brought, or came, in the year of the Conquest, or on the day of the Conquest, with his head and beard like thaghām (white plant), and he ordered, or ordered that he be taken to his women, and said:
"Change this with something."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are two qualities: whoever has them, Allah records him as grateful and patient; and whoever does not have them, Allah does not record him as grateful or patient. Whoever looks in matters of his religion to one who is above him and follows his example, and looks in matters of his worldly life to one who is below him and praises Allah for what He has favored him with over that person, Allah records him as grateful and patient. But whoever looks in matters of his religion to one who is below him, and looks in matters of his worldly life to one who is above him and grieves over what he has missed of it, Allah does not record him as grateful or patient."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day, and he said:

"Young man, I will teach you some words: Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the whole nation were to gather together to benefit you with something, they would not benefit you except with something Allah has already written for you; and if they were to gather together to harm you with something, they would not harm you except with something Allah has already written against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said: "Messenger of Allah, shall I tie it up and rely on Allah, or shall I let it loose and rely on Allah?" He said: "Tie it up and rely on Allah."
ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī said: Yaḥyā said: "In my view, this is a rejected (munkar) hadith."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ for his worship and diligence, and another was mentioned in his presence for his scrupulousness (waraʿ). The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do not equate anything with scrupulousness."
ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar is one of the descendants of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah; he is from Medina and is considered trustworthy by the scholars of hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever eats what is good, acts according to the Sunnah, and people are safe from his harm, will enter Paradise."
A man said: "Messenger of Allah, today such people are many among the people." He said:
"And there will be such people in the generations after me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no tree in Paradise except that its trunk is of gold."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"In Paradise there are one hundred levels; between each two levels is a distance of one hundred years."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever fasts Ramadan, performs the prayers, and performs Hajj to the House—I do not know whether he mentioned zakāh or not—it is a right upon Allah that He forgive him, whether he emigrates in the cause of Allah or remains in the land where he was born."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In Paradise there are one hundred levels; if all the worlds were gathered in one of them, it would hold them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman among the women of the people of Paradise will have the whiteness of her shin seen from behind seventy garments, until her marrow is seen. That is because Allah says:
'As if they were rubies and coral.' As for the ruby, it is a stone; if you were to pass a thread through it and then clear it, you would see the thread from behind it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The believer will be given in Paradise such and such strength for intercourse."
It was said: "Messenger of Allah, will he be able to do that?" He said:
"He will be given the strength of one hundred."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If what would fit on a fingernail of what is in Paradise were to appear, it would adorn everything between the horizons of the heavens and the earth. And if a man from the people of Paradise were to look out and his bracelets appeared, it would blot out the light of the sun, as the sun blots out the light of the stars."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The people of Paradise are hairless [of body], beardless, with kohl-darkened eyes; their youth will not fade and their garments will not wear out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying:
"And [there will be] raised couches," he said:
"Their height is like the distance between the sky and the earth, and the distance between them is a journey of five hundred years."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary was mentioned to him, and he said:

"A rider could travel in the shade of its branch for one hundred years, or one hundred riders could shelter in its shade"—Yaḥyā was unsure—"on it are moths of gold, and its fruits are like large jars."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked, "What is al-Kawthar?" He said:
"It is a river Allah gave me"—meaning in Paradise—"whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Along it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels."
ʿUmar said: "These must be delightful."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Those who eat them are more delighted than they are."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Usāmah ibn Zayd, and a man said, "What prevents you from going in to ʿUthmān and speaking to him about what he is doing?" And he narrated the hadith similarly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Abū Mūsā while he was in the house of the daughter of al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās. I sneezed, and he did not respond to me, then she sneezed and he responded to her. So I returned to my mother and told her. When he came to her, she said, "My son sneezed in your presence and you did not respond to him, and she sneezed and you responded to her."
He said, "Your son sneezed and did not praise Allah, so I did not respond to him, but she sneezed and praised Allah, so I responded to her. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'When one of you sneezes and praises Allah, respond to him; but if he does not praise Allah, do not respond to him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you yawns during prayer, let him suppress it as much as he can, for the devil enters."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The angels were created from light, the jinn were created from a smokeless flame of fire, and Adam was created from what has been described to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The rat is a transformed creature, and the sign of that is that if the milk of sheep is placed before it, it drinks it, but if the milk of camels is placed before it, it does not taste it."
Kaʿb said to him, "Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "Was the Torah revealed to me?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"How wonderful is the affair of the believer, for all of his affair is good, and that is not so for anyone except the believer: if good fortune befalls him, he is grateful, and that is good for him; and if hardship befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, from al-Aʿmash and Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from Hammām, from al-Miqdād,
from the Prophet ﷺ, similarly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do not write anything down from me, and whoever has written anything from me other than the Qur'an, let him erase it. Narrate from me, and there is no blame. And whoever lies about me—Hammām said: I think he said—deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ first came to Madinah, he stayed with his grandfathers—or he said, his maternal uncles—from the Ansar,
and that he prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen months,
or seventeen months,
but he liked that his direction of prayer be toward the House [the Kaʿbah],
and that the first prayer he prayed [in that direction] was the ʿAsr prayer,
and some people prayed with him.
Then a man who had prayed with him went out
and passed by the people of a mosque
who were bowing, and he said, "I bear witness by Allah that I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ facing Makkah."
So they turned just as they were toward the House.
The Jews, and the People of the Book, had been pleased when he used to pray toward Bayt al-Maqdis,
but when he turned his face toward the House, they disapproved of that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to tell the people about the Night of Qadr,
but two men from the Muslims were quarreling. The Prophet ﷺ said, "I came out to tell you about it,
but so-and-so and so-and-so quarreled, and it was lifted.
Perhaps that is better for you.
So seek it in the ninth, the seventh, and the fifth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked you whether they were increasing or decreasing,
and you claimed that they were increasing,
and so it is with faith until it is complete.
And I asked you whether anyone turns away from his religion in resentment of it after entering it,
and you claimed that none does,
and so it is with faith when its joy mixes with the hearts,
no one resents it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "You will never spend any expenditure seeking the Face of Allah by it except that you will be rewarded for it, even for what you put into your wife's mouth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Prophet ﷺ was in a gathering speaking to the people, a Bedouin came to him and said, "When is the Hour?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ continued speaking.
Some of the people said, "He heard what he said,
but disliked what he said."
And some of them said, "Rather, he did not hear."
When he finished his talk, he said,
"Where is—I think—the one who asked about the Hour?"
He said, "Here I am, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"When trust is lost, then wait for the Hour."
He said, "How is it lost?" He said,
"When authority is given to those who are not qualified for it, then wait for the Hour."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent his letter to Khosrow with ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥudhāfah as-Sahmī,
and he commanded him to hand it over to the governor of Bahrain,
so the governor of Bahrain handed it to Khosrow.
When he read it, he tore it up. I think Ibn al-Musayyib said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against them that they be torn to pieces completely.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān said: I heard Muʿāwiyah
speaking as a preacher, saying: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say,
"Whoever Allah wishes good for, He gives him understanding of the religion.
I am only a distributor, and Allah is the One who gives.
This nation will not cease to stand firm upon the command of Allah; those who oppose them will not harm them, until the command of Allah comes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"A servant remains in prayer as long as he is in the mosque waiting for the prayer,
so long as he does not break wind."
A non-Arab man said, "What is ḥadath, O Abū Hurayrah?" He said, "A sound," meaning the passing of wind.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us at midday,
and water for ablution was brought to him and he performed ablution.
The people began taking what was left of his ablution water and wiping themselves with it.
Then the Prophet ﷺ prayed Zuhr two rakʿahs and ʿAsr two rakʿahs,
with a short spear planted in front of him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he is the one in whose face the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spat a mouthful of water from their well when he was a boy.
ʿUrwah reported from al-Miswar and another, each of them confirming the other: When the Prophet ﷺ performed ablution, they nearly fought over his ablution water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The time of prayer came, so whoever had a house near the mosque got up to perform ablution, and some people remained.
Then a stone basin containing water was brought to the Prophet ﷺ,
and he put his palm down, but the basin was too small for him to spread his palm in it,
so he gathered his fingers and put them in the basin,
and all the people performed ablution together.
I said, "How many were they?" He said, "Eighty men."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ wiping over his turban and his leather socks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ:
label: machine translation

segments_en: We are the last, the foremost."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ spat into his garment.
Ibn Abī Maryam related it at greater length, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb informed us: Ḥumayd narrated to me, saying: I heard Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bathed from sexual impurity, he would wash his hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ did not come out to us for three days. Then the prayer was called, and Abū Bakr went forward to lead. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said, "[Raise] the curtain," and it was lifted. When the face of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ became visible to us, we had never seen a sight more wonderful to us than the face of the Prophet ﷺ when it appeared to us. He said: Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ gestured with his hand to Abū Bakr to go forward, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ lowered the curtain, and we were not able to reach him until he died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the first Emigrants arrived, they stayed at al-ʿUṣbah before the arrival of the Prophet ﷺ, and Sālim, the freed slave of Abū Ḥudhayfah, used to lead them in prayer, as he knew the most Qur'an among them.
Al-Haytham added: Among them were ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Asad.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Listen and obey, even if an Abyssinian slave whose head is like a raisin is appointed over you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us in our house, and I and an orphan of ours prayed behind him, and Umm Sulaym prayed behind us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the eclipse prayer. He stood and made the standing long, then bowed and made the bowing long, then rose and stood and made the standing long, then bowed and made the bowing long, then rose, then prostrated and made the prostration long, then rose, then prostrated and made the prostration long. Then he rose and stood and made the standing long, then bowed and made the bowing long, then rose and stood and made the standing long, then bowed and made the bowing long, then rose, then prostrated and made the prostration long, then rose, then prostrated and made the prostration long. Then he finished and said:
"Paradise came close to me, so much so that had I dared, I would have brought you a bunch of its fruit. And the Fire came close to me, so that I said, 'My Lord, and I am among them?'"
Nāfiʿ said: I think he said:

"And I saw a woman being scratched by a cat of hers, and I said, 'What is the matter with this one?' They said, 'She confined it until it died of hunger; she neither fed it nor released it to eat from the creatures of the earth.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man of the Anṣār used to lead them in prayer in the mosque of Qubāʾ. Every time he began a sūrah to recite for them in prayer, he would begin with "Say: He is Allah, the One" until he finished it, and then recite another sūrah with it. He did this in every rakʿah. His companions spoke to him and said, "You recite this sūrah and then you do not think it is sufficient for you until you recite another sūrah with it. Either recite it alone, or leave it and recite another sūrah."
He said, "I will not leave it. If you wish me to lead you with it, I will do so, and if you dislike it, I will leave you."
They considered him the best of them, and they disliked that anyone else should lead them. When the Prophet ﷺ came to them, they told him the matter, and he said:
"O so-and-so, what prevents you from doing what your companions instruct you, and what makes you recite this sūrah in every rakʿah?"
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I love it."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Your love for it has admitted you into Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr prayers, in the first two rakʿahs, Umm al-Qurʾān (al-Fātiḥah) and two sūrahs, and in the last two, Umm al-Qurʾān. Sometimes he would let us hear a verse, and he used to lengthen the first rakʿah of the Ẓuhr prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to lead us in prayer, lengthening the first rakʿah of Ẓuhr and shortening the second, and likewise in the Fajr prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He prayed with ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, in Basra, and said: This man reminded us of a prayer we used to pray with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He mentioned that he would say the takbīr whenever he rose and whenever he lowered himself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I do not fail to lead you in prayer just as I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lead us in prayer.
[Thābit] said: Anas used to do something that I do not see you doing: when he raised his head from bowing, he would stand upright until someone would say, "He has forgotten."
And when he raised his head from the prostration, he would stay [sitting] until someone would say, "He has forgotten."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying, "I have a slave woman, and I practice withdrawal with her."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"That will not prevent anything that Allah intends."
He said: Then the man came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the slave woman I mentioned to you has become pregnant."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this chain of narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "I practice withdrawal with my wife."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him,
"Why do you do that?"
The man said, "I fear for her child," or he said, "for her children."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"If that were harmful, it would have harmed the Persians and the Romans."
And Zuhayr said in his narration,
"If it were so, it would not have harmed the Persians or the Romans."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My paternal uncle through breastfeeding came and asked permission to enter upon me, but I refused to permit him until I consulted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, I said, "My paternal uncle through breastfeeding asked permission to enter upon me, but I refused to permit him."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Let your uncle enter upon you."
I said, "It was only the woman who nursed me; the man did not nurse me." He said,
"He is your uncle; let him enter upon you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We report that Zaynab bint Abī Salamah narrated to him that Umm Ḥabībah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated to her that she said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "O Messenger of Allah, marry my sister ʿAzzah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Do you like that?"
She said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah. I am not alone with you, and I would love for my sister to share with me in goodness."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"That is not lawful for me."
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, we have been saying that you want to marry Durrah bint Abī Salamah." He said,
"The daughter of Umm Salamah?" She said, "Yes."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Even if she were not my stepdaughter in my care, she would not be lawful for me, for she is the daughter of my foster brother. Thuwaybah nursed me and Abū Salamah. So do not offer me your daughters or your sisters."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
from Banū ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah said, "O Prophet of Allah, does a single nursing make [a person] unlawful [for marriage]?" He said, "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Salamah said to ʿĀʾishah, "A nearly grown boy enters upon you, and I do not like him to enter upon me."

He said: ʿĀʾishah said, "Do you not have an example in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" She said, "The wife of Abū Ḥudhayfah said, 'O Messenger of Allah, Sālim enters upon me, and he is a grown man, and Abū Ḥudhayfah feels something [of dislike] about it.'"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Nurse him so that he may enter upon you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, similar in meaning to his hadith, except that they said, "because of hunger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Saʿīd,
from Abū Hurayrah. As for
ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, he said, from Abū Salamah,
or from Saʿīd,
from Abū Hurayrah. And
Zuhayr said, from Saʿīd,
or from Abū Salamah,
one of them or both of them, from Abū Hurayrah. And
ʿAmr said: Sufyān narrated to us,
once from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd and Abū
Salamah, and once from Saʿīd,
or Abū Salamah, and once from Saʿīd, from Abū
Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ,
like the hadith of Maʿmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Umm Salamah and went in to her, he wanted to leave, but she took hold of his garment. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"If you wish, I will give you more, and I will account for it to you: seven [nights] for a virgin and three for a previously married woman."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
and [a second chain:] ʿĪsā ibn Ḥammād al-Miṣrī narrated to me: al-Layth informed us,
from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb,
and [a third chain:] he said: Hārūn ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated to me:
Ibn Abī Fudayk narrated to us:
aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn ʿUthmān narrated to us,
and [another chain:] he said: al-Muqaddamī narrated to us: Yaḥyā narrated to us,
—that is, al-Qaṭṭān—from Ibn ʿAjlān,
and [another chain:] Hārūn ibn Saʿīd al-Aylī narrated to me:
Ibn Wahb narrated to us:
Usāmah ibn Zayd narrated to me,
and [another chain:] he said: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb, Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr narrated to us; they said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
—meaning Ibn Jaʿfar—Muḥammad informed me,
who is Ibn ʿAmr; and [another chain:] he said: Hannād ibn as-Sarī narrated to me: ʿAbdah narrated to us,
from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq,
all of these [narrated] from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥunayn, from his father, from ʿAlī,
—except that aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn ʿAjlān added: from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAlī,

—from the Prophet ﷺ. All of them said: He forbade me from reciting the Qurʾān while I am bowing. In their narration they did not mention the prohibition of it during prostration, as az-Zuhrī, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Walīd ibn Kathīr, and Dāwūd ibn Qays mentioned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so make abundant supplication."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah
informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say in his bowing and his prostration:
"Most Pure, Most Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to spend the night with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I would bring him his water for ablution and what he needed. He said to me, "Ask."
I said, "I ask for your companionship in Paradise." He said, "Or something other than that?"
I said, "That is it." He said,
"Then help me [achieve] this for yourself by frequent prostration."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās saw ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥārith praying with his hair tied in a knot behind him. He stood behind him and began to untie it, while the other let him do so. When he finished [the prayer], he turned to Ibn ʿAbbās and said, "What do you want with my hair?" He said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The likeness of this is only that of one who prays with his hands bound."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah while he was at al-Abṭaḥ in a red leather tent of his. He said: Bilāl came out with the water of his ablution, and some people received some of it and some sprinkled themselves with it. He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ came out wearing a red garment; it is as though I am looking at the whiteness of his shins. He said: He performed ablution, and Bilāl called the adhān. He said: I kept following his mouth this way and that way—[turning] right and left—as he said, "Come to prayer, come to success." He said: Then a short spear was planted for him, and he went forward and prayed Ẓuhr two rakʿahs, while donkeys and dogs passed in front of him without being prevented. Then he prayed ʿAṣr two rakʿahs, and he continued to pray two rakʿahs until he returned to Madinah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed beside my father, and I put my hands between my knees. My father said to me, "Strike your knees with your palms."
He said: Then I did that a second time, and he struck my hand and said, "We were forbidden from this, and we were commanded to place our palms on the knees."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We asked Ibn ʿAbbās about sitting on the heels between the two prostrations.
He said, "It is the Sunnah."
He said: We said, "We consider it to be rudeness on the part of a man."
Ibn ʿAbbās said, "It is the Sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to al-Yashkurī with a group from Banū Layth. He said, "Who are the people?" We said, "Banū Layth. We have come to ask you about the hadith of Ḥudhayfah." Then he mentioned the hadith. [Ḥudhayfah] said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, after this good, will there be evil?" He said, "Trial and evil."
He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, after this evil, will there be good?" He said,
"O Ḥudhayfah, learn the Book of Allah and follow what is in it," [saying it] three times.
He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, after this evil, will there be good?" He said,
"A truce on a basis of dimness, and a community with impurities in it, or in them."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the truce on a basis of dimness?" He said,
"The hearts of people will not return to what they were upon."
He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, after this good, will there be evil?" He said,
"A blind, deaf trial, with callers at the gates of the Fire. If you die, O Ḥudhayfah, while biting onto the trunk of a tree, that is better for you than following any of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If on that day you do not find a caliph, then flee until you die. If you die, [it should be] while biting onto [a trunk]."
And at the end of it he said: I said, "Then what will happen after that?" He said,
"If a man were to breed a horse, its foal would not be [fully] bred before the Hour is established."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Successful is the one who restrains his hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The Muslims will soon be besieged in Medina, until the farthest of their outposts is Salāḥ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Salāḥ is near Khaybar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Allah has protected you from three things: that your Prophet will not invoke against you so that you all perish; that the people of falsehood will not prevail over the people of truth; and that you will not unite upon misguidance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The mill of Islam will turn for thirty-five, or thirty-six, or thirty-seven [years]. If they perish, then that is the path of those who perished; and if their religion stands firm for them, it will stand for them for seventy years."
He said: I said, "Is it from what remains or from what has passed?" He said, "From what has passed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"There will be a trial in which the one lying down will be better than the one sitting, the one sitting better than the one standing, the one standing better than the one walking, and the one walking better than the one running."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you command me?" He said,
"Whoever has camels, let him join his camels; whoever has sheep, let him join his sheep; and whoever has land, let him join his land."
He said, "And whoever has none of that?" He said,
"Let him take his sword and strike its edge against a rock, and then let him save himself if he is able."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ in this hadith, he said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what if someone enters my house and stretches out his hand to kill me?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Be like the son of Ādam."
And Yazīd recited: {If you should stretch out your hand toward me...} the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Then he mentioned part of the hadith of Abū Bakrah, saying:
"Those killed in it will all be in the Fire."
He said in it: I said, "When will that be, O Ibn Masʿūd?" He said, "Those are the days of al-harj, when a man will not feel safe from his own companion."
I said, "Then what do you command me [to do] if that time reaches me?" He said, "Restrain your tongue and your hand, and be a covering of your house."

When ʿUthmān was killed, my heart flew from its place. So I rode until I reached Damascus and met Khuraym ibn Fātik and told him. He swore by Allah, besides Whom there is no god, that he had heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ just as Ibn Masʿūd had narrated it to me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was holding the hand of Ibn ʿUmar on one of the roads of Medina when he came upon a severed head set up on display. He said, "Wretched is the one who killed this man."
When he had passed on, he said, "And I do not think this one but that he too was wretched. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say,
'Whoever walks toward a man of my Ummah to kill him, let him say thus: the killer will be in the Fire and the one killed in Paradise.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ travelled, he would say: "

O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey and the Successor [who watches over] the family. O Allah, accompany us on our journey and take care of our family in our absence. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, from the sorrow of returning, from decline after increase, from the supplication of the oppressed, and from an evil sight in family and wealth."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.

He said: It is also narrated as "al-ḥawr after al-kawr." He said: The meaning of the phrase "al-ḥawr after al-kawn" or "al-kawr" — both have a valid sense — is said to be returning from faith to disbelief, or from obedience to disobedience. It only means returning from one thing to something of evil.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no jalab, no janab, and no shighār in Islam, and whoever plunders a plunder is not one of us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, how much the dowry of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was. She said: His dowry for his wives was twelve ūqiyyah and a nashsh.
She said: Do you know what a nashsh is? He said: I said, No.
She said: Half an ūqiyyah.
That is five hundred dirhams. This was the dowry of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for his wives.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade the sale of [crops for] years.
And in the narration of Ibn Abī Shaybah: He forbade the sale of fruit for years.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Abū Salamah ibn
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

Any man who is given a lifetime grant (ʿumrā) for himself and his descendants, it belongs to the one to whom it was given; it does not return to the one who gave it, because he gave a gift on which the laws of inheritance have fallen."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hushaym informed us,
and [in another chain] Musaddad narrated to us: Hushaym narrated to us,
from ʿAbbād ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Your oath is according to what your companion confirms regarding it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The men [narrators]: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his mother, from ʿĀʾishah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
O ʿĀʾishah, a house without dates, its people go hungry. O ʿĀʾishah, a house without dates, its people go hungry," or "its people are hungry."
He said it twice or three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was
a Companion. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Name yourselves with the names of the prophets. The most beloved names to Allah are ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the truest are Ḥārith and Hammām, and the ugliest are Ḥarb and Murrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sufyān mentioned a man between himself and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ẓālim al-Māzinī. He said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl say: When so-and-so came to Kūfah, he set up so-and-so to give a sermon. Saʿīd ibn Zayd took me by the hand and said: Do you not see this wrongdoer? I bear witness regarding the nine that they are in Paradise, and if I were to bear witness regarding the tenth I would not be sinning. Ibn Idrīs said: The Arabs say "athima." I said: Who are the nine? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, while on Ḥirāʾ: "
Be still, Ḥirāʾ! There is on you only a prophet, a ṣiddīq, or a martyr."
I said: Who are the nine? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.
I said: And who is the tenth? He hesitated a little, then said: I am.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being asked about water that is in the open land and which beasts and animals come to. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When the water reaches two qullahs, it does not carry impurity."
ʿAbdah said: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: The qullah is the jars, the qullah from which water is drawn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about performing ablution after eating camel meat, and he said: "Perform ablution after it."
He was asked about mutton, and he said: "
Do not perform ablution after it."
He was asked about praying in camel resting places, and he said: "
Do not pray in camel resting places, for they are from the devils."
He was asked about praying in sheep pens, and he said: "
Pray in them, for they are a blessing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Among the nations before you there were people who were inspired [with true insight],
and if there is anyone like that in my nation, it is ʿUmar."
Zakariyyāʾ ibn Abī Zāʾidah added, on the authority of Saʿd,
from Abū Salamah,
from Abū Hurayrah, who said:
The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Among those before you from the Children of Israel there were men who were spoken to without being prophets,
and if there is anyone like them among my nation, it is ʿUmar."
Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said:
"...of a prophet or an inspired person."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir and Abū al-Naḍr,
the freed slave of ʿUmar ibn ʿUbaydillāh, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father,
that he heard him asking
Usāmah ibn Zayd: What did you hear from
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the plague? Usāmah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

The plague is a punishment or a torment that was sent upon the Children of Israel, or upon those before you. So when you hear of it in a land, do not go to it; and when it breaks out in a land while you are in it, do not leave it, fleeing from it."
Abū al-Naḍr said: "
Nothing should make you leave except fleeing from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no man who claims [descent from] someone other than his father while knowing [who his father is] except that he has disbelieved. Whoever claims what is not his is not one of us, and let him take his seat in the Fire. And whoever calls a man a disbeliever, or says, 'Enemy of Allah,'
when he is not so, it will return upon him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ called the Anṣār and said: "
Is there anyone among you who is not one of you?" They said: No,
except a son of our sister.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The son of a people's sister is one of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ, and al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, peace be upon them both, resembled him. I said to Abū Juḥayfah: Describe him to me.
He said: He was fair, with some gray hair.
And the Prophet ﷺ ordered for us thirteen young she-camels. He said: The Prophet ﷺ passed away before we could receive them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; this part of him was white—and Zuhayr placed some of his fingers on his chin-tuft. He was asked: What were you like at that time? He said: I used to shape arrows and fletch them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: People used to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about good, and I used to ask him about evil, fearing that it might overtake me. So I said: O Messenger of Allah, we were in ignorance and evil, then Allah brought us this good. Is there any evil after this good? He said: "Yes."
I said: Is there any good after that evil? He said: "
Yes, but it has some murkiness in it."
I said: What is its murkiness? He said: "
A people who follow a way other than my way and guide by other than my guidance. You will recognize some of them and disapprove of others."
I said: Is there any evil after that good? He said: "
Yes, callers at the gates of Hell; whoever responds to them, they will throw him into it."
I said: O Messenger of Allah, describe them to us. He said: "
Yes, they are from our own people and speak our language."
I said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you advise me to do if that overtakes me? He said: "
Stay with the community of the Muslims and their leader."
I said: And if they have no community and no leader? He said: "
Then withdraw from all those factions, even if you have to bite onto the root of a tree until death reaches you while you are in that state."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was resting his head on a cloak in the shade of the Kaʿbah. We complained to him and said: Will you not seek help for us? Will you not supplicate to Allah for us? He sat up, his face red, and said: "

Among those before you, a man would be seized and a pit would be dug for him in the ground, then a saw would be brought and placed on his head and he would be split in two, and that would not turn him away from his religion. His flesh and sinews, down to the bone, would be combed with iron combs, and that would not turn him away from his religion. By Allah, Allah will surely complete this matter until a rider travels from Ṣanʿāʾ to Ḥaḍramawt fearing none but Allah, the Exalted, and the wolf for his sheep. But you are hasty."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar about a man

who applies perfume and then enters the state of iḥrām in the morning. He said, "I would not like to enter iḥrām in the morning while giving off the scent of perfume; to be smeared with tar would be dearer to me than to do that."

Then I went in to ʿĀʾishah and told her that Ibn ʿUmar had said, "I would not like to enter iḥrām in the morning while giving off the scent of perfume; to be smeared with tar would be dearer to me than to do that."
ʿĀʾishah said, "I perfumed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he was about to enter iḥrām; then he went around among his wives, and then entered iḥrām in the morning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ:

"Moses, peace be upon him, was a modest and very covering man; none of his skin was ever seen, out of his shyness. Some of the Children of Israel harassed him and said, 'He covers himself like this only because of some defect in his skin: either leprosy, or a swelling of the groin, or some other affliction.' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wished to clear him of what they said. One day Moses, peace be upon him, was alone; he put his clothes on a rock and then bathed. When he had finished, he came toward his clothes to take them, but the rock had run off with his garment. Moses took his staff and went after the rock, saying, 'My garment, rock! My garment, rock!' until he reached a gathering of the Children of Israel, and they saw him naked, the finest of people in form, and he was cleared of what they had been saying." He said: "Then the rock stopped, and he took his garment and put it on, and began striking the rock with his staff. By Allah, there were marks on the rock from his staff, three or four or five. That is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted:"
"O you who believe, do not be like those who harassed Moses, and Allah cleared him of what they said; and he was honorable in the sight of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would bring his head close to me while I was in my room, and I would comb his hair while I was menstruating.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I was lying down

with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ under a blanket, I began to menstruate, so I slipped away and took my menstrual clothes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, "Have you started your period?" I said, "Yes."
He called me, and I lay down with him under the blanket.
She said: She and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to bathe from sexual impurity in one vessel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of us was menstruating,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to have contact with her,
he would order her to wrap an izār around herself at the height of her menstruation, and then he would have contact with her.
She said, "And which of you can control her desire as the Prophet ﷺ controlled his desire?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ performed iʿtikāf with him while she had irregular bleeding and saw blood,
and at times she would place a basin beneath her because of the blood.
He claimed that ʿĀʾishah saw the water of safflower [dye] and said, "This is like something that so-and-so used to find."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman

asked ʿĀʾishah, saying, "Should one of us make up the prayers [missed] during the days of her menses?" ʿĀʾishah said, "Are you a Ḥarūrī? One of us used to menstruate in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and then she was not commanded to make them up."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying, "I have irregular bleeding and am never clean. Should I give up prayer?" He said:
"No, but leave [prayer] for the number of days and nights in which you used to menstruate."
Abū Bakr said in his narration:
"And the equivalent of them in the month. Then bathe, bind yourself with a cloth, and pray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of Zuhayr and its meaning, and he said:
"When the menstrual period comes, leave the prayer; and when its duration has passed, wash the blood from yourself and pray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥassān said, "O Messenger of Allah, permit me [to satirize] Abū Sufyān." He ﷺ said, "
What about my kinship to him?"
He said, "By the One who has honored you, I will draw you out from among them as a hair is drawn out from dough."
Then Ḥassān said: "Indeed, the pinnacle of glory belongs to the family of Hāshim, the sons of the daughter of Makhzūm, while your father is the slave." This is [part of] his poem.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Satirize Quraysh, for it is harsher upon them than a volley of arrows."
So he sent for Ibn Rawāḥah and said, "Satirize them."

He satirized them, but [the Prophet ﷺ] was not satisfied. Then he sent for Kaʿb ibn Mālik, and then sent for Ḥassān ibn Thābit. When he came to him, Ḥassān said, "The time has come for you to send for this lion who strikes with his tail." Then he stuck out his tongue and began to move it, and said, "By the One who sent you with the truth, I will tear them apart with my tongue as leather is torn."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Do not be hasty, for Abū Bakr is the most knowledgeable of the Quraysh about their lineages, and I have lineage among them, so [wait] until he clarifies my lineage for you."

Ḥassān went to him and then returned and said, "O Messenger of Allah, he has clarified your lineage for me. By the One who sent you with the truth, I will draw you out from among them as a hair is drawn out from dough."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to call my mother to Islam while she was a polytheist. One day I called her, and she said about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ something I disliked. So I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weeping and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I was calling my mother to Islam and she refused me. I called her today and she said about you something I dislike. So pray to Allah to guide the mother of Abū Hurayrah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
O Allah, guide the mother of Abū Hurayrah."

So I went out happy at the supplication of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ. When I came and reached the door, it was closed. My mother heard the sound of my footsteps and said, "Stay where you are, Abū Hurayrah."

I heard the splashing of water. He said: She washed, put on her garment, and hurried without her head covering, then opened the door and said, "O Abū Hurayrah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger." He said: I returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and came to him weeping from joy. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, good news! Allah has answered your prayer and guided the mother of Abū Hurayrah."

He praised Allah, extolled Him, and said something good. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He make me and my mother beloved to His believing servants, and make them beloved to us." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
O Allah, make this servant of Yours, meaning Abū Hurayrah, and his mother beloved to Your believing servants, and make the believers beloved to them."
So no believer was created who hears of me or sees me except that he loves me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Muslims would not look at Abū Sufyān nor sit with him. He said to the Prophet ﷺ, "O Prophet of Allah, [grant me] three things." He said, "Yes."
He said, "I have the best and most beautiful of the Arabs, Umm Ḥabībah bint Abī Sufyān; I will marry her to you." He said, "Yes."
He said, "And Muʿāwiyah, make him a scribe before you." He said, "Yes."
He said, "And appoint me commander so that I may fight the disbelievers as I used to fight the Muslims." He said, "Yes."
Abū Zumayl said: Had he not asked this of the Prophet ﷺ, [the Prophet] would not have given it to him, because he was never asked for anything except that he said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Sufyān
came upon Salmān, Ṣuhayb and Bilāl among a group of people, and they said, "By Allah, the swords of Allah have not taken their due from the neck of the enemy of Allah."
Abū Bakr said, "Do you say this about the elder of Quraysh and their chief?" Then he went to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and he said, "
O Abū Bakr, perhaps you have angered them. If you have angered them, you have angered your Lord."
So Abū Bakr went to them and said, "My brothers, did I anger you?" They said, "No. May Allah forgive you, my brother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked forgiveness for the Anṣār. He said: and I think he said, "
and for the children of the Anṣār and for the freed slaves of the Anṣār."
I have no doubt about it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
The best of the households of the Anṣār are Banū al-Najjār, then Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal, then Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, then Banū Sāʿidah. And in all the households of the Anṣār there is good."
Saʿd said, "I see that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has preferred others over us."
It was said [to him], "He has preferred you over many."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ considered several things for the call to prayer, but he did not carry out any of them. He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd was shown the call to prayer in a dream, so he came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him. He said,
"Teach it to Bilāl."
So he taught it to him, and Bilāl gave the call to prayer. ʿAbd Allāh said, "I was the one who saw it, and I was the one who wanted it." He said, "Then you give the iqāmah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My grandfather ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd used to narrate this report. He said: So my grandfather gave the iqāmah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A woman] from Banū al-Najjār said: My house was one of the tallest houses around the mosque, and Bilāl used to give the dawn call to prayer from it. He would come before dawn and sit on the house, looking toward the dawn. When he saw it, he would stretch and then say, "O Allah, I praise You and seek Your help against Quraysh, that they establish Your religion." She said: Then he would give the call to prayer. She said: By Allah, I do not know that he ever left these words out for a single night—meaning these words.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah while he was in a red leather tent. Bilāl came out and gave the call to prayer, and I kept following his mouth this way and that way.
He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out wearing a red garment of Yemeni striped cloth, of the Qaṭarī type.
Mūsā said: He said, "I saw Bilāl go out to al-Abṭaḥ and give the call to prayer. When he reached 'Come to prayer, come to success,'
he turned his neck right and left without turning his whole body around. Then he went in and brought out the spear." And he went on with his narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
said, "O Messenger of Allah, the muʾadhdhins surpass us [in reward]."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Say as they say, and when you finish, ask and you will be given."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard the muʾadhdhin say the testification, he would say, "And I, and I."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] from the people of Syria, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab,
from Abū Umāmah,
or from some
of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: Bilāl began the iqāmah, and when he said "The prayer has been established," the Prophet ﷺ said,
"May Allah establish it and perpetuate it."
And for the rest of the iqāmah he said the same as in the hadith of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, about the call to prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Bilāl
gave the call to prayer before the rising of dawn, so the Prophet ﷺ ordered him to go back and announce:
"Indeed, the servant has slept! Indeed, the servant has slept!"
Mūsā added: So he went back and announced, "Indeed, the servant has slept."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him,
"Do not give the call to prayer until the dawn becomes clear to you, like this."
And he stretched out his hands horizontally. Abū Dāwūd said: Shaddād, the freed slave of ʿIyāḍ, did not meet Bilāl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn ʿUmar when a man made the tathwīb in the Ẓuhr or ʿAṣr prayer. He said, "Let us leave, for this is an innovation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Kahmas said: We stood for prayer at Minā while the imam had not come out, and some of us sat down. An old man from the people of Kūfah said to me, "What makes you sit?" I said, "Ibn Buraydah."
He said, "This is standing idly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the prayer was called in the mosque, if the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw that the people were few, he would sit and not pray, and if he saw that they were a congregation, he would pray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The same as that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are no three in a village or in the desert among whom the prayer is not established except that Satan has gained mastery over them. So keep to the congregation, for the wolf only eats the sheep that strays far away."
Zāʾidah said: al-Sāʾib said, "By 'the congregation' he means prayer in congregation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"I have been tempted to order my young men to gather bundles of firewood, then go to people who pray in their houses without any excuse and burn the houses down on them."

I said to Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm, "O Abū ʿAwf, did he mean the Friday prayer or another?" He said, "May my ears go deaf if I did not hear Abū Hurayrah relate it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; he did not mention Friday or any other."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever hears the caller and nothing prevents him from following it, no excuse—"
They asked, "What is an excuse?" He said, "Fear or illness—"
"the prayer he prays will not be accepted from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Whoever goes out from his house in a state of purity for an obligatory prayer, his reward is like the reward of a pilgrim in iḥrām. Whoever goes out for the voluntary Ḍuḥā prayer, wanting nothing but that, his reward is like the reward of one performing ʿUmrah. And a prayer after a prayer, with no idle talk between them, is recorded in ʿIlliyyīn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a cave,
[This is] like the hadith of Jarīr and Abū Muʿāwiyah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he entered upon Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī in his house. He said: I found him praying, so I sat waiting for him until he finished his prayer. Then I heard a rustling among some palm stalks in a corner of the house, and I turned and saw a snake. I jumped up to kill it, but he gestured to me to sit down.
So I sat down. When he finished, he pointed to a room in the house and said: Do you see this room? I said: Yes.

He said: In it there was a young man of ours who had recently been married. He said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the Trench, and that young man used to ask permission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at midday and return to his family. One day he asked his permission, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Take your weapon with you, for I fear Qurayẓah may harm you."

So the man took his weapon and then returned, and found his wife standing between the two doors. He lunged at her with the spear to stab her, overcome by jealousy. She said to him: Hold back your spear and go into the house until you see what made me come out.

He went in and there was a huge snake coiled on the bed. He lunged at it with the spear and pierced it, then went out and planted the spear in the courtyard. The snake writhed upon it, and it is not known which died first, the snake or the young man. He said: We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him about that, and said: Pray to Allah to bring him back to life for us. He said: "Ask forgiveness for your companion." Then he said:
"In Medina there are jinn who have accepted Islam. So if you see any of them, give them warning for three days. If it appears to you after that, then kill it, for it is a devil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: who was called al-Sāʾib, and he is Abū al-Sāʾib to us. He said: We entered upon Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, and while we were sitting we heard beneath
his bed a movement, and we looked and there was a snake.
And he related the hadith with its story, similar to the hadith of Mālik from Ṣayfī, and in it he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"These houses have inhabitants [among the jinn]. So if you see any of them, warn it three times. If it goes away, well and good; otherwise kill it, for it is a disbeliever." And he said to them:
"Go and bury your companion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"In Medina there are some of the jinn who have accepted Islam. So whoever sees any of these inhabitants, let him warn it three times. If it appears to him after that, let him kill it, for it is a devil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm,
and Ibn Abī ʿUmar,
Isḥāq said: Akhbaranā; and the others said:
Ḥaddathanā Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah,
from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jubayr,
ibn Shaybah, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab,
from Umm Sharīk,
that the Prophet ﷺ commanded her to kill geckos.
And in the hadith of Ibn Abī Shaybah: he commanded
label: machine translation

segments_en: that she
asked the Prophet ﷺ for his instruction about killing geckos, and he commanded that they be killed.
Umm Sharīk was one of the women of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy.
The wording of the hadith of Ibn Abī Khalaf and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd is the same, and the hadith of Ibn Wahb is close to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ, with similar meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ, to that effect.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A woman was punished because of a cat: she did not feed it or give it water, and she did not let it go to eat from the creatures of the earth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Do not say 'al-karm,'
but say 'al-ḥablah'", meaning the grape.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let none of you say 'my slave' or 'my slave woman.'
All of you are slaves of Allah, and all your women are slave women of Allah. But let him say 'my boy,' 'my girl,' 'my young man,' and 'my young woman.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked me to recite poetry for him.
[This is] like the hadith of Ibrāhīm ibn Maysarah, and he added: He said:
"He was almost about to become Muslim."
And in the hadith of Ibn Mahdī he said:
"He almost became Muslim in his poetry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to have dreams that made me shiver, though I did not [need to] be covered up, until I met Abū Qatādah and mentioned that to him. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"A good dream is from Allah and a bad dream is from the devil. So if one of you has a bad dream that he dislikes, let him spit lightly to his left three times and seek refuge with Allah from its evil, for it will not harm him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Jews
would not sit with a menstruating woman in a house, nor eat or drink with her.

He said: This was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, so Allah revealed: {They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is an impurity, so keep away from women during menstruation.} Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do everything except intercourse."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the courtyard of this mosque and called out at the top of his voice:
"The mosque is not permissible for someone in a state of major impurity, nor for a menstruating woman."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set a period of forty days for a woman in postnatal bleeding, unless she saw that she had become pure before that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered upon her, and a freedwoman of hers hid herself. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Has she begun menstruating?" She said, "Yes."
So he tore off a piece of his turban for her and said, "Cover your head with this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
asked ʿĀʾishah, saying: May a menstruating woman dye her hands with henna? She said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ and we used to dye our hands with henna, and he did not forbid us from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of my forearms was broken, so I asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he commanded me to wipe over the splints.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ carrying al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī on his shoulder, with the child's saliva running down onto him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ being brought a bucket. He rinsed his mouth from it and spat into it musk, or something more fragrant than musk, and he blew his nose outside the bucket.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never looked at—or: I never saw—the private part of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at all.
Abū Bakr said: Abū Nuʿaym used to say, "from a freedwoman of ʿĀʾishah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ bathed after sexual impurity and saw a spot that the water had not reached. So he took his lock of hair and wet it with that.
Isḥāq said in his narration: So he wrung out his hair over it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I bathed after sexual impurity and prayed the Fajr prayer, then morning came and I saw a spot the size of a fingernail that the water had not reached.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If you had wiped over it with your hand, it would have sufficed you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed the Ṣubḥ prayer with ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr in the darkness before dawn. When he finished the prayer, I turned to Ibn ʿUmar and said, "What is this prayer?" He said, "This was our prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. When ʿUmar was stabbed, ʿUthmān prayed it when it was lighter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Delay the Ẓuhr prayer until it cools down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"My nation will continue to be upon the fiṭrah as long as they do not delay the Maghrib prayer until the stars are crowded together."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ preferred to delay the ʿIshāʾ prayer, and he disliked sleeping before it and conversation after it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ criticized night conversation after the ʿIshāʾ prayer for us.
Ibn Mājah said: That is, he rebuked us for it and forbade us from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ consulted the people about what would call them to prayer. They mentioned the horn, but he disliked it because of the Jews. Then they mentioned the bell, but he disliked it because of the Christians. That night the call to prayer was shown in a dream to a man from the Anṣār called ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd, and to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. The Anṣārī came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at night, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Bilāl to give it, and he called the adhān.
Al-Zuhrī said: Bilāl added in the call for the morning prayer, "Prayer is better than sleep," and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ approved it.
ʿUmar said: O Messenger of Allah, I saw the same as what he saw, but he preceded me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Bilāl to put his fingers in his ears, and said:
"It will make your voice louder."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Abṭaḥ while he was in a red tent. Bilāl came out and called the adhān, turning around during his call and putting his fingers in his ears.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Two things are entrusted to the necks of the muʾadhdhins for the Muslims: their prayer and their fasting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Bilāl would not delay the adhān beyond its time, but he would sometimes delay the iqāmah somewhat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on a journey, he would draw lots among his wives. The lot fell to ʿĀʾishah and Hafsah, so both of them went out with him. When it was night, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would travel alongside ʿĀʾishah and talk with her. Hafsah said to ʿĀʾishah, "Will you not ride my camel tonight, and I ride yours, so that you may see [what you do not usually see] and I may see?" She said, "Yes."

So ʿĀʾishah rode Hafsah's camel and Hafsah rode ʿĀʾishah's camel. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to ʿĀʾishah's camel, on which Hafsah was riding, greeted her with salām, and then traveled alongside her until they stopped to camp. ʿĀʾishah missed him and became jealous. When they dismounted, she began to put her foot among the idhkhir grass and say, "My Lord, send a scorpion or a snake against me to sting me! He is Your Messenger, and I cannot say anything to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I found in my book, from Abū Usāmah: Hishām narrated to us,
and [in another chain] Abū Kurayb narrated to us,
Muhammad ibn al-ʿAlāʾ: Abū Usāmah narrated to us, from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me,
"I know when you are pleased with me and when you are angry with me."
She said: I asked, "How do you know that?" He said,
"When you are pleased with me, you say, 'No, by the Lord of Muhammad,' and when you are angry, you say, 'No, by the Lord of Ibrāhīm.'"
She said: I said, "Yes, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I only forsake your name."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I do not mind whether I give my wife the choice once, or a hundred times, or a thousand, after she chooses me. And I asked ʿĀʾishah, and she said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave us the choice; was that considered a divorce?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Shall I not tell you of the best houses of the Ansār, or the best of the Ansār?"
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"Banū an-Najjār, then those next to them, Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal, then those next to them, Banū al-Hārith ibn al-Khazraj, then those next to them, Banū Sāʿidah."
Then he gestured with his hand, closing his fingers and then spreading them out, like one throwing. He said,
"And in all the houses of the Ansār there is good."
This is a hasan sahīh hadith.
This has also been narrated from Anas, from Abū Usayd as-Sāʿidī, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from the Ansār accused his wife [of adultery], so the Prophet ﷺ had them both swear oaths, and then separated them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Ibn ʿUmar, "[What about] a man who accuses his wife?" He said, "The Prophet ﷺ separated the two siblings of Banū al-ʿAjlān, and said,
'Allah knows that one of you is lying,
so is either of you willing to repent?' But they refused. And he said,
'Allah knows that one of you is lying,
so is either of you willing to repent?' But they refused. Then he said,
'Allah knows that one of you is lying,
so is either of you willing to repent?'
But they refused, so he separated them."

Ayyūb said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār said to me, "There is something in the hadith that I do not see you mentioning." He said: The man said, "My property [what about it]?" He said: It was said, "You have no property;
if you were truthful, then you have already consummated [the marriage] with her,
and if you were lying, then it is even further from you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was narrated by] a wife of the Prophet ﷺ: A woman of Aslam called Subayʿah was married to her husband, and he died while she was pregnant. Abū as-Sanābil ibn Baʿkak proposed to her, but she refused to marry him. He said, "It is not proper for you to marry until you complete the longer of the two waiting periods."
So she stayed about twenty nights, then gave birth. She came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said, "Marry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He wrote to Ibn al-Arqam to ask
Subayʿah al-Aslamiyyah how the Prophet ﷺ had given her a ruling. She said, "He ruled for me that I may marry once I have given birth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He heard the two of them mention
that Yahyā ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀs

divorced the daughter of ʿAbd ar-Rahmān ibn al-Hakam with a final divorce, and ʿAbd ar-Rahmān moved her out. So ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, sent a message to Marwān ibn al-Hakam, who was the governor of Medina, saying to him, "Fear Allah and return the woman to her house."
Marwān said, in the narration of Sulaymān, "ʿAbd ar-Rahmān overpowered me."
And Marwān said, in the narration of al-Qāsim, "Has the matter of Fātimah bint Qays not reached you?" ʿĀʾishah said, "It will not harm you not to mention the hadith of Fātimah."
Marwān said, "If it is [only] evil that concerns you, then the evil that occurred between these two should suffice you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "
The one who becomes dizzy at sea and is overcome by vomiting has the reward of a martyr, and the one who drowns has the reward of two martyrs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are three, each of whom is under Allah's guarantee, Mighty and Majestic: a man who goes out to fight in the cause of Allah is under Allah's guarantee until He takes his soul and admits him to Paradise, or returns him with whatever reward and spoils he has gained; a man who goes out to the mosque is under Allah's guarantee until He takes his soul and admits him to Paradise, or returns him with whatever reward and spoils he has gained; and a man who enters his home with a greeting of peace is under the guarantee of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Prayer, fasting, and remembrance [of Allah] are multiplied over spending in the cause of Allah by seven hundred times."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is traced back through Makḥūl to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghanm al-Ashʿarī, that Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī
said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "

Whoever sets out in the cause of Allah and then dies or is killed is a martyr; or if his horse or camel throws him and breaks his neck, or a venomous creature stings him, or he dies in his bed, or by whatever manner of death Allah wills, he is a martyr, and he will have Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They travelled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Ḥunayn and pressed on with the journey until it was evening.
The time for prayer came while they were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a horseman came and said:

"O Messenger of Allah, I went ahead of you until I climbed such-and-such a mountain, and there were Hawāzin, all of them to the last man, with their women, their camels, and their sheep, gathered at Ḥunayn."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled and said: "
That will be the spoils of the Muslims tomorrow, if Allah wills." Then he said: "
Who will keep guard over us tonight?"
Anas ibn Abī Marthad al-Ghanawī said:
"I will, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Then mount."
So he mounted a horse of his and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "
Face this mountain pass until you are at its top, and let us not be taken by surprise from your side tonight."
When morning came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to his place of prayer and prayed two rakʿahs, then said: "
Have you sensed any sign of your horseman?" They said:
"O Messenger of Allah, we have not sensed him."
Then the call for prayer was made, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to pray while glancing toward the pass, until, when he had completed his prayer and given the salām, he said: "
Rejoice, for your horseman has come to you."
