segments_en: I entered upon ʿĀʾishah with some women of ʿAbd al-Qays and we asked her about dates and raisins. She said, "I would take a handful of dates and a handful of raisins, put them in a vessel, steep them, and then give it to the Prophet ﷺ to drink."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿIkrimah,
that they both disliked unripe dates alone, and they took that from Ibn ʿAbbās.
Ibn ʿAbbās said, "I fear that it is the muzāʾ that was forbidden to ʿAbd al-Qays."
I said to Qatādah, "What is the muzāʾ?" He said, "Nabīdh in green jars and tarred jars."
label: machine translation

segments_en: may Allah be pleased with her: She used to prepare nabīdh for the Prophet ﷺ in the morning, and when evening came and he had his supper, he would drink it with his supper, and if any remained I would pour it out—or empty it. Then she would prepare nabīdh for him at night, and when morning came he would have breakfast and drink it with his breakfast. She said, "We would wash the waterskin morning and evening." My father said to her, "Twice in a day?" She said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿAlī
called for water and drank it standing, then said, "Some men dislike to do this, yet I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do just as you have seen me do."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for a waterskin on the day of Uḥud and said:
"Bend back the mouth of the waterskin."
Then he drank from its mouth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Cover [or restrain] your children at nightfall." Musaddad said, "at evening."
"For the jinn spread out and snatch."
label: machine translation

segments_en: may Allah be pleased with her: Sweet water used to be fetched for the Prophet ﷺ from the houses of as-Suqyā.
Qutaybah said: It is a spring two days' journey from Madinah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of Ayyūb and its meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is invited and does not respond has disobeyed Allah and His Messenger, and whoever enters without an invitation has entered as a thief and left as a plunderer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this account, he said: He was invited on the third day and did not respond, and the messenger was pelted with stones.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah, he slaughtered a camel or a cow.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any man who hosts a people and the guest wakes up deprived, then helping him is a duty upon every Muslim, until he takes for him [what suffices] for a night's hospitality from his crops and wealth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Allah's saying:] {Do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, but only through trade by mutual consent.} After this verse was revealed, a man felt uneasy about eating at anyone's house. Then that was abrogated by the verse in Sūrat an-Nūr, where He said: {There is no blame upon you} {to eat from your homes} up to His saying {separately}. A wealthy man would invite a man from his relatives to a meal and he would say, "I feel uneasy about eating from it,
and the poor man is more deserving of it than I."
So it was made lawful for them in that regard to eat of that over which Allah's name was mentioned, and the food of the People of the Book was made lawful.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās used to say that the Prophet ﷺ forbade eating the food of two people competing in showing off [in hospitality].
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ that the Prophet ﷺ said:

"When two inviters [invite at once], respond to the one whose door is nearer, for the one whose door is nearer is the nearer neighbor; but if one of them came first, respond to the one who came first."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not delay the prayer for food or for anything else."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ set out at the time of al-Ḥudaybiyah with a little over a thousand of his Companions. When they reached Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, he garlanded the sacrificial animal, marked it, and entered the state of iḥrām for ʿUmrah.

And he narrated the rest of the hadith. He said: The Prophet ﷺ continued on until, when he reached the mountain pass from which one descends upon them, his camel knelt down with him. The people said, "Ḥal, ḥal! Al-Qaṣwāʾ has become stubborn!"
[They said it] twice. Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Al-Qaṣwāʾ has not become stubborn, and that is not her nature, but she was held back by the One who held back the elephant." Then he said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me today for any plan by which they honour the sacred things of Allah except that I will grant it to them."

Then he urged her on, and she sprang up. He turned away from them until he camped at the farthest end of al-Ḥudaybiyah by a pool with little water. Budayl ibn Warqāʾ al-Khuzāʿī came to him, and then ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd came to him and began speaking with the Prophet ﷺ. Every time he spoke to him, he took hold of his beard. Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah was standing over the Prophet ﷺ with a sword, wearing a helmet. He struck his hand with the base of the sword and said, "Take your hand away from his beard."
ʿUrwah raised his head and said, "Who is this?" They said, "Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah."

He said, "You traitor! Am I not striving to clean up your treachery?" Al-Mughīrah had accompanied a group of people in the Jāhiliyyah, killed them and taken their wealth, then came and embraced Islam. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"As for Islam, we accept it; as for the wealth, it is wealth taken by treachery, and we have no need of it."
Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Write: This is what Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed to."
And he related the account. Suhayl said, "And on the condition that no man from us comes to you, even if he is on your religion, except that you return him to us."
When he had finished the writing of the agreement, the Prophet ﷺ said to his Companions:
"Get up, slaughter your sacrificial animals, and then shave your heads."

Then believing women who had emigrated came, [and the verse was revealed]. Allah forbade them to send the women back, and commanded them to return the dowries. Then he returned to Madinah, and Abū Baṣīr, a man of Quraysh, came to him. They sent men to seek him, and he handed him over to the two men. They left with him, and when they reached Dhū al-Ḥulayfah they dismounted to eat some of their dates. Abū Baṣīr said to one of the two men, "By Allah, I see that this sword of yours, O so-and-so, is excellent."

The other drew it and said, "Yes, I have tested it." Abū Baṣīr said, "Let me see it." He let him take it, and he struck him until he died. The other fled until he reached Madinah and entered the mosque running. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"This man has seen something terrifying."

He said, "By Allah, my companion has been killed, and I will be killed too!" Then Abū Baṣīr came and said, "Allah has fulfilled your covenant: you returned me to them, and then Allah saved me from them." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Woe to his mother! A kindler of war, if only he had others with him!"
When he heard that, he knew that he would return him to them. So he went out until he reached the seashore. Then Abū Jandal escaped and joined Abū Baṣīr, until a band of them had gathered.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They agreed to lay down war for ten years, during which people would be safe, and that between us there would be a restrained heart, and that there would be no theft and no treachery.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Faith restrains treachery; a believer does not commit treachery."
label: machine translation

segments_en: {Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your leave} — this verse was abrogated by the verse in Sūrat an-Nūr: {The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger} up to His saying {Forgiving, Merciful}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ returned from a journey, he would begin with the mosque, pray two rakʿahs in it, and then sit with the people.

Ibn as-Sarḥ narrated the hadith and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the Muslims to speak to us, the three. When this had gone on a long time for me, I climbed over the wall of Abū Qatādah's garden, and he was my cousin. I greeted him with salām, and by Allah, he did not return my greeting. Then I prayed the Fajr prayer on the fiftieth morning on the roof of one of our houses, and I heard a caller shout, "O Kaʿb ibn Mālik, rejoice!"

When the man whose voice I had heard came to give me the good news, I took off my two garments and gave them to him to wear. Then I went until I entered the mosque, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sitting. Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydullāh got up and hurried to me until he shook my hand and congratulated me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: When some matter of joy came to him, or he was given good news of it, he would fall down in prostration, thanking Allah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib about the prayer

of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the day before the obligatory prayer. He said, "Who could bear that?" Then he told us: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray two rakʿahs when the sun passed its zenith, and four rakʿahs before midday, making the taslīm at the end of them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When he began the prayer he said the takbīr and raised his hands until they were level with his ears. Then he recited the Opening of the Book, and when he finished it he said, "Āmīn,"
raising his voice with it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah came to the mosque of Banū Zurayq and said: There are three things the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do which people have abandoned: he used to raise his hands fully in the prayer, he would pause briefly, and he would say the takbīr when he prostrated and when he rose.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man stood behind the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and said, "Allah is the Greatest, greatly so; and much praise is for Allah; and glory be to Allah morning and evening."
Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said,
"Who was the one who said those words?"
A man said, "I was, O Prophet of Allah." He said,
"Twelve angels raced to take it up."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw me with my left hand placed over my right in prayer, so he took my right hand and placed it over my left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh
saw a man praying with his feet placed side by side, and he said, "He has contradicted the Sunnah. Had he alternated between them, it would have been better."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to have a moment of silence when he began the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ began the prayer, he would say the takbīr and then say:

"Indeed my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, who has no partner. This I have been commanded, and I am among the Muslims. O Allah, guide me to the best of deeds and the best of character; none guides to the best of them except You. And protect me from evil deeds and evil character; none protects from their evil except You."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began the prayer, he would say the takbīr and then say:

"I have turned my face to the One who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining to the truth, and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, who has no partner. This I have been commanded, and I am among the Muslims. O Allah, You are the King; there is no god but You. You are my Lord and I am Your servant; I have wronged myself and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me all my sins; none forgives sins except You. Guide me to the best of character; none guides to the best of it except You. And turn away from me its evil; none turns away its evil from me except You. Here I am, at Your service, and all good is in Your hands, and evil is not attributed to You. I am by You and to You. You are blessed and exalted. I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he mentioned
another [narration] before it, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hurmuz al-Aʿraj,
from Muḥammad ibn Maslamah,
that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood to pray a voluntary prayer, he would say:

"Allah is the Greatest. I have turned my face to the One who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining to the truth, a Muslim, and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, who has no partner. This I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims. O Allah, You are the King; there is no god but You. Glory and praise be to You." Then he would recite.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed behind Abū Hurayrah. He recited, "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious," the Most Merciful, then he recited the Mother of the Qurʾān, until, when he reached "not those who have earned anger, nor those who are astray," he said, "Āmīn."
And the people said, "Āmīn."

Whenever he prostrated he would say, "Allah is the Greatest," and when he rose from the sitting after the second rakʿah he would say, "Allah is the Greatest." And when he finished the prayer with the salām, he said, "By the One in whose hand is my soul, I am the closest of you in prayer to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent me to collect charity (ṣadaqah). I passed by a man, and when he had gathered his wealth for me, I found nothing due from him except a bint makhāḍ [a one-year-old she-camel]. So I said to him, "Give a bint makhāḍ, for that is your charity."
He said, "That is an animal with no milk and no strength for riding. But here is a young, large, fat she-camel; take her."

I said to him, "I will not take what I have not been commanded to take. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is near you. If you like, go to him and present to him what you presented to me, and do so. If he accepts it from you, I will accept it, and if he rejects it, I will reject it."

He said, "Then I will do so." So he went out with me, and he took out the she-camel that he had offered me, until we came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said to him, "O Prophet of Allah, your messenger came to me to take the charity due on my wealth. By Allah, neither the Messenger of Allah ﷺ nor any of his messengers has ever before stood over my wealth. I gathered my wealth for him, and he claimed that what is due from me is a bint makhāḍ, but that is an animal with no milk and no strength for riding. I offered him a young, large she-camel for him to take, but he refused. Here she is; I have brought her to you, O Messenger of Allah."
Take her. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him,
"That is what is due from you. If you volunteer something good, Allah will reward you for it, and we will accept it from you."
He said, "Here she is, O Messenger of Allah; I have brought her to you, so take her."
He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that she be taken, and he prayed for blessing for him in his wealth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was called Daysam. Ibn ʿUbayd said: from Banū Sadūs. From Bashīr ibn al-Khaṣāṣiyyah,

Ibn ʿUbayd said in his narration: His name was not Bashīr, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named him Bashīr. He said: We said, "The collectors of charity (ṣadaqah) transgress against us. Should we conceal from our wealth an amount equal to what they transgress against us?" He said, "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Riders who dislike you will come to you. When they come to you, welcome them and let them be [free] to do what they seek. If they are just, it is for their own souls, and if they are unjust, it is against them. Satisfy them, for the completion of your zakāh is their satisfaction, and let them pray for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no jalab and no janab, and their charity (ṣadaqah) is only to be taken in their own homes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, regarding the saying:
"There is no jalab and no janab."

He said: It means that charity from livestock is to be taken at their [own] places and not brought to the collector. And janab, in this obligation as well, means that their owners are not to be made to take [the animals] away. He said: A man should not be at the farthest place from those liable for charity so that [the animals] are drawn to him; rather, it is taken at his place.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no zakāh on horses or slaves, except the zakāh of Fiṭr on slaves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Wakīʿ said: Al-baʿl, al-kabūs, is what grows from rainwater.
Ibn al-Aswad said: Yaḥyā, meaning Ibn Ādam, said: I asked Abū Iyās al-Asadī about al-baʿl, and he said: It is what is watered by rainwater.
And al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: Al-baʿl is rainwater.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A clan
of Fahm, meaning al-Mughīrah, said: From every ten qirab, a qirbah [is due].
And he said: Two valleys of theirs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to send ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah, and he would estimate the date palms when they became ripe, before any of it was eaten. Then he would give the Jews the choice: either they take it according to that estimate, or they hand it over to them according to that estimate, so that the zakāh could be counted before the fruits were eaten and dispersed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade that al-Jurʿūr and lawn al-Ḥubayq be taken as charity (ṣadaqah).
Al-Zuhrī said: They are two kinds of dates of Madīnah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It does not mention wheat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"One ṣāʿ of wheat or qamḥ on every two persons, young or old, free or slave, male or female. As for the wealthy among you, Allah will purify him; and as for the poor among you, Allah will return to him more than he gave."
Sulaymān added in his narration: wealthy or poor.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The hand of a thief is not to be cut off for [theft of] less than the price of a shield."
ʿĀʾishah was asked, "What is the price of a shield?" She said, "A quarter of a dinar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"The hand is not to be cut off except for [theft of] a shield or its price."
And he claimed that ʿUrwah said, "The shield is four dirhams."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The hand is not to be cut off except for five.
Hammām said: I met ʿAbdullāh al-Dānāj, and he narrated to me from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, who said: "The hand is not to be cut off except for five."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the hand was not cut off except for the price of a shield, and its value at that time was a dinar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mursal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever performs ablution and does it well, then prays—and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: then prays the last evening prayer—then prays four rakʿahs after it, completing—and Sawār said: perfecting—their bowing and prostration, and knows what he recites—and Sawār said: what he reads—in them, they will be for him equal to the Night of Qadr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever performs ablution and does it well, then attends the ʿatamah prayer in congregation, then prays four like it after it, reciting in them and completing their bowing and prostration, will have a reward like that of the Night of Qadr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: "For how much is the hand cut off?" He said:

"The hand is not cut off for fruit still hanging on the tree; but when the drying floor has gathered it, the hand is cut off [if it reaches] the price of a shield. And it is not cut off for [stealing] an animal grazing on the mountain; but when it has reached the fold, the hand is cut off [if it reaches] the price of a shield."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Jurayj said: Abū al-Zubayr said, from Jābir,
from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
"There is no cutting off [of the hand] for one who snatches."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A thief was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said, "Kill him."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, he only stole." He said, "Kill him."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, he only stole." He said, "Cut off his hand."

He said: Then he stole again and his foot was cut off. Then he stole in the time of Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, until all his limbs had been cut off. Then he stole a fifth time, and Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ knew best about this when he said, 'Kill him.'"
Then he handed him over to some young men of Quraysh to kill him, among them ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr—who loved leadership—and he said, "Make me your commander."
So they made him commander over them, and whenever he struck, they struck, until they killed him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The owner of the stolen property is not to be compensated by the thief once the prescribed punishment has been carried out on him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ distributed a share, giving some people and withholding from others. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, you gave so-and-so and withheld from so-and-so, and he is a believer." He said:
"Do not say 'a believer'; say 'a Muslim.'"
Ibn Shihāb said: [Allah says,] {The Bedouins say, 'We believe.'}
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ten things are from the Sunnah: using the siwāk, trimming the moustache, rinsing the mouth, sniffing water into the nose, letting the beard grow, trimming the nails, plucking the armpit hair, circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, and washing the private parts after relieving oneself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ was a governor in Egypt. One of his companions came to him and found him with disheveled, unkempt hair. He said, "Why do I see you unkempt when you are a governor?" He said, "The Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to forbid us from al-irfāh."
We said, "What is al-irfāh?" He said, "Combing the hair every day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved starting with the right: he would take with his right hand, give with his right hand, and he loved starting with the right in all his affairs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Masʿūd addressed us and said, "How can you order me to recite according to the recitation of Zayd ibn Thābit, after I recited seventy-odd sūrahs directly from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Indeed Zayd was with the boys, with two locks of hair."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When he came to the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Come near me."
So he came near him, and he placed his hand on his forelock, then passed his hand over it, blessed him, and prayed for him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and saw that he had colored his beard with yellow dye.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not dye his hair; there was only a little gray hair near the lower lip, a little at the temples, and a little on the head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: with henna. She said, "There is no harm in it, but I dislike this because my beloved ﷺ disliked its smell," meaning the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: We performed Hajj with the Prophet ﷺ and we poured forth [from Minā to the House] on the Day of Sacrifice, and Ṣafiyyah menstruated.
The Prophet ﷺ wished to have with her what a man wishes to have with his wife.
So I said, "O Messenger of Allah, she is menstruating." He said, "Is she going to detain us?"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah,
she has already performed the ṭawāf al-ifāḍah on the Day of Sacrifice." He said, "Then depart."
And it is related from al-Qāsim, ʿUrwah and al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her): Ṣafiyyah performed the ṭawāf al-ifāḍah on the Day of Sacrifice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only stayed at al-Muḥaṣṣab because it was easier for his departure, and it is not a sunnah; so whoever wishes may stay there, and whoever wishes may not stay there.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
and Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd,
they said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us,
from Zayd ibn Aslam,
and [another chain:] Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us
(and this is his wording), from Mālik ibn Anas,
from what was read to him, from Zayd ibn Aslam,
from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn Ḥunayn, from his father,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās
and al-Miswar ibn Makhramah,
that they disagreed at al-Abwāʾ. ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās said, "A person in iḥrām may wash his head."
And al-Miswar said, "A person in iḥrām may not wash his head."

So Ibn ʿAbbās sent me to Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī to ask him about that. I found him bathing between the two wooden posts of a well, screening himself with a cloth. He said: I greeted him with salām, and he said, "Who is this?" I said, "I am ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥunayn. ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās sent me to you to ask how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to wash his head while in iḥrām." Abū Ayyūb (may Allah be pleased with him) put his hand on the cloth and lowered it until his head appeared to me. Then he said to a person [who was pouring], "Pour."
So he poured over his head, then he moved his head with both hands, bringing them forward and back, then said, "This is how I saw him ﷺ do it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, in Paradise there is a gate called ar-Rayyān,
through which those who fast will enter on the Day of Resurrection;
no one other than them will enter through it. It will be said, 'Where are those who fast?' and they will stand up;
no one other than them will enter through it.
When they have entered, it will be closed,
and no one else will enter through it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The religion will remain prevalent as long as people hasten to break the fast, because the Jews and Christians delay it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
both of them from Ibn ʿUyaynah
(Abū Bakr said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us),
from Ibn Abī Labīd,
from Abū Salamah,
who said: I asked ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) about the fasting of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: He would fast until we said, "He has [continued to] fast."
And he would stop fasting until we said, "He has stopped fasting."
And I never saw him fasting more in any month than he did in Shaʿbān. He used to fast all of Shaʿbān; he used to fast Shaʿbān except for a little.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) about the fasting of the Prophet ﷺ. She said: He would fast until we said, "He keeps fasting, he keeps fasting."
And he would stop fasting until we said, "He has stopped, he has stopped." She said: And I did not see him fast a complete month since he came to Madinah, except Ramaḍān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should fast on Friday unless he fasts the day before it or the day after it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to encourage standing in prayer during Ramaḍān without commanding them to it as an obligation, and he would say:
"Whoever stands in prayer during Ramaḍān with faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away while the matter was like that, and it remained so during the caliphate of Abū Bakr and during the early part of the caliphate of ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: When the last ten nights began, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would spend the night in worship, wake his family, and tighten his waist-wrapper.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would be in iʿtikāf in the mosque, and he would extend his head to me through the opening of the room, and I would wash his head.
And Musaddad said: and I would comb his hair, while I was menstruating.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They both relate an account from the accounts of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning the ʿUmrah of al-Ḥudaybiyyah. Among what ʿUrwah informed me on their authority is that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the written agreement with Suhayl ibn ʿAmr,
on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, concerning the settlement of the truce period,
one of the conditions Suhayl ibn ʿAmr stipulated was that he said: "No one from us will come to you, even if he is on your religion, except that you will return him to us,
and you will leave him to us."
Suhayl refused to conclude the agreement with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except on that basis,
The believers disliked that and were deeply distressed, and they spoke about it.
But when Suhayl refused to conclude the agreement with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except on that basis,
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote it with him.
So on that day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned Abū Jandal ibn Suhayl to his father, Suhayl ibn ʿAmr.
And no man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during that period except that he returned him,
even if he was a Muslim.
Then believing women came as emigrants.
Umm Kulthūm bint ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ was among those who went out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she was a young unmarried woman.
Her family came asking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to send her back to them,
until Allah, the Exalted, revealed concerning the believing women what He revealed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the people of Khaybar dislocated the limbs of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,
ʿUmar stood up to give a speech and said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dealt with the Jews of Khaybar regarding their properties, and said:
'We will keep you as long as Allah keeps you.'
And ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar went out to his property there and was attacked during the night,
and his hands and feet were dislocated.
We have no enemy there other than them;
they are our enemy and the ones we suspect,
and I have decided to expel them."
When ʿUmar had resolved on that, one of the sons of Abū al-Ḥuqayq came to him
and said: "O Commander of the Faithful,
will you expel us when Muḥammad ﷺ allowed us to stay and dealt with us regarding the properties,
and made that a condition for us?" ʿUmar said: "Do you think I have forgotten the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
'How will you be when you are expelled from Khaybar, your young she-camel carrying you along,
night after night?'"
He said: "That was a joke from Abū al-Qāsim."
He said: "You lie, O enemy of Allah!"
So ʿUmar expelled them and gave them the value of what they owned of fruit, in money, camels, and goods,
such as saddles, ropes, and other things.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said one day on the pulpit: "
While some people were travelling on the sea, their food ran out, and an island appeared to them. They went out wanting bread, and the Jassāsah met them."
I said to Abū Salamah, "What is the Jassāsah?" He said, "A woman dragging the hair of her skin and her head."

She said, "[It is] in this palace." Then he mentioned the hadith, and he asked about the palm trees of Baysān and the spring of Zughar. He said, "He is the Messiah." Then Ibn Abī Salamah said to me, "There is something in this hadith that I did not memorize." He said, "Jābir testified that he is Ibn Ṣayyād." I said, "But he has died."
He said, "Even if he has died."
I said, "But he became Muslim."
He said, "Even if he became Muslim."
I said, "But he entered Madīnah."
He said, "Even if he entered Madīnah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar used to say, "By Allah, I have no doubt that the Antichrist, the Dajjāl, is Ibn Ṣayyād."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We lost Ibn Ṣayyād on the day of al-Ḥarrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were around the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he mentioned tribulation and said: "
When you see people whose covenants have become unreliable and whose trusts have become light, and they are like this,"
and he interlaced his fingers. [The narrator] said: I stood up to him and said, "What should I do at that time, may Allah make me your ransom?" He said: "
Stay in your house, control your tongue, take what you recognize and leave what you reject, attend to your own personal affair, and leave aside the affair of the general public."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a sin is committed on the earth, whoever witnesses it and hates it" — and once he said, "rejects it" — "
is like one who was absent from it; and whoever was absent from it but approved of it is like one who witnessed it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
People will not be destroyed until they have no excuse left, or until they bear the blame themselves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Allah will not leave this nation unable [to last] for half a day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
I truly hope that my nation will not fall short with its Lord, so that He would delay them by half a day."
Saʿd was asked, "How long is half a day?" He said, "Five hundred years."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿādh came to me while I was in Yemen, along with a man
who had been a Jew and had become Muslim, then apostatized from Islam.
When Muʿādh came, he said, "I will not dismount from my mount until he is killed." So he was killed.
One of the two said, "He had been asked to repent before that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this story, he said: A man who had apostatized from Islam was brought to Abū Mūsā,
and he called him [to repent] for twenty nights or about that. Then Muʿādh came and called him, but he refused, so he struck his neck.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this story, he said: He did not dismount until he had struck his neck, and he did not ask him to repent.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him: A Jewish woman
used to insult the Prophet ﷺ and speak ill of him. A man strangled her until she died, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ declared her blood unavenged.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He mentioned this hadith. Anas said: I saw one of them biting the ground with his mouth from thirst until they died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: This was before the prescribed punishments were revealed, meaning the hadith of Anas.
label: machine translation

segments_en: {The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon the earth to cause corruption is only that they be killed or crucified or have their hands and feet cut off from opposite sides or be exiled from the land} up to His words {Forgiving, Merciful}. This verse was revealed about the polytheists. Whoever of them repents before he is overpowered, that does not prevent the prescribed punishment from being carried out for what he committed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Overlook the slips of people of good standing, except for the prescribed punishments."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Māʿiz
came to the Prophet ﷺ and confessed before him four times, so he ordered that he be stoned. And he said to Hazzāl: "
If you had covered him with your garment, it would have been better for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hazzāl
told Māʿiz to go to the Prophet ﷺ and inform him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cut off the hand of a man for [stealing] a shield worth a dinar or ten dirhams.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū az-Zubayr said: Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
There is no hand-cutting for one who plunders, and whoever commits open plunder is not one of us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: A woman borrowed jewelry — she means — through the words of people who were known, while she herself was not known. Then she sold it and was caught. She was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he ordered her hand to be cut off. She is the one for whom Usāmah ibn Zayd interceded, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about her what he said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah about the prayer of

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the voluntary prayers. She said: He used to pray four [units] before Ẓuhr in my house, then go out and lead the people in prayer, then return to my house and pray two units. He would lead the people in the Maghrib prayer, then return to my house and pray two units. He would lead them in the ʿIshāʾ prayer, then enter my house and pray two units. At night he would pray nine units, including the Witr. He would pray for a long part of the night standing and a long part of the night sitting. When he recited while standing, he bowed and prostrated from a standing position; and when he recited while sitting, he bowed and prostrated from a sitting position. When dawn broke, he would pray two units, then go out and lead the people in the Fajr prayer, ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ did not die until he was praying much of his prayer while sitting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The night prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was ten units, and he would conclude with Witr of one unit, and he would pray the two units of Fajr. That makes thirteen units.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about the Witr,
and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"One unit at the end of the night."
And I asked Ibn ʿUmar, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"One unit at the end of the night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever among you fears that he will not wake up at the end of the night,
let him pray Witr at the beginning of the night and then sleep.
And whoever among you hopes to wake up at the end of the night,
let him pray Witr at the end of the night.
For recitation at the end of the night is witnessed [by the angels], and that is better."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah descends to the lowest heaven every night when the first third of the night has passed, and says: I am the King, I am the King! Who is it that calls upon Me, that I may answer him? Who is it that asks of Me, that I may give him? Who is it that seeks My forgiveness, that I may forgive him? He continues like that until the dawn shines."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I spent the night at the house of my maternal aunt Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also spent the night with her. I saw him get up to relieve himself; he went to the water skin, untied its mouth, and performed an ablution that was between two ablutions [i.e., moderate]. Then he came to his bed and slept. Then he got up another time, went to the water skin, untied its mouth, and performed a full ablution. Then he stood to pray, and in his prostration he would say: "

O Allah, place light in my heart, place light in my hearing, place light in my sight, place light beneath me, place light above me, light on my right, light on my left, place light in front of me, place light behind me, and make light great for me."
Then he slept until he breathed heavily, and Bilāl came to him and woke him for the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He slept at the house of the Prophet ﷺ and saw him wake up, use the tooth-stick, and perform ablution while saying:
"Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth..." until he finished the sūrah.
Then he stood and prayed two units, making the standing, bowing and prostration long in them.
Then he finished and slept until he breathed heavily.
Then he did that three times, for six units in all,
each time using the tooth-stick, then performing ablution and reciting these verses.
Then he prayed Witr — ʿUthmān said: with three units —
and the muʾadhdhin came to him and he went out to the prayer. Ibn ʿĪsā said:
Then he prayed Witr, and Bilāl came to him and informed him of the prayer when dawn broke,
so he prayed the two units of Fajr and then went out to the prayer — then both [narrators] agreed — saying: "
O Allah, place light in my heart,
place light in my tongue,
place light in my hearing,
place light in my sight,
place light behind me and light in front of me,
place light above me,
and light beneath me.
O Allah, and make light great for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I spent a night at the house of my aunt Maymūnah. The Prophet ﷺ stood to pray voluntarily during the night. The Prophet ﷺ went to the water skin and performed ablution, then stood and prayed. When I saw him do that, I got up, performed ablution from the water skin, and then stood on his left side. He took me by my hand from behind his back and moved me around, likewise from behind his back, to his right side.
I said: Was that in a voluntary prayer? He said: Yes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up at night to pray, he would begin his prayer with two light units.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was standing in the mosque when a man threw a pebble at me.
I looked, and it was ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. He said, "Go and bring me those two." So I brought them to him.
He said, "Who are you two?" or "Where are you two from?" They said, "We are from the people of aṭ-Ṭāʾif."
He said, "If you were from the people of this city, I would have punished you,
for raising your voices in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah,
the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: "I have not known my parents except that they followed the religion [of Islam],
and not a day passed for us without the Messenger of Allah ﷺ coming to us at both ends of the day, morning and evening.
Then it occurred to Abū Bakr to build a mosque in the courtyard of his house,
and he would pray in it and recite the Qurʾān.
The women of the polytheists would stand by it,
along with their children, marveling at him and looking at him.
Abū Bakr was a man who wept much; he could not control his eyes when he recited the Qurʾān.
This alarmed the nobles of Quraysh among the polytheists."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [I heard it] from my father, but I did not memorize it,
so Wāqid corrected it for me from his father.
He said: I heard my father
say: ʿAbdullāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr,
how will you be when you are left among the dregs of the people, like this?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Sālim ibn ʿAbdullāh seeking out certain places along the road and praying in them,
and he would relate that his father used to pray in them,
and that he had seen the Prophet ﷺ praying in those places.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ prayed where the small mosque stands, below the mosque at the high ground of ar-Rawḥāʾ,
and ʿAbdullāh knew the place where the Prophet ﷺ had prayed. He would say: "Then it is on your right when you stand in the mosque to pray,
and that mosque is on the edge of the right-hand side of the road,
as you are going toward Makkah,
between it and the larger mosque is about a stone's throw, or thereabouts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and he would pray facing toward the ʿIrq itself,
and ʿAbdullāh would set out in the afternoon from ar-Rawḥāʾ,
and would not pray Ẓuhr until he reached that place, and he would pray Ẓuhr there.
When he was coming from Makkah, if he passed by it an hour before dawn or at the end of the night, he would halt for the night's rest until he prayed the Ṣubḥ prayer there.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ used to stop under a huge tree before ar-Ruwaythah, on the right side of the road,
directly facing the road, in a low, level place,
until one comes out from a hill about two miles short of ar-Ruwaythah's post-station.
Its top had broken,
and folded over in its middle,
while it stood upright on a trunk,
and around its trunk were many mounds of sand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ prayed at the edge of a watercourse beyond al-ʿArj, as you are going toward a hillock; by that mosque there are two or three graves,
over the graves are heaps of stones, on the right of the road,
by the acacia trees of the road,
among those acacias. ʿAbdullāh would set out from al-ʿArj after the sun had passed its zenith in the midday heat,
and would pray Ẓuhr in that mosque.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped by some acacia trees on the left of the road,
in a watercourse near Harshā,
that watercourse is adjacent to the ridge of Harshā,
and between it and the road is about a bowshot.
ʿAbdullāh used to pray toward an acacia tree,
the one nearest to the road, and it is the tallest of them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ used to stop in the watercourse at the lower part of Marr aẓ-Ẓahrān,
on the Madinah side, when descending from aṣ-Ṣafrāwāt; he would stop in the bed of that watercourse on the left of the road,
as you are going toward Makkah,
and between the stopping place of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the road there is only a stone's throw.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that ʿAbdullāh
when he entered the Kaʿbah, would walk straight ahead as he entered,
and would leave the door behind his back,
and he would walk until there was about three cubits between him and the wall in front of him.
He would pray, seeking the place that Bilāl had told him the Prophet ﷺ had prayed in.
He said: "There is no harm for any of us in praying in whichever part of the House he wishes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith said: "My bed was opposite the place where the Prophet ﷺ prayed, and sometimes his garment would fall on me while I was on my bed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put on a new garment, he would name it by its name, whether a shirt or a turban, and then say:

"O Allah, to You belongs all praise; You have clothed me with it. I ask You for its goodness and the goodness of that for which it was made, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of that for which it was made."
Abū Naḍrah said: When one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ put on a new garment, it would be said to him, "May you wear it out, and may Allah the Exalted replace it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: a garment of humiliation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever imitates a people is one of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The king
of Dhū Yazan gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a ḥullah (a two-piece garment) which he had bought for thirty-three camels, or thirty-three she-camels, and he accepted it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bought a ḥullah for a little over twenty young she-camels, and then gave it as a gift to Dhū Yazan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Ḥarūriyyah rose in revolt, I went to ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said, "Go to these people."

So I put on the finest ḥullah of Yemen that I had. Abū Zumayl said: Ibn ʿAbbās was a handsome man with a commanding voice. Ibn ʿAbbās said: I went to them, and they said, "Welcome, Ibn ʿAbbās! What is this ḥullah?" He said, "What fault do you find with me? I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wearing the finest ḥullahs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this story, he said: a ḥullah of brocade.
And he said in it: Then he sent him a cloak of silk brocade, and said:
"Sell it and meet your need with it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade silk, except for this much and this much: two fingers, three, or four.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this [chain] he added: "And I do not say that he forbade it to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The king of the Romans

sent the Prophet ﷺ a fur-lined garment (mustuqah) of fine silk. He put it on, and it is as though I can see his hands swaying in it. Then he sent it to Jaʿfar, who put it on, and then came to him. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"I did not give it to you to wear."
He said, "Then what shall I do with it?" He said, "Send it to your brother, the Negus."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"I do not ride on crimson saddle-cloths, I do not wear clothes dyed with safflower, and I do not wear a shirt bordered with silk."
He said: Al-Ḥasan pointed to the opening of his shirt. He said that he also said:
"Beware: the perfume of men is that which has scent but no color, and the perfume of women is that which has color but no scent."
Saʿīd said: I think he said: They understood his statement about women's perfume to apply when she goes out; but when she is with her husband, she may perfume herself with whatever she wishes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Ibn ʿUmar in the market buy a Syrian garment; he saw a red thread in it and returned it. So I went to Asmāʾ and mentioned that to her. She said, "Girl, hand me the cloak of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
She brought out a cloak of thick woolen cloth (ṭayālisah) with the opening, the sleeves, and the two slits trimmed with silk brocade.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only forbade cloth that is made entirely of silk. As for the silk border and the warp of the cloth, there is no harm in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to remove it from the boys and leave it on the girls.
Misʿar said: I asked ʿAmr ibn Dīnār about it, but he did not know it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went with my father toward the Prophet ﷺ, and there he was with thick hair that had a trace of henna, wearing two green cloaks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hishām, meaning Ibn al-Ghāz, said: The muḍarrajah is that which is not deeply dyed, and not the rose-colored one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me, Abū ʿAlī al-Luʾluʾī said: I think, wearing a garment dyed with rose-colored safflower, and he said, "What is this?"
So I went and burned it. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"What did you do with your garment?" I said, "I burned it." He said:
"Why did you not give it to some of your family to wear?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Banū Ḥārithah, from Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj,
who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw on our mounts and our camels cloths with red woolen threads in them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I see that this redness has overcome you."
So we rose quickly at the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so much so that some of our camels bolted. We took the cloths and removed them from the camels.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"An army will march to attack this House [the Kaʿbah], until, when they are in a desert land, the earth will swallow up those in their middle. Then the first of them will call out to the last of them, and they will all be swallowed up together, and none will escape except a straggler who will tell about them."

Then a man said to him, "I bear witness about you that you did not lie about your grandfather, and I bear witness about your grandfather that he did not lie about Ḥafṣah, and I bear witness about Ḥafṣah that she did not lie about the Prophet ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Yūnus,
and al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ziyād, from al-Ḥasan,
from al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays,
from Abū Bakrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When two Muslims meet with their swords and one of them kills the other, both the killer and the one killed are in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When two Muslim men take up weapons, one against the other, they are both on the edge of the brink of Hell. And if one of them kills the other, they are both in the Fire.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in a prayer and made it long. When he finished, we said (or they said), "O Messenger of Allah, you made the prayer long today." He said:

"I prayed a prayer of hope and fear. I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, three things for my nation; He granted me two and refused me one. I asked Him not to let an enemy from outside them overpower them, and He granted me that. I asked Him not to destroy them by drowning, and He granted me that. And I asked Him not to make their violence be among themselves, and He refused me that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of men came to Marwān in Medina and heard him speaking about the signs, saying that the first of them is the Dajjāl. [The narrator] said: So I went to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr and told him. ʿAbdullāh said, "He has said nothing. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'The first of the signs to appear is the rising of the sun from its place of setting, or the emergence of the Beast against the people in the forenoon. Whichever of the two comes before the other, the other will follow right after it.'"
ʿAbdullāh said: He used to read the scriptures, and I think the first of them to appear is the rising of the sun from its place of setting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The world is the prison of the believer and the Paradise of the disbeliever."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting, {Competition in worldly increase diverts you}. He said:

"The son of Adam says, 'My wealth, my wealth.' [He said:] But do you have, O son of Adam, from your wealth anything except what you ate and consumed, or wore and wore out, or gave in charity and sent ahead?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Look at those who are below you, and do not look at those who are above you, for that is more likely to keep you from belittling the favor of Allah upon you."
This is an authentic hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man sneezed in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while I was present, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "May Allah have mercy on you."
Then he sneezed a second and a third time, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"This man has a cold."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey. He withdrew to relieve himself, then came back and asked for water for ablution, and performed ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said:]
"I am to you only like a father; I teach you. When one of you goes to relieve himself, he should not face the qiblah or turn his back to it, and he should not clean himself with his right hand."
And he used to command [the use of] three stones, and he forbade dung and bones.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ forbade us to face the qiblah when urinating, but I saw him, a year before he passed away, facing it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went with ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ
to the Prophet ﷺ. He came out carrying a leather shield, and he screened himself with it and then urinated. We said, "Look at him, urinating like a woman."
He heard that and said:

"Do you not know what befell the man among the Children of Israel? When urine got on them, they would cut off the part of them that urine had touched. He forbade them, and he was punished in his grave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿĀʾishah and heard her say:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out from the toilet, he would say, "Your forgiveness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said:]
"This verse was revealed about the people of Qubāʾ:
'In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves.'"
He said: They used to clean themselves with water, so this verse was revealed about them.
He said: This hadith is gharīb from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The key to prayer is purification, its entry into sanctity is the takbīr, and its release from it is the taslīm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: His paternal aunt said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you is fasting, let him break his fast with dates; if he does not find dates, then with water, for water is purifying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is overcome by vomiting while fasting does not have to make up the fast, but if he induces himself to vomit, let him make it up."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever breaks the fast of a day of Ramadan without a concession and without illness, fasting for all time will not make up for it, even if he were to fast it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not fast on Saturday except in what Allah has made obligatory upon you. If one of you finds nothing but the bark of a grapevine or the twig of a tree, let him chew it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he used to command fasting the White Days, the thirteenth, fourteenth and fifteenth, and he would say:
"It is like fasting all of time," or, "like the likeness of fasting all of time."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you is invited to a meal while he is fasting, let him say: I am fasting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to observe iʿtikāf during the last ten days of Ramadan. One year he did not observe it, and when the following year came, he observed iʿtikāf for twenty days.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir used to pass by me and say, "O Khālid, come out with us to practice shooting."
One day I was slow in coming to him, and he said, "O Khālid, come and I will tell you what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said." So I came to him, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah admits three people to Paradise through a single arrow: its maker, who seeks reward in making it, the one who shoots it, and the one who hands it to him. So shoot and ride, though that you shoot is dearer to me than that you ride. Amusement is only in three things: a man training his horse, his playing with his wife, and his shooting with his bow and arrows. Whoever gives up shooting after having learned it, out of dislike for it, has abandoned a blessing," or he said, "has been ungrateful for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have come wishing to fight in jihad with you, seeking the face of Allah and the Hereafter. I came while my parents were weeping." He said:
"Go back to them and make them laugh as you made them weep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The angels do not accompany a group of travellers in which there is a dog or a bell."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Seek out the weak for me, for you are only given provision and granted victory because of your weak."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ travelled and mounted his riding animal, he would say, pointing with his finger (and Shuʿbah extended his finger):
"O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey and the Successor over the family. O Allah, accompany us with Your good counsel and return us under Your protection.
O Allah, fold the earth up for us and make the journey easy for us. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel and the gloom of returning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, bless my nation in their early mornings."
He said: And whenever he sent out a detachment or an army, he would send them at the beginning of the day.
He said: Ṣakhr was a merchant, and he would send out his trade at the beginning of the day, so he became wealthy and his wealth increased.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Madinah with my uncles and entered one of its orchards. I rubbed some of its ears of grain, and the owner of the orchard came, took my cloak and beat me. So I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to seek redress against him. He sent for the man, and they brought him. He said:
"What made you do this?"
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, he entered my orchard and took some of its grain and rubbed it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You did not teach him when he was ignorant, and you did not feed him when he was hungry. Return his cloak to him."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered for me a wasq, or half a wasq, of grain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a detachment to Khathʿam, and some of the people sought protection by prostrating, but killing was swift among them. He said: This reached the Prophet ﷺ, so he ordered half the blood-money for them and said:
"I am free of every Muslim who dwells among the polytheists."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, why?" He said:
"Their fires should not be visible to one another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hudhayfah was in al-Madāʾin, and he used to mention things that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said in anger to some of his Companions. Some of the people who heard that from Hudhayfah would go to Salmān and tell him what Hudhayfah had said, and Salmān would say, "Hudhayfah knows best what he is saying." They would return to Hudhayfah and say to him, "We mentioned your words to Salmān, and he neither confirmed you nor denied you."

So Hudhayfah came to Salmān while he was in a vegetable garden and said, "O Salmān, what prevents you from confirming me regarding what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" Salmān said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would become angry and say things in anger to some of his Companions, and he would be pleased and say things in contentment to some of his Companions. Will you not stop until you instill in some men love for other men, and in some men hatred for other men, and until you cause discord and division? You know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave a sermon and said:

'Any man of my Ummah whom I have insulted or cursed in my anger—for I am only one of the children of Adam; I become angry as they become angry, and He sent me only as a mercy to the worlds—then make that a blessing (ṣalāh) for them on the Day of Resurrection.'
By Allah, you will stop, or I will write to ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the illness of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became severe, while I was with him among a group of Muslims, Bilāl called him to prayer. He said, "Order someone to lead the people in prayer."

Then ʿAbdullāh ibn Zamʿah went out, and there was ʿUmar among the people, and Abū Bakr was absent. I said, "O ʿUmar, get up and lead the people in prayer." He stepped forward and said the takbīr. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard his voice—and ʿUmar was a man with a loud voice—he said:
"Where is Abū Bakr? Allah refuses this, and the Muslims refuse this. Allah refuses this, and the Muslims refuse this."
So he sent for Abū Bakr, who came after ʿUmar had already prayed that prayer, and he led the people in prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ heard the voice of ʿUmar. Ibn Zamʿah said: The Prophet ﷺ came out until he put his head out of his room, and then said:
"No, no, no! Let the son of Abū Quḥāfah lead the people in prayer."
He said that in displeasure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hudhayfah said: There is no one among the people whom trial (fitnah) reaches but that I fear it for him, except Muḥammad ibn Maslamah, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The trial will not harm you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We entered upon Hudhayfah, and he said, "I know a man whom trials will not harm at all."

He said: So we went out, and there was a tent pitched. We entered, and in it was Muḥammad ibn Maslamah. We asked him about that, and he said, "I do not want anything of your cities to take hold of me until it clears away from what it clears away from."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, "Tell us about this march of yours: is it a covenant the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made with you, or an opinion you formed?" He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not make any covenant with me about anything; rather, it is an opinion I formed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I do not know whether Tubbaʿ was cursed or not, and I do not know whether ʿUzayr was a prophet or not."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have not seen any who are deficient in intellect and religion more able to overcome the sound-minded than you women."
She said, "What is the deficiency in intellect and religion?" He said:

"As for the deficiency in intellect, it is that the testimony of two women equals the testimony of one man. As for the deficiency in religion, it is that one of you breaks her fast in Ramadan and stays for days without praying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"Whoever loves for the sake of Allah, hates for the sake of Allah, gives for the sake of Allah, and withholds for the sake of Allah has perfected faith."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Zuhrī said regarding {Say: You have not believed, but say: We have submitted}: We hold that Islam is the word, and faith is the deed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any Muslim man who declares another Muslim man to be a disbeliever: if he is a disbeliever, [it stands]; otherwise, he himself is the disbeliever."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When a man commits fornication, faith leaves him and is over him like a canopy. When he stops, faith returns to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Abū Rāfiʿ, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, see al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī praying with his hair tied up in a knot. He untied it, or forbade him from it, and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a man to pray while his hair is tied in a knot.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Do not raise your eyes to the sky, [for] it may snatch away your sight."
That is, during prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prostrated with the Prophet ﷺ eleven prostrations, none of which were from the mufaṣṣal: al-Aʿrāf, ar-Raʿd, an-Naḥl, Banī Isrāʾīl, Maryam, al-Hajj, the prostration of al-Furqān, Sulaymān (sūrat an-Naml), as-Sajdah, Ṣād, and the prostration of the Ḥawāmīm.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ṭāwūs about the voluntary prayer
while traveling, and al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim ibn Yanāq was sitting with him. He said: Ṭāwūs narrated to me
that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made prayer obligatory when resident and when traveling. So when resident we would pray before it and after it, and when traveling we would pray before it and after it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us and said: "

O people, repent to Allah before you die, and hasten to righteous deeds before you become preoccupied. Connect what is between you and your Lord by remembering Him often and by giving much charity, secretly and openly; you will be given provision, granted victory, and made whole. And know that Allah has made the Friday prayer obligatory upon you, in this place of mine, on this day of mine, in this month of mine, in this year of mine, until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever abandons it during my life or after me, while he has a just or an unjust ruler, out of disregard for it or denial of it, may Allah not bring together his affairs and not bless him in his matters. Indeed, he has no prayer, no zakāh, no Hajj, no fasting, and no righteousness until he repents; and whoever repents, Allah turns to him in mercy. Indeed, a woman must not lead a man in prayer, a Bedouin must not lead a emigrant, and a wicked man must not lead a believer, unless he is forced by an authority whose sword and whip he fears."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to lead my father when he lost his sight.
When I took him out to the Friday prayer and he heard the call to prayer, he would ask forgiveness for Abū Umāmah,
Asʿad ibn Zurārah, and pray for him.
I remained a while hearing that from him,
then I said to myself:
By Allah, this is helplessness,
I hear him, whenever he hears the Friday call to prayer, ask forgiveness for Abū Umāmah and invoke blessings upon him,
and I do not ask him why he does it.
So I took him out as I used to take him out to the Friday prayer.
When he heard the call to prayer, he asked forgiveness as he used to do. I said to him:
Father, what about your praying for Asʿad ibn Zurārah whenever you hear the call to the Friday prayer, why is it? He said:
My son, he was the first to lead us in the Friday prayer before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came from Mecca,
at Naqīʿ al-Khaḍamāt,
in a low-lying area of the lava tract of Banū Bayāḍah. I said:
How many were you that day? He said: Forty men.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Friday is the master of days,
and the greatest of them in the sight of Allah.
It is greater in the sight of Allah than the day of Sacrifice and the day of Fitr.
It has five characteristics.
On it Allah created Adam.
On it Allah sent Adam down to the earth.
On it Allah caused Adam to die.
On it there is an hour in which the servant asks Allah for nothing but He gives it to him,
as long as he does not ask for something forbidden.
And on it the Hour will be established.
There is no angel brought near, no heaven, no earth, no wind, no mountain, and no sea, except that they are fearful of Friday."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave an example of Friday and then of going early: like one who offers a camel, like one who offers a cow, like one who offers a sheep,
until he mentioned the chicken.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with ʿAbdullāh to the Friday prayer and he found three had already preceded him. He said: The fourth of four, and the fourth of four is not far off. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
People will sit near Allah on the Day of Resurrection according to how early they went to the Friday prayers: the first, then the second, then the third."
Then he said: The fourth of four, and the fourth of four is not far off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the pulpit on Friday [he said]: "
What harm would it be for any of you, if he bought two garments for Friday,
besides the garment of his work clothes?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to give the call to prayer on Friday in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when the shadow was the length of a sandal strap.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to pray Friday prayer and then return and take the midday rest.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A famine afflicted us, and I had nothing left of my wealth with which to feed my family except some donkeys, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had forbidden the meat of domestic donkeys. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the famine has afflicted us, and I have nothing in my wealth with which to feed my family except my fattest donkeys, and you have forbidden the meat of domestic donkeys." He said, "
Feed your family from the fattest of your donkeys, for I only forbade them because of the scavengers of the town." Meaning the jallālah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Muzaynah, one of them narrating from the other,
one of them being ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUwaym and the other Ghālib ibn al-Abjar.
Misʿar said: I think it was Ghālib who came to the Prophet ﷺ with this hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a man
stayed at al-Ḥarrah with his family and children. A man said, "A she-camel of mine has strayed; if you find her, keep her."
He found her but did not find her owner. She fell ill, and his wife said, "Slaughter her."
But he refused, and she died. She said, "Skin her, so that we may dry her fat and meat and eat it."
He said, "Not until I ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." So he came to him and asked him, and he said, "
Do you have enough wealth to suffice you?" He said, "No." He said, "Then eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "What carrion is lawful for us?" He said, "What is your food?"
We said, "We drink the evening milk and the morning milk."
Abū Naʿīm said: ʿUqbah explained it to me as a cup in the morning and a cup in the evening. He said, "
By my father, that is hunger!"
So he made carrion lawful for them in that condition.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A cheese was brought to the Prophet ﷺ at Tabūk. He called for a knife, said Allah's name, and cut it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: What an excellent condiment vinegar is."
label: machine translation

segments_en: What an excellent condiment vinegar is."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That
garlic and onions were mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, the strongest of all of them is garlic; will you forbid it?" The Prophet ﷺ said, "
Eat it, but whoever among you eats it must not approach this mosque until its smell has gone from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever spits in the direction of the qiblah will come on the Day of Resurrection with his spittle between his eyes, and whoever eats from this foul plant must not come near our mosque." He said it three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I ate garlic and then came to the place where the Prophet ﷺ prayed, having already missed one rakʿah. When I entered the mosque, the Prophet ﷺ noticed the smell of garlic. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer, he said, "
Whoever eats from this plant must not come near us until its smell has gone," or he said, "his smell."
When I had completed the prayer, I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, you must give me your hand."
He said: So I put his hand inside the sleeve of my shirt to my chest, and he found that my chest was bandaged. He said, "
You have an excuse."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he asked ʿĀʾishah about onions,
and she said, "The last food the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ate was food containing onions."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Dates containing worms used to be brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he mentioned something similar in meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to go on expeditions with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and obtain some of the vessels and waterskins of the polytheists and make use of them, and he did not find fault with them for that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying, "We live next to the People of the Book, and they cook pork in their pots and drink wine in their vessels."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
If you find other vessels, eat and drink in them, but if you do not find others, then wash them with water and eat and drink."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ate or drank, he would say, "
Praise be to Allah, who fed and gave drink, made it easy to swallow, and made for it an outlet."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihān prepared food for the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions were invited. When they had finished, he said, "Reward your brother."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is rewarding him?" He said, "
When a man enters his house and eats his food and drinks his drink, and they pray for him, that is rewarding him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from his grandmother,
Salmā, the servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: No one complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of a pain in his head except that he said, "Have yourself cupped."
And no one complained of a pain in his legs except that he said, "Dye them with henna."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My maternal aunt was divorced three times, and she went out to pick the dates of her palm trees. A man met her and forbade her, so she came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him. He said to her:
"Go out and pick your dates; perhaps you will give charity from them or do some good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "And whoever compels them, then indeed, after their compulsion, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan said: Forgiving to them, the women who were compelled.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O you who believe, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you." In the time of the Prophet ﷺ, when people had prayed the late evening prayer, food, drink and women became forbidden to them, and they fasted until the next night. Then a man betrayed himself: he had relations with his wife after praying the evening prayer, before breaking his fast. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wished to make that easy for those who remained, and a concession and a benefit, so He, Glorified, said: "Allah knows that you used to betray yourselves."
This was among the things by which Allah benefited the people, granting them a concession and ease.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "And upon those who are able to fast it, there is a ransom: feeding a poor person." So whoever of them wished to pay the ransom by feeding a poor person did so, and his fast was complete. Then He said: "But whoever volunteers good, it is better for him; and that you fast is better for you." And He said: "So whoever of you witnesses the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey, then [let him fast] a number of other days."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was established for the pregnant woman and the nursing mother.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "And upon those who are able to fast it, there is a ransom: feeding a poor person." He said: It was a concession for the old man and the old woman, who were able to fast, to break the fast and feed one poor person for each day; and for the pregnant woman and the nursing mother, when they feared—Abū Dāwūd said: meaning for their children—they broke the fast and fed.
label: machine translation
