segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The month is twenty-nine days, so do not fast until you see it, and do not break the fast until you see it. If it is overcast for you, then calculate it as thirty."

He said: When it was the twenty-ninth of Shaʿbān, Ibn ʿUmar would look for it. If it was seen, then that was it; and if it was not seen and no cloud or dust prevented sight of it, he would begin the morning not fasting. But if a cloud or dust prevented sight of it, he would begin the morning fasting.
He said: Ibn ʿUmar would break the fast with the people and would not follow this calculation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ mentioned it, saying:

"Your breaking of the fast is the day you break the fast, and your sacrifice is the day you sacrifice. All of ʿArafah is a place of standing, all of Minā is a place of slaughter, all the mountain paths of Makkah are a place of slaughter, and all of Jamʿ is a place of standing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to take care in counting Shaʿbān in a way he did not for other months. Then he would fast upon seeing Ramadan. If it was overcast for him, he would count thirty days and then fast.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah stood among the people at Dayr Musaḥḥal, which is at the gate of Ḥimṣ, and said: O people, we saw the new moon on such and such a day, and I am going to begin the fast early, so whoever wishes to do so, let him do so.

He said: Mālik ibn Hubayrah as-Sabaʾī stood up to him and said: O Muʿāwiyah, is this something you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or is it your own opinion? He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Fast the month and its sirr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Its sirr is its beginning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿīd, meaning Ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, used to say: Its sirr is its beginning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the two of them saw the new moon on the night of Sunday. He said: That day is not to be made up by the man or the people of his town, unless they learn that the people of a town among the towns of the Muslims fasted on Sunday, in which case they make it up.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbbād ibn Kathīr came to Madinah and went over to the gathering of al-ʿAlāʾ. He took him by the hand and made him stand up, then said: O Allah, this man narrates from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When Shaʿbān is half over, do not fast."
Al-ʿAlāʾ said: O Allah, my father narrated to me from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Wealth was brought to the Prophet ﷺ from Bahrain, and he said: "
Spread it out in the mosque."
It was the greatest amount of wealth ever brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the prayer
and did not even look at it.
When he had finished the prayer, he came and sat beside it,
and he did not see anyone without giving him some.
Then al-ʿAbbās came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah,
give me some, for I paid ransom for myself and for ʿAqīl."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Take."
So he scooped up some in his garment,
then went to lift it but could not, and said: "O Messenger of Allah,
order one of them to lift it onto me." He said: "No."
He said: "Then you lift it onto me." He said: "No." So he spilled some of it out,
then went to lift it,
and said: "O Messenger of Allah,
order one of them to lift it onto me." He said: "No."
He said: "Then you lift it onto me." He said: "No." So he spilled some of it out,
then he carried it, put it on his shoulder, and went off.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept following him with his gaze until he was out of our sight,
amazed at his eagerness.
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not rise while a single dirham of it remained.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ asked permission to enter, and I permitted him. He said: "
Where would you like me to pray in your house?"
So I pointed out to him the place I liked,
and he stood, we lined up behind him, then he gave the salutation of peace and we gave the salutation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed, then said: "I was shown the Fire,
and I have never seen a sight as dreadful as today's."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to Sahl ibn Saʿd and said: "So-and-so," referring to the governor of Medina, "curses ʿAlī at the pulpit."
He said: "What does he say?" He said: "He calls him Abū Turāb."
Sahl laughed and said: "By Allah, no one gave him that name except the Prophet ﷺ,
and he had no name more beloved to him than it."
So I asked Sahl to tell me the story,
and I said: "O Abū ʿAbbās, how was it?" He said: ʿAlī came in to Fāṭimah, then went out and lay down in the mosque. The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Where is your cousin?"
She said: "In the mosque."
So he went out to him and found that his cloak had fallen from his back
and dust had reached his back,
and he began wiping the dust from his back, saying: "
Get up, O Abū Turāb!" twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw seventy of the People of the Ṣuffah,
not one of whom had a cloak,
only a waist-wrapper or a shawl,
tied around their necks.
Some reached halfway down the shins,
and some reached the ankles, and he would gather it with his hand,
disliking that his private parts be seen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman of the Anṣār said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah,
shall I make something for you to sit on? I have a slave who is a carpenter." He said: "If you wish."
He said: So she had the pulpit made for him.
When it was the day of Friday, the Prophet ﷺ sat on the pulpit that had been made,
and the palm trunk by which he used to give the sermon cried out until it almost split.
The Prophet ﷺ came down until he took it and held it to himself,
and it kept moaning like a child being quieted until it settled. He said: "
It wept over the remembrance it used to hear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men
left the Prophet ﷺ on a dark night,
and there was a light before them both until they parted,
and the light parted with them.
Maʿmar said, from Thābit, from Anas: They were Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr and a man of the Anṣār.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jundub said: I came on the day of al-Jarʿah, and there was a man sitting there. I said, "Blood will surely be shed here today."
That man said, "Never, by Allah!"
I said, "Indeed it will, by Allah!"
He said, "Never, by Allah!"
I said, "Indeed it will, by Allah!"
He said, "Never, by Allah! For it is a hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which he narrated to me."

I said, "What a bad companion you have been to me today! You hear me contradicting you, and you have heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, yet you do not stop me." Then I said, "What is this anger?" So I turned to him and asked him, and the man was Ḥudhayfah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was standing with Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and he said, "People will continue to stretch their necks in different directions in pursuit of this world." I said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Hour will not come until the Romans land at al-Aʿmāq or Dābiq. Then an army will come out to them from Medina, from the best of the people of the earth at that time. When they line up in ranks, the Romans will say, 'Leave us to fight those who took prisoners from among us.'
The Muslims will say, 'No, by Allah, we will never leave you to fight our brothers.'

So they will fight them. A third of them will flee, and Allah will never forgive them; a third will be killed, and they will be the best martyrs in the sight of Allah; and a third will conquer, and they will never be tried again. They will conquer Constantinople. While they are dividing the spoils, having hung their swords on olive trees, Satan will shout among them, 'The Antichrist has taken your place among your families!'

So they will set out, but that will be false. When they reach Syria, he will emerge. While they are preparing for battle and straightening the ranks, the prayer will be called, and Jesus, son of Mary, will descend and lead them. When the enemy of Allah sees him, he will melt as salt melts in water. If he left him alone, he would melt until he perished, but Allah will kill him by his hand, and he will show them his blood on his spear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:]
"The Hour will come while the Romans are the most numerous of people."

He said: That reached ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, and he said, "What are these hadith that are reported from you, which you claim to say from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" Al-Mustawrid said to him, "I said what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." ʿAmr said, "If you say that, then indeed they are the most forbearing of people during tribulation, the quickest of people to recover after a calamity, and the best of people to their poor and weak."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A red wind blew in Kufa, and a man came whose only cry was, "O ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, the Hour has come!"
He said: [ʿAbdullāh] sat up, having been reclining, and said, "The Hour will not come until inheritance is no longer divided and no one rejoices over war booty."
Then he gestured with his hand like this, pointing toward Syria, and said, "An enemy will gather against the people of Islam, and the people of Islam will gather against them."

I said, "Do you mean the Romans?" He said, "Yes. And during that fighting there will be fierce reversals. The Muslims will send forth a detachment pledged to death, not to return except victorious. They will fight until night separates them, and each side will withdraw without victory, and the detachment will be wiped out. Then the Muslims will send forth another detachment pledged to death, not to return except victorious. They will fight until night separates them, and each side will withdraw without victory, and the detachment will be wiped out. Then the Muslims will send forth another detachment pledged to death, not to return except victorious. They will fight until evening, and each side will withdraw without victory, and the detachment will be wiped out. On the fourth day, the remainder of the people of Islam will advance against them, and Allah will cause the enemy to be defeated. They will be slaughtered in a massacre—either he said, 'the like of which has not been seen,' or he said, 'the like of which was never seen'—so that a bird will pass by their flanks and not get beyond them before it falls dead. The sons of one father, who were a hundred, will count themselves and find only one man left of them. So what spoils could one rejoice over, or what inheritance could be divided? While they are in that state, they will hear of a calamity greater than that. A cry will come to them that the Antichrist has taken their place among their children. So they will throw down what is in their hands and advance, and they will send ten horsemen as a vanguard."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I know their names, the names of their fathers, and the colors of their horses. They are the best horsemen on the face of the earth on that day," or "among the best horsemen on the face of the earth on that day."
Ibn Abī Shaybah said in his narration, from Usayr ibn Jābir:
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in the house of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, and the house was full. He said: Then a red wind blew in Kufa.
Then he mentioned a hadith similar to the hadith of Ibn ʿUlayyah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in an upper room, and we were beneath it, talking.
And he related the hadith in the same way.
Shuʿbah said: I think he said, "[He] stops with them when they stop, and takes the midday rest with them wherever they say."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were talking, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked down upon us.
[The rest is] like the hadith of Muʿādh and Ibn Jaʿfar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that there was some dispute among the Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf at Qubāʾ,
so he went out with some of his Companions to reconcile them.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was detained, and the time of prayer came.
Bilāl came to Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both, and said: "O Abū Bakr,
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has been detained and the time of prayer has come.
Would you lead the people in prayer?" He said: "Yes, if you wish."
So Bilāl called the iqāmah for the prayer,
and Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, stepped forward and said the takbīr for the people.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, walking through the rows, cutting his way through them,
until he stood in the row.
The people began to clap.
Sahl said: Tasfīḥ means clapping.
He said: Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, would not turn around in his prayer,
but when the people did it a great deal, he turned and saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who gestured to him,
telling him to continue praying.
Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, raised his hands and praised Allah,
then stepped backward until he stood in the row.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went forward and led the people in prayer.
When he finished, he turned to the people and said:
"O people, what is the matter with you that when something happens to you in prayer you clap? Clapping is only for women.
Whoever experiences something in his prayer, let him say: Subḥān Allāh."
Then he turned to Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and said:
"O Abū Bakr,
what prevented you from leading the people in prayer when I gestured to you?"
Abū Bakr said: "It was not fitting for the son of Abū Quḥāfah to lead the prayer in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell ill, and some of his Companions came in to visit him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed sitting, and they prayed behind him standing, so he gestured to them to sit.
So they sat. When he finished, he said:
"The imam is appointed only to be followed. When he bows, bow; when he rises, rise; and when he prays sitting, pray sitting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿādh ibn Jabal
used to pray the late evening prayer (ʿishāʾ) with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then return to his people and lead them in that same prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿādh used to pray with the Prophet ﷺ, then come and lead his people in prayer. One night he prayed the ʿishāʾ prayer with the Prophet ﷺ, then went to his people and led them, and began with Sūrat al-Baqarah. A man turned away, finished with the salām, then prayed alone and left. They said to him: "Have you become a hypocrite, so-and-so?" He said: "No, by Allah! I will certainly go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and tell him."

He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are people who tend camels used for watering; we work during the day. Muʿādh prayed ʿishāʾ with you, then came and began with Sūrat al-Baqarah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to Muʿādh and said:
"O Muʿādh, are you a cause of trial? Recite such-and-such, and recite such-and-such."
Sufyān said: I said to ʿAmr: Abū az-Zubayr narrated to us from Jābir that he said:
"Recite: By the sun and its brightness;
By the morning brightness;
By the night when it covers; and: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High."
ʿAmr said: Something like this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never prayed behind any imam whose prayer was lighter or more complete than that of the Prophet ﷺ,
and when he heard a child crying, he would shorten it, fearing that the child's mother would be put to trial.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Straighten your rows, for straightening the rows is part of establishing the prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a small enclosure in the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would go out at night and pray in it. He said: Men prayed with him, following his prayer, and they came to him every night, until one night the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not come out to them. They cleared their throats, raised their voices, and threw pebbles at his door. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to them angry and said:
"O people, you kept on doing what you did until I feared it would be made obligatory upon you. So pray in your homes, for the best prayer of a person is in his home, except the obligatory prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ about a man turning around in prayer. He said:
"It is a snatching by which Satan snatches away from the prayer of any of you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, we were in evil, then Allah brought good, and we are in it. Is there any evil after this good?" He said, "Yes."
I said, "Is there any good after that evil?" He said, "Yes."
I said, "Is there any evil after that good?" He said, "Yes."
I said, "How?" He said,
"There will be leaders after me who will not be guided by my guidance and will not follow my Sunnah. And among them will arise men whose hearts are the hearts of devils in the bodies of humans."
He said: I said, "What should I do, O Messenger of Allah, if I live to see that?" He said,
"You should listen and obey the ruler, even if he strikes your back and takes your wealth. Listen and obey."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar came to ʿAbdullāh ibn Muṭīʿ at the time of the events of al-Ḥarrah during the reign of Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah. Ibn Muṭīʿ said, "Put out a cushion for Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān." He said, "I have not come to sit. I have come to tell you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:"

"Whoever withdraws his hand from obedience will meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection with no proof for himself, and whoever dies without a pledge of allegiance on his neck dies a death of pre-Islamic ignorance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he came to Ibn Muṭīʿ.
Then he mentioned from the Prophet ﷺ something similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And a man,
whom he named, all of them from Ziyād ibn ʿIlāqah, from ʿArfajah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it, except that in the narrations of all of them it says, "then kill him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever comes to you while your affair is united under one man, wanting to split your ranks or divide your community, kill him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When allegiance is pledged to two caliphs, kill the latter of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was asked whether the Prophet ﷺ took a pledge of allegiance at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah. He said, "No, but he prayed there. And he did not take a pledge under any tree except the tree at al-Ḥudaybiyah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Goodness is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Were it not that it would be hard on my community, I would love never to stay behind any expeditionary force." Similar to their narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was beside the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a man said, "I do not mind if I do no deed after Islam other than giving water to the pilgrims."
Another said, "I do not mind if I do no deed after Islam other than maintaining the Sacred Mosque."
Another said, "Jihad in the cause of Allah is better than what you have said."

ʿUmar rebuked them and said, "Do not raise your voices by the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ" — and it was the day of Friday — "but when I have prayed the Friday prayer, I will go in and ask his ruling on what you disagreed about."

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {Have you made the giving of water to pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in Allah and the Last Day...} the verse to its end.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Each of them said: Shuraḥbīl ibn
Sharīk narrated to me, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥubulī,
that he heard Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, exactly the same as it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, one of them adding to the other: that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was on the pulpit and said, "What do you think if I strike with my sword..."
with the meaning of the hadith of al-Maqburī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every sin of the martyr is forgiven except debt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a expedition to Banū Liḥyān, who were from Hudhayl, and said:
"Let one of every two men set out, and the reward is shared between them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Banū al-Nabīt came to the Prophet ﷺ. [Another chain:] And Aḥmad ibn Janāb al-Miṣṣīṣī narrated to us, ʿĪsā, meaning Ibn Yūnus, narrated to us, from Zakariyyāʾ, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ, who said: A man from Banū al-Nabīt, a clan of the Anṣār, came and said, "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are His servant and Messenger."
Then he advanced and fought until he was killed. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"He did little and was rewarded much."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Suhayl, "ʿAmr narrated to us from al-Qaʿqāʿ, from your father,"
and he said—I had hoped it would spare me from [naming] a man—

he said, "I heard it from the one from whom my father heard it; he was a friend of his in Syria." Then Sufyān narrated to us from Suhayl, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd, from Tamīm ad-Dārī, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The religion is sincere advice."
We said, "For whom?" He said:
"For Allah, for His Book, for His Messenger, and for the leaders of the Muslims and their common folk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Before the Hour there will be trials like pieces of a dark night, in which a man will wake as a believer and evening as a disbeliever, and will evening as a believer and wake as a disbeliever. The one sitting during them is better than the one standing, the one standing is better than the one walking, and the one walking is better than the one running. So break your bows, cut your bowstrings, and strike stones with your swords. And if someone enters upon any of you, let him be like the better of the two sons of Ādam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw a man who had not washed his heels, and he said:
"Woe to the heels from the Fire!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he came to the graveyard and greeted its inhabitants, saying:
"Peace be upon you, abode of believing people. And we, if Allah the Exalted wills, will be joining you." Then he said:
"I wish that we had seen our brothers."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, are we not your brothers?" He said:
"You are my Companions, and our brothers are those who will come after me, and I will precede you to the Basin."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize those of your nation who have not yet come?" He said:
"Do you not see that if a man had horses with white foreheads and white legs among horses that were pure black, would he not recognize them?" They said, "Yes." He said:
"They will come on the Day of Resurrection with bright faces and limbs from the traces of ablution." He said:
"I will precede them to the Basin."
Then he said, "Beware! Some men will be driven away from my Basin as a stray camel is driven away. I will call to them, 'Come here!'
It will be said, 'They changed [things] after you, and they kept turning back on their heels.'
So I will say, 'Away with them! Away with them!'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the killing of dogs, then said:
"What is the matter with them and with dogs?"
He said: and he permitted [keeping] a hunting dog and a sheepdog, and he said:
"When a dog licks a vessel, wash it seven times and scour it the eighth time with earth."
Abū Hurayrah differed with him and said: one of them with earth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A man must not look at the nakedness of another man, and a woman must not look at the nakedness of another woman. A man must not lie with another man under a single garment, and a woman must not lie with another woman under a single garment."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was urinating and greeted him, but he did not return the greeting until he had performed ablution. Then he apologized to him and said:
"I disliked to mention Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, except in a state of purity." Or he said, "in a state of cleanliness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ met him while he was in a state of major impurity. He said: I slipped away, that is, I withdrew, and I bathed, then came back, and he said:
"Where were you?" or "Where did you go?"
I said, "I was in a state of major impurity." He said:
"Indeed, a Muslim does not become impure."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father heard me
while I was in prayer, saying:
"Bismillāh ir-Raḥmān ir-Raḥīm." He said to me, "My son, an innovation! Beware of innovation!"
He said: I never saw any of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who disliked innovation in Islam more than him.
He said: I have prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, and with Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān, and I never heard any of them say it. So do not say it. When you pray, say:
"Al-ḥamdu lillāhi rabbil-ʿālamīn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yūsuf [reported] that Muʿāwiyah

led them in prayer and stood up [for an extra rak'ah] when he should have sat. The people said "Subḥānallāh," but he continued standing. Then, after completing the prayer, he performed two prostrations while sitting. Afterwards he sat on the pulpit and said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever forgets something of his prayer, let him perform two prostrations like these two.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ was in the two rak'ahs in which the prayer ended, he would draw his left foot back, sit on his side in the tawarruk position, and then give the salām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raise his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. And when he sat, he laid down his left foot and set up his right, placed his left hand on his left thigh and his right hand on his right thigh, closed two fingers, the middle finger and the thumb, and pointed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw the Prophet ﷺ sit in the prayer; he spread out his left foot, placed his forearms on his thighs, and pointed with his index finger, supplicating with it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat for the tashahhud, he would place his left palm on his left thigh and point with his index finger, his gaze not going beyond his pointing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed, Allah has angels who roam the earth and convey to me the greetings of peace from my Ummah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sulaymān, the freed slave of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, came to us in the time of al-Ḥajjāj and narrated to us from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came one day with joy visible on his face. We said, "We see joy in your face." He said:

"The angel came to me and said, 'O Muḥammad, your Lord says: Does it not please you that no one sends blessings upon you except that I send blessings upon him ten times, and no one greets you with peace except that I greet him with peace ten times?'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Zayd ibn Khārijah, and he said, "I asked
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
'Send blessings upon me and strive in supplication, and say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad and upon the family of Muḥammad.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir led us in a prayer which he kept brief. Some of the people said to him, "You have made the prayer light," or, "You have made it brief."

He said, "Even so, I made supplications in it that I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." When he got up, a man from the people followed him, and he was Ubayy, though he referred to himself indirectly, and asked him about the supplication. Then he came and informed the people of it:

"O Allah, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, keep me alive as long as You know life to be better for me, and cause me to die when You know death to be better for me. O Allah, I ask You for fear of You in the unseen and the seen; I ask You for the word of truth in contentment and anger; I ask You for moderation in poverty and wealth; I ask You for bliss that never ends; I ask You for a comfort of the eye that never ceases; I ask You for contentment after the decree; I ask You for the coolness of life after death; I ask You for the delight of looking upon Your Face and a longing to meet You, without any harmful hardship or misleading trial. O Allah, adorn us with the adornment of faith and make us guides who are rightly guided."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say in his prayer after the tashahhud:
"The best speech is the speech of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muḥammad ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw a man praying and not doing it fully. Ḥudhayfah said to him, "How long have you been praying this prayer?" He said, "For forty years."

He said, "You have not prayed for forty years, and if you died while praying this prayer, you would die upon other than the natural way (fiṭrah) of Muḥammad ﷺ." Then he said, "A man may keep the prayer light, yet complete it and perform it well."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar about the prayer of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said, "He would say 'Allāhu akbar' whenever he went down, and 'Allāhu akbar' whenever he rose up. Then he would say:
'Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah,' to his right, and 'Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah,' to his left."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat in a gathering or prayed, he would speak certain words. ʿĀʾishah asked him about those words, and he said:

"If one speaks good, they will be a seal upon it until the Day of Resurrection, and if one speaks otherwise, they will be an expiation for him: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise; I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Sulaym
took a dagger on the day of Ḥunayn, and kept it with her. Abū Ṭalḥah saw her and said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is Umm Sulaym, and she has a dagger with her." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her,
"What is this dagger?"
She said, "I took it so that if any of the polytheists comes near me, I will rip open his belly with it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to laugh. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, kill those of the freed Meccans (aṭ-ṭulaqāʾ) after us, who were routed before you."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"O Umm Sulaym, Allah has sufficed and has done well."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Najdah
wrote to Ibn ʿAbbās asking him about several matters.
[This is] like the hadith of Sulaymān ibn Bilāl, except that in the hadith of Ḥātim,
[it says]: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not kill children, so do not kill children, unless you know what al-Khiḍr knew about the boy whom he killed."
And Isḥāq added in his narration from Ḥātim: "and the believer is distinguished, so that you kill the disbeliever and leave the believer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with Ibn ʿAbbās when he read his letter and when he wrote his reply. Ibn ʿAbbās said, "By Allah, were it not that I wish to turn him away from an evil in which he is falling, I would not have written to him, nor [done him] any favor." He wrote to him: "You asked about the share of the near relatives which Allah mentioned, who they are. We used to think that the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were us, but our people refused that for us. You asked about the orphan, when his orphanhood ends: when he reaches the age of marriage and sound judgment is perceived in him, and his property is handed over to him, then his orphanhood has ended. You asked whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to kill any of the children of the polytheists: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not kill any of them, and so you should not kill any of them, unless you know about them what al-Khiḍr knew about the boy when he killed him. And you asked about the woman and the slave, whether they had a fixed share when they were present at the fighting: they had no fixed share, except that they would be given something from the spoils of the people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He mentioned part of the hadith, but did not complete the account as completely as those whose narrations we have mentioned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I took part in nineteen military expeditions with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Jābir said: I did not take part in Badr or Uḥud, as my father prevented me. But when ʿAbdullāh was killed on the day of Uḥud, I never stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in any expedition.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on nineteen military expeditions and fought in eight of them.
Abū Bakr did not say "of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"People are followers of Quraysh in good and in evil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The affairs of the people will continue to go on well as long as twelve men rule over them."
Then the Prophet ﷺ said a word that I could not hear, so I asked my father, "What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say?" He said,
"All of them are from Quraysh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abū Mūsā and Muʿādh ibn Jabal to Yemen.
He said: He sent each of them to a separate district, and Yemen had two districts. Then he said:
"Make things easy and do not make them difficult,
give glad tidings and do not drive people away."
Each of them then set off to his work.
Whenever either of them traveled in his land and was near his companion, he would renew his acquaintance with him and greet him with salām.
So Muʿādh traveled in his land near his companion Abū Mūsā,
and he came riding on his mule until he reached him,
and there he was, sitting,
with people gathered around him,
and beside him was a man whose hands were tied to his neck. Muʿādh said to him: O ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays,
who is this? He said: This is a man who disbelieved after having accepted Islam.
Muʿādh said: I will not dismount until he is killed.
He said: He was only brought for that. So dismount.
He said: I will not dismount until he is killed. So he ordered it, and the man was killed. Then he dismounted and said: O ʿAbdullāh,
how do you recite the Qur'an? He said: I recite it little by little, in portions.
He said: And how do you recite, O Muʿādh? He said: I sleep at the beginning of the night, then I rise after having had my share of sleep,
and I recite what Allah has decreed for me,
and I hope for reward for my sleep just as I hope for reward for my standing in prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent his grandfather Abū Mūsā
and Muʿādh to Yemen, and he said:
"Make things easy and do not make them difficult,
give glad tidings and do not drive people away, and cooperate with each other."
Abū Mūsā said: O Prophet of Allah,
in our land there is a drink made from barley, called mizr,
and a drink made from honey, called bitʿ. He said:
"Every intoxicant is forbidden."
The two set off, and Muʿādh said to Abū Mūsā: How do you recite the Qur'an? He said: Standing, sitting, and on my mount, and I recite it little by little.
He said: As for me, I sleep and then I rise,
and I hope for reward for my sleep just as I hope for reward for my standing in prayer. He pitched a tent, and they began visiting one another.
Muʿādh visited Abū Mūsā,
and there was a man bound in fetters.
He said: What is this? Abū Mūsā said: A Jew who accepted Islam and then apostatized.
Muʿādh said: I will strike off his neck.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Muʿādh, may Allah be pleased with him, came to Yemen, he led them in the dawn prayer and recited: {And Allah took Abraham as a close friend.} A man from the people said: The eye of Abraham's mother has indeed been cooled.
Muʿādh added, from Shuʿbah, from Ḥabīb, from Saʿīd, from ʿAmr: The Prophet ﷺ sent Muʿādh to Yemen,
and in the dawn prayer Muʿādh recited Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. When he said {And Allah took Abraham as a close friend}, a man behind him said: The eye of Abraham's mother has been cooled.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us to Yemen with Khālid ibn al-Walīd.
He said: Then after that he sent ʿAlī in his place and said: Tell the companions of Khālid,
whoever of them wishes to stay on with you, let him stay on,
and whoever wishes, let him return.
I was among those who stayed on with him,
and he said: I obtained several ounces of silver.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent ʿAlī to Khālid to collect the fifth of the spoils, and I used to dislike ʿAlī, and he had bathed.
I said to Khālid: Do you not see this? When we came to the Prophet ﷺ, I mentioned that to him, and he said:
"O Buraydah, do you dislike ʿAlī?" I said: Yes. He said:
"Do not dislike him, for he has a greater share than that in the fifth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAṭāʾ said: Jābir said: The Prophet ﷺ commanded ʿAlī to remain in his state of iḥrām.
Muḥammad ibn Bakr added, from Ibn Jurayj,
ʿAṭāʾ said: Jābir said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, arrived from his collection duty,
and the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"What did you declare your intention for, O ʿAlī?"
He said: For what the Prophet ﷺ declared. He said:
"Then offer a sacrificial animal and remain in iḥrām as you are."
He said: And ʿAlī offered a sacrificial animal on his behalf.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was mentioned to Ibn ʿUmar that Anas had narrated to them that the Prophet ﷺ declared intention for ʿUmrah and Hajj together.
He said: The Prophet ﷺ declared intention for Hajj,
and we declared it with him.
When we arrived in Makkah, he said:
"Whoever has no sacrificial animal with him, let him make it an ʿUmrah."
The Prophet ﷺ had a sacrificial animal with him,
and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib came to us from Yemen for Hajj, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"What did you declare your intention for? Your family is with us."
He said: I declared it for what the Prophet ﷺ declared. He said: "Then remain in iḥrām,
for we have a sacrificial animal with us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd was wounded in the forearm vein (akḥal) on the day of the Trench,
so the Prophet ﷺ pitched a tent for him in the mosque so that he could visit him from nearby.
Then, while a tent of Banū Ghifār was also in the mosque, they were alarmed only by blood flowing toward them, and they said, "O people of the tent,
what is this that is coming to us from your direction?" And there was Saʿd, his wound streaming blood; and he died in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to fix the ʿanazah in the ground (Abū Bakr said: "plant") and pray facing it.
Ibn Abī Shaybah added: ʿUbaydullāh said, "It is the short spear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: "ʿUmar was mistaken. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said:
'Do not deliberately time your prayer for the rising of the sun or its setting, for it rises between the two horns of Satan.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar called the call to prayer at Dajnān, then called out: "Pray in your lodgings." He said: then he narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he used to command the caller, who would call for prayer and then call out:
"Pray in your lodgings,"
on a cold night and on a rainy night during travel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said that Umm al-Faḍl bint al-Ḥārith heard him while he was

reciting {By those sent forth in succession}. She said, "My son, by your recitation of this sūrah you have reminded me that it was the last thing I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite in the Maghrib prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zayd ibn Thābit said to me: "Why do I see you reciting the short sūrahs of the Mufaṣṣal in the Maghrib prayer, when I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite the longer of the two long ones in Maghrib?" I said, "What is the longer of the two long ones?" He said, "Al-Aʿrāf, and the other is al-Anʿām."
He said: I asked Ibn Abī Mulaykah, and he told me on his own opinion: "Al-Māʾidah and al-Aʿrāf."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakrah
came while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was bowing, so he bowed before reaching the row, then walked to the row. When the Prophet ﷺ finished his prayer, he said:
"Which of you bowed before reaching the row and then walked to the row?"
Abū Bakrah said, "I did." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"May Allah increase you in eagerness, but do not repeat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar never rejected anyone's bequest.
Ibn Sīrīn said that the thing he liked most regarding an orphan's property was that the orphan's well-wishers and guardians gather and consider what is best for him.
And whenever Ṭāwūs was asked about any matter concerning orphans, he would recite: {And Allah knows the one who causes corruption from the one who sets things right}.
And ʿAṭāʾ said, regarding orphans, both young and old: The guardian may spend on each person according to his need from his share.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ gave orders for the building of the mosque, and he said:
"O Banū al-Najjār, name me a price for this garden of yours." They said: "No,
by Allah, we do not seek its price except from Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar,
may Allah be pleased with him, acquired some property at Khaybar,
so he came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him. He said:
"If you wish, you may give it as charity."
So he gave it as charity for the poor, the needy, the relatives, and the guest.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar,
stipulated in his endowment that its administrator may eat from it, and may feed his friend, provided he does not accumulate wealth from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, was besieged, he looked down upon them and said: "I adjure you by Allah, and I adjure only the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ:
Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Whoever digs the well of Rūmah will have Paradise'? So I dug it.
Do you not know that he said:
'Whoever equips the army of hardship will have Paradise'? So I equipped them."
He said: So they affirmed what he said.
And ʿUmar said in his endowment: There is no blame on the one who administers it if he eats from it.
The administrator may be the endower or someone else, so it is permissible for all.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Last night I saw two men who came to me and took me up a tree,
and they brought me into a house that was more beautiful and more excellent,
than any I had ever seen. They said: 'As for this house, it is the house of the martyrs.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said] to him: "I asked you how your fighting with him went, and you claimed that war alternates between victory and defeat,
and so it is with the messengers: they are tested, and then the final outcome is theirs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Anas
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Anas
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the written sheets were copied into the codices,
I found one verse missing from Sūrat al-Aḥzāb,
which I used to hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite.
I did not find it except with Khuzaymah ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī, whose testimony the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had made equal to the testimony of two men,
and it is His saying: {Among the believers are men who were true to what they pledged to Allah}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man covered in iron armor came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I fight or accept Islam?" He said:
"Accept Islam, then fight."
So he accepted Islam, then fought, and was killed.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He did little, yet he was rewarded greatly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people drank wine in the morning on the day of Uḥud,
and then were killed as martyrs.
Sufyān was asked: "Was that at the end of that day?" He said: "That is not in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Know that Paradise is beneath the shade of swords."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While he was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with the people, returning from Ḥunayn, some Bedouins clung to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him [for things] until they forced him toward a samurah tree, and it snatched away his cloak.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped and said: "Give me back my cloak.
If the number of these thorny trees were camels, I would divide them among you,
and then you would not find me stingy, nor a liar, nor a coward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I accompanied Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh, Saʿd, al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, may Allah be pleased with them, and I did not hear any,
of them narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
except that I heard Ṭalḥah narrate about the day of Uḥud.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ṭalḥah did not fast during the time of the Prophet ﷺ because of military campaigns,
but after the Prophet ﷺ passed away, I never saw him not fasting,
except on the day of Fiṭr or Aḍḥā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he mentioned the day of al-Yamāmah. He said: Anas came to Thābit ibn Qays, who had uncovered his thighs and was applying embalming perfume. He said: "Uncle, what keeps you from coming?" He said: "Now, nephew." And he continued applying the perfume,
meaning ḥanūṭ,
then he came and sat down.
In the hadith he mentioned that the people were giving way,
so he said: "Like this, away from our faces, until we strike the enemy,
this is not how we used to do it with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
How evil is what you have accustomed your opponents to!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had a horse in our garden called al-Laḥīf.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The she-camel of the Prophet ﷺ was called al-ʿAḍbāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some of us from the people of Basra gathered and went to Anas ibn Mālik, and we took Thābit along with us to ask him on our behalf about the hadith of intercession.
He was in his palace, and we found him praying the forenoon prayer, so we asked permission to enter,

and he permitted us while he was sitting on his bed. We said to Thābit, "Do not ask him about anything before the hadith of intercession." So he said, "O Abū Ḥamzah, these are your brothers from the people of Basra. They have come to ask you about the hadith of intercession."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qutaybah said: It is in my book from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He is not one of us who does not chant the Qurʾān beautifully."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is a Kūfan whose name is Salmān, the freed slave of ʿAzzah al-Ashjaʿiyyah, from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his uncle:
"Say: There is no god but Allah, and I will testify for you with it on the Day of Resurrection."
He said: "Were it not that the Quraysh would reproach me with it, saying that only anxiety drove me to it, I would have delighted your eyes with it." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
"Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon him while he was dying and I wept. He said, "Wait! Why are you weeping? By Allah, if I am asked to testify, I will testify for you; if I am permitted to intercede, I will intercede for you; and if I am able, I will benefit you." Then he said, "By Allah, there is no hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that contains good for you except that I have narrated it to you, apart from one hadith, and I will narrate it to you today now that my life is being encompassed. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, Allah has forbidden the Fire to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He has tasted the sweetness of faith who is pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Qutaybah and Ibn
Ḥujr, from Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar,
Ibn Ayyūb said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
he said: Al-ʿAlāʾ informed me, from his father,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Faith is Yemeni, and disbelief comes from the direction of the east. Tranquility is among the people of sheep, while pride and showing off are among the loud herdsmen, the people of horses and camel-hair tents."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jarīr ibn ʿAbdullāh used to narrate from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"When a slave runs away, no prayer of his is accepted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Rain fell on the people during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:

"Have you not heard what your Lord said last night? He said: I did not bestow any blessing upon My servants except that a group of them became disbelievers in it, saying, 'We were given rain by such-and-such a star.' As for the one who believed in Me and praised Me for the rain I gave, he is the one who believes in Me and disbelieves in the star. And whoever said, 'We were given rain by such-and-such a star,' he is the one who disbelieved in Me and believed in the star."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"No one who believes in Allah and the Last Day will hate the Anṣār."
This is a good and sound hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When the son of Adam recites the verse of prostration and prostrates, Satan withdraws, weeping, and says: 'Woe to him!' (in the narration of Abū Kurayb: 'Woe to me!') 'The son of Adam was commanded to prostrate and he prostrated, so Paradise is for him; I was commanded to prostrate and I refused, so the Fire is for me.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Qutaybah and Ibn
Ḥujr, all from Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar,
Ibn Ayyūb said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
he said: Al-ʿAlāʾ informed me, from his father,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a heap of food, put his hand into it, and his fingers touched dampness. He said:
"What is this, O owner of the food?"
He said, "The rain fell on it, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"Why did you not put it on top of the food so that people could see it? Whoever cheats is not of me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Khaybar, a group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ came and said, "So-and-so is a martyr, so-and-so is a martyr," until they passed by a man and said, "So-and-so is a martyr."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Never! I saw him in the Fire because of a cloak that he stole from the spoils," or he said, "a robe."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O son of al-Khaṭṭāb, go and announce to the people that only the believers will enter Paradise."
He said: So I went out and announced:
"Indeed, only the believers will enter Paradise!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qutaybah and Ibn
Ḥujr said—Ibn Ayyūb said: Ismāʿīl ibn
Jaʿfar narrated to us: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed me—
he is the son of Maʿmar ibn Ḥazm al-Anṣārī, Abū Ṭuwālah—that Abū Yūnus,
the freed slave of ʿĀʾishah, informed him from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that a man

came to the Prophet ﷺ asking for a ruling, while she was listening from behind the door. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, the time of prayer comes upon me while I am in a state of major impurity; may I fast?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The time of prayer also comes upon me while I am in a state of major impurity, and I fast."
The man said: "You are not like us, O Messenger of Allah; Allah has forgiven you your past and future sins." He said:
"By Allah, I hope to be the most fearful of Allah among you, and the most knowledgeable of you about what I should guard against."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to go on military expeditions with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Ramadan; some of us were fasting and some were not, and the one fasting did not hold it against the one not fasting, nor did the one not fasting hold it against the one fasting. They held that whoever found strength and fasted, that was good, and whoever found weakness and broke the fast, that was also good.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī while he was giving rulings to the people, who were crowding around him. I waited until he was alone, and when he was, I asked him about fasting in Ramadan while travelling. He said: We set out with the Prophet ﷺ in Ramadan in the year of the Conquest. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted and we fasted, until he reached one of the stopping places, and he said:
"You have come close to your enemy, and breaking the fast will make you stronger."
So in the morning some of us were fasting and some were not. He said: Then we travelled on and stopped at a stopping place, and he said:
"You will meet your enemy in the morning, and breaking the fast will make you stronger, so break your fast."
So it was a firm command from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Abū Saʿīd said: Yet I have seen myself fasting with the Prophet ﷺ both before that and after that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: may Allah be pleased with him—that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I find in myself the strength to fast while travelling; is there any blame on me?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is a concession from Allah; whoever takes it, that is good, and whoever prefers to fast, there is no blame on him."
Hārūn said in his narration: "It is a concession."
He did not mention "from Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: about the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ:
"This is a day which the people of the Jāhiliyyah used to fast. Whoever wishes to fast it, let him fast it, and whoever wishes to leave it, let him leave it."
And ʿAbdullāh, may Allah be pleased with him, did not fast it unless it coincided with his [regular] fasting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of us would break her fast in Ramadan and be unable to make it up until Shaʿbān came. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not fast in any month as much as he fasted in Shaʿbān; he would fast all of it except a little—indeed, he would fast all of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah: "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray the forenoon prayer?" She said: "No, except when he came back from an absence."

I asked: "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have a particular month that he fasted, other than Ramadan?" She said: "By Allah, he never fasted a particular month other than Ramadan until he passed away, and he never stopped fasting until he had fasted some of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Fast one day of the month, and you will have the reward of the rest."
I said: "I am able to do more than that." He said:
"Then fast two days, and you will have the reward of the rest."
I said: "I am able to do more than that." He said:
"Then fast three days, and you will have the reward of the rest."
I said: "I am able to do more than that." He said:
"Fast four days, and you will have the reward of the rest."
I said: "I am able to do more than that."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best fasting is the fasting of Dāwūd: he would fast one day and break his fast the next."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We observed iʿtikāf with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the middle ten days of Ramadan, and he said:
"I was shown the Night of Qadr, but I was made to forget it. So seek it in the last ten nights, on the odd-numbered ones."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not spy on one another, do not search for one another's faults, and do not outbid one another to deceive; and be, O servants of Allah, brothers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: Where are those who loved one another for the sake of My majesty? Today I will shade them in My shade, on a day when there is no shade but My shade."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ:

"A man visited a brother of his in another town, so Allah stationed an angel on his path. When he came upon him, the angel said: Where do you intend to go? He said: I intend to visit a brother of mine in this town.
The angel said: Do you owe him some favor that you are looking after? He said: No, except that I love him for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
The angel said: I am a messenger to you from Allah, [to tell you] that Allah loves you as you loved him for His sake."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say on the Day of Resurrection: O son of Adam, I was ill and you did not visit Me.
He will say: My Lord, how could I visit You when You are the Lord of the worlds?

He will say: Did you not know that My servant so-and-so was ill and you did not visit him? Did you not know that had you visited him, you would have found Me with him? O son of Adam, I asked you for food and you did not feed Me.
He will say: My Lord, how could I feed You when You are the Lord of the worlds?

He will say: Did you not know that My servant so-and-so asked you for food and you did not feed him? Did you not know that had you fed him, you would have found that with Me? O son of Adam, I asked you for water and you did not give Me to drink.

He will say: My Lord, how could I give You to drink when You are the Lord of the worlds? He will say: My servant so-and-so asked you for water and you did not give him to drink. Had you given him to drink, you would have found that with Me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of transmission of Jarīr,
the same as his report, except that in the report of Sufyān [it says]:
"And there has been assigned to him his companion from among the jinn and his companion from among the angels."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon Umm al-Sāʾib or Umm al-Musayyib and said:
"What is the matter with you, O Umm al-Sāʾib, or O Umm al-Musayyib, that you are shivering?"
She said: It is the fever, may Allah not bless it. He said:
"Do not curse the fever, for it takes away the sins of the children of Adam just as the bellows remove the impurities of iron."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, among what he reported from Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, that He said:

"O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. O My servants, all of you are astray except those whom I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I have fed, so ask Me for food and I will feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except those whom I have clothed, so ask Me for clothing and I will clothe you. O My servants, you sin by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me and I will forgive you. O My servants, you will never reach harming Me so as to harm Me, and you will never reach benefiting Me so as to benefit Me. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans of you and the jinn of you, were all as pious as the most pious heart of any one man among you, that would not add anything to My kingdom. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans of you and the jinn of you, were all as wicked as the most wicked heart of any one man, that would not decrease anything from My kingdom. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans of you and the jinn of you, were to stand on one plain and ask Me, and I gave every person what he asked, that would not decrease what I have except as a needle decreases [the sea] when it is put into it. O My servants, it is only your deeds that I record for you and then repay you for them. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds other than that, let him blame no one but himself."
Saʿīd said: When Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī narrated this hadith, he would kneel on his knees.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, among what he reported from his Lord, the Blessed and Exalted:
"I have forbidden injustice for Myself and for My servants, so do not wrong one another."
And he narrated the hadith similarly. The hadith of Abū Idrīs that we mentioned is more complete than this one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:
"Indeed gentleness is not found in anything except that it beautifies it, and it is not removed from anything except that it disfigures it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥuṣayn said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on one of his journeys, a woman of the Anṣār was on a she-camel. She became annoyed and cursed it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard that and said:
"Take what is on her and leave her, for she is cursed."
ʿImrān said: It is as if I see her now walking among the people, and no one pays any attention to her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: in his sitting place in the mosque. When the prayer came due, he stood, performed ablution, and prayed, then returned to his sitting place. When the ʿAṣr prayer came due, he stood, performed ablution, and prayed, then returned to his sitting place. When the Maghrib prayer came due, he stood, performed ablution, and prayed, then returned to his sitting place. So I said, "May Allah set you right. Is ablution at every prayer obligatory or a sunnah?" He said, "Did you notice this about me and about him?" I said, "Yes."
He said, "No. If I had performed ablution for the dawn prayer, I could pray all the prayers with it as long as I did not break it. But I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever performs ablution while already in a state of purity will have ten good deeds.'"
And I was only eager for the good deeds.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw as-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd smelling his garment, so I said, "Why is that?" He said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'There is no ablution [required] except for a smell or a sound.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about the ponds between Makkah and Madinah, which are visited by predators, dogs, and donkeys, and about purification from them. He said:
"They have what they carry in their bellies, and we have what remains; it is purifying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to a pool of water, and in it was the carcass of a donkey.
He said: We held back from it until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached us, and he said:
"Water is not made impure by anything."
So we drew water, quenched our thirst, and carried [water] with us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Water is not made impure by anything, except what overpowers its smell, its taste, and its color."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin entered the mosque while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting, and said, "O Allah, forgive me and Muḥammad, and do not forgive anyone else along with us."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and said:
"You have restricted something vast."
Then he turned away, and when he was in a corner of the mosque, he spread his legs and urinated.
After he had come to understand, the Bedouin said: He then got up and came to me—may my father and mother be ransomed for him—
he neither rebuked nor insulted [me]. He said:
"This mosque is not for urinating in; it was built only for the remembrance of Allah and for prayer."
Then he ordered a bucket of water, and it was poured over the urine.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Allah, have mercy on me and Muḥammad, and do not share your mercy with anyone else along with us." He said:
"You have restricted something vast, woe to you—or: alas for you."
He said: Then he spread his legs and urinated, and the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said, "Stop!"
But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Leave him."
Then he called for a bucket of water and it was poured over it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, we go to the mosque and walk over impure parts of the road."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Some parts of the ground purify other parts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us with water dripping from his head and led us in prayer in a single garment, wrapped around himself with its two ends crossed. When he finished, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said, "O Messenger of Allah, you lead us in prayer in a single garment?" He said:
"Yes, I pray in it and I was intimate in it."
That is, he had had marital relations in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ whether he may pray in the garment in which he comes to his wife. He said:
"Yes, unless he sees something on it, in which case he should wash it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw Saʿd ibn Mālik wiping over his leather socks, and said, "You really do that!" So we gathered with ʿUmar, and Saʿd said to ʿUmar, "Give my nephew a ruling on wiping over the leather socks."
ʿUmar said, "We used to wipe over our leather socks when we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we saw no harm in that."
Ibn ʿUmar said, "Even if he has come from relieving himself?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and he said:
"Is there any water?"
Then he performed ablution and wiped over his leather socks, then rejoined the army and led them in prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a man who was performing ablution and washing his leather socks. He motioned with his hand as though pushing him away, and said:
"I was only commanded to wipe."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ [showed] with his hand like this, from the tips of the fingers to the base of the shin, and he drew lines with his fingers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set three [days] for the traveler; and had the questioner continued with his question, he would have made it five.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he mentioned,
another [narrator] before him, from ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah,
from Abū az-Zubayr,
from Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh,

who said: On the day of Uhud, when the people turned back, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at one side with twelve men of the Anṣār, among them Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydullāh. The polytheists caught up with them, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned and said, "Who will [face] the enemy?"
Ṭalḥah said, "I will."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Stay where you are."
A man of the Anṣār said, "I will, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "You."
So he fought until he was killed. Then [the Prophet ﷺ] turned and saw the polytheists, and said, "Who will [face] the enemy?"
Ṭalḥah said, "I will." He said, "Stay where you are."
A man of the Anṣār said, "I will." He said, "You."

So he fought until he was killed. He kept saying this, and a man of the Anṣār would go out to them and fight as fiercely as those before him until he was killed, until only the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydullāh remained. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Who will [face] the enemy?"
Ṭalḥah said, "I will."
So Ṭalḥah fought the fight of the eleven, until his hand was struck and his fingers were cut off, and he said, "Ḥass!"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Had you said 'Bismillāh,' the angels would have lifted you up while the people looked on."
Then Allah drove the polytheists back.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"There is no soul among people, a Muslim soul that its Lord takes, that would love to return to you even if it were given the world and all that is in it, except the martyr."
Ibn Abī ʿUmayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"For me to be killed in the cause of Allah is more beloved to me than to have [all] the people of the tents and the houses."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"A man of the people of Paradise will be brought, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'O son of Adam, how did you find your dwelling?' He will say: 'O Lord, the best dwelling.'
He will say: 'Ask and wish.' He will say: 'I ask You to return me to the world so that I may be killed in Your cause ten times,' because of what he sees of the virtue of martyrdom."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"There are five; whoever dies by any of them is a martyr: the one killed in the cause of Allah is a martyr, the one who drowns in the cause of Allah is a martyr, the one who dies of a stomach illness in the cause of Allah is a martyr, the one who dies of the plague in the cause of Allah is a martyr, and the woman who dies in childbirth in the cause of Allah is a martyr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The martyrs and those who died on their beds will dispute before our Lord concerning those who die of the plague. The martyrs will say: 'They are our brothers; they were killed as we were killed.'

And those who died on their beds will say: 'They are our brothers; they died on their beds as we died.' Our Lord will say: 'Look at their wounds. If their wounds resemble the wounds of those who were killed, then they are of them and with them.' And their wounds will be found to resemble their wounds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ promised us the expedition to India. If I live to see it, I will spend myself and my wealth in it. If I am killed, I will be among the best of the martyrs, and if I return, then I am Abū Hurayrah, the freed one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Two groups of my Ummah Allah has protected from the Fire: a group that will fight in India, and a group that will be with ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, peace be upon them both."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He thought that he had
superiority over those below him among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, so the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said,
"Allah only grants victory to this Ummah through its weak ones, through their supplication, their prayer, and their sincerity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You must listen and obey, in your hardship and your ease, in what you like and what you dislike, and even when others are given preference over you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:

"Rulers will be appointed over you; you will recognize some of what they do and disapprove of some. Whoever dislikes it has been absolved, and whoever denounces it has been safe. But [the one at fault is] whoever approves and follows."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, should we not fight them?" He said:
"No, as long as they pray."
That is, whoever dislikes it in his heart and denounces it in his heart.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the women [pledging allegiance], she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never touched the hand of a woman, except that he would take her pledge; and when he had taken her pledge and she had given it to him, he said:
"Go, for I have accepted your pledge."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ, "What equals jihad in the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?" He said, "You are not able to do it."
The narrator said: They repeated the question to him two or three times, and each time he said, "You are not able to do it."
Then the third time he said:

"The likeness of the one who strives in the cause of Allah is like that of the one who fasts, stands in prayer, and is devoutly obedient to the verses of Allah, never slackening from fasting or prayer, until the one who strives in the cause of Allah, the Exalted, returns."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A morning or an evening journey in the cause of Allah is better than everything upon which the sun rises and sets."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Being killed in the cause of Allah expiates every sin."
Then Jibrīl said, "Except debt." And the Prophet ﷺ said, "Except debt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:

"Among the best livelihoods of people is a man who holds the reins of his horse in the cause of Allah, flying on its back whenever he hears a cry of alarm or a call of fear, flying to it, seeking killing and death in the places where it may be found; or a man with a small flock of sheep on the top of one of these mountain peaks or in the bottom of one of these valleys, who establishes prayer, gives zakāh, and worships his Lord until certainty [death] comes to him. He is of the people only in goodness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A disbeliever and the one who kills him will never be together in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Two things will not be together in the Fire: a Muslim who killed a disbeliever and then remained upright and sought to do what is right. And two things will not be together in the belly of a believer: dust in the cause of Allah and the heat of Hell. And two things will not be together in the heart of a servant: faith and envy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came with a she-camel that had a halter on it and said, "This is for the cause of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"For it you will have on the Day of Resurrection seven hundred she-camels, all of them with halters."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A young man
of Aslam said, "O Messenger of Allah, I want to go out for jihad, but I have no wealth with which to equip myself." He said:
"Go to so-and-so from the Anṣār, for he had equipped himself and then fell ill. Say to him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ greets you with peace, and tell him: Give me what you prepared."

He came to him and told him that, and the man said to his wife, "O so-and-so, give him what you prepared for me and do not withhold anything of it. By Allah, you will not withhold anything of it without Allah blessing it for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a expedition to Banū Liḥyān and said:
"Let one man out of every two go out."
Then he said to those who stayed behind:
"Whichever of you takes care of the family and property of the one who goes out in a good manner will have a reward equal to half the reward of the one who went out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the presence of the enemy, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The gates of Paradise are beneath the shades of swords."
A man of shabby appearance stood up and said, "O Abū Mūsā, did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say this?" He said, "Yes."
He said: So he returned to his companions and said, "I read you my greetings of peace."
Then he broke the scabbard of his sword and threw it away, walked with his sword toward the enemy, and fought with it until he was killed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever keeps guard for a day and a night in the cause of Allah will have a reward like that of fasting a month and standing in prayer through it. And whoever dies while keeping guard will have the same reward continue for him, his provision will continue to be granted to him, and he will be safe from the trial of the grave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān,

while still a young lad, during the governorship of Marwān, divorced the daughter of Saʿīd ibn Zayd, whose mother was the daughter of Qays, with a final (triple) divorce. Her maternal aunt Fāṭimah bint Qays sent word to her, instructing her to move out of the house of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr. Marwān heard of that and sent a message to the daughter of Saʿīd, ordering her to return to her dwelling, and he asked her what had driven her to move before completing her waiting period (ʿiddah) in her home until it ended. She sent word to him informing him that her aunt had ordered her to do so. Fāṭimah bint Qays claimed that she had been married to Abū ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ, and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib over Yemen, he went out with him and sent her a pronouncement of divorce, which was the last of her divorces, and he commanded al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām and ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah to provide her maintenance. She claimed that she sent word to al-Ḥārith and ʿAyyāsh asking for what her husband had ordered for her, and they said: By Allah, she has no maintenance from us unless she is pregnant, and she has no right to stay in our dwelling except with our permission. She claimed that she then came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he confirmed what the two men had said.
Fāṭimah said: Then where should I move, O Messenger of Allah? He said:
"Move to Ibn Umm Maktūm, the blind man whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, named in His Book."

Fāṭimah said: So I spent my waiting period with him. He was a man who had lost his sight, so I would put my clothes down in his presence, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her to Usāmah ibn Zayd. Marwān rejected that from her and said: I have not heard this ḥadīth from anyone before you, and I will adhere to the ruling on which we found the people. (Abridged.)
label: machine translation

He said: I cannot bear to be without her. He said: "Then enjoy her."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: Which women are best? He said:
"The one who pleases him when he looks at her, obeys him when he commands, and does not oppose him regarding herself or her wealth in a way he dislikes."
