segments_en: With this account he said: Ḥāṭib set out and wrote to the people of Makkah that Muḥammad ﷺ had marched toward them. And he said in it: She said, "I have no letter with me."
So we searched her but found no letter on her. Then ʿAlī said, "By the One by whom oaths are sworn, either you will bring out the letter or I will kill you." And he related the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that he be killed. He had been a spy for Abū Sufyān and was an ally of a man of the Anṣār. He passed by a circle of the Anṣār and said, "I am a Muslim."
A man of the Anṣār said, "O Messenger of Allah, he says that he is a Muslim."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Among you are men whom we entrust to their faith, and among them is Furāt ibn Ḥayyān."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ disliked raising the voice during fighting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, similar to that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ met the polytheists on the day of Ḥunayn and [the Muslims] gave way, he dismounted from his mule and went on foot.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was one of the companions of Abū Hurayrah, and he mentioned the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Uḥud the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed ʿAbdullāh ibn Jubayr over the archers—they were fifty men—and he said:

"If you see us being snatched away by the birds, do not leave this place of yours until I send for you; and if you see that we have defeated the enemy and trampled them, do not leave until I send for you."
He said: So Allah defeated them.

He said: By Allah, I saw the women hitching up their garments as they climbed the mountain. The companions of ʿAbdullāh ibn Jubayr said, "The spoils, people! The spoils! Your companions have prevailed, so what are you waiting for?" ʿAbdullāh ibn Jubayr said, "Have you forgotten what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to you?" They said, "By Allah, we will go to the people and take some of the spoils." So they went to them, but their faces were turned away and they came back defeated.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said on the day of Badr:
"When they come close to you, shoot them with arrows, and do not draw your swords until they are upon you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He—meaning ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah—stepped forward, followed by his son and his brother, and called out, "Who will duel?" Some young men of the Anṣār responded to him. He said, "Who are you?" They told him, and he said, "We have no need of you; we only wanted our cousins."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Get up, Ḥamzah! Get up, ʿAlī! Get up, ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith!"

Ḥamzah advanced on ʿUtbah, and I advanced on Shaybah. Between ʿUbaydah and al-Walīd two blows were exchanged, and each of them severely wounded the other. Then we turned on al-Walīd and killed him, and we carried ʿUbaydah away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
attended the Farewell Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He praised and extolled Allah, gave a reminder and an exhortation, and then said:
"Which day is the most sacred? Which day is the most sacred? Which day is the most sacred?"
He said: The people said, "The day of the Greater Hajj, O Messenger of Allah." He said:

"Your blood, your wealth, and your honor are sacred to you, like the sacredness of this day of yours, in this land of yours, in this month of yours. Truly, no offender commits an offense except against himself, and a father does not offend against his child, nor a child against his father. Truly, a Muslim is the brother of a Muslim, and nothing of his brother's is lawful to a Muslim except what he willingly gives. Truly, all usury of the Pre-Islamic Era is abolished. You have your capital: you do not wrong and you are not wronged. [This applies to all usury] except the usury owed to al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, for it is all abolished. Truly, all blood [vengeance] of the Pre-Islamic Era is abolished. The first of the bloodshed of the Pre-Islamic Era that I abolish is the blood of al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, who was being nursed among Banū Layth and whom Hudhayl killed. Truly, treat women well, for they are like captives with you; you do not own anything else of them beyond that, unless they commit a clear indecency. If they do, then forsake them in the beds and strike them in a manner that is not severe. If they obey you, then do not seek any way against them. Truly, you have a right over your women, and your women have a right over you. As for your right over your women, they must not allow anyone you dislike to tread on your bedding, nor admit into your homes anyone you dislike. And truly, their right over you is that you treat them well in their clothing and their food."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In his sermon in the year of the Farewell Hajj:
"A loan must be returned, a guarantor is liable, and a debt must be repaid."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ gave a boy the choice between his father and his mother, and said:
"O boy, this is your mother and this is your father."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Quraysh knocked out the tooth of a man from the Anṣār, so [the Anṣārī] appealed to Muʿāwiyah against him and said to Muʿāwiyah, "O Commander of the Faithful, this man knocked out my tooth."
Muʿāwiyah said, "We will satisfy you." But the other man kept pressing Muʿāwiyah, who grew weary of him, yet he was not satisfied. So Muʿāwiyah said to him, "It is your business with your opponent."
Abū al-Dardāʾ was sitting with him, and Abū al-Dardāʾ said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"No man is afflicted with an injury in his body and then gives it up as charity, except that Allah raises him one degree for it and removes one sin from him for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I had forbidden you from [keeping] the meat of sacrificial animals beyond three days, so that those with means could provide for those without means. Now eat as you wish, feed others, and store [it]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Mother of the Believers, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid the meat of sacrificial animals?" She said, "No, but few of the people used to offer sacrifice, so he wanted those who did not sacrifice to be fed. And we used to set aside the trotters and eat them ten days later."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade selling the spoils of war until they are divided, forbade having intercourse with pregnant women until they give birth to what is in their wombs, and forbade the meat of every predatory animal with fangs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever dies, with his soul having parted from his body, free of three things: hoarded wealth, misappropriation of war spoils, and debt, will enter Paradise."
Saʿīd said it thus: "hoarded wealth" (al-kanz). Abū ʿAwānah said in his narration: "arrogance" (al-kibr), and he did not mention Maʿdān in it. The narration of Saʿīd is more sound.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He] said to Kaʿb, "O Kaʿb ibn Murrah, narrate to us from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and be careful."
He said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah for rain." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands and said:
"O Allah, give us rain that is wholesome, fertile, abundant, widespread, swift, not delayed, beneficial, not harmful."
He said: They had not even gathered [to leave] before they were answered.
He said: Then they came to him and complained to him of the rain, saying, "O Messenger of Allah, the houses have collapsed." He said:
"O Allah, around us and not upon us."
He said: The clouds then began to break apart to the right and to the left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While he was on the pulpit, he said: I concealed from you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, because I disliked that you would disperse from me. Then it occurred to me to relate it to you, so that each man may choose for himself what he sees fit. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"A day of standing guard in the cause of Allah is better than a thousand days in any other place."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He heard Muʿāwiyah] delivering a sermon in Madinah—that is, upon a visit he made—on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and he said: "Where are your scholars, people of Madinah? I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say about this day:
'This is the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ. Allah has not prescribed its fasting for you, but I am fasting. Whoever among you wishes to fast, let him fast, and whoever wishes to break the fast, let him do so.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah and found the Jews fasting on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them:
"What is this day that you fast?"
They said: "This is a great day, on which Allah saved Moses and his people and drowned Pharaoh and his people. Moses fasted it in gratitude, so we fast it."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"We have more right to Moses, and are closer to him, than you."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted it and commanded that it be fasted.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to spend the last ten nights of Ramadan in seclusion in the mosque, and he would say:
"Seek the Night of Qadr in the last ten nights of Ramadan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It is narrated from] the wife of the Prophet ﷺ that she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to visit him while he was in iʿtikāf in the mosque during the last ten days of Ramadan. She spoke with him for a while in the evening, then got up to return home, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up with her to walk her back. When she reached the door of the mosque near the dwelling of Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, two men of the Anṣār passed by them and greeted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then went on. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them:
"Slow down; she is Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy."
They said: "Glory be to Allah, Messenger of Allah!" and this weighed heavily upon them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed, Satan runs in the son of Adam like the flowing of blood, and I feared that he might cast something into your hearts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "When we came to Madinah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a bond of brotherhood between me and Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ. Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ said: 'I am the wealthiest of the Anṣār,
so I will give you half of my wealth,
and look at whichever of my two wives you like, and I will give her up for you,
and when her waiting period is over, you may marry her.'
He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: 'I have no need of that.
Is there a market in which there is trade?' He said: 'The market of Qaynuqāʿ.'
He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān went out to it in the morning,
and came back with some dried cheese and ghee." He said: "Then he continued going out in the mornings,
and it was not long before ʿAbd al-Raḥmān came with a trace of yellow [perfume] on him,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Have you married?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'To whom?'
He said: 'A woman of the Anṣār.' He said: 'How much did you give as dowry?'
He said: 'The weight of a date-stone in gold,' or 'a date-stone of gold.'
So the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
'Hold a wedding feast, even if with a single sheep.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib about currency exchange,
and he said: "Ask Zayd ibn Arqam, for he is better than I and more knowledgeable."
So I asked Zayd, and he said: "Ask al-Barāʾ, for he is better than I and more knowledgeable." Then they both said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade [exchanging] silver for gold on credit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever is pleased to have his provision expanded for him,
and to have his lifespan extended, let him maintain his ties of kinship."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is better for one of you to gather a bundle of firewood, carry it on his back and sell it, than to ask a man who may either give him or refuse him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"The angels received the soul of a man from those before you. They said: 'Did you do any good?' He said: 'I used to instruct my servants to grant respite and to overlook [the debts of] the well-off.' He said: So they overlooked [his faults]."
And Abū Mālik reported from Ribʿī:
"I used to make things easy for the well-off and give respite to the one in hardship."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ made the charity of Fitr obligatory (or he said: of Ramadan) upon male and female, free and slave:
one ṣāʿ of dates or one ṣāʿ of barley.
Then the people made half a ṣāʿ of wheat equivalent to it.
Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) used to give dates.
Then the people of Madinah ran short of dates, so he gave barley.
Ibn ʿUmar used to give on behalf of the young and the old,
even on behalf of my sons.
And Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) used to give it to those who would accept it,
and they used to give it one or two days before the Fitr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Aḥmad ibn Ṣāliḥ said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Yūnus informed me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:
"Tomorrow, if Allah wills, we will camp at Khayf Banī Kinānah, where they swore together to maintain disbelief." He meant al-Muḥaṣṣab.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Masrūq, ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid.
They said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ʿUmrah in Dhū al-Qaʿdah before he performed Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm,
and Ibn Abī ʿUmar,
(the wording is that of Ibn Abī Shaybah) Isḥāq said: He informed us, and the others said:
Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from Usāmah,
that the Prophet ﷺ went up onto one of the fortresses of Madinah and then said:
"Do you see what I see? I see the places where trials will fall among your houses like the falling of raindrops."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, Abū Bakr and Bilāl fell ill with fever.

When the fever seized Abū Bakr, he would say: "Every man is greeted in the morning among his family, while death is nearer than the strap of his sandal." And when the fever left Bilāl, he would raise his voice and say: "Would that I knew whether I will spend a night in a valley, with idhkhir and jalīl grass around me, and whether I will come down one day to the waters of Majannah, and whether Shāmah and Ṭafīl will appear to me." He said: "O Allah, curse Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah,
and ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah,
and Umayyah ibn Khalaf,
for they drove us out of our land to a land of pestilence." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, make Madinah beloved to us as we love Makkah, or even more.
O Allah, bless us in our ṣāʿ and in our mudd,
make it healthy for us, and transfer its fever to al-Juḥfah."
She said: We came to Madinah,
and it was the most pestilent of Allah's lands.
She said: Buṭḥān was flowing with foul water.
She means stagnant water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was telling stories, saying in his storytelling: Whoever is overtaken by dawn in a state of janābah should not fast.
I mentioned that to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith, [that is] to his father, and he rejected it.

So ʿAbd al-Raḥmān went and I went with him until we entered upon ʿĀʾishah and Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with them both). ʿAbd al-Raḥmān asked them about that. He said: Both of them said: The Prophet ﷺ would wake up in the morning in a state of janābah, not from a wet dream, and then fast. He said: Then we went until we entered upon Marwān, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān mentioned that to him.

Marwān said: I adjure you to go to Abū Hurayrah and retract to him what he says. He said: So we came to Abū Hurayrah, and Abū Bakr was present for all of that. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān mentioned it to him, and Abū Hurayrah said: Did the two of them tell you that? He said: Yes.
He said: They know best.
Then Abū Hurayrah attributed what he used to say about that to al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās, and Abū Hurayrah said: I heard that from al-Faḍl, and I did not hear it from the Prophet ﷺ.
He said: So Abū Hurayrah retracted what he used to say about that.
I said to ʿAbd al-Malik: Did they both say it about Ramadan? He said: Yes, he would wake up in a state of janābah, not from a wet dream, and then fast.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to Khaybar.
When Allah gave him victory over the fortress, the beauty of Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab was mentioned to him,
her husband having been killed, and she was a bride.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ chose her for himself and set out with her,
until we reached Sadd al-Rawḥāʾ, where she became lawful for him, and he consummated the marriage with her.
Then he made ḥays on a small leather mat,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Invite those around you."
That was the wedding feast of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for Ṣafiyyah.
Then we set out for Madinah.
He said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrapping a cloak around her behind him,
then sitting by his camel and putting down his knee,
and Ṣafiyyah would place her foot on his knee until she mounted.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ...to Ibn ʿUmar, and he said: "There is no emigration (hijrah) today,
or after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," similar to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ had finished with Ḥunayn, he sent Abū ʿĀmir with an army to Awṭās. He met Durayd ibn al-Ṣimmah, and Durayd was killed, and Allah defeated his companions. Abū Mūsā said: He sent me with Abū ʿĀmir. He said: Abū ʿĀmir was hit in the knee; a man of Banū Jusham shot him with an arrow and it lodged in his knee. I went to him and said: "Uncle, who shot you?" Abū ʿĀmir pointed to Abū Mūsā and said: "That one is my killer; you see him, the one who shot me."

Abū Mūsā said: I went straight for him and caught up with him. When he saw me, he turned away and left, so I pursued him, saying to him: "Are you not ashamed? Are you not an Arab? Will you not stand firm?" So he stopped, and he and I met and exchanged two blows. I struck him with the sword and killed him. Then I went back to Abū ʿĀmir and said: "Allah has killed your man."

He said: "Pull out this arrow." So I pulled it out, and water gushed from it. He said: "Son of my brother, go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, convey my greetings of peace to him, and tell him: Abū ʿĀmir says to you, 'Ask forgiveness for me.'"

He said: Abū ʿĀmir appointed me over the people, and he stayed a short while and then died. When I returned to the Prophet ﷺ, I entered upon him while he was in a house on a bed woven of palm fibers, with a mattress on it, and the marks of the bed's weaving were on the back and sides of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I told him our news and the news of Abū ʿĀmir, and I said to him: "He told me to say to you: Ask forgiveness for me."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for water and performed ablution with it. Then he raised his hands and said:
"O Allah, forgive ʿUbayd, Abū ʿĀmir."
until I saw the whiteness of his armpits. Then he said:
"O Allah, on the Day of Resurrection place him above many of Your creation," or [he said] "of the people."
I said: "And for me, Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"O Allah, forgive ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays his sin, and admit him on the Day of Resurrection to a noble entrance."
Abū Burdah said: One of the two supplications was for Abū ʿĀmir and the other for Abū Mūsā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at Ṭāʾif, he said:
"We are going back tomorrow, if Allah wills."
Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "We will not leave until we conquer it." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Then go out in the morning to fight."
He said: So they went out in the morning and fought them fiercely, and many wounds were inflicted on them. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"We are going back tomorrow, if Allah wills."
He said: They fell silent, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ conquered Ḥunayn, he distributed the spoils and gave to those whose hearts were to be reconciled. Then word reached him that the Anṣār wished to receive what the other people had received. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and addressed them, praised Allah and extolled Him, and then said:
"O assembly of the Anṣār, did I not find you astray, and Allah guided you through me; poor, and Allah enriched you through me; and divided, and Allah united you through me?"
And they would say: "Allah and His Messenger are the most generous." He said: "Will you not answer me?"
They said: "Allah and His Messenger are the most generous." He said:
"If you wished, you could say such and such, and the matter was such and such," [mentioning] things he enumerated.
ʿAmr claimed that he did not remember them. Then he said:

"Are you not pleased that the people go off with sheep and camels, while you go back to your homes with the Messenger of Allah? The Anṣār are the inner garment and the people are the outer garment. Were it not for the Hijrah, I would be one of the Anṣār. If the people took one valley or mountain path, I would take the valley and path of the Anṣār. You will meet after me preferential treatment of others, so be patient until you meet me at the Pool."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"On the day Allah created the heavens and the earth, He created one hundred mercies, each mercy filling the space between heaven and earth. He placed one of them on the earth; by it a mother is tender toward her child, and wild animals and birds show tenderness toward one another. Then on the Day of Resurrection, He will complete it with this mercy [i.e., the other ninety-nine]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed Allah feels jealousy, and the believer feels jealousy. The jealousy of Allah is that the believer does what He has forbidden him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The likeness of the hypocrite is like that of a ewe wandering between two flocks of sheep: she goes to this one once and to that one another time, not knowing which of them to follow.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah will fold up the heavens on the Day of Resurrection, then take them in His right hand, and then say: I am the King. Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant? Then He will fold up the earths, then take them."
Ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said:
"in His other hand, and then say: I am the King. Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, while he was on the pulpit:

"The Almighty will take His heavens and His earths in His hand"—and he closed his hand, and began to clench it and open it—"then He will say: I am the Almighty, I am the King. Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?"
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ swayed to his right and to his left, until I looked at the pulpit shaking from its lowest part, so that I said: Will it fall with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
label: machine translation

segments_en: Satan has despaired of being worshipped by those who pray in the Arabian Peninsula, but [he has not despaired] of stirring up strife among them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A caller will call out: You are to live and never die, you are to be healthy and never fall ill, you are to be young and never grow old, and you are to enjoy comfort and never suffer misery."
That is the meaning of the saying of the Exalted:
"And that is Paradise which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"On that day Hell will be brought, with seventy thousand reins, and with each rein seventy thousand angels dragging it."
ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and al-Thawrī said: He did not attribute it to the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"On the Day of Resurrection the molar tooth of the disbeliever will be like Uḥud, his thigh like al-Bayḍāʾ, and his seat in the Fire the distance of a three-day journey, like [the distance to] al-Rabadhah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the Day of Resurrection the sun will be brought near to the people until it is a mile or two away."
Sulaym said: I do not know which of the two miles he meant, the measure of distance on land or the mile [i.e., the stick] with which the eye is applied with kohl. He said:

"The sun will melt them, and they will be in sweat according to their deeds: among them are those whom it will reach to their heels, among them those whom it will reach to their knees, among them those whom it will reach to their waists, and among them those whom it will bridle completely."
And I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ point with his hand to his mouth, meaning that it would bridle him completely.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever is cross-examined in the reckoning will be destroyed."
I said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah the Exalted says:
"Then as for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will be judged with an easy reckoning." He said: "That is the presentation [of deeds]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Hour will not come until the Euphrates uncovers a mountain of gold over which people will fight, and ninety-nine out of every hundred will be killed. Each man among them will say: Perhaps I will be the one who survives."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Iraq will withhold its dirham and its qafīz, Syria will withhold its mudd and its dinar, and Egypt will withhold its irdabb and its dinar, and you will return to where you began, you will return to where you began, you will return to where you began."
The flesh and blood of Abū Hurayrah bear witness to that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The night and the day will not pass away until a man from among the freed slaves, called Jahjāh, becomes king."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Abū Usāmah, "Did Hishām ibn ʿUrwah narrate to you from his father, from ʿAbdullāh ibn az-Zubayr, who said: When az-Zubayr stood [in battle] on the day of the Camel, he called me,
and I stood beside him. He said, "O my son,
no one will be killed today except a wrongdoer or one who is wronged,
and I see that I will surely be killed today as one who is wronged.
And among my greatest worries is my debt.
Do you think our debt will leave anything of our wealth?" Then he said, "O my son, sell our property and pay my debt." And he bequeathed a third, and a third of it for his sons,
meaning the sons of ʿAbdullāh ibn az-Zubayr, saying: a third of the third.
"If anything remains of our wealth after the debt is paid, then a third of it is for your children."
Hishām said: Some of the children of ʿAbdullāh were of the same age as some of the sons of az-Zubayr, Khubayb and ʿAbbād,
and on that day he had nine sons and nine daughters.
ʿAbdullāh said: He began to instruct me about his debt, saying, "O my son,
if you are unable to [pay] any of it, then seek help with it from my Master."
He said: By Allah, I did not understand what he meant until I said, "Father, who is your Master?" He said, "Allah."
He said: By Allah, whenever I fell into difficulty regarding his debt, I would say, "O Master of az-Zubayr,
pay his debt for him." And He would pay it.
Then az-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, was killed, and he left behind neither a dinar nor a dirham,
except for lands, among them al-Ghābah,
eleven houses in Madinah, two houses in Basrah, one house in Kufah, and one house in Egypt.
He said: His debt came about only because a man would come to him with money and entrust it to him, and az-Zubayr would say, "No, rather it is a loan,
for I fear it may be lost."
He never took up any governorship, nor the collection of land tax, nor anything [of the kind],

except when he was on a military expedition with the Prophet ﷺ, or with Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with them. ʿAbdullāh ibn az-Zubayr said: So I calculated the debt he owed and found it to be two million two hundred thousand. He said: Then Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām met ʿAbdullāh ibn az-Zubayr and said, "O son of my brother,
how much debt does my brother owe?" But he concealed it.
He said, "One hundred thousand."
Ḥakīm said, "By Allah, I do not think your wealth can cover this."
ʿAbdullāh said to him, "What if I told you it is two million two hundred thousand?" He said, "I do not think you can bear this,
so if you are unable to [pay] any of it, seek my help."
He said: Az-Zubayr had bought al-Ghābah for one hundred and seventy thousand,
and ʿAbdullāh sold it for one million six hundred thousand. Then he stood and said, "Whoever has a claim against az-Zubayr, let him meet us at al-Ghābah."
ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar came to him,
and he had a claim of four hundred thousand against az-Zubayr. He said to ʿAbdullāh, "If you wish, I will forgo it for you."
ʿAbdullāh said, "No."
He said, "If you wish, you may put it among what you defer [paying], if you defer any."
ʿAbdullāh said, "No."
He said, "Then mark out a plot for me."
ʿAbdullāh said, "You have from here to here."
He said: So he sold part of it and paid his debt in full,
and four and a half shares of it remained.

Then he went to Muʿāwiyah, who had with him ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, al-Mundhir ibn az-Zubayr, and Ibn Zamʿah. Muʿāwiyah said to him, "How much was al-Ghābah valued at?" He said, "Each share at one hundred thousand."
He said, "How much remains?" He said, "Four and a half shares."
Al-Mundhir ibn az-Zubayr said, "I will take a share for one hundred thousand."
ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān said, "I will take a share for one hundred thousand."
Ibn Zamʿah said, "I will take a share for one hundred thousand."
Muʿāwiyah said, "How much remains?" He said, "A share and a half."
He said, "I will take it for one hundred and fifty thousand."
He said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar sold his portion to Muʿāwiyah for six hundred thousand.
When Ibn az-Zubayr had finished paying his debt, the sons of az-Zubayr said, "Divide our inheritance among us." He said, "No,
by Allah, I will not divide it among you until I have announced at the pilgrimage season for four years: Whoever has a debt owed to him by az-Zubayr, let him come to us and we will pay it."
He said: So every year he would make the announcement at the pilgrimage season,
and when four years had passed, he divided it among them. He said: Az-Zubayr had four wives, and after setting aside the third,
each wife received one million two hundred thousand,
so his total wealth was fifty million two hundred thousand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"I give to Quraysh to win their hearts,
because they are close to [having left] the time of ignorance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: During our military expeditions we would come across honey and grapes, and we would eat them and not carry them away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no Arabian horse but that it is permitted, at every dawn, to make two supplications: 'O Allah, You have placed me in the service of whomever You have placed me in of the children of Adam, and You have made me his; so make me the one dearest to him of his family and his wealth,' or: 'of those whose wealth and family are dearest to him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say: In the year of Khaybar the Messenger of Allah ﷺ assigned four shares to az-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām: a share for az-Zubayr, a share for the near relative, for Ṣafiyyah bint ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the mother of az-Zubayr, and two shares for the horse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a piece of land of mine at Thamgh. He said:
"Hold its principal and make its fruit freely available [for charity]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUthmān,

looked down upon them when they besieged him and said: "I implore you by Allah: is there a man who heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of the mountain, when it shook, and he struck it with his foot and said:
'Be still, for upon you there is only a prophet, a truthful one, or two martyrs'?"
And I was with him. Some men testified for him. Then he said: "I implore you by Allah: is there a man who was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of the Pledge of Riḍwān, when he said:
'This is the hand of Allah, and this is the hand of ʿUthmān'?"
Some men testified for him. Then he said: "I implore you by Allah: is there a man who heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of the Army of Hardship say:
'Whoever spends an accepted expenditure'?"
So I equipped half of the army from my own wealth. Some men testified for him. Then he said: "I implore you by Allah: is there a man who heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever adds to this mosque will have a house in Paradise'?"

So I bought it from my own wealth. Some men testified for him. Then he said: "I implore you by Allah: is there a man who witnessed that the well of Rūmah was being sold, and I bought it from my own wealth and made it freely available to the traveler?" Some men testified for him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿUthmān was besieged in his house, the people gathered around his house. He said: So he looked down upon them. And he related the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: His saying
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died and there was no one with him but me. She said: And he had called for the basin.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The family of Saʿd said: Saʿd fell ill, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited him. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I bequeath all of my wealth?" He said: "No." And he related the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to visit Saʿd, and Saʿd said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I bequeath two-thirds of my wealth?" He said: "No."
He said: "Then half?" He said: "No."
He said: "Then a third?" He said:
"Yes, a third, and a third is a lot," or he said, "large. For you to leave your heirs wealthy is better than that you leave them poor, begging from people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jew had a claim of dates against my father, who was killed on the day of Uhud, leaving two orchards. The dates owed to the Jew would consume what was in the two orchards. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Would you take half this year and defer half?"
The Jew refused. Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Would you take the harvest [as it is cut]?"

He gave permission, and I gave him leave. So he came, along with Abū Bakr, and the dates were cut and measured from the base of the palms while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for blessing, until we paid him his full right from the smaller of the two orchards, as ʿAmmār reckoned. Then I brought them fresh dates and water, and they ate and drank. Then he said:
"This is part of the bounty about which you will be asked."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I listened,
from Ibn al-Qāsim, from Mālik,
from Saʿīd ibn ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl ibn Saʿīd ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah, from his father, from his grandfather,
who said: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah went out with the Prophet ﷺ on one of his campaigns, and his mother was approaching death in Madinah. She was told: "Make a bequest."
She said: "What should I bequeath? The wealth is Saʿd's wealth."
She died before Saʿd arrived. When Saʿd arrived, this was mentioned to him, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, will it benefit her if I give charity on her behalf?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Yes."
Then Saʿd said: "The orchard of such-and-such is charity on her behalf," naming an orchard.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "My mother has died, and she had a vow [unfulfilled]. Would it suffice for her if I free a slave on her behalf?" He said:
"Free a slave on behalf of your mother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: His father,
gave him a gift, and his mother said to him: "Make the Prophet ﷺ witness to what you have given my son."
So he came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and the Prophet ﷺ disliked to bear witness to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr bought a saddle from my father for thirteen dirhams, and he narrated the hadith in the sense of the hadith of Zuhayr from Abū Isḥāq. In his narration, from the transmission of ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar, he said: "When he came near, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against him, and his horse sank into the ground up to its belly, and he leapt off it. He said: 'O Muḥammad, I know that this is your doing, so supplicate to Allah to free me from what I am in, and I owe it to you that I will turn back those behind me. This is my quiver, so take an arrow from it, for you will pass by my camels and my boys at such and such a place, so take from them what you need.' He said: "
I have no need of your camels."
We arrived in Madinah at night, and they disputed over which of them the Messenger of Allah ﷺ should stay with. So he said: "
I will stay with Banū al-Najjār, the maternal uncles of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, to honor them by that."
Then the men and women went up onto the roofs, and the boys and servants scattered through the streets, calling out: "O Muḥammad! O Messenger of Allah! O Muḥammad! O Messenger of Allah!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said to me: "O son of my sister, they were commanded to seek forgiveness
for the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, yet they insulted them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said to me: "Do you know" — and Hārūn said, "Do you realize" — "the last sūrah of the Qurʾān to be revealed, revealed in its entirety?" I said: "Yes."
[It is] {When the help of Allah and the victory come}. He said: "You have spoken truly."
In the narration of Ibn Abī Shaybah: "Do you know which sūrah..."
and he did not say "last."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was only four years between our becoming Muslim and Allah rebuking us with this verse: {Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves at the remembrance of Allah?}
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās came to Basra, he used to narrate from Abū Mūsā,
so ʿAbd Allāh wrote to Abū Mūsā asking him about some matters,

and Abū Mūsā wrote back to him: "I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day, and he wanted to urinate. He came to a patch of soft ground at the base of a wall and urinated. Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "
'When one of you wants to urinate, let him look for a suitable place for his urine.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Ibn ʿUmar make his riding camel kneel facing the qiblah, then sit and urinate toward it. I said: "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, was this not forbidden?" He said: "Yes, but that was forbidden only in open country. When there is something between you and the qiblah that screens you, there is no harm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men must not go out to relieve themselves, uncovering their private parts and talking, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, hates that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And his hadith
is more complete: that Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥakam
narrated to them, saying: Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd informed us,
Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ narrated to me,
that Abū Saʿīd al-Ḥimyarī
narrated to him from Muʿādh ibn Jabal,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Beware of the three cursed acts: relieving oneself at water sources, in the middle of the road, and in the shade."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [One of the wives of] the Prophet ﷺ [said] that the Prophet ﷺ used to use his right hand for his food, his drink, and his clothing, and he used his left hand for anything other than that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The right hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was for his purification and his food, and his left hand was for his toilet and whatever was unclean.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He mentioned that while he was with him, stationed at the fortress of Bāb al-Yūn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A delegation of the jinn came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muḥammad, forbid your nation from cleaning themselves with a bone, dung, or charcoal, for Allah, the Exalted, has made provision for us in them."
He said: So the Prophet ﷺ forbade that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "Tell me about Ibn ʿUmar's performing ablution for every prayer, whether in a state of purity or not. Why was that?" He said: "Asmāʾ bint Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrated it to me, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥanẓalah ibn Abī ʿĀmir narrated to her that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded ablution for every prayer, whether in a state of purity or not. When that became difficult for him, he was commanded to use the toothstick for every prayer. Ibn ʿUmar believed he had the strength for it, so he never abandoned ablution for every prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was using the toothstick, and with him were two men, one older than the other. It was revealed to him about the virtue of the toothstick: "Let the elder have precedence."
"Give the toothstick to the elder of the two."
Aḥmad, who is Ibn Ḥazm, said: Abū Saʿīd, who is Ibn al-Aʿrābī, told us: This is among the reports unique to the people of Madinah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to use the toothstick and would give it to me to wash. I would begin by using it myself, then wash it and hand it to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man asked al-Barāʾ, "Was the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ like a sword?" He said, "No, like the moon."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out at midday to al-Baṭḥāʾ, performed ablution, then prayed two rakʿahs of Ẓuhr and two rakʿahs of ʿAṣr,
with a short spear planted in front of him.
Shuʿbah said: ʿAwn added on the authority of his father, Abū Juḥayfah, who said: Women used to pass behind it.
The people stood up and began taking hold of his hands,
and wiping their faces with them.
He said: I took his hand
and placed it on my face,
and it was cooler than ice
and more fragrant than musk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was radiant in complexion; his sweat was like pearls. When he walked, he leaned forward slightly. I never touched any brocade or silk softer than the palm of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I never smelled any musk or ambergris more fragrant than the scent of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ and his Companions were at az-Zawrāʾ—he said: az-Zawrāʾ is in Madinah near the market and the mosque, in the place there—and he called for a cup containing water and placed his palm in it. Water began to gush from between his fingers, and all of his Companions performed ablution.
I said, "How many were they, Abū Ḥamzah?" He said, "They were about three hundred."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people were thirsty on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, and in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was a small water-skin, from which he performed ablution.
Then the people came toward him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "What is the matter with you?"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, we have no water with which to perform ablution
and nothing to drink except what is in your water-skin."
He said: The Prophet ﷺ placed his hand in the water-skin,
and the water began to gush from between his fingers like springs.
He said: So we drank and performed ablution.
I said to Jābir, "How many of you were there that day?" He said, "Had we been a hundred thousand, it would have sufficed us.
We were fifteen hundred."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to regard miraculous signs as a blessing, while you regard them as a warning.
We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey when the water ran low, and he said,
"Look for some leftover water."
They brought a vessel with a little water in it,
and he put his hand into the vessel, then said,
"Come to the purifying, blessed water,
and the blessing is from Allah."
I saw the water gushing from between the fingers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
and we used to hear the glorification of the food while it was being eaten.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That his father

died while owing a debt. I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my father has died owing a debt, and he left nothing except what his date palms produce, and what his date palms produce would not cover his debt for years. So come with me, O Messenger of Allah, so that the creditors do not press me harshly." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went around the threshing floors, one by one, invoked peace around them and prayed for him, then sat upon it and called the creditors and paid them in full, and as much remained as they had taken.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"This tribe of Quraysh will destroy the people."
They said, "What do you command us to do?" He said,
"If only the people would keep away from them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While a man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ was reciting,
and his horse was tied in the courtyard, it began to shy and bolt.
The man went out and looked but saw nothing, and it kept shying.
When morning came, he mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, who said,
"That was the tranquility (sakīnah) which descended because of the Qur'an."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever enters the state of ihram for Hajj or ʿUmrah from the Masjid al-Aqṣā to the Masjid al-Ḥarām, his previous and later sins will be forgiven," or he said: "
Paradise will be obligatory for him."
ʿAbdullāh was unsure which of the two he said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was at Minā or at ʿArafāt, and the people were crowding around him. He said: The Bedouins would come, and when they saw his face they would say, "This is a blessed face."
He said: And the stated place for entering ihram at Dhāt ʿIrq is for the people of Iraq.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
When a menstruating woman or a woman in postnatal bleeding reaches the stated place, they should bathe and enter ihram, and perform all the rites except the circumambulation of the House."
Abū Maʿmar said in his narration: "until she is pure." Ibn ʿĪsā did not mention ʿIkrimah and Mujāhid; he said: from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās. Ibn ʿĪsā did not say "all." He said: "
the rites, except the circumambulation of the House."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ pronouncing the talbiyah with his hair matted.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ matted his hair with honey.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh, meaning Ibn Abī Najīḥ, said: Mujāhid narrated to me from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyah, included among his sacrificial offerings a camel that had belonged to Abū Jahl, with a silver nose ring in its head.
Ibn Minhāl said: a gold nose ring. Al-Nufaylī added: to anger the polytheists by that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent sheep as sacrificial offerings, garlanded.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb dedicated a fine camel as a sacrificial offering, and was offered three hundred dinars for it. He came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I dedicated a fine camel and have been offered three hundred dinars for it. Should I sell it and buy camels with its price?" He said: "
No, sacrifice that very one."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent sacrificial animals with him and said: "
If any of them is about to die, slaughter it, then dye its sandal in its blood, then leave it for the people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent so-and-so al-Aslamī and sent eighteen sacrificial camels with him. He said: "What if one of them becomes too exhausted to go on?" He said: "
Slaughter it, then dye its sandal in its blood, then strike it on its side. Neither you nor anyone among your companions should eat from it," or he said: "
anyone among your travelling party."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sacrificed his camels, he sacrificed thirty with his own hand, and he commanded me, and I sacrificed the rest.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The greatest of days with Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the Day of Sacrifice, then the Day of Qarr."
ʿĪsā said: Thawr said: It is the second day.

He said: Five or six camels were brought near to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they began to draw close to him, each one wanting to be the first he would begin with. When they had fallen on their sides, he said something softly that I did not understand. I said, "What did he say?" He said: "
Whoever wishes may cut off a portion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and the sacrificial camels were brought. He said: "
Call Abū al-Ḥasan for me."
So ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, was called for him, and he said to him: "
Take hold of the lower part of the spear."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of its upper part, then stabbed the camels with it. When he had finished, he rode his mule and had ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, ride behind him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ and his Companions used to sacrifice a camel with its left foreleg tied, standing on its remaining legs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When any one of us was in a state of janābah,
she would take three handfuls [of water] with her hands over her head,
then take [water] with her hand over her right side,
and with her other hand over her left side.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah: Did the Prophet ﷺ sleep while in a state of janābah? She said: Yes, and he would perform ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to bathe, I and the Prophet
ﷺ, from a single vessel, both of us in a state of janābah.
He would order me, and I would put on a waist-wrapper,
and then he would have contact with me while I was menstruating.
And he would put his head out to me while he was in iʿtikāf,
and I would wash it while I was menstruating.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A concession was granted to a menstruating woman to depart [from Makkah] if she began to menstruate.
Ibn ʿUmar used to say at first that she should not depart.
Then I heard him say that she may depart, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had granted them a concession.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmmār [reported] this,
and Shuʿbah struck the ground with his hands,
then brought them close to his mouth,
then wiped his face and his hands.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he was present with ʿUmar when ʿAmmār said to him: We were in a detachment and became in a state of janābah,
and he said: Blow into them [your hands].
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with ʿUmar when ʿAmmār said to him... and he related the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were on a journey with the Prophet ﷺ, and we travelled by night,
until, when we were at the end of the night,
we lay down to sleep, and there is no sleep sweeter to a traveller than that,
and nothing woke us except the heat of the sun.
The first to wake up was so-and-so, then so-and-so, then so-and-so, Abū Rajāʾ named them but ʿAwf forgot, and fourth was ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
Whenever the Prophet ﷺ slept, he was not woken until he woke by himself,
because we did not know what might be happening to him in his sleep.
When ʿUmar woke up
and saw what had befallen the people,
and he was a hardy man,
he said Allāhu Akbar and raised his voice with the takbīr,
and he kept saying the takbīr and raising his voice with it until the Prophet ﷺ woke at his voice. When he woke, they complained to him of what had befallen them. He said:
"There is no harm," or "It does no harm. Set out."
So he set out, travelled a short distance, then stopped and called for water for ablution,
and he performed ablution, the call to prayer was made, and he led the people in prayer.
When he turned away from his prayer, there was a man set apart who had not prayed with the people. He said:
"What prevented you, O so-and-so, from praying with the people?"
He said: I became in a state of janābah and there is no water. He said: "Use clean earth, for it is sufficient for you."
Then the Prophet ﷺ travelled on, and the people complained to him of thirst, so he stopped,
and he called so-and-so, whom Abū Rajāʾ named but ʿAwf forgot, and called ʿAlī, and said:
"Go and look for water."
So they set off and met a woman between two water-skins, or two large leather containers, of water on a camel of hers,
and they said to her: Where is the water? She said: I was last at water this time yesterday, and our men had stayed behind.
They said to her: Then come with us.
She said: Where to? They said: To the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
She said: The one who is called the Sabian? They said: He is the one you mean, so come.
So they brought her to the Prophet ﷺ and told him the account. He said: they made her get down from her camel, and the Prophet ﷺ called for a vessel,
and he poured into it from the mouths of the two water-skins, or the two containers, and tied their mouths, and opened the lower openings,
and it was announced among the people: Give water and take water.
So whoever wished gave water to others,
and whoever wished took water,
and the last of that was that the man who had been in janābah was given a vessel of water, and he said: "Go and pour it over yourself."
She was standing looking at what was being done with her water,
and by Allah, they stopped [drawing] from it,
and it seemed to us that it was fuller than when he began with it. Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "Gather [food] for her."
So they gathered for her dates, flour, and roasted barley meal,
until they had collected food for her,
and they put it in a cloth,
and loaded her onto her camel,
and placed the cloth in front of her. He said to her:
"You know that we have not taken anything from your water,
but it is Allah who gave us drink." Then she came to her family,
having been delayed from them. They said: What kept you, O so-and-so? She said: A wonder!
Two men met me and took me to this man who is called the Sabian,
and he did such and such.
By Allah, he is either the greatest sorcerer between this and this,
and she gestured with her middle finger and index finger,
raising them toward the sky, meaning the sky and the earth, or he truly is the Messenger of Allah.
After that the Muslims would raid the polytheists around her,
but would not attack the settlement she belonged to.
One day she said to her people: I think these people are leaving you alone deliberately,
so do you have any interest in Islam? They obeyed her and entered Islam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to teach some men of the Muhājirūn, among them ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.
While I was at his place in Minā,
and he was with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb during the last Hajj he performed,

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān came back to me and said: "If only you had seen a man who came to the Commander of the Faithful today and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, what do you think of so-and-so, who says: If ʿUmar were to die, I would pledge allegiance to so-and-so,
for by Allah, the pledge of allegiance to Abū Bakr was nothing but a sudden, hasty affair, yet it was carried through.'
ʿUmar became angry and then said: "Allah willing, I will stand among the people this evening
and warn them against those who want to seize their affairs from them."
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I said, "O Commander of the Faithful, do not do so, for the pilgrimage season gathers the rabble and riffraff of the people,
and they are the ones who will predominate in your vicinity when you stand among the people.
I fear that you will stand and say a statement that every carrier will spread about from you,
and that they will not grasp it,
and that they will not put it in its proper place.
So wait until you reach Medina, for it is the abode of the Hijrah and the Sunnah,
and there you can be alone with the people of understanding and the nobles among the people,
and say what you have to say with composure,
so that the people of knowledge will grasp your words
and put them in their proper places."
ʿUmar said: "Indeed, by Allah, Allah willing, I will do exactly that at the first occasion on which I stand in Medina."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: We reached Medina at the end of Dhū al-Ḥijjah.
When it was Friday, we hurried to go out as soon as the sun passed its zenith,
and I found Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl sitting by the corner of the pulpit.
I sat beside him, my knee touching his knee,
and it was not long before ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb came out.
When I saw him approaching, I said to Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl:
"This evening he will say a statement he has not said since he became Caliph."
He rejected that from me and said, "What could he possibly say that he has not said before?"
ʿUmar then sat on the pulpit,
and when the callers to prayer fell silent, he stood and praised Allah as He deserves, then said: "To proceed: I am going to say something to you that it has been decreed I should say.
I do not know, perhaps it is just before my death.
Whoever understands it and retains it, let him relate it wherever his mount takes him,
and whoever fears that he will not understand it, I do not permit anyone to lie about me.
Indeed, Allah sent Muḥammad ﷺ with the truth and revealed the Book to him, and among what Allah revealed was the verse of stoning.
We recited it, understood it, and retained it.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ carried out stoning, and we carried it out after him.
I fear that if a long time passes, someone will say: 'By Allah, we do not find the verse of stoning in the Book of Allah,'
and thus they will go astray by abandoning an obligation that Allah revealed.
Stoning, in the Book of Allah, is a right upon the one who commits illicit sex when married, whether men or women,
when the proof is established, or there is pregnancy, or confession.
Then, among what we used to recite from the Book of Allah was: 'Do not turn away from your fathers,
for it is disbelief on your part to turn away from your fathers,'
or: 'It is disbelief on your part that you turn away from your fathers.'
Beware! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Do not exaggerate in praising me as ʿĪsā, son of Maryam, was exaggerated about, but say: the servant of Allah and His Messenger.'
Then it has reached me that someone among you says: 'By Allah, if ʿUmar dies, I will pledge allegiance to so-and-so.'
Let no man be deluded into saying that the pledge to Abū Bakr was a sudden, hasty affair that was carried through. Indeed it was so, but Allah protected [us] from its evil,
and there is none among you to whom necks are stretched [in eagerness] like Abū Bakr.
Whoever pledges allegiance to a man without consultation of the Muslims, neither he nor the one to whom he pledged allegiance is to be followed, lest both be killed.
And it was part of our news when Allah took His Prophet ﷺ in death that the Anṣār opposed us and all gathered in the hall of Banū Sāʿidah,
and ʿAlī and az-Zubayr and those with them held back from us,
while the Muhājirūn gathered around Abū Bakr. I said to Abū Bakr: 'O Abū Bakr, let us go to these brothers of ours of the Anṣār.'
So we set out to meet them, and when we drew near them, two righteous men met us,
and they mentioned what the people had agreed upon, and said: 'Where are you going, O company of the Muhājirūn?' We said: 'We want these brothers of ours from the Anṣār.'
They said: 'There is no need for you to approach them; settle your own affair.'
I said: 'By Allah, we will go to them.'
So we went on until we came to them in the hall of Banū Sāʿidah,
and there was a man wrapped up among them. I said: 'Who is this?' They said: 'This is Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah.'
I said: 'What is wrong with him?' They said: 'He is ill with fever.'
When we had sat a little while, their speaker pronounced the testimony of faith,
praised Allah as He deserves, and then said: 'To proceed: we are the helpers of Allah and the army of Islam,
and you, O company of the Muhājirūn, are a small group,
and a group of your people has come hurrying,
and now they want to cut us off from our origin and to deprive us of the matter [of leadership].'
When he fell silent, I wanted to speak. I had prepared a speech that pleased me, and I wanted to present it before Abū Bakr,
and I was tempering for him some of my sharpness.
When I wanted to speak, Abū Bakr said: 'Gently, take your time.'
I disliked to anger him,
so Abū Bakr spoke, and he was more forbearing and dignified than I.

By Allah, he did not leave out any phrase that had pleased me in my preparation but that he said the like of it or better, extemporaneously, until he fell silent. He said: 'Whatever good you have mentioned about yourselves, you are deserving of it,
but this matter will not be recognized except for this clan of Quraysh,
who are the best of the Arabs in lineage and homeland,
and I am pleased for you with one of these two men,
so pledge allegiance to whichever of them you wish.'
He took my hand and the hand of Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ, who was sitting between us,
and I disliked nothing of what he said except that,
for by Allah, that I be brought forward and have my neck struck, without that bringing me close to sin,
was dearer to me than that I should be in command over a people among whom was Abū Bakr,
unless my soul should tempt me at death with something I do not find now.
One of the Anṣār said: 'I am the rubbing post [of this affair] and its well-propped palm; from us a leader, and from you a leader,
O company of Quraysh.' The clamor grew,
and voices rose until I feared disagreement.
So I said: 'Stretch out your hand, O Abū Bakr.'
He stretched out his hand and I pledged allegiance to him, and the Muhājirūn pledged allegiance to him,
then the Anṣār pledged allegiance to him,
and we leapt upon Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah. One of them said: 'You have killed Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah.'
I said: 'Allah has killed Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah.'

ʿUmar said: By Allah, in what we faced we found no matter stronger than the pledge to Abū Bakr. We feared that if we left the people without a pledge having been made, they would pledge allegiance to a man from among themselves after us,
and then we would either have to pledge to them for something we did not approve of,
or oppose them, and there would be corruption.
So whoever pledges allegiance to a man without consultation of the Muslims, neither he nor the one to whom he pledged allegiance is to be followed, lest both be killed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: No trait was more hateful to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than lying. A man would tell the Prophet ﷺ a lie, and it would stay on his mind until he knew that the man had repented from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The believer is not one who slanders, curses, is obscene, or speaks foul language."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not revile the dead, for you would be hurting the living."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"In Paradise there are rooms whose outsides can be seen from their insides and whose insides can be seen from their outsides."
A Bedouin stood up to him and said, "For whom are they, Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"They are for whoever speaks good words, feeds others, fasts continually, and prays to Allah at night while people sleep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"How excellent it is for one of them to obey his Lord and fulfill the right of his master," meaning the slave.
And Kaʿb said, "Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Three will be upon hills of musk—I think he said on the Day of Resurrection—envied by the first and the last: a man who calls to the five daily prayers every day and night, a man who leads a people in prayer while they are pleased with him, and a slave who fulfilled the right of Allah and the right of his masters."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Fear Allah wherever you are, follow a bad deed with a good deed and it will wipe it out, and treat people with good character."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They said, "Messenger of Allah, you joke with us." He said:
"I only say what is true."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is sin enough for you that you never stop quarreling."
This hadith is gharīb; we do not know it except through this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A man keeps exalting himself until he is recorded among the tyrants, and then what befalls them befalls him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: You tell me I am arrogant, when I have ridden a donkey, worn a coarse wrap, and milked a sheep, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever does this has no arrogance in him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Nothing is heavier in the believer's scale on the Day of Resurrection than good character, and Allah hates the obscene, foul-mouthed person."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He described good character, saying: It is a cheerful face, giving generously of good, and restraining harm.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "Messenger of Allah, I pass by a man who does not host me or entertain me as a guest, and then he passes by me. Should I repay him in kind?" He said, "No, host him."
He said: He saw me in shabby clothes and said:
"Do you have any wealth?"
I said, "Of every kind of wealth; Allah has given me camels and sheep." He said, "Then let it show on you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do not be people without a will of your own, saying, 'If people do good, we will do good, and if they wrong us, we will wrong them.' Rather, accustom yourselves: if people do good, you do good, and if they do evil, do not wrong them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Deliberation is from Allah, and haste is from Satan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah about the character of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said, "He was not obscene, nor did he seek to be obscene, nor was he loud in the markets. He did not repay a bad deed with a bad deed, but would pardon and overlook."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Among those most beloved to me and nearest to me in seat on the Day of Resurrection are those of you with the best character, and among those most hateful to me and farthest from me in seat on the Day of Resurrection are the thartharūn, the mutashaddiqūn, and the mutafayhiqūn."
They said, "Messenger of Allah, we know the thartharūn and the mutashaddiqūn, but who are the mutafayhiqūn?" He said, "The arrogant."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The practice according to the people of knowledge is that when a man performs iʿtikāf, he does not leave his iʿtikāf except for a human need, and they agreed that he may leave to relieve himself, for defecation and urination.

Then the people of knowledge differed regarding visiting the sick, attending the Friday prayer, and [attending] the funeral for the one in iʿtikāf. Some of the people of knowledge from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ and others held that he may visit the sick, accompany the funeral procession, and attend the Friday prayer if he made that a condition.
This is the view of Sufyān al-Thawrī and Ibn al-Mubārak.

Some of them said that he may not do any of this. They held that if the one in iʿtikāf is in a town where Friday prayer is held, he should perform iʿtikāf only in the congregational mosque, because they disliked his leaving his place of iʿtikāf for the Friday prayer, yet they did not think he should leave the Friday prayer. So they said he should perform iʿtikāf only in the congregational mosque, so that he would not need to leave his place of iʿtikāf for anything other than a human need, because for them, his leaving for anything other than a human need breaks the iʿtikāf.
This is the view of Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī.
Aḥmad said: He should not visit the sick or follow the funeral procession, based on the hadith of ʿĀʾishah.
Isḥāq said: If he made that a condition, then he may follow the funeral procession and visit the sick.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever has provisions and a mount that will take him to the House of Allah and does not perform Hajj, it makes no difference whether he dies a Jew or a Christian. That is because Allah says in His Book:
'And Allah has [made it] a duty upon mankind to perform Hajj to the House, for whoever is able to find a way to it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ performed Hajj three times: twice before he emigrated, and once after he emigrated, together with an ʿUmrah. He drove sixty-three camels, and ʿAlī came from Yemen with the rest of them, among which was a camel belonging to Abū Jahl with a ring of silver in its nose. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sacrificed them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that a piece from each camel be taken, and it was cooked, and he drank some of its broth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ wanted to perform Hajj, he announced it to the people, and they gathered. When he reached al-Baydāʾ, he entered the state of iḥrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Hajj alone [Ifrād].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed tamattuʿ, as did Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān, and the first to forbid it was Muʿāwiyah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] from the people of Syria was asking ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar about tamattuʿ, performing ʿUmrah followed by Hajj. ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: "It is lawful."
The Syrian said: "Your father forbade it."

ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: "What do you think: if my father forbade it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did it, do we follow my father's command or the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" The man said: "Rather, the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ certainly did it."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw the Prophet ﷺ take off his [sewn] clothes for his declaration of iḥrām and bathe.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw a Bedouin who had entered iḥrām while wearing a cloak, so he ordered him to take it off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had himself cupped while he was in iḥrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah while he was not in iḥrām, and consummated the marriage with her while he was not in iḥrām, and I was the messenger between the two of them.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her while he was not in iḥrām, and consummated the marriage with her while not in iḥrām. She died at Sarif, and we buried her in the canopy in which he had consummated the marriage with her.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever circumambulates the House fifty times will emerge from his sins as on the day his mother bore him."

segments_en: They used to consider ʿAbdullāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Jubayr to be better than his father.
ʿAbdullāh had a brother called ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who has also been narrated from.

segments_en: Fayrūz said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we are people of vineyards, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has revealed the prohibition of wine. What should we do?" He said, "Make it into raisins."
I said, "And what do we do with the raisins?" He said,
"Soak them in the morning for your midday meal and drink it at your evening meal, and soak them in the evening for your evening meal and drink it at your morning meal."
I said, "Shall we not keep it longer until it becomes strong?" He said,
"Do not put it in jars; put it in waterskins, for if it is kept longer it becomes vinegar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to have raisins soaked for him in a waterskin in the morning, and he would drink it at night, and have it soaked for him in the evening and drink it in the morning. He would wash the waterskins and not leave any sediment or anything else in them.
Nāfiʿ said: We used to drink it, and it was like honey.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Abū Jaʿfar about nabīdh,
and he said: ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with him, would have it prepared for him at night and drink it in the morning, and have it prepared for him in the morning and drink it at night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Soak it in the evening and drink it in the morning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And it is not,
the Nahdī [version]: Umm al-Faḍl

sent a message to Anas ibn Mālik asking him about nabīdh made in jars. He related to her from his son al-Naḍr that he used to make nabīdh in a jar, soaking it in the morning and drinking it in the evening.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He disliked that one put
naṭl of nabīdh into nabīdh so that it would become strong through the naṭl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In nabīdh with sediment there is wine.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Wine was only called khamr because it is left until its clear part is gone and its murkiness remains.
And he disliked anything that is soaked on top of dregs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They held that whoever
drank a drink and became intoxicated by it, it was not proper for him to return to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no harm in bukhtaj nabīdh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibrāhīm, saying: We take the dregs of wine or the ṭilāʾ, clean it, then soak raisins in it for three days, then strain it and leave it until it matures, and then we drink it. He said: It is disliked.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah have mercy on Ibrāhīm. He was strict with people about nabīdh, and yet he permitted it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I have not found an authentic concession regarding intoxicants from anyone except Ibrāhīm.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I have not seen a man more eager to seek knowledge than ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak: Syria, Egypt, Yemen and the Hijaz.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ubayy ibn Kaʿb about nabīdh,
and he said: Drink water, drink honey, drink barley meal, and drink milk, which does you good.
I asked him again, and he said: Is it wine you want? Is it wine you want?
label: machine translation

segments_en: People have invented drinks, and I do not know what they are. For twenty years, or he said forty years, I have had no drink but water and barley meal. However, he did not mention nabīdh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṭalḥah said to the people of Kūfah: In nabīdh there is trial; the young grow up in it and the old grow aged in it. He said: When there was a wedding among them, Ṭalḥah and al-Zubayr would serve milk and honey.
Ṭalḥah was asked, "Will you not serve them nabīdh?" He said, "I dislike that a Muslim become intoxicated because of me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Shubrumah would drink nothing but water and milk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whatever I command you, take it, and whatever I forbid you, refrain from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He narrated] a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, neither adding to it nor falling short of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us while we were mentioning poverty and fearing it, and he said,

"Is it poverty you fear? By the One in whose hand is my soul, the world will be poured out upon you in abundance, until no heart among you will go astray except because of it. By Allah, I have left you upon [a path] like a white, clear one, its night and its day alike."
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke the truth. By Allah, he left us upon [a path] like a white, clear one, its night and its day alike.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was
one who had prayed toward both qiblahs with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say,
"Allah will not cease to plant in this religion plantings whom He employs in obedience to Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah stood to deliver a sermon and said: Where are your scholars? Where are your scholars? I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say,
"The Hour will not come until a group from my nation remains dominant over the people, not caring about those who forsake them nor those who support them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ, and he drew a line, and drew two lines on his right and two lines on his left. Then he placed his hand on the middle line and said,
"This is the path of Allah."
Then he recited this verse: {And indeed, this is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, for they will separate you from His way.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun and the moon will be rolled up on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) said, from the Prophet ﷺ:
label: machine translation

segments_en: The angels descend in the clouds (that is, the cloud) and mention the matter that has been decreed in the heaven.
Then the devils eavesdrop,
and hear it, and pass it on to the soothsayers,
who then add to it a hundred lies of their own."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is as if I can see the dust rising in the alley of Banū Ghanm, [raised by] the procession of Jibrīl, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out to Banū Qurayẓah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord has made a grave claim,
but he saw Jibrīl in his [true] form,
and his creation filled what is between the horizons.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Tonight I saw two men come to me. They said: 'The one who kindles the Fire is Mālik, the keeper of the Fire, and I am Jibrīl, and this is Mīkāʾīl.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Paradise has eight gates,
