among them a gate called ar-Rayyān, which none will enter except those who fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the edge of the sun appears, leave the prayer until it has fully risen,
and when the edge of the sun disappears, leave the prayer until it has fully set."
"And do not time your prayer to coincide with the sun's rising or its setting,
for it rises between the two horns of a devil" or "of the devil."
Hishām said: I do not know which of the two he said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb told us
that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Moses said to his servant, 'Bring us our meal.'
He replied, 'Do you see? When we took refuge at the rock,
I forgot the fish,
and none made me forget to mention it except Satan.'
And Moses did not feel fatigue until he had passed the place that Allah had commanded."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Every son of Adam is poked by Satan in his sides with his finger when he is born,
except Jesus, son of Mary:
he went to poke him but poked the veil instead."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Syria and said, "Who is here?" They said, "Abū ad-Dardāʾ." He said, "Is there among you the one whom Allah protected from Satan on the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ?" Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Mughīrah. And he said: "the one whom Allah protected on the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ," meaning ʿAmmār.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Uḥud, the polytheists were routed,
and Iblīs, may Allah's curse be upon him, cried out, "O servants of Allah, [beware of] those behind you!"
So the front ranks turned back and fought with those behind them. Then Ḥudhayfah looked and saw his father, al-Yamān, and said, "O servants of Allah, my father, my father!"
She said: By Allah, they did not stop until they had killed him. Ḥudhayfah said, "May Allah forgive you."
ʿUrwah said: By Allah, Ḥudhayfah continued to have some goodness remaining until he met Allah. (Baṣurtu means "I knew,"
from baṣīrah, insight into a matter,
and abṣartu is from seeing with the eye. It is also said that baṣurtu and abṣartu are the same.)
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ commanded her to kill geckos.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar
used to kill snakes, then he stopped. He said that the Prophet ﷺ demolished a wall of his,
and found in it the shed skin of a snake. He said:
"Look where it is." They looked, and he said, "Kill it."
So I used to kill them because of that.
Then I met Abū Lubābah, and he told me that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do not kill the house snakes,
except every tail-less one with two stripes,
for it causes miscarriage and takes away eyesight, so kill it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) used to kill all snakes,
until Abū Lubābah al-Badrī told him
that the Prophet ﷺ forbade killing the snakes of the houses, so he refrained from killing them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the killing of dogs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The meaning is the same—all of them from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr,
from ʿAbdullāh,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"If only one day of this world remained,
Zāʾidah said in his narration:
"Allah would lengthen that day." Then they agreed:
"until He sends in it a man from me," or:
"from the people of my house, whose name matches my name and whose father's name matches my father's name."
In the narration of Fiṭr he added:
"He will fill the earth with fairness and justice as it was filled with injustice and oppression."
And in the narration of Sufyān he said:
"The world will not pass away," or "will not come to an end, until a man from the people of my house rules over the Arabs, whose name matches my name."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ ordered the trench to be dug, a rock came in their way and blocked them from digging. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, took the pickaxe, and laid his cloak aside at the edge of the trench, and said:
"The word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. None can change His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."
A third of the rock broke off while Salmān al-Fārisī stood watching, and a flash of light shone with the strike of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he struck a second time and said:
"The word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. None can change His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."
The next third broke off, and a flash shone, which Salmān saw. Then he struck the third time and said:
"The word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. None can change His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."
The remaining third broke off. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out, took his cloak, and sat down.
Salmān said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw you: whenever you struck a blow, a flash of light came with it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"O Salmān, did you see that?"
He said: "Yes, by the One who sent you with the truth, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"When I made the first strike, the cities of Chosroes and what surrounds them were raised before me, along with many other cities, until I saw them with my own eyes."
Those of his Companions who were present said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to give us victory over them, to grant us their lands as spoils, and to ruin their countries at our hands."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for that.
"Then I made the second strike, and the cities of Caesar and what surrounds them were raised before me, until I saw them with my own eyes."
They said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to give us victory over them, to grant us their lands as spoils, and to ruin their countries at our hands."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for that.
"Then I made the third strike, and the cities of Abyssinia were raised before me,
and the villages around them, until I saw them with my own eyes."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Leave the Abyssinians alone so long as they leave you alone, and leave the Turks alone so long as they leave you alone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In Sūrat an-Naḥl: "Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief—except one who is compelled" up to His saying "for them is a great punishment"; this was abrogated and an exception was made, for He said: "Then indeed your Lord, to those who emigrated after they had been persecuted, then struggled and were patient—indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful." This refers to ʿAbdullāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ, who was governor of Egypt. He used to write for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but Satan caused him to slip and he joined the disbelievers. So the Prophet ﷺ ordered that he be killed on the day of the Conquest, but ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān sought protection for him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted him protection.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
came to the Prophet ﷺ and confessed to adultery. He gave orders concerning her, and her clothes were tied tightly around her. Then he had her stoned, and then he prayed over her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah was brought to ʿUthmān after people had testified against him, he said to ʿAlī: "Take your cousin and carry out the punishment on him."
So ʿAlī flogged him and said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave forty lashes, Abū Bakr gave forty, and ʿUmar gave eighty, and each is a sunnah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And I only know it is from Abū Burdah,
from Abū Mūsā,
who said: A group of the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār disagreed about this. The Anṣār said: Ghusl is not obligatory except [when there is] ejaculation or [emission of] fluid.
And the Muhājirūn said: Rather, when [the two] have intercourse, ghusl has become obligatory.
Abū Mūsā said: I will settle this for you.
So I got up and asked permission to see ʿĀʾishah, and she permitted me. I said to her: O Mother, or: O Mother of the Believers, I want to ask you about something, but I am shy before you.
She said: Do not be shy to ask me about what you would ask your mother who gave birth to you, for I am your mother.
I said: What makes ghusl obligatory? She said: You have asked one who is well informed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When he sits between her four limbs and the circumcised part touches the circumcised part, ghusl has become obligatory."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said that a man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a man who has intercourse with his wife and then does not ejaculate: is ghusl required for them both? ʿĀʾishah was sitting [there].
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I do that, I and this one, and then we perform ghusl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, [reported] the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I bear witness that I used to roast the belly of a sheep for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then he would pray and not perform wuḍūʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered his garments around him, then went out to prayer. He was brought a gift of bread and meat, so he ate three morsels, then led the people in prayer, and he did not touch water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Should I perform wuḍūʾ after eating sheep meat? He said:
"If you wish, perform wuḍūʾ, and if you wish, do not."
He asked: Should I perform wuḍūʾ after eating camel meat? He said:
"Yes, perform wuḍūʾ after eating camel meat."
He asked: May I pray in sheep pens? He said: "Yes."
He asked: May I pray in camel resting places? He said: "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw ʿAlī ibn Waʿlah as-Sabaʾī wearing a fur garment, and I touched it. He said: Why do you touch it? I asked ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās; I said: We are in the West, and with us are Berbers and Zoroastrians. We are brought a ram that they have slaughtered, though we do not eat their slaughtered animals, and they bring us waterskins in which they put fat.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: We asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and he said: "Its tanning is its purification."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would raid when dawn broke, and he would listen for the call to prayer. If he heard a call to prayer, he held back; otherwise he raided. He heard a man say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "[He is] upon the natural religion (fiṭrah)."
Then [the man] said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah; I bear witness that there is no god but Allah.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You have come out of the Fire."
They looked, and he was a goatherd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Satan hears the call to prayer, he goes away until he is at [a place like] ar-Rawḥāʾ."
Sulaymān said: I asked him about ar-Rawḥāʾ.
He said: It is thirty-six miles from Medina.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father sent me to Banū Ḥārithah. He said: And with me was a boy of ours, or a companion of ours. A caller called him by name from an orchard wall. He said: The one with me looked over the wall and saw nothing. I mentioned that to my father, and he said: Had I known you would meet this, I would not have sent you. But when you hear a voice, call the adhān for prayer, for I heard Abū Hurayrah narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said:
"When the call to prayer is made, Satan turns away, passing wind loudly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah
used to say the takbīr in prayer whenever he rose and whenever he lowered himself.
We said: O Abū Hurayrah, what is this takbīr? He said: It is indeed the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said — and a transfer of chain: Muḥammad ibn Rāfiʿ narrated to me:
ʿAbd ar-Razzāq narrated to us:
Ibn Jurayj informed us:
al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Yaʿqūb informed me
that Abū as-Sāʾib,
the freed slave of Banū ʿAbdullāh ibn Hishām ibn Zuhrah, informed him that he
heard Abū Hurayrah
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever performs a prayer in which he does not recite the Mother of the Qurʾān (al-Fātiḥah)..."
[the narration continues] like the hadith of Sufyān, and in both of their narrations:
"Allah the Exalted said: I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves; half of it is for Me and half of it is for My servant."
label: machine translation

segments_en: By Allah, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī advanced to meet Muʿāwiyah with battalions like mountains. ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said, "I see battalions that will not turn back until they have killed their opponents."

Muʿāwiyah said to him—and by Allah he was the better of the two men—"O ʿAmr, if these kill those and those kill these, who will be left for me to take care of the affairs of the people? Who will look after their women,
who will look after their livelihoods?" So he sent to him two men of Quraysh from Banū ʿAbd Shams, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samurah and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Kurayz,
and said, "Go to this man, put a proposal to him, speak to him, and ask of him." So they went to him,
entered upon him, spoke, said to him [what they had been told], and asked of him.
Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī said to them, "We are the sons of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib;
we have received some of this wealth,
and this nation has been rampant in shedding its own blood."
They said, "He offers you such and such, and he asks and requests of you."
He said, "Who will guarantee this for me?" They said, "We will guarantee it for you."
He asked them for nothing but that they said, "We will guarantee it for you." So he made peace with him.
Al-Ḥasan [al-Baṣrī] said: I heard Abū Bakrah say: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the pulpit with al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī at his side,
and he would turn to the people at one moment and to him at another, and say:
"This son of mine is a master,
and perhaps Allah will use him to reconcile two great groups of the Muslims."
ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdullāh said to me: The hearing of al-Ḥasan from Abū Bakrah was established for us only through this ḥadīth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in any expedition he undertook until the expedition of Tabūk, except Badr. The Prophet ﷺ did not reproach anyone who stayed behind from Badr; he had only set out seeking the caravan, but Quraysh marched out to defend their caravan, and they met without an appointment, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said. By my life, the most honorable of the battles of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among the people is Badr, yet I would not wish to have been present at it instead of my pledge on the night of al-ʿAqabah, when we made a covenant on Islam. After that I never stayed behind from the Prophet ﷺ until the expedition of Tabūk, which was the last expedition he undertook, and the Prophet ﷺ gave permission for departure.

He then mentioned the ḥadīth at length. He said: I went to the Prophet ﷺ, and he was sitting in the mosque with the Muslims around him, and his face was shining like the shining of the moon; when he was pleased with something, his face would shine. I came and sat in front of him, and he said:
"Rejoice, O Kaʿb ibn Mālik, in the best day that has come upon you since your mother bore you."
I said, "O Prophet of Allah, is it from Allah or from you?" He said:
"Rather, it is from Allah."
Then he recited these verses:

"Certainly Allah has turned in mercy to the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship" until he reached "Allah is the Oft-Returning, the Merciful." He said: And it was also revealed concerning us:

"Fear Allah and be with the truthful." He said: I said, "O Prophet of Allah, part of my repentance is that I speak only the truth, and that I divest myself of all my wealth as charity to Allah and His Messenger." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Keep some of your wealth for yourself; that is better for you."

I said, "Then I will keep my share at Khaybar." He said: Allah has not bestowed on me any blessing after Islam greater in my estimation than my truthfulness to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when I told him the truth—I and my two companions—so that we did not lie and perish as those [others] perished. And I hope that Allah has not tested anyone in truthfulness as He has tested me. I have not deliberately told a lie since, and I hope that Allah will protect me in what remains [of my life].

He said: This ḥadīth has also been narrated from al-Zuhrī with an isnād different from this one. It has also been said [that it is] from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, from his uncle ʿUbaydullāh, from Kaʿb, and something other than this has also been said. Yūnus ibn Yazīd narrated this ḥadīth from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, that his father narrated to him from Kaʿb ibn Mālik.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions:

"Is there no one who will strive for Paradise? For Paradise has no equal, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah. It is a radiant light, a fragrant plant that sways, a lofty palace, a flowing river, abundant ripe fruit, a beautiful and lovely wife, and many garments, in an eternal abode, in joy and splendor, in a lofty, safe and magnificent dwelling."
They said, "We are the ones who will strive for it, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"Say: If Allah wills."
Then he mentioned jihād and urged them to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no one whom Allah admits into Paradise but that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, marries him to seventy-two wives: two of the ḥūr al-ʿīn, and seventy from his inheritance from the people of the Fire. There is not one of them but she has a desirable front, and he has a member that never goes limp."
Hishām ibn Khālid said: "From his inheritance from the people of the Fire" means men who entered the Fire, so the people of Paradise inherited their wives, just as the wife of Pharaoh was inherited.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is none among you but he has two abodes: an abode in Paradise and an abode in the Fire. When he dies and enters the Fire, the people of Paradise inherit his abode. That is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: {It is they who are the inheritors.}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Seven categories are forbidden through lineage,
and seven through marriage.
Then he recited: {Forbidden to you are your mothers...} [the verse].
ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar married together the daughter of ʿAlī and the wife of ʿAlī.
Ibn Sīrīn said: There is no harm in it.
Al-Ḥasan disliked it at first, then said: There is no harm in it.
Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī married two paternal cousins in one night,
and Jābir ibn Zayd disliked it because of the severing of family ties,

though there is no prohibition in it, because of the saying of the Exalted: {And lawful for you is whatever lies beyond that}. ʿIkrimah reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: If a man commits fornication with his wife's sister, his wife does not become forbidden to him.
It is narrated from Yaḥyā al-Kindī, from ash-Shaʿbī and Abū Jaʿfar,
concerning one who acts indecently with a boy, [that] if he penetrates him,
he must not marry the boy's mother,
but this Yaḥyā is not well known,
and he was not corroborated in this.
ʿIkrimah said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: If he commits fornication with her, his wife does not become forbidden to him.
It is mentioned from Abū Naṣr that Ibn ʿAbbās declared it forbidden.
But this Abū Naṣr is not known to have heard from Ibn ʿAbbās.
It is narrated from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, Jābir ibn Zayd, al-Ḥasan, and some of the people of Iraq that she becomes forbidden to him.
Abū Hurayrah said: She does not become forbidden until he clings to the ground, meaning until he has intercourse.
Ibn al-Musayyib, ʿUrwah, and az-Zuhrī permitted it.
Az-Zuhrī said: ʿAlī said: She does not become forbidden. And this is a mursal report.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade a woman to be married together with her paternal aunt, or a woman with her maternal aunt.
So we consider the maternal aunt of one's father to be in the same position,
because ʿUrwah narrated to me from ʿĀʾishah,
that she said: Treat as forbidden through nursing what is forbidden through lineage.
label: machine translation

segments_en: So he permitted it, and a freed slave of his said to him: That was only in times of hardship, when women were few, or words to that effect.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Yes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
"Any man and woman who agree [to a temporary marriage], their arrangement between them is three nights; if they wish to extend it or to part ways, they may do so."
I do not know whether that was specific to us or for people in general.
label: machine translation

segments_en: {in what you hint at...} He says: I wish to marry,
and I would love for a righteous woman to be made easy for me.
Al-Qāsim said: He says: You are dear to me,
and I have a desire for you,
and Allah will drive good toward you,
or something like this.
ʿAṭāʾ said: He hints and does not speak openly. He says: I have a need, and receive good news,
and you, praise be to Allah, are in demand.
She says: I hear what you say,
but she does not promise anything, and her guardian must not make a promise without her knowledge,
and if she promises a man during her waiting period and he then marries her afterward, they are not separated.
Al-Ḥasan said: {Do not make a secret promise to them} means fornication.
It is mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbās: {until the prescribed term reaches its end} means until the waiting period is completed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ḥafṣah bint ʿUmar was widowed from Ibn Ḥudhāfah as-Sahmī, who was among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, of those who fought at Badr, and who died in Madinah, ʿUmar said: I met ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān and offered Ḥafṣah to him. I said: If you wish, I will marry Ḥafṣah to you.
He said: I will think about my matter.
I waited some nights, then he met me and said: It has become clear to me that I should not marry at this time.
ʿUmar said: Then I met Abū Bakr and said: If you wish, I will marry Ḥafṣah to you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that it was revealed about him. He said: I gave a sister of mine in marriage to a man, and he divorced her.
Then when her waiting period ended, he came to propose to her again.
I said to him: I married her to you, made her your bedfellow, and honored you, and you divorced her,
and then you come to propose to her again?
No, by Allah, she will never return to you.
He was a man in whom there was no fault, and the woman wished to return to him. So Allah revealed this verse: {Do not prevent them}. I said: Now I will do it, O Messenger of Allah.
He said: So he married her to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said, transmitting from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Beware of suspicion,
for suspicion is the most false of speech. Do not spy, do not search for faults, do not hate one another, and be brothers."
And a man must not propose over the proposal of his brother until he marries or gives it up.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar said: I met Abū Bakr and said: If you wish, I will marry Ḥafṣah bint ʿUmar to you.

I waited some nights, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to her. Then Abū Bakr met me and said: Nothing prevented me from replying to you about what you offered except that I knew the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had mentioned her, and I would not disclose the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Had he left her, I would have accepted her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to a man:
"Marry, even if with an iron ring."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There were some women of the Anṣār in the house, and they said: With goodness and blessing,
and with the best of fortune.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Rabīʿah and ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣafwān entered, and I was with them,
upon Umm Salamah, the Mother of the Believers, and they asked her about the army that is swallowed by the earth. That was in the days of Ibn al-Zubayr. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A person seeking refuge will take refuge at the House, so an army will be sent against him, and when they are in an open desert of the land, they will be swallowed up."
I said: O Messenger of Allah, what about the one who was unwilling? He said:
"He will be swallowed up along with them, but he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection according to his intention."
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is the desert of Madīnah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A people will seek refuge at this House - meaning the Kaʿbah - who have no strength, no numbers and no equipment. An army will be sent against them, until when they are in an open desert of the land, they will be swallowed up."
Yūsuf said: The people of Syria at that time were marching toward Makkah. ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣafwān said: By Allah, this is not that army.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ moved about in his sleep, so we said: O Messenger of Allah, you did something in your sleep that you do not usually do. He said:
"It is amazing that some people of my nation will head for the House after a man of Quraysh who has taken refuge at the House, until when they are in the open desert, they will be swallowed up."
We said: O Messenger of Allah, the road may gather all kinds of people. He said:

"Yes, among them will be the one who acts with clear insight, the one who is compelled, and the traveler. They will perish in one destruction but will come out from it in different ways. Allah will resurrect them according to their intentions."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Shaḥḥām said: I set out with Farqad al-Sabakhī,

to Muslim ibn Abī Bakrah, who was on his land. We entered upon him and said: Have you heard your father narrate anything about trials? He said: Yes, I heard Abū Bakrah narrate. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There will be trials. Indeed, then there will be a trial in which the one sitting is better than the one walking, and the one walking in it is better than the one running toward it. Indeed, when it descends or occurs, whoever has camels should join his camels, whoever has sheep should join his sheep, and whoever has land should join his land."
He said: A man said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you think about someone who has no camels, no sheep and no land? He said:
"He should take his sword and strike its edge against a stone, then let him escape if he is able to escape. O Allah, have I conveyed? O Allah, have I conveyed? O Allah, have I conveyed?"

He said: A man said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if I am forced to go to one of the two lines or one of the two groups, and a man strikes me with his sword or an arrow comes and kills me? He said:
"He will bear his sin and your sin, and will be among the people of the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among a group of his Companions and passed by the mosque of Banū Muʿāwiyah.
[The rest is] like the hadith of Ibn Numayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say: Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān said: By Allah, I am the most knowledgeable of people about every trial that will occur between me and the Hour. It is not that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ confided something to me about that which he told no one else, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was speaking in a gathering in which I was present about trials, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while enumerating the trials, said:
"Among them are three that will hardly leave anything, and among them are trials like the summer winds, some small and some great."
Ḥudhayfah said: All of those men have gone except me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed me of what will happen until the Hour is established. There is nothing of it that I did not ask him about, except that I did not ask him what will make the people of Madīnah leave Madīnah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the dawn prayer, then ascended the pulpit and addressed us until the time of Ẓuhr came. He descended and prayed, then ascended the pulpit and addressed us until the time of ʿAṣr came. Then he descended and prayed, then ascended the pulpit and addressed us until the sun set. He informed us of what had been and what will be. The most knowledgeable of us is the one who best memorized it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were at al-Mirbad when a man with disheveled hair came, holding a piece of red tanned leather. We said, "It seems you are from the desert people." He said, "Yes."
We said, "Hand us this piece of leather that is in your hand." So he handed it to us, and we read it, and in it was written:

"From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to the Banū Zuhayr ibn Uqaysh: If you bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and you establish prayer, give zakāh, and pay the fifth of the war booty, together with the share of the Prophet ﷺ and the share of the ṣafī, then you are secure under the protection of Allah and His Messenger."
We said, "Who wrote this document for you?" He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf used to satirize the Prophet ﷺ and incite the disbelievers of Quraysh against him. When the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, its people were a mixture: among them were Muslims, polytheists who worshipped idols, and Jews, and they used to harm the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Prophet to be patient and forgiving, and about them Allah revealed: {And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you...} [to the end of] the verse. Then, when Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf refused to cease harming the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ ordered Saʿd ibn Muʿādh to send a group to kill him, so he sent Muhammad ibn Maslamah, and he mentioned the story of his killing. When they had killed him, the Jews and the polytheists were alarmed, and in the morning they went to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "Our companion was attacked at night and killed."

So the Prophet ﷺ reminded them of what he used to say, and the Prophet ﷺ called them to have a document written between him and them, by which they would abide. So the Prophet ﷺ wrote a charter between himself, them, and the Muslims in general.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had defeated Quraysh at Badr and came to Medina, he gathered the Jews in the marketplace of Banū Qaynuqāʿ and said:
"O company of Jews, accept Islam before there befalls you what befell Quraysh."

They said, "O Muhammad, do not let yourself be deluded because you killed a few men of Quraysh who were inexperienced and did not know how to fight. If you were to fight us, you would know that we are the [real] men, and that you have never met the like of us."

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning that: {Say to those who disbelieve: You will be overcome}. Muṣarrif recited up to His saying: {a company fighting in the cause of Allah}, at Badr, {and another disbelieving}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥayyiṣah [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whichever of the Jewish men you gain power over, kill him."

So Muḥayyiṣah leapt upon Shubayyah, a man among the Jewish merchants who used to associate with them, and killed him. At that time Ḥuwayyiṣah had not yet accepted Islam, and he was older than Muḥayyiṣah. When he had killed him, Ḥuwayyiṣah began to strike him and say, "O enemy of Allah! By Allah, much of the fat in your belly is from his wealth!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: "Ever since I could understand, my parents were following the religion [of Islam],
and not a day passed but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would visit us at both ends of the day, morning and evening.
When the Muslims were put to trial, Abū Bakr set out as an emigrant toward the land of Abyssinia.
When he reached Barkal-Ghimād, Ibn ad-Daghinah, the chief of the Qārah tribe, met him.
He said, "Where are you going, Abū Bakr?" Abū Bakr said, "My people have driven me out,
so I wish to travel through the land and worship my Lord."
Ibn ad-Daghinah said, "A man like you, Abū Bakr, should not leave and should not be driven out.
You earn for the destitute,
maintain the ties of kinship, bear the burden of the weak, honor the guest,
and help in the misfortunes that befall people in the cause of truth.
I am your protector.
Go back and worship your Lord in your own town."
So he returned, and Ibn ad-Daghinah traveled with him.
In the evening Ibn ad-Daghinah went around to the nobles of Quraysh
and said to them, "A man like Abū Bakr should not leave and should not be driven out.
Would you drive out a man who earns for the destitute, maintains the ties of kinship, bears the burden of the weak, and honors the guest,
and helps in the misfortunes that befall people in the cause of truth?" Quraysh did not reject Ibn ad-Daghinah's protection,
and they said to Ibn ad-Daghinah, "Tell Abū Bakr to worship his Lord in his house,
to pray there and recite whatever he wishes,
and not to harm us with that,
nor to make it public,
for we fear that he will tempt our women and children."
Ibn ad-Daghinah told that to Abū Bakr,
and Abū Bakr stayed like that, worshipping his Lord in his house,
not making his prayer public,
and not reciting in any place other than his house.
Then it occurred to Abū Bakr to build a mosque in the courtyard of his house, and he used to pray in it and recite the Qurʾān.
The women and children of the polytheists would crowd around him,
marveling at him and looking at him.
Abū Bakr was a man who wept a great deal;
he could not hold back his tears when he recited the Qurʾān.
That alarmed the nobles of Quraysh among the polytheists,
so they sent for Ibn ad-Daghinah, and he came to them.
They said, "We gave Abū Bakr protection through your pledge
on condition that he worship his Lord in his house,
but he has overstepped that,
and built a mosque in the courtyard of his house,
and made his prayer and recitation public in it.
We fear that he will tempt our women and children, so stop him.
If he is willing to confine himself to worshipping his Lord in his house, he may do so,
but if he refuses and insists on making it public, then ask him to return your pledge of protection to you,
for we dislike breaking our agreement with you,
and we cannot let Abū Bakr proclaim [his worship] openly."
ʿĀʾishah said: Ibn ad-Daghinah came to Abū Bakr and said, "You know the terms on which I made the agreement with you,
so either confine yourself to that,
or return to me my pledge of protection,
for I do not like the Arabs to hear that I broke an agreement made on behalf of a man."
Abū Bakr said, "I return to you your protection, and I am content with the protection of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."
At that time the Prophet ﷺ was in Makkah,
and the Prophet ﷺ said to the Muslims,
"I have been shown the abode of your emigration: a land of date palms between two rocky tracts." These are the two lava fields.
So those who emigrated did so toward Madinah,
and most of those who had emigrated to the land of Abyssinia returned to Madinah,
and Abū Bakr also prepared to go to Madinah.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Wait a while,
for I hope that I will be given permission."
Abū Bakr said, "Do you hope for that, may my father be your ransom?" He said, "Yes."
So Abū Bakr held himself back for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in order to accompany him,
and he fed two riding camels that he had with samur leaves, that is, khabat, for four months.

Ibn Shihāb said that ʿUrwah said that ʿĀʾishah said: One day, while we were sitting in the house of Abū Bakr at midday, someone said to Abū Bakr, "Here is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with his head covered, at an hour when he did not usually come to us." Abū Bakr said, "May my father and mother be his ransom!
By Allah, nothing but a matter of importance has brought him at this hour."
She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and asked permission to enter,
and he was given permission, so he entered.
The Prophet ﷺ said to Abū Bakr,
"Send away those who are with you."
Abū Bakr said, "They are only your family, may my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"I have been given permission to depart."
Abū Bakr said, "Together, may my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah?"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Yes."
Abū Bakr said, "Then take one of these two camels of mine, may my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "For the price."
ʿĀʾishah said: We prepared them with the utmost haste for the journey,
and we made a food bag for them in a leather pouch,
and Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr cut a piece from her waistband and tied the mouth of the pouch with it,
and for that she was called Dhāt an-Niṭāq. She said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abū Bakr reached a cave on Mount Thawr and hid in it for three nights.
ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr, a young man who was sharp and quick to learn, would spend the night with them,
and leave them before dawn,
and be with Quraysh in Makkah in the morning as if he had spent the night there.
He would not hear of any plot against them without retaining it,
until he brought them the news of it when darkness fell.
ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayrah, the freed slave of Abū Bakr, would graze a milch flock of sheep for them,
and bring it to them when an hour of the night had passed,
and they would spend the night with fresh milk, which is the milk of their milch animals, and their milk heated with hot stones,
until ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayrah drove the flock away in the darkness before dawn.
He did that on each of those three nights.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abū Bakr hired a man from Banū ad-Dīl,
from Banū ʿAbd ibn ʿAdī, as a skilled guide (the khirrīt is the one expert in guiding), who had dipped his hand in a pact of alliance with the family of al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil as-Sahmī,
and he was on the religion of the disbelievers of Quraysh. They trusted him,
and entrusted their two camels to him,
and arranged to meet him at the cave of Thawr after three nights, with their two camels, on the morning of the third day.
ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayrah and the guide set off with them, and the guide took them along the coastal route."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ wanted to wipe Usāmah's nasal mucus away. ʿĀʾishah said, "Leave it to me, leave it to me, so that I may be the one to do it." He said,
"O ʿĀʾishah, love him, for I love him."
This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when ʿAlī and al-ʿAbbās came asking permission to enter. They said, "O Usāmah, ask permission for us from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
So I said, "O Messenger of Allah, ʿAlī and al-ʿAbbās are asking permission to enter." He said,
"Do you know what has brought them?"
I said, "I do not know." The Prophet ﷺ said, "But I know."
So he permitted them, and they entered and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we have come to ask you: which of your family is dearest to you?" He said,
"Fāṭimah, the daughter of Muḥammad."
They said, "We did not come to ask you about your family." He said,
"The dearest of my family to me are those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor and upon whom I have bestowed favor: Usāmah ibn Zayd."
They said, "Then who?" He said,
"Then ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib."
Al-ʿAbbās said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have placed your uncle last of them?" He said,
"Because ʿAlī preceded you in migrating."
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
Shuʿbah used to regard ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah as weak.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he saw Jibrīl, peace be upon him, twice, and the Prophet ﷺ made supplication for him twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made supplication for me twice that Allah would grant me wisdom.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw a lamp in the house of az-Zubayr and said,
"O ʿĀʾishah, I do not see but that Asmāʾ has given birth. Do not name him until I name him."
So he named him ʿAbdullāh and softened a date and rubbed it on the baby's palate with his own hand.
This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me a kunyah after a vegetable that I used to pick.
This is a gharīb hadith that we know only through this route, from the hadith of Jābir al-Juʿfī, from Abū Naṣr.
Abū Naṣr is Khaythamah ibn Abī Khaythamah al-Baṣrī, who narrated several hadith from Anas.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas ibn Mālik said to me, "O Thābit, take from me, for you will not take from anyone more reliable than me. I took it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it from Jibrīl, and Jibrīl took it from Allah, the Exalted."
This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith that we know only from the hadith of Zayd ibn Ḥubāb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Abū al-ʿĀliyah, "Did Anas hear

from the Prophet ﷺ?" He said, "He served him for ten years, and the Prophet ﷺ made supplication for him. He had an orchard that bore fruit twice a year, and in it was a sweet basil from which one could smell the scent of musk."
This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
Abū Khaldah's name is Khālid ibn Dīnār, and he is trustworthy according to the people of hadith. He met Anas ibn Mālik and narrated from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and spread my garment before him. Then he took it and gathered it over my heart, and after that I never forgot a hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [They said] to Abū Hurayrah, "O Abū Hurayrah, you were the one who stayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ most among us and memorized his hadith best."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh and said, "O Abū Muḥammad, what do you think of this Yemeni, meaning Abū Hurayrah? Is he more knowledgeable about the hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than you, so that we hear from him what we do not hear from you? Or does he attribute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what he did not say?"

He said, "As for his having heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what we did not hear, I have no doubt that he heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what we did not hear. That is because he was a poor man who had nothing, a guest of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his hand with the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while we were people of houses and wealth, and we would come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only at the two ends of the day. So we have no doubt that he heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what we did not hear. And we do not find anyone with any good in him who would attribute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what he did not say."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said, "From which people are you?"
I said, "From Daws." He said,
"I never thought there was anyone with any good in Daws."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām to buy a sacrificial animal for him for a dīnār. He bought a sacrificial animal and made a profit of a dīnār on it, so he bought another in its place. He then brought the sacrificial animal and the dīnār to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Sacrifice the sheep, and give the dīnār in charity (ṣadaqah)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We had some wine belonging to an orphan. When [the sūrah of] al-Māʾidah was revealed, I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it and said, "It belongs to an orphan." He said, "Pour it out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do not go out to meet the [incoming] caravans to trade, do not leave animals unmilked to make them look full, and do not bid up prices against one another [merely to deceive]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the two parties to a sale disagree, the statement of the seller is accepted, and the buyer has the choice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
from Kilāb asked the Prophet ﷺ about the stud fee for a male animal, and he forbade him. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, we lend out the male animal for breeding and are given a gift in return."
So he permitted him to accept a gift.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Except for a hunting dog.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the freed slave of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Umāmah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:
"Do not sell singing girls, do not buy them, and do not teach them. There is no good in trading in them, and their price is unlawful."
It was regarding something like this that this verse was revealed to him:
"And among the people is he who buys idle talk to mislead [others] from the path of Allah..." to the end of the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever separates a mother from her child, Allah will separate him from his loved ones on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to throw stones at the date palms of the Anṣār, so they caught me and took me to the Prophet ﷺ. He said:
"O Rāfiʿ, why do you throw stones at their palms?"
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, [because of] hunger." He said:
"Do not throw stones, but eat what falls. May Allah fill your stomach and quench your thirst."
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb ḥadīth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Prophet of Allah, I bought wine for some orphans in my care." He said:
"Pour out the wine and break the jars."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade muḥāqalah and muzābanah, except that he permitted the people of ʿarāyā to sell it for an equivalent amount by estimate.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever gives respite to one in difficulty or waives [the debt] for him, Allah will shade him on the Day of Resurrection beneath the shade of His Throne, on the day when there is no shade except His shade."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed Allah loves the one who is lenient when selling, lenient when buying, and lenient when settling a debt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah forgave a man who lived before you, who was easygoing when he sold, easygoing when he bought, and easygoing when he demanded repayment."
He said: This is a ṣaḥīḥ ḥasan gharīb ḥadīth from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When you see someone selling or buying in the mosque, say: 'May Allah not bring you profit in your trade.' And when you see someone announcing a lost item in it, say: 'May Allah not return it to you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the people of Ḥimṣ, from Muʿādh,
from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed the most beloved of people to Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and the nearest of them to Him in position, is a just ruler; and the most hateful of people to Allah, and the farthest of them from Him in position, is an unjust ruler."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"When two men bring a dispute to you, do not judge in favor of the first until you hear the words of the other; then you will know how to judge."
ʿAlī said: I have continued to be a judge ever since.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr ibn Murrah said to Muʿāwiyah, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'There is no ruler who shuts his door against those in need, want, and poverty, except that Allah shuts the doors of the heavens against his own need, want, and poverty.'"
So Muʿāwiyah appointed a man to attend to people's needs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from the Prophet ﷺ, [narrated] something like this ḥadīth with the same meaning.
Yazīd ibn Abī Maryam is Syrian, Burayd ibn Abī Maryam is Kūfan, and Abū Maryam is ʿAmr ibn Murrah al-Juhanī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Yemen. When I had set out, he sent someone after me and I was brought back. He said:

"Do you know why I sent for you? Do not take anything without my permission, for it is misappropriation [of war spoils], and whoever misappropriates will come on the Day of Resurrection with what he misappropriated. It was for this that I called you. Now go on to your work."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about a man who deliberately killed a believer, then repented, believed, did righteous deeds, and then was guided.
He said: "Woe to him! How could he be guided? I heard your Prophet ﷺ say:
'On the Day of Resurrection the killer and the slain will come, with the slain holding onto the head of his killer, saying: My Lord, ask this one why he killed me.'
By Allah, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed it to your Prophet, and He did not abrogate it after He revealed it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever changes his religion, kill him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When two Muslims confront each other with their swords, each of them wanting to kill his companion, both of them are in the Fire."
It was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the killer, but what is the matter with the one who is killed?" He said:
"He was eager to kill his companion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, raising his voice, commanding the killing of dogs, and dogs were being killed, except a hunting dog or a dog for livestock.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to eat horse meat during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us to sacrifice an animal with its ear cut from the front, or cut from the back, or split lengthwise, or with a hole in its ear, or with its ear cut off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by one of the houses of the Anṣār and noticed the smell of roasting meat, and he said:
"Who is it who slaughtered?"
A man from among us came out to him and said: "I did, O Messenger of Allah. I slaughtered before I prayed, so that I could feed my family and my neighbors."
So he commanded him to repeat it.
He said: "No, by Allah, besides Whom there is no god, I have only a young goat of one year or a lamb of sheep." He said:
"Slaughter it, but a young goat of one year will not suffice for anyone after you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A wolf
tore at a sheep, so they slaughtered it with a sharp stone, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted them to eat it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, we will meet the enemy tomorrow and we have no knives."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whatever causes the blood to flow and has the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned over it, eat it, as long as it is not a tooth or a nail. I will tell you about that: as for the tooth, it is a bone, and as for the nail, it is the knife of the Abyssinians."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever sells fruit and it is struck by a calamity, let him not take from his brother anything. On what basis would one of you consume the wealth of his Muslim brother?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Before the Hijrah, I sold a pair of trousers to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he weighed out the price for me and gave me more than due.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ borrowed from him thirty or forty thousand when he went out on the campaign of Ḥunayn. When he returned, he repaid it to him, and then the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"May Allah bless you in your family and your wealth. The reward for a loan is only repayment and praise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Maymūnah was taking on debt, and some of her family said to her: "Do not do that," disapproving of it. She said: "Rather, I heard my Prophet and my intimate friend ﷺ say:
'There is no Muslim who takes on a debt, and Allah knows that he intends to repay it, except that Allah will repay it for him in this world.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah admitted a man to Paradise because he was easygoing as a seller and as a buyer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have land in which no one has any partnership or share, except the neighbor."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The neighbor has more right to what is near him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the killer of his relative, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Pardon him." He refused. He said: "Take your blood money." He refused. He said:
"Go and kill him, for you would be like him."
He said: So the man caught up with him, and it was said to him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said:
"Kill him, for you would be like him." So he let him go.
He said: Then he was seen dragging his strap, going to his family.
He said: It was as if he had bound him.
Abū ʿUmayr said in his narration: Ibn Shawdhab said, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim:
After the Prophet ﷺ, no one may say:
"Kill him, for you would be like him."
Ibn Mājah said: This is the hadith of the people of Ramlah; it is found only with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Māʿiz al-Aslamī came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "He has committed adultery."
He turned away from him. Then he came from the other side and said, "O Messenger of Allah, he has committed adultery."
He turned away from him. Then he came from the other side and said, "O Messenger of Allah, he has committed adultery."

On the fourth time he gave the order concerning him, and he was taken out to the lava plain (al-Ḥarrah) and stoned with rocks. When he felt the touch of the stones, he fled at a run until he passed a man who had the jawbone of a camel; he struck him with it, and the people struck him until he died. They mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he had fled when he felt the touch of the stones and the touch of death. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Why did you not leave him?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no cutting of the hand for one who betrays a trust, nor for one who plunders, nor for one who snatches."
Ibn Jurayj also did not hear it from Abū al-Zubayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman was forced [into intercourse] in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ averted the prescribed punishment from her and carried it out on the man who had assaulted her. He did not mention that he awarded her a dowry.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The thing I fear most for my Ummah is the act of the people of Lūṭ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Kill snakes, and kill the one with two stripes and the tailless one, for they take away eyesight and cause pregnant women to miscarry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"No deed a son of Adam does on the Day of Sacrifice is more beloved to Allah than shedding blood [in sacrifice]. It will come on the Day of Resurrection with its horns, its hair, and its hooves, and the blood reaches a place with Allah before it falls on the ground, so be glad in heart about it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī, "How were the sacrificial animals among you in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "In the time of the Prophet ﷺ a man would sacrifice one sheep on behalf of himself and his household; they would eat from it and feed others. Then people began to boast, and it became as you see."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
asked Ibn ʿUmar about the sacrificial animal,
whether it was obligatory. He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sacrificed, and the Muslims [did too]."
The man repeated it to him, and he said, "Do you understand? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sacrificed, and the Muslims [did too]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ at al-Ḥudaybiyah to ask him about the meat of the sacrificial animals, and I heard him say:
"For a boy, two sheep, and for a girl, one sheep. It does not harm you whether they are male or female."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whenever something came to the Prophet ﷺ that pleased him or made him glad, he would fall down in prostration in thanks to Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever commits open plunder is not one of us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever spends something in the cause of Allah, it is recorded for him sevenfold hundreds [seven hundred times over]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: No one weeps out of fear of Allah and is then fed to the Fire until milk returns to the udder; and the dust of the cause of Allah and the smoke of Hell will never gather in the nostrils of a Muslim.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The martyr has six privileges with Allah: he is forgiven with the first drop of his blood; he is shown his place in Paradise; he is protected from the punishment of the grave; he is safe from the greatest terror; the crown of dignity is placed on his head, a single ruby of which is better than the world and what is in it; he is married to seventy-two wives of the ḥūr al-ʿīn; and he is permitted to intercede for seventy of his relatives."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever meets Allah with no mark from the cause of Allah will meet Allah with a flaw in him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The banner
of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was black, and his flag was white.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The best horse is the jet-black one with a blaze and a white upper lip; then the one with a blaze and white legs, with the right foreleg unmarked. If it is not jet-black, then a dark bay with these markings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"The believers will be held back on the Day of Resurrection until they become distressed about it, and they will say, 'If only we could seek intercession with our Lord, so that He might relieve us from our place.'
So they will go to Adam and say, 'You are Adam, the father of mankind. Allah created you with His Hand, made you dwell in His Paradise,
made His angels prostrate to you,
and taught you the names of all things.
Intercede for us with your Lord, so that He may relieve us from this place of ours.'

He will say, 'I am not in that position.' And he will mention his error that he committed, eating from the tree though he had been forbidden from it. 'But go to Noah, the first prophet whom Allah sent to the people of the earth.'

So they will go to Noah, and he will say, 'I am not in that position,' and he will mention his error that he committed, asking his Lord without knowledge. 'But go to Abraham, the Intimate Friend of the Most Merciful.'

He said: So they will go to Abraham, and he will say, 'I am not in that position,' and he will mention three statements in which he spoke untruthfully. 'But go to Moses, a servant to whom Allah gave the Torah, whom He spoke to, and whom He drew near in intimate converse.'

He said: So they will go to Moses, and he will say, 'I am not in that position,' and he will mention his error that he committed, the killing of a person. 'But go to Jesus, the servant of Allah, His Messenger, His Spirit, and His Word.'
He said: So they will go to Jesus, and he will say, 'I am not in that position. But go to Muhammad ﷺ, a servant whose past and future sins Allah has forgiven.'
So they will come to me, and I will ask permission to enter upon my Lord in His abode, and I will be given permission.

When I see Him, I will fall down in prostration, and He will leave me as long as Allah wills. Then He will say, 'Raise your head, Muhammad. Speak, and you will be heard; intercede, and your intercession will be accepted;
ask, and you will be given.' He said: So I will raise my head and praise my Lord with a praise and glorification that He teaches me.
Then He will set a limit for me, and I will go out and admit them into Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people will certainly be touched by scorching from the Fire because of sins they committed, as a punishment,
then Allah will admit them into Paradise by the grace of His mercy. They will be called the Jahannamiyyūn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and the lame man.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Allah will say, 'O Adam.'
He will say, 'Here I am, at Your service, and Yours is all good.'
Then He will call out in a voice: 'Allah commands you to bring forth from your offspring a group to be sent to the Fire.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was never jealous of any woman as I was jealous of Khadījah,
and indeed his Lord had commanded him to give her the glad tidings of a house in Paradise.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and says: 'Who calls upon Me, that I may answer him?
Who asks of Me, that I may give him?
Who seeks My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Day of Resurrection comes, I will intercede,
and I will say, 'My Lord, admit into Paradise whoever has in his heart a mustard seed [of faith].' And they will enter.
Then I will say, 'Admit into Paradise whoever has in his heart the least thing [of faith].'"
Anas said: It is as though I am looking at the fingers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise,
and the last of the people of the Fire to come out of the Fire, is a man who will come out crawling. His Lord will say to him, 'Enter Paradise.'
He will say, 'My Lord, Paradise is full.'
He will say this to him three times, and each time he replies, 'Paradise is full.'
Then He will say, 'You will have the like of the world ten times over.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The believers will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection and will say, 'If only we could seek intercession with our Lord,
so that He might relieve us from this place of ours.'
So they will go to Adam and say to him, 'You are Adam, the father of mankind. Allah created you with His Hand, made the angels prostrate to you, and taught you the names of all things.
Intercede for us with our Lord so that He may relieve us.'
He will say to them, 'I am not in that position.'
And he will mention to them the error that he committed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Heraclius called his interpreter,
then called for the letter of the Prophet ﷺ and read it:
"In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the servant of Allah and His Messenger, to Heraclius.
'O People of the Book, come to a word that is equitable between us and you...'" — the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: People will emerge from the direction of the east and recite the Qur'an, but it will not go beyond their collarbones.
They will pass through the religion as an arrow passes through the game,
then they will not return to it until the arrow returns to its notch."
It was asked, "What is their sign?" He said, "Their sign is shaving [the head]," or he said, "shaving closely."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Maʿbad said what he said about the matter of divine decree, we disapproved of that.
He said: So Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥimyarī and I performed Hajj.
And they related the hadith with the same meaning as the hadith of Kahmas and its chain of narration.
In it there are some additions and omissions of a few words.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas said: We were forbidden in the Qur'an to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about anything.
And he related the hadith similarly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, with the like of this hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Mahdi is from my family, from the descendants of Fāṭimah."
ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū al-Malīḥ praising ʿAlī ibn Nufayl and mentioning his righteousness.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Mahdi is from me, with a broad, bright forehead and a high-bridged nose. He will fill the earth with justice and equity as it was filled with injustice and oppression. He will rule for seven years."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Umm Salamah], the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:

"There will be a dispute at the death of a caliph, and a man from the people of Medina will flee to Mecca. Some people from Mecca will come to him and bring him out while he is unwilling, and they will pledge allegiance to him between the Corner and the Station. An army will be sent against him from Syria, but it will be swallowed up by the earth in the desert between Mecca and Medina. When the people see that, the Abdāl of Syria and the companies of the people of Iraq will come to him and pledge allegiance to him between the Corner and the Station. Then a man from Quraysh will arise whose maternal uncles are from Kalb, and he will send an army against them, but they will prevail over them. That is the army of Kalb, and loss is for whoever does not witness the spoils of Kalb. He will divide the wealth and will deal with the people according to the Sunnah of their Prophet ﷺ, and Islam will settle firmly on the earth. He will remain for seven years, then he will die and the Muslims will pray over him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It is reported] from the Prophet ﷺ, in the story of the army swallowed by the earth, that I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the one who was unwilling?" He said:
"They will be swallowed up along with them, but he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection according to his intention."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, Allah will send to this Ummah at the head of every hundred years someone who will renew its religion for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The flourishing of Jerusalem is the ruin of Yathrib, the ruin of Yathrib is the outbreak of the great battle, the outbreak of the great battle is the conquest of Constantinople, and the conquest of Constantinople is the emergence of the Antichrist."
Then he struck with his hand the thigh of the one he was narrating to, or his shoulder, and said: "This is as true as that you are here," or, "as that you are sitting."
He meant Muʿādh ibn Jabal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The nations will soon summon one another against you, as diners summon one another to their dish."
Someone said: "Will it be because we are few on that day?" He said:
"No, on that day you will be many, but you will be like the foam of a torrent. Allah will remove the fear of you from the hearts of your enemies, and Allah will cast weakness into your hearts."
Someone said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is weakness?" He said:
"Love of the world and dislike of death."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"On the day of the great battle, the camp of the Muslims will be in al-Ghūṭah, beside a city called Damascus, one of the best cities of Syria."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah will never bring together two swords against this Ummah: a sword from among themselves and a sword from their enemy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, in a hadith:
"A people with small eyes will fight you."
He meant the Turks. He said:

"You will drive them back three times until you make them join the Arabian Peninsula. In the first driving, those who flee will escape; in the second, some will escape and some will perish; and in the third, they will be wiped out."
Or as he said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Some people of my Ummah will settle in a low-lying land which they call al-Baṣrah, by a river called the Tigris, over which there will be a bridge. Its people will be many, and it will be one of the cities of the Muhājirūn."
Ibn Yaḥyā said that Abū Maʿmar said:

"And it will be one of the cities of the Muslims. Then at the end of time, the Banū Qanṭūrāʾ, broad-faced and small-eyed, will come until they settle on the bank of the river. Its people will split into three groups: one group will take the tails of cattle and [go to] the wilderness, and they will perish; one group will take [security] for themselves, and they will disbelieve; and one group will place their children behind their backs and fight them, and they are the martyrs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:

"O Anas, people will found cities, and one of those cities will be called al-Baṣrah or al-Buṣayrah. If you pass by it or enter it, beware of its salt flats, its pasture, its market, and the gate of its rulers, and keep to its outskirts. For in it there will be swallowing up by the earth, pelting with stones, and quaking, and people who will go to sleep at night and wake up in the morning as apes and pigs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, what are the major sins?" He said, "Associating partners with Allah."
He said, "Then what?" He said,
"Then disobedience to parents."
He said, "Then what?" He said, "The false oath (al-yamīn al-ghamūs)."
I said, "What is the false oath?" He said,
"That by which a man unlawfully takes the property of a Muslim, while he is lying in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jew passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "As-sāmu ʿalayka (death be upon you)."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "And upon you."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Do you know what he said? He said, 'As-sāmu ʿalayka.'"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, should we not kill him?" He said, "No.
When the People of the Book greet you with salām, then say: 'And upon you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A slave belonging to the state's slaves had intercourse with a slave girl from the fifth [of the spoils],
and forced her against her will until he deflowered her.
So ʿUmar had him flogged with the prescribed punishment and exiled him,
but he did not flog the slave girl because he had forced her.
Az-Zuhrī said regarding a virgin slave woman whom a free man deflowers,
that the ruling for a virgin slave woman is that he pays her value, and he is flogged.
And in the case of a non-virgin slave woman, according to the rulings of the leaders, there is no compensation,
but the prescribed punishment is upon him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"On the Day of Resurrection, the treasure of one of you will be a bald-headed serpent,
from which its owner flees, but it pursues him and says, 'I am your treasure.'
He said: By Allah, it will keep pursuing him until he stretches out his hand and it swallows it in its mouth."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"When the owner of livestock does not give what is due on them,
they will be set upon him on the Day of Resurrection,
trampling his face with their hooves."
Some people said about a man who has camels,
and fears that charity (ṣadaqah) will become due on him,
so he sells them for similar camels, or for sheep, or cattle, or dirhams,
to escape the charity by a day,
as a trick, that there is no harm on him.
And he says that if he pays zakāh on his camels a day or a year before the year is completed, it is valid for him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade najsh (bidding up the price without intending to buy).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "A virgin is to be asked for her permission."
I said, "A virgin is shy." He said, "Her silence is her permission."
Some people said: If a man desires an orphan girl or a virgin,
and she refuses, so he uses a trick and brings two false witnesses that he married her,
then she reaches maturity and the orphan girl accepts,
and the judge accepts the false testimony,
while the husband knows that it is false,
then intercourse is lawful for him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"The neighbor has most right to what is close to him."
Some people said: If a man buys a house for twenty thousand dirhams,
there is no harm in using a trick, so that he buys the house for twenty thousand dirhams,
and pays the seller nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine dirhams in cash,
and pays him a dinar for what remains of the twenty thousand,
so if the preemptor demands it, he takes it for twenty thousand dirhams,
otherwise he has no claim on the house.
Then if the house is claimed by another with a rightful title,
the buyer returns to the seller for what he paid him,
which is nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine dirhams and a dinar,
because when the sale was invalidated, the exchange for the dinar was annulled.
And if he finds a defect in this house and it is not claimed by another,
he returns it to him for twenty thousand dirhams.
He said: So he permitted this deception among Muslims, whereas the Prophet ﷺ said,
"There is no disease, no vice, and no treachery."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Whoever sees me in a dream has truly seen me,
for Satan cannot take my form,
and the true dream of a believer is one of forty-six parts of prophethood."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this [chain], and he said,
"I do not know what will be done with him."
She said, "That grieved me, so I slept,
and I saw for ʿUthmān a flowing spring.
So I told the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said, 'That is his deeds.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would observe iʿtikāf for ten days every year. In the year in which he was taken, he observed iʿtikāf for twenty days. And the Qurʾān would be presented to him once every year; in the year in which he was taken, it was presented to him twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī
asked permission to enter upon ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, but he was not given permission,
as if [ʿUmar] were busy, so Abū Mūsā went back.
When ʿUmar was finished, he said, "Did I not hear the voice of ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays? Let him in." He was told, "He has gone back." So he called for him.
[Abū Mūsā] said, "We used to be commanded to do this."
[ʿUmar] said, "Bring me proof of that."
So he went to a gathering of the Anṣār and asked them.
They said, "No one will testify for you on this except the youngest of us, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī."
So he went with Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī.
ʿUmar said, "Has something of the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ been hidden from me? Trading in the markets distracted me,"
meaning going out for trade.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in one of the markets of Madinah. He left, and I left, and he said,
"Where is the little one?" three times. "Call al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī."
So al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī got up and walked, with a necklace around his neck.
The Prophet ﷺ gestured with his hand like this,
and al-Ḥasan gestured with his hand,
like this, and [the Prophet ﷺ] embraced him and said,
"O Allah, I love him, so love him,
and love whoever loves him."
Abū Hurayrah said, "After the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said what he said, no one was dearer to me than al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafiyyah fell to Diḥyah al-Kalbī, and afterwards she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he married her, making her freedom her dowry.
Ḥammād said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said to Thābit, "O Abū Muḥammad, did you ask Anas what he gave her as dowry?" He said, "He gave her herself as her dowry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Bilāl came with barnī dates, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him,
"Where is this from?"
Bilāl said, "We had some poor-quality dates, so I sold two ṣāʿ of them for one ṣāʿ, for the food of the Prophet ﷺ."
At that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Oh! That is the very essence of ribā. Do not do it. But if you want to buy dates, sell [yours] in a separate sale, then buy with the proceeds."
Ibn Sahl did not mention "at that" in his narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered upon Umm Mubashshir al-Anṣāriyyah in a palm grove of hers, and the Prophet ﷺ said to her,
"Who planted this palm grove, a Muslim or a disbeliever?"
She said, "A Muslim." He said,
"No Muslim plants a plant or sows a crop, and then a human being, an animal, or anything else eats from it, except that it is charity (ṣadaqah) for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ burned the palm trees of Banū al-Naḍīr. He said: And about this Ḥassān ibn Thābit said, "The chiefs of Banū Luʾayy took lightly a blazing fire at al-Buwayrah." He said: Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith replied to him, "May Allah make that deed endure, and may the flames blaze in its surroundings. You will know which of us is far from it, and which of our lands will be harmed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That his father

died and left a debt of thirty wasqs owed to a Jewish man. Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh asked him for a delay, but he refused to grant it. So Jābir spoke to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that he would intercede with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and spoke to the Jew to take the fruit of his palm trees in place of what was owed to him, but he refused. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke to him again, but he refused to grant a delay. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the palm grove, walked through it, and then said to Jābir,
"Pick [the dates] for him and pay him what he is owed."

So after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left, he picked thirty wasqs for him, and twelve wasqs were left over. Jābir came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to tell him what had happened, but found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ away. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned, he came to him and told him that he had paid him in full and told him of the surplus that remained. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Tell that to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb."
So Jābir went to ʿUmar and told him. ʿUmar said to him, "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ walked in it, I knew that Allah would surely bless it."
label: machine translation
