segments_en: When the Muslims came to Madinah, they would gather and wait for the times of prayer, and no one would call for it. One day they spoke about this, and some of them said, "Adopt a bell like the bell of the Christians."
And some of them said, "Adopt a horn like the horn of the Jews."
Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said, "Why not send a man to call for prayer?" So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"O Bilāl, get up and call for prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"When the call to prayer is made, Satan turns his back and passes wind so that he does not hear the call. When the call is finished, he comes back; then when the iqāmah is called, he turns his back again, and when the iqāmah is finished, he comes back, until he intrudes between a person and his own heart, saying to him, 'Remember such and such, remember such and such,' things he had not been thinking of before, until the man does not know how much he has prayed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ went to fight a people with us, he would not fight with us until morning came and he had watched;
if he heard a call to prayer, he held back from them,
and if he did not hear a call to prayer, he attacked them.
He [Anas] said: So we went out to Khaybar and reached them by night.
When morning came and he heard no call to prayer, he rode, and I rode behind Abū Ṭalḥah,
and my foot was touching the foot of the Prophet ﷺ.
He said: They came out to us with their baskets and their spades, and when they saw the Prophet ﷺ they said, "Muḥammad, by Allah! Muḥammad and the army!"
He said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw them, he said, "Allah is the Greatest! Allah is the Greatest! Khaybar is ruined!
When we descend upon a people's courtyard, evil is the morning of those who were warned."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When any of you enters the mosque, he is in prayer as long as the prayer is detaining him, and the angels invoke blessings upon any of you as long as he remains in his place where he prayed, saying, 'O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy on him; O Allah, accept his repentance,' as long as he does not break his ablution there and does not harm anyone there."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There are seven whom Allah will shade in His shade on the day when there is no shade but His: a just ruler; a young man who grew up in the worship of Allah; a man whose heart is attached to the mosque from the time he leaves it until he returns to it; two men who love each other for the sake of Allah, meeting on that and parting on that; a man who remembers Allah in private and his eyes overflow; a man whom a woman of status and beauty invites, and he says, 'I fear Allah'; and a man who gives charity and conceals it so that his left hand does not know what his right hand spends."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the illness of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became heavy, Bilāl came to inform him of the prayer, and he said,
"Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer."
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, Abū Bakr is a tenderhearted man; when he stands in your place, the people will not hear him. If only you would order ʿUmar." He said,
"Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer."
She said: So I said to Ḥafṣah, "Say to him, 'Abū Bakr is a tenderhearted man, and when he stands in your place the people will not hear him. If only you would order ʿUmar.'" So she said that to him.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"You are indeed the women companions of Yūsuf.
Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer."

She said: So they told Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer. She said: When he had begun the prayer, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ felt some lightness in himself, so he got up, supported between two men, his feet dragging on the ground. She said: When he entered the mosque, Abū Bakr sensed his presence and started to step back, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gestured to him, "Stay in your place."

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came until he sat to the left of Abū Bakr. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then led the people in prayer sitting, while Abū Bakr stood, following the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ, and the people followed the prayer of Abū Bakr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He called the call to prayer at Ḍajnān on a cold and windy night, and at the end of his call he said, "Pray in your dwellings! Pray in your dwellings!" Then he said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to order the mu'adhdhin, when it was a cold or rainy night during a journey, to say, 'Pray in your dwellings.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: He arrived from Egypt to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who asked, "Since when have you not removed your leather socks?" He said, "From one Friday to the next."
He said, "You have followed the Sunnah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Salmān when he saw a man removing his leather socks for ablution. Salmān said to him, "Wipe over your leather socks, and over your head covering, and over your forelock, for I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiping over the leather socks and the head covering."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah's necklace fell, so she stayed behind to look for it. Abū Bakr went to ʿĀʾishah and was angry with her for detaining the people, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed the concession of tayammum.
He said: "That day we wiped up to the shoulders."
He said: Abū Bakr went to ʿĀʾishah and said, "I did not know that you were so blessed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They asked ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā about tayammum,
and he said, "The Prophet ﷺ ordered ʿAmmār to do it like this," and he struck the ground with his hands, then shook them off and wiped his face.
Al-Ḥakam said: "and his hands."
And Salamah said: "and his elbows."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went with my paternal aunt and my maternal aunt, and we entered upon ʿĀʾishah and asked her how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do his ritual bath after sexual impurity. She said, "He would pour water over his hands three times, then put them into the vessel, then wash his head three times, then pour water over his body, then rise for prayer. As for us, we wash our heads five times because of the braids."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would perform the ritual bath after sexual impurity, then warm himself with me before I had bathed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would be in a state of sexual impurity, then sleep as he was, without touching water.
Sufyān said: One day I mentioned the hadith, and Ismāʿīl said to me, "Young man, this hadith is being strengthened by something."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I set out water for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to bathe, and he bathed after being with all of his wives in one night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The five prayers, and Friday to Friday, and the fulfillment of the trust are an expiation for what is between them."
I said, "What is the fulfillment of the trust?" He said:
"The ritual bath after sexual impurity, for beneath every hair there is impurity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a woman who sees in her sleep what a man sees, and he said:
"She does not have to bathe until she emits, just as a man does not have to bathe until he emits."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Water is from water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should bathe in an open desert, nor on a rooftop that does not conceal him, for even if he does not see [anyone], he is seen."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should stand for prayer while he is suffering from filth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to have heavy, prolonged bleeding outside my menstrual period.
She said: So I went to the Prophet ﷺ to seek his ruling and to inform him.
She said: I found him at my sister Zaynab's house.
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have a need to ask of you." He said:
"What is it, O woman?"
I said, "I have prolonged, heavy bleeding, and it has kept me from prayer and fasting. What do you command me regarding it?" He said:
"I recommend that you use cotton, for it will stop the blood."
I said, "It is more than that."
Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Sharīk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ under his blanket, and I felt what women feel of menstruation, so I slipped out of the blanket. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Have you begun menstruating?"
I said, "I felt what women feel of menstruation." He said:
"That is what Allah has decreed for the daughters of Ādam."
She said: So I slipped away and took care of myself, then returned, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Come and enter the blanket with me."
She said: So I entered with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A wife] of the Prophet ﷺ — he said: I asked her, "What did you do with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during menstruation?" She said, "When one of us was at the onset, as soon as she began to menstruate, she would tie a waist-wrapper around her down to the middle of her thighs, then lie down with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to her, while she was menstruating:
"Undo your hair and bathe."
ʿAlī said in his narration: "Undo your head."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr, from ʿAmrah, that ʿĀʾishah
informed her that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with her, and that she heard the voice of a man asking permission to enter in the house of Ḥafṣah.
ʿĀʾishah said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is a man asking permission to enter your house."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "I see that it is so-and-so,"
[referring to] Ḥafṣah's foster uncle.
ʿĀʾishah said, "O Messenger of Allah, if so-and-so were alive" — referring to her foster uncle — "would he be able to enter upon me?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Yes. Indeed, fosterage makes unlawful what birth makes unlawful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is mentioned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of you are my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them, then those who follow them."

I do not know whether he mentioned it twice or three times after that. Then he mentioned a people who will betray and not be trusted, who will give testimony without being asked to testify, who will make vows and not fulfil them, and among whom obesity will appear.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins?" [He said it] three times.
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "Associating partners with Allah, and disobedience to parents."
Then he sat up, having been reclining, and said:
"And beware of false speech!"
[The narrator] said: He kept repeating it until we said, "If only he would stop."
Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm said: Al-Jurayrī narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿĀʾishah,

the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: When believing women emigrated to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they were tested by the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: {O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you, that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse} to the end of the verse.
ʿĀʾishah said: Whichever of the believing women affirmed this had affirmed the test. And when they affirmed that by their words, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say to them:
"Go, for I have accepted your pledge."
No, by Allah, the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never touched the hand of a woman.

Rather, he took their pledge by words alone. ʿĀʾishah said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never took a pledge from women except by what Allah the Exalted commanded him, and the palm of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never touched the palm of a woman. When he took their pledge, he would say to them, "I have accepted your pledge," in words only.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he was travelling on a camel of his that had become exhausted,
and the Prophet ﷺ passed by, struck it, and made supplication for it,
and it moved along as it had never moved before. Then he said, "Sell it to me for an ūqiyyah." I said, "No." Then he said, "Sell it to me for an ūqiyyah."
So I sold it to him, stipulating that I could ride it to my family.
When we arrived, I brought him the camel, and he paid me its price in full. Then I left,
and he sent for me after I had gone, and said:
"I would not take your camel [from you].
Take your camel; it is yours."
Shuʿbah said, from Mughīrah, from ʿĀmir, from Jābir: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ lent me its back to Madinah.
Isḥāq said, from Jarīr, from Mughīrah: I sold it on condition that I had the use of its back until I reached Madinah.
ʿAṭāʾ and others said: You have its back to Madinah.
Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir said, from Jābir: He stipulated its back to Madinah.
Zayd ibn Aslam said, from Jābir: And you have its back until you return.
Abū al-Zubayr said, from Jābir: We lent you its back to Madinah.
Al-Aʿmash said, from Sālim, from Jābir: You may travel on it to your family.
ʿUbaydullāh and Ibn Isḥāq said, from Wahb, from Jābir: The Prophet ﷺ bought it for an ūqiyyah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names; whoever memorizes them will enter Paradise."
He said: In this hadith there is no mention of the names.
He said: This hadith is good and authentic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was mentioned in the presence of ʿĀʾishah that ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both, had been appointed as executor.
She said: When was he appointed as executor to him? I had him leaning against my chest — or she said, my lap — and he asked for the basin,
and he slumped down in my lap,
and I did not realize that he had died,
so when did he appoint him as executor?
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "They lead you in prayer;
if they pray correctly, it is for you [as well as for them],
and if they make mistakes, it is for you and against them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He entered upon ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān (may Allah be pleased with him) while he was besieged, and said: "You are the leader of the general public,
and what you see has befallen you, while a leader of discord leads us in prayer and we feel uneasy [about it]."
He said: "Prayer is the best of what people do,
so when people do good, do good along with them,
and when they do evil, avoid their evil."
Az-Zubaydī said: Az-Zuhrī said: We do not think one should pray behind an effeminate man except out of unavoidable necessity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
The martyrs are those who drown, those who die of plague, those who die of a stomach illness, and those killed by a collapsing structure." And he said: "
If they knew what is in coming early to the prayer, they would race to it; if they knew what is in the ʿishāʾ prayer and the dawn prayer, they would come to them even if crawling;
and if they knew what is in the first row, they would draw lots for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to Medina and was asked: "What have you disapproved of in us since the day you knew the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "I have not disapproved of anything except that you do not straighten the rows."
ʿUqbah ibn ʿUbayd related from Bashīr ibn Yasār: Anas ibn Mālik came to us in Medina, and [he mentioned] this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray at night in his room,
and the wall of the room was low,
so the people saw the figure of the Prophet ﷺ, and some people stood and prayed with his prayer.
In the morning they talked about that,
so he stood [to pray] on the second night,
and some people stood with him praying with his prayer.
They did that for two or three nights,
until, after that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat and did not come out.
In the morning, people mentioned that to him, and he said: "
I feared that the night prayer would be made obligatory upon you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had a mat which he would spread out during the day and make into a screened-off space at night,
so people gathered to him and prayed behind him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: People used to be commanded that a man place his right hand on his left forearm in prayer.
Abū Ḥāzim said: I only know that he attributed that to the Prophet ﷺ.
Ismāʿīl said: He attributes that.
And he did not say "he attributes".
label: machine translation

segments_en: (May Allah be pleased with them both) He said: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he prayed.
They said: "O Messenger of Allah,
we saw you reach out for something where you were standing,
then we saw you step back." He said: "
I was shown Paradise,
and I reached out for a cluster [of fruit] from it,
and had I taken it, you would have eaten from it for as long as the world remains."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer one day,
then he ascended the pulpit and gestured with his hand toward the direction of the mosque's qiblah, and said: "
Just now, since I prayed the prayer with you, Paradise and the Fire were shown to me, represented in front of this wall,
and I have never seen a day like today in regard to good and evil,
I have never seen a day like today in regard to good and evil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ recited where he was commanded,
and remained silent where he was commanded. {And your Lord is never forgetful.} {Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw a man at the Maqām saying the takbīr at every lowering and rising, and when he stood and when he went down [to prostrate].
I informed Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said: "Is that not the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ? May you have no mother!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed behind an old man in Mecca, and he said the takbīr twenty-two times,
so I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "He is a fool."
He said: "May your mother lose you!
It is the Sunnah of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ said: "
Allah hears whoever praises Him," he said: "
O Allah, our Lord, and to You belongs all praise."
And the Prophet ﷺ would say the takbīr when he bowed and when he raised his head,
and when he stood up from the two prostrations he said: "Allahu akbar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went to Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī and said: "Will you not come out with us to the date palms so we can talk?" So he came out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Saʿīd led us in prayer and said the takbīr aloud when he raised his head from prostration, when he prostrated, and when he raised [his head],
and when he stood up from the two rakʿahs, and he said: "This is how I saw the Prophet ﷺ [do it]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would have his water for ablution and his tooth-stick set out for him. When he rose during the night, he would relieve himself, and then use the tooth-stick.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would never sleep, by night or by day, and then wake up without using the tooth-stick before performing ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar. When the call to the Ẓuhr prayer was made, he performed ablution and prayed. When the call to the ʿAṣr prayer was made, he performed ablution again. I asked him about it, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:
"Whoever performs ablution while already in a state of purity, Allah will record for him ten good deeds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Her mistress

sent her with some harīsah to ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her. She found her praying, and ʿĀʾishah gestured to her to put it down. A cat came and ate some of it. When ʿĀʾishah finished her prayer, she ate from where the cat had eaten, and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not impure; it is one of those who go around among you."
And I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution with the water left over by a cat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd: Which of you was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Night of the Jinn? He said: None of us was with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He disliked performing ablution with milk or nabīdh, and said: Tayammum is more pleasing to me than that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Abū al-ʿĀliyah about a man
who was in a state of major impurity and had no water, but had nabīdh: should he wash with it? He said: No.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is not permissible for a man who believes in Allah and the Last Day to pray while he is holding back urine or stool, until he relieves himself."
Then he narrated something similar to it in this wording. He said:

"And it is not permissible for a man who believes in Allah and the Last Day to lead a people in prayer except with their permission, nor to single himself out for a supplication to the exclusion of them. If he does so, he has betrayed them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would perform ablution with a vessel that held two raṭls, and would bathe with a ṣāʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Abī Mulaykah was asked about ablution,
and he said: I saw ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān being asked about ablution,

so he called for water. A vessel for ablution was brought, and he tilted it over his right hand, then put it into the water. He rinsed his mouth three times, sniffed water into his nose and blew it out three times, and washed his face three times. Then he washed his right arm three times and his left arm three times. Then he put his hand in, took water, and wiped his head and his ears, washing the insides and the backs of them once. Then he washed his feet. Then he said: Where are those who ask about ablution? This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān wash his forearms three times each and wipe his head three times. Then he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: may Allah be pleased with him. He was asked about the ablution

of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned the hadith. He said: And he wiped his head until it almost dripped, and washed his feet three times each. Then he said: This is how the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī, meaning Ibn Abī Ṭālib, came in to see me after he had relieved himself, and called for water for ablution. We brought him a basin containing water and placed it before him. He said: O Ibn ʿAbbās, shall I show you how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform ablution? I said: Yes.

He said: He tilted the vessel over his hand and washed it. Then he put his right hand in and poured water with it over the other. Then he washed both palms, then rinsed his mouth and sniffed water into his nose and blew it out. Then he put both hands into the vessel together, took a handful of water with them, and struck it against his face, pressing his thumbs against the front of his ears. He did the same a second time and a third time. Then he took a handful of water in his right palm and poured it over his forehead, leaving it to flow down over his face. Then he washed his forearms up to the elbows, three times each. Then he wiped his head and the backs of his ears. Then he put both hands in together, took a handful of water, and poured it over his foot while the sandal was on it, and rubbed it with it; then he did the same with the other.
He said: I said: Even with the sandals on? He said: Even with the sandals on.
He said: I said: Even with the sandals on? He said: Even with the sandals on.
He said: I said: Even with the sandals on? He said: Even with the sandals on.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah

performed ablution for the people as he had seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution. When he reached his head, he scooped up a handful of water and received it in his left hand, then placed it on the middle of his head until the water dripped, or nearly dripped. Then he wiped from the front to the back, and from the back to the front.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution in her presence and wiped his entire head, from the hairline, on every side, following the direction of the hair's growth, without disturbing the hair from its arrangement.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over Ibn al-Daḥdāḥ. Then a horse without a saddle was brought, and a man tied it and mounted it, and it began to trot with him while we followed, running behind him. Then a man among the people said, “The Prophet ﷺ said:
‘How many a laden date-cluster, hanging or dangling, there is in Paradise for Ibn al-Daḥdāḥ!’”
Or Shuʿbah said, “for Abū al-Daḥdāḥ.”
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ was wounded, and the wound pained him, so he reached for his broad arrowheads and slaughtered himself with them, and the Prophet ﷺ did not pray over him.
He said: That was a form of discipline from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: As for him, he is beloved to me, and as for him, he is trustworthy to me: ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nine, or eight, or seven of us, and he said:
“Will you not pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah?”
We had only recently given a pledge, so we said, “We have already pledged allegiance to you, Messenger of Allah.” Then he said:
“Will you not pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah?”
So we said, “We have already pledged allegiance to you, Messenger of Allah.” Then he said:
“Will you not pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah?”
He said: So we stretched out our hands and said, “We have already pledged allegiance to you, Messenger of Allah; so what are we pledging to you?” He said:
“That you worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, [that you keep] the five prayers, and that you obey”—and he said a word quietly—“and that you do not ask people for anything.”
Indeed, I saw some of those men whose whip would fall, and he would not ask anyone to hand it to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ saying the talbiyah for ʿUmrah and Hajj together. I told Ibn ʿUmar about that, and he said, “He said the talbiyah for Hajj alone.”
Then I met Anas and told him what Ibn ʿUmar had said. Anas said, “You consider us nothing but children! I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
‘Labbayk, for ʿUmrah and Hajj together.’”
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Sacrifice at Jamrat al-ʿAqabah, riding a mule, and he said:
“O people, when you throw at the Jamrah, throw with pebbles like those used for flicking.”
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Khudrī [reported] that on the day of Ḥunayn the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent an army to Awṭās. They met an enemy and fought them, overcame them, and took captive women from them. Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ felt reluctant to have relations with them because of their husbands among the polytheists. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning that: {And [also forbidden are] married women, except those whom your right hands possess}, meaning: they are lawful for you once their waiting period has ended.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever grants a man a lifetime grant, it belongs to him and his heirs, and his statement has cut off his own right to it; it belongs to the one to whom it was granted and to his heirs.”
Except that Yaḥyā said at the beginning of his narration:
“Any man who grants a lifetime grant, it is his and his heirs’.”
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr, from his father,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān,
from Ibn Abī ʿAmrah al-Anṣārī,
from Zayd ibn Khālid
al-Juhanī that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Shall I not inform you of the best of witnesses? It is the one who comes with his testimony before he is asked for it.”
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was sitting with his Companions, a cloud came over them, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you know what this is?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"This is the clouds, the water-carriers of the earth. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, drives it to a people who neither thank Him nor call upon Him." Then he said:
"Do you know what is above you?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"It is the raqīʿ, a protected ceiling and a restrained wave." Then he said:
"Do you know how far it is between you and it?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"Between you and it is a journey of five hundred years." Then he said:
"Do you know what is above that?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"Above that are two heavens, and between them is a journey of five hundred years."
He went on until he had counted seven heavens, with the distance between every two heavens being like the distance between the heaven and the earth. Then he said:
"Do you know what is above that?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"Above that is the Throne, and between it and the heaven is a distance like that between two heavens." Then he said:
"Do you know what is beneath you?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said, "It is the earth." Then he said:
"Do you know what is beneath that?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"Beneath it is another earth, and between the two is a journey of five hundred years."
He went on until he had counted seven earths, with a journey of five hundred years between every two earths. Then he said:
"By the One in whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, if you were to lower a man by a rope to the lowest earth, he would land upon Allah."
Then he recited: "He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He has knowledge of all things."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this was revealed:
"O you who believe, when you privately consult the Messenger, offer a charity before your private consultation."
the Prophet ﷺ said to me:
"What do you think, a dinar?"
I said, "They cannot bear it." He said, "Then half a dinar?"
I said, "They cannot bear it." He said, "Then how much?" I said, "A barley grain." He said, "You are indeed frugal." He said: Then it was revealed:
"Do you fear that you will not be able to offer charities before your private consultation?" [to the end of] the verse.
He said: Through me, Allah lightened [the burden] for this Ummah.
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith; we know it only through this route.
The meaning of his saying "a barley grain" is the weight of a barley grain of gold. And Abū al-Jaʿd's name is Rāfiʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jewish man
came to the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions and said, "As-sāmu ʿalaykum." The people returned his greeting, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you know what this man said?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best. He gave the greeting of peace, O Prophet of Allah." He said:
"No, rather he said such and such. Bring him back to me." They brought him back, and he said:
"Did you say: As-sāmu ʿalaykum?" He said, "Yes."
Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of the People of the Book greets you, say: ʿAlayk." He said:
"Upon you be what you said." He said:
"And when they come to you, they greet you with a greeting with which Allah has not greeted you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots..."

He said: The līnah is the palm tree. [...and that He may disgrace the defiantly disobedient.] He said: They made them come down from their fortresses. He said: They were ordered to cut down the palm trees, and that troubled their hearts.

The Muslims said, "We have cut down some and left some, so let us ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whether we will have a reward for what we cut down, and whether we bear any sin for what we left." So Allah, the Exalted, revealed:
"Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots..." [to the end of] the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would test [women] only by the verse about which Allah said:
"When the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you..." [to the end of] the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman among the women said, "What is this good [command] in which we must not disobey you?" He said, "Do not wail."

I said, "O Messenger of Allah, the family of so-and-so helped me in mourning my uncle, and I must repay them." He refused me, and I appealed to him repeatedly, until he permitted me to repay them. After that I did not wail, either to repay them or otherwise, until this very moment. And there was no woman among them left who had not wailed except me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: he was asked about wiping over the leather socks, and he said:
"Three days for the traveller, and one day for the resident."
It is also mentioned that Yahyā ibn Maʿīn deemed authentic the hadith of Khuzaymah ibn Thābit concerning wiping.
And Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Jadalī's name is ʿAbd ibn ʿAbd, and it is also said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And she was,
[someone] in whose care she was raised, that a woman asked the Prophet ﷺ for a ruling about menstrual blood that gets on a garment, and he said:
"Scrape it off, then rub it with water, then sprinkle it, and pray in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to Qubāʾ to pray there. He said: The Anṣār came to him and greeted him with salām while he was praying.
He said: So I said to Bilāl, "How did you see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ respond to them when they greeted him while he was praying?" He said, "He would do like this," and he spread out his palm.
And Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn spread out his palm, making its inside face downward and its back face upward.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ahead us, the young boys of the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, on donkeys of ours from Jamʿ [Muzdalifah], and he began patting our thighs and saying:
"My little sons, do not throw the Jamrah until the sun rises."
Sufyān added in it:
"And I do not think anyone should throw it until the sun rises."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of people came to him and said, "A man among us married a woman, did not set a dowry for her, and did not consummate the marriage until he died."
ʿAbdullāh said, "Since I parted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I have not been asked anything harder for me than this. Go to someone other than me."

They kept coming back to him about it for a month, then at the end they said to him, "Whom shall we ask if we do not ask you, when you are among the most eminent of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ in this land, and we find no one other than you?"

He said, "I will give my opinion on it by my own best effort. If it is right, it is from Allah alone, who has no partner; and if it is wrong, it is from me and from Satan, and Allah and His Messenger are free of it. I hold that she should have a dowry equal to that of her peers, neither less nor more, and that she has the inheritance, and that she must observe the waiting period of four months and ten days."
He said: Some people from Ashjaʿ heard that, and they stood up and said, "We testify that you have judged as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged regarding a woman of ours called Barwaʿ bint Wāshiq."
He said: ʿAbdullāh was never seen happier than he was that day, except at his becoming Muslim.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And she was,
married to Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, that his sister al-Furayʿah bint Mālik,

said: "My husband went out in search of some slaves of his, and he caught up with them at the edge of al-Qadūm, and they killed him. The news of my husband's death came while I was in one of the houses of the Anṣār, far from my family's home. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, the news of my husband's death has come to me while I am in a house far from my family's house and my brothers' house. He left no money to spend on me and no wealth that I inherited,
and no house that he owned. So if you see fit to permit me, I will go to my family's house and my brothers' house, for that is dearer to me and better for me in some of my affairs.' He said:
'Do so, if you wish.'

She said: So I left, my eyes cooled by what Allah had decreed for me through the tongue of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then when I was in the mosque, or in one of the rooms, he called me and said, 'What did you say?'
She said: So I related it to him again, and he said:
'Stay in your house in which the news of your husband's death came to you, until the prescribed period reaches its end.'
She said: So I observed my waiting period in it for four months and ten days.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I did not see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fast two consecutive months, except that he would join Shaʿbān to Ramadān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, tell me about ablution." He said:
"Perform ablution thoroughly, run your fingers through between the digits, and sniff water deeply into the nose, unless you are fasting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast three days from the beginning of every month, and he rarely went without fasting on Friday.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was one of those who held up the branches of the tree away from the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was delivering a sermon, and he said:

"Were it not that dogs are a community among the communities, I would have ordered them to be killed. So kill every pure black one of them. And no household keeps a dog except that a qīrāṭ is deducted from their deeds every day, except for a hunting dog, a farming dog, or a sheep dog."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two women

from Hudhayl fought, and one killed the other. Each of them had a husband and a child. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the blood-money for the slain woman was to be paid by the ʿāqilah (paternal kinsmen) of the killer, and he exempted her husband and her child.
The narrator said: The kinsmen of the slain woman said, "Her inheritance belongs to us." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No, her inheritance belongs to her husband and her child."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman

threw a stone at another woman and caused her to miscarry. The matter was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he ruled that the compensation for her child was a ghurrah (a slave) valued at five hundred. On that day he forbade throwing stones.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A mukātab (slave contracting to buy his freedom) is freed in proportion to what he has paid, the legal punishment is applied to him in proportion to the part of him that has been freed, and he inherits in proportion to the part of him that has been freed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A boy
belonging to poor people cut off the ear of a boy belonging to rich people. His family came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we are poor people."
So he did not impose anything on him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Who among you has seen a dream?"

A man said, "I saw as if a scale came down from the sky. You and Abū Bakr were weighed, and you outweighed Abū Bakr. Then Abū Bakr and ʿUmar were weighed, and Abū Bakr outweighed ʿUmar. Then ʿUmar and ʿUthmān were weighed, and ʿUmar outweighed ʿUthmān. Then the scale was lifted." And we saw displeasure on the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"None of those who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ was turned toward the Kaʿbah, they said, "O Messenger of Allah, what about our brothers who died while praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis?" So Allah revealed:
"And Allah would never let your faith go to waste" (the verse).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The believers most complete in faith are those with the best character, and the best of you are those who are best to their wives in character."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave some men and gave nothing to one of them. Saʿd said, "O Messenger of Allah, you gave so-and-so and so-and-so, but you gave nothing to so-and-so, and he is a believer." The Prophet ﷺ said, "Or a Muslim."
Saʿd repeated it three times, and each time the Prophet ﷺ said, "Or a Muslim."
Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"I give some men while leaving out others who are dearer to me than they are, giving them nothing, out of fear that they would be thrown on their faces into the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Every nation has its Magians, and the Magians of this nation are those who say there is no divine decree. If one of them dies, do not attend his funeral, and if one of them falls ill, do not visit them. They are the party of the Dajjāl, and it is a right upon Allah to join them with the Dajjāl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah created Ādam from a handful that He took from all of the earth. So the children of Ādam came in keeping with the earth: among them came the red, the white, the black, and those in between, the easy and the rough, the evil and the good."
In the hadith of Yaḥyā he added: "and those in between."
And the reports are in the hadith of Yazīd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Dharr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to sit among his Companions, and a stranger would come and not know which of them he was until he asked. So we asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to let us make a place for him that a stranger could recognize when he came. So we built him a platform of clay on which he would sit. One day we were sitting, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in his place, when a man approached, the most handsome of people in face and the most fragrant of people in scent, as if his clothes had never been touched by dirt, until he greeted at the edge of the carpet and said, "Peace be upon you, O Muḥammad."
He returned the greeting. The man said, "May I come closer, O Muḥammad?" He said, "Come closer."
He kept saying, "May I come closer?" repeatedly, and he kept saying to him, "Come closer,"
until he put his hands on the knees of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said, "O Muḥammad, tell me what Islam is." He said:
"Islam is that you worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, establish the prayer, give zakāh, perform Hajj to the House, and fast Ramadan."
He said, "If I do that, have I become a Muslim?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The man in charge of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ sacrificial camels said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what should I do with those of the sacrificial camels that become unable to go on?" He said:
"Slaughter it, then dip its sandal in its blood, then leave it between the people and it, so that they may eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a woman to shave her head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever enters the state of ihram for Hajj and ʿUmrah together, one circumambulation suffices for both, and he does not leave the state of ihram until he has completed his Hajj and leaves the state of ihram for both together."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about the Stone:
"By Allah, Allah will raise it on the Day of Resurrection with two eyes with which it sees and a tongue with which it speaks, bearing witness against whoever touched it without right."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to oil his head with olive oil while in the state of ihram, [using oil] that was not perfumed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited me in my illness and said, "Have you made a will?" I said, "Yes." He said, "How much?"
I said, "All of my wealth, in the cause of Allah." He said:
"Then what have you left for your children?"
I said, "They are well-off." He said, "Bequeath a tenth."
He kept saying this and I kept replying, until he said:
"Bequeath a third, and a third is a lot," or "big."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as he was dying. Beside him was a cup of water, and he would put his hand into the cup, then wipe his face with the water, then say:
"O Allah, help me against the agonies of death," or "the pangs of death."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ went in to see a young man who was dying and said, "How do you find yourself?"
He said, "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I hope in Allah, and I fear my sins."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"These two do not come together in the heart of a servant in a situation like this except that Allah gives him what he hopes for and keeps him safe from what he fears."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When someone close to him died, Ḥudhayfah would say: Do not inform anyone of it, for I fear it would be an announcement of death. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with these two ears of mine forbidding the announcement of death.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about musk, and he said:
"It is the best of your perfumes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a funeral procession, and he saw some people riding. He said:
"Are you not ashamed? The angels of Allah are on their feet while you are on the backs of animals!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to visit the sick, follow funeral processions, accept the invitation of a slave, and ride a donkey. On the day of Qurayẓah and An-Naḍīr he was on a donkey, and on the day of Khaybar he was on a donkey bridled with a rope of palm fibre, with a saddle of palm fibre under him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to recite Fātiḥat al-Kitāb (the Opening of the Book) over the funeral.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Anas ibn Mālik pray over the funeral of a man, and he stood level with his head. Then another funeral was brought, of a woman, and they said, "O Abū Ḥamzah, pray over her."

He stood level with the middle of the bier. Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ziyād said to him, "O Abū Ḥamzah, is this how you saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stand at a funeral, [standing] where you stood for the man and where you stood for the woman?" He said, "Yes."
Then he turned to us and said, "Remember this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw a grave set apart, so he lined up his Companions behind him and prayed over it. He was asked, "Who told you of it?" He said, Ibn ʿAbbās [had].
label: machine translation

segments_en: A father is not to be executed for [killing] his child."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that for a fetus [lost through assault] the compensation is a slave, male or female. The one against whom the ruling was given said, "Should we pay blood-money for one who neither drank nor ate, nor cried out, nor made a sound at birth? Such a case should be nullified." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"This man speaks like a poet! In it is the compensation of a slave, male or female."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Isḥāq said: A man came to al-Barāʾ and said, "Did you [all] turn back on the day of Ḥunayn, O Abū ʿUmārah?" He said: "I bear witness that the Prophet ﷺ did not turn back. Rather, some hasty young men from among the people, with no weapons, went ahead toward this tribe of Hawāzin, who were a people of archers, and they showered them with a volley of arrows like a swarm of locusts, so they scattered. Then the people turned toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith was leading his mule. He dismounted, supplicated and asked for help, saying:
"I am the Prophet, no lie [in this]; I am the son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. O Allah, send down Your help."
Al-Barāʾ said: "By Allah, when the fighting grew fierce we would take shelter behind him, and the bravest among us was the one who stood level with him," meaning the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had a she-camel called al-ʿAḍbāʾ that was never outrun. Ḥumayd said: or was hardly ever outrun. Then a Bedouin came on a young camel and outran it,
and that was hard on the Muslims,
until he [the Prophet ﷺ] noticed it, and said:
"It is a duty upon Allah that nothing of this world rises up except that He brings it low."
Mūsā related it at greater length from Ḥammād, from Thābit, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed awake one night after arriving in Medina and said:
"If only a righteous man from among my Companions would guard me tonight."
She said: While we were like that, we heard the clinking of weapons, and he said, "Who is that?"
He said: "Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What brought you?"
He said: "Fear for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came into my heart, so I came to guard him."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made supplication for him, then slept.
In the narration of Ibn Rumḥ: We said, "Who is this?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey; some of us were fasting and some were not. He said: We stopped at a resting place on a hot day. Those with the most shade were those with a cloak, and some of us shielded ourselves from the sun with their hands. He said: The fasting people collapsed, while those who were not fasting stood up, pitched the tents and watered the mounts. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Those who did not fast have taken away the reward today."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us out in an expedition and said to us:
"If you meet so-and-so and so-and-so,"
two men from Quraysh whom he named, "burn them with fire."
He said: Then we came to him to bid him farewell when we wanted to set out, and he said:
"I had commanded you to burn so-and-so and so-and-so with fire,
but none punishes with fire except Allah,
so if you capture them, kill them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Umayyah, the son of my brother,

related to him that his father informed him that Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah said: I brought my father Abū Umayyah to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of the Conquest and said, "O Messenger of Allah, accept my father's pledge for emigration."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I will accept his pledge for jihad, for emigration has come to an end."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Aslam, from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, called ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā, wrote to ʿUmar ibn ʿUbaydillāh when he marched against the Ḥarūriyyah, informing him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, on one of the days when he met the enemy, waited until the sun had passed its zenith, then stood among them and said:
"O people, do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being. But when you meet them, be steadfast, and know that Paradise lies under the shade of swords."
Then the Prophet ﷺ stood and said:
"O Allah, Revealer of the Book, Driver of the clouds, Defeater of the factions, defeat them and grant us victory over them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Saʿīd,
he said: Yes, from Abū Hurayrah,
and [in another chain] Aḥmad ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Sarḥ informed us,
and al-Ḥārith ibn Miskīn,
by reading to him while I listened,
the wording being Aḥmad's; both said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Yūnus,
from Ibn Shihāb,
from Ibn al-Musayyab,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I was sent with concise yet comprehensive speech, and I was made victorious through terror [cast into enemies' hearts]. While I was sleeping, I was brought the keys of the treasures of the earth and they were placed in my hand."
Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has gone, and you are now extracting them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying, "Tell me: if I perform the obligatory prayers, fast Ramadan, treat as lawful what is lawful and treat as forbidden what is forbidden, and add nothing to that, will I enter Paradise?" He said, "Yes."
The man said, "By Allah, I will not add anything to that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, they said, "O Prophet of Allah, may Allah make us your ransom! Which drinks are suitable for us?" He said,
"Do not drink from the naqīr."
They said, "O Prophet of Allah, may Allah make us your ransom! Do you know what the naqīr is?" He said,
"Yes, it is a palm trunk whose middle is hollowed out. Nor [drink] from the gourd, nor from the ḥantamah [green jar]. Rather, you should use the waterskin that is tied at the mouth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever says, 'There is no god but Allah,' and disbelieves in whatever is worshipped besides Allah, his property and his blood become inviolable, and his reckoning is with Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever dies knowing that there is no god but Allah will enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey. He said: The provisions of the people ran out, until they were about to slaughter some of their pack animals. He said: Then ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah, if you were to gather what remains of the people's provisions and then supplicate to Allah over them..."

He said: So he did so. He said: Then the one with wheat came with his wheat, and the one with dates came with his dates. He said: Mujāhid said: And the one with date stones came with his date stones. I said, "What did they do with the date stones?" He said, "They would suck on them and drink water over them."
He said: Then he supplicated over them, until the people filled their provision bags. He said: Then at that point he said,

"I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. No servant will meet Allah with these two [testimonies], without doubting them, except that he will enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting around the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and with us were Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, among a group of people. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up from among us and was delayed in returning to us. We feared that he might be harmed [cut off] without us, and we were alarmed, so we got up. I was the first to be alarmed, so I went out seeking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until I came to a garden belonging to the Anṣār of Banū al-Najjār. I went around it looking for a gate but did not find one. Then I saw a channel entering the garden from an outside well — and the rabīʿ is a stream. So I squeezed myself together as a fox does, and entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said, "Abū Hurayrah?"
I said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "What is the matter with you?"

I said, "You were among us, then you got up and were delayed in returning, so we feared that you might be harmed without us, and we were alarmed. I was the first to be alarmed, so I came to this garden and squeezed myself together as a fox does, and these people are behind me." Then he said,
"O Abū Hurayrah!"
and he gave me his two sandals and said,
"Take these two sandals of mine, and whomever you meet beyond this garden who bears witness that there is no god but Allah, being certain of it in his heart, give him the glad tidings of Paradise."
The first person I met was ʿUmar, who said, "What are these two sandals, Abū Hurayrah?"

I said, "These are the sandals of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He sent me with them [to tell] whomever I meet who bears witness that there is no god but Allah, being certain of it in his heart, that I should give him the glad tidings of Paradise."

Then ʿUmar struck me with his hand on my chest, and I fell on my backside. He said, "Go back, Abū Hurayrah." So I returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and burst into tears, and ʿUmar followed me closely, right behind me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me,
"What is the matter with you, Abū Hurayrah?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was read to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, from Ibn Wahb,
from Ibn Jurayj,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have been commanded to prostrate on seven [parts of the body], and not to hold back the hair or the clothes: the forehead, the nose, the two hands, the two knees, and the two feet."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
used to see ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, sit cross-legged in prayer when he sat.
So I did the same, and I was young at the time,
but ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar forbade me and said, "The sunnah of the prayer is that you hold your right foot upright and fold the left."
I said, "But you do that."
He said, "My legs cannot carry me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [She was] the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and she said: People used to come to the Friday prayer from their homes and from the upper districts [of Madinah],
and they would come in the dust,
the dust and sweat would settle on them,
and sweat would pour from them.
One of them came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was with me, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"If only you would purify yourselves for this day of yours."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he asked ʿAmrah about the bath
on Friday, and she said that ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: People used to be busy working for themselves,
and when they went to the Friday prayer, they went as they were. So it was said to them, "If only you would bathe."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr and al-ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, passed by one of the gatherings of the Anṣār while they were weeping.
He said, "What makes you weep?" They said, "We remembered the gathering of the Prophet ﷺ with us."

So he went in to the Prophet ﷺ and told him about that. [The narrator] said: The Prophet ﷺ came out with the edge of a cloak bound around his head. He said: He ascended the pulpit, and he never ascended it after that day.
He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "I enjoin you to treat the Anṣār well,
for they are my inner circle and my trusted ones.
They have fulfilled what was upon them,
and what is due to them remains.
So accept from those of them who do good,
and overlook the wrongdoing of those of them who do wrong."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A year of drought struck the people in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was delivering the sermon from the pulpit on Friday, a Bedouin stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah,
the livestock have perished and the families are hungry,
so pray to Allah for us that He may give us rain."
He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands,
and there was not a wisp of cloud in the sky.
He said: Then clouds rose up like mountains,
and he did not descend from his pulpit until I saw the rain running down his beard.
He said: It rained on us that day,
and the next day, and the day after that, and the one following it, until the next Friday.
Then that Bedouin or another man stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah,
the buildings have collapsed and the livestock have drowned,
so pray to Allah for us."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands and said:
"O Allah, around us and not upon us."
He said: Whenever he pointed with his hand toward any part of the sky, it cleared, until Madinah was like a hollow [in the middle of the clouds],
and the valley, the valley of Qanāh, flowed for a month.
He said: No one came from any direction except that he spoke of the abundant rain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ stood on the day of al-Fiṭr and prayed, beginning with the prayer before the sermon, then he addressed the people. When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ had finished, he came down and went to the women and admonished them, while leaning on the hand of Bilāl, and Bilāl was spreading out his garment in which the women were putting charity. He said: A woman would throw in her ring, and they would throw in, and they would throw in. And Ibn Bakr said: her ring.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when the sun was eclipsed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out dragging his cloak until he reached the mosque, and the people gathered to him. He led us in two rakʿahs of prayer, and when the sun cleared, he said:

"The sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah, by which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, frightens His servants. They do not eclipse for the death of anyone nor for his life. So when you see that, pray until what is upon you is removed."
That was because a son of his, called Ibrāhīm, had died, and some people had said something about it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, used to pray on his riding animal and pray the Witr on it,
and he would report that the Prophet ﷺ used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to go to Qubāʾ, meaning every Saturday, going either riding or walking.
Ibn Dīnār said: And Ibn ʿUmar used to do the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "I saw my head being struck off, and I saw it rolling away." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Satan toys with one of you, frightening him in his sleep, and then in the morning he goes and tells people about it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Interpret [dreams] according to their names and their epithets, and a dream goes to the first interpreter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When the time draws near, the dream of the believer will hardly ever be false. The most truthful of them in dreams is the most truthful in speech. And the dream of a Muslim is one part of forty-six parts of prophecy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm al-Faḍl said, "O Messenger of Allah, I saw [in a dream] as if a limb of your body were in my house." He said:
"You have seen something good. Fāṭimah will give birth to a boy, and you will nurse him."

She gave birth to Ḥusayn or Ḥasan, and she nursed him with the milk of Qutham. She said: I brought him to the Prophet ﷺ and placed him in his lap, and he urinated. I struck his shoulder, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"You have hurt my son, may Allah have mercy on you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men

from Balī came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they had accepted Islam together. One of them was more diligent than the other. The diligent one went out on a military expedition and was martyred. The other stayed on after him for a year and then died.

Ṭalḥah said: I saw in a dream that I was at the gate of Paradise, and there I was with the two of them. Someone came out of Paradise and gave permission to the one who died last of the two. Then he came out and gave permission to the one who was martyred. Then he returned to me and said, "Go back, for your time has not yet come."
In the morning Ṭalḥah told people about it, and they were amazed at that, and it reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
They told him the story, and he said:
"What about it amazes you?"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, this one was the more diligent of the two, then he was martyred, and the other entered Paradise before him."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Did this one not remain a year after him?" They said, "Yes." He said:
"And he reached Ramadan and fasted it, and prayed so many prostrations during that year?"
They said, "Yes." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Then what is between them is farther than what is between the heaven and the earth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I dislike the iron collar and I like the shackle; the shackle is steadfastness in the religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq and his companions came to him and said, "You are ruined, O ʿImrān."
He said, "I am not ruined." They said, "Yes, you are."
He said, "What has ruined me?" They said, "Allah said: {And fight them until there is no more persecution and the religion is entirely for Allah.}"
He said, "We fought them until we drove them out, and the religion was entirely for Allah. If you wish, I will relate to you a hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us out on a military detachment, and a man of the Muslims attacked a man of the polytheists. He then mentioned the hadith and added: the earth cast him out. The Prophet ﷺ was informed, and he said:
"The earth receives one who is worse than him, but Allah wanted to show you the greatness of the sanctity of 'There is no god but Allah.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said during the Farewell Pilgrimage:

"Indeed, the most sacred of days is this day of yours; indeed, the most sacred of months is this month of yours; indeed, the most sacred of lands is this land of yours. Indeed, your blood and your wealth are sacred to you, like the sacredness of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours. Have I conveyed [the message]?" They said, "Yes." He said, "O Allah, bear witness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My companions, those who came with me on the ship, and I were staying at Baqīʿ Buṭḥān,

while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Madinah. A group of them would take turns attending the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the night prayer each night. Abū Mūsā said: My companions and I met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was busy with some matter of his, so he delayed the prayer until the night had well advanced. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out and led them in prayer. When he had finished his prayer, he said to those present: "
Stay where you are, and I will tell you, and rejoice: it is among the blessings of Allah upon you that none of the people is praying at this hour except you." Or he said: "
No one has prayed at this hour except you."
We do not know which of the two statements he said. Abū Mūsā said: So we returned rejoicing at what we had heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Whoever prays the two cool prayers will enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ and Zayd ibn Thābit ate the pre-dawn meal.
When they had finished their meal, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ stood up for prayer and prayed.
We asked Anas: How long was it between their finishing their meal and their starting the prayer? He said: The time it takes a man to recite fifty verses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never gave up the two units of prayer after the ʿAṣr prayer.
He said: ʿĀʾishah said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Do not seek out the rising of the sun or its setting to pray at that time."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of the Ṣuffah
were poor people, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ once said: "
Whoever has food for two should take a third with him, and whoever has food for four should take a fifth, or a sixth."
Or as he said.

Abū Bakr came with three, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ went with ten, and Abū Bakr with three. He said: So it was he, I, my father, and my mother, and I do not know whether he said, "and my wife," and a servant shared between our house and the house of Abū Bakr. He said: Abū Bakr dined with the Prophet ﷺ.

Then he stayed until I had prayed the night prayer, then he returned and stayed until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became drowsy. Then he came after a portion of the night had passed, as Allah willed. His wife said to him: What kept you from your guests? Or she said: your guest. He said: Did you not feed them dinner? She said: They refused until you came. They had offered it to them, but they had overpowered them. He said: So I went and hid, and he said: O Ghunthar!
He cut me off and cursed me, and said: Eat, may it not be pleasant for you!

And he said: By Allah, I will never eat it. He said: By Allah, we did not take a morsel but that more grew from beneath it. He said: Until we were full, and it became more than it had been before. Abū Bakr looked at it, and it was just as it was or more.

He said to his wife: O sister of Banū Firās, what is this? She said: No, by the delight of my eye, it is now three times more than it was before. He said: Then Abū Bakr ate from it and said: That was only from Satan, meaning his oath. Then he ate a morsel from it, then carried it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it remained with him until morning. He said: There was a treaty between us and a certain people, and its term expired. We identified twelve men, with each man were people; Allah knows how many with each man, except that he sent them along with them. And they all ate from it.
Or as he said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the people became many, he said: They discussed how to let people know the time of prayer by something they could recognize.
They mentioned lighting a fire or striking a bell.
Then Bilāl was ordered to say the words of the adhān in pairs and the iqāmah in single.
label: machine translation

segments_en: to him: "
I see that you love sheep and the desert.
So when you are with your sheep or in your desert and you call the adhān for prayer, raise your voice in the call,
for no jinn, human, or anything else hears the extent of the muʾadhdhin's voice except that it will bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The believer to the believer is like a building,
each part strengthening the other."
Then he interlaced his fingers.
The Prophet ﷺ was sitting when a man came asking, or seeking a need. He turned his face to us and said: "Intercede, and you will be rewarded,
and Allah will decree through the tongue of His Prophet whatever He wills."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to enter Makkah by the upper mountain pass. Both said, from Yaḥyā: The Prophet ﷺ used to enter Makkah from Kadāʾ, by the pass of al-Baṭḥāʾ, and he would leave by the lower pass.
Al-Barmakī added: meaning the two passes of Makkah. The narration of Musaddad is more complete.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Sumayy,
the freed slave of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Sammān,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"One ʿUmrah to the next is an expiation for what is between them, and an accepted Hajj has no reward except Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a woman of the Anṣār whom Ibn ʿAbbās named, but I forgot her name:
"What prevented you from performing Hajj with us?"
She said: "We had only two water-carrying camels. The father of her child and her son performed Hajj on one camel, and left us a camel to water [our land] with." He said:
"Then when Ramadan comes, perform ʿUmrah, for an ʿUmrah in it equals a Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: As for al-Qaʿnabī, he said: I read to Mālik ibn Anas; as for Qutaybah, he said: Mālik narrated to us; and Yaḥyā said, and the wording is his: I said to Mālik, "Did Ibn Shihāb narrate to you from Anas ibn Mālik that the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah in the year of the Conquest with a helmet on his head, and when he took it off, a man came and said, 'Ibn Khaṭal is clinging to the curtains of the Kaʿbah.' He said: 'Kill him.'"
Mālik said: "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
they said: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī,
from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"A city-dweller must not sell for a desert-dweller."
And Zuhayr said, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he forbade a city-dweller to sell for a desert-dweller.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Banū al-Ṣaʿiq, one of the Banū Kilāb, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him about the stud fee for a male animal's breeding, and he forbade him from that. He said: "We are honored for doing that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik; and Qutaybah narrated to us, Layth narrated to us;
both from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Surplus water must not be withheld in order to withhold grass by it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to my father: Ibn Numayr narrated to you,
he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Sumayy,
from al-Nuʿmān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh,
from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever fasts one day for the sake of Allah, Allah will distance his face from the Fire by that day by seventy years."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met Muḥārib ibn Dithār on a horse, as he was coming to the place where he used to judge, and I asked him about this hadith. He narrated to me and said: I heard ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever drags his garment out of arrogance,
Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection."
I said to Muḥārib, "Did he mention the lower garment?" He said: "He did not specify a lower garment or a shirt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should walk in one sandal; either put on both or take off both."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Bashīr Abū Ismāʿīl, from Mujāhid,
that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr,

had a sheep slaughtered for him among his family. When he came, he said: "Have you given a gift to our Jewish neighbor? Have you given a gift to our Jewish neighbor? I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Jibrīl kept advising me about the neighbor until I thought he would make him an heir.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no servant who raises his hands, until his armpits show, asking Allah for a request, except that He gives it to him, as long as he does not hurry."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, how does he hurry?" He said:
"He says, 'I have asked and asked, and I have not been given anything.'"
This hadith was also narrated by al-Zuhrī, from Abū ʿUbayd, the freed slave of Ibn Azhar, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"The supplication of any of you is answered as long as he does not hurry, saying, 'I supplicated but was not answered.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent a message to a woman from among the Muhājirīn,
and she had a slave who was a carpenter. He said to her: "
Tell your slave to make for us the wooden pieces of the pulpit." So she instructed her slave,
and he went and cut [wood] from the tamarisk trees,
and made a pulpit for him.
When he finished it, she sent word to the Prophet ﷺ that he had finished it. He ﷺ said: "
Send it to me."
So they brought it, and the Prophet ﷺ carried it and placed it where you see it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ somewhere between Makkah and Madīnah. They were in the state of iḥrām, while I was a man not in iḥrām, on a horse,
and I was a good climber of mountains.
While I was in that state, I saw the people looking intently at something, so I went to see,
and it was a wild donkey. I said to them, "What is this?" They said, "We do not know."
I said, "It is a wild donkey."
They said, "It is what you saw."
I had forgotten my whip, so I said to them, "Hand me my whip."
They said, "We will not help you with it." So I dismounted and took it,
then I went after it,
and it was only a moment until I had struck it down,
so I came to them and said to them, "Get up and carry it."
They said, "We will not touch it."
So I carried it until I brought it to them. Some of them refused, and some of them ate,
and I said, "I will go and make the Prophet ﷺ wait for you." I caught up with him and told him the story, and he said to me: "
Do you have any of it left with you?" I said, "Yes." He said: "
Eat, for it is food that Allah has fed you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wives
of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were two parties. One party included ʿĀʾishah, Ḥafṣah, Ṣafiyyah and Sawdah,
and the other party was Umm Salamah and the rest of the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Muslims knew the love of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for ʿĀʾishah,
so if any of them had a gift he wished to give to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would delay it,
until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the house of ʿĀʾishah; then the giver of the gift would send it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in ʿĀʾishah's house.
The party of Umm Salamah spoke about this,
and they said to her, "Speak to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that he speaks to the people,
and says: Whoever wishes to give a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, let him give it to him wherever he is among the houses of his wives."
So Umm Salamah spoke to him about what they had said,
but he said nothing to her. They asked her,
and she said, "He did not say anything to me."
They said to her, "Speak to him."
She said: I spoke to him when he came around to me again,
but he said nothing to her. They asked her,
and she said, "He did not say anything to me."
They said to her, "Keep speaking to him until he answers you."
So he came around to her and she spoke to him. He said to her: "
Do not trouble me concerning ʿĀʾishah,
for the revelation has not come to me
while I was in the garment of any woman except ʿĀʾishah."
She said: I said, "I repent to Allah for troubling you, O Messenger of Allah."

Then they called Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and sent her to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying, "Your wives adjure you by Allah to be just regarding the daughter of Abū Bakr." She spoke to him. He said: "O my daughter,
do you not love what I love?" She said, "Yes." So she returned to them and informed them.
They said, "Go back to him."
But she refused to go back,
so they sent Zaynab bint Jaḥsh. She came to him and spoke harshly,
