segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy after he had been placed in his grave, and he ordered that he be taken out,
and he placed him on his knees,
and blew some of his saliva on him and clothed him in his own shirt, and Allah knows best.
He had clothed ʿAbbās in a shirt.
Sufyān said: Abū Hārūn said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had two shirts on,
and the son of ʿAbdullāh said to him: O Messenger of Allah,
clothe my father in your shirt that is next to your skin.
Sufyān said: They think that the Prophet ﷺ clothed ʿAbdullāh in his shirt as a recompense for what he had done.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a burdah (he said: And what is a burdah? He said: A shamlah, a woolen wrap). She said: O Messenger of Allah, I wove this with my own hands to clothe you with it.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it, being in need of it, and came out to us wearing it as his lower garment. Then so-and-so, son of so-and-so (a man he named that day) said: O Messenger of Allah, how beautiful this burdah is! Clothe me with it. He said: "Yes."

When he went inside, he folded it and sent it to him. The people said to the man: By Allah, you did not do well. The Prophet ﷺ wore it because he was in need of it, then you asked him for it, though you knew that he never turns away one who asks.
He said: By Allah, I did not ask him for it to wear it, but I asked him for it so that it would be my shroud.
Sahl said: So it was his shroud on the day he died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A boy was born to me tonight, and I named him after my father, Ibrāhīm."

Then he handed him to Umm Sayf, the wife of a blacksmith called Abū Sayf. The Prophet ﷺ set out to him and I followed him. We reached Abū Sayf while he was blowing on his bellows, and the house was filled with smoke. I hurried ahead of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Abū Sayf, stop, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has come.
He stopped, and the Prophet ﷺ called for the child, held him close to him, and said what Allah willed him to say.
Anas said: I saw him breathing his last in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the eyes of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shed tears. He said:
"The eye weeps and the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord. By Allah, O Ibrāhīm, we are truly grieved by your departure."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Masrūq in a house that had statues of Mary.
Masrūq said, "These are statues of Khosrow."
I said, "No, these are statues of Mary."
Masrūq said, "Listen, I heard ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'The people who will be most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are the image-makers.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to see me when I had covered a niche of mine with a curtain that had images on it. When he saw it, he tore it down, and his face changed color, and he said:
"ʿĀʾishah, the people who will be most severely punished with Allah on the Day of Resurrection are those who imitate the creation of Allah."
ʿĀʾishah said, "So we cut it up and made one or two cushions from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years, and he never once said "Ugh" to me, and he never said about anything I had done, "Why did you do that?" nor about anything I had left undone, "Why did you not do it?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among the best of people in character. I never touched any silk or brocade or anything softer than the palm of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I never smelled any musk or perfume more fragrant than the sweat of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: one,

among them Mughīrah, so-and-so, and a third man, also from ash-Shaʿbī, from Warrād, the scribe of al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, that Muʿāwiyah wrote to al-Mughīrah: "Write to me with something you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." So al-Mughīrah wrote to him: "I heard him say when he finished the prayer:
'There is no god but Allah,
alone, without partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise,
and He has power over all things.'"

[He said it] three times. He said: And he forbade gossip, excessive questioning, wasting wealth, withholding [what one owes] and demanding [what is not one's due], disobedience to mothers, and burying daughters alive.
And from Hushaym: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr informed us, saying: I heard Warrād narrate this hadith from al-Mughīrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Ahead of you is a basin [as wide] as the distance between Jarbāʾ and Adhruḥ, in which are pitchers like the stars of the sky. Whoever comes to it and drinks from it will never be thirsty afterward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ash-Shaʿbī,
both said: Jarīr said, "I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said to him, 'I pledge allegiance to you to hear and obey, in what I like and in what I dislike.' The Prophet ﷺ said:
'Can you do that, Jarīr? Are you able to bear that?' He said:
'Say: as much as I am able.'
So he took my pledge, [along with] sincere advice for every Muslim."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that she
asked the Prophet of Allah ﷺ about a woman who sees in her sleep what a man sees. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If a woman sees that, she should perform a full bath."
Umm Sulaym said: I was embarrassed by that, and I said, "Does this happen?" The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:

"Yes. Then how else would resemblance occur? The man's fluid is thick and white, and the woman's fluid is thin and yellow. Whichever of the two rises above or comes first, the resemblance comes from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Qutaybah and Ibn
Ḥujr — Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said "he informed us," and the others said, "Ismāʿīl narrated to us,"
— that is, Ibn Jaʿfar — from Sharīk,
— that is, Ibn Abī Namir — from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from his father,

who said: I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on Monday to Qubāʾ. When we were among Banū Sālim, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at the door of ʿItbān and called out to him. He came out dragging his waist wrapper. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "We have made the man hurry."
ʿItbān said, "Messenger of Allah, what do you think about a man who is hurried away from his wife and does not ejaculate? What is required of him?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Water is only [required] because of water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the dawn prayer, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited, and the recitation became difficult for him. When he finished, he said:
"Perhaps you recite behind your imam."
We said, "Yes, that is so, Messenger of Allah." He said:
"Do not do so, except with the Opening of the Book, for there is no prayer for one who does not recite it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The last glance I took at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was when he lifted the curtain on Monday. I looked at his face, as if it were a page of the Qurʾān, while the people were behind Abū Bakr in prayer. He wanted to move, but [Abū Bakr] was signaled to stay in place, and he let the curtain fall. He died at the end of that day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās: "O Abū al-ʿAbbās, I am amazed at the disagreement among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began the talbiyah, when he made the pilgrimage binding upon himself."

He said: "I am the most knowledgeable of people about that. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed only one Hajj, and from that came their disagreement. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out intending Hajj, and when he had prayed his two rakʿahs in his mosque at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, he made it binding upon himself while still in his place of sitting, and he pronounced the talbiyah for Hajj when he finished his two rakʿahs. Some people heard that from him and memorized it from him. Then he mounted, and when his camel rose up with him, he pronounced the talbiyah, and other people heard it from him. This was because people used to come in separate groups, so they heard him pronouncing the talbiyah when his camel rose up with him, and they said: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only began the talbiyah when his camel rose up with him.' Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on, and when he ascended the high ground of al-Baydāʾ, he pronounced the talbiyah, and other people heard that from him, and they said: 'He only began the talbiyah when he ascended the high ground of al-Baydāʾ.' By Allah, he made it binding upon himself at his place of prayer, and he pronounced the talbiyah when his camel rose up with him, and he pronounced the talbiyah when he ascended the high ground of al-Baydāʾ."
Saʿīd said: "So whoever follows the statement of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās should begin the talbiyah at his place of prayer when he has finished his two rakʿahs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ said: "When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ took the road of al-Furʿ, he would pronounce the talbiyah when his mount rose up with him, and when he took the road of Uḥud, he would pronounce the talbiyah when he reached the height of the mountain of al-Baydāʾ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Hajj alone (ifrād).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to ʿĀʾishah, in part of this account. He said, at his saying: "And pronounce the talbiyah for Hajj."
"Then perform Hajj and do what the pilgrim does, except that you do not circumambulate the House and do not pray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions arrived on the fourth night of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. When they had circumambulated the House and [walked between] Ṣafā and Marwah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Make it an ʿUmrah, except for the one who has the sacrificial animal with him."

Then when it was the Day of Tarwiyah, they pronounced the talbiyah for Hajj, and when it was the Day of Sacrifice, they came and circumambulated the House, but they did not walk between Ṣafā and Marwah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ pronounced the talbiyah for Hajj. When he arrived, he circumambulated the House and [walked] between Ṣafā and Marwah (Ibn Shawkar said: and he did not shorten his hair; then the two agreed), and he did not come out of iḥrām because of the sacrificial animal. He commanded those who had not brought sacrificial animals to circumambulate, to walk between Ṣafā and Marwah, and to shorten their hair, and then come out of iḥrām.
Ibn Manīʿ added in his narration: "or shave, and then come out of iḥrām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, and testified before him that he had heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in his illness in which he was taken, forbidding ʿUmrah before Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said] to the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "Do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade such and such, and forbade riding on leopard skins?" They said: "Yes."
He said: "Do you know that he forbade combining Hajj and ʿUmrah?" They said: "As for this, no."
He said: "Indeed, it is among them, but you have forgotten."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until, when he was at ʿUsfān, Surāqah ibn Mālik al-Mudlijī said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, decide for us a ruling as for a people who were born today." He said:

"Indeed, Allah the Exalted has brought an ʿUmrah into this Hajj of yours. So when you arrive, whoever circumambulates the House and [walks] between Ṣafā and Marwah has come out of iḥrām, except the one who has a sacrificial animal with him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say about one who performed Hajj and then converted it into an ʿUmrah: "That was only for the group of riders who were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ pronounced the talbiyah, and he mentioned the talbiyah like the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar. He said: "And the people would add: 'Owner of the ascents (Dhā al-Maʿārij).'"
and similar words, while the Prophet ﷺ heard them and did not say anything to them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this account, he said in it: The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Take off your cloak."
So he took it off over his head, and he narrated the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah created the creation, and when He had finished with them, the womb [of kinship] stood up and said, 'This is the place of one who seeks refuge with You from being severed.'
He said, 'Yes. Are you not pleased that I join whoever joins you and sever whoever severs you?' It said, 'Yes.'
He said, 'Then that is yours.'"
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Recite, if you wish: {Would you then, if you were given authority, perhaps spread corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship? Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He made them deaf and blinded their eyes. Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting Sūrat aṭ-Ṭūr in the Maghrib prayer. When he reached this verse: {Or were they created by nothing, or are they the creators? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they have no certainty. Or do they possess the treasuries of your Lord, or are they the controllers?} my heart almost flew [out of me].
Sufyān said: As for me, I only heard az-Zuhrī narrate from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from his father: I heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting Sūrat aṭ-Ṭūr in the Maghrib prayer.
I did not hear him add what they told me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"In Paradise there are two gardens whose vessels and everything in them are of silver, and two gardens whose vessels and everything in them are of gold. Nothing stands between the people and their looking at their Lord except the cloak of majesty over His face, in the Garden of Eden."
And with this chain of narration, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

"In Paradise there is a tent made of a hollowed pearl, sixty miles in breadth. In every corner of it there is a family who cannot see those in the other corners, and the believer goes around visiting them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah,

the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ sent Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She asked permission to enter while he was lying down with me in my wrap, and he permitted her. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, your wives have sent me to you to ask you for fairness regarding the daughter of Abū Quḥāfah," while I remained silent. ʿĀʾishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"O my little daughter, do you not love what I love?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Then love this one."

She said: Fāṭimah got up when she heard that from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and went back to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and told them what she had said and what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said to her. They said to her: "We do not see that you have achieved anything for us. Go back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and say to him: Your wives implore you for fairness regarding the daughter of Abū Quḥāfah."
Fāṭimah said: "By Allah, I will never speak to him about her."

ʿĀʾishah said: So the wives of the Prophet ﷺ sent Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, who was the one among them who rivaled me in standing with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I never saw a woman better in religion than Zaynab, more fearful of Allah, more truthful in speech, more maintaining of family ties, greater in charity, or more devoted in giving of herself in the work by which she gave charity and drew near to Allah, the Exalted, except for a sharpness of temper she had, from which she quickly recovered. She said: She asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with ʿĀʾishah in her wrap, in the same condition in which Fāṭimah had entered upon him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted her, and she said: "O Messenger of Allah, your wives have sent me to you to ask you for fairness regarding the daughter of Abū Quḥāfah."

She said: Then she set upon me and spoke at length against me, while I was watching the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and watching his eyes to see whether he would permit me to answer her. She said: Zaynab did not stop until I realized that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not dislike my defending myself. She said: So when I took her on, I did not take long to overcome her, once I bore down on her. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, smiling:
"She is indeed the daughter of Abū Bakr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said to ʿUmar after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Come with us to Umm Ayman to visit her, just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to visit her."
When we reached her, she wept. They said to her: "What makes you weep? What is with Allah is better for His Messenger ﷺ."
She said: "I do not weep because I do not know that what is with Allah is better for His Messenger ﷺ, but I weep because the revelation has been cut off from the heavens."
This stirred them to weep, and they began weeping along with her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zurārah al-Ḥaḍramī, Suwayd ibn Saʿīd and al-Walīd ibn Shujāʿ. Sahl and Minjāb said: He informed us. And
the others said: ʿAlī ibn Mushir narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah,
from ʿAbdullāh,

who said: When this verse was revealed: {There is no blame on those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten, when they fear Allah and believe} to the end of the verse, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"I was told: You are one of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by, and my mother Umm Sulaym heard his voice and said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, [this is] Unays."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made three supplications for me; I have seen two of them in this world, and I hope for the third in the Hereafter.
This ḥadīth is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb from this route, and this ḥadīth has been narrated through more than one route from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A son of one of the daughters of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was dying, so she sent word to him asking him to come. He sent back to her, saying: "
Indeed, to Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives, and everything with Him has an appointed term. So let her be patient and hope for reward from Allah."

She sent for him again, swearing an oath that he must come. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up and I stood with him, and with him were Muʿādh ibn Jabal, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit. When we entered, they handed the child to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while his soul was rattling in his chest.
[The narrator] said: I think he said: It was like a worn waterskin.
He said: Then the eyes of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ filled with tears, and ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit said to him:
"What is this, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "
It is the mercy that Allah has placed in the hearts of the children of Adam. And Allah only shows mercy to those of His servants who are merciful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When you see a funeral procession, stand up; and whoever follows it should not sit until it is set down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ when a funeral procession passed by us, and he stood up for it. When we went to carry it, we found it was the funeral of a Jew. So we said: "O Messenger of Allah, it is only the funeral of a Jew." He said: "
Death is a cause of terror, so when you see a funeral procession, stand up."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to put two men from those killed at Uḥud together in one garment, then say: "
Which of them had learned more of the Qurʾān?"
When one of them was pointed out to him, he would put him first in the grave and say: "
I will be a witness over these on the Day of Resurrection."
And he commanded that they be buried in their blood,
and they were not washed, and the funeral prayer was not offered for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿAlī], peace be upon him, said: We were at a funeral at Baqīʿ al-Gharqad, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and sat down. He had a staff with him, and he began to scratch the ground with the staff. Then he raised his head and said: "
There is none among you, and no soul that has been created, except that Allah has written its place in the Fire or in Paradise, and [except that] it has been written as wretched or blessed."

He said: A man from the people said: "O Prophet of Allah, then should we not rely on what is written for us and abandon deeds? For whoever is of the people of happiness will surely end up with happiness, and whoever is of the people of wretchedness will surely end up with wretchedness." He said: "

Do deeds, for everyone is made ready [for what he was created]. As for the people of happiness, they will be made ready for happiness; and as for the people of wretchedness, they will be made ready for wretchedness."
Then the Prophet of Allah recited: "

{As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship.}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
— and the wording is his — from Ibn al-Qāsim, who said: Mālik narrated to me, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

When one of you dies, his place is shown to him morning and evening. If he is of the people of Paradise, then [he is shown his place] among the people of Paradise, and if he is of the people of the Fire, then among the people of the Fire. It is said: This is your place until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, resurrects you on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "My mother died suddenly and did not make a will, and I think that had she been able to speak she would have given charity. Will she have a reward if I give charity on her behalf, and will I have a reward too?" He said: "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Abū al-Mutawakkil
passed by them in the marketplace, and some people, of whom I was one, stood up to him. He said: We said, "We have come to you to ask about currency exchange."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Gold for gold, measure for equal measure."
Yaʿqūb did not mention "measure for equal measure."
Muʿāwiyah said, "This man does not know what he is saying."
ʿUbādah said, "By Allah, I do not care if I am not in a land where Muʿāwiyah is. I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Muʿāwiyah
sold a drinking vessel of gold or silver for more than its weight. Abū al-Dardāʾ said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid the like of this, except like for like."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Khaybar I acquired a necklace containing gold and beads, and I wanted to sell it. This was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Separate some of it from the rest, then sell it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no usury except in deferred transactions."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to sell gold for silver, or silver for gold. I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him about that, and he said:
"When you make a transaction with your partner, do not part from him while any ambiguity remains between you and him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he disliked taking
dinars in place of dirhams, and dirhams in place of dinars.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he saw nothing wrong—that is—in receiving dirhams in place of dinars and dinars in place of dirhams.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding receiving dinars in place of dirhams: he disliked it when it was from a loan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he saw nothing wrong with it, even if it was from a loan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, he called for a scale, weighed for me, and gave me extra.
label: machine translation

segments_en: As for what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade, it is that food be sold until it has been fully received.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām said: I bought some food from the charity food, and I made a profit on it before taking possession of it. So I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said:
"Do not sell it until you have taken possession of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not lawful to combine a loan with a sale, nor two conditions in one sale, nor to sell what you do not have."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A man has no right to sell what he does not own."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I sold a young camel to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I came to him to ask for payment. He said:
"Yes, I will pay you only with a choice camel."
He paid me and paid me well. A Bedouin also came to him demanding repayment of a camel of a certain age, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Give him a camel of that age."
That day they gave him a camel, and he said, "This is better than my camel." He said:
"The best of you are those who are best in repaying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A loan in the offspring of an offspring [of a camel] is usury."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ caught up with me while I was on a poor water camel of ours. I said, "We will always have a poor camel, alas!" The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Will you sell it to me, Jābir?"
I said, "Rather it is yours, Messenger of Allah." He said:
"O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy on him. I have taken it for such and such, and I lend you its back to Madinah."
When I reached Madinah, I prepared it and went to him with it. He said:
"Bilāl, give him its price."
When I turned away, he called me back, and I feared he would return it. He said, "It is yours."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the two parties to a sale disagree and there is no proof between them, then what is said by the owner of the goods stands, or they leave the deal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were present with Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd when two men came to him who had made a sale of some goods. One of them said, "I took it for such and such."
The other said, "I sold it for such and such."

Abū ʿUbaydah said, "Ibn Masʿūd was brought a case like this, and he said: I was present when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought a case like this, and he ordered the seller to swear an oath, then the buyer chooses: if he wishes he takes it, and if he wishes he leaves it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ sold a mudabbar [a slave promised freedom upon his master's death].
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade selling surplus water.
The manager of al-Wahṭ sold the surplus water of al-Wahṭ, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr disliked it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He held that a woman with irregular bleeding (mustaḥāḍah) does not have to perform ablution for every prayer, unless something other than the blood breaks her ablution, in which case she performs ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Ḥabībah used to have irregular bleeding, and her husband would have relations with her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She had irregular bleeding, and her husband would have intercourse with her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I performed Hajj and went in to see Umm Salamah, and I said, "O Mother of the Believers, Samurah ibn Jundub commands the women to make up the prayers missed during menstruation."

She said, "They are not to make them up. One of the Prophet's ﷺ wives would sit out for forty nights after childbirth, and the Prophet ﷺ never commanded her to make up the prayers of the postnatal period."
Muḥammad, meaning Ibn Ḥātim, said: Her name is Musah, and she is called Umm Busah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman from Banū Ghifār, whose name she gave me, said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made me ride behind him on the saddle-bag of his mount. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept travelling until morning, then made the camel kneel, and I got down from the back of his saddle-bag, and there was a stain of my blood on it. It was the first menstrual period I had ever had. I huddled up against the camel and felt ashamed. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw what was wrong with me and saw the blood, he said,
"What is the matter with you? Perhaps you have begun to menstruate?" I said, "Yes." He said,
"Then tidy yourself up, then take a vessel of water, put some salt in it, and wash the blood off the saddle-bag. Then go back to your mount."

She said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ conquered Khaybar, he gave us a modest share of the spoils. She said: And she never became clean from a menstrual period without putting salt in her water for purification, and when she died she instructed that salt be put in the water for her washing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She mentioned the women of the Anṣār, praised them, and spoke well of them. She said: A woman from among them came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he narrated something similar in meaning, except that he said, "a piece of cloth perfumed with musk."
Musaddad said: Abū ʿAwānah used to say "firṣah," and Abū al-Aḥwaṣ used to say "qurṣah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A report] similar to this ḥadīth. He said: The Muslims stood and struck the dust with their palms, and they did not take up any of the dust. Then he narrated something similar, but he did not mention the shoulders and the armpits.
Ibn al-Layth said: [He wiped] up to what is above the elbows.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In this ḥadīth he said:
"O ʿAmmār, it would have been enough for you to do this."
Then he struck the ground with his hands, then struck one hand against the other, then wiped his face and his forearms up to the middle of the forearms, not reaching the elbows, with a single strike.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this story, he said:
"It would have been enough for you."
The Prophet ﷺ struck the ground with his hand, then blew on it, and wiped his face and his hands with it. Salamah was uncertain, and he said, "I do not know whether it said 'up to the elbows.'"
That is, or up to the hands.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In this ḥadīth he said: Then he, meaning the Prophet ﷺ, said,
"It would have been enough for you to strike the ground with your hands and then wipe your face and your hands with them." And he went on to relate the rest of the ḥadīth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qatādah was asked about tayammum
during a journey, and he said: A narrator told me, from ash-Shaʿbī,
from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abzā,
from ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Up to the elbows."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I set out with Ibn ʿUmar on an errand to Ibn ʿAbbās. Ibn ʿUmar finished his errand, and part of what he related that day was this: A man passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in one of the lanes, after he had come out from relieving himself of stool or urine, and greeted him with salām, but he did not return the greeting. When the man was about to disappear into the lane, he struck the wall with his hands and wiped his face with them, then struck again and wiped his forearms. Then he returned the man's greeting and said,
"Nothing prevented me from returning your greeting except that I was not in a state of purity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some sheep and goats were gathered with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said,
"O Abū Dharr, go out into the desert with them."

So I went out to al-Rabadhah, and I would become in a state of major ritual impurity and stay like that for five or six days. I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said, "Abū Dharr." I stayed silent, and he said,
"May your mother lose you, Abū Dharr! Woe to your mother!"

Then he called a black slave girl for me, and she brought a large bowl containing water. She screened me with a garment, and I screened myself with the camel, and I washed, and it was as though I had cast off a mountain from myself. Then he said,
"Clean earth is the purifier of the Muslim, even for ten years. When you find water, let it touch your skin, for that is better."
Musaddad said: [They were] sheep and goats from the charity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She was
one of those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, a poor person stands at my door and I find nothing to give him."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her,
"If you find nothing to give him except a burnt hoof, then put it in his hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, tell me: is the cancelling of Hajj into ʿUmrah for us alone, or for people in general?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Rather, it is for us alone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ continued to recite the talbiyah until he threw the pebbles at Jamrat al-ʿAqabah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cupped while in a state of iḥrām, on the top of his foot, because of a pain he had.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh was asked about a man who,
on seeing the House, raises his hands. He said, "I did not think anyone did this except the Jews. We performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he did not do it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yaʿlā [reported] that the Prophet ﷺ performed the circumambulation with his right shoulder uncovered.
Qabīṣah said: and he was wearing a cloak.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"All of ʿArafah is a place of standing, all of Minā is a place of sacrifice, all of Muzdalifah is a place of standing, and all the paths of Makkah are a road and a place of sacrifice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Ibn] ʿAbbās [reported] that the Prophet ﷺ delayed the circumambulation of the Day of Sacrifice until night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not build you a house or a structure at Minā to shade you from the sun?" He said,
"No. It is only a resting place for whoever gets to it first."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to like to enter the House and pray in it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took me by the hand and brought me into the Ḥijr, and said,
"Pray in the Ḥijr if you want to enter the House, for it is a part of the House. Your people fell short when they built the Kaʿbah, and so they left it out of the House."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what will remove from me the obligation owed for nursing?" He said,
"A ghurrah: a male or female slave."
Al-Nufaylī said: [He is] Ḥajjāj ibn Ḥajjāj al-Aslamī, and this is his wording.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any slave who marries without the permission of his masters is a fornicator."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should propose to a woman already engaged to his brother until he marries her or abandons [the proposal]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Any woman who marries without the permission of her guardian, her marriage is invalid, her marriage is invalid, her marriage is invalid. If he consummates it with her, she is entitled to the dowry for what he made lawful of her private part. If they dispute, then the ruler is the guardian of one who has no guardian."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"An orphan girl is to be consulted about herself. If she remains silent, that is her permission, and if she refuses, then there is no compulsion upon her."
And the reports are in the hadith of Yazīd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ congratulated a person on marrying, he would say:
"May Allah bless you, and shower blessings upon you, and bring the two of you together in goodness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"There is no divorce except in what you own, no emancipation except in what you own, and no sale except in what you own."
Ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ added:
"And no fulfilment of a vow except in what you own."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There are three things whose seriousness is serious and whose joking is serious: marriage, divorce, and taking back [a wife]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Ayyūb, "Do you know of anyone who said regarding [the statement] 'Your affair is in your hand' that it counts as three [divorces], other than al-Ḥasan?" He said, "No, other than al-Ḥasan."
Then he said, "O Allah, forgive me, except for what Qatādah narrated to me from Kathīr, the freed slave of Ibn Samurah, from Abū Salamah, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: 'Three.'"
Ayyūb said: I met Kathīr, the freed slave of Ibn Samurah, and asked him, but he did not recognize it. So I returned to Qatādah and told him, and he said, "He forgot."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hilāl, one of the Banū Mutʿān, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a tenth of his honey and asked him to reserve for him a valley called Salabah, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reserved that valley for him. When ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, became ruler, Sufyān ibn Wahb wrote to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb asking him about that. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote back: If he pays you what he used to pay to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the tenth of his honey, then reserve Salabah for him; otherwise it is only a rain-fed fly, which whoever wishes may eat from.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that grapes be estimated just as dates are estimated, and that their zakāh be taken as raisins just as the zakāh on dates is taken as dried dates.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made zakāh al-fiṭr obligatory as a purification for the one fasting from idle talk and obscene speech, and as food for the poor. Whoever pays it before the prayer, it is an accepted zakāh, and whoever pays it after the prayer, it is one of the ordinary acts of charity (ṣadaqah).
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, delivered a sermon at the end of Ramadan on the pulpit of Basra and said: Give out the charity (ṣadaqah) of your fasting. It seemed that the people did not know about it, so he said: Who is here from the people of Madinah? Get up and go to your brothers and teach them, for they do not know. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made this charity obligatory: one ṣāʿ of dates or barley, or half a ṣāʿ of wheat, on every free person or slave, male or female, young or old. Then when ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, came and saw the cheapness of prices, he said: Allah has given you more abundance, so if you were to make it one ṣāʿ of everything [it would be better].
Ḥumayd said: And al-Ḥasan held that the charity of Ramadan is due on the one who fasted.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Ziyād,

or one of the governors, sent ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn to collect charity (ṣadaqah). When he returned, he said to ʿImrān: Where is the money? He said: Did you send me for money? We took it from where we used to take it in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we put it where we used to put it in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from the Banū Asad said: I and my family stayed

at Baqīʿ al-Gharqad. My family said to me: Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask him for something for us to eat. They began mentioning their need. So I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found a man with him asking him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was saying:
"I do not find anything to give you."
The man turned away from him angry, saying: By my life, you give to whomever you wish.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He is angry with me because I do not find what to give him. Whoever among you asks while he owns an ūqiyyah or its equivalent has asked with importunity."
The Asadī said: I said to myself, 'A milch camel we have is better than an ūqiyyah,' and an ūqiyyah is forty dirhams.
He said: So I returned and did not ask him. Afterwards, barley or raisins came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he distributed some of it to us, or as he said, until Allah made us self-sufficient.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My mother sent me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I came and sat down, and he turned to me and said:

"Whoever seeks to be self-sufficient, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will make him self-sufficient; whoever seeks to be chaste, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will keep him chaste; whoever seeks to be spared need, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will spare him; and whoever asks while he owns the value of an ūqiyyah has asked with importunity."
I said: My she-camel, al-Yāqūtah, is better than an ūqiyyah. So I went back and did not ask him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the two of them came to the Prophet ﷺ during the Farewell Hajj while he was distributing charity (ṣadaqah), and they asked him for some of it. He raised his gaze to us and lowered it, and saw that we were strong, and he said:
"If you wish, I will give you, but there is no share in it for a rich person or for a strong person able to earn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Charity (ṣadaqah) is not permissible for a rich person except for five: one who fights in the cause of Allah, or one who works to collect it, or one in debt, or a man who buys it with his own money, or a man who has a poor neighbor who was given charity and the poor person gave it as a gift to the rich man."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr prayer at al-Baydāʾ, then mounted and ascended the hill of al-Baydāʾ, and he declared the intention for Hajj and ʿUmrah when he had prayed Ẓuhr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ five nights before the end of Dhū al-Qaʿdah, thinking only of Hajj. When we drew near Makkah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded whoever did not have a sacrificial animal with him to leave the state of iḥrām after he circumambulated the House.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed beside Ibn ʿUmar and placed my hand on my waist. He struck my hand like this and said to me, "Like this?" When I had finished praying, I asked a man, "Who is this?" He said, "ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar."
I said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, what about me bothered you?" He said, "This is ṣalb (a posture of crucifixion), and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no one who performs ablution and does it well, then prays two rakʿahs, giving them his full attention with his heart and his face, except that Paradise becomes obligatory for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He narrated to us in the gathering of Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, while Ibn al-Musayyib was sitting there, that he heard Abū Dharr
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, continues to turn toward His servant in his prayer as long as he does not turn aside. When he turns his face away, Allah turns away from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to give greetings of peace during the prayer and ask for our needs. Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was praying and greeted him, but he did not return the greeting. I was seized by worry over what had passed and what had newly occurred. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he said:
"Allah brings about of His command whatever He wills, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has newly decreed that you do not speak during the prayer."
Then he returned my greeting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque and found a man who had finished his prayer and was reciting the tashahhud, saying: "O Allah, I ask You, O Allah, the One, the Eternal Refuge, who has not begotten and has not been begotten, and there is none comparable to Him, that You forgive me my sins. Indeed You are the Forgiving, the Merciful." He said: Then he ﷺ said:
"He has been forgiven! He has been forgiven!" three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is from the Sunnah to say the tashahhud quietly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ used to point with his finger when he made supplication, and he would not move it.
Ibn Jurayj said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār added: ʿĀmir informed me, from his father, that he saw the Prophet ﷺ supplicating in this way, and the Prophet ﷺ would lean with his left hand on his left thigh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to us while the people were raising their hands during the prayer. Zuhayr said: I think he said: during the prayer. Then he said:
"Why do I see you raising your hands as if they were the tails of unruly horses? Be still in the prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Shortening the salām is Sunnah.
ʿAlī ibn Ḥujr said: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak said, meaning that you should not draw it out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Is one of you unable
" (according to ʿAbd al-Wārith):
to step forward or step back, or to the right or to the left?"
In the narration of Ḥammād he added: "in the prayer,"
meaning in the voluntary prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed and gave the salām while one rakʿah of the prayer remained. A man caught up with him and said, "You forgot one rakʿah of the prayer." So he returned and entered the mosque, ordered Bilāl, who called the iqāmah, and he led the people in prayer for one rakʿah. Then I informed the people of that.
They said to me, "Do you know the man?" I said, "No, unless I see him." Then he passed by me and I said, "This is him."
They said, "This is Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydullāh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"If the imam stands up after two rakʿahs, then if he remembers before he is fully upright, he should sit down. But if he has become fully upright, he should not sit, and he should perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah led us in prayer and rose after two rakʿahs. The people said "Subḥān Allāh" to him, and he said it back to them. When he had finished the rest of his prayer, he gave the salām, then performed the two prostrations of forgetfulness while sitting. Then he told them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had done the same with them as he had done.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sālim said: Ibn ʿUmar said: I heard ʿUmar
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Indeed Allah forbids you to swear by your fathers."
ʿUmar said: By Allah, since I heard the Prophet ﷺ say that, I have not sworn by them, neither intentionally nor by repeating [the words of others].
Mujāhid said: {or a trace of knowledge} meaning: someone who transmits knowledge.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿUbayd Allāh,
and Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah,
(Transition to another chain.) And Muḥammad ibn Rāfiʿ narrated to us:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us:
Ibn Jurayj informed us:
Ismāʿīl ibn Umayyah informed me:
(Transition to another chain.) And Abū al-Ṭāhir narrated to me:
Ibn Wahb informed us,
from Ḥanẓalah ibn Abī Sufyān al-Jumaḥī,
and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar,
and Mālik ibn Anas, and Usāmah
ibn Zayd al-Laythī, all of them from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ,
like the hadith of Yaḥyā from Mālik, except that some of them said "its value" and some said "its price was three dirhams."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He said: My father wrote, and I wrote for him, to ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Bakrah, who was a judge in Sijistān, [saying] that you should not
judge between two people while you are angry, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"No one should judge between two people while he is angry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a man who was admonishing his brother about modesty, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Modesty is part of faith."
Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ said in his narration that the Prophet ﷺ heard a man admonishing his brother about modesty.
He said: This is a good and sound hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Abū Hurayrah striking his forehead with his hand and saying: O people of Iraq! Do you claim that I lie about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so that you may have the benefit and I bear the sin? I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"When a dog licks the vessel of one of you, let him wash it seven times."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Layth informed us,
from Ibn Shihāb,
from Ibn al-Musayyib and Abū
Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Hurayrah,
that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the heat becomes intense, delay the prayer until it cools, for the intensity of the heat is from the breath of Hell."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray the ʿAṣr prayer while the sun was still shining in my room, and the shadow had not yet appeared.
Mālik, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, Shuʿayb and Ibn Abī Ḥafṣah said: "while the sun was [still in it], before [the shadow] appeared."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Bilāl was commanded to say the words of the adhān
twice and the iqāmah once.
Yaḥyā added in his narration from Ibn ʿUlayyah: I narrated it to Ayyūb, and he said: "Except for the iqāmah [phrase]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is Abū al-Ḥārith al-Baṣrī, trustworthy, from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: Muḥammad ﷺ said:
"Does he not fear, the one who raises his head before the imam, that Allah may turn his head into the head of a donkey?"
Qutaybah said: Ḥammād said: Muḥammad ibn Ziyād said to me, and he only said: "Does he not fear".
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿĀʾishah: When did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray the Witr? She said: He did all of that; he prayed Witr at the beginning of the night, in the middle of it, and at the end of it, but his Witr ended, when he died, at the pre-dawn hour.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read before him while I listened,
and the wording is his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
he said: Mālik narrated to me, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,

that the Prophet ﷺ forbade the sale of ḥabal al-ḥabalah. It was a sale the people of the Jāhiliyyah used to practice: a man would buy a camel to be paid for until a she-camel gave birth, and then the one in her womb gave birth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That

when there was between ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr and ʿAnbasah ibn Abī Sufyān what there was, they prepared for fighting. Khālid ibn al-ʿĀṣ rode to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr and admonished him. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr said: Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿUmar about the containers that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had forbidden: Tell us in your language and explain it to us in our language.

He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the ḥantamah, which is the jar; he forbade the dubbāʾ, which is the gourd; he forbade the naqīr, which is the base of a palm trunk that is hollowed out or scooped out; and he forbade the muzaffat, which is the tar-coated [vessel]; and he commanded that nabīdh be made in waterskins.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ delivered a sermon during his Hajj and said:

"Time has come full circle to its form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred: three in succession—Dhū al-Qaʿdah, Dhū al-Ḥijjah, and Muḥarram—and Rajab of Muḍar, which falls between Jumādā and Shaʿbān."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"At every door of the mosque there is an angel who records the first arrivals, then the next—like one who offers a camel, then [lesser offerings] in descending order down to one who offers an egg. When the imam sits, the scrolls are folded up and they attend the remembrance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Ḥassān ibn Thābit on the day of Qurayẓah: "Satirize the polytheists,
for Jibrīl is with you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Jibrīl:
"What prevents you from visiting us more often than you do?"
He said: Then this verse was revealed:
"We do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us..." to the end of the verse.
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was said] to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, has any day come upon you harder than the day of Uḥud?" He said:

"I have faced much from your people, and the hardest of what I faced from them was the day of al-ʿAqabah, when I presented myself to Ibn ʿAbd Yālīl ibn ʿAbd Kulāl, and he did not respond to what I wanted. So I set off, grieved, not knowing where I was going, and I did not recover until I was at Qarn al-Thaʿālib. I raised my head and there was a cloud shading me. I looked, and in it was Jibrīl. He called out to me and said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has heard what your people said to you and how they rejected you, and He has sent the angel of the mountains to you so that you may command him as you wish concerning them. Then the angel of the mountains called to me and greeted me with peace.

Then he said: O Muḥammad, Allah has heard what your people said to you. I am the angel of the mountains, and your Lord has sent me to you so that you may command me as you wish. If you wish, I will crush them between the two mountains."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Rather, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their descendants those who worship Allah alone, associating nothing with Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw Jibrīl in a green garment of brocade, filling what is between the heaven and the earth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿĀʾishah: "Then where is His saying: {Then he drew near and descended, and was at a distance of two bows' length or nearer, and He revealed to His servant what He revealed}?" She said: "That was only Jibrīl; he used to come to him in the form of men, but this time he came to him in his true form, and he blocked the horizon of the sky."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Khalīfah said to me: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ told us: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah,
from Abū al-ʿĀliyah,
who said: The cousin of your Prophet told us,
meaning Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"On the night I was taken on the night journey, I saw Moses, a tall, brown man with curly hair,
as if he were one of the men of Shanūʾah;
and I saw Jesus, a man of medium height and build, of reddish-white complexion, with straight hair;
and I saw Mālik, the keeper of the Fire."
And [he mentioned] the Dajjāl among the signs that Allah showed him,
"so do not be in doubt about meeting him."
Anas and Abū Bakrah said, from the Prophet ﷺ:
"The angels guard Madinah from the Dajjāl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The tent is a hollowed pearl,
its height in the sky is thirty miles;
in every corner of it the believer has a family whom the others cannot see."
Abū ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUbayd said, from Abū ʿImrān: sixty miles.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Seventy thousand or seven hundred thousand of my nation will surely enter Paradise—Abū Ḥāzim was unsure which he said—holding on to one another, the first of them not entering until the last of them enters, their faces like the form of the moon on the night of the full moon."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was in the army that was with ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, who marched against the Khawārij. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O people, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'A people from my nation will emerge who recite the Qurʾān; your recitation is nothing compared to their recitation, nor your prayer compared to their prayer, nor your fasting compared to their fasting. They recite the Qurʾān thinking that it is in their favor, but it is against them. Their prayer does not go beyond their collarbones. They pass through Islam as the arrow passes through the game.'

If the army that fights them knew what has been decreed for them upon the tongue of their Prophet ﷺ, they would rely on that and abandon action. The sign of that is that among them is a man who has an upper arm but no forearm; at the end of his upper arm is something like the nipple of a breast, with white hairs on it. Would you go off to Muʿāwiyah and the people of Syria and leave these people to take your place among your children and your wealth? By Allah, I hope that they are these very people, for they have shed forbidden blood and raided the people's grazing livestock. So march in the name of Allah."

Salamah ibn Kuhayl said: Zayd ibn Wahb brought me to a stage of the account, until he said: We passed over a bridge, and when we met them, the leader of the Khawārij that day was ʿAbdullāh ibn Wahb al-Rāsibī. He said to his men: "Throw down the spears and draw your swords from their sheaths, for I fear they will adjure you as they adjured you on the day of Ḥarūrāʾ."

So they went back, threw their spears aside, and drew their swords, and the people thrust at them with their spears. He said: They were killed one upon another, and only two men of the people were struck down that day. Then ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Look among them for the one with the deformed arm."
They searched for him but did not find him. So ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, got up himself until he came to some people who had been killed one on top of another. He said: "Pull them out."

They found him at the bottom, next to the ground. He said "Allahu akbar," then said: "Allah has spoken the truth and His Messenger has conveyed it." He said: Then ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī stood up to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, by Allah besides Whom there is no god, did you hear this hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Yes, by Allah besides Whom there is no god."
He made him swear three times, and he kept swearing to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Her husband divorced her during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and he had spent on her a meagre maintenance. When she saw that, she said, "By Allah, I will certainly inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. If I am owed maintenance, I will take what suffices me, and if I am not owed maintenance, I will take nothing from him." She said: So I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"You have no maintenance and no lodging."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A child can never repay his father, unless he finds him a slave, buys him, and frees him."
And in the narration of Ibn Abī Shaybah: "A son [cannot repay] his father."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The price of a dog is filthy, the earnings of a prostitute are filthy, and the earnings of a cupper are filthy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A slave came and pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ to emigrate, while the Prophet ﷺ did not know that he was a slave. Then his master came seeking him, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "Sell him to me."
So he bought him for two black slaves. After that he would not accept a pledge from anyone until he asked him whether he was a slave. He said: And on this topic there is a narration from Anas.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib used to narrate that Maʿmar,
said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever hoards is a sinner."
It was said to Saʿīd, "But you hoard!" Saʿīd said, "Maʿmar, who used to narrate this hadith, used to hoard as well."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has a partner in a dwelling or in date palms is not permitted to sell until he notifies his partner. If he agrees, he takes it, and if he dislikes it, he leaves it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: ongoing charity (ṣadaqah), knowledge from which people benefit, or a righteous child who supplicates for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ left behind no dirham, no dinar, no sheep, and no camel, and he made no bequest.
Jaʿfar did not mention a dinar or a dirham.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever frees his share of a slave owned jointly, it is incumbent upon him to free him entirely if he has enough to cover his price. If he has no wealth, then his share is freed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman,
— he said in the hadith of Abān: from Juhaynah — came to the Prophet ﷺ and said that she had committed adultery and was pregnant.
So the Prophet ﷺ summoned her guardian, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Treat her well, and when she gives birth, bring her to me."

When she gave birth, he brought her, and the Prophet ﷺ gave orders concerning her. Her garments were fastened around her, then he ordered that she be stoned, and she was stoned. Then he ordered them and they prayed over her. ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah, you pray over her when she has committed adultery?" He said:

"By the One in whose hand is my soul, she has repented with a repentance that, if it were divided among seventy of the people of Medina, it would suffice them. Have you found anything better than that she gave her life for the sake of Allah?"
He did not say from Abān, "her garments were fastened around her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yazīd, the freed slave of al-Munbaʿith, from Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī,
said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked, and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Rabīʿah.
He said: And he was asked about a lost item that is found, and he said:
"Announce it for a year. If its owner comes, hand it over to him. Otherwise, know its string and its container, then spend it from your wealth. If its owner comes, then hand it over to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no military expedition that fights in the cause of Allah and gains spoils except that they have hastened two-thirds of their reward in this world, and one-third remains for them. And if they do not gain spoils, their reward is complete for them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not sacrifice anything except a musinnah, unless it is difficult for you, in which case sacrifice a jadhaʿah from the sheep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every intoxicant is wine, and every intoxicant is forbidden. Whoever drinks wine in this world and dies while addicted to it, not having repented, will not drink it in the Hereafter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Raisin infusion used to be prepared for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at night, and he would put it in a waterskin and drink it that day, the next day, and the day after. When the end of the third day came, he would give it to be drunk or drink it himself, and if anything remained of it by morning, he would pour it out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Rabīʿah,
with the chain of Qutaybah and its meaning, and he added in it:
"If its owner comes and identifies its container and its number, then give it to him."
Ḥammād also said, from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿUmar, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ with this [narration].
He said regarding a stray sheep:
"Keep it together until its owner comes to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
found a dinar and brought it to Fāṭimah. She asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he said:
"It is provision from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ate from it, and ʿAlī and Fāṭimah ate. Then after that a woman came looking for the dinar, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O ʿAlī, pay back the dinar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: may Allah be pleased with him, that he picked up a dinar and bought flour with it. The owner of the flour recognized it and returned the dinar to him. ʿAlī took it, cut two qīrāṭs off it, and bought meat with it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib entered upon Fāṭimah while Ḥasan and Ḥusayn were crying. He said, "What is making them cry?" She said, "Hunger." So ʿAlī went out and found a dinar in the market. He came to Fāṭimah and told her, and she said, "Go to so-and-so the Jew and get some flour." He went to the Jew and bought flour with it. The Jew said, "Are you the son-in-law of this man who claims to be the messenger of Allah?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "Then take your dinar, and the flour is yours."

ʿAlī went out until he came to Fāṭimah and told her. She said, "Go to so-and-so the butcher and get us a dirham's worth of meat." He went and pawned the dinar for a dirham's worth of meat and brought it. She kneaded, set up the oven, and baked, and she sent word to her father, who came to them. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, let me tell you about this: if you see it as lawful for us, we will eat it, and you eat with us. Its matter is such and such." He said:
"Eat in the name of Allah."
So they ate. While they were in their place, a boy appeared, appealing in the name of Allah and Islam for the dinar. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that he be called, and he asked him.
He said, "It fell from me in the market." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"O ʿAlī, go to the butcher and tell him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says to you: Send me the dinar, and your dirham is owed by me."
So he sent it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave it to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted us to pick up a staff, a whip, a rope, and the like, which a man finds and benefits from.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"A stray camel that is concealed—its compensation is its like along with it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Jarīr at al-Bawāzīj when the herdsman came with the cattle, and among them was a cow that was not of them. Jarīr said to him, "What is this?" He said, "It joined the cattle; we do not know whose it is."
Jarīr said, "Drive it out, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"None shelters a stray animal except one who is astray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: to his wives during the Farewell Hajj:
"This [Hajj], then [stay at home on] the backs of the mats."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that Ibn ʿUmar
used to let a freed woman of his, called Ṣafiyyah, ride behind him when she travelled with him to Makkah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no ṣarūrah in Islam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He recited this verse: {There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord}. He said, "They used not to trade at Minā, so they were commanded to trade when they departed from ʿArafāt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was a man who rented out [animals] on this route, and some people used to say to me, "You have no Hajj." So I met Ibn ʿUmar and said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, I am a man who rents out [animals] on this route, and some people say to me that I have no Hajj." Ibn ʿUmar said, "Do you not enter ihrām, recite the talbiyah, circle the House, depart from ʿArafāt, and throw the pebbles?" I said, "Yes."

He said, "Then you do have Hajj. A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about the same thing you asked me about, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent and did not answer him until this verse was revealed: {There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord}. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for him, recited this verse to him, and said: 'You have Hajj.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the people,

at the beginning of Hajj, used to trade at Minā, ʿArafah, the market of Dhū al-Majāz, and the Hajj seasons. They feared trading while in a sacred state, so Allah, Glorified, revealed {There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord} regarding the Hajj seasons.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out a detachment and appointed over them a man from the Anṣār, and he commanded them to listen to him and obey him. They angered him over something, so he said, "Gather firewood for me."
So they gathered it for him. Then he said, "Kindle a fire."
So they kindled it. Then he said, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not command you to listen to me and obey?" They said, "Yes." He said, "Then enter it."
He said: They looked at one another and said, "We only fled to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the Fire."
They remained like that until his anger subsided and the fire died down. When they returned, they mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Had they entered it, they would never have come out of it. Obedience is only in what is right."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to relieve himself. When he returned, I met him with a water container and poured water over him. He washed his hands, then washed his face, then went to wash his forearms, but the sleeve of his cloak was tight, so he brought them out from under the cloak and washed them. He wiped his head and wiped over his leather socks, then he led us in prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: During the illness in which he was taken, the Prophet ﷺ used to blow over himself with the Muʿawwidhāt.
When his illness became severe, I would blow over him with them,
and wipe him with his own hand, for its blessing.
I asked Ibn Shihāb, "How did he used to blow?" He said, "He would blow over his hands,
then wipe his face with them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Banū Sulaym passed by a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with his sheep. He greeted them with salām. They said, "He only greeted you to seek protection from you." So they got up, killed him, took his sheep, and brought them to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed: "O you who believe, when you go out in the cause of Allah, investigate, and do not say to one who offers you the greeting of peace, 'You are not a believer.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him escape."
Then he recited: "And such is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are doing wrong. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor silently," he said: It was revealed while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in hiding in Makkah. When he led his Companions in prayer, he would raise his voice with the Qurʾān, and when the polytheists heard that, they would revile the Qurʾān, the One who sent it down, and the one who brought it. So Allah, the Exalted, said to His Prophet ﷺ: "And do not recite your prayer aloud", so that the polytheists hear your recitation, "nor silently", so that your Companions do not hear. Let them hear the Qurʾān, but do not raise your voice that much, "and seek between that a way", meaning between speaking aloud and speaking silently.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās, "Is there repentance for one who deliberately kills a believer?" He said, "No."

He said: So I recited to him this verse in Sūrat al-Furqān: "And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right," to the end of the verse.
He said, "This is a Makkan verse; a Madinan verse abrogated it: 'And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein.'"
In the narration of Ibn Hāshim: So I recited this verse in al-Furqān: "Except for those who repent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to feel jealous of the women who gave themselves to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I would say, "Does a woman give herself?" Then when Allah, the Exalted, revealed: "You may defer whom you will of them and take to yourself whom you will; and there is no blame upon you if you seek one whom you had set aside," I said, "I do not see your Lord except hastening to fulfil your desire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAṭāʾ claimed that he heard ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr
say: I heard ʿĀʾishah
claim that the Prophet ﷺ used to stay with Zaynab bint Jaḥsh
and drink honey at her place.
So Ḥafṣah and I agreed that whichever of us the Prophet ﷺ entered upon should say, "I smell maghāfīr on you;
have you eaten maghāfīr?" He entered upon one of them and she said that to him. He said:
"No, rather I drank honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh,
and I will not do it again."
Then it was revealed: "O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you?"
"If you two repent to Allah", addressed to ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah,
"And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement", referring to his saying:
"Rather, I drank honey."
Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā told me from Hishām: "
I will not do it again, and I have sworn,
so do not tell anyone of that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I visited Anas ibn Mālik when he came to Madīnah and greeted him with salām. He asked, "Who are you from?" I said, "I am Wāqid ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿd ibn Muʿādh."
He said, "Saʿd was the greatest of people and the tallest."

Then he wept, and wept a great deal. Then he said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent an expedition to Ukaydir, the ruler of Dūmah, and he sent him a woven brocade robe with gold in it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wore it, then stood on the minbar and sat down without speaking, and then came down. The people began to touch it with their hands, and he said:
'Are you amazed at this? The handkerchiefs of Saʿd in Paradise are better than what you see.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about ghee, cheese, and furs. He said:
"The lawful is what Allah has made lawful in His Book, and the unlawful is what Allah has made unlawful in His Book, and what He has been silent about is among what He has pardoned."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He visited Abū Ṭalḥah al-Anṣārī to see him in his illness.
He said: I found Sahl ibn Ḥunayf with him.

He said: Abū Ṭalḥah called a man to remove a cloth spread from beneath him. Sahl said to him, "Why are you removing it?" He said, "Because it has images, and the Prophet ﷺ said about that what you know."
Sahl said, "Did he not also say:
'except for a pattern on a garment'?"
He said, "Yes, but this is more reassuring to me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Change gray hair, and do not imitate the Jews."
Both of them are not preserved [as authentic].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me from wearing qassī garments and red saddle-cloths, and from wearing my ring on this finger or this one.
And he pointed to the index finger and the middle finger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about eating hyena, and he said:
"Does anyone eat hyena?"
And I asked him about eating wolf, and he said:
"Does anyone eat wolf who has any good in him?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: She was a concubine who had borne a child
of Sinān ibn Salamah. She said: Nubayshah al-Khayr came in to us while we were eating from a large bowl, and he told us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever eats from a bowl and then licks it clean, the bowl will ask forgiveness for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stayed with them, and they went to trouble to prepare food for him which contained some of these vegetables. He disliked eating it, and said to his Companions:
"Eat it, for I am not like any of you; I fear that I would harm my companion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ supplicated against locusts, he would say:

"O Allah, destroy their large ones, kill their small ones, spoil their eggs, cut off their rear, and keep their mouths away from our livelihood and provisions. You are indeed the Hearer of supplication."
A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, how can you supplicate against one of the armies of Allah by cutting off their rear?" He said:
"Locusts are the sneeze of a fish in the sea."
Hāshim said: Ziyād said: Someone who saw the fish sneezing it out told me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people
from ʿUraynah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found Madīnah's climate unsuitable. He ﷺ said:
"If you went out to our herd of camels and drank from their milk and urine..." So they did so.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Is any of you unable each year to make a water-skin from the hide of her sacrificial animal?" Then she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade steeping drinks in clay jars and in such and such, except for vinegar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ we used to eat while walking and drink while standing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ drank, he would breathe twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A woman] called Kabshah al-Anṣāriyyah [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited her while a water-skin was hanging by her. He drank from it while standing, so she cut off the mouth of the water-skin, seeking blessing from the place where the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had touched.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, whom should I treat with the greatest kindness?" He said, "Your mother."
I said, "Then whom?" He said, "Your mother."
I said, "Then whom?" He said, "Your mother."
