I said, "Then whom?" He said:
"Then your father, then the next closest, and the next closest."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever has three daughters and is patient with them, feeds them, gives them drink, and clothes them from his means, they will be a barrier for him from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Vulgarity is never in anything except that it disgraces it, and modesty is never in anything except that it adorns it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar
used to press hard through the crowd at the two corners, such that I never saw any of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ do it.
So I said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, you press hard through the crowd at the two corners, such that I have not seen any of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ press through to them like this."
He said, "If I do so, it is because I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Wiping them is an expiation for sins.' And I heard him say:
'Whoever circles this House seven times and counts them, it is like freeing a slave.' And I heard him say:
'He does not place down a foot nor raise another except that Allah removes a sin from him by it and records a good deed for him by it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Saʿīd,
the two sons of ʿUbayd, from Abū Ḥātim al-Muzanī,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If someone whose religion and character you are pleased with comes to you, then marry [your daughter] to him. If you do not do so, there will be trial in the land and widespread corruption."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, even if there is something in him?" He said:
"If someone whose religion and character you are pleased with comes to you, then marry [her] to him," three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not enter the bathhouse without a waist-wrap. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not let his wife enter the bathhouse. And whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not sit at a table around which wine is passed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and I went in to Fāṭimah bint Qays, and she told us that her husband had divorced her with three divorces, and had not granted her lodging or maintenance.
She said: He set aside for me ten qafīz [of grain] with a cousin of his, five of barley and five of wheat.
She said: So I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him. She said: He said, "He spoke the truth."
She said: Then he commanded me to spend my waiting period in the house of Umm Sharīk. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:

"The house of Umm Sharīk is one that the Emigrants frequently visit. Rather, spend your waiting period in the house of Ibn Umm Maktūm, for you may take off your garments and he will not see you. Then when your waiting period ends, if anyone comes to propose to you, inform me."
When my waiting period ended, Abū Jahm and Muʿāwiyah proposed to me.
She said: So I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said:
"As for Muʿāwiyah, he is a man who has no wealth, and as for Abū Jahm, he is a man who is harsh toward women."
She said: Then Usāmah ibn Zayd proposed to me and I married him, and Allah blessed me through Usāmah.
This is a ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth.
Sufyān al-Thawrī also narrated it from Abū Bakr ibn Abī al-Jahm,
with a similar ḥadīth, and added in it: The Prophet ﷺ said to me, "Marry Usāmah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Nothing becomes prohibited through breastfeeding except that which opens the intestines from the breast, and that was before weaning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"If I were to command anyone to prostrate to another, I would command the wife to prostrate to her husband. And if a man were to order his wife to move from a red mountain to a black mountain, and from a black mountain to a red mountain, it would be her duty to do so."
label: machine translation

segments_en: No, by Allah, the Prophet ﷺ did not say that Jesus was ruddy; rather he said:
"While I was sleeping, circling the Kaaba,
I saw a man of brown complexion with straight hair,
supported between two men,
water dripping from his head, or water being poured from his head. I asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'The son of Mary.' Then I turned and looked,
and there was a ruddy man, heavily built, with curly hair,
blind in the right eye,
his eye like a floating grape.
I asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'This is the Dajjāl.'
The person who most resembles him is Ibn Qaṭan."
Az-Zuhrī said: He was a man from Khuzāʿah who died in the Time of Ignorance.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went with him to Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān, and ʿUqbah said to him, "Tell me what you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the Dajjāl." He said:

"The Dajjāl will emerge with water and fire with him. What people see as water will be a burning fire, and what people see as fire will be cool, sweet water. So whoever among you lives to see that, let him plunge into what he sees as fire, for it is sweet, good water."
Then ʿUqbah said, "And I too heard it," confirming what Ḥudhayfah had said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I sat with Abū Hurayrah for five years, and I heard him narrate
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"The Children of Israel were governed by prophets;
whenever one prophet died, another succeeded him.
But there will be no prophet after me,
and there will be caliphs, and they will be many."
They said, "What do you command us?" He said, "Fulfil the pledge of allegiance to the first, then the next. Give them their due,
for Allah will question them about those whom He entrusted to their care."
label: machine translation

segments_en: in this mosque,
and we have not forgotten it since he narrated it to us,
and we do not fear that Jundab would have lied about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Among those who came before you was a man who had a wound.
He became impatient, so he took a knife and cut his hand with it,
and the blood did not stop until he died.
Allah, the Exalted, said: 'My servant hastened his own end;
I have forbidden Paradise to him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would raise his hands with every takbīr in the obligatory prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Humayd, Abū Usayd, Sahl ibn Saʿd and Muḥammad ibn Maslamah gathered and mentioned the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Abū Humayd said, "I know the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ best of you." Then he mentioned some of it, saying: Then he bowed and placed his hands on his knees as if gripping them, and he made his hands taut like a bowstring, keeping them away from his sides. He said: Then he prostrated, pressing his nose and forehead [to the ground], keeping his hands away from his sides, and placing his palms level with his shoulders. Then he raised his head until every bone returned to its place, until he finished. Then he sat, spreading out his left foot and turning the toes of his right foot toward the qiblah, placing his right palm on his right knee and his left palm on his left knee, and he pointed with his finger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw the Prophet ﷺ, when he began the prayer, raise his hands until his thumbs were almost level with the lobes of his ears.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṭāwūs prayed beside me at Minā in the Mosque of al-Khayf. When he performed the first prostration and raised his head from it, he raised his hands in front of his face. I disapproved of that, so I said to Wuhayb ibn Khālid, "This man is doing something I have never seen anyone do."
Wuhayb said to him, "You are doing something we have never seen anyone do."
ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṭāwūs said, "I saw my father do it, and my father said, 'I saw Ibn ʿAbbās do it,' and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās said, 'I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ stood up after the two prostrations, he would say the takbīr and raise his hands until they were level with his shoulders, just as he did when he began the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught us the prayer. He said the takbīr and raised his hands, and when he bowed he joined his hands together between his knees." He said: That reached Saʿd, who said, "My brother spoke the truth. We used to do this, then we were commanded to do this," meaning to place the hands on the knees.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying a prayer—ʿAmr said, "I do not know which prayer it was"—and he said:

"Allah is the Greatest, greatly so; Allah is the Greatest, greatly so; Allah is the Greatest, greatly so; and abundant praise is for Allah; and abundant praise is for Allah; and abundant praise is for Allah; and glory be to Allah morning and evening," three times.
"I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, from his blowing, his spitting, and his whispering."
He said: His spitting is poetry, his blowing is arrogance, and his whispering is madness.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, "What made you decide

to take al-Anfāl, which is among the mathānī, and Barāʾah, which is among the miʾīn, and join them together, without writing between them a line of 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,' and place them among the seven long surahs? What made you do that?" ʿUthmān said, "Long periods of time would pass for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while surahs with many verses were being revealed to him. When something was revealed to him, he would call one of those who used to write and say, 'Put these verses in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned.' And when a verse was revealed to him, he would say, 'Put this verse in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned.' Al-Anfāl was among the first that were revealed in Madinah, and Barāʾah was among the last of the Qurʾān revealed, and its account resembled its account, so I thought that it was part of it. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away without having made clear to us that it was part of it. For that reason I joined them together and did not write between them a line of 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,' and I placed it among the seven long surahs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He mentioned the story of Muʿādh, and said that the Prophet ﷺ said to the young man:
"What do you do, O son of my brother, when you pray?"
He said, "I recite the Opening of the Book, and I ask Allah for Paradise and seek refuge in Him from the Fire. I do not know your murmuring nor the murmuring of Muʿādh."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I and Muʿādh [are] around these two [matters]."
Or words to that effect.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Ibn ʿAbbās along with some youths of Banū Hāshim, and we said to a young man among us, "Ask Ibn ʿAbbās whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr prayers." He said, "No, no."
It was said to him, "Perhaps he used to recite to himself."

He said, "Shame on you! This is worse than the first. He was a servant under command; he conveyed what he was sent with. He did not single us out from the people with anything except three matters: he commanded us to perfect the ablution, not to eat charity, and not to breed donkeys with horses."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When the believing servant performs ablution and rinses his mouth, the sins leave his mouth; when he sniffs water into his nose and blows it out, the sins leave his nose; when he washes his face, the sins leave his face, even from beneath his eyelashes; when he washes his hands, the sins leave his hands, even from beneath the nails of his hands; when he wipes his head, the sins leave his head, even from his ears; and when he washes his feet, the sins leave his feet, even from beneath the nails of his feet. Then his walking to the mosque and his prayer are an additional reward for him."
Qutaybah said, from aṣ-Ṣunābiḥī, that the Prophet ﷺ said:
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ asking him about ablution, so he showed him the ablution three times each, then said:
"This is the ablution. Whoever adds to this has done wrong, transgressed, and been unjust."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They took part in the expedition of as-Salāsil, but they missed the fighting, so they stayed on guard duty. Then they returned to Muʿāwiyah, and with him were Abū Ayyūb and ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir. ʿĀṣim said: "O Abū Ayyūb, we missed the fighting this year, and we have been told that whoever prays in the four mosques will have his sins forgiven."
He said: "O son of my brother, shall I guide you to something easier than that? I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever performs ablution as he was commanded and prays as he was commanded will have forgiven what he did before.'"
[Then he said:] "Is that so, ʿUqbah?" He said: "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would perform ablution, then kiss [his wife] and pray without performing ablution again, and perhaps he did that with me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to serve the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When he wanted to bathe, he would say: "Turn your back to me."
So I would turn my back to him and screen him with it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Maymūnah bathed from one vessel, a large bowl in which there was a trace of dough.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I remember that I would find it on the garment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and scrape it off from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We performed tayammum with earth together with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we wiped our faces and our hands up to the shoulders.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That one of
the wives of the Prophet ﷺ bathed after sexual impurity, and the Prophet ﷺ performed ablution with the water she had left. She mentioned that to him, and he said:
"Indeed, nothing makes water impure."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Following it. Abū ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān said: "I did not master it from ʿUrwah, from Busrah."
She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever touches his private part, let him perform ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas ibn Mālik and Ibn Ḥazm [reported]: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made fifty prayers obligatory upon my community. I returned with that until I passed by Mūsā, peace be upon him, and he said: 'What has your Lord made obligatory upon your community?' I said: 'He has made fifty prayers obligatory upon them.'
Mūsā said to me: 'Go back to your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, for your community cannot bear that.'
So I went back to my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and He reduced it by half. I returned to Mūsā and told him, and he said: 'Go back to your Lord, for your community cannot bear that.'
So I went back to my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and He said: 'They are five, and they are fifty; the word is not changed with Me.'
I returned to Mūsā, and he said: 'Go back to your Lord.' I said: 'I am truly ashamed before my Lord, Mighty and Majestic.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The sun rises between the two horns of Satan," or he said:
"the two horns of Satan rise with it. When it is high, he leaves it.
When it is in the middle of the sky, he joins it again.
When it has passed its zenith," or he said, "declined, he leaves it.
When it draws near to setting, he joins it again.
When it has set, he leaves it.
So do not pray at these three times."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about a man who sleeps through the prayer or is heedless of it. He said:
"Its expiation is to pray it when he remembers it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Isḥāq said: Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among the best of people in character. One day he sent me on an errand, and I said, "By Allah, I will not go."

Yet in my heart I intended to go, because of what the Prophet of Allah ﷺ had commanded me. So I went out until I passed by some boys who were playing in the marketplace. Then suddenly the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seized me by the back of my neck from behind. He said: I looked at him, and he was laughing, and he said:
"Unays, did you go where I commanded you?"
He said: I said, "Yes, I am going, O Messenger of Allah."

Anas said: By Allah, I served him for nine years, and I never knew him to say about anything I had done, "Why did you do such-and-such?" or about anything I had left undone, "Why did you not do such-and-such?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have a need to ask of you." He said to her:
"Mother of so-and-so, sit in whichever side street you like, and I will sit with you."
He said: So she sat, and the Prophet ﷺ sat with her until she had finished [stating] her need.
Ibn ʿĪsā did not mention "until she had finished her need."
And Kathīr said, from Ḥumayd, from Anas:
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to visit us and took a midday rest at our house, and he sweated. My mother came with a small bottle and began to collect the sweat in it. The Prophet ﷺ woke up and said:
"Umm Sulaym, what is this that you are doing?"
She said, "This is your sweat. We put it in our perfume, and it is among the finest of perfumes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was wide-mouthed, with reddish streaks in the whites of his eyes, and lean in the heels.
He said: I asked Simāk, "What is 'ḍalīʿ al-fam'?" He said, "Wide-mouthed."
He said: I asked, "What is 'ashkal al-ʿayn'?" He said, "Long in the slit of the eye."
He said: I asked, "What is 'manhūs al-ʿaqib'?" He said, "Having little flesh on the heel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ﷺ, and he said: When he oiled his head, none of it [the grey hair] could be seen, and when he did not oil it, it could be seen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Bunānī and Sulaymān al-Taymī, from Anas ibn Mālik:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I came upon—and in the narration of Hudbah, 'I passed by'—Mūsā on the night I was taken on the Night Journey, at the red sand dune, while he was standing in his grave, praying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān gave an order to Saʿd and said, "What prevents you from cursing Abū Turāb?" He said, "As for what I remember, there were three things the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, so I will never curse him; to have just one of them would be dearer to me than red camels. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say to him, when he left him behind on one of his expeditions, and ʿAlī said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, you are leaving me behind with the women and children?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Are you not pleased to be to me what Hārūn was to Mūsā, except that there is no prophet after me?"
And I heard him say on the day of Khaybar:
"I will surely give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love."
He said: We stretched ourselves up eagerly for it, but he said:
"Call ʿAlī for me."

So he was brought, with sore eyes. He spat in his eye and handed him the banner, and Allah gave victory through him. And when this verse was revealed: {Say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons}, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, Ḥasan and Ḥusayn, and said:
"O Allah, these are my family."
label: machine translation

segments_en: This verse was revealed about six of us: myself, Ibn Masʿūd, Ṣuhayb, ʿAmmār, al-Miqdād and Bilāl.
He said: The Quraysh said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "We are not pleased to be followers of these people, so drive them away from you."

He said: Then there entered the heart of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what Allah willed should enter it, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance} the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said to me, "ʿUrwah, your two parents were among those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after they had been struck by injury"—Abū Bakr and al-Zubayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I led the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, together with al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, on his grey mule until I brought him into the chamber of the Prophet ﷺ; this one was in front of him and this one behind.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from a journey, he would be met by the children of his household. He said: He returned from a journey once, and I was sent ahead to him, so he carried me in front of him. Then one of the two sons of Fāṭimah was brought, and he seated him behind him. He said: So the three of us entered Madinah on one riding animal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said: People say that Abū Hurayrah narrates too much.
Then I met a man and said, "What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite last night in the late evening prayer?" He said, "I do not know."
I said, "Did you not attend it?" He said, "Yes, I did."
I said, "But I know:
he recited such-and-such a sūrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Muḥammad, "Is there a tashahhud in the two prostrations of forgetfulness?" He said, "It is not in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman from among them, who had pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ, informed him that ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn's lot came up for housing when the Anṣār drew lots for housing the Muhājirūn.
Umm al-ʿAlāʾ said: So ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn lodged with us, and he fell ill.
We nursed him until he died, and we had placed him in his shrouds. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon us, and I said, "May Allah have mercy on you, Abū as-Sāʾib,
I bear witness about you that Allah has honored you."
The Prophet ﷺ said to me,
"How do you know that Allah has honored him?"
I said, "I do not know, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"As for ʿUthmān, certainty [death] has come to him, by Allah, and I truly hope good for him,
but by Allah, I do not know what will be done with me, even though I am the Messenger of Allah."
She said: By Allah, I will never declare anyone pure after him,
and that grieved me. She said: Then I slept and saw in a dream a flowing spring for ʿUthmān,
so I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him, and he said, "That is his deeds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a woman who was weeping at a grave, and he said,
"Fear Allah and be patient."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibrāhīm [reported] that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was brought food while he was fasting, and he said: Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr was killed, and he was better than me.
He was shrouded in a single cloak;
if his head was covered, his feet showed,
and if his feet were covered, his head showed. I think he also said: Ḥamzah was killed, and he was better than me.
Then the world was spread out for us as it has been spread out, or he said: we were given of the world what we were given, and we fear that our good deeds have been hastened for us.
Then he began to weep until he left the food.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And it was not made binding upon us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A son of Umm ʿAṭiyyah died, and on the third day she called for yellow perfume,
and she applied it and said: We were forbidden to mourn for more than three days, except for a husband.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We attended the burial of a daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting at the grave,
and I saw his eyes shedding tears. He said,
"Is there anyone among you who did not have relations last night?"
Abū Ṭalḥah said, "I." He said,
"Then descend into her grave."
So he descended into her grave and buried her.
Ibn al-Mubārak said: Fulayḥ said: I think he meant sin.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A son of Abū Ṭalḥah fell ill, [Anas] said, and he died while Abū Ṭalḥah was away.
When his wife saw that he had died, she prepared something and set the child aside in a corner of the house.
When Abū Ṭalḥah came, he said, "How is the boy?" She said, "He has become calm,
and I hope he has found rest."
Abū Ṭalḥah thought she was telling the truth. He said: So he spent the night,
and when morning came he washed,
and when he wanted to go out,
she told him that the boy had died.
He prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, and then informed the Prophet ﷺ of what had happened between them,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Perhaps Allah will bless you both in your night."
Sufyān said: A man of the Anṣār said: I saw nine children of theirs, all of whom had recited the Qurʾān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were at a funeral, and Abū Hurayrah took Marwān by the hand, and they sat down before it was set down.
Then Abū Saʿīd came, took Marwān by the hand, and said, "Stand up! By Allah, this man knows that the Prophet ﷺ forbade us from that."
Abū Hurayrah said, "He has spoken the truth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a grave in which someone had been buried at night, and he said,
"When was this person buried?" They said, "Last night." He said, "Why did you not inform me?"
They said, "We buried him in the darkness of the night and disliked to wake you."
So he stood up, and we formed rows behind him.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: And I was among them. Then he prayed over him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from his father,
that he asked Abū Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, about the saying of Allah the Exalted: {And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans, then marry those that please you of [other] women}. She said: "O son of my sister, this refers to the orphan girl who is in the care of her guardian and shares in his wealth. He is attracted to her wealth and her beauty, so he wants to marry her without being just in her dowry, by giving her what another man would give her. So they were forbidden to marry them unless they dealt justly with them and gave them the highest of their customary dowries, and they were commanded to marry other women that pleased them."

ʿUrwah said: ʿĀʾishah said: Then after this verse the people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a ruling about them, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: {And they request from you a ruling concerning women. Say: Allah gives you a ruling about them, and [also] what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been decreed for them, while you desire to marry them}. She said: What Allah mentioned as being recited to them in the Book is the first verse, in which Allah, Glorified and Exalted, said: {And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans, then marry those that please you of [other] women}. ʿĀʾishah said: And the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic in the later verse, {and you desire to marry them}, refers to one of you turning away from the orphan girl in his care when she has little wealth and beauty. So they were forbidden to marry those orphan women whose wealth and beauty they desired except with justice, because of their disinclination toward them [when they lacked these].

Yūnus said: Rabīʿah said, regarding the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic {And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans}: He says, leave them if you fear, for I have made four [wives] lawful for you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A pledged animal may be ridden in return for its upkeep when it is pledged,
and the milk of a milch animal may be drunk in return for its upkeep when it is pledged,
and the one who rides and drinks must bear the upkeep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

from the Anṣār arranged for a slave of his to be freed after his death, and then he died, leaving no wealth other than him. So the Prophet ﷺ sold him, and Nuʿaym ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Naḥḥām bought him.
Jābir said: He was a Coptic slave who died the first year, during the governorship of Ibn al-Zubayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has a slave woman and supports her,
treats her well, then frees her and marries her,
will have two rewards."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Ḥufayd, the maternal aunt of Ibn ʿAbbās, gave the Prophet ﷺ some dried yogurt, ghee, and a lizard as a gift.
The Prophet ﷺ ate some of the dried yogurt and the ghee,
and left the lizard, finding it distasteful.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: It was eaten at the table of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
and had it been forbidden, it would not have been eaten at the table of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When food was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would ask about it: was it a gift or charity? If it was said to be charity,
he would say to his Companions, "Eat," and he would not eat.
But if it was said to be a gift,
the Prophet ﷺ would reach out his hand and eat with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: His mother, the daughter of Rawāḥah,

asked his father to give some of his wealth as a gift to her son. He put her off for a year, then it occurred to him [to do it]. She said: "I will not be satisfied until you have the Messenger of Allah ﷺ witness what you have given to my son."

So my father took me by the hand, and I was a boy at that time, and went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the mother of this boy, the daughter of Rawāḥah, wanted me to have you witness what I have given to her son."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Bashīr, do you have another son besides this one?" He said: Yes. He said:
"Have you given each of them the like of this?" He said: No. He said:
"Then do not ask me to bear witness, for I do not bear witness to injustice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A silk-striped garment was given as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he sent it to me. I put it on, and I saw anger in his face. He said:
"I did not send it to you for you to wear it. I only sent it to you so that you would cut it into head coverings for the women."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ ruled that a ʿumrā [lifetime grant] belongs to the one to whom it was given.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of
Madinah were once alarmed,
so the Prophet ﷺ rode a horse belonging to Abū Ṭalḥah that was slow-paced, or had some slowness in it. When he returned, he said:
"We found this horse of yours to be like a sea [swift]."
After that, it could not be raced against.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
that Sahl ibn Saʿd

as-Sāʿidī informed him that ʿUwaymir al-ʿAjlānī came to ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī al-Anṣārī and said to him, "What do you think, ʿĀṣim: if a man finds another man with his wife, should he kill him, so that you would then kill him [in retaliation]? Or what should he do? Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this for me, ʿĀṣim."

So ʿĀṣim asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked such questions and condemned them, until what ʿĀṣim heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weighed heavily on him. When ʿĀṣim returned to his family, ʿUwaymir came to him and said, "ʿĀṣim, what did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say to you?" ʿĀṣim said to ʿUwaymir, "You have not brought me any good. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked the question that I asked him about."
ʿUwaymir said, "By Allah, I will not stop until I ask him about it."

So ʿUwaymir went until he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the midst of the people and said, "Messenger of Allah, what if a man finds another man with his wife: should he kill him, so that you would then kill him? Or what should he do?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"A ruling has been revealed concerning you and your wife. Go and bring her."

Sahl said: So they carried out the invocation of curses (liʿān) while I was with the people in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they had finished, ʿUwaymir said, "I would have lied about her, Messenger of Allah, if I were to keep her."
So he divorced her three times before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him to.
Ibn Shihāb said: That became the established practice for those who carry out liʿān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the husband of
Barīrah was a slave called Mughīth. It is as if I can see him now, walking around behind her weeping, with his tears running down his beard. The Prophet ﷺ said to al-ʿAbbās,
"ʿAbbās, are you not amazed at Mughīth's love for Barīrah, and at Barīrah's hatred for Mughīth?"
Then the Prophet ﷺ said to her,
"If only you would take him back, for he is the father of your child."
She said, "Messenger of Allah, are you commanding me?" He said,
"I am only interceding."
She said, "Then I have no need of him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The one who takes care of an orphan, whether the orphan is his own or someone else's, he and I will be like these two in Paradise."
And Mālik pointed with the index finger and the middle finger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the couple who had carried out liʿān,
"Your reckoning is with Allah; one of you is lying. You have no claim over her."
The man said, "Messenger of Allah, what about my property?" He said,
"You have no property [to reclaim]. If you told the truth about her, it is in return for what you made lawful of her private part; and if you lied about her, then that is even further from you."
Zuhayr said in his narration: Sufyān narrated to us from ʿAmr, who heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a woman
from Quraysh came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "My daughter's husband has died, and I fear for her eye, and she wants to use kohl." He said,
"One of you used to throw a piece of dung at the head of the year, but it is only four months and ten days."

I said to Zaynab, "What is the head of the year?" She said, "In the Jahiliyyah, when a woman's husband died, she would go to the worst room she had and sit in it, until a year had passed over her; then she would come out and throw a piece of dung behind her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ finished his meal—and once he said: when he lifted his table-cloth—he would say:
"Praise be to Allah, who has sufficed us and given us drink, [a praise] not insufficient,
nor denied." And once he said: "Praise be to Allah, our Lord, [a praise] not insufficient,
nor abandoned, nor dispensed with, our Lord."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "Messenger of Allah, I send out trained dogs and they catch game for me; may I eat from it?" He said,
"When you send out the dogs—meaning trained ones—and mention the name of Allah, and they catch [game] for you, then eat."
I said, "Even if they kill it?" He said,
"Even if they kill it, as long as no dog that is not one of them joins in."
I said, "I also throw at game with a miʿrāḍ and hit it; may I eat?" He said,
"If you throw with the miʿrāḍ and mention Allah's name, and it pierces [the game], then eat; but if it strikes with its side, do not eat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was cupped three times: on the two veins of the neck and on the upper back.
Maʿmar said: I was cupped and my mind went, until I had to be reminded of the Opening of the Book (al-Fātiḥah) in my prayer.
And he was cupped on the crown of his head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is cupped on the seventeenth, nineteenth, or twenty-first [of the month], it will be a cure from every illness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Kabshah bint Abī Bakrah (and someone other than Mūsā said: Kayyisah bint Abī Bakrah) [reported] that her father
used to forbid his family from cupping
on Tuesday, and he claimed from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that Tuesday is the day of blood, and that it has an hour in which the bleeding does not stop.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was cupped on his hip because of a sprain he had.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used a nasal medicine.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about nushrah (a kind of charm to remove sorcery), and he said:
"It is from the work of Satan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I do not care what I do if I drink an antidote, or hang an amulet, or say poetry of my own accord."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A physician
asked the Prophet ﷺ about a frog, [whether] he could put it in a medicine, and the Prophet ﷺ forbade him from killing it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I fell ill with an illness, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to visit me. He placed his hand between my breasts until I felt its coolness upon my heart, and he said:

"You are a man afflicted in the heart. Go to al-Ḥārith ibn Kaladah, the brother of Thaqīf, for he is a man who practices medicine. Let him take seven ʿajwah dates of Madinah, crush them with their pits, and then administer them to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Wear white from your clothes, for it is among the best of your clothes, and shroud your dead in it. And the best of your kohl is ithmid; it clears the vision and makes the hair grow."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "The evil eye is real."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], may Allah be pleased with her, said: The one who caused the evil eye would be ordered to perform ablution, and then the one affected would wash himself with that water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he entered upon Thābit ibn Qays (Aḥmad said:) while he was ill, and said:
"Remove the affliction, Lord of the people."
From Thābit ibn Qays: Then he took some dust from Buṭḥān, put it in a cup, blew into it with water, and poured it over him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me while I was with Ḥafṣah, and he said to me:
"Will you not teach this one the incantation for ant-bite, just as you taught her writing?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We passed by a stream, and I entered and washed in it, and came out feverish. That was reported to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Tell Abū Thābit to seek refuge [in Allah]."
She said: I said, "O my master, are incantations permissible?" He said:
"There is no incantation except for the evil eye, a venomous sting, or a bite."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever among you is suffering from something, or his brother is suffering from it, let him say: 'Our Lord is Allah, who is in the heavens, hallowed be Your name. Your command is in the heaven and the earth. As Your mercy is in the heaven, place Your mercy on the earth. Forgive us our sins and our wrongs. You are the Lord of the good. Send down a mercy from Your mercy and a healing from Your healing upon this pain,' and he will be healed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and accepted Islam, then turned back from him and passed by a people who had with them a madman bound in iron. His family said: "We have been told that this companion of yours has brought something good. Do you have anything with which you can treat him?" So I recited over him with the Opening of the Book, and he recovered, and they gave me a hundred sheep. I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him, and he said:
"Was it only this?"
And Musaddad said in another place:
"Did you say anything other than this?" I said, "No." He said:
"Take it. By my life, whoever eats by a false incantation [has sinned], but you have eaten by a true incantation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We returned from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and came upon a tribe of the Arabs. They said: "We have been told that you have come from this man with something good. Do you have any medicine or incantation? For we have a mentally disturbed man in shackles." We said, "Yes."

They brought a disturbed man in shackles. He said: So I recited the Opening of the Book over him for three days, morning and evening; every time I finished it I would gather my saliva and then spit, and it was as if he were released from a tether. They gave me a payment, but I said, "Not until I ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said:
"Eat. By my life, whoever eats by a false incantation [has sinned], but you have eaten by a true incantation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a judge eats a gift, he has eaten what is unlawful; and when he accepts a bribe, it brings him to disbelief.
Masrūq said: Whoever drinks wine has disbelieved, and his disbelief is that he has no prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He] said, may Allah be pleased with him: Avoid wine, for it is the mother of evils. There was a man among those before you who devoted himself to worship, and a misguided woman became infatuated with him. She sent her slave girl to him, who said to him: We are inviting you to bear witness. So he went with her slave girl, and every time he entered a door she locked it behind him, until he reached a beautiful woman who had a boy with her and a bowl of wine. She said: By Allah, I did not invite you to bear witness, but I invited you so that you would have relations with me, or drink a cup of this wine, or kill this boy.
He said: Then pour me a cup of this wine. So she poured him a cup.

He said: Give me more. He did not leave until he had relations with her and killed the boy. So avoid wine, for by Allah, faith and addiction to wine never come together without one of them soon driving out the other.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever drinks wine without becoming intoxicated, his prayer is not accepted for as long as any of it remains in his stomach or his veins, and if he dies, he dies a disbeliever. And if he becomes intoxicated, his prayer is not accepted for forty nights, and if he dies during them, he dies a disbeliever.
Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād differed from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ibn Ādam [reported] from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said:
Whoever drinks wine and puts it into his belly, Allah does not accept a prayer from him for seven [days], if he dies during them.
And Ibn Ādam said:
if he dies during them, he dies a disbeliever. And if it takes away his reason from any of the obligations.
And Ibn Ādam said:
the Qur'an, his prayer is not accepted for forty days, if he dies during them.
And Ibn Ādam said:
he dies during them a disbeliever.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ while he was in an orchard of his in Ṭāʾif called al-Wahṭ, and he was walking with his arm around the waist of a young man of Quraysh who was suspected of drinking wine. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

Whoever drinks a single drink of wine, his repentance is not accepted for forty mornings. If he repents, Allah accepts his repentance. If he returns, his repentance is not accepted for forty mornings. If he repents, Allah accepts his repentance. If he returns, it is a right upon Allah to make him drink from the mud of khabāl on the Day of Resurrection. The wording is ʿAmr's.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever dies addicted to wine, boiling water will be sprinkled on his face when he departs this world.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, exiled Rabīʿah ibn Umayyah to Khaybar over wine, so he joined Heraclius and became a Christian. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I will never exile a Muslim after him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
Drink in the containers, but do not become intoxicated.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Drink, but do not become intoxicated.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people asked her, all of them asking about nabīdh,
saying: We steep dates in the morning and drink it in the evening, and we steep it in the evening and drink it in the morning.
She said: I do not permit anything intoxicating, even if it is bread, even if it is water.
She said it three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Then she turned to the women and said: Beware of the green jar. Even if your water-jar intoxicates you, do not drink from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She was asked about drinks,
and she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to forbid every intoxicant.
And they pleaded the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn Shaddād from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās:
label: machine translation

segments_en: Wine was made forbidden, a little of it and a lot of it, and intoxication from every drink.
Ibn Shubrumah did not hear it from ʿAbdullāh ibn Shaddād.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās [said]: Whoever is pleased to be in a state of prohibition,
if what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden is forbidden, let him forbid nabīdh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said to Ibn ʿAbbās: I am a man from the people of Khurasan, and our land is cold, and we make a drink from raisins, grapes and other things, and it has become confusing to me.

He mentioned to him many kinds of drinks, so much that I thought he had not understood him. Ibn ʿAbbās said to him: You have said too much to me. Avoid whatever intoxicates, whether from dates, raisins or anything else.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nabīdh of unripe dates alone is not lawful.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to translate between Ibn ʿAbbās and the people. A woman came to him asking about nabīdh in jars, and he forbade it.
I said: O Abū ʿAbbās, I steep sweet nabīdh in a green jar and drink from it, and my stomach rumbles.
He said: Do not drink from it, even if it is sweeter than honey.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Drink it for three days, unless it starts to ferment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We visited al-Ḥasan to see him in his illness until we filled the house. He drew in his legs and then said: We visited Abū Hurayrah to see him in his illness until we filled the house, and he drew in his legs and then said: We visited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we filled the house, while he was lying on his side. When he saw us, he drew in his legs and then said:
"Soon there will come to you, after me, people seeking knowledge. So welcome them, greet them, and teach them."
He said: By Allah, we met people who did not welcome us, did not greet us, and did not teach us, except after we had gone to them and they had treated us harshly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people from my nation will become learned in the religion and recite the Qurʾān, and they will say: 'We will go to the rulers and obtain some of their worldly goods, and keep apart from them with our religion.'
But that will not be so. Just as nothing is gathered from the thorny qatād tree except thorns, so too nothing is gathered from nearness to them except"
Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ said: It is as if he meant sins.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If the people of knowledge

had protected knowledge and placed it with those worthy of it, they would have been leaders through it over the people of their time. But they gave it freely to the people of this world so that they might gain some of their worldly goods through it, so they became insignificant to them. I heard your Prophet ﷺ say: "

Whoever makes all his concerns a single concern, the concern of his Hereafter, Allah will suffice him in the concern of his worldly life. And whoever is scattered by concerns over the conditions of the world, Allah will not care in which of its valleys he perishes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: By Allah, were it not for two verses in the Book of Allah, the Exalted, I would never narrate anything from him, meaning from the Prophet ﷺ. Were it not for the words of Allah: {Indeed, those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book...} up to the end of the two verses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When the last of this nation curses its first, whoever conceals a hadith has concealed what Allah has sent down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
A mudd suffices for ablution and a ṣāʿ for the full bath."
A man said: It does not suffice us.
He said: It sufficed one who was better than you and had more hair, meaning the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He traced the hadith back [to the Prophet ﷺ] and said: "
Be upright, and how excellent it is if you are upright. The best of your deeds is prayer, and none maintains ablution except a believer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

When a servant performs ablution and washes his hands, his sins fall away from his hands. When he washes his face, his sins fall away from his face. When he washes his forearms and wipes his head, his sins fall away from his forearms and his head. When he washes his feet, his sins fall away from his feet."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said: O Messenger of Allah, how do you recognize those of your nation whom you have not seen? He said: "
[They will be] blaze-faced and white-limbed, from the traces of ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān sitting at the seats. He called for water for ablution and performed ablution, then said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in this very place of mine perform ablution like this ablution of mine, and then he said: "
Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, what has preceded of his sins will be forgiven."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not be deceived."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray at night two units at a time, then he would finish and use the siwāk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed your mouths are pathways for the Qurʾān, so make them pleasant with the siwāk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Let none of you fail, when he enters his toilet, to say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the filthy, impure, wicked, and malicious one, the accursed Satan.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ came out of the toilet, he would say: "
Praise be to Allah, who removed harm from me and granted me well-being."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me urinating while standing, and he said: "
O ʿUmar, do not urinate standing."
So I have not urinated standing since.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade urinating while standing.

I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd Abū ʿAbd Allāh say: I heard Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Makhzūmī say: Sufyān al-Thawrī said, regarding the hadith of ʿĀʾishah, "I saw him urinate sitting": The man knows better about this than she does.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Urinating while standing was customary among the Arabs. Do you not see in the hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasanah that he says: He sat down to urinate as a woman urinates?
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
What the sea casts up or leaves behind as it recedes, eat it; but what dies in it and floats on the surface, do not eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Peace be upon him. He said: Eating garlic was forbidden, except when it is cooked.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some old dates were brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he began to examine them, removing the weevils from them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade eating two dates together, unless you ask permission of your companions.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Busr, of the Sulamīs, and his brother said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered, and we placed beneath him a velvet cloth of ours, which we spread out for him, and he sat on it. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down revelation to him in our house. We presented him with butter and dates, and he ﷺ loved butter.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
If a mouse falls into clarified butter, then if it is solid, throw away the mouse and what is around it; but if it is liquid, do not go near it."
Al-Ḥasan said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Perhaps Maʿmar narrated it from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Maymūnah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah, who brought bread and olive oil, and he ate. Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "
The fasting have broken their fast with you, the righteous have eaten your food, and the angels have invoked blessings upon you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to be cupped on the crown of his head and between his shoulders, and he would say: "
Whoever lets out some of this blood, it will not harm him if he does not treat anything with anything else."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is mentioned that Ṭāriq ibn Suwayd, or Suwayd ibn Ṭāriq, asked the Prophet ﷺ about wine, and he forbade it. Then he asked him again, and he forbade it. He said to him: O Prophet of Allah, it is a medicine. The Prophet ﷺ said: "
No, rather it is a disease."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Do not kill your children secretly. For by the One in whose hand is my soul, the ghayl [suckling a child while pregnant] overtakes the horseman on the back of his horse until it throws him down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zaynab, the wife of ʿAbdullāh, from Zaynab,

said: An old woman used to visit us and perform ruqyah for erysipelas. We had a bed with long legs, and whenever ʿAbdullāh came in, he would clear his throat and make a noise. One day he entered, and when I heard his voice I veiled myself from him. He came and sat beside me and touched me, and he felt a thread. He said: What is this? I said: A ruqyah was performed for me with it for erysipelas. He pulled it and cut it, and threw it away, and said: The family of ʿAbdullāh have no need of polytheism. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
Spells, amulets, and love charms are polytheism."
I said: One day I went out and so-and-so saw me, and my eye on his side began to water. When I perform ruqyah on it, its tears subside, and when I leave it, it waters.

He said: That is Satan. If you obey him, he leaves you, and if you disobey him, he pokes your eye with his finger. But if you did as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did, it would be better for you and more fitting for your cure: sprinkle water in your eye and say: "
Remove the affliction, O Lord of the people, heal, for You are the Healer. There is no healing except Your healing, a healing that leaves no illness behind."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to the Prophet ﷺ. ʿUthmān said: I had a pain that had almost destroyed me. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Wipe it with your right hand seven times and say: I seek refuge in the might of Allah and His power from the evil of what I feel."
He said: I did that, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, removed what I had. I have continued to instruct my family and others to do it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

If one of you is frightened in his sleep, let him say: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from His anger and His punishment, and from the evil of His servants, and from the whisperings of the devils, and lest they be present with me.
Then it will not harm him."
He said: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr used to teach it to those of his children who had reached maturity, and for those who had not, he would write it on a sheet and hang it around their necks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Aslam: He said: I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a man from his Companions came and said: O Messenger of Allah, I was stung last night and did not sleep until morning. He said: "What was it?" He said: A scorpion. He said: "
Had you said when evening came: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created, it would not have harmed you, if Allah wills."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The dwellings will reach Ihāb or Yuhāb."
Zuhayr said: I asked Suhayl, "How far is that from Madinah?" He said, "So many miles."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The drought year is not the one in which you receive no rain, but the drought year is that you receive rain and keep receiving rain, yet the earth produces nothing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out from the house of ʿĀʾishah and said: "
The head of disbelief is from here, from where the horn of Satan rises," meaning the east.
label: machine translation

segments_en: O people of Iraq, how is it that you ask me about minor matters while you commit major ones? I heard my father ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
Indeed, tribulation comes from here."
And he gestured with his hand toward the east: "
From where the two horns of Satan rise."

And you strike one another's necks! Moses only killed the man he killed from the family of Pharaoh by mistake, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to him: {And you killed a person, then We saved you from distress and tried you with a [severe] trial.} Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar said in his narration from Sālim that he did not say, "I heard."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Night and day will not pass away until Al-Lāt and Al-ʿUzzā are worshipped."

I said: O Messenger of Allah, when Allah revealed {It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists dislike it}, I thought that this was complete. He said: "

There will be of that what Allah wills. Then Allah will send a pleasant wind that will take the life of everyone who has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of faith, and those in whom there is no good will remain, and they will return to the religion of their forefathers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
By the One in whose hand is my soul, this world will not pass away until a day comes upon the people when the killer will not know why he killed, nor the victim why he was killed."
It was asked, "How will that be?" He said: "Chaos (harj).
The killer and the killed will both be in the Fire."
In the narration of Ibn Abān, he said: He is Yazīd ibn Kaysān, from Abū Ismāʿīl.
He did not mention al-Aslamī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh, and he said: The people of Iraq are about to be left with no qafīz or dirham collected for them.
We said: From where will that come? He said: From the non-Arabs, who will prevent that.
Then he said: The people of Syria are about to be left with no dīnār or mudy collected for them.
We said: From where will that come? He said: From the Romans.
Then he was silent for a while, then said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
At the end of my nation there will be a caliph who will scoop up wealth and distribute it without counting it."
He said: I asked Abū Naḍrah and Abū al-ʿAlāʾ, "Do you think he is ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz?" They said, "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is better than me. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAmmār when he began digging the trench and wiping his head, saying: "
Alas for the son of Sumayyah! A rebellious group will kill you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and passed by some boys, among them Ibn Ṣayyād. The boys fled and Ibn Ṣayyād sat down, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seemed to dislike that. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "
May your hands be covered in dust! Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?" He said: No.
Rather, you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah.
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: Let me kill him, O Messenger of Allah.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
If he is the one you think he is, you will not be able to kill him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ met Ibn Ṣāʾid, and with him were Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, while Ibn Ṣāʾid was with the boys.
Then he mentioned a hadith similar to the hadith of al-Jurayrī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Ibn Ṣāʾid: "
What is the soil of Paradise?"
He said: It is white flour, musk, O Abū al-Qāsim. He said: "You have spoken truly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ set out] with a group of his Companions, among them ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, until he found Ibn Ṣayyād, a boy approaching puberty, playing with the boys by the fortress of Banū Maʿāwiyah.

And he related the hadith like the hadith of Yūnus up to the end of the hadith of ʿUmar ibn Thābit. In the hadith from Yaʿqūb, he said: My father said, meaning regarding his statement "if you left him, it would become clear": He said, "If his mother had left him, his affair would have become clear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He narrated] from his grandfather, who was called Masʿūd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abū Bakr passed by me, and Abū Bakr said to me, "O Masʿūd, go to Abū Tamīm"—meaning his master—"and tell him to give us a camel to ride and send us provisions and a guide to lead us."

So I went to my master and informed him, and he sent with me a camel and a skin of milk. I began leading them along the hidden paths. The time of prayer came, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood to pray, with Abū Bakr standing at his right. I had come to know Islam and I was with them, so I came and stood behind them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ pushed Abū Bakr in the chest, and we stood behind him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his mother and his maternal aunt were together, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed, placing Anas on his right, and his mother and maternal aunt behind them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said: I prayed beside the Prophet ﷺ, while ʿĀʾishah was behind us praying with us, and I was beside the Prophet ﷺ praying with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I was in the mosque,

in the front row, a man pulled me firmly from behind, moved me aside and stood in my place. By Allah, I could not make sense of my prayer. When he finished, it was Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. He said, "Young man, may Allah not cause you distress. This is a covenant the Prophet ﷺ made with us, that we should stand right behind him." Then he faced the qiblah and said three times, "The people of the covenant are ruined, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah." Then he said, "By Allah, I do not grieve for them, but I grieve for those whom they led astray."
I said, "O Abū Yaʿqūb, whom do you mean by the people of the covenant?" He said, "The rulers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
"Straighten up, straighten up, straighten up! By the One in whose hand is my soul, I see you from behind me just as I see you in front of me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: He used to invoke blessings upon the first row three times, and upon the second once.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command brevity [in prayer], and he would lead us in prayer with [Sūrat] aṣ-Ṣāffāt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from the Anṣār came when the prayer had been called, entered the mosque and prayed behind Muʿādh, who made the prayer long for them. The man left and prayed on one side of the mosque, then went off. When Muʿādh finished the prayer, he was told, "So-and-so did such and such."
Muʿādh said, "If morning comes, I will certainly mention that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
Muʿādh came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned it to him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for the man and said:
"What made you do what you did?"

He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I had been working all day with my water-carrying camel. I came when the prayer had been called, entered the mosque and joined him in the prayer. He recited such and such a sūrah and made it long, so I left and prayed on one side of the mosque."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Are you a cause of trial, O Muʿādh? Are you a cause of trial, O Muʿādh? Are you a cause of trial, O Muʿādh?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū ad-Dardāʾ said to me, "Where is your dwelling?" I said, "In a village near Ḥimṣ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Ḥunayn and rain fell on us, so the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ announced: "Pray in your dwellings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] from Banū ad-Dīl called Busr ibn Miḥjan [narrated] from Miḥjan,

that he was sitting in a gathering with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when the call to prayer was made. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up, then returned while Miḥjan was still in his place, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"What prevented you from praying? Are you not a Muslim man?"
He said, "Indeed I am, but I had already prayed with my family." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"When you come, pray with the people, even if you have already prayed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed ʿAṣr, he would go to Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal and talk with them until he went down toward Maghrib.
Abū Rāfiʿ said: While the Prophet ﷺ was hurrying to Maghrib, we passed by al-Baqīʿ, and he said:
"Uff to you! Uff to you!"
He said: That weighed heavily on me, so I held back, thinking he meant me. Then he said:
"What is the matter with you? Walk on."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Samurah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"The hand is responsible for what it has taken until it returns it."
Then al-Ḥasan forgot and said: "He is your trustee; there is no liability upon him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Settlement is permissible between the Muslims." Aḥmad added:
"except a settlement that makes lawful what is unlawful or makes unlawful what is lawful."
Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd added: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Muslims are bound by their conditions."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ judged on the basis of an oath together with one witness.
He said: And ʿAlī judged by it among you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Delaying repayment by one who is able to pay makes his honour and his punishment permissible."
Ibn al-Mubārak said: "His honour being permissible means one may speak harshly to him, and his punishment means he may be imprisoned."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the descendants of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abān ibn ʿUthmān
narrating from his father, who said:

Zayd ibn Thābit came out from Marwān's presence at midday. We said: "He would not have sent for him at this hour except to ask him about something." So we got up and asked him, and he said: "Yes, he asked us about things we had heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'May Allah make radiant the person who hears a saying from us and memorizes it until he conveys it to another. For many a bearer of understanding conveys it to one who understands better than he, and many a bearer of understanding is not himself a person of understanding.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever goes to a soothsayer."
Mūsā said in his narration:
"and believes what he says." Then they agreed:
"or goes to a woman." Musaddad said:
"his wife during menstruation, or goes to a woman." Musaddad said:
"his wife in her rear, has disavowed what Allah revealed to Muḥammad."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My brother left a bequest to me of a portion of his wealth. I met Abū al-Dardāʾ and said: "My brother has left me a portion of his wealth as a bequest; where do you think I should place it: among the poor, the needy, or those striving in the cause of Allah?" He said: "As for me, I would not give anything precedence over those striving. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'The likeness of one who frees a slave at the time of death is like one who gives a gift after he is full.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever eats food and then says, 'Praise be to Allah who fed me this food and provided it for me without any power or strength from myself,' his earlier and later sins will be forgiven. And whoever puts on a garment and then says, 'Praise be to Allah who clothed me with this garment and provided it for me without any power or strength from myself,' his earlier and later sins will be forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Hamdān called Abū Aflaḥ, from Ibn Zarīr,
that he heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took some silk and held it in his right hand, and took some gold and held it in his left hand, then said:
"These two are forbidden for the males of my nation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Ibn ʿUmar dyeing his beard yellow with khalūq, so I said: "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, you dye your beard yellow with khalūq."
He said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dye his beard with it, and no dye was dearer to him than it. He would even dye all his garments with it, even his turban."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man called Ziyād, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There will be a trial that will engulf the Arabs; those slain in it will be in the Fire. The tongue in it is more severe than the striking of the sword."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr said, after praising Allah and extolling

Him: "O people, you recite this verse and place it in the wrong context: {Take care of yourselves; those who go astray cannot harm you if you are guided.}" Khālid's narration says: "And we heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
'When people see the wrongdoer and do not seize his hands, Allah is about to include them all in a punishment.'"
ʿAmr, from Hushaym, said: "And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'There is no people among whom sins are committed, and who are able to change it yet do not change it, except that Allah is about to include them all in punishment from Him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to learn for him the writing of the Jews. He said: "
By Allah, I do not trust the Jews with my correspondence."
He said: Half a month had not passed before I had learned it for him. When I had learned it, whenever he wrote to the Jews I wrote to them, and whenever they wrote to him I read their letter to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Whoever speaks about the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, according to his own opinion, and happens to be correct, has still made an error."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

Whoever learns knowledge of the kind by which the Face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is sought, but he learns it only to gain some worldly goods by it, will not find the fragrance of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection." He meant its scent.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
No one should address the people as a storyteller except a ruler, or one appointed by a ruler, or one who is showing off."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Every intoxicant is forbidden, and whatever intoxicates in a large quantity (a faraq), even a handful of it is forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, you know who we are and where we are from, so to whom do we belong? He said: "
To Allah and to His Messenger."
We said: O Messenger of Allah, we have grapevines; what should we do with them? He said: "Make them into raisins."
We said: What should we do with raisins? He said: "

Soak them in the morning and drink them in the evening, and soak them in the evening and drink them in the morning. Soak them in waterskins, and do not soak them in jars, for if it is delayed beyond its pressing time it becomes vinegar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "

Close the door, tie up the waterskin, cover the vessel or turn it over, and put out the lamp. For Satan does not open a closed door, does not untie a tied skin, and does not uncover a vessel, and the little vermin may set the people's house on fire over them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The night of the guest is a right upon every Muslim. Whoever has a guest come to his courtyard in the morning, it is a debt upon him; if he wishes he may claim it, and if he wishes he may leave it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
hosted ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and he prepared food for him. Fāṭimah said: If only we invited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that he could eat with us.

So they invited him and he came. He put his hands on the two sides of the doorframe and saw a decorated curtain hung in a corner of the house, so he turned back. Fāṭimah said to ʿAlī: Go after him and see what made him turn back.
I followed him and said: O Messenger of Allah, what made you turn back? He said: "
It is not fitting for me, or for any prophet, to enter a house that is ornately decorated."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read in the Torah that the blessing of food is in the washing after it. I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ and told him what I had read in the Torah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The blessing of food is in washing before it and washing after it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Companions of the Prophet
ﷺ said: O Messenger of Allah, we eat but are not satisfied. He said: "Perhaps you eat separately." They said: Yes. He said: "
Then gather around your food and mention the name of Allah over it; it will be blessed for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was eating food with six of his Companions when a Bedouin came and ate it in two mouthfuls. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

Had he said 'In the name of Allah,' it would have been enough for all of you. So when any of you eats food, let him say 'In the name of Allah.' If he forgets to say 'In the name of Allah' at the beginning, let him say: 'In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was never seen eating while reclining, nor did two men walk behind his heels.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade two kinds of eating: sitting at a table at which wine is being drunk, and a man eating while lying on his stomach.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a man asked him, saying: There is some food that I feel uneasy about. He said: "
Let nothing trouble your heart in which you would be resembling Christianity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I ate the meat of a bustard with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Khaybar, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the meat of domestic donkeys, and forbade riding the jallālah and eating its meat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about locusts, and he said: "
They are among the greatest of Allah's armies. I do not eat them, nor do I forbid them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) said, regarding {And those with whom your right hands have made a pact, give them their share}: A man would make a pact with another man, with no kinship between them, and one would inherit from the other. Then this was abrogated by [the verse in] al-Anfāl, where Allah the Exalted said: {And those who are bound by blood are closer to one another}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to recite to Umm Saʿd bint ar-Rabīʿ, who was an orphan raised in the care of Abū Bakr. I recited {And those with whom your right hands have made a pact}, and she said: Do not recite {ʿāqadat}, but rather {ʿaqadat aymānukum}. It was revealed only about Abū Bakr and his son ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, when he refused Islam. Abū Bakr swore that he would not give him an inheritance. Then when he became Muslim, Allah the Exalted commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, to give him his share.
ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz added: He did not become Muslim until he was compelled to accept Islam by the sword.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And those who

believed and emigrated, and those who believed but did not emigrate. So the Bedouin would not inherit from the emigrant, nor would the emigrant inherit from him. Then it was abrogated, and He said: {And those who are bound by blood are closer to one another}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a pact of brotherhood between the Emigrants and the Helpers in our house.
It was said to him: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not say:
"There is no pact of alliance in Islam"?
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a pact between the Emigrants and the Helpers in our house.
[He said it] two or three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went with two men to the Prophet ﷺ. One of them recited the testimony of faith, then said: We have come so that you may employ us in your administration.
The other said the same as his companion. Then he said:
"The most dishonest among you in our sight is the one who seeks it."
Abū Mūsā apologized to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I did not know why they had come.
So he did not employ them for anything until he died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ appointed Ibn Umm Maktūm as his deputy over Madinah twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck him on his shoulder and then said to him:
"You will be successful, O Qudaym, if you die without having been a ruler, a secretary, or a chief."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They were at one of the watering places. When Islam reached them, the owner of the water gave his people a hundred camels on condition that they accept Islam, and they accepted Islam. He distributed the camels among them, but then he decided to take them back from them.
