segments_en: His father was killed as a martyr on the day of Uḥud,
and the creditors pressed hard for their rights.
So I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke to him,
and he asked them to accept the fruit of my orchard and to release my father from the debt, but they refused.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not give them my orchard,
nor did he divide it up for them, but he said: "I will come to you in the morning."
He came to us in the morning,
and walked among the date palms,
and prayed for blessing in their fruit. Then I harvested it, and paid them their rights,
and some of its fruit remained for us.
Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was sitting, and told him about that,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿUmar:
"Listen, O ʿUmar," while he was sitting.
ʿUmar said: "Is it not the case that we already knew that you are the Messenger of Allah?
By Allah, you are indeed the Messenger of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Delay by a wealthy person [in paying a debt] is injustice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ﷺ [recite] differently, so I took him by the hand,
and brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Both of you are doing well."
Shuʿbah said: I think he said:
"Do not differ, for those before you differed and were destroyed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting, a Jewish man came,
and said: "O Abū al-Qāsim, a man of your Companions struck my face." He said: "Who?"
He said: "A man of the Anṣār." He said: "Call him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said: I found a purse containing one hundred dinars and came to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Announce it for a year."
So I announced it for a year, but did not find anyone who recognized it,
then I came to him, and he said: "Announce it for a year."
So I announced it, but found no one.
Then I came to him a third time, and he said:
"Keep its container, its count, and its string,
and if its owner comes,
[give it to him]; otherwise, make use of it."
So I made use of it. Afterward I met him in Mecca, and he said: I do not know whether it was three years or one year.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I set out,
and there was a shepherd driving his sheep. I said: "To whom do you belong?" He said: "To a man of Quraysh," and he named him, and I knew him.
I said: "Is there any milk in your flock?" He said: "Yes."
I said: "Will you milk for me?" He said: "Yes."
So I told him, and he tied up one sheep from his flock.
Then I told him to wipe the dust from its udder,
then I told him to wipe his hands.
He said: "Like this," striking one palm against the other. Then he milked a small amount of milk. I had prepared for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a leather container with a piece of cloth over its mouth,
and I poured [the milk] over it,
until its bottom became cool,
then I reached the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Drink, O Messenger of Allah."
He drank until I was satisfied.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "And We shall remove whatever rancor is in their hearts." He said: Saʿīd narrated to us from Qatādah, from Abū al-Mutawakkil al-Nājī, that Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The believers will be saved from the Fire,
and they will be held on a bridge between Paradise and the Fire,
and retribution will be taken for some of them from others
for wrongs that were between them in the world,
until, when they have been cleansed and purified, they will be permitted to enter Paradise.
By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, each of them will know his dwelling in Paradise better than he knew his dwelling in the world."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Allah took His Prophet ﷺ in death, the Anṣār gathered in the hall of Banū Sāʿidah,
and I said to Abū Bakr: "Come with us."
So we came to them in the hall of Banū Sāʿidah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say: Whoever prays at night, let him make the last of his prayer an odd-numbered prayer (witr) before dawn. That is how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was asked whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had recited the qunūt in the dawn prayer, and he said: Yes.
It was said to him: Before bowing or after bowing? He said: After bowing.
Musaddad said: [It was] for a short while.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ went out with the people to pray for rain for them.
He stood and supplicated to Allah while standing,
then he turned toward the qiblah,
and he turned his cloak around, and they were given rain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr,
that he heard ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm
say: I heard ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd al-Māzinī
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the place of prayer and prayed for rain, and he turned his cloak around when he faced the qiblah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not raise his hands in any of his supplications,
except in the prayer for rain,
for he would raise his hands until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen.
Abū Mūsā said: The Prophet ﷺ supplicated and raised his hands, and I saw the whiteness of his armpits.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Minā, when the people were at their most numerous, and he led us in two rakʿahs during the Farewell Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUthmān prayed four rakʿahs at Minā. ʿAbdullāh said: I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ two rakʿahs, with Abū Bakr two rakʿahs, and with ʿUmar two rakʿahs. In the narration from Ḥafṣ he added: and with ʿUthmān in the early part of his caliphate, then he completed it.
From here the narration from Abū Muʿāwiyah adds: Then the paths diverged with you, and I wish that in place of four rakʿahs I had two that are accepted.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw the Prophet ﷺ praying the forenoon prayer (ḍuḥā), except for Umm Hāniʾ, for she related that the Prophet ﷺ entered her house on the day of the conquest of Makkah and prayed eight rakʿahs. I never saw him pray a lighter prayer than it, except that he completed the bowing and the prostration.
Ibn Bashshār did not mention the word “ever” in his narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to combine the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers while traveling, without anything hurrying him, without an enemy pursuing him, and without his fearing anything.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out before the sun passed its zenith, he would delay the Ẓuhr prayer until the time of ʿAṣr,
then he would stop and combine the two.
If the sun passed its zenith before he set out, he would pray Ẓuhr and then mount.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray the night prayer sitting until he grew old.
He would recite while sitting, until when he wished to bow, he would stand,
and recite about thirty or forty verses, then bow.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to ʿĀʾishah and said: O Mother, tell me about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
She said: His prayer, in the month of Ramaḍān and other than it, was thirteen rakʿahs at night, including the two rakʿahs of Fajr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who had slept a whole night until morning. He said:
That is a man in whose ears Satan has urinated.” Or he said: “in whose ear.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
O ʿAbdullāh,
do not be like so-and-so;
he used to pray at night, then he gave up praying at night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

Whoever wakes during the night and says when he awakens: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise, and He has power over all things. Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, and there is no power and no might except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great; then he says: My Lord, forgive me—he will be forgiven.
Al-Walīd said, or he said:
If he supplicates, he will be answered; and if he gets up, performs ablution, and prays, his prayer will be accepted.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to greet the Prophet ﷺ while he was praying, and he would return the greeting to us.
When we returned from the Negus, we greeted him but he did not return it to us.
We said: O Messenger of Allah, we used to greet you and you would return the greeting to us. He said:
Indeed, in prayer there is preoccupation.
I said to Ibrāhīm: How do you do it? He said: I return it within myself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on an extremely hot day. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led his Companions in prayer and prolonged the standing until they began to fall down. Then he bowed and prolonged it, then raised his head and prolonged it, then bowed and prolonged it, then raised his head and prolonged it, then prostrated twice. Then he stood and did something similar, so there were four bowings and four prostrations. Then he said:

"Everything that you will enter was shown to me. Paradise was shown to me, so that if I had reached out for a cluster of fruit from it I would have taken it" – or he said, "I reached for a cluster from it – but my hand fell short of it. And the Fire was shown to me, and I saw in it a woman from the Children of Israel being punished because of a cat of hers that she had tied up; she neither fed it nor let it eat from the vermin of the earth. And I saw in it Abū Thumāmah ʿAmr ibn Mālik dragging his intestines in the Fire.

They used to say that the sun and the moon are eclipsed only for the death of a great man. But they are two signs among the signs of Allah, which He shows you. So when they are eclipsed, pray until it clears."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked al-Aswad ibn Yazīd about what ʿĀʾishah narrated to him concerning the prayer of

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: He would sleep at the beginning of the night and keep the end of it alive in worship. Then, if he had need of his wife, he would fulfil his need, then sleep. When it was the first call to prayer, she said, he would leap up – and by Allah, she did not say "he stood up" – and pour water over himself – and by Allah, she did not say "he bathed" –
and I know what she meant. And if he was not in a state of major impurity, he would perform ablution as a man does for prayer, then pray the two units.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik ibn Anas, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ announced to the people the death of the Negus on the day he died, and went out with them to the prayer ground, arranged them in rows, and said the takbīr four times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the news of the killing of Ibn Ḥārithah, Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib, and ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he sat, and grief could be recognised in him. She said: I was watching from the gap of the door – the crack in the door. A man came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the women of Jaʿfar," and he mentioned their weeping. So he ordered him to go and forbid them. He went, then came back and said that they had not obeyed him. He ordered him a second time to go and forbid them. He went, then came back and said, "By Allah, they have overpowered us, O Messenger of Allah."
She said: I think that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Go and throw dust into their mouths."
ʿĀʾishah said: I said, "May Allah rub your nose in the dust! By Allah, you will not do what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered you, and you have not spared the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from hardship."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed behind Ibn ʿAbbās at a funeral prayer, and I heard him recite
the Opening of the Book. When he finished, I took his hand and asked him, saying, "Do you recite it?" He said, "Yes, it is the truth and the Sunnah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah stood on the day of the Conquest and said:
"Indeed Allah made Makkah sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth,
so it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection.
It was not permitted to anyone before me,
and it will not be permitted to anyone after me,
and it was permitted to me only for an hour of a day.
Its game is not to be scared away,
its thorns are not to be cut,
its fresh grass is not to be cut, and its lost property is not permitted to be picked up except by one who will announce it."
Then al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said, "Except the idhkhir, O Messenger of Allah,
for it is indispensable for the blacksmiths and for houses."
He was silent, then said:
"Except the idhkhir, for it is permitted."
And from Ibn Jurayj: ʿAbd al-Karīm informed me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, something like this or similar to this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was read to him while I listened,
- and the wording is his - from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl,
from Anas ibn Mālik,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of fruits until they show ripeness (tuzhī).
It was asked, "O Messenger of Allah, what does 'show ripeness' mean?" He said, "Until they turn red."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Tell me: if Allah withholds the fruit, by what right would one of you take the wealth of his brother?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was read to him while I listened,
- and the wording is his - from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from ʿAbd al-Majīd ibn Suhayl,
from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab,
from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī,
and from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed a man over Khaybar, and he came with fine-quality dates (janīb). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Are all the dates of Khaybar like this?"
He said, "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we take one ṣāʿ of this for two ṣāʿs, and two ṣāʿs for three."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Do not do that. Sell the mixed dates for dirhams, then buy fine dates with the dirhams."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that,
while he was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ, a man from the Anṣār came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we take captives and we love wealth;
what is your view on withdrawal (ʿazl)?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Do you really do that?
There is no harm on you if you do not,
for there is no soul that Allah has decreed will come into being except that it will come to be."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Burdah and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād disagreed about salam sales, so they sent me to Ibn Abī Awfā. I asked him and he said, "We used to make salam transactions in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and in the time of Abū Bakr and in the time of ʿUmar, in wheat, barley, raisins and dates, with people whom we did not see to have [those goods] with them."
And I asked Ibn Abzā, and he said the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had himself cupped,
and he gave the cupper his payment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to have himself cupped,
and he would never wrong anyone of his payment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Prophet ﷺ demanding repayment of a camel,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Give it to him."
They said, "We can only find one older and better than his."
The man said, "You have paid me in full; may Allah repay you in full."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Give it to him, for among the best of people are those who are best in repaying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were the people of Madinah with the most farmland.
We used to rent out land, designating for the landowner a certain portion of it.
He said: Sometimes that portion would be struck by blight while the rest of the land was safe,
and sometimes the land would be struck while that portion was safe, so we were forbidden.
As for gold and silver, they were not [used for this] at that time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Ṭāwus, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, if only you would give up this mukhābarah, for they claim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it."

He said, "O ʿAmr, I help them and give to them, and Muʿādh ibn Jabal took people on this basis among us. The most knowledgeable of them - meaning Ibn ʿAbbās - informed me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not forbid it, but said,
'That one of you grant his brother [the land] is better for him than that he take a fixed payment for it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he handed over to the Jews of Khaybar the date palms of Khaybar and its land on the condition that they work it with their own wealth, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have half of its fruit.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ẓuhayr came to me and said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has forbidden something that was beneficial to us."
I said, "What is that? Whatever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says is true."
He said: He asked me, "How do you deal with your fields?" I said, "We rent them out, O Messenger of Allah, for [produce of] the stream-banks, or for [fixed] wasqs of dates or barley." He said,
"Do not do that. Cultivate them yourselves, or have them cultivated, or keep them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"There are three to whom Allah will not look on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them,
and for them is a painful punishment: a man who had surplus water on the road,
and withheld it from the traveler;
a man who pledged allegiance to a leader, pledging only for worldly gain,
so if he gives him some of it he is pleased,
and if he does not give him any of it he is angry;
and a man who displayed his merchandise after the ʿAṣr prayer,
and said, 'By Allah, besides Whom there is no god, I was offered such and such for it,' and a man believed him."
Then he recited this verse: {Indeed, those who exchange Allah's covenant and their oaths for a small price}
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father and I went out seeking knowledge among this tribe of the Anṣār before they passed away. The first person we met was Abū al-Yasar, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and with him was a servant boy of his carrying a bundle of pages. Abū al-Yasar was wearing a cloak and a Maʿāfirī garment, and his servant was wearing a cloak and a Maʿāfirī garment. My father said to him, "Uncle, I see a mark of anger in your face."
He said, "Yes. I was owed money by so-and-so son of so-and-so of Banū Ḥarām. I went to his family, greeted them with salām, and said, 'Is he there?' They said, 'No.'
Then a sturdy young son of his came out to me, and I said to him, 'Where is your father?' He said, 'He heard your voice and went into my mother's canopied couch.'
So I said, 'Come out to me, for I know where you are.'

He came out, and I said, 'What made you hide from me?' He said, 'By Allah, I will tell you and I will not lie to you. I feared, by Allah, that I would speak to you and lie to you, or promise you and break my promise to you. You were a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and by Allah, I was in hardship.'
I said, 'By Allah?' He said, 'By Allah.' I said, 'By Allah?' He said, 'By Allah.' I said, 'By Allah?' He said, 'By Allah.'

Then his ledger was brought, and he erased it with his own hand and said, 'If you find the means to pay, then pay me; otherwise you are released from it.' I testify that these two eyes of mine saw it—and he placed his two fingers on his eyes—and these two ears of mine heard it, and this heart of mine retained it—and he pointed to the vessel of his heart—the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying:
'Whoever gives respite to one in hardship, or remits [the debt] for him, Allah will shade him in His shade.'"

He said: I said to him, "Uncle, if only you had taken your servant's cloak and given him your Maʿāfirī garment, and taken his Maʿāfirī garment and given him your cloak, then you would have a matching set and he would have a matching set."

He wiped my head and said, "O Allah, bless him. Nephew, these two eyes of mine saw it, these two ears of mine heard it, and this heart of mine retained it—and he pointed to the vessel of his heart—the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying:
'Feed them from what you eat, and clothe them from what you wear.'
And that I give him some of the goods of this world is easier for me than that he take from my good deeds on the Day of Resurrection."

Then we went on until we came to Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh in his mosque. He was praying in a single garment wrapped around himself. I stepped over the people until I sat between him and the qiblah, and I said, "May Allah have mercy on you! Do you pray in a single garment while your cloak is beside you?" He struck his hand against my chest like this, spreading his fingers and curving them, and said, "I wanted a fool like you to come in and see how I do it, so that he would do the same.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us in this mosque of ours, with a branch of an Ibn Ṭāb date palm in his hand. He saw phlegm on the qiblah wall of the mosque and scraped it off with the branch. Then he turned to us and said:
'Which of you would like Allah to turn away from him?'
He said: We were humbled. Then he said:
'Which of you would like Allah to turn away from him?'
He said: We were humbled. Then he said:
'Which of you would like Allah to turn away from him?'
We said, "None of us, O Messenger of Allah." He said:

'When any one of you stands to pray, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is before his face. So let him not spit in front of him, nor to his right; let him spit to his left, beneath his left foot. And if something urgent comes over him, let him do like this with his garment.'
Then he folded his garment over itself and said, "Bring me some perfume."

A young man from the tribe got up and ran to his family, and came back with some khalūq perfume in his palm. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it, put it on the end of the branch, and smeared it over the mark of the phlegm.
Jābir said: "It is from that that you people put khalūq in your mosques."

We travelled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the expedition of Buṭn Buwāṭ, while he was pursuing al-Majdī ibn ʿAmr al-Juhanī. We took turns on a water-carrying camel, five, six, or seven of us per camel. The turn of a man of the Anṣār came on his camel. He made it kneel and mounted it, then urged it up, but it hesitated somewhat under him, and he said to it, "Go on, may Allah curse you!"
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Who is this who is cursing his camel?'
He said, "I am, O Messenger of Allah." He said:

'Get down from it. Do not accompany us with something cursed. Do not invoke [harm] upon yourselves, do not invoke [harm] upon your children, and do not invoke [harm] upon your wealth, lest you coincide with an hour in which Allah is asked for something and grants it to you.'
We travelled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until, when evening came and we drew near one of the watering places of the Arabs, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Who will go ahead of us, plaster the basin, and drink and give us water?'
Jābir said: I stood up and said, "Here is a man, O Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Which man will go with Jābir?'

Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr stood up, and we went to the well. We drew a bucket or two into the basin, then plastered it, then drew water into it until we filled it to the brim. The first to appear before us was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said, "Do you allow?"
We said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah."

He let his she-camel approach, and she drank. He pulled her rein tight, so she spread her hind legs and urinated. Then he turned her aside and made her kneel. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to the basin and performed ablution from it. Then I stood and performed ablution from the place where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had performed ablution. Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr went to relieve himself, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood to pray. I was wearing a cloak; I tried to cross its two ends over, but it did not reach, and it had fringes. So I turned it upside down, then crossed its two ends, then bent my neck over it to hold it. Then I came and stood to the left of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He took my hand and turned me around until he stood me on his right. Then Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr came, performed ablution, and stood to the left of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took both of us by the hands and pushed us back until he stood us behind him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept watching me out of the corner of his eye without my realizing it. Then I noticed him, and he gestured like this with his hand, meaning: tie your waist. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished, he said, "O Jābir."
I said, "At your service, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
'If it is wide, cross its two ends over; and if it is narrow, tie it around your waist.'

We travelled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the provision of each of us per day was one date. He would suck on it and then tie it up in his garment. We used to beat down leaves with our bows and eat them until our mouths became sore. One day one of us missed out on his date, so we took him along to revive him. We testified that he had not been given it, so it was given to him, and he got up and took it.

We travelled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we stopped in a wide valley. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to relieve himself, and I followed him with a container of water. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked and saw nothing to screen himself with, but there were two trees at the edge of the valley. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to one of them, took hold of one of its branches, and said:
'Yield to me, by the permission of Allah.'
So it yielded to him like a camel with a nose-ring that is gentle with its leader, until he came to the other tree, took hold of one of its branches, and said:
'Yield to me, by the permission of Allah.'
So it yielded to him in the same way, until, when he was at the midpoint between them, he brought them together—meaning he joined them—and said:
'Join together over me, by the permission of Allah.'

And they joined together. Jābir said: I went out hurrying, fearing that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would sense my nearness and move farther away—and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād said, "and withdraw"—so I sat down talking to myself. Then I happened to glance and saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ coming, and the two trees had separated, each standing on its own trunk. I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stop for a moment and gesture with his head like this—and Abū Ismāʿīl gestured with his head to the right and left—then he came forward. When he reached me, he said:
'O Jābir, did you see where I stood?'
I said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
'Then go to the two trees and cut a branch from each of them, and come back with them. When you reach the place where I stood, let one branch go to your right and one branch to your left.'

Jābir said: I got up, took a stone, broke it and sharpened it, and it became sharp for me. I went to the two trees, cut a branch from each, then came back dragging them until I stood where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had stood. I let one branch go to my right and one to my left. Then I caught up with him and said, "I have done it, O Messenger of Allah, but for what purpose?" He said:
'I passed by two graves whose occupants were being punished, and I wished by my intercession that it be eased for them for as long as the two branches remain moist.'
He said: Then we came to the camp, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'O Jābir, call out for water for ablution.'

So I called, "Is there no water for ablution? Is there no water for ablution? Is there no water for ablution?" I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have not found a drop in the caravan." A man of the Anṣār used to cool water for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his water-skins on a frame of palm branches. He said to me:
'Go to so-and-so son of so-and-so, the Anṣārī, and see whether there is anything in his water-skins.'
He said: I went to him and looked in them, but found nothing in them except a drop in the mouth of one skin; if I were to pour it out, its dry part would drink it up.
I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I found nothing in them except a drop in the mouth of one skin; if I were to pour it out, its dry part would drink it up." He said:
'Go and bring it to me.'
So I brought it to him. He took it in his hand and began saying something I do not know what it was, while pressing it with his hands. Then he gave it to me and said:
'O Jābir, call for a large bowl.'
So I called, "Bring the caravan's bowl!"

It was brought, carried, and I set it down before him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ put his hand in the bowl like this, spreading it and separating his fingers, and placed it at the bottom of the bowl. He said:
'Take [the skin], O Jābir, pour over me, and say: In the name of Allah.'
So I poured over him and said, "In the name of Allah."
Then I saw water gushing forth from between the fingers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then the bowl bubbled and swirled until it was full. He said:
'O Jābir, call out to whoever needs water.'
He said: The people came and drew water until they were quenched. I said, "Is there anyone left who needs any?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ lifted his hand from the bowl, and it was full.
The people complained of hunger to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
'Perhaps Allah will feed you.'
Then we came to the seashore, and the sea surged and cast up a creature. We lit a fire on its side, and we cooked, roasted, and ate until we were full.

Jābir said: So I went in, along with so-and-so and so-and-so—until he counted five—into the socket of its eye, and no one could see us until we came out. Then we took one of its ribs and arched it. Then we called for the biggest man in the caravan, the biggest camel in the caravan, and the biggest rump in the caravan, and he passed beneath it without lowering his head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the year 195 he said: Sufyān narrated to us, in the gathering of al-Aʿmash fifty years ago, [saying]: ʿAmr ibn Murrah al-Jamalī narrated to us, in the time of Khālid, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥārith al-Muktib, from Ṭulayq ibn Qays al-Ḥanafī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet ﷺ used to say in his supplication:

"My Lord, help me and do not help [others] against me; grant me victory and do not grant victory over me; plan for me and do not plan against me; guide me and make guidance easy for me; and grant me victory over whoever wrongs me. My Lord, make me ever grateful to You, ever remembering You, ever fearful of You, obedient to You, humble before You, constantly turning to You in contrition and repentance. My Lord, accept my repentance, wash away my sin, answer my prayer, guide my heart, make my tongue true, make my argument firm, and remove the rancor from my heart."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It used to be counted for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in a single sitting, a hundred times before he stood up [that he would say]:
"My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance; indeed You are the Ever-Accepting of repentance, the Most Forgiving."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was a man who, whenever I heard

a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Allah benefited me by it as much as He willed. And when one of his Companions narrated to me, I would make him swear an oath, and if he swore to me, I believed him. Abū Bakr narrated to me, and Abū Bakr spoke the truth, that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"There is no man who commits a sin, then gets up and purifies himself, then prays, then asks Allah for forgiveness, except that Allah forgives him."
Then he recited this verse:

"And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins—and who forgives sins except Allah—and do not persist in what they have done while they know."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to recite the two Muʿawwidhatayn (the last two sūrahs of the Qurʾān) at the end of every prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There are three supplications that are answered, about which there is no doubt: the supplication of the oppressed, the supplication of the traveler, and the supplication of a father against his child."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from hunger, for it is an evil bedfellow; and I seek refuge in You from betrayal, for it is an evil inner companion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, teach me a supplication of refuge by which I may seek refuge.
He said: He took me by the shoulder and said:

"Say: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing, from the evil of my sight, from the evil of my tongue, from the evil of my heart, and from the evil of my semen." He meant his private part.
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith; we do not know it except through this route, from the hadith of Saʿd ibn Aws, from Bilāl ibn Yaḥyā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The one who transgresses in [collecting] charity is like the one who withholds it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathmah came to our gathering and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us, saying:
"When you estimate [the produce], take [your share] and leave a third; and if you do not leave a third, or cannot find a third, then leave a quarter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque with us, with a stick in his hand, and one of us had hung a cluster of poor-quality dates. He poked that cluster with the stick and said:
"If the owner of this charity wished, he could have given better than this." And he said:
"Indeed, the owner of this charity will eat poor-quality dates on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-ʿAbbās
asked the Prophet ﷺ about paying his charity early, before it was due, and he granted him permission to do so.
On another occasion [the narrator] said: So he permitted him to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Begging is a form of scratching with which a man scratches his own face; so whoever wishes may keep his face [unmarked], and whoever wishes may leave it—except that a man asks one in authority, or [asks] in a matter for which he has no alternative."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Buraydah [narrated] that a woman
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: I gave a slave girl as charity to my mother, and she has died and left that slave girl. He said:
"Your reward has been established, and she has returned to you through inheritance."
She said: And she died owing a month of fasting; will it suffice—or be made up—on her behalf if I fast for her? He said: "Yes."
She said: And she never performed Hajj; will it suffice—or be made up—on her behalf if I perform Hajj for her? He said: "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us out and appointed Abū ʿUbaydah over us, to intercept a caravan of Quraysh. He provisioned us with a bag of dates; he could find nothing else for us. Abū ʿUbaydah would give us one date at a time. [The narrator] said: I asked, "What did you do with it?" He said: "We would suck on it as a child sucks, then drink water after it, and that would suffice us from our day until night. We would also beat our sticks to knock down leaves, then moisten them with water and eat them." He said: We set off along the seashore, and something like a huge dune was raised before us on the shore. We went to it, and it was a creature called the ʿanbar [whale]. Abū ʿUbaydah said, "It is carrion." Then he said, "No, rather we are messengers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and are in the cause of Allah, and you are in dire need, so eat." He said: We stayed there a month, and we were three hundred, until we grew fat. He said: I remember us scooping oil out of the socket of its eye with jars, and cutting out from it pieces of flesh as large as a bull, or like the size of a bull. Abū ʿUbaydah took thirteen men of us and seated them in the socket of its eye, and he took one of its ribs and set it upright, then saddled the biggest camel we had and it passed beneath it. We also took provisions of its flesh, dried strips. When we arrived in Madinah, we went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said:
"It is a provision that Allah brought forth for you. Do you have any of its meat with you that you could feed us?"
He said: So we sent some of it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he ate it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We ate horse meat and wild donkey at the time of Khaybar, and the Prophet ﷺ forbade us from the domestic donkey.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade eating the meat of sacrificial animals after three days.

ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr said: I mentioned that to ʿAmrah, and she said: "He spoke the truth. I heard ʿĀʾishah say: Some households of the desert people came in need at the time of the Sacrifice during the era of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Store [meat] for three days, then give in charity what remains.'"
Later on, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, people make water-skins from their sacrificial animals and melt fat from them." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "What is that?"
They said: "You forbade eating the meat of sacrificial animals after three days." He said:
"I only forbade you because of the needy people who came in. So eat, store, and give in charity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"When the ten days begin and one of you intends to offer a sacrifice, let him not touch anything of his hair or skin."
Sufyān was asked: "Some of them do not attribute it to the Prophet ﷺ." He said: "But I do attribute it to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿUmar about nabīdh prepared in the jarr [clay jar].
He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade nabīdh of the jarr."
Then I went to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: "Do you not hear what Ibn ʿUmar says?" He said: "What does he say?" I said: "He says the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade nabīdh of the jarr."
He said: "Ibn ʿUmar spoke the truth. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade nabīdh of the jarr."
I asked: "And what is nabīdh of the jarr?" He said: "Everything that is made from clay."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to Ibn ʿUmar and said: "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid nabīdh of the jarr?" He said: "Yes."
Ṭāwūs said: "By Allah, I heard it from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I forbade you from [using certain] containers, but containers, or a container, neither make anything lawful nor make it unlawful. And every intoxicant is forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "I know it only to be from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
'Every intoxicant is khamr, and every khamr is forbidden.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a man enters his house and mentions Allah upon entering and when eating his food, the Devil says: 'You have no place to spend the night and no supper.'
But if he enters and does not mention Allah upon entering, the Devil says: 'You have found a place to spend the night.'
And if he does not mention Allah at his meal, he says: 'You have found a place to spend the night and supper.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ rebuked drinking while standing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ate food, he would lick his three fingers, and he said:
"If a morsel of one of you falls, let him remove any dirt from it and eat it, and not leave it for the Devil."
And he commanded us to wipe the dish clean, and said:
"None of you knows in which part of his food the blessing lies."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I and the Messenger of Allah

ﷺ, Abū al-Qāsim, used to lie in a single garment while I was menstruating, in my period. If any of it from me touched him, he would wash the part it touched and not go beyond it to anywhere else, and he would pray in it. Then he would return to me, and if any of it from me touched him, he would do the same, not going beyond it to anywhere else.
Then he would return to me, and if any of it from me touched him, he would do the same, not going beyond it to anywhere else.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Umm Salamah], the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, [reported] that a woman used to bleed heavily in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so Umm Salamah asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a ruling on her behalf, and he said:

"Let her count the number of nights and days in the month that she used to menstruate before what afflicted her afflicted her, and let her leave prayer for that length of time of the month. When she has passed that, let her bathe, then bind [herself] with a cloth, and then pray in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That she used to have irregular bleeding, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"When it is menstrual blood, it is dark blood that is recognized, so refrain from prayer. And when it is the other, perform ablution, for it is only a vein."
Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā said: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us; this is from his book.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman had irregular bleeding in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she was commanded to bring the ʿAṣr prayer forward and delay the Ẓuhr prayer, and to bathe once for the two.
And to delay the Maghrib prayer and bring the ʿIshāʾ prayer forward, and to bathe once for the two, and to bathe once for the Ṣubḥ prayer.
I said to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: [Is this] from the Prophet ﷺ? He said: I do not narrate anything to you from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to narrate that they performed wiping with clean earth together with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the dawn prayer. They struck the earth with their palms, then wiped their faces once; then they returned and struck the earth with their palms a second time, and wiped all of their arms up to the shoulders and armpits, using the inner sides of their hands.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made camp at Awlāt al-Jaysh, and ʿĀʾishah was with him. A necklace of hers made of Ẓafār beads broke, and the people were held up searching for her necklace until dawn broke, and the people had no water. Abū Bakr became angry with her and said: You have held up the people and they have no water. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed to His Messenger ﷺ the concession of purifying oneself with clean earth. So the Muslims stood with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and struck the ground with their hands, then lifted their hands without taking any of the dust, and wiped their faces and their arms up to the shoulders, and from the inner sides of their hands up to the armpits.
Ibn Yaḥyā added in his narration: Ibn Shihāb said in his narration: The people do not rely on this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a man
came to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: I am in a state of major ritual impurity and I did not find water.
ʿUmar said: Do not pray.

ʿAmmār said: Do you not remember, O Commander of the Faithful, when you and I were on a military expedition and we became ritually impure and found no water? As for you, you did not pray, while as for me, I rolled in the dust and then prayed. When we came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I mentioned that to him, and he said: "It would have been enough for you."

And the Prophet ﷺ struck the ground with his hands, then blew into them, and wiped his face and his palms with them. Salamah doubted and said: I do not know whether it was up to the elbows or up to the palms. ʿUmar said: We entrust you with what you took charge of. Shuʿbah said: He used to say: the palms, the face, and the forearms.
Manṣūr said to him: What are you saying? No one other than you mentions the forearms.
Then Salamah doubted and said: I do not know whether he mentioned the forearms or not.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a man

suffered a wound in his head in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then he had a wet dream and was commanded to bathe. He bathed, then was seized by cold and died. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"They killed him; may Allah kill them! Was not the cure for ignorance to ask?"
ʿAṭāʾ said: It reached us that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"If only he had washed his body and left his head where the wounds were."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not pray in our hair garments or in our quilts.
ʿUbayd Allāh said: My father was unsure [of the wording].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not pray in our quilts.
Sufyān said: [meaning] our outer wraps.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us and said:
"You will travel through the evening and the night, and, Allah willing, you will reach water tomorrow."

So the people set off, none of them paying attention to anyone else. Abū Qatādah said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was travelling until the middle of the night, and I was beside him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dozed and leaned away from his mount. I came to him and supported him, without waking him, until he was upright on his mount again. Then he travelled on until the night had waned further, and he leaned away from his mount again. I supported him without waking him until he was upright on his mount. Then he travelled on until, at the last part of the pre-dawn, he leaned over a lean stronger than the first two, until he almost fell. I came to him and supported him, and he raised his head and said, "Who is this?"
I said, "Abū Qatādah." He said:
"Since when have you been travelling like this beside me?"
I said, "I have been travelling like this since last night." He said:
"May Allah protect you as you have protected His Prophet." Then he said:
"Do you think we are hidden from the people?" Then he said:
"Do you see anyone?"
I said, "This is a rider."
Then I said, "This is another rider."
until we gathered and were seven riders. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned off the road and laid down his head, then said:
"Watch over our prayer for us."
The first of them to wake up was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with the sun on his back. He said: We got up in alarm, and then he said, "Mount up."

So we mounted and travelled on until, when the sun had risen, he dismounted. Then he called for a small water container that I had, which had a little water in it. He said: He performed a light ablution from it, and some water remained in it. Then he said to Abū Qatādah:
"Keep your water container safe for us, for it will have an important story."

Then Bilāl called the adhān for prayer, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed two rakʿahs, then prayed the morning prayer, doing as he did every day. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mounted and we mounted with him. He said: Some of us began whispering to others, "What is the expiation for what we did, falling short in our prayer?" Then he said:
"Do you not have an example in me?" Then he said:

"Indeed, there is no negligence in sleep. Negligence is only on the one who does not pray the prayer until the time of the next prayer comes. Whoever does that, let him pray it when he becomes aware of it, and when the next day comes, let him pray it at its time." Then he said:
"What do you think the people have done?"
He said: Then he said:
"In the morning the people found their Prophet missing. Abū Bakr and ʿUmar said, 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is behind you; he would not leave you behind.'
And the people said, 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is ahead of you. If they obey Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, they will be rightly guided.'"
He said: We reached the people when the day had grown long and everything had become hot, and they were saying, "O Messenger of Allah, we are perishing, we are thirsty!" He said:
"There is no ruin for you." Then he said:
"Bring me my large drinking cup."

He said: He called for the water container, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to pour while Abū Qatādah gave them to drink. No sooner did the people see water in the container than they crowded over it.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Behave well in your filling; all of you will be quenched."

He said: They did so, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept pouring and I kept giving them to drink until no one was left except me and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ poured and said to me, "Drink."
I said, "I will not drink until you drink, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"The one who serves the people drink is the last of them to drink."
He said: So I drank, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank. He said: Then the people came to the water, refreshed and fully satisfied.
He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabāḥ said: I was relating this hadith in the congregational mosque when ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn said, "Look, young man, how you narrate, for I was one of the riders that night."
He said: I said, "Then you know the hadith better."
He said, "Which people are you from?" I said, "From the Anṣār."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and the people began to raise their voices in saying takbīr. So the Prophet ﷺ said:
"O people, be gentle with yourselves. You are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent. You are calling upon One who is All-Hearing and Near, and He is with you."
He said: I was behind him, saying, "There is no power and no strength except with Allah," so he said:
"O ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays, shall I not guide you to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise?"
I said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"Say: There is no power and no strength except with Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, marvelled at a people who are led to Paradise in chains."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent my father and Muʿādh ibn Jabal to Yemen and said:
"Make things easy and do not make them difficult,
give glad tidings and do not drive people away, and cooperate with one another."
Abū Mūsā said to him, "In our land a drink called al-bitʿ is made." He said:
"Every intoxicant is forbidden."
An-Naḍr, Abū Dāwūd, Yazīd ibn Hārūn and Wakīʿ said, from Shuʿbah, from Saʿīd, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out before the call to the first prayer had been made,

and the milch camels of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were grazing at Dhū Qarad. He said: A slave boy of ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf met me and said, "The milch camels of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have been taken." I said, "Who took them?" He said, "Ghaṭafān." He said: So I cried out three times, "Yā ṣabāḥāh!"

He said: I made everyone between the two lava tracts of Medina hear it. Then I rushed forward until I caught up with them at Dhū Qarad, when they had begun to water their animals. I started shooting them with my arrows, and I was a skilled archer, saying, "I am the son of al-Akwaʿ, and today is the day of the suckling ones," reciting verses of rajaz until I had rescued the milch camels from them and taken thirty cloaks from them. He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ and the people came. I said, "O Prophet of Allah, I have kept the people from the water while they are thirsty, so send [men] to them now." He said:
"O son of al-Akwaʿ, you have gained power, so be gentle."
He said: Then we returned, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had me ride behind him on his she-camel until we entered Medina.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Khudrī said: The people of Qurayẓah surrendered on the judgment of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for Saʿd, and he came on a donkey. When he came near the mosque, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Anṣār:
"Stand for your chief," or he said, "for the best of you." Then he said:
"These people have surrendered to your judgment."
He said, "Let their fighters be killed and their children be taken captive."
He said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"You have judged by the judgment of Allah," and sometimes he said, "You have judged by the judgment of the King."
Ibn al-Muthannā did not mention "and sometimes he said,"
"You have judged by the judgment of the King."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Feed the hungry, visit the sick, and free the captive."
Sufyān said: Al-ʿānī means the prisoner.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A spy from the polytheists came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was on a journey. He sat with the Companions and then slipped away. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Seek him out and kill him."
He said: I reached him before them, killed him, and took his belongings, and the Prophet ﷺ gave them to me as an additional award.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The day of Thursday,
and what a day Thursday was! Then he wept until his tears wet the pebbles. He said: The illness of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ grew severe on Thursday, and he said:
"Bring me something to write on, so that I may write for you a document after which you will never go astray."
They disputed, and it is not fitting to dispute in the presence of a prophet. They said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is delirious." He said:
"Leave me, for what I am in is better than what you call me to."
And at his death he gave three instructions:
"Expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula,
and give delegations gifts similar to what I used to give them." And I forgot the third.
Yaʿqūb ibn Muḥammad said: I asked al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān about the Arabian Peninsula.
He said: Makkah, Medina, al-Yamāmah and Yemen.
Yaʿqūb said: And al-ʿArj is the beginning of Tihāmah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah,
I have been enlisted for such and such a military expedition, and my wife is going for Hajj." He said:
"Go back and perform Hajj with your wife."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, concerning the expedition of Tabūk, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in the morning. Whenever he returned from a journey, he would begin with the mosque, pray two rakʿahs in it, and then sit with the people. When he did that, those who had stayed behind came to him and began to make excuses to him and swear oaths to him. They were a little over eighty men. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted their outward statements, took their pledge, asked forgiveness for them, and left their inner secrets to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Then I came, and when I greeted him, he smiled the smile of one who is angry, and then said, "Come."
So I came until I sat in front of him, and he said to me,
"What kept you behind? Had you not purchased your mount?"

I said, "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, if I were sitting with anyone other than you from among the people of this world, I would see that I could escape his anger, for I have been given skill in argument. But by Allah, I know that if I tell you a false account today to make you pleased with me, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will soon make you angry with me. And if I tell you a truthful account, at which you will be displeased with me, I hope for Allah's pardon in it. By Allah, I was never stronger or better off than when I stayed behind from you."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"As for this man, he has spoken the truth. So get up until Allah decides your matter." So I got up and went on. [Abridged]
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to go out in the morning to the market during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we would pass by the mosque and pray in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Sulaym

asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to come to her and pray in her house so that she could take it as a place of prayer. He came to her, and she went to a mat and sprinkled it with water. He prayed on it, and they prayed with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited ʿAbbās in a desert area of ours, where we had a small dog and a she-donkey grazing. The Prophet ﷺ prayed the ʿAṣr prayer while the two were in front of him, and they were neither driven away nor held back.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he passed in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he and a boy from Banū Hāshim, on a donkey, in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was praying. They dismounted and entered the prayer with him and prayed, and he did not stop. Then two girls from Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib came running and grabbed hold of his knees, and he separated them, and he did not stop.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was praying, and when I wanted to get up, I disliked to get up and pass in front of him, so I slipped away gradually.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am out hunting and I have nothing on but a shirt. May I pray in it?" He said:
"Fasten it on you, even with a thorn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When my people returned from the Prophet ﷺ, they said that he had said:
"Let the one among you who knows the most Qurʾān lead you."

He said: They called me and taught me bowing and prostration, so I would lead them in prayer. I had on a cloak that was torn open, and they would say to my father, "Will you not cover your son's backside from us?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out wearing a red garment, planted a short spear in the ground, and prayed facing it, while dogs, women, and donkeys passed behind it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away, the Anṣār said, "From us a leader, and from you a leader."

So ʿUmar came to them and said, "Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer? Which of you would be content to put himself ahead of Abū Bakr?" They said, "We seek refuge in Allah from putting ourselves ahead of Abū Bakr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her, that Abū Bakr
led the people in prayer while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the row.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you visits a people, he should not lead them in prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Riders used to pass by us and we would learn the Qurʾān from them. Then my father came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Let the one among you who knows the most Qurʾān lead you."
So my father came and said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said:
"Let the one among you who knows the most Qurʾān lead you."
They looked, and I was the one who knew the most Qurʾān among them, so I would lead them in prayer when I was eight years old.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer. She said: The Prophet ﷺ was in front of Abū Bakr, and he prayed sitting, while Abū Bakr led the people in prayer and the people were behind Abū Bakr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAlqamah,
both said: We entered upon ʿAbdullāh at midday, and he said, "There will be rulers who are distracted from the time of prayer, so pray at its proper time."
Then he stood and prayed between me and him, and said, "This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the funeral of a man from the Ansār,
and we came to the grave before the niche had been dug.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat down and we sat around him, as though birds were perched on our heads.
In his hand was a stick with which he was scratching the ground.
Then he raised his head and said:
"Seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the grave."
Two or three times. (In the narration of Jarīr there is an addition here:) And he said:
"Indeed, he hears the sound of their sandals when they turn away and leave, when it is said to him:
'O you, who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your prophet?'"
Hannād said: He said:
"Two angels come to him, make him sit up, and say to him:
'Who is your Lord?' He says: 'My Lord is Allah.' They say to him:
'What is your religion?' He says: 'My religion is Islam.' They say to him:
'What do you say about this man who was sent among you?' He said: He says:
'He is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.' They say:
'And how do you know?' He says:
'I read the Book of Allah, believed in it, and held it to be true.'"
In the narration of Jarīr there is an addition:
"That is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: {Allah keeps firm those who believe}." [to the end of] the verse.
Then the two narrators agree. He said:
"Then a caller calls from the heaven:
'My servant has spoken the truth, so spread out a bed for him from Paradise,
open for him a door to Paradise, and clothe him from Paradise.'" He said:
"Then some of its breeze and fragrance comes to him." He said:
"And his grave is made spacious for him as far as his sight reaches." He said: "And as for the disbeliever..."
and he mentioned his death. He said:
"His soul is returned to his body, and two angels come to him, make him sit up, and say:
'Who is your Lord?' He says:
'Hah, hah, hah, I do not know.' They say to him:
'What is your religion?' He says:
'Hah, hah, I do not know.' They say:
'What do you say about this man who was sent among you?' He says:
'Hah, hah, I do not know.'
Then a caller calls from the heaven:
'He has lied, so spread out a bed for him from the Fire, clothe him from the Fire,
and open for him a door to the Fire.'" He said:
"Then some of its heat and scorching wind comes to him." He said:
"And his grave is constricted upon him until his ribs are pressed together."
In the narration of Jarīr there is an addition. He said:
"Then there is appointed over him one who is blind and mute, with a mace of iron,
such that if a mountain were struck with it, it would become dust." He said:
"He strikes him with it a blow that is heard by everything between the east and the west except the two weighty creations [jinn and mankind], and he becomes dust." He said:
"Then the soul is returned to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Forty years ago, from Abū Hurayrah,

who said: The Prophet ﷺ said. (Transition to another chain:) And Wahb ibn Baqiyyah narrated to us: Khālid informed us from Dāwūd, meaning Ibn Abī Hind, and this is his wording, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Khayrah, from al-Ḥasan, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There will certainly come a time upon people when no one will remain who has not consumed usury, and whoever does not consume it will be touched by its vapor."
Ibn ʿĪsā said:
"He will be touched by its dust."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I knew that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted on some of the days on which he used to fast, so I watched for the time of his breaking the fast with a nabīdh I had made in gourds. When evening came, I came to him carrying it, and said: O Messenger of Allah, I knew that you were fasting on this day, so I waited for the time of your breaking the fast with this nabīdh. He said:
"Bring it near me, Abū Hurayrah."
So I raised it to him, and it was fizzing. He said:
"Take this and strike the wall with it, for this is the drink of one who does not believe in Allah and the Last Day."
And among what they used as evidence was the action of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye, a venomous sting, or blood [that keeps flowing]."
Al-ʿAbbās did not mention the evil eye, and this is the wording of Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said: The Prophet ﷺ delivered a sermon on the day of the conquest of Makkah and said:

"Beware! The one slain by mistake, resembling intentional killing, with a whip, a staff, or a stone, the blood money is one hundred camels, among them forty pregnant ones, from those in their fifth year up to those in their ninth year."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever kills by mistake, his blood money is one hundred camels: thirty bint makhāḍ, thirty bint labūn, thirty ḥiqqah, and ten male ibn labūn."

He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to assess it for the people of the towns at four hundred dinars or its equivalent in silver, and he would assess it for the owners of camels: when camels became expensive he raised its value, and when they became cheap he lowered its value, according to the times. So its value in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ranged between four hundred dinars and eight hundred dinars, or their equivalent in silver.

He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also ruled that those whose blood money was in cattle, the people of cattle pay two hundred cows, and those whose blood money was in sheep pay two thousand sheep. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the blood money is inherited among the heirs of the slain person according to their shares, and whatever remains goes to the male paternal relatives. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the blood money for a woman is to be paid by her male paternal relatives, whoever they may be, and they inherit nothing from it except what remains after her heirs. If she is killed, her blood money is shared among her heirs, and they may put her killer to death.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He slept in the mosque, using his cloak as a pillow, and it was taken from beneath his head. He brought the thief to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ ordered that his hand be cut off. Ṣafwān said: O Messenger of Allah, I did not want this; my cloak is charity for him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Why did you not do that before you brought him to me?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A prescribed punishment carried out on the earth is better for the people of the earth than their being given rain for forty mornings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Carrying out one of the prescribed punishments of Allah is better than forty nights of rain in the lands of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
from Muzaynah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about an animal stolen from the mountain pasture? He said:

"It must be returned along with its like, and a deterrent punishment. There is no cutting of the hand for any livestock except what the pen has sheltered; if its value reaches the price of a shield, then the hand is cut off, and if it does not reach the price of a shield, then there is a fine of twice its value and lashes as a deterrent."
He said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about fruit hanging on the tree? He said:

"It must be returned along with its like, and a deterrent punishment. There is no cutting of the hand for any hanging fruit except what the drying place has sheltered; what is taken from the drying place, if its value reaches the price of a shield, then the hand is cut off, and if it does not reach the price of a shield, then there is a fine of twice its value and lashes as a deterrent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when a man came, with extremely white clothes and extremely black hair, with no sign of travel on him, and none of us knew him.
He sat down before the Prophet ﷺ, rested his knees against his knees, and placed his hands on his thighs.
Then he said: O Muhammad, what is Islam? He said:

"It is to testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah, to establish prayer, to give zakāh, to fast Ramadan, and to perform Hajj to the House." He said: You have spoken truly.
We were amazed at him, asking him and then confirming the answer.
Then he said: O Muhammad, what is faith? He said:
"That you believe in Allah, His angels, His messengers, His books, the Last Day, and in the divine decree, its good and its evil." He said: You have spoken truly.
We were amazed at him, asking him and then confirming the answer.
Then he said: O Muhammad, what is excellence (iḥsān)? He said:
"That you worship Allah as if you see Him, for even if you do not see Him, He sees you."
He said: Then when is the Hour? He said:
"The one asked about it knows no more than the one asking."
He said: Then what are its signs? He said:
"That the slave woman gives birth to her mistress."
Wakīʿ said: meaning that non-Arabs will give birth to Arabs.
"And that you see barefoot, unclothed, destitute shepherds competing in constructing tall buildings."
He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ met me after three days and said:
"Do you know who the man was?"
I said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said:
"That was Jibrīl. He came to teach you the fundamentals of your religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ: The disbelievers of Quraysh wrote to Ibn Ubayy and those with him who worshipped idols from the Aws and the Khazraj, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Medina before the Battle of Badr: "You have given refuge to our man. We swear by Allah that you must either fight him or expel him, or else we will march against you all together until we kill your fighters and take your women as lawful."
When this reached ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy and those of the idol-worshippers with him, they gathered to fight the Prophet ﷺ. When that reached the Prophet ﷺ, he met them and said:

"The threat of Quraysh has reached you in full measure. Quraysh would not plot against you more than what you intend to plot against yourselves, for you want to fight your own sons and your own brothers."

When they heard that from the Prophet ﷺ, they dispersed. This reached the disbelievers of Quraysh, so after the Battle of Badr the disbelievers of Quraysh wrote to the Jews: "You are the people of arms and fortresses, and you must fight our man or else we will do such and such to you, and nothing will stand between us and the anklets of your women." When their letter reached the Prophet ﷺ, Banū al-Naḍīr resolved on treachery and sent to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Come out to us with thirty of your Companions, and thirty of our rabbis will come out, so that we meet at a midway place and they hear from you.

If they believe you and have faith in you, we will believe in you." He then related their news. The next morning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to them with his battalions and besieged them. He said to them:
"By Allah, you will not be safe with me unless you make a covenant with me."

They refused to give him a covenant, so he fought them that day. Then the next morning he went with the battalions against Banū Qurayẓah and left Banū al-Naḍīr, and called them to make a covenant with him, and they made a covenant with him. He left them and the next morning went against Banū al-Naḍīr with the battalions and fought them until they agreed to leave. Banū al-Naḍīr went into exile and carried off whatever their camels could bear of their goods, and the doors and timber of their houses. The date palms of Banū al-Naḍīr belonged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alone; Allah gave them to him and singled him out for them, and said: {And whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not press forward against it with horses or camels}, meaning without fighting. The Prophet ﷺ gave most of it to the Emigrants and divided it among them, and he gave a share of it to two men of the Anṣār who were in need; he gave no one else of the Anṣār a share. What remained of it was the charity (ṣadaqah) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that is in the hands of the descendants of Fāṭimah, may Allah be pleased with her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I think it was from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar:

That the Prophet ﷺ fought the people of Khaybar and overcame them over the date palms and the land, and drove them into their fortress. They made peace with him on the terms that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have the gold, the silver and the armor, and that they would have what their camels could carry, on condition that they not conceal or hide anything; if they did, they would have no protection and no covenant. But they hid a skin containing wealth belonging to Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab, who had been killed before Khaybar; he had carried it with him on the day of Banū al-Naḍīr, when Banū al-Naḍīr were exiled, and it held their jewelry. The Prophet ﷺ said to Saʿyah:
"Where is the skin of Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab?"
He said: "The wars and expenses have used it up."

Then they found the skin. Ibn Abī al-Ḥuqayq was killed, and their women and children were taken captive. He wanted to expel them, but they said: "Muḥammad, leave us to work this land, and we will have half, for as long as you wish, and you will have half."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give each of his wives eighty wasqs of dates and twenty wasqs of barley.
label: machine translation

segments_en: O people, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dealt with the Jews of Khaybar on the condition that we could expel them whenever we wished. So whoever has property there should join it, for I am going to expel the Jews. Then he expelled them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raided Khaybar and we took it by force, and he gathered the captives.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided Khaybar into two halves: one half for his needs and emergencies, and one half among the Muslims, which he divided among them into eighteen shares.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man was struck in his chest or in his throat by an arrow and died, so he was wrapped in his clothes just as he was. He said: And we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The martyrs of Uhud were not washed; they were buried in their blood, and the funeral prayer was not performed over them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by Ḥamzah, whose body had been mutilated, and he did not pray over any of the martyrs other than him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When they wanted to wash the Prophet ﷺ, they said: "By Allah, we do not know whether we should strip the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of his clothes as we strip our dead, or wash him while he is in his clothes." When they disagreed, Allah cast sleep upon them until there was not a man among them but that his chin was on his chest. Then someone spoke to them from a corner of the house, and they did not know who he was: "Wash the Prophet ﷺ while he is in his clothes." So they stood to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and washed him while he was in his shirt, pouring water over the shirt and rubbing him with the shirt rather than with their hands. ʿĀʾishah used to say: "If I could go back in my affair what I have left behind, no one would have washed him except his wives."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We combed her hair into three braids.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to take the method of washing the dead from Umm ʿAṭiyyah:
[the body] was washed twice with lote-tree leaves, and the third time with water and camphor.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you dies and finds [the means], let him be shrouded in a Ḥibarah garment."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was shrouded in three white Yemeni garments, among which there was no shirt and no turban.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Do not be extravagant for me in the shroud, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Do not be extravagant in the shroud, for it is quickly taken away."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] from the descendants of ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd, called Dāwūd, whom Umm Ḥabībah bint Abī Sufyān, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, had given birth to, [narrated] from Laylā bint Qānif ath-Thaqafiyyah, who said: I was among those who washed Umm Kulthūm, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, at her death. The first thing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave us was the waist wrapper, then the shirt, then the head covering, then the large wrap, and then she was enfolded in the other garment. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting at the door with her shroud, handing it to us piece by piece.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of your perfumes is musk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṭalḥah ibn al-Barāʾ
fell ill, so the Prophet ﷺ came to visit him and said:
"I do not see but that death has befallen Ṭalḥah. So inform me of it, and hasten, for it is not fitting that the body of a Muslim be kept among his family."
label: machine translation

segments_en: People saw a fire in the graveyard and went to it, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the grave, saying: "Hand me your companion."
And it was the man who used to raise his voice in remembrance [of Allah].
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no Muslim who dies and has forty men stand over his funeral, none of whom associate anything with Allah, except that their intercession for him will be accepted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the people of Madinah, from his father,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"A funeral procession is not to be followed with a voice or with fire." Hārūn added:
"And one should not walk in front of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A mount was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was with a funeral procession, but he refused to ride it. When he left, a mount was brought and he rode it. He was asked about it, and he said:
"The angels were walking, so I did not want to ride while they walked. When they left, I rode."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was at the funeral of ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ, and we were walking at a slow pace. Abū Bakrah caught up with us, raised his whip, and said: "I have seen us with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we used to walk at a brisk pace."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever gives up lying while it is false [i.e., a falsehood], a house will be built for him on the outskirts of Paradise; whoever gives up disputation while he is in the right, a house will be built for him in the middle of it; and whoever makes his character good, a house will be built for him in the highest part of it."
This hadith is ḥasan; we do not know it except through the narration of Salamah ibn Wardān from Anas ibn Mālik.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about what most often admits people into Paradise, and he said:
"Fear of Allah and good character."
And he was asked about what most often admits people into the Fire, and he said: "The mouth and the private part."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
