"Whoever visits a sick person or visits a brother of his for the sake of Allah, a caller calls out: 'May you be well, may your walking be blessed, and may you take for yourself a dwelling in Paradise.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Modesty is part of faith, and faith is in Paradise; obscene speech is part of harshness, and harshness is in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When any of the family of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was afflicted with fever, he would order that a soup be made, then order them and they would sip it, and he would say:
"It strengthens the heart of the grieving and relieves the heart of the sick, just as one of you wipes the dirt from her face with water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not force your sick to eat, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, feeds them and gives them drink."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ related about the night
in which he was taken on the Night Journey, that he did not pass by any gathering of the angels except that they commanded him: "Order your Ummah to practice cupping."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Salmā, who used to serve the Prophet ﷺ, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never had a sore or a wound except that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to put henna on it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has himself cauterized or seeks a ruqyah [for himself], has cleared himself of reliance [on Allah]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is Abū Ḥātim ibn ʿĀmir, from ʿUbayd ibn Rifāʿah az-Zuraqī,
that Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays
said: "O Messenger of Allah, the evil eye afflicts the children of Jaʿfar quickly; may I seek ruqyah for them?" He said:
"Yes, for if anything were to outstrip the decree, the evil eye would outstrip it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us out on an expedition, and we stopped at a people and asked them for hospitality, but they did not host us. Then their chief was stung, and they came to us and said: "Is there anyone among you who can perform ruqyah for a scorpion sting?" I said: "Yes, I can, but I will not perform ruqyah for him until you give us sheep."
They said: "We will give you thirty sheep."
We accepted, and I recited over him "Al-Ḥamdu lillāh" [Sūrat al-Fātiḥah] seven times, and he was cured, and we took the sheep.
He said: Something about it troubled us, so we said: "Do not hurry until you come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said: When we came to him, I told him what I had done, and he said:
"How did you know that it is a ruqyah? Take the sheep and assign a share for me along with you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of ruqyahs we use, medicine with which we treat ourselves, and protections we seek; do they repel anything of Allah's decree?" He said:
"They are part of Allah's decree."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to teach them to say, for fever and for all pains:
"In the name of Allah, the Great. I seek refuge in Allah, the Magnificent, from the evil of every swelling vein and from the evil of the heat of the Fire."
Abū ʿĀmir said: I differ from the people in this; I say "yaʿār."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"What did you use to loosen your bowels?"
I said: "Shubrum." He said: "Hot, sharp."
Then I used senna to loosen my bowels, and he said:
"If anything could cure death, it would be senna; senna is a cure from death."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you visit a sick person, give him hope regarding his life span, for that does not change anything, and it pleases the sick person's heart."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he visited a sick man who had a fever, and Abū Hurayrah was with him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Receive glad tidings, for Allah says: 'It is My fire which I inflict upon My believing servant in this world so that it will be his share of the Fire in the Hereafter.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Umm Salamah, "O Mother of the Believers, what was the supplication the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made most often when he was with you?" She said: "His most frequent supplication was:
'O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.'"
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, why do you make this supplication so often: 'O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion'?" He said:

"O Umm Salamah, there is no human being except that his heart is between two of the fingers of Allah; so whomever He wills He makes steadfast, and whomever He wills He lets deviate." Then Muʿādh recited:

"Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us." He said: There are narrations on this topic from ʿĀʾishah, al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān, Anas, Jābir, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, and Nuʿaym ibn Hammār.
He said: This is a good (ḥasan) hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Khālid ibn al-Walīd al-Makhzūmī complained to the Prophet ﷺ, saying, "O Messenger of Allah, I cannot sleep at night because of sleeplessness." The Prophet ﷺ said:

"When you go to your bed, say: 'O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and all that they cover, Lord of the earths and all that they carry, and Lord of the devils and all whom they lead astray: be a protector for me from the evil of all Your creation together, lest any of them transgress against me or wrong me. Mighty is Your protection, and majestic is Your praise, and there is no god besides You; there is no god but You.'"
He said: This is a hadith whose chain is not strong.
Al-Ḥakam ibn Ẓuhayr's narrations were abandoned by some of the scholars of hadith, and this hadith is also narrated from the Prophet ﷺ as a mursal report through another route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My brother Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from al-Raqāshī,
from Anas ibn Mālik,
who said: When a matter distressed the Prophet ﷺ, he would say:
"O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining, in Your mercy I seek relief."
And with this chain he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Persist in saying: 'O Possessor of Majesty and Honor.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Persist in saying: 'O Possessor of Majesty and Honor.'"
He said: This is a gharīb hadith and is not preserved (maḥfūẓ).

It is only narrated from Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Ḥumayd, from al-Ḥasan, from the Prophet ﷺ, and this is more authentic. Muʾammal made an error in it, saying: from Ḥammād, from Ḥumayd, from Anas, and he is not supported in this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever goes to his bed in a state of purity, remembering Allah until drowsiness overtakes him, then does not turn over at any hour of the night asking Allah for anything of the good of this world and the Hereafter, except that Allah gives it to him."
He said: This is a good and gharīb hadith.
This has also been narrated from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Abū Ẓabyah, from ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ heard a man supplicating, saying, "O Allah, I ask You for the completion of Your favor." So he said:
"What is the completion of the favor?"
He said, "A supplication I made, hoping good by it." He said:
"Indeed, part of the completion of the favor is entering Paradise and being saved from the Fire."
And he heard a man saying, "O Possessor of Majesty and Honor," so he said:
"Your prayer has been answered, so ask."
And the Prophet ﷺ heard a man saying, "O Allah, I ask You for patience." So he said:
"You have asked Allah for trial; so ask Him for well-being."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-ʿAbbās came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as though he had heard something [said], so the Prophet ﷺ stood on the pulpit and said, "Who am I?" They said, "You are the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you." He said, "I am Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. Indeed Allah created the creation and placed me in the best of them as a group; then He made them two groups and placed me in the better of them as a group; then He made them tribes and placed me in the best of them as a tribe; then He made them households and placed me in the best of them as a household, and the best of them in lineage." Abū ʿĪsā said: This is a good (ḥasan) hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a tree with dry leaves, and he struck it with his staff so that the leaves scattered. Then he said:
"Indeed, 'Praise be to Allah,' 'Glory be to Allah,' 'There is no god but Allah,' and 'Allah is the Greatest' cause the sins of a servant to fall away just as the leaves of this tree fall."
He said: This is a gharīb hadith.
We do not know of al-Aʿmash having heard directly from Anas, except that he saw him and looked at him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, some gift, and ʿUmar would say, "Give it to someone who needs it more than I do, O Messenger of Allah."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him,

"Take it, then keep it as your property or give it away in charity. And whatever of this wealth comes to you when you are not eagerly desiring it and not asking for it, take it; and whatever does not come in that way, do not let your soul pursue it."
Sālim said: "For that reason Ibn ʿUmar would never ask anyone for anything, and would never refuse anything he was given."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to us,
from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father,
who said: I heard ʿUmar

say: "I gave a horse for the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, but the one who had it neglected it. I wanted to buy it from him, thinking he would sell it cheaply, so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and he said,
'Do not buy it, even if he gives it to you for one dirham, for the one who takes back his charity is like a dog that returns to its vomit.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: She wanted to buy Barīrah,
but they stipulated that the right of walāʾ be theirs,
so this was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "Buy her and set her free,
for walāʾ belongs only to the one who sets free."
Some meat was given as a gift to her,
and it was said to the Prophet ﷺ, "This was given in charity to Barīrah." The Prophet ﷺ said,
"It is charity for her, and a gift for us." And she was given the choice.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Her husband was a free man or a slave. Shuʿbah said: I asked ʿAbd al-Raḥmān about her husband.
He said: "I do not know whether he was free or a slave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed a man to collect charity, and when the man had finished his work he came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is for you, and this was given to me as a gift." He said to him,
"Why did you not sit in the house of your father and your mother and see whether you would be given gifts or not?"
Then in the evening, after the prayer, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, recited the testification of faith, praised Allah as He deserves, and then said, "To proceed:
What is the matter with the official whom we appoint,
and who then comes to us and says,
'This is from your work,
and this was given to me as a gift'?
Why did he not sit in the house of his father and his mother and see whether he would be given gifts or not?
By the One in whose Hand is the soul of Muḥammad, none of you will take anything from it unlawfully,
except that he will come with it on the Day of Resurrection, carrying it on his neck:
if it is a camel, it will come with a groan;
if it is a cow, it will come lowing;
and if it is a sheep, it will come bleating. I have conveyed [the message]."
Abū Ḥumayd said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hand so high that we could see the whiteness of his armpits.
Abū Ḥumayd said: "Zayd ibn Thābit also heard that from the Prophet ﷺ along with me, so ask him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said, "O Messenger of Allah, will the people return with two rewards while I return with one?" So he commanded ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr to take her to al-Tanʿīm.
She said: So he seated me behind him on a camel of his. She said: I began to lift my head covering and uncover it from my neck, and he would strike my foot with the sandal-strap of the mount.
I said to him, "Do you see anyone?" She said: Then I entered the state of iḥrām for ʿUmrah, and we came back until we reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was at al-Ḥaṣbah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Dhū al-Ḥulayfah as the place for entering iḥrām for the people of Medina,
al-Juḥfah for the people of Syria,
Qarn al-Manāzil for the people of Najd,
and Yalamlam for the people of Yemen.
These are for those people, and for those who come by them from other than their people,
who intend Hajj and ʿUmrah.
As for whoever is within them, his place for entering iḥrām is from where he lives,
and likewise, even the people of Makkah enter iḥrām from Makkah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Tonight someone came to me from my Lord, while I was at al-ʿAqīq, [saying]: Pray in this blessed valley, and say: ʿUmrah and Hajj."
And Hārūn ibn Ismāʿīl said: ʿAlī narrated to us: "ʿUmrah within Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "You have made usurious sales lawful."
Marwān said, "I did not do that."
Abū Hurayrah said, "You have made the sale of written receipts lawful, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of foodstuff until it has been fully received."
He said: So Marwān addressed the people and forbade selling them.
Sulaymān said: Then I saw guards taking them from the hands of the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not buy fruit until its goodness appears and the blight has gone from it." He said: Its goodness appearing means its turning red and yellow.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of muzābanah and muḥāqalah. Muzābanah is that the fruit of the palm tree is sold for dried dates, and muḥāqalah is that standing crops are sold for wheat, and that land is rented for wheat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted a concession regarding ʿarāyā, that they may be sold for their estimated amount by measure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the people of his house [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade.
Then he mentioned it like the hadith of Sulaymān ibn Bilāl from Yaḥyā, except that Isḥāq and Ibn al-Muthannā put "zabn" in place of "ribā," while Ibn Abī ʿUmar said "ribā."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade renting out land, selling it for [several] years, and selling fruit until it is good.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade taking payment or a share for land.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade mukhābarah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever has land, let him give it as a gift or lend it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade selling barren land for two or three years.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We saw no harm in khabar until the year before last, when Rāfiʿ claimed that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ had forbidden it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar said, "Rāfiʿ has deprived us of the benefit of our land."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to Rāfiʿ, and he mentioned this hadith from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ we used to practice muḥāqalah on land, renting it out for a third, a quarter, or a specified amount of grain. One day a man from among my paternal uncles came to us and said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has forbidden us something that was beneficial to us, but obedience to Allah and His Messenger is more beneficial to us. He forbade us to practice muḥāqalah on land by renting it out for a third, a quarter, or a specified amount of grain. He commanded the owner of the land to cultivate it himself or have it cultivated, and he disliked renting it out and anything besides that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ with this [wording], and he did not mention [it] from his uncle Ẓuhayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿAbdullāh ibn Maʿqil about sharecropping,
and he said, "Thābit ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk informed me
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade sharecropping."
In the narration of Ibn Abī Shaybah: "He forbade it."
And he said: I asked Ibn Maʿqil.
And he did not name ʿAbdullāh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to practice mukhābarah. ʿAmr said: I said to him, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, if only you would give up this mukhābarah, for they claim that the Prophet ﷺ forbade mukhābarah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever has land, it is better for him to give it to his brother as a gift."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no Muslim who plants a plant, except that what is eaten from it is charity for him, what is stolen from it is charity for him, what wild animals eat from it is charity for him, and what birds eat is charity for him, and no one diminishes it except that it is charity for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr added in his narration, from ʿAmmār,
and Abū Kurayb in his narration, from Abū Muʿāwiyah,
and they both said: from Umm Mubashshir.
In the narration of Ibn Fuḍayl: from a woman,
of Zayd ibn Ḥārithah. And in the narration of Isḥāq from Abū Muʿāwiyah,
he said: Sometimes he said, "from Umm Mubashshir, from the Prophet ﷺ."
And sometimes he did not say [it]. All of them said, "from the Prophet ﷺ," similar to the hadith of ʿAṭāʾ, Abū al-Zubayr, and ʿAmr ibn Dīnār.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"If Allah does not cause it to bear fruit, then by what right would one of you take his brother's property?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the descendants of Saʿd, they said: Saʿd fell ill in Makkah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to visit him.
Similar to the hadith of al-Thaqafī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my mother died suddenly and did not make a bequest. I think that had she been able to speak, she would have given charity. Will she have a reward if I give charity on her behalf?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had become enamored of an opinion among the opinions of the Khawārij, so we set out in a sizeable band intending to perform Hajj and then to rise up against the people. He said: We passed through Medina, and there was Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh, sitting beside a pillar, narrating to the people from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He mentioned the Jahannamites [those brought out of the Fire]. I said to him: O Companion of the Messenger of Allah, what is this that you are narrating, when Allah says: "Whoever You admit to the Fire, You have disgraced him," and: "Every time they want to come out of it, they are returned to it"? What then is this that you are saying? He said: Do you recite the Qur'an? I said: Yes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Four will be brought out of the Fire and presented before Allah. One of them will turn around and say: 'My Lord, since You have brought me out of it, do not return me to it.'
So Allah will save him from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A large bowl of tharīd and meat was placed before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He took the foreleg, which was the part of the sheep he liked best, and took a bite from it, and said:
"I am the master of the people on the Day of Resurrection."
Then he took another bite and said:
"I am the master of the people on the Day of Resurrection."
When he saw that his Companions were not asking him, he said:
"Will you not ask how?"
They said: How, O Messenger of Allah? He said:
"The people will stand before the Lord of the worlds."
He then related the hadith in the same sense as the hadith of Abū Ḥayyān from Abū Zurʿah, and added in the story of Ibrāhīm: He mentioned his words about the star, "This is my Lord,"
and his words to their gods, "Rather, this, the biggest of them, did it,"
and his words, "I am sick." He said:

"By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the distance between the two leaves of the gates of Paradise, from one doorpost to the other, is like the distance between Mecca and Hajar, or Hajar and Mecca."
He said: I do not know which of the two he said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will gather the people, and the believers will stand until Paradise is brought near to them. They will come to Adam and say: 'O our father, ask for Paradise to be opened for us.'

He will say: 'Was it not the sin of your father Adam that expelled you from Paradise? I am not the one for this. Go to my son Ibrāhīm, the Friend of Allah.' He said: Ibrāhīm will say: 'I am not the one for this. I was only a friend from behind, from behind. Go to Mūsā ﷺ, to whom Allah spoke directly.'
So they will come to Mūsā ﷺ and he will say: 'I am not the one for this. Go to ʿĪsā, the Word of Allah and His Spirit.'
ʿĪsā ﷺ will say: 'I am not the one for this.'

Then they will come to Muhammad ﷺ, and he will stand and be given permission. Trustworthiness and kinship will be sent, and they will stand on the two sides of the Bridge, right and left. The first of you will pass like lightning."
He said: I said: May my father and mother be ransomed for you, what is like the passing of lightning? He said:

"Have you not seen lightning, how it passes and returns in the blink of an eye? Then like the wind, then like a bird, and like the swift running of men; their deeds will carry them along, while your Prophet stands on the Bridge saying: 'My Lord, keep them safe, keep them safe,' until the deeds of the servants fall short, until a man comes who cannot move except by crawling. He said: On the two sides of the Bridge are hooks hanging, commanded to seize whomever they are commanded to seize. Some will be scratched but saved, and some will be piled into the Fire."
By the One in whose hand is the soul of Abū Hurayrah, the bottom of Jahannam is seventy autumns deep.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I will be the first of the people to intercede for entry into Paradise, and I am the one among the prophets with the greatest number of followers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I am the one among the prophets with the most followers on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to knock on the gate of Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas ibn Mālik said: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"I will be the first intercessor for Paradise. No prophet among the prophets was believed as much as I have been believed, and among the prophets there is one who was believed by only a single man from his nation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I will come to the gate of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection and ask for it to be opened. The keeper will say: 'Who are you?' I will say: 'Muhammad.'
He will say: 'It is for you that I was commanded; I am not to open for anyone before you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Every deed of the son of Adam is his own, except fasting; it is for Me, and I [Myself] reward it.' Fasting is a shield. So when it is the day of fasting for any of you, let him not engage in obscene talk on that day, nor raise his voice in quarrel. If anyone insults him or fights him, let him say: 'I am a person fasting.'

By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, the odor from the mouth of the fasting person is better with Allah on the Day of Resurrection than the fragrance of musk. And the fasting person has two joys which he rejoices in: when he breaks his fast he rejoices in his breaking of the fast, and when he meets his Lord he rejoices in his fasting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said, or he said: Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ said: "Fast when you see it [the crescent], and break your fast when you see it,
and if it is obscured from you, then complete the count of Shaʿbān as thirty [days]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: None of you should anticipate Ramadan by fasting a day or two,
unless it is a man who [habitually] fasts a certain fast of his; then let him fast that day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Qāsim ibn Muhammad [narrated] from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that Bilāl
used to call the adhān at night, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktūm calls the adhān,
for he does not call the adhān until the dawn has risen."
Al-Qāsim said: There was no [time] between their two calls except that one would go up and the other would come down.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet ﷺ forbade continuous fasting [without breaking it at night]. They said: "But you fast continuously." He said:
"I am not like you; I am fed and given drink."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent word on the morning of ʿĀshūrāʾ to the villages of the Anṣār around Madinah:
"Whoever began the morning fasting, let him complete his fast, and whoever began the morning not fasting, let him complete the rest of his day."

After that, we used to fast it, and we used to make our small children fast, if Allah willed, and we would go to the mosque and make them a toy of wool; and when one of them cried for food, we would give it to him at the time of breaking the fast.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah,
the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: The dawn would overtake the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Ramadan while he was in a state of janābah, not from a wet dream, and he would bathe and fast.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from ʿAbd Rabbihi ibn Saʿīd, from Abū
Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, from ʿĀʾishah

and Umm Salamah, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, that they both said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would find the morning upon him in a state of janābah from intercourse, not from a wet dream, in Ramadan, and then he would fast.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever forgets while he is fasting, and eats or drinks, let him complete his fast, for it is only Allah who fed him and gave him drink."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the mosque in Ramadan and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am ruined, I am ruined!"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him: "What is the matter with him?"
He said: "I had relations with my wife." He said: "Give charity."
He said: "By Allah, O Prophet of Allah, I have nothing and I am not able to." He said: "Sit down."
So he sat down, and while he was like that, a man came driving a donkey carrying food, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Where is the one who was ruined just now?"
The man stood up, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Give this in charity."
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, to someone other than us? By Allah, we are hungry; we have nothing." He said: "Then eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I am ruined." He said: "What is that?"
He said: "I had relations with my wife in Ramadan." He said: "Can you find a slave to free?" He said: "No." He said:
"Are you able to fast two consecutive months?" He said: "No." He said:
"Are you able to feed sixty poor people?" He said: "No."
He said: Then a man from the Anṣār came with an ʿaraq, and the ʿaraq is a basket containing dates. He said: "Take this and give it in charity."

He said: "To someone poorer than us, O Messenger of Allah? By the One Who sent you with the truth, there is no household between its two lava plains more in need than us." Then he said: "Go, and feed it to your family."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "
Say: 'O Allah, guide me and keep me on the right course.'"
And he forbade me to place the ring on this finger and this one—and Bishr pointed to the index finger and the middle finger.
He said: And ʿĀṣim said, "One of the two."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wore a gold ring for three days. When his Companions saw it, gold rings became widespread, so he threw it away, and we do not know what became of it. Then he ordered a ring of silver, and ordered that "Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah" be engraved on it. It remained on the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he died, then on the hand of Abū Bakr until he died, then on the hand of ʿUmar until he died, then on the hand of ʿUthmān for six years of his rule. When the letters became many for him, he gave it to a man of the Anṣār, who would seal with it. The Anṣārī went out to a well of ʿUthmān's and it fell in; it was searched for but not found. So he ordered a ring like it, and "Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah" was engraved on it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with Sālim when a riding party of Umm al-Banīn passed by us, with bells on them. Sālim narrated to Nāfiʿ from his father that the Prophet ﷺ said: "
The angels do not accompany a riding party that has a bell with them."
How many bells do you see with these people?
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he saw me in poor appearance. The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Do you have any property?"
I said: Yes, Allah has given me every kind of wealth. He said: "
When Allah has given you wealth, let the effect of it be seen on you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade qazaʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbidding qazaʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade qazaʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He had thick hair down to the shoulders, so he asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he commanded him to take good care of it and to comb it every day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Quḥāfah was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and his head and beard were as white as thaghāmah. The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Change this, or dye it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: O people, the Prophet ﷺ forbade you from falsehood (zūr).
He said: And he brought a piece of black cloth and threw it before them, and said: It is this—a woman puts it on her head, then wraps her head-cover over it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade zūr, and zūr is when a woman wraps something around her head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the woman who adds hair extensions.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When perfume was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, he would not refuse it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a ring and wore it. He said: "
This has distracted me from you since today: one glance at it and one glance at you." Then he threw it away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar
went out and saw a silk brocade garment being sold in the market. He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, buy this and wear it on Friday and when delegations come to you.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Only one who has no share [in the Hereafter] wears this."

Then three garments of that sort were brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He gave one garment to ʿUmar, one to ʿAlī, and one to Usāmah. ʿUmar came to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, you said about it what you said, then you sent it to me? He said: "
Sell it and meet your need with it, or cut it up into head-covers for your women."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman came to me asking for a ruling, and I said to her: This is Ibn ʿUmar.
So she followed him asking, and I followed her to hear what he would say.
She said: Give me a ruling about silk.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to do seven things and forbade us seven things. He forbade us gold rings, silver vessels, saddle-cushions of silk (mayāthir), qasī garments, istabraq, dībāj, and silk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He did not permit dībāj except for the width of four fingers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to the Prophet ﷺ wearing two garments dyed with safflower, and the Prophet ﷺ became angry and said: "
Go and throw them off."
He said: Where, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "In the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not look at the one who lets his garment hang down below the ankles."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ mentioned what he mentioned about the lower garment, Umm Salamah said: What about women? He said: "They should lower it a hand-span."
She said: Then their feet would show. He said: "
Then a forearm's length, and they should not add to that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ wearing a black ḥurqāniyyah turban.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he said: Abū Salamah said, "Abū Qatādah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
'Whoever has seen me has seen the truth.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar would sometimes say, "from Ibn ʿAbbās," and sometimes he would say, "from Abū Hurayrah," that a man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "I saw a cloud of shade last night," with a meaning similar to their narrations.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He narrates it, saying: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Whoever sees something in his ruler that he dislikes, let him be patient,
for there is no one who separates from the community by even a handspan and then dies, except that he dies a death of ignorance (jāhiliyyah)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We entered upon ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit while he was ill, and we said, "May Allah restore your well-being. Narrate to us
a hadith by which Allah will bring benefit, which you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called us and we pledged allegiance to him, and among what he took from us was that we pledged to hear and obey, in our energy and in our reluctance, in our hardship and in our ease, and even when others are given preference over us, and that we would not contest the matter with those entitled to it. He said,
"Unless you see clear disbelief for which you have a proof from Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mūsā al-Ashʿarī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said. And [in another chain] al-Qāsim ibn Zakariyyāʾ narrated to me:
Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from Sulaymān, from Shaqīq,
who said: I was sitting with ʿAbdullāh and Abū Mūsā while they were conversing, and they said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, [and he gave] a narration like the hadith of Wakīʿ and Ibn Numayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to Anas ibn Mālik and complained to him about what we were suffering from al-Ḥajjāj. He said, "Be patient,
for no time comes upon you except that the one after it is worse than it,
until you meet your Lord."
I heard this from your Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"None of you should point a weapon at his brother, for you do not know: perhaps Satan may cause it to slip from his hand, and he will fall into a pit of the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"When Allah sends down a punishment upon a people,
it strikes whoever is among them;
then they are resurrected according to their deeds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, informed me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The Hour will not come until the buttocks of the women of Daws sway around Dhū al-Khalaṣah."
Dhū al-Khalaṣah was the idol of Daws, which they used to worship in the Time of Ignorance.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ together with two men from my cousins. One of the two men said, "O Messenger of Allah, appoint us over some of what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has entrusted to you."
The other said the same. Then he said,
"By Allah, we do not appoint to this work anyone who asks for it, nor anyone who is eager for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbaydullāh ibn Ziyād visited Maʿqil ibn Yasār al-Muzanī during the illness in which he died.

Maʿqil said, "I am going to narrate to you a hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; had I known that I would have [more] life, I would not have narrated it to you. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say,
'There is no servant whom Allah places in charge of subjects, who dies on the day he dies while being deceitful toward his subjects, except that Allah forbids Paradise to him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qays ibn Saʿd was to the Prophet ﷺ in the position of the chief of the guard to the ruler.
The Anṣārī said: meaning, in regard to what concerned his affairs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Numayr [narrated] that Ḥuwayṭib ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā
informed him that ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Saʿdī informed him that he
came to ʿUmar during his caliphate, and ʿUmar said to him, "Was I not told that you take charge of some of the people's work,
and when you are given your payment you dislike it?" I said, "Yes."
ʿUmar said, "What do you intend by that?" I said, "I have horses and slaves, and I am well off,
and I want my payment to be charity for the Muslims."
ʿUmar said, "Do not do so, for I once wanted what you want, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would give me a gift and I would say, 'Give it to someone who needs it more than I do.'
Until once he gave me some money and I said, 'Give it to someone who needs it more than I do.' The Prophet ﷺ said,
'Take it, then make it your own wealth and give it in charity.
Whatever comes to you of this wealth while you are not eagerly desiring it and not asking for it, take it;
and if not, do not let your soul follow after it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, direct me to an action which, if I do it, I will enter Paradise." He said:
"Worship Allah, associating nothing with Him; establish the obligatory prayer; pay the obligatory zakāh; and fast Ramadan."
The man said, "By the One in whose hand is my soul, I will never add anything to this, nor will I take anything away from it."
When he turned to leave, the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever would be pleased to look at a man of the people of Paradise, let him look at this man."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Camels will come to their owner in the best condition they have ever been, if he did not give what is due on them; they will trample him with their hooves. And sheep and goats will come to their owner in the best condition they have ever been, if he did not give what is due on them; they will trample him with their hooves and gore him with their horns." He said: "And part of what is due on them is that they be milked at the water. Beware! Let none of you come on the Day of Resurrection carrying on his neck a camel that groans, and he says, 'O Muhammad!'
And I will say, 'I have no power to do anything for you; I have conveyed [the message].'
Beware! Let none of you come on the Day of Resurrection carrying on his neck a sheep that bleats, and he says, 'O Muhammad!'

And I will say, 'I have no power to do anything for you; I have conveyed [the message].'" He said: "And the hoarded wealth of one of them on the Day of Resurrection will be a bald-headed snake from which its owner flees, while it pursues him [saying], 'I am your treasure.' It will keep on until it makes him swallow his finger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, and a Bedouin caught up with him and said to him, "What about the saying of Allah: 'And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah'?" Ibn ʿUmar said to him, "Whoever hoards it and does not pay its zakāh, woe to him. This was only before zakāh was revealed; when it was revealed, Allah made it a purification for wealth."
Then he turned and said, "I would not care if I had the mountain of Uḥud in gold, whose amount I knew, and I paid zakāh on it and used it in obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The Hour will not be established until wealth becomes abundant among you and overflows,
until the owner of wealth is concerned about who will accept his charity,
and until he offers it, and the one to whom he offers it says, 'I have no need of it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A time will certainly come upon people when a man will go around with charity of gold and then find no one to take it from him, and a single man will be seen followed by forty women seeking refuge with him, because of the fewness of men and the abundance of women."
And in the narration of Ibn Barrād: "and you will see the man."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her, that some
of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Which of us will join you soonest?" He said, "The one with the longest hand."
So they took a reed and measured their hands,
and Sawdah had the longest hand of them.
Afterwards we realized that the length of her hand was [her giving of] charity,
and she was the soonest of us to join him, and she loved charity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām, may Allah be pleased with him, had freed one hundred slaves in the Jāhiliyyah,
and had given one hundred camels [for riding in Allah's cause],
and when he accepted Islam, he gave one hundred camels and freed one hundred slaves.
He said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I said, "O Messenger of Allah,
what do you think of things I used to do in the Jāhiliyyah,
by which I sought to draw near [to Allah],
meaning, to do good deeds?"
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You have accepted Islam with the good you did in the past."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"There is no day on which people wake up in the morning but two angels descend, and one of them says, 'O Allah, give the one who spends [in charity] a replacement,'
and the other says, 'O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A sheep from the charity was sent to me by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I sent some of it to ʿĀʾishah. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to ʿĀʾishah, he said:
"Do you have anything?" She said, "No,
except that Nusaybah sent us some of the sheep that you sent to her." He said:
"It has reached its [rightful] place."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, which supplication is best?" He said:
"Ask your Lord for well-being and safety in this world and the Hereafter."
Then he came to him on the second day and said, "O Messenger of Allah, which supplication is best?" and he told him the same. Then he came to him on the third day and he told him the same. He said:
"If you are granted well-being in this world and are granted it in the Hereafter, then you have succeeded."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan gharīb from this route. We know it only from the hadith of Salamah ibn Wardān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, if I know which night is the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), what should I say in it?" He said:
"Say: O Allah, You are Pardoning and Generous; You love to pardon, so pardon me."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of a servant as long as the death rattle has not reached his throat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:
"O Allah, cool my heart with snow, hail, and cold water. O Allah, cleanse my heart of sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, put on a new garment and said, "Praise is for Allah who has clothed me with what covers my private parts and with which I beautify myself in my life."
Then he took the garment that had worn out and gave it in charity. Then he said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'Whoever puts on a new garment and says: Praise is for Allah who has clothed me with what covers my private parts and with which I beautify myself in my life, and then takes the garment that had worn out and gives it in charity, will be under the protection of Allah, in the keeping of Allah, and under the covering of Allah, alive and dead.'"
He said: This hadith is gharīb.
It was also narrated by Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb from ʿUbaydullāh ibn Zaḥr, from ʿAlī ibn Yazīd, from al-Qāsim, from Abū Umāmah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
who was blind came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "Supplicate to Allah to cure me." He said:
"If you wish I will supplicate, and if you wish you may be patient, and that is better for you." He said, "Then supplicate."
He said: So he commanded him to perform ablution and make his ablution well, and to supplicate with this supplication:

"O Allah, I ask You and turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of mercy. O Muhammad, I have turned through you to my Lord regarding this need of mine so that it may be fulfilled for me. O Allah, accept him as an intercessor for me."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb. We know it only from this route, from the hadith of Abū Jaʿfar, who is not al-Khaṭmī. ʿUthmān ibn Ḥunayf is the brother of Sahl ibn Ḥunayf.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"O Allah, benefit me with what You have taught me, teach me what will benefit me, and increase me in knowledge. Praise is for Allah in every circumstance, and I seek refuge in Allah from the state of the people of the Fire."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan gharīb from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered Medina, everything in it was illuminated. On the day he died, everything in it became dark. We had not yet wiped the dust from our hands after burying the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when we found our hearts changed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿĀʾishah, "Which of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was most beloved to the Messenger of Allah?" She said, "Abū Bakr."
I said, "Then who?" She said, "ʿUmar."
I said, "Then who?" She said, "Then Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ."
I said, "Then who?" He said: She remained silent.
He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and al-Aʿmash,
and ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṣahbān,
and Ibn Abī Laylā, and Kathīr al-Nawwāʾ,
all of them from ʿAṭiyyah,
from Abū Saʿīd,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed the people of the highest ranks will be seen by those beneath them, as you see the rising star on the horizon of the sky. And indeed Abū Bakr and ʿUmar are among them, and they are well deserving of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: We were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when he said:
"I do not know how long I will remain among you, so follow the two after me,"
and he pointed to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and entered the mosque, with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, one on his right and the other on his left, while he held their hands, and he said:
"Thus will we be raised on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said to the Prophet ﷺ, "I performed the ṭawāf before throwing the pebbles." He said, "There is no harm."
He said, "I shaved my head before slaughtering." He said, "There is no harm."
He said, "I slaughtered before throwing the pebbles." He said, "There is no harm."
ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Rāzī said, on the authority of Ibn Khuthaym: ʿAṭāʾ informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ.
And al-Qāsim ibn Yaḥyā said: Ibn Khuthaym narrated to me, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ.
And ʿAffān said: I think it is from Wuhayb,
Ibn Khuthaym narrated to us,
from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr,
from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ.
And Ḥammād said, from Qays ibn Saʿd and ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah,
by Allah, I stay behind from the morning prayer because of so-and-so,
since he prolongs it for us."
[The narrator] said: I never saw the Prophet ﷺ more angry in an admonition than he was on that day. Then he said,
"O people,
among you are those who drive others away.
So whichever of you leads the people in prayer, let him be brief,
for among them are the elderly, the weak, and those with needs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I bear witness for the Prophet ﷺ — or ʿAṭāʾ said: I bear witness for Ibn ʿAbbās — that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and Bilāl was with him,
and he thought that the women had not heard, so he admonished them and commanded them to give charity.
So the woman would throw down her earring and her ring,
and Bilāl would collect them in the edge of his garment.
And Ismāʿīl said, from Ayyūb, from ʿAṭāʾ, and he said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: I bear witness for the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Do not lie about me, for whoever lies about me will enter the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, relating from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, who said:

"Any servant of Mine who goes out striving in the cause of Allah, seeking My pleasure, I guarantee that I will return him, if I return him, with whatever reward or spoils he has gained; and if I take his soul, I will forgive him and have mercy on him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The example of the one who strives in the cause of Allah—and Allah knows best who strives in His cause—is like that of the one who fasts, stands in prayer, is humble, and bows and prostrates."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever establishes prayer, gives zakāh, and dies without associating anything with Allah, it is a right upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to forgive him, whether he emigrated or died in the place of his birth."
We said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not inform the people of this so that they may rejoice?" He said:

"Indeed, Paradise has one hundred levels, between each two of which is like the distance between the heavens and the earth. Allah has prepared them for those who strive in His cause. Were it not that I would burden the believers, and I do not find the means to carry them, and it would not please them to stay behind me, I would not stay behind any expedition. And I would love to be killed, then brought back to life, then killed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I am a guarantor—and the guarantor is the one who takes responsibility—for whoever believes in me, submits, and emigrates: a house on the edge of Paradise and a house in the middle of Paradise. And I am a guarantor for whoever believes in me, submits, and strives in the cause of Allah: a house on the edge of Paradise, a house in the middle of Paradise, and a house in the highest chambers of Paradise. Whoever does that has left no good unsought and no evil unescaped; he may die wherever he wishes to die."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Satan sits in wait for the son of Adam on his paths. He sat in wait for him on the path of Islam and said, 'Will you submit and abandon your religion and the religion of your fathers and forefathers?' But he disobeyed him and submitted. Then he sat in wait for him on the path of emigration and said, 'Will you emigrate and leave your land and your sky? The example of the emigrant is only like a horse on a long tether.' But he disobeyed him and emigrated. Then he sat in wait for him on the path of striving and said, 'Will you strive? That is the struggle of self and wealth: you will fight and be killed, then your wife will be married and your wealth divided.' But he disobeyed him and strove."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever does that, it is a right upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to admit him into Paradise. Whoever is killed, it is a right upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to admit him into Paradise. If he drowns, it is a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise, or if his mount throws him and breaks his neck, it is a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever goes out on a military expedition in the cause of Allah and intends nothing but a camel's hobbling rope, he will have what he intended."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "What do you think of a man who fights seeking reward and renown? What does he get?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He gets nothing."
The man repeated it three times, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him each time:
"He gets nothing." Then he said:
"Indeed, Allah accepts only those deeds that are done purely for Him and seeking His Face."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever delivers an arrow in the cause of Allah, it will be a level for him in Paradise."
On that day I delivered sixteen arrows.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and beware.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah, narrate to us a hadith that you heard from
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with no forgetting and no omission in it."
