segments_en: "Thus We make it enter the hearts of the criminals" — he said: [It is] polytheism (shirk).
label: machine translation

segments_en: Someone other than Ibn Kathīr named him, from Sufyān,
from ʿUbayd aṣ-Ṣayd, from al-Ḥasan,
regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire" — he said: Between them and faith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was traveling in Syria when a man called out to me from behind. I turned, and it was Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah. He said, "O Abū ʿAwn, what is this that they mention about al-Ḥasan?" I said, "They tell many lies about al-Ḥasan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two kinds of people have lied about al-Ḥasan: a people whose opinion is [belief in] qadar, who want to promote their opinion by this; and a people who harbor hatred and ill will toward him in their hearts, saying, "Is it not from his sayings such-and-such? Is it not from his sayings such-and-such?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qurrah ibn Khālid used to say to us, "O young men, do not be overcome [by prejudice] regarding al-Ḥasan, for his opinion was the Sunnah and what is correct."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If we had known that a statement,

[that of] al-Ḥasan, would spread as far as it did, we would have written a document of his retraction and had witnesses attest to it. But we said, "It is merely a word that slipped out; it should not be held against him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥasan said to me, "I will never return
to anything of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥasan never interpreted any verse except in the affirmative sense.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sālim ibn ʿAbdillāh said that Ibn ʿUmar said: We used to say, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was alive, "The best of the nation of the Prophet ﷺ after him are Abū Bakr, then ʿUmar, then ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with them all."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever claims that ʿAlī,

peace be upon him, was more deserving of the leadership than the two of them has judged Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, the Emigrants and the Helpers to be mistaken. And I do not see that, with this, any deed of his would be raised to the heavens.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The [rightly guided] caliphs are five: Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, may Allah be pleased with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ with this account; he said: So he refused to inform him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Which of you has seen a dream?"
Then he mentioned its meaning, but did not mention the disliking.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was displeased by it, meaning it distressed him, and he said:
"A caliphate of prophethood, then Allah will give kingship to whomever He wills."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Tonight a righteous man was shown [in a dream] that Abū Bakr was attached to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ʿUmar was attached to Abū Bakr, and ʿUthmān was attached to ʿUmar."

Jābir said: When we got up from being with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we said, "As for the righteous man, he is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and as for their being attached to one another, they are the rulers of this matter with which Allah sent His Prophet ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

said, "O Messenger of Allah, I saw [in a dream] a bucket lowered from the sky. Abū Bakr came and took hold of its crossbars and drank a weak drink. Then ʿUmar came and took hold of its crossbars and drank until he was full. Then ʿUthmān came and took hold of its crossbars and drank until he was full. Then ʿAlī came and took hold of its crossbars, and it jerked and some of it splashed onto him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Romans will ravage Syria for forty mornings, and none will hold out against them except Damascus and ʿAmmān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There will come a king from the kings of the non-Arabs who will overcome all the cities except Damascus.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was delivering a sermon and saying: "The likeness of ʿUthmān with Allah is like the likeness of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam." Then he recited this verse, reciting it and explaining it: "[Remember] when Allah said, 'O ʿĪsā, I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve,'" gesturing with his hand toward us and toward the people of Syria.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was delivering a sermon and said in his sermon, "Is the messenger of one of you [sent] on his errand dearer to him, or his deputy among his family?" So I said to myself, "I owe it to Allah that I will never pray behind you, and if I find people fighting you, I will fight you alongside them."
Isḥāq added in his narration: He said: So he fought at Dayr al-Jamājim until he was killed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent seventy men for a need; they were called the Qurrāʾ (the Qur'an reciters).
Two clans of Banū Sulaym, Riʿl and Dhakwān, confronted them
at a well called Biʾr Maʿūnah.
The men said, "By Allah, it is not you that we intended;
we are only passing through on a mission for the Prophet ﷺ."
But they killed them, and the Prophet ﷺ invoked [Allah's curse] against them for a month in the dawn prayer.
That was the beginning of the qunūt, and we had not been performing qunūt before.
ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: A man asked Anas about the qunūt, whether it was after bowing
or after finishing the recitation. He said, "No, rather after finishing the recitation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ḥarām ibn Milḥān, who was his maternal uncle, was stabbed on the day of Biʾr Maʿūnah, he said, with blood [on his hand], like this,
and he sprinkled it over his face and his head,
then said, "I have succeeded, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr asked the Prophet ﷺ for permission to leave [Makkah] when the harm against him grew severe, but he said to him, "Stay."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, do you hope that you will be given permission?"
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say,
"I certainly hope for that."
She said: So Abū Bakr waited for him, and one day at noon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and called him, saying,
"Send out those who are with you."
Abū Bakr said, "They are only my two daughters." He said,
"Do you know that I have been given permission to leave?"
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, [may I have] companionship?" The Prophet ﷺ said, "Companionship."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have two she-camels that I had prepared for leaving."
So the Prophet ﷺ took one of them, which was al-Jadʿāʾ.
The two rode and set out until they reached the cave, which is on [Mount] Thawr, and hid in it.
ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayrah was a servant of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ṭufayl ibn Sakhbarah, the maternal half-brother of ʿĀʾishah,
and Abū Bakr had a milk-giving animal [lent for use].
He would take it out to pasture in the evening and come back to them [in the morning],
and at dawn he would travel by night to the two of them, and then go off to graze [the flock],
so none of the shepherds noticed him.
When they left, he went out with them, following behind them in turn, until they reached Madīnah,
and ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayrah was killed on the day of Biʾr Maʿūnah.

And from Abū Usāmah: Hishām ibn ʿUrwah said: My father told me: When those at Biʾr Maʿūnah were killed and ʿAmr ibn Umayyah al-Ḍamrī was taken captive, ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl said to him, "Who is this?" and pointed to a slain man.
ʿAmr ibn Umayyah said to him, "This is ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayrah."
He said, "I saw him after he was killed, raised up to the sky, until I could see the sky between him and the earth; then he was set down."
The news of them reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he announced their death, saying,
"Your companions have been struck down,
and they asked their Lord,
saying: 'Our Lord, inform our brothers about us, that we are pleased with You and You are pleased with us.' So He informed them about them."
On that day ʿUrwah ibn Asmāʾ ibn al-Ṣalt was among those struck down,
and ʿUrwah was named after him,
and Mundhir ibn ʿAmr, after whom Mundhir was named.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said: On the day of the Trench we were digging, and a very hard lump of earth appeared.
They came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "This hard lump has appeared in the trench." He said, "I will go down."
Then he stood up, with a stone tied to his belly,
and we had stayed three days without tasting any food.
The Prophet ﷺ took the pickaxe and struck,
and it turned into a heap of soft, crumbling sand.
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to go home."
I said to my wife, "I saw something in the Prophet ﷺ
that I cannot bear.
Do you have anything?" She said, "I have some barley and a young goat."
So I slaughtered the kid and she ground the barley,
until we put the meat in the pot,
then I came to the Prophet ﷺ while the dough had risen,
and the pot was on its stones, nearly cooked. I said, "I have a little food,
so please come, O Messenger of Allah, with one or two men." He said, "How much is it?" I told him, and he said, "That is plenty and good." He said,
"Tell her not to take the pot off the fire nor the bread out of the oven until I come." Then he said, "Get up."
So the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār got up.
When he went in to his wife, he said, "Woe to you! The Prophet ﷺ has come with the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār and those with them."
She said, "Did he ask you?" I said, "Yes." Then he said,
"Enter, and do not crowd one another."
He began breaking the bread and putting meat on it,
covering the pot and the oven whenever he took from it,
and bringing it near to his Companions, then withdrawing it.
He kept breaking bread and ladling until they were all full, and some was left over. He said,
"Eat this and give some as a gift,
for the people have been struck by hunger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Salamah was asked, "Should a woman bathe together with a man?" She said, "Yes, if she is sensible. I remember bathing with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from a single basin. We would pour water over our hands until we had cleaned them, and then we would pour water over ourselves."
Al-Aʿraj said: "She did not mention the private parts, nor did she pay any heed to them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], may Allah be pleased with her, said that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bathed after sexual impurity, a vessel would be placed for him, and he would pour water over his hands before putting them into the vessel. Then, after washing his hands, he would put his right hand into the vessel, pour with his right hand, and wash his private parts with his left. When he had finished, he would pour with his right hand over the left and wash them both. Then he would rinse his mouth and sniff water into his nose three times. Then he would pour two handfuls of water over his head three times, and then pour water over his body.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah described the Prophet's ﷺ bath after sexual impurity. She said: He would wash his hands three times, then pour water with his right hand over his left and wash his private parts and whatever had touched them. ʿUmar said: "I think he said that he would pour with his right hand over his left three times." Then he would rinse his mouth three times, sniff water into his nose three times, and wash his face three times. Then he would pour water over his head three times, and then pour water over [the rest of his body].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would rest his head in the lap of one of us and recite the Qur'an while she was menstruating, and one of us would carry the prayer mat to the mosque and spread it out while she was menstruating.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The same as that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would place his mouth on the spot from which I had drunk, and he would drink from what I had left, while I was menstruating.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would hand me the vessel and I would drink from it while I was menstruating. Then I would give it back to him, and he would seek out the spot where my mouth had been and place it on his mouth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a woman among the Jews menstruated, they would not eat with them, nor drink with them, nor live with them in the houses. So they asked the Prophet of Allah ﷺ about that, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is an impurity} — the verse. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ instructed them to eat with them, drink with them, and live with them in the houses, and to do everything with them except intercourse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh and asked him about the Farewell Hajj,
and he told us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out when five days remained of Dhū al-Qaʿdah.
We set out with him, and when he reached Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays gave birth to Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr. She sent word to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [asking], "What should I do?" He said:
"Bathe, then bind yourself with a cloth, and then enter the state of iḥrām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to see it on the garment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I would scrape it off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ took the edge of his cloak and spat into it, and then rubbed one part of it against the other.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I became sexually impure while I was with the camels,
and I could not find water, so I rolled in the dust the way an animal rolls. Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him about that, and he said:
"It would have been enough for you to perform tayammum."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
became sexually impure and did not pray. He came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said, "You did right."
Then another man became sexually impure, performed tayammum, and prayed. He came to him, and he said something like what he had said to the other, meaning, "You did right."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to the Prophet ﷺ, "She has abnormal bleeding." He said:

"She should wait for the days of her menstrual period, then bathe, delay the Ẓuhr prayer and hasten the ʿAṣr prayer, and bathe and pray; then delay the Maghrib prayer and hasten the ʿIshāʾ prayer, and bathe and pray the two together; and she should bathe for the Fajr prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is Concealing. So when one of you wants to bathe, let him conceal himself with something."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I set out water for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, she said, and I screened him. She mentioned the bath. She said: Then I brought him a piece of cloth, but he did not want it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She entered upon the Prophet ﷺ on the day of the conquest of Mecca while he was bathing, and she had screened him with a cloth, [with water] in a large bowl that had traces of dough in it.
She said: Then he prayed the Ḍuḥā prayer, and I do not know how many units he prayed when he finished his bath.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I remember that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I would bathe from this [vessel]: a small pot placed there, about the size of a ṣāʿ or smaller, and we would dip into it together. I would pour water over my head with my hands three times, and I would not undo my hair.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Those who walk to the mosques in the darkness are the ones who plunge into the mercy of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Ansār lived far from the mosque, so they wanted to move closer. Then the verse was revealed: {And We record what they have sent forth and their footprints.} He said: So they stayed [where they were].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever hears the call to prayer and does not come to it, has no prayer, unless he has an excuse."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let men stop neglecting the congregational prayer, or else I will burn their houses down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is from the Prophet ﷺ that he used to say:
"Whoever prays in congregation in a mosque for forty nights, not missing the first rakʿah of the ʿIshāʾ prayer, Allah will write for him by it freedom from the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: No Muslim man makes the mosques his regular place for prayer and remembrance of Allah, except that Allah welcomes him with joy, just as the family of an absent person rejoice at him when he comes back to them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We prayed Maghrib with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Some people returned, and some stayed behind to continue [praying]. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came hurrying, out of breath, with his garment drawn back from his knees, and he said:

"Rejoice! This is your Lord, who has opened a door from the doors of heaven, boasting of you to the angels, saying: Look at My servants, they have performed one obligation and are waiting for another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by me while I had placed my left hand over my right. He took my right hand and placed it over my left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited {Al-Muʾminūn} in the Fajr prayer, and when he came to the mention of ʿĪsā, he was seized by a choke, so he bowed. That is, a cough.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I have not seen anyone whose prayer resembled the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ more than so-and-so.
He said: He used to lengthen the first two [rakʿahs] of Ẓuhr and shorten the last two, and he would shorten ʿAṣr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite for us in the first two rakʿahs of the Ẓuhr prayer, and he would sometimes let us hear the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿādh ibn Jabal
led his companions in the ʿIshāʾ prayer and made it long for them, so the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"Recite {By the sun and its brightness}, {Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High}, {By the night when it covers}, and recite {In the name of your Lord}."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever prays a prayer in which he does not recite the Mother of the Qurʾān, it is deficient, incomplete."
I said: O Abū Hurayrah, sometimes I am behind the imam.
He pinched my arm and said: O Persian, recite it to yourself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no prayer for the one who does not recite in every rakʿah {Al-ḥamdu lillāh} and a sūrah, in an obligatory prayer or otherwise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the imam recites, be silent. And when it is time for the sitting, let the first thing any of you says be the tashahhud."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has an imam, the recitation of the imam is a recitation for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Jews have not envied you for anything as much as they have envied you for [saying] āmīn, so say āmīn often."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raise his hands in prayer level with his shoulders when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he prostrated.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Humayd, Abū Usayd as-Sāʿidī, Sahl ibn Saʿd and Muḥammad ibn Maslamah gathered and mentioned the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Abū Humayd said: I know best among you the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, said the takbīr, and raised his hands,
then he raised them when he said the takbīr for bowing,
then he stood and raised his hands,
and stood upright until every bone returned to its place.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed, he would neither raise his head up nor lower it,
but kept it between the two.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying, and when he bowed he made his back level, so that if water were poured on it, it would stay in place.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ held the wedding feast for Zaynab bint Jahsh with bread and meat. I was sent to invite people to the meal, and a group would come, eat, and leave.
Then another group would come, eat, and leave.
I kept inviting until I could find no one left to invite. So I said, "O Prophet of Allah, I cannot find anyone else to invite." He said, "Take away the food."
Three men remained in the house, talking.
Then the Prophet ﷺ went out and made his way to the room of ʿĀʾishah, and said,
"Peace be upon you, people of the house, and the mercy of Allah."
She replied, "And upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah.
How did you find your wife? May Allah bless you." Then he went around to the rooms of all his wives,
saying to them what he had said to ʿĀʾishah,
and they said to him what ʿĀʾishah had said.
Then the Prophet ﷺ returned, and there were the three men still in the house, talking.
The Prophet ﷺ was extremely shy.
So he went out again toward the room of ʿĀʾishah, and I do not know whether I told him or he was told that the people had left.
He returned, and when he had put one foot over the threshold, inside, and the other outside, he drew the curtain between me and him,
and the verse of the veil was revealed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I will be the first to raise his head after the second blowing of the trumpet,
and there I will find Moses holding on to the Throne. I do not know whether he was like that before, or whether it was after the blowing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Between the two blowings there are forty."
They said, "O Abū Hurayrah, forty days?" He said, "I refuse to say."
They said, "Forty years?" He said, "I refuse to say."
They said, "Forty months?" He said, "I refuse to say."
Everything of the human being will decay except the tailbone,
from which creation will be reassembled.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Marwān was governor of the Hijaz, appointed by Muʿāwiyah.
He delivered a sermon in which he began to mention Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah,
so that the pledge of allegiance would be given to him after his father.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr said something to him, and Marwān said, "Seize him."

He entered the house of ʿĀʾishah, and they could not get to him. Marwān said, "This is the one about whom Allah revealed: {And the one who says to his parents, 'Uff to you both! Do you promise me...'}"
ʿĀʾishah said from behind the screen, "Allah did not reveal anything of the Qurʾān about us, except that Allah revealed my exoneration."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥudaybiyah
label: machine translation

segments_en: I am one of those who witnessed the tree [pledge].
The Prophet ﷺ forbade throwing pebbles.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning urinating in the place of washing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās: He commanded him to glorify Allah
after all the prayers.
He means His saying: {and after the prostrations}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with them both, concerning His saying {al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā}: Al-Lāt was a man who used to mix the barley meal for the pilgrims.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The moon split into two parts.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I mentioned to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis the hadith of Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah,

from ʿAbdullāh, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the woman who attaches hair [to another's]. He said, "I heard it from a woman called Umm Yaʿqūb, from ʿAbdullāh, like the hadith of Manṣūr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I advise the caliph [who succeeds me] regarding the first Emigrants, that he recognize their right.
And I advise the caliph regarding the Anṣār, who settled in the abode and in faith before the Prophet ﷺ emigrated, that he accept from those of them who do good and pardon those of them who do wrong.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the saying of the Exalted {and they will not disobey you in what is right}, he said: It is only a condition that Allah set for the women.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ gathered together out of jealousy toward him, so I said to them, "Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you."
Then this verse was revealed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Quraysh who had a mark like the mark of a sheep.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said, {You will surely ride from stage to stage}: state after state.
He said: This is your Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some rough Bedouin men used to come to the Prophet ﷺ and ask him when the Hour would be.
He would look at the youngest of them and say:
"If this one lives, old age will not overtake him before your Hour comes upon you."
Hishām said: meaning their death.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the Day of Resurrection the earth will be one loaf of bread, which the Almighty will turn over with His hand, just as one of you turns over his loaf while traveling, as a hospitality gift for the people of Paradise."

He said: Then a man from the Jews came and said, "May the Most Merciful bless you, Abū al-Qāsim! Shall I not tell you about the hospitality gift of the people of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection?" He said, "Yes."

He said: "The earth will be one loaf," just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at us and laughed until his molar teeth showed. [The man] said, "Shall I not tell you about their side dish?" He said, "Yes."
He said: "Their side dish will be bālām and nūn."
They said, "What is that?" He said, "An ox and a fish, from the extra lobe of whose livers seventy thousand will eat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the Day of Resurrection people will be gathered on a white, reddish-white earth, like a loaf of pure white bread."
Sahl or someone else said: There will be no landmark on it for anyone.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"On the Day of Resurrection sweat will sink into the earth seventy cubits, and it will reach the mouths of the people or their ears."
Thawr was unsure which of the two he said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No one will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection except that he will be destroyed."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, has Allah the Most High not said: {As for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will be judged with an easy account}?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"That is only the presentation of deeds,
but no one who is examined closely in the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection except that he will be punished."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to say:
"On the Day of Resurrection the disbeliever will be brought and it will be said to him: 'Do you think that if you had the earth full of gold, you would ransom yourself with it?' He will say: 'Yes.'
Then it will be said to him: 'You were asked for something far easier than that.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When the people of Paradise have gone to Paradise and the people of the Fire have gone to the Fire, Death will be brought and placed between Paradise and the Fire, then it will be slaughtered. Then a caller will call out: 'O people of Paradise, no more death! O people of the Fire, no more death!'
So the people of Paradise will increase in joy upon their joy, and the people of the Fire will increase in grief upon their grief."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The distance between the shoulders of the disbeliever in the Fire is the journey of three days for a fast rider."
Al-Wakīʿī did not mention "in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Some will come out of the Fire through intercession, as if they were thaʿārīr."
I said, "What are thaʿārīr?" He said, "Ḍaghābīs."
His front teeth had fallen out. I said to ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, "Abū Muḥammad, did you hear Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh say: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
'Some will come out of the Fire through intercession'?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We met ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar and mentioned to him the divine decree and what they say about it, and he mentioned something similar, adding: A man from Muzaynah or Juhaynah asked him, saying, "O Messenger of Allah, regarding what do we act? Is it regarding something that has already passed and been completed, or something that is only now being begun?" He said:
"Regarding something that has already passed and been completed."
The man, or some of the people, said, "Then what is the point of acting?" He said:
"The people of Paradise are made ready for the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of the Fire are made ready for the deeds of the people of the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit said to his son: "My son, you will never find the taste of the reality of faith until you know that what afflicted you could never have missed you, and what missed you could never have afflicted you. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'The first thing Allah created was the Pen. He said to it, "Write."
It said, "My Lord, what shall I write?" He said, "Write the decrees of everything until the Hour is established."'
My son, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever dies upon anything other than this is not from me.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Khaḍir saw a boy playing with the other boys; he took hold of his head and pulled it off. Mūsā said: {Have you killed an innocent soul?}" [to the end of] the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not sit with the people of [the denial of] divine decree, and do not open a conversation with them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, [what about] the children of the believers?" He said:
"They are from their fathers."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, without any deeds?" He said:
"Allah knows best what they would have done."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, and the children of the polytheists?" He said, "From their fathers."
I said, "Without any deeds?" He said:
"Allah knows best what they would have done."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He explained the hadith:
"Every child is born upon the natural disposition (fiṭrah)."
He said: This, in our view, refers to when Allah took the covenant from them in the loins of their fathers, when He said: {Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The one who buries a baby girl alive and the one buried alive are in the Fire."
Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā said: My father said: Abū Isḥāq narrated to me that ʿĀmir narrated this to him from ʿAlqamah, from Ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, people are exhausted, families are starving, wealth is depleted, and livestock are perishing. So pray to Allah for rain for us; we seek your intercession with Allah, and we seek Allah's intercession with you."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Woe to you! Do you know what you are saying?"
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ glorified Allah, and he kept on glorifying Him until it was seen in the faces of his Companions. Then he said:
"Woe to you! Allah's intercession is not sought with any of His creation; the station of Allah is greater than that. Woe to you! Do you know what Allah is? His Throne is over His heavens like this,"
and he gestured with his fingers, [making] a shape like a dome over it,
"and it creaks under Him as a saddle creaks under its rider."
Ibn Bashshār said in his narration:
"Allah is above His Throne, and His Throne is above His heavens."

And he continued the hadith. ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, Ibn al-Muthannā and Ibn Bashshār said, [narrating] from Yaʿqūb ibn ʿUtbah and Jubayr ibn Muḥammad ibn Jubayr, from his father, from his grandfather. Abū Dāwūd said: The hadith with the chain of Aḥmad ibn Saʿīd is the sound one; a group agreed with him on it, among them Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn and ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, and a group narrated it from Ibn Isḥāq as Aḥmad also said. The reception of ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, Ibn al-Muthannā and Ibn Bashshār was from a single manuscript, as has reached me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I have been given permission to narrate about one of the angels of Allah, among the bearers of the Throne: the distance between the lobe of his ear and his shoulder is a journey of seven hundred years."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He recited this verse: {Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners} up to His saying, the Exalted: {All-Hearing, All-Seeing}. He said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placing his thumb on his ear and the finger next to it on his eye. Abū Hurayrah said:
I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite it and place his two fingers. Ibn Yūnus said: Al-Muqriʾ said, meaning {Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing}, meaning that Allah has hearing and sight.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Negus, and a son of his recited a verse from the Gospel, and I laughed. He said:
Do you laugh at the words of Allah?
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said to a man sitting with him: "
What is your opinion of this man?"
A man from the nobles of the people said,
"By Allah, this man is worthy that if he proposes marriage, he be married,
and if he intercedes, his intercession be accepted."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent. Then another man passed by, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "
What is your opinion of this man?"
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is a man from the poor Muslims.
He is worthy that if he proposes marriage, he not be married,
and if he intercedes, his intercession not be accepted,
and if he speaks, his words not be listened to."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
This man is better than an earthful of the likes of that other."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding the saying of Allah, {And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans}, she said: It was revealed about a man who has an orphan girl under his guardianship, and he is her heir, and she has wealth but no one to dispute on her behalf. He does not marry her for the sake of her wealth, and so he harms her and treats her badly. So Allah said: {If you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans, then marry those women who seem good to you}. He means: what I have made lawful for you, and leave this one whom you harm.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The herald of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has permitted you to take temporary marriage."
He means the temporary marriage with women.
label: machine translation

segments_en: to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "We have been told that you are going to marry Durrah bint Abī Salamah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Even over Umm Salamah? If I had not married Umm Salamah, she would still not be lawful for me, for her father was my foster brother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihāb said: ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ʿĀʾishah,

may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, informed him that marriage in the Pre-Islamic Era was of four types. One was the marriage that people have today: a man proposes to another man for the woman under his guardianship, gives her a dowry, and then marries her. Another type: a man would say to his wife, when she had become pure from her menses, "Send for so-and-so and seek intercourse from him," and her husband would keep away from her and never touch her until her pregnancy from that man, from whom she sought intercourse, became clear. Once her pregnancy was clear, her husband would have relations with her if he wished. He did that only out of desire for a noble child. This marriage was called the marriage of istibḍāʿ. Another type: a group of fewer than ten men would gather and all of them would go in to the woman and have relations with her. When she conceived and gave birth, and some nights had passed after she delivered, she would send for them, and none of them could refuse, so they would gather at her place. She would say to them, "You know what your affair was, and I have given birth, and he is your son, O so-and-so," naming whomever she liked among them, and the child would be attached to him. The fourth type: many people would gather and go in to a woman, and she would not refuse anyone who came to her. These were the prostitutes, who used to fix flags at their doors as a sign; whoever wished could enter them. When one of them conceived and gave birth, they would gather for her and call the physiognomists, who would then attach her child to whomever they saw fit; he would take the child, and the child would be called his son, and he would not refuse that. Then, when Allah sent Muḥammad ﷺ, he abolished all the marriages of the people of the Pre-Islamic Era except the marriage of the people of Islam today.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was ten years old when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Madinah,
and he said: I served the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for ten years of his life,
and I was the most knowledgeable of the people about the matter of the ḥijāb when it was revealed,
and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb used to ask me about it.
The first thing revealed about it was on the occasion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ consummating his marriage with Zaynab bint Jaḥsh.
The Prophet ﷺ was a bridegroom with her in the morning, so he invited the people,
and they ate some of the food and then left,
but a group of them remained with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and stayed long. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up and went out, and I went out with him so that they would leave.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ walked and I walked with him until he reached the threshold of ʿĀʾishah's room,
then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ thought that they had left, so he returned and I returned with him,
until he entered upon Zaynab, and there they were, still sitting, not having dispersed.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went back and I went back with him,
until he reached the threshold of ʿĀʾishah's room,
and he thought that they had left,
so he returned and I returned with him,
and there they had left.
Then he revealed the verse of the ḥijāb,
and he put a curtain between me and him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When Allah intends good for a servant, He employs him."
It was asked, "How does He employ him, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"He enables him to do a righteous deed before death."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"No servant truly believes until he believes in the divine decree, its good and its bad, until he knows that what afflicted him could never have missed him, and that what missed him could never have afflicted him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When Allah decrees that a servant will die in a certain land, He gives him a need that takes him to it," or he said, "a need there."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is ʿImrān al-Qaṭṭān, from Qatādah,
from Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, from his father,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The example of the son of Adam is that beside him are ninety-nine deaths; if the deaths miss him, he falls into old age."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Part of the happiness of the son of Adam is his contentment with what Allah has decreed for him, and part of the misery of the son of Adam is his abandoning of seeking Allah's guidance in choosing, and part of the misery of the son of Adam is his displeasure with what Allah has decreed for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ:
"In my nation there will be swallowing by the earth and transformation [into animals], and that will be among those who deny the divine decree."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There are six whom I have cursed, and Allah has cursed them, as has every prophet who was answered: the one who adds to the Book of Allah; the one who denies the decree of Allah; the one who seizes power by tyranny so as to honor thereby those whom Allah has humiliated and humiliate those whom Allah has honored; the one who treats as lawful what Allah has made sacred; the one who treats as lawful regarding my family what Allah has forbidden; and the one who abandons my Sunnah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Makkah and met ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ and said to him, "O Abū Muḥammad, the people of Basra say things about the divine decree."
He said, "My son, do you recite the Qurʾān?" I said, "Yes."
He said, "Then recite Sūrat al-Zukhruf." So I recited:

"Ḥā Mīm. By the clear Book. Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qurʾān so that you may understand. And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and full of wisdom." He said, "Do you know what the Mother of the Book is?" I said, "Allah and His Messenger know best."
He said, "It is a book that Allah wrote before He created the heavens and before He created the earth. In it is that Pharaoh is of the people of the Fire, and in it:

"Perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and perish he."" ʿAṭāʾ said: Then I met al-Walīd ibn ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and asked him, "What was your father's counsel at death?" He said: My father called me and said, "My son, fear Allah, and know that you will never truly fear Allah until you believe in Allah and believe in the divine decree entirely, its good and its bad. If you die on other than this, you will enter the Fire. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it, 'Write.'
It said, 'What shall I write?' He said, 'Write the decree of what has been and what will be, forever.'""
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yazīd performed Hajj with the Prophet ﷺ, the Farewell Hajj, when I was seven years old.

ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf was reliable, a man of ḥadīth, and al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd was his grandfather. Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf used to say, "Al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd narrated to me, and he is my grandfather on my mother's side."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The hand of Allah is with the community."
This ḥadīth is ḥasan gharīb; we do not know it from the narration of Ibn ʿAbbās except through this chain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah will not unite my nation," or he said, "the nation of Muḥammad ﷺ, upon misguidance. The hand of Allah is with the community, and whoever deviates deviates into the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, or else Allah will soon send upon you a punishment from Himself; then you will call upon Him, and it will not be answered for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned a trial and spoke of its nearness. She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, who are the best of people in it?" He said:
"A man with his livestock, fulfilling their due and worshipping his Lord, and a man holding the head of his horse, frightening the enemy and being frightened by them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Madinah and entered the mosque, and it was crowded with people, with black banners fluttering, and Bilāl was wearing a sword in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I said, "What is the matter with the people?" They said, "He wants to send ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ on a mission." Then he mentioned the hadith at length, similar in meaning to the narration of Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah.
He said: And he is also called al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥassān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The "setting of the stars" refers to the two units of prayer before the dawn prayer, and "the end of prostration" refers to the two units of prayer after the sunset prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās met Kaʿb at ʿArafah and asked him about something,
and he exclaimed "Allāhu akbar" until the mountains echoed him. Ibn ʿAbbās said, "We are the sons of Hāshim."
Kaʿb said, "Allah divided His vision and His speech between Muḥammad and Mūsā. So Mūsā spoke with Him twice, and Muḥammad saw Him twice."
Masrūq said: I went to ʿĀʾishah and said, "Did Muḥammad see his Lord?" She said, "You have said something that made my hair stand on end." I said, "Gently," and then I recited:

"He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord." She said, "Where are you being led? That was only Jibrīl. Whoever tells you that Muḥammad saw his Lord, or concealed anything of what he was commanded [to convey], or knew the five things about which Allah the Exalted said:

"Indeed, with Allah is the knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain..." has uttered a tremendous lie. Rather, he saw Jibrīl, and he did not see him in his [true] form except twice: once at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and once at Jiyād, when he had six hundred wings and filled the horizon."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad saw his Lord.
I said, "Does Allah not say:
"Vision cannot grasp Him, but He grasps all vision"?" He said, "Woe to you! That is when He manifests with His light, which is His own light. And Muḥammad did see his Lord twice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the saying of Allah: "And he certainly saw him in another descent, at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary" "And He revealed to His servant what He revealed" "And he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or nearer."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ did see Him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw Him with his heart.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Abū Dharr, "If I had met the Prophet ﷺ, I would have asked him."
He said, "What would you have asked him?" I said, "I would have asked him whether Muḥammad saw his Lord." He said, "I did ask him, and he said:
"[It was] a light; how could I see Him?""
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"If You forgive, O Allah, You forgive abundantly; and which servant of Yours has not committed a minor sin?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of Makkah asked the Prophet ﷺ for a sign, so the moon was split in Makkah twice, and [the verse] was revealed:
"The Hour has come near, and the moon has split" up to His saying:
"[This is] continuous magic." He said: meaning, passing away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The moon was split in the time of the Prophet ﷺ until it became two parts, one on this mountain and one on that mountain. They said, "Muḥammad has bewitched us." Some of them said, "If he had bewitched us, he could not bewitch all the people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to his Companions and recited to them Sūrat ar-Raḥmān from its beginning to its end, and they remained silent. He said:
"I recited it to the jinn on the night of the jinn, and they responded better than you. Every time I reached His saying:
"So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?" they said, 'We deny none of Your favors, our Lord; to You belongs all praise.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined. And recite, if you wish:

"No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do." And in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. And recite, if you wish:
"And extended shade." And a place the size of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it. And recite, if you wish:
"So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has indeed succeeded, and the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.""
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
""And you make your denial [of it] your provision" - he said: Your [way of] thanks is that you say, 'We were given rain by such-and-such a star, and by such-and-such a star.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said [concerning]:
"Indeed, We have produced them [the women of Paradise] in a new creation" - he said:
"Among those newly created are women who were in the world old women, weak-sighted and with bleary eyes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have turned grey." He said:
"Hūd, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā ash-shamsu kuwwirat have made me grey."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a person complained of something, or had a sore or a wound, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would do thus with his finger—and Sufyān placed his forefinger on the ground, then raised it—[and say]:
"In the name of Allah, the soil of our earth, with the saliva of some of us, may our sick be healed, by the permission of our Lord."
Ibn Abī Shaybah said: "may he be healed." And Zuhayr said: "may our sick be healed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Abū Saʿīd: Did you hear from
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ anything about the lower garment? He said: Yes, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"The lower garment of the believer reaches to the middle of his shins. There is no blame on him for what is between that and the ankles, but whatever is below the ankles is in the Fire." He said this three times.
"Allah will not look at the one who drags his lower garment out of arrogance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd
al-Laythī, from Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"It is not lawful for a Muslim to forsake his brother for more than three nights, the two meeting and this one turning away and that one turning away. The better of the two is the one who begins with the greeting of peace."
label: machine translation

segments_en: His name is Ḥumayd ibn Hāniʾ al-Khawlānī, from Abū ʿAlī al-Janbī,
from Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The rider should greet the one walking, the one walking should greet the one sitting, and the few should greet the many."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said. [Another chain:] And Ismāʿīl ibn Sālim narrated to me: Hushaym narrated to us,
ʿUbaydullāh ibn Abī Bakr informed us, from his grandfather,
Anas ibn Mālik, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the People of the Book greet you with peace, say: 'And upon you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah curse the thief:
he steals an egg and his hand is cut off,
and he steals a rope and his hand is cut off."
Al-Aʿmash said: They used to think that it meant an egg of iron [a helmet],
and the rope, they used to think, was of the kind that is worth some dirhams.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah will send blessings upon him ten times, ten sins will be erased from him, and he will be raised ten degrees."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Jābir ibn Zayd: What invalidates the prayer? He said: Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: a menstruating woman and a dog.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Masʿūd
performed the two prostrations of forgetfulness after the salutation, and mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ did that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the qunūt for a month—Shuʿbah said: he cursed some men, and Hishām said: he supplicated against some clans of the Arabs—then he abandoned it after rising from the bowing.
This is the version of Hishām. Shuʿbah said, from Qatādah, from Anas: The Prophet ﷺ recited the qunūt for a month, cursing Riʿl, Dhakwān and Liḥyān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no Muslim servant who prays twelve rakʿahs to Allah every day, voluntarily, other than the obligatory prayers, but Allah will build for him a house in Paradise," or, "a house will be built for him in Paradise."
Umm Ḥabībah said: I have not ceased praying them since.
ʿAmr said: I have not ceased praying them since.
And al-Nuʿmān said the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah,

that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray eleven rakʿahs at night, making one of them the witr. When he finished, he would lie on his right side until the muʾadhdhin came to him, and then he would pray two light rakʿahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He went out to perform Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Farewell Hajj, and with him was his wife Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays al-Khathʿamiyyah. When they reached Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, Asmāʾ gave birth to Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr. Abū Bakr came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him to tell her to bathe, then to enter the state of iḥrām for Hajj and do what the people do, except that she should not circumambulate the House.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard her say:

I performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Farewell Hajj, and I saw him when he had thrown the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah and departed, while he was on his mount, and with him were Bilāl and Usāmah, one of them leading his mount and the other holding up his garment over the head of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to shade him from the sun. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said much, then I heard him say:
"Even if a mutilated slave—I think she said, a black one—is appointed over you, leading you by the Book of Allah, the Exalted, listen to him and obey."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ demanding repayment of a debt he was owed, and he was harsh with him, even saying to him, "I insist that you pay me what you owe!"
His Companions rebuked him and said, "Woe to you! Do you know whom you are speaking to?" He said, "I am only asking for my right." Then the Prophet ﷺ said,
"Why were you not on the side of the one who has the right?"
Then he sent for Khawlah bint Qays and said to her,
"If you have any dates, lend them to us until our dates come to us, and then we will repay you."
She said, "Yes, may my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah."
She said: So he borrowed from her, repaid the Bedouin, and fed him. The Bedouin said, "You have paid in full; may Allah repay you in full." The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Those are the best of people. A community in which the weak cannot take their right without being made to suffer is not sanctified."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ with a debtor of mine, and he said to me, "Stay with him."
Then he passed by me at the end of the day and said,
"What has your prisoner done, O brother of Banū Tamīm?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sulaymān ibn Udhnān used to lend ʿAlqamah a thousand dirhams until his stipend came. When his stipend was paid, he demanded the money from him and was hard on him, so he paid him. ʿAlqamah was angry and stayed away for months. Then he came to him and said, "Lend me a thousand dirhams until my stipend." He said, "Gladly and with honor. O Umm ʿUtbah, bring that sealed purse that you have."
She brought it, and he said, "By Allah, these are the very dirhams you paid me; I have not touched a single one of them."
He said, "May Allah bless your father! What made you do to me what you did?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw written on the gate of Paradise: 'Charity is rewarded tenfold, and a loan eighteenfold.'
I said, 'O Jibrīl, why is a loan better than charity?'
He said, 'Because the one who asks for charity asks while he has something, whereas the one who asks for a loan only asks out of need.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Anas ibn Mālik about a man among us who lends money to his brother and [the borrower] then gives him a gift. He said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"If one of you lends a loan and [the borrower] gives him a gift or offers him a ride on his animal, he should not ride it or accept it, unless that was already the custom between the two of them beforehand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That his brother
had died and left three hundred dirhams and dependents, and he wanted to spend it on his brother's family. The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Your brother is held back because of his debt, so pay it off for him."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have paid off for him everything except two dinars that a woman claimed, and she has no proof." He said,
"Give it to her, for she is truthful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"A debt will be taken from its owner on the Day of Resurrection if he dies, except for one who takes on debt for three reasons: a man whose strength is weakened in the cause of Allah, so he borrows to strengthen himself against the enemy of Allah and his own enemy; a man at whose home a Muslim dies and who finds nothing to shroud and bury him except by borrowing; and a man who fears for himself the state of being unmarried, so he marries out of concern for his religion. Allah will settle the debts of these on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"A pledge is not forfeited."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Give the hired worker his wage before his sweat dries."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he recited Ṭā-Sīn-Mīm until he reached the story of Mūsā, then said,
"Mūsā, peace be upon him, hired himself out for eight years or ten, in return for preserving his chastity and for food for his stomach."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I grew up an orphan, I migrated as a poor man, and I was a hired servant of the daughter of Ghazwān for the food of my stomach and a turn riding on my feet: I would gather firewood for them when they stopped, and drive their camels with songs when they rode. So praise be to Allah, who made religion a firm support and made Abū Hurayrah an imam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ was struck by hunger. When that reached ʿAlī, he went out looking for work by which he could earn something to relieve the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He came to the orchard of a Jewish man and drew water for him, seventeen buckets, each bucket for one date. The Jewish man let him choose seventeen ʿajwah dates from his dates, and he brought them to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to draw a bucket for a date, and I stipulated that it be a hard, dry one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ rose at night to pray the night prayer, he would say:
"O Allah, to You belongs all praise; You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and all who are in them. To You belongs all praise.
To You belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all who are in them.
To You belongs all praise; You are the Light of the heavens and the earth.

To You belongs all praise; You are the Truth, Your promise is true, the meeting with You is true, Your word is true, Paradise is true, the Fire is true, the Prophets are true, Muhammad ﷺ is true, and the Hour is true.
O Allah, to You I have submitted,
in You I have believed, in You I have placed my trust, to You I have turned in repentance, by You I have disputed, and to You I have brought my judgment.
So forgive me what I have sent forward and what I have left behind,
what I have concealed and what I have made known.
You are the One who brings forward and the One who puts back.
There is no god but You," or "There is no god other than You."
Sufyān said: ʿAbd al-Karīm Abū Umayyah added:
"There is no power and no strength except with Allah."
Sufyān said: Sulaymān ibn Abī Muslim said that he heard it from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Manṣūr and Hishām.
As for Khālid and Hishām, they said, from Muḥammad and Ḥafṣah; and Manṣūr said, from Muḥammad, from Umm ʿAṭiyyah, who said: One of the daughters of the Prophet ﷺ died, and he said:

"Wash her an odd number of times, three or five or more than that, if you see fit. Wash her with water and lote-tree leaves, and in the last washing put camphor, or a little camphor. When you have finished, let me know."
When we had finished, we informed him, and he threw down to us his waist-wrapper and said, "Wrap her in it next to her skin."
Hushaym said: In the report of others than these—and I do not know whether Hishām was among them—she said: We braided her hair into three plaits.
Hushaym said: I think he said: And we placed it behind her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We memorized it from az-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib,
from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Hasten with the funeral.
If it is a righteous one, then it is a good that you are sending forward to it;
and if it is otherwise, then it is an evil that you are putting off your necks."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ["Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word, in the life of this world and in the Hereafter."] He said: It was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave. The person is asked, "Who is your Lord?" and he says, "My Lord is Allah, and my religion is the religion of Muhammad ﷺ." That is the meaning of His saying: ["Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word, in the life of this world and in the Hereafter."]
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge, saying:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the trial of the Fire and from the punishment of the Fire,
and I seek refuge in You from the trial of the grave,
and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave,
and I seek refuge in You from the trial of wealth,
and I seek refuge in You from the trial of poverty,
and I seek refuge in You from the trial of the Antichrist, the False Messiah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent Muʿādh ibn Jabal to Yemen and said:

"You are going to a people of the Book. Invite them to testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. If they obey you in that, then inform them that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory upon them five prayers every day and night. If they obey you in that, then inform them that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory upon them charity (ṣadaqah) from their wealth, to be taken from their rich and given to their poor. If they obey you in that, then beware of taking the best of their wealth, and fear the supplication of the wronged, for there is no veil between it and Allah, Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When a woman spends [from the food]—and my father said in his report: when a woman feeds [others]—from her husband's house, without causing waste, she will have her reward, and he will have the like of it for what he earned, and she will have [the reward] for what she spent; and the treasurer will have the same, without any decrease in their rewards."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr. Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said: "He informed us," and the others said:
"Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us,
from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār,
that he heard Ibn
ʿUmar say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Ghifār—may Allah forgive them; Aslam—may Allah keep them safe; and ʿUṣayyah disobeyed Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar taught him that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had mounted his camel to set out on a journey, he would say "Allahu Akbar" three times, and then say:

"Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, though we could never have subdued it [ourselves]. And indeed, to our Lord we will surely return. O Allah, we ask You on this journey of ours for righteousness and piety, and for deeds that please You. O Allah, make this journey of ours easy for us, and fold up its distance for us. O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey and the Successor [who guards] the family and wealth."
And when he returned, he would say the same words and add to them:
"Returning, repenting, worshipping, and praising our Lord."
And when the Prophet ﷺ and his armies ascended the mountain passes, they would say "Allahu Akbar," and when they descended, they would say "Subhan Allah." So the prayer was set accordingly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Ibn al-Musayyab,
who said: ʿĀʾishah said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no day on which Allah frees more servants from the Fire than the Day of ʿArafah. He draws near, then boasts of them to the angels, saying: What do these people want?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman fell ill with a sickness and said, "If Allah cures me, I will surely go out and pray in Bayt al-Maqdis."

She recovered, then made preparations wanting to set out. Then Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, came to greet her, and she told her about it. Maymūnah said, "Sit down, eat what you have prepared, and pray in the Mosque of the Messenger ﷺ, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'A prayer in it is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except the Mosque of the Kaʿbah.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Khudrī passed by me. I said to him, "What did you hear your father say about the mosque that was founded on piety?" He said: My father said: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the house of one of his wives and said, "O Messenger of Allah, which of the two mosques is the one founded on piety?" He took a handful of pebbles, struck the ground with it, and then said:
"It is this mosque of yours,"
meaning the mosque of Madinah. He said: I said, "I bear witness that I heard your father mention it in just this way."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a woman, so he went to his wife Zaynab, who was tanning a hide of hers, and he fulfilled his need. Then he went out to his Companions and said:
"Indeed, a woman approaches in the form of a devil and departs in the form of a devil. So when one of you sees a woman, let him go to his wife, for that will repel what is in his soul."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he forbade a man in a state of iḥrām to marry, to give [another] in marriage, or to propose marriage.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A woman previously married has more right over herself than her guardian, and a virgin is to be consulted about herself."
It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, a virgin is shy to speak." He said, "Her silence is her consent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married me when I was seven years old—Sulaymān said: or six—and he consummated the marriage with me when I was nine.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ married her when she was seven years old, she was brought to him when she was nine, her toys were with her, and he died leaving her when she was eighteen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you is invited to a meal, let him accept; if he wishes he may eat, and if he wishes he may leave it."
Ibn al-Muthannā did not mention "to a meal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you is invited, let him accept. If he is not fasting, let him eat, and if he is fasting, let him pray [for the host]."
Hishām said: "Prayer here means supplication."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about a man who divorces his wife three times, then another man marries her, closes the door, lowers the curtain, and then divorces her before consummating the marriage with her. He said:
"She is not lawful for the first [husband] until the other has had intercourse with her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Withdrawal [coitus interruptus] was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Why would one of you do that?"
Ibn Abī ʿUmar added in his narration: "And he did not say, 'None of you should do that.'"
Both said in their narration:
"For there is no soul that is [destined to be] created except that Allah is its Creator."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
I saw Jaʿfar flying in Paradise with the angels."
This hadith is gharīb from the narration of Abū Hurayrah; we do not know it except from the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn and others declared him weak. ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar is the father of ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: No one has worn sandals, put on footwear, ridden riding animals, or mounted a saddle after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who was better than Jaʿfar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib: "
You resemble me in both my appearance and my character."
There is a story in the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to call Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, "the father of the poor." When we came to him, he would offer us whatever was available. One day we came to him and he found nothing with him, so he brought out a jar of honey and broke it open, and we began to lick from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ one night about a need of mine, and the Prophet ﷺ came out wrapped in something I did not know what it was. When I had finished with my need, I said, "What is this that you are wrapped in?" He uncovered it, and there were al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon them, on his hips. He said: "
These are my sons and the sons of my daughter. O Allah, I love them, so love them, and love whoever loves them."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Umm Salamah while she was weeping. I said, "What makes you weep?" She said, "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—meaning in a dream—with dust on his head and beard. I said, 'What is the matter, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: "
'I have just witnessed the killing of al-Ḥusayn.'"
This hadith is gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked, "Which of the members of your household is most beloved to you?" He said, "Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn."
He would say to Fāṭimah: "
Call my two sons for me."
Then he would smell them and embrace them.
This hadith is gharīb from this route, from the narration of Anas.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn Ziyād when the head of al-Ḥusayn was brought. He began to poke at its nose with a stick he had and said, "I have not seen the like of this in beauty," and the rest was not mentioned.
I said, "Indeed, he was one of those most resembling the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥasan most resembled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the chest to the head, and al-Ḥusayn most resembled the Prophet ﷺ in what was below that.
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the head of ʿUbaydullāh ibn Ziyād and the heads of his companions were brought and set out in the courtyard of the mosque, I came to them while they were saying, "It has come! It has come!"

Then a snake came, passing between the heads until it entered the nostrils of ʿUbaydullāh ibn Ziyād. It stayed a little while, then came out and went off until it disappeared. Then they said, "It has come! It has come!"
It did that two or three times.
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn and said: "
O Allah, I love them, so love them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was carrying al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī on his shoulder, and a man said, "What an excellent mount you are riding, young man!" The Prophet ﷺ said: "
And what an excellent rider he is."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb; we do not know it except from this route.
Zamʿah ibn Ṣāliḥ was declared weak by some of the scholars of hadith because of his memory.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Every prophet was given seven noble companions, or he said, leaders, and I have been given fourteen."
We said, "Who are they?" He said, "I, my two sons, Jaʿfar, Ḥamzah, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr, Bilāl, Salmān, ʿAmmār, al-Miqdād, Ḥudhayfah, and ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during his Hajj on the day of ʿArafah, on his she-camel al-Qaṣwāʾ, delivering a sermon, and I heard him say: "
O people, I have left among you that which, if you hold to it, you will never go astray: the Book of Allah and my family, the people of my household."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with both of them, they said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

I am leaving among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray after me—one of them is greater than the other: the Book of Allah, a rope extended from the heaven to the earth, and my family, the people of my household. They will not separate until they come to me at the Pond. So look how you succeed me in regard to them."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Muʿādh returned from Syria, he prostrated to the Prophet ﷺ. He said:
"What is this, Muʿādh?"
He said, "I went to Syria and found them prostrating to their bishops and patriarchs, so I wished in myself that we would do that for you."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do not do so. For if I were to command anyone to prostrate to other than Allah, I would command the woman to prostrate to her husband. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, a woman does not fulfil the right of her Lord until she fulfils the right of her husband, even if he asks her for herself while she is on a camel saddle, she must not refuse him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When what was revealed about silver and gold was revealed, they said, "Then what wealth should we keep?" ʿUmar said, "I will find out that for you."
So he urged his camel on and caught up with the Prophet ﷺ, with me right behind him. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, what wealth should we keep?" He said:
"Let one of you take a grateful heart, a tongue that remembers Allah, and a believing wife who helps him with the matter of the Hereafter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to say:

"The believer gains nothing better after fear of Allah than a righteous wife: if he commands her, she obeys him; if he looks at her, she pleases him; if he swears an oath concerning her, she fulfils it for him; and if he is away from her, she is sincere to him regarding herself and his wealth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do not marry women for their beauty, for their beauty may lead them to ruin; and do not marry them for their wealth, for their wealth may make them rebellious. Rather, marry them for religion. A slave woman with a slit nose, dark-skinned, who is religious is better."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Marry virgins, for they have sweeter mouths, more fertile wombs, and are more content with little."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever wishes to meet Allah pure and purified, let him marry free women."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I proposed to a woman, and I would hide to watch her until I looked at her among her palm trees. It was said to him, "Do you do this while you are a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"When Allah puts into a man's heart the proposal to a woman, there is no harm in his looking at her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The previously married woman speaks for herself, and the virgin's consent is her silence."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man among them called Khidhām married off a daughter of his, and she disliked the marriage her father had arranged. So she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned it to him, and he annulled the marriage her father had made. Then she married Abū Lubābah ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir.
Yaḥyā mentioned that she had been previously married.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn died, he left a daughter.

Ibn ʿUmar said, "My maternal uncle Qudāmah, who was her paternal uncle, married her to me without consulting her, and that was after her father had died. She disliked that marriage, and the girl wished that al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah would marry her, so he married her to him."
label: machine translation

"A woman must not marry off a woman, nor may a woman marry herself off, for it is the adulteress who marries herself off."

"Every matter of importance that is not begun with praise of Allah is cut off [from blessing]."
