segments_en: We were in Medina on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and the girls were beating tambourines and singing. We went in to al-Rubayyiʿ bint Muʿawwidh and mentioned that to her.

She said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me on the morning of my wedding, while I had two girls with me singing and lamenting my fathers who were killed on the day of Badr. Among what they said was, 'Among us is a Prophet who knows what will be tomorrow.' So he said:
'As for this, do not say it. None knows what will be tomorrow except Allah.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a part of Medina and there were girls beating their tambourines and singing, saying, "We are girls of Banū al-Najjār; how wonderful is Muhammad as a neighbour!" So the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Allah knows that I love you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Usāmah stumbled on the threshold of the door and gashed his face. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Wipe the filth away from him."
But I found it distasteful, so he began sucking the blood from him and spitting it out from his face. Then he said:
"If Usāmah had been a girl, I would have adorned him and clothed him until he was well provided for."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out on the campaign of Ḥunayn with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When we faced the enemy, I advanced and climbed a mountain pass, and a man from the enemy came toward me. I shot an arrow at him, and he disappeared from me, and I did not know what he had done. Then I looked at the people, and they had come up from another pass and met the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ turned back, and I too returned in retreat. I was wearing two cloaks, wrapping one around my waist and wearing the other over my shoulders, and my waistcloth came loose, so I gathered both together. I passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in retreat while he was on his white mule, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Ibn al-Akwaʿ has seen something frightening."
When they pressed upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he dismounted from the mule, took a handful of dust from the ground, then faced them with it and said, "May the faces be disfigured!"

Allah did not create a single one of them except that his eyes were filled with dust from that handful. They turned and fled, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, defeated them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ distributed their spoils among the Muslims.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Delegations came to Muʿāwiyah, and that was in Ramadan. We would prepare food for one another, and Abū Hurayrah would often invite us to his lodging. I said, "Shall I not prepare food and invite them to my lodging?" So I ordered food to be prepared. Then I met Abū Hurayrah in the evening and said, "The invitation is at my place tonight." He said, "You have beaten me to it." I said, "Yes."

So I invited them, and Abū Hurayrah said, "Shall I not tell you a hadith from among your own accounts, O company of the Anṣār?" Then he mentioned the conquest of Makkah and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ advanced until he reached Makkah. He sent al-Zubayr over one of the two flanks, and sent Khālid over the other flank, and sent Abū ʿUbaydah over those without armor. They took the middle of the valley, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in a squadron. He said: He looked and saw me, and said, "Abū Hurayrah?"
I said, "At your service, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"Let no one come to me except an Anṣārī."
Someone other than Shaybān added: He said,
"Call the Anṣār for me."
He said: So they gathered around him. And Quraysh had gathered their rabble and followers.
They said, "We will send these forward; if they gain something, we will be with them,
and if they are struck down, we will give what is asked of us." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Do you see the rabble of Quraysh and their followers?"
Then he gestured with his hands, one over the other, and said,
"Until you meet me at aṣ-Ṣafā."

He said: So we set out, and none of us wished to kill anyone except that he killed him, and none of them offered us any resistance. He said: Then Abū Sufyān came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the greenery of Quraysh has been made lawful to destroy. There will be no Quraysh after today." Then he said,
"Whoever enters the house of Abū Sufyān is safe."
The Anṣār said to one another, "As for the man, desire for his hometown and compassion for his kinsfolk have overtaken him."

Abū Hurayrah said: Then revelation came, and when revelation came it was not hidden from us. When it came, no one would raise his gaze to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until the revelation ended. When the revelation ended, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"O company of the Anṣār!"
They said, "At your service, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"You said: As for the man, desire for his hometown has overtaken him."
They said, "That was indeed said." He said,
"Never! I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger. I emigrated to Allah and to you. The living is your living, and the dying is your dying."
They came to him weeping and saying, "By Allah, we said what we said only out of our attachment to Allah and His Messenger."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Indeed, Allah and His Messenger believe you and excuse you."

He said: Then the people went to the house of Abū Sufyān, and the people closed their doors. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ advanced until he came to the Black Stone, touched it, then circled the House. He said: Then he came upon an idol beside the House which they used to worship. He said: In the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was a bow, and he was holding it by its curved tip. When he came to the idol, he began to poke it in the eye, saying,
"Truth has come and falsehood has vanished."
When he finished his circling, he came to aṣ-Ṣafā and climbed it until he could see the House, and he raised his hands, praising Allah and supplicating as he wished.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of the conquest of Makkah, [he said:]
"No man of Quraysh shall be killed in captivity after this day until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That one of them,

if he slept before eating his evening meal, it was not permitted for him to eat or drink anything that night and the following day until the sun set, until this verse was revealed: {And eat and drink} up to {the black thread}. He said: It was revealed about Abū Qays ibn ʿAmr, who came to his family after sunset while fasting and said, "Is there anything [to eat]?" His wife said, "We have nothing, but I will go out and look for some supper for you."

So she went out, and he laid down his head and fell asleep. She returned to him and found him asleep, and she woke him, but he ate nothing. He spent the night and rose in the morning fasting until midday, when he fainted. That was before this verse was revealed, so Allah revealed concerning him
label: machine translation

"Whoever among you has the means, let him marry, for it is more restraining for the gaze and more protective of chastity. And whoever does not, let him fast, for it will be a protection for him."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a man in the shade of a tree who was being sprinkled with water. He said:
"What is the matter with this companion of yours?"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, he is fasting." He said:
"It is not righteousness to fast while traveling. Take the concession of Allah that He has granted you, and accept it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was brought food at Marr al-Ẓahrān, and he said to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, "Come near and eat."
They said, "We are fasting." He said:
"Saddle up for your two companions! Work for your two companions!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taking his midday meal at Marr al-Ẓahrān, with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar with him, he said, "The meal." (Mursal.)

segments_en: I went out with Abū Qilābah on a journey, and he brought food near. I said, "I am fasting."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on a journey and food was brought near. He said to a man, "Come near and eat."
He said, "I am fasting." He said:
"Allah has lifted from the traveler half of the prayer, and fasting while traveling."
"So come near and eat." So I came near and ate.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah has lifted from the traveler half of the prayer and fasting, and from the pregnant woman and the nursing mother."

He invited me to his food, and I said, "I am fasting." He said:

segments_en: The Quraysh
made a treaty with the Prophet ﷺ, and among their representatives was Suhayl ibn ʿAmr. The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAlī: "
Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful."
Suhayl said: "As for 'In the name of Allah,' we do not know what 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful' is. Rather, write what we know: 'In Your name, O Allah.'" So he said: "
Write: From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah."
They said: "If we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would follow you. Rather, write your name and the name of your father." So the Prophet ﷺ said: "
Write: From Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullāh."

They stipulated to the Prophet ﷺ that whoever of them came to him would not be returned to them, and whoever of his side came to them would be returned to them. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we write this?" He said: "
Yes. Whoever of us goes to them, Allah has put him far away; and whoever of them comes to us, Allah will make for him relief and a way out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When {Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, so that Allah may forgive you} up to His saying {a great success} was revealed, on his return from al-Ḥudaybiyah, while sorrow and grief mingled among them and he had already sacrificed the sacrificial animal at al-Ḥudaybiyah, he said: "
A verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than the whole world."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nothing prevented me from being present at
Badr except that I went out, I and my father Ḥusayl. He said: The disbelievers of Quraysh seized us and said, "You want Muhammad!" We said, "We do not want him; we want only Medina."

So they took from us the covenant and pledge of Allah that we would go back to Medina and would not fight alongside him. Then we came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him what had happened, and he said: "
Go back. We will fulfil our covenant with them, and we seek Allah's help against them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Ḥudhayfah when a man said, "Had I met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would have fought alongside him and done my utmost." Ḥudhayfah said, "Would you have done that? You saw us with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of al-Aḥzāb, when a fierce, bitterly cold wind seized us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Is there not a man who will bring me news of the enemy? Allah will make him my companion on the Day of Resurrection."
We stayed silent, and none of us answered him. Then he said: "
Is there not a man who will bring us news of the enemy? Allah will make him my companion on the Day of Resurrection."
We stayed silent, and none of us answered him. Then he said: "
Is there not a man who will bring us news of the enemy? Allah will make him my companion on the Day of Resurrection."
We stayed silent, and none of us answered him. So he said: "
Get up, Ḥudhayfah, and bring us news of the enemy."
Since he called me by my name, I had no choice but to get up. He said: "
Go and bring me news of the enemy, and do not alarm them against me."

When I left him, it was as though I were walking in a warm bath, until I reached them. I saw Abū Sufyān warming his back at the fire. I placed an arrow in the middle of the bow and wanted to shoot it, but I remembered the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "
Do not alarm them against me."

Had I shot him, I would have hit him. So I returned, walking as though in a warm bath. When I came to him and told him the news of the enemy, and I had finished, I felt the cold. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ covered me with the spare part of a cloak he was wearing while praying. I kept sleeping until morning. When morning came, he said: "
Get up, you sleepyhead!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Uḥud, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was left with only seven of the Anṣār and two men of Quraysh. When the enemy pressed hard upon him, he said: "
Who will drive them away from us, and he will have Paradise," or: "he will be my companion in Paradise?"
A man of the Anṣār came forward and fought until he was killed. Then they pressed upon him again, and he said: "
Who will drive them away from us, and he will have Paradise," or: "he will be my companion in Paradise?"
Another man of the Anṣār came forward and fought until he was killed. It continued like that until the seven were killed. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his two companions: "
We have not been fair to our companions."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jibrīl was delayed in coming to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so the polytheists said, "Muhammad has been abandoned." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {By the morning brightness, and by the night when it grows still, your Lord has not abandoned you, nor has He detested you.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"My Basin is farther across than the distance from Aylah to ʿAdan. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, its vessels outnumber the stars, and it is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will drive men away from it just as a man drives strange camels away from his own basin."
He was asked, "O Messenger of Allah, will you recognize us?" He said:
"Yes. You will come to me with bright faces and bright limbs from the traces of ablution, which belongs to no one other than you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was behind Abū Hurayrah while he was performing ablution for prayer. He would extend his hand until it reached his armpit. I said to him, "O Abū Hurayrah, what is this ablution?" He said, "O sons of Farrūkh, you are here? Had I known you were here, I would not have performed this ablution. I heard my dear friend ﷺ say:
"The adornment of the believer will reach as far as the ablution reaches."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade wiping oneself with a bone or with dung.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered a walled garden, and a boy followed him carrying a small vessel of water; he was the youngest of us. He placed it by a lote tree. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ relieved himself and then came out to us having cleaned himself with water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Sulaymān ibn Yasār about semen

that gets on a man's garment: should he wash it, or wash the whole garment? He said, "ʿĀʾishah informed me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would wash off the semen, then go out to prayer in that garment, and I would see the mark of the washing in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: We sent al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he asked him about prostatic fluid that comes out of a person, what one should do about it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Perform ablution and sprinkle water on your private part."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah about the Witr prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Then he mentioned the hadith. I said, "What would he do regarding ritual impurity after sexual relations? Would he wash fully before sleeping, or sleep before washing?" She said, "He did both. Sometimes he washed fully and then slept, and sometimes he performed ablution and then slept."
I said, "Praise be to Allah, Who has made allowance in the matter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a woman who sees in her sleep what a man sees in his sleep. He said:
"If she experiences what a man experiences, then she should wash fully."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Maymūnah said: I brought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ water for his ritual washing after sexual impurity. He washed his hands twice or three times, then put his hand into the vessel and poured water over his private part and washed it with his left hand. Then he struck the ground with his left hand and rubbed it vigorously. Then he performed ablution as for prayer. Then he poured three handfuls of water, filling his palm, over his head. Then he washed the rest of his body. Then he moved away from that spot and washed his feet. Then I brought him a towel, but he returned it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was brought a towel but did not touch it, and he began to say with the water like this, meaning he shook it off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to wash from one vessel. He would hurry ahead of me and I would hurry ahead of him, until he would say, "Leave some for me,"
and I would say, "Leave some for me."
Suwayd said: He would hurry ahead of me and I would hurry ahead of him, and I would say, "Leave some for me, leave some for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It reached ʿĀʾishah that ʿAbd

Allah ibn ʿAmr was commanding women, when they washed fully, to undo their hair. She said, "How strange of Ibn ʿAmr! He commands women to undo their hair when they wash fully. Why does he not command them to shave their heads? I used to wash together with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from a single vessel, and I did no more than pour water over my head three times."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, together with my father and my grandfather, and he ﷺ engaged me [to a woman] and married me [to her]. I also brought a dispute before him: my father Yazīd had taken out some dinars to give in charity and had placed them with a man in the mosque.
I came, took them, and brought them to him. He said, "By Allah, I did not intend you [to have it]."
So I took the dispute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:

and you have what you took, O Maʿn."

segments_en: My husband divorced me and I wanted to move out, so I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Move to the house of your cousin ʿAmr ibn Umm Maktūm and observe your waiting period there."
Al-Aswad threw a pebble at him and said: Woe to you! Why do you give a ruling like this?

ʿUmar said: Unless you bring two witnesses who testify that they heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we will not abandon the Book of Allah because of the word of a woman: {Do not expel them from their homes, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear indecency.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: My husband Abū ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ ibn al-Mughīrah sent ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah to me with my divorce, and he sent with him five ṣāʿs of dates and five ṣāʿs of barley. I said: Do I have no maintenance except this, and am I not to observe my waiting period in your house? He said: No.
She said: So I put on my garments tightly and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "How many times did he divorce you?" I said: Three. He said:
"He spoke truly; you have no maintenance.
Observe your waiting period in the house of your cousin Ibn Umm Maktūm, for he is a blind man and you can take off your garment in his presence. When your waiting period ends, let me know."
She said: Then several men proposed to me, among them Muʿāwiyah and Abū al-Jahm. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Muʿāwiyah is poor and has little wealth, and Abū al-Jahm is harsh with women—or he strikes women, or something like this—but you should marry Usāmah ibn Zayd."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah said: O Messenger of Allah, if I found a man with my wife, should I not touch him until I bring four witnesses? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes."
He said: No, by the One who sent you with the truth, I would hasten to strike him with the sword before that.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Listen to what your chief says. He is indeed very jealous, and I am more jealous than he, and Allah is more jealous than I."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to rent out a piece of land of his for farming. A man came to him and informed him, on the authority of Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had forbidden renting out farmland. So Ibn ʿUmar went, and I went with him, until he came to him at al-Balāṭ and asked him about that. He informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had forbidden renting out farmland, so ʿAbdullāh gave up renting it out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"If a man sells goods and the buyer goes bankrupt, and the seller has not received any of the price, and he finds his goods exactly as they were, he has a better right to them. If the buyer dies, the owner of the goods is like the other creditors."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to provide us with dates from the jamʿ dates, and we would exchange them for dates that were better than them and add something to the price. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"One ṣāʿ of dates for two ṣāʿs is not permissible, nor one dirham for two dirhams. A dirham is for a dirham and a dinar for a dinar, with no excess between them except by weight."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Gold for gold, whether raw or minted, weight for weight; silver for silver, whether raw or minted, weight for weight; salt for salt, dates for dates, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, like for like, equal for equal. Whoever gives more or asks for more has engaged in ribā."
The wording is Muḥammad's; Yaʿqūb did not mention "barley for barley."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṭāriq
ruled that a ʿumrā gift belongs to the heir, because of the saying of Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man who had killed another man was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the guardian of the slain man took retribution from him. He was led away with a leather strap around his neck, which he was dragging. When he turned away, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The killer and the killed are in the Fire."
A man went to the guardian and told him what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said, so he released him.
Ismāʿīl ibn Sālim said: I mentioned that to Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, and he said: Ibn Ashwaʿ told me that the Prophet ﷺ had only asked him to pardon him, but he refused.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade picking up the lost property of pilgrims.
Aḥmad said: Ibn Wahb said, meaning regarding the lost property of pilgrims, that one should leave it until its owner finds it. Ibn Mawhab related it from ʿAmr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Samurah [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to deliver the sermon standing, then sit, then stand and deliver the sermon standing. So whoever tells you that he used to deliver the sermon sitting has lied. By Allah, I prayed with him more than two thousand prayers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: upon the steps of his pulpit:
"Let people stop neglecting the Friday prayers, or Allah will certainly seal their hearts, and then they will surely be among the heedless."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
delivered a sermon in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been rightly guided, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What a bad speaker you are!
Say: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger.'"
Ibn Numayr said: "has gone astray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I only memorized Qāf from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; he used to recite it in the sermon every Friday. She said: The oven of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and our oven were one. Abū Dāwūd said: Rawḥ ibn ʿUbādah reported from Shuʿbah that he said: the daughter of Ḥārithah ibn al-Nuʿmān. And Ibn Isḥāq said: Umm Hishām, the daughter of Ḥārithah ibn al-Nuʿmān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ruwaybah al-Thaqafī [said]:
[I saw] Bishr ibn Marwān

delivering a sermon, and he raised his hands in supplication. ʿUmārah said: "May Allah disfigure these two short hands! I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do no more than say thus," and Hushaym pointed with his index finger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That when he had prayed the Friday prayer, he would leave and perform two prostrations in his house. Then he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The most truthful—and I thought he meant ʿĀʾishah—[reported] that she said: The sun was eclipsed during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he stood with the people in a very long standing. He stood with the people, then bowed, then stood, then bowed, then stood, then bowed; he bowed twice in each rak'ah, three bowings [in all], bowing the third time, then he prostrated. So much so that some men that day fainted, to the point that buckets of water were poured over them, because of how long he had made them stand. When he bowed he would say: "Allah is the Greatest."
And when he raised his head:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him."
He did not leave until the sun had cleared. Then he stood, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said:

"The sun and the moon are not eclipsed for the death of anyone nor for his life, but they are two signs among the signs of Allah, with which He frightens you. So when they are eclipsed, hasten to the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until they clear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was shooting some arrows of mine in Madinah during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when the sun was eclipsed. So I threw them aside and said: "By Allah, I will surely look at what happens with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the eclipse of the sun." He said: I came to him while he was standing in prayer with his hands raised, glorifying, praising, declaring that there is no god but Allah, declaring Allah's greatness, and supplicating, until the sun cleared.
He said: When it had cleared, he recited two surahs and prayed two rak'ahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stand, so we stood, and he sat, so we sat.
He means: at the funeral.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In his illness in which he died: "Dig a niche-style grave (laḥd) for me and set up bricks over me, just as was done for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd in the land of the Romans, at Rhodes, and a companion of ours died. Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd gave orders concerning his grave, and it was leveled. Then he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ command that graves be leveled."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach them, when they went out to the graveyards, that one of them should say—in the narration of Abū Bakr—"Peace be upon the people of the dwellings," and in the narration of Zuhayr, "Peace be upon you, people of the dwellings, among the believers and the Muslims. And we, if Allah wills, will join you. I ask Allah for well-being for us and for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people—meaning Bedouins—came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Some of the zakāh collectors come to us and wrong us." He said: So he said: "Satisfy your collectors."
They said: "Messenger of Allah, even if they wrong us?" He said: "Satisfy your collectors." ʿUthmān added: "Even if you are wronged."
Abū Kāmil said in his narration: Jarīr said: "No collector has departed from me since I heard this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except that he was pleased with me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Uhud, some of the people were routed away from the Prophet ﷺ, while Abū Ṭalḥah stood in front of the Prophet ﷺ, shielding him with a shield. He said: Abū Ṭalḥah was an archer who drew his bow forcefully, and on that day he broke two or three bows. He said: When a man passed by carrying a quiver of arrows, he would say, "Spill them out for Abū Ṭalḥah."

He said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ would raise himself up to look at the enemy, and Abū Ṭalḥah would say, "O Prophet of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, do not raise yourself up, lest an arrow from the enemy's arrows strike you. My neck is before your neck." He said: And I saw ʿĀʾishah bint Abī Bakr and Umm Sulaym, with their garments tucked up so that I could see the anklets on their legs, carrying water skins on their backs and pouring the water into the mouths of the men; then they would return and fill them, and come back and pour it into the mouths of the men. And the sword fell from Abū Ṭalḥah's hand two or three times because of drowsiness.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Wretched is the slave of the dinar, the dirham, the velvet cloak, and the striped garment:
if he is given, he is pleased,
and if he is not given, he is not pleased."
Isrāʾīl did not narrate it as raised to the Prophet ﷺ from Abū Ḥaṣīn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abū Ṭalḥah: "
Find me one of your boys to serve me."
So Abū Ṭalḥah took me out, having me ride behind him, and I served the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whenever he stopped. In the narration he said: Then he proceeded until Uhud came into view, and he said: "
This is a mountain that loves us and we love it."
When he came in sight of Madinah, he said: "
O Allah, I declare sacred what lies between its two mountains, just as Ibrāhīm declared Makkah sacred. O Allah, bless them in their mudd and their ṣāʿ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

A day of guarding the frontier in the cause of Allah is better than the world and everything in it. The place of one of your whips in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it. And an evening journey or a morning journey that a servant makes in the cause of Allah is better than the world and everything in it."
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī claimed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

A time will come upon the people when an expedition will be sent out from them, and they will say, 'See whether you find among you anyone from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ.' A man will be found, and victory will be opened for them through him. Then a second expedition will be sent, and they will say, 'Is there among them anyone who saw the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ?' and victory will be opened for them through him. Then a third expedition will be sent, and it will be said, 'See whether you find among them anyone who saw those who saw the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ.' Then there will be a fourth expedition, and it will be said, 'See whether you find among them anyone who saw someone who saw those who saw the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ.' A man will be found, and victory will be opened for them through him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A clan of the Arabs, from Abū Ḥāzim,
from Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met the polytheists, and they fought.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned back to his camp and the others turned back to theirs, among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ there was a man who would not leave any straggler of theirs without pursuing him and striking him with his sword. They said, "No one has done as much for us today as so-and-so has done."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Indeed, he is among the people of the Fire."
A man from the people said, "I will be his companion always."

He said: So he went out with him; whenever the man stopped, he stopped with him, and when he hurried, he hurried with him. He said: Then the man was badly wounded and, hastening death, he placed the hilt of his sword on the ground with its point between his breasts, then leaned on his sword and killed himself. Then the other man went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah." He said, "What is that?"

The man said, "The one you mentioned a little while ago as being among the people of the Fire. The people considered that grave, so I said, 'I will find out about him for you.' I went out searching for him until he was badly wounded and, hastening death, he placed the hilt of his sword on the ground with its point between his breasts, then leaned on it and killed himself."
At that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

A man may do the deeds of the people of Paradise, as it appears to the people, while he is among the people of the Fire; and a man may do the deeds of the people of the Fire, as it appears to the people, while he is among the people of Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a military expedition, and we were struck by hardship, so much so that we considered slaughtering some of our riding animals. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ ordered us, so we gathered our provision bags and spread out a leather mat for him, and the people's provisions were gathered on the mat. He said: I stretched up to estimate how much it was, and I estimated it to be like the crouching of a goat, and we were fourteen hundred. He said: We ate until we were all full, then we filled our sacks. Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"Is there any water for ablution?"
He said: A man came with a small water-skin of his that had a little water in it, and he poured it into a bowl. Then all of us, fourteen hundred, performed ablution, pouring the water out freely.
He said: Then after that eight more came and said, "Is there any water for purification?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "The ablution water is finished."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He dictated it to us, dictating it fully. (Transition to another chain.)
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out a commander or a detachment, he would call him and give him instructions.
And he related the hadith similar to the hadith of Sufyān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this [chain].
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this chain of transmission.
And in the hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān there is not [the statement]:
"It will be said: This is the treachery of so-and-so."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "War is deception."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say on the day of Uḥud:
"O Allah, if You will, You will not be worshipped on the earth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
both from Ibn ʿUyaynah,
Yaḥyā said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah informed us, from al-Zuhrī,
from ʿUbaydullāh,
from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Ṣaʿb
ibn Jaththāmah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about the children of the polytheists who are attacked by night, such that their women and children are struck. He said, "They are from them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ: "What if cavalry raided at night and struck some of the children of the polytheists?" He said:
"They are from their fathers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Verses of the Qur'an were revealed concerning him. He said: Sa'd's mother swore that she would never speak to him until he renounced his religion, and that she would neither eat nor drink.
She said: "You claim that Allah has enjoined you to be good to your parents, and I am your mother, and I command you to do this."

He said: She remained like that for three days until she fainted from exhaustion. A son of hers called ʿUmārah got up and gave her a drink, and she began to invoke against Saʿd. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed in the Qur'an this verse: {And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents} {but if they strive to make you associate with Me} and in it: {but accompany them in this world with kindness}. He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ obtained a great deal of spoils, and among them was a sword. I took it and brought it to the Messenger ﷺ and said, "Grant me this sword as an extra share, for you know my situation." He said:
"Return it to where you took it from."
So I went off, until when I was about to throw it down among the spoils, my soul reproached me, so I went back to him and said, "Give it to me."
He said: He raised his voice at me:
"Return it to where you took it from."

He said: Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {They ask you about the spoils of war}. He said: And I became ill, so I sent word to the Prophet ﷺ and he came to me. I said, "Let me divide my wealth as I wish." He refused. I said, "Then half." He refused. I said, "Then a third."
He said: He was silent, and so a third thereafter was permissible.
He said: And I came upon a group of the Anṣār and the Muhājirūn, and they said, "Come, we will feed you and give you wine to drink."

And that was before wine was prohibited. He said: So I went to them in a ḥashsh, meaning a garden, and there was a roasted camel's head with them and a skin of wine. He said: I ate and drank with them. He said: Then the Anṣār and the Muhājirūn were mentioned in their company, and I said, "The Muhājirūn are better than the Anṣār." He said: A man took one of the jawbones of the head and struck me with it, wounding my nose. So I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning me, meaning himself, the matter of wine: {Wine, gambling, idolatrous altars and divining arrows are but an abomination of Satan's work}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I wrote to Nāfiʿ asking him about extra shares of spoils,
and he wrote back to me that... And Ibn Rāfiʿ narrated to us,
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us,
Ibn Jurayj informed us, Mūsā informed me,
and [another chain:] Hārūn ibn Saʿīd al-Aylī narrated to us,
Ibn Wahb narrated to us,
Usāmah ibn Zayd informed me,
all of them from Nāfiʿ,
with this chain, similar to their hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave us an extra share besides our portion of the fifth, and I received a shārif, and a shārif is an old, aged camel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was
a companion in the gathering of Abū Qatādah. He said: Abū Qatādah said. And he related the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he related the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the wives of

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to go out at night, when they relieved themselves, to al-Manāṣiʿ, which is a wide open space. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb used to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "Have your wives veiled."

But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not do so. Then one night, at the time of ʿishāʾ, Sawdah bint Zamʿah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, went out. She was a tall woman, and ʿUmar called out to her, "We have recognized you, O Sawdah!"
He was eager that the verse of the veil be revealed.
ʿĀʾishah said: So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed the verse of the veil.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sawdah went out after the veil had been imposed on her to relieve herself. She was a heavyset woman, taller in build than the other women, and she could not be hidden from anyone who knew her. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb saw her and said, "O Sawdah, by Allah, you are not hidden from us, so see how you go out."

She said: So she turned back, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in my house eating his supper, with a bone with meat in his hand. She entered and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I went out, and ʿUmar said such and such to me."
She said: Then revelation came to him, and when it lifted, the bone was still in his hand; he had not put it down. He said:
"You have been permitted to go out for your needs."
In the narration of Abū Bakr: "She was taller in build than the women."
Abū Bakr added in his narration: Hishām said, meaning, to relieve oneself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar said: I used to spend the night in the mosque during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when I was a young, unmarried man. The dogs used to urinate, and come and go in the mosque, and they did not sprinkle water over any of that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
asked ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān. He said: I said, "What do you think about a man who has intercourse with his wife and does not ejaculate?" ʿUthmān said:
"He performs ablution as he would for prayer and washes his private part."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present when ʿAmr ibn Abī Ḥasan asked ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd about the ablution of the Prophet
ﷺ. He called for a brass basin of water and performed ablution for them.
He tilted it over his hands and washed them three times.
Then he put his hand into the vessel, rinsed his mouth and sniffed water into his nose,
and blew it out, three times, with three handfuls of water.
Then he put his hand into the vessel,
and washed his face three times.
Then he put his hand into the vessel,
and washed his arms up to the elbows, twice each.
Then he put his hand into the vessel,
and wiped his head, moving his hands forward and backward over it.
Then he put his hand into the vessel and washed his feet.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ while he was staying at al-Jiʿrānah, between Makkah and Madinah, and Bilāl was with him. A Bedouin man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "Will you not fulfil for me, O Muḥammad, what you promised me?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Receive glad tidings."
The Bedouin said to him, "You have said 'Receive glad tidings' to me too much."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to Abū Mūsā and Bilāl like one who is angry and said:
"This man has rejected the glad tidings, so you two accept them."
They said, "We accept, O Messenger of Allah."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for a cup containing water, washed his hands and his face in it, and spat into it. Then he said:
"Drink from it, and pour some over your faces and chests, and receive glad tidings."
So they took the cup and did what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had commanded them. Then Umm Salamah called to them from behind the curtain, "Leave some for your mother from what is in your vessel."
So they left a portion of it for her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me while I was ill and not conscious. He performed ablution, and they poured some of his ablution water over me, and I regained consciousness. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, only a kalālah will inherit from me."
Then the verse of inheritance was revealed.
I said to Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, "They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning kalālah." He said, "It was revealed in this way."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) about the mutʿah [ʿUmrah followed by Hajj], and he commanded me to do it.
Then I asked him about the sacrificial animal,
and he said: "For it, a camel, a cow, a sheep, or a share in the blood [of a sacrifice]." He said: Some people disliked it.
Then I slept and saw in a dream as if someone were calling out: "An accepted Hajj and an accepted mutʿah!"

So I went to Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) and told him, and he said: "Allahu Akbar! It is the Sunnah of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ." [The narrator] said: Ādam, Wahb ibn Jarīr and Ghundar reported from Shuʿbah: "an accepted ʿUmrah and an accepted Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Makkah performing tamattuʿ with an ʿUmrah four days before the Day of Tarwiyah. The people said: "Your Hajj has now become a Makkan one." So I went to ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ and asked his ruling. ʿAṭāʾ said: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī (may Allah be pleased with them both) told me that he performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year he brought the sacrificial animal with him, and they had entered ihrām for Hajj alone. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Come out of your state of iḥrām: circle the House and [walk] between Ṣafā and Marwah, shorten your hair, and stay in the state of being lawful until the Day of Tarwiyah; then enter iḥrām for Hajj, and make what you came with an ʿUmrah [of tamattuʿ]."
They said: "How can we make it a tamattuʿ when we have already named it Hajj?" He said:

"Do what I have commanded you. Had I not brought the sacrificial animal, I would have done as I commanded you; but nothing forbidden becomes lawful for me until the sacrificial animal reaches its place of sacrifice." So they did so.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, crying out loudly for Hajj. When we came to Makkah, he commanded us to make it an ʿUmrah, except for those who had brought the sacrificial animal. Then when it was the Day of Tarwiyah and we went out to Minā, we entered iḥrām for Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to her:
"O ʿĀʾishah, were it not that your people are close to the time of ignorance, I would have commanded that the House be demolished,
and I would have included in it what was taken out of it, and made it level with the ground,
and made two doors for it, an eastern door and a western door,
and thus I would have brought it to the foundations of Ibrāhīm."
That is what prompted Ibn al-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them both) to demolish it.
Yazīd said: I was present when Ibn al-Zubayr demolished it and rebuilt it and included part of the Ḥijr in it,
and I saw the foundations of Ibrāhīm: stones like the humps of camels.
Jarīr said: I asked him, "Where is its location?" He said, "I will show you now."
So I entered the Ḥijr with him, and he pointed to a place and said, "Here."
Jarīr said: I estimated it from the Ḥijr to be about six cubits or so.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ʿUmrah, circled the House, and prayed two rakʿahs behind the Maqām,
and with him were people who screened him from the others. A man said to him: "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ enter the Kaʿbah?" He said: "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Makkah, he refused to enter the House while idols were in it, so he commanded that they be taken out. He said: Then they brought out the images of Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl, with divining arrows in their hands. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"May Allah fight them! By Allah, they certainly knew that the two of them never sought to divine with these."
He said: Then he entered the House, said Allahu Akbar in its corners and in its sides, then came out and did not pray in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Perhaps you will live to see people who pray the prayer after its proper time.
If you come across them, then pray in your homes at the time that you know [to be correct],
and then pray with them, and make it a voluntary prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my eyesight has weakened, and the floodwater comes and comes between me and the mosque of my people, and it is difficult for me to cross it. If you see fit, please come to my house and pray in a place that I can take as a place of prayer." He said, "I will do so."
Early the next morning, after the day had grown hot, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me with Abū Bakr. He asked permission to enter and I permitted him, and he did not sit down until he said,
"Where would you like me to pray in your house?"

So I pointed out to him the place where I wanted him to pray. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, we lined up behind him, and he led us in two rakʿahs of prayer. Then I kept him back for a khazīrah (a dish of meat and flour) that was being prepared for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked, "Is there recitation in every prayer?" He said, "Yes."
A man from the Anṣār said, "Then it is obligatory."
He turned to me, and I was the closest of the people to him, and said, "I do not think that when the imam leads the people, he has done anything other than suffice them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to lead us in the Ẓuhr prayer, and we would hear from him a verse here and there from Sūrah Luqmān and Sūrat adh-Dhāriyāt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stood in prayer repeating a single verse until morning came; the verse was: "If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, then indeed You are the Almighty, the All-Wise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to hear the recitation of the Prophet ﷺ at night while I was on my bed made of palm branches.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī said: "I had two times of entering upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: one entry at night and one entry during the day. When I entered at night, he would clear his throat for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you is in doubt about his prayer, let him aim for what he thinks is correct, complete [the prayer] accordingly, and then perform two prostrations."
And I did not understand some of its words as I wished.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to deliver the sermon standing, then he would sit,
then he would stand and recite some verses
and mention Allah. His sermon was moderate, and his prayer was moderate.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar said: "The Friday prayer is two rakʿahs, the prayer of al-Fiṭr is two rakʿahs, the prayer of al-Aḍḥā is two rakʿahs, and the travel prayer is two rakʿahs, complete and not shortened, in the words of Muḥammad ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man said] to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, "We find the prayer of the resident and the prayer of fear in the Qur'an, but we do not find the travel prayer in the Qur'an."
Ibn ʿUmar said to him, "O son of my brother, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent Muḥammad ﷺ to us when we knew nothing, so we only do as we saw Muḥammad ﷺ do."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Abū Kāhil, who had been a Companion, and my brother narrated to me,
from him, that he said: "I saw the Prophet ﷺ delivering a sermon on a she-camel, with an Abyssinian man holding her reins."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
used to spend the night at the door of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he would hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say during the night:
"Glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."
[This continued] for a long while, then he would say:
"Glory be to Allah and with His praise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray eight rakʿahs at night, pray Witr with three, and pray two rakʿahs before the Fajr prayer.
ʿAmr ibn Murrah differed with him and narrated it from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from Umm Salamah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray Witr with seven or with five, not separating between them with a salutation [of tasleem] or speech.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "

Whoever goes to his bed intending to get up to pray during the night, but sleep overcomes him until morning, what he intended will be recorded for him, and his sleep will be charity (ṣadaqah) for him from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic." Sufyān differed with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man died in Madinah who had been born in Madinah, and the Prophet ﷺ prayed over him and said: "
If only he had died somewhere other than his birthplace."
A man among the people said, "Why, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "
When a man dies somewhere other than his birthplace, a space is measured for him in Paradise from his birthplace to the end of his footsteps."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, and we mentioned a hadith from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd,
so he said: I will never cease to love that man after something I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I heard him say:
"Take the Qur'an from four: from Ibn Umm ʿAbd"—and he began with him—"and from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, from Sālim the freed slave of Abū Hudhayfah, and from Muʿādh ibn Jabal."
And there is a phrase that Zuhayr did not mention: his words "he said it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He was] giving a sermon before Ibn ʿUtbah, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of the houses of the Anṣār is the house of Banū al-Najjār, then the house of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal, then the house of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, then the house of Banū Sāʿidah."
By Allah, if I were to give preference to anyone with it, I would have given preference to my own clan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Uḥud is a mountain that loves us and we love it, and it stands upon one of the gates of Paradise; and ʿAyr stands upon one of the gates of the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he freed Ṣafiyyah and made her freedom her dowry.
And in the hadith of Muʿādh, from his father: He married Ṣafiyyah and made her freedom her dowry.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of the Conquest, on a she-camel of his, reciting Sūrat al-Fatḥ,
or part of Sūrat al-Fatḥ. He said: He recited it with a lilting repetition. He said: Then Muʿāwiyah recited, imitating the recitation of Ibn Mughaffal, and said:
"Were it not that people would gather around you, I would recite with repetition just as Ibn Mughaffal did."
He was imitating the Prophet ﷺ. I said to Muʿāwiyah: How was his repetition? He said: "Ā, ā, ā," three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Will you not relieve me of Dhū al-Khalaṣah?" I said: Yes.
So I set out with one hundred and fifty horsemen from Aḥmas, who were skilled horsemen, and I could not stay firm on horses,
so I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he struck his hand on my chest until I saw the mark of his hand on my chest, and he said:
"O Allah, make him steadfast, and make him a guide, rightly guided."
He said: I never fell from a horse after that.
He said: Dhū al-Khalaṣah was a house in Yemen belonging to Khathʿam and Bajīlah,
in which there were idols that were worshipped,
and it was called the Kaʿbah.
He said: So he went to it, burned it with fire, and broke it down.

He said: When Jarīr arrived in Yemen, there was a man there who would seek decisions by divining arrows, and it was said to him: The messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is here; if he gets hold of you, he will strike your neck.
He said: While he was casting them, Jarīr stood over him and said: You will break them and testify that there is no god but Allah, or I will strike your neck.
He said: So he broke them and testified.
Then Jarīr sent a man from Aḥmas, called Abū Arṭāh, to the Prophet ﷺ to give him the good news of that,
and when he came to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: O Messenger of Allah, by the One who sent you with the truth, I did not come until I had left it like a mangy camel.
He said: So the Prophet ﷺ blessed the horses of Aḥmas and its men five times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qatādah asked Anas which supplication the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made most often. He said: The supplication he made most often was:
"O Allah, our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."
Ziyād added: And whenever Anas wanted to make a supplication, he made this one, and whenever he wanted to make another supplication, he included this in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When it was revealed: {Not equal are those of the believers who sit [at home] and those who strive in the cause of Allah}, the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Call Zayd for me, and let him bring the tablet, the inkwell, and the shoulder blade"—or: "the shoulder blade and the inkwell"—then he said:
"Write: Not equal are those who sit."

Behind the back of the Prophet ﷺ was ʿAmr ibn Umm Maktūm, the blind man. He said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you command me, for I am a man with impaired sight? So in its place was revealed: {Not equal are those of the believers who sit} in the cause of Allah {except those with a disability}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Who will deal with Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf? For he has harmed Allah and His Messenger."
So Muḥammad ibn Maslamah stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, do you want me to kill him?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "Then permit me to say something." He said, "Say it."
So Muḥammad ibn Maslamah came to him and said, "This man has asked us for charity,
and he has burdened us,
and I have come to you to borrow from you."
He said, "And moreover, by Allah, you will grow weary of him!" He said, "We have followed him, and we do not like to leave him until we see what his affair will come to.
We would like you to lend us a wasq,
or two wasqs." And ʿAmr narrated to us more than once,
and he did not mention a wasq or two wasqs; or I said to him, "In it is a wasq or two wasqs?" He said, "I think it has a wasq or two wasqs." He said, "Yes, give me a pledge."
They said, "What do you want?" He said, "Give me your women as a pledge."
They said, "How can we pledge our women to you when you are the most handsome of the Arabs?" He said, "Then give me your sons as a pledge."
They said, "How can we pledge our sons to you? One of them would be insulted,
and it would be said, 'He was pledged for a wasq or two wasqs.'
That would be a disgrace to us,
but we will pledge you the weapons (Sufyān said: meaning arms)." So he promised him that he would come to him,
and he came to him at night, with Abū Nāʾilah, who was Kaʿb's foster brother,
and he called them to the fortress,
and he came down to them. His wife said to him, "Where are you going at this hour?" He said, "It is only Muḥammad ibn Maslamah,
and my brother Abū Nāʾilah." Someone other than ʿAmr said: She said, "I hear a voice as if blood were dripping from it."

He said, "It is only my brother Muḥammad ibn Maslamah and my foster brother Abū Nāʾilah. A noble man, if called to a stabbing at night, would answer." He said: And Muḥammad ibn Maslamah entered with two men. (It was said to Sufyān, "Did ʿAmr name them?" He said, "He named some of them." ʿAmr said, "He came with two men." Someone other than ʿAmr said: Abū ʿAbs ibn Jabr,
al-Ḥārith ibn Aws, and ʿAbbād ibn Bishr. ʿAmr said: He came with two men.) He said, "When he comes, I will take hold of his hair and smell it,
and when you see that I have got a firm hold of his head, then go for him and strike him."
And once he said, "Then I will let you smell it."
So he came down to them wrapped in his garment, with the fragrance of perfume wafting from him,

and he said, "I have never smelled a scent like today's" (meaning, more pleasant). Someone other than ʿAmr said: He said, "I have with me the most perfumed of the women of the Arabs and the most complete of the Arabs." ʿAmr said: He said, "Do you permit me to smell your head?" He said, "Yes." So he smelled it,
then he let his companions smell it. Then he said, "Do you permit me?" He said, "Yes."
And when he had a firm hold of him, he said, "Take him!"
So they killed him, then they came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

Whoever frees his share of a slave owned jointly between him and another, the slave is to be valued for him at his fair price from his wealth, without undervaluing or overvaluing; then the slave is freed on his account from his wealth, if he is well-off."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ṣirmah and I entered upon Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, and Abū Ṣirmah asked him, saying, "O Abū Saʿīd, did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mention withdrawal (ʿazl)?" He said, "Yes. We went on the expedition of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and took captive some of the noblest of the Arabs. Our abstinence became long, and we desired ransom, so we wanted to enjoy them and practice withdrawal. We said, 'Shall we do it while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is among us, without asking him?'
So we asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "
It does not matter if you do not do it; for Allah has not decreed the creation of any soul that is to exist until the Day of Resurrection except that it will come into being."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My mother came to me while she was a polytheist, in the time of the treaty with Quraysh,
when they had made a treaty with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and for their term, along with her father,
so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a ruling, saying, "O Messenger of Allah,
my mother has come to me, and she desires [my help]. Should I maintain ties with her?" He said, "Yes, maintain ties with her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ we used to take land [to farm] for a third or a quarter, [in return for the produce of] the water channels. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up concerning that and said: "
Whoever has land, let him cultivate it; if he does not cultivate it, let him lend it to his brother; and if he does not lend it to his brother, let him keep it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was a man from Basra. He said: I asked ʿĀʾishah about the Witr prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, how he used to pray Witr, at the beginning of the night or at its end. She said: He did all of that. Sometimes he prayed Witr at the beginning of the night, and sometimes at the end of it.

I said: Praise be to Allah, who has made room in the matter. I said: How was his recitation? Did he recite quietly or aloud? She said: He did all of that; sometimes he recited quietly and sometimes aloud. I said: Praise be to Allah, who has made room in the matter. I said: And what did he do when in a state of major impurity? Did he wash before sleeping, or sleep before washing? She said: He did all of that; sometimes he washed and then slept, and sometimes he performed ablution and then slept. I said: Praise be to Allah, who has made room in the matter.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥumayḍah bint Yāsir, from her grandmother,
Yusayrah, who was one of the female emigrants, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:

"Hold fast to glorifying Allah (tasbīḥ), declaring His oneness (tahlīl), and sanctifying Him (taqdīs), and count on your fingertips, for they will be questioned and made to speak. And do not be heedless, lest you forget [Allah's] mercy."
He said: This hadith is gharīb; we only know it from the narration of Hāniʾ ibn ʿUthmān. Muḥammad ibn Rabīʿah also narrated it from Hāniʾ ibn ʿUthmān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: For Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq, from Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq,
he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"One who seeks forgiveness has not persisted [in sin], even if he returns to it seventy times in a day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever intends to perform Hajj should hasten, for a sick person may fall ill, a mount may go astray, and a need may arise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set the miqāt for the people of Madinah at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, for the people of Syria and Egypt at al-Juḥfah, for the people of Iraq at Dhāt ʿIrq, for the people of Najd at Qarn, and for the people of Yemen at Yalamlam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never failed to touch the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone in every circuit. He said: And ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar used to do the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Abū Hind
cupped the Prophet ﷺ on the crown of his head, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"O Banū Bayāḍah, marry Abū Hind [to your women] and seek marriage from him." He said:
"If there is any good in what you use for treatment, it is in cupping."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was a guest of ʿUmar one night. In the middle of the night he got up and went to his wife and began to hit her, so I intervened between them. When he went back to his bed, he said to me: O Ashʿath, remember from me something I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
"A man is not to be asked why he hit his wife, and do not sleep except after praying Witr." And I forgot the third.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to live in Īliyā. He said: I went out with ʿAdī ibn ʿAdī al-Kindī until we reached Makkah, and he sent me to Ṣafiyyah bint Shaybah, who had memorized [hadith] from ʿĀʾishah. She said: I heard ʿĀʾishah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"There is no divorce and no manumission in ighlāq."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding the saying of Allah: {We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten except that We bring forth one better than it or similar to it}, and He said: {And when We substitute one verse in place of another, and Allah knows best what He sends down} the verse, and He said: {Allah erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book}. The first thing abrogated of the Qur'an was the direction of prayer (qiblah). And He said: {Divorced women shall wait for three periods, and it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs} up to His saying {if they desire reconciliation}. That is because when a man divorced his wife, he had more right to take her back, even if he had divorced her three times; so that was abrogated, and He said: {Divorce is twice, then either retention in a proper manner or release with kindness}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "

When you send out your dog, mention the name of Allah. If it catches [game] for you and you reach it alive, slaughter it. If you reach it after it has been killed and the dog has not eaten from it, then eat it. If you find another dog with your dog and the game has been killed, do not eat, for you do not know which of them killed it. And if you shoot your arrow, mention the name of Allah. If it is gone from you for a day and you find nothing on it except the mark of your arrow, then eat if you wish. But if you find it drowned in water, do not eat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the Mothers of the Believers had a sheep, and it died. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by it and said: "
What harm would it have done its owners if they had made use of its hide?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: He said that he

entered with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith, who was his maternal aunt. Roasted lizard meat was presented to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not eat anything until he knew what it was. Some of the women said: "Will you not tell the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what he is about to eat?" So they told him it was lizard meat, and he left it. Khālid said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "Is it forbidden?" He said: "
No, but it is food that is not found in the land of my people, and I find that I dislike it."
Khālid said: So I drew it toward me and ate it while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was looking on.
Ibn al-Aṣamm also narrated to him from Maymūnah, as he was in her care.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ distributed sacrificial animals among his Companions, and he gave me a young goat that was a year old. He said: I returned to him with it and said to him, "It is only a jadhaʿ." He said: "Sacrifice it." So I sacrificed it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to sacrifice two horned rams, mostly white with some black, and he would mention Allah's name and say the takbīr. I saw him slaughter them with his own hand, placing his foot on their sides.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood on the day of al-Aḍḥā and said: "
Whoever faces our qiblah, prays our prayer, and performs our rite of sacrifice, let him not slaughter until he has prayed."
Then my maternal uncle stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I hastened my sacrifice in order to feed my family and the people of my household," or he said, "my family and my neighbors."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Slaughter another animal."
He said: "I have a milk-fed young female goat that is dearer to me than two sheep for meat." He said: "
Slaughter it, for it is the better of your two sacrifices. But a jadhaʿah will not suffice on behalf of anyone after you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sacrificed two horned rams, mostly white with some black. He slaughtered them with his own hand, mentioned Allah's name, said the takbīr, and placed his foot on their sides.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was serving drink to Abū Ṭalḥah, Abū Dujānah, and Muʿādh ibn Jabal among a group of the Anṣār, when someone came in to us and said: "News has occurred: the prohibition of wine has been revealed."
That sufficed us that day, and it was a mixture of unripe dates and ripe dates.
Qatādah said: Anas ibn Mālik said: Wine was prohibited, and most of their wine at that time was a mixture of unripe dates and ripe dates.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade [the use of certain] containers, the Anṣār complained and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have no [other] vessel." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Then [it is] not [forbidden] now."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade drinking directly from the mouth of a waterskin, and riding the jallālah [animal that feeds on filth], and [eating] the mujaththamah [an animal bound and used as a target].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥudhayfah was in al-Madāʾin and asked for a drink. A village chief came to him with a silver vessel, and he threw it at him and said: "I would not have thrown it at him except that I had forbidden him and he did not stop. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade silk and brocade, and drinking from vessels of gold and silver, and he said: "
They are for them in this world, and for you in the Hereafter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: "I never saw a man whose pain was more severe than that of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
In the narration of ʿUthmān, [the word] waja' is replaced by wajaʿan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ. And Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah and ʿAmr al-Nāqid narrated to us,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
and Ibn Abī ʿUmar,
they said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us,
and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us,
ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us,
and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Dārimī narrated to us,
Abū al-Yamān informed us: Shuʿayb informed us,
all of them from al-Zuhrī,
from Abū Salamah,
from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ,
similar to the hadith of ʿUqayl. In the narration of Sufyān and Yūnus [it says] "the black seed."
He did not say "shūnīz."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed {And warn your closest kinsmen}, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up and said:
"O company of Quraysh" — or words like these — "buy yourselves [from the Fire].
I cannot avail you anything against Allah.
O Banū ʿAbd Manāf, I cannot avail you anything against Allah.
O ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah.
O Ṣafiyyah, paternal aunt of the Messenger of Allah, I cannot avail you anything against Allah.
And O Fāṭimah, daughter of Muhammad, ask me for whatever you wish of my wealth, but I cannot avail you anything against Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [This was] read to him while I listened,
from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah laughs at two men, one of whom kills the other, [yet] both enter Paradise: this one fights in the cause of Allah and is killed; then Allah turns in mercy to the killer, so he fights and is martyred."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade traveling with the Qurʾān to the land of the enemy.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never turned me away since I accepted Islam, and he never saw me except that he smiled in my face.
Ibn Numayr added in his narration from Ibn Idrīs: I complained to him that I could not stay firm on horses, so he struck my chest with his hand and said:
"O Allah, make him steadfast, and make him one who guides and is guided."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Abū Mūsā, and between us and this clan of Jarm there was brotherhood and goodwill. He said: Food was brought, and in his food there was chicken meat. He said: Among the people was a man of Banū Taym Allāh, reddish in complexion, as if he were a freed slave. He said: He did not come near, so Abū Mūsā said to him, "Come closer,
for I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eating from it."
He said: "I saw it eating something that I found filthy,
so I swore that I would never eat it."
He said: "Come closer and I will tell you about that.
We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a group of the Ashʿarīs asking him for mounts,
while he was distributing some camels from the charity camels." Ayyūb said: I think he said that he was angry. He said:
"By Allah, I will not provide you with mounts,
and I do not have anything with which to provide you."
He said: "So we left. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought some plundered camels,
and it was asked, 'Where are those Ashʿarīs?' So we came, and he ordered for us five white-humped camels.
He said: We set off, and I said to my companions: 'We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him for mounts,
and he swore that he would not provide us with mounts,
then he sent for us and provided us.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forgot his oath.
By Allah, if we take advantage of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being unmindful of his oath, we will never succeed.
Return with us to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that we may remind him of his oath.'
So we returned and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we came to you asking for mounts,
and you swore that you would not provide us, then you provided us, so we thought' — or 'we knew' — 'that you had forgotten your oath.' He said: 'Go,
for it is Allah who has provided for you.
As for me, by Allah, if Allah wills, I never swear an oath
and then see something else to be better than it,
except that I do what is better and absolve myself of the oath.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: [From ʿĀʾishah,] the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that she said: When the wind blew violently, the Prophet ﷺ would say:

"O Allah, I ask You for its good, the good of what is in it, and the good of what it was sent with; and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil of what is in it, and the evil of what it was sent with."

She said: And when the sky became overcast, his color would change, and he would go out and come in, and go forward and backward; then when it rained, it would be lifted from him, and I could recognize that in his face.
ʿĀʾishah said: So I asked him, and he said:
"Perhaps, O ʿĀʾishah, it is as the people of ʿĀd said: {Then when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, 'This is a cloud bringing us rain.'}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to observe iʿtikāf, he would pray the Fajr prayer and then enter his place of seclusion.
She said: Once he wished to observe iʿtikāf during the last ten days of Ramadan.
She said: He ordered that his tent be set up, and it was pitched. When I saw that, I ordered that my tent be set up, and it was pitched.
She said: Other wives of the Prophet ﷺ also ordered their tents to be set up, and they were pitched. When he had prayed Fajr, he looked at the tents and said:
"What is this? Is it piety that you intend?"

She said: Then he ordered his tent to be taken down, and it was taken down, and he ordered his wives' tents and they were taken down. Then he postponed the iʿtikāf to the first ten days, meaning of Shawwāl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the narration of Manṣūr from al-Ḥakam: Al-Ṣaʿb ibn Jaththāmah gave the Prophet ﷺ the leg of a wild donkey as a gift.
And in the narration of Shuʿbah from al-Ḥakam: the hindquarter of a wild donkey, dripping with blood.
And in the narration of Shuʿbah from Ḥabīb: A side of a wild donkey was given as a gift to the Prophet ﷺ, and he returned it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the wild donkey.
It is like the hadith of Abū al-Naḍr, except that in the hadith of Zayd ibn Aslam, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you have any of its meat with you?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh while we were in iḥrām, and a bird was given to him as a gift while Ṭalḥah was asleep. Some of us ate it and some of us abstained. When Ṭalḥah woke up, he approved of those who had eaten it and said: We ate it with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with them both: Ḍubāʿah
wished to perform Hajj, so the Prophet ﷺ commanded her to stipulate a condition, and she did that on the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, arriving at the time of the new moon of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, intending only Hajj. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever among you wishes to enter iḥrām for ʿUmrah, let him do so for ʿUmrah."
And he narrated the rest of the hadith like the hadith of ʿAbdah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We entered iḥrām with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for Hajj. When we reached Makkah, he commanded us to leave iḥrām and make it ʿUmrah. That was hard on us and our hearts were constrained by it. This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and we do not know whether something reached him from the heavens or something from the people. He said:
"O people, leave iḥrām. Were it not for the sacrificial animals I have with me, I would have done as you have done."
He said: So we left iḥrām, until we had relations with our wives and did what a person not in iḥrām does, until the Day of Tarwiyah, when we left Makkah behind us and entered iḥrām for Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was camped at al-Baṭḥāʾ. He said to me, "Have you performed Hajj?" I said, "Yes." He said, "With what intention did you enter iḥrām?"
He said: I said, "I responded, with an intention like the intention of the Prophet ﷺ." He said:
"You have done well. Circle the House, and go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and leave iḥrām."
He said: So I circled the House and went between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, then I came to a woman of Banū Qays, who combed my hair, and then I entered iḥrām for Hajj.

He said: I used to give people rulings on this until the caliphate of ʿUmr, may Allah be pleased with him. A man said to him: O Abū Mūsā, or O ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays, go easy with some of your rulings, for you do not know what the Commander of the Faithful has introduced regarding the rites after you.
He said: O people, whoever we have given a ruling to, let him wait, for the Commander of the Faithful is coming to you, so follow him.

He said: Then ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, came, and I mentioned that to him.
