He said: If we follow the Book of Allah, the Book of Allah commands completion; and if we follow the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not leave iḥrām until the sacrificial animal reached its place of sacrifice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Hajj tamattuʿ was specifically for the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding Hajj tamattuʿ: It is not for you, and you have no part in it. It was only a concession for us, the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, and I said: I have intended to combine Hajj and ʿUmrah this year.
Ibrāhīm said: If your father were here, he would not have intended that.
He said: And Ibrāhīm al-Taymī said, from his father, from Abū Dharr, who said: Tamattuʿ was only for us specifically.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the two of them
witnessed Abū Burdah narrating to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from his father,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"No Muslim man dies except that Allah will put in his place a Jew or a Christian in the Fire."

He said: So ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz made him swear three times by Allah, besides Whom there is no god, that his father had narrated it to him from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he swore to him. [The narrator] said: Saʿīd did not tell me that he had made him swear, and ʿAwn did not object to what I said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the Day of Resurrection, some of the Muslims will come with sins like mountains, and Allah will forgive them and place them upon the Jews and the Christians."
This is what I think [he said].
Abū Rawḥ said: I do not know which of them had the doubt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on the expedition of Tabūk, intending the Romans and the Christians of the Arabs in Syria.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Kaʿb—who was Kaʿb's guide when he lost his sight, and who was the most knowledgeable of his people and the best preserver of the hadith of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—said: I heard my father Kaʿb ibn Mālik, one of the three whose repentance was accepted, narrate that he never stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in any expedition he undertook, except two expeditions.
And he related the hadith, and said in it: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on expedition with a great many people, numbering more than ten thousand, whom no written register could encompass.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that a man
was accused regarding the concubine of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAlī:
"Go and strike off his neck."
ʿAlī came to him and found him in a well, cooling himself in it. ʿAlī said to him, "Come out."

He gave him his hand and brought him out, and it turned out that he was castrated and had no male organ. So ʿAlī held back from him, then came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, he is castrated; he has no male organ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl died, his son ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him to give him his shirt in which to shroud his father, and he gave it to him. Then he asked him to pray over him, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up to pray over him. ʿUmar stood up and took hold of the garment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, will you pray over him when Allah has forbidden you to pray over him? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah gave me a choice and said: 'Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times...' and I will increase beyond seventy."
He said: "He is a hypocrite."
Yet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over him, and then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {And never pray over any of them who has died, and do not stand at his grave}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ went out to Uḥud, and some of the people who were with him turned back. The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ were divided about them into two groups; some of them said, "We should kill them."
And some of them said, "No."
So it was revealed: {What is the matter with you that you are two groups concerning the hypocrites?}
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said to ʿAmmār: Tell us about your fighting—was it an opinion you formed, for opinion may err or be right, or was it a covenant the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made with you? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not make any covenant with us that he did not make with all the people.
And he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Among my nation..."
Shuʿbah said: I think he said: Ḥudhayfah narrated to me.
And Ghundar said: I think he said:

"Among my nation are twelve hypocrites who will not enter Paradise and will not even smell its fragrance until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. Eight of them will be dealt with by the dubaylah, a lamp of fire that will appear on their shoulders until it comes out from their chests."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was between a man from the people of al-ʿAqabah and Ḥudhayfah some of what occurs between people. He said: I ask you by Allah, how many were the people of al-ʿAqabah? The people said to him, "Tell him, since he has asked you." He said: We were told that they were fourteen; if you are one of them, then the group was fifteen. And I bear witness by Allah that twelve of them are at war with Allah and His Messenger in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand, and three were excused; they said, "We did not hear the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we did not know what the people intended."
He had been on rocky ground, and he walked and said:
"The water is little, so let no one get to it before me."
Then he found some people who had reached it before him, and he cursed them that day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was on one of his military expeditions, and Allah granted him spoils of war. He said to his Companions, "
Are you missing anyone?"
They said, "Yes, so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so." Then he said, "
Are you missing anyone?"
They said, "Yes, so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so." Then he said, "
Are you missing anyone?" They said, "No." He said, "
But I am missing Julaybīb, so look for him."
So he was searched for among the slain, and they found him beside seven [men] whom he had killed before they killed him. The Prophet ﷺ came, stood over him, and said, "
He killed seven, then they killed him. This one is from me, and I am from him. This one is from me, and I am from him."
He said: Then he placed him upon his forearms, and he had nothing but the forearms of the Prophet ﷺ [to carry him]. He said: A grave was dug for him and he was placed in his grave.
He did not mention any washing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Dharr said: We set out from our people, Ghifār, who used to treat the sacred month as lawful. My brother Unays and I and our mother went out, and we stayed with a maternal uncle of ours. Our uncle honored us and treated us well, but his people envied us and said, "Whenever you go away from your family, Unays goes to them secretly." Our uncle came and reproached us with what had been said to him. I said to him, "As for the kindness you showed before, you have muddied it, and we can no longer keep company with you after this."

So we brought our herd of camels near and loaded our belongings onto them, while our uncle covered himself with his garment and began to weep. We set out until we stopped near Makkah. Unays competed in a poetry contest over our herd and the like of it, and they went to a soothsayer, who judged in favor of Unays. So Unays came to us with our herd and the like of it with it. He said: And I had prayed, O son of my brother, three years before I met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
I said, "For whom did you pray?" He said, "For Allah."

I said, "And in which direction did you face?" He said, "I faced wherever my Lord directed me. I would pray the night prayer, and when it was the end of the night, I would fall down like a cloak until the sun rose over me."
Unays said, "I have a need in Makkah, so take care of [things] for me."

So Unays went until he reached Makkah and was late in returning to me. Then he came, and I said, "What did you do?" He said, "I met a man in Makkah who follows your religion and claims that Allah sent him."
I said, "And what do the people say?" He said, "They say he is a poet, a soothsayer, a sorcerer."
And Unays was one of the poets.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Dharr said: O son of my brother, I prayed for two years before the Prophet ﷺ was sent.
He said: I said, "And in which direction did you face?" He said, "Wherever Allah directed me."
And he related the hadith similar to the hadith of Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah, and said in the hadith: They two went to compete before a man from among the soothsayers.
He said: My brother Unays kept praising him until he prevailed over him. He said: Then we took his herd and added it to our herd.

And he also said in his narration: He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ came, circled the House, and prayed two rakʿahs behind the Maqām. He said: I came to him, and I was the first of people to greet him with the greeting of Islam. He said: I said, "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "
And upon you be peace. Who are you?"
And in his narration also: He said, "
Since when have you been here?"
He said: I said, "For fifteen [days]."
And in it: Abū Bakr said, "Grant me the honor of hosting him tonight."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to spend the night in the mosque, and I had no family. Then I saw in a dream as if I was being taken to a well.
Then he related from the Prophet ﷺ with the meaning of the hadith of az-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My mother, Umm Anas, brought me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She had wrapped me in half of her headscarf and covered me with the other half. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is my son Unays. I have brought him to you to serve you, so supplicate to Allah for him." He said, "
O Allah, increase his wealth and his children."
Anas said: By Allah, my wealth is indeed great, and my children and my children's children today number about one hundred.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The same as that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me while I was playing with the boys. He said: He greeted us with peace and sent me on an errand, so I was late returning to my mother. When I came, she said, "What kept you?" I said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me on an errand."
She said, "What was his errand?" I said, "It is a secret."
She said, "Do not tell anyone the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
Anas said: By Allah, if I had told anyone of it, I would have told you, O Thābit.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In this chain of transmission, and he said: She said, "He used to defend the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
And he did not mention "Ḥaṣān Razān."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Maqburī,
from ʿUbayd ibn Juraij,
that he said to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both: "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, I have seen you do four things that I have not seen any of your companions do."

He said: "What are they, O Ibn Juraij?" He said: "I saw that you touch none of the corners [of the Kaʿbah] except the two Yemeni ones; I saw you wear tanned leather sandals; I saw you dye [your clothes] with yellow; and I saw that when you were in Makkah, the people would start the talbiyah when they saw the new moon, but you did not do so until the Day of Tarwiyah."

ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: "As for the corners, I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ touch any except the two Yemeni ones. As for the tanned sandals, I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wear sandals that had no hair on them and perform ablution while wearing them, so I like to wear them. As for the yellow, I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dye with it, so I like to dye with it. And as for the talbiyah, I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ start it until his mount set off with him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a delegation
of Thaqīf asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: "Our land is a cold land, so what about the ritual bath?" He said:
"As for me, I pour water over my head three times."
Ibn Sālim said in his narration: Hushaym narrated to us, Abū Bishr informed us, and he said: The delegation of Thaqīf said, "O Messenger of Allah,
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ met me on one of the roads of Madīnah while I was in a state of major ritual impurity, so I slipped away, went and bathed, and then came back. He said:
"Where were you, O Abū Hurayrah?"
I said: "I was in a state of major impurity and disliked sitting with you without being purified." He said:
"Glory be to Allah! The believer does not become impure."
And in the narration of Bishr he said: Ḥumayd narrated to us, Bakr narrated to me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with ʿAbdullāh and Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, and Abū Mūsā said to him: "If a man were in a state of major impurity
and did not find water for a month,

would he not perform tayammum and pray? What then would you do about this verse in Sūrat al-Māʾidah: {and you do not find water, then seek clean earth}?" ʿAbdullāh said: "If they were given this concession, they would soon, when the water was cold for them, resort to tayammum with earth."
I said: "Was it for this reason that you disliked it?" He said: "Yes."
Abū Mūsā said: "Did you not hear ʿAmmār's words to ʿUmar: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me on an errand and I became impure,
and I could not find water,
so I rolled in the earth as an animal rolls,
and I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"It would have been enough for you to do like this."
Then he struck the ground once with his palm, shook it off,
then wiped with it the back of his hand with his left,
or the back of his left with his palm,

then wiped his face with both.'" ʿAbdullāh said: "Did you not see that ʿUmar was not satisfied with ʿAmmār's statement?" Yaʿlā added, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq: I was with ʿAbdullāh and Abū Mūsā, and Abū Mūsā said: "Did you not hear ʿAmmār's words to ʿUmar: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me and you, and I became impure and rolled in the earth,
then we came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him, and he said:
"It would have been enough for you to do like this."
And he wiped his face and his hands once."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib,
from Abū Hurayrah, that a questioner
asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about praying in a single garment, and he said: "Does each of you have two garments?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: [She,] the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray on a small mat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Dīnār,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray on his mount in whatever direction it was facing.
ʿAbdullāh ibn Dīnār said: Ibn ʿUmar used to do the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
entered Medina and found a man around whom people had gathered. He asked, "Who is this?" They said, "Abū Hurayrah."

So I approached him until I sat before him while he was speaking to the people. When he fell silent and was alone, I said to him, "I ask you by the right of Allah, and by the right [of what is due], to narrate to me a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which you understood and knew."
Abū Hurayrah said, "I will. I will narrate to you a hadith that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to me, which I understood and knew."

Then Abū Hurayrah gasped sharply, remained a little while, then recovered and said, "I will narrate to you a hadith that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to me in this house, where no one was with us but me and him."

Then Abū Hurayrah gasped sharply again, then recovered and wiped his face and said, "I will narrate to you a hadith that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to me while he and I were in this house, where no one was with us but me and him."

Then Abū Hurayrah gasped sharply once more, then recovered and wiped his face and said, "I will. I will narrate to you a hadith that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to me while I was with him in this house, where no one was with him but me and him."

Then Abū Hurayrah gasped violently, then leaned and fell on his face. I supported him against me for a long while, then he recovered and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to me that when it is the Day of Resurrection, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will descend to the servants to judge between them, and every nation will be kneeling. The first to be called will be a man who memorized the Qur'an, a man who was killed in the cause of Allah, and a man of great wealth. Allah will say to the reciter, "Did I not teach you what I revealed to My Messenger?" He will say, "Yes, my Lord."
He will say, "Then what did you do with what you were taught?" He will say, "I would stand with it during the hours of the night and the hours of the day."
Allah will say to him, "You have lied," and the angels will say to him, "You have lied." Allah will say, "Rather, you wanted it to be said, 'So-and-so is a reciter,' and that was said."
Then the owner of wealth will be brought, and Allah will say to him, "Did I not give you abundance until I left you in need of no one?" He will say, "Yes, my Lord."
He will say, "Then what did you do with what I gave you?" He will say, "I maintained family ties and gave charity."
Allah will say to him, "You have lied," and the angels will say to him, "You have lied." Allah, Exalted, will say, "Rather, you wanted it to be said, 'So-and-so is generous,' and that was said."

Then the one who was killed in the cause of Allah will be brought, and Allah will say to him, "For what were you killed?" He will say, "I was commanded to strive in Your cause, so I fought until I was killed."
Allah, Exalted, will say to him, "You have lied," and the angels will say to him, "You have lied." Allah will say, "Rather, you wanted it to be said, 'So-and-so is courageous,' and that was said."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck my knee and said:
"O Abū Hurayrah, those three are the first of Allah's creation with whom the Fire will be kindled on the Day of Resurrection."
Al-Walīd Abū ʿUthmān said: ʿUqbah ibn Muslim informed me that Shufayy was the one who went in to Muʿāwiyah and informed him of this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Trials will continue to befall the believing man and the believing woman in their person, their children, and their wealth, until they meet Allah with no sin upon them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed Allah says: When I take away the two dearest things of My servant in the world, he will have no reward with Me except Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"On the Day of Resurrection, when the people of affliction are given their reward, the people of well-being will wish that their skins had been cut with scissors in the world."
This is a gharīb hadith; we do not know it with this chain except through this route.
Some of them narrated this hadith from al-Aʿmash, from Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif, from Masrūq, as his own statement, something like this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no one who dies but that he will regret."
They said, "And what is his regret, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"If he was a doer of good, he will regret that he did not do more; and if he was a wrongdoer, he will regret that he did not desist."
label: machine translation

segments_en: To his father: "Father, I hear you every morning supplicating: 'O Allah, grant me well-being in my body. O Allah, grant me well-being in my hearing. O Allah, grant me well-being in my sight. There is no god but You,' repeating it three times when you rise in the morning and three times when you reach the evening."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It reached him that when the Prophet ﷺ saw the new moon, he would say:
"A moon of goodness and right guidance; a moon of goodness and right guidance; a moon of goodness and right guidance. I believe in the One who created you," three times. Then he would say:
"Praise be to Allah, who has taken away such-and-such month and brought such-and-such month."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw the new moon, he would turn his face away from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When a man enters his house, let him say: 'O Allah, I ask You for the best of entering and the best of leaving. In the name of Allah we enter, and in the name of Allah we leave, and upon Allah our Lord we rely.' Then let him greet his family with salām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her: When the Prophet ﷺ saw a cloud rising on the horizon of the sky, he would leave his work, even if he was in prayer, and then say:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from its evil."
And if it rained, he would say:
"O Allah, [make it] a beneficial, pleasant downpour."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not curse the rooster, for it wakes [people] for prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you hear the barking of dogs and the braying of donkeys at night, seek refuge in Allah, for they see what you do not see."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and others,
both said: The Messenger of Allah said:
"Go out less after people have quieted down, for Allah the Exalted has creatures that He disperses over the earth."
Ibn Marwān said:
"At that hour." And he said:
"For Allah has creatures."

Then he mentioned the barking of dogs and the braying of donkeys similarly, and added in his narration: Ibn al-Hād said: Shuraḥbīl al-Ḥājib narrated to me from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the like of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Has there been seen among you—or he used another word—the mughribūn?"
I said: What are the mughribūn? He said:
"Those in whom the jinn share."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿUmar al-Jushamī,
both said: Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us: Saʿīd narrated to us,
—Naṣr said: Ibn Abī ʿArūbah—from Qatādah,
from Abū Nahīk,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever seeks refuge in Allah, grant him refuge; and whoever asks you by the Face of Allah, give him."
ʿUbaydullāh said:
"Whoever asks you by Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās, saying: There is something I find in my chest. He said: What is it? I said: By Allah, I will not speak of it.
He said to me: Is it something of doubt? And he laughed.

He said: No one has been free of that, until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {So if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you} [the verse]. He said to me: When you find something in yourself, then say: {He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, one of us finds in himself—hinting at something—[a thought] such that he would rather be a lump of charcoal than speak of it. He said:
"Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. Praise be to Allah, who has turned his scheming back to whispering."
Ibn Qudāmah said: "turned his affair back," in place of "turned his scheming back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever supports his people in what is not right is like a camel that has fallen into a well and is being pulled out by its tail.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I reached the Prophet ﷺ while he was in a tent made of leather, and he mentioned something similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: O Messenger of Allah, what is tribalism? He said:
"That you help your people in wrongdoing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us and said:
"The best of you is the one who defends his clan, so long as he does not commit sin."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He is not one of us who calls to tribalism, and he is not one of us who fights for the sake of tribalism, and he is not one of us who dies upholding tribalism."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a man loves his brother, let him tell him that he loves him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ:

that he mentioned a man among those who came before, or among those before you—he said a word, meaning—Allah had given him wealth and children. When death approached, he said to his sons, "What kind of father was I to you?" They said, "The best of fathers."
He said, "He has not stored up any good with Allah,
and if Allah gets hold of him, He will punish him.
So look: when I die, burn me, and when I have become charcoal, crush me"—or he said, "grind me"—"and when there is a day of violent wind, scatter me in it."
The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"He took their solemn pledges to that effect, by my Lord,
and they did so. Then they scattered him on a stormy day,
and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said, 'Be!'
And there he was, a man standing.

Allah said, 'My servant, what made you do what you did?' He said, 'Fear of You,' or 'Dread of You.' So nothing saved him except that He had mercy on him because of it," and on another occasion he said, "nothing else saved him."
I narrated it to Abū ʿUthmān, and he said, "I heard this from Salmān, except that he added: 'Scatter me in the sea.'"
Or as he narrated.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a man who was extravagant in sinning against himself.
When death came to him, he said to his sons, 'When I die, burn me, then grind me, then scatter me in the wind.
By Allah, if my Lord gets hold of me, He will punish me with a punishment He has not given to anyone.'
When he died, that was done to him.
Then Allah commanded the earth,
and said, 'Gather what you have of him.'
It did so, and there he was, standing.
Allah said, 'What made you do what you did?' He said, 'My Lord, fear of You.' So He forgave him." Another narrator said:
"Dread of You, my Lord."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUrwah said: ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Prophet ﷺ used to say during his illness in which he died:
"O ʿĀʾishah, I still feel the pain of the food that I ate at Khaybar,
and this is the time when I feel my aorta being severed by that poison."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī, that is, Ibn Abī Ṭālib, went out from the Prophet ﷺ. Aḥmad ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us: ʿAnbasah narrated to us: Yūnus narrated to us from Ibn Shihāb, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik informed me that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās informed him that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him) went out from the Prophet ﷺ during his illness in which he passed away. The people said, "O Abū Ḥasan, how is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ this morning?" He said, "By the grace of Allah, he has woken up recovered." Then al-ʿAbbās took him by the hand and said, "Do you not see? By Allah, after three days you will be a slave of the staff. By Allah, I think the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will die of this illness of his,
and I know the face of death in the faces of the sons of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
So come with us to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and let us ask him in whom the authority will rest. If it is with us, we will know that,
and if it is with others, we will ask him to give instructions concerning us."
ʿAlī said, "By Allah, if we ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for it and he refuses us, the people will never give it to us,
and I will never ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the illness of the Prophet ﷺ became severe, he began to be overcome by it,
and Fāṭimah (peace be upon her) said, "Oh, the distress of my father!" He said to her:
"There will be no distress on your father after today."
When he died, she said, "O my father,
you answered a Lord who called you!
O my father, whose abode is the Paradise of Firdaws!
O my father, to Jibrīl we announce your death."
When he was buried, Fāṭimah (peace be upon her) said, "O Anas,
did your hearts find it agreeable to throw earth upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: The Prophet ﷺ stayed in Makkah for ten years while the Qurʾān was being revealed to him, and in Madīnah for ten years.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ appointed Usāmah to a command, and the people spoke critically about him. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"It has reached me that you have said things about Usāmah,
and he is the most beloved of people to me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He said to him, "When did you emigrate?" He said: We left Yemen as emigrants and arrived at al-Juḥfah,
when a rider came, and I asked him for the news. He said, "We buried the Prophet ﷺ five [days ago]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I took part in fifteen military campaigns with the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar said: Ubayy is the best reciter among us, yet we leave aside some of what Ubayy gets wrong in recitation,

while Ubayy says, "I took it from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so I will not leave it for anything." Allah the Exalted said: {Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or similar to it.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic to the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not believe the People of the Book,
and do not disbelieve them, but say: {We believe in Allah and what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to you}." [to the end of] the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: None remains of those who prayed towards both qiblahs except me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Book of Allah is retaliation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ramadan was revealed, he said:
"Whoever wishes may fast,
and whoever wishes may break the fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He recited {a ransom of feeding the poor} and said, "It has been abrogated."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the fasting of Ramadan was prescribed, they would not approach women during the whole of Ramadan,
and some men used to betray themselves,
so Allah revealed: {Allah knows that you used to betray yourselves, so He accepted your repentance and pardoned you.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī while people were crowding around him. When the people had dispersed from him, I said, "I am not going to ask you what these people have been asking you." I said, "I am asking you about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said, "There is no benefit in that for you."

So I repeated the question to him, and he said, "The Ẓuhr prayer would be called, and one of us would go out to al-Baqīʿ, relieve himself, then come to his family and perform ablution, and then return to the mosque, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was still in the first rakʿah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and complained to him about the heat of the scorching ground, but he did not accommodate our complaint.
Zuhayr said: I asked Abū Isḥāq, "Was that about the Ẓuhr prayer?" He said, "Yes."
I said, "Was it about praying it early?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever prays the Fajr prayer is under the protection of Allah, so let Allah not hold you to account for anything of His protection. For whoever Allah holds to account for anything of His protection, He will overtake him, then throw him on his face into the Fire of Hell."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā al-Māzinī,
from Saʿīd ibn Yasār,
from Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying on a donkey while he was facing toward Khaybar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon Abū Salamah, whose eyes had remained open [in death]. He closed them and then said:
"When the soul is taken, the sight follows it."
Some of his family cried out in distress, so he said:
"Do not pray against yourselves except for good, for the angels say 'Āmīn' to what you say." Then he said:

"O Allah, forgive Abū Salamah, raise his rank among those who are guided, be his successor among his descendants who remain, and forgive us and him, O Lord of the worlds, and make his grave spacious for him,
and illuminate it for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A foster-son of ʿĀʾishah] from ʿĀʾishah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"No Muslim dies and has a congregation of Muslims, reaching a hundred, pray over him, all interceding for him, except that their intercession for him is accepted."
ʿAlī ibn Ḥujr said in his narration:
"A hundred or more."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A red velvet cloak was placed in the grave of the Prophet ﷺ.
He said: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār said in another place: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah,
from Abū Jamrah,
from Ibn ʿAbbās. And this is more authentic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade plastering graves, sitting on them, and building over them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
they said: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān,
from Ismāʿīl ibn Umayyah,
from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabbān,
from Yaḥyā ibn ʿUmārah,
from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no charity (ṣadaqah) due on less than five awsāq of dates or grain."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best dīnār a man spends is a dīnār he spends on his family, a dīnār he spends on his animal in the cause of Allah, and a dīnār he spends on his companions in the cause of Allah."

Abū Qilābah said: He began with the family. Then Abū Qilābah said: Which man has a greater reward than a man who spends on young dependents, keeping them chaste or [such that] Allah benefits them through him and makes them self-sufficient?
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every act of kindness is charity (ṣadaqah), and among acts of kindness is that you meet your brother with a cheerful face, and that you pour from your bucket into your brother's vessel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"As for the people of the Fire who are its [true] inhabitants, they will neither die in it nor live. But there are people whom the Fire strikes because of their sins—or their wrongdoings—and it causes them to die, until, when they have become charcoal, permission is given for intercession. They are brought out in groups and scattered over the rivers of Paradise. Then it is said: 'O people of Paradise, pour [water] over them.' So they sprout like the seed that sprouts in the silt carried by a flood."
Then a man from among the people said: "It is as if the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been in the desert."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Moses asked his Lord: 'What is the lowest rank of the people of Paradise?' He said: 'He is a man who comes after the people of Paradise have entered Paradise, and it is said to him: Enter Paradise.'

He says: 'My Lord, how, when people have already taken their places and taken what they were given?' It is said to him: 'Would you be pleased to have the like of the kingdom of one of the kings of the world?' He says: 'I am pleased, my Lord.'
He says: 'You shall have that, and the like of it, and the like of it, and the like of it, and the like of it.'
At the fifth, he says: 'I am pleased, my Lord.'
He says: 'This is yours, and ten times its like, and you shall have whatever your soul desires and your eye delights in.'
He says: 'I am pleased, my Lord.'

[Moses] said: 'My Lord, and the highest of them in rank?' He said: 'Those are the ones I chose. I planted their honor with My own hand and sealed it, so no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and it has never occurred to the heart of any human.'"
He said: "And its confirmation is in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: {No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes}"—the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I surely know the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise and the last of the people of the Fire to come out of it: a man who will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: 'Present to him his minor sins and set aside his major ones.'
So his minor sins are presented to him, and it is said: 'You did such and such on such and such a day, and such and such on such and such a day.' He says: 'Yes.'
He cannot deny it, while he is fearful that his major sins will be presented to him.
Then it is said to him: 'For every evil deed you shall have a good deed.'
He says: 'My Lord, I did things that I do not see here.'"
[The narrator said:] I indeed saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh until his molar teeth showed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
said: "O Messenger of Allah, where is my father?" He said: "In the Fire."
When the man turned away, he called him and said:
"Indeed, my father and your father are in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever performs ablution for prayer and perfects the ablution, then walks to the obligatory prayer and prays it with the people—or with the congregation, or in the mosque—Allah will forgive him his sins."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, serving ourselves, taking turns tending our camels. It was my turn to tend the camels, so I brought them back in the evening and found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressing the people, and I heard him say:
"There is none among you who performs ablution and does it well, then stands and prays two rak'ahs, turning to them with his heart and his face, except that [Paradise] is guaranteed for him."
I said: "Wow, wow! How excellent this is!"
A man in front of me said: "The one before it was better than it, O ʿUqbah."
I looked, and it was ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. I said: "What is it, O Abū Ḥafṣ?" He said: "He said just before you came:

'There is none among you who performs ablution and does it well, then says when he finishes his ablution: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, except that the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him, and he may enter from whichever he wishes.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, on the day Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ died. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr came in and performed ablution in her presence, and she said: "O ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, perfect the ablution, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Woe to the heels from the Fire.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When a Muslim servant—or a believer—performs ablution and washes his face, every sin that he looked at with his eyes comes out of his face with the water—or with the last drop of water. When he washes his hands, every sin that his hands committed comes out of his hands with the water—or with the last drop of water. When he washes his feet, every sin toward which his feet walked comes out with the water—or with the last drop of water—until he emerges purified of sins."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was
the reciter of the Azd, from Abū al-Kanūd, from Khabbāb,

concerning the saying of the Most High: {And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening} up to His saying {lest you be among the wrongdoers}. He said: Al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis at-Tamīmī and ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn al-Fazārī came and found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with Ṣuhayb, Bilāl, ʿAmmār and Khabbāb, sitting among a group of the weak among the believers. When they saw them around the Prophet ﷺ, they looked down on them. So they came to him, took him aside, and said: We want you to set aside for us a sitting of your own by which the Arabs will recognize our merit, for delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed for the Arabs to see us with these slaves. So when we come to you, make them leave you, and when we have finished, sit with them if you wish. He said: "Yes."
They said: Then write us a document to that effect.

He said: So he called for a sheet and called ʿAlī to write, while we were sitting to one side. Then Jibrīl, peace be upon him, descended and said: {And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face. You are not accountable for anything of their reckoning, and they are not accountable for anything of yours, so that you would drive them away and be among the wrongdoers.} Then He mentioned al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis and ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn, saying: {And thus We have tried some of them through others, so that they say: Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us? Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?}
Then He said: {And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed mercy upon Himself.}

He said: So we drew near to him until we placed our knees against his knee. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to sit with us, and when he wished to get up, he would get up and leave us. Then Allah revealed: {And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face, and do not let your eyes pass beyond them} meaning, do not sit with the nobles, {desiring the adornment of worldly life, and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance} meaning ʿUyaynah and al-Aqraʿ, {and who follows his desire and whose affair has been in excess} he said: ruin. He said: the affair of ʿUyaynah and al-Aqraʿ.
Then He gave them the parable of the two men and the parable of worldly life.
Khabbāb said: We used to sit with the Prophet ﷺ, and when we reached the time at which he would rise, we would get up and leave him until he rose.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"Woe to those who have much, except one who says of wealth thus, thus, thus, and thus,"
four: on his right, on his left, in front of him, and behind him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Those who have the most will be the lowest on the Day of Resurrection, except one who says of wealth thus and thus, and earned it from a pure source."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"O Allah, whoever believes in me, affirms my truthfulness, and knows that what I have brought is the truth from You, make his wealth and children few, make the meeting with You beloved to him, and hasten his appointed end. And whoever does not believe in me, does not affirm my truthfulness, and does not know that what I have brought is the truth from You, increase his wealth and children and lengthen his life."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to a man to ask him for the loan of a she-camel, but he refused him. Then he sent me to another man, who sent a she-camel to him. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw it, he said:
"O Allah, bless it and the one who sent it."
Naqādah said: I said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "And the one who brought it?" He said:
"And the one who brought it."
Then he ordered that it be milked, and it gave plenty of milk. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, increase the wealth of so-and-so," meaning the first one who refused, "
and make the provision of so-and-so day by day,"
meaning the one who sent the she-camel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Wretched is the slave of the dīnār, the slave of the dirham, and the slave of the velvet cloak. Wretched and reversed is he, and if he is pricked by a thorn, may it not be removed for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"He has succeeded who has been guided to Islam, been given sufficient provision, and been content with it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no rich person or poor person except that on the Day of Resurrection he will wish that he had been given only bare sustenance from this world."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Unaysah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When Ibn Umm Maktūm gives the call to prayer, eat and drink; but when Bilāl gives the call, do not eat or drink."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and Bilāl came out and gave the call to prayer. In his call he began to say it like this, turning to the right and to the left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to give the call to prayer for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and in the first call for the Fajr prayer I would say: "Come to success; prayer is better than sleep, prayer is better than sleep; Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest; there is no god but Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The last call to prayer given by Bilāl was: "Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest; there is no god but Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The like of that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ﷺ, meaning on a rainy night during a journey, he would say: "Come to prayer, come to success; pray in your lodgings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out until he reached Muzdalifah. There he prayed Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ with one call to prayer and two iqāmahs, and he did not pray anything between them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of the Trench the polytheists kept us busy from the Ẓuhr prayer,

until the sun had set. That was before what was revealed about fighting was revealed. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting}. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Bilāl, and he gave the iqāmah for Ẓuhr, and he prayed it just as he used to pray it in its time. Then he had the iqāmah given for ʿAṣr and prayed it just as he used to pray it in its time. Then he had the call to prayer given for Maghrib and prayed it just as he used to pray it in its time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and he heard the voice of a man giving the call to prayer. He said the like of what he said, then he said: "This is surely a shepherd of sheep, or one far away from his family."
They looked, and it was indeed a shepherd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in the row of prayer... (the hadith).
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when Bilāl stood up and called out. When he fell silent, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever says the like of this with certainty will enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf when the muʾadhdhin gave the call and said: "Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest." He said the takbīr twice. Then [the muʾadhdhin] said: "I testify that there is no god but Allah," and he testified twice. Then [the muʾadhdhin] said: "I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," and he testified twice. Then he said: Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān narrated to me like this from the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The like of what he said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Muʿāwiyah when his muʾadhdhin gave the call to prayer. Muʿāwiyah said as the muʾadhdhin said, until, when [the muʾadhdhin] said "Come to prayer," he said: "There is no might and no power except with Allah." When [the muʾadhdhin] said "Come to success," he said: "There is no might and no power except with Allah." After that he said what the muʾadhdhin said. Then he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say the like of that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The posts of this pulpit of mine are fixed posts in Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out as a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ, pledged allegiance to him, prayed with him, and informed him that in our land we had a church. We asked him to give us some of the water left from his purification. He called for water, performed ablution and rinsed his mouth, then poured it into a small waterskin and instructed us, saying:
"Go out, and when you reach your land, destroy your church, sprinkle its place with this water, and make it a mosque."
We said: "The land is far, the heat is intense, and the water will dry up." He said:
"Add more water to it, for that will only make it better."
So we went out until we reached our land. We destroyed our church, sprinkled its place, made it a mosque, and called the adhān in it.
He said: The monk was a man from Ṭayyiʾ. When he heard the adhān, he said: "A true call."
Then he headed toward one of our hillside streams, and we did not see him after that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a man goes out from his house to his mosque, one foot records a good deed and the other erases a bad deed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came announcing a lost animal in the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "May you not find it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlqamah and I entered
upon ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, and he said to us: "Have those people prayed?" We said: "No."
He said: "Stand and pray."

We went to stand behind him, but he placed one of us on his right and the other on his left. He prayed without adhān or iqāmah. When he bowed, he interlaced his fingers and put them between his knees, and he said: "This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to al-Ḥudaybiyah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we were fourteen hundred. There were fifty sheep with us that the well could not satisfy. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat on the edge of the well, and he either supplicated or spat into it. He said: Then it gushed forth, and we gave drink to ourselves and our animals and drew water.
He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called us to pledge allegiance at the foot of the tree.
He said: I pledged allegiance to him among the first of the people. Then he continued taking pledges until, when he was in the middle of the people, he said:
"Pledge allegiance, O Salamah."
He said: I said: I already pledged allegiance to you, O Messenger of Allah, among the first of the people. He said: "Again."

He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me unarmed, meaning without a weapon. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me a shield, either a ḥajafah or a daraqah. Then he continued taking pledges until, when he was at the last of the people, he said:
"Will you not pledge allegiance to me, O Salamah?"
He said: I said: I already pledged allegiance to you, O Messenger of Allah, among the first of the people and among the middle of the people. He said: "Again."
He said: So I pledged allegiance to him a third time. Then he said to me:
"O Salamah, where is your shield, either the ḥajafah or the daraqah, that I gave you?"
He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, my uncle ʿĀmir met me while unarmed, so I gave it to him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and said:
"You are like the one of old who said: O Allah, grant me a dear friend who is dearer to me than myself."
Then the polytheists sent messages to us seeking peace, until some of us went among the others and we made peace.

He said: I was a servant to Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh; I would water his horse, tend to it, serve him, and eat from his food, and I had left my family and my wealth as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ. He said: When we and the people of Makkah made peace and mixed with one another, I came to a tree, cleared away its thorns, and lay down at its base. He said: Then four of the polytheists from the people of Makkah came to me and began to speak ill of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I hated them, so I moved to another tree. They hung up their weapons and lay down. While they were like that, a caller called out from the bottom of the valley: O emigrants! Ibn Zunaym has been killed!
He said: So I drew my sword and charged at those four while they were asleep, and I took their weapons.
I made them into one bundle in my hand. He said: Then I said: By the One who honored the face of Muḥammad, none of you will raise his head but I will strike the place where his eyes are.
He said: Then I brought them, driving them to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: And my uncle ʿĀmir came with a man from the ʿAbalāt called Mikraz.
He was leading him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on an armored horse, together with seventy of the polytheists. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at them and said:
"Leave them; let the beginning of the wrongdoing and its repetition be theirs."

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pardoned them, and Allah revealed: {And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them within Makkah after He had given you victory over them} the whole verse.

He said: Then we set out returning to Madinah and stopped at a halting place between which and Banū Liḥyān was a mountain, and they were polytheists. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked forgiveness for whoever climbed this mountain that night, as a lookout for the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions. Salamah said: I climbed it that night two or three times. Then we arrived in Madinah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent his riding camels with Rabāḥ, the servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I was with him. I went out with Ṭalḥah's horse, watering it along with the camels. When morning came, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Fazārī had raided the camels of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, driven them all off, and killed their herdsman. He said: I said: O Rabāḥ, take this horse and deliver it to Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh, and tell the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that the polytheists have raided his pasturing camels. He said: Then I stood on a hillock, faced Madinah, and called out three times: Yā ṣabāḥāh!

Then I went out in pursuit of the people, shooting them with arrows and chanting, saying: I am the son of al-Akwaʿ, and today is the day of the suckling ones! I caught up with a man among them and shot an arrow into his saddle until the arrowhead reached his shoulder. He said: I said: Take that! I am the son of al-Akwaʿ, and today is the day of the suckling ones! He said: By Allah, I kept shooting them and wounding their mounts, and when a horseman turned back toward me, I would come to a tree, sit at its base, then shoot him and wound his mount. When the mountain narrowed and they entered its narrow pass, I climbed the mountain and began to hurl stones down at them. He said: I continued following them like that until there was no camel that Allah had created from the herd of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except that I had left it behind my back, and they left it to me. Then I kept following them, shooting them, until they threw down more than thirty cloaks and thirty spears to lighten themselves. They would not throw down anything without my placing a pile of stones on it, which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions would recognize, until they came to a narrow place in a mountain pass, where so-and-so son of Badr al-Fazārī had joined them. They sat down to eat their morning meal, and I sat on top of a peak. al-Fazārī said: Who is this that I see? They said: We have suffered hardship from this fellow. By Allah, he has not left us since the darkness of dawn, shooting us, until he took away everything in our hands.
He said: Let four of you get up and go to him.

He said: So four of them climbed up the mountain toward me. He said: When they were within speaking distance of me, I said: Do you know me? They said: No, who are you? I said: I am Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ. By the One who honored the face of Muḥammad ﷺ, I will not pursue any man among you but I will catch him, and none of you can pursue me
and catch me. One of them said: I think so.

He said: So they went back, and I did not leave my place until I saw the horsemen of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ moving through the trees. He said: The first of them was al-Akhram al-Asadī, behind him Abū Qatādah al-Anṣārī, and behind him al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad al-Kindī. He said: I took hold of al-Akhram's rein. He said: They turned and fled. I said: O Akhram, beware of them, lest they cut you off, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions catch up.
He said: O Salamah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day and know that Paradise is true and the Fire is true, then do not come between me and martyrdom.

He said: So I let him go, and he met ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. He said: He wounded ʿAbd al-Raḥmān's horse, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān thrust at him and killed him and took over his horse. Then Abū Qatādah, the horseman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, caught up with ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, thrust at him, and killed him. By the One who honored the face of Muḥammad ﷺ, I pursued them, running on my feet, until I could see nothing behind me of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, not even their dust, until, before sunset, they turned aside to a mountain gorge with water in it called Dhū Qarad, to drink from it, for they were thirsty. He said: They looked and saw me running behind them, so I drove them away from it, meaning I made them leave it, and they did not taste a drop of it. He said: They went out and ran hard up a mountain pass. He said: I ran and caught up with a man among them and struck him with an arrow in the top of his shoulder blade.

He said: I said: Take that! I am the son of al-Akwaʿ, and today is the day of the suckling ones! He said: May his mother be bereaved of him! Is it al-Akwaʿ from this morning? I said: Yes, O enemy of yourself, your al-Akwaʿ from this morning. He said: They left two horses behind on a mountain pass, and I brought them, driving them to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: ʿĀmir caught up with me carrying a small water-skin with a little diluted milk in it and a small water-skin with water in it. I performed ablution and drank, then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was at the water from which I had driven them away. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had taken those camels and everything I had rescued from the polytheists, every spear and cloak. Bilāl had slaughtered a she-camel from the camels I had rescued from the people, and he was roasting for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ some of its liver and hump. He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, let me choose a hundred men from the people and pursue the enemy, so that none of them is left to tell the tale but I will kill him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed until his molars showed in the light of the fire, and he said:
"O Salamah, do you think you would have done it?"
I said: Yes, by the One who honored you. He said:
"They are now being hosted in the land of Ghaṭafān."
He said: Then a man from Ghaṭafān came and said: So-and-so slaughtered a camel for them, and when they removed its skin they saw dust, so they said: The enemy has come to you! And they fled.
When morning came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of our horsemen today was Abū Qatādah, and the best of our foot soldiers was Salamah."

He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me two shares, the share of the horseman and the share of the foot soldier, combining them for me. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seated me behind him on al-ʿAḍbāʾ as we returned to Madinah. He said: While we were traveling, there was a man of the Anṣār who could not be beaten in running. He said: He kept saying: Is there no one to race to Madinah? Is there anyone who will race? He kept repeating that. He said: When I heard his words, I said: Do you not respect a noble person or fear an honorable one? He said: No, unless it is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I said: O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, let me race the man. He said: "If you wish."

He said: I said: I am coming to you, and I bent my leg, leapt, and ran. He said: I held back a little, pacing myself over a hill or two, to conserve my strength, then ran after him, and held back over a hill or two. Then I put on speed until I caught up with him. He said: I struck him between his shoulders. He said: I said: You have been beaten, by Allah! He said: I think so.

He said: So I beat him to Madinah. He said: By Allah, we stayed only three nights before we set out for Khaybar with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: My uncle ʿĀmir began chanting for the people: By Allah, had it not been for Allah, we would not have been guided, nor given charity, nor prayed. We cannot do without Your bounty, so make our feet firm if we meet [the enemy], and send down tranquility upon us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Who is this?"
He said: I am ʿĀmir. He said:
"Your Lord has forgiven you."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never asked forgiveness specifically for a person but that he was martyred.
He said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb called out, while on a camel of his: O Prophet of Allah, if only you had let us enjoy ʿĀmir's company!

He said: When we came to Khaybar, their king Marḥab came out brandishing his sword and saying: Khaybar knows that I am Marḥab, fully armed, a seasoned, tested hero, when wars come blazing. He said: My uncle ʿĀmir went out to face him and said: Khaybar knows that I am ʿĀmir, fully armed, a hero who plunges into danger. He said: They exchanged two blows. Marḥab's sword struck ʿĀmir's shield, and ʿĀmir went down low to strike at him, but his sword rebounded on him and cut his main arm vein, and that was the cause of his death.

Salamah said: I went out and found a group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ saying: ʿĀmir's deeds have come to nothing; he killed himself. He said: So I came to the Prophet ﷺ weeping and said: O Messenger of Allah, ʿĀmir's deeds have come to nothing! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Who said that?"
He said: I said: Some of your Companions. He said:
"Whoever said that has lied. Rather, he will have his reward twice."
Then he sent me to ʿAlī, who had sore eyes, and said:
"I will give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, or whom Allah and His Messenger love."

He said: So I went to ʿAlī and brought him, leading him while his eyes were sore, until I brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He spat in his eyes and he was healed, and gave him the banner. Marḥab came out and said: Khaybar knows that I am Marḥab, fully armed, a seasoned, tested hero, when wars come blazing. ʿAlī said: I am the one whose mother named him Ḥaydar, like a lion of the forests, fearsome in appearance; I will give them the full measure in return, the measure of the sandara. He said: He struck Marḥab's head and killed him, and then the victory came at his hands.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That his father
used to recite in the Maghrib prayer something like what you recite: "By the racers..." (Sūrat al-ʿĀdiyāt) and similar sūrahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no short or long sūrah of the Mufaṣṣal except that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lead the people with it in the obligatory prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he prayed Maghrib behind Ibn Masʿūd, and he recited "Say: He is Allah, [who is] One."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He heard the Prophet ﷺ recite in the dawn prayer "When the earth is shaken..." in both rakʿahs, and I do not know whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forgot or recited that deliberately.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were commanded to recite
the Opening of the Book and whatever is easy [for us].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "
Go out and announce in Medina that there is no prayer without a recitation of the Qurʾān, even if it is only the Opening of the Book, or more."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to announce that there is no prayer without reciting the Opening of the Book and more.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us while we were reciting the Qurʾān, and among us were the Bedouin and the non-Arab. He said: "
Recite, for all of it is good. There will come people who will straighten it as an arrow is straightened; they will hasten [its reward] and not defer it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us while we were reciting, and he said: "

Praise be to Allah, the Book of Allah is one, and among you are the red, the white, and the black. Recite it before people recite it who will straighten it as an arrow is straightened; they will hasten its reward and not defer it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to pray voluntary prayers, making supplication while standing and sitting, and glorifying Allah in bowing and prostration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he would not complete the takbīr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people behind the imām do not say "Allah hears whoever praises Him," but they say "Our Lord, to You belongs all praise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Of Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr, from Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr,
she said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
Whoever among you women believes in Allah and the Last Day, let her not raise her head until the men raise their heads."
[This was] out of dislike that they might see the private parts of the men.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this story he said: "

When you stand and face the qiblah, say the takbīr, then recite the Mother of the Qurʾān and whatever Allah wills for you to recite. When you bow, place your palms on your knees and stretch out your back." And he said: "
When you prostrate, settle firmly in your prostration, and when you raise [your head], sit on your left thigh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ with this story, he said: "
When you stand in your prayer, say the takbīr to Allah, the Exalted, then recite whatever is easy for you of the Qurʾān." And he said in it: "
When you sit in the middle of the prayer, be at ease and spread your left thigh [beneath you], then recite the tashahhud. Then when you stand, do likewise until you finish your prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ... and he related this hadith, in which he said: "

Perform ablution as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you, then recite the tashahhud, then say the iqāmah, then say the takbīr. If you know some Qurʾān, recite it; otherwise praise Allah, declare His greatness, and declare that there is no god but Him." And he said in it: "
If you diminish anything of it, you have diminished from your prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Banū Salīṭ, from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ with this meaning, he said: "
Then zakāh is the same, then deeds will be taken into account in accordance with that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ recited "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High," he would say: "
Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man used to pray on top of his house, and whenever he recited "Is not He [who does this] able to give life to the dead?" he would say: "Glory be to You, yes indeed!" They asked him about that, and he said: I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I observed the Prophet ﷺ in his prayer, and he would remain in his bowing and prostration for about the time it takes to say: "
Glory be to Allah and praise Him," three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was seen with a trace of mud on his forehead and the tip of his nose from a prayer he had led the people in.
Abū ʿAlī said: Abū Dāwūd did not recite this hadith in the fourth presentation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ from behind and saw the whiteness of his armpits as he was holding his arms apart, keeping them spread away from his sides.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [reported] that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated, he would hold his upper arms away from his sides until [the whiteness of his armpits] could be seen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to give zakāh al-fiṭr, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among us, for every young and old person, free or enslaved: one ṣāʿ of food, or one ṣāʿ of dried yogurt (aqiṭ), or one ṣāʿ of barley, or one ṣāʿ of dates, or one ṣāʿ of raisins. We continued to give it so until Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān came to us, performing Hajj or ʿUmrah, and spoke to the people from the pulpit. Among what he said to the people was: "I see that two mudds of Syrian wheat equal one ṣāʿ of dates." So the people adopted that.
Abū Saʿīd said: As for me, I will continue to give it as I used to give it, for as long as I live.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Abū az-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man driving a sacrificial camel, and he said, "Ride it."
The man said, "O Messenger of Allah, it is a sacrificial camel." He said, "Ride it, woe to you!"
[He said this] the second or the third time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj and ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Mujāhid,
from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā,
from Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah,
that the Prophet ﷺ passed by him while he was at al-Ḥudaybiyah, before entering Makkah, while he was in a state of iḥrām, lighting a fire under a pot, with lice falling down over his face. He said,
"Are these pests of yours bothering you?" He said, "Yes." He said,
"Shave your head and feed a faraq among six poor people,"
and the faraq is three ṣāʿs,
"or fast three days, or offer a sacrifice."
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said,
"or slaughter a sheep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I would owe fasting from Ramadan,
and I could not make it up except in Shaʿbān.
Yaḥyā said: [This was] because of being occupied with the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
from Ibn Wahb,
who said: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me,
from al-Mundhir ibn ʿUbayd,
from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
that the Prophet ﷺ forbade anyone to sell food that he had bought by measure until he has taken full possession of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ said: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said in the year of the Conquest, while he was in Makkah,
"Allah and His Messenger have forbidden the sale of wine, dead animals, pigs, and idols."
He was then asked, "O Messenger of Allah, what about the fat of dead animals? Ships are coated with it, skins are treated with it, and people use it for lamps." He said,
"No, it is forbidden."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"May Allah fight the Jews! Allah forbade them fats, so they melted it, then sold it and ate its price."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Yazīd ibn Khuṣayfah, that as-Sāʾib
ibn Yazīd informed him that he
heard Sufyān ibn Abī Zuhayr
— a man from Shanūʾah and one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say,
"Whoever keeps a dog that is of no use to him for farming or for livestock, a qīrāṭ is deducted from his deeds every day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He disputed with a man of the Anṣār, who had been present at Badr with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, over the water channels of al-Ḥarrah, with which they both used to irrigate their date palms. The Anṣārī said, "Let the water flow past."
But [az-Zubayr] refused, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Irrigate, O Zubayr, then send the water to your neighbor."
The Anṣārī became angry and said, "O Messenger of Allah, [is it] because he is your cousin?" The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed colour, then he said,
"O Zubayr, irrigate, then hold back the water until it returns to the walls."

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave az-Zubayr his full right. Before that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had advised az-Zubayr to take a course that was generous to him and to the Anṣārī; but when the Anṣārī angered the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he gave az-Zubayr his full right in a clear judgment.

Az-Zubayr said, "I think that this verse was revealed only about that: {But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge concerning what is in dispute among them.}" One of the two narrators adds to the other in the account.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
all from Ibn ʿUyaynah,
Zuhayr said: Sufyān narrated to us,
from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should pray in a single garment with nothing of it over his shoulders."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said.
Transfer of isnād: And Yūsuf ibn ʿĪsā al-Marwazī narrated to me,
he said: al-Faḍl narrated to us,
he said: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to us,
from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀʾishah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"Bilāl calls the adhān at night,
so eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktūm calls the adhān."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We only knew that the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished by the takbīr.
ʿAmr said: I mentioned that to Abū Maʿbad, but he denied it and said: I did not narrate this to you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he asked Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the Friday prayer. He said: He would pray, then we would go to our camels and let them rest.
ʿAbdullāh added in his narration: when the sun passed its zenith, meaning the water-carrying camels.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What is between my house and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise."
This is a ḥasan gharīb ḥadīth from this route, from the ḥadīth of ʿAlī, and it has also been narrated by another route from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The right of a Muslim over a Muslim is five."
Transfer of isnād: And ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us,
ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn
al-Musayyab, from Abū Hurayrah,
he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Five are obligatory for a Muslim toward his brother: returning the greeting of peace, saying 'May Allah have mercy on you' to one who sneezes, accepting an invitation, visiting the sick, and following funeral processions."
ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar used to narrate this ḥadīth from al-Zuhrī as a mursal report, and once he narrated it with a connected chain from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Hurayrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said: In how many garments did you shroud the Prophet ﷺ? She said: In three white Saḥūlī garments,
among which there was no shirt and no turban.
And he said to her: On which day did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ die? She said: On Monday.
He said: And what day is this? She said: Monday.
He said: I hope [to die] between now and the night.
Then he looked at a garment he used to wear during his illness,
which had a stain of saffron on it, and said: Wash this garment of mine,
and add two garments to it, and shroud me in them.
I said: This one is worn out.
He said: The living are more deserving of the new than the dead,
for it is only for the pus [of the body].
He did not die until the evening of Tuesday night, and he was buried before the morning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only hastened around the House and between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah in order to show the polytheists his strength.
al-Ḥumaydī added: Sufyān narrated to us, ʿAmr narrated to us, I heard ʿAṭāʾ,
from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: a man from Banū Layth said to him: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī transmits this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — in the narration of Qutaybah — so ʿAbdullāh went, and Nāfiʿ with him.

And in the ḥadīth of Ibn Rumḥ, Nāfiʿ said: ʿAbdullāh went, and I was with him, and the Laythī, until he entered upon Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī and said: This man has informed me that you report that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of silver for silver except like for like, and the sale of gold for gold except like for like.
Abū Saʿīd pointed with his two fingers to his eyes and ears and said: My eyes saw and my ears heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"Do not sell gold for gold, and do not sell silver for silver, except like for like, and do not make one exceed the other, and do not sell something absent of it for something present, except hand to hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ only made the right of preemption (shufʿah) apply to everything that has not been divided,
so when boundaries are set and roads are separated, there is no preemption.
And some people said: Preemption is due to neighborliness.
Then he went to what he had made strict and nullified it,
and said: If someone buys a house and fears that the neighbor will take it by preemption,
he buys a share of one hundred shares,
then buys the rest,
and the neighbor has the right of preemption in the first share,
but has no right of preemption in the rest of the house,
and he may use a legal trick in that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Wailing over the dead is from the affairs of the Jāhiliyyah. If the wailing woman does not repent before she dies, she will be raised on the Day of Resurrection wearing garments of tar, and over them a coat of mail of blazing flame."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a funeral procession from being followed by a woman who wails.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the woman who scratches her face, the woman who tears her garment at the neckline, and the woman who calls out for woe and destruction.
label: machine translation
