segments_en: When Ibrāhīm, the son of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wept. The one offering condolences said to him—either Abū Bakr or ʿUmar—"You are the most deserving of those who honor the right of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The eye sheds tears and the heart grieves, and we do not say anything that angers the Lord. Were it not that [the promise] is true, and the appointment is gathering all, and that the last will follow the first, we would have grieved for you, O Ibrāhīm, even more than we have grieved, and indeed we are saddened by your loss."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said to her, "Your brother has been killed."
She said, "May Allah have mercy on him. Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return."
They said, "Your husband has been killed." She said, "Oh, my grief!"
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed, a husband has a place in a woman's heart that nothing else has."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by the women of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal, who were weeping over their dead on the day of Uḥud. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"But Ḥamzah has no one to weep for him."
So the women of the Anṣār came weeping for Ḥamzah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke up and said:
"Woe to them! Have they not gone back yet?
Tell them to go back, and not to weep over anyone who has died after today."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade elegies.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The dead person is punished by the weeping of the living, when they say: 'Oh, my supporter! Oh, my provider of clothing!
Oh, my helper! Oh, my mountain!' and the like—he is jolted and told: 'Are you really so? Are you really so?'"
Usayd said, "I said: Glory be to Allah! Allah says: {No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another.}"
He said, "Woe to you! I am telling you that Abū Mūsā narrated to me from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Do you think Abū Mūsā lied about the Prophet ﷺ, or do you think I lied about Abū Mūsā?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah, Glorified is He, says:
'Son of Adam, if you are patient and seek reward at the first shock [of calamity], I will not accept for you any reward less than Paradise.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ opened a door between himself and the people, or lifted a curtain, and there were the people praying behind Abū Bakr. He praised Allah for the good state of them that he saw, hoping that Allah would make him succeed him among them with what he saw of them. Then he said:

"O people, whichever of the people or of the believers is struck by a calamity, let him console himself for his calamity by [remembering] my loss, over the calamity that strikes him through someone else. For none of my Ummah will be struck after me by a calamity more severe for him than my loss."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Whoever is struck by a calamity, then remembers his calamity and renews his saying of istirjāʿ ["Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we will return"]—even if it was long ago—Allah will write for him a reward like that of the day he was struck."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"There is no believer who consoles his brother in a calamity except that Allah, Glorified is He, will clothe him with garments of honor on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUtbah ibn ʿAbd as-Sulamī met me and said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"There is no Muslim who has three of his children die before reaching the age of accountability, except that they will meet him at the eight gates of Paradise; he may enter from whichever he wishes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A miscarried child that I send ahead of me is dearer to me than a horseman that I leave behind me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The miscarried child will confront its Lord angrily if He has caused its parents to enter the Fire.
Then it will be said: 'O miscarried child, confronting your Lord, cause your parents to enter Paradise.'
So it will pull them by its umbilical cord until it brings them into Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: By the One in whose Hand is my soul, the miscarried child will pull its mother by its umbilical cord to Paradise, if she sought reward from Allah for [her loss of] it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from leprosy (baraṣ), madness, elephantiasis (judhām), and from evil diseases."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
from the people of Yemen came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, together with a daughter of hers who had two thick bracelets of gold on her arm. He said:
"Do you pay the zakāh on this?" She said, "No." He said:
"Would it please you that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, put two bracelets of fire on you in their place on the Day of Resurrection?"
She said: So she took them off and threw them to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said, "They are for Allah and His Messenger ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote the document of charity (ṣadaqah) but did not send it out to his officials until he passed away; he attached it to his sword. When he passed away, Abū Bakr acted upon it until he passed away, and then ʿUmar until he passed away. It stated:

"For five camels, one sheep; for ten, two sheep; for fifteen, three sheep; for twenty, four sheep; for twenty-five, a bint makhāḍ up to thirty-five. If they exceed that, then a bint labūn up to forty-five. If they exceed that, then a ḥiqqah up to sixty. If they exceed that, then a jadhaʿah up to seventy-five. If they exceed that, then two bint labūn up to ninety. If they exceed that, then two ḥiqqah up to one hundred and twenty. If they exceed one hundred and twenty, then for every fifty a ḥiqqah, and for every forty a bint labūn.

And for sheep: for every forty sheep, one sheep up to one hundred and twenty. If they exceed that, two sheep up to two hundred. If they exceed that, three sheep up to three hundred. If they exceed three hundred, then for every hundred sheep, one sheep; then there is nothing more until they reach four hundred. Separate animals are not to be combined, nor combined animals separated, out of fear of the charity. What belongs to two partners, they settle between themselves equally. An old animal or one with a defect is not to be taken as charity."
Az-Zuhrī said: When the collector comes, he divides the sheep into three parts: a third of the best, a third of the average, and a third of the poorest, and the collector takes from the average.
Az-Zuhrī did not mention cattle.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"For every herd of grazing camels, for forty there is a bint labūn, and camels are not to be separated from their count. Whoever gives it seeking reward,"
Ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "seeking reward with it,"

"will have its reward. And whoever withholds it, we will take it and half of his wealth, as an obligation from the obligations of our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. None of it is for the family of Muhammad."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāfiʿ ibn ʿAlqamah appointed my father as chief of his people and commanded him to collect their charity. He said: My father sent me with a group of them, and I came to a very old man called Saʿr ibn Daysam. I said, "My father has sent me to you," meaning to collect your charity. He said, "Son of my brother, what method do you follow in taking it?" I said, "We choose, until we even examine the udders of the sheep."

He said: Son of my brother, I will tell you that I was in one of these mountain paths in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with my sheep, when two men came to me on a camel and said to me, "We are the two messengers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to you, so that you pay the charity due on your sheep."
I said, "What is due from me on them?" They said, "One sheep."
So I went to a sheep whose place I knew, full of milk and fat, and brought it out to them.
They said, "This is a shāfiʿ sheep, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has forbidden us to take a shāfiʿ."
I said, "Then what will you take?" They said, "A young female goat of a year (ʿanāq), jadhaʿah or thaniyyah."
He said: So I went to a young female goat that was muʿtāṭ.
The muʿtāṭ is one that has not yet given birth, though the time of its giving birth has come. I brought it out to them, and they said, "Hand it over to us."
So they put it with them on their camel and then went off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to Yemen and said to him:
"Take grain from grain, a sheep from sheep, a camel from camels, and a cow from cattle."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"For the inside of one of you to be filled with pus is better for him than for it to be filled with poetry."

Abū ʿAlī said: It has reached me from Abū ʿUbayd that he said: The meaning is that his heart is filled with it until it distracts him from the Qur'an and the remembrance of Allah. But if the Qur'an and knowledge predominate, then in our view such a person's inside is not filled with poetry. [And the Prophet ﷺ said:] "Indeed, some eloquence is [like] magic."

He said: The meaning was that his eloquence reaches the point that he praises a person and is believed in it, until he turns hearts to his words, then he criticizes him and is believed in that too, until he turns hearts to his other statement, so that it is as if he had bewitched the listeners by that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, some eloquence is magic, some knowledge is ignorance, some poetry is wisdom, and some speech is a burden."
Then Ṣaʿṣaʿah ibn Ṣūḥān said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ spoke the truth. As for his saying: "
Indeed, some eloquence is magic,"
it is the man who owes a right yet is more skilled in arguments than the one to whom it is owed, so he bewitches the people with his eloquence and takes away the right. As for his saying: "
Some knowledge is ignorance,"
it is that the scholar burdens himself, beyond his knowledge, with what he does not know, and so that makes him ignorant. As for his saying: "
Some poetry is wisdom,"
it is these admonitions and proverbs by which people take heed. As for his saying: "
Some speech is a burden,"
it is your presenting your words and talk to someone who has no concern with it and does not want it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar passed by Ḥassān while he was reciting poetry in the mosque, and he cast a glance at him. Ḥassān said: I used to recite in it when there was in it one better than you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "And as for the poets, it is the deviators who follow them." Then part of that was abrogated and an exception was made, so He said: "Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, and remember Allah often."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the morning prayer, he would say: "
Did any of you see a dream last night?" And he would say: "
Nothing remains of prophethood after me except the true dream."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father was one of the People of the Ṣuffah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Come with us to the house of ʿĀʾishah." So we went, and he said: "
ʿĀʾishah, feed us."
She brought a dish of coarsely ground grain, and we ate. Then he said: "
ʿĀʾishah, feed us."
She brought a small dish of ḥaysah, [as little] as a sandgrouse, and we ate. Then he said: "
ʿĀʾishah, give us something to drink."
She brought a large cup of milk, and we drank. Then he said: "
ʿĀʾishah, give us something to drink."
She brought a small cup, and we drank. Then he said: "
If you wish, you may spend the night, and if you wish, you may go to the mosque."
He said: While I was lying in the mosque before dawn on my stomach, a man was nudging me with his foot and said: "
This is a way of lying that Allah dislikes."
He said: I looked, and it was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever spends the night on the roof of a house that has no barrier, protection is withdrawn from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no Muslim who spends the night in a state of remembrance and purity, then wakes during the night and asks Allah for something good of this world and the Hereafter, except that He gives it to him."

Thābit al-Bunānī said: Abū Ẓabyah came to us and narrated this hadith to us from Muʿādh ibn Jabal from the Prophet ﷺ. Thābit said: So-and-so said: I tried hard to say it when I woke up, but I was not able to.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Umm Salamah, who said: The bed of the Prophet ﷺ was about the size of what a person is laid on in his grave, and the place of prayer was at his head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"When you retire to your bed while you are in a state of purity, then rest on your right side."
Then he mentioned something similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ with this [wording]. Sufyān said: One of them said: "
When you come to your bed in a state of purity," and the other said: "
Perform your ablution as for prayer."
And he narrated the like of the meaning of Muʿtamir.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he used to say when lying down to sleep:

"O Allah, I seek refuge in Your Noble Face and Your perfect words from the evil of everything You hold by the forelock. O Allah, You remove debt and sin. O Allah, Your army is not defeated, Your promise is not broken, and the might of the mighty does not benefit him against You. Glory and praise be to You."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lay down on his side at night, he would say:
"In the name of Allah I lay down my side. O Allah, forgive my sin, drive away my devil, release my pledge, and place me in the highest assembly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he

spent a night with the Prophet ﷺ. Towards the end of the night the Prophet of Allah ﷺ got up and went out, looked at the sky, and then recited this verse from Āl ʿImrān: "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day..." until he reached "...and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." Then he returned to the house, cleaned his teeth with the siwāk, performed ablution, stood and prayed, then lay down. Then he got up again and went out, looked at the sky, and recited this verse. Then he returned, cleaned his teeth with the siwāk, performed ablution, then stood and prayed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to ʿĀʾishah to ask her about wiping
over the leather socks. She said, "Go to the son of Abū Ṭālib and ask him, for he used to travel with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
So we asked him, and he said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set three days and nights for the traveler, and a day and a night for the resident."
He said: Whenever Sufyān mentioned ʿAmr, he would praise him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the narration of Abū Muʿāwiyah, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said.
And in the narration of Wakīʿ, he said: He attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ, with similar wording.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
they said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī,
from Abū Salamah,
Transfer: And Muḥammad ibn Rāfiʿ narrated it to me,
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī,
from Ibn al-Musayyab,
both of them from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, with similar wording.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Mughīrah,
all of these from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾishah,
regarding scraping semen from the garment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, similar to the narration of Khālid from Abū Maʿshar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was staying with ʿĀʾishah and had a wet dream in my garments, so I soaked them in water. One of ʿĀʾishah's maidservants saw me and told her. ʿĀʾishah sent for me and said, "What made you do what you did to your garments?" I said, "I saw what a sleeper sees in his dream."
She said, "Did you see anything on them?" I said, "No."
She said, "If you had seen anything, you would have washed it. I have seen myself scraping it with my fingernail from the garment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when it was dry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to have contact with his wives above the waist-wrapper while they were menstruating.
label: machine translation

segments_en: the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to lie down with me while I was menstruating, with a garment between me and him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a woman
said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "Must a woman perform a full bath if she has a wet dream and sees fluid?" He said, "Yes."
ʿĀʾishah said to her, "May your hands be covered in dust, and may you be disgraced!"
She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Leave her. Does resemblance come from anything other than that? When her fluid prevails over the man's fluid, the child resembles his maternal uncles; and when the man's fluid prevails over hers, the child resembles his paternal uncles."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When great battles break out, Allah will send a force from among the freed slaves (mawālī). They will be the noblest of the Arabs in horsemanship and the finest of them in weaponry. Through them Allah will support the religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Hour will not come until the outermost garrisons of the Muslims are at Bawlāʾ." Then he ﷺ said:
"O ʿAlī, O ʿAlī, O ʿAlī!"
He said: "May my father and mother be your ransom." He said:

"You will fight the Banū al-Aṣfar, and those after you will fight them, until the best of Islam, the people of the Hijaz, who fear no blame from anyone who blames them in the matter of Allah, march out against them. They will conquer Constantinople with glorification (tasbīḥ) and magnification (takbīr), and they will gain spoils the like of which they have never gained, so that they will divide them out by the shieldful. Then someone will come and say, 'The Antichrist (al-Masīḥ) has emerged in your lands.' But it is a lie. The one who takes it up will regret it, and the one who leaves it will regret it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you see a man who has been given detachment from this world and little speech, draw near to him, for he is imparted wisdom."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, direct me to a deed that, if I do it, Allah will love me and people will love me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Renounce this world and Allah will love you, and renounce what is in the hands of people and they will love you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Salmān fell ill and Saʿd visited him and saw him weeping. Saʿd said to him, "What makes you weep, my brother? Did you not keep company with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Did you not? Did you not?" Salmān said, "I am weeping for neither of two reasons: I do not weep out of longing for this world or dislike of the Hereafter. Rather, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a covenant with me, and I think I have surely exceeded it."

He said, "What was the covenant he made with you?" He said, "He made a covenant with me that what suffices each of you is the like of a traveler's provision, and I think I have surely exceeded it. As for you, Saʿd, fear Allah in your judgment when you judge, in your division when you divide, and in your intention when you intend."
Thābit said: It reached me that he left behind only some twenty-odd dirhams, from living expenses he had with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Shall I not tell you about the kings of Paradise?" I said, "Yes." He said:
"A weak man, considered weak, wearing two worn-out garments, to whom no one pays attention; if he were to swear by Allah, Allah would fulfill his oath."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Shall I not inform you of the best among you?"
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"The best among you are those who, when they are seen, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is remembered."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed, Allah loves His believing servant who is poor, abstains from begging, and has a large family to support."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to Umm Ayman, and I went with him. She was offered a vessel containing a drink. [Anas] said: I do not know whether he came upon her while he was fasting or whether he did not want it. She began to protest loudly at him and to scold him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered Paradise and heard a soft rustling sound. I said: 'Who is this?' They said: 'This is al-Ghumayṣāʾ bint Milḥān, the mother of Anas ibn Mālik.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I was shown Paradise, and I saw the wife of Abū Ṭalḥah. Then I heard a rustling in front of me, and it was Bilāl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A son of Abū Ṭalḥah by Umm Sulaym died. She said to her family: "Do not tell Abū Ṭalḥah about his son until I myself tell him." [Anas] said: He came, and she served him his evening meal, and he ate and drank. Then she adorned herself for him more beautifully than she had ever done before, and he had relations with her. When she saw that he was satisfied and had been intimate with her, she said: "O Abū Ṭalḥah, what do you think: if some people lent something to a household, and then asked for their loan back, would they have the right to refuse it to them?" He said: "No."
She said: "Then seek reward with Allah for your son."
He said: He became angry and said: "You left me until I was defiled, and then you told me about my son!"
He went until he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him what had happened. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"May Allah bless you both in your night that has passed."

He said: She conceived. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on a journey and she was with him. It was the practice of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that when he returned to Madinah from a journey he would not arrive at night unannounced. They drew near to Madinah, and the pains of labour seized her, so Abū Ṭalḥah stayed behind with her, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on. [Anas] said: Abū Ṭalḥah said: "You know, my Lord, that I love to go out with Your Messenger when he goes out and to enter with him when he enters, and I have been held back as You see." He said: Umm Sulaym said: "O Abū Ṭalḥah, I no longer feel what I was feeling. Go on."

So we went on. He said: The labour pains seized her just as they arrived, and she gave birth to a boy. My mother said to me: "O Anas, let no one nurse him until you take him in the morning to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
When morning came, I carried him and took him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: I found him with a branding iron in his hand. When he saw me he said:
"Perhaps Umm Sulaym has given birth." I said: "Yes."

So he put down the branding iron. He said: I brought the child and placed him in his lap. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for some ʿajwah dates of Madinah, chewed them in his mouth until they softened, then placed them in the child's mouth, and the child began to smack his lips on them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Look at how the Anṣār love dates."
He said: Then he wiped the child's face and named him ʿAbdullāh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I thought that ʿAbdullāh was one of the members of the household.
Or he mentioned something like this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were in the house of Abū Mūsā with a group of the Companions of ʿAbdullāh, and they were looking at a copy of the Qur'an. ʿAbdullāh stood up, and Abū Masʿūd said: "I do not know of anyone the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left behind him who knows more of what Allah revealed than this man who is standing."
Abū Mūsā said: "If you say that, well, he used to be present when we were absent, and he would be given permission to enter when we were kept out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of Jarīr and Wakīʿ, in the narration of Abū Bakr from Abū Muʿāwiyah:
he put Muʿādh before Ubayy.
And in the narration of Abū Kurayb: Ubayy before Muʿādh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A garment of silk was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Then he mentioned the hadith. Then Ibn ʿAbdah said: Abū Dāwūd informed us: Shuʿbah narrated to us: Qatādah narrated to me from Anas ibn Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to this or like it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a sword on the Day of Uhud and said:
"Who will take this from me?"
They stretched out their hands, each of them saying: "I will, I will." He said:
"Then who will take it with its due right?"
He said: The people held back. Then Simāk ibn Kharashah, Abū Dujānah, said: "I will take it with its right."
He said: He took it and split open with it the heads of the polytheists.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father was brought on the Day of Uhud with his nose and ears cut off, and he was placed in front of the Prophet ﷺ.
Then he mentioned something like their hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to wear his ring on his left hand, and its stone was on the inner side of his palm.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar
used to wear his ring on his left hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw on aṣ-Ṣalt ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib a ring on his right little finger, so I said, "What is this?" He said, "I saw Ibn ʿAbbās wear his ring like this," and he placed its stone on the back of the finger.
He said: I think that Ibn ʿAbbās only did so because he used to mention that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wore his ring in that way.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A freed slave woman of theirs took the daughter of az-Zubayr to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and on her leg were bells. ʿUmar cut them off, then said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'With every bell there is a devil.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The freed slave woman of ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥassān al-Anṣārī, from ʿĀʾishah,

said: While she was with her, a girl was brought in to her wearing anklets that made a sound. She said, "Do not bring her in to me unless you cut off her anklets." And she said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'The angels do not enter a house in which there is a bell.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever loves to put a ring of Fire on his beloved, let him put on him a ring of gold. Whoever loves to put a collar of Fire on his beloved, let him put on him a collar of gold. And whoever loves to put a bracelet of Fire on his beloved, let him put on him a bracelet of gold. But you should use silver; so play with it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There will be four trials in this Ummah, and at the end of them is annihilation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned the trials and spoke at length about them, until he mentioned the trial of the aḥlās. Someone said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the trial of the aḥlās?" He said:

"It is flight and fighting. Then the trial of as-sarrāʾ: its smoke is from under the feet of a man from my family who claims that he is from me, but he is not from me; my friends are only the God-fearing. Then the people will agree upon a man like a hip on a rib. Then the trial of ad-duhaymāʾ: it will not leave anyone of this Ummah without striking him a blow. When it is said that it has ended, it will continue. A man will be a believer in it in the morning and a disbeliever in the evening, until the people become two camps: a camp of faith in which there is no hypocrisy, and a camp of hypocrisy in which there is no faith. When that happens, then expect the Dajjāl that day or the next."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān said: By Allah, I do not know whether my Companions forgot or pretended to forget. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not leave out any leader of a trial, up until the end of the world, who would have three hundred or more followers, except that he named him to us by his name, his father's name, and his tribe's name.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Kūfah at the time Tustar was conquered, to bring back mules from there. I entered the mosque and saw a group of men, and a man sitting whom you could tell, on seeing him, was one of the men of the Hijaz. I said, "Who is this?" The people looked at me sternly and said, "Do you not know him? This is Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān, the Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." Ḥudhayfah said: People used to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about good, and I used to ask him about evil. The people stared at him, so he said: I see what you disapprove of. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, do you think that after this good which Allah has given us there will be evil, as there was before it?" He said, "Yes."
I said, "What is the protection from that?" He said, "The sword."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, then what will happen?" He said:
"If Allah has a caliph on the earth, and he strikes your back and takes your wealth, obey him; otherwise, die while biting onto the trunk of a tree."
I said, "Then what?" He said:

"Then the Dajjāl will come out with a river and a fire. Whoever falls into his fire, his reward is established and his burden is removed; and whoever falls into his river, his burden is established and his reward is removed."
I said, "Then what?" He said:
"Then it is the establishment of the Hour."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Gog and Magog will be let loose, and they will come forth as Allah the Exalted said: {and they descend from every elevation}. They will cover the earth, and the Muslims will withdraw from them until the remnant of the Muslims are in their cities and fortresses, having gathered their livestock to them. They will pass by a river and drink it until they leave nothing in it, and the last of them will pass by in their wake and say, 'There was once water in this place.' They will prevail over the earth, and one of them will say, 'These are the people of the earth; we have finished with them. Now let us fight the people of heaven.' One of them will even shake his spear toward the sky, and it will come back stained with blood, and they will say, 'We have killed the people of heaven.'

While they are in that state, Allah will send upon them worms like the worms of locusts, which will seize them by their necks, and they will die like locusts, one piled upon another. The Muslims will wake up and hear no sound from them, and they will say, 'Who will sacrifice himself and go see what they have done?' A man from among them will go down, having resigned himself to being killed, and he will find them dead. He will call out, 'Rejoice, for your enemy has perished!'

Then the people will come out and let their livestock go free, and they will have no pasture except the flesh of the dead, and the animals will grow fat on it better than they ever grew fat on any vegetation they had ever eaten."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the night the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, he met Ibrāhīm, Mūsā and ʿĪsā, and they discussed the Hour. They began with Ibrāhīm and asked him about it, but he had no knowledge of it. Then they asked Mūsā, and he had no knowledge of it. Then the matter was referred to ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, who said: "I have been given a covenant concerning what comes before its occurrence, but as for when it will occur, none knows it except Allah."

He then mentioned the emergence of the Dajjāl, and said: "I will descend and kill him. Then the people will return to their lands, and Gog and Magog will meet them, descending from every elevation. They will not pass by any water except that they drink it, nor anything except that they ruin it. The people will cry out to Allah, so I will supplicate Allah to destroy them, and the earth will stink from their smell. They will cry out to Allah again, and I will supplicate Allah, and He will send rain from the sky that will carry them and throw them into the sea. Then the mountains will be shattered and the earth will be stretched out like leather. I have been given a covenant that when that happens, the Hour will be to the people like a pregnant woman whose family do not know when she will suddenly give birth."
Al-ʿAwwām said: The confirmation of that is found in the Book of Allah the Exalted: {Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose and they descend from every elevation}
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, some youths from Banū Hāshim came. When the Prophet ﷺ saw them, his eyes filled with tears and his color changed. I said, "We still see something in your face that we dislike." He said:

"We are a household for whom Allah has chosen the Hereafter over this world. After me, my household will meet with affliction, displacement and expulsion, until a people come from the east carrying black banners. They will ask for good but will not be given it, so they will fight and be victorious, and they will be given what they asked for, but they will not accept it, until they hand it over to a man from my household, who will fill it with justice just as they filled it with injustice. So whoever among you lives to see that, let him go to them, even if crawling over snow."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"In my Ummah there will be the Mahdī. If his time is short, it will be seven years; otherwise, nine. My Ummah will enjoy in it a blessing the like of which they never enjoyed before; the earth will give its produce and withhold nothing from them, and wealth in those days will be heaped up in piles. A man will stand and say, 'O Mahdī, give me,' and he will say, 'Take.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Three will fight at your treasure, each of them the son of a caliph, and it will not pass to any of them. Then the black banners will appear from the east, and they will kill you in a manner no people have ever killed."
Then he mentioned something I do not remember, and said:
"When you see him, pledge allegiance to him, even if crawling over snow, for he is the Caliph of Allah, the Mahdī."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Mahdī is from us, the People of the House. Allah will set him right in a single night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Umm Salamah and we discussed the Mahdī. She said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The Mahdī is from the descendants of Fāṭimah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We, the children of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, are the leaders of the people of Paradise: myself, Ḥamzah, ʿAlī, Jaʿfar, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn and the Mahdī."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"People will come forth from the east and pave the way for the Mahdī," meaning his authority.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Sulaym made a loaf of bread for the Prophet ﷺ and put some ghee on it. Then she said, "Go to the Prophet ﷺ and invite him." He said: So I came to him and said, "My mother invites you."
He said: So he got up and said to those of the people who were with him, "Get up."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The family of Muhammad ﷺ never had their fill of barley bread until he was taken [in death].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wore wool and wore patched sandals.
And he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ate coarse food and wore rough clothing.
Al-Ḥasan was asked, "What is the coarse food?" He said, "Coarse barley, which he could only swallow with a gulp of water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was pressed,
to eat some food, and he said, "It is enough for me that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'The people who are most full in this world will be the hungriest on the Day of Resurrection.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is among extravagance that you eat everything you desire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered the house and saw a piece of bread lying there. He took it, wiped it, and then ate it, and said:
"ʿĀʾishah, honor what is good for you, for it never fled from a people and then returned to them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not give up supper, even if it is with a handful of dates, for leaving it causes one to grow old."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Goodness reaches the house in which food is eaten faster than the knife reaches the camel's hump."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is part of the Sunnah that a man goes out with his guest to the door of the house."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar entered upon him while he was at his table, so he made room for him at the head of the gathering and said, "In the name of Allah."
Then he reached out with his hand and took a morsel, then took another, and then said, "I find the taste of fat that is not the fat of meat."

ʿAbd Allāh said, "Commander of the Faithful, I went out to the market looking for fat meat to buy, but found it expensive. So I bought lean meat for a dirham and added ghee for a dirham, because I wanted my family to go back and forth, bone by bone."
ʿUmar said, "The two were never together with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except that he ate one of them and gave the other in charity."
ʿAbd Allāh said, "Take it, Commander of the Faithful; the two will never be together with me but that I will do that."
He said, "I would not do that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of men
came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he found the smell of leeks on them, and said:
"Did I not forbid you from eating this plant? The angels are harmed by what harms human beings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions:
"Do not eat onions."
Then he said a word quietly: "raw."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Grapes from Ṭāʾif were given as a gift to the Prophet ﷺ, and he called me and said:
"Take this bunch and deliver it to your mother."
But I ate it before I delivered it to her. After some nights, he said to me:
"What happened to the bunch? Did you deliver it to your mother?" I said, "No."
He said: So he called me "treacherous."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while he had a quince in his hand, and he said:
"Take it, Ṭalḥah, for it strengthens the heart."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My close friend ﷺ advised me:

"Do not associate anything with Allah, even if you are cut to pieces and burned; do not deliberately leave an obligatory prayer, for whoever leaves it deliberately, the protection is lifted from him; and do not drink wine, for it is the key to every evil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"Beware of wine, for its sin branches out into sins just as its tree branches out into trees."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"One who is addicted to wine is like a worshipper of idols."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the sons of Ṣuhayb,
the freedman of Ibn Jadʿān, claimed [ownership of] two houses and a room,
saying that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had given that to Ṣuhayb.
Marwān said, "Who testifies for you two to that?" They said, "Ibn ʿUmar."
So he called him, and he testified: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did give Ṣuhayb two houses and a room."
So Marwān ruled in their favor on the basis of his testimony.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "The ʿumrā [gift] is permissible."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and she was wearing a coarse cotton shift worth five dirhams.
She said, "Raise your eyes to my maidservant,
and look at her, for she is too proud to wear it at home.
I once had one of these shifts in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
and there was no woman in Madinah who was being adorned [for her husband] except that she would send to me to borrow it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"How excellent a charity is a milch she-camel of choice, lent for her milk,
and a milch sheep of choice, lent for her milk: she goes out in the morning with one vessel [of milk] and returns in the evening with another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With that—meaning Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both—[he reported] that the Prophet ﷺ went out to a land swaying with crops and said, "Whose is this?"
They said, "So-and-so has rented it." He said,
"Had he lent it to him [freely], that would have been better for him than taking a fixed payment for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Abraham migrated with Sarah, and they gave her a reward [or: gift],
and she returned and said, 'Did you realize that Allah has humbled the disbeliever and given [me] a servant girl?'"
Ibn Sīrīn said, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "And he gave her Hagar as a servant."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah said, concerning] the people of the slander: She said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Usāmah ibn Zayd when the revelation was delayed, asking them
and consulting them about separating from his wife.
As for Usāmah, he advised according to what he knew of his wife's innocence.
As for ʿAlī, he said, 'Allah has not placed any restriction upon you,
and there are many women besides her,
and ask the maidservant; she will tell you the truth.' So he said,
'Have you seen anything that made you doubt?'
She said, 'I have seen nothing more than that she is a young girl who sleeps through her family's dough, and the domestic animal comes and eats it.'
Then he stood on the pulpit and said,
'O Muslims, who will excuse me regarding a man whose harm to my family has reached me?
By Allah, I know nothing of my family but good.'"
Then she mentioned the declaration of ʿĀʾishah's innocence.
And Abū Usāmah said, from Hishām:
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb al-Anṣārī set out toward the palm grove in which Ibn Ṣayyād was. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to shield himself behind the trunks of the palm trees,
trying to catch something of what Ibn Ṣayyād said before he could see him.
Ibn Ṣayyād was lying on his bed in a velvet cloth of his, in which he was murmuring—or humming. Ibn Ṣayyād's mother saw the Prophet ﷺ as he was shielding himself behind the palm trunks,
and she said to Ibn Ṣayyād, "Ṣāfi, this is Muḥammad!"
So Ibn Ṣayyād stopped.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"If she had left him alone, he would have made [things] clear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people used to be held to account through revelation in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
and revelation has now ceased,
and we now hold you to account only by what appears to us of your deeds.
So whoever shows us good, we trust him and bring him close,
and nothing of his inner self is our concern;
Allah will take him to account for his inner self.
But whoever shows us evil, we will not trust him nor believe him,
even if he says that his inner self is good.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
stole during the expedition of the Conquest [of Makkah],
and she was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who then gave the order, and her hand was cut off.
ʿĀʾishah said, "Her repentance was good, and she married,
and she used to come to me afterwards, and I would present her need to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he ordered, concerning one who committed unlawful sexual intercourse and was not married, a flogging of one hundred lashes and banishment for a year.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ heard a man reciting in the mosque and said, "May Allah have mercy on him.
He has reminded me of such and such verses
that I had dropped from such and such sūrah."
ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allāh added, from ʿĀʾishah: The Prophet ﷺ was praying at night in my house and heard the voice of ʿAbbād praying in the mosque, and he said, "O ʿĀʾishah,
is that the voice of ʿAbbād?" I said, "Yes." He said,
"O Allah, have mercy on ʿAbbād."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Is the testimony of a woman not equal to half the testimony of a man?" We said, "Yes." He said,
"That is due to the deficiency of her intellect."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ went out at an hour when he did not usually go out, and when no one would meet him. Abū Bakr came to him, and he said, "
What brought you out, Abū Bakr?"
He said, "I went out to meet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to look at his face, and to greet him with peace."
Before long ʿUmar came, and he said, "
What brought you out, ʿUmar?"
He said, "Hunger, O Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
I have found some of that as well."

So they set out for the house of Abū al-Haytham ibn at-Tayyihān al-Anṣārī. He was a man with many date palms and sheep, but he had no servants. They did not find him, so they asked his wife, "Where is your husband?" She said, "He has gone to fetch fresh water for us."

Before long Abū al-Haytham came with a water skin that he was carrying with effort. He put it down, then came and embraced the Prophet ﷺ and said, "May my father and mother be your ransom." Then he took them to his garden and spread out a mat for them. Then he went to a palm tree, brought a cluster of dates and set it down. The Prophet ﷺ said, "
Why did you not pick out some of the ripe dates for us?"
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I wanted you to choose," or he said, "to pick for yourselves, from its ripe dates and its half-ripe dates."
They ate and drank of that water. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
By the One in whose hand is my soul, this is part of the bounty about which you will be asked on the Day of Resurrection: cool shade, good ripe dates, and cool water."
Then Abū al-Haytham went off to prepare food for them, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "
Do not slaughter an animal that gives milk."
So he slaughtered a young she-goat or a kid for them and brought it to them, and they ate. Then the Prophet ﷺ said, "
Do you have a servant?" He said, "No." He said, "
When captives come to us, come to us."
Then two captives were brought to the Prophet ﷺ, with no third. Abū al-Haytham came to him, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "Choose one of them."
He said, "O Prophet of Allah, choose for me." The Prophet ﷺ said, "
The one who is consulted is trusted. Take this one, for I saw him praying, and treat him well."

Abū al-Haytham went to his wife and told her what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said. His wife said, "You will not fulfil what the Prophet ﷺ said about him unless you set him free." He said, "Then he is free." Then the Prophet ﷺ said, "

Allah has not sent any prophet or caliph except that he has two kinds of close advisers: one who commands him to do good and forbids him from evil, and one who spares no effort in corrupting him. Whoever is protected from the evil adviser has indeed been protected."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, and he mentioned a hadith similar to this, but did not mention in it [a narration] from Abū Hurayrah. The hadith of Shaybān is more complete and longer than the hadith of Abū ʿAwānah.
Shaybān is considered reliable by them, a man of [written] books.
This hadith has also been narrated from Abū Hurayrah by another route, and it has also been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about hunger, and we lifted up our garments from our bellies to show a stone tied on each. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lifted his garment to show two stones.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She was
married to Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. She said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, "

This wealth is green and sweet. Whoever takes it by its right will be blessed in it. But many who plunge into the wealth of Allah and His Messenger as their own desires lead them will have nothing on the Day of Resurrection except the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Cursed is the slave of the dinar; cursed is the slave of the dirham."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Two hungry wolves let loose among sheep would not do more damage to them than a man's greed for wealth and status does to his religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Whoever does deeds to be seen, Allah will expose him; and whoever does deeds to be heard, Allah will make it known."
He said, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Whoever does not show mercy to people, Allah will not show mercy to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding the saying of the Almighty:

"When believing women come to you as emigrants, test them" [60:10], he said: When a woman came to the Prophet ﷺ to accept Islam, he would make her swear by Allah that she had not left out of hatred for her husband, and that she had not left except out of love for Allah and His Messenger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of us Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat together and discussed, and we said: If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, we would do them. So Allah the Almighty revealed:

"Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise. O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?" [61:1-2] ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to us. Abū Salamah said: Ibn Salām recited it to us.
Yaḥyā said: Abū Salamah recited it to us.
Ibn Kathīr said: Al-Awzāʿī recited it to us.
ʿAbdullāh said: Ibn Kathīr recited it to us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went on a military expedition with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and some of the Bedouins were with us. We would rush to the water, but the Bedouins would beat us to it. A Bedouin would get ahead of his companions, fill the basin, place stones around it, and spread a leather mat over it until his companions arrived.

He said: Then a man of the Anṣār came to a Bedouin and loosened the rein of his camel so that it could drink, but the Bedouin refused to let him. So he pulled out the water's barrier, and the Bedouin raised his stick and struck the Anṣārī on the head and wounded him. The Anṣārī went to ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, the chief of the hypocrites, and told him, and he was one of his companions. ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy became angry and then said:
"Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse" [63:7], from around him.

He meant the Bedouins, who used to attend the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at mealtimes. ʿAbdullāh said: When they have dispersed from Muḥammad, bring Muḥammad the food, so that he and those with him may eat. Then he said to his companions: If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely drive out the more humble from it.

Zayd said: I was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I heard ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, so I told my uncle. He went and told the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for him, but he swore and denied it.

He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ believed him and disbelieved me. He said: Then my uncle came to me and said: You only wanted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims to despise you and call you a liar.
He said: Then a distress came over me such as had not come over anyone.

He said: While I was traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, my head nodding from distress, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me, pinched my ear, and smiled in my face. I would not have been happier to have eternity in this world in exchange for that.
Then Abū Bakr caught up with me and said: What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say to you? I said: He said nothing, except that he pinched my ear and smiled in my face. He said: Be glad.
Then ʿUmar caught up with me, and I told him the same as I had told Abū Bakr. When morning came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with them both. He said: Whoever has wealth sufficient to reach the house of his Lord for Hajj, or on which zakāh is due, and does not do so, will ask to return [to life] at the time of death.
A man said: O Ibn ʿAbbās, fear Allah! Only the disbelievers ask to return. He said: I will recite to you a Qurʾānic verse about that:
"O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah":
"And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you," up to His saying:
"And Allah is Aware of what you do." [63:9-11] The man said: What makes zakāh obligatory? He said: When wealth reaches two hundred dirhams or more.
He said: And what makes Hajj obligatory? He said: Provisions and a mount.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O you who believe, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them." He said: These were men from the people of Mecca who accepted Islam and wanted to come to the Prophet ﷺ, but their wives and children refused to let them go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then when they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they saw that people had gained understanding of the religion, and they were inclined to punish their families. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed:
"O you who believe, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them" [64:14], the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ lagged behind, and he mentioned this story.

He said: We came to the people while ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was leading them in the dawn prayer. When he saw the Prophet ﷺ, he wanted to step back, but he signaled to him to continue. He said: So I and the Prophet ﷺ prayed one rakʿah behind him. When he had given the salām, the Prophet ﷺ stood up and prayed the rakʿah that he had missed, without adding anything to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He witnessed ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf asking Bilāl about the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: He would go out to relieve himself, then I would bring him water, and he would perform ablution and wipe over his turban and his leather socks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiped over the two leather socks.
I said: O Messenger of Allah, did you forget? He said:
"Rather, you have forgotten. My Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded me to do this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution and wiped over his sandals and his feet.

ʿAbbād said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ come to the water channel of a people, meaning the place of ablution. Musaddad did not mention the place of ablution or the channel, and then they agreed: He performed ablution and wiped over his sandals and his feet.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If the religion were based on opinion, the underside of the leather sock would be more deserving of wiping than its top. Yet I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wipe over the top of his leather socks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ urinated, he would perform ablution and sprinkle water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, with a meaning similar to that of Qatādah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the Companions of the Prophet reported that the Prophet ﷺ saw a man praying with a spot on the top of his foot, about the size of a dirham, which the water had not reached. So the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to repeat the ablution and the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ kissed her and did not perform ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was a guest of the Prophet ﷺ one night, and he ordered that a side of meat be roasted. He took a knife and began cutting some of it for me. He said: Then Bilāl came and informed him that it was time for prayer. He said: So he threw down the knife and said:
"What is wrong with him? May his hands be covered in dust!" And he stood up to pray.
Al-Anbārī added: My mustache had grown long, so he trimmed it for me over a siwāk.
Or he said: I will trim it for you over a siwāk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I brought bread and meat to the Prophet ﷺ, and he ate. Then he called for water for ablution and performed ablution with it, and then prayed the Ẓuhr prayer. Then he called for the rest of his food and ate, then stood for the prayer without performing ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Jazʾ, one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, came to us in Egypt, and I heard him narrating in the mosque of Egypt. He said: I remember being the seventh of seven, or the sixth of six, with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a man's house. Bilāl passed by and called him to prayer, so we went out and passed by a man whose cooking pot was on the fire. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Is your pot cooked well?"
He said: Yes, may my father and mother be your ransom.
So he took a piece from it and kept chewing it until he began the prayer, while I was looking at him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank milk, and he did not rinse his mouth or perform ablution, and he prayed.
Zayd said: Shuʿbah directed me to this shaykh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, meaning on the expedition of Dhāt al-Riqāʿ. A man struck the wife of one of the polytheists, and he swore that he would not stop until he had shed blood among the Companions of Muḥammad. So he set out following the trail of the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ stopped at a camping place and said, "Who will keep watch for us?" A man from the Muhājirūn and a man from the Anṣār volunteered, and he said:
"Stay at the mouth of the mountain pass."

He said: When the two men went out to the mouth of the pass, the Muhājir lay down and the Anṣārī stood praying. The man came, and when he saw his figure he knew he was a lookout for the people, so he shot him with an arrow and lodged it in him. He pulled it out, until the man had shot him with three arrows. Then he bowed and prostrated. Then his companion woke up, and when the man realized that they had been alerted to him, he fled. When the Muhājir saw the blood on the Anṣārī, he said: Glory be to Allah! Why did you not wake me at the first shot? He said: I was in the middle of a sūrah that I was reciting, and I did not like to cut it short.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to wait for the last evening prayer until their heads nodded, then they would pray without performing ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that Riʿl,
Dhakwān, ʿUṣayyah and Banū Liḥyān asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for reinforcements against an enemy,
so he reinforced them with seventy men of the Anṣār,
whom we used to call the Qurrāʾ (the Qur'an reciters) in their time,
who would gather firewood by day and pray by night,
until, when they reached Biʾr Maʿūnah, [the tribes] killed them and betrayed them. The news reached the Prophet ﷺ,
so he made Qunūt for a month, supplicating in the dawn prayer against some of the Arab tribes,
against Riʿl, Dhakwān, ʿUṣayyah and Banū Liḥyān.
Anas said: We used to recite a verse concerning them, then it was lifted: 'Convey to our people on our behalf
that we have met our Lord,
and He is pleased with us and has made us pleased.'
And from Qatādah, from Anas ibn Mālik, who related to him that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ made Qunūt for a month in the dawn prayer, supplicating against some of the Arab tribes,
against Riʿl, Dhakwān, ʿUṣayyah and Banū Liḥyān.
Khalīfah added: Ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, Anas narrated to us
that those seventy
of the Anṣār were killed at Biʾr Maʿūnah; we recited a Qurʾanic text about them. Similar to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He would quote the poetry of Abū Ṭālib: "A fair-faced one by whose face the clouds are petitioned for rain, a refuge for orphans, a protector of widows." And ʿUmar ibn Ḥamzah said: Sālim narrated to us, from his father:
Often I would recall the poet's words while looking
at the face of the Prophet ﷺ as he prayed for rain,
and he would not step down until every gutter was flowing.
"A fair-faced one by whose face the clouds are petitioned for rain, a refuge for orphans, a protector of widows" — and this is the saying of Abū Ṭālib.
label: machine translation

segments_en: the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: When there was a day of wind and clouds, it would be noticed in the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; he would pace forward and back. When it rained, he would be pleased by it and that [worry] would leave him.
ʿĀʾishah said: I asked him, and he said:
"I feared it might be a punishment sent upon my community."
And when he saw the rain he would say: "A mercy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "I was given victory by the east wind,
and ʿĀd were destroyed by the west wind."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, bless us in our Shām; O Allah, bless us in our Yemen."
They said: And in our Najd. He said:
"O Allah, bless us in our Shām and bless us in our Yemen."
They said: And in our Najd. He said:
"There are the earthquakes and the trials, and from there—or he said: in it—the horn of Satan will emerge."
This ḥadīth is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb from this route, from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAwn.
This ḥadīth has also been narrated from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed on the day Ibrāhīm died,
and the people said: It was eclipsed because of Ibrāhīm's death.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah;
they are not eclipsed for the death of anyone nor for his life.
So when you see them, call upon Allah and pray until it clears."
label: machine translation

segments_en: the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: The sun was eclipsed during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, so he went out to the mosque, and the people formed rows behind him.
He said the takbīr, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited at length.
Then he said the takbīr and bowed for a long time.
Then he said: "Allah hears whoever praises Him."
Then he stood and did not prostrate,
and he recited at length,
though less than the first recitation.
Then he said the takbīr and bowed for a long time,
though less than the first bowing.
Then he said: "Allah hears whoever praises Him,
our Lord, and to You belongs all praise." Then he prostrated.
Then he did the same in the other rakʿah,
so he completed four bowings and four prostrations,
and the sun cleared before he finished.
Then he stood and praised Allah as He deserves, then said:
"They are two signs among the signs of Allah;
they are not eclipsed for the death of anyone nor for his life.
So when you see them, hasten to prayer."
Kathīr ibn ʿAbbās used to relate that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, related on the day the sun was eclipsed the like of the ḥadīth of ʿUrwah from ʿĀʾishah.
I said to ʿUrwah: Your brother, on the day the sun was eclipsed in Madinah, did no more than two rakʿahs like the dawn prayer.
He said: Yes, because he erred regarding the Sunnah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ indeed commanded the freeing of slaves during an eclipse of the sun.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When he finished his recitation, he said the takbīr and bowed,
and when he rose from the bowing he said: "Allah hears whoever praises Him,
our Lord, and to You belongs all praise."
Then he would resume the recitation in the eclipse prayer,
four bowings in two rakʿahs and four prostrations.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated in it—meaning Sūrat an-Najm—and so did the Muslims, the polytheists, the jinn and mankind.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of them adding to the other, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr:
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The first women to use a girdle were from the side of the mother of Ismāʿīl.
She used a girdle so as to hide her tracks from Sarah.
Then Ibrāhīm brought her
and her son Ismāʿīl, while she was nursing him, until he placed them near the House, by a large tree
above Zamzam, in the upper part of the mosque.
At that time there was no one in Makkah,
and there was no water there. So he left them there,
and he placed beside them a bag containing dates and a water-skin containing water.

Then Ibrāhīm turned and set off, and the mother of Ismāʿīl followed him and said, "O Ibrāhīm, where are you going, leaving us in this valley in which there is no person and nothing?" She said this to him several times,
but he did not turn to her. Then she said to him, "Is it Allah who has commanded you to do this?" He said, "Yes."
She said, "Then He will not let us be lost." Then she returned.
Ibrāhīm went on until, when he reached the mountain pass where they could no longer see him, he faced the House,
then he made supplication with these words, raising his hands,
and said: {Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a valley without cultivation} until he reached {that they may be grateful}.
The mother of Ismāʿīl kept nursing Ismāʿīl
and drinking from that water,
until, when what was in the water-skin ran out, she became thirsty and her son became thirsty.
She began to look at him writhing—or he said, tossing about—and she went off, not wanting to look at him.
She found that Ṣafā was the closest mountain on the earth to her,
so she stood on it, then faced the valley, looking to see whether she could see anyone, but she saw no one. Then she came down from
Ṣafā, and when she reached the valley, she lifted the edge of her garment,
then she hurried like a person in distress,
until she crossed the valley,
then she came to Marwah,
and stood on it and looked to see whether she could see anyone,
but she saw no one.
She did that seven times. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"That is why people run between the two."
When she climbed up on Marwah, she heard a voice, and she said, "Hush!"—meaning herself. Then she listened closely and heard it again,
and she said, "You have made your voice heard;
if you have any help [for us]..."
And behold, there was the angel
at the place of Zamzam,
and he dug with his heel—or he said, with his wing—until water appeared.
She began to make a basin around it, and she said with her hand like this,
and she began to scoop up water into her water-skin,
while it gushed up after she had scooped. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"May Allah have mercy on the mother of Ismāʿīl! Had she left Zamzam—or he said, had she not scooped from the water—Zamzam would have been a flowing spring."
He said: So she drank and nursed her child.
The angel said to her, "Do not fear being lost,
for here is the House of Allah,
which this boy and his father will build,
and Allah does not let His people be lost."
The House was raised above the ground like a hillock,
the floods would come and pass by its right and its left. It remained so
until a company from Jurhum—or a family from Jurhum—passing by, coming from the way of Kadāʾ, camped in the lower part of Makkah,
and they saw a bird circling.
They said, "This bird must be circling over water.
We know this valley, and there was no water in it."
So they sent one or two scouts,
and they found water.
They returned and told them about the water, and they came.
He said: The mother of Ismāʿīl was by the water, and they said, "Will you permit us to settle near you?" She said, "Yes,
but you have no right to the water." They said, "Yes."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The mother of Ismāʿīl found this to be so,
and she loved company."
So they settled and sent for their families,
and they settled with them, until there were households of them there, and the boy grew up,
and learned Arabic from them,
and he impressed them, and they admired him as he grew up.
When he reached maturity, they married him to a woman from among them.
Then the mother of Ismāʿīl died. Then Ibrāhīm came,
after Ismāʿīl had married, to look in on what he had left behind,
but he did not find Ismāʿīl,
so he asked his wife about him, and she said, "He went out to seek [provision] for us."
Then he asked her about their livelihood and condition, and she said, "We are in misery,
in hardship and distress," and she complained to him.
He said, "When your husband comes, convey my greetings of peace to him,
and tell him to change the threshold of his door."
When Ismāʿīl came,
he seemed to sense something,
and he said, "Has anyone come to you?" She said, "Yes,
an old man of such and such description came to us,
and he asked us about you and I told him,
and he asked me how we were living and I told him we are in hardship and distress."
He said, "Did he instruct you with anything?" She said, "Yes,
he commanded me to convey greetings of peace to you,
and he says: Change the threshold of your door."
He said, "That was my father, and he has commanded me to separate from you. Go back to your family." So he divorced her,
and married another from among them.
Ibrāhīm stayed away from them as long as Allah willed, then came to them afterwards, but did not find him,
so he went in to his wife and asked her about him.
She said, "He went out to seek [provision] for us."
He said, "How are you?" and he asked her about their livelihood and condition.
She said, "We are well and in ease,"
and she praised Allah.
He said, "What is your food?" She said, "Meat."
He said, "And what is your drink?" She said, "Water."
He said, "O Allah, bless them in their meat and water." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"At that time they had no grain,
and had they had it, he would have supplicated for them regarding it."
He said: So no one outside Makkah lives on these two alone without it not agreeing with him.
He said, "When your husband comes, convey my greetings of peace to him,
and tell him to keep firm the threshold of his door."
When Ismāʿīl came, he said, "Has anyone come to you?" She said, "Yes, an old man of fine appearance came to us," and she praised him,
"and he asked me about you and I told him,
and he asked me how we were living and I told him we are well."
He said, "Did he instruct you with anything?" She said, "Yes,
he conveys greetings of peace to you,
and he commands you to keep firm the threshold of your door."
He said, "That was my father, and you are the threshold;
he has commanded me to keep you."
Then he stayed away from them as long as Allah willed,
then came after that,
while Ismāʿīl was sharpening arrows of his under a large tree near Zamzam.
When he saw him, he stood up to him,
and they did as a father does with his son and a son with his father.
Then he said, "O Ismāʿīl,
Allah has commanded me with a command."
He said, "Then do what your Lord has commanded you."
He said, "And will you help me?" He said, "I will help you."
He said, "Allah has commanded me to build a house here,"
and he pointed to a mound raised above its surroundings.
He said: At that point they raised the foundations of the House,
Ismāʿīl began bringing the stones and Ibrāhīm building,
until when the structure rose high, he brought this stone and placed it for him,
and he stood on it while he built,
and Ismāʿīl handed him the stones,
and they were saying: {Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.}
He said: They kept building until they went around the House,
saying: {Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"These toilets are frequented [by jinn and devils]. So when one of you enters, let him say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the male and female evil spirits.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he had been a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us to face the two qiblahs when relieving ourselves of excrement or urine.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ wanted to relieve himself, he would not lift his garment until he was close to the ground.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umaymah bint Ruqayqah said: The Prophet ﷺ had a wooden cup in which he would urinate, and he would put it under the bed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade urinating in a hole.
He said: They asked Qatādah, "Why is urinating in a hole disliked?" He said: It used to be said that they are dwellings of the jinn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"Whoever applies kohl, let him do so an odd number of times; whoever does so has done well, and whoever does not, there is no harm. Whoever cleans himself with stones, let him do so an odd number of times; whoever does so has done well, and whoever does not, there is no harm. Whoever eats, let him spit out what he dislodges with a toothpick, and swallow what he moves around with his tongue; whoever does so has done well, and whoever does not, there is no harm. Whoever goes to relieve himself, let him screen himself; if he finds nothing but a heap of sand to gather, let him turn his back to it, for the devil plays with the seats of the children of Adam; whoever does so has done well, and whoever does not, there is no harm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Maslamah ibn Mukhallad appointed Ruwayfiʿ ibn Thābit as governor,
over the lower land.

Shaybān said: We traveled with him from Kawm Sharīk to ʿAlqamāʾ, or from ʿAlqamāʾ to Kawm Sharīk, and Ruwayfiʿ said: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, one of us would take his brother's emaciated camel on the condition that he would have half of what was gained as spoils and we would have half; and one of us would receive the arrowhead and the feathers, while the other received the shaft.
Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:

"O Ruwayfiʿ, perhaps you will live long after me, so inform the people that whoever ties his beard in knots, or hangs a bowstring around his neck, or cleans himself with the dung of an animal or with a bone, then Muhammad ﷺ is free of him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you goes to relieve himself, let him take three stones with him to clean himself with, for they will suffice him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about cleaning oneself after relieving oneself, and he said:
"With three stones, none of which is dung."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ urinated, and ʿUmar stood behind him with a jug of water. He said:
"What is this, ʿUmar?"
He said: This is water for you to perform ablution with. He said:
"I was not commanded to perform ablution every time I urinate; and if I did so, it would become a sunnah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I spent a night with the Prophet ﷺ. When he woke from his sleep, he went to his water for purification, took his tooth-stick and cleaned his teeth. Then he recited these verses: "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding," until he was close to finishing the chapter, or he finished it. Then he performed ablution, went to his place of prayer and prayed two rakʿahs. Then he returned to his bed and slept for as long as Allah willed. Then he woke and did the same, then returned to his bed and slept, then woke and did the same, then returned to his bed and slept, then woke and did the same. Each time he would clean his teeth and pray two rakʿahs. Then he prayed the witr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: None of you should urinate in standing water that does not flow, and then wash himself with it.

Sufyān said: They said to Hishām, meaning Ibn Ḥassān: Ayyūb only takes this hadith back as far as Abū Hurayrah. He said: If Ayyūb could have avoided attributing a hadith to the Prophet, he would not have done so.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sometimes my hand and the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would cross each other as we performed ablution from a single vessel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: O Allah, I ask You for the white palace on the right side of Paradise when I enter it.
He said: My son, ask Allah for Paradise and seek refuge in Him from the Fire, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"There will be among this nation people who transgress in purification and in supplication."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Companion of the Prophet ﷺ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us, and we brought out water for him in a brass basin, and he performed ablution with it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he saw Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ pray the Witr prayer with a single rakʿah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge [with Allah], saying:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from laziness,
and I seek refuge in You from cowardice,
and I seek refuge in You from decrepit old age,
and I seek refuge in You from miserliness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ called for water and performed ablution,
then he raised his hands and said:
"O Allah, forgive ʿUbayd Abū ʿĀmir."
And I saw the whiteness of his armpits. Then he said:
"O Allah, on the Day of Resurrection, place him above many of Your creation among the people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever says [it] ten times is like one who has freed a slave from the descendants of Ismāʿīl.
ʿUmar ibn Abī Zāʾidah said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī as-Safar narrated to us from ash-Shaʿbī, from Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, the same.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
