segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah said: Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war on him.
My servant draws near to Me with nothing more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him,
and My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary deeds until I love him.
And when I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears,
his sight with which he sees,
his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks.
If he asks Me, I will surely give him,
and if he seeks refuge in Me, I will surely protect him.
I do not hesitate about anything I do as I hesitate about taking the soul of the believer,
who dislikes death, and I dislike causing him harm."

"The first to be called on the Day of Resurrection will be Adam,
and his offspring will appear, and it will be said: This is your father Adam.
He will say: Here I am, at Your service.
[Allah] will say: Bring out the party destined for Hell from your offspring.
He will say: My Lord, how many shall I bring out? He will say: Bring out ninety-nine out of every hundred."
They said: O Messenger of Allah, if ninety-nine out of every hundred are taken from us,
what will remain of us? He said:
"My Ummah among the nations is like a white hair on a black ox."

segments_en: That he

went on the expedition to Tabūk with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Mughīrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went off to relieve himself before the Fajr prayer, and I carried a water-skin with him. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came back to me, I began to pour water over his hands from the water-skin, and he washed his hands three times. Then he washed his face. Then he went to take his arms out of his cloak, but its sleeves were too tight, so he put his hands inside the cloak until he brought his arms out from underneath it.

He washed his arms up to the elbows, then wiped over his leather socks, and then came forward. Al-Mughīrah said: I came forward with him until we found that the people had put ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf forward and he was leading them in prayer. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ caught up with one of the two rakʿahs and prayed the last rakʿah with the people. When ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf gave the salām, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up to complete his prayer. That alarmed the Muslims and they said "Subḥān Allāh" many times. When the Prophet ﷺ finished his prayer, he turned to them and said, "You did well," or he said, "You were right,"
admiring them for having prayed the prayer at its proper time.
label: machine translation

"Which of you recited {Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High}?" A man among the people said: I did, and I intended nothing by it but good. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"I realized that some of you were contending with me over it."

segments_en: One day, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among us, he dozed for a moment, then raised his head smiling. We said: What made you laugh, Messenger of Allah? He said:
"A sūrah was just revealed to me." Then he recited:
"In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. {Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice. Indeed, it is your enemy who is cut off.}" Then he said:
"Do you know what al-Kawthar is?"
We said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said:

"It is a river that my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, promised me; it has abundant good. It is a pond to which my nation will come on the Day of Resurrection. Its vessels are as numerous as the stars. Then a servant of them will be driven away, and I will say: My Lord, he is of my nation.
He will say: You do not know what he introduced after you."
Ibn Ḥujr added in his narration: "among us in the mosque." And he said:
"what he introduced after you."
label: machine translation

I had forbidden you to visit graves, but now visit the graves, for they make one detached from this world and remind one of the Hereafter."

segments_en: A man

held on to a debtor of his for ten dinars in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The debtor said, "I have nothing to give you." He said, "No, by Allah, I will not leave you until you pay me or bring me a guarantor." So he dragged him to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him, "How long will you give him?"
He said, "A month." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Then I will stand guarantor for him."
He came to him at the time the Prophet ﷺ had stated, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "
Where did you get this?"
He said, "From a mine." He said: "
There is no good in it." And he paid it off on his behalf.

segments_en: The Hour will not come until you fight a people whose sandals are made of hair,
and until you fight the Turks, small-eyed, red-faced,
flat-nosed, as if their faces were flattened shields."
"And you will find that among the best of people are those who most dislike this matter,
until he falls into it. And people are [like] mines;
the best of them in the Jāhiliyyah are the best of them in Islam."

segments_en: While I was with the Prophet
ﷺ, a man came to him and complained to him of poverty,
then another came to him
and complained of highway robbery. He said:
"O ʿAdī, have you seen al-Ḥīrah?"
I said: "I have not seen it, but I have been told about it." He said:
"If you live long, you will see the woman in her howdah travel from al-Ḥīrah
until she circumambulates the Kaʿbah,
fearing no one except Allah."
I said to myself: "Then where will the bandits of Ṭayyiʾ be, who have set the lands aflame?"
"And if you live long, the treasures of Khosrow will be conquered."
I said: "Khosrow son of Hurmuz?" He said:
"Khosrow son of Hurmuz.
And if you live long,
you will see a man go out with a handful of gold or silver,
seeking someone to accept it from him,
and he will find no one to accept it from him.
And each of you will meet Allah on the day he meets Him,
with no interpreter between him and Allah to interpret for him.
Allah will say: 'Did I not send a messenger to you who conveyed [the message] to you?' He will say: 'Yes.'
He will say: 'Did I not give you wealth and favor you?' He will say: 'Yes.'
Then he will look to his right and see only Hell,
and he will look to his left and see only Hell."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There will be trials,
in which the one sitting is better than the one standing,
and the one standing is better than the one walking,
and the one walking is better than the one running.
Whoever exposes himself to them, they will overwhelm him,
and whoever finds a refuge or shelter, let him take refuge in it."
And from Ibn Shihāb:
Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to me,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muṭīʿ ibn al-Aswad,
from Nawfal ibn Muʿāwiyah,
[a report] like this ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah,
except that Abū Bakr adds:
"Among prayers is a prayer such that whoever misses it, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth."

segments_en: I was sitting with Abū Hurayrah in the mosque of the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah, and with us was Marwān. Abū Hurayrah said: I heard the truthful one, whose truthfulness is confirmed, say:
"The destruction of my Ummah will be at the hands of some youths from Quraysh."
Marwān said: "May Allah curse them as youths!"
Abū Hurayrah said: "If I wished to say 'the sons of so-and-so and the sons of so-and-so,' I could."
I used to go out with my grandfather to the sons of Marwān when they ruled in Syria,
and when he saw them as young boys, he said to us: "Perhaps these are among them." We said: "You know best."

He went to him and found him sitting in his house with his head lowered. He said to him: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "Evil.
He used to raise his voice above the voice of the Prophet ﷺ, so his deeds have come to nothing,
and he is among the people of the Fire."
The man came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him that he had said such and such. Mūsā said: Then he returned to him a second time with great glad tidings, and he said:

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered upon a Bedouin to visit him when he was sick. He said: Whenever the Prophet ﷺ visited a sick person, he would say: "No harm, it is a purification, if Allah wills." So he said to him:
"No harm, it is a purification, if Allah wills."

segments_en: On the pulpit of Kufah, he said:

"When it is Friday, the devils go out in the morning with their banners to the markets, and they throw doubts and distractions at the people and hold them back from Friday prayer. The angels go out in the morning and sit at the doors of the mosque, recording a man who came in the first hour and a man who came in the second hour, until the imam comes out. When a man sits in a place where he is able to listen and to see, and he stays silent and does not speak idly, he will have two portions of reward. If he sits far away where he cannot hear, and he stays silent and does not speak idly, he will have one portion of reward. And if he sits in a place where he is able to listen and to see, but he speaks idly and does not stay silent, he will bear one portion of sin. And whoever says to his companion on Friday, 'Be quiet,'
has spoken idly, and whoever speaks idly has nothing from that Friday prayer of his."

label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Hasten to pray witr before the morning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When half the night or two-thirds of it has passed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, descends to the lowest heaven and says: Is there anyone asking, so that he may be given? Is there anyone calling, so that he may be answered? Is there anyone seeking forgiveness, so that he may be forgiven? until the dawn breaks."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah descends to the lowest heaven at half the night or the last third of the night and says: Who calls upon Me, so that I may answer him? Or asks Me, so that I may give him?
Then He says: Who will lend to One who is neither poor nor unjust?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hurayrah, both said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah gives respite until, when the first third of the night has passed, He descends to the lowest heaven and says: Is there anyone seeking forgiveness? Is there anyone repenting? Is there anyone asking? Is there anyone calling? until the dawn breaks."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that all the doors be closed except the door of ʿAlī.
This ḥadīth is gharīb. We do not know it from Shuʿbah with this chain except through this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the hands of Ḥasan and Ḥusayn and said:
"Whoever loves me, and loves these two, and their father and their mother, will be with me in my rank on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The first to pray was ʿAlī.
He said: This ḥadīth is gharīb from this route. We do not know it from the narration of Shuʿbah from Abū Balj except through the narration of Muḥammad ibn Ḥumayd.
Abū Balj's name is Yaḥyā ibn Abī Sulaym.
The people of knowledge differed about this. Some of them said: The first to accept Islam was Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq.
And some of them said: The first to accept Islam was ʿAlī.

And some of the people of knowledge said: The first of the men to accept Islam was Abū Bakr, and ʿAlī accepted Islam when he was a boy of eight years, and the first of the women to accept Islam was Khadījah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The first to accept Islam was ʿAlī.
ʿAmr ibn Murrah said: I mentioned that to Ibrāhīm an-Nakhaʿī, and he rejected it and said: The first to accept Islam was Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent out an army, among whom was ʿAlī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was saying:
"Ṭalḥah and az-Zubayr are my two neighbors in Paradise."
He said: This ḥadīth is gharīb. We do not know it except through this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the morning of the Battle of the Camel, az-Zubayr gave his final instructions to his son ʿAbdullāh and said: There is no part of me that was not wounded in the company of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
even to the point that this reached his private part.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A group of people reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Ten are in Paradise: Abū Bakr is in Paradise, ʿUmar is in Paradise, and ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, az-Zubayr, Ṭalḥah, ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, Abū ʿUbaydah, and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ."

He said: He counted these nine and was silent about the tenth. The people said: We ask you by Allah, O Abū al-Aʿwar, who is the tenth? He said: You have asked me by Allah: Abū al-Aʿwar is in Paradise. Abū al-Aʿwar is Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl.
And I heard Muḥammad say: This is more authentic than the first ḥadīth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:
"Your affairs are among the things that concern me after I am gone, and none will be patient with you except the patient."
He said: Then ʿĀʾishah would say: May Allah give your father to drink from the Salsabīl of Paradise.
She meant ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who had given the wives of the Prophet ﷺ a property that was sold for forty thousand.
This ḥadīth is ḥasan gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf
bequeathed a garden to the Mothers of the Believers, which was sold for four hundred thousand.
This ḥadīth is ḥasan gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, answer Saʿd when he supplicates to You."
This ḥadīth has also been narrated from Ismāʿīl from Qays that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"O Allah, answer Saʿd when he supplicates to You." And this is more authentic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd approached, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"This is my maternal uncle. Let a man show me his maternal uncle."
This ḥadīth is ḥasan gharīb. We do not know it except through the narration of Mujālid.
Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ was from Banū Zuhrah, and the mother of the Prophet ﷺ was from Banū Zuhrah, which is why the Prophet ﷺ said: "This is my maternal uncle."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿUmar concerning al-ʿAbbās:
"A man's paternal uncle is the likeness of his father."
ʿUmar had spoken to him about his charity (ṣadaqah).
This ḥadīth is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Al-ʿAbbās is the paternal uncle of the Messenger of Allah, and a man's paternal uncle is the likeness of his father," or [he said], "of the likeness of his father."
This ḥadīth is ḥasan gharīb. We do not know it from the narration of Abū az-Zinād except through this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to al-ʿAbbās:
"When it is Monday morning, come to me, you and your sons, so that I may make a supplication for them by which Allah will benefit you and your sons."
So he went early, and we went early with him, and he covered us with a cloak. Then he said:

"O Allah, forgive al-ʿAbbās and his sons with a forgiveness, outward and inward, that leaves no sin behind. O Allah, protect him in his children." This ḥadīth is ḥasan gharīb. We do not know it except through this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Khālid al-Athbaj, the son of my brother
Ṣafwān ibn Muḥriz, narrated from Ṣafwān ibn Muḥriz,

that it was narrated to him that Jundab ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Bajalī sent for ʿAsʿas ibn Salāmah during the time of the turmoil of Ibn al-Zubayr and said: "Gather for me a group of your brothers so that I may narrate to them."
So he sent a messenger to them, and when they had gathered, Jundab came wearing a yellow hooded cloak and said: "Talk about what you were talking about."

The conversation continued until it came around to him. When it came to him, he drew the hood back from his head and said: "I have come to you only because I want to tell you something about your Prophet. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a detachment of Muslims against a people of the polytheists, and the two sides met. There was a man among the polytheists who, whenever he wished to go after a man among the Muslims, would aim for him and kill him. And a man among the Muslims aimed for his moment of heedlessness" — he said: "We used to say that it was Usāmah ibn Zayd — "and when he raised the sword over him, the man said: 'There is no god but Allah.'"

But he killed him. Then the bearer of good news came to the Prophet ﷺ, who asked him, and he informed him, even telling him how the man had acted. So he called him and asked him, and said: "Why did you kill him?"

He said: "O Messenger of Allah, he inflicted great harm on the Muslims and killed so-and-so and so-and-so" — and he named several men for him — "and I charged at him, but when he saw the sword, he said: 'There is no god but Allah.'"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Did you kill him?" He said: "Yes." He said:
"Then what will you do with 'There is no god but Allah' when it comes on the Day of Resurrection?"
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me." He said:
"And what will you do with 'There is no god but Allah' when it comes on the Day of Resurrection?"
He said: He did not add anything more than to keep saying:
"What will you do with 'There is no god but Allah' when it comes on the Day of Resurrection?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ. And Ḥajjāj ibn al-Shāʿir narrated it to me (a second chain),
ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us,
he said: My father narrated to me; Dāwūd narrated to us,
meaning Ibn Abī Hind; ʿĀṣim narrated to us,
from Ṣafwān ibn Muḥriz,
from Abū Mūsā,
from the Prophet ﷺ. And al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥulwānī narrated to me (a third chain),
ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us; Shuʿbah informed us,
from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr,
from Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh,
from Abū Mūsā,
from the Prophet ﷺ, with this hadith.
except that in the hadith of ʿIyāḍ al-Ashʿarī he said: "He is not one of us." And he did not say: "He is free of [us]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with Ḥudhayfah in the mosque when a man came and sat with us. Ḥudhayfah was told: "This man carries things to the ruler."
So Ḥudhayfah said — wanting him to hear — "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'The tale-bearer will not enter Paradise.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a man who used to carry reports to the governor. We were sitting in the mosque, and the people said: "This is one of those who carries reports to the governor."
He said: So he came and sat with us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There are three whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify — Abū Muʿāwiyah said: nor look at them — and for them is a painful punishment: an old man who commits adultery, a king who lies, and a poor man who is arrogant."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There are three whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor look at, nor purify, and for them is a painful punishment: a man who has surplus water in a desert and withholds it from the traveler; a man who sells goods to another after the ʿAṣr prayer and swears to him by Allah that he took it for such and such a price, and the buyer believes him, though it is not as he said; and a man who pledges allegiance to a ruler, doing so only for worldly gain: if the ruler gives him some of it, he is faithful, and if he does not give him any of it, he is not faithful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are three whom Allah will not speak to, nor look at, and for them is a painful punishment: a man who swore an oath after the ʿAṣr prayer concerning the property of a Muslim and thereby took it unlawfully."
And the rest of his hadith is like the hadith of al-Aʿmash.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man is not bound by a vow concerning what he does not own. Cursing a believer is like killing him. Whoever kills himself with something in this world will be punished with it on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever makes a false claim in order to increase his wealth, Allah will only decrease him. And whoever swears a binding oath falsely..."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The mother of Ḥārithah
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after Ḥārithah had been killed on the day of Badr, struck by a stray arrow.
She said, "O Messenger of Allah,
you know the place Ḥārithah held in my heart.
If he is in Paradise, I will not weep for him,
but if not, you will see what I will do." He said to her, "You have lost your senses!
Is it only one Paradise?
There are many gardens, and he is in the highest Firdaws."
(He said: "A morning or an evening spent in the cause of Allah is better than the world and everything in it.
And a space in Paradise the size of the bow of one of you, or the place of a foot, is better than the world and everything in it.
If a woman from the women of the people of Paradise were to look down upon the earth,
she would light up everything between them,
and fill everything between them with fragrance,
and her head covering" meaning the veil "is better than the world and everything in it.")
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with Jarīr ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Bajalī on a journey, and he used to serve me. I said to him, "Do not do that."
He said, "I saw the Anṣār doing something for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I swore that I would never accompany any of them without serving him."
Ibn al-Muthannā and Ibn Bashshār added in their narration: Jarīr was older than Anas.
And Ibn Bashshār said: he was of greater age than Anas.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a group of the Aslam tribe who were competing in archery,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Shoot, O sons of Ismāʿīl,
for your father was an archer,
and I am with the sons of so-and-so."
He said: One of the two groups held back their hands,
so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What is the matter with you that you are not shooting?"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah,
how can we shoot when you are with them?" He said:
"Shoot, and I am with all of you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a man of the people of Madinah, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse:

"And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be like you." They said, "Who is it that will replace us?" So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck Salmān's shoulder and then said:
"This man and his people; this man and his people."
He said: This hadith is gharīb, and there is some criticism concerning its chain of narration.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar also narrated this hadith from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "O Messenger of Allah, who are these people whom Allah mentioned, that if we turn away they will replace us, and then they will not be like us?" He said: Salmān was beside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck Salmān's thigh and said:
"This man and his companions. By the One in whose hand is my soul, if faith were hanging at the Pleiades, men from Persia would reach it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, who said: There was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ,
"That Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what is to follow," on his return from al-Ḥudaybiyah. The Prophet ﷺ said:

"A verse has been revealed to me that is more beloved to me than everything on earth." Then the Prophet ﷺ recited it to them, and they said, "Congratulations, may it be pleasant for you, O Prophet of Allah! Allah has made clear what He will do with you, so what will He do with us?" Then there was revealed to him:
"That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow," until he reached:
"a great success." He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ, and there is a report on this topic from Mujammiʿ ibn Jāriyah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ,
regarding the verse: "And He bound them to the word of piety," he said: "[It is] there is no god but Allah."

He said: This hadith is gharīb; we do not know it as a raised report except from the hadith of al-Ḥasan ibn Qazaʿah. He said: I asked Abū Zurʿah about this hadith, and he did not know it as a raised report except through this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding His words:

"Indeed, those who call you from behind the chambers, most of them do not use reason," he said: A man stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, indeed my praise brings honor and my criticism brings disgrace." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"That is Allah, the Exalted."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī recited:
"And know that among you

is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty." He said: This is your Prophet ﷺ, to whom revelation comes, and the best of your leaders; if he were to obey them in much of the matter, they would be in difficulty. So how would it be with you today? Abū ʿĪsā said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb.
ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: I asked Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān about al-Mustamirr ibn al-Rayyān, and he said, "He is trustworthy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed the people on the day of the conquest of Makkah and said:

"O people, Allah has removed from you the arrogance of the Days of Ignorance and its boasting about forefathers. People are of two kinds: a righteous, God-fearing man who is honored by Allah, and a wicked, wretched man who is insignificant to Allah. And people are the children of Adam, and Allah created Adam from dust." Allah said:

"O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Aware."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Rabīʿah, who said: I came to Madinah and went in to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the delegate of ʿĀd was mentioned in his presence. I said, "I seek refuge in Allah from being like the delegate of ʿĀd."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"And what was the delegate of ʿĀd?"

He said: I said, "You have fallen upon one who knows. When ʿĀd suffered drought, they sent Qayl, who stayed with Bakr ibn Muʿāwiyah. He gave him wine to drink, and the two singing girls called al-Jarādatān sang for him. Then he set out, heading for the mountains of Mahrah, and said: O Allah, I have not come to You for a sick person to heal him, nor for a captive to ransom him, so give Your servant water as You would give water to him, and give Bakr ibn Muʿāwiyah water with him,

in thanks for the wine he had given him to drink." Then clouds were raised for him, and it was said to him, "Choose one of them." He chose the black one among them, and it was said to him, "Take it as scattered ashes; it will leave none of ʿĀd." He mentioned that only as much wind was sent upon them as this ring, meaning the ring of a signet ring. Then he recited:
"When We sent upon them the barren wind. It left nothing of what it came upon except that it made it like decayed bones," the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I was praying
with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man among the people sneezed, so I said, "May Allah have mercy on you."
The people shot me looks with their eyes, so I said, "Woe to my mother's loss of me! What is the matter with you that you stare at me?"

They began striking their thighs with their hands. When I saw them trying to silence me, I fell silent. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished the prayer—may my father and mother be ransomed for him, I never saw a teacher before him or after him who taught better than he did; by Allah, he neither scolded me, nor struck me, nor insulted me—he said,
"Indeed, in this prayer nothing of the speech of people is suitable. It is only glorification, magnification, and recitation of the Qur'an."

Or as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am newly out of the Days of Ignorance, and Allah has brought Islam. Among us are men who go to soothsayers." He said, "Do not go to them."
He said, "And among us are men who take omens from birds." He said,
"That is something they find in their hearts, so let it not turn them back."
Ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ said: "so let it not turn you back."
I said, "And among us are men who draw lines [in the sand]." He said,
"A prophet among the prophets used to draw lines; whoever's lines match his, then that is fine."

He said: I had a slave girl who used to graze sheep of mine near Uhud and al-Jawāniyyah. One day I looked and found that a wolf had taken a sheep from her flock. I am a man from the children of Adam; I get angry as they get angry, but I slapped her with a slap. Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it weighed heavily on me. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, should I not free her?" He said, "Bring her to me."
So I brought her to him, and he said to her, "Where is Allah?"
She said, "In the heaven." He said, "Who am I?"
She said, "You are the Messenger of Allah." He said,
"Free her, for she is a believer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever hears a man announcing a lost item in the mosque, let him say: 'May Allah not return it to you,' for mosques were not built for this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the ʿAṣr prayer and concluded with the salām after two rakʿahs. Dhū al-Yadayn stood up and said, "Has the prayer been shortened, O Messenger of Allah, or have you forgotten?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"None of that has happened."
He said, "Some of that has happened, O Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to the people and said,
"Is Dhū al-Yadayn right?"
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ completed what remained of the prayer, then performed two prostrations while sitting, after the salām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Muslim ibn Abī Maryam,
from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muʿāwī,
that he said: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar saw me playing with pebbles during prayer. When he finished, he forbade me and said, "Do as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do."

I said, "And how did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do it?" He said, "When he sat in prayer, he would place his right palm on his right thigh, close all his fingers, and point with the finger next to the thumb, and he would place his left palm on his left thigh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn al-Zubayr used to say at the end of every prayer, when he gave the salām,

"There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. There is no might and no power except with Allah. There is no god but Allah, and we worship none but Him. His is the favor, and His is the grace, and His is the beautiful praise. There is no god but Allah, [we are] sincere to Him in religion, even if the disbelievers dislike it."
And he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite these words of tahlīl at the end of every prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the prayer while out of breath, and said, "Allah is the Greatest. Praise be to Allah, abundant, good, and blessed praise." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer, he said,
"Which of you spoke these words? He said nothing wrong."
The man said, "I did, O Messenger of Allah. I came out of breath and said them." He said,
"I saw twelve angels racing to it, each wanting to be the one to raise it."
And Ḥumayd added to it:
"When one of you comes [to prayer], let him walk as he normally walks, and let him pray what he catches and make up what he missed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were praying with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man among the people said: "Allahu akbar kabīran, walḥamdu lillāhi kathīran, wa subḥānallāhi bukratan wa aṣīlā" (Allah is greatest of all; much praise be to Allah; and glory be to Allah morning and evening).
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Who was the one who said such and such words?"
A man from among the people said, "I was, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "I was amazed at them."
And he mentioned words to the effect that
"the gates of heaven were opened for them."
Ibn ʿUmar said: I have not abandoned them since I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The muʾadhdhin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would wait and not give the iqāmah until he saw that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had come out; when he saw him, he would give the iqāmah for the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the times of the prayers, and he said:

"The time of the Fajr prayer lasts as long as the first edge of the sun has not risen. The time of the Ẓuhr prayer is when the sun has passed the middle of the sky, as long as the time of ʿAṣr has not arrived. The time of the ʿAṣr prayer lasts as long as the sun has not turned yellow and its first edge has not set. The time of the Maghrib prayer is when the sun has set, as long as the twilight has not disappeared. And the time of the ʿIshāʾ prayer lasts until the middle of the night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray the midday prayer, which you call Ẓuhr, when the sun had passed its zenith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One night we stayed waiting for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the last ʿIshāʾ prayer. He came out to us when a third of the night had passed or later, and we did not know whether something had kept him busy with his family or something else. When he came out, he said:
"You are waiting for a prayer that no followers of any other religion besides you are waiting for. Had it not been that it would burden my Ummah, I would have prayed it with them at this hour."
Then he ordered the muʾadhdhin, who gave the iqāmah for the prayer, and he prayed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led a woman from his family and me in prayer,
and he made me stand on his right, and the woman prayed behind us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Jābir ibn Samurah, "Did you sit with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "Yes, often. He would not get up from the place of prayer where he had prayed the Ṣubḥ or Ghadāh prayer until the sun rose. When the sun had risen, he would get up. They used to talk and bring up matters from the Jāhiliyyah and laugh, while he would smile."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from the campaign of Khaybar, he travelled during the night until, when drowsiness overcame him, he halted to rest, and he said to Bilāl:
"Keep watch over the night for us."

So Bilāl prayed as much as was decreed for him, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions slept. When dawn drew near, Bilāl leaned against his mount, facing the dawn, but his eyes overcame him while he was leaning against his mount. Neither the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor Bilāl, nor any of his Companions woke until the sun struck them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the first of them to wake, and he was alarmed and said, "O Bilāl!"
Bilāl said, "The very thing that seized your soul, may my father and mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of Allah, seized mine." He said, "Lead on your mounts."

So they led their mounts on a little way. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution and ordered Bilāl, who gave the iqāmah for the prayer, and he led them in the Ṣubḥ prayer. When he had finished the prayer, he said:
"Whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray it when he remembers it, for Allah says: {Establish prayer for My remembrance.}"
Yūnus said: Ibn Shihāb used to recite it as "lildhikrā" (for the remembrance).
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed two rakʿahs with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Minā, when the people were at their safest and most numerous.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey and it rained on us, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let whoever of you wishes pray in his lodging."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Abū az-Zubayr,
from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr together, and Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ together, without fear or travel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a man who was praying after the iqāmah for the Ṣubḥ prayer had been given, and he said something to him that we did not know. When we finished, we gathered around him, saying, "What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say to you?" He said, he said to me:
"It is almost the case that one of you would pray Ṣubḥ as four [rakʿahs]."
Al-Qaʿnabī said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Mālik ibn Buḥaynah, from his father.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ swore an oath to keep away from his wives only because Zaynab had returned his gift to him.
Then ʿĀʾishah said, "She has truly shamed you."
So he ﷺ became angry and swore to keep away from them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said, "Blessed is He whose hearing encompasses everything.

I could hear the words of Khawlah bint Thaʿlabah, while some of them were hidden from me, as she complained about her husband to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She was saying, 'O Messenger of Allah, he consumed my youth and I bore him many children, until when I grew old and could no longer bear children, he declared ẓihār against me. O Allah, I complain to You.'
She had not left her place when Jibrīl came down with these verses: {Allah has certainly heard the speech of the one who disputes with you concerning her husband and directs her complaint to Allah}."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṭalḥah ibn Nāfiʿ mentioned, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,

who said: A man from the Anṣār married a woman from Banū ʿAjlān and consummated the marriage with her and spent the night with her. When morning came he said, "I did not find her a virgin." Her case was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, so he called the girl and asked her, and she said, "Yes, I was a virgin."
So he ordered the two of them, and they performed the mutual invocation of curses (liʿān), and he gave her the dowry.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"There are four categories of women between whom and their husbands there is no liʿān: a Christian woman married to a Muslim, a Jewish woman married to a Muslim, a free woman married to a slave, and a slave woman married to a free man."
label: machine translation

He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went up on the pulpit and said:
"O people, what is the matter with one of you who marries his slave to his slave woman and then wants to separate them? Divorce belongs only to the one who holds the leg."
label: machine translation

was ordered by his father or his mother (Shuʿbah was unsure) to divorce
his wife, so he made himself liable to free a hundred slaves.

He came to Abū ad-Dardāʾ and found him praying the forenoon prayer, lengthening it, and he also prayed between Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr. He asked him, and Abū ad-Dardāʾ said, "Fulfil your vow and be dutiful to your parents."

and by the One in whose hand is my soul."

"Do not swear by your fathers. Whoever swears by Allah, let him be truthful; whoever is sworn to by Allah, let him be satisfied; and whoever is not satisfied with Allah has nothing to do with Allah."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"An oath ends either in breaking it or in regret."

"Whoever swears an oath to cut off family ties, or to do something improper, his way of fulfilling it is not to carry it through."

segments_en: On the day of the conquest of Makkah, he came with his father and said, "O Messenger of Allah, give my father a share in the Hijrah." He said:
"There is no Hijrah anymore."
So he went off and came to al-ʿAbbās and said, "You know me." He said, "Yes."

So al-ʿAbbās came out in a shirt without a cloak and said, "O Messenger of Allah, you know so-and-so and the relationship between us and him. He has come with his father to pledge allegiance to you for Hijrah." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"There is no Hijrah anymore."
Then al-ʿAbbās said, "I adjure you by oath."
So the Prophet ﷺ stretched out his hand and touched his hand and said:
"I have fulfilled the oath for my uncle, but there is no Hijrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you swears an oath, let him not say, 'What Allah wills and you will.'
Rather let him say, 'What Allah wills, and then what you will.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eight rakʿahs together and seven together.
I said, "O Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ, I think he delayed the Ẓuhr and brought forward the ʿAṣr, and brought forward the ʿIshāʾ and delayed the Maghrib."
He said, "I think so too."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to come to the mosque of Qubā' riding and walking, and he would pray two rakʿahs in it.
Abū Bakr said in his narration: Ibn Numayr said, "and he would pray two rakʿahs in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"One came to me from my Lord and informed me," or he said, "gave me glad tidings, that whoever of my nation dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise."
I said, "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said:
"Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to do seven things and forbade us from seven. He commanded us to follow funeral processions, visit the sick, say "Yarḥamukallāh" to one who sneezes, answer the one who invites, help the oppressed, fulfil oaths, and return the greeting of peace. And he forbade us from seven: gold rings, or a gold ring, silver vessels, wearing silk, brocade, heavy silk, and qasiyy garments.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
both from Sufyān.
ʿUbaydullāh said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us,
he said: I heard Ibn al-Munkadir
say: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh

say: On the day of Uḥud my father was brought, covered, and he had been mutilated. He said: I wanted to lift the cloth, but my people forbade me; then I wanted to lift the cloth again, but my people forbade me. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lifted it, or ordered it to be lifted, and it was lifted. Then the voice of a weeping or wailing woman was heard, and he said, "Who is this?"
They said, "The daughter of ʿAmr," or "the sister of ʿAmr." He said:
"Why does she weep? The angels continued to shade him with their wings until he was lifted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are no two Muslims who lose three children who had not reached puberty, except that Allah will admit them to Paradise by the grace of His mercy toward the children." He said:
"It will be said to them, 'Enter Paradise.' They will say, 'Not until our parents enter.' Then it will be said, 'Enter Paradise, you and your parents.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: They made the hair of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into three braids: they undid it, then washed it, then made it into three braids.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While a man was standing with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at ʿArafah, he fell from his mount. Ayyūb said: and it broke his neck, or he said: and it killed him instantly. ʿAmr said: and it broke his neck. This was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:

"Wash him with water and lote-tree leaves, shroud him in two garments, do not apply perfume to him, and do not cover his head." Ayyūb said: "For Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection saying the talbiyah." And ʿAmr said: "For Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection reciting the talbiyah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr,
from Ḥumayd ibn Nāfiʿ,
from Zaynab bint Abī Salamah,
that she informed him of these three hadith.

Zaynab said: I entered upon Umm Ḥabībah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, when her father Abū Sufyān died. Umm Ḥabībah called for perfume containing yellow dye, khalūq or other, and she applied some to a girl, then touched her own cheeks with it. Then she said, "By Allah, I have no need of perfume, except that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say on the pulpit:
'It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband: four months and ten days.'"

Zaynab said: Then I entered upon Zaynab bint Jaḥsh when her brother died. She called for perfume and applied some, then said, "By Allah, I have no need of perfume, except that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say on the pulpit:
'It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband: four months and ten days.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: to a woman of his household, "Do you know so-and-so?" She said, "Yes."
He said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by her while she was weeping at a grave, and he said:
"Fear Allah and be patient."
She said, "Go away from me,
for you have not been afflicted with my calamity."
He said: He went past her and continued on. Then a man passed by her and said, "What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say to you?"

She said, "I did not recognize him." He said, "It was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: She came to his door and found no doorkeeper there, and said, "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I did not recognize you." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Patience is at the first strike of calamity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he used to sleep in the mosque of the Prophet ﷺ during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was a young, unmarried man with no family.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the mosque was built of mud bricks and palm branches—Mujāhid said: and its pillars were of palm trunks. Abū Bakr added nothing to it. ʿUmar added to it and rebuilt it on its original structure from the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with mud bricks and palm branches, and he replaced its pillars—Mujāhid said: its pillars with wood. Then ʿUthmān changed it: he enlarged it considerably, built its walls of dressed stones and plaster, made its pillars of dressed stone, and roofed it with teak.
Mujāhid said: and its roof was of teak.
label: machine translation

segments_en: At the time when people were speaking about him as the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was being built.
"You have said too much. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, the Exalted—Bukayr said: I think he said—seeking thereby the face of Allah, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise.'"
And Ibn ʿĪsā said in his narration:
"the like of it in Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He called Abū Hurayrah to witness and said: "O Abū Hurayrah, I ask you by Allah, did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'O Ḥassān, respond on behalf of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
O Allah, support him with the Holy Spirit'?"
Abū Hurayrah said: "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon one day and said:
"A man was given a choice by his Lord between living in this world as long as he wished and eating in this world as much as he wished, and meeting his Lord; and he chose to meet his Lord."

He said: Abū Bakr wept. The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said: "Do you not marvel at this old man? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned a righteous man whose Lord gave him a choice between this world and meeting his Lord, and he chose to meet his Lord."
He said: Abū Bakr was the most knowledgeable of them about what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said. Abū Bakr said: "Rather, we would ransom you with our fathers and our wealth."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no one among the people who has been more generous to us in his companionship and his property than Ibn Abī Quḥāfah. Had I been taking a close friend, I would have taken Ibn Abī Quḥāfah as a close friend. But there is affection and brotherhood of faith—affection and brotherhood of faith," two or three times, "and your companion is the close friend of Allah."
This hadith has also been narrated from Abū ʿAwānah, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, with a different chain than this.
The meaning of his saying "amanna ilaynā" is "amanna ʿalaynā" (the most generous to us).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent cavalry toward Najd,
and they brought a man from Banū Ḥanīfah called Thumāmah ibn Uthāl, the chief of the people of al-Yamāmah,
and they tied him to one of the pillars of the mosque.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to him and said:
"What do you have, O Thumāmah?"
He said: "I have good, O Muḥammad."
Then he mentioned the hadith, saying: "Release Thumāmah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ faced the two gaps of the mountain between him and the long mountain, in the direction of the Kaʿbah, placing the mosque that was built there to the left of the mosque at the edge of the hillock. The place where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed was below it, on the black hillock, leaving ten cubits or so from the hillock. Then he would pray facing the two gaps of the long mountain that is between you and the Kaʿbah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the muezzin gave the call to prayer, some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ would hurry to the pillars until the Prophet ﷺ came out, and they were still like that, praying the two rakʿahs before the Maghrib prayer,
and there was nothing between the call to prayer and the iqāmah.
ʿUthmān ibn Jabalah and Abū Dāwūd said, from Shuʿbah: There was only a short time between them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was mentioned in her presence what interrupts prayer, and they said: "The dog, the donkey, and the woman interrupt it."
She said: "You have made us into dogs!
I saw the Prophet ﷺ praying,
while I was between him and the qiblah,
lying on the bed.
I would have a need,
and I disliked to face him, so I would slip away gently."
And from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾishah, something similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Zayd ibn Ḥārithah as commander in the expedition of Mu'tah,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If Zayd is killed, then Jaʿfar [is the commander];
and if Jaʿfar is killed, then ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah."
ʿAbdullāh said: I was among them in that expedition, and we searched for Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib,
and we found him among the slain,
and we found in his body more than ninety stab and arrow wounds.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Mu'tah, nine swords broke in my hand,
and nothing remained in my hand except a Yemeni broad blade.
label: machine translation

and his sister ʿAmrah began to weep, saying: "O my mountain! O such-and-such! O such-and-such!"
She was enumerating his virtues. When he regained consciousness, he said: Nothing that you said was uttered except that I was asked, "Are you truly like that?"
label: machine translation

and when he died, she did not weep for him.

and I fought alongside Ibn Ḥārithah, whom he appointed over us.

segments_en: I fought seven battles alongside the Prophet ﷺ.
He mentioned Khaybar, al-Ḥudaybiyah, the day of Ḥunayn, and the day of al-Qarad.
Yazīd said: I have forgotten the rest of them.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ set out in Ramadan for Ḥunayn,
and the people differed, some fasting and some not fasting.
When he had settled on his mount, he asked for a vessel of milk or water,
and he placed it on his palm or on his mount,
then he looked at the people, and those who were not fasting said to those who were fasting: Break your fast.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marched in the year of the Conquest and that reached Quraysh,
Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb, Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām, and Budayl ibn Warqāʾ went out seeking news about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They kept travelling until they reached Marr al-Ẓahrān,
and there they saw fires, as though they were the fires of ʿArafah.
Abū Sufyān said: What are these? They seem like the fires of ʿArafah.
Budayl ibn Warqāʾ said: They are the fires of Banū ʿAmr.
Abū Sufyān said: ʿAmr are fewer than that.
Some of the guards of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw them, caught up with them, and seized them,
and brought them to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Abū Sufyān accepted Islam.
When [the Prophet ﷺ] set out, he said to al-ʿAbbās:
"Detain Abū Sufyān at the narrowing of the valley, where the cavalry crowd, so that he may see the Muslims." So al-ʿAbbās detained him,
and the tribes began to pass by with the Prophet ﷺ, battalion by battalion, before Abū Sufyān.
One battalion passed and he said: O ʿAbbās, who are these? He said: These are Ghifār.
He said: What have I to do with Ghifār? Then Juhaynah passed,
and he said the same.
Then Saʿd ibn Hudhaym passed,
and he said the same; and Sulaym passed,
and he said the same,
until a battalion came the like of which he had not seen.
He said: Who are these? He said: These are the Anṣār, led by Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah, who carries the banner.
Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah said: O Abū Sufyān, today is the day of great battle;
today the Kaʿbah will be made lawful.
Abū Sufyān said: O ʿAbbās, how excellent is the day of vengeance!
Then another battalion came,
and it was the smallest of the battalions,
and in it were the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions,
and the banner of the Prophet ﷺ was with az-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by Abū Sufyān, he said: Do you not know what Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah said? He said: "What did he say?"
He said: Such and such. He said: "Saʿd was mistaken,
rather, this is a day on which Allah will exalt the Kaʿbah,
and a day on which the Kaʿbah will be covered."
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that his banner be planted at al-Ḥajūn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man,
in the state of iḥrām, was thrown from his camel,
and his neck was broken. It was reported that he had died, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Wash him with water and lote-tree leaves, and shroud him in two garments."
Then he said after that, "With his head uncovered." He said:
"And do not touch him with perfume, for he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection reciting the talbiyah."
Shuʿbah said: I asked him ten years later, and he narrated the hadith just as he used to narrate it, except that he said:

segments_en: A man from the Anṣār called Qaraẓah ibn Kaʿb died, and he was wailed over. Then al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah came and ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said, "What is this wailing in Islam? Indeed, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever is wailed over will be punished for that which he is wailed over.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed, an-Najāshī has died."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions went out to al-Baqīʿ.
We lined up behind him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went forward and said the takbīr four times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us that zakāh al-fiṭr be paid before the people go out to the prayer.
He said: Ibn ʿUmar used to pay it one or two days before that.

from Ibn Wahb,
who said: Yūnus informed me,
from Ibn Shihāb, from Sālim, from his father,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would touch only the Black Corner of the House, and the one next to it on the side of the houses of the Banū Jumaḥ.

segments_en: I gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ water from Zamzam to drink, and he drank while standing.
ʿĀṣim said: ʿIkrimah swore that he was on nothing but a camel that day.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed four ʿUmrahs, all of them in Dhū al-Qaʿdah except the one with his Hajj. Abū Dāwūd said: I have preserved it precisely from this point from Hudbah, and I heard it from Abū al-Walīd but did not retain it precisely. The ʿUmrah at the time of al-Ḥudaybiyah, or from al-Ḥudaybiyah; the ʿUmrah of al-Qaḍāʾ in Dhū al-Qaʿdah; the ʿUmrah from al-Jiʿrānah, when he distributed the spoils of Ḥunayn, in Dhū al-Qaʿdah; and the ʿUmrah with his Hajj.
