segments_en: And Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr. Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said "He informed us," and the others said,
"Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Dīnār,
that he heard ʿAbd
Allāh ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There are five [creatures] that there is no sin on one who kills them while in the state of iḥrām: the scorpion, the mouse, the biting dog, the crow, and the kite."
The wording is that of Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ giving a sermon, Hishām said: on the pulpit, and he said:
"Whoever does not find a waist-wrapper, let him wear trousers, and whoever does not find sandals, let him wear leather socks."
And Hishām said in his narration:
"Let him wear trousers, unless he cannot find [a waist-wrapper]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this verse was revealed: {until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread},
he said: I took a white cord and a black cord and put them under my pillow, and I looked but could not distinguish [them]. I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he laughed and said:
"Your pillow is indeed broad and long. It is only the night and the day." ʿUthmān said:
"It is only the blackness of the night and the whiteness of the day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Shuʿbah, from al-Ḥakam, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad,
from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet ﷺ would kiss and have physical contact [with his wives] while fasting,
and he was the one among you who had the most control over his desire.
And he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said, {mārib} means need.
Ṭāwūs said, {those without desire}: the foolish one who has no need of women.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out and fasted, and they said to me, "Repeat it."

He said: I said, "Anas informed me that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to travel, and the one fasting would not find fault with the one not fasting, nor the one not fasting with the one fasting."
Then I met Ibn Abī Mulaykah, and he informed me from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, something similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: {Whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed—those are the disbelievers} up to His saying {the defiantly disobedient}: these three verses were revealed specifically concerning the Jews, namely Qurayzah and al-Naḍīr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men entered through the gates of Kindah while Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī was sitting in a circle. They said, "Is there no man who will settle [a matter] between us?" A man from the circle said, "I will."
So Abū Masʿūd took a handful of pebbles and threw them at him, and said, "Stop! He used to dislike haste in judgment."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever seeks the position of judge and seeks help to obtain it will be left to himself; and whoever does not seek it and does not seek help to obtain it, Allah will send down an angel to guide him aright."
Wakīʿ said, from Isrāʾīl, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Bilāl ibn Abī Mūsā, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ.
And Abū ʿAwānah said, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Bilāl ibn Mirdās al-Fazārī, from Khaythamah al-Baṣrī, from Anas.
label: machine translation

segments_en: (ʿAlī), peace be upon him, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Yemen as a judge. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, you are sending me while I am young and have no knowledge of judging?" He said,

"Allah will guide your heart and make your tongue firm. When two litigants sit before you, do not give judgment until you hear from the other as you heard from the first, for that is more likely to make the judgment clear to you."
He said: I have continued to be a judge ever since, or: I have never doubted a judgment since.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disputing over inheritances of theirs for which they had no proof except their claims. The Prophet ﷺ said the like of it, and the two men wept, and each of them said, "My right is yours."
The Prophet ﷺ said to them,
"Since you have done what you have done, divide it between you, aiming at the truth,
then draw lots, and then each release the other from any claim."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While he was on the pulpit, [he said], "O people, opinion was correct only from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, because Allah used to show him [the right course]; as for us, it is only conjecture and presumption."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I do not think I have seen a Syrian better than him, meaning Ḥarīz ibn ʿUthmān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the two litigants sit in front of the judge.
label: machine translation

segments_en: {If they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them}; this was abrogated. He said: {So judge between them by what Allah has revealed}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From some of the companions of Muʿādh, from Muʿādh ibn Jabal,
that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to Yemen... and he mentioned its meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We sat waiting for ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, and he came out to us and sat down. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say,

"Whoever's intercession stands in the way of one of the prescribed punishments of Allah has opposed Allah. Whoever disputes in falsehood while knowing it remains in Allah's displeasure until he desists. And whoever says about a believer what is not in him, Allah will make him dwell in the mire of khabāl until he retracts what he said."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rejected the testimony of the dishonest man and the dishonest woman, and of one who harbors enmity against his brother, and rejected the testimony of one who is dependent on a household [when testifying] for its members, but allowed it for others.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Then he mentioned its meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a man

from among the Muslims was approaching death at this Daqūqāʾ and could not find any Muslim to witness his will, so he made two men of the People of the Book witness it. They came to Kufa and went to Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, informed him, and brought his estate and his will.
Al-Ashʿarī said, "This is a matter that has not occurred since the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

So he made them swear after the afternoon prayer by Allah that they had not betrayed, lied, altered, concealed, or changed anything, and that it was truly the man's will and estate, and he upheld their testimony.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled on the basis of an oath and one witness.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of Abū Muṣʿab and its meaning.
Sulaymān said: I met Suhayl and asked him about this hadith, and he said, "I do not know it."
I said to him, "Rabīʿah informed me of it from you."
He said, "If Rabīʿah informed you from me, then narrate it from Rabīʿah, from me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were in the mosque on a Friday night when a man of the Anṣār entered the mosque and said: "If a man finds another man with his wife and speaks about it, you lash him; or if he kills him, you kill him; and if he stays silent, he stays silent in rage. By Allah, I will surely ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it."

The next day he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him. He said: "If a man finds another man with his wife and speaks about it, you lash him; or if he kills him, you kill him; or if he stays silent, he stays silent in rage." So he ﷺ said: "O Allah, grant a decision."

And he began to supplicate, and the verse of invoking curses (liʿān) was revealed: {And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves} — this verse. That man was tested by it from among all the people. So he and his wife came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and they invoked curses on one another. The man testified four times by Allah that he was among the truthful, then the fifth time [invoked] the curse upon himself if he was among the liars. He said: Then she went to invoke the curse, and the Prophet ﷺ said to her: "Stop!"
But she refused, and went ahead with it. When the two had turned away, he said:
"Perhaps she will bring forth a child
dark and curly-haired." And she gave birth to a dark, curly-haired child.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, if a man finds another man with his wife, may he kill him?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No."
Saʿd said: "Yes, by the One who honored you with the truth!" The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Listen to what your chief says."
ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said:
"to what Saʿd says."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not go out to meet the imported goods [on the way].
Whoever meets them and buys from them, then when the owner comes to the market, he has the option [to cancel]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were forbidden that a town-dweller sell for a desert-dweller,
even if he is his brother or his father.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I was listening,
— and the wording is his — from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me, from Nāfiʿ,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,

who said: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ we used to buy foodstuffs, and he would send someone to us who ordered us to move it from the place where we had bought it to another place before we sold it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of date palms [fruit] until it ripens, and of grain ears until they whiten and are safe from blight; he forbade both the seller and the buyer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Khaybar I bought a necklace for twelve dinars; it had gold and beads in it. I separated them and found in it more than twelve dinars [worth of gold]. I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"It is not to be sold until it is separated."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled for pre-emption (shufʿah) in every joint property that has not been divided, whether a dwelling or an orchard.

It is not permissible for him to sell until he notifies his partner; then if he wishes he may take it, and if he wishes he may leave it. If he sells without notifying him, [the partner] has more right to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "My father died and left wealth and made no bequest. Will it expiate for him if I give charity on his behalf?" He said: "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not make vows, for a vow does not avert anything of what is decreed; rather, it is only a means of extracting [wealth] from the miser."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not swear by the false idols, nor by your fathers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I slapped a freed slave of ours and ran away. Then I came shortly before noon and prayed behind my father. He called him and called me, then said: "Retaliate against him."

So he forgave. Then [my father] said: "We, the sons of Muqarrin, in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had only one servant, and one of us slapped her. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: 'Free her.'
They said: 'They have no servant other than her.' He said:
'Then let them make use of her, and when they no longer need her, let them let her go free.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ only gouged out the eyes of those men because they had gouged out the eyes of the shepherds.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

of the Jews killed a girl of the Anṣār for her jewelry, then threw her into a well and crushed her head with stones. He was seized and brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who ordered that he be stoned until he died, so he was stoned until he died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Whoever swears an oath
by which he takes [another's] property unjustly, while lying in it,
will meet Allah while He is angry with him.

Then Allah revealed the confirmation of that: {Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price} and he recited up to {a painful punishment}. Then al-Ashʿath ibn Qays came out to us and said: What is Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān telling you? We told him. He said: He spoke the truth; by Allah, it was revealed about me.
There was a dispute between me and another man over a well, so we took our dispute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Your witness, or his oath."
I said: Then he will swear without caring.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever swears an oath by which he takes property unjustly, while lying in it,
will meet Allah while He is angry with him."
Then Allah revealed the confirmation of that,
and then he recited this verse: {Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price} up to {and for them is a painful punishment}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two brothers of Banū al-Mughīrah, one of whom had vowed never to let a beam be fixed in his wall, [were in a dispute]. Then Mujammiʿ ibn Yazīd and many men of the Anṣār came and said: We testify that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should prevent his neighbor from fixing a beam in his wall."
So he said: My brother, the ruling is in your favor against me, and I have sworn; so set up a pillar apart from my wall, or my wall, and place your beam on it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ ruled that when people dispute over a road, it is to be seven cubits [wide].
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to give a ruling regarding a male or female slave owned jointly by partners,
when one of them frees his share of him.
He would say: The freeing of the whole slave becomes obligatory upon him,
if the one who freed his share has enough wealth to cover it.
The slave is valued from his wealth at a fair value,
and the partners are given their shares,
and the freed slave is set free.
Ibn ʿUmar reported that from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever frees his share in a slave, his release [of the whole] is to be borne by his own wealth if he has wealth. If he has no wealth, the slave is valued at a fair value, then made to work to earn [the rest of] his value for his [other] owner, without being burdened."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When one of you has his servant prepare his food, then [the servant] brings it to him after having borne its heat and smoke, he should seat him with him and let him eat. And if the food is scarce and little, he should put a bite or two in his hand from it."
Dāwūd said: That is, a morsel or two.
label: machine translation

segments_en: His father,
Makhramah, said to him: My son, it has reached me that some cloaks have come to the Prophet ﷺ and he is distributing them,
so go with us to him.
So we went and found the Prophet ﷺ in his house.
He said to me: My son, call the Prophet ﷺ for me. I found that a grave matter.
So I said: Shall I call the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for you? He said: My son, he is not a tyrant.
So I called him, and he came out wearing a brocade cloak fastened with gold buttons, and he said:
"O Makhramah, I kept this aside for you." And he gave it to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn, [descendant of] Fāṭimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah
ﷺ, narrated from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"The example of one who gives charity and then takes it back is like a dog that vomits and then returns to its vomit and eats it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me while a man was sitting with me. That was hard on him, and I saw anger on his face. I said: O Messenger of Allah, he is my brother by nursing. He said:
"Look carefully at who your brothers are"—and another time—"Look carefully at who your brothers by nursing are, for nursing [counts] only when it is from hunger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas ibn Mālik mentioned to us, from Abū Ṭalḥah,
that on the day of Badr the Prophet of Allah ﷺ gave orders concerning twenty-four men from the leaders of Quraysh, and they were thrown into one of the wells of Badr, a foul and filthy pit.
Whenever he gained victory over a people, he would stay at the battlefield for three nights.
When he was at Badr on the third day,
he ordered that his mount be saddled with its riding gear,
then he set out walking, and his Companions followed him, saying, "We think he is going only for some need of his,"
until he stood at the edge of the well.
He began calling them by their names and the names of their fathers:
"O so-and-so, son of so-and-so,
and O so-and-so, son of so-and-so,
would it please you that you had obeyed Allah and His Messenger? For we have found what our Lord promised us to be true,
so have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?"
He said: ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah,
how can you speak to bodies that have no souls?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad,
you do not hear what I am saying any better than they do."
Qatādah said: Allah brought them back to life so that they would hear his words, as a rebuke, a humiliation, a retribution, and as regret and remorse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever Allah wants good for, He gives him understanding of the religion.
Allah is the Giver, and I am only the distributor.
This community will continue to prevail over those who oppose them until the command of Allah comes while they are still prevailing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came, together with ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, to speak to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about what he had distributed of the fifth among Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have given a share to our brothers Banū al-Muṭṭalib and given us nothing, though our kinship to you and theirs is the same." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib are only one thing."
Jubayr said: He did not give a share of that fifth to Banū ʿAbd Shams or to Banū Nawfal, as he gave to Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib.

He said: Abū Bakr used to distribute the fifth in the same manner as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ distributed it, except that he did not give the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what the Prophet ﷺ used to give them.
He said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb used to give them from it, and ʿUthmān after him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of al-Aḥzāb, ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah and I were placed among the women.
I looked, and there was al-Zubayr on his horse,
going to Banū Qurayẓah and coming back two or three times.
When I returned, I said, "Father, I saw you going back and forth."
He said, "Did you really see me, my son?" I said, "Yes."
He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said:
'Who will go to Banū Qurayẓah and bring me news of them?' So I went.
When I returned, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined his parents for me, saying:
'May my father and mother be ransomed for you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid, the two leaders of Najrān, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanting to engage in mutual imprecation (mubāhalah) with him.
He said: One of them said to his companion, "Do not do it.
By Allah, if he is a prophet and he invokes a curse with us,
neither we nor our descendants after us will prosper."
They said, "We will give you what you ask of us,
and send a trustworthy man with us,
and send with us only a trustworthy man." He said:
"I will send with you a man who is truly trustworthy."
The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stretched themselves up eagerly for it, but he said:
"Get up, O Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ."
When he stood up, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"This is the trustworthy one of this community."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding the fear prayer (ṣalāt al-khawf), he said: The imam stands facing the qiblah, and one group of them stands with him while another group faces the enemy, their faces toward the rows. He prays one rakʿah with those who are with him, and they perform a rakʿah for themselves and make two prostrations for themselves in their place. Then they go to the position of the others, and the others come, and he prays one rakʿah with them and makes two prostrations with them. So for him it is two rakʿahs and for them one. Then they pray one more rakʿah and make two prostrations.

Muhammad ibn Bashshār said: I asked Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān about this hadith, and he narrated to me from Shuʿbah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, from his father, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Khawwāt, from Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathmah, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to the hadith of Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd.
He said: Yaḥyā said to me, "Write it next to it; I do not remember the hadith, but it is like the hadith of Yaḥyā."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited a household of the Anṣār and ate some food with them.
When he wished to leave, he asked for a place in the house [to pray],
so a mat was sprinkled with water for him, and he prayed on it and made supplication for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"I saw two men come to me. They said: 'The one you saw whose jaw was being split is a liar who would tell a lie that would be carried from him until it reached the farthest horizons; so he will be treated like this until the Day of Resurrection.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Advise me." He said, "Do not become angry." The man repeated his request several times, and each time he said, "Do not become angry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
from the desert-dwellers came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, when will the Hour be established?" He said:
"Woe to you! What have you prepared for it?"
The man said, "I have prepared nothing for it, except that I love Allah and His Messenger." He said:
"You will be with those whom you love."
We said, "And are we the same?" He said, "Yes."
So we rejoiced greatly that day.
Then a servant boy of al-Mughīrah passed by, and he was of my age, and he said:
"If this one lives on, old age will not overtake him until the Hour is established."
Shuʿbah abridged it from Qatādah: I heard Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I sat with Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, and he told me that his grandfather, Ḥazn, came to the Prophet ﷺ. He said, "What is your name?"
He said, "My name is Ḥazn." He said:
"Rather, you are Sahl."
He said, "I will not change a name my father gave me."
Ibn al-Musayyib said: Harshness has continued to be among us ever since.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed on the day Ibrāhīm died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I spent the night in the house of Maymūnah, while the Prophet ﷺ was with her.

When it was the last third of the night, or part of it, he sat up and looked at the sky and recited: {Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: I have not seen anything more similar to the lamam [minor sins] than what Abū Hurayrah said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik—who was the guide of Kaʿb among his sons when he went blind—said: I heard Kaʿb ibn Mālik say,
when he stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the expedition of Tabūk—and he mentioned his account—and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the Muslims to speak to us,
we remained in that state for fifty nights,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ announced Allah's acceptance of our repentance.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the courtyard of the Kaʿbah, sitting wrapped with his hands around his knees like this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to Syria.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Sulaym
used to spread a leather mat for the Prophet ﷺ, and he would take his midday rest with her on that mat. He said: When the Prophet ﷺ slept, she would take some of his sweat and his hair,
and gather it in a bottle,

then gather it into sukk [a perfume]. He said: When death approached Anas ibn Mālik, he instructed that some of that sukk be put in his embalming perfume. He said: So it was put in his embalming perfume.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked, "How old were you when the Prophet ﷺ passed away?" He said, "I was circumcised by then."
He said: They would not circumcise a boy until he reached maturity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed away when I was circumcised.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr said: Ibn ʿUmar said, "By Allah, I have not placed a brick upon a brick,
nor planted a palm tree,
since the Prophet ﷺ passed away."
Sufyān said: I mentioned it to one of his family, and he said, "By Allah, he did build a house."
Sufyān said: I said, "Perhaps he said it before he built."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

label: machine translation

segments_en: "Once every Friday;
if you refuse, then twice;
if you want more, then three times, and do not make people weary of this Qur'an.
And let me not find you coming to people while they are engaged in their conversation and then you start preaching to them,
cutting off their conversation and wearying them. Rather, stay silent,
and when they ask you, speak to them while they are eager for it.
And beware of rhymed prose in supplication and avoid it,
for I knew the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions to do nothing but that."
That is, they did nothing but avoid it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiped his ears: he wiped the inside of them with his two index fingers, and placed his thumbs against the outside of his ears, so he wiped both the outside and the inside of them.

"The ears are part of the head."

"The ears are part of the head."

label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās came to me and asked me about this hadith,

meaning her hadith in which she mentioned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution and washed his feet. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "The people insist on nothing but washing, yet I find nothing in the Book of Allah but wiping."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Jibrīl taught me ablution, and he commanded me to sprinkle water beneath my garment for whatever urine comes out after ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you perform ablution, sprinkle water."

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to us, and we placed water for him, and he bathed. Then we brought him a sheet dyed with wars, and he wrapped himself in it. It is as if I can see the trace of the wars on the folds of his belly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Maymūnah said: I brought a cloth to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he had bathed from sexual impurity, but he returned it and began shaking off the water.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution, then turned over a woolen cloak he was wearing and wiped his face with it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She had a brass basin, and she said: I would comb the hair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ performed ablution from a small brass vessel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would sleep until he snored, then he would get up and pray without performing ablution.
Al-Ṭanāfisī said: Wakīʿ said: She means while he was prostrating.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ slept until he snored, then he got up and prayed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That sleep of his was while he was sitting, meaning the Prophet ﷺ.

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being asked about touching the private part, and he said:
"There is no ablution because of it; it is only a part of you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar ate bread and meat, and they did not perform ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I attended the dinner of al-Walīd, or ʿAbd al-Malik. When the time for prayer came, I got up to perform ablution. Jaʿfar ibn ʿAmr ibn Umayyah said: "I testify about my father that he witnessed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eat food that had been changed by fire, then pray without performing ablution."
ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās said: "And I testify,
about my father, to the same."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ate a shoulder of lamb, then rinsed his mouth, washed his hands and prayed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to perform ablution after eating camel meat, and not to perform ablution after eating sheep meat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not perform ablution after [drinking] sheep's milk, but perform ablution after [drinking] camel's milk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you drink milk, rinse your mouths, for it has fat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and ʿUmar was with him, and he came out to them and said: "I found prostatic fluid, so I washed my private part and performed ablution."
ʿUmar said: "Is that sufficient?" He said: "Yes."
He said: "Did you hear it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh pray several prayers with a single ablution.
I said: "What is this?" He said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do this, so I do as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, except that Maḥmūd said in his narration from Bishr: "
"And the likeness of the disbeliever is like the pine tree."
As for Ibn Ḥātim, he said: "The likeness of the hypocrite,"
as Zuhayr said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

Iblīs places his throne upon the water, then sends out his troops. The nearest of them to him in rank is the greatest of them in causing tribulation. One of them comes and says, 'I did such and such,' and he says, 'You have done nothing.' Then another comes and says, 'I did not leave him until I separated him from his wife.' He then draws him close and says, 'Yes, you are the one!'"
Al-Aʿmash said: I think he said, "And he embraces him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
There is none among you except that his companion from the jinn has been assigned to him."
They said, "And you too, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "
Me too, except that Allah has helped me against him, so he has submitted and commands me only to do good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out from her during the night.
She said: I felt jealous, and he came back and saw what I was doing, and he said: "
What is the matter, ʿĀʾishah? Are you jealous?"
I said, "How could someone like me not feel jealous over someone like you?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Has your devil come to you?"
She said, "O Messenger of Allah, do I have a devil with me?" He said, "Yes."
I said, "And with every person?" He said, "Yes."
I said, "And with you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "
Yes, but my Lord has helped me against him until he submitted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Through both chains of transmission, the same as the narration of Ibn Numayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I attended a gathering with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in which he described Paradise until he finished. Then he ﷺ said at the end of his talk: "
In it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never occurred to the heart of any human being."

Then he recited this verse: {Their sides forsake their beds; they call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and spend from what We have provided them. No soul knows what has been hidden for them of delight for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Among the people of my ummah who love me most intensely are people who will come after me. One of them would wish to see me even at the cost of his family and his wealth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

In Paradise there is a market that they will come to every Friday. The north wind will blow and scatter [fragrance] over their faces and clothes, and they will increase in beauty and loveliness. Then they will return to their families having increased in beauty and loveliness, and their families will say to them, 'By Allah, you have increased in beauty and loveliness since you left us.'
And they will say, 'And you too, by Allah, have increased in beauty and loveliness since we left you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever enters Paradise will enjoy bliss and will never suffer hardship; his clothes will not wear out and his youth will not fade."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Sayḥān, Jayḥān, the Euphrates and the Nile are all among the rivers of Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There will enter Paradise people whose hearts are like the hearts of birds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he heard a loud thud, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "
Do you know what this is?"
We said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "
This is a stone that was thrown into the Fire seventy years ago, and it has been falling in the Fire until now, when it reached its bottom."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "

Among them are those whom the Fire will seize up to their ankles, some whom the Fire will seize up to their knees, some whom the Fire will seize up to their waists, and some whom the Fire will seize up to their collarbones."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Paradise and the Fire disputed."
Then he mentioned something like the hadith of Abū Hurayrah up to his words: "
And for each of you it is upon Me to fill it."
He did not mention the additional part that follows.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "
Of Paradise there will remain what Allah wills to remain. Then Allah, the Exalted, will create for it a new creation of whatever He wills."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
I saw ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy ibn Qamʿah ibn Khindif, the father of these Banū Kaʿb, dragging his intestines in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
If you live long, you may soon see people with whips like the tails of cattle in their hands; they go out in the morning in the wrath of Allah and return in the evening in the anger of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked the Prophet ﷺ about fasting, and he said: "
Fast one day of every month."
He asked for more, saying, "May my father and mother be ransomed for you, I find myself strong." So he increased it for him, saying: "
Fast two days of every month."
He said, "May my father and mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of Allah, I find myself strong."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
I find myself strong, I find myself strong."
He was hardly willing to increase it for him, but when he insisted, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Fast three days of every month."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And from Abū Saʿīd, the two of them said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us one day and said: "
By the One in whose hand is my soul,"

three times. Then he bowed his head, and every man among us bowed his head weeping, not knowing about what he had sworn. Then he raised his head, and good news was in his face, which was dearer to us than red camels. Then he said: "

There is no servant who prays the five prayers, fasts Ramadan, pays zakāh, and avoids the seven major sins, except that the gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and it will be said to him: Enter in peace."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Any man who has camels and does not give what is due on them, in their hardship and their ease."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is their hardship and their ease?" He said: "

Their hardship and their ease. For they will come on the Day of Resurrection as vigorous, as fat, and as frisky as they ever were, and he will be laid out for them on a flat, level plain, and they will trample him with their hooves. Whenever the last of them has passed, the first of them will be returned to him, on a day whose length is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his way. And any man who has cattle and does not give what is due on them, in their hardship and their ease, they will come on the Day of Resurrection as vigorous, as fat, and as frisky as they ever were, and he will be laid out for them on a flat, level plain, and every horned one will gore him with its horn and every cloven-hoofed one will trample him with its hoof. Whenever the last of them has passed over him, the first of them will be returned to him, on a day whose length is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his way. And any man who has sheep and does not give what is due on them, in their hardship and their ease, they will come on the Day of Resurrection as numerous, as fat, and as frisky as they ever were, and he will be laid out for them on a flat, level plain, and every cloven-hoofed one will trample him with its hoof and every horned one will gore him with its horn; none of them will be twisted-horned or broken-horned. Whenever the last of them has passed over him, the first of them will be returned to him, on a day whose length is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his way."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent a collector, who came to a man, and he gave him a weak, emaciated young camel. The Prophet ﷺ said: "
We sent one to collect for Allah and His Messenger, and so-and-so gave him a weak, emaciated young camel. O Allah, do not bless him or his camels."
This reached the man, so he came with a fine she-camel and said, "I repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to His Prophet ﷺ." The Prophet ﷺ said: "
O Allah, bless him and his camels."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAlqamah [reported] that
he appointed his father over the charity of his people, and he narrated the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "I was almost killed after you left over a young goat or a sheep from the charity." He said: "
Were it not that it is given to the poor among the Emigrants, I would not have taken it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
I have exempted horses and slaves, and there is no zakāh on less than two hundred [dirhams]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with her daughter, and on her daughter's hand were two bracelets, similar to it, in a mursal form.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
There is no charity due on less than five awāq."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I listened,
from Ibn Wahb,
who said: ʿAbd al-Jalīl ibn Ḥumayd al-Yaḥṣubī told me,
that Ibn Shihāb
related to him, saying: Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf told me,

about the verse in which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: {And do not aim toward the bad of it to spend}, he said: It is al-Jurʿūr and lawn ḥubayq. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade taking the worst quality in charity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about lost property, and he said: "

What is found on a well-traveled road or in an inhabited village, announce it for a year. If its owner comes, [give it to him]; otherwise it is yours. And what is not found on a well-traveled road or in an inhabited village, then on it and on buried treasure is a fifth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A military expedition was levied against the people of Medina, and I enrolled my name in it.
Then I met ʿIkrimah, the freed slave of Ibn ʿAbbās, and told him about it,
and he forbade me from that in the strongest terms.
Then he said: Ibn ʿAbbās told me that some Muslims used to be with the polytheists, swelling the numbers of the polytheists against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. An arrow would come and be shot,
and it would hit one of them and kill him, or he would be struck and killed.
So Allah revealed: {Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while wronging themselves...} the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My mother was among those whom Allah excused.
label: machine translation

segments_en: {If you are troubled by rain or you are ill...} ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was wounded.
label: machine translation

segments_en: So the Prophet ﷺ made his camel kneel and dismounted,
and he laid his head in my lap and slept.
Abū Bakr came and gave me a hard poke, and said: You have detained the people because of a necklace!
I nearly died, out of regard for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, although he had hurt me.

Then the Prophet ﷺ woke up, and the time of the dawn prayer had come. He looked for water but none was found, so this was revealed: {O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer...} the verse.
Then Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr said: Allah has indeed blessed the people through you, O family of Abū Bakr!
You are nothing but a blessing for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was sitting behind ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz,
and they discussed and discussed, and said this and that, [saying] that the caliphs had carried out retaliation for it.
Then he turned to Abū Qilābah, who was behind his back,

and said: What do you say, O ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd? Or he said: What do you say, O Abū Qilābah? I said: I do not know of any person whose killing is permitted in Islam except a man who committed adultery after being married,
or a man who killed a person without [it being for] a life,
or a man who waged war against Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yes indeed, by Allah!
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, never used to break an oath,
until Allah revealed the expiation for oaths. Then he said: I do not swear an oath and then see something else to be better than it,
except that I do what is better,
and I make expiation for my oath.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The prohibition of wine was revealed, and at that time there were five drinks in Medina,
none of which was grape wine.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people used to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ questions mockingly,

so one man would say: Who is my father? and another whose camel had strayed would say: Where is my camel? So Allah revealed concerning them this verse: {O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if shown to you, would distress you} until he finished the whole verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah,
may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
I saw Hell, with parts of it smashing into other parts,
and I saw ʿAmr dragging his intestines,
and he was the first to set free animals [dedicated to idols].
label: machine translation

segments_en: You will be gathered,
and some people will be taken away to the left,
and I will say as the righteous servant said: {And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them} up to His saying {the Almighty, the Wise}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn ibn Ḥudhayfah came and stayed with his nephew al-Ḥurr ibn Qays,
who was among those whom ʿUmar kept close,
for the Qurʾān reciters were the people of ʿUmar's gatherings and consultation, whether old or young.
ʿUyaynah said to his nephew: O my nephew,
you have standing with this leader, so ask permission for me to see him.
He said: I will ask permission for you.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: So al-Ḥurr asked permission for ʿUyaynah, and ʿUmar permitted him.
When he entered upon him, he said: Come on, son of al-Khaṭṭāb!
By Allah, you do not give us generously,
and you do not judge between us with justice.
ʿUmar became angry, so much so that he was about to strike him,

but al-Ḥurr said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, Allah the Most High said to His Prophet ﷺ: {Take to forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant}, and this man is among the ignorant.
By Allah, ʿUmar did not go beyond it when it was recited to him,
and he would always stop at the Book of Allah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd,
and ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd,
informed him from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī, who said:
I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever sleeps through his portion [of the Qur'an recited at night], or part of it, and then recites it between the Fajr prayer and the Ẓuhr prayer, it will be recorded for him as if he had recited it during the night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,
that he described the voluntary prayers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: He would not pray after the Friday prayer until he had left, and then he would pray two rakʿahs in his house.
Yahyā said: I think I read "he would pray" or "definitely."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he delivered a sermon one day and mentioned a man from his Companions who had died and been shrouded in an inadequate shroud and buried at night. The Prophet ﷺ forbade burying a man at night until the funeral prayer has been offered for him, unless a person is compelled to do so. And the Prophet ﷺ said:
"When one of you shrouds his brother, let him make his shroud good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, from Sufyān,
from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUqbah, from Kurayb,
from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out, and when he was at al-Rawḥāʾ he met some people and said: "Who are you?" They said: "The Muslims."
They said: "And who are you?" He said: "The Messenger of Allah."
He said: A woman then lifted a boy out of a litter and said: "Is there Hajj for this one?" He said:
"Yes, and for you there is a reward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered Makkah—and Qutaybah said: he entered on the day of the conquest of Makkah—wearing a black turban, without being in iḥrām.
And in the narration of Qutaybah he said: Abū al-Zubayr narrated to us from Jābir.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ said: "None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself." Al-Qāḍī, meaning Ibn al-Kassār, said: I heard ʿAbd al-Ṣamad al-Bukhārī say: Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar, who narrates from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī, I do not know him, unless the letter wāw dropped from Ḥafṣ ibn ʿAmr al-Rabālī, who is well known for narrating from the Basrans, and he is reliable. He mentioned it in this report, in the hadith of Manṣūr ibn Saʿd, in the chapter on the description of the Muslim. I heard him say: I do not know of anyone who narrated the raised hadith of Anas ibn Mālik, "I have been commanded to fight the people," with the addition of the words "and face our qiblah, and eat our slaughtered animals, and pray our prayer," from Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl, except ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak and Yahyā ibn Ayyūb al-Baṣrī. And it is in this section, in the chapter on whom the people are to be fought.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"When a man sits between her four limbs and then exerts himself, ghusl has become obligatory for him."
And in the hadith of Muṭar:
"Even if he does not ejaculate."
Zuhayr said, among them:
"Between her four parts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Prayer in congregation is superior to the prayer of an individual by twenty-seven degrees."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the prayer is called and the evening meal is present, begin with the meal."
Wuhayb and Yahyā ibn Saʿīd said, from Hishām:
"When the evening meal has been set out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from his father,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to travel a day and a night's journey except with a mahram."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque and there was a rope stretched between two pillars. He said:
"What is this rope?"
It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is Ḥamnah bint Jaḥsh; she prays, and when she grows tired she hangs on to it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let her pray as long as she is able, and when she grows tired let her sit."
Ziyād said: He said, "What is this?"
They said: "It is for Zaynab; she prays, and when she becomes sluggish or weak she holds on to it." He said: "Untie it." Then he said:
"Let one of you pray while he is energetic, and when he becomes sluggish or weak, let him sit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he forbade a man to pray with his hand on his hip.
And in the narration of Abū Bakr, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade
label: machine translation

segments_en: Patience is at the first shock."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd ibn Hishām ibn ʿĀmir
wanted to go out to fight

in the cause of Allah. He came to Madinah and wanted to sell some property he had there and spend the proceeds on weapons and horses, and fight the Romans until he died. When he came to Madinah, he met some of its people, and they forbade him from doing that. They told him that a group of six men had wanted to do the same during the lifetime of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ forbade them and said:
"Do you not have in me an example?"

When they told him that, he took back his wife, whom he had divorced, and called witnesses to his taking her back. Then he went to Ibn ʿAbbās and asked him about the Witr prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Ibn ʿAbbās said, "Shall I not direct you to the one who knows best of all people on earth about the Witr of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He asked, "Who is that?" He said, "ʿĀʾishah."

"Go to her and ask her, then come back to me and tell me her answer to you." So I set out to her and passed by Ḥakīm ibn Aflaḥ and asked him to accompany me to her. He said, "I will not go near her, because I forbade her from saying anything about these two factions, but she insisted on going ahead with it."
He said: I adjured him, so he came, and we went to ʿĀʾishah and asked permission to enter. She allowed us, and we went in.
She said, "Is that Ḥakīm?" She recognized him. He said, "Yes."
She said, "Who is with you?" He said, "Saʿd ibn Hishām."
She said, "Which Hishām?" He said, "Ibn ʿĀmir." She asked Allah to have mercy on him and spoke well of him. Qatādah said: He had been killed on the day of Uḥud.
I said, "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
She said, "Do you not read the Qurʾān?" I said, "Yes."
She said, "The character of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was the Qurʾān."
He said: I thought of getting up and not asking anyone about anything until I died, but then it occurred to me, and I said, "Tell me about the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
She said, "Do you not read {O you who wrap yourself up}?" I said, "Yes."

She said, "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made the night prayer obligatory at the beginning of this sūrah, so the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and his Companions stood in prayer for a year, and Allah withheld its end for twelve months in the heavens, until Allah revealed the relief at the end of this sūrah. So the night prayer became voluntary after having been obligatory."
He said: I said, "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the Witr of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

She said, "We would prepare for him his tooth-stick and his water for purification, and Allah would wake him whenever He willed during the night. He would use the tooth-stick, perform ablution, and pray nine rakʿahs, sitting only in the eighth. He would remember Allah, praise Him, and supplicate to Him, then get up without giving the salutation. Then he would stand and pray the ninth, then sit, remember Allah, praise Him, and supplicate to Him, then give the salutation loudly enough for us to hear. Then he would pray two rakʿahs after giving the salutation, while sitting. That is eleven rakʿahs, my son. When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ grew older and put on weight, he prayed Witr with seven, and did in the two rakʿahs as he had done before. That is nine, my son. And when the Prophet of Allah ﷺ prayed a prayer, he liked to keep doing it regularly. If sleep or illness overcame him and kept him from the night prayer, he would pray twelve rakʿahs during the day. I do not know that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ recited the whole Qurʾān in one night, or prayed a whole night until morning, or fasted a complete month other than Ramadan."

He said: I went to Ibn ʿAbbās and told him what she had said. He said, "She has spoken the truth. If I were close to her or could enter upon her, I would go to her so that she could tell me it directly."
He said: I said, "Had I known that you do not visit her, I would not have related her account to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did a deed, he would keep it up. And when he slept through the night or was ill, he would pray twelve rakʿahs during the day.
She said: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stand in prayer a whole night until morning, nor fast a month continuously except Ramadan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked, "Which prayer is best?" He said, "A long standing [in devotion]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jewish man from the Jews of Banū Zurayq, called Labīd ibn al-Aʿṣam, cast a spell on the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: So much so that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would imagine that he had done something when he had not done it. Then one day, or one night, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ supplicated, then supplicated, then supplicated, and then said:
"ʿĀʾishah, do you realize that Allah has answered me concerning what I asked Him about? Two men came to me; one sat by my head and the other by my feet.
The one by my head said to the one by my feet, or the one by my feet said to the one by my head: 'What is the man's ailment?' The other said: 'He has been bewitched.'
He said: 'Who bewitched him?' He said: 'Labīd ibn al-Aʿṣam.'
He said: 'With what?' He said: 'With a comb and the hair caught in it.'
He said: 'And in what?' He said: 'In the spathe of a male palm tree.'
He said: 'Where is it?' He said: 'In the well of Dhū Arwān.'"
She said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to it with some of his Companions, and then said:
"ʿĀʾishah, by Allah, its water was like the infusion of henna, and its palm trees were like the heads of devils."
She said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, why did you not burn it? He said:
"No. As for me, Allah has healed me, and I disliked stirring up evil among the people. So I ordered that it be buried."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When night falls, or when you reach evening, keep your children in,
for the devils spread out at that time.
Then when an hour of the night has passed, let them go.
Close the doors and mention the name of Allah,
for the devil does not open a closed door.
Tie up your water-skins and mention the name of Allah,
and cover your vessels and mention the name of Allah,
even if you only lay something across them, and put out your lamps."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in ʿitikāf,
and I came to visit him at night. I spoke with him, then I got up
to return, and he got up with me to walk me back.
Her dwelling was in the house of Usāmah ibn Zayd.
Two men of the Anṣār passed by,
and when they saw the Prophet ﷺ they hurried. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Take it easy. She is Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy."
They said: Glory be to Allah, O Messenger of Allah! He said:
"Indeed the devil flows through the human being like blood,
and I feared that he might cast evil into your hearts," or he said, "something."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yawning is from the devil,
so when one of you yawns, let him suppress it as much as he can,
for when one of you says 'Hā,' the devil laughs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you wakes from his sleep, I think he said, and performs ablution, let him blow his nose three times,
for the devil spends the night in the upper part of his nose."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ commanded the killing of the snake with two stripes, for it takes away eyesight and causes miscarriage.
He means a harmful snake.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The first to enter Paradise."
Another chain: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
the wording being Qutaybah's, they both said: Jarīr narrated to us, from ʿUmārah,
from Abū Zurʿah,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The first group to enter Paradise will be in the form of the moon on the night of the full moon, and those who follow them will be like the most brilliantly shining star in the sky. They will not urinate, nor defecate, nor blow their noses, nor spit. Their combs will be of gold, their sweat will be musk, their incense burners will be aloeswood, and their spouses will be the wide-eyed houris. Their character will be as the character of one man, in the form of their father Adam, sixty cubits tall in the sky."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sālim said that Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among the people and praised Allah as He deserves,
then he mentioned the Dajjāl and said: "I warn you about him,
and there was no prophet but that he warned his people.
Indeed Nūḥ warned his people,
but I will tell you something about him that no prophet told his people:
you know that he is one-eyed,
and that Allah is not one-eyed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Banū ʿĀmir said: I entered Islam, and my religion became a concern for me, so I went to Abū Dharr. Abū Dharr said: I found Medina unhealthy for me, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered for me a herd of camels and some sheep, and he said to me:
"Drink from their milk."
Ḥammād said: And I am unsure whether he said, "and their urine."
This is the statement of Ḥammād.

Abū Dharr said: I used to be far from water while my family was with me, and I would become impure from sexual impurity and pray without purification. So I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at midday while he was among a group of his Companions in the shade of the mosque. He said: "Abū Dharr?"
I said: Yes, I am ruined, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "What has ruined you?"

I said: I used to be far from water while my family was with me, and I would become impure from sexual impurity and pray without purification. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered water for me, and a black girl brought it in a large bowl that was sloshing, not full. I took cover behind my camel and washed, then I came back. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Abū Dharr, clean earth is a means of purification, even if you do not find water for ten years. And when you find water, let it touch your skin."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had a nocturnal emission on a cold night during the expedition of Dhāt as-Salāsil, and I feared that if I washed I would perish, so I performed tayammum and then led my companions in the Fajr prayer. They mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"O ʿAmr, you led your companions in prayer while you were in a state of sexual impurity?"
So I told him what had prevented me from washing, and I said: I heard Allah say, {And do not kill yourselves; indeed Allah is ever Merciful to you.} The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and said nothing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out on a journey, and a stone struck one of our men and split his head. Then he had a nocturnal emission, so he asked his companions, saying: Do you find a concession for me to perform tayammum? They said: We find no concession for you while you are able to use water. So he washed and died. When we came to the Prophet ﷺ, he was told of that, and he said:

"They killed him; may Allah kill them! Why did they not ask when they did not know? Indeed the cure for ignorance is asking. It would have been enough for him to perform tayammum and to squeeze—or: to bind—" (Mūsā was unsure)
"a piece of cloth over his wound, then wipe over it and wash the rest of his body."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men went out on a journey, and the time for prayer came while they had no water, so they performed tayammum with clean earth and prayed. Then they found water while the prayer time was still in effect. One of them repeated the prayer and the ablution, and the other did not. Then they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him. He said to the one who did not repeat:
"You have acted in accordance with the Sunnah, and your prayer is sufficient for you."
And he said to the one who performed ablution and repeated:
"You will have the reward twice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Going out for Friday prayer is obligatory on every adult, and washing is required for everyone who goes out to Friday prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever washes on Friday, wears his finest clothes, and applies some perfume if he has any, then comes to the Friday prayer without stepping over people's necks, then prays what Allah has decreed for him, then stays silent when the imam comes out until he finishes his prayer, that will be an expiation for the sins between it and the previous Friday."
He said: And Abū Hurayrah would say:
"And an additional three days." And he would say:
"Indeed a good deed is rewarded tenfold."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:

"Whoever washes on Friday, applies some of his wife's perfume if she has any, wears his good clothes, then does not step over people's necks and does not engage in idle talk during the sermon, it will be an expiation for the sins between the two Fridays. But whoever engages in idle talk and steps over people's necks, it will count for him as only a noon prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to wash for four things: for sexual impurity, on Friday, after cupping, and after washing the dead.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Makḥūl about this saying, "ghassala wa-ightasala."
He said: He washed his head and washed his body.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah said: By the One in whose Hand is my soul, this verse was revealed about me, and it was I whom it meant:

"And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head, then [let him make] a ransom of fasting, or charity, or a sacrifice." He said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ at al-Ḥudaybiyah while we were in a state of iḥrām, and the polytheists had besieged us. I had thick hair, and lice began to fall onto my face. The Prophet ﷺ passed by me and said,
"Are the lice of your head troubling you?"
I said: Yes. He said, "Then shave it."
And this verse was revealed.
Mujāhid said: The fasting is three days, the feeding is of six poor people, and the sacrifice is a sheep or more.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I sat with Kaʿb, may Allah be pleased with him, in the mosque and asked him about this verse: "a ransom of fasting, or charity, or a sacrifice." Kaʿb, may Allah be pleased with him, said: It was revealed about me. I had an ailment of my head, so I was carried to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while the lice were scattering over my face. He said,
"I did not think that hardship had reached you to the extent that I see. Can you find a sheep?"

I said: No. Then this verse was revealed: "a ransom of fasting, or charity, or a sacrifice." He said: Fasting three days, or feeding six poor people, half a ṣāʿ of food for each poor person. He said: It was revealed about me in particular, but it applies to all of you in general.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Prophet ﷺ in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyah. His Companions entered iḥrām, but I did not.
Then we were informed of an enemy at Ghayqah, so we headed toward them.
My companions caught sight of a wild donkey,
and some of them began to laugh with one another.
I looked and saw it, so I charged at it on my horse, stabbed it, and brought it down. I asked them for help,
but they refused to help me, so we ate from it.
Then I set off to catch up with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as we feared being cut off.
I would urge my horse on for a stretch,
and walk it for a stretch.
In the middle of the night I met a man from Banū Ghifār and said: Where did you leave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: I left him at Taʿhin, and he was to rest at midday at as-Suqyā.
So I caught up with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until I came to him and said: O Messenger of Allah,
your Companions send you greetings of peace, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings,
and they fear that the enemy may cut them off from you, so wait for them.
He did so. Then I said: O Messenger of Allah,
we hunted a wild donkey,
and we have some left over.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions, "Eat," though they were in a state of iḥrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man stood up and said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you command us to wear of clothing in iḥrām? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Do not wear shirts, nor trousers, nor hooded cloaks, nor turbans, nor leather socks, unless someone has no sandals, in which case let him wear leather socks and cut them off below the ankles. And do not wear any garment touched by saffron or wars. And a woman in iḥrām must not wear a face veil nor gloves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that he used to say: If I saw gazelles grazing in Medina, I would not startle them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"What lies between its two lava plains is sacred."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Indeed, faith will retreat to Medina as a snake retreats to its hole."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nuʿaym ibn ʿAbdullāh,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Over the mountain passes of Medina are angels; neither the plague nor the Antichrist will enter it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ fasted on ʿĀshūrāʾ and commanded fasting on it.
When the fasting of Ramadan was made obligatory, it was abandoned.
ʿAbdullāh would not fast on it,
unless it coincided with his [regular] fasting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ibn Muslim mentioned from Uways ibn Abī Uways,
an ally of Banū Taym, from Anas ibn Mālik,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"This is Ramadan, which has come to you. In it the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of the Fire are closed, and the devils are chained."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed from ʿArafāt with Usāmah ibn Zayd riding behind him. The she-camel veered with him, while he was raising his hands no higher than his head, and he continued to proceed at an easy pace until he reached Jamʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed from ʿArafah while I was riding behind him. He kept pulling back his mount's reins until its head nearly touched the front of the saddle, and he was saying:
"O people, hold to calmness and dignity, for righteousness does not lie in hurrying the camels."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set off, he pulled his she-camel's reins in so tightly that her head nearly touched the middle of his saddle, and he was saying to the people on the evening of ʿArafah: "Calmness, calmness!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ departed from ʿArafah and kept saying:
"Calmness, servants of Allah!"
He would say it with his hand like this, and Ayyūb gestured with the palm of his hand toward the sky.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ commanded the weak ones of Banū Hāshim to depart from Jamʿ during the night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ commanded her to set out in the darkness before dawn from Jamʿ to Minā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ permitted Sawdah to depart from Jamʿ before the dawn prayer only because she was a heavy, slow-moving woman.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever reaches Jamʿ with the imam and the people until he departs from it has reached the Hajj, and whoever does not reach it with the people and the imam has not reached it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me with the weak ones of his family, so we prayed the dawn prayer at Minā and threw the pebbles at the Jamrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Minā in the darkness before dawn with Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr, and I said to her, "We have come to Minā in the darkness."
She said, "We used to do this with one who was better than you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the people when they departed on the evening of ʿArafah and the morning of Jamʿ: "Hold to calmness."
He was holding back his she-camel until, when he entered Minā and descended into Muḥassir, he said:
"Take the small pebbles with which the Jamrah is thrown."
And the Prophet ﷺ said, gesturing with his hand as a person flicks a pebble.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went in to Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh, and I said, "Tell me about the Hajj of the Prophet ﷺ."

He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out from Muzdalifah before the sun rose, and he had al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās ride behind him. When he reached Muḥassir, he hastened a little, then took the middle road that brings you out to the greatest Jamrah, until he came to the Jamrah by the tree. He threw seven pebbles, saying the takbīr with each pebble, small pebbles of the kind that are flicked, throwing from the bottom of the valley.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, the Mother of the Believers, [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded one of his wives to depart from Jamʿ on the night of Jamʿ, then to come to Jamrat al-ʿAqabah and throw at it, and to be in her dwelling by morning.
And ʿAṭāʾ used to do this until he died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mujāhid said: Saʿd said, "We returned from the Hajj with the Prophet ﷺ, and some of us would say, 'I threw seven pebbles,' and some of us would say, 'I threw six,' yet none of them found fault with the others."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and some companions of his
came to the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we were in might while we were polytheists, but when we believed we became humiliated." He said:
"I have been commanded to pardon, so do not fight."

Then when Allah moved us to Madinah, we were commanded to fight, but they held back, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {Have you not seen those who were told, 'Restrain your hands and establish prayer'}
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jāhimah
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I wish to go out on a military expedition, and I have come to consult you." He said:
"Do you have a mother?" He said, "Yes." He said:
"Then stay with her, for Paradise is beneath her feet."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the year of Tabūk, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was addressing the people while leaning his back against his mount, and he said:

"Shall I not tell you who are the best of people and the worst of people? Among the best of people is a man who works in the cause of Allah on the back of his horse, or on the back of his camel, or on his feet, until death comes to him. And among the worst of people is a wicked man who recites the Book of Allah yet is not deterred by any of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When Allah speaks the revelation, the inhabitants of the heavens hear a clanging sound like a chain being dragged over rock, and they fall unconscious,
and they remain so until Jibrīl comes to them. When Jibrīl comes to them, the fear is lifted from their hearts." He said: "They say:
'O Jibrīl, what did your Lord say?' He says: 'The truth.' They say: 'The truth, the truth.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and we stopped at a resting place. He said: "
You are not even one part in a hundred thousand parts of those who will come to me at the Pool." He said, I asked:
How many were you on that day?
He said: Seven hundred or eight hundred.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was taken up into Paradise, or as he said, a river appeared before him, its two banks of hollowed pearl-like jewels (or he said, hollowed-out rubies),
and the angel who was with him struck his hand and brought out musk. Muḥammad ﷺ said to the angel who was with him: "What is this?" He said:
This is al-Kawthar, which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has given you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present when Abū Barzah entered upon ʿUbaydullāh ibn Ziyād, and so-and-so told me,
Muslim named him, and he was seated in the row. When ʿUbaydullāh saw him, he said:
"This Muḥammadan of yours is a stumbling dwarf,"

and the old man understood the remark and said, "I never thought I would remain among a people who would taunt me for having been a Companion of Muḥammad ﷺ." ʿUbaydullāh said to him, "The companionship of Muḥammad ﷺ is an adornment for you, not a disgrace." Then he said:
"I only sent for you to ask you about the Pool. Did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mention anything about it?" Abū Barzah said:
"Yes, not once, nor twice, nor three times, nor four, nor five times,
and whoever denies it, may Allah not give him a drink from it." Then he went out angry.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ entered a palm grove belonging to Banū al-Najjār and heard a sound, and was alarmed. He said: "
Who are the occupants of these graves?" They said:
"O Messenger of Allah, people who died in the Time of Ignorance." He said: "
Seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the Fire and from the trial of the Dajjāl." They said:
"Why is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "
When a believer is placed in his grave, an angel comes to him and says to him:
'What did you worship?' Allah guides him, and he says:
'I worshipped Allah.' Then it is said to him:
'What did you say about this man?' He says:
'He is the servant of Allah and His Messenger.' He is asked about nothing else. Then he is taken to a house that was his in the Fire, and it is said to him:
'This was your house in the Fire, but Allah protected you and had mercy on you, and replaced it for you with a house in Paradise.' He says:
'Let me go and give the good news to my family.' It is said to him: 'Stay.'
And when a disbeliever is placed in his grave, an angel comes to him and rebukes him, saying to him:
'What did you worship?' He says: 'I do not know.' It is said to him:
'You did not know, and you did not follow.' Then it is said to him:
'What did you say about this man?' He says:
'I used to say what the people said.'
Then he is struck with a hammer of iron between his ears, and he screams a scream that all creatures hear except the two groups of jinn and mankind."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She mentioned the Fire and wept. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What makes you weep?" She said:
"I remembered the Fire and wept.
Will you remember your families on the Day of Resurrection?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
As for three places, no one will remember anyone else:
at the Scale, until he knows whether his scale is light or heavy;
at the Record, when it is said, 'Here, read my record!' until he knows where his record will fall, in his right hand, or his left, or from behind his back;
and at the Bridge, when it is laid across the back of Hell." Yaʿqūb said:
from Yūnus, and this is the wording of his narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
How will you be when there are leaders after me who monopolize this war booty?" I said:
"By the One who sent you with the truth, then I would put my sword on my shoulder
and strike with it until I meet you or join you." He said: "
Shall I not guide you to something better than that? Be patient until you meet me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
There will be leaders over you, some of whose actions you will recognize as right and some you will disapprove of. Whoever disapproves of it..."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Indeed the lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters." Sometimes he said: "
and between them are doubtful things." He said: "

And I will give you an example of this: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has a protected preserve, and the preserve of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is what He has forbidden. Whoever grazes around the preserve is about to stray into it." Sometimes he said: "
Whoever grazes around the preserve is about to graze within it, and whoever mixes with doubt is about to dare [to commit the forbidden]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The measure is the measure of the people of Madinah, and the weight is the weight of the people of Makkah." The wording is that of Isḥāq.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us and said: "
Is there anyone here from the family of so-and-so?"
No one answered him. Then he said: "
Is there anyone here from the family of so-and-so?"
No one answered him. Then he said: "
Is there anyone here from the family of so-and-so?"
A man stood up and said, "I am, O Messenger of Allah." The Prophet ﷺ said: "
What prevented you from answering me the first two times? I mentioned you only for good. Your companion is held captive by his debt."
Then I saw the debt paid on his behalf until no one remained who was claiming anything from him.
label: machine translation
