segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not pray over a man who died owing a debt. A dead man was brought to him and he asked, "Does he owe a debt?"
They said, "Yes, two dīnārs." He said: "
Pray over your companion."
Abū Qatādah al-Anṣārī said, "They are my responsibility, O Messenger of Allah."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over him. Then when Allah gave conquests to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: "
I am closer to every believer than himself. Whoever leaves a debt, its repayment is upon me, and whoever leaves wealth, it is for his heirs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbādah stood to give a sermon and said: O people, you have introduced transactions that I do not know, except that gold for gold must be weight for weight, whether unrefined or minted, and silver for silver must be weight for weight, whether unrefined or minted. There is no harm in selling silver for gold hand to hand, with the silver being the greater amount, but deferred payment is not valid. Wheat for wheat and barley for barley must be a measure for a measure. There is no harm in selling barley for wheat hand to hand, with the barley being the greater amount, but deferred payment is not valid. And dates for dates must be a measure for a measure, until he mentioned salt, a measure for a measure. Whoever gives more or asks for more has engaged in usury.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zayd ibn Thābit said: May Allah forgive Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj. By Allah,
I know the hadith better than he does. Two men came to him—Musaddad said, "of the Anṣār," and then they agreed—who had been fighting each other, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
If this is your situation, then do not rent out farmland."
Musaddad added: So he heard his words: "
Do not rent out farmland."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of us no longer needed his land,

he would give it out for a third, a quarter, or a half, and would stipulate three channels, the stalks, and whatever the spring watering irrigated. Life was hard at that time, and he would work it with iron tools and whatever Allah willed, and would gain some benefit from it. Then Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj came to us and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has forbidden you something that was beneficial to you, but obedience to Allah and His Messenger is more beneficial to you. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade you ḥaql and said: "
Whoever does not need his land, let him lend it to his brother or leave it alone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade muḥāqalah and muzābanah, and said: "
Only three people should cultivate: a man who owns land and cultivates it; a man who is lent land and cultivates what he was lent; and a man who rents land for gold or silver."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ conquered Khaybar, he stipulated for himself the land and everything yellow and white,
meaning gold and silver.
The people of Khaybar said to him, "We know the land better, so give it to us on condition that we work it and have half the fruit, and you have half."

He related that he gave it to them on that basis. Then when the time came to harvest the dates, he sent Ibn Rawāḥah to them, and he estimated the date palms, which the people of Madinah call khars, and said, "In this there is such and such."
They said, "You have estimated too much against us, O Ibn Rawāḥah."
He said, "Then I will estimate the palms and give you half of what I have said."
He said: They said, "This is the truth, and by it the heavens and the earth stand."
They said, "We are content to take what you have said."
label: machine translation

segments_en: This is the hadith of Qutaybah: The poor among the Emigrants
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "The wealthy have gone off with the highest ranks and lasting bliss." He said, "How is that?"
They said, "They pray as we pray and fast as we fast, and they give charity while we cannot, and they free slaves while we cannot."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Shall I not teach you something by which you will overtake those who have gone ahead of you and stay ahead of those who come after you, and no one will be better than you except one who does the same as you have done?"
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"Glorify Allah, declare His greatness, and praise Him after every prayer, thirty-three times each."
Abū Ṣāliḥ said: The poor among the Emigrants returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "Our brothers, the people of wealth, heard of what we did, and they have done the same."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whomever He wills."
Someone other than Qutaybah added in this hadith, from al-Layth, from Ibn ʿAjlān: Sumayy said: I related this hadith to some of my family, and he said, "You are mistaken. He only said,
'Glorify Allah thirty-three times, praise Allah thirty-three times, and declare Allah's greatness thirty-three times.'"

So I went back to Abū Ṣāliḥ and told him that. He took me by the hand and said, "Allahu akbar, subḥān Allāh, and al-ḥamdu lillāh; Allahu akbar, subḥān Allāh, and al-ḥamdu lillāh," until you reach thirty-three of each of them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed the ʿAṣr prayer with the Prophet ﷺ in Medina. Then he left, quickly stepping over the necks of the people, so that they were amazed at his haste. Some of his Companions followed him, and he entered the room of one of his wives, then came out and said,
"While in the ʿAṣr prayer I remembered a piece of gold that we had in the house, and I disliked that it should remain with us overnight, so I ordered that it be distributed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Whoever eats from this plant"—meaning garlic—"let him not come near us in our mosques."
I said, "What does he mean by it?" He said, "I think he means only when it is raw."
And Makhlad ibn Yazīd said, from Ibn Jurayj: "Only its foul smell."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He passed with the Prophet ﷺ by a grave set apart, and he led them in prayer, and they prayed behind him.
I said, "Who related this to you, O Abū ʿAmr?" He said, "Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said,]
"When your women ask your permission to go to the mosque at night, give them permission."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"No man bathes on Friday,
purifies himself as much as he can,
uses some of his oil,
or touches some of the perfume of his house, then goes out,
does not separate between two people,
then prays what has been decreed for him,
then listens quietly when the imam speaks,
except that he is forgiven what is between that and the next Friday."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He mentioned the saying of the Prophet ﷺ about bathing on Friday.
Ṭāwūs said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās, "And [should he] use perfume or oil, if his family has it?" He said, "I do not know."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"I have said much to you about the siwāk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The first Friday prayer held in Islam, after the Friday prayer held in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Medina, was a Friday prayer held at Juwāthā, a village of Bahrain.
ʿUthmān said: a village of ʿAbd al-Qays.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the fear prayer. He stood and said the takbīr, and a group of us prayed behind him while another group faced the enemy. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed with them once and prostrated twice. Then they left without giving the salām and turned toward the enemy, taking up their position in rows. The other group came and formed rows behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he prayed one rakʿah with them with two prostrations. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the salām, having completed two rakʿahs and four prostrations. Then both groups stood up, and each person prayed one rakʿah with two prostrations by himself.
Abū Bakr ibn al-Sunnī said: al-Zuhrī heard two hadith from Ibn ʿUmar, but he did not hear this one from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, and the people stood with him. He said the takbīr and they said the takbīr; then he bowed and some of them bowed; then he prostrated and they prostrated. Then he stood for the second rakʿah, and those who had prostrated with him stayed back and guarded their brothers. The other group came and bowed and prostrated with the Prophet ﷺ, and all the people were in prayer, saying the takbīr, but some of them guarded others.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There will be disagreement and division among my nation:
a people who speak well but act badly, and who recite the Qur'an but it does not go beyond their collarbones.

They pass out of the religion as an arrow passes through its target, and they do not return until the arrow returns to its notch. They are the worst of creation and of mankind. Blessed is the one who kills them and the one whom they kill.
They call to the Book of Allah, yet they have nothing to do with it.
Whoever fights them is closer to Allah than they are." They said:
"O Messenger of Allah, what is their sign?" He said: "Shaving the head."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said: "Look for the one with the deformed hand."
Then he mentioned the hadith, and they pulled him out from beneath the slain, in the mud.
Abū al-Waḍīʾ said:
"It is as though I can see him now: an Abyssinian wearing a short tunic, with one of his hands like a woman's breast, with small hairs on it like the hairs on the tail of a jerboa."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "That deformed man was indeed with us in the mosque at that time; we would sit with him night and day,
and he was poor. I saw him with the poor, attending the meals of ʿAlī, peace be upon him, together with the people, and I had clothed him with a hooded cloak of mine."
Abū Maryam said:
"The deformed man was called Nāfiʿ Dhū al-Thudayyah (the one with the little breast),
and on his hand was something like a woman's breast, with a nipple on its top like the nipple of a breast, with hairs on it like the whiskers of a cat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years in Medina while I was a boy. Not everything I did was as my master wished it to be, yet he never said "Ugh" to me in all that time, and he never said to me, "Why did you do this?" or "Why did you not do that?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Narrated] by one of the sons of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said something similar, and he said:
"Allah will fill him with security and faith."
He did not mention the account of "Allah called him." He added:
"And whoever gives up wearing a fine garment while he is able to,
" Bishr said: I think he said:
"out of humility, Allah will clothe him with a garment of honor; and whoever marries [someone] for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, Allah will crown him with the crown of kingship."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:
"When one of you becomes angry while standing, let him sit down. If the anger leaves him, [well and good]; otherwise, let him lie down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went to ʿUrwah ibn Muḥammad al-Saʿdī, and a man spoke to him and made him angry. He got up and performed ablution, then returned, having performed ablution, and said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather ʿAṭiyyah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Anger is from Satan, and Satan was created from fire, and fire is only extinguished with water. So when one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her. She said: When something about a man reached the Prophet ﷺ, he would not say, "What is wrong with so-and-so, that he says..." Rather, he would say:
"What is wrong with people who say such and such?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her: that a man
asked permission to see the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"What an evil brother of the tribe."
When he entered, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ received him warmly and spoke with him. When he left, I said: "O Messenger of Allah, when he asked permission you said:
'What an evil brother of the tribe.'
Then when he entered, you received him warmly." He said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, Allah does not love the one who is obscene and who affects obscenity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In this account she said: He, meaning the Prophet ﷺ, said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, among the worst of people are those who are honored out of fear of their tongues."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw a man put his mouth to the ear of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and have him pull his head away, until the man himself pulled his head away; and I never saw a man take him by the hand and have him let go of his hand, until the man himself let go of his hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, by his good character the believer attains the rank of one who fasts [by day] and stands in prayer [by night]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nothing is heavier in the Scale than good character."
Abū al-Walīd said: I heard ʿAṭāʾ al-Kaykhārānī [say this].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I guarantee a house on the outskirts of Paradise for one who gives up arguing even if he is in the right, a house in the middle of Paradise for one who gives up lying even in jest, and a house in the highest part of Paradise for one who makes his character good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The jawwāẓ and the jaʿẓarī will not enter Paradise."
He said: The jawwāẓ is the coarse, harsh one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is a right upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that nothing of this world rises up except that He brings it down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "The people have been neglected,
and you are the son of ʿUmar and a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ. What prevents you from going out?" He said, "What prevents me is that Allah has forbidden the blood of my brother."
They said, "Did Allah not say: {And fight them until there is no more fitnah}?" He said, "We fought until there was no more fitnah,
and the religion was for Allah,
whereas you want to fight until there is fitnah,
and the religion is for other than Allah."
ʿUthmān ibn Ṣāliḥ added, from Ibn Wahb,
who said: So-and-so informed me,
and Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ,
from Bakr ibn ʿAmr al-Maʿāfirī,
that Bukayr ibn ʿAbdullāh
narrated to him from Nāfiʿ that a man
came to Ibn ʿUmar and said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, what makes you perform Hajj one year and ʿUmrah another year,
and abandon jihad in the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic,

when you know how much Allah has encouraged it?" He said, "O son of my brother, Islam is built upon five: belief in Allah and His Messenger, the five prayers, fasting Ramadan, paying zakāh, and Hajj to the House."
He said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,

do you not hear what Allah mentions in His Book: {And if two groups of the believers fight each other, make peace between them} {until it returns to the command of Allah} {and fight them until there is no more fitnah}?" He said, "We did that in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when Islam was small in number,
and a man would be persecuted for his religion; they would either kill him or torture him,
until Islam grew, and there was no more fitnah."
He said, "Then what do you say about ʿAlī and ʿUthmān?" He said, "As for ʿUthmān, Allah pardoned him,
but you disliked that He pardon him.
As for ʿAlī, he is the cousin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his son-in-law."
And he pointed with his hand and said, "That is his house, where you see it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, recited the Qur'an, he would not speak until he had finished it.
One day I took the book to read to him,
and he recited Sūrat al-Baqarah until he reached a certain place. He said, "Do you know concerning what this was revealed?" I said, "No."
He said, "It was revealed concerning such and such." Then he continued.
And from ʿAbd al-Ṣamad: My father narrated to me: Ayyūb narrated to me, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
{So come to your place of tilth however you wish}, he said: "He approaches her in"
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, "Concerning what do you think this verse was revealed: {Would any of you like to have a garden}?" They said, "Allah knows best."
ʿUmar became angry and said, "Say, 'We know' or 'We do not know.'"
Ibn ʿAbbās said, "I have something in my mind about it, O Commander of the Faithful."
ʿUmar said, "O son of my brother, speak, and do not belittle yourself."
Ibn ʿAbbās said, "It is a parable struck for a deed."
ʿUmar said, "Which deed?" Ibn ʿAbbās said, "For a deed."
ʿUmar said, "For a rich man who does acts of obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic,
then Allah sends Satan to him, and he does acts of disobedience until he drowns his deeds." {Ṣurrahunna}: cut them into pieces.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I think he was Ibn ʿUmar, regarding {Whether you reveal what is within yourselves or conceal it}, he said: "The verse after it abrogated it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: So he gave it to Ḥassān and Ubayy,
though I was closer to him,
and he gave me nothing of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The best of people for the people:
you bring them in chains around their necks until they enter Islam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to supplicate against someone or for someone, he would recite the qunūt after bowing.
Often he would say, after saying:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him,
O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs all praise.
O Allah, save al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd,
Salamah ibn Hishām,
and ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah.
O Allah, press down Your tread upon Muḍar and make it years like the years of Yūsuf."
He would say this aloud. And in some of his prayers, in the Fajr prayer, he would say: "
O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so,"
naming some of the Arab tribes,
until Allah revealed: {You have no say in the matter} the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: {Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.} Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, said it when he was thrown into the Fire,

and Muḥammad ﷺ said it when they said: {Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them; but it increased them in faith, and they said: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The last words of Ibrāhīm when he was thrown into the Fire were: "Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is muḥkam (definitive) and not abrogated.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās
recited {except the oppressed among men, women, and children}, and said, "I and my mother were among those whom Allah excused."
It is also mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbās: {ḥaṣirat} means constrained; {talwū} means you twist your tongues in testimony.
Someone else said: al-murāghama means the emigrant.
"Rāghamtu" means I emigrated from my people.
{Mawqūt} means timed; He appointed its time for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They mentioned their negligence in sleeping, and he said: They slept until the sun had risen.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no negligence in sleep; negligence is only in wakefulness. So if any of you forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, let him pray it when he remembers it, and [again] at its time on the next day."
ʿAbdullāh ibn Rabāḥ said: ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥusayn heard me while I was narrating
the hadith, and he said: Young man, be careful how you narrate, for I was a witness to this hadith with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said: I did not find anything in his narration to object to.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When any of you breaks his fast, let him break it with dates, for they are a blessing; and if he finds no dates, then with water, for it is pure." And he said:
"Charity given to a poor person is [one] charity, and given to a relative it is two: charity and maintaining family ties."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Wear white among your garments, for it is purer and better, and shroud your dead in it."
Yaḥyā said: I did not write it down.
I said: Why? He said: I was satisfied with the hadith of Maymūn ibn Abī Shabīb from Samurah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Allah gave His Messenger victory over Makkah, he stood among the people, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said:
"Whoever has a relative killed has the better of two options: either to pardon or to take retaliation by killing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: What if she gives birth? He said: Slaughter her offspring along with her.
I said: What about a lame one? He said: If it reaches the place of sacrifice.
I said: What about one with a broken horn? He said: There is no harm. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us, or commanded us, to examine the eyes and the ears carefully.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever swears by a religion other than Islam, lying, is as he said."
Qutaybah said in his narration: deliberately. And Yazīd said:
"lying, he is as he said; and whoever kills himself with something, Allah will punish him with it in the Fire of Hell."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Good is in the forelocks of horses," or he said, "Horses have good tied to their forelocks" (Suhayl said: I am unsure whether it was "good") "until the Day of Resurrection. Horses are of three kinds: for one man they are a reward, for another a covering, and for another a burden. As for the one for whom they are a reward, he is the man who keeps them for the cause of Allah and prepares them for it. Nothing enters their bellies except that a reward is recorded for him, and if he lets them graze in a meadow, nothing they eat but a reward is recorded for him for it. If he waters them from a flowing river, he has a reward for every drop that enters their bellies," until he mentioned reward even for their urine and dung, "and if they break loose and run over one or two hills, a reward is recorded for him for every step they take.
As for the one for whom they are a covering, he is the man who keeps them out of honor and for beauty, and does not forget Allah's right in their backs and their bellies, in hardship and in ease.
As for the one for whom they are a burden, he is the one who keeps them out of arrogance, ostentation, extravagance, and showing off to people; for him they are a burden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Ibn Abī Rāfiʿ wearing a ring on his right hand, so I asked him about that,
and he said: I saw ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar wearing a ring on his right hand.
And ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar said: The Prophet ﷺ used to wear a ring on his right hand.
He said: And Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl said: This is the most authentic thing reported on this subject.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz
brought his throne out one day for the people,
then gave them permission and they entered. He said, "What do you say about the qasāmah?" They said, "We say that retaliation by it is right,
and the caliphs have carried out retaliation by it."
He said to me, "What do you say, Abū Qilābah?" and he set me before the people.
I said, "O Commander of the Faithful, you have with you the heads of the armies and the nobles of the Arabs.
Tell me: if fifty of them testified against a married man in Damascus that he had committed adultery,
without having seen it, would you stone him?" He said, "No."
I said, "Tell me: if fifty of them testified against a man in Homs that he had stolen, would you cut off his hand, though they had not seen it?" He said, "No."
I said, "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never killed anyone
except in one of three cases: a man who killed [someone] and was killed for his own crime,
or a man who committed adultery after being married,
or a man who waged war against Allah and His Messenger and apostatized from Islam."
The people said, "Did Anas ibn Mālik not narrate that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cut off [limbs] for theft and gouged out eyes with heated nails,
then cast them out in the sun?"
I said, "I will narrate to you the hadith of Anas.
Anas narrated to me that a group of eight men from ʿUkl came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and pledged allegiance to him on Islam,
but they found the land unhealthy and their bodies fell ill,
so they complained of that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said:
"Will you not go out with our shepherd among his camels,
and take some of their milk and urine?" They said, "Yes."
So they went out and drank of their milk and urine and recovered,
then they killed the shepherd of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and drove off the camels.
That reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he sent [men] in their tracks.
They were caught and brought back,
and he ordered concerning them, so their hands and feet were cut off, and their eyes were gouged with heated nails,
then he cast them out in the sun until they died."
I said, "What could be worse than what these men did? They apostatized from Islam, killed, and stole."
ʿAnbasah ibn Saʿīd said, "By Allah, I have never heard the like of today."
I said, "Do you reject my hadith, ʿAnbasah?" He said, "No,
but you have brought the hadith in its proper form.
By Allah, these troops will continue to be well as long as this shaykh lives among them."
I said, "There was also a precedent in this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: a group of the Anṣār came to him and talked with him,
then one of them went out ahead of them and was killed. They went out after him
and found their companion writhing in blood.
They returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, our companion was talking with us,
then he went out ahead of us,
and we found him writhing in blood."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out and said:
"Whom do you suspect or think killed him?"
They said, "We think the Jews killed him."
So he sent for the Jews and summoned them. He said:
"Did you kill this man?" They said, "No." He said:
"Will you accept the oath of fifty of the Jews that they did not kill him?"
They said, "They would not mind killing us all and then swearing." He said:
"Then will you claim the blood money on the oaths of fifty of you?"
They said, "We would not swear."
So he paid the blood money from himself.

I said, "Hudhayl had also disowned one of their outlaws in the Jāhiliyyah. He came by night to a household from Yemen in al-Baṭḥāʾ, and one of them woke to him and struck him with a sword and killed him.
Hudhayl came and seized the Yemeni and brought him to ʿUmar at the season [of Hajj], saying, 'He killed our companion.'
He said, 'They had disowned him.'
[ʿUmar] said, 'Let fifty of Hudhayl swear that they did not disown him.'
He said: Forty-nine men of them swore,
and a man of them came from Syria, and they asked him to swear, but he ransomed his oath from them for a thousand dirhams,
so they put another man in his place,
who was handed over to the brother of the slain man, and his hand was joined with his.
They said: The two set out, with the fifty who had sworn, until they were at Nakhlah,
when rain overtook them and they entered a cave in the mountain,
and the cave collapsed upon the fifty who had sworn, and they all died,
while the two companions escaped, and a rock pursued them and broke the leg of the brother of the slain man,
who lived a year and then died."
I said, "ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān also carried out retaliation on a man by the qasāmah, then regretted what he had done,
so he ordered the fifty who had sworn, and they were struck from the register and he exiled them to Syria."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He heard the Prophet ﷺ judged in the case of a miscarried fetus, and al-Mughīrah said, "I heard him judge in it with a slave, male or female, as a ghurrah."
[ʿUmar] said, "Bring someone who will testify with you to this." Muḥammad ibn Maslamah said, "I testify to the like of this from the Prophet ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿAlī
label: machine translation

segments_en: I set out with ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Khiyār.
When we reached Ḥimṣ, ʿUbaydullāh said to me, "Would you like to see Waḥshī so that we may ask him about the killing of Ḥamzah?" I said, "Yes."
Waḥshī was living in Ḥimṣ. We asked about him and were told, "There he is, in the shade of his palace, as if he were a water-skin."
He said: So we came until we stood a short distance from him, and we greeted him, and he returned the greeting.
He said: ʿUbaydullāh had wrapped his turban around his face,
so that Waḥshī could see nothing of him but his eyes and his feet.
ʿUbaydullāh said, "O Waḥshī, do you know me?" He looked at him and then said, "No, by Allah, except that I know that ʿAdī ibn al-Khiyār married a woman called Umm Qitāl bint Abī al-ʿĪṣ,
and she bore him a boy in Makkah,
and I was looking for a wet nurse for him.
I carried that boy along with his mother and handed him to her,
and it is as if I am looking at your feet."
He said: ʿUbaydullāh then uncovered his face and said, "Will you not tell us about the killing of Ḥamzah?" He said, "Yes.
Ḥamzah killed Ṭuʿaymah ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Khiyār at Badr,
so my master Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim said to me, 'If you kill Ḥamzah in revenge for my uncle, you are free.'"
He said: "So when the people set out in the year of ʿAynayn—ʿAynayn being a mountain opposite Uḥud,
with a valley between the two—I went out with the people to the battle.

When they had drawn up their ranks for battle, Sibāʿ came out and said, 'Is there any challenger?' Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib came out to him and said, 'O Sibāʿ, O son of Umm Anmār, the woman who cuts off [girls'] genitals,

do you oppose Allah and His Messenger ﷺ?' Then he charged at him, and he became like yesterday gone by." He said: "And I lay in wait for Ḥamzah beneath a rock, and when he came near me, I threw my spear at him,
and I drove it into his lower abdomen until it came out from between his hips." He said: "That was the last of him.
When the people returned, I returned with them and stayed in Makkah,
until Islam spread in it.
Then I went out to Aṭ-Ṭāʾif,
and they [the people of Aṭ-Ṭāʾif] sent a messenger to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
I was told that he does not harm envoys." He said: "So I went out with them until I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When he saw me he said, 'Are you Waḥshī?' I said, 'Yes.' He said,
'Did you kill Ḥamzah?'
I said, 'What happened is what has reached you.' He said,
'Can you keep your face out of my sight?'" He said: "So I left.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away and Musaylimah the Liar appeared, I said, 'I will go out to Musaylimah, perhaps I may kill him and so make up for Ḥamzah.'" He said: "So I went out with the people,
and what happened in his affair happened." He said: "Then there was a man standing in a breach of a wall,
like an ash-colored camel, with disheveled hair." He said: "So I threw my spear at him,
and I drove it between his breasts until it came out from between his shoulders." He said: "Then a man of the Anṣār leaped upon him
and struck him on the head with a sword."
ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Faḍl said: Sulaymān ibn Yasār informed me that he heard ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar say: A servant girl on top of a house said, "Alas, O Commander of the Faithful!
The black slave has killed him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [She said] to ʿUrwah, "O son of my sister, your fathers were among them—az-Zubayr and Abū Bakr.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ suffered what he suffered on the day of Uḥud,
and the polytheists turned away from him, he feared that they would return, so he said,
'Who will go after them?'
Seventy men of them responded,
and among them were Abū Bakr and az-Zubayr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We do not know of any tribe of the Arabs that had more martyrs and was more honored on the Day of Resurrection than the Anṣār.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to put two of the men slain at Uḥud together in one cloth, then say,
"Which of them knew more of the Qurʾān?"
When one was pointed out to him,
he would put him first in the grave, and he said,
"I will be a witness over these on the Day of Resurrection."
He ordered that they be buried with their blood,
and he did not pray over them, and they were not washed.
Abū al-Walīd said, from Shuʿbah,
from Ibn al-Munkadir,
who said: I heard Jābir say:
When my father was killed, I began to weep and to uncover the cloth from his face,
and the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ began to forbid me, but the Prophet ﷺ did not forbid me, and the Prophet ﷺ said,
"Do not weep for him," or, "Why do you weep for him?
The angels continued to shade him with their wings until he was lifted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The one who killed Khubayb was Abū Sirwaʿah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever drinks wine and becomes intoxicated, his prayer will not be accepted for forty mornings, and if he dies he will enter the Fire. If he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he returns and drinks and becomes intoxicated, his prayer will not be accepted for forty mornings, and if he dies he will enter the Fire. If he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he returns and drinks and becomes intoxicated, his prayer will not be accepted for forty mornings, and if he dies he will enter the Fire. If he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. But if he returns again, it will be a duty upon Allah to make him drink from the radghat al-khabāl on the Day of Resurrection."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is radghat al-khabāl?" He said:
"The discharge of the people of the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every intoxicant is forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every intoxicant is forbidden."
Ibn Mājah said: This is a hadith of the Egyptians.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every intoxicant is forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah commanded us to cover the vessel, to tie the waterskin, and to turn the vessel upside down.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade drinking from vessels of gold and silver, and he said:
"They are for them in this world, and they are for you in the Hereafter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade folding over the mouths of waterskins [to drink from them]. After the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had forbidden that, a man got up at night, went to a waterskin and folded its mouth over to drink, and a snake came out of it at him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought milk, with Ibn ʿAbbās on his right and Khālid ibn al-Walīd on his left. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Ibn ʿAbbās:
"Will you permit me to give Khālid a drink?"
Ibn ʿAbbās said, "I do not like to prefer anyone over myself with the leftover of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
So Ibn ʿAbbās took it and drank, and then Khālid drank.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you drinks, he should not breathe into the vessel. If he wants to drink again, he should move the vessel away from his mouth, then return to it if he wishes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us to drink lying on our stomachs, which is al-karaʿ, and he forbade us to scoop up water with one hand. He said:

"None of you should lap like a dog laps, and none should drink with one hand like the people with whom Allah was angry. And none should drink at night from a vessel until he has moved it, unless it is a covered vessel. Whoever drinks with his hand while able to use a vessel, wishing to be humble, Allah will record for him good deeds for the number of his fingers. That is the vessel of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, peace be upon them both, when he threw away the cup and said, 'Uff! This goes with the world.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We passed by a pool and began to drink from it directly with our mouths. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not drink with your mouths directly, but wash your hands, then drink from it, for there is no vessel better than the hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a glass cup from which he would drink.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣuhayb said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and in front of him were bread and dates. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Come closer and eat."
I began to eat from the dates, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"You eat dates while you have sore eyes?"
He said: I said, "I am chewing on the other side."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman of Quraysh called Kulthum narrated from ʿĀʾishah,
who said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Make use of the disliked yet beneficial talbīnah," meaning the broth.
She said: When any of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ family fell ill, the pot would not leave the fire until one of the two ends was reached,
meaning either he recovered or died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever licks honey three mornings each month will not be afflicted by any great calamity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Honey was given as a gift to the Prophet ﷺ, and it was divided among us, a lick for each. I took my lick, then said, "O Messenger of Allah, may I have another?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a man

from the people of Iraq said to him: "Ask ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr for me about a man who enters ihram for Hajj: when he circumambulates the House, is he released from ihram or not? If he tells you he is not released,
then say to him that a man says so." He said: So I asked him, and he said: "No one who enters ihram for Hajj is released except by completing the Hajj."
I said: "But a man used to say that."

He said: "What an evil thing he said!" Then the man confronted me and asked me, so I told him. He said: "Then say to him: a man used to report that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did that, and what of Asmāʾ and al-Zubayr, who did that?"
He said: So I came to him and mentioned that to him, and he said: "Who is this?" I said: "I do not know."
He said: "Then why does he not come to me himself to ask me? I think he is an Iraqi."
I said: "I do not know."

He said: "He has lied. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Hajj, and ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, informed me that the first thing he began with when he arrived in Makkah was that he performed ablution, then circumambulated the House. Then Abū Bakr performed Hajj, and the first thing he began with was circumambulating the House, and it was nothing else. Then ʿUmar did likewise. Then ʿUthmān performed Hajj, and I saw that the first thing he began with was circumambulating the House, and it was nothing else. Then Muʿāwiyah and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar. Then I performed Hajj with my father, al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, and the first thing he began with was circumambulating the House, and it was nothing else. Then I saw the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār doing that, and it was nothing else. Then the last one I saw do that was Ibn ʿUmar, and he did not turn it into an ʿUmrah. And here is Ibn ʿUmar among them; do they not ask him? Nor [did they ask] anyone of those who have passed. They used to begin with nothing, when they set their feet down, before circumambulating the House, and then they would not be released from ihram. I also saw my mother and my aunt when they arrived: they began with nothing before the House, circumambulating it, and then they were not released. My mother told me that she, her sister, al-Zubayr, and so-and-so and so-and-so came for an ʿUmrah, and when they touched the corner, they were released. And he has lied in what he mentioned of that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the first circumambulation, he would walk briskly for three rounds and walk normally for four,
and he would run in the bottom of the valley when he went between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.
I said to Nāfiʿ: "Did ʿAbdullāh walk when he reached the Yemeni corner?" He said: "No,
unless the crowd pressed him at the corner, for he would not leave it until he touched it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, while he was in Makkah and intended to leave,
and Umm Salamah had not yet circumambulated the House and wished to leave,
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"When the dawn prayer is called, circumambulate on your camel while the people are praying." So she did that,
and she did not pray until she had left."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and we pronounced the talbiyah for Hajj, and we arrived in Makkah on the fourth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah,
and the Prophet ﷺ commanded us to circumambulate the House and between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah,
and to make it an ʿUmrah and come out of ihram,
except for whoever had sacrificial animals with him. He said: None of us had a sacrificial animal except the Prophet ﷺ and Ṭalḥah.

ʿAlī came from Yemen with the sacrificial animal and said: "I have entered ihram with the same intention as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." The people said: "Shall we set out for Minā while our private parts are dripping?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If I had known beforehand what I came to know afterward, I would not have brought the sacrificial animals,
and if I did not have the sacrificial animals with me, I would have come out of ihram."
He said: Surāqah met him while he was stoning Jamrat al-ʿAqabah and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this for us specially?" He said:
"No, rather it is for all time."
He said: ʿĀʾishah had arrived in Makkah while menstruating,
so the Prophet ﷺ commanded her to perform all the rites,
except that she was not to circumambulate or pray until she was pure.
When they camped at al-Baṭḥāʾ, ʿĀʾishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, are you all going back with a Hajj and an ʿUmrah, while I go back with only a Hajj?"
He said: Then he commanded ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq to go with her to al-Tanʿīm,
and she performed an ʿUmrah in Dhū al-Ḥijjah after the days of Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr said:
"O Messenger of Allah, tell me about jihad and military expeditions." He said: "
O ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr,
if you fight patiently, seeking reward from Allah, Allah will raise you patiently, seeking reward;
and if you fight for show and for boasting of numbers, Allah will raise you showing off and boasting.
O ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr,
in whatever state you fight or are killed, Allah will raise you in that state."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When your brothers were struck at Uhud, Allah placed their souls inside green birds that go down to the rivers of Paradise,
eating of its fruits,
and take shelter in lanterns of gold hanging in the shade of the Throne.
When they found the goodness of their food, drink, and resting place, they said:
'Who will convey to our brothers about us that we are alive in Paradise, provided for, so that they will not lose interest in jihad and will not shrink back during war?' Allah, Glorified is He, said:
'I will convey it to them on your behalf.' He said:
So Allah revealed: {Do not think of those who were killed in the cause of Allah as dead}."
—to the end of the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to the Prophet ﷺ:
"Who will be in Paradise?" He said: "
The prophet is in Paradise,
the martyr is in Paradise,
the newborn child is in Paradise,
and the girl buried alive is in Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We entered upon Umm al-Dardāʾ while we were orphans, and she said:
"Rejoice, for I heard Abū al-Dardāʾ say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The martyr will intercede for seventy of his family members."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Dāwūd said: Aḥmad said:
Thus he said—meaning Ibn Wahb—and ʿAnbasah—meaning Ibn Khālid—both from Yūnus. Aḥmad said:
The correct [narrator] is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbdullāh, that Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ said:
On the day of Khaybar, my brother fought fiercely,
and his sword rebounded on him and killed him. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke about that, doubting him, saying:
"A man who died by his own weapon."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
He died striving, a fighter in the cause of Allah."
Ibn Shihāb said:
Then I asked a son of Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ, and he narrated to me from his father the like of that,
except that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
They are wrong. He died striving, a fighter in the cause of Allah, so he will have his reward twice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
We raided a clan of Juhaynah, and one of the Muslims pursued one of them, struck at him but missed and hit himself with the sword. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Your brother, O company of Muslims!"
The people rushed to him and found that he had died.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrapped him in his clothes and his blood, prayed over him, and buried him. They said:
"O Messenger of Allah, is he a martyr?" He said: "Yes,
and I am a witness for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Two [supplications] are not rejected,
or are seldom rejected:
supplication at the call to prayer,
and at the time of battle when they are engaged closely with one another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Take for yourselves every chestnut horse with a white blaze and white leg markings,
or a dark bay with a white blaze." Then he mentioned something similar.
Muḥammad—meaning Ibn Muhājir—said: I asked him:
"Why is the chestnut preferred?" He said:
"Because the Prophet ﷺ sent out a detachment, and the first one to come with the news of victory was the rider of a chestnut horse."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to call the female of horses a faras.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a camel whose back had become joined to its belly, and said: "
Fear Allah regarding these speechless animals. Ride them while they are fit, and eat them while they are fit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When we halted at a stopping place, we would not pray voluntary prayers until we had unloaded the saddles.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Keep horses tied [for the cause of Allah], and stroke their forelocks and their hindquarters," or he said, "their rumps." "
Put collars on them, but do not put bowstrings as collars on them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said about the bell: "The flute of the Devil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade riding the jallālah among camels, or drinking its milk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: To proceed: the Prophet ﷺ called our horses "the horses of Allah" when we were called to alarm, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command us, when we were alarmed, to keep together, and to be patient and calm, and when we fought
label: machine translation

segments_en: Measure your food, and you will be blessed in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Ibrāhīm made Makkah sacred and supplicated for its people, and I have made Madīnah sacred as Ibrāhīm made Makkah sacred, and I have supplicated for its ṣāʿ and its mudd twice what Ibrāhīm supplicated for the people of Makkah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, bless them in their measure,
and bless them in their ṣāʿ and their mudd."
He meant the people of Madīnah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should sell over the sale of another,
and do not go out to meet the goods [of caravans] until they are brought down to the market."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade the sale of fruit until it is good [for use],
and nothing of it is to be sold except for dinars and dirhams, except for the ʿarāyā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Abū az-Zinād about selling fruit
before its goodness appears,

and what was mentioned about that. He said: ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr used to narrate from Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathmah, from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: People used to buy and sell fruit before its goodness appeared. Then when the people harvested and the time came to settle their payments, the buyer would say, "The fruit has been afflicted by damān, it has been afflicted by qushām, it has been afflicted by murāḍ," [various] blights, which they would use as arguments. When their disputes before the Prophet ﷺ became many, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, as a piece of advice that he was giving:
"If you will not [stop], then do not sell the fruit until its goodness appears."
[He said this] because of the many disputes and disagreements among them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding the saying of the Most High: {Whoever is rich, let him abstain; and whoever is poor, let him eat in a fair manner}, she said: It was revealed concerning the guardian of an orphan, that he may take from the orphan's wealth, if he is in need, an amount in proportion to his work, in a fair manner.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the boundaries are set and the roads are divided, there is no right of preemption.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A woman without a husband has more right over herself than her guardian, and a virgin is to be asked for her permission regarding herself, and her permission is her silence."
This ḥadīth is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
Shuʿbah and Sufyān al-Thawrī also narrated this ḥadīth from Mālik ibn Anas.

Some people have used this ḥadīth as proof for the permissibility of marriage without a guardian, but there is nothing in this ḥadīth that supports what they argue, because it has been narrated through more than one route from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"There is no marriage without a guardian."
And so Ibn ʿAbbās gave his ruling after the Prophet ﷺ, saying: there is no marriage without a guardian.
The meaning of the saying of the Prophet ﷺ:
"A woman without a husband has more right over herself than her guardian,"

according to most of the people of knowledge, is that the guardian may not marry her off except with her consent and instruction. If he marries her off [without it], the marriage is annulled, based on the ḥadīth of Khansāʾ bint Khidhām, whose father married her off while she was previously married and she disliked that, so the Prophet ﷺ rejected his marriage contract.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The guardian has no say over a woman who was previously married, and an orphan girl is to be consulted, and her silence is her consent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: When ʿAlī, peace be upon him, married Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, may Allah be pleased with her, he wanted to consummate the marriage, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prevented him until he gave her something. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have nothing."
The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "Give her your coat of mail."
So he gave her his coat of mail, and then consummated the marriage with her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Jurayj said, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr,
that the Prophet ﷺ said:

"Any woman who is married on the basis of a dowry, a gift, or a promise before the marriage contract is concluded, it belongs to her. What is given after the marriage contract is concluded belongs to the one to whom it is given. The most deserving of what a man honors is his daughter or his sister."
The wording is that of ʿAbdullāh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do not beat the female servants of Allah."
Then ʿUmar came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the women have become bold against their husbands," so he permitted beating them.
So they were beaten, and many women went around visiting the family of Muḥammad ﷺ. When morning came, he said:
"Last night seventy women visited the family of Muḥammad, every woman complaining about her husband. Those are not the best among you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAlī:
"O ʿAlī, do not follow one glance with another, for the first is yours, but the second is not."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When one of you buys a female slave, let him say: 'O Allah, I ask You for her goodness and the goodness of the nature You have given her, and I seek refuge in You from her evil and the evil of the nature You have given her.' And let him pray for blessing. And when one of you buys a camel, let him take hold of the top of its hump, and pray for blessing, and say the same."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah has not made lawful anything more hateful to Him than divorce."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn
was asked about a man
who divorces his wife and then has relations with her, without having had witnesses to her divorce or to her taking her back. He said: "You divorced contrary to the Sunnah,
and you took her back contrary to the Sunnah. Have witnesses for her divorce and for her taking back, and do not repeat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She was married to Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out for the dawn prayer and found Ḥabībah bint Sahl at his door in the darkness. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Who is this?"
She said, "I am Ḥabībah bint Sahl, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "What is the matter with you?"
She said, "I and Thābit ibn Qays cannot [remain together],"
referring to her husband. When Thābit ibn Qays came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"This is Ḥabībah bint Sahl. She has mentioned what Allah willed that she mention."
Ḥabībah said, "O Messenger of Allah, everything he gave me is with me."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Thābit, "Take it from her."
So he took it from her, and she stayed with her family.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah,

that she said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on one of his journeys, until, when we were at al-Baydāʾ—or Dhāt al-Jaysh—a necklace of mine broke. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed to look for it, and the people stayed with him, though they were not at a water source and had no water with them. So the people came to Abū Bakr and said, "Do you not see what ʿĀʾishah has done? She has made the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the people with him stay, though they are not at a water source and have no water with them."

Then Abū Bakr came while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asleep with his head on my thigh. He said, "You have detained the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the people, though they are not at a water source and have no water with them."

She said: So Abū Bakr rebuked me and said what Allah willed him to say, and he began to poke my side with his hand. Nothing stopped me from moving except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lying on my thigh. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ slept until morning without there being any water. Then Allah revealed the verse of tayammum, and they performed tayammum.
Usayd ibn al-Ḥuḍayr—who was one of the chiefs—said, "This is not the first of your blessings, O family of Abū Bakr."
ʿĀʾishah said: Then we made the camel I had been riding rise, and we found the necklace beneath it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man became ritually impure through sexual impurity and came to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, and said, "I am in a state of sexual impurity and I could not find water."
He said, "Do not pray."

ʿAmmār said to him, "Do you not remember that we were in a detachment, and we became sexually impure and could not find water? As for you, you did not pray; as for me, I rolled in the dust and prayed. Then I came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said:
'It would have been enough for you...'"
And Shuʿbah struck the ground once with his palms, blew into them, then rubbed one against the other, then wiped his face with them.
Then ʿUmar said something, I do not know what it was.
He said, "If you wish, I will not narrate it."
And he mentioned something in this chain of transmission from Abū Mālik, and Salamah added: He said, "Rather, we will entrust to you what you have taken upon yourself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh while he was praying in a single garment, wrapped in it, with his cloak placed aside.
When he finished, we said, "O Abū ʿAbd Allāh, you pray while your cloak is placed aside?" He said, "Yes.
I wanted the ignorant ones like you to see me.
I saw the Prophet ﷺ pray like this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed eight rakʿahs in her house in the year of the Conquest, in a single garment, with its two ends crossed over each other.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fought at Khaybar. He said: We prayed the dawn prayer near it while it was still dark. Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ mounted, and Abū Ṭalḥah mounted, and I was riding behind Abū Ṭalḥah. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ rode swiftly through the lanes of Khaybar, and my knee was touching the thigh of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ. The garment slipped back from the thigh of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, and I saw the whiteness of the thigh of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ. When he entered the town, he said:
"Allah is the Greatest! Khaybar is ruined. Indeed, when we descend upon a people's courtyard, evil is the morning of those who were warned."
He said it three times. He said: The people had gone out to their work, and they said, "Muḥammad, by Allah!"
ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: Some of our companions said, "Muḥammad and the army!"
He said: We took it by force, and the captives were gathered. Then Diḥyah came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, give me a girl from among the captives." He said:
"Go and take a girl."

So he took Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy. Then a man came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Prophet of Allah, you gave Diḥyah Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy, the leader of Qurayẓah and al-Naḍīr; she is suitable only for you." He said, "Call him with her."
He said: So he came with her, and when the Prophet ﷺ looked at her, he said:
"Take another girl from among the captives."
He said: And he freed her and married her.

Thābit said to him, "O Abū Ḥamzah, what did he give her as dowry?" He said, "Herself; he freed her and married her." Then, when they were on the road, Umm Sulaym prepared her for him and presented her to him at night. So the Prophet ﷺ became a bridegroom in the morning, and he said:
"Whoever has anything, let him bring it."
He said: And he spread out a leather mat. He said: One man began to bring dried curds, another began to bring dates, and another began to bring ghee, and they mixed them into a ḥays.
And that was the wedding feast of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ never abandoned four rakʿahs before Ẓuhr and two rakʿahs before Fajr.
Most of the companions of Shuʿbah who narrated this hadith disagreed with him and did not mention Masrūq.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sahl ibn Ḥunayf and Qays ibn Saʿd were sitting in al-Qādisiyyah,
when a funeral procession passed by them, and they stood up.
It was said to them, "It is [the funeral] of one of the people of the land,"
that is, of the people under protection [dhimmah]. They said, "A funeral passed by the Prophet ﷺ and he stood up. It was said to him, 'It is the funeral of a Jew.' He said, 'Is it not a soul?'"
Abū Ḥamzah said, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr,
from Ibn Abī Laylā,
who said: I was with Qays and Sahl, may Allah be pleased with them both, and they said, "We were with the Prophet ﷺ."
Zakariyyā said, from ash-Shaʿbī, from Ibn Abī Laylā: Abū Masʿūd and Qays used to stand for a funeral.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ announced to us the death of an-Najāshī, the ruler of Abyssinia,
on the day he died, and said, "Seek forgiveness for your brother."
And from Ibn Shihāb,
who said: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab told me
that Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said that the Prophet ﷺ lined them up in rows at the prayer ground and pronounced the takbīr over him four times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever among you is able to shield himself from the Fire, even with half a date, let him do so."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [This was] read to him while I was listening,
and the wording is his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik told me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a dead sheep that had been given to a freed slave woman of Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said, "
Why did you not make use of its hide?"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, it is dead."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Only eating it has been made unlawful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
asked Ibn ʿUmar about touching the Black Stone,
and he said, "I saw the Prophet ﷺ touch it and kiss it."
The man said, "What if I am overpowered? What if I am crowded out?" Ibn ʿUmar said, "Leave 'what if' in Yemen! I saw the Prophet ﷺ touch it and kiss it."

He said: This is az-Zubayr ibn ʿArabī, from whom Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated. Az-Zubayr ibn ʿArabī was a Kūfan whose kunyah was Abū Salamah; he heard from Anas ibn Mālik and more than one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and Sufyān ath-Thawrī and more than one of the leading scholars narrated from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Numayr and Abū Kurayb, both from Ibn Fuḍayl
— Zuhayr said: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us — ʿUmārah narrated to us,
from Abū Zurʿah, from Abū
Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
O Allah, forgive those who shave their heads."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, and those who shorten [their hair]?" He said, "
O Allah, forgive those who shave their heads."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, and those who shorten?" He said, "
O Allah, forgive those who shave their heads."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, and those who shorten?" He said, "And those who shorten."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "

Beware of injustice, for injustice will be darknesses on the Day of Resurrection. And beware of stinginess, for stinginess destroyed those before you; it led them to shed their blood and to treat as lawful what was sacred to them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Sumayy,
from Abū Ṣāliḥ,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
While a man was walking along a road, he found a thorny branch on the road and removed it. Allah appreciated that from him and forgave him." And he said, "

There are five types of martyrs: the one who dies of plague, the one who dies of a stomach illness, the one who drowns, the one who is crushed by a collapsed structure, and the martyr in the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ prostrated, he held his arms apart [from his body] so much that if a lamb wanted to pass beneath his arms, it could have passed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray at night while I was beside him, and I was menstruating, wearing a woollen wrap, part of which was over him beside me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When one of you is in doubt about his prayer and does not know how many [units] he has prayed, three or four, let him discard the doubt and build upon what he is certain of, then perform two prostrations before giving the salutation. If he had prayed five, they make his prayer even; and if he had prayed the full four, they are a humiliation for Satan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the ʿAṣr prayer and gave the salutation after three units. Then he entered his house, and a man called al-Kharbāq, whose arms were long, stood up to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah..."
and he mentioned to him what he had done.
He came out angry, dragging his cloak, until he reached the people and said, "Is this man right?" They said, "Yes."
So he prayed one unit, then gave the salutation, then performed two prostrations, then gave the salutation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ sat in the prayer, he would place his hands on his knees and raise his right finger, the one next to the thumb, and supplicate with it, while his left hand was spread out upon his left knee.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He visited Anas ibn Mālik in his house in Basra when he had finished the Ẓuhr prayer, and his house was beside the mosque. When we went in to him, he said, "Have you prayed ʿAṣr?" We said, "No, we have only just finished Ẓuhr."
He said, "Then pray ʿAṣr."
He said: So we stood and prayed, and when we finished, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"That is the prayer of the hypocrite: he sits watching for the ʿAṣr prayer until, when the sun is between the two horns of Satan, he gets up and pecks out four [units], remembering Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in them only a little."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Zayd ibn Aslam,
from al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Ḥakīm,
from Abū Yūnus,

the freedman of ʿĀʾishah, that he said: ʿĀʾishah ordered me to write a copy of the Qurʾān for her, and she said, "When you reach this verse, let me know: {Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer}." When I reached it, I informed her, and she dictated to me: "Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, and the ʿAṣr prayer.
And stand before Allah devoutly obedient."
ʿĀʾishah said, "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While he was sitting with Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, Abū ʿAbdullāh, the son-in-law of Zayd ibn Zabbān, the freedman of the Juhaynah, passed by them. Nāfiʿ called him over, and he said: I heard Abū Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A prayer with the imam is better than twenty-five prayers that one prays alone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say: Whoever would be pleased to meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, tomorrow as a Muslim, let him guard these five prayers wherever the call is made for them. For Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prescribed for His Prophet ﷺ the ways of guidance, and these are among the ways of guidance. I do not think any of you but has a place in his house where he prays. If you were to pray in your houses and leave your mosques, you would be abandoning the Sunnah of your Prophet, and if you abandoned the Sunnah of your Prophet, you would go astray. There is no Muslim servant who performs ablution and does it well, then walks to a prayer, except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, records for him a good deed for every step he takes, or raises him a degree by it, or erases a sin from him by it. And we have seen ourselves taking short steps close together. And we have seen ourselves [at that time] when no one stayed away from it except a hypocrite whose hypocrisy was known. And I have seen a man being carried between two men until he was stood in the row.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"One of you remains in prayer as long as he is waiting for it, and the angels keep praying for one of you as long as he is in the mosque: 'O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy on him,' so long as he does not break his ablution."
A man from Ḥaḍramawt said, "What is breaking ablution, O Abū Hurayrah?" He said, "Passing wind, silently or audibly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ had prayed the Fajr prayer, he would sit cross-legged in his place until the sun rose beautifully.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to us and said:

"O company of the Emigrants, there are five things with which you may be tested, and I seek refuge in Allah that you should live to see them. Immorality never becomes widespread among a people to the point that they commit it openly, except that plague and ailments spread among them which were not known among their predecessors who passed before them.
They do not give short measure and weight, except that they are seized with years of famine, severe hardship, and the tyranny of the ruler over them.

They do not withhold the zakāh due on their wealth, except that rain is withheld from them from the sky, and were it not for the animals, they would not be given rain at all. They do not break the covenant of Allah and the covenant of His Messenger, except that Allah sets over them an enemy from other than themselves, who takes some of what is in their hands.
And as long as their leaders do not rule by the Book of Allah and pick and choose from what Allah has revealed, Allah will cause their strife to be among themselves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"{Allah curses them and those who curse [also] curse them}." He said: "[They are] the creatures of the earth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was suffering from fever. I placed my hand on him and felt his heat through the blanket over it. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how severe it is on you!" He said:
"That is how it is with us: our trial is doubled and our reward is doubled."
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the people are most severely tested?" He said: "The prophets."
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, then who?" He said:
"Then the righteous. One of them might be tested with poverty until he finds nothing but a cloak to wrap around himself, and one of them would rejoice in trial just as one of you rejoices in ease."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day Jibrīl, peace be upon him, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was sitting sad, stained with blood; some of the people of Makkah had struck him. He said: "What is wrong with you?" He said:
"These people did such-and-such to me."
He said: "Would you like me to show you a sign?" He said: "Yes, show me."
So he looked at a tree beyond the valley and said: "Call that tree."

He called it, and it came walking until it stood before him. He said: "Tell it to go back." So he told it, and it went back until it returned to its place. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "That is enough for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that on the night he was taken on the Night Journey he found a pleasant fragrance, and he said:
"O Jibrīl, what is this pleasant fragrance?" He said: "This is the fragrance of the grave of the hairdresser, her two children, and her husband.

He said: The beginning of that was that al-Khiḍr was from the nobles of the Children of Israel. His route passed by a monk in his hermitage, and the monk would look out at him and teach him Islam. When al-Khiḍr reached adulthood, his father married him to a woman. Al-Khiḍr taught her and took a pledge from her that she would not tell anyone about him. He did not approach women, so he divorced her. Then his father married him to another, and he taught her and took a pledge from her that she would not tell anyone about him. One of them kept it secret while the other disclosed it, so he left, fleeing, until he reached an island in the sea. Two men came to gather firewood and saw him. One of them kept it secret and the other disclosed it, saying: I have seen al-Khiḍr.

It was asked: Who saw him with you? He said: So-and-so. He was questioned and kept it secret. It was part of their religion that whoever lied was killed. He said: So al-Khiḍr married the woman who had kept the secret. Then, while she was combing the hair of Pharaoh's daughter, the comb fell, and she said: May Pharaoh perish!
She told her father. The woman had two sons and a husband. He sent for them and tried to persuade the woman and her husband to give up their religion, but they refused. He said: I will kill you both.

They said: As a kindness to us, if you kill us, place us in one house. He did so. Then when the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, he found a pleasant fragrance and asked Jibrīl, who informed him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nothing remains of this world except trial and tribulation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There will come upon the people years of deception, in which the liar will be believed and the truthful will be called a liar, the traitor will be trusted and the trustworthy will be accused of treachery, and the ruwaybiḍah will speak." It was asked: "What is the ruwaybiḍah?" He said: "The insignificant man who speaks on matters of public concern."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You will be sifted just as dates are sifted from their inferior ones; your best will surely depart and your worst will surely remain, so die if you are able."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was eating his morning meal, and he said, "Come closer and eat."
I said, "I am fasting." How I regret it! If only I had eaten from the food of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we used to eat bread and meat in the mosque.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ loved gourd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Sulaym sent me with a basket of fresh dates to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but I did not find him. He had gone out nearby to a freed slave of his who had invited him and made food for him, so I came to him while he was eating.
He said: He called me to eat with him.
He said: He had made a thareed of meat and gourd.
He said: I saw that he liked the gourd.

He said: I began gathering it and bringing it closer to him. When we had eaten from it, he returned to his house, and I set the basket before him. He began eating from it and distributing it until he had finished the last of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ in his house, and these gourds were with him. I said, "What is this?" He said,
"This is gourd, it is the dubbāʾ; we add more of it to our food."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The master of the food of the people of this world and the people of Paradise is meat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was never invited to meat except that he accepted, and meat was never given to him as a gift except that he accepted it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The best meat is the meat of the back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Never was leftover roasted meat taken away from before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and never was a cushion carried along with him ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We ate food with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the mosque, roasted meat. We wiped our hands on the pebbles, then stood, and he led the prayer without performing ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and spoke to him, and his shoulder muscles began to tremble. So he said to him,
"Take it easy, for I am not a king; I am only the son of a woman who ate dried meat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The master of your condiments is salt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"What an excellent condiment vinegar is."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"What an excellent condiment vinegar is."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon ʿĀʾishah while I was with her, and he said,
"Is there any morning meal?"
She said, "We have bread, dates, and vinegar."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"What an excellent condiment vinegar is. O Allah, bless vinegar, for it was the condiment of the prophets before me, and a house that has vinegar is never poor."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When milk was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would say,
"A blessing, or two blessings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My mother used to treat me to make me fatter, wanting to bring me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but it did not work for her until I ate cucumbers with fresh dates, and I became fat in the best way.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Eat unripe dates with ripe dates, and eat the old with the new, for Satan becomes angry and says, 'The son of Adam has lived on until he eats the old with the new.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: She sifted some flour and made a loaf of bread from it for the Prophet ﷺ, and he said, "What is this?"
She said, "It is food we prepare in our land, and I wanted to make a loaf from it for you." He said,
"Put it back into it, then knead it again."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never saw a loaf of fine white bread with either of his eyes until he met Allah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah visited his people in Bayna, and they brought him thin loaves of the kind made in earlier times. He wept and said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never saw this with his own eyes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Gabriel,

peace be upon him, came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "The earth will be opened up to your nation, and the world will be poured out upon them, until they will eat al-fālūdhaj." The Prophet ﷺ said, "What is al-fālūdhaj?"
He said, "They mix clarified butter and honey together."
So the Prophet ﷺ gasped at that with a deep gasp.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You will certainly follow the ways of those who came before you, span by span and cubit by cubit, until even if they entered a lizard's hole, you would enter it too."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews and the Christians?" He said, "Who else?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:

"Among those who came before you was a man who had killed ninety-nine people. He asked about the most knowledgeable person on earth and was directed to a monk. He came to him and said that he had killed ninety-nine people, and asked whether there was any repentance for him. The monk said, 'No.'
