So he killed him too and completed one hundred. Then he asked about the most knowledgeable person on earth and was directed to a learned man. He said that he had killed one hundred people, and asked whether there was any repentance for him. The man said, 'Yes. Who can stand between him and repentance? Go to such and such a land, for there are people there who worship Allah. Worship Allah with them, and do not return to your own land, for it is an evil land.'

So he set out, and when he had gone halfway, death came to him. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. The angels of mercy said, 'He came repenting, turning to Allah with his heart.'
The angels of punishment said, 'He never did any good at all.'
Then an angel in the form of a human being came to them, and they made him judge between them. He said, 'Measure the distance between the two lands; to whichever he was nearer, he belongs.'
So they measured, and found him nearer to the land he had intended, so the angels of mercy took him."
Qatādah said: Al-Ḥasan said, "It was mentioned to us that when death came to him, he drew himself forward with his chest."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A man bought a piece of land from another man, and the buyer found in the land a jar containing gold. The buyer said to the seller, 'Take your gold from me; I only bought the land from you, and did not buy the gold from you.'

The one who had sold the land said, 'I sold you the land and whatever is in it.' So they took their dispute to a man for judgment. The man they came to said, 'Do you have children?' One said, 'I have a boy,' and the other said, 'I have a girl.'
He said, 'Marry the boy to the girl, spend on yourselves from it, and give in charity.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh said, "It is as if I can see the Prophet ﷺ relating about one of the prophets whose people beat him and made him bleed,
as he wiped the blood from his face and said, 'My Lord, forgive my people,
for they do not know.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUqbah said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Among what people have preserved of the words of earlier prophethood is:
'If you have no shame, then do as you wish.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A man from among those before you went out in a fine garment of his, walking proudly in it. So Allah commanded the earth, and it seized him, and he will keep sinking in it until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān came to Madinah on the last visit he made,
and addressed us. He brought out a ball of hair and said, "I did not think anyone did this except the Jews,
and the Prophet ﷺ called it deceit," meaning attaching hair to hair.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Anṣār, Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Ghifār, Ashjaʿ, and those of the Banū ʿAbd al-Dār are allies; they have no ally besides Allah, and Allah and His Messenger are their ally."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Aslam, may Allah keep them safe, and Ghifār, may Allah forgive them. I did not say it myself; rather Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis

came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "Only the thieves of the pilgrims have pledged allegiance to you: Aslam, Ghifār, Muzaynah, and I think Juhaynah" (Muḥammad, the narrator, was unsure). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What do you think: if Aslam, Ghifār, Muzaynah, and I think Juhaynah, are better than Banū Tamīm, Banū ʿĀmir, Asad, and Ghaṭafān, have they failed and lost?" He said, "Yes." He said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, they are indeed better than them."
The report of Ibn Abī Shaybah does not include the words "Muḥammad, the narrator, was unsure."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with my father, in the time of Ibn al-Zubayr, beside ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, when ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn al-Zubayr said, "We have heard that he
would begin with the evening meal before the prayer."
So ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said, "Woe to you! What was their evening meal? Do you think it was like your father's evening meal?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came back from a mountain pass after relieving himself, and in front of us were dates on a shield or a small leather shield. We invited him, and he ate with us, and he did not touch water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting while a man was eating, and he did not say the name of Allah until nothing remained of his food except a morsel. When he raised it to his mouth, he said, "In the name of Allah, at its beginning and its end." The Prophet ﷺ laughed, then said:
"The devil kept eating with him, but when he mentioned the name of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, he vomited what was in his belly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I do not eat while reclining."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you eats food, let him not eat from the top of the dish, but let him eat from its lower part, for blessing descends upon its top."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not cut meat with a knife, for that is the practice of the non-Arabs. Rather, tear it with your teeth, for it is more wholesome and more easily digested."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was eating with the Prophet ﷺ, and I took the meat from the bone with my hand. He said:
"Bring the bone close to your mouth, for it is more wholesome and more easily digested."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The bones with meat most beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were the bones of the sheep.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a man of the people of Basra, from ʿIkrimah,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: The food most beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was tharīd made with bread and tharīd made with ḥays.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Khaybar we slaughtered horses, mules, and donkeys. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us from the mules and donkeys, but he did not forbid us from the horses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr was at al-Ṣifāḥ—Muḥammad said: in Makkah—and a man came with a hare he had hunted and said, "O ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, what do you say?" He said, "It was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while I was sitting. He did not eat it, and he did not forbid eating it," and he claimed that it menstruates.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade eating the meat of the dabb (spiny-tailed lizard).
label: machine translation

segments_en: I accompanied the Prophet ﷺ, and I never heard him declare the creeping creatures of the earth forbidden.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn ʿUmar when he was asked about eating the hedgehog.

He recited, "Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden..." the verse. An old man who was with him said, "I heard Abū Hurayrah say: It was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
'It is one of the filthy things.'"
Ibn ʿUmar said, "If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said this, then it is as he said, as long as we do not know otherwise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of the Jāhiliyyah used to eat some things and leave other things out of disgust. Then Allah the Exalted sent His Prophet, revealed His Book, made lawful what He made lawful, and made unlawful what He made unlawful. So what He made lawful is lawful, what He made unlawful is unlawful, and what He was silent about is pardoned. And he recited, "Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden..." to the end of the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the hyena, and he said:
"It is game, and a ram is [required as compensation] for it if a person in ihrām hunts it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:

"Beware! I have been given the Book and something like it along with it. Beware! A man replete with food, reclining on his couch, may soon say, 'Hold to this Qurʾān alone. Whatever you find in it to be lawful, treat as lawful, and whatever you find in it to be unlawful, treat as unlawful.' Beware! The meat of the domestic donkey is not lawful for you, nor any beast of prey with a fang, nor the lost property of a person under a covenant, unless its owner does without it. And whoever stays with a people, it is their duty to host him. If they do not host him, he may take from them the equivalent of his hospitality."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I fought with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Khaybar. The Jews came and complained that the people had rushed to their enclosures. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Beware! The property of those under a covenant is not lawful except by right. And forbidden to you are the domestic donkeys, and their horses, and their mules, and every beast of prey with a fang, and every bird with talons."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Companions of ʿAbdullāh came to Abū al-Dardāʾ, and he looked for them and found them. He said, "Which of you can recite to me according to the recitation of ʿAbdullāh?" They said, "All of us."
He said, "Then which of you has memorized it?" And they pointed to ʿAlqamah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ, and he mentioned the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was started was the true dream. Then the angel came to him and said: 'Recite in the name of your Lord who created; created man from a clinging substance. Recite, and your Lord is the Most Generous.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Prophet ﷺ returned to Khadījah and said, "Cover me, cover me." Then he mentioned the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is a river that was given to your Prophet ﷺ. Its two banks are of hollowed pearls, and its vessels are as numerous as the stars.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning al-Kawthar, he said: "It is the abundant good that Allah gave him."
Abū Bishr said: I said to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, "People claim that it is a river in Paradise."
Saʿīd said, "The river that is in Paradise is part of the good that Allah gave him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, asked them about the saying of the Exalted, "When the help of Allah and the conquest come." They said, "The conquest of the cities and the palaces." He said, "What do you say, Ibn ʿAbbās?" He said, "Indeed, or rather it is a parable set forth for Muḥammad ﷺ, in which his own death was announced to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the verse was revealed, "And warn your closest relatives," and your group among them who are sincere,
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out until he ascended aṣ-Ṣafā and cried out, "O morning danger!"
They said, "Who is this?" And they gathered to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. I said, "O Abū al-Mundhir, your brother Ibn Masʿūd says such and such."
Ubayy said, "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said to me, 'It was said to me,' and I said [it]."
He said, "So we say as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I learned "Glorify the name of your Lord" before the Prophet ﷺ arrived.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ died, and none had gathered the Qurʾān except four: Abū al-Dardāʾ, Muʿādh ibn Jabal, Zayd ibn Thābit, and Abū Zayd.
He said, "And we inherited it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever recites the two verses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
stood up in the time of the Prophet ﷺ reciting at the late pre-dawn hour "Say: He is Allah, the One," adding nothing to it.
When morning came, a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said something similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Shaddād ibn Maʿqil and I entered
upon Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both. Shaddād ibn Maʿqil said to him, "Did the Prophet ﷺ leave anything behind?" He said, "He left nothing except what is between the two covers."
He said: Then we entered upon Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah and asked him, and he said, "He left nothing except what is between the two covers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, what you call the mufaṣṣal is the muḥkam.
He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died when I was ten years old, and I had already recited the muḥkam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said to me,
"Recite the Qurʾān to me."
I said, "Shall I recite to you when it was revealed to you?" He said,
"I love to hear it from someone other than myself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Shubrumah said to me: I looked into how much of the Qurʾān is sufficient for a man, and I found no sūrah shorter than three verses.
So I said, "It is not proper for anyone to recite less than three verses."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to me,
"In how many [days] do you recite the Qurʾān?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yaḥyā [narrated] part of the hadith from ʿAmr ibn Murrah,
[who said]: The Prophet ﷺ said to me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said to me, "Have you married?" I said, "No."
He said, "Then marry, for the best of this Ummah are those with the most wives."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if you came down into a valley in which there was a tree from which something had been eaten,
and you found trees from which nothing had been eaten,
from which of them would you let your camel graze?" He said,
"From the one from which none has been grazed."
She means that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not marry any virgin other than her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ proposed for ʿĀʾishah to Abū Bakr, and Abū Bakr said to him, "I am only your brother." He said,
"You are my brother in the religion of Allah and His Book, and she is lawful for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us for one of the two evening prayers, carrying Ḥasan or Ḥusayn. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went forward and put him down, then said the takbīr for the prayer and prayed. In the course of his prayer he performed a prostration and made it long.

My father said: I raised my head, and there was the child on the back of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was prostrating, so I went back to my prostration. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, the people said: O Messenger of Allah, you performed a prostration in the middle of your prayer and made it so long that we thought something had happened or that you were receiving revelation. He said:
"None of that happened, but my son made me his mount, and I disliked hurrying him until he had finished what he wanted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayrith used to come to us and say: Shall I not tell you about the prayer of

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He would pray at a time other than the time of prayer. When he raised his head from the second prostration at the end of the first rakʿah, he sat upright, then stood up, leaning on the ground.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and saw him raise his hands when he began the prayer until they were level with his shoulders, and also when he wanted to bow. When he sat after two rakʿahs, he laid down his left foot and set up his right, placed his right hand on his right thigh, raised his finger for supplication, and placed his left hand on his left thigh.
He said: Then I came to them the following year and saw them raising their hands inside their hooded cloaks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat after two rakʿahs or after four, he would place his hands on his knees, then point with his finger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He would recite this tashahhud in the obligatory and the voluntary prayer, and he said: Abū Isḥāq narrated to us from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ from ʿAbdullāh from the Prophet ﷺ; and [by another chain] Manṣūr and Ḥammād narrated to us from Abū Wāʾil from ʿAbdullāh from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas ibn Mālik was asked about the takbīr
in prayer. He said: He would say the takbīr when he bowed, when he prostrated, when he raised his head from prostration, and when he stood up after two rakʿahs.
Ḥuṭaym said: From whom do you remember this? He said: From the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both. Then he fell silent.
Ḥuṭaym said to him: And ʿUthmān? He said: And ʿUthmān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He greeted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with salām while he was praying, and he returned the greeting to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When any of you is in prayer, let him not raise his gaze to the sky, lest his sight be snatched away."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had a time with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when I would come to him. When I came, I would ask permission if I found him praying, and if he cleared his throat I would enter; and if I found him free, he would permit me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī said to me: I had a standing with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that none of creation had. I would come to him every pre-dawn and say: Peace be upon you, O Prophet of Allah. If he cleared his throat, I would go back to my family; otherwise, I would enter to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was praying, and from his chest came a sound like the bubbling of a boiling pot, meaning he was weeping.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to come to the Prophet ﷺ while he was praying and greet him, and he would return my greeting. Then I came to him and greeted him while he was praying, and he did not return it. When he finished the prayer, he gestured to the people and said:

"Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has introduced a new ruling regarding prayer: that you do not speak in it except with the remembrance of Allah and what is fitting for you, and that you stand before Allah in devout obedience."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Salamah, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ibn Abī Ḥathmah, from Abū Hurayrah,
that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not perform a prostration that day, either before the salām or after it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ performed a prostration for his mistake after the salām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr prayer, then turned his face to them. They said: Has something new been decreed in the prayer? He said: "What is that?"
They told him what he had done, so he folded his leg and faced the qiblah, performed two prostrations, then said the salām. Then he turned his face to them and said:
"I am only a human being; I forget as you forget. So when I forget, remind me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They used to say: When a person is unsure, he should aim for what is correct, then perform two prostrations.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlqamah ibn Qays made a mistake in his prayer, and they reminded him after he had spoken. He said: Is that so, O one-eyed man? He said: Yes.
So he undid his wrap, then performed the two prostrations of forgetfulness and said: This is what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in one of the two evening prayers, either Ẓuhr or ʿAṣr. He said: He led us in two rakʿahs and then gave the salām. Then he stood up and went to a piece of wood at the front of the mosque and placed one hand over the other, and anger could be seen on his face. The hasty ones among the people went out, saying, "The prayer has been shortened! The prayer has been shortened!" Among the people were Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, but they were too awed to speak to him. Then a man whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to call Dhū al-Yadayn stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, have you forgotten, or has the prayer been shortened?" He said:
"I have not forgotten, and the prayer has not been shortened."
He said, "But you have forgotten, O Messenger of Allah."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to the people and said:
"Is Dhū al-Yadayn right?"

They gestured, meaning, "Yes." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went back to his place and prayed the two remaining rakʿahs, then gave the salām. Then he said the takbīr and prostrated like his usual prostration or longer, then raised his head and said the takbīr. Then he said the takbīr and prostrated like his usual prostration or longer, then raised his head and said the takbīr.

He said: Muḥammad was asked, "Did he give the salām after the prostrations of forgetfulness?" He said, "I did not memorize that from Abū Hurayrah, but I was informed that ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn said: Then he gave the salām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said — and in the narration of Bakr, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Tell me, if there were a river at the door of one of you, and he bathed in it five times every day, would any dirt remain on him?"
They said, "No dirt would remain on him." He said:
"That is like the five prayers; Allah erases sins by means of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Be moderate in prostration,
and do not stretch out your forearms like a dog.
If one spits, let him not spit in front of him or to his right,
for he is conversing privately with his Lord."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray ʿAṣr while the sun was still high and bright,
and someone would go to al-ʿAwālī and reach them while the sun was still high,
and some of al-ʿAwālī were about four miles from Madinah, or thereabouts.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do not let the Bedouins overcome you regarding the name of your prayer" — Ibn Ḥarmalah added — "for it is ʿIshāʾ; they only call it ʿAtamah because of their milking the camels late."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever says, when he hears the call to prayer: 'O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and the prayer that is established, grant Muḥammad the means of nearness and the excellence, and raise him to the praiseworthy station that You have promised him,' intercession will be permitted for him on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the prayer is called [iqāmah], do not stand until you see me."
And Ibn Ḥātim said:
"When the iqāmah is given or the call is made."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I spent a night at the house of Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith, my maternal aunt,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with her on her night. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood to pray during the night,
and I stood on his left. He said: So he took hold of my forelock and placed me on his right.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The imam is appointed only to be followed. So when he says the takbīr, say the takbīr; when he recites, be silent; when he says {not those who have earned anger, nor those who are astray}, say 'Āmīn'; when he bows, bow; and when he says 'Sami'a Allāhu liman ḥamidah,'
say 'Allāhumma rabbanā wa laka al-ḥamd'; when he prostrates, prostrate; and when he prays sitting, pray sitting, all of you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh
used to raise his hands when he began the prayer, and when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing he did likewise, and he would say: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do the same.
And Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭahmān raised his hands to his ears.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the takbīr in prayer, he would remain silent for a short while before reciting. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, tell me about your silence between the takbīr and the recitation, what do you say?" He said:

"I say: O Allah, put distance between me and my sins as You have put distance between the east and the west. O Allah, cleanse me of my sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt. O Allah, wash me of my sins with snow, water, and hail."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was not a liar: they used to pray behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when he raised his head from bowing, I did not see anyone bend his back until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had placed his forehead on the ground; then those behind him would fall down in prostration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My maternal aunt took me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my sister's son
is ill." So he wiped my head and prayed for blessing for me,
and he performed ablution, and I drank from the water of his ablution.
Then I stood behind his back and looked at the seal [of prophethood] between his shoulders.
Ibn ʿUbaydullāh said: Al-ḥajalah is from ḥajl al-faras, the white mark between the horse's eyes.
Ibrāhīm ibn Ḥamzah said: It was like the button of a bridal canopy.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among a group of riders, and I had a water container with me. He went out to relieve himself, then came back, and I met him with the water container and poured water over him. He washed his palms and his face, then wanted to bring his forearms out, and he was wearing a woolen cloak of the Roman kind with narrow sleeves, which was tight, so he drew them out from beneath it. Then I reached down to the two leather socks to take them off, but he said to me, "
Leave the socks, for I put my feet into them while they were clean." And he wiped over them.
My father said: ash-Shaʿbī said: ʿUrwah testified for me about his father, and his father testified about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ went to relieve himself, I would bring him water in a basin or a small waterskin, and he would clean himself with it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Mūsā used to be strict about urine and would urinate in a bottle. He would say, "When urine touched the skin of one of the Children of Israel, he would cut it off with scissors."

Ḥudhayfah said: I wish your companion were not so strict about this. I remember that I was walking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he came to a refuse dump behind a wall. He stood as one of you would stand and urinated. I moved away from him, but he signaled to me, so I came and stood by his heels until he had finished.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah,
what do you think about one of us when blood from menstruation gets on her garment,
what should she do?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
When blood from menstruation gets on the garment of one of you,
let her rub it, then sprinkle it with water,
then let her pray in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was prostrating—[Another chain:] Aḥmad ibn ʿUthmān told me: Sharīḥ ibn Maslamah told us: Ibrāhīm ibn Yūsuf told us, from his father, from Abū Isḥāq: ʿAmr ibn Maymūn told me that ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd narrated to him that the Prophet ﷺ was praying at the House,
and Abū Jahl and some companions of his were sitting.

Some of them said to others, "Which of you will bring the afterbirth of the slaughtered camel of the family of so-and-so and place it on the back of Muhammad when he prostrates?" The most wretched of the people got up and brought it.
He waited until the Prophet ﷺ prostrated, then placed it on his back between his shoulders, while I was watching,
unable to change anything,
for I had no protection.
He said: They began to laugh and to lean on one another [in mirth],
while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in prostration, not raising his head,
until Fāṭimah came
and removed it from his back.
Then he raised his head and said, "
O Allah, take care of Quraysh," three times.
It was hard on them that he invoked against them—he said: they used to believe that supplication in that city was answered—then he named them: "
O Allah, take care of Abū Jahl,
and ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah,
and Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah,
and al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah,
and Umayyah ibn Khalaf,
and ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ."
He also counted a seventh, but [the narrator] did not remember him. He said: By the One in whose hand is my soul,
I saw those whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had named lying dead in the well, the well of Badr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Every drink that intoxicates is forbidden."
Qutaybah said: from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went in to ʿĀʾishah, I and her brother
by milk-kinship, and he asked her about the Prophet's
ﷺ bath for sexual impurity. She called for a vessel about the size of a ṣāʿ and bathed, with a screen between us and her, and she poured water over her head three times.
He said: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ used to trim their hair until it was like a short lock.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jābir said to me, "Your cousin came to me"—alluding to al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah—"and asked, 'How is the bath for sexual impurity done?'" I said, "The Prophet ﷺ would take three handfuls and pour them over his head,
then pour water over the rest of his body."
Al-Ḥasan said to me, "I am a man with a lot of hair."
I said, "The Prophet ﷺ had more hair than you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays
asked al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr: "What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite on Friday after Sūrat al-Jumuʿah?" He said: "He used to recite: {Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming [event]?}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I attended the ʿĪd with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He led us in the ʿĪd prayer, then said:
"We have completed the prayer.
Whoever would like to sit for the sermon, let him sit,
and whoever would like to leave, let him leave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: The people disagreed about the last day of Ramadan, so two Bedouins came and testified before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, swearing by Allah, that they had sighted the new moon the previous evening. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the people to break their fast. Khalaf added in his narration: and to go out in the morning to their place of prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he saw the Prophet ﷺ praying for rain at Aḥjār al-Zayt, near al-Zawrāʾ, standing, supplicating and asking for rain, raising his hands in front of his face, not raising them above his head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He went out dragging his garment in alarm until he came to the mosque, and he kept praying with us until the eclipse cleared. When it had cleared, he said:

"Some people claim that the sun and the moon are eclipsed only because of the death of one of the great men. It is not so. The sun and the moon are not eclipsed for the death or life of anyone, but they are two signs among the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When something of His creation is manifested to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, it humbles itself before Him. So when you see that, pray as you would pray the most recent obligatory prayer you have prayed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which part of the night is most likely to be heard [by Allah]?" He said:

"The middle of the latter part of the night. So pray as much as you wish, for the prayer is witnessed and recorded, until you pray the morning prayer. Then refrain until the sun rises and climbs the height of a spear or two, for it rises between the two horns of a devil, and the disbelievers pray to it. Then pray as much as you wish, for the prayer is witnessed and recorded, until the spear stands without a shadow. Then refrain, for Hell is being fueled and its gates are opened. When the sun has passed its zenith, pray as much as you wish, for the prayer is witnessed until you pray the afternoon prayer. Then refrain until the sun sets, for it sets between the two horns of a devil, and the disbelievers pray to it."

And he related a long hadith. Al-ʿAbbās said: "This is how Abū Sallām narrated it to me from Abū Umāmah, unless I have made some mistake that I did not intend, so I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The prayer is two [rakʿahs] by two: that you recite the tashahhud after every two rakʿahs, that you show humility and neediness, that you raise your hands and say, 'O Allah, O Allah.' Whoever does not do that, his prayer is deficient."
Abū Dāwūd was asked about the night prayer being two by two. He said: "If you wish, two by two, and if you wish, four."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib:

"O ʿAbbās, O my uncle, shall I not give you, shall I not grant you, shall I not bestow upon you, shall I not do for you ten things which, if you do them, Allah will forgive your sin, the first of it and the last, the old and the new, the unintentional and the deliberate, the small and the great, the secret and the open? Ten things: that you pray four rakʿahs, reciting in each rakʿah Fātiḥat al-Kitāb and a sūrah. When you finish the recitation in the first rakʿah, while standing, say: 'Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest' fifteen times. Then bow and say it ten times while bowing. Then raise your head from the bowing and say it ten times. Then go down in prostration and say it ten times while prostrating. Then raise your head from the prostration and say it ten times. Then prostrate and say it ten times. Then raise your head and say it ten times. That is seventy-five in every rakʿah. Do that in the four rakʿahs. If you are able to pray it once every day, do so; if not, then once every week; if not, then once every month; if not, then once every year; and if not, then once in your lifetime."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the Maghrib prayer in the mosque of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal. When he had finished, some people stood up to pray voluntary prayers, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"You should pray this prayer [the voluntary prayers] in your homes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer,
and the one who drinks wine does not drink it while he is a believer,
and the thief does not steal while he is a believer,
and no one plunders something so that people raise their eyes to him because of it while he is a believer."
And from Ibn Shihāb,
from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and Abū
Salamah, from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, the same, except for the mention of plundering.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Khaybar, and then Allah gave them victory over it. When evening came on the day it was conquered, the people lit many fires. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What are these fires? What are you lighting them for?"
They said: "For meat." He said:
"What kind of meat?"
They said: "The meat of domestic donkeys."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Pour it out and break the pots."
A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, may we pour it out and wash them?" He said: "Or that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A partner of mine sold some dirhams in the market on credit, and I said, "Glory be to Allah! Is this permissible?" He said, "Glory be to Allah!
By Allah, I sold them in the market and no one found fault with it."
So I asked al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, and he said: The Prophet ﷺ arrived while we were engaged in this kind of sale, and he said:
"What is hand to hand, there is no harm in it,
but what is on credit is not permissible."
[He said:] "And meet Zayd ibn Arqam and ask him, for he was the greatest of us in trade."
So I asked Zayd ibn Arqam, and he said the same.
Sufyān said on another occasion: He said, "The Prophet ﷺ came to us in Medina while we were engaged in trade,"
and he said, "on credit until the season or Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among some people with me, he said: We, the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, declared the intention for Hajj alone, purely. ʿAṭāʾ said that Jābir said: The Prophet ﷺ arrived on the morning of the fourth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah and ordered us to leave the state of iḥrām.
ʿAṭāʾ said: He said:
"Leave iḥrām and have relations with your wives."
ʿAṭāʾ said: He did not make it obligatory upon them, but he made them lawful for them.
So we said: When there were only five days between us and ʿArafah, we were ordered to go to our wives, and then we would come to ʿArafah with our private parts dripping with semen.
He said: Jābir gestured with his hand, as if I can see him moving it. He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ stood among us and said:

"You know that I am the most God-fearing of you, the most truthful of you, and the most righteous of you. Were it not for my sacrificial animal, I would leave iḥrām as you do. And if I had known beforehand what I came to know afterward, I would not have brought the sacrificial animal. So leave iḥrām."
So we left iḥrām, and we heard and obeyed.
ʿAṭāʾ said that Jābir said: ʿAlī came back from his mission and he said: "With what intention did you enter iḥrām?"
He said: "With the same intention as the Prophet ﷺ."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Then offer a sacrifice and remain in iḥrām."
He said: ʿAlī offered a sacrificial animal for him. Surāqah ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this for this year of ours only, or forever?" He said: "Forever."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever throws himself down from a mountain and kills himself will be in the Fire of Hell, throwing himself down in it, abiding therein forever. Whoever drinks poison and kills himself, his poison will be in his hand, and he will sip it in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever. And whoever kills himself with a piece of iron—then the narrator broke off on something [and] Khālid said—his iron will be in his hand, and he will stab his belly with it in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah has cursed the woman who attaches hair [to another's] and the one who has it attached, and the woman who tattoos and the one who has herself tattooed."
Nāfiʿ said: The tattooing is on the gums.
He said: This is a good and sound (ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ) hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Then he mentioned a word meaning "from ʿAmrah, from ʿĀʾishah,"
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The hand is not to be cut off except for a quarter of a dinar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to bathe with a ṣāʿ and perform ablution with a mudd.
In the narration of Ibn Ḥajar, or he said: "and a mudd would purify him."
He said: He had grown old, and I did not trust his narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said. Transmitter switch: He said: Abū al-Ṭāhir and Ḥarmalah narrated to me,
both from Ibn Wahb,
the wording being Ḥarmalah's, who said: Yūnus informed me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
that ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr
narrated to him from ʿĀʾishah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever catches one prostration of the ʿAṣr prayer before the sun sets, or of the Fajr prayer before it rises, has caught it."
And the prostration is only the rakʿah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever catches one rakʿah of the prayer has caught the prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī,
from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you hear the call to prayer, say the same as what the muʾadhdhin says."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and Abū
Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, that both informed him from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the imam says āmīn, say āmīn, for whoever's saying of āmīn coincides with the angels' saying of āmīn will have his previous sins forgiven."
Ibn Shihāb said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say, "Āmīn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I listened,
the wording being his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
from Ibn al-Musayyab,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If you say to your companion, 'Be quiet,' while the imam is delivering the sermon, you have engaged in idle talk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and al-Muqaddamī,
and Abū Kāmil and Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd, all from Ḥammād,
Khalaf said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us,
from ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal,
from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sarjis,

who said: I saw the bald one, meaning ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, kissing the Stone and saying: By Allah, I am kissing you, and I know that you are only a stone and that you neither harm nor benefit. Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kiss you, I would not have kissed you.
In the narration of al-Muqaddamī and Abū Kāmil: I saw the little bald one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade muḥāqalah, muzābanah, mukhābarah and muʿāwamah. He said from Ḥammād: One of them said muʿāwamah and the other said the sale of years, then they agreed. And he forbade thunyā (exceptions in a sale), and he permitted the ʿarāyā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I listened, and the wording
is his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A wealthy person's delaying [payment of a debt] is injustice. And if one of you is referred to a wealthy person [to collect a debt], let him accept the referral."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah al-Anṣārī asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a ruling about a vow that his mother had owed,
and she died before fulfilling it.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Fulfil it on her behalf."
Some people said: When camels reach twenty,
four sheep are due on them.
If he gives them away before the year is complete, or sells them,
to escape and as a trick to avoid zakāh,
nothing is due from him,
and likewise if he destroys them and [then] dies,
nothing is due from his wealth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a man of the people of Basrah, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn:
That the Prophet ﷺ was asked about the even and the odd, and he said:
"It is the prayer: some of it is even and some of it is odd."
He said: This hadith is gharīb; we do not know it except from the hadith of Qatādah.
Khālid ibn Qays al-Ḥuddānī also narrated it from Qatādah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ in a cave, and his finger was wounded and bled, so the Prophet ﷺ said:
"You are nothing but a finger that has bled, and what you have met was in the cause of Allah."
He said: Jibrīl, peace be upon him, was delayed in coming to him, so the polytheists said, "Muhammad has been abandoned." So Allah, the Exalted, revealed:
"Your Lord has not abandoned you, nor has He detested you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from his people [reported] that the Prophet ﷺ said:

"While I was at the House, between sleep and wakefulness, I heard a speaker say, 'One of the three.' Then a golden basin containing Zamzam water was brought to me, and my chest was opened up to such and such a point."
Qatādah said: I said to Anas ibn Mālik, "What does he mean?" He said:
"To the bottom of my belly. My heart was taken out and washed with Zamzam water, then it was returned to its place, then it was filled with faith and wisdom."
There is a long story in the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was praying, and Abū Jahl came and said, "Did I not forbid you from this? Did I not forbid you from this? Did I not forbid you from this?" The Prophet ﷺ turned away and rebuked him sharply. Abū Jahl said, "You know that no one in it has a greater gathering than I." So Allah revealed:
"Let him call his gathering. We will call the guards of Hell." Ibn ʿAbbās said: By Allah, had he called his gathering, the guards of Allah would have seized him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man stood up to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī after he had pledged allegiance to Muʿāwiyah and said, "You have blackened the faces of the believers."
Or [he said], "O you who blackened the faces of the believers!"
He said: "Do not rebuke me, may Allah have mercy on you, for the Prophet ﷺ was shown the Banū Umayyah on his pulpit, and that distressed him, so there was revealed:
'Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar,' O Muhammad, meaning a river in Paradise; and there was revealed:

'Indeed, We sent it down on the Night of Decree. And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months,' [meaning] the Banū Umayyah will rule it after you, O Muhammad."
Al-Qāsim said: We counted it, and it was a thousand months, neither a day more nor a day less.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave until there was revealed:
"Competition in increase diverts you." Abū Kurayb said once, from ʿAmr ibn Abī Qays—he is from Rayy, while ʿAmr ibn Qays al-Mulāʾī is from Kūfah—from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed, the first thing about which a servant will be asked on the Day of Resurrection concerning the blessings is that it will be said to him: 'Did We not make your body healthy for you, and give you cold water to drink?'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The polytheists said] to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "Trace your Lord's lineage for us." So Allah revealed:

"Say: He is Allah, [who is] One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge." The Eternal Refuge is the One who neither begets nor is begotten, because nothing is born except that it will die, and nothing dies except that it will be inherited from, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not die and is not inherited from:
"Nor is there to Him any equivalent." He said:
"There is none like Him, nor any equal, and there is nothing like unto Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ mentioned their gods, and they said, "Trace your Lord's lineage for us."
He said: Then Jibrīl came to him with this sūrah:
"Say: He is Allah, [who is] One."

Then he mentioned something similar, but did not mention in it [the chain] from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. This is more authentic than the hadith of Abū Saʿd. Abū Saʿd's name is Muḥammad ibn Maysar; Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī's name is ʿĪsā; Abū al-ʿĀliyah's name is Rufayʿ, and he was a slave whom a Sabian woman freed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ looked at the moon and said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, seek refuge with Allah from the evil of this, for this is the darkness when it settles."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "There will not cease to be a group of my Ummah standing firm upon the command of Allah,
and those who forsake them or oppose them will not harm them, until the command of Allah comes while they are in that state."
ʿUmayr said: Mālik ibn Yukhāmir said: Muʿādh said, "And they are in ash-Shām."
Then Muʿāwiyah said: "This is Mālik, who claims that he heard Muʿādh say, 'And they are in ash-Shām.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said about the Anṣār: "
None loves them except a believer, and none hates them except a hypocrite. Whoever loves them, Allah loves him, and whoever hates them, Allah hates him."
Shuʿbah said: I asked ʿAdī, "Did you hear it from al-Barāʾ?" He said, "He narrated it to me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
from the Anṣār said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have appointed so-and-so to office but you have not appointed me."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
You will see after me favoritism [toward others], so be patient until you meet me at the Pond."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
The truest word a poet has spoken is the word of Labīd: 'Indeed, everything other than Allah is false.' And Umayyah ibn Abī aṣ-Ṣalt was almost a Muslim."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married me when I was six years old. Then we came to Madinah and stayed among the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj. I fell ill with a fever and my hair fell out until it became [only] a little tuft. Then my mother, Umm Rūmān, came to me while I was on a swing with some of my girlfriends. She called out to me, and I went to her, not knowing what she wanted. She took me by the hand and stood me at the door of the house, while I was panting, until my breathing calmed somewhat. Then she took some water and wiped my face and head with it. Then she brought me into the house, and there were women of the Anṣār in a room, who said, "With goodness and blessing, and with the best of fortune!"
She handed me over to them, and they got me ready. Nothing startled me except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ coming in the forenoon.
So she handed me over to him, and I was at that time nine years old.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh
died and left behind nine daughters, or he said seven, and I married a previously married woman. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "
O Jābir, have you married?"
I said, "Yes." He said: "
A virgin or a previously married woman?"
I said, "A previously married woman, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "
Why not a young girl, with whom you could play and who could play with you?" Or he said: "with whom you could laugh and who could laugh with you?"

I said to him, "ʿAbdullāh died and left nine daughters, or seven, and I disliked to bring them [a woman] like themselves, so I wanted to bring a woman who would take care of them and set them right." He said: "
May Allah bless you."
Or he said something good to me. In the narration of Abū ar-Rabīʿ: "
[a girl] you could play with and who could play with you, and laugh with and who could laugh with you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From one who prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Dhāt ar-Riqāʿ the prayer of fear: one group formed a row with him while another group faced the enemy. He prayed one rakʿah with those who were with him, then remained standing while they completed [the rest] for themselves. Then they left and formed a row facing the enemy, and the other group came, and he prayed with them the rakʿah that remained of his prayer. Then he remained sitting while they completed [the rest] for themselves, and then he ended the prayer with them with the salām.
Mālik said: The hadith of Yazīd ibn Rūmān is the one I like best of what I have heard.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Prophet ﷺ to Khaybar, and Allah gave us victory. We did not take gold or silver as spoils; we took goods, food, and clothing. Then we went on to the valley. With the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was a slave of his, whom a man from Judhām called Rifāʿah ibn Zayd of the Banū aḍ-Ḍubayb had given him. When we stopped in the valley, the slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up to unload his saddle, and he was struck by an arrow in which was his death. We said, "Congratulations to him on martyrdom, O Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
No! By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, the cloak is blazing as fire upon him; he took it from the spoils on the day of Khaybar before they were distributed."
He said: The people were alarmed.
Then a man came with one or two sandal straps.
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I got this on the day of Khaybar."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
A strap of fire, or two straps of fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said] to ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Umayyah: "O ʿAbdullāh, what do you think: if Allah gives you victory over aṭ-Ṭāʾif tomorrow, then [take] the daughter of Ghaylān,
for she approaches with four [folds] and departs with eight." And the Prophet ﷺ said: "
These [men] must not enter upon you."
Ibn ʿUyaynah said: Ibn Jurayj said: The effeminate man was Hīt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me while I had covered [a shelf] with a curtain that had a picture on it. His face changed colour, then he took hold of the curtain and tore it down. Then he said:
"Among the people who will be most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are those who imitate the creation of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The angels do not accompany a company of travellers in which there is a dog or a bell."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The bell is the musical instrument of the Shaytan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāʿim Abū ʿAbd Allāh,
the freed slave of Umm Salamah, narrated that he
heard Ibn ʿAbbās say:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a donkey that had been branded on the face, and he disapproved of that. He said, "By Allah, I will brand [an animal] only on the farthest part of the face."
Then he ordered that one of his own donkeys be branded on its haunches, so he was the first to brand the haunches.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw in the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the branding iron, and he was branding the camels of charity (ṣadaqah).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade qazaʿ.
He said: I asked Nāfiʿ, "What is qazaʿ?" He said, "Part of a boy's head is shaved and part is left."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ to the same effect.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sternly forbade a woman to attach anything to her hair.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day [Muʿāwiyah said]: "You have introduced an evil fashion, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ forbade deceit (zūr)."
He said: A man came with a stick that had a piece of cloth at its end. Muʿāwiyah said, "Indeed, this is deceit."
Qatādah said: He means what women add to their hair, of pieces of cloth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There are two types of the people of the Fire whom I have not seen: people who have whips like the tails of cattle with which they beat people, and women who are clothed yet naked, who go astray and lead others astray, their heads like the tilted humps of Bactrian camels. They will not enter Paradise and will not even smell its fragrance, though its fragrance can be detected from such and such a distance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: with the chain of transmission of Zuhayr.
As for the report of Jarīr and Rawḥ, it is like the report of Zuhayr, with his account.
As for the report of Shuʿbah, it contains only the mention of naming the boy, and it does not mention the four statements.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ wished to forbid naming [children] Yaʿlā, Barakah, Aflaḥ, Yasār, Nāfiʿ, and the like. Then I saw that he remained silent about them afterwards and said nothing. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away without having forbidden that. Then ʿUmar wished to forbid it, but then he left it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Juwayriyah's name was Barrah, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed her name to Juwayriyah. He disliked it being said, "He has come out from Barrah."
And in the report of Ibn Abī ʿUmar, from Kurayb, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās [say]
label: machine translation

segments_en: My name was Barrah, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named me Zaynab.
She said: Zaynab bint Jaḥsh came in to him, and her name was Barrah, so he named her Zaynab.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Fāṭimah bint al-Mundhir ibn al-Zubayr,

both said: Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr set out when she emigrated, while she was pregnant with ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr. She came to Qubāʾ and gave birth to ʿAbd Allāh at Qubāʾ. Then, after giving birth, she went out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that he might perform taḥnīk for him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took him from her and placed him in his lap. Then he called for a date. ʿĀʾishah said: We spent a while looking for it before we found it. He chewed it, then put his saliva into the baby's mouth, so the first thing to enter his stomach was the saliva of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then Asmāʾ said: Then he rubbed [the baby's palate], prayed for him, and named him ʿAbd Allāh. Then, when he was seven or eight years old, he came to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; his father al-Zubayr had commanded him to do so. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled when he saw him coming towards him, then accepted his pledge.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She emigrated to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while she was pregnant with ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr.
Then he mentioned [a report] like the report of Abū Usāmah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We brought ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr to the Prophet ﷺ so that he might perform taḥnīk for him. We looked for a date, but finding one was difficult for us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Abū Usāmah: Did ʿUbaydullāh narrate to you, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: A woman was found killed during one of the military expeditions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the killing of women and children.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, brought out to us a thick patched cloak and said: The soul of the Prophet ﷺ was taken in this.
Sulaymān added, from Ḥumayd, from Abū Burdah, who said: ʿĀʾishah brought out to us a coarse waist-wrapper of the kind made in Yemen,
and a cloak of the kind they call 'mulabbadah' (patched).
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he was praying when a son of Marwān passed in front of him. He tried to stop him, but the boy would not turn back, so he struck him. The boy went out crying until he came to Marwān and told him. Marwān said to Abū Saʿīd: Why did you strike your nephew? He said: I did not strike him; I only struck Satan. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"When one of you is praying and someone wants to pass in front of him, let him stop him as much as he can; if he refuses, let him fight him, for he is a devil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd
al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, that he heard Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān

in the year he performed Hajj, while he was on the pulpit, taking a lock of hair that was in the hand of a guard, say: O people of Madinah, where are your scholars? I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid the like of this, and he said:
"The Children of Israel were destroyed only when their women took up this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm,
the wording being ʿAmr's. ʿAmr and Qutaybah said: Sufyān narrated to us, and
Isḥāq said: Sufyān informed us,
from Ibn al-Munkadir, from Jābir,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me when I married: "Have you taken carpets?"
I said: How could we have carpets? He said:
"Indeed, you will have them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿīd said: There was a dispute between Khālid ibn al-Walīd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and Khālid insulted him. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not insult any of my Companions, for if one of you were to spend gold equal to Uḥud, it would not reach a mudd of one of them, nor even half of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met Abū Masʿūd at the House and said: A hadith has reached me from you about the two verses in Sūrat al-Baqarah. He said: Yes.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The two verses at the end of Sūrat al-Baqarah: whoever recites them in a night, they will suffice him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Khaybar the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us from eating the meat of donkeys and commanded us to eat the meat of horses. ʿAmr said: I told this report to Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ, and he said: Al-Ḥakam al-Ghifārī used to say this among us, but that great ocean refused it, meaning Ibn ʿAbbās.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Jurayj said: The verse {O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you} was revealed concerning ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥudhāfah ibn Qays ibn ʿAdī al-Sahmī, whom the Prophet ﷺ sent out in a military detachment.
Yaʿlā ibn Muslim informed me of it, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah has cursed women who tattoo and women who have themselves tattooed,

Muḥammad said: and women who attach hair extensions; ʿUthmān said: and women who pluck their eyebrows; then they agreed: and women who file their teeth for beauty, altering the creation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
This reached a woman of Banū Asad called Umm Yaʿqūb.
ʿUthmān added: she used to recite the Qurʾān. Then they agreed: She came to him and said: It has reached me that you have cursed women who tattoo and women who have themselves tattooed,

Muḥammad said: and women who attach hair extensions; ʿUthmān said: and women who pluck their eyebrows; then they agreed: and women who file their teeth. ʿUthmān said: for beauty, altering the creation of Allah, the Exalted.

He said: Why should I not curse those whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed, when it is in the Book of Allah, the Exalted? She said: I have read what is between the two covers of the Muṣḥaf and have not found it.

He said: By Allah, if you had read it, you would have found it. Then he recited: {And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it.} She said: I see some of this on your wife.
He said: Then go in and look.
She went in, then came out. He said: What did you see? ʿUthmān said: She said: I saw nothing.
He said: If that were the case, she would not be with us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he wrote to him, from Abū Salamah,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A woman is not to be married together with her paternal aunt, nor together with her maternal aunt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Do not say the tathwīb in any of the prayers except in the Fajr prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: None should call the adhān except one who is in a state of wudūʾ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said: None should call to prayer except one who is in a state of wudūʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the night he was taken on the Night Journey, fifty prayers were made obligatory upon the Prophet ﷺ. Then they were reduced until they were made five. Then he was called: "O Muhammad, the Word is not changed with Me, and for these five you will have [the reward of] fifty."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] who fasts by day and stands in prayer by night, but does not attend the Friday prayer or the congregational prayer; he said: He is in the Fire.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished praying, and he said:
"Which of you will do a profitable deed with this man?"
So a man stood up and prayed with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us that when we were three, one of us should go forward to lead us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The key to prayer is purification, its consecration is the takbīr, and its release is the taslīm. There is no prayer for the one who does not recite the Opening [Sūrah al-Fātiḥah]
and a sūrah, in an obligatory prayer or otherwise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the takbīr for prayer, he would spread his fingers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever prays for Allah forty days in congregation, catching the first takbīr, two exemptions will be recorded for him: an exemption from the Fire and an exemption from hypocrisy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to begin his prayer with "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ḥumayd al-Sāʿidī's name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿd ibn al-Mundhir.
Abū Usayd al-Sāʿidī's name is Mālik ibn Rabīʿah.
Abū Ḥuṣayn's name is ʿUthmān ibn ʿĀṣim al-Asadī.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī's name is ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥabīb.
Abū Yaʿfūr is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUbayd ibn Nisṭās.
Abū Yaʿfūr al-ʿAbdī's name is Wāqid, and it is said Waqdān, and he is the one who narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā.
Both of them were from the people of Kūfah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ḥumayd, Abū Usayd, Sahl ibn Saʿd and Muḥammad ibn Maslamah gathered and mentioned the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Abū Ḥumayd said: I am the most knowledgeable of you about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed, he placed his hands on his knees as though grasping them, and he drew his hands taut, keeping them away from his sides.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ prostrated, he pressed his nose and forehead firmly to the ground, kept his hands away from his sides, and placed his palms in line with his shoulders.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib: Where did the Prophet ﷺ place his face when he prostrated? He said: Between his palms.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ commanded placing the hands [on the ground] and setting the feet upright.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was such that his bowing, his rising from bowing, his prostrating, and his rising from prostration were nearly equal in duration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to rise in prayer on the fronts of his feet.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] among ten of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, among them Abū Qatādah ibn Ribʿī. He then mentioned a report similar in meaning to the hadith of Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, and Abū ʿĀṣim, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jaʿfar, added this phrase: They said, "You have spoken truly; this is how the Prophet ﷺ prayed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever prays a rakʿah in which he does not recite the Mother of the Qurʾān has not prayed, unless he is behind the imām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When he entered, he would say:
"My Lord, open for me the door of Your mercy," and when he left, he would say, "My Lord, open for me the door of Your bounty."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he forbade reciting poetry aloud in the mosque, buying and selling in it, and people sitting in circles in it on Friday before the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the prayer is called, do not come to it hurrying, but come to it walking, with tranquility upon you. Pray what you catch, and complete what you miss."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed on a mat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ liked to pray in walled gardens.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was riding behind al-Faḍl on a she-donkey, and we arrived while the Prophet ﷺ was leading his Companions in prayer at Minā.
He said: So we dismounted from it and joined the row, and it passed in front of them, and it did not break their prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They were bowing in the dawn prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"The best supplication is the supplication on the Day of ʿArafah, and the best that I and the prophets before me have said is: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise, and He has power over all things.'"
He said: This hadith is hasan gharīb from this chain.
Ḥammād ibn Abī Ḥumayd is Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥumayd, and he is Abū Ibrāhīm al-Anṣārī al-Madanī, and he is not strong according to the scholars of hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me, saying:

"Say: 'O Allah, make my inner self better than my outward appearance, and make my outward appearance righteous. O Allah, I ask You for the good of what You give people of wealth, family, and children, [provided they are] not astray and not leading others astray.'"
He said: This hadith is gharīb; we do not know it except from this chain, and its chain is not strong.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was praying. He had placed his left hand on his left thigh and his right hand on his right thigh, and he had closed his fingers and extended the index finger, and he was saying:
"O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He said to me: "O Muḥammad, when you are in pain, place your hand where you feel the pain and say: 'In the name of Allah. I seek refuge in the might of Allah and His power from the evil of what I feel of this pain of mine.' Then lift your hand, then repeat that an odd number of times. For Anas ibn Mālik narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated that to him."
He said: This hadith is hasan gharīb from this chain, and this Muḥammad ibn Sālim is a shaykh from Basra.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No servant ever says 'There is no god but Allah' sincerely, except that the gates of the heaven are opened for him until it reaches the Throne, so long as he avoids the major sins."
He said: This hadith is hasan gharīb from this chain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from evil character, deeds, and desires."
He said: This hadith is hasan gharīb.
Ziyād ibn ʿIlāqah's paternal uncle is Quṭbah ibn Mālik, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The mufarridūn have taken the lead."
They said: "Who are the mufarridūn, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Those who are devoted to the remembrance of Allah. The remembrance removes their burdens from them, so they come on the Day of Resurrection light."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever says in the evening three times: 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created,' no poisonous sting will harm him that night."
Suhayl said: Our family learned it and used to say it every night, and a girl of theirs was stung but she felt no pain from it.
This hadith is hasan.

Mālik ibn Anas narrated this hadith from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ. ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and more than one other narrated this hadith from Suhayl and did not mention in it "from Abū Hurayrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [This is] a supplication I memorized from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I never leave it:
"O Allah, make me one who thanks You abundantly, remembers You often, follows Your counsel, and preserves Your instruction."
This hadith is gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no man who supplicates to Allah with a supplication except that it is answered for him: either it is hastened for him in this world, or it is stored up for him in the Hereafter, or some of his sins are expiated in proportion to his supplication, so long as he does not supplicate for something sinful or for severing family ties, or become impatient."
They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how does one become impatient?" He said:
"He says: 'I supplicated to my Lord, but He has not answered me.'"
This hadith is gharīb from this chain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let each of you consider what he wishes for, for he does not know what will be written for him of his wish."
This hadith is hasan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate, saying:
"O Allah, let me enjoy my hearing and my sight, and make them my inheritors. Grant me victory over whoever wrongs me, and take my revenge from him for me."
This hadith is hasan gharīb from this chain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let each of you ask his Lord for all of his needs, even for the strap of his sandal when it breaks."
This hadith is gharīb.
More than one narrator reported this hadith from Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from the Prophet ﷺ.
They did not mention in it "from Anas."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāfiʿ ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥārith
met ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb at ʿUsfān—ʿUmar had appointed him over Makkah—and ʿUmar said, "Whom have you left in charge of the people of the valley?" He said, "I left Ibn Abzā in charge of them."
He said, "And who is Ibn Abzā?" He said, "A man from among our freed slaves."
ʿUmar said, "You have left a freed slave in charge of them?" He said, "He is a reciter of the Book of Allah, the Exalted, knowledgeable in the laws of inheritance, and a judge."
ʿUmar said, "Indeed, your Prophet ﷺ said:
'Indeed, Allah raises some people by this Book and lowers others by it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man called Nahīk ibn Sinān came to ʿAbdullāh and said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, how do you recite this word: is it with an alif or a yāʾ—'min māʾin ghayri āsin' or 'min māʾin ghayri yāsin'?" ʿAbdullāh said, "Have you counted all of the Qurʾān except this?" He said, "I recite the Mufaṣṣal in a single rakʿah."

ʿAbdullāh said, "[That is] a hurried recitation like the reciting of poetry. There are people who recite the Qurʾān but it does not go beyond their collarbones; rather, when it settles in the heart and takes root there, it benefits. The best of prayer is bowing and prostration. I know the similar surahs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pair, two surahs in each rakʿah."
Then ʿAbdullāh stood up and ʿAlqamah went in after him, then came out and said, "He has told me of them."
Ibn Numayr said in his narration: A man from Banū Bajīlah came to ʿAbdullāh, and he did not say Nahīk ibn Sinān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to Syria and Abū al-Dardāʾ came to us and said, "Is there anyone among you who recites according to the recitation of ʿAbdullāh?" He said: They pointed to me, so I said, "Yes, I do."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the rim of the sun appears, delay the prayer until it has fully risen; and when the rim of the sun disappears, delay the prayer until it has fully set."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the ʿAṣr prayer at al-Mukhammaṣ and said:

"This prayer was presented to those before you, but they neglected it. Whoever preserves it will have his reward twice over. And there is no prayer after it until the shāhid appears." The shāhid is the star.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qutaybah,
and ʿAlī ibn Ḥujr,
Ibn Ayyūb said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
—he is Ibn Jaʿfar—Muḥammad informed me,
—he is Ibn Abī Ḥarmalah—he said: Abū Salamah informed me,
that he asked ʿĀʾishah about the two prostrations [two rakʿahs],

that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray after ʿAṣr. She said, "He used to pray them before ʿAṣr, then he became occupied from them, or forgot them, so he prayed them after ʿAṣr. Then he made them permanent, and whenever he prayed a prayer, he made it permanent."
Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb said: Ismāʿīl said, "She means he kept doing it regularly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Anas ibn Mālik about voluntary prayer
after ʿAṣr. He said, "ʿUmar used to strike hands [to stop people] from praying after ʿAṣr, and we used to pray two rakʿahs at the time of the Prophet ﷺ after sunset, before the Maghrib prayer."
I said to him, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray them?" He said, "He used to see us praying them,
and he neither commanded us nor forbade us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the fear prayer on one of his days. One group stood with him while another group faced the enemy. He prayed one rakʿah with those who were with him, then they left and the others came, and he prayed one rakʿah with them. Then each of the two groups completed one more rakʿah. He said: Ibn ʿUmar said, "If the fear is greater than that, then pray riding or standing, gesturing with signs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I witnessed the fear prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We formed two rows, one row behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with the enemy between us and the qiblah. The Prophet ﷺ said the takbīr and we all said the takbīr. Then he bowed and we all bowed. Then he raised his head from bowing and we all raised ours. Then he went down to prostration, together with the row nearest him, while the rear row stood facing the enemy. When the Prophet ﷺ finished the prostration and the row nearest him stood up, the rear row went down to prostration and then stood. Then the rear row advanced and the front row moved back. Then the Prophet ﷺ bowed and we all bowed. Then he raised his head from bowing and we all raised ours. Then he went down to prostration, together with the row nearest him, which had been the rear row in the first rakʿah, while the rear row stood facing the enemy. When the Prophet ﷺ and the row nearest him finished the prostration, the rear row went down to prostration and prostrated. Then the Prophet ﷺ gave the salām and we all gave the salām.
Jābir said, "Just as these guards of yours do with their commanders."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They say that Abū Hurayrah narrates too many hadith. Allah is the One with whom we will meet.
And they say, "Why do the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār not narrate hadith like his?" Yet my brothers among the Muhājirūn were occupied with trading in the markets,
and my brothers among the Anṣār were occupied with tending their wealth,
while I was a poor man who stayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the sake of [filling] my stomach,
so I was present when they were absent, and I remembered when they forgot.
One day the Prophet ﷺ said,
"None of you will spread out his garment until I finish this saying of mine,
and then gather it to his chest,
and forget anything of what I say."
