So I spread out a striped cloak I had, and I had no other garment,
until the Prophet ﷺ finished his speech,
then I gathered it to my chest.
By the One who sent him with the truth, I have not forgotten anything of that speech of his to this day.

By Allah, were it not for two verses in the Book of Allah, I would never have narrated anything to you: {Indeed, those who conceal what We sent down of clear proofs} up to His saying {the Most Merciful}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I hear many things from you but I do not remember them." He said, "Spread out your cloak."
So I spread it out, and he narrated a great deal, and I did not forget anything he told me.
This is a good, sound hadith, and it has been narrated through more than one route from Abū Hurayrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ, with Muʿādh ibn Jabal riding behind him on the saddle, said, "O Muʿādh!"
He replied, "At your service, O Messenger of Allah, and at your pleasure." He said, "O Muʿādh!"
He replied, "At your service, O Messenger of Allah, and at your pleasure." He said, "O Muʿādh!"
He replied, "At your service, O Messenger of Allah, and at your pleasure." He said,
"There is no servant who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, except that Allah forbids him from the Fire."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, should I not tell the people so that they may rejoice?" He said, "Then they would rely on it."
So Muʿādh told it at the time of his death, to avoid sin [of concealing knowledge].
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Abū Hurayrah performing ablution. He washed his face and completed the ablution, then washed his right arm until he reached the upper arm, then his left arm until he reached the upper arm, then wiped his head, then washed his right foot until he reached the shin, then his left foot until he reached the shin. Then he said, "This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution."
And he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"You will be those with shining faces and limbs on the Day of Resurrection because of the completeness of ablution. So whoever among you can lengthen his shining brow and limbs, let him do so."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ slept until he breathed heavily, then prayed (or he may have said: he lay down until he breathed heavily), then he got up and prayed.
Then Sufyān narrated it to us time after time from ʿAmr, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: I spent a night at the house of my maternal aunt Maymūnah,
and the Prophet ﷺ got up during the night.
When it was part of the night, the Prophet ﷺ got up and performed a light ablution from a hanging water-skin (ʿAmr made it light and few), and stood to pray. So I performed ablution similarly,
then I came and stood on his left (Sufyān sometimes said: on his left side), and he turned me around and placed me on his right.
Then he prayed as much as Allah willed, then lay down,
and slept until he breathed heavily.
Then the caller came to him and informed him of the prayer,
so he got up with him for the prayer,
and he prayed without performing ablution.
We said to ʿAmr, "Some people say that the eyes of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sleep but his heart does not sleep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He performed ablution and washed his face.
Then he took a handful of water,
rinsed his mouth and sniffed water into his nose with it.
Then he took a handful of water,
and did like this with it,
joining it to his other hand,
and washed his face with both.
Then he took a handful of water
and washed his right arm with it.
Then he took a handful of water
and washed his left arm with it.
Then he wiped his head.
Then he took a handful of water and sprinkled it on his right foot until he had washed it,
then he took another handful
and washed his foot with it, meaning the left. Then he said, "This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ went to the toilet, and I placed water for ablution for him. When he came out, he said,
"Who put this?"
In the narration of Zuhayr: they said.
In the narration of Abū Bakr: I said, "Ibn ʿAbbās." He said, "O Allah, grant him understanding of the religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Shaddād said: The two who had sworn the oath of mutual imprecation were mentioned in the presence of Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ibn Shaddād said: Are they the two about whom the Prophet ﷺ said: "
If I were to stone anyone without clear proof, I would have stoned her."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: No, that was a woman who made her [misconduct] public.
Ibn Abī ʿUmar said in his narration, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās [say this].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ said: "
If a man were to look into your house without permission, and you struck him with a pebble and put out his eye,
there would be no blame on you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: O Messenger of Allah, will we be held accountable for what we did in the pre-Islamic period of ignorance? He said: "
Whoever among you does good in Islam will not be held accountable for it, and whoever does evil will be held accountable for his deeds in both the pre-Islamic period and Islam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A good dream is from Allah and a bad dream is from Satan. So if one of you sees something he dislikes, let him spit lightly to his left three times and seek refuge [with Allah] from its evil, and it will not harm him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The dream of a righteous Muslim man is one of seventy parts of prophethood."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Messengership and prophethood have come to an end, so there will be no messenger after me and no prophet."
He said: That was hard on the people, so he said: "But there are the glad tidings."
They said: O Messenger of Allah, what are the glad tidings? He said: "
The dream of a Muslim, and it is one of the parts of prophethood."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw in a dream as if in my hand was a piece of brocade, and I did not point it toward any place in Paradise except that it flew me to it. I told it to Ḥafṣah, and Ḥafṣah told it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "
Your brother is a righteous man," or [he said]: "
ʿAbdullāh is a righteous man."
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
I saw a black woman with disheveled hair going out of Madinah until she stood at Mahyaʿah, which is al-Juḥfah, and I interpreted it to mean that the plague of Madinah would be moved to al-Juḥfah."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he commanded a man who was giving arrows as charity in the mosque not to pass by with them except while holding their heads [arrowheads].
Ibn Rumḥ said: He used to give arrows as charity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with my weapon during the nights of the turmoil, and Abū Bakrah met me and said: Where are you going? I said: I want to help the cousin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When two Muslims confront each other with their swords, both of them are among the people of the Fire."
It was said: This is the killer,
but what about the one killed? He said: "
He intended to kill his companion."

Ḥammād ibn Zayd said: I mentioned this hadith to Ayyūb and Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd, wanting them to narrate it to me, and they said: This hadith was only narrated by al-Ḥasan, from al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays, from Abū Bakrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

By the One in whose Hand is my soul, the world will not pass away until a man passes by a grave and rolls upon it, and says: I wish I were in the place of the occupant of this grave, and it is not religion that drives him, but affliction."
label: machine translation

segments_en: No one asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the Dajjāl more than I asked him about him, and he said to me: "
My son, what troubles you about him? He will never harm you."
He said: I said: They claim that he will have rivers of water and mountains of bread. He said: "
He is more insignificant to Allah than that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥudhayfah and Abū Masʿūd met, and Ḥudhayfah said: "

I know better than he what the Dajjāl will have with him: he will have a river of water and a river of fire. What you see as fire is water, and what you see as water is fire. So whoever among you reaches that and wants water, let him drink from what he sees as fire, for he will find it to be water."
Abū Masʿūd said: This is how I heard the Prophet ﷺ say.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah used to narrate that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "

Whatever I have forbidden you, avoid it, and whatever I have commanded you, do of it what you are able. Those before you were destroyed only by their many questions and their disagreeing with their prophets."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The greatest offender among the Muslims against the Muslims is the one who asks about something that was not forbidden to the Muslims, and it is made forbidden to them because of his asking."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We saw nothing wrong with sharecropping until I heard Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it.
I mentioned that to Ṭāwūs, and he said: Ibn ʿAbbās told me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not forbid it, but he said:
"For one of you to lend his land [freely] is better than for him to take a fixed rent for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to rent out land in return for the crops that grew by the water channels and what was watered by the flow of the streams. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us from that and commanded us to rent it out for gold or silver.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [This is] similar to the chain of transmission of ʿUbayd Allāh and his narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Rāfiʿ came to us from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has forbidden us a matter that used to be of benefit to us, but obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger is of more benefit to us. He forbade us from any of us cultivating land unless he owns the land itself, or [land] that a man lends to him as a gift.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My uncle sent me, along with a boy of his,
to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab. We said to him: Something has reached us from you about sharecropping.

He said: Ibn ʿUmar saw nothing wrong with it until a report reached him from Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj. He went to him, and Rāfiʿ informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Banū Ḥārithah and saw crops in the land of Ẓuhayr. He said:
"How good are Ẓuhayr's crops!"
They said: They are not Ẓuhayr's. He said:
"Is it not the land of Ẓuhayr?"
They said: Yes, but it is the crop of so-and-so. He said:
"Take your crops and return to him his expenses."
Rāfiʿ said: So we took our crops and returned his expenses to him.
Saʿīd said: Lend [the land] to your brother, or rent it out for dirhams.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was an orphan under the guardianship of Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj, and I performed Hajj with him. My brother ʿImrān ibn Sahl came to him and said: We rented out such-and-such land of ours for two hundred dirhams. He said: Leave it, for the Prophet ﷺ forbade renting out land.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He cultivated some land, and the Prophet ﷺ passed by him while he was watering it, and asked him:
"Whose is the crop, and whose is the land?"
He said: The crop is mine, from my seed and my labor; I have half, and the sons of so-and-so have half. He said:
"You have both engaged in usury. Return the land to its owners and take back your expenses."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever does not give up sharecropping (mukhābarah), let him be notified of war from Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade mukhābarah.
I said: What is mukhābarah? He said: That you take the land for a half, a third, or a quarter [of its produce].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah gave Khaybar to His Messenger as spoils, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept them [the people] as they were and made [the land] shared between him and them. Then he sent ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah, who estimated [the yield of] it for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Rawāḥah estimated it at forty thousand wasqs, and he claimed that when Ibn Rawāḥah gave the Jews the choice, they took the fruit and were responsible for twenty thousand wasqs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It is] similar to this report, and the first is more complete. I said: What do you think of it, O Messenger of Allah? He said:
"An ember between your shoulders that you have hung around your neck." Or: "that you have hung on yourself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He passed by a people, and they came to him and said: You have come from this man with good, so recite a ruqyah for this man of ours.

They brought a man who was mentally disturbed, in shackles, and he recited over him Umm al-Qurʾān [al-Fātiḥah] for three days, morning and evening. Each time he finished it, he gathered his spittle and then spat, and it was as if he had been released from a rope. They gave him something, and he came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned it to him. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Eat. By my life, whoever eats by means of a false ruqyah [is at fault]; but you have eaten by means of a true ruqyah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Rāfiʿ ibn Rifāʿah came to a gathering of the Anṣār and said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ forbade us today from [several] things, and he mentioned them. He forbade us from the earnings of a female slave, except what she earns with her own hands.
And he gestured thus with his fingers, [meaning] such as baking bread, spinning, and carding wool.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A boy's ear was cut—or my ear was cut. Then Abū Bakr came to us on Hajj, and we gathered to him, and we brought the matter before ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. ʿUmar said: This [boy] has reached the age for retaliation. Call a cupper for me so that retaliation may be taken from him. When the cupper was called, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"I gave my maternal aunt a boy as a gift, hoping that she would be blessed in him. I said to her: Do not hand him over to a cupper, nor a goldsmith, nor a butcher."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with the story of the slave; and from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the story of the date palms.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not artificially bid up prices against one another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The night prayer is two [units] by two, and the Witr is one rakʿah."
I said: "What if sleep overcomes me? What if I fall asleep?" He said: "Make 'what if' be at that star."
So I raised my head, and there was as-Simāk. Then he repeated and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The night prayer is two [units] by two,
and the Witr is one rakʿah before the dawn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man asked Ibn ʿUmar, saying: "How should I pray Witr?" He said: "Pray Witr with one [rakʿah]."
The man said: "I fear that people will say it is the 'truncated' prayer." He said: "It is the Sunnah of Allah and His Messenger."
He meant: this is the Sunnah of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When you supplicate to Allah, supplicate with the palms of your hands and not with the backs of them. And when you have finished, wipe your faces with them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray Witr and make qunūt before bowing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He was asked] about the dawn prayer, and he said: "We used to make qunūt before bowing and after it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Anas ibn Mālik about qunūt,
and he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made qunūt after bowing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray two rakʿahs when travelling.
He did not add to them.
And he would pray tahajjud at night.
I said: "And did he pray Witr?" He said: "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Ibn ʿAbbās and] ʿUmar both said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ established the travel prayer as two rakʿahs; they are complete, not shortened. And Witr while travelling is a Sunnah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray Witr with one [rakʿah].
Then he would pray two rakʿahs, reciting in them while sitting.
And when he wanted to bow, he would stand and bow.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never found, or came upon, the Prophet ﷺ in the last part of the night except that he was sleeping at my place.
Wakīʿ said: "She means after the Witr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abū Bakr: "
At what time do you pray Witr?"
He said: "At the beginning of the night, after the ʿatamah." He said: "
And you, ʿUmar?"
He said: "At the end of the night." The Prophet ﷺ said: "
As for you, Abū Bakr, you have taken hold of the most trustworthy handhold; and as for you, ʿUmar, you have taken hold of strength."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If one of you is in doubt between two and one, let him make it one; if he is in doubt between two and three, let him make it two; and if he is in doubt between three and four, let him make it three. Then let him complete what remains of his prayer, so that the doubt falls on the extra. Then let him perform two prostrations while sitting before he gives the salām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Satan comes to one of you during his prayer,
and comes between him and his own self, until he does not know whether he has added or omitted.
When that happens,
let him perform two prostrations before he gives the salām, and then give the salām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ went out to the prayer and said the takbīr, then gestured to them [to stay], so they remained. Then he went off and washed, his head dripping with water, and led them in prayer. When he finished, he said: "
I came out to you in a state of janābah,
and I forgot until I had stood in the prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Whoever is afflicted by vomiting, a nosebleed, regurgitation, or prostatic fluid [madhy], let him leave, perform ablution,
and then build upon his prayer,
provided that he does not speak during that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ pray sitting on his right side while he was in pain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: By the One who took his soul ﷺ, he did not die until most of his prayer was performed sitting. And the most beloved of deeds to him was the righteous deed that a servant keeps up, even if it is small.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by him while he was praying sitting, and said: "
The prayer of one sitting is half the prayer of one standing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and saw people praying sitting, and said: "
The prayer of one sitting is half the prayer of one standing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Ḥunayn. We marched on a scorching day of intense heat, and we stopped in the shade of a tree. When the sun had passed its zenith, I put on my armor, mounted my horse, and went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in his tent. I said, "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. The time to depart has come." He said, "Yes." Then he said,
"O Bilāl, get up."
So he sprang up from beneath an acacia tree whose shade was like the shade of a bird, and said, "At your service, at your pleasure, and I am your ransom!" He said,
"Saddle the horse for me."
So he brought out a saddle whose two sides were of palm fiber, with no arrogance or showiness in it. He mounted, and we mounted. And he narrated the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed, and Abū Bakr or ʿUmar said to him, "May Allah keep you smiling." And he narrated the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me while my mother and I were plastering a wall of ours with mud, and he said,
"What is this, O ʿAbdullāh?"
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, it is something I am repairing." He said,
"The matter [of death] is swifter than that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and saw a lofty domed building. He said, "What is this?"
His Companions said to him, "This belongs to so-and-so," a man from the Anṣār.

He said: He remained silent and kept it in himself. Then when its owner came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and greeted him among the people, he turned away from him. He did this several times, until the man recognized the anger and the turning away directed at him. He complained of that to his Companions, saying, "By Allah, I perceive a change in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
They said, "He came out and saw your dome."
He said: So the man went back to his dome and tore it down until he leveled it with the ground. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day and did not see it. He said,
"What happened to the dome?"
They said, "Its owner complained to us of your turning away from him, so we told him, and he tore it down." He said,
"Indeed, every building is a burden on its owner, except what is necessary, except what is necessary."
meaning: what is indispensable.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him for food, and he said,
"O ʿUmar, go and give them [some]."
So he took us up to an upper room, took the key from the fold of his garment, and opened it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever cuts down a lote tree, Allah will plunge his head into the Fire."

Abū Dāwūd was asked about the meaning of this hadith and said: This hadith is abridged. It means: whoever cuts down a lote tree in an open desert, in which travelers and animals take shade, wantonly and wrongfully without right, Allah will plunge his head into the Fire for it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Hishām ibn ʿUrwah about cutting down lote trees,

while he was leaning against the palace of ʿUrwah. He said, "Do you see these doors and panels? They are only from the lote wood of ʿUrwah. ʿUrwah used to cut it from his land," and he said, "There is no harm in it."

Ḥumayd added: He said, "Is it so, O Iraqi? You have come to me with an innovation!" I said, "The innovation is only from your side. I heard someone in Makkah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed whoever cuts down lote trees."
Then he narrated its meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the human being there are three hundred and sixty joints, and he must give charity (ṣadaqah) on behalf of each joint."
They said, "And who is able to do that, O Prophet of Allah?" He said,
"Phlegm in the mosque, which you bury, and something which you remove from the road. And if you cannot find [that], then two rakʿahs of the forenoon prayer will suffice you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A mouse came and began dragging the wick, and it brought it and threw it in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ onto the mat on which he was sitting, and it burned a spot the size of a dirham. Then he said,
"When you sleep, put out your lamps, for the Devil guides the like of this to this and it burns you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The hadith is traced back, as I think, to Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever leaves the snakes alone out of fear of [retaliation for] killing them is not one of us. We have not made peace with them since we fought them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: To the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "We want to clean out Zamzam, and there are some of these jinn-snakes in it," meaning small snakes. So the Prophet ﷺ commanded that they be killed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed Ibn ʿUmar,
after that, meaning after Abū Lubābah had narrated to him, found a snake in his house and commanded that it be taken out, meaning to al-Baqīʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In this hadith Nāfiʿ said: Then I saw it afterward in his house.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, when will the Hour come?" The Prophet ﷺ stood up for prayer, and when he had finished his prayer, he said,
"Where is the one who asked about the Hour?"
The man said, "I am, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"What have you prepared for it?"
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have not prepared for it much prayer or fasting, except that I love Allah and His Messenger."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"A person is with those whom he loves, and you are with those whom you love."
I never saw the Muslims rejoice after Islam as they rejoiced at this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"None of you should say 'karm' for grapes.
Rather, the karm is the Muslim man."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah loves sneezing and dislikes yawning.
So when one of you sneezes and praises Allah, it is a right upon every Muslim who hears him to say to him, 'May Allah have mercy on you.'
As for yawning, it is only from Satan.
So when one of you yawns, let him suppress it as much as he can,
for when one of you yawns, Satan laughs at him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The rider should greet the one walking, the one walking should greet the one sitting, and the few should greet the many."
Ibn al-Muthannā added in his narration:
"And the young should greet the old."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

looked in through one of the rooms of the Prophet ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up and went toward him with an arrowhead or arrowheads. [The narrator] said: It is as if I can see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stalking him in order to stab him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in the mosque one day—Rifāʿah said, "and we were with him"—a man like a Bedouin came in and prayed, and he prayed briefly. Then he left and greeted the Prophet ﷺ with salām, and the Prophet ﷺ said,
"And upon you. Go back and pray, for you have not prayed."
So he went back and prayed, then came and greeted him, and he said,
"And upon you. Go back and pray, for you have not prayed."
He did that twice or three times, each time coming to the Prophet ﷺ and greeting him, and the Prophet ﷺ would say,
"And upon you. Go back and pray, for you have not prayed."

The people became afraid, and it weighed heavily on them that one who prayed briefly had not prayed. At the end of that, the man said, "Show me and teach me, for I am only a human being; I get things right and I make mistakes." So he said,

"Yes. When you stand up for prayer, perform ablution as Allah has commanded you, then recite the testimony of faith and the iqāmah. If you have some Qur'an with you, recite it; if not, praise Allah, declare His greatness, and declare that there is no god but Him. Then bow and be at ease in bowing, then stand upright, then prostrate and be at ease in prostration, then sit and be at ease sitting, then stand. When you do that, your prayer is complete, and if you reduce anything from it, you have reduced from your prayer."
He said: This was easier for them than the first, [for it meant] that whoever reduced something of that would have reduced from his prayer, but it would not be entirely lost.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A house in Medina burned down over its occupants during the night. When the matter of those people was reported to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said,
"This fire is only an enemy to you, so when you go to sleep, extinguish it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If Allah wills, from Abū Hurayrah,
he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge from these three: the reaching of misery, the gloating of enemies, the evil of what is decreed, and the hardship of trial.
Sufyān said: It is three, yet I mentioned four, because I do not remember the one that is not among them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two old women of the old women of the Jews of Medina came to me and said that the people of the graves are punished in their graves.

She said: I denied them, and I did not feel comfortable believing them. They left, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me. I said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, two old women of the old women of the Jews of Medina came to me and claimed that the people of the graves are punished in their graves." He said,
"They spoke the truth. They are punished with a punishment that the animals hear."
She said: After that I never saw him in any prayer without his seeking refuge from the punishment of the grave.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to sleep lying across,
in the direction of the qiblah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray while I was in front of him. When he wished to pray the Witr,
ʿUthmān added: he would nudge me. Then both narrators agreed [on the rest], and he said: "Move aside."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were discussing what interrupts the prayer in the presence of Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: I came, along with a boy from the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, on a donkey while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying. He dismounted and I dismounted, and we left the donkey in front of the row, and he paid it no heed. Then two girls from the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib came and passed between the row, and he paid that no heed either.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us while we were in our desert dwelling, and with him was ʿAbbās. He prayed in an open plain with no sutrah in front of him, while a she-donkey of ours and a bitch were playing in front of him, and he paid that no heed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A young man of Quraysh passed in front of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī while he was praying, so he pushed him away. The man came back, and he pushed him away three times. When he finished, he said: Nothing interrupts the prayer, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Repel [anyone who passes] as much as you can, for he is a devil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was a boy who did not understand my father's prayer. He said: Then Wāʾil ibn ʿAlqamah narrated to me from Wāʾil ibn Ḥujr, who said: I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When he said the takbīr, he raised his hands. He said: Then he wrapped himself in his garment, then took hold of his left hand with his right and put his hands inside his garment. He said: When he wished to bow, he brought his hands out and raised them; and when he wished to raise his head from bowing, he raised his hands. Then he prostrated and placed his face between his palms. And when he raised his head from prostration, he also raised his hands, until he finished his prayer.
Muḥammad said: I mentioned that to al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan, and he said: It is the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; whoever did it did it, and whoever left it left it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw the Prophet ﷺ, when he stood for prayer, raise his hands until they were level with his shoulders, with his thumbs level with his ears, and then he said the takbīr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ, when he began the prayer, raise his hands level with his ears. He said: Then I came to them [later] and saw them raising their hands to their chests at the start of the prayer, while they were wearing hooded cloaks and heavy garments.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ in winter and saw his Companions raising their hands inside their garments in prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in a gathering of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they were discussing the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Abū Ḥumayd said, and he mentioned part of this hadith: When he bowed, he set his palms firmly on his knees and spread his fingers apart, then bent his back, neither lowering his head nor raising it, nor turning his cheek aside. He said: When he sat after two rakʿahs, he sat on the sole of his left foot and kept the right upright. In the fourth, he pressed his left hip to the ground and brought both feet out on one side.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Similar to this. He said: When he prostrated, he placed his hands neither spread out nor clenched, and he faced the qiblah with the tips of his fingers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the Banū Mālik, from ʿAbbās,

or ʿAyyāsh, ibn Sahl al-Sāʿidī, that he was in a gathering in which was his father, who was one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and in the gathering were Abū Hurayrah, Abū Ḥumayd al-Sāʿidī and Abū Usayd, with this report, with slight additions or omissions. He said in it: Then he raised his head, meaning from bowing, and said:
"Sami'a Allāhu liman ḥamidah. O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs all praise."
And he raised his hands, then said: "Allah is the Greatest."

Then he prostrated, resting on his palms, his knees and the fronts of his feet while prostrating. Then he said the takbīr and sat, resting on his hip and keeping the other foot upright. Then he said the takbīr and prostrated, then said the takbīr and stood up without sitting on his hip. Then he went on with the hadith. He said: Then he sat after the two rakʿahs, until when he wished to rise to stand, he stood with a takbīr, then prayed the last two rakʿahs. He did not mention sitting on the hip in the tashahhud.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ in this hadith, he said: When he prostrated, his knees reached the ground before his palms did. He said: When he prostrated, he placed his forehead between his palms and kept his arms away from his sides.

Ḥajjāj said: Hammām said, Shaqīq narrated to us, ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb narrated to me from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of this. In the hadith of one of the two, and I think most likely it is the hadith of Muḥammad ibn Juḥādah: When he rose, he rose on his knees and leaned on his thighs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reciting the talbiyah, saying:

"Labbayk Allāhumma labbayk, labbayk lā sharīka laka labbayk. Innal-ḥamda wan-niʿmata laka wal-mulk, lā sharīka lak (Here I am, O Allah, here I am; here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Indeed all praise and favor are Yours, and the dominion; You have no partner)."

And ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray two units of prayer at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, then when his she-camel stood upright with him at the mosque of Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, he would begin the talbiyah with these words.
label: machine translation

segments_en: During the Hajj of the Prophet ﷺ, when he came to Dhū al-Ḥulayfah he prayed, and he remained silent until he reached al-Baydāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Isḥāq, and Mālik ibn Anas, from al-Maqburī,
from ʿUbayd ibn Jurayj,
who said: I said to Ibn ʿUmar, "I saw you begin the talbiyah when your she-camel stood upright."
He said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would begin the talbiyah when his she-camel stood upright and set off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed nine years without performing Hajj. Then he announced to the people that he would perform Hajj, and no one who was able to come, riding or on foot, remained behind but that he came. The people hurried to set out with him until he came to Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, where Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays gave birth to Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr. She sent word to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Wash yourself, bind [your private area] with a cloth, then begin the talbiyah." So she did so. [Abridged]
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ marked his sacrificial camels.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ marked his sacrificial camels on the right side, and he wiped the blood off them, and marked them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to send sheep as sacrificial offerings.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When they were present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Medina, he would send the sacrificial animals; whoever wished would enter iḥrām, and whoever wished would not.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ drove sacrificial animals on his Hajj.

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, do you see this ʿUmrah of ours: is it for this year only, or for all time?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "It is for all time."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Surāqah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed tamattuʿ and we performed it with him. We said, "Is it for us alone, or for all time?" He said, "Rather, for all time."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah, and his Companions entered iḥrām for Hajj. He commanded whoever did not have sacrificial animals with him to leave iḥrām. Among those who did not have sacrificial animals with them were Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh and another man, so they left iḥrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I was listening,
and the wording is his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd,
who said: Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥārith informed me,
from ʿĪsā ibn Ṭalḥah,
from ʿUmayr ibn Salamah al-Ḍamrī,
that he informed him from al-Bahzī,

that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out intending Makkah while in iḥrām, until, when they were at ar-Rawḥāʾ, there was a wounded wild donkey. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Leave it, for its owner will soon come."
Then al-Bahzī, who was its owner, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the donkey is yours to deal with as you wish."

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Abū Bakr, who divided it among the companions. Then he went on until, when he was at al-Uthāyah between ar-Ruwaythah and al-ʿArj, there was a resting antelope in the shade with an arrow in it. He claimed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded a man to stand by it so that no one would disturb it until they had passed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They were on a journey, some of them in iḥrām and some not. He said: I saw a wild donkey, so I mounted my horse and took my spear. I asked them for help, but they refused to help me, so I snatched a whip from one of them, charged at the donkey and struck it down. They ate from it, then felt apprehensive. He said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about that, and he said:
"Did you point it out or help?" They said, "No." He said, "Then eat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
entered upon ʿĀʾishah with a staff in her hand and said, "What is this?" She said, "This is for the gecko, because the Prophet of Allah ﷺ told us:
'There was nothing that fanned the fire against Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, except this creature.'
So he commanded us to kill it, and he forbade killing snakes, except the one with two stripes and the tailless one, for those two destroy eyesight and cause miscarriage."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married while in iḥrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped while in iḥrām.

segments_en: The example of the Muslims, the Jews, and the Christians is like that of a man who hired some people to work for him from morning until night for a known wage.
They worked for him until midday, then said, "We have no need of your wage that you stipulated for us,
and what we have done is worthless."
He said to them, "Do not do that. Complete the rest of your work,
and take your full wage." But they refused and left.
Then he hired two other workers after them and said to them, "Complete the rest of this day of yours,
and you will have the wage that I stipulated for them."
So they worked until, when it was the time of the ʿAṣr prayer, they said, "What we have done is worthless for you,
and the wage you set for us is yours to keep."
He said to them, "Complete the rest of your work,
for what remains of the day is little." But they refused.
Then he hired another people to work for the rest of their day,
and they worked for the rest of their day until the sun set,
and they received the full wages of both groups.
That is their example, and the example of what they have accepted of this light."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to eat the pre-dawn meal with my family, and then I would hurry to catch the Fajr prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade two kinds of transactions, two ways of dressing, and two prayers: he forbade prayer after Fajr until the sun rises,
and after ʿAṣr until the sun sets,
and he forbade wrapping oneself up completely in a garment [leaving no opening for the arms], and sitting wrapped in a single garment with one's private parts exposed to the sky,
and the transactions of munābadhah and mulāmasah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: You offer a prayer
for which we accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we never saw him pray it,
and he indeed forbade them,
meaning the two rakʿahs after ʿAṣr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I pray as I saw my Companions pray.
I do not forbid anyone to pray at night or by day as he wishes,
except that you should not deliberately seek the time of sunrise or sunset [for prayer].
label: machine translation

segments_en: By the One Who took him away, he never abandoned them until he met Allah,
and he did not meet Allah, the Exalted, until he had become heavy [with weakness] in prayer,
and he used to pray much of his prayer sitting, meaning the two rakʿahs after ʿAṣr, and the Prophet ﷺ used to pray them,
but he would not pray them in the mosque, fearing that it would be burdensome on his Ummah,
for he loved what lightened [burdens] for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We waited for al-Ḥasan, and he was late for us until we were close to his time of rising [for night prayer],
then he came and said, "These neighbors of ours invited us."
Then he said, "Anas said: We waited for the Prophet ﷺ one night until about half the night had passed,
then he came and led us in prayer,
then he addressed us and said:"
"Indeed, the people have prayed and then gone to sleep,
but you remain in prayer as long as you are waiting for the prayer."
Al-Ḥasan said: Indeed, people remain in good as long as they wait for good.
Qurrah said: It is from the hadith of Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Indeed, Bilāl calls the adhān at night, so eat and drink until he calls the adhān," or he said, "until you hear the adhān of Ibn Umm Maktūm."
Ibn Umm Maktūm was a blind man,
who would not call the adhān until people said to him, "It is morning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Abṭaḥ, and Bilāl came and informed him that it was time for prayer,
then Bilāl went out with a short spear until he planted it in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Abṭaḥ, and he called the iqāmah for the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw Bilāl calling the adhān, and I began to follow his mouth this way and that way as he called the adhān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū ad-Dardāʾ came to me angry, and I said, "What has angered you?" He said, "By Allah, I do not recognize anything of the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ except that they all pray together."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"While a man was walking on a road, he found a thorny branch on the road and removed it,
so Allah thanked him and forgave him." Then he said:
"The martyrs are five: the one who dies of plague, the one who dies of a stomach disease, the one who drowns, the one who dies under a collapsed building,
and the martyr in the cause of Allah." And he said:
"If people knew what is in the call to prayer and the first row, and they could find no way except to draw lots for it, they would draw lots for it.
And if they knew what is in going early to the prayer, they would race to it,
and if they knew what is in the ʿIshāʾ and Fajr prayers, they would come to them even if crawling."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a man.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, and he said: A cloud came and it rained until the roof leaked,
and it was made of palm branches. Then the prayer was called,
and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrating in water and mud,
until I saw the mark of the mud on his forehead.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"When one of you is at his meal, let him not hurry until he has satisfied his need from it,
even if the prayer has been called."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was one of the three whose repentance was accepted. He had never stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in any expedition he undertook, except for two: the expedition of ʿUsrah (Tabūk) and the expedition of Badr.
He said: So I resolved to tell the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the truth, in the forenoon,
for he would seldom return from a journey except in the forenoon, and he would begin with the mosque and pray two rakʿahs.
The Prophet ﷺ forbade [people] from speaking to me and to my two companions,
and he did not forbid speaking to any of the others who had stayed behind besides us,
so the people avoided speaking to us.
I remained like that until the matter grew long for me,
and nothing was more worrying to me than that I might die and the Prophet ﷺ would not pray over me, or that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ might die and I would be left in that position among the people,
so that none of them would speak to me
and none would pray over me.
Then Allah revealed the acceptance of our repentance to His Prophet ﷺ when the last third of the night remained,
while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with Umm Salamah,
and Umm Salamah was kind to me and concerned about my affair.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Umm Salamah, Kaʿb's repentance has been accepted."
She said: Should I not send word to him and give him the good news? He said:
"Then the people would crowd you and keep you from sleep for the rest of the night."
Then when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had prayed the Fajr prayer, he announced Allah's acceptance of our repentance.
When he was delighted, his face would light up until it was like a piece of the moon.
And we, the three who had been left behind, were [dealt with] differently from those who had made excuses, when Allah sent down our repentance.
When those who lied to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were mentioned, those who stayed behind and made false excuses,

they were mentioned with the worst that anyone has been mentioned with. Allah, Glorified is He, said: {They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say: Make no excuses; we will never believe you. Allah has already informed us of your affairs, and Allah and His Messenger will see your deeds} the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, who was the guide of Kaʿb ibn Mālik, said: I heard Kaʿb ibn Mālik
relating, when he stayed behind, the account of Tabūk.
By Allah, I do not know anyone whom Allah tested in truthfulness of speech better than He tested me.
Since I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until this day of mine, I have not deliberately told a lie,
and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Messenger ﷺ: {Allah has certainly accepted the repentance of the Prophet and the Muhājirūn} up to His saying {and be with the truthful}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās

recited: {Truly, they fold up their breasts}. I said: O Abū al-ʿAbbās, what does "they fold up their breasts" mean? He said: A man would be intimate with his wife and feel shy, or relieve himself and feel shy, so {Truly, they fold up their breasts} was revealed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās recited: {Truly, they fold up their breasts to hide from Him. Indeed, when they cover themselves with their garments}. Someone else reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: {they cover themselves} means they cover their heads; {he was distressed for them} means he thought ill of his people.
{and he was constrained on account of them} means on account of his guests; {in a part of the night} means in darkness.
Mujāhid said: {anīb} means: I return.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh [narrated] the account of
ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, when the people of the slander said about her what they said, and Allah declared her innocent.
Each of them narrated to me a portion of the account. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"If you are innocent, Allah will declare your innocence,
and if you have fallen into a sin, seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him."

I said: By Allah, I find no likeness for myself except the father of Yūsuf: {So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the one sought for help against what you describe}. And Allah revealed: {Indeed, those who brought forth the slander} the ten verses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She is the mother of ʿĀʾishah. She said: While I and ʿĀʾishah were [together], fever seized her, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Perhaps it is because of a story that was told."
She said: Yes. And ʿĀʾishah sat up and said: My likeness and yours is that of Yaʿqūb and his sons: and Allah is the one sought for help against what you describe.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Hayta lak" (Come, I am yours). He said: We only recite it as we were taught. {Mathwāh} means his dwelling place. {Alfaya} means he found. {Alfaw ābāʾahum} means they found their fathers. {Alfaynā} likewise. And from Ibn Masʿūd: {Rather, I marvel, while they mock}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They believed in some and disbelieved in some: the Jews and the Christians.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The souls of the martyrs are in green birds that feed from the fruits of Paradise," or he said, "from the trees of Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The first three to enter Paradise were shown to me: a martyr, a chaste person who restrains himself from what is unlawful, and a servant who worshipped Allah well and was sincere toward his masters."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The martyrs are of four types: a believer of excellent faith who meets the enemy, is true to Allah, and is killed. It is he to whom people will raise their eyes on the Day of Resurrection like this."
And he raised his head until his cap fell off.
He (the narrator) said: I do not know whether he meant the cap of ʿUmar or the cap of the Prophet ﷺ. He said:

"The second is a believer of excellent faith who meets the enemy, and it is as if his skin were pricked with the thorns of the ṭalḥ tree out of cowardice. A stray arrow comes to him and kills him; he is in the second rank. The third is a believer who mixed a righteous deed with another, evil one, who meets the enemy, is true to Allah, and is killed; he is in the third rank. The fourth is a believer who transgressed against himself, who meets the enemy, is true to Allah, and is killed; he is in the fourth rank."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a mountain pass in which there was a small spring of sweet water. Its goodness impressed him, and he said: "If only I were to withdraw from the people and settle in this pass. But I will not do so until I ask permission from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:

"Do not do so. For the standing of one of you in the cause of Allah is better than his praying in his house for seventy years. Do you not love that Allah forgive you and admit you to Paradise? Fight in the cause of Allah. Whoever fights in the cause of Allah for the time it takes to milk a she-camel, Paradise becomes obligatory for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Shall I not tell you who the best of people are? A man holding the reins of his horse in the cause of Allah. Shall I not tell you who comes next? A man who keeps apart with his flock of sheep, fulfilling Allah's due in it. Shall I not tell you who the worst of people are? A man who is asked in the name of Allah and does not give."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever asks Allah for being killed in His cause, sincerely from his heart, Allah will grant him the reward of a martyr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Salmān al-Fārisī passed by Shuraḥbīl ibn al-Simṭ, who was at a frontier post of his, and it was hard on him and his companions. He said: "Shall I not tell you, O Ibn al-Simṭ, a hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nothing is more beloved to Allah than two drops and two marks: a drop of tears shed out of fear of Allah, and a drop of blood spilled in the cause of Allah.
As for the two marks: a mark made in the cause of Allah, and a mark made in performing one of the obligations of Allah."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If people knew what I know about being alone, no rider would travel at night," meaning alone.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "War is deception."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ drew us up in battle formation at Badr at night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If the enemy attacks you by night, then say:
Ḥā Mīm, they will not be helped."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I made my sword on the pattern of the sword of Samurah ibn Jundab, and Samurah claimed that he made his sword on the pattern of the sword of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which was a Ḥanafī sword.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ reached Marr al-Ẓahrān in the year of the Conquest, he informed us that we would meet the enemy, and he ordered us to break our fast, so we all broke our fast.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw us on the day of Ḥunayn when the two armies were turning back in flight, and there were not even a hundred men with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mazīdah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered [Mecca] on the day of the Conquest with gold and silver on his sword.
Ṭālib said: I asked him about the silver, and he said: The hilt-guard of the sword was silver.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ wore two coats of mail on the day of Uḥud. He tried to climb onto the rock but could not, so he made Ṭalḥah sit beneath him, and the Prophet ﷺ climbed on him until he was level with the rock. He said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "Ṭalḥah has made [Paradise] obligatory for himself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was a servant under command. He did not single us out from other people with anything except three: he commanded us to perform ablution thoroughly, not to eat charity, and not to breed donkeys with horses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on one of his military expeditions, and he passed by a group of people and said, "Who are these people?" They said, "We are Muslims."

And there was a woman kindling her oven with a son of hers beside her, and whenever the flame of the oven rose, she moved him away from it. She came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "Are you the Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Yes."
She said, "May my father and mother be ransomed for you! Is Allah not the Most Merciful of those who show mercy?" He said, "Yes."
She said, "And is Allah not more merciful to His servants than a mother is to her child?" He said, "Yes."
She said, "Then a mother would never throw her child into the Fire."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed his head and wept, then he raised his head to her and said:
"Allah punishes none of His servants except the rebellious, defiant one who defies Allah and refuses to say: There is no god but Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None enters the Fire except the wretched."
It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, who is the wretched?" He said:
"The one who does not do any act of obedience for Allah and does not abandon any act of disobedience for His sake."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"I have a Pond [stretching] between the Kaʿbah and Bayt al-Maqdis, white like milk, its vessels as many as the stars. And I will have the most followers of all the prophets on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I was given a choice between intercession and having half of my nation enter Paradise, so I chose intercession, because it is more general and more sufficient. Do you think it is for the God-fearing? No, rather it is for the sinners, the wrongdoers, the defiled."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Three will intercede on the Day of Resurrection: the prophets, then the scholars, then the martyrs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the Day of Resurrection comes, I will be the leader of the prophets, their spokesman, and the one entrusted with their intercession, and this is no boast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"This fire of yours is one part of seventy parts of the fire of Jahannam. Had it not been extinguished with water twice, you would not benefit from it. And it prays to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, not to return it into [Jahannam]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"On the Day of Resurrection, the one among the disbelievers who had lived the most comfortable life in this world will be brought, and it will be said: Dip him once in the Fire.
So he will be dipped in it, then it will be said to him: O so-and-so, did you ever experience any comfort? He will say: No, I never experienced any comfort.
And the believer who suffered the most hardship and affliction will be brought.
It will be said: Dip him once in Paradise.
So he will be dipped in it once, and it will be said to him: O so-and-so, did you ever experience any hardship or affliction? He will say: I never experienced any hardship or affliction."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The disbeliever will be made so huge that his molar will be greater than [Mount] Uhud, and the excess of his body over his molar will be like the excess of the body of one of you over his molar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Abū Burdah one night when al-Ḥārith ibn Aqyash came in to us, and al-Ḥārith narrated to us
that night that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Among my nation are those through whose intercession more people than [the tribe of] Muḍar will enter Paradise, and among my nation are those who will be made so huge for the Fire that one will be one of its corners."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Weeping will be sent upon the people of the Fire, and they will weep until the tears run dry, then they will weep blood until channels like trenches form in their faces; if ships were launched in them, they would sail."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and made to stand on the Bridge, and it will be said: O people of Paradise!

They will look out, afraid and apprehensive that they might be removed from their place in which they are. Then it will be said: O people of the Fire! They will look out, cheerful and joyful that they might be removed from their place in which they are. It will be said: Do you know this? They will say: Yes, this is Death.
He said: Then it will be ordered, and it will be slaughtered on the Bridge. Then it will be said to both groups: Eternity in what you find yourselves in, with no death in it ever."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays said: When Jaʿfar was killed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned to his family and said:
"The family of Jaʿfar have been preoccupied with the affair of their deceased, so prepare food for them."
ʿAbd Allāh said: It continued to be a established practice until it became something new, and then it was abandoned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to regard gathering at the house of the deceased and preparing food as a form of wailing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Death in a foreign land is martyrdom."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever dies ill dies a martyr, and is protected from the trial of the grave, and his provision from Paradise is brought to him morning and evening."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah, saying:
O Mother, tell me about the illness of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said:

He fell ill and began to blow lightly; we likened his blowing to the blowing of one who eats raisins. He used to go round to his wives, but when his illness became heavy he asked their permission to stay in the house of ʿĀʾishah and that they take turns attending him. She said:
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me between two men, his feet dragging on the ground, one of them being al-ʿAbbās. I related this to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said:
Do you know who the man was whom ʿĀʾishah did not name?
He was ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When they wanted to dig a grave

for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they sent for Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ, who used to dig graves in the style of the people of Makkah, and they sent for Abū Ṭalḥah, who used to dig for the people of Madinah and would dig a niche-grave (laḥd). They sent two messengers to them and said: O Allah, choose what is best for Your Messenger.
They found Abū Ṭalḥah and he was brought, but Abū ʿUbaydah was not found, so a niche-grave was dug for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said: When they finished his preparation on Tuesday, he was placed on his bed in his house.
Then the people entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in successive groups.
They prayed over him; when they finished, the women were admitted, and when they finished, the children were admitted. No one led the people in prayer over the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Muslims differed about the place where the grave should be dug. Some said: He should be buried in his mosque.
Others said: He should be buried with his Companions.
Then Abū Bakr said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"No prophet's soul is taken except that he is buried where it is taken."
He said: So they lifted the bedding of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on which he had died and dug the grave for him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was buried in the middle of the night of Wednesday.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, al-Faḍl and Qutham, the sons of al-ʿAbbās, and Shuqrān, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, went down into his grave.
Aws ibn Khawlī, who is Abū Laylā, said to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: I implore you by Allah, [grant] us our share in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
ʿAlī said to him: Go down.
Shuqrān, his freed slave, took a velvet cloak that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to wear and buried it in the grave, saying: By Allah, no one will ever wear it after you.
So it was buried with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ experienced the agony of death that he experienced, Fāṭimah said: Oh, the distress of my father!
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There will be no distress for your father after today. There has come upon your father that which will leave no one, until the meeting on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah said to me: O Anas, how could your hearts bear to throw dust upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and we had but one direction; when he passed away, we looked this way and that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ said: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when a person stood to pray, his gaze would not go beyond the place of his feet. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, and when people stood to pray, their gaze would not go beyond the place of their foreheads. Then Abū Bakr died and ʿUmar came, and when people stood to pray, their gaze would not go beyond the direction of the qiblah. Then ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān came, and the turmoil occurred, so people turned to the right and to the left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Phlegm in the mosque..." and he mentioned the like of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever enters this mosque and spits in it or clears phlegm, let him dig and bury it. If he does not, then let him spit into his garment and then go out with it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was delivering a sermon one day, he saw phlegm on the qiblah wall of the mosque. He became angry with the people, then scraped it off. He said: and I think he said: Then he called for saffron and smeared it on the spot, and said:
"Indeed Allah is in front of the face of any of you when he prays, so let him not spit in front of him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to like palm stalks, and he would usually have one in his hand. He entered the mosque and saw phlegm on the qiblah wall of the mosque, so he scraped it off. Then he turned to the people, angry, and said:

"Would any of you be pleased to be spat at in his face? Indeed, when any of you faces the qiblah, he is facing his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and the angel is on his right. So let him not spit to his right or toward the qiblah; let him spit to his left or under his foot. And if something urgent comes over him, let him do like this."
Ibn ʿAjlān described that to us: that he spits into his garment and then folds one part of it over the other.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: a man led some people in prayer and spat toward the qiblah while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was watching. When the man had finished, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He must not lead you in prayer."
After that he wanted to lead them in prayer, but they prevented him and told him what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said. He mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Yes."
And I think he said:
"You have harmed Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was praying, and he spat under his left foot.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Wāthilah ibn al-Asqaʿ in the mosque of Damascus; he spat on the mat and then rubbed it with his foot. It was said to him: Why did you do this? He said: Because I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us in this mosque of ours, with a palm stalk of the Ibn Ṭāb variety in his hand. He looked and saw phlegm on the qiblah wall of the mosque, so he went toward it and scraped it off with the stalk. Then he said:
"Which of you would like Allah to turn His face away from him?" Then he said:

"Indeed, when any of you stands to pray, Allah is in front of his face, so let him not spit in front of his face or to his right. Let him spit to his left, under his left foot. And if something urgent comes over him, let him do like this with his garment."
And he put it to his mouth and then rubbed it. Then he said: "Bring me some perfume."

A young man from the neighborhood got up and ran to his family, and came with some khalūq perfume in his palm. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it, put it on the head of the stalk, and then smeared it over the mark of the phlegm.
Jābir said: It is from there that you put khalūq in your mosques.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this verse was revealed:

"Whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will hold you accountable for it," he said: Something entered their hearts from it that had never entered them from anything else. So they told the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Say: We hear and we obey."
So Allah cast faith into their hearts, and Allah revealed:
"The Messenger believes in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and so do the believers," the verse:

"Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have what it has earned, and it will bear what it has earned. Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or make a mistake." He said: "I have done so."
"Our Lord, do not place upon us a burden as You placed upon those before us." He said: "I have done so."
"Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no strength to bear, and pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us," the verse. He said: "I have done so."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people from among his Companions came to him and said: "Messenger of Allah, we find within ourselves things so grave that we regard it as terrible to speak of them, and we would not like to speak of them even if we were given [the world]." He said: "Have you really found that?" They said: "Yes." He said:
"That is the clear [sign of] faith."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"People will keep asking questions until it is said: 'Allah created creation, so who created Allah?' Whoever finds anything of that in himself should say: 'I believe in Allah.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Hour will not come until 'Allah, Allah' is no longer said on earth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ distributed some goods, and I said: "Messenger of Allah, give so-and-so, for he is a believer." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Or a Muslim?" I said it three times,
and he repeated to me three times: "Or a Muslim?" Then he said:
"I give to a man while another is dearer to me than him, out of fear that Allah would cast him on his face into the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of my nation will not cease fighting for the truth, prevailing until the Day of Resurrection." He said: "Then ʿĪsā ibn Maryam ﷺ will descend, and their leader will say: 'Come, lead us in prayer.' He will say: 'No.
Some of you are leaders over others,
as an honour from Allah to this nation.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Three things, when they appear, will not benefit a soul whose faith was not already believed in before, or which has not earned some good through its faith: the rising of the sun from its west, the Dajjāl, and the Beast of the earth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We travelled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ between Makkah and Madīnah, and we passed a valley. He said:
"Which valley is this?"
They said: "The valley of al-Azraq." He said:

"It is as if I see Mūsā ﷺ" and he mentioned something of his complexion and hair that Dāwūd did not remember, "with his two fingers in his ears, raising his voice to Allah in the talbiyah, passing through this valley." He said:
"Then we travelled on until we came to a mountain pass. He said:
"Which pass is this?"
They said: "Harshā," or "Laft." He said:
"It is as if I see Yūnus on a red camel, wearing a woollen cloak, the halter of his camel made of palm fibre, passing through this valley, reciting the talbiyah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Prophets were shown to me. Mūsā was a lean, well-built man, as if he were one of the men of Shanūʾah. I saw ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, and the one I have seen who most resembles him is ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd. I saw Ibrāhīm, blessings of Allah be upon him, and the one I have seen who most resembles him is your companion," meaning himself. "And I saw Jibrīl, peace be upon him, and the one I have seen who most resembles him is Dihyah."
In the narration of Ibn Rumḥ:
"Dihyah ibn Khalīfah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us and told us five things. He said:

"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not sleep, and it is not fitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the night are raised to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the deeds of the night. His veil is light", and in the narration of Abū Bakr, "fire", "were He to remove it, the glories of His Face would burn up everything His sight reaches of His creation."
In the narration of Abū Bakr, from al-Aʿmash, and he did not say: "He narrated to us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah made Makkah sacred, and the people did not make it sacred. So whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day must not shed blood in it, nor cut down a tree in it. If anyone seeks a concession by saying, 'It was made lawful for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,'

[then say]: Allah made it lawful for me and did not make it lawful for the people, and it was made lawful for me only for an hour of a day. Then it returned to being sacred until the Day of Resurrection. Then you, O tribe of Khuzāʿah, killed this man of Hudhayl, and I am to pay his blood money. So whoever has a relative killed after today, his family have a choice between two options: either they kill [the killer], or they take the blood money."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr ibn Ḥazm brought me a letter written on a piece of tanned leather from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
"This is a declaration from Allah and His Messenger: {O you who believe, fulfil your contracts.}"
Then he recited several verses from it, and then said:

"For a life, one hundred camels; for an eye, fifty; for a hand, fifty; for a foot, fifty; for a wound reaching the membrane of the brain, one third of the blood money; for a wound penetrating the body cavity, one third of the blood money; for a wound that dislodges the bone, fifteen camels; for the fingers, ten each; for the teeth, five each; and for a wound exposing the bone, five."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Something about this divine decree entered my mind, and I feared it would ruin my religion and my affairs. So I went to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and said, "Abū al-Mundhir, something about this decree has entered my heart, and I fear for my religion and my affairs. Tell me something about it, perhaps Allah will benefit me through it."

He said, "If Allah were to punish the inhabitants of His heavens and the inhabitants of His earth, He would punish them without being unjust to them, and if He were to have mercy on them, His mercy would be better for them than their deeds.
If you had gold like Mount Uḥud, or like Mount Uḥud in gold, and spent it in the cause of Allah, it would not be accepted from you until you believe in the decree,
and you know that what afflicted you could never have missed you, and what missed you could never have afflicted you.
And if you die believing otherwise, you will enter the Fire. But there is no harm in your going to my brother ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd and asking him."
So I went to ʿAbdullāh and asked him, and he said the same as Ubayy had said, and he said to me, "There is no harm in your going to Ḥudhayfah."
So I went to Ḥudhayfah and asked him, and he said the same as they had said, and he said, "Go to Zayd ibn Thābit and ask him."
So I went to Zayd ibn Thābit and asked him, and he said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'If Allah were to punish the inhabitants of His heavens and the inhabitants of His earth, He would punish them without being unjust to them, and if He were to have mercy on them, His mercy would be better for them than their deeds. If you had gold like Uḥud, or like Mount Uḥud in gold, and spent it in the cause of Allah, He would not accept it from you until you believe in the whole of the decree, and you know that what afflicted you could never have missed you, and what missed you could never have afflicted you. And if you die believing otherwise, you will enter the Fire.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with them both. He said: A Bedouin said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the Trumpet?" He said:
"A horn that is blown."
He said: This is a good (ḥasan) hadith; we know it only from the narration of Sulaymān al-Taymī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I was brought the Burāq—a white, long animal, taller than a donkey and smaller than a mule, which places its hoof at the furthest point of its sight." He said: "I rode it until I reached Bayt al-Maqdis. I tied it to the ring to which the prophets used to tie [their mounts]. Then I entered the mosque and prayed two units of prayer in it, then came out. Jibrīl, peace be upon him, came to me with a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk, and I chose the milk. Jibrīl said: 'You have chosen the natural disposition (fiṭrah).'
Then we were taken up to the heaven, and Jibrīl asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibrīl.'
It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muḥammad.'
It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.'
So it was opened for us, and there I met Ādam, who welcomed me and supplicated for good for me.
Then we were taken up to the second heaven, and Jibrīl, peace be upon him, asked for it to be opened.
It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibrīl.'
It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muḥammad.'
It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.'

So it was opened for us, and there I met the two sons of the maternal aunt, ʿĪsā ibn Maryam and Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā, may the blessings of Allah be upon them both. They welcomed me and supplicated for good for me.
Then I was taken up to the third heaven, and Jibrīl asked for it to be opened.
It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibrīl.'
It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muḥammad ﷺ.'
It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.'
So it was opened for us, and there I met Yūsuf, peace be upon him, who had been given half of all beauty. He welcomed me and supplicated for good for me.
Then we were taken up to the fourth heaven, and Jibrīl, peace be upon him, asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibrīl.'
