It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muḥammad.'
It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.'

So it was opened for us, and there I met Idrīs, who welcomed me and supplicated for good for me. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: {And We raised him to a high station.} Then we were taken up to the fifth heaven, and Jibrīl asked for it to be opened.
It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibrīl.'
It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muḥammad.'
It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.'
So it was opened for us, and there I met Hārūn, peace be upon him, who welcomed me and supplicated for good for me.
Then we were taken up to the sixth heaven, and Jibrīl, peace be upon him, asked for it to be opened.
It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibrīl.'
It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muḥammad.'
It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.'
So it was opened for us, and there I met Mūsā, peace be upon him, who welcomed me and supplicated for good for me.
Then we were taken up to the seventh heaven, and Jibrīl asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibrīl.'
It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muḥammad ﷺ.'
It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.'

So it was opened for us, and there I met Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, resting his back against al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr. Every day seventy thousand angels enter it, never to return to it. Then I was taken to the Lote Tree of the Farthest Boundary. Its leaves were like the ears of elephants and its fruits like large jars." He said: "When what covered it of the command of Allah covered it, it changed, and none of Allah's creation can describe it because of its beauty.

Then Allah revealed to me what He revealed, and He made obligatory upon me fifty prayers every day and night. I went down to Mūsā, peace be upon him, and he said: 'What has your Lord made obligatory upon your nation?' I said: 'Fifty prayers.'
He said: 'Return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction, for your nation will not be able to bear that. I have tested the Children of Israel and experienced them.'
He said: "So I returned to my Lord and said: 'My Lord, lighten it for my nation.'
He took away five for me. Then I returned to Mūsā and said: 'He has taken away five for me.'
He said: 'Your nation will not be able to bear that. Return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction.'

He said: "I kept going back and forth between my Lord, Blessed and Exalted, and Mūsā, peace be upon him, until He said: 'O Muḥammad, they are five prayers every day and night, and for each prayer there are ten, so that is fifty prayers.

Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, one good deed is written for him; if he does it, ten are written for him. Whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, nothing is written; if he does it, one evil deed is written.'" He said: "Then I went down until I reached Mūsā, peace be upon him, and told him. He said: 'Return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction.'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I said: 'I have returned to my Lord until I feel shy before Him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was riding behind Abū Ṭalḥah on the day of Khaybar, and my foot was touching the foot of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: We came upon them as the sun was rising, and they had brought out their cattle and come out with their axes, their baskets, and their spades. They said, "Muhammad and the army!" He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Khaybar is ruined! Indeed, when we descend upon the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning of those who were warned."

He said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, defeated them. A beautiful girl fell to the share of Diḥyah, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bought her for seven heads [of slaves]. Then he handed her over to Umm Sulaym to prepare her and make her ready for him. He said: And I think he said: and that she should observe her waiting period in her house. She was Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made her wedding feast of dates, dried curd, and ghee. The ground was cleared into hollows, leather mats were brought and laid in them, and the dried curd and ghee were brought, and the people ate their fill. He said: The people said, "We do not know whether he has married her or taken her as a concubine."

They said, "If he veils her, then she is his wife, and if he does not veil her, then she is a concubine." So when he wanted to mount, he veiled her, and she sat on the hindquarters of the camel, and they knew that he had married her.

When they drew near Madinah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ hastened, and we hastened. He said: Then the she-camel al-ʿAḍbāʾ stumbled, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell, and she fell. He got up and covered her, while the women had looked on and said, "May Allah keep the Jewish woman far away!"
He said: I said, "O Abū Ḥamzah, did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fall?" He said, "Yes, by Allah, he indeed fell."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I was listening,
from Ibn al-Qāsim, who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm, from his father,
from ʿAmr ibn Sulaym az-Zuraqī,
who said: Abū Ḥumayd as-Sāʿidī informed me
that they said: "O Messenger of Allah, how should we send blessings upon you?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad, his wives, and his offspring,
" — in the narration of al-Ḥārith:
"just as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrāhīm, and bless Muḥammad, his wives, and his offspring." Both said:
"just as You blessed the family of Ibrāhīm. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Salamah said that Abū Hurayrah said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [said]... (and a second chain:) Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā informed us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yūnus informed me, from Ibn Shihāb, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, who informed him from Abū Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Jews and the Christians do not dye [their hair], so be different from them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Bashshār and Abū Bakr ibn Nāfiʿ — the wording is that of Ibn al-Muthannā and Ibn Nāfiʿ — said: Ibn Abī ʿAdī informed us, from Shuʿbah,
from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār,
from Abū Salamah,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade combining a woman with her paternal aunt, or a woman with her maternal aunt [in marriage].
label: machine translation

segments_en: ...from the Prophet ﷺ. (And a second chain:) Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us,
— and the wording is his — saying: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever carries arms against us is not one of us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have been commanded to fight the people."
[This is] like the hadith of Ibn al-Musayyab from Abū Hurayrah. (And a second chain:) Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me: Wakīʿ narrated to us,
(and a third chain:) Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to me:
ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān narrated to us,
— that is, Ibn Mahdī — and both said: Sufyān narrated to us,
from Abū az-Zubayr, from Jābir,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no god but Allah. When they say: There is no god but Allah, they protect from me their lives and their wealth, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah."
Then he recited: {You are only a reminder. You are not a controller over them.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution and wiped his forelock.

And he mentioned [wiping] over the turban. — He said, from al-Muʿtamir: I heard my father narrate from Bakr ibn ʿAbdullāh, from al-Ḥasan, from Ibn al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, from al-Mughīrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to wipe over the two leather socks, over his forelock, and over his turban.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the saying of the Exalted: {Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it}, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to experience hardship from the revelation,
and he used to move his lips. Ibn ʿAbbās said: I am moving them for you as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to move them.
Saʿīd said: I am moving them as I saw Ibn ʿAbbās moving them.

Then he moved his lips. So Allah the Exalted revealed: {Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.} He said: Its collection in your chest for him,

and your reciting it. {So when We have recited it, follow its recitation.} He said: So listen to it and be silent. {Then indeed, upon Us is its clarification.} Then indeed, it is upon Us that you recite it.
After that, whenever Jibrīl came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would listen,
and when Jibrīl left, the Prophet ﷺ would recite it as he had recited it [to him].
label: machine translation

segments_en: that a man
said to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar: "Will you not go on military expeditions?" He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but Allah, establishing the prayer, giving zakāh, fasting Ramadan, and Hajj to the House."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe,
and the emigrant is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: "Which of the Muslims is best?" He said:
"The one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe."
This hadith is ṣaḥīḥ gharīb through this route, from the hadith of Abū Mūsā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited Sūrat al-Aʿrāf in the Maghrib prayer, dividing it between the two rakʿahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ recited al-Baqarah, Āl ʿImrān and an-Nisāʾ in one rakʿah; he would not pass by a verse of mercy without asking [Allah for it], nor a verse of punishment without seeking refuge [in Allah from it].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Beautify the Qurʾān with your voices."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Beautify the Qurʾān with your voices."
Ibn ʿAwsajah said: I had forgotten this [saying], "Beautify the Qurʾān,"
until aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim reminded me of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said [or did]: he stood and raised his hands the first time, then did not repeat it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and al-Aswad,
that they were with ʿAbdullāh in his house, and he said, "Have these people prayed?" We said, "Yes."
So he led the two of them in prayer, standing between them, without adhān or iqāmah.

He said: "When you are three, do it this way, and when you are more than that, let one of you lead you. And let him spread his palms over his thighs." It is as though I can see the spreading of the fingers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAlqamah,

both said: We prayed with ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd in his house, and he stood between us. We placed our hands on our knees, but he removed them and interlaced our fingers, and said, "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ bowed, he was level: he did not raise his head up nor lower it, and he placed his hands on his knees.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he mentioned,
another before him, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj,
from Muḥammad ibn Maslamah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he stood to pray a voluntary prayer, would say when he bowed:

"O Allah, to You I have bowed, in You I have believed, to You I have submitted, and in You I have placed my trust. You are my Lord. My hearing, my sight, my flesh, my blood, my marrow and my nerves are humbled before Allah, Lord of the worlds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his head from bowing, he would say:
"O Allah, our Lord, and to You belongs all praise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he did not perform qunūt; I prayed behind Abū Bakr and he did not perform qunūt; I prayed behind ʿUmar and he did not perform qunūt; I prayed behind ʿUthmān and he did not perform qunūt; I prayed behind ʿAlī and he did not perform qunūt. Then he said, "My son, it is an innovation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to pray the Ẓuhr prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I would take a handful of pebbles in my palm to cool them, then move them to my other palm; when I prostrated, I would place them for my forehead.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that I would not fall [in prostration] except standing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Read] to him while I was listening,
and the wording is his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Yazīd ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn al-Hād,
from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥārith,
from Abū Salamah,
from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī,
who said: My eyes saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with traces of water and mud on his forehead and nose, on the morning of the twenty-first night. Abridged.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ lowered himself to the ground in prostration, he held his upper arms away from his armpits and spread the toes of his feet. Abridged.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Madīnah and said, "I will surely watch the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said the takbīr and raised his hands until I saw his thumbs close to his ears. When he wanted to bow, he said the takbīr and raised his hands. Then he raised his head and said:
"Sami'a Allāhu liman ḥamidah."
Then he said the takbīr and prostrated, and his hands were by his ears, in the same position as when he began the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If I had been in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would have seen his armpits.
Abū Mijlaz said: It is as if he said that because he was in prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: I missed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from his bed, and I began searching for him, thinking he had gone to one of his slave women. Then my hand fell upon him while he was prostrating, saying:
"O Allah, forgive me what I have concealed and what I have made public."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with Abū Hurayrah and Abū Saʿīd, and one of them narrated,

the hadith of intercession while the other listened silently. He said: Then the angels will come and intercede, and the messengers will intercede. And he mentioned the Bridge (aṣ-Ṣirāṭ). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I will be the first to cross. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has finished judging between His creation and has brought out of the Fire whomever He wishes to bring out, Allah will command the angels and the messengers to intercede. They will be recognized by their marks, for the Fire consumes every part of the son of Adam except the place of prostration. Then the water of Paradise will be poured over them, and they will sprout as a seed sprouts in the silt carried by a flood."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever comes to his Muslim brother to visit him when he is ill walks in the harvest of Paradise until he sits; and when he sits, mercy envelops him. If it is in the morning, seventy thousand angels pray for him until the evening; and if it is in the evening, seventy thousand angels pray for him until the morning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When death approached Kaʿb, Umm Bishr bint al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr came to him and said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, if you meet so-and-so, convey my greetings of peace to him."
He said, "May Allah forgive you, Umm Bishr; we are too preoccupied for that."
She said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, have you not heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'The souls of the believers are in green birds, hanging from the trees of Paradise'?" He said, "Yes."
She said, "Then that is it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh while he was dying, and I said, "Convey my greetings of peace to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon her while a close relative of hers was with her, being choked by death. When the Prophet ﷺ saw her state, he said to her:
"Do not grieve over your close relative, for that is part of his good deeds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "When does a person's recognition of people cease?" He said, "When he sees [the angels of death]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you are present with your dying, close their eyes, for the eye follows the soul, and say what is good, for the angels say 'Āmīn' to what the people of the household say."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let your dead be washed by the trustworthy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever washes a deceased person, shrouds him, perfumes him, carries him, prays over him, and does not disclose what he saw, comes out of his sins as on the day his mother bore him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Had I known beforehand what I came to know afterwards, no one but his wives would have washed the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from al-Baqīʿ and found me suffering a headache, and I was saying, "Oh, my head!" He said:
"Rather, I [say], 'Oh, my head!', ʿĀʾishah." Then he said:
"What harm would it do you if you died before me? I would take charge of you, wash you, shroud you, pray over you, and bury you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When they began to wash the Prophet ﷺ, a caller from within called out to them, "Do not take off the shirt of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ was washed, [ʿAlī] went to look for on him what is looked for on the dead, but did not find it.
He said, "May my father be your ransom, you who are pure: you were pure in life and pure in death."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When I die, wash me with seven skins [of water] from my well, the well of Ghars."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best shroud is the ḥullah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ibrāhīm, the son of the Prophet ﷺ, passed away, the Prophet ﷺ said to them:
"Do not wrap him in his shrouds until I look at him."
Then he came to him, bent over him, and wept.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said: Whoever follows a funeral procession should carry the bier from all its sides, for that is from the Sunnah. Then, if he wishes, let him do more voluntarily, and if he wishes, let him leave it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: he saw a funeral procession being hurried along, and he said:
"Let there be calm and tranquility upon you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Barzah... they said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a funeral procession, and he saw some people who had thrown off their outer garments and were walking in their shirts. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Are you adopting the practice of the Jāhiliyyah, or imitating the deeds of the Jāhiliyyah? I was about to make a supplication against you that would return you in other than your forms."
He said: So they took their outer garments and did not repeat that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to al-Faḍl ibn Maysarah, from Abū Ḥarīz,
that Abū Burdah
narrated to him, saying: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī gave instructions when death came to him, saying, "Do not follow me with an incense burner."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever has a hundred Muslims pray over him will be forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had nine wives. When he divided his time among them, he would not return to the first one except after nine [nights]. They would gather every night in the house of the one he was to visit. Once he was in the house of ʿĀʾishah, and Zaynab came, so he stretched out his hand toward her. ʿĀʾishah said, "This is Zaynab."
So the Prophet ﷺ withdrew his hand.

The two women began to argue, until they grew loud, and the prayer was called. Abū Bakr passed by, heard their voices, and said, "Go out to the prayer, O Messenger of Allah, and throw dust into their mouths!"
So the Prophet ﷺ went out. ʿĀʾishah said, "Now the Prophet ﷺ will finish his prayer, and Abū Bakr will come and do such and such to me."
When the Prophet ﷺ finished his prayer, Abū Bakr came to her and spoke harshly to her, and said, "Do you do this?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I have not seen any woman whom I would rather be in her skin than Sawdah bint Zamʿah, a woman with a sharp temper. She said: When she grew old, she gave her day with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to ʿĀʾishah. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have given my day with you to ʿĀʾishah."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would allot two days to ʿĀʾishah: her own day and the day of Sawdah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A believing man must not hate a believing woman. If he dislikes one trait in her, he will be pleased with another," or he said, "another one."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sīrīn said: For twenty years someone whom I did not doubt told me that Ibn ʿUmar divorced his wife with three [pronouncements] while she was menstruating, and was ordered to take her back. I did not doubt them, yet I did not know the hadith, until I met Abū Ghallāb Yūnus ibn Jubayr al-Bāhilī.

He was a reliable man, and he told me that he asked Ibn ʿUmar, who told him that he had divorced his wife with one divorce while she was menstruating, and was ordered to take her back. He said: I said, "Was it counted against him?" He said, "What else?
Would it be that he was incapable or acted foolishly?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Similar to this account.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muslim said: He made a mistake when he said ʿUrwah; it is only the freed slave of ʿAzzah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, of Abū Bakr, and during two years of the caliphate of ʿUmar, a divorce of three [pronouncements] counted as one. Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said, "People have hurried in a matter in which they had a period of deliberation. Should we not enforce it upon them?" So he enforced it upon them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr came seeking permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he found people sitting at his door, none of them having been given permission. He said: Abū Bakr was given permission and entered. Then ʿUmar came and asked permission, and was given permission. He found the Prophet ﷺ sitting, with his wives around him, sad and silent. He said: ʿUmar said, "I will certainly say something that makes the Prophet ﷺ laugh." He said, "O Messenger of Allah, if you had seen the daughter of Khārijah asking me for maintenance, and I got up and struck her neck!"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and said:
"They are around me as you see, asking me for maintenance."
Then Abū Bakr got up and went to ʿĀʾishah to strike her neck, and ʿUmar got up and went to Ḥafṣah to strike her neck, both saying, "You ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for what he does not have!"

They said, "By Allah, we will never ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for anything he does not have." Then he withdrew from them for a month, or twenty-nine days. Then this verse was revealed to him: {O Prophet, say to your wives...} until it reached {...for the doers of good among you a great reward.} He said: He began with ʿĀʾishah and said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, I want to present to you a matter, and I would like you not to hasten in it until you consult your parents."

She said, "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He recited the verse to her. She said, "Concerning you, O Messenger of Allah, should I consult my parents? Rather, I choose Allah, His Messenger, and the home of the Hereafter. And I ask you not to tell any of your wives what I have said." He said:
"No woman among them will ask me but that I will inform her that Allah did not send me to be harsh or to cause hardship, but He sent me as a teacher and one who makes things easy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came with ʿUmar until we were at Marr al-Ẓahrān.
And he narrated the hadith at length, like the hadith of Sulaymān ibn Bilāl, except that he said: I said, "Who were the two women?" He said, "Ḥafṣah and Umm Salamah."
And he added in it: I came to the apartments, and in every house there was weeping.
And he also added: He had vowed to stay away from them for a month, and when it was twenty-nine days, he came down to them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of Ḥunayn: "
Whoever has proof that he killed a man, then he may have the man's spoils."
So I stood up to look for proof of the man I had killed,
but I did not see anyone to testify for me, so I sat down.
Then it occurred to me [to speak], so I mentioned the matter to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. A man among those sitting with him said: "The weapons of this slain man that he mentions are with me."
[The man] said: "Then compensate him [with something] for it."
Abū Bakr said: "Never! He will not give it to a small weakling of Quraysh while leaving a lion from among the lions of Allah who fights for Allah and His Messenger."
He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded, and he handed it over to me. I bought some date-palm saplings with it, and it was the first property I acquired.
ʿAbdullāh said to me, from al-Layth: So the Prophet ﷺ stood up and handed it over to me.
The people of the Hijaz said: A judge does not rule by his own knowledge,
whether he witnessed it during his time in office or before it.
And if one litigant admitted to another a right in the court session,
then, according to some of them, he does not rule against him
until he calls two witnesses and makes them present at his admission.
Some of the people of Iraq said: What he heard or saw in the court session, he rules by it,
but what was outside of it, he does not rule except by two witnesses.
Others of them said: Rather, he rules by it, because he is trustworthy,
and what is intended by testimony is knowing the truth,
and his own knowledge is greater than testimony.
Some of them said: He rules by his knowledge in matters of property,
but not in other matters.
Al-Qāsim said: It is not appropriate for a judge to enforce a ruling by his own knowledge without the knowledge of others,
even though his knowledge is greater than the testimony of others,
because in it he exposes himself to suspicion among the Muslims,
and casts them into conjecture.
And the Prophet ﷺ disliked suspicion, so he said: "
This is only Ṣafiyyah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man called out to another man in al-Baqīʿ, "O Abū al-Qāsim!"
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to him.
The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I did not mean you; I only called so-and-so."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Name yourselves with my name, but do not use my kunyah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade a town-dweller from selling on behalf of a desert dweller, and forbade [people] from bidding up prices deceptively, a man from proposing marriage over his brother's proposal, or selling over his brother's sale, and a woman from asking for the divorce of her sister so as to empty what is in her vessel or in her dish.
ʿAmr added in his narration: "and a man must not bid over his brother's bid."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, [narrated] from the Prophet ﷺ: "
Do not leave the udders of camels and sheep tied up [to make them look full].
Whoever buys them afterward has the better of the two options after he has milked them: if he wishes, he may keep them,
and if he wishes, he may return them along with a ṣāʿ of dates."
It is mentioned from Abū Ṣāliḥ, Mujāhid, al-Walīd ibn Rabāḥ and Mūsā ibn Yasār, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "a ṣāʿ of dates."
Some of them said, from Ibn Sīrīn: a ṣāʿ of food, and he has the option for three days.
Some of them said, from Ibn Sīrīn: a ṣāʿ of dates.
He did not mention three days, and the narrations of dates are more numerous.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade meeting [the caravans] before they reach the market,
and that a town-dweller buy for a desert dweller,
and that a woman stipulate the divorce of her sister,
and that a man bid over his brother's bid.
He also forbade deceptive bidding and tying up the udders [of animals].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade muzābanah, and muzābanah is that what is on the tops of palm trees is sold for dates by a specified measure: if it exceeds, it is mine, and if it falls short, it is on me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us from selling silver for silver except hand to hand, equal for equal, and from selling gold for gold except hand to hand, equal for equal. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Sell gold for silver however you wish, and silver for gold however you wish."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A dinar for a dinar and a dirham for a dirham, like for like. Whoever gives more or takes more has engaged in ribā.
I said to him: "Ibn ʿAbbās says otherwise."

He said: "I met Ibn ʿAbbās and said: 'Do you see this that you say, is it something you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or did you find it in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?' He said: 'I did not hear it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor did I find it in the Book of Allah, but Usāmah ibn Zayd narrated to me that the Prophet ﷺ said: "
Ribā is in deferred [exchange].""
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a woman of the Makhzūm [tribe] who used to borrow goods and then deny it, so the Prophet ﷺ ordered that her hand be cut off. Her family came to Usāmah ibn Zayd and spoke to him, and he spoke to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about her.
Then he mentioned [the rest] similar to the hadith of al-Layth and Yūnus.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to Māʿiz ibn Mālik:
"Is what has reached me about you true?"
He said: "What has reached you about me?" He said:
"It has reached me that you had relations with the slave girl of the family of so-and-so." He said: "Yes."
So he testified four times.
Then he ordered that he be stoned, and he was stoned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jewish man, his face blackened with soot and having been flogged, was passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He called them [the Jews] and said:
"Is this how you find the punishment for the adulterer?" They said: "Yes."
Then he called one of their scholars and said to him:
"I ask you by Allah, Who revealed the Torah to Moses, is this how you find the punishment for the adulterer in your Book?"

He said: "No, by Allah, and had you not adjured me with this, I would not have told you. We find the punishment for the adulterer in our Book to be stoning, but it became widespread among our nobles, so when we seized a noble man we would leave him, and when we seized a weak man we would carry out the punishment on him. So we said: Come, let us agree on something we can apply to both the noble and the lowly. So we agreed on blackening [the face] with soot and flogging, and we abandoned stoning."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, I am the first to revive Your command when they had let it die."

Then he ordered that the man be stoned, and he was stoned. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {O Messenger, let them not grieve you, those who hasten into disbelief} up to His saying {They say, "If you are given this, take it, but if you are not given it, beware"} up to His saying {And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, it is they who are the disbelievers} concerning the Jews, up to His saying {And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, it is they who are the wrongdoers} concerning the Jews, up to His saying {And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, it is they who are the defiantly disobedient}. He said: "This [last] verse is entirely about the disbelievers," meaning this verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We raided Fazārah, and Abū Bakr was in command over us; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had appointed him over us. When we were within an hour of the water, Abū Bakr ordered us to halt for the night's rest, then he launched the attack. He reached the water, and those who were to be killed there were killed, and some were taken captive. I looked at a column of people among whom were the children, and I feared they would get ahead of me to the mountain, so I shot an arrow between them and the mountain. When they saw the arrow, they stopped. I came driving them along, and among them was a woman of Banū Fazārah wearing a leather garment, and with her was her daughter, one of the most beautiful of the Arabs. I drove them until I brought them to Abū Bakr, and Abū Bakr granted me her daughter as a bonus. We came to Medina, and I had not uncovered a garment of hers. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met me in the market and said:
"O Salamah, give me the woman."
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, she has pleased me, and I have not uncovered a garment of hers." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met me the next day in the market and said to me:
"O Salamah, give me the woman, may Allah bless your father."

I said: "She is yours, O Messenger of Allah. By Allah, I have not uncovered a garment of hers." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent her to the people of Mecca, and with her ransomed some Muslims who had been taken captive in Mecca.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I will certainly expel the Jews and the Christians from the Arabian Peninsula, until I leave none but Muslims."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was wounded in his face, his incisor tooth was broken, and he was struck with a missile on his shoulder. Blood began to flow down his face, and he wiped it away and said:
"How can a people prosper who did this to their Prophet while he was calling them to Allah?"
Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed:
(You have no part in the matter, whether He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.)
I heard ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd say: Yazīd ibn Hārūn made an error in this [narration].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Eighty

men from the people of Mecca came down upon the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions from the mountains of Tanʿīm at the time of the dawn prayer, intending to kill them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ seized them without a fight, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set them free. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca} to the end of the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on a military expedition, he would take Umm Sulaym and some women of the Anṣār with him, and they would give water [to the fighters] and treat the wounded.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ, and he recited to us: {that they will not associate anything with Allah}, and he forbade us from wailing for the dead.
One woman among us withdrew her hand and said: So-and-so helped me [in mourning], and I want to repay her.
He ﷺ said nothing, and she went away and then returned.
No woman fulfilled the pledge except Umm Sulaym, Umm al-ʿAlāʾ,
and the daughter of Abū Sabrah, the wife of Muʿādh, or the daughter of Abū Sabrah and the wife of Muʿādh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When a servant is placed in his grave
and his companions turn away from him,
he hears the sound of their sandals.
Two angels come to him, make him sit up, and say: What did you used to say about this man, Muḥammad ﷺ?
As for the believer, he says: I bear witness that he is the servant of Allah and His Messenger.
Then it is said to him: Look at your place in the Fire;
Allah has replaced it for you with a place in Paradise. And he sees both of them."
Qatādah said: It was mentioned to us that his grave is made spacious for him.
Then he returned to the hadith of Anas, who said:
"As for the hypocrite and the disbeliever, it is said to him: What did you used to say about this man? He says: I do not know;
I used to say what the people said.
Then it is said: You did not know, and you did not follow [the guidance].
And he is struck with iron hammers with a single blow,
and he screams a scream that is heard by all those near him except humans and jinn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Angel of Death came to Moses, peace be upon him, and said to him: Answer your Lord. He said: Moses, peace be upon him, slapped the eye of the Angel of Death and put it out. He said: The angel returned to Allah, the Exalted, and said: You sent me to a servant of Yours who does not want to die, and he has put out my eye. He said: Allah restored his eye and said: Go back to My servant and say: Do you want life? If you want life, place your hand on the back of an ox, and for every hair that your hand covers you will live a year. [Moses] said: Then what? [The angel] said: Then you will die.
He said: Then let it be now, my Lord! Cause me to die within a stone's throw of the Holy Land.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By Allah, if I were there, I would show you his grave beside the road, by the red sand dune."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed over a man the night after he had been buried; he and his Companions stood [for the prayer],
and he had asked about him, saying: "Who is this?" They said: So-and-so, who was buried last night. So they prayed over him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood at the door of Ḥafṣah and gestured with his hand toward the east, saying:
"Tribulation is right here, from where the horn of Satan rises."
He said it twice or three times.
And ʿUbaydullāh ibn Saʿīd said in his narration: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood at the door of ʿĀʾishah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [This was] read to him while I listened,
from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to us,
from Abū az-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has guaranteed for the one who strives in His cause, whom nothing sends out except striving in His cause and belief in His word, that He will admit him into Paradise, or return him to his home from which he set out, together with whatever reward or spoils he has gained."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a detachment toward Najd, and I went out with it. We took many camels, and our commander gave each person one camel as an additional share. Then we came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he divided our spoils among us, so each man among us received twelve camels after the fifth. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not hold us to account for what our commander had given us, nor did he criticize him for what he had done. So each man among us had thirteen camels, including his additional share.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give additional shares to some of those he sent out in detachments, for themselves in particular, apart from the general division among the whole army; and the fifth is obligatory in all of that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Jiʿrānah as he was returning from Ḥunayn. Bilāl's garment held silver, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taking handfuls of it and giving it to the people. The man said, "O Muḥammad, be just!" He said:
"Woe to you! Who will be just if I am not just? You would be disappointed and lost if I were not just."
Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "Let me, O Messenger of Allah, kill this hypocrite!" He said:

"Allah forbid that people should say that I kill my Companions. This man and his companions recite the Qur'an, but it does not go beyond their throats; they pass out of it as the arrow passes through the game."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Ḥunayn, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ favored some people in the distribution. He gave al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis a hundred camels, gave ʿUyaynah the same, and gave some of the nobles of the Arabs, favoring them that day in the distribution. A man said, "By Allah, this is a distribution in which there was no justice, and by which the face of Allah was not sought."

He said: I said, "By Allah, I will surely inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: So I went to him and told him what the man had said. He said: His face changed until it was like red dye, then he said:
"Who then will be just if Allah and His Messenger are not just?"
He said: Then he said:
"May Allah have mercy on Moses. He was harmed with more than this, and he was patient."
He said: I said, "Certainly, I will never again report any speech to him after this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā about the meat of domestic donkeys,

and he said: Hunger struck us on the day of Khaybar while we were with the Prophet ﷺ. The people had obtained donkeys outside the city, so we slaughtered them, and our pots were boiling when the Prophet's ﷺ caller called out: "Overturn the pots, and do not eat anything of the meat of donkeys." So we overturned them.
I said to ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā, "Did he forbid them absolutely?" He said: We discussed it among ourselves, and [some] said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade them absolutely because they eat filth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was a secretary for Jazʾ ibn Muʿāwiyah, the paternal uncle of al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays, when ʿUmar's letter came to us a year before his death: "Kill every sorcerer, separate every Magian from his close female relatives, and forbid them from murmuring [during meals]." So in one day we killed three sorcerers, and we separated every Magian man from his female relatives, in accordance with the Book of Allah. He prepared a great deal of food and invited them, and he laid a sword across his thigh. They ate and did not murmur, and they threw down the load of a mule or two of silver. ʿUmar had not taken the jizyah from the Magians until ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf testified that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had taken it from the Magians of Hajar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no one among my Companions who dies in any land except that he will be raised as a leader and a light for them on the Day of Resurrection."
This hadith is gharīb.
This hadith has been narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muslim Abū Ṭaybah, from Ibn Buraydah, from the Prophet ﷺ as a mursal report, and that is more correct.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you see those who revile my Companions, say: 'May Allah's curse be upon the worse of you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The most beloved of women to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was Fāṭimah, and of men, ʿAlī.
Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd said: Meaning, from among the members of his household.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ covered al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, ʿAlī and Fāṭimah with a cloak, then said:
"O Allah, these are the people of my household and my close ones. Remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly."
Umm Salamah said: "And I am with them, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"You are upon goodness."
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ, and it is the best thing narrated on this subject.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of the Conquest, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Fāṭimah and spoke to her privately, and she wept. Then he spoke to her again, and she laughed.

She said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had passed away, I asked her about her weeping and her laughing. She said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ told me that he would die, so I wept. Then he told me that I would be the leader of the women of Paradise, except for Maryam the daughter of ʿImrān, so I laughed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered with my paternal aunt upon ʿĀʾishah, and she was asked: "Which of the people was most beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" She said: "Fāṭimah."
It was said: "And among the men?" She said: "Her husband, as far as I know, he was one who fasted much and stood much in night prayer."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb.
Abū al-Jaḥḥāf's name is Dāwūd ibn Abī ʿAwf. He narrates from Sufyān al-Thawrī, who said: "Abū al-Jaḥḥāf narrated to us," and he was well-regarded.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was not jealous of anyone as I was jealous of Khadījah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not marry me until after she had died. That was because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave her glad tidings of a house in Paradise made of qaṣab, in which there is no noise and no toil.
This hadith is ḥasan.
Regarding "of qaṣab", he said: It only means qaṣab of pearls.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Sufficient for you among the women of the world are Maryam the daughter of ʿImrān, Khadījah the daughter of Khuwaylid, Fāṭimah the daughter of Muḥammad, and Āsiyah the wife of Pharaoh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jibrīl
came to the Prophet ﷺ with her image in a piece of green silk and said:
"This is your wife in this world and the Hereafter."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb; we do not know it except from the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAlqamah.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated this hadith from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAlqamah with this chain as mursal, and he did not mention ʿĀʾishah in it. Abū Usāmah also narrated from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, from the Prophet ﷺ something of this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, were never confused by any hadith and then asked ʿĀʾishah, except that we found knowledge of it with her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw anyone more eloquent than ʿĀʾishah.
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
spoke ill of ʿĀʾishah in the presence of ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, so he said: "Get away, despised and driven off! Would you harm the beloved of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?"
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She is his wife in this world and the Hereafter. Meaning ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her.
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me after some words from Ḥafṣah and ʿĀʾishah had reached me, so I mentioned that to him, and he said:
"Could you not have said: 'How can you two be better than me, when my husband is Muḥammad, my father is Hārūn, and my uncle is Mūsā?'"
What had reached her was that they said: "We are more honored to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than she is."
And they said: "We are the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and the daughters of his uncle."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It reached Ṣafiyyah that Ḥafṣah
had said: "The daughter of a Jew."
So she wept. The Prophet ﷺ came in to her while she was weeping and said: "What makes you weep?"
She said: "Ḥafṣah said to me that I am the daughter of a Jew." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"You are indeed the daughter of a prophet, your uncle is indeed a prophet, and you are indeed married to a prophet. So what is there for her to boast over you?" Then he said:
"Fear Allah, O Ḥafṣah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:
"If any of you has a mukātab [a slave contracting to buy his freedom] who has what he needs to pay [his debt], then let her observe hijāb from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was
one who had met the Prophet ﷺ. From ʿĀʾishah: The Prophet ﷺ forbade men and women from the public baths, then he permitted men to enter them wearing waist wrappers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what of our private parts: what should we show of them and what should we leave?" He said:
"Guard your private parts except from your wife or what your right hand possesses."
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what if the people are together, some of them with others?" He said:
"If you are able to let no one see it, then let no one see it."
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what if one of us is alone?" He said:
"Allah is more deserving that one feel shame before Him than before people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was no garment more beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than the shirt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father said to me: "My son, if you had seen us with our Prophet ﷺ when the rain fell on us, you would have thought our smell was the smell of sheep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me from [wearing] a gold ring, from wearing qassī garments, and from the red saddle-cloth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever drags his garment out of arrogance, Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection."
Umm Salamah said: "What should women do with their hems?" He said: "Let them lower them a span."
She said: "Then their feet would be exposed." He said:
"Then let them lower it a forearm's length and not add to it."
He said: This is a good, sound hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [One of] the wives of the Prophet ﷺ [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that the skins of dead animals be made use of when they have been tanned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a man to put on sandals while standing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If a woman applies perfume and passes by people so that they find her scent, then she is such and such."
He said something severe.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The brother of Qabīṣah and Muʿāwiyah ibn Hishām both said: Sufyān narrated to us,
He said: ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb narrated to us, from his father,
from Wāʾil ibn Ḥujr,
who said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while I had [long] hair, and he said: "Dhubāb [an ill omen]."
I thought he meant me, so I cut some of my hair. Then I came to him again and he said to me:
"I did not mean you, and this is better."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Prophet ﷺ wearing a brass ring, and he said to him:
"Why do I find on you the smell of idols?"
So he threw it away. Then he came wearing an iron ring, and he said:
"Why do I see on you the adornment of the people of the Fire?"
So he threw it away and said: "O Messenger of Allah, from what should I make it?" He said:
"Make it from silver, and do not make it a full mithqāl."
He did not say Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Muslim.
And he did not say al-Ḥasan al-Sulamī al-Marwazī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The great war, the conquest of Constantinople, and the emergence of the Antichrist [will occur] within seven months."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When deficiency befell the Children of Israel, a man among them would see his brother committing a sin and forbid him from it. Then the next day, what he had seen of him would not stop him from being his dining companion, his drinking companion, and his associate. So Allah made their hearts alike, and Qur'an was revealed about them, saying:
'Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressing.'"
Then he recited until he reached:

"'And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies; but many of them are defiantly disobedient.'" He said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ had been reclining, then he sat up and said:
"No, not until you take the wrongdoer by the hand and compel him firmly to [follow] the truth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl died, his son ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him to give him his shirt so that he could shroud his father in it, and he gave it to him. Then he asked him to pray over him, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up to pray over him. But ʿUmar got up and took hold of the garment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, will you pray over him when Allah has forbidden you to pray over him?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Allah gave me a choice, and said: 'Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times...' So I will ask more than seventy."
ʿUmar said, "He is a hypocrite."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over him, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: 'And never pray over any of them who has died, and do not stand at his grave.'
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr. Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said: "Akhbaranā," and the others said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
meaning Ibn Jaʿfar, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥarmalah, from ʿAṭāʾ and Sulaymān,
the two sons of Yasār, and Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, that ʿĀʾishah

said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was lying down in my house with his thighs or his shins uncovered. Abū Bakr asked permission to enter, and he allowed him while he was in that state, and they conversed. Then ʿUmar asked permission, and he allowed him while he was still like that, and they conversed. Then ʿUthmān asked permission, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat up and arranged his clothes. Muḥammad said: I do not say that this was on one single day. Then he entered and they conversed. When he left, ʿĀʾishah said: "Abū Bakr came in and you did not show concern for him or pay him any heed; then ʿUmar came in and you did not show concern for him or pay him any heed; then ʿUthmān came in and you sat up and arranged your clothes." He said,
"Should I not feel shy before a man before whom the angels feel shy?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was lying on his bed wearing ʿĀʾishah's wrap. He allowed Abū Bakr in while he was like that, and [Abū Bakr] had his need met by him and then left. Then ʿUmar asked permission, and he allowed him in while he was in that same state, and [ʿUmar] had his need met by him and then left.
ʿUthmān said: Then I asked permission to enter upon him, and he sat up and said to ʿĀʾishah,
"Gather your clothes around you."

So I had my need met and then left. ʿĀʾishah said, "O Messenger of Allah, why did I not see you concerned for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, as you were concerned for ʿUthmān?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"ʿUthmān is a man of modesty, and I feared that if I admitted him while I was in that state, he would not convey to me his need."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Then he mentioned [a narration] like the hadith of ʿUqayl from al-Zuhrī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this chain of narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of Khaybar,
"I will surely give this banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, at whose hands Allah will grant victory."

ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: I never loved leadership except on that day. He said: I stretched myself up for it, hoping that I would be called for it. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and gave it to him, and said,
"Go, and do not turn around, until Allah grants you victory."
He said: ʿAlī went on a little, then stopped without turning around, and cried out, "O Messenger of Allah, on what basis should I fight the people?" He said,

"Fight them until they bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. When they do that, they have protected from you their blood and their wealth, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿUmar

asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the ritual bath after sexual impurity, and the reports agree on this: He would begin by pouring water over his right hand two or three times, then put his right hand into the vessel and pour water with it over his private parts, with his left hand on his private parts, washing what was there until he had cleaned it. Then he would place his left hand on the earth if he wished, then pour water over his left hand until he had cleaned it. Then he would wash his hands three times, rinse his nose and mouth, and wash his face and forearms three times each, until, when he reached his head, he did not wipe it but poured water over it. This is how the washing of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was, according to what was mentioned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That two men

performed dry ablution (tayammum) and prayed, then found water within the time of the prayer. One of them performed ablution and repeated his prayer, which was still within its time, while the other did not repeat it. They asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to the one who did not repeat it: "
You have followed the Sunnah, and your prayer is sufficient for you." And he said to the other: "
As for you, you have the like of the reward of a share of Jamʿ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That two men, and he narrated the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, sent al-Miqdād to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to ask him about a man who finds prostatic fluid (madhy). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
He should wash his private part, then perform ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He asked about] ablution after touching the private part. Marwān said: Busrah bint Ṣafwān informed me of it.
So ʿUrwah sent [someone to her], and she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned what requires ablution, and he said: "
Touching the private part."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

I was brought a mount larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, its stride reaching as far as its sight extended. I rode, and Jibrīl, peace be upon him, was with me, and I set off. He said: Dismount and pray.
I did so, and he said: Do you know where you prayed? You prayed at Ṭaybah, and to it is the migration. Then he said: Dismount and pray.
So I prayed, and he said: Do you know where you prayed? You prayed at Mount Sinai, where Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, spoke to Mūsā, peace be upon him. Then he said: Dismount and pray.
So I dismounted and prayed, and he said: Do you know where you prayed? You prayed at Bethlehem, where ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, was born.

Then I entered Bayt al-Maqdis, and the prophets, peace be upon them, were gathered for me, and Jibrīl put me forward until I led them in prayer. Then he ascended with me to the lowest heaven, and there was Ādam, peace be upon him. Then he ascended with me to the second heaven, and there were the two maternal cousins, ʿĪsā and Yaḥyā, peace be upon them both. Then he ascended with me to the third heaven, and there was Yūsuf, peace be upon him. Then he ascended with me to the fourth heaven, and there was Hārūn, peace be upon him. Then he ascended with me to the fifth heaven, and there was Idrīs, peace be upon him. Then he ascended with me to the sixth heaven, and there was Mūsā, peace be upon him. Then he ascended with me to the seventh heaven, and there was Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him. Then he ascended with me above the seven heavens, and we came to the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and a mist covered me, so I fell down in prostration. Then it was said to me: On the day I created the heavens and the earth, I made obligatory upon you and upon your nation fifty prayers, so establish them, you and your nation.
Then I returned to Ibrāhīm, and he did not ask me about anything. Then I came to Mūsā, and he said: How much has Allah made obligatory upon you and your nation? I said: Fifty prayers.
He said: You and your nation will not be able to keep them up, so return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction.

So I returned to my Lord, and He reduced ten for me. Then I came to Mūsā, and he told me to return, so I returned, and He reduced ten for me. [This continued] until it was brought down to five prayers.
He said: Return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction, for He made two prayers obligatory upon the Children of Israel, and they did not keep them up.

So I returned to my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and asked Him for a reduction, and He said: On the day I created the heavens and the earth, I made obligatory upon you and your nation fifty prayers; so five are in place of fifty, so establish them, you and your nation.

So I knew that it was a final decree (ṣarī) from Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Then I returned to Mūsā, peace be upon him, and he said: Return. But I knew that it was a final decree from Allah — meaning a binding decision — so I did not return."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the prayers

were made obligatory in Makkah, and that two angels came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and took him to Zamzam. They split open his belly and took out its contents in a basin of gold, washed it with Zamzam water, then filled his insides with wisdom and knowledge.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman from Banū Asad said: One day I was with Zaynab, the wife of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we were dyeing some of her garments with red ochre. While we were doing so, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appeared before us. When he saw the ochre, he turned back. When Zaynab saw that, she realized that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked what she had done. So she took her garments and washed them, and hid every trace of redness. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came back and looked in, and when he saw nothing, he entered.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I made a black cloak for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he wore it. When he sweated in it, he noticed the smell of wool, so he threw it off.
He said: And I think he said: He liked pleasant scents.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was sitting wrapped in a single garment with his arms around his knees, and its fringe had fallen onto his feet.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrapped a turban on me and let its end hang down in front of me and behind me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Az-Zuhrī said: ʿUrwah said: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: While we were sitting in our house at the height of noon, someone said to Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him: Here is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ coming, with his head covered, at an hour when he did not usually come to us. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and asked permission, and he was given permission, and he entered.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In Damascus there was a man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ called Ibn al-Ḥanẓaliyyah. He was a man who kept to himself and seldom sat with people; he was only in prayer, and when he finished he was only engaged in glorifying Allah and saying takbīr until he returned to his family. He passed by us while we were with Abū ad-Dardāʾ, and Abū ad-Dardāʾ said to him: Tell us a word that will benefit us and not harm you. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out a detachment. When it returned, one of its men came and sat in the gathering where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to sit, and he said to the man beside him: If only you had seen us when we met the enemy! So-and-so attacked and thrust his spear, and said: Take that from me, I am the Ghifārī youth! What do you think of what he said? The other said: I think his reward has been nullified. Another man heard that and said: I see no harm in it. They disagreed until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard them, and he said:
"Glory be to Allah! There is no harm in him being rewarded and praised."
I saw Abū ad-Dardāʾ delighted by that. He kept raising his head to him and saying: Did you hear that from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? And he would say: Yes.
He kept repeating it to him until I thought he would fall on his knees.
He said: Then another day he passed by us, and Abū ad-Dardāʾ said to him: Tell us a word that will benefit us and not harm you. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:
"The one who spends on horses is like one who stretches out his hand in charity and does not withdraw it."
Then another day he passed by us, and Abū ad-Dardāʾ said to him: Tell us a word that will benefit us and not harm you.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:
"What an excellent man Khuraym al-Asadī is, were it not for the length of his forelock and the trailing of his lower garment."
That reached Khuraym, so he hurried, took a blade, and cut his forelock off up to his ears, and raised his lower garment to the middle of his shins.
Then another day he passed by us, and Abū ad-Dardāʾ said to him: Tell us a word that will benefit us and not harm you. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"You are going to meet your brothers, so put your saddles in good order and make your clothing neat, until you are like a beauty mark among the people. For Allah does not love obscenity or affected obscenity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he was a handsome man. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I am a man to whom beauty has been made dear, and I have been given of it what you see, so that I do not like anyone to surpass me in it, whether it be the strap of my sandal,
or the thong of my sandal. Is that pride? He said:
"No, but pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whatever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about the lower garment applies also to the shirt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw Ibn ʿAbbās wrapping his lower garment so that the front edge of it rested on the tops of his feet and he raised it at the back.
I said: Why do you wear your lower garment this way? He said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wearing it this way.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the man who wears women's clothing and the woman who wears men's clothing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, was told: A woman wears sandals like men.
She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the woman who imitates men.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The fornicator does not commit fornication while he is a believer,
and the thief does not steal while he is a believer,
and the one who drinks [intoxicants] does not drink while he is a believer,
and the one who kills does not kill while he is a believer."

ʿIkrimah said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās, "How is faith removed from him?" He said, "Like this," and he interlaced his fingers, then pulled them apart. "Then if he repents, it returns to him like this," and he interlaced his fingers again.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any hide that has been tanned has become pure."
This ḥadīth is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
Most of the people of knowledge act upon this; they said regarding the skins of dead animals that when they are tanned, they become pure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Numayr, Abū Kurayb and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb, all from Wakīʿ,
Abū Kurayb said: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Al-Awzāʿī narrated to us,
from Ḥassān ibn ʿAṭiyyah,
from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿĀʾishah,
from Abū Hurayrah,
and from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr,
from Abū Salamah,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When one of you recites the tashahhud, let him seek refuge with Allah from four things, saying: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, from the punishment of the grave, from the trials of life and death, and from the evil of the trial of the False Messiah (the Dajjāl)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, (Ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ said:)
"Whoever is going to pray after the Friday prayer, let him pray four [rakʿahs]."
His narration was completed, and Ibn Yūnus said:
"When you have prayed the Friday prayer, pray four after it."
He said: My father said to me, "My son, if you pray two rakʿahs in the mosque, then come to your house or home, pray two [more] rakʿahs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Prompt your dying to say: There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, what about the living?" He said, "[It is] even better, even better."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ died, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ sent word that his funeral procession should pass through the mosque so that they could pray over him. They did so, and he was stopped by their rooms so they could pray over him. Then he was taken out through the Gate of the Funerals, which led to al-Maqāʿid. It reached them that people had criticized this and said, "Funeral biers were never brought into the mosque."
That reached ʿĀʾishah, and she said, "How quick people are to criticize what they have no knowledge of!
They criticized us for a funeral passing through the mosque, yet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over Suhayl ibn Bayḍāʾ only inside the mosque."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sālim ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar informed me from his father,
may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with his hair matted, making the call (talbiyah), saying:
"Labbayk Allāhumma labbayk, labbayk lā sharīka laka labbayk. Inna al-ḥamda wa al-niʿmata laka wa al-mulk, lā sharīka lak."
He did not add to these words.
And ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray two rakʿahs at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah.

Then, when his camel stood upright with him at the mosque of al-Ḥulayfah, he would make the call with these words. And ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, used to say: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, would make the call with the call of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, using these words, and would say: "Labbayk Allāhumma labbayk, labbayk wa saʿdayk, wa al-khayru fī yadayk, labbayk, wa al-raghbāʾu ilayk, wa al-ʿamal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who consumes usury, the one who feeds it to others, its witness, its scribe, the woman who tattoos and the woman who has it done—[he said:] "unless for an illness," and he said, "Yes"—and the one who marries a woman to make her lawful [to her ex-husband] and the one for whom it is done, and the one who withholds charity (ṣadaqah). And he used to forbid wailing [over the dead], but he did not say he cursed [for it].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ disliked the shikāl in horses. And the shikāl is
when a horse has white on its right hind leg and white on its left foreleg,
or on its right foreleg and its left hind leg.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ wiped his head with the water that remained in his hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wipe his head once, until he reached the nape—which is the beginning of the back of the neck. Musaddad said: He wiped his head from its front to its back, until he brought his hands out from beneath his ears.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performing ablution.
Then he mentioned the whole hadith, [with each act done] three times, and said: He wiped his head and his ears with a single wipe.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, how is purification done?" So he called for water in a vessel and washed his hands three times, then washed his face three times, then washed his forearms three times, then wiped his head, inserting his two index fingers into his ears, wiping the outer part of his ears with his thumbs and the inner part of his ears with his index fingers. Then he washed his feet three times each, and then said:
"This is the ablution. Whoever adds to this or subtracts from it has done wrong and has been unjust." Or [he said]: "has been unjust and has done wrong."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ performed ablution washing [each part] twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said to us, "Would you like me to show you

how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform ablution?" So he called for a vessel containing water and scooped up a handful with his right hand, and rinsed his mouth and sniffed water into his nose. Then he took another handful and joined his hands with it, then washed his face. Then he took another and washed his right hand with it, then took another and washed his left hand with it. Then he grasped a handful of water, then shook his hand, and wiped his head and his ears with it. Then he grasped another handful of water and sprinkled it over his right foot, while the sandal was on it, then wiped it with both hands, one hand over the top of the foot and one hand beneath the sandal. Then he did the same with the left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he performed ablution washing [each part] once.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered—meaning—upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was performing ablution, and the water was running from his face and his beard onto his chest. And I saw him separate between rinsing the mouth and sniffing water into the nose.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was the delegate of Banū al-Muntafiq—or [I was] among the delegation of Banū al-Muntafiq—to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: When we came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we did not find him in his house, but we met ʿĀʾishah, the Mother of the Believers. He said: She ordered a khazīrah [meat and flour dish] for us, and it was prepared for us. He said: And we were brought a qināʿ—Qutaybah did not say "al-qināʿ"; the qināʿ is a tray containing dates. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and said:
"Have you had anything, or has anything been ordered for you?"
He said: We said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah."
He said: While we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the shepherd drove his sheep into the pen, and with him was a lamb [newborn] that was bleating. He said:
"What has [the ewe] given birth to, O so-and-so?" He said, "A female lamb."
He said: "Then slaughter a sheep for us in its place."

Then he said, "Do not think—" and he did not say "Do not think" [as an accusation]—"that we slaughtered it for your sake. We have a hundred sheep and do not want the number to increase; so when the shepherd has a lamb born, we slaughter a sheep in its place."
He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have a wife, and there is something in her tongue," meaning foul speech. He said: "Then divorce her."
He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, she has been my companion for a long time, and I have a child by her." He said:
"Then instruct her"—meaning admonish her—"and if there is good in her, she will do so. And do not strike your wife as you would strike your slave woman."
Then I said, "O Messenger of Allah, tell me about ablution." He said:
"Perform ablution thoroughly, run [water] between the fingers, and sniff water into the nose deeply, unless you are fasting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The delegate of Banū al-Muntafiq
came to ʿĀʾishah, then he mentioned a similar meaning.
He said: It was not long before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, walking with a vigorous gait, leaning forward. And he said "ʿaṣīdah" [a thick porridge] in place of "khazīrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution, he would take a handful of water and put it beneath his chin, and run it through his beard with it, and he said:
"This is how my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out a detachment, and they were struck by the cold. When they came back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he ordered them to wipe over their turbans and their footwear.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a man called Marthad ibn Abī Marthad, who used to carry prisoners from Makkah until he brought them to Madinah. He said: There was a prostitute in Makkah called ʿAnāq, who had been his friend, and he had promised a man among the prisoners of Makkah that he would carry him. He said: So I came until I reached the shade of one of the walls of Makkah on a moonlit night.
He said: Then ʿAnāq came and saw the darkness of my shadow beside the wall. When she reached me she recognised me and said: Marthad? I said: Marthad.
She said: Welcome! Come and spend the night with us.
He said: I said: O ʿAnāq, Allah has forbidden fornication.
She said: O people of the tents, this man is carrying off your prisoners!

He said: Eight men followed me, and I took the way of al-Khandamah until I reached a cave or hollow and entered it. They came and stood over my head and urinated, and their urine dripped onto my head, but Allah made them blind to me.

He said: Then they went back, and I returned to my companion and carried him, and he was a heavy man, until I reached al-Idhkhir, where I loosened his shackles. I kept carrying him and he kept helping me until I reached Madinah. I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, shall I marry ʿAnāq? I said it twice. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent and did not reply to me at all, until this was revealed:

"The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or a idolatress, and the fornicatress none marries except a fornicator or an idolater, and that has been forbidden to the believers." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Marthad, the fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress none marries except a fornicator or an idolater, so do not marry her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The divorce of a slave woman is two pronouncements, and her waiting period is two menstrual cycles."
Abū ʿĀṣim said: I mentioned it to Muẓāhir and said: Narrate to me as you narrated to Ibn Jurayj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he divorced his wife with the irrevocable divorce (al-battah). He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him, and he said:
"What did you intend by it?" He said: One. He said:
"By Allah, you intended only one?" He said: By Allah, I intended only one.
He said: So he returned her to him.
