Muḥammad ibn Mājah said: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭanāfisī say: How noble is this hadith!
Ibn Mājah said: Abū ʿUbayd set it aside, and Aḥmad shied away from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do not advance the month by fasting a day or two days before it, unless it is a fast that one of you habitually observes. Do not fast until you see the crescent, then fast until you see it. If clouds come between you and it, complete the count as thirty days, then break the fast. And the month is twenty-nine days."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The chape of the sword of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was of silver, the pommel of his sword was silver, and between them were rings of silver.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bid farewell to a man, he would take his hand and not let go of it until the man himself let go of the hand of the Prophet ﷺ, and he would say:
"I entrust to Allah your religion, your trust, and the end of your deeds."
He said: This hadith is gharīb from this route.
And this hadith has been narrated by more than one route from Ibn ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of companions is four, the best of detachments is four hundred, the best of armies is four thousand, and twelve thousand will not be defeated for being few."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb. No one of note narrates it as a connected chain except Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim. It has only been narrated from al-Zuhrī from the Prophet ﷺ as mursal.
It was also narrated by Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī al-ʿAnazī from ʿUqayl from al-Zuhrī from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh from Ibn ʿAbbās from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Make use of the two cures: honey and the Qur'an."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The ʿajwah dates and the rock are from Paradise."
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I memorized [the mention of] the rock from his mouth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was [one],
who had prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ toward both qiblahs. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
Make use of sanā and sanūt, for in them is a cure for every disease except sām.
It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what is sām? He said: "Death."
ʿAmr said: Ibn Abī ʿAblah said: Sanūt is dill.

Others said: Rather, it is the honey found in ghee skins, and it is the saying of the poet: They smear the ghee with sanūt, there is no lack among them, and they protect their neighbor from being wronged.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ set out early for the prayer, so I set out early too and prayed, then sat down. The Prophet ﷺ turned to me and said: "Does your stomach hurt?"
I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "
Get up and pray, for in prayer there is healing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The cure for sciatica is the fat tail of a Bedouin sheep, melted and then divided into three portions, and one portion is drunk each day on an empty stomach."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I know very well, on the day of Uḥud, who wounded the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who used to stop the bleeding of the wounds on the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and treat it, who carried the water in the shield, and with what the wound was treated until it healed.

He said: As for the one who carried the water in the shield, it was ʿAlī. As for the one who treated the wound, it was Fāṭimah: when it would not heal, she burned a piece of an old mat, placed its ashes on it, and the wound healed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prescribed for pleurisy: wars, qusṭ, and oil, to be poured into the side of the mouth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Make use of Indian aloeswood, meaning qusṭ, for in it are seven cures, among them pleurisy."
Ibn Samʿān said in the ḥadīth: "
For in it is a cure for seven diseases, among them pleurisy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fever was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a man cursed it. The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Do not curse it, for it removes sins just as the fire removes the impurities of iron."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
How excellent a servant is the cupper: he removes blood, lightens the back, and clears the eyesight."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jibrīl came down to the Prophet ﷺ with [the instruction of] cupping the two veins of the neck and the upper back.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ fell from his horse onto the trunk of a palm tree and his foot was dislocated.
Wakīʿ said: He means that the Prophet ﷺ had himself cupped on it because of the sprain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Whoever wishes to be cupped should seek the seventeenth, nineteenth, or twenty-first [of the month], so that the blood does not surge in any of you and kill him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar said: O Nāfiʿ, my blood is surging; bring me a cupper, and make him a young man, not an old man or a boy.
He said: Ibn ʿUmar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "

Cupping on an empty stomach is best. It increases intellect, increases memory, and increases the memory of one who already has a good memory. So whoever intends to be cupped, let it be on Thursday, in the name of Allah. Avoid cupping on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, and be cupped on Monday and Tuesday. Avoid cupping on Wednesday, for it is the day on which Job was afflicted with trial, and leprosy and white leprosy appear only on Wednesday or the night of Wednesday."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yaḥyā said: I have not met a man among us resembling him, narrating to the people that Saʿd ibn Zurārah, who was the maternal grandfather of Muḥammad, was seized by a pain in his throat called the diphtheria, so the Prophet ﷺ said: "
I will certainly try, or I will certainly test [myself], to excuse myself regarding Abū Umāmah."
So he cauterized him with his own hand, and he died. The Prophet ﷺ said: "
What a bad death for [Saʿd]! The Jews say: Why did he not ward it off from his companion?
And I have no power to do anything for him, nor for myself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb fell ill, so the Prophet sent a physician to him, who cauterized him on his arm vein.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He met the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays who had come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Saʿīd said: Qatādah mentioned Abū Naḍrah, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, in this narration of his:

that some people from ʿAbd al-Qays came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Prophet of Allah, we are a clan of Rabīʿah, and between us and you are the disbelievers of Muḍar, and we cannot reach you except in the sacred months. So command us with something that we may instruct those we left behind to do, and by which we may enter Paradise if we adopt it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I command you to do four things and forbid you from four: Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him; establish prayer; give zakāh; fast Ramadan; and give the fifth of the spoils of war. And I forbid you from four: the gourd [containers], the green jars, the tarred vessels, and the hollowed-out [palm trunk]."
They said, "O Prophet of Allah, what do you know of the naqīr?" He said:

"Indeed, [I know it]: a trunk that you hollow out and throw into it some fresh dates"—Saʿīd said, or he said, "some dates"—"then you pour water over them, until, when its boiling subsides, you drink it, so that one of you—or one of them—may strike his cousin with the sword."
He said: Among the people was a man who had been wounded in just such a way.
He said: I had been hiding it out of shyness before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then I said, "Then what should we drink from, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"From skin containers whose mouths are tied."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, our land has many rats, and skin containers do not last there."
The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"Even if the rats eat them, even if the rats eat them, even if the rats eat them."
He said: And the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said to the one with the wound on his face from ʿAbd al-Qays:
"Indeed, you have two qualities that Allah loves: forbearance and deliberateness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ wished to write to a group of non-Arabs, or some people among the non-Arabs,
and it was said to him that they would not accept a letter unless it bore a seal.
So the Prophet ﷺ had a silver ring made, its engraving reading "Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah." It is as if I can see the gleam of the ring on the finger of the Prophet ﷺ, or in his palm.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"If one of you, when he wishes to come to his wife, says, 'In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us, and keep Satan away from what You provide for us,' and then it is decreed that they have a child from that, Satan will never harm it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Makhramah ibn Sulaymān, from Kurayb,
the freed slave of Ibn ʿAbbās, that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him that

he spent a night at the house of Maymūnah, the Mother of the Believers—who was his maternal aunt. He said: I lay down across the width of the pillow, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his wife lay along its length. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ slept until the middle of the night, or a little before it or a little after it. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke up and began wiping the sleep from his face with his hand. Then he recited the last ten verses of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān. Then he got up and went to a hanging water-skin, performed ablution from it, and did his ablution well. Then he stood and prayed.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: So I got up and did as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had done, then went and stood beside him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed his right hand on my head and took hold of my right ear, twisting it. Then he prayed two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then prayed witr. Then he lay down until the muʾadhdhin came. Then he stood and prayed two light rakʿahs, then went out and prayed the Fajr prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up during the night,
[the narration is] similar to it, but they did not say "to pray the night prayer (tahajjud)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Maymūnah said: I set out water for the Prophet ﷺ to bathe with after sexual impurity. He tilted the vessel over his right hand and washed it two or three times. Then he poured water over his private parts and washed them with his left hand. Then he struck the ground with his hand and washed it. Then he rinsed his mouth, sniffed water into his nose, and washed his face and his hands. Then he poured water over his head and body. Then he moved aside and washed his feet. I handed him a towel, but he did not take it, and he began shaking the water off his body.
I mentioned that to Ibrāhīm, and he said: They saw no harm in the towel, but they disliked making it a habit.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "May one of us sleep while in a state of sexual impurity?" He said:
"Yes, when one of you has performed ablution, he may sleep while in a state of sexual impurity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] said to Ibn ʿUmar, "How is the prayer shortened, when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, only said: {There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, if you fear...}?" Ibn ʿUmar said, "O son of my brother, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us while we were astray, and he taught us. Among what he taught us was that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded us to pray two rakʿahs when traveling."
Ash-Shuʿayṭī said: Az-Zuhrī used to narrate this hadith from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying, "O Messenger of Allah, how many prayers has Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made obligatory upon His servants?" He said:
"Allah has made five prayers obligatory upon His servants."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, is there anything before them or after them?" He said:
"Allah has made five prayers obligatory upon His servants."
The man swore that he would not add anything to it nor decrease anything from it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If he is truthful, he will surely enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They kept us busy from the middle prayer until the sun had set."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the times of the prayers, and he said, "Pray with me."

So he prayed Ẓuhr when the sun had passed its zenith, ʿAṣr when the shadow of everything was equal to it, Maghrib when the sun had set, and ʿIshāʾ when the twilight had disappeared. Then he prayed Ẓuhr when a person's shadow was equal to his height, ʿAṣr when a person's shadow was twice his height, and Maghrib shortly before the twilight disappeared.
ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥārith said: Then he said regarding ʿIshāʾ, "I think [it is] up to a third of the night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jibrīl

came to the Prophet ﷺ to teach him the times of the prayers. Jibrīl stepped forward with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ behind him and the people behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he prayed Ẓuhr when the sun had passed its zenith. He came to him when the shadow was equal to a person's height and did as he had done, so Jibrīl stepped forward with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ behind him and the people behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he prayed ʿAṣr. Then he came to him when the sun had set, and Jibrīl stepped forward with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ behind him and the people behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he prayed Maghrib. Then he came to him when the twilight had disappeared, and Jibrīl stepped forward with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ behind him and the people behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he prayed ʿIshāʾ. Then he came to him when dawn broke, and Jibrīl stepped forward with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ behind him and the people behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he prayed the morning prayer. Then he came to him on the second day when a man's shadow was equal to his height, and did as he had done the day before, and he prayed Ẓuhr. Then he came to him when a man's shadow was twice his height, and did as he had done the day before, and he prayed ʿAṣr. Then he came to him when the sun had set, and did as he had done the day before, and he prayed Maghrib. We slept, then got up, then slept, then got up, and he came to him and did as he had done the day before, and he prayed ʿIshāʾ. Then he came to him when the dawn had spread and it was morning, with the stars still visible and crowded together, and did as he had done the day before, and he prayed the morning prayer. Then he said:
"The time for these prayers is between these two [times]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among those of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ who had accepted Islam: they used to pray Maghrib with the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, then return to their families at the farthest edge of Madinah, shooting arrows and seeing where their arrows landed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī and I entered
upon Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī, and we said to him, "Tell us about the prayer of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." This was in the time of al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf.

He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out and prayed Ẓuhr when the sun had passed its zenith, when the shadow was the length of a sandal strap. Then he prayed ʿAṣr when the shadow was the length of a sandal strap plus a man's shadow. Then he prayed Maghrib when the sun had set, then prayed ʿIshāʾ when the twilight had disappeared, then prayed Fajr when dawn broke. The next day he prayed Ẓuhr when the shadow was a man's height, then prayed ʿAṣr when a man's shadow was twice his height, about the time it takes a rider traveling at a steady pace to reach Dhū al-Ḥulayfah. Then he prayed Maghrib when the sun had set, then prayed ʿIshāʾ at a third of the night or half the night (Zayd was unsure), then prayed Fajr when it was bright.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he asked Ibn ʿAbbās about what is pressed from grapes. Ibn ʿAbbās said: A man gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a large skin of wine as a gift, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"Did you know that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden it?"
The man whispered to someone, and I did not understand what he whispered as I wished, so I asked a person beside him. The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "What did you whisper to him about?"
He said: I told him to sell it. Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Indeed, the One who has forbidden drinking it has forbidden selling it."
So the man opened the two waterskins until what was in them poured out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, regarding things that He has forbidden: "and the price of a dog."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that if a man finds his stolen property in the hand of a person who is not suspected, then if he wishes he may take it for the price at which that person bought it, and if he wishes he may pursue the one who stole it from him. Abū Bakr and ʿUmar also ruled in this way.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
was a governor over al-Yamāmah, and that Marwān wrote to him that Muʿāwiyah had written to him that any man from whom something has been stolen is more entitled to it wherever he finds it.

Then Marwān wrote this to me, and I wrote back to Marwān that the Prophet ﷺ ruled that if the one who bought it from the thief is not suspected, its owner is given a choice: if he wishes, he takes it from the one from whom it was stolen by paying its price, and if he wishes, he pursues the thief. Then Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān ruled likewise. So Marwān sent my letter to Muʿāwiyah, and Muʿāwiyah wrote back to Marwān: You and Usayd do not pass judgment over me; rather, I pass judgment over what I have been appointed to govern over you both, so carry out what I commanded you.
So Marwān sent me Muʿāwiyah's letter, and I said: I will not rule by what Muʿāwiyah said for as long as I am in office.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he raised his head to the sky, then placed his palm on his forehead and said:
"Glory be to Allah! What severity has been sent down!"
We remained silent and were alarmed. The next day I asked him: O Messenger of Allah, what is this severity that has been sent down? He said:

"By the One in whose hand is my soul, if a man were killed in the cause of Allah, then brought back to life, then killed, then brought back to life, then killed, while he owed a debt, he would not enter Paradise until his debt is paid on his behalf."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Maymūnah,
the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, took a loan. It was said to her: O Mother of the Believers, you take a loan while you have nothing to repay it with? She said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Whoever takes a debt intending to repay it, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will help him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The best of you are those who are best in repaying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The neighbor has more right to what is near him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled for pre-emption (shufʿah) based on neighborhood.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the son of Muḥayyiṣah the younger
was found killed at the gates of Khaybar. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Bring two witnesses against the one who killed him, and I will hand him over to you in full."
He said: O Messenger of Allah, where can I get two witnesses, when he was only found killed at their gates? He said:
"Then you swear fifty oaths."
He said: O Messenger of Allah, how can I swear about what I do not know? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Then we will have them swear fifty oaths."
He said: O Messenger of Allah, how can we have them swear when they are Jews? So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided his blood money among them and helped them by paying half of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a man came with a leather strap around his neck and said: O Messenger of Allah, this man and my brother were in a well digging it, and he raised the pickaxe and struck his companion on the head with it and killed him. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Pardon him."

But he refused and said: O Prophet of Allah, this man and my brother were in a well digging it, and he raised the pickaxe and struck his companion on the head with it and killed him. He said: "Pardon him."

But he refused. Then he stood up and said: O Messenger of Allah, this man and my brother were in a well digging it, and he raised the pickaxe, I think he said, and struck his companion on the head and killed him. He said: "Pardon him." But he refused. He said:
"Go, if you kill him you will be like him."

So he left with him until he had gone some distance, and we called to him: Do you not hear what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said? So he came back and said: If I kill him, I will be like him? He said: "Yes. Pardon."
Then he went out dragging his strap until he disappeared from us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) was in the lap of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and urinated on him. I said, "Put on another garment and give me your lower garment so that I may wash it." He said:
"Only the urine of a female [infant] is washed, and the urine of a male is sprinkled with water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: (May Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said concerning the urine of a nursing baby boy:
"The urine of the boy is sprinkled with water, and the urine of the girl is washed."
Qatādah said: This applies as long as they have not started eating food; once they have started eating, both are washed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin

entered the mosque while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting, and he prayed two rakʿahs (Ibn ʿAbdah said this), then said, "O Allah, have mercy on me and Muḥammad, and do not have mercy on anyone else along with us." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"You have restricted something wide."
Then it was not long before he urinated in a corner of the mosque, and the people hurried toward him, but the Prophet ﷺ forbade them and said:
"You were sent to make things easy, and you were not sent to make things difficult. Pour a bucket of water over it." Or he said:
"A large bucket of water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A woman] from Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, we have a foul-smelling road to the mosque. What should we do when it rains?" He said:
"Is there not a road after it that is cleaner than it?"
She said: I said, "Yes." He said, "Then this makes up for that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The time of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ Ẓuhr prayer in summer was when the shadow was three to five feet long, and in winter when it was five to seven feet long.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Pray the Fajr prayer when the morning is bright, for that is greater for your reward." Or: "greater for the reward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said that Abū Qatādah ibn Ribʿī informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah the Exalted said: I have made obligatory upon your nation five prayers, and I have made a covenant with Myself that whoever comes having maintained them at their proper times, I will admit him to Paradise; and whoever does not maintain them, he has no covenant with Me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on one of his journeys, and he slept through the Fajr prayer until the sun rose. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke up and said:
"Move away from this place."

He said: Then he ordered Bilāl, who called the adhān. Then they performed ablution and prayed the two rakʿahs of Fajr. Then he ordered Bilāl, who called the iqāmah, and he led them in the Fajr prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ commanded him to make the mosque of Ṭāʾif at the place where their idols had been.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The rewards of my nation were shown to me, even the speck of dust that a man removes from the mosque. And the sins of my nation were shown to me, and I saw no sin greater than a sūrah of the Qurʾān or a verse that a man was given and then forgot."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Command your children to pray when they are seven years old, and discipline them for [neglecting] it when they are ten years old, and separate them from one another in their beds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came—ʿUthmān said: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ—and stood at the door of the Prophet ﷺ asking permission to enter. He stood right at the door—ʿUthmān said: facing the door—so the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "
Move away from there, to this side or that side, for the asking of permission is only because of the sight."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Banū ʿĀmir asked permission to enter upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was in a house, saying: "Shall I come in?" The Prophet ﷺ said to his servant: "
Go out to this man and teach him how to ask permission. Say to him: Say, 'Peace be upon you, may I enter?'"
The man heard him and said, "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" So the Prophet ﷺ permitted him, and he entered.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Banū ʿĀmir asked permission to enter upon the Prophet ﷺ, with similar meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: one,
of their scholars, concerning this. Then ʿUmar said to Abū Mūsā: "I did not suspect you, but I feared that people might falsely attribute statements to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited us in our house and said: "
Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah."
Saʿd replied in a low voice.
Qays said: I said, "Will you not give permission to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?"
He said, "Leave him; he will give us plenty of greetings of peace." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah."
Saʿd again replied in a low voice. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah."

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned back, and Saʿd followed him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I was hearing your greeting and replying to you in a low voice, so that you would give us plenty of greetings of peace."

He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went back with him, and Saʿd ordered water for him to wash, and he washed. Then Saʿd handed him a cloak dyed with saffron or wars, and he wrapped himself in it. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands and said: "
O Allah, send Your blessings and Your mercy upon the family of Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah."

He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ate some of the food. When he wished to leave, Saʿd brought him a donkey over which he had spread a velvet cloth, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mounted. Saʿd said, "O Qays, accompany the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
Qays said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, "Ride."
But I declined. Then he said: "
Either you ride or you go back." He said: So I went back.
Hishām Abū Marwān said, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Asʿad ibn Zurārah
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to the door of a people, he would not face the door directly, but would stand to its right or left side and say: "
Peace be upon you, peace be upon you."
That was because at that time houses had no curtains over their doors.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until I entered a garden. He said to me, "Hold the door."
Then someone knocked on the door and I said, "Who is this?" And he narrated the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
A man's messenger to another man is his permission."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
If one of you is invited to a meal and comes with the messenger, that is his permission."
Abū ʿAlī al-Luʾluʾī said: I heard Abū Dāwūd say: Qatādah did not hear anything from Abū Rāfiʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Most people have not been commanded to act upon it, the verse of permission. And I command this slave girl of mine to ask permission before entering upon me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group

of the people of Iraq said: "O Ibn ʿAbbās, what do you think of this verse in which we were commanded to do what we were commanded, yet no one acts upon it? The words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: {O you who believe, let those whom your right hands possess and those of you who have not reached puberty ask your permission three times: before the dawn prayer, and when you put off your garments at noon, and after the night prayer. These are three times of privacy for you. There is no blame on you or on them after these, as you go around attending to one another} —al-Qaʿnabī recited up to {All-Knowing, All-Wise}. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Allah is Forbearing and Merciful toward the believers and loves concealment. People's houses then had no curtains or canopies, so sometimes a servant, a child, or a man's orphan girl would enter while the man was with his wife. So Allah commanded them to ask permission during those times of privacy. Then Allah brought them curtains and prosperity, and I have not seen anyone act upon that since.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ traced the narration back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [who said]:
"An angel is assigned to the womb. When Allah wills to create something, by Allah's permission, after forty-some nights..."
Then he mentioned a narration similar to theirs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥuṣayn said to me: "What do you think about what people do today and strive for: is it something that has been decreed for them and has already passed, from a destiny that was set beforehand, or is it for what lies ahead of them, based on what their Prophet brought them and the proof established against them?" I said: "Rather, it is something decreed for them and already passed." He said: "Then is that not injustice?" I was extremely alarmed by that, and I said: "Everything is Allah's creation and within His control, so He is not asked about what He does, but they are asked."

Then he said to me: "May Allah have mercy on you. I only asked you in order to test your understanding. Two men from Muzaynah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you think about what people do today and strive for: is it something decreed for them and already passed, from a destiny that was set beforehand, or is it for what lies ahead of them, based on what their Prophet brought them and the proof established against them?' He said:

'No, rather it is something decreed for them and already passed upon them, and the confirmation of that is in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "And [by] the soul and He who proportioned it, and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness."'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A man may do the deeds of the people of Paradise for a long time, then his deeds are sealed with the deeds of the people of the Fire; and a man may do the deeds of the people of the Fire for a long time, then his deeds are sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ. (Another chain follows.)
label: machine translation

segments_en: The hearts of all the children of Adam are between two fingers of the Most Merciful, like a single heart; He turns it however He wills."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, Turner of hearts, turn our hearts to Your obedience."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik ibn Anas. (Another chain:) And Qutaybah narrated to us,
ibn Saʿīd, from Mālik,
in what was read to him, from Ziyād ibn Saʿd,
from ʿAmr ibn Muslim, from Ṭāwūs,
that he said: "I met people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who used to say: 'Everything is by decree.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of Yūnus and Ibn Abī Dhiʾb,
[a narration] like theirs, except that in
the narration of Shuʿayb and Maʿqil, [it says that he] was asked about the children of the polytheists.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Ḥabībah said: "O Allah, let me enjoy my husband, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and my father Abū Sufyān, and my brother Muʿāwiyah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:

"You have asked Allah for appointed terms, numbered footsteps, and apportioned provisions. He will not hasten any of them before its time, nor delay any of them after its time. If you had asked Allah to protect you from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave, it would have been better for you."
A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, are apes and pigs among those who were transformed?" The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not destroy a people or punish a people and then give them offspring. Apes and pigs existed before that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I set out early to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day. He said: He heard the voices of two men who disagreed about a verse, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us, anger visible on his face, and said:
"Those before you were destroyed only because of their disagreement about the Book."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Those who go to extremes in speech and action are ruined." He said it three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
In the narration of Ibn Bishr and ʿAbdah: "No one will narrate it to you after me. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say..." and then he mentioned the like of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave a sermon and urged giving charity.
With the meaning of the narration of Jarīr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jarīr ibn ʿAbdullāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No servant establishes a good practice that is acted upon after him..."
Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ. (Another chain:) And Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us,
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us,
(Another chain:) And Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us,
Abū Usāmah narrated to us,
(Another chain:) And ʿUbaydullāh ibn Muʿādh narrated to us,
my father narrated to us; they said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAwn,
ibn Abī Juḥayfah, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarīr, from his father,
from the Prophet ﷺ, with this hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about a slave woman who commits adultery without being married. He said:
"If she commits adultery, flog her; then if she commits adultery, flog her; then if she commits adultery, flog her; then sell her, even for a rope of hair."
Ibn Shihāb said: "I do not know whether that was after the third time or the fourth."
And al-Qaʿnabī said in his narration: Ibn Shihāb said, "The ḍafīr is the rope."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Barīrah

came to seek help from ʿĀʾishah, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her. ʿĀʾishah said to her, "If your owners would like me to pay your price to them in one payment so that I may free you, I will do so."
Barīrah mentioned that to her owners, and they said no,
unless her walāʾ [right of patronage] would be theirs.
Mālik said: Yaḥyā said: ʿAmrah claimed that ʿĀʾishah mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said, "Buy her and free her,
for the walāʾ belongs only to the one who frees."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Gold for silver is ribā unless it is hand to hand; dates for dates is ribā unless it is hand to hand; wheat for wheat is ribā unless it is hand to hand; and barley for barley is ribā unless it is hand to hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came forward saying, "Who will exchange dirhams?" Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydullāh, who was with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, said, "Show us your gold, then come to us when our servant arrives, and we will give you your silver."
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said, "Never! By Allah, either you give him his silver or you return his gold to him, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

'Silver for gold is ribā unless it is hand to hand; wheat for wheat is ribā unless it is hand to hand; barley for barley is ribā unless it is hand to hand; and dates for dates is ribā unless it is hand to hand.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar, from Zayd
ibn Thābit, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted the owner of an ʿarīyah to sell it for its estimated amount in dates.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade muzābanah: that a man sell the fruit of his orchard, if it is date palms, for dates by measure; if it is grapevines, that he sell it for raisins by measure; and if it is standing crops, that he sell it for a measure of food.
He forbade all of that.
And in the narration of Qutaybah: "or if it was standing crops."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"By Allah, the son of Mary will surely descend as a just ruler. He will break the cross, kill the swine, and abolish the jizyah. Young she-camels will be abandoned so that no one strives after them. Rancor, mutual hatred, and envy will vanish. And he will call people to take wealth, but no one will accept it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was reported to ʿUmar that Samurah
had sold wine. He said, "May Allah fight Samurah! Did he not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'May Allah fight the Jews! Fats were forbidden to them, so they melted them down and sold them.'"
Sufyān said: "That is, they melted them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I took part in the campaign of al-ʿUsrah with the Prophet ﷺ. [ʿAṭāʾ] said: Yaʿlā used to say, "That expedition was the most trustworthy of my deeds in my view."
ʿAṭāʾ said: Ṣafwān said: Yaʿlā said, "I had a hired man who fought with another person, and one of them bit the hand of the other."
ʿAṭāʾ said: Ṣafwān told me which of them bit the other, but I have forgotten.
He said: The one who was bitten pulled his hand out of the biter's mouth,
and pulled out one of the biter's front teeth.
They came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he declared the tooth without compensation.
ʿAṭāʾ said: I think he said that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Should he leave his hand in your mouth for you to chew on it
as if it were in the mouth of a stallion chewing it?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to her, "I think that if a man did not walk between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, it would not harm him."
She said, "Why do you say that?" I said, "Because Allah, the Exalted, says: {Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah} to the end of the verse."

She said, "Allah does not complete the Hajj of anyone, nor his ʿUmrah, who does not walk between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. If it were as you say, it would have read: 'There is no blame on him if he does not walk between them.'
Do you know why that was revealed? It was because the Anṣār, in the pre-Islamic period, used to declare their pilgrim sacred state for two idols on the seashore called Isāf and Nāʾilah.
Then they would come and walk between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and then shave their heads.

When Islam came, they disliked walking between them because of what they used to do in the pre-Islamic period." She said, "So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah} to its end." She said, "So they walked [between them]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed from ʿArafah with Usāmah riding behind him. Usāmah said: He continued to travel at his [steady] pace until he reached Jamʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me out in the last part of the night from Jamʿ, with the baggage of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ.
I said, "Did it reach you that Ibn ʿAbbās said, 'He sent me in the long dark of the night'?" He said, "No, it was only like that: in the last part of the night."
I said to him, "Ibn ʿAbbās said, 'We threw the pebbles at the Jamrah before dawn.'"
[He asked,] "And where did he pray the dawn prayer?" He said, "No, it was only like that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While he was delivering a sermon on the pulpit, [he said:] "Compile the Qurʾān as Jibrīl compiled it: the sūrah in which al-Baqarah is mentioned, then the sūrah in which al-Nisāʾ is mentioned, then the sūrah in which Āl ʿImrān is mentioned."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Cleaning oneself with stones is an odd number, throwing the pebbles is an odd number, running between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah is an odd number, and the circumambulation is an odd number. When one of you cleans himself with stones, let him do so with an odd number."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"May Allah have mercy on those who shave their heads."
They said, "And those who shorten [their hair], O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"May Allah have mercy on those who shave their heads."
They said, "And those who shorten [their hair], O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"May Allah have mercy on those who shave their heads."
They said, "And those who shorten [their hair], O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "And those who shorten [their hair]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Minā, went to the Jamrah and threw pebbles at it, then came to his lodging in Minā and sacrificed. Then he said to the barber, "Take."
And he indicated his right side, then the left, then began giving [his hair] to the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood on his mount and people began asking him. One of them said, "O Messenger of Allah, I did not realize that the stoning comes before the sacrifice, so I sacrificed before stoning."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Throw, and there is no harm."
He said: Another began saying, "I did not realize that the sacrifice comes before the shaving, so I shaved before I sacrificed." He said:
"Sacrifice, and there is no harm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when a man came to him on the Day of Sacrifice as he was standing at the Jamrah, and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I shaved my head before I threw the pebbles." He said:
"Throw, and there is no harm."
Another came to him and said, "I slaughtered before I threw the pebbles." He said:
"Throw, and there is no harm."
Another came to him and said, "I went to the House [for ṭawāf] before I threw the pebbles." He said:
"Throw, and there is no harm."
He said: I did not see him asked about anything that day except that he said:
"Do it, and there is no harm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar
considered stopping at al-Muḥaṣṣab to be a sunnah, and he would pray the Ẓuhr prayer at al-Ḥaṣbah on the day of departure.
Nāfiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at al-Muḥaṣṣab, and so did the caliphs after him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Rāfiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not instruct me to stop at al-Abṭaḥ when he left Minā, but I came and pitched his tent there, and he came and stopped.
Abū Bakr said, in the narration of Ṣāliḥ: He said, I heard Sulaymān ibn Yasār.
And in the narration of Qutaybah he said, from Abū Rāfiʿ, who was in charge of the baggage of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥātim and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, both from Muḥammad ibn Bakr,
Ibn Jurayj informed us,
both from ʿUbaydullāh,
ibn ʿUmar, with this chain, the same [narration].
label: machine translation

segments_en: To Abū Maḥdhūrah: "Uncle, I am going out to Syria and I will be asked about your call to prayer, so tell me." He said that Abū Maḥdhūrah said: "I went out with a group of people, and while we were somewhere on the road, the muʾadhdhin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called the adhān for prayer in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We heard the voice of the muʾadhdhin while we were away from him, so we shouted, imitating him in mockery. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard, and he sent some men to us, who made us sit before him. He said:
'Which of you is the one whose voice I heard raised?'
The people all pointed to me, and they spoke the truth. So he released all of them and kept me back, and he said to me: 'Stand and call the adhān.'

So I stood, and nothing was more hateful to me than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ or than what he was ordering me to do. I stood before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah himself taught me the adhān. He said:
'Say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh; ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlullāh, ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlullāh.'
Then he said to me:

'Go back and raise your voice: ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh; ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlullāh, ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlullāh; ḥayya ʿalā aṣ-ṣalāh, ḥayya ʿalā aṣ-ṣalāh; ḥayya ʿalā al-falāḥ, ḥayya ʿalā al-falāḥ; Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; lā ilāha illā Allāh.'

Then, when I had finished the adhān, he called me and gave me a pouch containing some silver. Then he placed his hand on the forelock of Abū Maḥdhūrah and passed it over his face from the front, then over his chest, until the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached Abū Maḥdhūrah's navel. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'May Allah bless you and bestow blessings upon you.'
I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you are ordering me to call the adhān in Makkah?' He said:
'Yes, I have ordered you.'

So all the hatred I had felt toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went away, and it all turned into love for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then I went to ʿAttāb ibn Asīd, the governor of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Makkah, and I called the adhān for prayer with him by the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:

"When Solomon son of David ﷺ built Bayt al-Maqdis, he asked Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for three things: he asked Allah for judgment that would coincide with His judgment, and he was given it; he asked Allah for a kingdom that would not be fitting for anyone after him, and he was given it; and when he finished building the mosque, he asked Allah that no one who comes to it, driven only by the desire to pray in it, would leave it except free of his sins as on the day his mother bore him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb

stood on Friday to deliver the sermon, or he delivered a sermon on Friday, and he praised Allah and extolled Him. Then he said: "O people, you eat two plants which I only consider foul: this garlic and this onion. I saw a man in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whose smell could be detected on him, and he would be taken by the hand until he was brought out to al-Baqīʿ. So whoever must eat them, let him kill their smell by cooking."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade buying and selling, and the reciting of poetry to one another, in the mosques.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw phlegm on the qiblah wall of the mosque and became angry until his face turned red. A woman of the Anṣār stood up and scraped it off and put khalūq perfume in its place. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"How excellent this is!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I and al-Faḍl came

on a donkey of ours while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was leading the people in prayer at ʿArafah. Then he mentioned a phrase to the effect that: we passed in front of part of the row, so we dismounted and left the donkey to graze, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said nothing to us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he had finished his seven circuits, come until he was level with the corner, and pray two rakʿahs at the edge of the circumambulation area, with no one between him and those performing ṭawāf.
Ibn Mājah said: This applies to Makkah specifically.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he delivered a sermon in war,
would deliver it leaning on a bow.
And when he delivered the sermon on Friday,
he would deliver it leaning on a staff.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was asked: "Did the Prophet ﷺ deliver the sermon standing or sitting?"
He said: "Have you not read: {and they left you standing}?" Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: This is a rare report; only Ibn Abī Shaybah narrates it, on his own.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ ascended the pulpit, he would give the greeting of peace.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited Sūrat Tabārak on Friday while standing.
He reminded us of the Days of Allah, while Abū al-Dardāʾ or Abū Dharr was nudging me. He said:
"When was this sūrah revealed?
I had not heard it until now." So he gestured to him to be quiet.
When they finished the prayer, he said:
"I asked you when this sūrah was revealed and you did not tell me?" My father said:
"You have nothing from your prayer today except what you wasted in idle talk."
So he went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, mentioned that to him, and told him what my father had said.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ubayy spoke the truth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever catches one rakʿah of the Friday prayer, let him add another to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of Qubāʾ used to pray the Friday prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Beware! Perhaps one of you will keep a small flock of sheep a mile or two away,
and the pasture becomes scarce for him, so he moves on.
Then Friday comes and he does not come or attend it; and Friday comes and he does not attend it,
and Friday comes and he does not attend it,
until his heart is sealed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray four rakʿahs before the Friday prayer,
without separating between any of them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ stood on the pulpit, his Companions would turn their faces toward him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting: "We find in the Book of Allah that on Friday there is an hour which no believing servant meets while praying and asking Allah for something in it, except that Allah fulfils his need."
ʿAbd Allāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gestured to me: "or part of an hour." I said: "You have spoken the truth,
or part of an hour." I said:
"Which hour is it?" He said: "
It is the last hour of the hours of the day." I said:
"It is not an hour of prayer." He said: "Yes it is.
When the believing servant prays and then sits,
nothing detaining him except the prayer,
he is in prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ made ablution, he would pray two rakʿahs and then go out to the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray the two rakʿahs at the time of the iqāmah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ slept through the two rakʿahs of the dawn prayer.
So he made them up after the sun had risen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father sent a message to ʿĀʾishah: "Which prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was most beloved to him to keep up regularly?" She said:
He used to pray four rakʿahs before Ẓuhr.
He would lengthen the standing in them,
and perform the bowing and prostration well in them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah sent someone to Umm Salamah, and I went with the messenger, who asked Umm Salamah. She said: "While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was performing ablution in my house for Ẓuhr, he had sent out a collector, and many of the Emigrants were with him, and their affairs concerned him, when the door was knocked. He went out to it, prayed Ẓuhr, then sat dividing what had come.
She said: He continued like that until ʿAṣr.
Then he entered my house and prayed two rakʿahs, then said:
"The matter of the collector kept me busy from praying these two after Ẓuhr, so I have prayed them after ʿAṣr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the muʾadhdhin would call the adhān, and one would think it was the iqāmah because of the many people who stood and prayed the two rakʿahs before Maghrib.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us among Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal and led us in the Maghrib prayer in our mosque. Then he said:
"Pray these two rakʿahs in your homes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah is Witr (One) and loves the Witr, so pray Witr, O people of the Qurʾān."
A Bedouin said: "What is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying?" He said: "
It is not for you nor for your companions."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to fast on Mondays and Thursdays.
It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, you fast on Monday and Thursday?" He said,
"On Mondays and Thursdays Allah forgives every Muslim, except two who have forsaken each other. He says: Leave them until they reconcile."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Prophet of Allah, I am the man who came to you last year." He said,
"Why do I see your body so emaciated?"
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have not eaten any food during the day; I have only eaten at night." He said,
"Who commanded you to torment yourself?"
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am strong." He said,
"Fast the month of patience and one day after it."
I said, "I am strong." He said,
"Fast the month of patience and two days after it."
I said, "I am strong." He said,
"Fast the month of patience and three days after it, and fast the sacred months."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade fasting in Rajab.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Usāmah ibn Zayd
used to fast during the sacred months.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Fast Shawwāl."
So he left off the sacred months and continued to fast Shawwāl until he died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Everything has its zakāh, and the zakāh of the body is fasting."
Muḥriz added in his narration that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Fasting is half of patience."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Bilāl,
"Come to the meal, O Bilāl."
He said, "I am fasting."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"We eat of our provisions, while the surplus of Bilāl's provision is in Paradise. Did you know, O Bilāl, that the fasting person's bones glorify Allah, and the angels seek forgiveness for him as long as food is eaten in his presence?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Indeed, the fasting person has, at the time of breaking his fast, a supplication that is not rejected."
Ibn Abī Mulaykah said: I heard ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr say, when he broke his fast: "O Allah, I ask You by Your mercy which encompasses everything, that You forgive me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would not go out in the morning on the day of Fiṭr until he had fed his Companions from the charity of Fiṭr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [to announce] the conversion of Thaqīf to Islam.
He said: They came to him in Ramadan, and he pitched a tent for them in the mosque. When they became Muslims, they fasted the remainder of the month.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade women to fast except with the permission of their husbands.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that when he observed iʿtikāf, his bedding was laid out for him, or his bed was placed for him, behind the Pillar of Repentance.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ observed iʿtikāf in a Turkish tent, at whose doorway was a piece of matting.
He said: He took the matting in his hand and moved it aside to one side of the tent, then looked out with his head and spoke to the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The one in iʿtikāf follows funeral processions and visits the sick."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about the one in iʿtikāf,
"He is restrained from sins, and good deeds are recorded for him like the doer of all good deeds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever stands in prayer during the two nights of the two Eids for the sake of Allah, seeking reward, his heart will not die on the day when hearts die."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"The camels from which the due right was not given will come and trample their owner with their hooves; the cattle and sheep will come and trample their owner with their cloven hooves and gore him with their horns; and the treasure will come as a bald-headed serpent and meet its owner on the Day of Resurrection. Its owner will flee from it twice, then it will confront him and he will flee, and he will say, 'What do I have to do with you?'
It will say, 'I am your treasure, I am your treasure.'
He will shield himself from it with his hand, and it will swallow it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿĀʾishah,
that the Prophet ﷺ used to take from every twenty dinars and above half a dinar, and from forty dinars, one dinar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"When you give zakāh, do not forget its reward: say, 'O Allah, make it a gain and do not make it a loss.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this [chain].
And from Ḥabīb ibn Abī ʿAmrah,
from ʿĀʾishah bint Ṭalḥah,
from ʿĀʾishah, the Mother of the Believers,
from the Prophet ﷺ: His wives asked him about jihad, and he said:
"The best jihad is Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Thaʿlabah ibn Abī Mālik [reported] that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, distributed some woollen garments among women of the women of Madinah,
and one fine garment was left over.
Some of those with him said to him, "O Commander of the Faithful, give this to the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who is with you,"
meaning Umm Kulthūm, the daughter of ʿAlī.
ʿUmar said, "Umm Salīṭ has more right to it."
Umm Salīṭ was one of the women of the Anṣār who had pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
ʿUmar said, "She used to carry the water-skins for us on the day of Uḥud."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to go on expeditions with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, giving the people water and serving them,
and returning the slain and the wounded to Madinah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū ʿĀmir was struck by an arrow in his knee,
so I came to him, and he said, "Pull out this arrow." So I pulled it out,
and water gushed out from it.
Then I went to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and he said:
"O Allah, forgive ʿUbayd Abū ʿĀmir."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Wretched is the slave of the dinar, the slave of the dirham, and the slave of the velvet cloak:
if he is given, he is pleased,
and if he is not given, he is displeased. May he be wretched and fall back,
and if a thorn pricks him, may he not find it removed.
Blessed is the servant who takes hold of the reins of his horse in the cause of Allah,
with disheveled hair and dusty feet:
if he is assigned to the guard, he is at the guard,
and if he is assigned to the rear, he is at the rear.
If he asks permission, he is not given permission,
and if he intercedes, his intercession is not accepted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to Abū Ṭalḥah:
"Look for one of your boys to serve me until I go out to Khaybar."
So Abū Ṭalḥah took me out, having me ride behind him,
and I was a boy who had nearly reached puberty.
I would serve the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whenever he stopped,
and I often heard him say:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from miserliness and cowardice, from the burden of debt and from being overpowered by men."
Then we arrived at Khaybar,
and when Allah gave him victory over the fortress, the beauty of Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab was mentioned to him,
her husband having been killed, and she being a bride,
so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ chose her for himself,
and he set out with her until, when we reached Sadd aṣ-Ṣahbāʾ, she became lawful for him, and he consummated the marriage with her.
Then he made ḥays on a small leather mat,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Invite those around you."
That was the wedding feast of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for Ṣafiyyah.
Then we set out for Madinah. [Anas] said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrapping a cloak around her behind him,
then sitting by his camel and putting down his knee,
and Ṣafiyyah would place her foot on his knee until she mounted.
We traveled on until, when we came in sight of Madinah, he looked at Uḥud and said:
"This is a mountain that loves us and we love it."
Then he looked at Madinah and said:
"O Allah, I declare sacred what lies between its two lava plains, just as Ibrāhīm declared Makkah sacred.
O Allah, bless them in their mudd and their ṣāʿ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd, may Allah be pleased with him, thought that he had superiority over those below him, so the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Are you given victory and provision except because of your weak ones?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ṭalḥah used to shield himself together with the Prophet ﷺ behind a single shield,
and Abū Ṭalḥah was a good archer,
so whenever he shot, the Prophet ﷺ would raise himself up and look to where his arrow landed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said, while in his tent on the day of Badr:
"I implore You by Your covenant and Your promise.
O Allah, if You will, You will not be worshipped after today ever."
Then Abū Bakr took him by the hand and said, "That is enough for you, O Messenger of Allah; you have pleaded earnestly with your Lord."
He was wearing his coat of mail, and he went out saying:
"{Their multitude will be defeated and they will turn their backs. Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more grievous and more bitter.}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ṭalḥah sent me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to invite him, for he had prepared food. I came, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with the people. He looked at me and I felt shy, so I said, "Answer Abū Ṭalḥah's invitation." Then he said to the people, "Get up."
Abū Ṭalḥah said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have only prepared a little something for you." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ touched it, invoked blessing upon it, and then said,
"Let ten of my Companions come in." And he said, "Eat."
And he brought out something for them from between his fingers, and they ate until they were full and went out. Then he said, "Let ten come in."
They ate until they were full.
He kept on letting ten in and ten out until not one of them remained but had entered, eaten, and been filled. Then he prepared it, and it was as it had been when they began eating from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked him about performing ablution after eating what fire had touched.
He said, "No. In the time of the Prophet ﷺ we would find such food only rarely,
and when we did find it, we had no napkins,
except our palms, our forearms, and our feet.
Then we would pray and not perform ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A boy was born to me,
and I brought him to the Prophet ﷺ, who named him Ibrāhīm and softened a date and rubbed it on his palate,
and invoked blessing upon him and handed him back to me.
He was the eldest child of Abū Mūsā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A son of Abū Ṭalḥah was ill.
Abū Ṭalḥah went out,
and the boy died. When Abū Ṭalḥah returned, he said, "What has become of my son?" Umm Sulaym said, "He is more at rest than he has ever been."
Then she served him his supper and he ate,
and then he was intimate with her.
When he had finished, she said, "Bury the boy."
In the morning Abū Ṭalḥah went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him. He said, "Were you intimate last night?" He said, "Yes." He said,
"O Allah, bless them both."
She gave birth to a boy. Abū Ṭalḥah said to me, "Look after him until you bring him to the Prophet ﷺ." So he brought him to the Prophet ﷺ, and she sent some dates with him.
The Prophet ﷺ took him and said, "Is there anything with him?"
They said, "Yes, some dates."
The Prophet ﷺ took them and chewed them,
then took them from his mouth and put them in the boy's mouth and rubbed his palate with them,
and named him ʿAbdullāh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughaffal saw one of his companions throwing pebbles with his fingers. He said to him, "Do not throw pebbles, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked—or he said, forbade—throwing pebbles, because no game is hunted with it and no enemy is harmed by it, but it may break a tooth and put out an eye."

Later he saw him throwing pebbles again and said to him, "I tell you that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked or forbade throwing pebbles, and then I see you throwing pebbles! I will not speak to you for such and such a time."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, one of us shoots game and follows its trail for two or three days, then finds it dead with his arrow in it. May he eat it?" He said,
"Yes, if he wishes." Or he said,
"He may eat it if he wishes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whatever causes blood to flow and has the name of Allah mentioned over it, eat it, except for a tooth or a nail."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn ʿUmar when they passed by some youths, or a group of people, who had set up a hen and were shooting at it.
When they saw Ibn ʿUmar, they scattered away from it,
and Ibn ʿUmar said, "Who did this? The Prophet ﷺ cursed whoever does this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to sacrifice two rams.
Anas said, "And I sacrifice two rams."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us on the day of Aḍḥā, then turned to two white-and-black rams and slaughtered them. (Abridged)
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Burdah slaughtered before the prayer, so the Prophet ﷺ said to him, "Replace it."
He said, "I have only a young ram [jadhaʿah]." Shuʿbah said, "I think he said: it is better than a full-grown one." He said, "Make it [the sacrifice] in its place,
but it will not suffice for anyone after you."
Ḥātim ibn Wardān said, from Ayyūb, from Muḥammad, from Anas,
from the Prophet ﷺ, and he said, "a young kid [ʿanāq jadhaʿah]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Whoever among you offers a sacrifice, let him not be left after the third day with any of it in his house."
The following year they said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall we do as we did last year?" He said,
"Eat, feed others, and store [it], for that year the people were in hardship, and I wanted you to help them in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in the state of iḥrām, and the lice on my head became many. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, so he came to me while I was cooking a pot [of food] for my companions. He touched my head with his finger and said:
"Go and shave it, and give charity (ṣadaqah) to six poor people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ set out at night from al-Jiʿrānah when he went to perform ʿUmrah. He spent the morning in al-Jiʿrānah as one who had spent the night there, until, when the sun had passed its zenith, he left al-Jiʿrānah through the valley of Sarif until he joined the road, the road to Madinah, from Sarif.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ set out from al-Jiʿrānah at night, as if he were a bar of silver, and performed ʿUmrah. Then he spent the morning there as one who had spent the night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of the conquest of Makkah:

"This city is sacred; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made it sacred. Fighting in it was not permitted to anyone before me, and it was permitted to me for an hour of a day. So it is sacred by the sanctity [decreed] by Allah, Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Armies will not cease to attack this House until an army of them is swallowed up by the earth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"An army will be sent to this Sanctuary, and when they are in an open desert of the land, the first and last of them will be swallowed up by the earth, and the middle of them will not be saved."
I said: "What if there are believers among them?" He said:
"The [earth] will be their graves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Khayf in Minā when {By those sent forth in succession} was revealed. A snake came out, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Kill it."
So we rushed toward it, but it entered its hole.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of ʿArafah, the one before the day of ʿArafah, when [we] sensed a snake. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Kill it."
It entered a crack in a hole. We put a stick in and dug out part of the hole, then took a palm frond and set fire to it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah protected it from your evil and protected you from its evil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The gecko is a wrongdoer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I not enter the House?" He said:
"Enter the Ḥijr, for it is part of the House."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He entered the House together with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. [The Prophet ﷺ] commanded Bilāl, who closed the door, and the House at that time was on six pillars. He went on until, when he was between the two pillars nearest the door of the Kaʿbah, he sat, praised Allah and extolled Him, asked Him and sought His forgiveness. Then he stood until he came to the part facing the back wall of the Kaʿbah, and placed his face and cheek against it, praised Allah and extolled Him, asked Him and sought His forgiveness. Then he went to each corner of the Kaʿbah and faced it with takbīr, tahlīl, tasbīḥ, praise of Allah, supplication and seeking forgiveness. Then he went out and prayed two rakʿahs facing the front of the Kaʿbah. Then he turned away and said:
"This is the qiblah, this is the qiblah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered the House with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He sat, praised Allah and extolled Him, said takbīr and tahlīl. Then he leaned toward the part of the House in front of him and placed his chest, cheek and hands against it. Then he said takbīr and tahlīl and supplicated. He did that at all the corners. Then he went out and turned to face the qiblah while at the door, and said:
"This is the qiblah, this is the qiblah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out of the House, prayed two rakʿahs in front of the Kaʿbah, and then said: "This is the qiblah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a man who was being led by another man with something, which he mentioned, tied on account of a vow. The Prophet ﷺ took hold of it and cut it. [The man] said: "It is a vow."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He met the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"Circumambulation of the House is prayer, so speak little during it." The wording is Yūsuf's.
Ḥanẓalah ibn Abī Sufyān differed from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: "Speak little during circumambulation, for you are only in prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She came to Makkah while she was ill, and mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:
"Circumambulate behind the people praying, while riding."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to Aṣ-Ṣafā and climbed it until the House became visible to him. Then he declared the oneness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and glorified Him, and said:
"There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise. He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things."

Then he walked until, when his feet came down into the valley, he ran; then, when his feet rose out of it, he walked until he reached Al-Marwah. There he did as he had done on Aṣ-Ṣafā, until he completed his circuits.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I trimmed some of the ends of the hair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a broad arrowhead that I had with me, after he had circled the House and [walked between] Aṣ-Ṣafā and Al-Marwah, in the ten days.
Qays said: The people disapprove of this regarding Muʿāwiyah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, thinking only of Hajj. She said: When he had circled the House and [walked] between Aṣ-Ṣafā and Al-Marwah, he said:
"Whoever has brought a sacrificial animal with him should remain in his state of iḥrām, and whoever has not brought a sacrificial animal should leave iḥrām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Farewell Hajj. Some of us entered iḥrām for Hajj, and some for ʿUmrah and brought a sacrificial animal. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah and did not bring a sacrificial animal should leave iḥrām; whoever entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah and brought a sacrificial animal should not leave iḥrām; and whoever entered iḥrām for Hajj should complete his Hajj."
ʿĀʾishah said: I was among those who entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Abū Qurrah Mūsā ibn Ṭāriq, from Ibn Jurayj,
who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym told me,
from Abū az-Zubayr, from Jābir,

that when the Prophet ﷺ returned from the ʿUmrah of Al-Jiʿrānah, he sent Abū Bakr to lead the Hajj. We set out with him, and when he was at Al-ʿArj, the call for the dawn prayer was made. Then he stood straight to say the takbīr, and he heard a groaning sound behind him, so he paused before the takbīr and said: "That is the groaning of the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Al-Jadʿāʾ. Something must have occurred to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding the Hajj; perhaps it is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself, and we will pray with him." But it was ʿAlī on her. Abū Bakr said to him: "Are you a commander or a messenger?" He said: "Rather a messenger. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me with [the declaration of] Barāʾah to recite to the people at the standing places of the Hajj."

We came to Makkah, and the day before the Day of Tarwiyah, Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and addressed the people, telling them about their rites until he finished. Then ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and recited Barāʾah to the people until he completed it. Then we went out with him, and on the Day of ʿArafah Abū Bakr stood and addressed the people, telling them about their rites until he finished; then ʿAlī stood and recited Barāʾah to the people until he completed it. Then on the Day of Sacrifice we poured forth [from ʿArafah and Muzdalifah]. When Abū Bakr returned, he addressed the people, telling them about their pouring forth, their sacrifice and their rites; when he finished, ʿAlī stood and recited Barāʾah to the people until he completed it. Then on the Day of the First Departure, Abū Bakr stood and addressed the people, telling them how to depart and how to throw the pebbles, and he taught them their rites. When he finished, ʿAlī stood and recited Barāʾah to the people until he completed it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [This was] a reading to him while I listened,
from Ibn al-Qāsim, who said: Mālik told me,
from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥalḥalah ad-Duʾalī,
from Muḥammad ibn ʿImrān al-Anṣārī, from his father,
who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar turned aside toward me while I was stopping
beneath a tree on the road to Makkah, and said: "What made you stop under this tree?" I said: "Its shade made me stop."
ʿAbdullāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When you are between the two rugged mountains of Minā"—and he blew with his hand toward the east—"there is a valley there called As-Sarabah"—and in the narration of Al-Ḥārith, "called As-Sarar"—"in which there is a tree beneath which seventy prophets had their umbilical cords cut."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās at ʿArafāt, and he said: "Why do I not hear the people saying the Talbiyah?" I said: "They fear Muʿāwiyah."
So Ibn ʿAbbās came out of his tent and said: "Labbayk, Allāhumma labbayk, labbayk!" For they have abandoned the Sunnah out of hatred for ʿAlī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray each prayer at its proper time, except at Jamʿ [Muzdalifah] and ʿArafāt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Usāmah ibn Zayd said: I was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ at ʿArafāt, and he raised his hands in supplication. His she-camel tilted with him and her halter fell, so he took hold of the halter with one hand while keeping the other hand raised.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When the time draws near, the dream of the believer will hardly ever be false,
and the dream of the believer is one forty-sixth part of prophecy."
Muḥammad said: And I say this. He said: It used to be said that dreams are of three kinds: the talk of the soul, the frightening by Satan,
and glad tidings from Allah.
So whoever sees something he dislikes, let him not relate it to anyone, and let him get up and pray.
He said: He used to dislike the iron collar in sleep,
and they were pleased with the shackle [in a dream],
and it used to be said that the shackle is steadfastness in religion.
Qatādah, Yūnus, Hishām and Abū Hilāl narrated it from Ibn Sīrīn, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, and some of them included all of it within the hadith,
while the hadith of ʿAwf is clearer.
And Yūnus said: I think it is only from the Prophet ﷺ regarding the shackle.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh and Abū Mūsā sat and conversed, and Abū Mūsā said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
