Before the Hour there will be days in which knowledge will be taken away,
and ignorance will descend,
and harj will become abundant, and harj is killing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The Euphrates is about to uncover a treasure of gold,
so whoever is present at it should not take anything from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
No prophet was sent except that he warned his people about the one-eyed liar,
Indeed, he is one-eyed,
and indeed your Lord is not one-eyed,
and between his eyes is written: Disbeliever."
On this topic there are reports from Abū Hurayrah and Ibn ʿAbbās from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah."
And he used to seek refuge from the punishment of the grave, the punishment of Hellfire, the trial of the living and the dead, and the trial of the Antichrist, the Dajjāl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd,
who said: ʿUbādah ibn al-Walīd ibn ʿUbādah informed me,
who said: My father narrated to me, from ʿUbādah,

who said: We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to hear and obey in ease and hardship, in what we like and dislike, not to dispute the matter with those entrusted with it, and to speak, or to stand for, the truth wherever we may be, fearing no blame from any critic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with my father when he was wounded, and they praised him and said: May Allah reward you with good.

He said: [I am] one hoping and fearing. They said: Appoint a successor. He said: Shall I bear the burden of your affair both in my life and in my death? I wish that my share of it would be just enough, neither against me nor for me. If I appoint a successor, then one who was better than me appointed a successor, meaning Abū Bakr, and if I leave you, then one who was better than me left you, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
ʿAbdullāh said: So I knew that when he mentioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would not appoint a successor.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Allah, the Exalted, says: I am as My servant thinks of Me,
and I am with him when he remembers Me.
If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself,
and if he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than them.
If he draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by an arm's length,
and if he draws near to Me by an arm's length, I draw near to him by a fathom,
and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no good deed that the son of Adam does except that ten good deeds are recorded for him, up to seven hundred fold. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: Except fasting, for it is for Me and I reward for it. He gives up his desire and his food for My sake. Fasting is a shield for the one who fasts. The one who fasts has two joys: a joy when he breaks his fast and a joy when he meets his Lord. And the odor from the mouth of the one fasting is better with Allah than the fragrance of musk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked which deeds are best, and he said: "
Prayer at the beginning of its time."
Al-Khuzāʿī said in his narration, from a paternal aunt of his called Umm Farwah, who had pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ, that the Prophet ﷺ was asked.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "

The disease of the nations before you has crept upon you: envy and hatred. It is the shaver. I do not say it shaves hair, but it shaves religion. By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not tell you of what will establish that for you? Spread greeting of peace among yourselves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The unlettered Prophet ﷺ made a covenant with me: "
None will love you except a believer, and none will hate you except a hypocrite."
ʿAdī ibn Thābit said: I am of the generation for whom the Prophet ﷺ prayed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out on a rainy night, and when I returned I asked to be let in. My father said, "Who is this?" He said, "Abū al-Malīḥ."
He said: "I saw us with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Ḥudaybiyah, when rain fell on us that did not even wet the soles of our sandals. Then the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called out:
'Pray in your dwellings.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said on a rainy Friday:
"Pray in your dwellings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās
ordered the muʾadhdhin to call the adhān
on Friday, and that was a rainy day. So he said: "Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah. I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah."
Then he said, "Call out to the people to pray in their homes."

The people said to him, "What is this that you have done?" He said, "This was done by one who is better than me. Would you have me make the people leave their homes and come to me trampling through mud up to their knees?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A short spear used to be brought out for the Prophet ﷺ when travelling,
and he would plant it and pray facing it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"If one of you knew what [sin] he bears for passing in front of his brother while he is praying, it would be better for him to stand still for a hundred years than to take that step."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was praying in the room of Umm Salamah, and ʿAbdullāh or ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah passed in front of him. He gestured with his hand, and the boy turned back. Then Zaynab, the daughter of Umm Salamah, passed, and he gestured with his hand likewise, but she went on. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished the prayer, he said: "They are stronger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the presence of Ibn ʿAbbās, mention was made of what breaks the prayer, and they mentioned the dog, the donkey, and the woman. He said, "What do you say about the kid? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying one day when a kid went to pass in front of him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ hurried toward the qiblah [wall] to prevent it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to teach us not to precede the imam in bowing and prostrating, and [that] when he says the takbīr, we say the takbīr, and when he prostrates, we prostrate.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have become heavy [with age],
so when I bow, bow,
and when I rise, rise,
and when I prostrate, prostrate,
and let me not find a man who gets ahead of me into bowing,
or into prostration."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Among the signs of coarseness is that a man repeatedly wipes his forehead
before he has finished his prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not crack your knuckles while you are in prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a man to cover his mouth during prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man who had interlaced his fingers in prayer, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated his fingers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you yawns, let him put his hand over his mouth and not howl,
for Satan laughs at him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Spitting, nasal mucus, menstruation, and drowsiness in prayer are from Satan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There are three whose prayer is not accepted: a man who leads a people in prayer while they dislike him,
and a man who comes to the prayer only late, meaning after its time has passed, and one who enslaves a freed person."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Three whose prayer does not rise a hand's span above their heads: a man who leads a people while they dislike him,
a woman who spends the night while her husband is angry with her, and two brothers who have cut off relations with each other."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Two or more constitute a congregation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying the Maghrib prayer,
and I came and stood on his left,
so he made me stand on his right.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah liked the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār to stand right behind him, so that they might learn from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī used to put forward the young men of his people to lead them in prayer. It was said to him, "You do this, when you have the seniority that you have?" He said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'The imam is a guarantor. If he does well, the reward is for him and for them,
and if he does badly,' meaning, 'the fault is on him and not on them.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A mouse fell
into some clarified butter and died.
The Prophet ﷺ was asked about it, and he said:
"Throw it out along with what is around it, and eat [the rest]."
Sufyān was told: Maʿmar narrates it from az-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Hurayrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Musaddad said: We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him for mounts, and I saw him cleaning his tongue with the siwāk. Abū Dāwūd said: Sulaymān said: I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was using the siwāk, and he had placed the siwāk on the tip of his tongue, and he was saying, "Uh, uh," meaning, as if retching.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Abū an-Naḍr,
that Abū Murrah,
the freed slave of Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib, informed him that he
heard Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib

say: I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year of the Conquest and found him bathing, while his daughter Fāṭimah was screening him with a garment. She said: I greeted him with salām, and he said, "Who is this?"
I said, "Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib." He said,
"Welcome, Umm Hāniʾ."
When he finished his bath, he stood and prayed eight rakʿahs, wrapped in a single garment.
When he finished, I said: O Messenger of Allah, my mother's son ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib claims that he will kill a man to whom I have granted protection, so-and-so the son of Hubayrah.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"We have protected whomever you have protected, Umm Hāniʾ."
Umm Hāniʾ said: And that was in the forenoon.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We did not regard yellowish or brownish discharge as anything.
Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh ar-Raqāshī narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Ḥafṣah,
from Umm ʿAṭiyyah,
who said: We did not count yellowish or brownish discharge as anything.
Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā said: Wuhayb's [wording] is the preferable of the two according to us in this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man stood up before the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about praying in a single garment, and he said:
"Does each of you have two garments?"
Then a man asked ʿUmar, and he said: When Allah has given you abundance, be generous [in dress].
A man may gather his clothes upon himself:
a man may pray in a waist-wrapper and a cloak,
in a waist-wrapper and a shirt,
in a waist-wrapper and a long coat,
in trousers and a cloak,
in trousers and a shirt,
in trousers and a long coat,
in shorts and a long coat,
in shorts and a shirt. He said: And I think he said: in shorts and a cloak.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
that Ḥafṣah, the Mother of the Believers,
informed him that when the muʾadhdhin fell silent after the call to the dawn prayer, and dawn had appeared, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray two brief rakʿahs before the prayer was established.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ led us in the Ẓuhr or ʿAṣr prayer and ended it with the salām.
Dhū al-Yadayn said to him: Has the prayer been shortened, O Messenger of Allah? The Prophet ﷺ said to his Companions:
"Is what he says true?" They said: Yes.
So he prayed the other two rakʿahs, then performed two prostrations.
Saʿd said: I saw ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr pray two rakʿahs of Maghrib, end with the salām and speak, then pray what remained and perform two prostrations, and he said: This is what the Prophet ﷺ did.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that when he stood for the obligatory prayer, he would say the takbīr and raise his hands level with his shoulders. He would do the same when he finished his recitation and when he wished to bow, and he would do it when he rose from bowing. He would not raise his hands in any part of his prayer while sitting. And when he stood up after the two prostrations, he would raise his hands likewise and say the takbīr, and he supplicated like the narration of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz regarding the supplication, with some additions and omissions. He did not mention:
"And all good is in Your hands, and evil is not attributed to You."
And he added in it that he would say upon finishing the prayer:
"O Allah, forgive me what I have sent forth and what I have left behind, what I have concealed and what I have made public. You are my God; there is no god but You."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said: In every prayer there is recitation. What the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made us hear, we make you hear, and what he concealed from us, we conceal from you.
A man said to him: What if I do not add anything to the Mother of the Qurʾān? He said: If you add to it, that is better, and if you stop at it, it is sufficient for you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man named Fasīḥ fell ill, so his neighbor came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said to him, "He has died." He said, "How do you know?"
He said, "I saw him."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"He has not died."
He said: So the neighbor went back to Fasīḥ, then came again to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "He has died." The Prophet ﷺ said,
"He has not died."
Then he returned to Fasīḥ, and the man's wife said, "Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and tell him."
The man said, "O Allah, curse him."

He said: Then the man went and saw that he had killed himself with a broad-headed arrowhead that he had with him. So he went to the Prophet ﷺ and told him that he had died. He said, "How do you know?"
He said, "I saw him killing himself with the arrowheads he had." He said, "You saw him?" He said, "Yes." He said,
"Then I will not pray over him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the people of Basra, from Abū Barzah al-Aslamī:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pray over Māʿiz ibn Mālik, but he did not forbid praying over him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibrāhīm, the son of the Prophet ﷺ, died when he was eighteen months old, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pray over him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ibrāhīm, the son of the Prophet ﷺ, died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over him at al-Maqāʿid.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in the Mirbad lane when a funeral passed with a great many people. They said, "It is the funeral of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmayr." So I followed it, and there was a man wearing a thin cloak, on his small pack horse, with a piece of cloth on his head to protect him from the sun. I said, "Who is this landowner?" They said, "This is Anas ibn Mālik."

When the funeral was set down, Anas stood and prayed over it, and I was behind him with nothing between him and me. He stood at the head of the deceased, said four takbīrs, neither prolonging nor hurrying, and then went to sit. They said, "O Abū Ḥamzah, the Anṣārī woman!" So they brought her forward, on a green bier, and he stood at her hips and prayed over her like his prayer over the man, then sat. Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ziyād said, "O Abū Ḥamzah, was this how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over the funeral, like your prayer, saying four takbīrs over it, and standing at the head of a man and the hips of a woman?" He said, "Yes."

He said, "O Abū Ḥamzah, did you fight in battle with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "Yes, I fought with him at Ḥunayn. The polytheists came out and charged us until we saw our horses behind our backs. Among the enemy was a man who kept attacking us, striking us and crushing us. Then Allah routed them, and they were brought and pledged allegiance to him on Islam. A man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said, 'I have taken a vow that if Allah brings the man who has been crushing us since today, I will strike off his neck.'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent, and the man was brought. When he saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I repent to Allah.'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ held back and did not accept his pledge, so that the other man could fulfill his vow.

He said: The man kept presenting himself before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for him to order the man's killing, but he was too awed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to kill him. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw that he was doing nothing, he accepted the man's pledge. Then the man said, 'O Messenger of Allah, my vow!' He said,
"I held back from him since today only so that you would fulfill your vow."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, why did you not give me a sign?" The Prophet ﷺ said,
"It is not fitting for a prophet to give a covert sign."

Abū Ghālib said: I asked about Anas's action in standing at the woman's hips, and they told me that it was only because there were no biers [with covers], so the imam would stand opposite her hips to screen her from the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I witnessed Marwān ask Abū Hurayrah, "How did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray over a funeral?" He said, "Are you with what I said [before]?" He said, "Yes."
He said: There had been some words between them before that.
Abū Hurayrah said,
"O Allah, You are its Lord, You created it, You guided it to Islam, and You took its soul. You know best its secret and its open [state]. We have come to You as intercessors, so forgive him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from the people of Iraq called Shaqīq ibn Salamah, Abū Wāʾil, [reported] that a man from Banū Taghlib called aṣ-Ṣubayy ibn Maʿbad, who had been a Christian and then accepted Islam, set out on the first Hajj he performed and made the talbiyah for Hajj and ʿUmrah together. He kept on making the talbiyah for both together, and he passed by Salmān ibn Rabīʿah and Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān. One of them said, "You are more astray than this camel of yours!"
Aṣ-Ṣubayy said: That stayed in my mind until I met ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and mentioned it to him. He said, "You have been guided to the Sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ."
Shaqīq said: Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ and I used to go to aṣ-Ṣubayy ibn Maʿbad to have him recount it to us. We went to him many times, Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ and I.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with ʿUthmān when he heard ʿAlī

making the talbiyah for ʿUmrah and Hajj. He said, "Did you not use to forbid this?" He said, "Yes, but I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ make the talbiyah for both together, so I would not abandon the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for your saying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUthmān
forbade the combined [Hajj and ʿUmrah] (mutʿah),
and forbade a man to combine Hajj and ʿUmrah. So ʿAlī said, "Labbayka, for Hajj and ʿUmrah together."
ʿUthmān said, "Do you do it when I forbid it?" ʿAlī said, "I would not abandon the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the sake of anyone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed him over Yemen. When ʿAlī came to the Prophet ﷺ, ʿAlī said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, "What did you do?"
I said, "I declared the same intention as you declared." He said,
"I have brought sacrificial animals and combined [Hajj and ʿUmrah]."
He said: And he ﷺ said to his Companions,
"If I had known beforehand of my affair what I came to know afterwards, I would have done as you have done; but I have brought the sacrificial animals and combined [Hajj and ʿUmrah]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn said to me: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined Hajj and ʿUmrah, then he died before forbidding it, and before any Qurʾān was revealed prohibiting it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ making the talbiyah for both.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī and ʿUthmān performed Hajj. When we were part-way along the road, ʿUthmān forbade tamattuʿ. ʿAlī said, "When you see that he has set off, set off."
Then ʿAlī and his companions made the talbiyah for ʿUmrah, and ʿUthmān did not forbid them. ʿAlī said, "Was I not told that you forbid tamattuʿ?" He said, "Yes."
ʿAlī said to him, "Did you not hear that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed tamattuʿ?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: By Allah, I forbid you from the mutʿah, and it is
in the Book of Allah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did it"—meaning ʿUmrah within the Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah said to Ibn ʿAbbās, "Did you know that I trimmed the hair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Marwah?" He said, "No."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Here is Muʿāwiyah forbidding people from the mutʿah, when the Prophet ﷺ performed it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh and asked him about the Hajj of the Prophet

ﷺ. He told us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in Medina for nine years without performing Hajj, then he announced to the people that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would be performing Hajj this year. So a great multitude of people came to Medina, all of them seeking to follow the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and to do what he did. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with five days remaining of Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and we set out with him. Jābir said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among us, the Qurʾān was being revealed to him, and he knew its interpretation; whatever he did, we did. So we set out intending nothing but Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh and asked him about the Hajj of the Prophet
ﷺ. He told us that ʿAlī came from Yemen with sacrificial animals, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had driven sacrificial animals from Medina. He said to ʿAlī, "What did you declare?"
He said: I said, "O Allah, I declare the same as what Your Messenger ﷺ declared, and I have the sacrificial animals with me." He said, "Then do not leave ihrām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAṭāʾ said: Jābir said: ʿAlī came back from his collection duty, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him,
"What did you declare, O ʿAlī?"
He said, "What the Prophet ﷺ declared." He said,
"Then offer a sacrifice and remain in ihrām as you are."
He said: And ʿAlī offered a sacrificial animal on his behalf.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Syria and prayed two rakʿahs,
then I said, "O Allah, make easy for me a righteous companion."
So I came to some people and sat with them,
and an elderly man came and sat beside me.
I asked, "Who is this?" They said, "Abū al-Dardāʾ."
I said to him, "I asked Allah to make easy for me a righteous companion, and He has made you [one] for me."
He asked, "Where are you from?" I said, "From the people of Kufa."

He said, "Do you not have with you the son of Umm ʿAbd, the keeper of the sandals, the cushion, and the purification vessel? And among you is the one whom Allah protected from Satan upon the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ. And do you not have among you the keeper of the secret of the Prophet ﷺ, which no one else knows?" Then he said, "How does ʿAbdullāh recite {By the night when it covers}?"
So I recited to him: {By the night when it covers, and the day when it appears, and He who created the male and female.}
He said, "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught it to me directly from his mouth to mine."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

from the people of Iraq asked Ibn ʿUmar about the blood of mosquitoes on clothing. Ibn ʿUmar said, "Look at this one, asking about the blood of mosquitoes, when they have killed the grandson of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ! And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn are my two sweet-scented flowers of this world.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to Ḥudhayfah and said, "Tell us about the person who

is closest to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in conduct and manner, so that we may learn from him and listen to him." He said, "The closest of people in conduct, manner, and demeanor to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was Ibn Masʿūd, until he would disappear from us into his house. And those among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who preserved [the knowledge] know that the son of Umm ʿAbd is among those closest of them to Allah in nearness."
This ḥadīth is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Mecca was conquered, he distributed the spoils among Quraysh. The Anṣār said, "This is truly astonishing: our swords drip with their blood, yet our spoils are given back to them."
This reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he gathered them and said:
"What is this that has reached me from you?"
They said, "It is what has reached you."
And they did not lie. He said:

"Are you not pleased that the people return to their homes with worldly goods, while you return to your homes with the Messenger of Allah? If the people were to take one valley or mountain pass and the Anṣār took another valley or pass, I would take the valley of the Anṣār or the pass of the Anṣār."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw children and women coming back from a wedding, so the Prophet of Allah ﷺ stood up energetically and said:
"O Allah, you are among the people most beloved to me. O Allah, you are among the people most beloved to me." He meant the Anṣār.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman of the Anṣār came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a child of hers,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke with her and said:
"By the One in Whose hand is my soul,
you are among the people most beloved to me." [He said it] twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Usayd [reported that] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of the households of the Anṣār are Banū al-Najjār,
then Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal,
then Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj,
then Banū Sāʿidah. And in all the households of the Anṣār there is good."
Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah, who had precedence in Islam, said, "I see that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has favored others over us."
It was said to him, "He has favored you over many people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We conquered Makkah, and then we went on the expedition to Ḥunayn. The polytheists came in the best battle lines I have ever seen. He said: The cavalry formed ranks, then the fighters, then the women behind them, then the sheep, then the camels. He said: We were a great number, we had reached six thousand, and on the flank of our cavalry was Khālid ibn al-Walīd. He said: Our horses began to turn back behind us, and it was not long before our cavalry broke apart and the Bedouins and those of the people we knew fled. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called out:
"O Emigrants! O Emigrants!" Then he said:
"O Helpers! O Helpers!"
He said: Anas said: This is a hadith from my paternal uncles.

He said: We said, "At your service, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ advanced. He said: By Allah, we had barely reached them when Allah defeated them. He said: We took that wealth, then we set out for Ṭāʾif and besieged them for forty nights, then we returned to Makkah and camped. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began giving a man a hundred camels.
Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith like the hadith of Qatādah, Abū al-Tayyāḥ and Hishām ibn Zayd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb, Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah, ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn and al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis a hundred camels each, and he gave ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās less than that.

So ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās said: "Will you make my spoils and the spoils of my horse al-ʿUbayd go to ʿUyaynah and al-Aqraʿ? Neither Badr nor Ḥābis surpassed Mirdās in the gathering, and I was not lower than either of them, and whoever you lower today will not be raised." He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ completed a hundred for him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to distribute spoils of war. And he narrated the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Bakr al-Muqaddamī and Abū Bakr ibn Nāfiʿ both said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us: Sufyān narrated to us,
both of them from al-Aʿmash, with this chain, like it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I will not narrate to you except what I heard from him.
Then he mentioned from ʿAlī,
something like the hadith of Ayyūb, raised to the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Ḥarūriyyah rebelled, while he was with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, they said: "There is no judgment except Allah's."
ʿAlī said: "A word of truth by which falsehood is intended. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ described some people, and I certainly recognize their description in these people:

They speak the truth with their tongues, but it does not go beyond this," and he pointed to his throat, "Among the most hateful of Allah's creatures to Him among them is a black man, one of whose arms is like the teat of a sheep or the nipple of a breast."
When ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, had killed them, he said: "Look."
They looked but found nothing. He said: "Go back, for by Allah, I have not lied and I have not been lied to."
Twice or three times. Then they found him in a ruin, and they brought him and laid him before him.
ʿUbaydullāh said: I was present at that event of theirs,
and the statement of ʿAlī about them. Yūnus added in his narration: Bukayr said: A man narrated to me from Ibn Ḥunayn that he said: I saw that black man.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A people will arrive arrogantly from the direction of the east, with their heads shaved."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Juwayriyah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to see her and said:
"Is there any food?"
She said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we have no food except a bone from a sheep that I gave to my freed slave woman as charity." He said:
"Bring it near, for it has reached its place."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, like that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When Ramadan begins," and he mentioned the like of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The month is twenty-nine [days]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out for ʿUmrah, and when we stopped at Baṭn Nakhlah, he said: we looked for the new moon, and some of the people said, "It is three nights old."
Some of the people said, "It is two nights old." He said: We met Ibn ʿAbbās and said, "We saw the new moon, and some of the people said it is three nights old and some said it is two nights old."
He said, "Which night did you see it?" He said: We said, "Such and such night."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah has extended it for sighting, so it belongs to the night you saw it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we are in the land of a people from the People of the Book; we eat from their vessels. And it is a land of game, where I hunt with my bow, with my trained dog, or with my dog that is not trained. Tell me, what of that is lawful for us?" He said:

"As for what you mentioned, that you are in the land of a people from the People of the Book and eat from their vessels: if you find vessels other than theirs, do not eat from them; but if you do not find any, wash them and then eat from them. As for what you mentioned, that you are in a land of game: whatever you hit with your bow, mention the name of Allah and then eat; whatever you catch with your trained dog, mention the name of Allah and then eat; and whatever you catch with your dog that is not trained, and you reach it while it is still alive and slaughter it, then eat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbidding the bending back of the mouths of water skins [to drink from them].
ʿAbd Allāh said: Maʿmar or someone else said, "It means drinking from their mouths."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said to Anas, meaning Ibn Mālik, "Which garment was most beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," or "most pleasing to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "The ḥibarah [a striped Yemeni cloth]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him:
"And seek forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"I seek forgiveness from Allah seventy times a day."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
It is also narrated from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"I seek forgiveness from Allah a hundred times a day."
And it has been narrated through more than one route from the Prophet ﷺ:
"I seek forgiveness from Allah a hundred times a day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Allah created Paradise and the Fire, He sent Jibrīl to Paradise and said, 'Look at it and at what I have prepared for its people in it.' He came to it and looked at it and at what Allah had prepared for its people in it. Then he returned to Him and said, 'By Your might, no one who hears of it will fail to enter it.'

So He commanded that it be surrounded with hardships, and said, 'Go back to it and look at what I have prepared for its people in it.' He went back to it and found it surrounded with hardships. He returned to Him and said, 'By Your might, I fear that no one will enter it.'
He said, 'Go to the Fire and look at it and at what I have prepared for its people in it.'
He found it with parts of it riding upon other parts. He returned to Him and said, 'By Your might, no one who hears of it will enter it.'
So He commanded that it be surrounded with desires, and said, 'Go back to it.'
He went back to it and said, 'By Your might, I fear that no one will escape from it without entering it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Then he mentioned a phrase with the same meaning, from ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl,
from ʿAbd Allāh,
who said: The first matter to be judged between people on the Day of Resurrection will be bloodshed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:

"O ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samurah, do not ask for a position of authority, for if you are given it after asking, you will be left to it; but if you are given it without asking, you will be helped in it. And when you swear an oath and see something else that is better than it, then make expiation for your oath and do what is better."
Abū Aḥmad al-Jūdhī said: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Māsarjisī narrated to us,
Shaybān ibn Farrūkh narrated to us, with this hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The dream of a Muslim, which he sees or which is shown to him."
And in the hadith of Ibn Mushir:
"A righteous dream is one of forty-six parts of prophecy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: None of you should urinate in standing water and then perform ablution from it."
ʿAwf said: Khilās also said, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you has relations with his wife and then wishes to return to her, let him perform ablution."
Abū Bakr added in his narration, "between the two," ablution, and he said, "then wishes to repeat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say the takbīr at every lowering and rising, standing and sitting, and he would give the salām to his right and to his left, saying:
"Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah; peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah,"
until the whiteness of his cheek could be seen. And I saw Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, do the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I observed the Prophet ﷺ for a month, and he would recite in the two rakʿahs before the Fajr prayer:
"Say: O disbelievers" and "Say: He is Allah, [who is] One." He said: There are also narrations on this topic from Ibn Masʿūd, Anas, Abū Hurayrah, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ḥafṣah, and ʿĀʾishah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: until he traced it back to al-Mughīrah—Ibn ʿAwn said: I do not remember the report of one from the report of the other—that al-Mughīrah said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and he tapped my back with a staff he had with him. He turned aside and I turned aside with him until he reached such-and-such a place on the ground, where he made his camel kneel, and then he went off.
He said: He went until he was out of my sight, then he came back and said, "Do you have water with you?"

I had a small water-skin with me, so I brought it to him and poured water over him. He washed his hands and his face, and went to wash his forearms, but he was wearing a Syrian cloak with narrow sleeves, so he brought his hand out from under the cloak and washed his face and his forearms. He mentioned that he wiped part of his forelock and part of his turban—Ibn ʿAwn said: I do not remember it as exactly as I would like—then he wiped over his leather socks. Then he said, "Do you need anything?"

I said: O Messenger of Allah, I have no need. Then we came, and the people were being led in prayer by ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who had already prayed one rakʿah of the dawn prayer with them. I went to alert him, but he forbade me. So we prayed what we caught up with, and we made up what we had missed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ let the water flow [over his limbs] three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He called for water for ablution, then rinsed his mouth, sniffed water into his nose, and blew it out with his left hand. He did this three times, then said: This is the purification of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father called me to bring water for ablution, so I brought it close to him. He began by washing his palms three times before putting them into the water. Then he rinsed his mouth three times and blew out his nose three times. Then he washed his face three times, then washed his right arm up to the elbow three times, and the left likewise. Then he wiped his head once. Then he washed his right foot up to the ankles three times, and the left likewise. Then he stood up and said, "Hand it to me." So I handed him the vessel that held the remainder of his ablution water, and he drank from the remainder of his ablution water while standing. I was surprised, and when he saw me, he said: Do not be surprised, for I saw your father, the Prophet ﷺ, do just as you saw me do. He would say of this ablution of his, and he drank the remainder of his ablution water while standing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sālim Sablān said: ʿĀʾishah used to admire his trustworthiness and would hire him. She showed me how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution: she rinsed her mouth and blew out her nose three times, and washed her face three times, then washed her right hand three times and the left three times. She placed her hand on the front of her head and wiped her head once, to the back of it, then passed her hands over her ears, then passed them over the cheeks. Sālim said: I used to come to her as a slave under a contract for his freedom; she did not hide from me, and she would sit before me and talk with me, until I came to her one day and said: Pray for blessing for me, O Mother of the Believers.
She said: What is that? I said: Allah has set me free.
She said: May Allah bless you.
And she let down the screen between us, and I did not see her after that day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are two matters about which I will ask no one after what I witnessed from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: We were with him on a journey, and he went out to relieve himself, then came back and performed ablution. He wiped his forelock and the two sides of his turban, and wiped over his leather socks. He said: And the matter of the leader praying behind one of his subjects: I witnessed from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he was on a journey and the time for prayer came, but the Prophet ﷺ was delayed. So they established the prayer and put forward Ibn ʿAwf, who led them. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and prayed behind Ibn ʿAwf what remained of the prayer. When Ibn ʿAwf gave the salam, the Prophet ﷺ stood up and made up what he had missed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and water was brought. He poured water from the vessel over his hands and washed them once, and washed his face and forearms once each, and washed both his feet with his right hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Duḥaym and Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd—the wording is his—from Ibn Nāfiʿ,
from Dāwūd ibn Qays,
from Zayd ibn Aslam,
from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār,
from Usāmah ibn Zayd,

who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Bilāl entered the markets, and he went to relieve himself, then came out. Usāmah said: I asked Bilāl what he had done. Bilāl said: The Prophet ﷺ went to relieve himself, then performed ablution: he washed his face and hands, wiped his head, and wiped over the two leather socks, then prayed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding wiping over the leather socks: that there is no harm in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to wish that I would meet

a man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ so that I could ask him about the Khawārij. Then I met Abū Barzah on the day of ʿĪd, among a group of his companions, and I said to him, "Did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mention the Khawārij?" He said, "Yes. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with my own ears and saw him with my own eyes. Some wealth was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he divided it. He gave those on his right and those on his left, but he gave nothing to those behind him. Then a man stood up from behind him and said, 'O Muhammad, you have not been just in the division.'"
He was a black man with closely cropped hair, wearing two white garments. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became extremely angry and said:
"By Allah, after me you will not find a man more just than I." Then he said:

"In the last days there will emerge a people of whom this man is one. They recite the Qur'an but it does not go beyond their collarbones. They pass out of Islam as the arrow passes through the game. Their mark is shaving the head. They will keep emerging until the last of them emerges with the Antichrist (al-Masīḥ ad-Dajjāl). So when you meet them, kill them. They are the worst of creation and of created beings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "The share of the near relatives (dhawī al-qurbā): for whom is it?" Yazīd ibn Hurmuz said: I wrote the letter of Ibn ʿAbbās to Najdah. He wrote to him: "You wrote asking me about the share of the near relatives, for whom it is. It is for us, the Ahl al-Bayt. ʿUmar had called us to use it to marry off our unmarried ones, to provide for our needy, and to pay off the debts of our debtors. But we refused unless he handed it over to us entirely, and he refused that, so we left it to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that I send to you someone to cut your hair, the hair of evil.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the saying of the Almighty: {And know that whatever you obtain of war booty, one-fifth of it is for Allah, for the Messenger, and for the near relatives}, he said: The fifth of Allah and the fifth of His Messenger are one. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would provide mounts from it, give from it, and put it wherever he wished and do with it whatever he wished.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad about the saying of the Almighty: {And know that whatever you obtain of war booty, one-fifth of it is for Allah}. He said: This is the opening of the words of Allah; the world and the Hereafter belong to Allah. He said: They differed about these two shares after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the share of the Messenger and the share of the near relatives. One said, "The share of the Messenger ﷺ is for the caliph after him." Another said, "The share of the near relatives is for the relatives of the Messenger ﷺ." Another said, "The share of the near relatives is for the relatives of the caliph." Then they agreed to put these two shares toward horses and equipment in the cause of Allah. So it was that way during the caliphates of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār about this verse,
{And know that whatever you obtain of war booty, one-fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger}. He said: I said, "How much of the fifth did the Prophet ﷺ have?" He said, "A fifth of the fifth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ash-Shaʿbī was asked about the share of the Prophet

ﷺ and his chosen portion (ṣafī). He said: As for the share of the Prophet ﷺ, it was like the share of a man among the Muslims. As for the share of the ṣafī, it was a choice item that he would select from whatever he wished.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I was with

Muṭarrif at the Mirbad, a man came in with a piece of tanned leather. He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote this for me. Is there anyone among you who can read?" I said, "I can read." In it was written:

"From Muhammad the Prophet ﷺ to the Banū Zuhayr ibn Uqaysh: If they bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, separate from the polytheists, and acknowledge the fifth of their war booty and the share of the Prophet ﷺ and his chosen portion, then they are secure under the protection of Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The fifth that is for Allah and the Messenger was for the Prophet ﷺ and his relatives, who would not eat anything from charity. So the Prophet ﷺ had a fifth of the fifth, his relatives had a fifth of the fifth, the orphans had the same, the poor had the same, and the wayfarer had the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

There is none among you but that Allah will speak to him, with no interpreter between him and Allah. He will look to his right and see only what he sent forth; he will look to his left and see only what he sent forth; and he will look ahead of him and see only the Fire facing him. So protect yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date."
Ibn Ḥajar added: al-Aʿmash said: ʿAmr ibn Murrah narrated to me from Khaythamah something similar, and he added in it: "
even with a good word."
And Isḥāq said: al-Aʿmash said, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Khaythamah:
label: machine translation

segments_en: A people will come out of the Fire after it has scorched them, and they will enter Paradise,
and the people of Paradise will call them the Jahannamites."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
I certainly know the last of the people of the Fire to come out of it, and the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise.
He is a man who will come out of the Fire crawling, and it will be said to him: 'Go and enter Paradise.'
He will come to it, and it will appear to him that it is full, so he will return and say: 'My Lord, I found it full.'
Allah will say: 'Go and enter Paradise.'
He will come to it, and it will appear to him that it is full, so he will return and say: 'My Lord, I found it full.'
Allah, Glorified is He, will say: 'Go and enter Paradise.'
He will come to it, and it will appear to him that it is full, so he will return and say: 'My Lord, it is full.'
Allah will say: 'Go and enter Paradise.

You will have the like of the world and ten times its like'—or: 'You will have ten times the like of the world'—and he will say: 'Are You mocking me'—or: 'Are You laughing at me'—'when You are the King?'"
He said: Indeed I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh until his molar teeth showed.
And it used to be said: This is the lowest of the people of Paradise in rank.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was sitting in the shade of the Kaʿbah.
He said: He saw me approaching and said: "
They are the greatest losers, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah, on the Day of Resurrection."
He said: I said: What is wrong with me? Perhaps something has been revealed about me.
He said: I said: Who are they? May my father and mother be your ransom.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
They are the ones with the most wealth, except for those who say thus, and thus, and thus."
And he scooped with his hands in front of him, to his right, and to his left. Then he said: "

By the One in whose hand is my soul, no man dies leaving behind camels or cattle for which he did not pay the zakāh, except that they will come to him on the Day of Resurrection bigger and fatter than they ever were, trampling him with their hooves and goring him with their horns. Whenever the last of them has passed, the first of them will return to him, until judgment is passed among the people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Whoever vows to obey Allah, let him obey Him,
and whoever vows to disobey Allah, let him not disobey Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to Abū Mūsā and Salmān ibn Rabīʿah and asked them about a daughter, a son's daughter, and a sister
from both father and mother. They both said: The daughter gets half, and the sister from father and mother gets what remains.
And they said to him: Go to ʿAbdullāh and ask him, for he will agree with us.

So he went to ʿAbdullāh and mentioned that to him and told him what they had said. ʿAbdullāh said: Then I would have gone astray, and I would not be among the rightly guided. Rather, I will judge in the matter as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged: the daughter gets half, the son's daughter gets a sixth to complete the two-thirds, and the sister gets what remains.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The last verse revealed, or the last thing revealed, was:
(They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the one who leaves no parents or children [kalālah].)
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ, the Prophet of repentance, said: "
Whoever accuses his slave of something of which he is innocent, the prescribed punishment will be carried out against him on the Day of Resurrection, unless the slave is as he said."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two women of Hudhayl fought each other,
and one of them struck the other with a stone and killed her and what was in her womb,
so they brought their dispute to the Prophet ﷺ, and he ruled that the blood money for her unborn child was a male or female slave,
and he ruled that the blood money for the woman was to be paid by her ʿāqilah (paternal kinsmen).
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar
consulted the people about a woman who miscarries because of an assault. Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah said: I witnessed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rule in her case a male or female slave.
He said: Bring me someone who will testify with you.
So he brought Muḥammad ibn Maslamah—Hārūn added: and he testified for him—meaning a man striking the belly of his wife.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the men have taken your teachings for themselves,
so set aside for us a day of your own,
on which we may come to you and you may teach us from what Allah has taught you." He said,
"Gather on such and such a day, at such and such a place."
They gathered, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to them and taught them from what Allah had taught him. Then he said,
"There is no woman among you who sends ahead of her three of her children,
but they will be a screen for her from the Fire."
A woman among them said, "O Messenger of Allah, what about two?" She repeated it twice, then he said,
"And two, and two, and two."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Saʿīd,
both of them from al-Walīd,
Zuhayr said: al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us: al-Awzāʿī narrated to us:
Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr narrated to me:
Abū Salamah narrated to me,
he being the son of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: Abū Hurayrah narrated to me,
He said: When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ victory over Mecca, he stood among the people, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said,

"Indeed, Allah held back the elephant from Mecca and gave His Messenger and the believers power over it. It was never lawful for anyone before me, it was made lawful for me for an hour of a day, and it will never be lawful for anyone after me. So its game must not be scared off, its thorns must not be cut, and what is dropped in it is not lawful to pick up except for one who will announce it. Whoever has a relative killed has the better of two options: either that blood-money be taken, or that the killer be killed."
Then al-ʿAbbās said, "Except the idhkhir, O Messenger of Allah, for we use it in our graves and our houses."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Except the idhkhir."
Then Abū Shāh, a man from the people of Yemen, stood up and said, "Write it down for me, O Messenger of Allah."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Write it down for Abū Shāh."
al-Walīd said: I asked al-Awzāʿī, "What was his saying, 'Write it down for me, O Messenger of Allah'?" He said, "This sermon, which he heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: None among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated more hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than I did, except ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, for he used to write them down and I did not write.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was nearing death, and there were men in the house, among them ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, the Prophet ﷺ said,
"Come, let me write for you a document after which you will not go astray."
ʿUmar said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is overcome by pain, and you have the Qur'an. The Book of Allah is sufficient for us."
The people of the house differed and disputed. Some of them said, "Bring it near, so that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ may write for you a document after which you will not go astray."
And some of them said what ʿUmar said.
When they made much idle talk and disagreement in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Get up."

ʿUbayd Allāh said: Ibn ʿAbbās used to say, "The calamity, the whole calamity, was that which came between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his writing that document for them, because of their disagreement and their noise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ woke up and said,
"Glory be to Allah! What has been sent down of the treasures,
and what has been sent down of trials!
Who will wake the women of the rooms"—meaning his wives—"so that they may pray?
Many a woman clothed in this world
will be naked in the Hereafter."
Ibn Abī Thawr said, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿUmar,
that he said: I said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Have you divorced your wives?" He said, "No."
I said, "Allahu akbar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I spent the night in the house of my maternal aunt Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ was with her on her night.
The Prophet ﷺ prayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer,
then came to his dwelling,
and prayed four rakʿahs, then slept. Then he got up and said, "The little boy has gone to sleep,"
or a similar expression.
Then he stood up to pray, and I stood on his left,
so he placed me on his right.
He prayed five rakʿahs, then prayed two rakʿahs,
then slept until I heard his deep breathing, or snoring, then went out to the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among a group of men of knowledge, ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say, while he was healthy:
"No prophet is ever taken in death until he is shown his place in Paradise, and then he is given the choice."
ʿĀʾishah said: When death came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with his head on my thigh, he lost consciousness for a while, then he recovered and fixed his gaze on the ceiling, and then said:
"O Allah, [grant me] the Highest Companion."
ʿĀʾishah said: I said, "Then he is not choosing us."
ʿĀʾishah said: And I knew that this was the statement he used to tell us while he was healthy, when he said:
"No prophet is ever taken in death until he is shown his place in Paradise, and then he is given the choice."
ʿĀʾishah said: And that was the last word the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke, his saying:
"O Allah, [grant me] the Highest Companion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah,

the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: I went back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that [matter], and what moved me to repeat it so often was only that it did not occur to my heart that people would ever love a man who took his place after him, and that I thought no one would ever take his place without the people regarding him as an ill omen. So I wanted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to turn away from [choosing] Abū Bakr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died while he was between my chest and my throat, so I do not dislike the severity of death for anyone ever after having seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: We poured medicine into the side of the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during his illness,
and he kept gesturing to us, "Do not pour medicine into my mouth."
She said: We said, "[It is] the sick person's dislike of medicine."
When he recovered, he said:
"Did I not forbid you to pour medicine into my mouth?"
She said: We said, "[It was] out of dislike of the medicine."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No one of you will remain without having medicine poured into his mouth while I look on, except al-ʿAbbās, for he did not witness you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He fought sixteen campaigns with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among the Children of Israel there was retaliation (qiṣāṣ),

and there was no blood money (diyah) among them. So Allah the Exalted said regarding this nation: {Prescribed for you is retaliation for those killed: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. But whoever is pardoned something by his brother...} Pardon means that he accepts blood money in the case of intentional killing. {...then there should be a suitable follow-up and payment to him in good manner}: he follows up in a suitable way and pays in a good manner.
{That is an alleviation from your Lord} and a mercy, compared with what was prescribed for those before you.
{But whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment}: [that is,] he kills after accepting the blood money.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding the saying of the Almighty: {And for those who are able to do it [fasting] there is a ransom: feeding a poor person}: "able to do it" means they are burdened with it; the ransom is feeding one poor person. {And whoever volunteers good}: feeding another poor person. It is not abrogated. {Then it is better for him; but to fast is better for you}. No concession is granted in this except to one who cannot bear fasting, or a sick person who will not recover.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn said: The verse of the temporary enjoyment (mutʿah) was revealed in the Book of Allah, meaning the mutʿah of Hajj, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to do it. Then no verse was revealed abrogating the verse of the mutʿah of Hajj, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not forbid it until he died.
A man said what he wished by his own opinion afterwards.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in a circle in which was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, and his companions held him in great esteem.
He mentioned the longer of the two periods, so I related the hadith of Subayʿah bint al-Ḥārith from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUtbah. He said: Some of his companions motioned disapprovingly at me.
Muḥammad said: I realized what he meant, so I said, "Then I would be bold indeed if I lied about ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUtbah while he is in a part of Kufa."
He felt ashamed and said, "But his uncle did not say that."

Then I met Abū ʿAṭiyyah Mālik ibn ʿĀmir and asked him, and he began to relate to me the hadith of Subayʿah. I said, "Did you hear anything from ʿAbdullāh about it?" He said: We were with ʿAbdullāh, and he said, "Do you impose the harsher ruling on her and not grant her the concession?
Surely the shorter Sūrat al-Nisāʾ was revealed after the longer one: {And for those who are pregnant, their term is that they give birth to their burden}."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to Khaybar, he passed by a tree belonging to the polytheists called Dhāt Anwāṭ, on which they would hang their weapons. They said, "O Messenger of Allah, make for us a Dhāt Anwāṭ just as they have a Dhāt Anwāṭ." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Glory be to Allah! This is just like what the people of Moses said:
'Make for us a god just as they have gods.' By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will surely follow the ways of those who came before you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"By the One in whose hand is my soul, the Hour will not come until predatory animals speak to humans, and until a man is spoken to by the tip of his whip and the strap of his sandal, and his thigh informs him of what his family did after him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If the people of Syria become corrupt, there is no good in you. A group of my Ummah will remain victorious; those who abandon them will not harm them, until the Hour is established."
Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl said: ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said, "They are the people of ḥadīth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: During the trial of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, [he said]: I bear witness that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There will be a trial in which the one sitting is better than the one standing, the one standing is better than the one walking, and the one walking is better than the one running."
He said: "What if someone enters my house and stretches out his hand to kill me?" He said:
"Be like the son of Adam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say in this ḥadīth:
"A man will wake up a believer and end the evening a disbeliever, or end the evening a believer and wake up a disbeliever."

He said: A man will wake up regarding the blood, honor, and wealth of his brother as sacred, and by evening will regard them as lawful; and he will end the evening regarding the blood, honor, and wealth of his brother as sacred, and wake up regarding them as lawful.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the sword is placed among my Ummah, it will not be lifted from it until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said about the trial:
"Break your bows in it, cut your bowstrings, stay in the depths of your houses, and be like the son of Adam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Hour will not come until the happiest of people in worldly life is the lowly son of a lowly man."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When my Ummah does fifteen things, calamity will befall it."
It was said, "What are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:

"When war booty is treated as private wealth passed among a few, trusts are treated as booty, zakāh is treated as a burden, a man obeys his wife and disobeys his mother, is kind to his friend and harsh to his father, voices are raised in the mosques, the leader of a people is the worst of them, a man is honored out of fear of his evil, wine is drunk, silk is worn, singing girls and musical instruments are taken up, and the last of this Ummah curse the first of it, then let them await a red wind, or being swallowed by the earth, or transformation into animals."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"In this Ummah there will be swallowing by the earth, transformation, and showers of stones."
A man from among the Muslims said, "O Messenger of Allah, when will that be?" He said:
"When singing girls and musical instruments appear and wine is drunk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A fire will come out of Ḥaḍramawt, or from the direction of Ḥaḍramawt, before the Day of Resurrection, gathering the people."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you command us [to do]?" He said, "Stay in Syria."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Hour will not come until tribes from my Ummah join the polytheists and until they worship idols. And there will be among my Ummah thirty liars, each claiming that he is a prophet, while I am the Seal of the Prophets; there is no prophet after me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"In Thaqīf there will be a great liar and a destroyer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"The best of people are my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them, then those who follow them" — three times — "then after them will come a people who will grow fat and love being fat, and who will give testimony before being asked for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Abū Bakrah beneath the pulpit of Ibn ʿĀmir while he was giving a sermon, wearing thin garments. Abū Bilāl said, "Look at our commander, wearing the clothes of the wicked!"
Abū Bakrah said, "Be quiet! I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever disgraces the authority of Allah on earth, Allah will disgrace him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said] that he should not

oppose Ibn ʿUmar in a matter of Hajj. So on the Day of ʿArafah, when the sun had passed its zenith, Ibn ʿUmar came to him while I was with him, and he called out at his tent, "Where is this man?" Al-Ḥajjāj came out to him wearing a garment dyed with safflower. He said to him, "What is the matter, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān?" He said, "Set out at once, if you want to follow the Sunnah."
He said to him, "At this hour?" He said to him, "Yes."
He said, "Let me pour some water over myself, then I will come out to you."
So he waited for him until he came out, and he walked between me and my father. I said, "If you want to follow the Sunnah, keep the sermon short and hasten the standing."
He kept looking at Ibn ʿUmar, wanting to hear that from him. When Ibn ʿUmar saw that, he said, "He has spoken the truth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUrwah [said]: In the pre-Islamic era people used to circle the House naked, except for the Ḥums,
and the Ḥums were Quraysh and their offspring.
The Ḥums used to give to people: a man would give a man garments in which to circle the House,
and a woman would give a woman garments in which to circle the House.
Whoever the Ḥums did not give to would circle the House naked.
The general body of people would depart from ʿArafāt,
while the Ḥums would depart from Jamʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sālim [said]: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, used to send ahead the weak members of his family,
and they would stand at al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām in Muzdalifah by night,
and remember Allah as much as they wished,
then they would return before the Imam stopped there
and before he set out.
Some of them would arrive at Minā for the Fajr prayer,
and some would arrive after that,
and when they arrived they would throw the pebbles at the Jamrah.
Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, used to say, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave a concession for those people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That she stopped at Jamʿ by night at Muzdalifah, and she stood up to pray, and prayed for a while,
then she said, "My son, has the moon set?" I said, "No." She prayed for a while,
then said, "Has the moon set?" I said, "Yes." She said, "Then set out." So we set out,
and we went on until she threw the pebbles at the Jamrah.
Then she returned and prayed the Subḥ prayer in her camp.
I said to her, "O lady, I think we have set out too early in the dark."
She said, "My son,
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted the women in howdahs [to do so]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding his combining ʿUmrah with Hajj [tamattuʿ], and the people combining them with him, similar to what Sālim ibn ʿAbdullāh informed me from ʿAbdullāh, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ slaughtered seven camels with his own hand, standing,
and in Madinah he sacrificed two horned rams, black and white in color. [This is] abridged.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We would not eat from the meat of our sacrificial camels beyond three days at Minā,
then the Prophet ﷺ gave us a concession and said, "Eat and take provisions." So we ate and took provisions.
I said to ʿAṭāʾ, "Did he say [that] until we came to Madinah?" He said, "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ was asked about slaughtering, shaving, throwing the pebbles, and doing things earlier or later, and he said, "There is no harm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
witnessed the Prophet ﷺ giving a sermon on the Day of Sacrifice,
and a man stood up to him
and said, "I thought that this came before that."
Then another stood up and said, "I thought that this came before that: I shaved before I sacrificed,
I sacrificed before I threw the pebbles," and similar things. The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Do it, and there is no harm," about all of them.
And he was not asked that day about anything except that he said, "Do it, and there is no harm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said at Minā,
"Do you know what day this is?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said,
"This is a sacred day.
Do you know what land this is?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said, "A sacred land.
Do you know what month this is?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said,
"A sacred month." He said, "Indeed Allah has made your blood, your property, and your honor sacred for you,
like the sacredness of this day of yours,
in this month of yours,
in this land of yours."
Hishām ibn al-Ghāz said: Nāfiʿ informed me from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both: The Prophet ﷺ stood on the Day of Sacrifice between the Jamarāt during the Hajj he performed, and said,
"This is the day of the greater Hajj,"
and the Prophet ﷺ began to say, "O Allah, bear witness." And he bade the people farewell.
So they said, "This is the Farewell Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿUmar, "When should I throw the pebbles at the Jamarāt?" He said, "When your Imam throws, then throw."
I repeated the question to him, and he said, "We used to wait for the sun to pass its zenith, and when the sun had passed it, we would throw."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar used to prolong the prayer before Friday prayer and would pray two rakʿahs after it in his house, and he would report that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When he was in Makkah and had prayed the Friday prayer, he would move forward and pray two rakʿahs, then move forward and pray four. And when he was in Madinah, he would pray the Friday prayer, then return to his house and pray two rakʿahs, and he would not pray in the mosque. He was asked about that, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he saw Ibn ʿUmar pray after the Friday prayer; he would move a little, not far, from the place of prayer in which he had prayed the Friday prayer,

He said: Then he would pray two rakʿahs. He said: Then he would walk further than that and pray four rakʿahs. I said to ʿAṭāʾ: How many times did you see Ibn ʿUmar do that? He said: Many times. Abū Dāwūd said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān narrated it but did not complete it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this report, he said:
"And the menstruating women keep apart from the place where the Muslims pray."
And he did not mention the garment.

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, he gathered the women of the Anṣār in a house and sent ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb to us. He stood at the door and greeted us with salām, and we returned the greeting. Then he said: I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to you.

He commanded us to bring out, for the two Eids, the menstruating women and the slave girls, [and said] that Friday prayer is not obligatory on us, and he forbade us from following funeral processions.

Ibn Kathīr said: Shuʿbah was most knowledgeable of it. He commanded them to give charity, and they began to throw [their jewelry].

segments_en: In this ḥadīth he said: The women began giving earrings and rings, and Bilāl began putting them in his garment. He said: Then he distributed it among the poor Muslims.

"The takbīr on Fiṭr is seven in the first rakʿah and five in the last, and the recitation comes after both of them."

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to say seven takbīrs in the first rakʿah on Fiṭr, then recite, then say takbīr, then stand and say four takbīrs, then recite, then bow.

segments_en: A companion of Abū Hurayrah [reported] that Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ
asked Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī and Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say the takbīr on Aḍḥā and Fiṭr. Abū Mūsā said: He used to say four takbīrs, like his takbīr over funerals.
Ḥudhayfah said: He is right.
Abū Mūsā said: That is how I used to say it in Basrah when I was in charge of them.
Abū ʿĀʾishah said: And I was present when Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ [asked].
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to go out in the morning with the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the place of prayer on the day of Fiṭr and the day of Aḍḥā. We would take the route through Baṭn Buṭḥān until we reached the place of prayer, and we would pray with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then return from Baṭn Buṭḥān to our homes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read in the book of ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, meaning al-Ḥimṣī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sālim, from al-Zubaydī,
from Muḥammad ibn Muslim,

this ḥadīth with its chain of narration, without mentioning the prayer. He said: He turned his cloak around, placing its right side over his left shoulder and its left side over his right shoulder, then he supplicated to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Weeping women came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"O Allah, give us rain that relieves, that is wholesome, plentiful, beneficial and not harmful, soon and not delayed."
He said: Then the sky became overcast above them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Sale is only valid by mutual consent."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not lawful to sell what you do not have, nor to take profit on what you have not taken responsibility for."

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to Makkah, he forbade him from [taking] profit on what had not come under his responsibility.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade buying what is in the wombs of livestock until they give birth, and what is in their udders except by measure; and buying a slave who has run away; and buying war spoils until they are divided; and buying charity (ṣadaqah) [property] until it is received; and the diver's cast.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during one of his ʿUmrahs, at al-Marwah, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a woman who buys and sells. When I want to buy something, I offer a price lower than what I am willing to pay, then I increase it, and increase it again, until I reach the price I want. And when I want to sell something, I name a price higher than what I want, then I lower it until I reach the price I want."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not do that, Qaylah. When you want to buy something, offer the price you are willing to pay, whether it is accepted or refused." And he said:
"When you want to sell something, ask the price you want, whether it is given or refused."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on a military expedition, and he said to me:
"Will you sell this camel of yours for a dinar, and may Allah forgive you?"
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, it is your camel when I reach Madinah." He said:
"Then will you sell it for two dinars, and may Allah forgive you?"
He said: He kept increasing [the price] for me by a dinar at a time, and for every dinar he would say:
"And may Allah forgive you,"
until it reached twenty dinars. When I came to Madinah, I took the camel by its head and brought it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"O Bilāl, give him twenty dinars from the bag." And he said:
"Go off with your camel and take it to your family."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade haggling over prices before sunrise, and the slaughtering of milk-producing animals.
label: machine translation

"Whoever sells a date palm and sells a slave, [the sale] includes both together."

"When you weigh, give a little extra."

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, they were among the worst of people in measuring, so Allah, Glorified is He, revealed: {Woe to those who give less [than due]}, and after that they measured properly.

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pass by the side of a man who had food in a container. He put his hand into it and said:
"Perhaps you have cheated in it. Whoever cheats us is not one of us."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade selling food until two ṣāʿ measures have been passed over it: the seller's ṣāʿ and the buyer's ṣāʿ.

segments_en: I used to sell dates in the market and would say: "I measured such-and-such in this wasq of mine."
Then I would hand over loads of dates by that measure and take my profit, and something about that troubled me, so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"When you state the measure, then measure it out."
