segments_en: And ʿAlī,
the two sons of al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan al-Barrād, that al-Zubayr ibn al-Mundhir ibn Abī Usayd al-Sāʿidī
narrated to them that his father al-Mundhir narrated to him, from Abū Usayd,
that Abū Usayd
narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the market of the Nabaṭ, looked at it, and said:
"This is not a market for you."
Then he went to [another] market, looked at it, and said:
"This is not a market for you."
Then he returned to this market and walked around in it, then said:
"This is your market, so let it not be diminished, and let no tax be imposed on it."

segments_en: I bear witness about the truthful, the one declared truthful, Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ, that he told us, saying:
"Selling animals whose milk has been withheld [to make them look full] is deception, and deception is not lawful for a Muslim."

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, and they were pollinating the date palms; they said they were fertilizing the palms. He said: "What are you doing?"
They said: "We used to do it." He said:
"Perhaps if you did not do it, it would be better."
So they abandoned it, and the yield fell off—or diminished. Then they mentioned that to him, and he said:
"I am only a human being. When I command you to do something from your religion, take it; and when I command you to do something from [my own] opinion, then I am only a human being."
ʿIkrimah said: Or words like this.
Al-Maʿqirī said: "So it fell off," and he did not doubt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr an-Nāqid,
both from al-Aswad ibn ʿĀmir,
Abū Bakr said: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us,
Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us,
from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, and from Thābit, from Anas,
that the Prophet ﷺ passed by some people who were pollinating [date palms], and he said:
"If you did not do it, it would be fine."
He said: So [the dates] came out poor. He passed by them and said: "What is wrong with your palms?"
They said: "You said such and such." He said:
"You know better about the affairs of your worldly life."

"If I were to take a close friend (khalīl), I would have taken Abū Bakr as a close friend, but he is my brother and my companion. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has taken your companion as a close friend."

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ five days before he died, saying:

"I declare before Allah that I have no close friend (khalīl) among you, for Allah the Most High has taken me as a close friend just as He took Ibrāhīm as a close friend. If I were to take a close friend from my Ummah, I would have taken Abū Bakr as a close friend. Beware! Those before you used to take the graves of their prophets and righteous people as places of prayer. Beware! Do not take graves as places of prayer. I forbid you from that."

segments_en: I said to my father, "Who are the best of people after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "Abū Bakr."
I said, "Then who?" He said, "Then ʿUmar."
He said: Then I feared that if I said, "Then who?" he would say, "ʿUthmān," so I said, "Then you, O father?" He said, "I am only a man among the Muslims."

segments_en: [Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī], may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited:
"And warn them of the Day of Regret," and he said:

"Death will be brought as if it were a black-and-white ram, until it is made to stand on the wall between Paradise and the Fire. Then it will be said: 'O people of Paradise!' and they will stretch their necks to look.
And it will be said: 'O people of the Fire!' and they will stretch their necks to look.
Then it will be said: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, this is Death.'

Then it will be laid down and slaughtered. Had Allah not decreed life and eternal stay in Paradise for the people of Paradise, they would die of joy; and had Allah not decreed life and eternal stay in the Fire for the people of the Fire, they would die of grief."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning His saying:
"And We raised him to a high station," he said: Anas ibn Mālik narrated to us
that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"When I was taken up [in the Night Ascent], I saw Idrīs in the fourth heaven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I once asked al-Hamdānī about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
"And there is none of you except that he will come to it [the Fire]," and he narrated to me that ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd had narrated to them, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The people will come to the Fire, then they will emerge from it according to their deeds. The first of them will be like a flash of lightning, then like the wind, then like the running of a horse, then like a rider on his mount, then like a man running, then like his walking."
He said: This is a good (ḥasan) hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from Khaybar, he traveled by night until drowsiness overtook him. He made his camel kneel and halted for the rest of the night, then said:
"O Bilāl, keep watch for us tonight."

He said: Bilāl prayed, then leaned against his riding camel facing the dawn, but his eyes overcame him and he slept. None of them woke up, and the first of them to wake was the Prophet ﷺ. He said: "O Bilāl!"
Bilāl said: May my father be ransomed for you, O Messenger of Allah! The same [sleep] that seized your soul seized mine.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Lead [the animals] on."
Then he made his camel kneel, performed ablution, had the prayer called, and prayed as he would pray at its proper time, without haste. Then he said:
"And establish prayer for My remembrance."

He said: This hadith is not preserved (ghayr maḥfūẓ). More than one of the memorizers narrated it from az-Zuhrī from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab that the Prophet ﷺ [did so], and they did not mention Abū Hurayrah in it.
And Ṣāliḥ ibn Abī al-Akhḍar is considered weak in hadith; Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān and others graded him weak because of his memory.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Wayl is a valley in Hell into which the disbeliever will fall for forty autumns before reaching its bottom."

segments_en: A man
sat before the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have two slaves who lie to me, betray me, and disobey me, and I insult them and beat them. What is my position regarding them? He said:

"Their betrayal, disobedience, and lying to you will be reckoned against your punishment of them. If your punishment of them equals their wrongdoing, it is even, neither for you nor against you. If your punishment of them is less than their wrongdoing, it is a merit for you. If your punishment of them exceeds their wrongdoing, the excess will be taken from you in retribution for them."
He said: The man moved aside and began to weep and cry out. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you not read the Book of Allah:
'And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged at all, even if it be the weight of...'" [to the end of] the verse?
The man said: By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I find nothing better for me and for these than to part from them. I make you witnesses that they are all free."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Najdah
wrote to Ibn ʿAbbās asking him about five matters.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Were it not that I would be concealing
knowledge, I would not have written back to him.

Najdah wrote to him: To proceed: Tell me, did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ go out to battle with women? Did he assign them a share? Did he kill children? When does an orphan's orphanhood end? And to whom does the fifth belong? So Ibn ʿAbbās wrote back to him: You wrote asking me whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to battle with women; he did go out with them, and they would treat the wounded and be given a gift from the spoils. As for a [fixed] share, he did not assign them one. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not kill children, so do not kill children. You also wrote asking me when an orphan's orphanhood ends. By my life, a man may grow a beard and yet be weak in taking for himself and weak in giving from himself; but when he takes for himself what is sound, as people do, then orphanhood has left him. And you wrote asking me about the fifth, to whom it belongs. We used to say that it was for us,
but our people refused us that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Imam is only a shield: people fight behind him and are protected by him. If he commands fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and acts justly, he will have a reward for that; but if he commands otherwise, he will bear the burden of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:

"Whoever withdraws from obedience and separates from the community and then dies, dies a death of the Days of Ignorance. And whoever fights under a blind banner, becoming angry for the sake of tribal partisanship, or calling to partisanship, or supporting partisanship, and is killed, dies a death of the Days of Ignorance. And whoever rises against my Ummah, striking its righteous and its wicked alike, not sparing its believers, and not fulfilling the covenant of those who have a covenant, is not of me, and I am not of him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I remember being present on the day of the Tree, when the Prophet ﷺ was taking the pledge from the people, while I was holding up one of its branches away from his head. We were one thousand four hundred. He said: We did not pledge to him to the death, but we pledged to him that we would not flee.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Abū Saʿīd, whoever is content with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muhammad as Prophet, Paradise becomes obligatory for him."
Abū Saʿīd marveled at it and said: Repeat it for me, O Messenger of Allah.
So he did so. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"And there is another [deed] by which a servant is raised a hundred degrees in Paradise, the distance between each two degrees being like that between the heavens and the earth."
He said: What is it, O Messenger of Allah? He said:
"Jihad in the cause of Allah, jihad in the cause of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the miʿrāḍ [a headless arrow], and he said:
"If it hits with its sharp edge, eat; but if it hits with its side and the animal is killed, then it is a waqīdh [beaten to death], so do not eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] called Anas said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Has Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, not said: {Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it}? I said: Yes.
He said: Has Allah not said: {It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in their affair}? I said: Yes.
He said: Then I bear witness that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ forbade the naqīr, the muqayyar, the dubbāʾ, and the ḥantam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he forbade a man to drink while standing.
Qatādah said: We said, What about eating? He said: That is worse or fouler.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād,
and Ibn Abī ʿUmar
— the wording is that of Abū Bakr — they said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us,
from Ayyūb ibn Mūsā, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn
ʿUmar, who said: The Prophet ﷺ made a ring of gold, then threw it away. Then he made a ring of silver and had engraved on it: Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah. And he said:
"Let no one engrave anything like the engraving on this ring of mine."
When he wore it, he would place its stone on the inner side of his palm. It is the one that fell from Muʿayqīb into the well of Arīs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with my father to Syria, and they began passing by monasteries in which there were Christians, and [the people] would greet them with salām. My father said: Do not initiate the greeting to them, for Abū Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:
"Do not initiate the greeting to them, and when you meet them on the road, force them to its narrowest part."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with my father, and a young man was with him. He got up, then returned, and my father narrated
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"When a man gets up from a gathering and then returns to it, he has more right to [his place in] it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had set out, and Hamdān said to me, "Will you go to this man and scout on our behalf? If you are pleased with something for us, we will accept it, and if you dislike something, we will dislike it." I said, "Yes."

So I went until I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I was pleased with his affair, and my people accepted Islam. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote this letter to ʿUmayr Dhū Murān. He said: And he sent Mālik ibn Murārah al-Rahāwī to Yemen, all of it, and ʿAkk Dhū Khaywān accepted Islam.
He said: ʿAkk was told, "Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and take from him a guarantee of security for your town and your property." So he came, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote for him:

"In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. From Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah, to ʿAkk Dhū Khaywān: if he is truthful regarding his land, his property and his slaves, then he has security and the protection of Allah and the protection of Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah."
And Khālid ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ wrote [it].
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he spoke to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about charity (ṣadaqah) when he came to him as part of a delegation, and he said:
"O brother of Sabaʾ, there must be charity (ṣadaqah)."
He said, "We only planted cotton, O Messenger of Allah, and Sabaʾ has been scattered; only a few of them remain in Mārib."

So the Prophet of Allah ﷺ made a settlement for seventy garments of cloth, valued at the cloth of Maʿāfir, every year, from those of Sabaʾ who remained in Mārib. They continued to pay it until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away. After the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the officials broke the agreement with them regarding what Abyaḍ ibn Ḥammāl had settled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the seventy garments. Abū Bakr restored it to what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had set, until Abū Bakr died. When Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, died, that was broken, and it became charity (ṣadaqah) upon them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave three instructions, saying:
"Expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula, and give gifts to the delegations similar to what I used to give them."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: He was silent about the third, or he said: I forgot it.
And al-Ḥumaydī said, from Sufyān: Sulaymān said, "I do not know whether Saʿīd mentioned the third and I forgot it, or whether he remained silent about it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There are not to be two qiblahs in one land."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿīd, meaning Ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, said: The Arabian Peninsula is what lies from the valley to the farthest part of Yemen, to the borders of Iraq, to the sea.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mālik said: ʿUmar, may Allah have mercy on him, expelled the Jews of Najrān and Fadak.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd to Ukaydir of Dūmah, and he was captured and they brought him to him. So he spared his blood and made peace with him on payment of the jizyah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī said: If I remain alive, as for the Christians of Banū Taghlib, I will certainly kill the fighters and take their offspring captive, for I wrote the document between them and the Prophet ﷺ on the condition that they would not make their children Christians.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a settlement with the people of Najrān for two thousand garments, half in Ṣafar and the remainder in Rajab, which they would pay to the Muslims, and a loan of thirty coats of mail, thirty horses, thirty camels, and thirty of every type of weapon, with which they would fight, the Muslims being guarantors of it until they return it to them, if there should be any treachery or betrayal in Yemen; on the condition that none of their churches be demolished, no priest of theirs be expelled, and they not be pressured away from their religion, so long as they do not introduce an innovation or consume usury.
Ismāʿīl said: They have indeed consumed usury.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet of the Persians died, Iblīs wrote Zoroastrianism for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man of the Asbadhiyyīn from the people of Bahrain, who were the Zoroastrians of Hajar, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and stayed with him, then left. I asked him, "What have Allah and His Messenger decreed concerning you?" He said, "Something evil."
I said, "Stop! [What is it?]" He said, "Islam or death."
He said: And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said, "He accepted the jizyah from them."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The people took the statement of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and left what I heard from the Asbadhī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The tithes are only upon the Jews and the Christians, and there are no tithes upon the Muslims."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, give me a mount." The Prophet ﷺ said,
"We will give you the offspring of a she-camel to ride."
He said, "What would I do with the offspring of a she-camel?" The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Are camels born to anything other than she-camels?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: None of you should take his brother's belongings, whether in jest or in earnest." Sulaymān said, "
in play or in earnest." "
And whoever takes his brother's staff must return it."
Ibn Bashshār did not say "Ibn Yazīd," and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, despises the eloquent man who twists his tongue about [in speech] as a cow twists its tongue."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to set up a pulpit for Ḥassān in the mosque, on which he would stand to boast on behalf of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or he said, to defend the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say,
"Indeed Allah supports Ḥassān with the Holy Spirit as long as he boasts on behalf of, or defends, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sneezed, he would put his hand or his garment over his mouth and lower or muffle his voice with it. Yaḥyā was unsure [which word].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Respond to your brother's sneeze up to three times; anything more than that is a cold.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Jews used to pretend to sneeze in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, hoping he would say to them, "May Allah have mercy on you." Instead he would say,
"May Allah guide you and set your affairs right."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [May Allah be pleased with him], that the Prophet ﷺ would not sleep until he recited the Musabbiḥāt, and he would say,
"Among them is a verse better than a thousand verses."
This is a ḥasan gharīb ḥadīth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and said to him, "Narrate to us something of what you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

He handed me a scroll and said, "This is what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote down for me." I looked in it, and in it was that Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "O Messenger of Allah, teach me what to say when I rise in the morning and when I enter the evening." He said,

"O Abū Bakr, say: O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, there is no god but You, Lord and Sovereign of everything, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul, and from the evil of Satan and his polytheism, and from committing wrong against myself or bringing it upon a Muslim."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb ḥadīth by way of this chain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never gave up these supplications in the evening and in the morning:

"O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, my worldly life, my family, and my wealth. O Allah, cover my faults and calm my fears, and protect me from before me and from behind me, from my right and from my left, and from above me, and I seek refuge in You from being struck down from beneath me."
Wakīʿ said, "He means being swallowed up by the earth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man brought an Abyssinian to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "This man killed my brother's son." He ﷺ said, "How did you kill him?"
He said, "I struck his head with an axe, and I did not intend to kill him." He ﷺ said,
"Do you have any wealth with which to pay his blood money?" He said, "No." He ﷺ said,
"What if I let you go to ask the people until you collect his blood money?" He said, "No." He ﷺ said,
"Would your allies give you his blood money?" He said, "No." Then he ﷺ said to the man, "Take him."
So he went out with him to kill him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Indeed, if he kills him, he will be like him."
So the man took him to where he could hear his words and said, "Here he is; do with him as you wish."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Release him," and on another occasion he said, "Leave him; he will bear the sin of his companion and his own sin, and he will be among the people of the Fire." He said: So he released him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A believer is not to be killed for a disbeliever. Whoever kills a believer deliberately is handed over to the guardians of the one killed; if they wish they may kill him, and if they wish they may take the blood money."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"I will not pardon anyone who kills after taking the blood money."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
from the Jews presented a poisoned sheep to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: The Prophet ﷺ did not take any action against her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh used to narrate that a Jewish woman

from the people of Khaybar poisoned a roasted sheep and then presented it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the foreleg and ate from it, and a group of his Companions ate with him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them, "Lift your hands."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for the Jewish woman, called her, and said to her,
"Did you poison this sheep?"
The Jewish woman said, "Who told you?" He said,
"This one in my hand told me," meaning the foreleg. She said, "Yes." He said,
"What made you do that?"
She said, "I said: if he is a prophet, it will not harm him, and if he is not, we will be rid of him."

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pardoned her and did not punish her. Some of his Companions who had eaten from the sheep died, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had cupping done on his shoulder because of what he had eaten from the sheep. Abū Hind cupped him with a horn and a blade; he was a freed slave of Banū Bayāḍah of the Anṣār.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Mubashshir
— Abū Saʿīd ibn al-Aʿrābī said: He said it thus, "from his mother," but the correct version is "from his father" —
from Umm Mubashshir,

entered upon the Prophet ﷺ. Then he mentioned the meaning of the hadith of Mukhallad ibn Khālid, similar to the hadith of Jābir. He said: Bishr ibn al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr died, so he sent for the Jewish woman and said,
"What made you do what you did?"
Then he mentioned something like the hadith of Jābir, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that she be executed, and she was killed. He did not mention the cupping.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to accept a gift but would not eat charity (ṣadaqah).
label: machine translation

segments_en: [She said] to the Prophet ﷺ during the illness in which he died, "What is it that afflicts you, O Messenger of Allah? I suspect nothing for my son except the poisoned sheep he ate with you at Khaybar." And the Prophet ﷺ said,
"I too suspect nothing for myself except that. This is the time when my aorta has been cut."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A free man is not to be put to death in retaliation for a slave.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he had a man of Banū Naṣr ibn Mālik put to death on the basis of the qasāmah oath, at Baḥrat al-Ruġāʾ on the shore of Liyyat al-Baḥrah. He said: The killer and the one killed were both from them.
This is the wording of Maḥmūd: "at Baḥrah"; Maḥmūd alone established it as "on the shore of Liyyat al-Baḥrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man of the Anṣār was found killed at Khaybar in the morning. His guardians went to the Prophet ﷺ and told him of that, and he said,
"Do you have two witnesses who will testify to the killing of your companion?"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, there was no Muslim there; they are only Jews, and they could dare something even greater than this." He said,
"Then choose fifty of them and have them swear."
But they refused, so the Prophet ﷺ paid the blood money for him from his own funds.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sahl—by Allah—was mistaken in the hadith: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the Jews,
"A slain man has been found among you, so pay his blood money."
So they wrote back that they swore by Allah fifty oaths that they had not killed him and did not know who the killer was.
He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ paid his blood money from his own funds, one hundred camels.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: Tell me about the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr),
O Abū al-Mundhir, for our companion was asked about it.
He said: Whoever stands in prayer throughout the year will find it.

He said: May Allah have mercy on Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. By Allah, he knew that it is in Ramadān — Musaddad added: but he disliked that they would rely on it, or he preferred that they not rely on it; then both narrators agree — By Allah, it is in Ramadān, on the twenty-seventh night; he made no exception.
I said: O Abū al-Mundhir, how do you know that? He said: By the sign that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ told us.
I said to Zirr: What is the sign? He said: The sun rises on the morning of that night like a basin, without any rays, until it has risen high.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He said: I will certainly watch the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ tonight. He said:
So I laid my head down on his threshold, or his tent,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed two short units of prayer,
then he prayed two long, long, long units,
then he prayed two units, shorter than the two before them,
then he prayed two units, shorter than the two before them,
then he prayed two units, shorter than the two before them,
then he prayed two units, shorter than the two before them, and then he prayed the Witr,
making thirteen units in all.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: when he stood for the obligatory prayer, he would raise his hands level with his shoulders. He would do the same when he finished his recitation and wished to bow, and he would do it when he raised his head from bowing. He would not raise his hands in any part of his prayer while sitting. And when he stood up after the two prostrations, he would raise his hands likewise and say the takbīr. When he began the prayer, after the takbīr, he would say:

"I have turned my face to the One who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward the truth, and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, who has no partner. This I have been commanded, and I am of the Muslims. O Allah, You are the Sovereign; there is no god but You. Glory be to You; You are my Lord and I am Your servant. I have wronged myself and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me all my sins; none forgives sins but You. Guide me to the best of character; none guides to the best of it but You. Turn away from me its evil; none turns away its evil from me but You. Here I am at Your service, and happy to serve You. I am through You and to You. There is no refuge from You and no shelter except in You. I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You."
Then he would recite. When he bowed, his words in his bowing were:
"O Allah, to You I have bowed, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. You are my Lord. My hearing, my sight, my brain and my bones are humbled before Allah, Lord of the worlds."
When he raised his head from bowing, he said:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him," and then he followed it with:
"O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs all praise, filling the heavens and the earth and filling whatever else You will."
When he prostrated, he said in his prostration:

"O Allah, to You I have prostrated, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. You are my Lord. My face has prostrated to the One who created it and opened its hearing and sight. Blessed is Allah, the best of creators."
And when he finished the prayer he would say:
"O Allah, forgive me what I have sent ahead and what I have left behind, what I have done in secret and what I have done openly. You are my God; there is no god but You."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
And the practice is in accordance with this according to al-Shāfiʿī and some of our companions.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned several hadith, among them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you stands up at night and the Qur'an becomes difficult on his tongue so that he does not know what he is saying, let him lie down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Sūrat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjāl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was at the pond of Banū Ghifār. He said: Jibrīl, peace be upon him, came to him and said: Allah commands you to have your nation recite the Qur'an in one mode. He said:
"I ask Allah for His pardon and forgiveness; my nation cannot bear that."
Then he came to him a second time and said: Allah commands you to have your nation recite the Qur'an in two modes. He said:
"I ask Allah for His pardon and forgiveness; my nation cannot bear that."
Then he came to him a third time and said: Allah commands you to have your nation recite the Qur'an in three modes. He said:
"I ask Allah for His pardon and forgiveness; my nation cannot bear that."
Then he came to him a fourth time and said: Allah commands you to have your nation recite the Qur'an in seven modes, and whichever mode they recite it in, they will be correct.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, thinking that it was only for Hajj. When we arrived in Makkah, we circled the House, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded those who had not brought sacrificial animals to leave the state of iḥrām. She said: So those who had not brought sacrificial animals left iḥrām, and his wives had not brought sacrificial animals, so they left iḥrām too.

ʿĀʾishah said: I began my menstrual period and so I did not circle the House. When it was the night of al-Ḥaṣbah, she said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, the people are returning with an ʿUmrah and a Hajj, while I return with only a Hajj." He said:
"Did you not circle the House on the nights we arrived in Makkah?"
She said: I said, "No." He said:
"Then go with your brother to at-Tanʿīm and enter iḥrām for ʿUmrah, and then your meeting place will be such and such a place."
Ṣafiyyah said: "I think I am only holding you all back." He said:
"May she be barren and shaven-headed! Did you not circle on the Day of Sacrifice?" She said, "Yes." He said:
"There is no harm. Depart."
ʿĀʾishah said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met me as he was ascending from Makkah while I was descending toward it, or I was ascending while he was descending from it.
And Isḥāq said: [she was] descending and [he was] descending.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Abū al-Aswad,
Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Nawfal, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah,

may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year of the Farewell Hajj. Some of us entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah, some for Hajj and ʿUmrah together, and some for Hajj alone, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered iḥrām for Hajj. Those who entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah left iḥrām, while those who entered iḥrām for Hajj, or combined Hajj and ʿUmrah, did not leave iḥrām until the Day of Sacrifice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They used to consider that ʿUmrah,

during the months of Hajj, was among the most wicked of wrongdoings on earth. They would treat Muḥarram as Ṣafar and say: "When the backs of the camels have healed, the hair has grown back, and Ṣafar has passed," or he said, "Ṣafar has begun, then ʿUmrah becomes lawful for whoever wishes to perform it." The Prophet ﷺ and his Companions arrived on the morning of the fourth, having entered iḥrām for Hajj, and he commanded them to make it an ʿUmrah. This weighed heavily upon them, and they said, "O Messenger of Allah, what [kind of] release [from iḥrām] is it?" He said, "Complete release."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn said to me: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed tamattuʿ, and we performed it with him. He said: Then a man said something about it according to his own opinion.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That whenever he came [to Makkah], he would spend the night at Dhū Ṭuwā,
until, when morning came, he would enter,
and when he departed, he would pass by Dhū Ṭuwā and spend the night there until morning,
and he used to mention that the Prophet ﷺ used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered [Makkah] in the year of the Conquest from Kadāʾ, from the upper part of Makkah, and in the ʿUmrah he entered from Kudā. He said: ʿUrwah used to enter from both, but he most often entered from Kudā, which was the closer of the two to his home.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Sālim ibn ʿAbd
Allāh, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq
informed ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from ʿĀʾishah,
the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Have you not seen that when your people rebuilt the Kaʿbah, they fell short of the foundations of Ibrāhīm?"
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, will you not restore it to the foundations of Ibrāhīm?"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Were it not that your people have only recently left disbelief, I would have done so."

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: "If ʿĀʾishah heard this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then I think the only reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not touch the two corners next to the Ḥijr is that the House was not completed on the foundations of Ibrāhīm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the Ḥijr. He said:
"It is part of the House."
I said, "What prevented them from including it in the House?" He said:
"Their funds ran short."
I said, "Then why is its door raised, so that no one can reach it except by a ladder?" He said:

"Your people did that so that they could admit whom they wished and keep out whom they wished. Were it not that your people have only recently left disbelief, and I fear their hearts would be averse, I would have considered changing it, so that I would include in it what was left out of it, and make its door level with the ground."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:

"Were it not that your people have only recently left disbelief, I would have demolished the Kaʿbah and built it on the foundation of Ibrāhīm, for when Quraysh built the House they fell short, and I would have made a back door for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Ṭāʾif and visited ʿAnbasah ibn Abī Sufyān as he was dying, and I saw him in distress, so I said, "You are upon good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [She,] the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, [reported] that her beloved, Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ, told her; he said:
"There is no believing servant who prays four rakʿahs after the noon prayer, and then the Fire touches his face, ever, if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ said:

"When the believer is at the point of death, the angels of mercy come to him with a white silk cloth and say: 'Come out, content and with Allah's pleasure upon you, to the mercy of Allah, to fragrance, and to a Lord who is not angry.'

So the soul comes out like the finest scent of musk, such that they pass it from one to another until they bring it to the gate of heaven, and they say: 'How wonderful is this fragrance that has come to you from the earth!'

Then they bring it to the souls of the believers, and they are more delighted with it than one of you is with his absent loved one when he returns to him. They ask him, 'What did so-and-so do? What did so-and-so do?' They say, 'Leave him, for he was in the distress of the world.' Then if he says, 'Has he not come to you?' they say, 'He has been taken to his mother, the Abyss.' And when the disbeliever is at the point of death, the angels of punishment come to him with a coarse cloth and say: 'Come out, displeased and with displeasure upon you, to the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'
So it comes out like the foulest stench of a carcass, until they bring it to the gate of the earth, and they say: 'How foul is this smell!' until they bring it to the souls of the disbelievers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a young daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was dying, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took her and held her to his chest, then placed his hand upon her, and she passed away in the hands of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Umm Ayman wept, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"Umm Ayman, are you weeping while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is with you?"
She said, "Why should I not weep when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is weeping?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I am not weeping; rather, it is mercy."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The believer is in good in every state: his soul is drawn out from between his sides while he praises Allah, Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Fāṭimah

wept over the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he died, and she said, "O my father, who answered the call of his Lord! O my father, how near he is to him! O my father, to Jibrīl we announce his death! O my father, whose abode is the Paradise of Firdaws!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Do not wail over me, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not wailed over. [Abridged]
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the pledge of allegiance from the women, he took it from them that they would not wail. They said, "O Messenger of Allah, some women helped us [in mourning] in the Pre-Islamic Era; may we help them in return?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no helping [in wailing] in Islam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibn Abī Mulaykah
say: Ibn ʿAbbās said: ʿĀʾishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said:
"Allah, Mighty and Majestic, increases the disbeliever in punishment because of some of his family's weeping over him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He fell unconscious, and a concubine of his who had borne him a child wept. When he recovered, he said to her, "Has what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said not reached you?" So we asked her, and she said that he said:
"He is not one of us who strikes his cheeks, shaves his head, or tears his garments [in mourning]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Abū Mūsā became gravely ill, his wife cried out. He said, "Do you not know what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said?" She said, "Yes."

Then she fell silent. Afterwards it was said to her, "What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say?" She said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who shaves [his head], or strikes [his cheeks], or tears [his garments] in mourning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him: that a man
came to the Prophet ﷺ with a son of his, and he said to him, "Do you love him?"
He said, "May Allah love you as I love him."
Then the boy died, and [the Prophet ﷺ] missed him and asked about him. Then he said:
"Would it not please you that you will not come to any of the gates of Paradise except that you will find him there, hastening to open it for you?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb

wrote to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ḥusayn to console him over a son of his who had died, and he mentioned in his letter that he heard his father narrate from his grandfather ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah is not pleased to give His believing servant any reward less than Paradise when He takes away his dearest one from the people of the earth, and he is patient, hopes for reward from Allah, and says what he has been commanded to say."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣāliḥ and Abū Sufyān, from Jābir,
from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the mention of licking [the fingers].
And from Abū Sufyān, from Jābir, from the Prophet ﷺ, and he mentioned the morsel, similar to their hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ. And from al-Aʿmash,
from Abū Sufyān, from Jābir, with this hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A neighbor
of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a Persian who made good broth, prepared [a meal] for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then came to invite him. He said, "And this one?"
— meaning ʿĀʾishah — and the man said, "No."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "No."
He came back to invite him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "And this one?" The man said, "No."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "No."
Then he came back again to invite him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "And this one?" He said, "Yes," the third time.
So the two of them got up, hurrying one another along, until they came to his house.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day or one night, and there were Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. He said,
"What has brought you out of your houses at this hour?"
They said, "Hunger, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"And I, by the One in whose hand is my soul, what brought me out is what brought you out. Get up."
So they got up with him, and he came to a man of the Anṣār, but he was not in his house. When his wife saw him, she said, "Welcome, and greetings."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her, "Where is so-and-so?"
She said, "He went to fetch us some fresh water."

Then the Anṣārī came, looked at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his two companions, and said, "Praise be to Allah, no one today has more honorable guests than I." He went off and came back to them with a cluster of dates containing unripe dates, ripe dates, and moist dates, and said, "Eat from this."
He took up a knife, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Beware of the milch animal."
So he slaughtered a sheep for them, and they ate of the sheep and of that cluster and drank. When they were full and satisfied, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar,

"By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will surely be asked about this bounty on the Day of Resurrection. Hunger brought you out of your houses, and you did not return until you received this bounty."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While Abū Bakr was sitting, and ʿUmar with him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to them and said,
"What has made you sit here?"
They said, "By the One who sent you with the truth, hunger drove us out of our houses."
Then he mentioned [the rest] similar to the hadith of Khalaf ibn Khalīfah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ṭalḥah sent me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

And he related the hadith similar to the hadith of Ibn Numayr, except that at the end he said: Then he took what was left, gathered it together, and invoked blessing upon it. He said: It returned to what it had been, and he said, "Here, take this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ṭalḥah ordered Umm Sulaym to prepare
food for the Prophet ﷺ for himself alone, then he sent me to him.
And he related the hadith and said in it: The Prophet ﷺ placed his hand on it, mentioned the name of Allah over it, and then said, "Admit ten people."
So he admitted them and they entered. He said,
"Eat, and mention the name of Allah."
They ate, until he had done that for eighty men.
Then after that the Prophet ﷺ and the people of the house ate, and they left some leftovers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this story about the food of Abū Ṭalḥah, from the Prophet ﷺ, and he said in it: Abū Ṭalḥah stood at the door until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, and he said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, it was only a small amount." He said,
"Bring it, for Allah will put blessing in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ṭalḥah saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lying down in the mosque, turning over from back to belly. He went to Umm Sulaym and said, "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lying down in the mosque, turning over from back to belly, and I think he is hungry."
And he related the hadith and said in it: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Ṭalḥah, Umm Sulaym, and Anas ibn Mālik ate, and some food was left over, so we gave it as a gift to our neighbors.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Dhakwān, the freed slave of ʿĀʾishah, said: I heard ʿĀʾishah say,
"I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a girl whose family are marrying her off: is she to be consulted or not?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her, "Yes, she is to be consulted."
ʿĀʾishah said: So I said to him, "But she is shy."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"That is her permission when she remains silent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman

from the descendants of Jaʿfar feared that her guardian would marry her off while she was unwilling, so she sent word to two elders of the Anṣār, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Mujammiʿ, the sons of Jāriyah. They said, "Do not worry,
for Khansāʾ bint Khidhām was married off by her father while she was unwilling,
and the Prophet ﷺ rejected that marriage."
Sufyān said: As for ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, I heard him narrate from his father that Khansāʾ
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men
came during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and delivered speeches, and the people were amazed at their words. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to us and said,
"Indeed, some eloquence is [like] magic," or [he said],
"Indeed, part of eloquence is magic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf
married a woman for the weight of a date-stone [in gold],
and the Prophet ﷺ saw the glow of a wedding on him and asked him. He said, "I have married a woman for the weight of a date-stone."
And from Qatādah, from Anas: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf married a woman for the weight of a date-stone of gold.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is not lawful for a woman to ask for her sister's divorce in order to empty her dish,
for she will have only what has been decreed for her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Abū Usayd al-Sāʿidī married, he invited the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions,
and no one prepared food for them or served it to them except his wife, Umm Usayd.
She had soaked some dates in a stone basin during the night.
When the Prophet ﷺ had finished eating, she mashed them for him and gave him [the drink] to drink, offering it to him as a gift.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Woman was created from a rib and will never be straight for you on one path. If you enjoy her, you enjoy her while she still has some crookedness; and if you try to straighten her, you will break her, and breaking her is divorcing her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Beware of entering upon women."
A man of the Anṣār said, "O Messenger of Allah, what about the in-law?" He said, "The in-law is death."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"A woman should not be in close contact with another woman and then describe her to her husband as though he were looking at her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a man, when he has been away for a long time, to come to his family at night unexpectedly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a military expedition, and when we reached Medina we went to enter, but he said,
"Wait until we enter at night, that is, at nightfall, so that the woman with unkempt hair may comb it and the woman whose husband has been away may shave her pubic hair."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked al-Zuhrī: Which of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ sought refuge from him? He said: ʿUrwah informed me from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that when the daughter of al-Jawn was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he approached her, she said, "I seek refuge with Allah from you." He said to her,
"You have sought refuge with One Who is Great. Return to your family."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about a man who divorced his wife, meaning three times, and she married another husband, who consummated the marriage with her, then divorced her before having intercourse with her: is she lawful for her first husband? She said: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"She is not lawful for the first until the other has tasted her sweetness and she has tasted his sweetness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥabībah bint Sahl was married to Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās, who was an ugly man.
She said, "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, if it were not for fear of Allah, I would spit in his face when he comes in to me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Will you return his garden to him?" She said, "Yes."
He said: So she returned his garden to him.
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"I was sent, and the Hour, like these two."
Abū Dāwūd pointed with the index and middle fingers, [showing] how much one exceeds the other.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
I was brought [to Zamzam], and they took me to Zamzam, where my chest was opened; then it was washed with Zamzam water, and then I was set down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jibrīl came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was playing with the boys. He took him, laid him down, split open his chest and took out his heart. He extracted a clot from it and said, "This was Satan's share of you."

Then he washed it in a golden basin with Zamzam water, then put it back together, and returned it to its place. The boys came running to his mother, meaning his wet nurse, and said, "Muhammad has been killed!"
They went to meet him, and his face was pale.
Anas said: I used to see the mark of that stitching on his chest.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
I saw myself in al-Ḥijr while Quraysh were questioning me about my night journey. They asked me about things in Bayt al-Maqdis that I had not memorized.

I was distressed with a distress the like of which I had never known." He said: "Then Allah raised it up for me so that I could look at it, and they did not ask me about anything but I told them about it. And I saw myself among a group of the prophets. There was Mūsā standing in prayer, a lean man with curly hair, as if he were one of the men of Shanūʾah. And there was ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, standing in prayer; the person most resembling him was ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī. And there was Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, standing in prayer; the person most resembling him is your companion," meaning himself. "Then the time for prayer came and I led them. When I finished the prayer, someone said: 'O Muhammad, this is Mālik, the keeper of the Fire; greet him with peace.'
I turned to him, but he preceded me in greeting me with peace."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw Him with his heart.
label: machine translation

segments_en: {The heart did not lie about what it saw.} {And he certainly saw him in another descent.} He said: He saw Him with his heart, twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah: Did Muhammad ﷺ see his Lord? She said: "Glory be to Allah! My hair stood on end at what you said."
And he narrated the hadith with its story.
The hadith of Dāwūd is more complete and longer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Abū Dharr: If I had seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would have asked him. He said: What would you have asked him? He said: I would have asked him whether he saw his Lord. Abū Dharr said: I did ask, and he said: "I saw a light."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Someone said] to the Prophet ﷺ: O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection? And he narrated the hadith with a meaning similar to the hadith of Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He mentioned several hadith, among them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The lowest seat of any of you in Paradise is that he will be told: Wish.
So he wishes and wishes, and He says to him: Have you wished? He says: Yes.
He says to him: Then you have what you wished for and the like of it with it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yes.

I said to ʿĪsā ibn Ḥammād: Did al-Layth ibn Saʿd inform you, from Khālid ibn Yazīd, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: We said, O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Do you have difficulty seeing the sun on a clear day?" We said: No.
I recounted the hadith until its end, and it is similar to the hadith of Ḥafṣ ibn Maysarah.
And he added after the words "without any deed they had done or any good they had sent ahead":
"It will be said to them: You have what you have seen and the like of it with it."
Abū Saʿīd said: It has reached me that the bridge is thinner than a hair and sharper than a sword.
And in the hadith of al-Layth there is not:
"They will say: Our Lord, You have given us what You have not given to anyone among the worlds."
nor what comes after it. And ʿĪsā ibn Ḥammād acknowledged it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to bring two men from among those killed at Uhud together [in one grave].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Bury them in their blood."
He meant on the day of Uhud, and he did not wash them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the battle of Uhud drew near, my father called me during the night and said: "I think I will be among the first of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ to be killed,
and I am leaving behind no one dearer to me than you,
except the soul of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
I have a debt, so repay it,
and treat your sisters well."
When morning came, he was the first to be killed,
and another man was buried with him in one grave.
Then I was not at ease leaving him with the other man, so I took him out after six months,
and he was just as he had been on the day I laid him down, except for a little [damage to] his ear.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbaydullāh said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: I and my mother were
among the oppressed: I was among the children, and my mother among the women.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Shihāb said: Funeral prayer is offered for every child who has died, even if he is born of illegitimate union,
because he was born upon the natural disposition of Islam,
[provided] his parents, or his father alone, claimed Islam,
even if his mother was not a Muslim.
If he cried out at birth, the prayer is offered for him,
but it is not offered for one who did not cry out, because he is considered miscarried.
For Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, used to narrate that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"There is no child but is born upon the natural disposition (fiṭrah),
and then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian,
just as an animal gives birth to a perfectly formed young one. Do you see any of them born with a cut-off ear?"
Then Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, would recite: {The natural disposition of Allah upon which He created mankind} [and the rest of] the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever deliberately swears falsely by a religion other than Islam is as he said,
and whoever kills himself with a piece of iron will be punished with it in the fire of Hell."
Ḥajjāj ibn Minhāl said: Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan:
Jundab, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us in this mosque, and we have not forgotten,
nor do we fear that Jundab would lie about the Prophet ﷺ. He said:
"A man had a wound and he killed himself. Allah said: 'My servant hastened his own end; I have forbidden Paradise to him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The one who strangles himself will strangle himself in the Fire,
and the one who stabs himself will stab himself in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mūsā [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"If any of you passes through a gathering or a marketplace while carrying arrows in his hand, let him hold them by their heads [blades], then let him hold them by their heads, then let him hold them by their heads."
He said: Abū Mūsā said, "By Allah, we did not die until we had pointed them at one another's faces."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A black man, or woman, used to sweep the mosque, and then died,
and the Prophet ﷺ was not informed of the death. One day he mentioned that person and said:
"What happened to that person?"
They said, "He died, Messenger of Allah." He said, "Why did you not inform me?"
They said, "He was such and such, and his story was such and such."
He said: They made light of his affair. He said:
"Show me his grave."
So he went to the grave and prayed over him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on the day of ʿĪd, he would order that a spear be brought and set before him,
and he would pray facing it, with the people behind him,
and he would do this when traveling as well,
and from that time the rulers adopted it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of the Conquest, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the Kaaba, and with him were Bilāl and ʿUthmān ibn Shaybah, and they closed it upon themselves from the inside. When they came out, I asked Bilāl where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had prayed, and he told me that he prayed facing forward when he entered, between the two pillars on his right. Then I blamed myself for not having asked him how many [units] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [This was] a recitation to him while I listened,
from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me, from Nāfiʿ,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,

that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the Kaaba, he together with Usāmah ibn Zayd, Bilāl and ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥah al-Ḥajabī, and he had it closed upon him. ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: I asked Bilāl when he came out, "What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do?" He said, "He placed one pillar on his left, two pillars on his right, and three pillars behind him" — the House then stood on six pillars — "then he prayed, with about three cubits between himself and the wall."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray his night prayer while she was lying across between him and the qiblah, asleep on the bed on which she slept, until, when he wished to pray the Witr, he would wake her and I would pray Witr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Mālik, "Did ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr narrate to you,
from ʿAmr ibn Sulaym al-Zuraqī,
from Abū Qatādah,

that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray while carrying Umāmah, the daughter of Zaynab, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and of Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn al-Rabīʿ; when he stood he would carry her, and when he prostrated he would put her down?" Yaḥyā said: Mālik said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with ʿUmar, and he said, "Which of you remembers the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the trial (fitnah) exactly as he said it?" He said: I said, "I do."
He said, "You are bold indeed! How did he say it?" He said: I said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'A man's trial concerning his family, his wealth, himself, his children and his neighbor is expiated by fasting, prayer, charity, enjoining good and forbidding evil.'"

ʿUmar said, "This is not what I want. I want the one that surges like the waves of the sea." He said: I said, "What concern is it of yours, Commander of the Faithful? Between you and it is a closed door." He said, "Will the door be broken or opened?" He said: I said, "No, broken."
He said, "Then it is more likely never to be closed again."
He said: We said to Ḥudhayfah, "Did ʿUmar know who the door was?" He said, "Yes, as he knows that tomorrow is preceded by night. I narrated to him a narration that was not made of falsehoods."
He said: We were afraid to ask Ḥudhayfah who the door was, so we said to Masrūq, "Ask him." So he asked, and he said: ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

got from a woman something short of illicit sexual intercourse; I do not know how far it went, except that it was less than fornication. He came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and Allah, Glorified, revealed: {Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.} The man said, "Messenger of Allah, is this for me?" He said:
"For whoever acts upon it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ received some captives, so my sister and I went, along with Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We complained to him about the hardship we were in, and asked him to order that we be given some of the captives.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The orphans of Badr have preceded you. But I will direct you to something better for you than that: declare Allah's greatness after every prayer thirty-three times, glorify Him thirty-three times, and praise Him thirty-three times, and [say]: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things."
ʿAyyāsh said: The two of them were the cousins of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī said to Ibn Aʿbud: Shall I not tell you about myself and Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? She was the dearest of his family to him, and she was my wife. She pulled the millstone until it left marks on her hand, carried water in the waterskin until it left marks on her chest, and swept the house until her clothes were dusty, and lit the fire under the pot until her clothes were darkened. She suffered hardship from that. Then we heard that some servants had been brought to the Prophet ﷺ, so I said: If only you would go to your father and ask him for a servant to help you.

So she went to him and found some people talking with him, and she felt shy and returned. The next morning he came to us while we were in our blanket, and he sat by her head. She put her head inside the blanket out of shyness before her father. He said:
"What was your need of the family of Muḥammad yesterday?"

She remained silent twice, so I said: By Allah, I will tell you, Messenger of Allah. She pulled the millstone until it left marks on her hand, carried water in the waterskin until it left marks on her chest, and swept the house until her clothes were dusty, and lit the fire under the pot until her clothes were darkened. And it reached us that some servants had come to you, so I told her to ask you for a servant.
Then he mentioned the meaning of the hadith of al-Ḥakam, and completed it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this story, he said: And he did not give her a servant.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Jaʿfar, meaning Ibn ʿĪsā, said: We used to say that he was one of the Abdāl, before we heard that the Abdāl were from among the freed slaves. He said: ad-Dakhīl ibn Iyās ibn Nūḥ ibn Mujjāʿah narrated to me from Hilāl ibn Sirāj ibn Mujjāʿah, from his father, from his grandfather Mujjāʿah, that he came to the Prophet ﷺ seeking blood-money for his brother, whom Banū Sadūs of Banū Dhuhl had killed. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"If I were to grant blood-money to a polytheist, I would grant it to your brother. But I will give you something from it as compensation."

So the Prophet ﷺ wrote for him [an order] for one hundred camels from the first fifth to come out from the polytheists of Banū Dhuhl. He took a portion of them, then Banū Dhuhl accepted Islam. After that Mujjāʿah sought the rest from Abū Bakr, and brought him the letter of the Prophet ﷺ. So Abū Bakr wrote for him [an order] for twelve thousand ṣāʿ from the charity (ṣadaqah) of al-Yamāmah: four thousand of wheat, four thousand of barley, and four thousand of dates. The letter of the Prophet ﷺ to Mujjāʿah read:

"In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is a letter from Muḥammad the Prophet to Mujjāʿah ibn Murārah of Banū Sulmā: I have given him one hundred camels from the first fifth to come out from the polytheists of Banū Dhuhl, as compensation for his brother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had a share called aṣ-Ṣafī: a male slave if he wished, or a female slave if he wished, or a horse, which he would choose before the fifth was taken.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Muḥammad about the share of the Prophet,
ﷺ, and aṣ-Ṣafī. He said: A share would be allotted to him along with the Muslims, even if he was not present, and aṣ-Ṣafī was an item taken for him from the fifth before anything else.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on a military expedition, he had a chosen share (ṣāfī) which he would take from wherever he wished. Ṣafiyyah was from that share. When he did not go out on the expedition himself, a share was allotted to him, and he was not given a choice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafiyyah was from aṣ-Ṣafī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The captives were gathered, meaning at Khaybar. Then Diḥyah came and said: Messenger of Allah, give me a female captive from the captives. He said:
"Go and take a girl."

So he took Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy. Then a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Prophet of Allah, you have given Diḥyah Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy, the lady of Qurayẓah and an-Naḍīr. She is suitable only for you. He said: "Call him with her."
When the Prophet ﷺ looked at her, he said to him:
"Take another girl from the captives instead of her."
And the Prophet ﷺ set her free and married her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Banū ʿAbdullāh ibn Kaʿb said: The cavalry of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raided us, so I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found him eating his morning meal. He said, "Come closer and eat."
I said, "I am fasting." He said,

"Come closer and I will tell you about fasting: Allah, the Exalted, has lifted fasting from the traveler, along with half of the prayer, and has lifted fasting from the pregnant woman and the nursing mother."
By Allah, the Prophet ﷺ said both of them, or one of them. How I regret that I did not eat from the food of the Prophet ﷺ!
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no wagering in a contest except in [racing with] a camel's foot, a horse's hoof, or an arrow."
label: machine translation

segments_en: His banner on the day he entered Makkah was white.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were standing with the Prophet ﷺ at ʿArafah, he said:
"O people, every household must offer a sacrifice [aḍḥāh] and an ʿatīrah every year."
Muʿādh said: Ibn ʿAwn used to offer the ʿatīrah; I saw him with my own eyes in Rajab.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to sacrifice a horned, strong ram that looked in black, ate in black, and walked in black.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade sacrificing an animal with a broken horn or a torn ear.
Qatādah said: I mentioned that to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, and he said: Broken [ʿaḍb] means that which reaches half or more than that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, is slaughter only valid at the throat and the upper chest?" He said:
"Even if you stabbed it in its thigh, it would suffice you."
Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn said: This applies in cases of necessity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The lahd [niche grave] is for us, and the shaqq [trench grave] is for others."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed women who visit graves, and those who build mosques over them and place lamps on them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever swears an oath and says, 'If Allah wills,' has the choice: if he wishes, he may carry it out, and if he wishes, he may leave it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I was listening,
from Ibn Wahb,
who said: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me,
from Kaʿb ibn ʿAlqamah,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shimāsah,
from ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The expiation for a vow is the expiation for an oath."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Makhramah al-ʿAbdī and I brought cloth

from Hajar and came with it to Makkah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us walking and bargained with us over a pair of trousers, and we sold it to him. There was a man there who weighed for payment, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Weigh, and give extra."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade the sale of an animal for an animal on deferred terms.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to trade, but he was weak in judgment in his dealings. His family came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Prophet of Allah, place a restriction on so-and-so, for he trades but is weak in judgment in his dealings." The Prophet ﷺ called him and forbade him from trading. He said, "O Prophet of Allah, I cannot refrain from trading."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If you will not give up trading, then say: 'Here, take it, and there is no deception.'"
Abū Thawr said, from Saʿīd:
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying, "O Messenger of Allah, a man comes to me asking me to sell him something I do not have; may I sell it to him and then buy it for him from the market?" He said:
"Do not sell what you do not have."
label: machine translation

segments_en: …ʿAbbās, both attributing the report to the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

"It is not lawful for a man to give a gift and then take it back, except a father with regard to what he gives his child. The likeness of one who gives a gift and then takes it back is that of a dog that eats until it is full, then vomits, and then returns to its vomit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every intoxicant is forbidden, and whatever intoxicates in large amounts, a small amount of it is forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It reached him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best thing with which you change gray hair is henna and katam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were presented before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Qurayẓah. Whoever had grown [pubic hair] was killed, and whoever had not grown any was released. I was among those who had not grown any, so I was released.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We asked Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd about hanging the hand
around the neck of a thief: is it a Sunnah? He said: A thief was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his hand was cut off. Then he ordered that it be hung around his neck.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There were three times at which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to forbid us to pray or to bury our dead: when the sun is rising until it has risen high, when the sun stands at its zenith at midday until it passes the meridian, and when the sun inclines toward setting until it has set—or as he said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ḍamrah ibn Saʿīd al-Māzinī,
from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh,
that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb

asked Abū Wāqid al-Laythī: "What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite in the prayers of al-Aḍḥā and al-Fiṭr?" He said: "He used to recite in them 'Qāf. By the glorious Qurʾān' and 'The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:
"When you attend the sick or the dead, say what is good, for the angels say 'Āmīn' to what you say."
She said: When Abū Salamah died, I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, Abū Salamah has died." He said:
"Say: 'O Allah, forgive me and him, and grant me after him a good compensation.'"
She said: I said it, and Allah gave me in his place one who is better than him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zayd ibn Arqam used to say four takbīrs over our funerals, but once he said five takbīrs over a funeral. We asked him about that, and he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say takbīr over them [that many times]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ throwing pebbles from his mount on the Day of Sacrifice in the forenoon; after that day, it was after the sun had passed its zenith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sister of ʿUkkāshah said: I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among some people, and he was saying:
"I had intended to forbid ghīlah, but I looked at the Romans and the Persians, and they practice ghīlah with their children, and it does their children no harm at all."
Then they asked him about withdrawal (ʿazl), and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"That is the hidden burying alive."
ʿUbaydullāh added in his narration from al-Muqriʾ: "And it is [the verse]: 'And when the girl buried alive is asked.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm,
all of them from al-Muʿtamir,
—and the wording is Yaḥyā's—al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān informed us, from Ayyūb,
who narrated from Abū al-Khalīl, from ʿAbd
Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from Umm al-Faḍl,

who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ while he was in my house and said, "O Prophet of Allah, I had a wife and then married another woman besides her, and my first wife claims that she nursed my younger wife once or twice."
The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"One suckling or two sucklings do not make marriage unlawful."
ʿAmr said in his narration: from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He divorced his wife while she was menstruating. He said: "Do you know ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar?" He said, "Yes."

He said: "He divorced his wife while she was menstruating, so ʿUmar went to the Prophet ﷺ and told him what had happened, and he commanded him to take her back." He said: I did not hear him add anything to that, from his father.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale by throwing pebbles and the sale involving uncertainty (gharar).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A resident must not sell for a desert dweller. Leave people, Allah provides for some of them through others."
except that in Yaḥyā's narration it is "He provides."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ said:

"Whoever buys an animal whose milk has been held back in the udder, or a muṣarrāh, has the choice for three days: if he wishes he may keep it, and if he wishes he may return it along with a ṣāʿ of dates, not wheat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī said: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a man suffered loss in fruits he had bought, and his debt grew large. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Give charity to him."
The people gave him charity, but it did not reach enough to pay off his debt, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his creditors:
"Take what you find; you have nothing but that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the family of Ibn al-Azraq, that al-Mughīrah ibn Abī Burdah,
who was from Banū ʿAbd al-Dār, informed him that he
heard Abū Hurayrah

say: A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we travel by sea and carry a little fresh water with us; if we perform ablution with it we will go thirsty. May we perform ablution with sea water?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Its water is purifying, and its dead [creatures] are lawful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he saw
people selling water, so he said: "Do not sell water, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid the selling of water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Muʿāwiyah, and he said, "What has brought us the favor of your visit, Abū so-and-so?"
This is a phrase the Arabs use. So I said, "[It is] a hadith I heard and will tell you. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'Whoever Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, places in charge of any of the affairs of the Muslims, and then shuts himself away from their needs, their want and their poverty, Allah will shut Himself away from his needs, his want and his poverty.'"
He said: So [Muʿāwiyah] appointed a man to attend to the needs of the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb mentioned the fayʾ and said, "I am not more deserving than you of

this fayʾ, and none of us is more deserving of it than another, except that we are [ranked] according to our positions in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the distribution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: the man and his precedence, the man and his trials [in the cause of Islam], the man and his dependents, and the man and his need."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar

entered upon Muʿāwiyah, who said, "What do you need, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān?" He said, "The stipend of the freed slaves, for I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the first time anything came to him, begin with the freed slaves."
label: machine translation
