segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], may Allah be pleased with her, [reported] that a leather pouch containing beads was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he divided it between the free woman and the slave woman.
ʿĀʾishah said, "My father, may Allah be pleased with him, used to give shares to the free man and the slave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the fayʾ came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would distribute it on the same day, giving two shares to the married man and one share to the unmarried man.

Ibn al-Muṣaffā added: "We were called, and I used to be called before ʿAmmār. I was called and he gave me two shares, as I had a family. Then after me ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir was called, and he was given one share."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He went out on Hajj, and when he was at al-Suwaydāʾ, there was a man who had come as if seeking medicine and aloe. He said, "Tell me, [you] who heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the Farewell Hajj, as he was admonishing the people, commanding them and forbidding them. He said:
'O people, take the stipend as long as it is a stipend. But when the Quraysh contend with one another over kingship, and it comes at the expense of the religion of any of you, then leave it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: An army

of the Anṣār was in the land of Persia with their commander. ʿUmar used to relieve the armies every year, but ʿUmar was occupied and neglected them. When the period had passed, the people of that frontier returned. He was harsh with them and threatened them, though they were Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They said, "O ʿUmar, you neglected us and abandoned among us what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded, that some of the troops relieve others."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz
wrote: Whoever asks about the proper uses of the fayʾ,
it is what ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, ruled concerning it, and the believers considered it just, in agreement with the saying of the Prophet ﷺ:
"Allah has placed the truth upon the tongue and heart of ʿUmar."
He fixed the stipends and made a covenant of protection for the people of other religions in return for the jizyah imposed on them; he did not apply a fifth or [the rules of] war booty to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this story, he said: And the two of them, meaning ʿAlī and al-ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them, were disputing over what Allah had granted to His Messenger of the wealth of Banū al-Naḍīr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar said: "And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not spur horses or camels for it."

Al-Zuhrī said: ʿUmar said, "This was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: the villages of ʿUraynah, Fadak, and such and such. 'What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah, the Messenger, the near of kin, the orphans, the needy and the wayfarer,' and 'for the poor emigrants who were driven out of their homes and their wealth,' and 'those who had settled in the abode and in faith before them.'
'And those who came after them.' So this verse encompassed all the people, and no Muslim remained who did not have a right in it.
Ayyūb said, or he said, a share, except for some of those whom you own as slaves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among the arguments ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, put forward was that he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had three special properties: Banū al-Naḍīr, Khaybar and Fadak. As for Banū al-Naḍīr, it was reserved for his emergencies. As for Fadak, it was reserved for the wayfarers. As for Khaybar, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided it into three parts: two parts for the Muslims, and one part for the maintenance of his family. Whatever remained after the maintenance of his family, he gave to the poor among the Emigrants."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by Ibn Ṣāʾid with a group of his Companions, among them ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, while he was playing with the boys near the fortress of Banū Maghālah. He was a young boy, and he did not notice until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck his back with his hand. Then he said:
"Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?"
He said: Ibn Ṣayyād looked at him and said, "I testify that you are the messenger of the unlettered people."
Then Ibn Ṣayyād said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?" The Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"I believe in Allah and His messengers."
Then the Prophet ﷺ said to him, "What comes to you?"
He said, "A truthful one and a liar come to me."
The Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"The matter has been confused for you."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have concealed something for you."
He had concealed for him the verse: {The Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke}. Ibn Ṣayyād said, "It is the dukh."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Be gone! You will never go beyond your limit."
ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to strike his neck."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If he is [the one], you will not be given power over him," meaning the Dajjāl,
"and if he is not him, there is no good for you in killing him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A boy
from among the Jews fell ill, so the Prophet ﷺ came to visit him. He sat by his head and said to him, "Accept Islam."
The boy looked at his father, who was at his head, and his father said to him, "Obey Abū al-Qāsim."
So he accepted Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ stood up saying:
"Praise be to Allah, who has saved him from the Fire through me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no child born except that he is born upon the fiṭrah. Then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a whole animal. Do you find any of them born with a cut-off ear?"
Then Abū Hurayrah would say, "Recite, if you wish: {The fiṭrah of Allah upon which He created mankind. There is no change in the creation of Allah}" [Qurʾān 30:30], the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stood at the well of Badr and said:
"Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?" He said: "They are hearing now what I say to them."
That was mentioned to ʿĀʾishah, and she said, "Did Ibn ʿUmar [really say that]? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said:
'They now know that what I used to tell them is the truth.'"
Then she recited His words: {Indeed, you do not make the dead hear}, until she had recited the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jewish woman came to her,
and mentioned the punishment of the grave,
and said to her, "May Allah protect you from the punishment of the grave."
Then ʿĀʾishah asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the punishment of the grave, and he said:
"Yes, the punishment of the grave [is real]."
ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: After that I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray any prayer without seeking refuge from the punishment of the grave. Ghundar added:
"The punishment of the grave is true."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to ask during his illness in which he died, saying:
"Where will I be tomorrow? Where will I be tomorrow?"
He meant the day of ʿĀʾishah.
So his wives permitted him to be wherever he wished,
and he stayed in the house of ʿĀʾishah until he died there.
ʿĀʾishah said: He died on the day on which it was my turn for him to be with me in my house,
and Allah took him while his head was between my chest and my throat,

and his saliva mixed with mine. Then she said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr came in with a siwāk with which he was cleaning his teeth, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at it. So I said to him, "Give me this siwāk, O ʿAbd al-Raḥmān." He gave it to me, and I bit it,
then chewed it and gave it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he used it to clean his teeth while he was leaning against my chest.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do not curse the dead, for they have reached what they sent forth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent Abū Bakr and commanded him to proclaim these words. Then he sent ʿAlī after him. While Abū Bakr was on the way, he heard the groaning of the camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, al-Qaswāʾ. Abū Bakr came out alarmed, thinking it was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but it was ʿAlī. ʿAlī handed him the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and [the Prophet ﷺ] had commanded ʿAlī to proclaim these words. So they set out and performed Hajj. Then ʿAlī stood during the days of Tashrīq and proclaimed: "The protection of Allah and His Messenger is withdrawn from every polytheist, so travel freely in the land for four months. After this year no polytheist is to perform Hajj, no one is to circumambulate the House naked, and none will enter Paradise except a believer." ʿAlī would make the proclamation, and when his voice grew hoarse, Abū Bakr would stand and proclaim it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When it was revealed:
"And those who hoard gold and silver..." he said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on one of his journeys, and some of his Companions said, "What has been revealed about gold and silver has been revealed.
If only we knew which wealth is best, so that we might acquire it." He said: "
The best is a remembering tongue, a grateful heart, and a believing wife who helps him in his faith."
He said: This is a good hadith.
I asked Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, saying to him, "Did Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd hear from Thawbān?" He said, "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ with a cross of gold around my neck. He said: "
ʿAdī, throw this idol off you."
And I heard him reciting in Sūrat Barāʾah:
"They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah." He said: "
They did not worship them, but when they declared something lawful for them, they considered it lawful, and when they declared something forbidden for them, they considered it forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "

When Allah drowned Pharaoh, he said, 'I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe.' Jibrīl said, 'Muḥammad, if only you had seen me taking mud from the sea and thrusting it into his mouth, fearing that mercy would reach him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he mentioned:
"Jibrīl began thrusting mud into Pharaoh's mouth, fearing that he would say 'There is no god but Allah' and Allah would have mercy on him, or fearing that Allah would have mercy on him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this verse was revealed:

"Among them are the wretched and the blessed," I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying, "Prophet of Allah, for what are we working? For something already finished, or for something not yet finished?" He said: "
Rather, for something already finished, and the pens have run with it, ʿUmar. But everyone is eased toward that for which he was created."
This hadith is good and gharīb from this route; we only know it from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "Messenger of Allah, what do you say about a man who met a woman, with no acquaintance between them, and he did everything with her that a man does with his wife, except that he did not have intercourse with her?"
He said: So Allah revealed:

"Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early part of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember." So he commanded him to perform ablution and pray.
Muʿādh said, "Messenger of Allah, is this for him alone, or for the believers in general?" He said: "
Rather, for the believers in general."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman came to me to buy dates, and I said, "There are better dates than these in the house."
She entered the house with me, and I reached for her and kissed her. Then I went to Abū Bakr and told him about it. He said, "Conceal yourself, repent, and tell no one."
But I could not bear it, so I went to ʿUmar and told him. He said, "Conceal yourself, repent, and tell no one."
Still I could not bear it, so I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him. He said to him: "
Did you betray a man who went out to fight in the cause of Allah, [by acting] with his family like this?"
[He felt so ashamed] that he wished he had not become Muslim until that very moment, until he thought he was one of the people of the Fire.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ lowered his head for a long time, until Allah revealed to him:
"Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early part of the night" up to His words: "a reminder for those who remember."
Abū al-Yusr said: I came to him, and he recited it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. His Companions said, "Messenger of Allah, is this for him alone, or for people in general?" He said: "
Rather, for people in general."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Among us were those who entered iḥrām for Hajj alone, among us were those who combined [Hajj and ʿUmrah], and among us were those who performed tamattuʿ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah came for Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her. (Transition to another chain.)
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying the talbiyah, without mentioning Hajj or ʿUmrah.
And he narrated the hadith with the same meaning as the hadith of Manṣūr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived on the fourth or fifth day of Dhū al-Ḥijjah and came in to see me while he was angry. I said, "Who has made you angry, O Messenger of Allah? May Allah admit him to the Fire." He said:

"Did you not realize that I commanded the people to do something, and yet they are hesitating?" Al-Ḥakam said: "As if they were hesitating," I think. "If I had known beforehand what I know now, I would not have brought the sacrificial animal with me until I bought it [later], and then I would have come out of iḥrām as they have come out of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She had entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah and arrived, but she did not circle the House until she began menstruating, so she performed all the rites.
And she had entered iḥrām for Hajj.
The Prophet ﷺ said to her on the day of departure:
"Your circling is sufficient for both your Hajj and your ʿUmrah."
But she refused, so he sent her with ʿAbd al-Raḥmān to at-Tanʿīm, and she performed ʿUmrah after the Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She began menstruating at Sarif and became pure at ʿArafah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"Your circling between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah is sufficient for both your Hajj and your ʿUmrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came in to see ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) while she was weeping.
Then he narrated it like the hadith of al-Layth up to its end, but he did not mention what came before this in the hadith of al-Layth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah
(may Allah be pleased with her) entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah during the Hajj of the Prophet ﷺ.

And he narrated the hadith with the meaning of the hadith of al-Layth and added to the hadith: He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was an easygoing man; whenever she desired something, he would follow her in it. So he sent her with ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr, and she entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah from at-Tanʿīm."
Maṭar said: Abū az-Zubayr said: "Whenever ʿĀʾishah performed Hajj, she did as she had done with the Prophet of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, having entered iḥrām for Hajj, with women and children among us. When we arrived in Makkah, we circled the House and between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:
"Whoever does not have a sacrificial animal with him should come out of iḥrām."
He said: We said, "What kind of release?" He said: "Complete release."

He said: So we went to our wives, put on [regular] clothes, and applied perfume. When the Day of Tarwiyah came, we entered iḥrām for Hajj, and the first circling between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah sufficed us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to share in the camels and cattle, seven of us for each animal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When we came out of iḥrām, the Prophet ﷺ commanded us to enter iḥrām again when we headed toward Minā.
He said: So we entered iḥrām from al-Abṭaḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās used to command tamattuʿ, while Ibn az-Zubayr used to forbid it. [The narrator] said: I mentioned that to Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and he said: "The hadith passed through my hands: we performed tamattuʿ with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Then when ʿUmar took charge, he said: 'Allah used to permit for His Messenger whatever He wished, in whatever way He wished. And the Qurʾān has been revealed in its [final] stages, so complete the Hajj and ʿUmrah for Allah as Allah has commanded you, and put an end to marriage with these women [temporary marriage]. If I am brought a man who married a woman for a fixed term, I will stone him with rocks.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh and asked him about the Hajj of

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He narrated the hadith similar to the hadith of Ḥātim ibn Ismāʿīl and added in it: "The Arabs used to be carried by Abū Sayyārah on a bare-backed donkey. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed through from Muzdalifah by al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām,
the Quraysh had no doubt that he would stop there and make it his lodging. But he passed on and did not stop there until he reached ʿArafah and dismounted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq said: ʿUthmān used to forbid tamattuʿ, and
ʿAlī used to command it. ʿUthmān said something to ʿAlī, then ʿAlī said: "You know that we performed tamattuʿ with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "Yes, but we were afraid."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The two temporary pleasures are not appropriate except for us in particular."
He meant temporary marriage and tamattuʿ in Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ (may Allah be pleased with him) about tamattuʿ,
and he said: "We did it, and this man at that time was a disbeliever in the ʿarsh."
He meant the houses of Makkah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this chain; and Ibn Ḥātim said in his narration: "A man gave his own opinion as he wished," meaning ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, who is my father?" He said, "Your father is so-and-so."
And [the verse] was revealed: "O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if made plain to you, would distress you" — to the end of the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh swearing by Allah that Ibn Ṣāʾid was the Dajjāl.
I said, "You swear by Allah?" He said, "I heard ʿUmar swear to that in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not deny it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmrah bint ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who was in the care of ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, [reported] from ʿĀʾishah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a man in command of a expedition. He used to recite for his companions in their prayer and would conclude with "Say: He is Allah, the One." When they returned, that was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Ask him why he does that."
So they asked him, and he said, "Because it is the description of the Most Merciful, and I love to recite it."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Tell him that Allah loves him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you have any difficulty in seeing the moon on the night of the full moon? Do you have any difficulty in seeing the sun?" They said, "No." He said:
"Then you will see your Lord just as you see the moon on the night of the full moon; you will have no difficulty in seeing Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said—and His word is the truth—'When My servant intends a good deed, record it for him as one good deed; if he does it, record it for him ten times its like. When he intends an evil deed, do not record it; if he does it, record it as its like; and if he leaves it'—and sometimes he said, 'does not act on it'—'record it for him as a good deed.' Then he recited:
'Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah says: I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he calls upon Me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, and I increase it further. Whoever brings an evil deed, its recompense is the like of it, or I forgive. Whoever draws near to Me by a hand's span, I draw near to him by an arm's length; whoever draws near to Me by an arm's length, I draw near to him by a fathom; and whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him rushing. Whoever meets Me with sins nearly the size of the earth, not associating anything with Me, I will meet him with forgiveness the like of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They said: O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection? He said:
"Do you have difficulty seeing the sun at noon when there is no cloud?" They said: No. He said:
"Do you have difficulty seeing the moon on the night of the full moon when there is no cloud?" They said: No. He said:

"By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will have no difficulty seeing your Lord except as you have in seeing one of the two. He said: A servant will be met, and [the Lord] will say: O so-and-so, did I not honor you, make you a chief, marry you [to a spouse], subjugate horses and camels for you, and leave you to rule and take a quarter [of the spoils]? He will say: Yes.
He said: Then [Allah] will say: Did you think that you would meet Me? He will say: No.
So [Allah] will say: Then today I forget you as you forgot Me.

Then the second will be met, and [Allah] will say: O so-and-so, did I not honor you, make you a chief, marry you [to a spouse], subjugate horses and camels for you, and leave you to rule and take a quarter [of the spoils]? He will say: Yes, my Lord.
[Allah] will say: Did you think that you would meet Me? He will say: No.
So [Allah] will say: Then today I forget you as you forgot Me.
Then the third will be met, and [Allah] will say the same to him. He will say: My Lord, I believed in You, in Your Book, and in Your messengers, and I prayed, fasted, and gave charity.
And he will praise [himself] with as much good as he can. [Allah] will say: Then [stay] here. He said: Then it will be said to him: Now We will raise up Our witness against you.

He will think to himself: Who is it that will testify against me? Then his mouth will be sealed, and it will be said to his thigh, his flesh, and his bones: Speak! So his thigh, his flesh, and his bones will speak of his deeds. That is so that he has no excuse.
That is the hypocrite, and that is the one with whom Allah is angry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
passed by the Prophet ﷺ while he was urinating and greeted him with salaam. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"If you see me in a state like this, do not greet me, for if you do that, I will not return your greeting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution and wiped over his two socks and his sandals.
Al-Muʿallā said in his narration: I only know that he said "and the sandals."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Hannād,
and Abū Kurayb, Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ, Maḥmūd ibn Ghaylān, and Abū ʿAmmār al-Ḥusayn ibn Ḥurayth said: Wakīʿ narrated to us from al-Aʿmash,
from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah,
that the Prophet ﷺ kissed one of his wives, then went out to prayer without performing ablution.
[ʿUrwah] said: I said, "Who is she but you?" He said: So she laughed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When it was the first adhān for the dawn prayer, he — meaning the Prophet ﷺ — commanded me, so I gave the adhān. Then I kept saying, "Shall I give the iqāmah, O Messenger of Allah?" But he kept looking toward the east, at the dawn, and saying, "No."

Until, when the dawn appeared, he got down and went aside [to relieve himself], then returned to me, and his Companions had gathered — meaning he performed ablution. Bilāl wanted to give the iqāmah, but the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"The man from Ṣudāʾ gave the adhān, and whoever gives the adhān is the one who gives the iqāmah." He said: So I gave the iqāmah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the front rows, and the muʾadhdhin is forgiven as far as his voice reaches, and everything moist and dry that hears him testifies for him, and he has a reward like that of whoever prays with him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said, "Yes."
He said: Abū Dharr said, "I was a man from Ghifār,
and news reached us that a man had appeared in Makkah
claiming to be a prophet.
So I said to my brother, 'Go to this man, speak with him, and bring me news of him.' He went and met him,
then returned. I said, 'What do you have?' He said, 'By Allah, I saw a man who commands good and forbids evil.'
I said to him, 'You have not satisfied me with this news.'
So I took a traveling bag and a staff,
then headed to Makkah. I did not know him,
and I disliked asking about him,
so I would drink from the water of Zamzam and stay in the mosque.
He said: ʿAlī passed by me and said, 'It seems the man is a stranger.'
I said, 'Yes.'
He said, 'Then come along to the house.'
So I went with him. He did not ask me about anything, and I did not tell him anything.
When morning came, I went out to the mosque to ask about him,
but no one was telling me anything about him.
Then ʿAlī passed by me and said, 'Has the man not yet learned his lodging?' I said, 'No.'
He said, 'Come with me.'
He said, 'What is your affair, and what brought you to this town?' I said to him, 'If you keep it secret for me, I will tell you.'
He said, 'I will.'
I said to him, 'News reached us that a man has appeared here who claims to be a prophet,
so I sent my brother to speak with him, but he returned and did not satisfy me with the news,
so I wanted to meet him myself.'
He said to him, 'You have indeed been guided rightly.
I am heading toward him now, so follow me.
Enter wherever I enter,
for if I see anyone I fear for you,
I will stand by the wall,
as if I were fixing my sandal, and you go on.'
So he went on and I went with him,
until he entered and I entered with him to the Prophet ﷺ. I said to him, 'Present Islam to me.'
He presented it, and I accepted Islam right there. Then he said to me,
'Abū Dharr, keep this matter secret,
and return to your land,
and when news of our emergence reaches you, then come.'
I said, 'By the One who sent you with the truth, I will proclaim it openly among them.'
So he came to the mosque,
where the Quraysh were, and said, 'People of Quraysh,
I bear witness that there is no god but Allah,
and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.'
They said, 'Get up and go to this apostate!'
They got up and beat me until I was nearly dead, but al-ʿAbbās reached me,
threw himself over me, then turned to them
and said, 'Woe to you! Would you kill a man from Ghifār,
when your trade and your route pass through Ghifār?' So they left me alone.
The next morning I returned and said the same as I had said the day before,
and they said, 'Get up and go to this apostate!'
They did to me the same as they had done the day before, and al-ʿAbbās reached me and threw himself over me,
and said the same as he had said the day before."
He said: This was the beginning of the Islam of Abū Dharr, may Allah have mercy on him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If it pleases you to know the ignorance of the Arabs, then read what is above one hundred and thirty in Sūrat al-Anʿām: "Those who kill their children out of foolishness, without knowledge, have indeed lost" up to His saying: "They have indeed gone astray and were not guided."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When [the verse] "And warn your closest kinsfolk" was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ began calling them, tribe by tribe.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, aged ninety-four, strong and upright. He said, "I know that I have been granted my hearing and my sight only through the supplication of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
My maternal aunt took me to him and said, 'Messenger of Allah, my sister's son is ailing, so supplicate to Allah for him.'
He said: So he supplicated for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, prayed the ʿAṣr prayer,
then went out walking and saw al-Ḥasan playing with the boys,
so he lifted him onto his shoulder and said, "My father be ransom for him! He resembles the Prophet ﷺ, not ʿAlī." And ʿAlī was laughing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ, and I saw whiteness beneath his lower lip, the tuft of hair.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When I greeted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his face was shining with joy,
and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pleased, his face would light up,
until it was as if it were a piece of the moon,
and we would recognize that in him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"I was sent from the best of the generations of the children of Adam, generation after generation,
until I was in the generation in which I was [sent]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: You consider the conquest to be the conquest of Makkah,
and the conquest of Makkah was indeed a conquest,
but we consider the conquest to be the Pledge of Riḍwān on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah.
We were with the Prophet ﷺ fourteen hundred,
and al-Ḥudaybiyah was a well, and we drew it dry,
leaving not a drop in it.
That reached the Prophet ﷺ, so he came to it,
and sat on its edge,
then called for a vessel of water, performed ablution, rinsed his mouth, and supplicated,
then poured it into the well. We left it for a short while, and then it supplied us with all we wanted, we and our mounts.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sleeping in the mosque on a cloak of mine worth thirty dirhams, when a man came and snatched it from me. The man was seized and brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who ordered that his hand be cut off.
He said: I went to him and said, "Will you cut off his hand for the sake of thirty dirhams? I will sell it to him and defer the payment of its price." He said:
"Why did you not do this before you brought him to me?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A thief was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said, "Kill him."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, he only stole." He said, "Cut off his hand."
So his hand was cut off. Then he was brought a second time, and he said, "Kill him."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, he only stole." He said, "Cut off his hand."
So it was cut off. Then he was brought a third time, and he said, "Kill him."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, he only stole." He said, "Cut off his hand."
Then he was brought a fourth time, and he said, "Kill him."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, he only stole." He said, "Cut it off."
Then he was brought a fifth time, and he said, "Kill him."

Jābir said: So we took him to the camel enclosure and put him on [a camel]. He lay on his back, then spread out his hands and feet, and the camels scattered. Then they put him on again a second time, and he did the same. Then they put him on a third time, so we pelted him with stones and killed him. Then we threw him into a well and threw stones on top of him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled concerning a man who had relations with his wife's slave girl: if he had forced her, she is free and he must give her mistress one like her; but if she had consented, she belongs to him and he must give her mistress one like her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever you find having had intercourse with an animal, kill him and kill the animal."

Ibn ʿAbbās was asked, "What is the animal's offence?" He said, "I did not hear anything from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, but I think that the Messenger of Allah disliked that its meat be eaten or that any benefit be taken from it, after that act has been done to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: I would not grieve over anyone upon whom I carried out the prescribed punishment, except the drinker of wine, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not establish any fixed punishment for it; it is only something we ourselves set.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There were [the tribes of] Qurayẓah and an-Naḍīr, and an-Naḍīr were nobler than Qurayẓah. When a man of Qurayẓah killed a man of an-Naḍīr, he was killed for him; but when a man of an-Naḍīr killed a man of Qurayẓah, it was settled by paying a hundred wasqs of dates. When the Prophet ﷺ was sent, a man of an-Naḍīr killed a man of Qurayẓah, and they said, "Hand him over to us so that we may kill him."

Then they said, "Between us and you is the Prophet ﷺ," and they came to him. Then it was revealed: {And if you judge, judge between them with justice}, and justice is a life for a life. Then it was revealed: {Is it the judgement of the Days of Ignorance that they seek?}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever suffers bloodshed or a wound (khabl, meaning a wound), he has a choice among three things; if he wants a fourth, restrain his hands: either to kill, or to pardon, or to take the blood money. Whoever does any of that and then transgresses again, for him is the Fire of Hell, to remain in it forever and ever."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when the killer was brought, being led by the heir of the slain man in a leather strap. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the heir of the slain man, "Will you pardon?" He said, "No." He said, "Will you take the blood money?" He said, "No." He said, "Will you kill him?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Take him away."
When he left and turned away from him, he called him back and said, "Will you pardon?"
He said, "No." He said, "Will you take the blood money?" He said, "No." He said, "Will you kill him?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Take him away."

When he left and turned away from him, he called him back and said, "Will you pardon?" He said, "No." He said, "Will you take the blood money?" He said, "No." He said, "Will you kill him?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Take him away."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said at that point:
"Know that if you pardon him, he will bear his own sin and the sin of your companion."
So he pardoned him and let him go, and I saw him dragging his leather strap.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with ʿUthmān while he was besieged in the house. There was an entrance in the house, and whoever entered it could hear the speech of those on the paved ground outside. ʿUthmān entered it, then came out to us with his face changed in colour, and said, "They have just been threatening me with death."
We said, "Allah will suffice you against them, O Commander of the Faithful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any people who rise from a gathering in which they did not remember Allah have risen from the likeness of the carcass of a donkey, and it will be a cause of regret for them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever lies down in a place of rest without remembering Allah, the Exalted, in it, it will be a source of loss for him on the Day of Resurrection; and whoever sits in a place without remembering Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in it, it will be a source of loss for him on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are words that no one says three times in his gathering when he rises, except that they will serve as an expiation for what took place in it; and no one says them in a gathering of goodness or a gathering of remembrance except that they will be sealed upon it, as a seal is stamped upon a scroll: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. There is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That was reported by ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAmr, from al-Maqburī,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Towards the end, when he wanted to rise from a gathering, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say:
"Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You."
A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are saying something that you did not used to say in the past." He said:
"It is an expiation for whatever takes place in the gathering."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called me, as he wanted to send me with money to Abū Sufyān to distribute among the Quraysh in Mecca after the conquest. He said: "Look for a companion."
He said: Then ʿAmr ibn Umayyah al-Ḍamrī came to me and said: "It has reached me that you want to set out and are looking for a companion."
I said: "Yes."
He said: "Then I am your companion."
He said: So I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I have found a companion." He said: "Who?"
I said: "ʿAmr ibn Umayyah al-Ḍamrī." He said:
"When you descend into the land of his people, beware of him, for the saying goes: 'Your brother is the one from Bakr, yet do not trust him.'"

So we set out, and when I was at al-Abwāʾ, he said: "I have a need to attend to with my people at Waddān, so wait for me." I said: "Go right ahead." When he turned away, I remembered the words of the Prophet ﷺ, so I tightened my camel's saddle and set out, urging it on at speed, until I reached al-Aṣāfir, where I found him coming alongside me with a group of men. I urged my camel on and outpaced him. When he saw that I had left him behind, they turned back, and he came to me and said: "I had a need to attend to with my people."
I said: "Yes." We continued until we reached Mecca, and I handed the money over to Abū Sufyān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ walked, it was as though he were leaning on something.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
I asked: "How did you see him?" He said: "He was fair and handsome. When he walked, it was as though he were descending a slope."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb,
may Allah be pleased with him, and ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nāfiʿ, who said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed me,
from the son of the brother of
Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Gatherings are [held in] trust, except for three gatherings: [one for] shedding forbidden blood, [one for] a forbidden sexual relation, or [one for] seizing property unjustly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has two faces in this world will have two tongues of fire on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among the worst forms of usury is to speak unjustly against the honour of a Muslim."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Among the greatest of the major sins is for a man to speak at length against the honour of a Muslim man without right; and among the major sins is to insult twice for one insult."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When I was taken up [to the heavens], I passed by a people who had nails of copper with which they were scratching their faces and chests. I said: 'Who are these, O Jibrīl?' He said: 'These are those who eat the flesh of people and attack their honour.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: As Ibn al-Muṣaffā said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Whoever eats a meal through [wronging] a Muslim man, Allah will feed him the like of it from Hell; whoever is clothed in a garment through [wronging] a Muslim man, Allah will clothe him with the like of it from Hell; and whoever stands in a position of ostentation and showing off because of a man, Allah will make him stand in a position of ostentation and showing off on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever protects a believer from a hypocrite," – I think he said –

"Allah will send an angel to protect his flesh on the Day of Resurrection from the fire of Hell; and whoever accuses a Muslim of something intending to disgrace him by it, Allah will detain him on the bridge of Hell until he comes out from what he said."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Whether you reveal what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills, and Allah has power over all things," it weighed heavily on the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, knelt on their knees, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we were charged with deeds that we are able to do: prayer, fasting, jihad, and charity. But now this verse has been revealed to you, and we are not able to bear it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do you want to say as the People of the two Scriptures said before you: 'We hear and we disobey'? Rather, say: 'We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'When My servant intends a good deed but does not do it, I record it for him as one good deed. If he does it, I record it as ten good deeds, up to seven hundred times over. And when he intends an evil deed but does not do it, I do not record it against him. If he does it, I record it as one evil deed.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about the whispering [of doubts in the heart], and he said:
"That is pure faith."
label: machine translation

segments_en: People will keep asking you about knowledge until they say: 'This is Allah who created us, so who created Allah?'"
He said, while holding the hand of a man: Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. Two people have already asked me, and this is the third.
Or he said: One person has already asked me, and this is the second.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"They will keep asking you, O Abū Hurayrah, until they say: 'This is Allah, so who created Allah?'"

He said: While I was in the mosque, some of the Bedouins came to me and said: "O Abū Hurayrah, this is Allah, so who created Allah?" He said: So he took a handful of pebbles and threw them at them, then said: "Get up, get up! My beloved friend spoke the truth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when two men came to him disputing over a piece of land. One of them said: "O Messenger of Allah, this man seized my land during the Jāhiliyyah" (he was Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿĀbis al-Kindī, and his opponent was Rabīʿah ibn ʿAbdān). He said: "Your proof?"
He said: "I have no proof." He said: "His oath."
He said: "Then he will take it away." He said:
"You have nothing but that."
He said: When he got up to swear, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever takes a piece of land unjustly will meet Allah while He is angry with him."
Isḥāq said in his narration: Rabīʿah ibn ʿAydān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what if a man comes wanting to take my wealth?" He said:
"Do not give him your wealth."
He said: "What if he fights me?" He said: "Fight him."
He said: "What if he kills me?" He said: "Then you are a martyr."
He said: "What if I kill him?" He said:
"He is in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ḥudhayfah came back from ʿUmar, he sat and spoke to us. He said: "Yesterday, when I sat with the Commander of the Faithful, he asked his companions: 'Which of you remembers the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the trials?'" And he went on to narrate the hadith like the hadith of Abū Khālid, but he did not mention Abū Mālik's explanation of the phrase "murbadd^an mujakhkhiy^an."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Who will tell us," or he said, "Which of you will tell us"—and Ḥudhayfah was among them—"what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about the trial?" Ḥudhayfah said: "I will."

And he went on to narrate the hadith like the hadith of Abū Mālik from Ribʿī. In the hadith he said: Ḥudhayfah said: "I told him a hadith that contains no errors." He said, meaning that it was from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange as it began, and it will retreat between the two mosques as a snake retreats into its hole."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In his narration: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck me with his hand between my neck and my shoulder, then said:
"Do you fight [over this], O Saʿd? I give [wealth] to a man..."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If Allah wills. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Asmāʾ al-Ḍubaʿī narrated to us: Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Mālik, from al-Zuhrī,
that Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and Abū
ʿUbayd informed him from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, like the hadith of Yūnus from al-Zuhrī. And in the hadith of Mālik: "
"but so that my heart may be at rest."
He said: Then he recited this verse until he had passed beyond it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have come to ask you about the vermin of the earth. What do you say about the lizard (ḍabb)?" He said: "
I do not eat it, and I do not forbid it."
I said: "Then I will eat what you have not forbidden. But why, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "
A nation among the nations was lost, and I saw a creature that made me uneasy."
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the hare?" He said: "I do not eat it, and I do not forbid it."
I said: "Then I will eat what you have not forbidden. But why, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "
I was told that it menstruates."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Who would eat the crow, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called it "wicked" (fāsiq)?
By Allah, it is not among the good things.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The snake is wicked, the scorpion is wicked, the mouse is wicked, and the crow is wicked."
It was said to al-Qāsim: "Is the crow eaten?" He said: "Who would eat it after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, 'It is wicked'?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Spread the greeting of peace, feed others, and be brothers, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Whoever loves that Allah increase the good of his house, let him perform ablution when his lunch is served and when it is taken away."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
I do not eat while reclining."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A sheep was given as a gift to the Prophet ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ knelt on his knees to eat. A Bedouin said: "What is this way of sitting?" He said: "
Allah has made me a noble servant, and He has not made me a stubborn tyrant."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to me while I was eating: "Say the name of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
None of you should wipe his hand until he has licked it, for he does not know in which part of his food the blessing lies."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When the dining spread is set out, let each eat from what is nearest to him, and not reach for what is in front of his companion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of the top of a dish of tharīd and said: "
Eat, in the name of Allah, from its sides, and leave its top alone, for the blessing descends upon it from above."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When food is set down, take from its edge and leave its middle, for the blessing descends in its middle."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While he was having lunch, a morsel fell from him. He picked it up, removed whatever dirt was on it, and ate it. The local landlords (dahāqīn) nudged one another and winked about him, and it was said: "May Allah set the governor right! These landlords are winking at one another because you took up the morsel while this food is before you."

He said: "I would not abandon what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ because of these non-Arabs. We used to be commanded, when one of us dropped a morsel, to pick it up, remove whatever dirt was on it, and eat it, and not leave it for Satan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When a morsel falls from the hand of one of you, let him wipe off whatever dirt is on it and eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Eat together and do not separate, for the blessing is with the group."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not blow on food or drink, and would not breathe into the vessel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When one of you has his servant bring him food that has spared him its toil and heat, let him invite him to eat with him. If he does not, let him take a morsel and place it in his hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade getting up from the meal until it has been taken away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

When the dining spread is set out, no man should get up until the spread is taken away, and he should not withdraw his hand, even if he is full, until the people have finished, and he should make excuse, for a man may embarrass his companion, who then withdraws his hand, though perhaps he still has need of the food."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Food was brought to the Prophet ﷺ and was offered to us, and we said: "We have no desire for it." He said: "
Do not combine hunger with lying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Asmāʾ
asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about washing after menstruation, and he said:

"One of you should take her water and lotus leaves and purify herself, doing the purification well, or thoroughly. Then she should pour [water] over her head and rub it vigorously until she reaches the roots of her hair. Then she should pour water over herself. Then she should take a piece of cloth perfumed with musk and purify herself with it."
Asmāʾ said: "How should I purify myself with it?" He said:
"Glory be to Allah! Purify yourself with it."
ʿĀʾishah said, as if concealing it: "Follow with it the traces of blood."
She said: And she asked him about washing after sexual impurity. He said:

"One of you should take her water and purify herself, doing the purification well, or thoroughly, until she pours water over her head and rubs it until she reaches the roots of her hair, then she should let the water flow over her body."
ʿĀʾishah said: "How excellent are the women of the Anṣār! Shyness did not prevent them from seeking understanding in the religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he said:
In the year of the Conquest, I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in the upper part of Makkah.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up to wash, and Fāṭimah screened him. Then he took his garment, wrapped himself in it, and prayed eight rakʿahs, the Ḍuḥā prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ relieved himself, then food was brought to him and he ate, without touching water.
He said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār added for me, from Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥuwayrith, that it was said to the Prophet ﷺ: "You have not performed ablution." He said:
"I did not intend to pray, that I should perform ablution."
And ʿAmr claimed that he heard it from Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥuwayrith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to sleep and then pray without performing ablution. He said: I said, "Did you hear it from Anas?" He said: "Yes, by Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Umm Maktūm
was a muʾadhdhin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was blind.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the muʾadhdhin says, 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest,'
and one of you says, 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest,'
then he says, 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah,'
[and the listener] says, 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah,' then he says, 'I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,'
[and the listener] says, 'I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,'
then he says, 'Come to prayer,'
[and the listener] says, 'There is no power and no strength except with Allah,'
then he says, 'Come to success,'
[and the listener] says, 'There is no power and no strength except with Allah,'
then he says, 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest,'
[and the listener] says, 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest,'
then he says, 'There is no god but Allah,'
[and the listener] says, 'There is no god but Allah,'
sincerely from his heart, he will enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me the tashahhud with my hand between his hands, just as he taught me a sūrah of the Qurʾān.
And he related the tashahhud like what they related.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer with Abū Bakr behind him, and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the takbīr, Abū Bakr said the takbīr so that we could hear.
Then he mentioned [a narration] similar to the hadith of al-Layth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer one day, then turned away and said:
"O so-and-so, will you not perfect your prayer? Does the one praying not see how he prays? He only prays for himself. By Allah, I see behind me just as I see in front of me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And the wording
is Abū Bakr's. Ibn Ḥujr said: "He informed us," and Abū Bakr said:
ʿAlī ibn Mushir narrated to us,
from al-Mukhtār ibn Fulfulُ, from Anas,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer one day, and when he finished the prayer he turned his face to us and said:

"O people, I am your imām, so do not precede me in bowing, nor in prostration, nor in standing, nor in leaving [the prayer], for I see you in front of me and behind me." Then he said: "By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if you saw what I have seen, you would laugh little and weep much."
They said: "What did you see, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"I saw Paradise and the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when we gave the salām we would gesture with our hands, saying, "as-salāmu ʿalaykum, as-salāmu ʿalaykum." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at us and said:
"What is the matter with you, gesturing with your hands as if they were the tails of unruly horses? When one of you gives the salām, he should turn to his companion and not gesture with his hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let those of you who are mature and sensible stand closest to me, then those who come next to them," three times, "and beware of the commotion of the marketplaces."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmrah bint ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [reported] that ʿĀʾishah,

the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: "I would enter the house for a need while there was a sick person in it, and I would not ask about him except while passing by. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would bring his head close to me while he was in the mosque, and I would comb his hair. And he would not enter the house except for a need when he was in iʿtikāf."
And Ibn Rumḥ said: "when they are in iʿtikāf."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zayd ibn Thābit informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted the sale of ʿarāyā in exchange for fresh dates or dried dates, and did not permit it in anything other than that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: "The wife of Rifāʿah al-Quraẓī came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while I was sitting and Abū Bakr was with him. She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I was married to Rifāʿah and he divorced me, finalizing my divorce.
Then after him I married ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Zubayr,
and by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, he has with him only something like this fringe.'
And she took a fringe from her outer garment.
Khālid ibn Saʿīd heard her words while he was at the door, not having been given permission to enter.
She said: Khālid said: 'O Abū Bakr, will you not stop this woman from what she says openly in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?' By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did nothing more than smile.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
'Perhaps you want to return to Rifāʿah? No,
not until he has tasted your sweetness and you have tasted his sweetness.'"
And that became the established practice afterward.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā: "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ make a bequest of anything?" He said: "No."
I said: "Then how were the Muslims commanded to make bequests?" He said: "He bequeathed [adherence to] the Book of Allah."

Mālik said: Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif said: Al-Hudhayl ibn Shuraḥbīl said: "Abū Bakr would have ruled as successor over the bequest of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?! Abū Bakr wished he had found some covenant from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, even if he had to have his nose pierced with a nose-ring for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ, with nothing between me and him but the back of the saddle. He said:
"O Muʿādh ibn Jabal."
I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah, and at your pleasure."
Then he traveled for a while, then said:
"O Muʿādh ibn Jabal."
I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah, and at your pleasure."
Then he traveled for a while, then said:
"O Muʿādh ibn Jabal."
I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah, and at your pleasure." He said:
"Do you know what the right of Allah over His servants is?"
I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"The right of Allah over His servants is that they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him."
Then he traveled for a while, then said:
"O Muʿādh ibn Jabal."
I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah, and at your pleasure." He said:
"Do you know what the right of the servants over Allah is if they do that?"
I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"That He does not punish them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the people of Medina renounced their allegiance to Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah, Ibn ʿUmar gathered his household and his children and said: "I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
'A banner will be raised for every traitor on the Day of Resurrection.'
And we have pledged allegiance to this man on the pledge of Allah and His Messenger,
and I know of no treachery greater than that a man be pledged allegiance on the pledge of Allah and His Messenger,
and then war be waged against him.
And I do not know of any one of you who has renounced him,
or has pledged allegiance to anyone else in this matter,
except that it will be a parting of ways between me and him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Qutaybah and Ibn
Rumḥ, from al-Layth ibn Saʿd, from Nāfiʿ, that Ṣafiyyah,
daughter of Abū ʿUbayd, narrated to him from Ḥafṣah,
or from ʿĀʾishah,
or from both of them,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day — or: who believes in Allah and His Messenger — to mourn for a deceased person for more than three days, except for her husband."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to eat watermelon with fresh dates, and he would say:
"We break the heat of this with the coolness of that, and the coolness of this with the heat of that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ conquered Makkah, he said in his sermon:
"And for the fingers, ten [camels] for each."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked the people [under oath] about the ruling of the Prophet ﷺ on this, meaning on the unborn child. So Ḥamal ibn Mālik ibn an-Nābighah stood up and said: "I was between two wives of mine, and one of them struck the other with a tent pole, killing her and her unborn child." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that for the unborn child there was a ghurrah, a male or female slave, and that she [the killer] be put to death for her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a mukātab incurs a prescribed punishment or receives an inheritance, he is to inherit in proportion to the part of him that has been freed." And the Prophet ﷺ said:
"The mukātab pays the blood money of a free man in proportion to what he has paid off, and the blood money of a slave for what remains."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They came to my father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any physician who practises medicine on a people without being known for practising it before that, and then causes harm, is liable."
ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: It is not a matter of description; rather it refers to cutting the veins, lancing, and cauterizing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah, who was among those about whom it was revealed: {Nor [is there blame] upon those who, when they came to you for you to provide them with mounts, you said, "I can find nothing on which to mount you."} We greeted him and said: "We have come to you as visitors, to see how you are, and to learn."

Al-ʿIrbāḍ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer one day, then turned to us and gave us an eloquent exhortation that made the eyes shed tears and the hearts tremble. Someone said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is like the exhortation of one bidding farewell, so what do you charge us with?" He said:

"I advise you to have fear of Allah, and to hear and obey, even if it is an Abyssinian slave. For whoever among you lives after me will see much disagreement. So hold fast to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly guided, rightly directing successors; cling to it and bite onto it with your molar teeth. And beware of newly invented matters, for every newly invented matter is an innovation, and every innovation is misguidance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to present himself to the people at the standing place [of Hajj], and he said:
"Is there no man who will carry me to his people? For Quraysh have prevented me from conveying the words of my Lord."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever suppresses his anger while he is able to act on it, Allah will call him before all of creation on the Day of Resurrection until He lets him choose whichever of the ḥūr he wishes."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no sin more deserving that Allah hasten its punishment for its doer in this world, in addition to what is stored up for him in the Hereafter, than oppression and severing the ties of kinship."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: This verse was revealed about us, the Banū Salimah: {And do not insult one another by nicknames; wretched is the name of wickedness after faith.} He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us, and there was no man among us who did not have two or three names. So the Prophet ﷺ would say: "O so-and-so."
They would say: "Stop, O Messenger of Allah, he becomes angry at this name." So this verse was revealed: {And do not insult one another by nicknames.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The dream of the believer is one of forty parts of prophecy, and it rests on the leg of a bird as long as it is not told; when it is told, it falls."
He said: And I think he said:
"And it should only be told to someone sensible or someone beloved."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [One of] the wives of the Prophet ﷺ [reported] that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to sleep, he would place his right hand under his cheek and then say:
"O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the Day You resurrect Your servants." Three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach his Companions, saying:

"When one of you reaches the morning, let him say: O Allah, by You we have reached the morning, and by You we have reached the evening, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the final return.
And when he reaches the evening, let him say: O Allah, by You we have reached the evening, and by You we have reached the morning, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The ring of the Prophet ﷺ was on his hand,
and after him on the hand of Abū Bakr,
and after Abū Bakr on the hand of ʿUmar.
Then when ʿUthmān [became caliph], he sat at the well of Arīs, took out the ring,
and began to toy with it, and it fell [into the well]. He said: We searched for three days with ʿUthmān, draining the well, but we did not find it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Wahb added from Ibn Jurayj: Then he came to the women, and they began to throw their rings and finger-rings into the garment of Bilāl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas was asked about the dyeing of the Prophet's hair,
ﷺ, and he said: He had not reached the point of needing to dye;
if I wished, I could count the gray hairs in his beard.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My family sent me to Umm Salamah with a cup of water—and Isrāʾīl held three fingers together [to show its size]—in which was some of the hair of the Prophet ﷺ. When a person was afflicted by the evil eye or something else, he would send her his washing bowl [for water].
I looked into the container and saw some reddish hairs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had large hands;
I have not seen anyone like him after him.
And the hair of the Prophet ﷺ was neither tightly curled nor completely straight, but in between.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had large hands and feet and a handsome face;
I have not seen anyone like him, either after him or before him.
And his palms were broad and full.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever braids his hair should shave it,
and do not imitate the matting of the hair.
And Ibn ʿUmar used to say: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with his hair matted.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade shaving part of the head while leaving other parts.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered a house in Madinah with Abū Hurayrah, and he saw a painter painting images at the top of it.
He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Who is more unjust than one who sets out to create like My creation? Let them create a grain, let them create an atom."

Then he called for a basin of water and washed his hands up to his armpits. I said: O Abū Hurayrah, is this something you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: [Adornment extends] to the furthest reach of the ornament.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The three evil ones were mentioned in the presence of ʿIkrimah, and he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was met, with Qutham carried in front of him and al-Faḍl behind him,
or Qutham behind him
and al-Faḍl in front of him,
so which of them is the worse, or which of them is the better?
label: machine translation

segments_en: Heraclius sent for him and said—meaning about the Prophet ﷺ: He commands us to pray, to give charity, to be chaste, and to maintain family ties.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he would seat al-Ḥasan on his other thigh,
then embrace them both and say:
"O Allah, have mercy on them, for I have mercy on them." And from ʿAlī,
who said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Sulaymān narrated to us,
from Abū ʿUthmān.
At-Taymī said: Something of doubt arose in my heart about it,
and I said: I have narrated it in such and such a way,
but I had not heard it from Abū ʿUthmān.
So I looked and found it written with me among what I had heard.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"By Allah, he does not believe;
by Allah, he does not believe;
by Allah, he does not believe."
It was asked: Who, O Messenger of Allah? He said:
"The one whose neighbor is not safe from his harm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Every act of kindness is charity (ṣadaqah)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is Fulayḥ ibn Sulaymān, from Hilāl ibn Usāmah,
from Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was not one who insulted, nor one who spoke indecently, nor one who cursed.
When he wished to rebuke one of us, he would say: "What is wrong with him? May his forehead be covered with dust."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade a man to laugh at what comes out of people [of wind], and he said:
"Why does one of you beat his wife as a stallion is beaten,
when perhaps he will embrace her afterward?"
And ath-Thawrī, Wuhayb and Abū Muʿāwiyah said from Hishām: "the flogging of a slave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: No man accuses another of wickedness,
or accuses him of disbelief,
except that it returns upon him
if his companion is not as he said."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this [chain], and she said: The Prophet ﷺ came in to me one day and said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, I do not think that so-and-so and so-and-so know our religion, the one we are upon."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah,
the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: Since I became aware, my parents were following the religion,
and no day passed over them without the Messenger of Allah ﷺ coming to us at both ends of the day, morning and evening.
While we were sitting in the house of Abū Bakr at the height of noon, someone said: Here is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, at an hour when he did not usually come to us.
Abū Bakr said: Nothing brought him at this hour except a matter [of importance]. He said:
"I have been given permission to depart."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The first qasāmah (oath of compurgation) took place in the Jāhiliyyah. A man from Banū Hāshim hired a man from Quraysh, from one of their clans. He said: So he set out with him with his camels. A man from Banū Hāshim passed by him, whose sack's loop had broken, and he said: "Help me with a hobbling rope to fasten the loop of my sack, so that the camels do not bolt." So he gave him a rope to fasten the loop of his sack. When they stopped and the camels were hobbled, except for one camel, the one who had hired him said: "What is the matter with this camel, that it alone among the camels has not been hobbled?" He said: "It has no rope."

He said: "Then where is its rope?" He said: "A man from Banū Hāshim passed by me whose sack's loop had broken, and he asked me for help. He said: 'Help me with a hobbling rope to fasten the loop of my sack, so that the camels do not bolt.'

So I gave him a rope." The hirer struck him with a staff in which was his death. Then a man from the people of Yemen passed by him and said: "Do you attend the season [of Hajj]?" He said: "I do not attend, but I may well attend."
He said: "Will you deliver a message from me some time?" He said: "Yes."

He said: "When you attend the season, call out: 'O family of Quraysh!' When they answer you, call out: 'O family of Hāshim!' When they answer you, ask for Abū Ṭālib and tell him that so-and-so killed me over a rope." And the hired man died. When the one who had hired him returned, Abū Ṭālib came to him and said: "What happened to our man?" He said: "He fell ill and I looked after him well, then he died, so I stopped and buried him."
[Abū Ṭālib] said: "He deserved that from you."
He remained for a while. Then the Yemeni man whom he had entrusted to deliver the message came to the season and said: "O family of Quraysh!"
They said: "This is Quraysh."
He said: "O family of Banū Hāshim!"
They said: "This is Banū Hāshim."
He said: "Where is Abū Ṭālib?" They said: "This is Abū Ṭālib."
He said: "So-and-so told me to deliver a message to you: that so-and-so killed him over a rope."

Abū Ṭālib came to him and said: "Choose one of three things from us: if you wish, pay a hundred camels, for you killed our man by mistake; or if you wish, fifty men of your people swear that you did not kill him; and if you refuse, we will kill you for him."
He went to his people and mentioned that to them, and they said: "We will swear."

Then a woman of Banū Hāshim, who was married to one of them and had borne him a child, came to him and said: "O Abū Ṭālib, I would like you to count this son of mine as one of the fifty and not make him take his oath."

He did so. Then a man from among them came to him and said: "O Abū Ṭālib, you want fifty men to swear in place of a hundred camels, so that each man owes two camels. Here are two camels; accept them from me and do not make me take my oath where oaths are taken."
So he accepted them, and forty-eight men came and swore.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, a year did not pass while any of the forty-eight still had an eye that blinked."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ delivered a sermon when the sun was eclipsed, and he said: "To proceed..."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the prayer for rain: he faced the qiblah, turned his cloak over, and raised his hands.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "O Allah, give us rain."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, withheld the rain from His servants for five years and then sent it down, a group of people would wake up disbelieving, saying, 'We have been given rain by the star al-Mijdah.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The rain was withheld for a year, so on a Friday one of the Muslims stood up before the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the rain has been withheld, the land has become barren, and the livestock have perished."

He said: He raised his hands, and we saw no cloud in the sky. He stretched out his hands until I saw the whiteness of his armpits, asking Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for rain. He said: We had not yet finished the Friday prayer when even a young man whose home was nearby was worried about returning to his family, and the rain continued until the next Friday. When the following Friday came, they said, "O Messenger of Allah, the houses have collapsed and the travellers are held up."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled at how quickly the son of Adam grows weary, and he said with his hands:
"O Allah, around us and not upon us."
And the clouds cleared away from Madinah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, like the prayer of Ḥudhayfah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The fear prayer was only two prostrations, like the prayer of these guards of yours today behind these imams of yours, except that it was done in turns. One group of them stood, all of them being with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and one group prostrated with him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and they all stood with him, then he bowed and they all bowed with him, then he prostrated, and those who had been standing the first time prostrated with him. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and those who had prostrated with him sat at the end of their prayer, those who had been standing prostrated by themselves, then sat, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ brought them all together in the closing salutation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led them in the fear prayer. One row stood in front of him and one row behind him. He prayed with those behind him one rak'ah and two prostrations. Then these advanced until they stood in the place of their companions, and the others came and stood in the place of these. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed with them one rak'ah and two prostrations, then ended the prayer with the salutation. So the Prophet ﷺ had two rak'ahs and they had one rak'ah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when the prayer was called. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, and one group stood behind him while another group faced the enemy. He prayed one rak'ah with those behind him and performed two prostrations with them. Then they went off and stood in the place of those who had been facing the enemy, and that other group came, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed one rak'ah with them and performed two prostrations with them. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the salutation, and those behind him gave the salutation, and so did the others.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Nakhl, with the enemy between us and the qiblah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the takbīr and they all said the takbīr. Then he bowed and they all bowed. Then the Prophet ﷺ prostrated, along with the row next to him, while the others stood guarding them. When they stood up, the others prostrated in the place where those had been. Then these advanced to the positions of those. He bowed and they all bowed, then he rose and they all rose. Then the Prophet ﷺ prostrated, along with the row next to him, while the others stood guarding them. When they had prostrated and sat, the others prostrated in their place. Then he gave the salutation.
Jābir said: Just as your commanders do.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī
appointed Abū Masʿūd to take charge of the people. He went out on the day of the festival and said, "O people, it is not from the Sunnah to pray before the imam."
label: machine translation
