segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to bring out a short spear on the day of Fitr and the day of Aḍḥā, plant it in the ground, and pray facing it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two festivals coincided in the time of Ibn al-Zubayr. He delayed going out until the day was well advanced, then he went out and delivered a sermon, making it long, then came down and prayed. He did not lead the people in the Friday prayer that day.
This was mentioned to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said, "He has followed the Sunnah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon her while two girls were with her, beating tambourines. Abū Bakr rebuked them, so the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Leave them, for every people have a festival."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar sent people out to the various regions of the lands to fight the polytheists,
and al-Hurmuzān accepted Islam. He said, "I want to consult you about these campaigns of mine." He said, "Yes.
The likeness of it, and of those people in it who are enemies of the Muslims, is that of a bird with a head, two wings, and two legs.
If one of the wings is broken, the two legs rise up with the other wing and the head.
If the other wing is broken, the two legs and the head rise up.
But if the head is crushed, the two legs, the two wings, and the head are all lost. The head is Khosrow, one wing is Caesar,
and the other wing is Persia.
So order the Muslims to march out against Khosrow."
Bakr and Ziyād both said, from Jubayr ibn Ḥayyah, who said: ʿUmar called us to arms and appointed an-Nuʿmān ibn Muqarrin over us,
until we were in the land of the enemy,
and the governor of Khosrow came out against us with forty thousand men.
An interpreter stood up and said, "Let one of you speak to me."
Al-Mughīrah said, "Ask whatever you wish."
He said, "Who are you?" He said, "We are people of the Arabs. We were in severe hardship and severe affliction,
sucking on hides and date pits out of hunger,
wearing camel hair and animal hair,
and worshipping trees and stones.
While we were in that state,
the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earths, exalted be His mention and majestic His greatness, sent to us a Prophet from among ourselves,
whose father and mother we knew.
Our Prophet, the messenger of our Lord ﷺ, commanded us to fight you until you worship Allah alone or pay the jizyah.
And our Prophet ﷺ informed us, on the authority of the message of our Lord, that whoever of us is killed will go to Paradise, into bliss the like of which has never been seen,
and whoever of us survives will become master of your necks."
An-Nuʿmān said, "Perhaps Allah has let you witness the like of this with the Prophet ﷺ, and he did not cause you regret or disgrace you.
But I witnessed fighting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: when he did not fight at the beginning of the day, he would wait until the winds began to blow and the times of prayer arrived."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Give us advice, O Commander of the Faithful."
He said, "I advise you to observe the covenant of Allah,
for it is the covenant of your Prophet and the provision of your families."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Khaybar was conquered, a poisoned sheep was given as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Gather for me all the Jews who are here."
They were gathered for him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them,
"I am going to ask you about something. Will you be truthful to me about it?"
They said, "Yes, O Abū al-Qāsim."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them, "Who is your father?"
They said, "Our father is so-and-so."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"You have lied; rather, your father is so-and-so."
They said, "You have spoken truly and rightly." He said,
"Will you be truthful to me about something if I ask you about it?"
They said, "Yes, O Abū al-Qāsim,
and if we lie to you, you will know our lie just as you knew it about our father."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them,
"Who are the people of the Fire?"
They said, "We will be in it for a short while,
and then you will succeed us in it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them, "Be despised in it!
By Allah, we will never succeed you in it."
Then he said to them,
"Will you be truthful to me about something if I ask you about it?" They said, "Yes." He said,
"Did you put poison in this sheep?" They said, "Yes." He said,
"What made you do that?"
They said, "We wanted, if you were a liar, to be rid of you,
and if you were a prophet, it would not harm you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was bewitched, so that it seemed to him that he had done something when he had not done it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "How will you be when you do not collect a dinar or a dirham?" It was said to him, "And do you see that happening, O Abū Hurayrah?" He said, "Yes, by the One in whose hand is the soul of Abū Hurayrah, on the word of the Truthful, the Believed ﷺ."
They said, "Because of what?" He said, "The covenant of Allah and the covenant of His Messenger ﷺ will be violated,
so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will harden the hearts of the people of the covenant,
and they will withhold what is in their hands."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stood among us in one place,
and he told us about the beginning of creation until the people of Paradise entered their dwellings
and the people of the Fire entered their dwellings.
Whoever remembered it remembered it,
and whoever forgot it forgot it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to Abū Dharr when the sun had set,
"Do you know where it goes?"
I said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said,
"It goes until it prostrates beneath the Throne,
then it asks permission, and permission is given to it.
But it is about to prostrate and not be accepted from it,
and to ask permission and not be given permission.
It will be said to it: Return from where you came.
Then it will rise from its place of setting,
and that is the saying of the Exalted: {And the sun runs to a place of rest for it. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ narrated to them about the night in which he was taken on the Night Journey:
"While I was in the Ḥaṭīm"—and perhaps he said, "in the Ḥijr"—"lying down,

someone came to me and split"—and he said, and I heard him say, "he split what is between this point and this point." I said to al-Jārūd, who was beside me, "What does he mean by that?" He said, "From the hollow of his throat to his pubic hair."
And I heard him say, "from his chest to his pubic hair." "Then he took out my heart.
Then a golden basin full of faith was brought to me,
and my heart was washed, then filled, and returned.
Then a mount was brought to me, smaller than a mule and bigger than a donkey, white."
Al-Jārūd said to him, "Was it the Burāq, O Abū Ḥamzah?" Anas said, "Yes.
It places its stride at the farthest reach of its sight." "I was mounted upon it,
and Jibrīl set off with me until he came to the lowest heaven and asked for it to be opened.
It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'And who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
It was said, 'Welcome to him,
how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!' Then it was opened. When I passed through,
there was Adam,
and he said, 'This is your father Adam; greet him.'
So I greeted him and he returned the greeting, then said, 'Welcome to the righteous son and the righteous prophet.'
Then he ascended until he came to the second heaven and asked for it to be opened.
It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'And who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
It was said, 'Welcome to him, how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!' Then it was opened. When I passed through,
there were Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā,
who are maternal cousins. He said, 'This is Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā; greet them.' So I greeted them and they returned the greeting,
then they said, 'Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet.'
Then he ascended with me to the third heaven,
and asked for it to be opened. It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'And who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
It was said, 'Welcome to him,
how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!' Then it was opened.
When I passed through, there was Yūsuf.
He said, 'This is Yūsuf; greet him.'
So I greeted him and he returned the greeting,
then said, 'Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet.'
Then he ascended with me until he came to the fourth heaven and asked for it to be opened.
It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'And who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
It was said, 'Welcome to him,
how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!' Then it was opened.
When I reached Idrīs, he said, 'This is Idrīs; greet him.'
So I greeted him and he returned the greeting, then said, 'Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet.'
Then he ascended with me until he came to the fifth heaven and asked for it to be opened.
It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'And who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad ﷺ.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
It was said, 'Welcome to him,
how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!'
When I passed through, there was Hārūn. He said, 'This is Hārūn; greet him.'
So I greeted him and he returned the greeting, then said, 'Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet.'
Then he ascended with me until he came to the sixth heaven and asked for it to be opened.
It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'Who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
He said, 'Welcome to him,
how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!' When I passed through,
there was Mūsā. He said, 'This is Mūsā; greet him.'
So I greeted him and he returned the greeting, then said, 'Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet.'
When I went past him, he wept.
It was said to him, 'What makes you weep?' He said, 'I weep because a young man was sent after me,
and more of his nation will enter Paradise than of mine.'
Then he ascended with me to the seventh heaven, and Jibrīl asked for it to be opened.
It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'And who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
He said, 'Welcome to him,
how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!' When I passed through,
there was Ibrāhīm. He said, 'This is your father; greet him.'
He said: So I greeted him,
and he returned the greeting and said, 'Welcome to the righteous son and the righteous prophet.'
Then the Lote Tree of the Furthest Limit was raised up for me,
and its fruits were like the jars of Hajar,
and its leaves were like the ears of elephants. He said, 'This is the Lote Tree of the Furthest Limit.'
And there were four rivers: two hidden and two visible.
I said, 'What are these two, O Jibrīl?' He said, 'As for the hidden ones,
they are two rivers in Paradise,
and as for the visible ones, they are the Nile and the Euphrates.'
Then the Frequented House was raised up for me.
Then I was brought a vessel of wine,
a vessel of milk, and a vessel of honey. I took the milk,
and he said, 'This is the natural way, which you and your nation are upon.'
Then the prayers were made obligatory upon me: fifty prayers every day.
I returned and passed by Mūsā,
and he said, 'What were you commanded?' I said, 'I was commanded fifty prayers every day.'
He said, 'Your nation cannot bear fifty prayers every day,
and by Allah, I have tested people before you,
and I dealt with the Children of Israel with the utmost effort,
so return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction for your nation.' So I returned,
and He took ten away from me.
I returned to Mūsā and he said the same.
I returned and He took ten away from me.
I returned to Mūsā and he said the same.
I returned and He took ten away from me.
I returned to Mūsā and he said the same.
I returned and was commanded ten prayers every day.
I returned and he said the same.
I returned and was commanded five prayers every day.
I returned to Mūsā,
and he said, 'What were you commanded?' I said, 'I was commanded five prayers every day.'
He said, 'Your nation cannot bear five prayers every day,
and I have tested people before you,
and I dealt with the Children of Israel with the utmost effort,
so return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction for your nation.'
He said, 'I have asked my Lord until I feel shy,
but I am content and submit.'" He said: "When I passed on, a caller called out: 'I have established My obligation and lightened it for My servants.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and accepted Islam, and he taught me Islam and taught me how to collect charity (ṣadaqah) from my people who had accepted Islam. Then I returned to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have memorized everything you taught me except the charity. Should I take a tenth from them?" He said,
"No. The tenth is only [taken] from the Christians and the Jews."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We camped at Khaybar with the Prophet ﷺ, and with him were those of his Companions who were with him. The master of Khaybar was a rebellious, defiant man. He approached the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Muhammad, is it right for you to slaughter our donkeys, eat our fruit, and strike our women?" The Prophet ﷺ became angry and said,
"O Ibn ʿAwf, mount your horse, then call out: Paradise is not lawful except for a believer, and let them gather for prayer."
He said: So they gathered, then the Prophet ﷺ led them in prayer, then he stood and said,

"Does one of you think, reclining on his couch, that Allah has forbidden nothing except what is in this Qurʾān? Indeed, by Allah, I have exhorted, commanded, and forbidden things that are like the Qurʾān or even greater. And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has not made it lawful for you to enter the houses of the People of the Book without permission, nor to strike their women, nor to eat their fruit, when they give you what is due from them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] from Juhaynah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Perhaps you will fight a people and prevail over them, and they will protect themselves from you with their wealth rather than their lives and their children."
Saʿīd said in his narration,
"They will make a peace settlement with you." Then the two [narrators] agreed:
"So do not take anything from them beyond that, for it is not right for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the sons of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from their fathers, close relatives, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said,

"Beware! Whoever wrongs a person under a covenant, or diminishes his right, or burdens him beyond his capacity, or takes anything from him without his willing consent, I will be his adversary on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sufyān was asked about the explanation of
this, and he said: If he accepts Islam, then no jizyah is due from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Shall I not tell you about the people of Paradise?" They said, "Yes." He ﷺ said: "
Every weak person who is regarded as weak; if he were to swear by Allah, He would fulfil it for him." Then he said: "
Shall I not tell you about the people of the Fire?" They said, "Yes." He said: "
Every harsh, coarse, arrogant person."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, regarding {the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds}, he said: "
One of them will stand in his sweat up to the middle of his ears."
In the narration of Ibn al-Muthannā, he said: "The people will stand."
He did not mention "the Day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Allah does not listen to anything as He listens to a Prophet ﷺ chanting the Qur'an melodiously."
And a companion of his said: [meaning] reciting it aloud.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
all of them from Ibn ʿUyaynah,
—Zuhayr said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us—: al-Zuhrī narrated to us, from Sālim, from his father,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "

There is no envy except in two cases: a man whom Allah has given the Qur'an, so he stands [in prayer] with it during the hours of the night and the hours of the day; and a man whom Allah has given wealth, so he spends it during the hours of the night and the hours of the day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The example of the one who knows the Qur'an by heart is like that of a person who owns hobbled camels: if he keeps watch over them, he holds on to them, and if he lets them loose, they go away."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh said: "Keep up with these copies of the Qur'an—and perhaps he said: the Qur'an—for it escapes from the hearts of men faster than camels escape from their tethers."
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
None of you should say, 'I forgot such and such verse,' rather, he was made to forget."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas was asked how the recitation of the Prophet ﷺ was.
He said: "It was prolonged."
Then he recited: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,"
prolonging "In the name of Allah," prolonging "the Most Gracious," and prolonging "the Most Merciful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed Ṣafiyyah and made her freedom her dowry. The wording is that of Muḥammad.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "
I have not left behind me any trial among the people more harmful to men than women."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Three rulings came from the case of Barīrah.
ʿĀʾishah wished to buy her and free her, but her owners said, "The right of walāʾ is ours."
She mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "
If you wish, you may stipulate it for them,
for walāʾ belongs only to the one who frees."
He said: She was freed and was given the choice to stay with her husband or leave him.
One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the house of ʿĀʾishah while a pot was boiling on the fire,
and he asked for his meal, so bread and a condiment from the household's condiments were brought. He said: "
Did I not see meat?"
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah,
but that is meat given in charity to Barīrah, and she gave it to us as a gift." He said: "
It is charity for her, and a gift for us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not hold a wedding feast for any of his wives greater or better than the one he held for Zaynab.
Thābit al-Bunānī said, "With what did he hold the feast?" He said: "He fed them bread and meat until they left it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to al-Zuhrī, "O Abū Bakr, how is this hadith, 'The worst food is the food of the rich'?" He laughed and said, "The worst food is not the food of the rich."

Sufyān said: My father was wealthy, and this hadith alarmed me when I heard it, so I asked al-Zuhrī about it. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj narrated to me that he heard Abū Hurayrah say, "The worst food is the food of the wedding feast."
Then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Mālik.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a woman
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my daughter is a bride, and she fell ill and her hair fell out. Would it be sinful for me to attach hair to it for her?" He said: "
Allah has cursed the woman who attaches hair and the one who has it attached."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is from the Sunnah that when a man marries a virgin while already having a previously married wife, he stays with her seven [nights] and then divides his time,
and when he marries a previously married woman while already having a virgin wife, he stays with her three [nights] and then divides his time.
Abū Qilābah said: "If I wished, I could say that Anas attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Abū Thaʿlabah al-Khushanī and said to him, "What do you do with this verse?" He said, "Which verse?" I said, [it is] the saying of Allah:

"O you who believe, take care of yourselves; those who have gone astray will not harm you when you are guided." He said, "By Allah, you have asked someone well-informed about it. I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he said:

'Rather, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, until you see greed being obeyed, desire being followed, the world being preferred, and every person of opinion being pleased with his own opinion. Then take care of yourself in particular and leave the common people, for ahead of you are days in which patience will be like holding on to burning coals. The one who acts in those days will have a reward like that of fifty men who do the like of your deeds.'"
ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak said: Someone other than ʿUtbah added for me: It was asked, "O Messenger of Allah, the reward of fifty men from among us or from among them?" He said:
"No, rather the reward of fifty of you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A thief who had confessed fully was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, though no stolen goods were found with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"I do not think you stole." He said, "Yes, I did." He said:
"Take him away and cut off his hand, then bring him back to me."
They cut off his hand and brought him back. He said to him:
"Say: I seek Allah's forgiveness and I repent to Him."
He said, "I seek Allah's forgiveness and I repent to Him." He said:
"O Allah, accept his repentance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If a slave steals, sell him, even for a nashsh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever you find doing the deed of the people of Lūṭ, kill the one who does it and the one to whom it is done."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], may Allah be pleased with her, said: When my innocence was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ stood on the pulpit, mentioned that, and recited—meaning the Qurʾān. When he came down from the pulpit, he gave orders about the two men and the woman, and they were given the prescribed punishment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade retaliation from being carried out in the mosque, poetry from being recited in it, and prescribed punishments from being carried out in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I only know it to be from Anas ibn Mālik.
He said: No case involving retaliation was ever brought before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except that he commanded pardon in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent Abū Jahm ibn Ḥudhayfah to collect charity (ṣadaqah). A man disputed with him over his charity, and Abū Jahm struck him and wounded his head. They came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "Retaliation, O Messenger of Allah!" The Prophet ﷺ said:
"You shall have such and such."
They were not satisfied, so he said:
"You shall have such and such."
They were not satisfied, so he said:
"You shall have such and such." They were satisfied. Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"I will address the people this evening and inform them of your satisfaction." They said, "Yes."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave a speech and said:
"These men of Layth came to me wanting retaliation, and I offered them such and such, and they were satisfied. Are you satisfied?" They said, "No."

The Emigrants were about to attack them, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered them to hold back from them, and they held back. Then he called them and increased [the offer] for them, and said, "Are you satisfied?" They said, "Yes." He said:
"I will address the people and inform them of your satisfaction." They said, "Yes."
So the Prophet ﷺ gave a speech and said, "Are you satisfied?" They said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever is killed.
Ibn ʿUbayd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever is killed in a blind [confused] melee, such as stone-throwing among them, or being struck with whips or with a stick, it is a mistake, and its blood-money is the blood-money for a mistaken killing. Whoever is killed intentionally is subject to retaliation."
Ibn ʿUbayd said: "retaliation by hand." Then they agreed:
"Whoever stands in the way of that, upon him is the curse of Allah and His wrath; no obligatory or voluntary act will be accepted from him."
The narration of Sufyān is more complete.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave a sermon in Makkah on the day of the conquest. He said "Allahu akbar" three times, then said:
"There is no god but Allah alone; He fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and defeated the factions alone."
Up to here I memorized it from Musaddad; then they agreed:
"Beware: every claim of honor from the Pre-Islamic Period, whether of blood or wealth, is under my feet, except the giving of water to the pilgrims and the custodianship of the House." Then he said:
"Beware: the blood-money for a mistaken killing resembling an intentional one, [killed] with a whip or a stick, is one hundred camels, forty of them pregnant."
The narration of Musaddad is more complete.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Manṣūr, Ziyād, and Bakr,
— that is, Ibn Wāʾil — all of them mentioned that they heard from al-Zuhrī,
who narrated that Sālim
informed him that his father informed him that he
saw the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān walking in front of the funeral procession.
Bakr alone did not mention ʿUthmān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: His name is Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Yūsuf. Ayyūb ibn Sulaymān ibn Bilāl narrated to us:
Abū Bakr ibn Abī Uways narrated to us,
from Sulaymān ibn Bilāl,
from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah,
and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī ʿAtīq, from al-Zuhrī,
from Sulaymān ibn Arqam,
from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr,
from Abū Salamah, from ʿĀʾishah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"There is no vow in disobedience to Allah, and its expiation is the expiation of an oath."
label: machine translation

segments_en: may Allah be pleased with her, that a man

bought a slave, and the slave stayed with him as long as Allah willed. Then he found a defect in him and took his dispute to the Prophet ﷺ, who returned the slave to the seller. The man said, "O Messenger of Allah, he has already made use of my slave and gained income from him."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "The yield goes with liability."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The ʿumrā is permissible for the one to whom it is given, and the ruqbā is permissible for the one to whom it is given, and the one who takes back his gift is like one who returns to his vomit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that a man

from the Anṣār freed six slaves of his at the time of his death, and he had no wealth other than them. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he spoke harshly about him. Then he called them, divided them into three groups, cast lots among them, and freed two and kept four in slavery.
It has been narrated through more than one route from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the first Jamrah and said, "O Messenger of Allah, which jihād is best?" He was silent toward him. When he reached the second Jamrah, the man asked him, and he was silent toward him. When he had stoned the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah and put his foot in the stirrup to mount, he said, "Where is the questioner?"
He said, "I am, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"A word of truth before a tyrannical ruler."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever drinks wine, flog him; if he does it again, flog him; if he does it again, flog him; and if he does it a third or fourth time, kill him."

Then a man who had drunk was brought, and he flogged him; then he was brought again, and he flogged him; then he was brought again, and he flogged him; then he was brought again, and he flogged him, and the killing was lifted, so it was a concession.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man killed another man during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ set his blood-money at twelve thousand. He also mentioned the saying, "...except that Allah and His Messenger have enriched them from His bounty," regarding their taking the blood-money.
The wording is that of Abū Dāwūd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh said: "Three traits—whoever has them is a hypocrite: when he speaks, he lies; when he is entrusted, he betrays; and when he promises, he breaks his promise. Whoever has one of them still has a trait of hypocrisy in him until he gives it up."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed, and the people with him.
He stood for a long time, about the length of Sūrat al-Baqarah,
then he bowed for a long time,
then he raised his head and stood for a long time, shorter than the first standing,
then he bowed for a long time, shorter than the first bowing, then he prostrated.
Then he stood and remained standing for a long time, shorter than the first standing,
then he bowed for a long time, shorter than the first bowing,
then he raised his head and stood for a long time, shorter than the first standing,
then he bowed for a long time, shorter than the first bowing,
then he raised his head, then prostrated, then he finished,
and the sun had cleared. Then he said:
"The sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah; they are not eclipsed for the death of anyone nor for his life.
So when you see that, remember Allah."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, we saw you reach out for something at this place of yours,
then we saw you draw back." He said:
"I saw Paradise"—or, "I was shown Paradise"—"and I reached for a bunch of grapes from it. Had I taken it, you would have eaten from it for as long as the world remains.
And I saw the Fire, and I have never seen a sight like today's, and I saw that most of its people were women."
They said, "Why, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Because of their ingratitude."
It was asked, "Do they disbelieve in Allah?" He said, "They are ungrateful to their husbands and ungrateful for kindness.
If you were to treat one of them well for all time,
then she saw something [displeasing] from you, she would say, 'I have never seen any good from you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and he stood up in alarm, fearing that it might be the Hour, until he came to the mosque and stood praying with the longest standing, bowing and prostration I had ever seen him do in any prayer. Then he said:

"These signs which Allah sends are not for the death of anyone nor for his life, but Allah sends them to frighten His servants with them. So when you see any of them, hasten to His remembrance, supplication to Him, and seeking His forgiveness."
In the narration of Ibn al-ʿAlāʾ: "The sun was eclipsed," and he said, "He frightens His servants."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ led them in prayer during a solar eclipse with four bowings in two prostrations [units],
the first being the longest.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited Sūrat al-Najm and prostrated in it, and no one among the people remained except that he prostrated. One man among them took a handful of pebbles or dust, raised it to his face, and said, "This is enough for me."
ʿAbdullāh said, "I later saw him killed as a disbeliever."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrate in Sūrah Ṣād.
Ibn ʿAbbās said, "It is not among the obligatory prostrations."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿUbaydullāh ibn Saʿīd,
and Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā,
all from Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān,
Zuhayr said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us,
from ʿUbaydullāh,
who said: Nāfiʿ informed me,
from Ibn ʿUmar,

that the Prophet ﷺ used to recite the Qurʾān, and he would recite a sūrah containing a prostration and prostrate, and we would prostrate with him, until some of us could not find a place for his forehead.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he prayed the traveller's prayer at Minā and elsewhere as two units, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar [did so] as well, and ʿUthmān [did so] as two units in the early part of his caliphate, then he completed it as four.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ and his Companions arrived on the morning of the fourth [of Dhū al-Ḥijjah], calling out the talbiyah for Hajj,
and he commanded them to make it an ʿUmrah, except for those who had brought the sacrificial animal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in a hurry to travel, he would combine the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when travel pressed him on a journey, delay the Maghrib prayer
until he combined it with ʿIshāʾ.
Sālim said: ʿAbdullāh used to do the same when travel pressed him,
and he would give the iqāmah for Maghrib and pray it as three units, then give the salām,
then he would wait only a short while before giving the iqāmah for ʿIshāʾ and praying it as two units,
then give the salām, and he would not offer any voluntary prayer, not even one unit, between them,
nor any prostration after ʿIshāʾ until he rose in the middle of the night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had hemorrhoids, so I asked the Prophet ﷺ about prayer, and he said, "Pray standing,
and if you cannot, then sitting,
and if you cannot, then on your side."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fasting was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Fast one day out of every ten days, and you will have the reward of the other nine."
I said, "I am able to do more than that." He said:
"Fast one day out of every nine days, and you will have the reward of the other eight."
I said, "I am able to do more than that." He said:
"Then fast one day out of every eight days, and you will have the reward of the other seven."
I said, "I am able to do more than that." He continued [in this way] until he said:
"Fast one day and break the fast one day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Fast one day and you will have the reward of ten." I said, "Give me more." He said:
"Fast two days and you will have the reward of nine." I said, "Give me more." He said:
"Fast three days and you will have the reward of eight."
Thābit said: I mentioned that to Muṭarrif, and he said, "I think he was only increasing in deeds while decreasing in reward." The wording is that of Muḥammad.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It has reached me that you stand in prayer at night and fast during the day."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I intended nothing by that except good." He said:
"There is no fasting for the one who fasts perpetually. But let me show you what is [equal to] fasting all of time: three days of each month."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am able to do more than that." He said:
"Fast five days."
I said, "I am able to do more than that." He said, "Then fast ten."
I said, "I am able to do more than that." He said:
"Fast the fast of Dāwūd, peace be upon him: he would fast one day and break the fast one day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, and he narrated the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Recite the Qur'an in a month."
I said, "I am able to do more than that."
I kept asking him [for more] until he said:
"In five days." And he said:
"Fast three days of the month."
I said, "I am able to do more than that."
I kept asking him [for more] until he said:
"Fast the most beloved fasting to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: the fast of Dāwūd. He would fast one day and break the fast one day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to do three things: to sleep only after praying the witr, to perform the ritual bath on Friday, and to fast three days of every month.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever fasts three days of every month has completed the fasting of the month," or [he said], "he has the fasting of the month." ʿĀṣim was unsure [of the wording].
label: machine translation

segments_en: A good fast is three days of the month."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There were four things the Prophet ﷺ never abandoned: fasting on ʿĀshūrāʾ, [fasting] the ten [days], three days of every month, and two rak'ahs before the morning prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command fasting three days: the first Thursday, and the Monday, and the [next] Monday.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father said: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a hare he had roasted, and bread. He placed it before the Prophet ﷺ and then said, "I found that it bleeds."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions:
"It does no harm; eat." And he said to the Bedouin, "Eat."
He said, "I am fasting." He said, "What fast?"
He said, "Fasting three days of the month." He said:
"If you are fasting, then keep to the bright white days: the thirteenth, the fourteenth and the fifteenth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to fast three days of the month, the white days: the thirteenth, the fourteenth and the fifteenth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to a man:
"Keep to fasting the thirteenth, the fourteenth and the fifteenth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A hare that a man had roasted was brought to the Prophet ﷺ. When he presented it to him, he said, "O Messenger of Allah, I saw blood in it." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left it and did not eat it, and said to those with him:
"Eat, for if I desired it, I would eat it."
A man was sitting [there], and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Come closer and eat with the people."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am fasting." He said:
"Why did you not fast the white days?"
He said, "What are they?" He said:
"The thirteenth, the fourteenth and the fifteenth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command [fasting] these three white days, and he would say:
"They are the fasting of the [whole] month."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Allah be pleased with her] said: My mother wanted to make me fatten up before I went in to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but I did not respond to anything she wanted until she fed me cucumbers with fresh dates, and I became plump on that, with the finest plumpness.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"Augury from the flight of birds, omens from birds, and striking [lines] are from jibt (superstition)."
Ṭarq is divination by bird omens, and ʿiyāfah is drawing lines.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar said: ʿAwf said: ʿIyāfah is divining from the flying of birds, and ṭarq is the lines that are drawn on the ground.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: O Messenger of Allah, there are men among us who draw lines. He said:
"There was a prophet among the prophets who used to draw lines; whoever's lines match his, then that is [correct]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Miqsam,
and Zayd ibn Aslam,
from Abū Ṣāliḥ,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no ghoul."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mālik was asked about the saying "There is no Ṣafar."
He said: The people of the Jāhiliyyah used to treat Ṣafar as permissible, making it permissible one year and forbidden another year. So the Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no Ṣafar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Muḥammad, meaning Ibn Rāshid, about the saying "hāmah."
He said: The people of the Jāhiliyyah used to say that nobody dies and is buried except that an owl (hāmah) comes out of his grave.
I said: And what about the saying ṣafar?
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard a word and liked it, so he said:
"We have taken our good omen from your mouth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: People say that ṣafar is a pain that seizes the belly.
I said: Then what is the hāmah? He said: People say the hāmah is the one that cries out, the hāmah of people, and it is not the head of a human being; rather it is a creature.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Bad omens were mentioned in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:

"The best of them is the good omen, and it should not turn a Muslim back. If one of you sees something he dislikes, let him say: O Allah, none brings good things but You, and none repels evil things but You, and there is no power and no strength except through You."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used not to take bad omens from anything. When he sent a governor, he would ask about his name; if he liked his name, he was pleased with it and the joy of that was seen on his face, and if he disliked his name, the dislike of that was seen on his face. When he entered a town, he would ask about its name; if he liked its name, he was pleased with it and the joy of that was seen on his face, and if he disliked its name, the dislike of that was seen on his face.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: O Messenger of Allah, we have a land called the land of Abyan; it is our land of farming and provisions, but it is pestilential, or he said: its plague is severe. So the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Leave it, for being near the disease is [a cause of] destruction."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said: O Messenger of Allah, we were in a house where our numbers were many and our wealth was abundant, then we moved to another house and our numbers dwindled and our wealth dwindled.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Leave it, it is blameworthy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"The mukātab (slave contracted for freedom) remains a slave as long as a dirham of his contract remains owing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Juwayriyah bint al-Ḥārith ibn al-Muṣṭaliq fell to the share of Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās, or a cousin of his, and she made a contract for her own freedom. She was a very beautiful woman who captivated the eye. ʿĀʾishah, Allah be pleased with her, said: She came to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for help with her contract. When she stood at the door I saw her and disliked her being there, and I knew that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would see in her what I had seen. She said: O Messenger of Allah, I am Juwayriyah bint al-Ḥārith, and what has happened in my affair is not hidden from you. I fell to the share of Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās, and I made a contract for my freedom, so I have come to ask you for help with my contract. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Would you like something better than that?"
She said: What is it, O Messenger of Allah? He said:
"I will pay off your contract on your behalf and marry you."

She said: I have done so. She [ʿĀʾishah] said: The people heard, meaning the Companions, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had married Juwayriyah, so they released what was in their hands of captives and freed them, saying: They are in-laws of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We did not see any woman who was a greater blessing to her people than she; because of her, a hundred households of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq were freed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
freed his share of a slave, and that was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"Allah has no partner."
Ibn Kathīr added in his narration: So the Prophet ﷺ permitted his freeing [of the slave].
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
freed his share of a slave, so the Prophet ﷺ permitted his freeing of him and made him liable for the rest of his price.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the dawn prayer one day and said, "Is so-and-so present?" They said, "No." He said, "Is so-and-so present?" They said, "No." He said, "

These two prayers are the heaviest of prayers on the hypocrites. If you knew what is in them, you would come to them even if crawling on your knees. The first row is like the row of the angels, and if you knew its virtue, you would race to it. A man's prayer with another man is purer than his prayer alone, and his prayer with two men is purer than his prayer with one man; and the more there are, the more beloved it is to Allah, the Exalted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "

Whoever attends the ʿIshāʾ prayer in congregation will have the reward of standing in prayer for half the night, and whoever prays ʿIshāʾ and Fajr in congregation will have the reward of standing in prayer for the whole night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The farther one is from the mosque, the greater his reward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever performs ablution and does it well, then goes out intending the mosque, and finds that the people have already prayed, Allah will record for him the like of the reward of those who attended it, and that will not diminish their rewards in the least."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Ibn ʿUmar sitting on the paved ground while the people were praying. I said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, why do you not pray?" He said, "I have already prayed. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say,
"The prayer is not to be repeated twice in one day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She who was called ʿAqīlah, from Salāmah bint al-Ḥurr,
the sister of Kharashah, said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say, "
A time will come upon the people when they will stand for an hour,
not finding an imam to lead them in prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayrith used to come to us at this place of prayer of ours. Once the prayer was called, and we said to him, "Go forward and lead it."
He said to us, "Put forward one of your own men to lead you in prayer, and I will tell you why I do not lead you. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say,
'Whoever visits a people should not lead them in prayer; rather, a man from among them should lead them.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: He prayed the dawn prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when he finished the prayer, he turned away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
The imam should not pray [a voluntary prayer] in the same place where he prayed the obligatory prayer until he moves away from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Do not rush ahead of me in bowing or in prostration,
for whatever I get ahead of you in when I bow,
you will catch up with me in it when I rise;
and whatever I get ahead of you in when I prostrate,
you will catch up with me in it when I rise,
for I have become heavy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw Abū Rāfiʿ, the freed slave of the Prophet ﷺ, pass by al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, may peace be upon them both, while he was praying standing, with his braided hair tied at the back of his neck. Abū Rāfiʿ untied it, and al-Ḥasan turned to him angrily. Abū Rāfiʿ said, "Turn back to your prayer and do not be angry, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say,
'That is the seat of Satan.'"
Meaning the place where Satan sits, that is, where his braid is tied.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray barefoot and wearing sandals.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to move through the rows from one side to the other, wiping our chests and shoulders, and he would say, "
Do not be disordered, or your hearts will be at odds." And he used to say, "
Indeed Allah and His angels send blessings upon the first rows."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said, "

Close your rows, bring them near one another, and align your necks. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, I see the devils entering through the gaps in the row as if they were small sheep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Complete the front row, then the one that follows it; and if there is any shortfall, let it be in the last row."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "

When one of you prays, let him place something in front of him. If he cannot find anything, let him set up a staff. If he has no staff, let him draw a line; then what passes in front of him will not harm him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade praying behind someone who is talking or someone who is sleeping.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ, he said, "
When one of you prays toward a screen, let him come close to it, so that Satan does not cut off his prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
When one of you prays, let him pray toward a screen and let him come close to it.
Let him not allow anyone to pass in front of him.
If someone comes to pass, let him fight him, for he is a devil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in the house of Maymūnah when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered, and with him was Khālid ibn al-Walīd. They brought two roasted lizards on two thumāmah-stalks, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spat. Khālid said, "Do I take it that you find it repulsive, Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Yes."
Then milk was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he drank. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you eats food, let him say: O Allah, bless us in it and feed us better than it.
And when he is given milk to drink, let him say: O Allah, bless us in it and give us more of it.
For there is nothing that suffices in place of food and drink except milk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A one-eyed man from Thaqīf who was called Maʿrūf, meaning he was spoken of well (if his name was not Zuhayr ibn ʿUthmān, then I do not know what his name was), [reported] that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"The wedding feast on the first day is a duty, on the second day it is a kindness, and on the third day it is for show and ostentation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had a large bowl called al-Gharrāʾ, which four men would carry. When they reached the forenoon and had prayed the forenoon prayer, that bowl was brought, meaning that tharīd had been prepared in it, and they gathered around it. When they became many, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ knelt down. A Bedouin said, "What is this way of sitting?" The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Allah has made me a noble servant, and He has not made me a stubborn tyrant."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Eat from its sides and leave its top; blessing will be placed in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I would love to have a white loaf of brown wheat, smeared with ghee and milk."
A man from among the people got up and prepared it and brought it, and he said:
"In what was this [ghee]?"
He said, "In a lizard-skin container." He said, "Take it away."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mūsā, in another place, from Samurah ibn Jundub, as Ḥammād thought, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever owns a relative within the prohibited degrees of kinship, he is free."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, {Allah is He who created you from weakness}, and he said, "{From weakness}. I recited it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as you have recited it to me, and he corrected me as I have corrected you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Umm Salamah how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite this verse: {Indeed, it is a deed that is not righteous}. She said, "He recited it: {Indeed, it is a deed that is not righteous}." Abū Dāwūd said: Hārūn al-Naḥwī and Mūsā ibn Khalaf also narrated it from Thābit as ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb taught me to recite as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught him: {in a spring of ḥamiʾah}, without the ʾalif (lightened).
label: machine translation

segments_en: Maʿmar said, and at times he mentioned Ibn al-Musayyib: The Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān used to recite {Mālik yawm al-dīn}, and the first to recite it {Malik yawm al-dīn} was Marwān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yaʿlā and Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn, both from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād ibn Anʿum al-Ifrīqī,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Rāfiʿ,
from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The land of the non-Arabs will be opened to you, and you will find in it houses called bathhouses. Men must not enter them except in a waist-wrapper, and keep women from entering them, except one who is sick or in postnatal bleeding."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us and saw a man with disheveled hair, his hair scattered, and he said:
"Could this man not find something to settle his hair?"
And he saw another man wearing dirty clothes, and he said:
"Could this man not find water with which to wash his garment?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the world in his presence, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you not hear? Do you not hear? Plain living is part of faith; plain living is part of faith." Meaning austerity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ with my father, and he said to a man, or to my father, "Who is this?" He said, "My son." He said:
"Do not commit a crime against him."
And he had dyed his beard with henna.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿItbān ibn Mālik, who was
one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ from the Anṣār who had taken part in Badr, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Shihāb said: Then I asked al-Ḥuṣayn ibn Muḥammad—who was one of Banū Sālim and one of their nobles—about the hadith of
Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ from ʿItbān ibn Mālik, and he confirmed it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was
among the eldest of Banū ʿAdī, and his father had taken part in Badr with the Prophet ﷺ. ʿUmar appointed Qudāmah ibn Maẓʿūn over Bahrain,
and he had taken part in Badr,
and he was the maternal uncle of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and of Ḥafṣah, may Allah be pleased with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade renting out farmland.
I said to Sālim: Do you rent it out? He said: Yes,
Rāfiʿ had burdened himself too much [with this].
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Rifāʿah ibn Rāfiʿ al-Anṣārī,
who had taken part in Badr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: to Abū Bakr: Come with us to our brothers from the Anṣār.
So we met two righteous men from them who had taken part in Badr.
Then I told ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, and he said: They are ʿUwaym ibn Sāʿidah,
and Maʿn ibn ʿAdī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The stipend of those who fought at Badr was five thousand each.
And ʿUmar said: I will certainly give them precedence over those after them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from the hadith of

ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ—each of them related to me a portion of the hadith—she said: Umm Misṭaḥ and I came forward, and Umm Misṭaḥ stumbled on her cloak and said: May Misṭaḥ perish!
So I said: What an evil thing you have said!
Do you curse a man who took part in Badr? Then he mentioned the hadith of the slander.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Badr, a hundred shares were allotted to the Emigrants.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah, peace be upon her, and al-ʿAbbās came to Abū Bakr seeking their inheritance:
his land at Fadak,
and his share at Khaybar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Uḥud, the Prophet ﷺ appointed ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jubayr over the foot soldiers, and [the others] came back in retreat,
and that is [the meaning of]: "when the Messenger was calling them from behind them,"
and no more than twelve men remained with the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to invoke [Allah] against Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah, Suhayl ibn ʿAmr and al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, so [the verse] was revealed: {You have no say in the matter} up to His saying {for they are wrongdoers}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Suddī claimed, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from his father, who said:
On the day of the conquest of Makkah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted safety to the people, except for four men and two women, and he said:
"Kill them, even if you find them clinging to the curtains of the Kaʿbah."

They were ʿIkrimah ibn Abī Jahl, ʿAbdullāh ibn Khaṭal, Miqyas ibn Ṣubābah, and ʿAbdullāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī al-Sarḥ. As for ʿAbdullāh ibn Khaṭal, he was caught while clinging to the curtains of the Kaʿbah, and Saʿīd ibn Ḥurayth and ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir raced to him. Saʿīd beat ʿAmmār to him, as he was the younger of the two men, and he killed him. As for Miqyas ibn Ṣubābah, the people caught up with him in the marketplace and killed him. As for ʿIkrimah, he boarded a ship at sea, and a violent storm struck them. The people of the ship said, "Be sincere in your devotion [to Allah alone], for your gods are of no avail to you here."

ʿIkrimah said, "By Allah, if nothing but sincere devotion saves me from the sea, then nothing else will save me on land either. O Allah, I make a covenant with You that if You deliver me from this situation, I will go to Muḥammad ﷺ and place my hand in his, and I will surely find him pardoning and generous."

So he came and accepted Islam. As for ʿAbdullāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī al-Sarḥ, he hid with ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called the people to give the pledge of allegiance, ʿUthmān brought him and made him stand before the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, accept the pledge of ʿAbdullāh."
He said: He raised his head and looked at him three times, each time refusing, and then after the third time he accepted his pledge. Then he turned to his Companions and said:
"Was there not among you a man of sound judgment who would stand up to this man when he saw me withhold my hand from accepting his pledge, and kill him?"
They said, "We did not know what was in your heart, O Messenger of Allah. Why did you not signal to us with your eye?" He said:
"It is not fitting for a prophet to have a treacherous eye."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a delegation of Hawāzin came to him. They said, "O Muḥammad, we are of [your] origin and kin, and a calamity has befallen us which is not hidden from you, so show us favor, and may Allah show you favor." He said:
"Choose either your wealth or your women and children."
They said, "You have given us a choice between our lineage and our wealth. Rather, we choose our women and children."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"As for what belongs to me and to the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, it is yours. When I have prayed the noon prayer, stand up and say: 'We seek the help of the Messenger of Allah against the believers,' or 'the Muslims,' 'concerning our women and children.'"
When they had prayed the noon prayer, they stood up and said that, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What belongs to me and to the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib is yours."
The Muhājirūn said, "What belongs to us belongs to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
And the Anṣār said, "What belongs to us belongs to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
Al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis said, "As for me and Banū Tamīm, no."
ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn said, "As for me and Banū Fazārah, no."
Al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās said, "As for me and Banū Sulaym, no."
Banū Sulaym stood up and said, "You have spoken falsely. What belongs to us belongs to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O people, return to them their women and children. Whoever holds on to anything of this spoils, he shall have six shares from the first spoils that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, grants us."
Then he mounted his riding beast and the people mounted, [saying], "Distribute to us our spoils!" They pressed him toward a tree, and it snatched his cloak. He said:
"O people, give me back my cloak. By Allah, if you had as many camels as the trees of Tihāmah, I would distribute them among you, and then you would not find me stingy, nor cowardly, nor a liar."
Then he went to a camel, took a hair from its hump between his two fingers, and said:
"Behold, I have no share of the spoils, not even this, except the fifth, and the fifth is returned to you."
A man stood up to him with a ball of wool and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I took this to mend the packsaddle of a camel of mine." He said:
"As for what belongs to me and to the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, it is yours."
The man said, "Has it come to this? Then I have no need of it." And he threw it away. And he said:
"O people, return the thread and the needle, for misappropriation of spoils will be a disgrace and a shame upon those who commit it on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār reported that Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: Dhū al-Majāz and ʿUkāẓ were marketplaces for the people in the Pre-Islamic Era of Ignorance,
and when Islam came, it was as if they disliked that [trading], until [the verse] was revealed: {There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord} during the seasons of Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid
asked Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) about ʿUmrah
before Hajj, and he said: There is no harm in it.
ʿIkrimah said: Ibn ʿUmar said: The Prophet ﷺ performed ʿUmrah before he performed Hajj.
Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd said, from Ibn Isḥāq: ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid narrated to me: I asked Ibn ʿUmar, [and he said] the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I and ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr entered the mosque,
and there was ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) sitting near the room of ʿĀʾishah,
and some people were praying the Ḍuḥā prayer in the mosque.
He said: We asked him about their prayer, and he said: It is an innovation.
Then he said to him: How many times did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ʿUmrah? He said: Four, one of them in Rajab.
We disliked to contradict him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), and she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not perform ʿUmrah in Rajab.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) set out for Makkah to perform ʿUmrah during the time of the trial, he said: If I am prevented from the House, I will do as we did with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So he assumed ihrām for ʿUmrah,
because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had assumed ihrām for ʿUmrah in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That some of the sons of ʿAbdullāh
said to him: If only you would stay [behind]. And so on.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was prevented [from completing ʿUmrah], so he shaved his head, had relations with his wives, and slaughtered his sacrificial animal,
until he performed ʿUmrah the following year.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ slaughtered [his sacrificial animal] before shaving,
and he commanded his Companions to do so.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ at al-Qāḥah, three [nights' distance] from Madinah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of Makkah refused to let him enter Makkah,
until he made an agreement with them that he would not enter Makkah carrying weapons except in their sheaths.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a woman,
label: machine translation

segments_en: to al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd,
and he had performed Hajj with him among the baggage party of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmr (may Allah be pleased with him) gave permission to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ in the last Hajj he performed,
and he sent ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ said:
"What lies between the two lava fields of Madinah is sacred, by my word."
He said: The Prophet ﷺ came to the Banū Ḥārithah and said:
"I see, O Banū Ḥārithah, that you have gone out of the sanctuary." Then he turned and said:
"Rather, you are within it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "This is Ṭābah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The terror of the Antichrist will not enter Madinah.
On that day it will have seven gates,
and at every gate there will be two angels."
He said: Ibn Isḥāq said, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father,
who said: I came to Basrah and Abū Bakrah said to me: I heard the Prophet ﷺ [say] this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: O Allah, grant me martyrdom in Your cause,
and make my death in the city of Your Messenger ﷺ.
Ibn Zurayʿ said, from Rawḥ ibn al-Qāsim,
from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his mother,
from Ḥafṣah bint ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: I heard ʿUmar [say] something similar.
Hishām said, from Zayd, from his father, from Ḥafṣah: I heard ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Fasting is a shield,
so let him not speak obscenely or act ignorantly,
and if a man fights him or insults him, let him say: I am fasting—twice.
By the One in whose hand is my soul, the breath of the fasting person's mouth is better with Allah, the Exalted, than the scent of musk.
He leaves his food, his drink, and his desire for My sake. Fasting is for Me,
and I will reward it,
and a good deed is rewarded tenfold."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was asking Anas ibn Mālik (may Allah be pleased with him): Did you dislike cupping for the fasting person? He said: No,
except because of weakness.
Shabābah added: Shuʿbah narrated to us: in the time of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He said: It has been abrogated.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Is it not that when she menstruates she does not pray
and does not fast? That is the deficiency in her religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The brother-in-law of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the brother of Juwayriyah bint al-Ḥārith, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not leave behind at his death any dirham or dinar, nor any male slave or female slave, nor anything else,
except his white mule, his weapons, and a piece of land which he had made charity (ṣadaqah).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah and he had no servant.
So Abū Ṭalḥah took me by the hand
and went with me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, Anas is a clever boy; let him serve you.
Anas said: So I served him while traveling and while at home.
He never said to me about anything I did, 'Why did you do this like that?' nor about anything I did not do, 'Why did you not do this like that?'
label: machine translation

segments_en: His father was martyred on the day of Uḥud
and left behind six daughters,
and left a debt owing.
When the time for harvesting the dates came, I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, you know that my father was martyred on the day of Uḥud and left a great debt,
and I would like the creditors to see you.' He said:
"Go and put each kind of dates in its own heap."
I did so and then invited him.
When they saw him, they pressed me hard for payment at that moment.
When he saw what they were doing, he walked around the biggest heap three times, then sat on it and said, "Call your companions."
He kept measuring out to them until Allah had discharged the trust of my father.
By Allah, I was content that Allah discharge my father's trust even if I did not return to my sisters with a single date.
By Allah, all the heaps were left intact, so that I looked at the heap on which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been, as though it had not decreased by a single date.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: Direct me to a deed equal to jihad. He said:
"I do not find one." Then he said: "Are you able, when the mujāhid goes out, to enter your mosque and stand in prayer without ceasing, and to fast without breaking your fast?"
The man said: Who is able to do that? Abū Hurayrah said: The horse of the mujāhid walks about on its tether, and good deeds are recorded for him [because of it].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent his maternal uncle, the brother of Umm Sulaym, with seventy riders.
The leader of the polytheists, ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl, offered three options and said: You shall have the people of the plains,
and I shall have the people of the settled villages,
or I shall be your successor,
or I shall attack you with the tribe of Ghaṭafān with a thousand and a thousand.

Then ʿĀmir was stricken with a plague sore in the house of Umm so-and-so, and he said: A swelling like the swelling of a young camel, in the house of a woman of the family of so-and-so! Bring me my horse.
So he died on the back of his horse.
Ḥarām, the brother of Umm Sulaym, set out with a lame man and a man from the Banū so-and-so. He said: Stay close by until I go to them.
If they give me protection, you will be with me,
and if they kill me, you go to your companions.
He said: Will you give me protection so that I may convey the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
He began speaking to them, and they gestured to a man,
who came at him from behind and stabbed him—Hammām said: I think he said: until it went right through him—with a spear.
He said: Allah is the Greatest! By the Lord of the Kaʿbah, I have succeeded! Then the man caught up with the rest,
and they were all killed except the lame man, who was on top of a mountain.
Then Allah revealed to us [a verse],
which was later abrogated: 'We have met our Lord, and He is pleased with us and has made us pleased.'
The Prophet ﷺ then invoked [Allah's curse] upon them for thirty mornings,
against Riʿl, Dhakwān, Banū Liḥyān, and ʿUṣayyah,
who disobeyed Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Prophet ﷺ was walking, a stone struck him and he stumbled, and his finger bled. He said:
"You are only a finger that has bled, and what you have met is in the cause of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said that al-Rubayyiʿ bint al-Naḍr

came to the Prophet ﷺ. Her son Ḥārithah ibn Surāqah had been struck by a stray arrow on the day of Badr. She came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: Tell me about Ḥārithah. If he has attained good, I will be patient and hope for reward from Allah, and if he has not attained good, I will strive hard in supplication. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"O Umm Ḥārithah, they are gardens within Paradise, and your son has attained al-Firdaws al-Aʿlā, and al-Firdaws is the highest part of Paradise, its middle and its best."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb hadith from the narration of Anas.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ threw pebbles at the jamrah that is next to the mosque of Minā, he would throw seven pebbles,
saying the takbīr with each pebble he threw.
Then he would move forward in front of it and stand facing the qiblah, raising his hands and making supplication,
and he would stand for a long time.
Then he would come to the second jamrah
and throw seven pebbles at it,
saying the takbīr with each pebble he threw.
Then he would descend to the left, on the side of the valley,
and stand facing the qiblah, raising his hands and making supplication.
Then he would come to the jamrah at the ʿAqabah and throw seven pebbles at it,
saying the takbīr with each pebble.
Then he would leave and not stand at it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He ordered the people that the last thing they do
be at the House [the Kaʿbah], except that it was made lighter for the woman in menstruation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, the people return with two rites, and I return with one rite?" He said: "

Wait, and when you are pure, go out to at-Tanʿīm and enter ihrām for ʿUmrah from there, then meet us at such and such a place." [The narrator said:] I think he said, "Tomorrow. But it is in proportion to your effort," or he said, "your expenditure."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ʿUmrah and we performed ʿUmrah with him. When he entered Makkah, he performed ṭawāf and we performed ṭawāf with him,
and he went to Ṣafā and Marwah and we went to them with him,
and we shielded him from the people of Makkah, lest anyone hit him with something.
A companion of mine said to him: "Did he enter the Kaʿbah?" He said: "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he

used to hear Asmāʾ, every time she passed by al-Ḥajūn, say: "May Allah send blessings and peace upon His Messenger. We camped here with him, and on that day we were light in baggage, with few mounts and little provisions. I performed ʿUmrah, along with my sister ʿĀʾishah, az-Zubayr, and so-and-so and so-and-so. When we had touched the House, we came out of ihrām, then in the evening we entered ihrām for Hajj."
Hārūn said in his narration that [he was] the freed slave of Asmāʾ.
And he did not name ʿAbdullāh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Makkah, the young boys of the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib met him,
and he carried one in front of him and another behind him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would not come to his family at night unannounced;
he would enter only in the morning or the evening.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a man from coming to his family at night unexpectedly, suspecting them of betrayal or seeking out their faults.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ came back from a journey
and looked at the walls of Madinah, he would make his mount go faster,
and if he was on an animal,
he would urge it on out of his love for it [Madinah].
label: machine translation

segments_en: This verse was revealed about us.
When the Anṣār performed Hajj and then returned, they would not enter their houses through the doors,
but rather from the backs of them.
Then a man of the Anṣār came
and entered through his door,
and it was as if he was reproached for that,
so it was revealed: {It is not righteousness to enter houses from the back, but righteousness is [in] one who fears Allah. And enter houses through their doors.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out for Hajj and we set out with him. He sent some of his Companions off in another direction, among them Abū Qatādah, and said: "
Take the coast of the sea until you meet me."
So they took the coast of the sea.

When they turned back toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they all entered ihrām except Abū Qatādah, who did not. While they were traveling, they saw wild donkeys. Abū Qatādah attacked them and wounded a female donkey, so they stopped and ate some of its meat. They said: "We have eaten meat while we are in ihrām." So they carried what remained of the donkey's meat. When they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, we were in ihrām and Abū Qatādah was not. We saw wild donkeys and Abū Qatādah attacked them and wounded a female donkey. We stopped and ate some of its meat, then we said, 'We are eating the meat of game while we are in ihrām.'
So we carried what remained of its meat." He said: "
Did any of you order him or point to it for him in any way?"
They said: "No." He said: "
Then eat what remains of its meat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a cave when {By those [winds] sent forth in succession} was revealed, and we were receiving it from his mouth,
when a snake came out of its hole, and we hurried to kill it,
but it got ahead of us and entered its hole.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It was protected from your harm,
just as you were protected from its harm."
And from Isrāʾīl, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbdullāh, similarly. He said: "And we were receiving it from his mouth while it was still fresh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ called the gecko a little transgressor.
I did not hear him order that it be killed.
But Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ claimed that the Prophet ﷺ ordered it to be killed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father took me on Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Farewell Hajj, when I was seven years old.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [This was] read to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Maqburī,
from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
that he informed him that he

asked ʿĀʾishah, the Mother of the Believers, how the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Ramadan. She said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not add to eleven rakʿahs, in Ramadan or at any other time. He would pray four, and do not ask about their beauty and length; then he would pray four, and do not ask about their beauty and length; then he would pray three." ʿĀʾishah said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, do you sleep before praying Witr?" He said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, my eyes sleep but my heart does not sleep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray any of the night prayer except standing, until he grew old; then he would pray sitting, and when about forty or thirty verses of his recitation remained, he would stand, recite them, and prostrate.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Khāl al-Qaʿnabī and Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, with the meaning being the same, said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Mawāl narrated to us,
Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to me,
that he heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us the istikhārah just as he taught us a sūrah of the Qurʾān. He would say to us:

"When one of you is concerned about a matter, let him pray two rakʿahs other than the obligatory prayer, and then say: O Allah, I seek Your guidance through Your knowledge, I seek ability through Your power, and I ask You of Your great favor. For You are able and I am not able, You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen.
