O Allah, if You know that this matter—and he names it specifically—is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, my return, and the outcome of my affair, then decree it for me, make it easy for me, and bless me in it. O Allah, and if You know it to be bad for me, like the first, then turn me away from it and turn it away from me, and decree for me the good wherever it may be, then make me content with it." Or he said:
"in my present affair and its future."
Ibn Maslamah and Ibn ʿĪsā said, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jābir.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Journeys are not to be undertaken except to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, the Farthest Mosque, and this mosque of mine."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Abū Ṣāliḥ whether he had heard Abū Hurayrah

mention the virtue of prayer in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: "No, but ʿAbdullāh ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Qāriẓ informed me that he heard Abū Hurayrah narrate that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"One prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers—or like a thousand prayers—in any other mosque, except the Sacred Mosque."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zayd ibn Arqam said to me: We used to speak during prayer in the time of the Prophet ﷺ,
with one of us speaking to his companion about his need, until [the verse] was revealed: {Guard strictly the prayers} — the verse — and we were commanded to be silent.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you stands to pray, the devil comes to him and confuses him until he does not know how much he has prayed. So if one of you finds that, let him perform two prostrations while sitting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
said: Sufyān narrated to us,
ibn ʿUyaynah; and [by another chain] ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn
Rāfiʿ narrated to us from ʿAbd al-Razzāq, who said: Maʿmar informed us,
both from al-Zuhrī,
with the chain of Mālik and with the meaning of his hadith, except that in the hadith of Sufyān:
"he will enter the Fire only to fulfill the oath."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ delayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer one night until most of the night had passed and the people in the mosque had fallen asleep. Then he came out and prayed, and said:
"This is its proper time, were it not that I would be placing a burden on my Ummah."
And in the narration of ʿAbd al-Razzāq:
"Were it not that it would be a burden on my Ummah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was occupied one night and delayed the prayer until we had fallen asleep in the mosque, then woken up, then slept again, then woken up. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and said:
"None of the people of the earth is waiting for the prayer tonight except you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We waited for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night until it was close to the middle of the night. Then he came and prayed, and then turned to us with his face, and it is as though I can see the gleam of his silver ring on his hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He arrived at al-Rabadhah when the prayer had been called, and there was a slave leading them in prayer. It was said, "This is Abū Dharr."
He started to step back, but Abū Dharr said, "My beloved friend ﷺ advised me to listen and obey, even if it is an Abyssinian slave with severed limbs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Ziyād delayed the prayer, so ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ṣāmit came to me. I placed a chair for him and he sat on it. I told him about what Ibn Ziyād had done, and he bit his lip and struck my thigh and said, "I asked Abū Dharr just as you have asked me, and he struck my thigh as I have struck yours, and said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ just as you have asked me, and he struck my thigh as I have struck yours, and said:
'Pray the prayer at its proper time. Then if the prayer finds you with them, pray [with them], and do not say, "I have already prayed, so I will not pray."'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Yaʿqūb al-Dawraqī,
all of them from Marwān al-Fazārī,
— Qutaybah said: Al-Fazārī narrated to us —
from ʿUbaydullāh ibn al-Aṣamm,
who said: Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm narrated to us,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: A blind man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have no guide to lead me to the mosque."
He asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to grant him a concession to pray in his house, and he granted him the concession. But when the man turned to leave, he called him and said:
"Do you hear the call to prayer?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Then respond."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a man—I do not know anyone among the people of Madinah who prayed toward the qiblah whose home was farther from the mosque than that man's—and he never missed a prayer in the mosque. So I said, "If only you would buy a donkey to ride in the scorching heat and the darkness."

He said, "I would not like my house to be beside the mosque." The matter reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he asked him about what he had said. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I wanted my walking to the mosque and my return to my family, when I return, to be recorded for me." Then he said:
"Allah has given you all of that. Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has given you everything you sought reward for, all of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a man of the Anṣār whose house was the farthest house in Madinah, and yet he never missed the prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: We felt sorry for him, so I said to him, "O so-and-so, if only you would buy a donkey to protect you from the scorching ground and from the vermin of the earth."

He said, "By Allah, I would not like my house to be adjoined to the house of Muḥammad ﷺ." He said: I was greatly troubled by this, so I went to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and told him. He said: He called the man, and he said the same thing to him, and told him that he hoped for reward in his footsteps.
So the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"You will have what you sought reward for."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The areas around the mosque became empty, so Banū Salimah wanted to move closer to the mosque. This reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said to them:
"It has reached me that you want to move close to the mosque."
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, we wanted that." He said:
"O Banū Salimah, your homes! Your footsteps are being recorded. Your homes! Your footsteps are being recorded."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If there are three, let one of them lead them, and the most deserving of them to lead is the one who recites best."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had a kohl container from which he would apply kohl three times to each eye.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, in our land there are grapes which we press and drink from." He said, "No."
I went back to him and said, "We use it as a cure for the sick." He said,
"That is not a cure, but a disease."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best medicine is the Qur'an."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "The evil eye is real."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "The evil eye is real."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Seek refuge with Allah, for the evil eye is real."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah passed by Sahl ibn Ḥunayf while he was bathing, and said, "I have never seen the like of today, not even the skin of a maiden kept in seclusion."
Before long Sahl collapsed. He was brought to the Prophet ﷺ and it was said to him, "Come to Sahl, who has fallen ill." He said,
"Whom do you suspect of this?"
They said, "ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah." He said,
"Why would one of you kill his brother? If one of you sees something in his brother that impresses him, let him pray for blessing for him."

Then he called for water and ordered ʿĀmir to perform ablution, washing his face, his hands up to the elbows, his knees, and the inside of his lower garment, and he ordered that it be poured over Sahl.
Sufyān said: Maʿmar said, from al-Zuhrī: He also ordered that the vessel be tipped over from behind him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Khālidah bint Anas, Umm Banī Ḥazm al-Sāʿidiyyah,
came to the Prophet ﷺ and presented to him the ruqyah [recitations for healing], and he commanded her to use them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The matter of a snakebite was presented to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he gave permission for ruqyah to be used for it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to visit me when I was ill and said to me:
"Shall I not perform ruqyah for you with one that Jibrīl brought me?"
I said, "Yes, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah." He said,

"In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, and Allah heals you from every illness within you, from the evil of those who blow on knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies." Three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to blow lightly while performing ruqyah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw a man with a brass ring on his hand and said:
"What is this ring?"
He said, "It is for weakness." He said,
"Take it off, for it only adds to your weakness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stone the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah from the bottom of the valley on the Day of Sacrifice. Then he left, and a woman from Khathʿam followed him with a son of hers who was afflicted and could not speak. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is my son and the last of my family, and he is afflicted and cannot speak."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Bring me some water."
Water was brought, and he washed his hands and rinsed his mouth, then gave it to her and said:
"Give him some of it to drink, pour some over him, and ask Allah to heal him."
She said: I met the woman and said, "If only you would give me some of it."
She said, "It is only for this afflicted child."
She said: I met the woman a year later and asked her about the boy. She said he had recovered and had become intelligent, with an intellect unlike the intellects of other people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The best medicine is the Qur'an.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ liked a good omen and disliked bad omens.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah bint al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do not keep looking at those with leprosy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Salamah said, "O Messenger of Allah, every year you keep suffering pain from the poisoned sheep that you ate." He said,
"Nothing has afflicted me from it except what was written for me while Adam was still in his clay."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying in a single garment, wrapped in it, with its two ends crossed over each other.
ʿĪsā ibn Ḥammād added in his narration: He said, "over his shoulders."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
all of them from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah,
(ʿAmr said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us) from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah:
that the believing women
used to pray the Fajr prayer with the Prophet ﷺ, then return wrapped in their cloaks, and no one would recognize them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr prayer with five units.
It was said to him, "Has the prayer been increased?" He said, "What is that?"
They said, "You prayed five."
So he performed two prostrations after he had given the salām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Make part of your prayers in your houses,
and do not turn them into graves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He sent him to Abū Juhaym to ask him what he had heard from
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the one who passes in front of a person praying. Abū Juhaym said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If the one who passes in front of a person praying knew what [burden] is upon him, standing for forty would be better for him than passing in front of him."

Abū al-Naḍr said: I do not know whether he said forty days, or months, or years. Abū ʿĪsā said: There are also narrations on this topic from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Abū Hurayrah, Ibn ʿUmar, and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabbān, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade prayer after the ʿAṣr prayer until the sun sets, and prayer after the Fajr prayer until the sun rises.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ said to him, or to a companion of his:
"When the time for prayer comes, call the adhān, then give the iqāmah, then let the elder of you two lead you."
In the narration of Maslamah he said: And we were close to each other in knowledge at that time.
And in the narration of Ismāʿīl he said: Khālid said: I said to Abū Qilābah, "So where is the Qurʾān [i.e., recitation]?" He said: The two of them were close to each other [in it].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell from a horse (and Sufyān sometimes said: off a horse) and his right side was scraped.
We went in to visit him, and the time for prayer came,
so he led us in prayer sitting, and we sat (and Sufyān once said: we prayed sitting). When he finished the prayer, he said:
"The imam is appointed only to be followed.
So when he says takbīr, say takbīr, and when he bows, bow,
and when he rises, rise,
and when he says, 'Sami'a Allāhu liman ḥamidah,'
then say, 'Rabbanā wa lakal-ḥamd.'
And when he prostrates, prostrate."
Sufyān said: Thus Maʿmar narrated it. I said, "Yes."
He said, "He has memorized well.
Thus al-Zuhrī said: 'wa lakal-ḥamd.'
I memorized it as 'his right side.'"
When we left al-Zuhrī, Ibn Jurayj said (and I was with him): "His right shin was scraped."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"I begin the prayer intending to make it long,
then I hear the crying of a child,
so I shorten my prayer, because I know how intensely his mother is distressed by his crying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood for prayer, he would raise his hands until they were level with his shoulders, then say the takbīr while they were so, and then bow. Then when he wanted to raise his back [from bowing], he would raise them until they were level with his shoulders, then say, "Sami'a Allāhu liman ḥamidah." He would not raise his hands in prostration, but he would raise them at every takbīr he said before bowing, until his prayer was finished.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ used to recite in the Fajr prayer on Friday "Alif, Lām, Mīm. The revelation" [Sūrat al-Sajdah] and "Has there not come upon man a period of time" [Sūrat al-Insān], and that the Prophet ﷺ used to recite in the Friday prayer Sūrat al-Jumuʿah and Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Jābir: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ deliver the sermon standing? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to deliver the sermon standing, then he would sit for a short while, then stand again.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was

one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day to pray for rain; he turned his back to the people, supplicating to Allah and facing the qiblah, and he turned his cloak around, then prayed two units.
Ibn Abī Dhiʾb said in the hadith: And he recited in them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Khaybar was conquered, the Jews asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to let them remain on the condition that they work [the land] for half of what it produced. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I will let you remain in it on that basis for as long as we wish."

So they remained on that basis, and the dates were divided into shares from half of Khaybar, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would take the fifth. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give each of his wives from the fifth one hundred wasqs of dates and twenty wasqs of barley. When ʿUmar wished to expel the Jews, he sent word to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and said to them: "Whoever among you wishes, I will apportion to her palm trees by estimate at one hundred wasqs, so that she will have the trees themselves, the land and the water, and, of the crops, a field estimated at twenty wasqs; we will do so. And whoever prefers that we set aside for her what she receives from the fifth as it is, we will do so."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the man who becomes insolvent, when the goods [he bought] are found in his possession and he has not disposed of them:
"They belong to the one who sold them to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of the stud services of the male camel, the sale of water, and the sale of land for cultivation, where a man sells his land and its water. It was concerning that the Prophet ﷺ forbade.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the killing of dogs, except a hunting dog or a dog for sheep or livestock.
It was said to Ibn ʿUmar: "Abū Hurayrah says: or a dog for crops."
Ibn ʿUmar said: "Abū Hurayrah has a farm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered us to kill dogs, until a woman would come from the desert with her dog and we would kill it. Then the Prophet ﷺ forbade killing them and said:
"Stick to the pure black one with two spots, for it is a devil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the killing of dogs, then he said:
"What is the matter with them and dogs?"
Then he granted them a concession regarding the dog for crops and the dog for the ʿayn.
Bundār said: The ʿayn refers to the orchards of Medina.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Dates for dates, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, and salt for salt, like for like, hand to hand. Whoever gives more or asks for more has engaged in usury, except where their types differ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Khaybar, and we would trade with the Jews one ounce of gold for a dinar.
Someone other than Qutaybah said: for two or three dinars.
Then they agreed, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not sell gold for gold except weight for weight."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and I was on a camel. He said:
"Why are you at the back of the people?"

I said: "My camel is exhausted." So he took hold of its tail and then urged it on, and from then on I was at the front of the people, struggling to hold its head back. When we drew near Medina, he said:
"What has become of the camel? Sell it to me."
I said: "No, rather it is yours, Messenger of Allah." He said:
"No, rather sell it to me."
I said: "No, rather it is yours." He said:
"No, rather sell it to me. I have bought it for an ounce; ride it, and when you reach Medina, bring it to us."
When I reached Medina, I brought it to him, and he said to Bilāl:
"Bilāl, weigh out an ounce for him and add a qīrāṭ."

I said: "This is something the Messenger of Allah ﷺ added for me, so it never left me." I put it in a purse, and it stayed with me until the people of Syria came on the day of al-Ḥarrah and took from us what they took.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ borrowed a camel of a certain age, and he gave back one of a better age than it, and he said:
"The best of you are those who are best in repaying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: His father had given him a boy servant, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"What is this boy?"
He said: "My father gave him to me." He said:
"Did you give all his brothers the like of what you gave this one?" He said: "No." He said: "Then take him back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The ʿumrā that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted is when one says: "It is yours and your descendants'."
But if he says: "It is yours for as long as you live,"
then it returns to its owner.
Maʿmar said: Al-Zuhrī used to give rulings accordingly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O company of the Anṣār, keep hold of your property—do not grant it as ʿumrā—for whoever grants something as ʿumrā, it belongs to the one to whom it was granted, during his life and after his death."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade falsehood (zūr).
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān on the pulpit, holding in his hand a bundle of women's hair, and he said, "What is the matter with Muslim women that they do this? I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Any woman who adds to her head hair that is not her own, it is falsehood (zūr) that she is adding to it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the woman who attaches hair to another's and the woman who has hair attached to her own.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
came to ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd and said, "I am a woman with sparse hair. Is it permissible for me to attach hair to my own?" He said, "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The one who consumes usury, the one who feeds it to others, and its recorder, when they know it, the woman who tattoos and the woman who is tattooed for beauty, the one who withholds charity, and the one who reverts to being a Bedouin after having made the Hijrah are all cursed, on the tongue of Muhammad ﷺ, on the Day of Resurrection.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mughīrah and Ibn
ʿAwn, from ash-Shaʿbī, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who consumes usury, the one who feeds it to others, its recorder, and the one who withholds charity, and he used to forbid wailing for the dead.
Ibn ʿAwn and ʿAṭāʾ ibn as-Sāʾib transmitted it as a mursal report.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He and a companion of his used to stay close to Abū Rayḥānah to learn good from him. He said: One day my companion attended and told me that he heard Abū Rayḥānah say, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prohibited filing the teeth to make them sharp, tattooing, and plucking [hair]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade filing the teeth to make them sharp and tattooing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar
used to dye his garments with saffron. He was asked about it, and he said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to dye [his garments]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ use perfume?" She said, "Yes, with the perfumes of men: musk and ambergris."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ with a stain of khalūq (a saffron perfume) on him. The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "Go and wash it off thoroughly."
Then he came to him again, and he said, "Go and wash it off thoroughly."
Then he came to him again, and he said,
"Go and wash it off thoroughly, and do not do it again."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When a woman goes out to the mosque, let her wash off perfume as she washes from sexual impurity." Abridged.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whichever of you goes out to the mosque, let her not come near perfume."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to keep his family from [wearing] jewelry and silk, and he would say:
"If you love the jewelry of Paradise and its silk, then do not wear them in this world."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The daughter of Hubayrah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with large rings (fatakh) on her hand—he said: this is how it is in my father's book, meaning large rings—and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to strike her hand. She went in to Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, complaining to her of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had done to her. So Fāṭimah removed a gold chain from her neck and said, "Abū Ḥasan gave this to me as a gift." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered while the chain was in her hand, and he said:
"O Fāṭimah, does it please you that people should say, 'The daughter of the Messenger of Allah has a chain of fire in her hand'?"

Then he went out and did not sit. So Fāṭimah sent the chain to the market and sold it, and with its price she bought a slave boy—and once he said, a slave—and he mentioned a word with a similar meaning, and she freed him. When this was reported to him, he said:
"Praise be to Allah, Who saved Fāṭimah from the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when a woman came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, [what about] a pair of gold bracelets?" He said:
"A pair of bracelets of fire."
She said, "O Messenger of Allah, a gold necklace?" He said:
"A necklace of fire."
She said, "A pair of gold earrings?" He said:
"A pair of earrings of fire."

He said: She was wearing a pair of gold bracelets and she threw them off. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, if a woman does not adorn herself for her husband, she becomes unattractive to him." He said:
"What prevents any of you from making a pair of earrings of silver and then coloring them yellow with saffron or with perfume?"
The wording is that of Ibn Ḥarb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a pair of gold bangles on her, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Shall I not tell you of something better than this? If you took this off and made a pair of bangles of silver, then colored them yellow with saffron, they would be beautiful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn said to me: "Shall I narrate to you a hadith by which Allah may perhaps benefit you? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined Hajj and ʿUmrah, then he did not forbid it until he died, and no Qurʾān was revealed prohibiting it. And [the angels] used to greet me with salām until I was cauterized, so it stopped; then I gave up cauterization, and it returned."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar intended to perform Hajj when al-Ḥajjāj advanced against Ibn al-Zubayr.

And he related the hadith with a story like this, and at the end of the hadith he said: He used to say: Whoever combines Hajj and ʿUmrah, one ṭawāf suffices him, and he does not leave iḥrām until he leaves iḥrām from both of them together.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this story.
He did not mention the Prophet ﷺ except at the beginning of the hadith, when it was said to him: "They will prevent you from the House."
He said: "Then I will do as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did."
And he did not mention at the end of the hadith: "Thus the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did."
As al-Layth mentioned it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ saying the talbiyah for Hajj and ʿUmrah together.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Anas], may Allah be pleased with him, saw the Prophet ﷺ combine the two, Hajj and ʿUmrah. He said: I asked Ibn ʿUmar, and he said: "We declared our intention for Hajj [only]."
So I returned to Anas and told him what Ibn ʿUmar had said, and he said: "It is as if we were children!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with Ibn ʿUmar when a man came to him and said: "Is it permissible for me to perform ṭawāf around the House before I come to the place of standing [at ʿArafah]?" He said: "Yes."
He said: "But Ibn ʿAbbās says: Do not perform ṭawāf around the House until you come to the place of standing."

Ibn ʿUmar said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Hajj and made ṭawāf around the House before coming to the place of standing. So is it the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that is more deserving to be followed, or the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, if you are truthful?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, about the Hajj mutʿah,

and he permitted it. But Ibn al-Zubayr used to forbid it. [Ibn ʿAbbās] said: "This is the mother of Ibn al-Zubayr, narrating that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted it. Go in to her and ask her." He said: So we went in to her, and she was a large, blind woman, and she said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did permit it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In this chain of transmission, as for Rawḥ and Yaḥyā ibn Kathīr, they said as Naṣr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ declared his intention for Hajj.
As for Abū Shihāb, in his narration: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, declaring our intention for Hajj.
And in all of their narrations: Then he prayed the morning prayer at al-Baṭḥāʾ.
Except al-Jahḍamī, who did not say it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the morning prayer at Dhū Ṭuwā, and he arrived on the fourth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, and he commanded his Companions to convert their iḥrām into ʿUmrah, except those who had the sacrificial animal with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Banū al-Hujaym said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "What is this legal ruling of yours that has captivated, or stirred up, the people: that whoever performs ṭawāf around the House has left iḥrām?" He said: "It is the Sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ, even if you dislike it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh when someone came to him and said: "Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn al-Zubayr have differed about the two mutʿahs." Jābir said: "We did both with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then ʿUmar forbade us from both, so we did not return to them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
all of them from Ibn ʿUyaynah,
Saʿīd said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us: al-Zuhrī narrated to me,
from Ḥanẓalah al-Aslamī,
who said: I heard Abū Hurayrah,
may Allah be pleased with him, narrating from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, the son of Maryam will surely declare the talbiyah at Fajj al-Rawḥāʾ, for Hajj or ʿUmrah, or he will combine the two."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul," like their hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Anas how many times the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Hajj. He said: "One Hajj, and he performed ʿUmrah four times."
Then he mentioned [the rest] like the hadith of Hudbah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "I think I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said: "Describe him to me."
I said: "I saw him at al-Marwah on a she-camel, with a great crowd of people around him."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: "That was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They would not be driven away from him, nor rebuked."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Ibn ʿUmar touch the Stone with his hand, then kiss his hand, and he said: "I have not given it up since I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, in the Time of Ignorance I vowed to spend a night in devotional retreat (iʿtikāf) in the Sacred Mosque."
The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "Fulfil your vow." So he spent a night in devotional retreat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I send out my dog and mention the name of Allah." The Prophet ﷺ said,
"When you send out your dog and mention the name of Allah,
and it seizes the game, kills it, and eats from it, then do not eat it,
for it only caught it for itself."
I said, "I send out my dog and find another dog with it,
and I do not know which of them caught it." He said,
"Do not eat it, for you mentioned Allah's name only over your dog and not over the other."
And I asked him about game hunted with a miʿrāḍ (a pointless-edged shaft), and he said,
"If you hit the game with its sharp edge, then eat it,
but if you hit it with its side and it dies, then it is waqīdh (beaten to death), so do not eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, some people who only recently left the Time of Ignorance bring us meat, and we do not know whether they mentioned the name of Allah over it or not. May we eat from it?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Mention the name of Allah and eat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I walked to the Prophet ﷺ with barley bread and rancid fat. His armor had been pawned to a Jew for twenty ṣāʿ of food that he had taken for his family. And I heard him one day say,
"In the household of Muhammad ﷺ there is not a ṣāʿ of dates nor a ṣāʿ of grain by evening."
And at that time he had nine wives.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A tailor invited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to food he had prepared. Anas said: I went with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to that meal,
and he brought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ barley bread and a broth containing gourd and dried meat. Anas said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ picking out the gourd from around the dish,
and I have loved gourd ever since that day.
And Thumāmah related from Anas:
So I began gathering the gourd in front of him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When two men engage in a sale, each of them has the option [to cancel] until they part."
And on another occasion he said,

"As long as they have not parted and are still together, or one gives the other the choice. If one gives the other the choice and they conclude the sale on that basis, then the sale is binding. And if they part after having made the sale, and neither of them has abandoned the sale, then the sale is binding."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They
used to buy food from caravans in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he forbade them from selling it in the place where they had bought it until they moved it to the food market.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command the killing of dogs, so we would set out in Madinah and its outskirts and would not leave a dog without killing it, to the point that we would even kill the dog of a woman from the desert dwellers that was following her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
from the Anṣār made a slave of his a mudabbar (freed upon his death),
and he had no other property. This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said,
"Who will buy him from me?"
So Nuʿaym ibn al-Naḥḥām bought him for eight hundred dirhams.
And I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh say: He was a Coptic slave, and he died in the first year.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade two ways of dressing and two kinds of sale.
He forbade mulāmasah and munābadhah in sales.
Mulāmasah is when a man touches the garment of another with his hand, by night or by day,
and does not examine it except by that touch.
Munābadhah is when a man throws his garment to another man,
and the other throws his garment,
and that constitutes the sale between them,
without inspection and without mutual consent.
As for the two ways of dressing, one is ishtimāl aṣ-ṣammāʾ,
and aṣ-ṣammāʾ is when he puts his garment over one of his shoulders,
so that one side of him is exposed with no garment on it.
The other way of dressing is his sitting wrapped in his garment with his knees drawn up,
with nothing of it covering his private part.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned several hadith, among them that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"When any of you buys a milch camel or sheep whose milk has been held back in the udder, he has the better of the two options after he milks it: either he keeps it, or he returns it along with a ṣāʿ of dates."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the slave woman of any of you commits fornication and her guilt is established, let him flog her with the prescribed punishment and not rebuke her further. Then if she commits it again, let him flog her with the prescribed punishment and not rebuke her further. Then if she commits it a third time and her guilt is established, let him sell her, even for a rope of hair."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī led us in prayer, and when he sat at the end of his prayer, a man from the people said, "The prayer has been joined with righteousness and zakāh."

When Abū Mūsā finished, he turned to the people and said, "Which of you said such-and-such a word?" The people were silent. He said again, "Which of you said such-and-such a word?" The people were silent. He said, "Perhaps it was you, Ḥiṭṭān, who said it."
He said, "I did not say it, and I feared that you would rebuke me for it."
Then a man from the people said, "I said it, and I intended nothing by it except good."
Abū Mūsā said, "Do you not know what you should say in your prayer? Indeed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us, taught us, explained our Sunnah to us, and taught us our prayer. He said:

'When you pray, straighten your rows, then let one of you lead you. When he says takbīr, say takbīr; and when he recites {not those who have earned Your anger, nor those who are astray}, say "Āmīn"; Allah will answer you. When he says takbīr and bows, say takbīr and bow, for the imām bows before you and rises before you.'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

'That is in return for that. And when he says, "Allah hears whoever praises Him," say, "O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs all praise"; Allah will hear you, for Allah, the Exalted, said on the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ, "Allah hears whoever praises Him." And when he says takbīr and prostrates, say takbīr and prostrate, for the imām prostrates before you and rises before you.'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

'That is in return for that. And when you are at the sitting, let the first thing any of you says be: "All greetings, good words, and prayers are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger."'
Aḥmad did not say "and His blessings," nor did he say "and I bear witness." He said, "and that Muhammad..."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When we prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and one of us gave the salām, he would gesture with his hand to those on his right and on his left. When he had finished the prayer, he said:

"What is the matter with one of you, that he flings his hand as though it were the tails of skittish horses? It is enough for one of you—or: Is it not enough for one of you—to say thus," and he gestured with his finger,
"giving the greeting of peace to his brother on his right and on his left."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any woman who has applied incense should not attend the ʿIshāʾ prayer with us."
Ibn Nufayl said, "the last ʿIshāʾ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the Fajr prayer between sixty and a hundred verses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿādh ibn Jabal al-Anṣārī led his companions in the ʿIshāʾ prayer and made it long for them, so a man from among us left and prayed on his own. Muʿādh was told about him and said, "He is a hypocrite."
When that reached the man, he went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him what Muʿādh had said about him. The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Do you want to be a cause of trial, O Muʿādh? When you lead the people in prayer, recite {By the sun and its brightness}, {Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High}, {By the night when it covers}, and {Recite in the name of your Lord}."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I observed Muḥammad ﷺ—and Abū Kāmil said, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—in prayer, and I found his standing, his bowing, his prostration, his rising from the bowing, his sitting between the two prostrations, and his prostration, between the salām and the departure, to be nearly equal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say, when he said "Allah hears whoever praises Him,"
"O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs all praise, filling the heaven,

" Muʾammal said, "filling the heavens and filling the earth, and filling whatever else You will. You are worthy of praise and glory; the truest thing a servant has said, and we are all Your servants: none can withhold what You give," Maḥmūd added,
"and none can give what You withhold." Then they agreed:
"and the fortune of the fortunate cannot benefit him against You." Bishr said,
"Our Lord, to You belongs all praise."
Maḥmūd did not say "O Allah." He said:
"Our Lord, and to You belongs all praise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I was leading the Messenger of Allah ﷺ through one of those mountain passes, he said:
"Will you not ride, O ʿUqbah?"
I held the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in too much reverence to ride his mount. Then he said:
"Will you not ride, O ʿUqbah?"
I feared that it would be disobedience. So he dismounted, and I rode for a short while and then dismounted, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rode. Then he said:
"Shall I not teach you two surahs that are among the best two surahs the people recite?"

Then he taught me {Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak} and {Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind}. The prayer was then called, so he went forward and recited them both. Then he passed by me and said:
"How did you find it, O ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir? Recite them whenever you go to sleep and whenever you get up."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It will be said, meaning to the one who kept company with the Qurʾān: Recite and ascend, and recite slowly as you used to recite slowly in the world, for your rank will be at the last verse you recite."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard a man supplicating in his prayer who had neither glorified Allah, the Exalted, nor sent blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This one was hasty."
Then he called him and said to him, or to someone else:
"When any of you prays, let him begin by praising his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and extolling Him, then send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, and then supplicate afterward for whatever he wishes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he entered with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon a woman who had date stones, or he said pebbles, in front of her with which she was glorifying Allah. He said:

"Shall I not tell you of something easier for you than this, or better? Glory be to Allah as many times as what He created in the heavens, and glory be to Allah as many times as what He created on the earth, and glory be to Allah as many times as what is between that, and glory be to Allah as many times as what He is going to create. And Allah is the Greatest, the same; and praise be to Allah, the same; and there is no power and no strength except with Allah, the same."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan gharīb from the narration of Saʿd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever says: I seek forgiveness from Allah, the Magnificent, there is no god but Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, and I repent to Him,
he will be forgiven, even if he fled from the battlefield."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever persists in seeking forgiveness, Allah will make for him a way out from every hardship, a relief from every worry, and will provide for him from where he does not expect."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took him by the hand and said:
"O Muʿādh, by Allah, I truly love you; by Allah, I truly love you." Then he said:
"I advise you, O Muʿādh: never fail to say at the end of every prayer: O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You, and to worship You well."
Muʿādh advised aṣ-Ṣunābiḥī with that, and aṣ-Ṣunābiḥī advised Abū ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān with it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Shall I not teach you words that you should say at times of distress, or during distress: Allah, Allah is my Lord; I associate nothing with Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a military expedition, and when we were returning and came in sight of Medina, the people said the takbīr and raised their voices with it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Your Lord is not deaf and not absent; He is between you and the necks of your mounts." Then he said: "O ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays, shall I not teach you a treasure from the treasures of Paradise? There is no power and no strength except with Allah." Abū ʿĪsā said: This hadith is ḥasan. Abū ʿUthmān an-Nahdī's name is ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Mull, and Abū Nuʿāmah as-Saʿdī's name is ʿAmr ibn ʿĪsā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: No supplication is answered more quickly than the supplication of one absent for another absent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from poverty, and I seek refuge in You from scarcity and humiliation, and I seek refuge in You from wronging or being wronged." Al-Awzāʿī differed with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ṣāliḥ said that Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from discord, hypocrisy, and bad character."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Thus he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:

"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from being crushed under a collapse, and I seek refuge in You from falling from a height, and I seek refuge in You from drowning and burning, and I seek refuge in You that Satan should strike me at the time of death, and I seek refuge in You from dying while turning my back in Your cause, and I seek refuge in You from dying of a venomous sting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father heard me
as I was saying, "O Allah,
I ask You for Paradise, its bliss, its splendor, and so on, and I seek refuge in You from the Fire, its chains, its shackles, and so on." He said, "My son, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'There will be a people who transgress in supplication.'

So beware of being one of them. If you are given Paradise, you will be given it along with all the good in it, and if you are protected from the Fire, you will be protected from it along with all the evil in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to like the comprehensive supplications and would leave aside whatever else.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do not cover the walls. Whoever looks into his brother's letter without his permission is only looking into the Fire. Ask Allah with the palms of your hands, and do not ask Him with their backs. When you have finished, wipe your faces with them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read it in the original manuscript of Ismāʿīl, meaning Ibn ʿAyyāsh: Ḍamḍam narrated to me from Shurayḥ, who said: Abū Ẓabyah narrated to us that Abū Baḥriyyah as-Sakūnī narrated to him from Mālik ibn Yasār as-Sakūnī, then al-ʿAwfī, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you ask Allah, ask Him with the palms of your hands, and do not ask Him with their backs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ supplicating like this, with the insides of his palms and with their backs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ made supplication and raised his hands, he would wipe his face with his hands.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A cloak of hers was stolen, so she began to invoke [Allah] against the one who had stolen it. The Prophet ﷺ kept saying:
"Do not lighten it for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Dharr said: O Messenger of Allah, the wealthy have gone off with the rewards. They pray as we pray and fast as we fast, and they have surplus wealth with which they give charity, while we have no wealth to give in charity.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Abū Dharr, shall I not teach you words by which you will overtake those who have gone ahead of you, and none who come after you will catch up with you, except one who does the same as you do?"
He said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said:

"Declare the greatness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, thirty-three times after every prayer, praise Him thirty-three times, and glorify Him thirty-three times, and conclude with: 'There is no god but Allah, alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things.' His sins will be forgiven, even if they are like the foam of the sea."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sulaymān said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say after his prayer:

"O Allah, our Lord and the Lord of everything, I bear witness that You alone are the Lord, with no partner. O Allah, our Lord and the Lord of everything, I bear witness that Muḥammad is Your servant and Messenger. O Allah, our Lord and the Lord of everything, I bear witness that all the servants are brothers. O Allah, our Lord and the Lord of everything, make me and my family sincere to You in every hour, in this world and the Hereafter. O Possessor of Majesty and Honor, hear and respond. Allah is the Greatest, the Most Great. O Allah, Light of the heavens and the earth."
Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd said:
"Lord of the heavens and the earth."
"Allah is the Greatest, the Most Great. Allah is enough for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Allah is the Greatest, the Most Great."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ finished the prayer with the salām, he would say:

"O Allah, forgive me what I have sent forward and what I have left behind, what I have done in secret and what I have done openly, what I have done excessively, and what You know better than I. You are the One who brings forward and You are the One who puts back. There is no god but You."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ liked to supplicate three times and seek forgiveness three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They were with the Prophet ﷺ as they were climbing a mountain pass, and each time a man reached the top of the pass he would call out, "There is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest."
The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"You are not calling upon someone deaf or absent." Then he said:
"O ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays." Then he mentioned the rest with similar meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do not invoke against yourselves, do not invoke against your children, do not invoke against your servants, and do not invoke against your wealth, lest you coincide with an hour from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in which something is asked of Him and He grants it to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Pray for me and for my husband." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"May Allah bless you and your husband."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ feared a people, he would say:
"O Allah, we place You against their throats, and we seek refuge in You from their evils."
label: machine translation

segments_en: You recite this verse:

"...after any bequest you may have made or any debt." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that a debt is to be settled before a bequest, and that full siblings (children of the same mother and father) inherit from one another, to the exclusion of half-siblings through the father only: a man inherits from his full brother, but not from his brother by his father alone.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any man who commits fornication with a free woman or a slave woman, the child is a child of fornication; he does not inherit and none inherits from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Nothing increases lifespan except righteousness, and nothing repels the decree except supplication, and a man is indeed deprived of provision because of a sin he commits."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ often used to say:
"O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, we believe in you and in what you have brought; do you fear for us?" He said:
"Yes. Hearts are between two of the fingers of Allah; He turns them however He wills."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"No servant truly believes until he believes in four things: he bears witness that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah, whom He sent with the truth; and he believes in death, and in the resurrection after death, and he believes in the divine decree."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Two groups of my Ummah have no share in Islam: the Murjiʾah and the Qadariyyah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to him and said, "So-and-so sends you greetings of peace."

He said to him, "It has reached me that he has introduced an innovation. If he has indeed introduced an innovation, then do not convey my greetings of peace to him, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'In this Ummah' or 'in my Ummah'—the narrator was unsure—'there will be swallowing by the earth, or transformation [into animals], or showers of stones, upon the people of the Qadar.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar addressed us at al-Jābiyah and said, "O people, I stand among you as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us, and he said:

'I advise you to follow my Companions, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. Then lying will spread, until a man will swear without being asked to swear, and a witness will testify without being asked to testify. Beware! No man is alone with a woman except that Satan is the third of them. Hold to the community and beware of division, for Satan is with the one, and he is farther from two. Whoever wishes for the middle of Paradise, let him hold to the community. Whoever is pleased by his good deeds and distressed by his bad deeds, that is the believer.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, the Hour will not come until you kill your leader, strike one another with your swords, and the worst of you inherit your worldly affairs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ mentioned the army that would be swallowed up by the earth. Umm Salamah said, "O Messenger of Allah, perhaps there will be among them someone who was compelled?" He said:
"They will be resurrected according to their intentions."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"At the end of this Ummah there will be swallowing by the earth, transformation, and showers of stones."
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, will we be destroyed while the righteous are among us?" He said:
"Yes, when corruption becomes widespread."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib came here to Basrah, he entered upon my father and said, "O Abū Muslim, will you not help me against these people?" He said, "Yes."
He said: So he called a servant girl of his and said, "O girl, bring out my sword."

He said: She brought it out, and he drew about a handspan of it, and it was wood. He said, "My dear friend and your cousin ﷺ made a covenant with me that when there is strife among the Muslims, I should make a sword of wood. So if you wish, I will go out with you."
He said, "I have no need of you or of your sword."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to us:
"The Dajjāl will emerge from a land in the east called Khurāsān. He will be followed by people whose faces are like layered shields."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not fitting for a believer to humiliate himself."
They said, "How does he humiliate himself?" He said:
"By exposing himself to trials that he cannot bear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever claims to have had a dream that he did not have will be required on the Day of Resurrection to tie together two grains of barley, and he will never be able to tie them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Hajj alone (ifrād).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān performed Hajj alone (ifrād).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"At your service with ʿUmrah and Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was a Christian man and then I accepted Islam, so I declared the intention for Hajj and ʿUmrah together. Salmān ibn Rabīʿah and Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān heard me while I was reciting the call for both of them together at al-Qādisiyyah, and they said, "This man is more astray than his camel." It was as if they had placed a mountain upon me with their words. So I came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and mentioned that to him. He turned to the two men and rebuked them, then turned to me and said, "You have been guided to the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ; you have been guided to the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ."
Hishām said in his narration: Shaqīq said:
Many times Masrūq and I went to ask him about it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined Hajj and ʿUmrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He arrived combining Hajj and ʿUmrah, so he circled the House seven times and walked between Ṣafā and Marwah, then said, "This is how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions set out, and we entered the state of iḥrām for Hajj. When we arrived in Makkah, he said:
"Make your Hajj an ʿUmrah."
The people said, "O Messenger of Allah, we have already entered iḥrām for Hajj, so how can we make it an ʿUmrah?" He said:
"Look at what I have commanded you and do it."
They answered him back, so he became angry and went until he entered upon ʿĀʾishah angry. She saw the anger in his face and said, "Who has angered you? May Allah anger him!" He said:
"Why should I not be angry when I command something and it is not followed?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never performed ʿUmrah except in Dhū al-Qaʿdah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever enters iḥrām for ʿUmrah from Bayt al-Maqdis, it will be an expiation for the sins before it."
She said: So I set out from there, meaning from Bayt al-Maqdis, for ʿUmrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to pray the five prayers at Minā, then inform them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"All of ʿArafah is a place of standing, but move away from the bottom of ʿUranah. All of Muzdalifah is a place of standing, but move away from the bottom of Muḥassir. All of Minā is a place of sacrifice, except what is behind al-ʿAqabah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the evening of ʿArafah the Prophet ﷺ supplicated for his nation for forgiveness, and was answered: "I have forgiven them, except the wrongdoer, for I will take from him on behalf of the wronged." He said:
"O my Lord, if You wish, You could give the wronged person Paradise and forgive the wrongdoer."
He was not answered that evening. Then when morning came at Muzdalifah, he repeated the supplication and was answered with what he had asked.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed.
Or he said: he smiled.
Abū Bakr and ʿUmar said to him, "May my father and mother be your ransom! This is an hour in which you did not usually laugh, so what made you laugh? May Allah keep you smiling." He said:

"When the enemy of Allah, Iblīs, learned that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had answered my supplication and forgiven my nation, he took dust and began throwing it on his head, calling out for woe and destruction. What I saw of his distress made me laugh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Quraysh said, "We are the residents of the House; we do not go beyond the Sacred Precinct."
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: {Then depart from where the people depart.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the morning of Jamʿ, the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"O Bilāl, make the people be quiet," or, "make the people listen." Then he said:

"Allah has been gracious to you in this gathering of yours: He has given the sinner among you to the one who does good, and has given the one who does good what he asked. Depart in the name of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Sacrifice at Jamrat al-ʿAqabah. He went down into the middle of the valley and threw seven pebbles at the Jamrah, saying the takbīr with each pebble, then he left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He threw the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah and did not stand at it, and he mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ did likewise.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and with us were women and children. We recited the talbiyah on behalf of the children and threw the pebbles for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, why did you make supplication three times for those who shave their heads and once for those who shorten their hair?" He said:
"Because they did not doubt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out in the middle of the night and prayed in the mosque, and some men prayed behind him. In the morning the people were talking about it, and more people gathered. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on the second night and they prayed with him. In the morning the people spoke of it again, and the people of the mosque increased on the third night. He went out and they prayed with him. When the fourth night came, the mosque could not hold its people, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not come out to them, so some of the men began to call out, "Prayer!"
But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not come out to them until he came out for the Fajr prayer. When he had finished the Fajr prayer, he turned to the people, recited the testimony of faith, and said:
"To proceed: your situation last night was not hidden from me, but I feared that the night prayer would be made obligatory upon you and that you would be unable to perform it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That when they came to Medina from Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah after the killing of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both,
al-Miswar ibn Makhramah met him and said to him, "Do you have any need of me that you would command me to fulfil?" He said: I said to him, "No."

He said to him, "Will you give me the sword of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? For I fear that the people will overpower you and take it. By Allah, if you give it to me, no one will ever get to it as long as I live. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib proposed to the daughter of Abū Jahl while married to Fāṭimah, and I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ speaking to the people about that from this pulpit of his, and I had reached puberty at that time. He said:
'Fāṭimah is part of me, and I fear that she will be tried in her religion.'
He said: Then he mentioned a son-in-law of his from Banū ʿAbd Shams, and praised him for his relationship by marriage with him, and did so well. He said:

'He spoke to me and was truthful with me, and he promised me and fulfilled his promise to me. I do not make lawful what is forbidden, nor forbid what is lawful. But by Allah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah and the daughter of the enemy of Allah will never be together in one place.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to go out to the prayer ground on the day of Fiṭr and the day of Aḍḥā.
The first thing he began with was the prayer, and then he would turn away,
and stand facing the people,
while the people remained seated in their rows.
He would admonish them, counsel them, and instruct them.
If he wanted to dispatch an expedition, he would do so,
or if he wanted to command something, he would command it, and then he would depart.
Abū Saʿīd said: The people continued in that way until I went out with Marwān, who was the governor of Medina, on a day of Aḍḥā or Fiṭr.
When we came to the prayer ground, there was a pulpit that Kathīr ibn al-Ṣalt had built.
Marwān wanted to climb it before the prayer,
so I pulled him by his garment, but he pulled me back and ascended,
and he delivered the sermon before the prayer.
I said to him, "By Allah, you have changed it!"
He said, "Abū Saʿīd,
what you know is gone."
I said, "What I know, by Allah, is better than what I do not know."
He said, "The people did not used to sit for us after the prayer, so I put the sermon before the prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm ʿAṭiyyah never mentioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ without saying, "May I be sacrificed for him."
I said, "Did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say such and such?" She said, "Yes, may I be sacrificed for him." He said:

"Let the young women, those who are secluded in their quarters, and the menstruating women go out, so that they may witness the good and the supplication of the Muslims, but let the menstruating women keep away from the place of prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to slaughter his sacrificial animal at the prayer ground, and Ibn ʿUmar used to do the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I attended the Aḍḥā with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. As soon as he had prayed and finished his prayer, he gave the salutation of peace, and he saw the meat of sacrificial animals that had been slaughtered before he finished his prayer. He said:
"Whoever slaughtered his sacrificial animal before praying, or before we prayed, let him slaughter another in its place, and whoever has not yet slaughtered, let him slaughter in the name of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ went out to the ʿĪd prayer, he would return by a different road from the one he had taken.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He went out on the day of an ʿĪd and did not pray before it or after it, and he mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ had done so.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
asked the Prophet ﷺ while I was between him and the questioner. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, how is the night prayer?" He said:
"Two by two, and if you fear the dawn, pray one rakʿah, and make the last of your prayer an odd number (witr)."

Then a man asked him at the turn of the year, while I was in the same place in relation to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I do not know whether he was the same man or another man, and he said the same to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We entered the state of ihram with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for Hajj alone, not mixing it with ʿUmrah. We arrived in Makkah on the fourth night of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. When we had circumambulated the House and walked between Ṣafā and Marwah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to make it an ʿUmrah and to become lawful for our wives.
So we said among ourselves, "There are only five days between us and ʿArafah, and we are to go out to it with our private parts dripping semen?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I am the most righteous and truthful of you, and were it not for the sacrificial animal I would have come out of ihram."
Then Surāqah ibn Mālik said, "Is this enjoyment [of combining ʿUmrah with Hajj] for this year of ours only, or is it forever?" He said:
"No, rather it is forever, for all time."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with ʿAlī when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to Yemen. He said: I obtained some ounces [of silver] with him. When ʿAlī came back from Yemen to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he found Fāṭimah, may Allah be pleased with her, wearing dyed garments and having perfumed the house with fragrance. She said, "What is the matter with you? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has commanded his Companions and they have come out of ihram." He said: I said to her, "I have declared my intention with the same declaration as the Prophet ﷺ."
He said: Then I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to me, "What did you do?"
He said: I said, "I declared the same intention as the Prophet ﷺ." He said:
"Then I have driven the sacrificial animals and combined [Hajj and ʿUmrah]."
He said: Then he said to me:
"Slaughter sixty-seven or sixty-six of the camels, and keep thirty-three or thirty-four for yourself, and keep for me a piece from each camel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ṣubayy ibn Maʿbad said: I was a Christian Bedouin and I became Muslim. I was eager for jihad, but I found Hajj and ʿUmrah written [obligatory] upon me. So I went to a man of my clan called Hudhaym ibn ʿAbdullāh and asked him. He said, "Combine them both, then sacrifice whatever animal is easily available." So I declared my intention for both. When I reached al-ʿUdhayb, Salmān ibn Rabīʿah and Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān met me while I was reciting the talbiyah for both, and one of them said to the other, "This man is no better informed than his camel."

So I went to ʿUmar and said, "Commander of the Faithful, I became Muslim and I was eager for jihad, but I found Hajj and ʿUmrah written upon me. So I went to Hudhaym ibn ʿAbdullāh and said, 'Friend, I found Hajj and ʿUmrah written upon me.'

He said, 'Combine them both, then sacrifice whatever animal is easily available.' So I declared my intention for both. When we reached al-ʿUdhayb, Salmān ibn Rabīʿah and Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān met me, and one of them said to the other, 'This man is no better informed than his camel.'"
ʿUmar said, "You have been guided to the Sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ heard a man saying, "Labbayk on behalf of Shubrumah." He said, "Who is Shubrumah?"
He said, "A brother of mine," or "a relative of mine." He said:
"Have you performed Hajj for yourself?" He said, "No." He said:
"Perform Hajj for yourself, then perform Hajj for Shubrumah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as pilgrims, until we were at al-ʿArj, where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped and we stopped. ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, sat beside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I sat beside my father. The baggage camel of Abū Bakr and that of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were one and the same, in the charge of a servant of Abū Bakr. Abū Bakr sat waiting for him to appear. He appeared without his camel. [Abū Bakr] said, "Where is your camel?" He said, "I lost it last night."
He said: Abū Bakr said, "One camel, and you lose it?" And he began to strike him, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled and said:
"Look at this man in ihram, what he is doing!"
Ibn Abī Razmah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did no more than say:
"Look at this man in ihram, what he is doing!" and smile.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Why the brisk walking today, and the uncovering of the shoulders,
when Allah has firmly established Islam and driven out disbelief and its people? Even so, we will not abandon anything we used to do in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Circumambulating the House, walking between Ṣafā and Marwah, and stoning the Jamarāt have only been prescribed for establishing the remembrance of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ went out on the expedition of Badr, she said: I said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to go on the expedition with you, so that I may nurse your sick, perhaps Allah will grant me martyrdom." He said: "
Stay in your house, for Allah the Exalted will grant you martyrdom."
He said: So she used to be called the Martyr.

He said: She had learned the Qur'an, and she asked permission of the Prophet ﷺ to appoint a muezzin in her house, and he permitted her. He said: She had made a mudabbar of her male slave and her female slave [freeing them upon her death]. They came upon her at night and smothered her with a sheet of hers until she died, and then they fled. In the morning ʿUmar stood among the people and said: Whoever has any knowledge of these two, or has seen them, let him bring them. Then he ordered that they be crucified, and they were the first to be crucified in Medina.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: "
Three people from whom Allah does not accept prayer: one who leads a people in prayer while they dislike him, and a man who comes to the prayer late (dibār),"
and dibār means that he comes to it after it has passed him by, "
and a man who enslaves his freed slave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Jihad is obligatory upon you under every ruler, whether righteous or wicked,
and prayer is obligatory upon you behind every Muslim, whether righteous or wicked, even if he commits major sins,
and prayer is obligatory upon every Muslim, whether righteous or wicked, even if he commits major sins."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ appointed Ibn Umm Maktūm as his deputy to lead the people in prayer, and he was blind.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥudhayfah led the people in prayer

in al-Madāʾin while standing on a raised platform, so Abū Masʿūd took hold of his shirt and pulled him. When he had finished his prayer, he said: "Did you not know that they used to forbid that?" He said: "Yes, I remembered when you pulled me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was with ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir in al-Madāʾin when the prayer was called. ʿAmmār went forward and stood on a raised platform to pray while the people were below him. Ḥudhayfah went forward, took hold of his hands, and ʿAmmār followed him until Ḥudhayfah brought him down. When ʿAmmār finished his prayer, Ḥudhayfah said to him: "Did you not hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
When a man leads people in prayer, he should not stand in a place higher than where they stand,"
or words to that effect?" ʿAmmār said: "For that reason I followed you when you took hold of my hands."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rode a horse in Medina and it threw him onto the trunk of a palm tree, and his foot was dislocated. We came to visit him and found him in an upper room of ʿĀʾishah, praying voluntarily while sitting. He said: We stood behind him, and he did not say anything to us. Then we came to him another time to visit him, and he prayed the obligatory prayer sitting. We stood behind him, and he gestured to us, so we sat.
He said: When he finished the prayer, he said: "
When the imam prays sitting, pray sitting; and when the imam prays standing, pray standing. And do not do as the Persians do with their great men."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the descendants of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, on the authority of Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr,
that he used to lead them in prayer. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to visit him, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, our imam is sick." He said: "
When he prays sitting, pray sitting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon Umm Ḥarām, and they brought him ghee and dates. He said: "
Return this to its container and this to its waterskin, for I am fasting."
Then he stood and led us in two rakʿahs of voluntary prayer, and Umm Sulaym and Umm Ḥarām stood behind us.
Thābit said: I only know that he said: He made me stand on his right, on a mat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led him and a woman of theirs in prayer; he placed him on his right and the woman behind that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad asked permission to enter upon ʿAbdullāh, and we had been sitting at his door for a long time. The slave girl came out and asked permission for them, and he permitted them. Then he stood and prayed, with me between him and [them]. Then he said: "This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When the imam has completed the prayer and sat, and then breaks his wudūʾ before he speaks, his prayer is complete, and so is the prayer of whoever is behind him and has completed the prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ urged them to pray and forbade them from leaving before he left the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a man who hunts; may I pray in a single shirt?" He said: "
Yes, and fasten it, even with a thorn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh led us in prayer in a shirt, with no cloak upon him. When he finished, he said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray in a shirt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The first case of li'ān (mutual imprecation) in Islam was that Hilāl ibn Umayyah accused Sharīk ibn Saḥmā' of [adultery] with his wife. He came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of that, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"Four witnesses, or else the prescribed punishment will be on your back."

He repeated this to him several times. Hilāl said to him, "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows that I am truthful, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will surely send down to you something that will free my back from the lashing."

While they were in that state, the verse of li'ān was revealed to him: {And those who accuse their wives...} to the end of the verse. He called Hilāl, who testified four times by Allah that he was among the truthful, and the fifth time [he invoked] that the curse of Allah be upon him if he was among the liars. Then the woman was called, and she testified four times by Allah that he was among the liars. When it came to the fourth or the fifth, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Stop her, for it is binding [if she swears]."
She hesitated and held back, so that we thought she would confess. Then she said, "I will not disgrace my people for the rest of the days."
So she went on with the oath. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Watch her. If she gives birth to him white, with straight hair, and with eyes lined [with long lashes], then he is Hilāl ibn Umayyah's; but if she gives birth to him brown, with curly hair, of medium build, and with thin calves, then he is Sharīk ibn Saḥmā's."
She gave birth to him brown, with curly hair, of medium build, and with thin calves. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Had it not been for what has already been decreed in the Book of Allah, I would have had a matter to deal with concerning her."
The Shaykh said: Al-qaḍī' means having long eyelashes, [eyes] neither wide open nor bulging. And Allah, Glorified and Exalted, knows best.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to give his wives the choice, he began with me and said:
