"I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm if you do not hurry until you consult your parents."
She said: He knew that my parents would never have commanded me to part from him. She said: Then he said:

"Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: {O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will give you provision and release you with a gracious release. But if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter, then indeed Allah has prepared for the doers of good among you a great reward.}" She said: I said, "About what in this should I consult my parents? I desire Allah, His Messenger, and the home of the Hereafter."
She said: Then the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did the same as I did.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Az-Zuhrī was asked, "How is divorce done in accordance with the waiting period?" He said: Sālim ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar informed me that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: I divorced my wife during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while she was menstruating.
ʿUmar mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry about it and said:

"Let him take her back, then keep her until she has menstruated a period and become pure. If it then occurs to him to divorce her while she is pure, before touching her, that is the divorce in accordance with the waiting period, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed."
ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: So I took her back, and the divorce I had pronounced was counted for her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The one who recites the Qur'an and is proficient in it will be with the noble and obedient scribes [angels]; and the one who recites it"—Hishām said, "and it is difficult for him," and Shuʿbah said, "and it is hard on him"—"will have two rewards."
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque and heard a man reciting, and he said, "Who is this?"
It was said, "This is ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays." He said:
"This man has been given one of the flutes [beautiful voices] of the family of Dāwūd."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with ʿAbdullāh when ʿUthmān met him at Minā and said, "O Abū ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, I have a need with you."
The two withdrew privately, and ʿUthmān said, "O Abū ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, would you like us to marry you to a young virgin
who would remind you of what you used to know [of your youth]?"
When ʿAbdullāh saw that he had no need for this, he motioned to me and said, "O ʿAlqamah."
I came to him as he was saying, "If you say that, then the Prophet ﷺ said to us:
'O young people, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry,
and whoever is unable, let him fast, for it is a protection for him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn wanted to devote himself to celibacy,
but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade him. Had he permitted that for him, we would have castrated ourselves.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no harm in qarāmil [hair extensions of wool or similar material].
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to my family at night, and my hands were cracked, so they perfumed me with saffron. In the morning I went to the Prophet ﷺ and greeted him with salām, but he did not return my greeting or welcome me. He said:
"Go and wash this off yourself."
So I went and washed it, then came back, though a trace of it remained on me. I greeted him, but he did not return my greeting or welcome me, and he said:
"Go and wash this off yourself."
So I went and washed it, then came and greeted him, and he returned my greeting and welcomed me, and said:
"The angels do not attend the funeral of a disbeliever for any good, nor [the presence of] one smeared with saffron, nor one in a state of major ritual impurity."
He said: He permitted the person in a state of major impurity, if he wished to sleep, eat or drink, to perform ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I perfumed myself with khalūq, with this story.
The first version is much more complete, and it mentions the washing. He said: I said to ʿUmar, "They were in a state of iḥrām?" He said: "No, the people were resident [not travelling]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah the Exalted does not accept the prayer of a man who has any khalūq [perfume] on his body."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Three [kinds of people] the angels do not approach: the carcass of a disbeliever, the one smeared with khalūq, and the one in a state of major impurity, unless he performs ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ conquered Mecca, the people of Mecca began bringing their children to him, and he would pray for blessings for them and wipe their heads. He said: I was brought to him while I was perfumed with khalūq, and he did not touch me because of the khalūq.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a trace of yellow [perfume] on him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rarely confronted a man to his face with something he disliked. When the man left, he said:
"If only you would tell this man to wash this off."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had a forelock, and my mother said to me, "Do not cut it, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pull it and take hold of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We entered upon Anas ibn Mālik, and my sister al-Mughīrah told me,
she said: You were a boy at that time and had two locks or two forelocks. He wiped your head, blessed you, and said:
"Shave these two off or cut them short, for this is the way of the Jews."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān, and ʿAbd al-Malik recited it to Abū al-Zubayr, and Abū al-Zubayr narrated it from Jābir,
who said: We used to let the mustache grow long, except during Hajj or ʿUmrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not pluck out gray hair. There is no Muslim who grows a gray hair in Islam,"
He said, from Sufyān:
"but it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection."
And he said in the narration of Yaḥyā:
"but Allah will record for him a good deed for it and erase a sin from him because of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In this report he said: My father said to him, "Show me this [swelling] on your back, for I am a physician." He said:
"Allah is the Physician. Rather, you are a gentle man; its physician is the One who created it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was asked about the dyeing of the Prophet's hair,
ﷺ, and he mentioned that he did not dye it, but Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, did dye theirs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ travelled, the last of his family he would see was Fāṭimah, and the first he would visit on his return was Fāṭimah. He returned from one of his expeditions, and she had hung a coarse cloth or curtain at her door and had adorned al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn with two silver bracelets. He came back but did not enter, and she thought that what had kept him from entering was what he had seen. So she tore down the curtain, removed the two bracelets from the boys and cut them in two between them. They went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weeping, and he took it from them and said:
"O Thawbān, take this to the family of so-and-so,"
a household in Medina.
"These are my family; I dislike that they should consume their good things in their worldly life. O Thawbān, buy Fāṭimah a necklace of ʿaṣab and two bracelets of ivory."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They searched for it but did not find it, so ʿUthmān made a ring and engraved on it:
"Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah."
He said: He used to seal with it or wear it as a ring.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Say: O Allah, guide me and keep me on the right course. And remember, by guidance, the guidance of the road, and remember, by right course, your aiming of an arrow."
He said: And he forbade me to put the ring on this finger or this one, the index and the middle finger—ʿĀṣim was unsure—and he forbade me [to wear] qassiyyah and mītharah.

Abū Burdah said: We asked ʿAlī, "What is qassiyyah?" He said: "Garments that come to us from Syria or Egypt, ribbed, with patterns like citrons." He said: "And the mītharah is something women used to make for their husbands."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out for Hajj, and there was a man who said to us, "Next to you is a town called al-Ubullah." We said, "Yes."

He said, "Who among you will guarantee for me that he will pray two or four rak'ahs for me in the mosque of al-ʿAshshār and say, 'This is for Abū Hurayrah'? I heard my beloved friend Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ say:
'Indeed, on the Day of Resurrection Allah will raise up from the mosque of al-ʿAshshār martyrs; none will stand with the martyrs of Badr except them.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Leave the Abyssinians alone as long as they leave you alone, for none will extract the treasure of the Kaʿbah except Dhū as-Suwayqatayn (the one with the two small legs) from Abyssinia."
label: machine translation

segments_en: K-F-R
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ in this hadith, he said:
"Every Muslim will read it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever hears of the Dajjāl, let him keep away from him. For by Allah, a man will come to him thinking that he is a believer, and will follow him because of the doubts he is sent with," or "because of what he is sent with of doubts." Thus he said it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I have told you about the Dajjāl so much that I feared you would not understand. The Messiah, the Dajjāl, is a short man, bow-legged, with curly hair, one-eyed, with his eye wiped out, neither protruding nor sunken. If it is made confusing for you, then know that your Lord is not one-eyed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"There is no prophet between me and him", meaning ʿĪsā, "and he will descend. When you see him, recognize him: a man of medium height, with a complexion of red and white, wearing two lightly dyed garments. His head will appear to drip even though no wetness has touched it. He will fight the people for the sake of Islam; he will break the cross, kill the pig, and abolish the jizyah. In his time Allah will destroy all religions except Islam, and He will destroy the Messiah, the Dajjāl. He will remain on earth for forty years, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the late evening prayer one night, then came out and said:

"I was kept back by a story that Tamīm ad-Dārī used to tell me about a man who was on one of the islands of the sea. He said: Suddenly I met a woman dragging her hair. I said, 'What are you?' She said, 'I am al-Jassāsah. Go to that palace.' So I went to it, and there was a man dragging his hair, chained in shackles, leaping about between heaven and earth. I said, 'Who are you?' He said, 'I am the Dajjāl. Has the Prophet of the unlettered people come forth?' I said, 'Yes.'
He said, 'Did they obey him or disobey him?' I said, 'Rather, they obeyed him.'
He said, 'That is better for them.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was announcing, "The prayer is being gathered for."
So I went out and prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he sat on the pulpit, smiling, and said:
"Let every person remain in his place of prayer." Then he said:
"Do you know why I have gathered you?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:

"I have not gathered you out of fear or desire, but I have gathered you because Tamīm ad-Dārī was a Christian man who came, pledged allegiance, and accepted Islam, and he told me a story that agrees with what I told you about the Dajjāl. He told me that he sailed in a sea-going ship with thirty men of Lakhm and Judhām, and the waves tossed them about for a month in the sea. Then they came ashore at an island at sunset, and sat in the small boats of the ship. They entered the island and a beast with thick hair met them. They said, 'Woe to you, what are you?' It said, 'I am al-Jassāsah. Go to this man in this monastery, for he is eager to hear news of you.'

He said: When she named a man to us, we feared that she might be a female devil. So we hurried until we entered the monastery, and there was the largest human being we had ever seen in build, and the most firmly bound, with his hands tied to his neck."

Then he mentioned the hadith: he asked them about the palm trees of Baysān, the spring of Zughar, and the unlettered Prophet. He said, "I am the Messiah, and I am about to be given permission to go out." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"He is in the Sea of Syria or the Sea of Yemen. No, rather from the direction of the East; he is from the East."
Twice, and he pointed with his hand toward the East. She said, "I memorized this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." And he narrated the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed the Zuhr prayer, then ascended the pulpit, and he did not ascend it before that day except on Friday. Then he mentioned this story.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the Witr prayer with three rakʿahs. In the first he would recite {Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High}, in the second {Say: O disbelievers}, and in the third {Say: He is Allah, the One}. He would make the qunūt before bowing, and when he finished he would say:
"Glory be to the King, the Most Holy."
[He said it] three times, prolonging [his voice] on the last of them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he got up during the night and cleaned his teeth with the siwāk, then prayed two rakʿahs, then slept, then got up and cleaned his teeth with the siwāk and performed ablution and prayed two rakʿahs, until he had prayed six; then he prayed Witr with three and prayed two rakʿahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke up and cleaned his teeth with the siwāk, and he related the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray Witr with thirteen rakʿahs. When he grew old and weak, he prayed Witr with nine.
ʿUmārah ibn ʿUmayr differed with him, and narrated it from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from ʿĀʾishah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray nine rakʿahs at night. When he grew old and heavy, he prayed seven.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Witr is seven; and no fewer than five." I mentioned that to Ibrāhīm, and he said, "From whom did he relate it?" I said, "I do not know."
Al-Ḥakam said: Then I performed Hajj and met Miqsam, and I asked him, "From whom?" He said, "From the trustworthy one, from ʿĀʾishah and from Maymūnah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
came to Ibn ʿAbbās and asked him about the Witr of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said, "Shall I not guide you, or: shall I not inform you, of the most knowledgeable of the people of the earth about the Witr of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?"
I said, "Who is that?" He said, "ʿĀʾishah."
So we went to her, greeted her with salām, and entered, and we asked her. I said, "Inform me about the Witr of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

She said: We used to prepare his siwāk and his water for ablution for him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would raise him whenever He willed to raise him during the night. He would use the siwāk and perform ablution, then pray nine rakʿahs, not sitting during them except in the eighth. He would praise Allah, remember Him, and supplicate, then rise without giving the salām. Then he would pray the ninth, then sit, praise Allah, remember Him, and supplicate, then give the salām aloud enough for us to hear. Then he would pray two rakʿahs while sitting. That is eleven rakʿahs, my son. Then when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ grew old and put on flesh, he prayed Witr with seven, then prayed two rakʿahs while sitting after giving the salām. That is nine, my son. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he prayed a prayer, loved to keep to it regularly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to prepare for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ his siwāk and his water for ablution, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would raise him whenever He willed to raise him during the night. He would use the siwāk, perform ablution, and pray nine rakʿahs, not sitting during them except at the eighth. He would praise Allah, send blessings upon His Prophet ﷺ, and supplicate between them, and he would not give the salām. Then he would pray the ninth and sit, and she mentioned a similar word, and he would praise Allah, send blessings upon His Prophet ﷺ, and supplicate, then give the salām aloud enough for us to hear. Then he would pray two rakʿahs while sitting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he came as part of a delegation to the Mother of the Believers, ʿĀʾishah, and asked her about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: He used to pray eight rakʿahs during the night and pray Witr with the ninth, and he would pray two rakʿahs while sitting. [Abridged.]
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Abū Mūsā

was between Makkah and Madinah, and he prayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer with two rakʿahs. Then he stood and prayed one rakʿah with which he made it Witr, reciting in it a hundred verses from [Sūrat] an-Nisāʾ. Then he said: I have not failed to place my feet where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed his feet, and I recite what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [This is] mursal.
ʿAṭāʾ ibn as-Sāʾib also narrated it from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abzā, from his father.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray Witr with {Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High}. Shabābah differed with the two of them, and narrated it from Shuʿbah, from Qatādah, from Zurārah ibn Awfā, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ used to pray Witr. And he related the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Shurayḥ al-Ḥaḍramī
was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"That is a man who does not use the Qurʾān as a pillow."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever has a prayer that he [regularly] prays at night, then sleep overcomes him and he misses it, that will be a charity (ṣadaqah) which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestows upon him, and the reward of his prayer will be written for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Narrated] as mawqūf.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever misses his nightly portion [of prayer or recitation] should recite it in a prayer before Ẓuhr, for it is equal to the night prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He had been present at Badr with the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I meet a disbeliever and we fight,
and he strikes my hand with the sword and cuts it off,
then takes refuge behind a tree and says, 'I have submitted to Allah,'
may I kill him after he has said it?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not kill him."
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, he cut off one of my hands,
and then said this after he had cut it off. May I kill him?" He said: "Do not kill him,
for if you kill him, he will be in the position you were in before you killed him,
and you will be in the position he was in before he said the words he said."
Ḥabīb ibn Abī ʿAmrah said, from Saʿīd,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: The Prophet ﷺ said to al-Miqdād:"
"If a believing man conceals his faith among a disbelieving people, then he reveals his faith, and you kill him,
you are just like that, for you used to conceal your faith in Makkah before."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Jews of Banū al-Naḍīr and Qurayẓah

fought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ expelled Banū al-Naḍīr and let Qurayẓah remain and showed them favor, until Qurayẓah fought after that, so their men were killed and their women, children, and wealth were divided among the Muslims, except for some of them who joined the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who granted them safety, and they accepted Islam. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ expelled all the Jews of Medina: Banū Qaynuqāʿ, who were the people of ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām, the Jews of Banū Ḥārithah, and every Jew who was in Medina.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said: "Where will I be, O
Messenger of Allah, if I am killed?" He said: "In Paradise."
So he threw down some dates that were in his hand, then fought until he was killed.
In the narration of Suwayd: A man said to the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Uḥud
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made supplication (qunūt) for a month after bowing in the dawn prayer, invoking against Riʿl and Dhakwān, and saying:"
"ʿUṣayyah disobeyed Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me at the time of al-Ḥudaybiyah while I was lighting a fire under a pot of mine—al-Qawārīrī said: a pot for me,
and Abū al-Rabīʿ said: a stone pot of mine—and lice were falling over my face. He said:"
"Do the vermin of your head bother you?"
I said: "Yes." He said:"
"Then shave, and fast three days, or feed six poor people, or offer a sacrifice."
Ayyūb said: I do not know which of these he began with.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Khaybar we got some donkeys outside the village and cooked them. Then the caller of the Prophet ﷺ announced that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had forbidden the meat of donkeys, and said: "Overturn the pots with what is in them." So we overturned them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the campaign of Khaybar the Prophet ﷺ commanded us to throw away the meat of domestic donkeys, raw and cooked,
and after that he did not command us to eat it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered some of the Anṣār and said:"
"Come here. Is there anyone among you who is not one of you?"
They said: "No, except a son of our sister." The Prophet ﷺ said:"
"The son of a people's sister is one of them." Then he said:"

"The Quraysh are still close to the time of ignorance and affliction, and I wished to console them and win their hearts. Are you not pleased that the people go back with worldly goods while you go back to your homes with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" They said: "Yes."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:"
"If the people were to take one valley or mountain path, and the Anṣār were to take another valley or mountain path, I would take the valley of the Anṣār or their path."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Yemen, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, there are drinks there. What may I drink and what should I leave?" He said: "What are they?"
I said: "Al-bitʿ and al-mizr." He said:"
"What are al-bitʿ and al-mizr?"
I said: "Al-bitʿ is a fermented drink of honey, and al-mizr is a fermented drink of corn."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:"
"Do not drink any intoxicant, for I have forbidden every intoxicant."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Mūsā said: News of the emigration of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached us while we were in Yemen, so we set out to him as emigrants, I and two brothers of mine, I being the youngest of them; one was Abū Burdah and the other Abū Ruhm, along with some—or he said fifty-three or fifty-two—men of my people. He said: We boarded a ship, and our ship cast us ashore at the Negus in Abyssinia. There we met Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib and his companions with him. Jaʿfar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us here and commanded us to stay, so stay with us.

So we stayed with him until we all came [to Madinah]. He said: We met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ just when he had conquered Khaybar, and he gave us a share—or he said he gave us something from it. He did not apportion anything from it to anyone who was absent from the conquest of Khaybar except those who had been present with him, apart from the people of our ship who were with Jaʿfar and his companions; he apportioned to them along with the rest. He said: Some of the people used to say to us—meaning the people of the ship—We preceded you in emigration.

He said: Then Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays—who was among those who came with us—went in to visit Ḥafṣah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ. She had emigrated to the Negus among those who emigrated to him. Then ʿUmar came in to Ḥafṣah while Asmāʾ was with her, and when ʿUmar saw Asmāʾ he said: Who is this? She said: Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays.
ʿUmar said: The Abyssinian one? The sea-voyager? Asmāʾ said: Yes.
ʿUmar said: We preceded you in emigration, so we have a greater right to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than you.

She became angry and said a word: You lie, ʿUmar! Never, by Allah! You were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who fed your hungry and admonished your ignorant, while we were in the land of the distant and the hateful in Abyssinia, and that was for the sake of Allah and His Messenger. By Allah, I will not eat any food nor drink any drink until I mention what you said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We were harmed and in fear, and I will mention that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask him. By Allah, I will not lie, nor deviate, nor add to that.
He said: When the Prophet ﷺ came, she said: O Prophet of Allah, ʿUmar said such and such.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He is not more deserving of me than you. He and his companions have one emigration, but you, the people of the ship, have two emigrations."

She said: I saw Abū Mūsā and the people of the ship coming to me in groups, asking me about this hadith. Nothing in the world was more joyful to them, or greater in their eyes, than what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said to them.
Abū Burdah said: Asmāʾ said: I saw Abū Mūsā asking me to repeat this hadith to him again and again.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"I recognize the voices of the company of the Ashʿarīs by the Qurʾān,
when they enter at night,
and I recognize their dwellings from their voices reciting the Qurʾān at night,
even though I did not see their dwellings when they stopped by day. Among them is Ḥakīm,
who, when he meets the cavalry—or he said the enemy—says to them: My companions command you to wait for them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ in command of a expedition from Madinah toward Najd. Abān ibn Saʿīd and his companions came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Khaybar after he had conquered it, and the girths of their horses were made of palm fiber. Abān said: Apportion to us, O Messenger of Allah.
Abū Hurayrah said: I said: Do not apportion to them, O Messenger of Allah.
Abān said: You say that, O badger, coming down upon us from the peak of Ḍalāl! Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Sit down, O Abān."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not apportion anything to them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about salam (advance payment) for date palms.
He said: The Prophet ﷺ forbade the sale of date palms
until [their fruit] can be eaten and until it can be weighed.
A man asked, "And what is it that is weighed?" A man beside him said, "Until it is harvested and stored."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah,
I have two neighbors; to which of them should I give a gift?" He said,
"To the one whose door is nearer to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah did not send any prophet except that he was a shepherd of sheep."
His Companions said to him, "And you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Yes, I used to tend them for the people of Makkah in exchange for qīrāṭs."
Suwayd said: He means for each sheep, one qīrāṭ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ set out on a journey they were making, until they stopped at one of the Arab tribes and asked them for hospitality.
They refused to host them.
Then the chief of that tribe was stung.
They tried every remedy for him, but nothing helped him.
Some of them said, "If only you would go to those people who stopped here; perhaps one of them has something." So they went to them
and said, "O group,
our chief has been stung,
and we have tried everything for him, but nothing has helped him.
Does any of you have anything?" One of them said, "Yes, by Allah, I can perform ruqyah,
but by Allah, we asked you for hospitality and you did not host us,
so I will not perform ruqyah for you unless you give us a payment."
They agreed with them on a flock of sheep.
He went and began to spit on him and recite, {Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds}, and it was as if he were released from a shackle,
and he walked off with nothing wrong with him.
He said: So they paid them their agreed payment,
and some of them said, "Divide it."
But the one who had performed the ruqyah said, "Do not do so,
until we come to the Prophet ﷺ and tell him what happened,
and see what he commands us."
So they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him, and he said:
"How did you know that it is a ruqyah?" Then he said, "You did right. Divide [it] and give me a share along with you."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ called a boy who was a cupper, and he cupped him,
and he ordered that he be given a ṣāʿ or two ṣāʿs,
or a mudd or two mudds,
and he spoke to [his master] about him, so he reduced his daily fixed payment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Rāfiʿ, who is Ibn Khadīj, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the earnings of a slave woman until it is known where it comes from.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding the saying of Allah {And to those with whom your oaths have made a pledge, give them their share}, he said: When the Emigrants came to Madinah, the Anṣār would inherit from them instead of their own blood relatives, because of the brotherhood the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had established between them. When this verse was revealed, {And for each We have made heirs of what [parents and relatives] leave}, he said: It abrogated it, {And to those with whom your oaths have made a pledge, give them their share}, meaning support, sincere advice, and aid; and a bequest may be made for him, while inheritance has gone.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas ibn Mālik was asked, "Has it reached you that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'There is no alliance in Islam'?"
Anas said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made an alliance between Quraysh and the Anṣār in my house."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"If the wealth of Bahrain comes, I will give you this much, and this much, and this much," three times.

The wealth of Bahrain did not arrive until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had passed away. When it came to Abū Bakr, he ordered a caller to announce: Whoever is owed a debt or a promise by the Prophet ﷺ, let him come to me.
Jābir said: So I went to Abū Bakr
and told him that the Prophet ﷺ had said to me:
"If the wealth of Bahrain comes, I will give you this much, and this much, and this much," three times. He said: So he gave me.
Jābir said: Later I met Abū Bakr and asked him, but he did not give me.
Then I came to him, but he did not give me.
Then I came to him a third time, but he did not give me.
So I said to him, "I came to you and you did not give me,
then I came to you and you did not give me,
then I came to you and you did not give me,
so either give me,
or you are being stingy with me."
He said, "Did you say 'You are being stingy with me'? And what disease is worse than stinginess?" He said it three times. "Each time I held back from you, it was only because I intended to give you."
And from ʿAmr, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh say: I came to him,
and Abū Bakr said to me, "Count it."
So I counted it and found it to be five hundred,
and he said, "Take twice that amount."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"My Basin is a month's journey across, and its corners are equal. Its water is whiter than silver, its fragrance is better than musk, and its cups are like the stars of the sky. Whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty afterward."
He said: And Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I will be at the Basin until I see who among you comes to me, and some people will be taken away from me. I will say: 'My Lord, they are from me and from my Ummah.'
It will be said: 'Did you not know what they did after you? By Allah, they kept turning back on their heels after you.'"
He said: Ibn Abī Mulaykah used to say: O Allah, we seek refuge with You from turning back on our heels or from being tried and turned away from our religion.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Rāfiʿ, the freed slave of Umm Salamah, [narrated] from Umm Salamah,

the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that she said: I used to hear people mention the Basin, but I had not heard that from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then one day, while the girl was combing my hair, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "O people!"
I said to the girl: Move away from me.
She said: He only called the men; he did not call the women.
I said: I am one of the people.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I will be your forerunner at the Basin, so let none of you come to me and then be driven away from me as a stray camel is driven away. I will say: 'Why is this?' It will be said: 'You do not know what they introduced after you.' So I will say: 'Away, away!'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Salamah used to relate that she heard the Prophet ﷺ say on the pulpit, while she was having her hair combed: "O people!"
She said to the woman who was combing her hair: Hold back from my head.
[This is] like the hadith of Bukayr from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbbās.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I will be your forerunner at the Basin, and I will surely contend for certain people, and then I will be overpowered concerning them. I will say: 'My Lord, my Companions! My Companions!'
It will be said: 'You do not know what they introduced after you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"I will be at the far end of my Basin, driving people away from it for the people of Yemen. I will strike with my staff until the water flows over them."
He was asked about its width, and he said:
"From where I stand to ʿUmān."
And he was asked about its drink, and he said:
"It is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Two spouts pour into it, supplying it from Paradise, one of gold and the other of silver."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, the hadith of the Basin. I said to Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād: This is a hadith I heard from Abū ʿAwānah. He said: I also heard it from Shuʿbah. I said: Look into it for me. So he looked into it for me and then narrated it to me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

asked the Prophet ﷺ for a flock of sheep between two mountains, and he gave it to him. The man went to his people and said: O my people, accept Islam! By Allah, Muhammad gives such gifts that he does not fear poverty.
Anas said: A man might accept Islam wanting nothing but this world, but he would not remain so until Islam became dearer to him than the world and everything in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw anyone more merciful toward his family than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: Ibrāhīm was being nursed in the outskirts of Medina. He would go out, and we were with him, and he would enter the house, which was full of smoke, for his foster father was a blacksmith. He would take him, kiss him, and then return.
ʿAmr said: When Ibrāhīm died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Ibrāhīm is my son, and he died while still nursing, and he has two nurses who will complete his nursing in Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ. And Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us,
and Ibn Abī ʿUmar,
and Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdah,
they said: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr,
from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, from Jarīr,
from the Prophet ﷺ, like the hadith of al-Aʿmash.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, and he did not mention Ḥammād's words "with a good voice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had prayed the morning prayer, the servants of Medina would come with their vessels containing water. Whenever a vessel was brought, he would dip his hand into it. Sometimes they came to him on a cold morning, and he would still dip his hand into it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while the barber was shaving his head and his Companions were gathered around him; they wanted no hair to fall except into the hand of a man.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the narration of Fuḍayl ibn Shihāb, and in the narration of Jarīr, Muḥammad al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:

"A good dream is from Allah, and a bad dream is from Satan. Whoever sees a dream and dislikes something about it should spit lightly to his left and seek refuge with Allah from Satan; then it will not harm him, and he should not tell anyone about it. But if he sees a good dream, he should rejoice, and he should not tell it except to someone he loves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When time draws near.
And he narrated the hadith, without mentioning the Prophet ﷺ in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
And he inserted into the hadith the statement: "and I dislike al-ghull (shackles)."
[He continued] to the end of the passage, and he did not mention:
"The dream is one of forty-six parts of prophecy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, the same as that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The dream of a righteous man is one of forty-six parts of prophecy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Then he mentioned both hadith with their two chains of narration, the same as the hadith of Yūnus.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among the things the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say to his Companions was:
"Whoever among you sees a dream, let him relate it, and I will interpret it for him."
He said: A man came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I saw a canopy," and so on, like their hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Mālik

used to present ghee to the Prophet ﷺ in a small skin container of hers. Her sons would come and ask for something to eat with their bread, and they had nothing, so she would go to the container in which she used to present gifts to the Prophet ﷺ and find ghee in it. It kept supplying the seasoning for her household until she squeezed it out. Then she came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said, "Did you squeeze it out?" She said, "Yes." He said:
"If you had left it, it would have kept on going."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Prophet ﷺ asking for food, and he gave him half a wasq of barley. The man, his wife, and their guest kept eating from it until he measured it. Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"If you had not measured it, you would have kept eating from it, and it would have lasted for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year of the expedition to Tabūk. He used to combine the prayers: he prayed Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr together, and Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ together. Then one day he delayed the prayer, then came out and prayed Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr together, then went in, and after that came out and prayed Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ together. Then he said:

"Tomorrow, Allah willing, you will come to the spring of Tabūk, and you will not reach it until the morning is well advanced. Whoever of you comes to it should not touch any of its water until I come."
We came to it, and two men had reached it before us. The spring was like a thin shoelace, trickling with a little water. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked them,
"Have you touched any of its water?" They said, "Yes."

The Prophet ﷺ rebuked them and said to them what Allah willed him to say. He said: Then they scooped up a little water from the spring with their hands, little by little, until it was collected in a vessel. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ washed his hands and face in it, then poured it back into the spring, and the spring gushed with abundant water—or he said, plentiful water (Abū ʿAlī was unsure which he said)—until the people had all drawn water. Then he said:
"O Muʿādh, if you live long, you may soon see what is here filled with gardens."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among those who narrated that
from him is Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd al-Jawharī: Abū Usāmah narrated to us,
Burayd ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated to me,
from Abū Burdah,
from Abū Mūsā,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

"When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wants mercy for a nation of His servants, He takes its prophet before it, making him a forerunner and a predecessor for them. And when He wants the destruction of a nation, He punishes it while its prophet is alive, and destroys it while he is looking on, so He gladdens his eyes with its destruction, because they denied him and disobeyed his command."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, and from al-Nuʿmān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh,
from Abū Saʿīd
al-Khudrī, from the Prophet ﷺ, the same as the hadith of Yaʿqūb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And around him were
some of the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār. He said to them, "Do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the wearing of silk?" They said, "By Allah, yes."
He said, "And he forbade the wearing of gold, except in small pieces?" They said, "Yes."
ʿAlī ibn Gharāb differed with him; he narrated it from Bayhas, from Abū Shaykh, from Ibn ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were with Muʿāwiyah on one of his Hajj journeys, he gathered a group of the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ and said to them, "Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the wearing of gold, except in small pieces?" They said, "By Allah, yes."
Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr differed with him, with disagreement among his students about him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Muʿāwiyah,

in the year he performed Hajj, gathered a number of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Kaʿbah and said to them, "I ask you by Allah: did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid the wearing of gold?" They said, "Yes."
He said, "And I bear witness [to that]."
Ḥarb ibn Shaddād differed with him; he narrated it from Yaḥyā, from Abū Shaykh, from his brother Ḥimmān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar said to Ṣuhayb, "Why do I see a gold ring on you?" He said, "One who is better than you saw it and did not find fault with it."
He said, "Who is he?" He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣaʿṣaʿah ibn Ṣūḥān came to ʿAlī and said, "Forbid us from what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade you."

He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us from the gourd vessel, the green jar, the hollowed palm-trunk vessel, and barley beer. He also forbade us from the gold ring, wearing silk, wearing qassī garments, and the red saddle-cloth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And wearing qassī garments, and the gold ring.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And gold rings.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came from Najrān to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wearing a gold ring. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from him and said,
"You have come to me with a burning coal of fire in your hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a man

was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ wearing a gold ring, and in the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was a staff or a palm branch. The Prophet ﷺ struck his finger with it. The man said, "What is wrong, Messenger of Allah?" He said,
"Will you not throw away that which is on your finger?"
So the man took it off and threw it away. The Prophet ﷺ saw him afterwards and said,
"What happened to the ring?"
He said, "I threw it away." He said,
"I did not command you with this. I only commanded you to sell it and make use of its price."
And this is a munkar hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ saw a gold ring on his hand, so he began tapping it with a rod he had with him. When the Prophet ﷺ was inattentive, he threw it away. [The Prophet ﷺ] said,
"I think we have only pained you and cost you [your ring]."
Yūnus differed with him; he narrated it from az-Zuhrī, from Abū Idrīs, as a mursal report.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a man
from among those who met the Prophet ﷺ wore a gold ring, similar to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ saw a gold ring on a man's hand and struck his finger with a rod he had with him until he threw it away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, [reported as] mursal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ used to wear his ring on his right hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ used to wear a ring on his right hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Bahrain came to the Prophet ﷺ and greeted him with salām, but he did not return it. In the man's hand was a gold ring, and he wore a silk cloak. He took them off, then greeted again, and [the Prophet ﷺ] returned the greeting. Then he said, "Messenger of Allah, I came to you a moment ago and you turned away from me." He said,
"There was a burning coal of fire in your hand."
He said, "Then I have come with a great many coals." He said,
"What you have brought is of no more use to us than the stones of the lava field, but it is the enjoyment of the life of this world."
He said, "Then what should I wear as a ring?" He said,
"A ring of iron, or silver, or brass."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out, having made a ring of silver, and said,
"Whoever wishes to have one made like it may do so, but do not engrave [anything] on its engraving."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Do not seek light from the fire of the polytheists, and do not engrave Arabic on your rings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me,
"O ʿAlī, ask Allah for guidance and right direction."
And he forbade me to place the ring on this [finger] and this one.
And he pointed, meaning the index finger and the middle finger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said to him, "Will you not go to ʿUthmān and speak to him?" He said, "Do you think I only speak to him when I can let you hear? By Allah, I have spoken to him privately, without opening a matter that I would not like to be the first to open. And I will not say to anyone who becomes a ruler over me that he is the best of people,
after I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and thrown into the Fire, and his intestines will spill out, and he will go around with them as a donkey goes around a mill. The people of the Fire will gather around him and say, 'O so-and-so, what is wrong with you? Did you not used to enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong?' He will say, 'Yes, I used to enjoin what is right but did not do it myself, and I used to forbid what is wrong but did it myself.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Satan comes to one of you and says, 'Who created this? Who created that?' until he says, 'Who created your Lord?' When it reaches that point, let him seek refuge in Allah and stop."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥulwānī and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd; ʿAbd said: He informed me, and [the other] said:
Ḥasan: Yaʿqūb narrated to us,
who is the son of Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd, who said: My father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ,
from Ibn Shihāb,
who said: ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed me,
ibn Zayd, that Muḥammad ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ

informed him that his father Saʿd said: ʿUmar asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while some women of Quraysh were with him, speaking to him and asking much of him, with their voices raised. When ʿUmar asked permission, they got up and hurried behind the screen. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted him to enter, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was laughing. ʿUmar said, "May Allah keep you smiling, O Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I was amazed at these women who were with me; when they heard your voice, they hurried behind the screen."
ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have more right to be feared."
Then ʿUmar said, "O enemies of yourselves, do you fear me and not fear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" They said, "Yes, you are harsher and sterner than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, Satan never meets you walking along a path without taking a path other than yours."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The head of disbelief is toward the East; pride and arrogance are among the owners of horses and camels, the loud-voiced herdsmen, the people of tents; and tranquility is among the people of sheep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ pointed with his hand toward Yemen and said:
"Faith is Yemeni, right here.
Indeed, harshness and hardness of hearts are among the loud-voiced herdsmen, at the base of the camels' tails,
where the two horns of Satan rise, in Rabīʿah and Muḍar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A community of the Children of Israel was lost, and it is not known what became of it.
I do not think it was anything but the rat: when the milk of camels is put before it, it does not drink,
and when the milk of sheep is put before it, it drinks."
I related this to Kaʿb, and he said, "Did you hear the Prophet ﷺ say it?" I said, "Yes."
He said it to me several times.
So I said, "Do I read the Torah?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Cover the vessels, tie the water-skins, close the doors,
and keep your children close in the evening,
for the jinn spread out and snatch.
Put out the lamps when you go to sleep,
for the little mischief-maker may drag the wick and burn the people of the house."
Ibn Jurayj and Ḥabīb said, from ʿAṭāʾ: "for the devils"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A woman was punished because of a cat that she tied up; she did not feed it, nor give it water, nor let it eat from the creatures of the earth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"While a dog was circling a well, thirst almost killing it, a prostitute from among the prostitutes of the Children of Israel saw it. She took off her leather sock, drew water for it with it, and gave it to drink, and she was forgiven because of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And others, and the wording
is that of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī. They said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī,
from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUtbah,
that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās
say: I heard Abū Ṭalḥah
say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The angels do not enter a house in which there is a dog or images of figures."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me on an errand of his, so I set off,
then I returned after having completed it,
and I came to the Prophet ﷺ and greeted him with salām,
but he did not return my greeting.
So something entered my heart that only Allah knows, and I said to myself: Perhaps the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is displeased with me because I was slow in coming back to him.
Then I greeted him again, and he did not return my greeting,
and what entered my heart was stronger than the first time.
Then I greeted him once more, and he returned my greeting and said:
"The only thing that prevented me from returning your greeting was that I was praying."
He was on his mount, facing a direction other than the qiblah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy died, his son ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he gave him his shirt and told him to shroud him in it. Then he stood to pray over him,
and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb took hold of his garment and said: "Will you pray over him while he is a hypocrite, when Allah has forbidden you to seek forgiveness for them?" He said:

"Allah gave me a choice, or He informed me, and said: {Seek forgiveness for them or do not seek forgiveness for them; even if you seek forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them.} So I will add to more than seventy."

He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over him, and we prayed with him. Then Allah revealed to him: {And never pray over any of them who dies, ever, and do not stand at his grave. Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died while being disobedient.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: We migrated with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, seeking the Face of Allah,
so our reward became due from Allah.
Among us were those who passed on, or departed, without having eaten any of their reward.
Among them was Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr, who was killed on the day of Uḥud,
and he left behind nothing except a striped cloak.
When we covered his head with it, his feet were exposed,
and when his feet were covered with it, his head was exposed.
So the Prophet ﷺ said to us:
"Cover his head with it,
and put idhkhir [grass] over his feet," or he said: "Place some idhkhir over his feet."
And among us are those whose fruit has ripened for them, and they are gathering it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zaynab entered upon Umm Ḥabībah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, when her father Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb died,
and Umm Ḥabībah called for perfume that had a yellow color, khalūq or something else, and she applied some of it to a young girl,
then she touched her own cheeks with it,
then she said: "By Allah, I have no need of perfume,
except that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three nights,
except for a husband, [for whom she mourns] four months and ten [days].'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: "The dead person is punished because of the wailing of his family over him."

A man said to him: "What do you think of a man who died in Khurasan, and his family wailed over him here? Would he be punished because of his family's wailing?" He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke the truth, and you are mistaken."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ visited me in the year of the Farewell Hajj during an illness from which I was close to death,
and I said: "O Messenger of Allah,
the pain has reached me as you see,
and I am a man of wealth, and no one inherits from me except one daughter of mine.
Shall I give two-thirds of my wealth in charity?" He said: "No."
He said: "Then half of it?" He said:
"One-third, O Saʿd, and one-third is a lot.
It is better for you to leave your heirs wealthy than to leave them poor, begging from people."
Aḥmad ibn Yūnus reported from Ibrāhīm:
"That you leave your offspring...
and you will not spend any expenditure seeking the Face of Allah except that Allah will reward you for it,
even the morsel that you put into the mouth of your wife."
I said: "O Messenger of Allah,
shall I be left behind after my companions?" He said:
"You will not be left behind and do any deed seeking the Face of Allah except that you will increase thereby in rank and elevation,
and perhaps you will be left behind until some people benefit from you
and others are harmed by you.
O Allah, complete their Hijrah for my companions,
and do not turn them back on their heels.
But the unfortunate one is Saʿd ibn Khawlah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ grieved for him because he died in Makkah.
Aḥmad ibn Yūnus and Mūsā said, from Ibrāhīm:
"That you leave your heirs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib addressed us and said: Whoever claims that we have

anything that we recite other than the Book of Allah and this sheet—and he said, a sheet hanging from the sheath of his sword—has lied. In it are the ages of camels [for blood-money] and some rulings on wounds, and in it the Prophet ﷺ said:

"Medina is a sanctuary between ʿAyr and Thawr. Whoever introduces an innovation in it, or gives shelter to one who introduces an innovation, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people. Allah will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any obligatory or voluntary act. The protection of the Muslims is one; the lowest of them may extend it. Whoever claims lineage to someone other than his father, or attaches himself to someone other than his own masters, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people. Allah will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any obligatory or voluntary act."
The narration of Abū Bakr and Zuhayr ended at his saying:
"the lowest of them may extend it."
They did not mention what comes after it, and their narration does not include "hanging from the sheath of his sword."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jābir
ibn ʿAbdullāh, that a Bedouin
pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then the Bedouin was struck by a fever in Medina, so he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Muhammad, release me from my pledge.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ refused. Then he came to him again and said: Release me from my pledge.
He refused. Then he came to him again and said: Release me from my pledge.
He refused. So the Bedouin left, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Medina is like a bellows: it expels its impurity and purifies and brightens its good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I listened,
from Ibn Wahb,
who said: Mālik and Yūnus informed me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:

"Whoever spends a pair in the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will be called in Paradise: O servant of Allah, this is good. Whoever was among the people of prayer will be called from the gate of prayer; whoever was among the people of jihad will be called from the gate of jihad; whoever was among the people of charity (ṣadaqah) will be called from the gate of charity; and whoever was among the people of fasting will be called from the gate of Rayyān."

Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq said: O Messenger of Allah, one who is called from any one of those gates has no need [of the others], but will anyone be called from all of those gates? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Yes, and I hope that you will be one of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I listened,
—and the wording is his—from Ibn al-Qāsim, from Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned Ramadan and said:
"Do not fast until you see the crescent, and do not break the fast until you see it. If it is hidden from you by clouds, then estimate it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered with ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad upon ʿAbdullāh, and ʿAbdullāh said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ as young men who had nothing, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:
"O company of young men, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry,
for it lowers the gaze and protects the chastity.
And whoever is not able, let him fast,
for it is a shield for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We are an unlettered nation; we neither write nor calculate. The month is like this, like this, and like this—and he folded his thumb on the third—and the month is like this, like this, and like this."
Meaning: a full thirty.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to spend the retreat in Ramadan during the ten days in the middle of the month.
When the evening of the twentieth night had come,
and the twenty-first was approaching,
he would return to his dwelling, and those who had been in retreat with him would return.
In one month in which he observed the retreat, he stayed on the night on which he would usually return, and he addressed the people,
instructing them as Allah willed, then said:
"I used to observe the retreat in these ten days,
then it appeared to me that I should observe it in these last ten.
So whoever has been in retreat with me, let him remain in his place of retreat.
I was shown this night and then made to forget it, so seek it in the last ten, and seek it on every odd night.
And I saw myself prostrating in water and mud."
The sky poured down that night and it rained,
and the mosque leaked at the Prophet's ﷺ place of prayer on the twenty-first night.
So my eyes saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I looked at him as he finished from the dawn prayer,
with his face covered in mud and water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to observe iʿtikāf in the last ten days of Ramadan until Allah took his soul,
and then his wives observed iʿtikāf after him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When you see the crescent, fast; and when you see it, break the fast. If it is cloudy and you cannot see it, then complete Shaʿbān as thirty days, unless you see the crescent before that. Then fast Ramaḍān for thirty days, unless you see the crescent before that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿIkrimah on a day when it was unclear whether it was [the last day] of Ramaḍān or of Shaʿbān, and he was eating bread, vegetables and milk. He said to me, "Come and eat."
I said, "I am fasting."

He said, and he swore by Allah, "You will certainly break your fast." I said, "Glory be to Allah," twice. When I saw him swearing without making any exception, I stepped forward and said, "Now bring what you have." He said, "I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

'Fast when you see it and break the fast when you see it. If a cloud or darkness comes between you and it, then complete the count of Shaʿbān. Do not anticipate the month, and do not join Ramaḍān with a day of Shaʿbān.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn Abī Thawr narrated to him; and [another chain:]
ʿAmr ibn Manṣūr informed us,
he said: Al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us,
he said: Shuʿayb informed us, from az-Zuhrī,
he said: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn Abī Thawr informed me,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,

who said: I had long been eager to ask ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb about the two women among the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning whom Allah said: {If you two repent to Allah, then your hearts have indeed inclined}. He then related the hadith, and said in it: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ withdrew from his wives because of that matter, when Ḥafṣah disclosed it to ʿĀʾishah, for twenty-nine nights.
ʿĀʾishah said: He had said:
"I will not go in to them for a month."

[This was] because of his intense displeasure with them, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed him of their talk. When twenty-nine nights had passed, he entered upon ʿĀʾishah and began with her. ʿĀʾishah said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, you had sworn not to enter upon us for a month, but we have woken up on the twenty-ninth morning, counting the nights one by one." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The month is twenty-nine nights."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jibrīl, peace be upon him, came to me and said: The month is twenty-nine days."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The month may be twenty-nine and may be thirty. So when you see it, fast; and when you see it, break the fast. If it is cloudy for you, then complete the count."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The month is twenty-nine."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "The month is like this."

Shuʿbah described, from the description of Jabalah, from the description of Ibn ʿUmar, that it is twenty-nine, as was reported of his demonstration: twice with the fingers of his hands, and the third time he held back one finger of his hands.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The month is twenty-nine."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I ate the pre-dawn meal with Ḥudhayfah, then we went out to prayer. When we reached the mosque, we prayed two rakʿahs and the prayer was called to begin, and there was only a short while between them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿĀʾishah, "Among us are two men from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: one hastens the breaking of the fast and delays the pre-dawn meal, and the other delays the breaking of the fast and hastens the pre-dawn meal."
She said, "Which of them hastens the breaking of the fast and delays the pre-dawn meal?" I said, "ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd."
She said, "This is how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was eating the pre-dawn meal, and he said:
"It is a blessing that Allah has given you, so do not leave it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Take the morning meal of the pre-dawn meal, for it is the blessed morning meal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, at the time of the pre-dawn meal:
"O Anas, I wish to fast; give me something to eat."
So I brought him dates and a vessel containing water, and that was after Bilāl had given the call. He said:
"O Anas, look for a man to eat with me."
So I called Zayd ibn Thābit, and he came and said, "I have drunk a drink of barley meal, and I intend to fast."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"And I intend to fast."
So he ate the pre-dawn meal with him, then stood and prayed two rakʿahs, then went out to the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Whoever wears a garment of fame in this world, Allah will clothe him in a garment of humiliation on the Day of Resurrection, and then set it ablaze with fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever wears a garment of fame, Allah turns away from him until he takes it off, whenever he takes it off."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Quḥāfah was brought to the Prophet ﷺ on the day of the Conquest, and his head was as white as thaghāmah [a white-flowered plant]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Take him to one of his wives so that she may change it, and keep him away from black."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣuhayb al-Khayr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The best thing with which you can dye this gray hair is black; it makes your wives more fond of you and makes you more awe-inspiring in the hearts of your enemy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The gray hairs of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ numbered about twenty hairs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to place the stone of his ring on the side facing his palm.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me to wear a ring on this finger and this one, meaning the little finger and the thumb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Her husband was away on one of the military expeditions, and she asked his permission to make a picture of a palm tree in her house, but he refused her or forbade her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I covered a recess of mine, meaning the inner part, with a curtain that had pictures on it. When the Prophet ﷺ arrived, he tore it down, so I made two cushions from it, and I saw the Prophet ﷺ reclining on one of them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Companion of the Prophet ﷺ said: The Prophet ﷺ used to forbid riding on leopard skins.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "

I enjoin upon a person [good treatment of] his mother; I enjoin upon a person his mother; I enjoin upon a person his mother, three times. I enjoin upon a person his father. I enjoin upon a person his client who is closest to him, even if he suffers harm from him that hurts him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The qinṭār is twelve thousand ounces, each ounce better than what lies between the heavens and the earth."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
A man's rank in Paradise will be raised, and he will say: 'How has this come to me?' It will be said: 'Through your child's seeking forgiveness for you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Allah enjoins you to [honor] your mothers, three times. Allah enjoins you to [honor] your fathers. Allah enjoins you to [honor] those closest, and then the next closest."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of parents over their child? He said: "
They are your Paradise and your Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The father is the middle gate of Paradise, so either lose that gate or preserve it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn came running to the Prophet ﷺ, and he drew them close to him and said: "
Children make one miserly and cowardly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Shall I not tell you of the best charity? Your daughter who is returned to you, having no provider other than you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The paternal uncle of al-Aḥnaf said: A woman with her two daughters came to ʿĀʾishah, and she gave her three dates. The woman gave each of them one date, and then split the remaining one between them.
ʿĀʾishah said: Then the Prophet ﷺ came and I told him, and he said: "
Why are you surprised? By it she has entered Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
There is no man who has two daughters reach maturity and treats them well for as long as they are with him, or he is with them, except that they will admit him into Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "
Honor your children and make their upbringing good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
O Allah, I declare it sinful to wrong the rights of the two weak ones: the orphan and the woman."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The best house among the Muslims is a house with an orphan who is treated well, and the worst house among the Muslims is a house with an orphan who is mistreated."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

Whoever supports three orphans is like one who stands in prayer by night, fasts by day, and goes out morning and evening with his sword drawn in the cause of Allah. And he and I will be in Paradise as brothers, like these two sisters."
And he joined his two fingers, the index and the middle finger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he and al-Ḥurr ibn Qays ibn Ḥiṣn al-Fazārī disagreed about the companion of Moses, peace be upon him. Ibn ʿAbbās said, "He is al-Khiḍr."

Ubayy ibn Kaʿb al-Anṣārī passed by them, and Ibn ʿAbbās called him and said, "O Abū al-Ṭufayl, come to us. My companion and I have disagreed about the companion of Moses, who asked for a way to meet him. Did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mention his affair?" Ubayy said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'While Moses was among a gathering of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said to him, "Do you know anyone more knowledgeable than you?" Moses said, "No."

So Allah revealed to Moses, "Rather, Our servant al-Khiḍr." He said: Moses asked for a way to meet him, so Allah made the fish a sign for him, and it was said to him, "When you lose the fish, return, for you will meet him." So Moses travelled as long as Allah willed, then said to his servant boy, "Bring us our morning meal."
Moses' servant boy said, when he asked him for the meal, "Do you see? When we took refuge at the rock, I forgot the fish, and none made me forget it except Satan, that I should mention it."
Moses said to his servant boy, "That is what we were seeking."
So they went back retracing their footsteps, and found al-Khiḍr.
And what happened between them is what Allah has related in His Book.'"
Except that Yūnus said: "And he used to follow the trace of the fish in the sea."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The likeness of the guidance and knowledge with which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sent me is like abundant rain that fell on land. Some of it was good soil that absorbed the water and brought forth plenty of grass and herbage. Some of it was hard ground that held the water, and Allah benefited people with it: they drank from it, gave drink to others, and grazed their animals. And some of it fell on another portion that was only barren flats, which neither hold water nor grow grass. That is the likeness of one who understands the religion of Allah and benefits from what Allah has sent me with, so he learns and teaches, and the likeness of one who does not raise his head to it and does not accept the guidance of Allah with which I was sent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, while the people were praying. I said, "What is the matter with the people?" She gestured with her head toward the sky.
I said, "A sign?" She gestured with her head, meaning yes.
She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prolonged it very much, until I was overcome by faintness. Beside me was a waterskin with water in it, so I opened it and began to pour from it over my head.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished, and the sun had cleared. He addressed the people,
and praised Allah as He deserves, then said, "Now then."
She said: Some women of the Anṣār made a noise,
so I turned to them to quiet them. Then I said to ʿĀʾishah, "What did he say?" She said, he said:
"There is nothing I had not been shown except that I have seen it in this place of mine, even Paradise and the Fire.
And it has been revealed to me that you will be tested in the graves in a manner like, or close to, the trial of the Antichrist (al-Masīḥ al-Dajjāl). One of you will be brought,
and it will be said to him, 'What do you know of this man?' As for the believer, or he said the one with certainty—Hishām was unsure—he will say, 'He is the Messenger of Allah,
he is Muḥammad ﷺ. He came to us with clear proofs and guidance, so we believed, responded, followed, and affirmed his truth.'
Then it will be said to him, 'Sleep in peace,
we knew that you indeed believed in him.'
But as for the hypocrite, or he said the doubter—Hishām was unsure—it will be said to him, 'What do you know of this man?' He will say, 'I do not know,
I heard people saying something, so I said it.'"
Hishām said: Fāṭimah told me, and I retained it,
except that she mentioned something stern that will be said to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about things he disliked, and when they asked too much, he became angry. Then he said to the people:
"Ask me about whatever you wish."
A man said, "Who is my father?" He said, "Your father is Ḥudhāfah."
Another stood up and said, "Who is my father, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Your father is Sālim, the freed slave of Shaybah."
When ʿUmar saw the anger on the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said, "O Messenger of Allah, we repent to Allah."
In the narration of Abū Kurayb: he said, "Who is my father, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Your father is Sālim, the freed slave of Shaybah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: when he spoke a word, he would repeat it three times until it was understood from him,
and when he came to a people and greeted them with salām, he would greet them three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman instructed Sinān ibn Salamah al-Juhanī to ask
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that her mother had died without having performed Hajj, and whether it would suffice for her mother if she performed Hajj on her behalf. He said:
"Yes. If your mother had owed a debt and you paid it for her, would that not suffice for her? So let her perform Hajj on behalf of her mother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
asked the Prophet ﷺ about her father, who had died without performing Hajj. He said:
"Perform Hajj on behalf of your father."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Khathʿam came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "My father is a very old man who cannot ride, and the obligation of Allah regarding Hajj has come upon him. Will it suffice if I perform Hajj on his behalf?" He said:
"Are you his eldest child?" He said, "Yes." He said:
"Do you think that if he owed a debt, you would pay it?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Then perform Hajj on his behalf."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, my father died without having performed Hajj. Shall I perform Hajj on his behalf?" He said:
"Do you think that if your father owed a debt, you would pay it?" He said, "Yes." He said:
"Then the debt owed to Allah is more deserving."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ when a man came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my mother is a very old woman; if I carry her she cannot hold on, and if I tie her I fear I will kill her."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you think that if your mother owed a debt, you would pay it?" He said, "Yes." He said:
"Then perform Hajj on behalf of your mother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to a man:
"You are the eldest child of your father, so perform Hajj on his behalf."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [This was] read to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, from his father,
from Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays,
that she gave birth to Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq at al-Baydāʾ. Abū Bakr mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Tell her to wash, and then to enter the state of iḥrām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "I wish I could see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while revelation comes to him." While we were at al-Jiʿrānah, the Prophet ﷺ was in a tent when revelation came to him. ʿUmar signaled to me to come, so I put my head into the tent. A man came to him who had entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah wearing a cloak and smeared with perfume, and said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about a man who has entered iḥrām wearing a cloak?" Then revelation came upon him, and the Prophet ﷺ began to breathe heavily because of it. When it had passed, he said:
