"Where is the man who asked me just now?"
The man was brought, and he said:
"As for the cloak, take it off; as for the perfume, wash it off; then renew your iḥrām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Do not wear in iḥrām shirts, trousers, turbans, hooded cloaks, or leather socks."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [This was] read to him while I listened, and the wording
is his, from Ibn Wahb, who said: Yūnus informed me,
from Ibn Shihāb, from Sālim, from his father,
who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pronouncing the talbiyah with his hair matted.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I perfumed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he came out of iḥrām, and I perfumed him for his iḥrām, with a perfume unlike this perfume of yours, meaning that it had no lasting trace.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said regarding the person in iḥrām:
"If his head or his eyes pain him, he may apply aloe to them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to Jābir and asked him about the Hajj of the Prophet,
ﷺ, and he told us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"If I had known beforehand what I came to know afterwards, I would not have brought sacrificial animals, and I would have made it an ʿUmrah. So whoever has no sacrificial animal with him, let him leave iḥrām and make it an ʿUmrah."

ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, came from Yemen with a sacrificial animal, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had brought a sacrificial animal from Madinah. Then there was Fāṭimah, who had put on dyed clothes and applied kohl.

He said: So I went, stirred up, to seek a ruling from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I said, "O Messenger of Allah, Fāṭimah has put on dyed clothes and applied kohl, and she said, 'My father ﷺ commanded me to do this.'" He said:
"She has spoken the truth, she has spoken the truth, she has spoken the truth. I commanded her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Hajj alone, without ʿUmrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From his book in his house, Salamah ibn Nubayṭ said: He informed us from Nuʿaym ibn Abī Hind, from Nubayṭ ibn Sharīṭ, from Sālim ibn ʿUbayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fainted during his illness, then recovered and said, "Has the time for prayer come?" They said, "Yes." He said, "
Tell Bilāl to call the adhān, and tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer" — or he said, "for the people."
Then he fainted again, then recovered and said, "Has the time for prayer come?" They said, "Yes." He said, "
Tell Bilāl to call the adhān, and tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer."
Then he fainted again, then recovered and said, "Has the time for prayer come?" They said, "Yes." He said, "
Tell Bilāl to call the adhān, and tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer."
Then ʿĀʾishah said, "My father is a tender-hearted man; when he stands in that place he weeps and cannot [continue]. So if only you would order someone else."
Then he fainted again, then recovered and said, "
Tell Bilāl to call the adhān, and tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer, for you are the companions of Yūsuf."
He said: So Bilāl was told and he called the adhān, and Abū Bakr was told and he led the people in prayer. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ felt some relief and said, "
Find me someone on whom I can lean."

Then Barīrah and another man came, and he leaned on them. When Abū Bakr saw him, he went to step back, but he signaled to him to stay in his place. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and sat beside Abū Bakr until Abū Bakr finished his prayer. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell ill with the illness in which he died, he was in the house of ʿĀʾishah. He said, "
Call ʿAlī for me."
ʿĀʾishah said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall we call Abū Bakr for you?" He said, "Call him."
Ḥafṣah said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall we call ʿUmar for you?" He said, "Call him."
Umm al-Faḍl said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall we call al-ʿAbbās for you?" He said, "Yes."
When they had gathered, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his head and looked, then was silent. So ʿUmar said, "Get up and leave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
Then Bilāl came to notify him of the prayer, and he said, "
Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer."

ʿĀʾishah said, "O Messenger of Allah, Abū Bakr is a soft-hearted man who is easily overcome, and whenever he does not see you he weeps, and the people weep. So if only you would order ʿUmar to lead the people in prayer."

So Abū Bakr went out and led the people in prayer. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ felt some relief in himself and came out, supported between two men, his feet dragging on the ground. When the people saw him, they said "Subḥān Allāh" to alert Abū Bakr, and he went to step back, but the Prophet ﷺ signaled to him, meaning: stay in your place. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and sat on his right, and Abū Bakr stood. Abū Bakr was following the Prophet ﷺ in prayer, and the people were following Abū Bakr.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took up the recitation from the point where Abū Bakr had reached.
Wakīʿ said: And such is the Sunnah.
He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died in that illness of his.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed behind, and we reached the people when ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf had already led them in one rakʿah. When he sensed the Prophet ﷺ, he went to step back, but the Prophet ﷺ signaled to him to complete the prayer. He said, "
You have done well; do likewise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the qunūt in the Fajr prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A scorpion stung the Prophet ﷺ while he was in prayer, and he said, "
May Allah curse the scorpion; it spares neither one who prays nor one who does not pray. Kill it, whether in the sacred precinct or outside it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ killed a scorpion while he was in prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We entered upon ʿAbdullāh, and with us were ʿAlqamah, al-Aswad and a group of others. He narrated to us a hadith, and I did not see him narrate it to the people except for my sake, because I was the youngest of them in age. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O company of young men, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, for it is more restraining for the gaze and more protective of chastity."
ʿAlī said: al-Aʿmash was asked about the hadith of Ibrāhīm, and he said: From Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbdullāh, the same. He said: Yes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥumayd — ʿAbd said: Ḥaddathanī; and the other two said: Ya ʿqūb narrated to us,
— meaning Ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd — my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ,
— that is, Ibn Kaysān — from Ibn Shihāb,
who said: Anas ibn
Mālik informed me that Allah,

Mighty and Majestic, sent the revelation continuously to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before his death, until he passed away, and the revelation was most frequent on the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Wā'il said: One day, after we had prayed the morning prayer, we went early to ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd. We greeted with salām at the door and he permitted us to enter. He said: We stayed at the door for a short while. He said: Then the servant girl came out and said, "Will you not come in?" So we entered, and found him sitting, glorifying Allah. He said, "What prevented you from entering when you had been given permission?" We said, "Nothing, except that we thought some of the household were asleep."

He said, "You thought the family of Ibn Umm ʿAbd were heedless?" He said: Then he went on glorifying Allah until he thought the sun had risen, and he said, "O girl, look whether it has risen." She looked and it had not yet risen, so he went on glorifying Allah until, when he thought the sun had risen, he said, "O girl, look whether it has risen." She looked and it had risen.

He said, "Praise be to Allah, who has let us off this day of ours" — Mahdī said: and I think he said — "and did not destroy us for our sins." He said: A man among the people said, "Last night I recited all of the Mufaṣṣal." He said: ʿAbdullāh said, "Reciting it hurriedly like poetry! We have heard the paired surahs, and I remember the paired surahs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite: eighteen from the Mufaṣṣal and two surahs from the Ḥā-Mīm group."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married one of his wives, and he sent me, so I invited some people to the meal. When they had eaten and left, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up and set off toward the house of ʿĀʾishah, and he saw two men sitting. So he turned back, and the two men got up and left. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
"O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are permitted to do so for a meal, without waiting for its preparation..." There is a story in the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The food of two is enough for three, and the food of three is enough for four."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There will be among my nation people who will deem lawful fornication, silk, wine and musical instruments.
And some people will camp at the side of a mountain, and their shepherd will return to them in the evening with their livestock,
and a needy person — meaning a poor man — will come to them for a need, and they will say, 'Come back to us tomorrow.'
Then Allah will destroy them at night and cause the mountain to fall,
and He will transform others into apes and pigs until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recall being with the Prophet ﷺ when the time of ʿAṣr had come, and we had no water except a little left over, which was put in a vessel.
It was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he put his hand into it and spread his fingers, then said:
"Come to those who wish to perform ablution.
The blessing is from Allah."
And I saw the water gushing out from between his fingers.
The people performed ablution and drank,
and I did not hold back from putting some of it into my belly,
for I knew that it was a blessing.
I said to Jābir, "How many were you that day?" He said, "One thousand four hundred."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I fell severely ill in Makkah,
and the Prophet ﷺ came to visit me.
I said, "O Prophet of Allah, I am leaving wealth, and I have only one daughter.
Shall I bequeath two thirds of my wealth and leave a third?" He said, "No."
I said, "Then shall I bequeath half and leave half?" He said, "No."
I said, "Then shall I bequeath a third and leave two thirds for her?" He said,
"A third, and a third is a lot."
Then he placed his hand on my forehead,
then passed his hand over my face and my belly, and said:
"O Allah, heal Saʿd and complete his emigration."
And I have continued to feel its coolness upon my liver, as it seems to me, until this very moment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him; and whoever dislikes to meet Allah, Allah dislikes to meet him."
He said: I went to ʿĀʾishah and said, "O Mother of the Believers, I heard Abū Hurayrah mention from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a hadith which, if it is so, then we are ruined."
She said, "The one who is ruined is the one ruined by a saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. What is it?" He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him; and whoever dislikes to meet Allah, Allah dislikes to meet him."
And none of us is free of disliking death.

She said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did say that, but it is not what you are taking it to mean. Rather, when the eyes roll upward, the chest rattles, the skin shivers and the fingers contract, at that moment whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes to meet Allah, Allah dislikes to meet him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited a man among the Muslims who had grown weak and become like a fledgling, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Were you praying to Allah for something or asking Him for something?"
He said, "Yes, I used to say: O Allah, whatever punishment You would give me in the Hereafter, hasten it for me in this world."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Glory be to Allah! You cannot bear it, or you are not able to. Why did you not say: O Allah, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire?"
He said: So he prayed to Allah for him, and He cured him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"For me to say: Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, is dearer to me than everything upon which the sun rises."
He said: This is a good and sound hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ heard a man who had come to him say, "O Messenger of Allah, what should I say when I ask my Lord?" He said:
"Say: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, grant me well-being, and provide for me."
And he gathered his four fingers, except the thumb, and said:
"For these gather for you your religion and your worldly life."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Is any of you unable to earn a thousand good deeds every day?"
One of those sitting with him asked, "How can any of us earn a thousand good deeds?" He said:
"He glorifies Allah a hundred times, and a thousand good deeds are recorded for him or a thousand sins are wiped away from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ heard me saying:
"There is no power and no strength except with Allah." He said:
"O ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays, shall I not guide you to a phrase that is among the treasures of Paradise?"
I said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"Say: There is no power and no strength except with Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on a journey and reached the last part of the night, he would say:
"A listener has heard our praise of Allah, His favor, and His good trial of us. O Allah, accompany us and show favor to us."
[He said this] seeking refuge with Allah from the Fire.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mālik said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed Allah is pleased with a servant who eats a meal and praises Him for it, or drinks a drink and praises Him for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among the supplications of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the loss of Your blessing, the change of Your protection, the suddenness of Your vengeance, and all of Your displeasure."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed the world is sweet and green, and Allah is making you successors in it, and He will see how you act. So beware of the world and beware of women, for the first trial of the Children of Israel was concerning women."
And in the narration of Ibn Bashshār:
"So that He may see how you act."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The storyteller of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Abū Ṣirmah,
from Abū Ayyūb,
that when death approached him he said: I concealed from you something I heard from the Messenger of Allah. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"If you did not commit sins, Allah would create a people who would sin and whom He would forgive."
He said: This is a good, gharīb hadith.
And this has been narrated
from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb,
from Abū Ayyūb,
from the Prophet ﷺ, similarly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who mentioned several hadiths, among them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed, there is a bone in a human being that the earth never consumes, and from it he will be reconstituted on the Day of Resurrection."
They said, "Which bone is it, Messenger of Allah?" He said, "The tailbone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the lavatory, he would take off his ring.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should urinate in the place where he bathes and then wash in it." Aḥmad said:
"Or perform ablution in it, for most whisperings of doubt come from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Prayer is not accepted without purification, nor charity from ill-gotten gains."
Hannād said in his narration, "except with purification."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was al-Aqraʿ: The Prophet ﷺ forbade a man to perform ablution with the water left over from a woman's purification.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jarīr ibn ʿAbdullāh urinated, then performed ablution and wiped over his leather socks. It was said to him, "Do you do this?" He said, "What prevents me, when I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do it?"
Ibrāhīm said: They were pleased with the hadith of Jarīr because his accepting Islam came after the revelation of Sūrat al-Māʾidah.
This is the statement of Ibrāhīm, meaning that they were pleased with it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would bathe and pray the two rakʿahs and the morning prayer, and I do not think he would renew ablution after the bath.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a man had intercourse with his wife while she was menstruating, the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to give half a dinar in charity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever bathes on Friday and has his wife bathe, goes out early and arrives at the beginning, draws near, listens and keeps silent, will have for every step he takes the reward of a year of fasting and night prayer."
Maḥmūd said: Wakīʿ said, "He bathed and had his wife bathe."
He said: It is reported from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak that he said regarding this hadith:
"Whoever washed and bathed."
meaning, he washed his head and bathed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever performs ablution on Friday, that is fine and good, and it suffices for the obligation; and whoever bathes, the bath is better."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished from a prayer in which the recitation was aloud, and said:
"Did any of you recite along with me just now?"
A man said, "Yes, Messenger of Allah." He said:
"I was saying to myself, why am I being contended with in the Qurʾān?"
He said: So the people stopped reciting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the prayers in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited aloud, when they heard that from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"When one of you prostrates, he should not spread out his forearms as a dog spreads them, and he should draw his thighs together."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded killing the two black creatures during prayer: the snake and the scorpion.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When he said the takbīr, he raised his hands to below his ears, and when he recited {not those who have earned Your anger, nor those who are astray}, he said, "Āmīn."
I heard him while I was behind him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you stands for prayer, mercy is facing him, so he should not wipe away the pebbles."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard Buraydah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was giving us a sermon when al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon them, came wearing two red shirts, walking and stumbling. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came down from the pulpit, picked them up and placed them in front of him. Then he said, "Allah has spoken the truth:
'Your wealth and your children are only a trial.' I looked at these two boys walking and stumbling, and I could not be patient until I interrupted my talk and picked them up."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah sent me, ʿUthmān ibn ʿUqbah said, and he was the governor of Madinah, to Ibn ʿAbbās to ask him about the prayer of

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for rain. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out in plain clothes, humble and imploring, until he came to the place of prayer. ʿUthmān added: He ascended the pulpit. Then they agreed: He did not give a sermon like these sermons of yours, but he continued in supplication, humble entreaty and takbīr. Then he prayed two rakʿahs as he prays on the festival.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When death came upon ʿAnbasah, he began to be restless, and this was mentioned to him. He said: I heard Umm Ḥabībah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, narrate from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:
"Whoever prays four rakʿahs before Ẓuhr and four after it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will forbid his flesh to the Fire."
I have not abandoned them since I heard it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The prayer of the night and the day is two by two."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, he slaughtered a camel or a cow.
Muʿādh added, from Shuʿbah, from Muḥārib, who heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh say: The Prophet ﷺ bought a camel from me for two ūqiyahs and a dirham, or two dirhams.
When he reached Ṣirār, he ordered that a cow be slaughtered, and they ate from it.
When he arrived in Madinah, he instructed me to go to the mosque and pray two rakʿahs,
and he weighed out for me the price of the camel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah, peace be upon her, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, asked Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq, after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to divide her inheritance for her,
from what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had left of the spoils that Allah had granted him.
Abū Bakr said to her: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity."
Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, became angry and stopped speaking to Abū Bakr,
and she continued to avoid him until she died. She lived six months after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
She said: Fāṭimah used to ask Abū Bakr for her share of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had left from Khaybar, Fadak, and his charity in Madinah,
but Abū Bakr refused her that,
and said: I will not leave anything that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do, except that I will do it,
for I fear that if I leave any part of his practice, I will go astray.
As for his charity in Madinah, ʿUmar handed it over to ʿAlī and al-ʿAbbās,
but as for Khaybar and Fadak, ʿUmar kept them and said: These two are the charity of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; they were for the needs that arose for him and for his emergencies,
and their administration is for whoever is in charge of the affairs of the Muslims.
He said: And they remain so to this day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, and in my house there was nothing that a living creature could eat,
except some barley on a shelf of mine,
and I ate from it for a long time. Then I measured it, and it ran out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, became caliph, he sent him to Bahrain,
and wrote for him this letter and sealed it.
The engraving on the seal was in three lines: Muḥammad on one line, Messenger on one line, and Allah on one line.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ. And Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī narrated to us,
and Isḥāq ibn Manṣūr,
both said: an-Naḍr informed us,
Ibn Shumayl, who said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, Manṣūr, Sulaymān,
and Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān.
They said: We heard Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd,
from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh, from the Prophet ﷺ,
similar to the hadith of those whose narrations we mentioned before.
In the narration of an-Naḍr from Shuʿbah, he said: Ḥuṣayn and Sulaymān added to it. Ḥuṣayn said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I was sent only as a distributor, to distribute among you." And Sulaymān said:
"I am only a distributor, distributing among you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I do not give you anything, nor do I withhold it from you; I am only a treasurer, placing things where I am commanded."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"One of the prophets went out on a military expedition and said to his people: Let no man follow me who has married a woman and wishes to consummate the marriage but has not yet done so, nor one who has built a house but has not yet raised its roof, nor one who has bought sheep or pregnant she-camels and is waiting for them to give birth.

He went on the expedition and came near the town at the time of the ʿAṣr prayer or close to it. He said to the sun: You are under command and I am under command. O Allah, hold it back for me a little.

So it was held back for him until Allah gave him victory." He said: "They gathered the spoils, and the fire came to consume them, but it refused to eat them. He said: There is misappropriation among you. Let one man from each tribe pledge allegiance to me.
They pledged allegiance to him, and one man's hand stuck to his hand. He said: The misappropriation is among you, so let your tribe pledge allegiance to me.

They pledged allegiance to him," he said, "and the hands of two or three men stuck to his. He said: The misappropriation is among you; you have misappropriated. They then brought out for him something like the head of a cow made of gold, and placed it with the spoils, which were on the open ground. The fire came and consumed it.
Spoils were not lawful for anyone before us. That was because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, saw our weakness and incapacity, so He made them lawful for us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said to me,
"If the wealth of Bahrain comes to us, I will give you this much, and this much, and this much."
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away and the wealth of Bahrain came, Abū Bakr said, "Whoever was promised something by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ should come to me."
So I came to him and said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said to me,
'If the wealth of Bahrain comes to us, I will give you this much, and this much, and this much.'"
He said to me, "Take a handful."
So I took a handful, and he said to me, "Count it."
I counted it, and it was five hundred,
so he gave me one thousand five hundred.
Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭahmān reported from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Ṣuhayb, from Anas:
Wealth from Bahrain was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said,
"Spread it out in the mosque."
It was the most wealth ever brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then al-ʿAbbās came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah,
give me some, for I paid ransom for myself and for ʿAqīl." He said, "Take."
So he scooped it up into his garment,
then went to lift it, but he was unable to.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And I advise him to observe the covenant of Allah and the covenant of His Messenger ﷺ: that he fulfil their covenant with them,
that he fight on behalf of those behind them,
and that they not be burdened beyond their capacity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar said: The Prophet ﷺ and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb set out toward the palm grove in which Ibn Ṣayyād was.
When he entered the palm grove, the Prophet ﷺ began to shield himself behind the trunks of the palm trees, trying to catch Ibn Ṣayyād unawares so as to hear something from him before he saw him,
while Ibn Ṣayyād was lying on his bed, wrapped in a velvet cloth of his, from which came a murmuring sound.
Ibn Ṣayyād's mother saw the Prophet ﷺ as he shielded himself behind the trunks of the palm trees,
and she said to Ibn Ṣayyād, "O Ṣāf!"—that was his name—and Ibn Ṣayyād sprang up. The Prophet ﷺ said,
"If she had left him alone, he would have made things clear."
Sālim said: Ibn ʿUmar said: Then the Prophet ﷺ stood among the people and praised Allah as He deserves,
then he mentioned the Dajjāl and said, "I warn you about him,
and there was no prophet but that he warned his people about him.
Nūḥ warned his people about him,
but I will tell you something about him that no prophet told his people:
you know that he is one-eyed, and that Allah is not one-eyed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, appointed a freed slave of his called Hunayy over the protected pasture, and said, "O Hunayy,
lower your wing toward the Muslims,
and beware the supplication of the oppressed,
for the supplication of the oppressed is answered,
and admit the owner of a few camels and sheep and the owner of a few goats,
but beware of letting in the livestock of Ibn ʿAwf
and of Ibn ʿAffān,
for if their livestock perish, they can return to their date palms and crops,
whereas if the livestock of the owner of a few camels and sheep and the owner of a few goats perish, he will come to me with his children and say, 'O Commander of the Faithful!
Am I to abandon them?' Woe to you! Water and pasture are easier for me than gold and silver. By Allah,
they think that I have wronged them.
It is their land; they fought over it in the Jāhiliyyah,
and they accepted Islam on it in Islam.
By Him in whose hand is my soul, were it not for the property that I carry [people] on in the cause of Allah, I would not have protected a single handspan of their land for them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ performed ʿUmrah from al-Jiʿrānah,
where he had distributed the spoils of Ḥunayn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A slave of Ibn ʿUmar's
ran away and joined the Byzantines,
then Khālid ibn al-Walīd gained victory over them and captured him,
and returned him to ʿAbd Allāh.
And a horse of Ibn ʿUmar's bolted and joined the Byzantines,
then [the Muslims] gained victory over them, and they returned it to ʿAbd Allāh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was on a horse on the day the Muslims met [the enemy],
and the commander of the Muslims that day was Khālid ibn al-Walīd,
whom Abū Bakr had sent. The enemy seized it,
and when the enemy was defeated, Khālid returned his horse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with my father, wearing a yellow shirt.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Sanah, sanah!"
ʿAbd Allāh said: In Abyssinian, that means "good."
She said: I went and began playing with the seal of prophethood, and my father scolded me.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Leave her."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Wear it out and tear it,
then wear it out and tear it,
then wear it out and tear it."
ʿAbd Allāh said: She lived on until it was mentioned.
That is, [it was mentioned] because of her long life.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr and Ibn Jurayj [said]: I heard ʿAṭāʾ

say: I went with ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr to ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, while she was staying near Thabīr, and she said to us, "There is no more emigration since Allah gave His Prophet ﷺ victory over Mecca."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ criticize any food. If he desired it, he ate it, and if he did not desire it, he stayed silent.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The superiority of ʿĀʾishah over other women is like the superiority of tharīd over all other foods.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:
"Your brother an-Najāshī has died, so rise and pray over him."
He said: So we stood and formed rows for him as rows are formed for the deceased, and we prayed over him as one prays over the deceased.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ burned and cut down the palm trees of Banū an-Naḍīr, at a place called al-Buwayrah.

Qutaybah and Ibn Rumḥ added in their narration: So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by Allah's permission, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was presented before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for an army when I was fourteen years old, and he did not accept me. Then I was presented to him the following year for an army when I was fifteen, and he accepted me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the fear prayer with one of the two groups for one rak'ah, while the other group faced the enemy. Then they left and took the places of their companions, facing the enemy, and the others came. Then the Prophet ﷺ prayed one rak'ah with them, then the Prophet ﷺ gave the salām. Then this group completed one rak'ah and that group completed one rak'ah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Narrated by one] of the Companions of the Tree, who said: We used to pray the Friday prayer with the Prophet ﷺ and then leave,
and the walls had no shade in which we could take shelter.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Narrated by] the two sons of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from their father:
It was said to ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that Ibn ʿAbbās saw no harm in temporary marriage with women.
So he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it on the day of Khaybar,
and also the meat of domestic donkeys.
Some people said: If someone uses a ruse until he contracts such a marriage, the marriage is invalid.
And some of them said: The marriage is valid and the condition is void.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh said: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest with Allah?" He said:
"That you set up a rival to Allah, while He created you."
He said: "Then which?" He said:
"Then that you kill your child
for fear that he will eat with you."
He said: "Then which?" He said:
"Then that you commit adultery with your neighbor's wife."

So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed confirmation of that: {And those who do not call upon another god along with Allah, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse; and whoever does that will meet a penalty} — the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In Ramadan, in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whoever wished would fast and whoever wished would break the fast and give as ransom the feeding of a poor person, until this verse was revealed: {So whoever of you witnesses the month, let him fast it.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: Quraysh and those who followed their religion used to stand at Muzdalifah, and they were called the Ḥums, while the rest of the Arabs used to stand at ʿArafah. She said: When Islam came, Allah, the Exalted, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to go to ʿArafāt and stand there, and then to depart from it. That is the saying of the Exalted: {Then depart from where the people depart.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Jews
used to say: If a man approaches a woman from behind in her front passage and she then conceives, her child will be cross-eyed.
He said: So this was revealed: {Your women are a place of tillage for you, so come to your place of tillage however you wish.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Recite the Qur'an to me."
He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall I recite to you when it was revealed to you?" He said:
"I like to hear it from someone other than myself."

So I recited Sūrat an-Nisāʾ until I reached: {So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and bring you as a witness over these?} I raised my head, or a man beside me nudged me, so I raised my head and saw his tears flowing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever says three times: 'In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,' no sudden affliction will befall him until the morning; and whoever says it three times in the morning, no sudden affliction will befall him until the evening."

He said: Abān ibn ʿUthmān was struck by paralysis, and the man who had heard the hadith from him began to look at him. He said to him: "What is the matter with you, looking at me? By Allah, I did not lie about ʿUthmān, and ʿUthmān did not lie about the Prophet ﷺ. But on the day this befell me, I was angry and forgot to say it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"When a man goes out of the door of his house, two angels are assigned to him. When he says, 'In the name of Allah,' they say, 'You have been guided.'
When he says, 'There is no power and no strength except with Allah,' they say, 'You have been protected.'

When he says, 'I put my trust in Allah,' they say, 'You have been taken care of.' Then his two companions [from the devils] meet him and say to each other, 'What do you want from a man who has been guided, taken care of, and protected?'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had a wife whom I loved, but my father disliked her. My father ordered me to divorce her, but I refused. I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"O ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, divorce your wife."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No two Muslims meet and shake hands except that they are forgiven before they part."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever tells you that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ urinated standing, do not believe him. I saw him urinating while sitting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"When you perform ablution, blow water out of your nose, and when you clean yourself with stones, use an odd number."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution. He washed his hands, then rinsed his mouth and snuffed water into his nose from a single handful, and washed his face. He washed his hands once each, and wiped his head and ears once.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you stand for prayer, perform ablution thoroughly, and let the water pass between the fingers of your hands and your toes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiping over the head covering and the leather socks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when standing in prayer, grasp his left hand with his right.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us during his illness with his head bandaged and led the Maghrib prayer, reciting Sūrat al-Mursalāt. She said: He did not pray it again after that until he met Allah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, whether small or large, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sahl ibn Ḥunayf said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever purifies himself in his house,
then comes to the Mosque of Qubāʾ
and prays a prayer in it,
will have a reward like that of an ʿUmrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The brother of Umm Ḥabībah, from Umm Ḥabībah,

said: Whoever prays twelve units of prayer in a day and night besides the obligatory prayers, a house will be built for him in Paradise: four before Ẓuhr and two after it, two before ʿAṣr, two after Maghrib, and two before Fajr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We asked ʿAlī about the voluntary prayer
of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the day. He said: "You would not be able to do it." We said: "Tell us about it, and we will take what we are able to."

He said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed Fajr, he would wait until the sun was from here—meaning from the east—at the height it is from there at the time of ʿAṣr prayer—meaning from the west—then he would stand and pray two units.
Then he would wait until the sun was from here—meaning from the east—at the height it is from there at the time of Ẓuhr prayer, then he would stand and pray four units.
And four before Ẓuhr when the sun had passed its zenith, and two after it.
And four before ʿAṣr.
He would separate every two units with the salutation of peace upon the angels brought near and the prophets,
and those who follow them among the Muslims and the believers. ʿAlī said:
That is sixteen units.
This was the voluntary prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the day.
And few are those who keep to it regularly. Wakīʿ said:
My father added in it:
Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit said:
"O Abū Isḥāq, I would not want to have this mosque of yours filled with gold in exchange for this hadith of yours."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray at night two units at a time, and he would pray Witr with one unit.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah how the Prophet's ﷺ recitation was at night: did he recite quietly or aloud? She said, "He did both. Sometimes he recited quietly and sometimes aloud."
I said, "Praise be to Allah, Who has made allowance in the matter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the eclipse prayer, and we did not hear any sound from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you are praying, do not spit in front of you or to your right. Spit behind you or to your left if it is vacant; otherwise, do it like this."
And he spat beneath his foot and rubbed it in.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me, when he sent me to Yemen, not to take anything from cattle until they reached thirty. When they reached thirty, the due is a calf, a tabīʿ that is a year old (jadhaʿ), male or female, until they reach forty. When they reach forty, the due is a mature cow (musinnah).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever fasts three days of every month, that is fasting for a lifetime."
Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed confirmation of that in His Book:
"Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times the like thereof."
One day is equal to ten days.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Follow Hajj with ʿUmrah and ʿUmrah with Hajj, for they remove poverty and sins just as the bellows remove the impurities of iron, gold and silver. And an accepted Hajj has no reward except Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh, "Is the hyena game?" He said, "Yes."
I said, "Can I eat it?" He said, "Yes."
I said, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say that?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoning the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah on the Day of Sacrifice, riding a reddish-white she-camel of his, with no striking, no driving away, and no cries of "Out of the way! Out of the way!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey when the time of sacrifice arrived, so we shared a camel for ten people and a cow for seven.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was shrouded in three white Yemeni cotton garments, with no shirt and no turban. It was mentioned to ʿĀʾishah that people said he was shrouded in two garments and a striped Yemeni cloak (burd ḥibarah). She said, "The cloak was brought, but they returned it and did not shroud him in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A funeral was brought to the Prophet ﷺ for him to pray over it, and he said:
"Pray over your companion, for he has a debt."
Abū Qatādah said, "I will take responsibility for it." The Prophet ﷺ said, "To settle it in full?" He said, "To settle it in full."
The debt owed was eighteen or nineteen dirhams.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What separates the lawful from the unlawful is the duff and the voice [of announcement] in marriage."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Subayʿah gave birth, after her husband's death, twenty-three or twenty-five nights later. When she recovered from her postnatal bleeding, she adorned herself for suitors, and this was criticized in her. That was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"What prevents her? Her term has ended."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We heard it from al-Zuhrī:
Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed me,
and Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān,
from al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, that his father
gave him a slave as a gift, and he came to the Prophet ﷺ to have him witness it. He said:
"Have you given the like to all your children?" He said, "No." He said, "Then take it back." The wording is that of Muḥammad.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, we are people of hunting. One of us shoots game and it is lost to him for a night or two, then he follows the trail and finds it dead with his arrow in it." He said:
"If you find your arrow in it and find no trace of a predator, and you know that your arrow killed it, then eat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The martyr feels the touch of being killed only as one of you feels the pinch of a bite."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Yazīd, and Muʿtamir,
and Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal,
they said: ʿUbaydullāh narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ,
from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hind,
from Abū Mūsā,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has made silk and gold lawful for the females of my Ummah and has made them unlawful for its males."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of the lower part of the muscle of my calf, or of his calf, and said:
"This is where the lower garment should reach. If you refuse,
then lower; if you refuse, then lower; if you refuse, then the lower garment has no right to be below the ankles."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

from Bakr ibn Layth came to the Prophet ﷺ and confessed four times that he had committed unlawful intercourse with a woman. So he flogged him one hundred lashes, as he was unmarried. Then he asked him for proof against the woman, but she said, "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, he has lied." So he flogged him with the punishment for slander, eighty lashes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the Ansār [reported] that one of them fell ill until he became emaciated, his skin clinging to his bones. A slave woman belonging to one of them came in to him, and he was aroused by her and had relations with her. When the men of his people came to visit him, he told them about that and said, "Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a ruling on my behalf, for I have had relations with a slave woman who came in to me."

So they mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "We have never seen anyone afflicted with such hardship as he is in. If we carried him to you, his bones would fall apart; he is nothing but skin over bone." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that they take a hundred stalks of a palm cluster and strike him with them one single stroke.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: A slave woman of the household of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ committed unlawful intercourse, and he said,
"O ʿAlī, go and carry out the prescribed punishment on her."
So I went, and there was blood flowing from her that had not stopped. I came to him and he said,
"O ʿAlī, have you finished?"
I said, "I came to her while her blood was still flowing." He said,
"Leave her until her blood stops, then carry out the prescribed punishment on her. And carry out the prescribed punishments on those whom your right hands possess."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not set a prescribed punishment for wine.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: A man drank and became intoxicated, and he was found swaying in the road. He was taken to the Prophet ﷺ, and when he came opposite the house of al-ʿAbbās, he broke free, entered upon al-ʿAbbās, and clung to him. That was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he laughed and said, "Did he do that?"
And he did not command anything concerning him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said something to the same effect. He said: And I think he said on the fifth occasion,
"If he drinks it, then kill him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is as if I am looking at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ right now, in the camp, looking for the saddle of Khālid ibn al-Walīd. While he was like that, a man who had drunk wine was brought, and he said to the people, "Strike him."

Some of them struck him with sandals, some with a stick, and some with a mītakhah — Ibn Wahb said: a fresh palm branch. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took some earth from the ground and threw it in his face.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I found in the book of my maternal uncle ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from ʿUqayl, that Ibn Shihāb informed him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Azhar informed him, from his father, who said: A drinker was brought to the Prophet ﷺ while he was at Ḥunayn. He threw dust in his face, then commanded his Companions, and they struck him with their sandals and whatever was in their hands, until he said to them, "Stop."

So they stopped. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away. Then Abū Bakr flogged forty for wine. Then ʿUmar flogged forty in the early part of his rule, then flogged eighty at the end of his caliphate. Then ʿUthmān flogged both punishments, eighty and forty. Then Muʿāwiyah established the punishment at eighty.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the morning of the Conquest, while I was a young lad, making his way among the people, asking about the dwelling of Khālid ibn al-Walīd. A drinker was brought, and he commanded them, and they struck him with what was in their hands: some struck him with a whip, some with a stick, and some with his sandal, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ threw dust. When Abū Bakr [was ruler], a drinker was brought, and he asked them about the beating the Prophet ﷺ had given, and they estimated it at forty, so Abū Bakr flogged forty. When ʿUmar [was ruler], Khālid ibn al-Walīd wrote to him that the people had become immersed in drinking and were treating the punishment and penalty lightly.
He said, "They are with you, so ask them."
The earliest Emigrants were with him, so he asked them, and they agreed that he should be flogged eighty.
He said: ʿAlī said, "When a man drinks, he raves, and when he raves he slanders, so I think he should be given the punishment for slander."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Then he mentioned its meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik ibn Anas, and to al-Ḥārith ibn Miskīn as he listened, a reading before him:
from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me, from Sumayy,
from Abū Ṣāliḥ,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"If people knew what is in the call to prayer and in the first row, and then found no way [to get it] except by drawing lots for it, they would draw lots. And if they knew what is in going early to the prayer, they would race to it. And if they knew what is in the ʿIshāʾ prayer and the Fajr prayer, they would come to them even if they had to crawl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He and Nāfiʿ [narrated] from Ibn ʿUmar, from Ḥafṣah,
that the Prophet ﷺ used to pray two brief units of prayer between the call to prayer and the iqāmah, the two units of Fajr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said] to his companions: "Shall I not inform you of the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: That was at a time other than the time of prayer. So he stood,
then he bowed, saying the takbīr, then raised his head and stood for a short while,
then he prostrated, then raised his head for a short while,
and he prayed the prayer of ʿAmr ibn Salimah, this elder of ours.
Ayyūb said: He used to do something I did not see them doing:
he would sit in the third and the fourth [units].
He said: Then we came to the Prophet ﷺ and stayed with him, and he said:
"When you return to your families, pray such-and-such prayer at such-and-such time,
pray such-and-such prayer at such-and-such time,
and when the time for prayer comes, let one of you call the adhān, and let the eldest among you lead you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were praying with the Prophet ﷺ, he heard the commotion of men. When he had finished the prayer, he said: "What is the matter with you?"
They said: "We hurried to the prayer." He said: "Do not do that.
When you come to the prayer, [keep to] calmness.
Pray what you catch up with, and complete what you miss."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, I had intended to order that firewood be gathered,
then to order the prayer and have the call to prayer made for it,
then to order a man to lead the people,
then to go to men [who stay behind] and burn their houses down on them.
By the One in whose hand is my soul, if any of you knew that he would find a fat bone or two fine cuts of meat, he would attend the ʿIshāʾ prayer."

Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf said: Yūnus said: Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān said: Abū ʿAbdillāh said: A mirmāh is the [portion of] meat between the two hooves of a sheep, like minsāh and mīḍāh. The mīm is pronounced with a kasrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayrith came to us and led us in prayer in this mosque of ours. He said: "I am praying with you,
though I do not intend [only] the prayer,
but I want to show you how I saw the Prophet ﷺ pray."
Ayyūb said: I asked Abū Qilābah, "How was his prayer?" He said: "Like the prayer of this elder of ours," meaning ʿAmr ibn Salimah. Ayyūb said: That elder used to complete the takbīr,
and when he raised his head from the second prostration, he would sit and lean on the ground, then stand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said during his illness:
"Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer."
ʿĀʾishah said: I said, "When Abū Bakr stands in your place, the people will not be able to hear [him] because of weeping,
so tell ʿUmar to lead the prayer." He said:
"Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer."
ʿĀʾishah said to Ḥafṣah: "Say to him, 'When Abū Bakr stands in your place, the people will not be able to hear [him] because of weeping,
so tell ʿUmar to lead the people in prayer.'" So Ḥafṣah did so.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Enough!
You are indeed the companions of Yūsuf.
Tell Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer."
Ḥafṣah said to ʿĀʾishah: "I never received any good from you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer during his illness, and he used to lead them.

ʿUrwah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ felt some lightness in himself, so he came out, and Abū Bakr was leading the people. When Abū Bakr saw him, he stepped back, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gestured to him, [meaning] stay as you are. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat beside Abū Bakr, at his side.
Abū Bakr would pray following the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the people would pray following the prayer of Abū Bakr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I traveled with the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān, and they would pray Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr as two rak'ahs each, not praying before them or after them.
And ʿAbd Allāh said: If I were to pray before them or after them, I would have completed them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn was asked about the prayer of the traveler,

and he said: I performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he prayed two rak'ahs; I performed Hajj with Abū Bakr and he prayed two rak'ahs; [I was] with ʿUmar and he prayed two rak'ahs; and with ʿUthmān for six years of his caliphate, or eight years, and he prayed two rak'ahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ while resident and while traveling. While resident, I prayed Ẓuhr with him as four rak'ahs followed by two rak'ahs. While traveling, I prayed Ẓuhr with him as two rak'ahs followed by two rak'ahs, and ʿAṣr as two rak'ahs, and he did not pray anything after it. Maghrib is the same whether resident or traveling: three rak'ahs, not shortened either when resident or when traveling, and it is the witr of the daytime, followed by two rak'ahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led the people in prayer. He lengthened the recitation, then bowed and lengthened the bowing, then raised his head and lengthened the recitation, though it was shorter than the first. Then he bowed and lengthened the bowing, though it was shorter than the first. Then he raised his head and prostrated. Then he did the same in the second rak'ah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever prays the morning prayer in congregation, then sits remembering Allah until the sun rises, then prays two rak'ahs, will have a reward like that of a Hajj and an ʿUmrah."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Complete, complete, complete."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The companions of ʿIkrimah [reported] that the Prophet ﷺ used to glance sideways during prayer. Then he mentioned something similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas ibn Mālik said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"My son, beware of turning around during prayer, for turning around during prayer is ruin. If it must be done, then let it be in voluntary prayer, not in the obligatory prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"When one of you comes to the prayer and the imam is in a certain position, let him do as the imam does."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was praying, and the Prophet ﷺ was there with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. When I sat, I began with praise of Allah, then invoked blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, then supplicated for myself. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Ask and you will be given; ask and you will be given."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr said: Yazīd ibn Khumayr informed me,
from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"On the Day of Resurrection my nation will have radiant faces from prostration and shining limbs from ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Two raṭls of water suffice for ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this [chain/wording].
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ giving a sermon during the Farewell Hajj, and he said:
"Fear Allah your Lord, pray your five [prayers], fast your month, pay the zakāh on your wealth, and obey those in authority over you, and you will enter the Paradise of your Lord."
He said: I asked Abū Umāmah: How old were you when you heard this hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: I heard it when I was thirty years old.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allāh: Do you remember anything from ʿAbd Allāh? He said: No.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Shuʿbah,
and Mālik ibn Anas,
from ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā, from his father,
from Abū Saʿīd,
from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to the hadith of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz from ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"On honey, [one ziqq] from every ten zuqq."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz asked me about the charity (ṣadaqah) on honey.
I said: We have no honey from which to give charity, but al-Mughīrah ibn Ḥakīm informed us that he said: There is no charity due on honey.
ʿUmar said: [He is] upright and acceptable.
So he wrote to the people that it be waived, meaning from them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zaynab, the wife of ʿAbd Allāh, from Zaynab,
the wife of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us and said:
"O company of women, give charity (ṣadaqah), even from your jewelry, for you are the majority of the people of Hell on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zaynab, the wife of ʿAbd Allāh, from Zaynab,
the wife of ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah came and placed his hand on my shoulder,
and I went with him to Saʿd. Then Abū Rāfiʿ said to al-Miswar, "Will you not instruct this man to buy my house that is in your compound from me?"
[Saʿd] said, "I will not add to four hundred,
either in installments or in parts."
[Abū Rāfiʿ] said, "I was offered five hundred in cash, and I refused it.
Had I not heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
'The neighbor has more right to what is next to him,'
I would not have sold it to you," or he said, "I would not have given it to you."
I said to Sufyān, "Maʿmar did not say it this way."
He said, "But he said it to me this way."

Some people said: If someone wishes to sell [property subject to] preemption (shufʿah), he may devise a stratagem to nullify the right of preemption: the seller gives the house to the buyer as a gift,
defines its boundaries and hands it over to him,
and the buyer compensates him with a thousand dirhams,
so that the preemptor has no right of preemption over it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and he was following the religion of the disbelievers of Quraysh.
They trusted him and handed over their two riding camels to him,
and they agreed to meet at the Cave of Thawr after three nights. He came to them with their two camels
on the morning of the third night, and they set out.
ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayrah went with them,
and the guide from the Banū ad-Dīl took them along the lower part of Makkah, which is the coastal road.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abū Bakr hired a man from the Banū ad-Dīl
as an expert guide, and he was following the religion of the disbelievers of Quraysh.
They handed over their two riding camels to him,
and they arranged with him to meet at the Cave of Thawr with their two camels on the morning of the third night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: one of them adding to the other,
and others said: I heard him narrate it from Saʿīd, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said to me: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"So the two set off and found a wall that was about to collapse."
Saʿīd [demonstrated] with his hand like this,
and raised his hands, [saying] it became upright.
Yaʿlā said: I think Saʿīd said:
He wiped it with his hand and it became upright. [Mūsā] said, "If you wished, you could have taken payment for it."
Saʿīd said: A payment that we could eat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave Khaybar [to its people] to work and cultivate it, in return for half of what it produced,
and Ibn ʿUmar narrated to him that the farmlands used to be rented out for something that Nāfiʿ named, which I do not remember.
And Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj narrated that the Prophet ﷺ forbade renting out farmlands.
ʿUbaydullāh said, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: until ʿUmar expelled them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, sent him to collect charity (ṣadaqah).
A man had relations with his wife's slave girl,
so Ḥamzah took a guarantor from the man until he came to ʿUmar.
ʿUmar had [already] flogged him one hundred lashes, so he believed them and excused him on account of ignorance.
Jarīr and al-Ashʿath said to ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd regarding the apostates: Call them to repent, and take guarantors for them.
So they repented, and their clans stood as guarantors for them.
Ḥammād said: If someone becomes a guarantor for a person and he dies, nothing is due from him.
Al-Ḥakam said: He is liable.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
He mentioned a man from the Children of Israel who asked another man from the Children of Israel to lend him a thousand dinars.
He said, "Bring me witnesses so that I may have them testify."
He said, "Allah is sufficient as a witness."
He said, "Then bring me a guarantor."
He said, "Allah is sufficient as a guarantor." He said, "You have spoken truly."
So he gave it to him for a set term.
The man went out to sea and completed his need,
then looked for a ship to board
so that he could reach the lender by the term he had set,
but he found no ship. So he took a piece of wood,
hollowed it out, and put into it a thousand dinars
and a letter from him to the lender,
then sealed up the place [where he had cut].
Then he brought it to the sea
and said, "O Allah, You know that I borrowed a thousand dinars from so-and-so, and he asked me for a guarantor.
I said, 'Allah is sufficient as a guarantor,' and he was satisfied with You, and he asked me for a witness,
and I said, 'Allah is sufficient as a witness,' and he was satisfied with You.
I strove to find a ship
to send him what is his, but I was unable, and I entrust it to You."
Then he threw it into the sea until it went in, and then he left,
while still looking for a ship
to travel to his town.
Meanwhile the man who had lent him went out
to look, hoping that a ship had come with his money,
and there was the piece of wood containing the money.
He took it for his family as firewood,
but when he sawed it open, he found the money and the letter.
Then the borrower came
with a thousand dinars
and said, "By Allah, I kept striving to find a ship to bring you your money,
but I did not find a ship before the one I came on."
[The lender] said, "Had you sent me anything?" He said, "I am telling you that I found no ship before the one I came on."
He said, "Allah has delivered on your behalf what you sent in the piece of wood, so go back with your thousand dinars, rightly guided."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith reported that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to have contact with one of his wives while she was menstruating, he would order her to put on a waist-wrapper, and then he would have contact with her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [She was] a wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and she said: If one of us menstruated, she would scrape the blood from her garment when she became pure and wash it, then sprinkle water over the rest of it, and then pray in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: None of us had more than a single garment in which she menstruated. If any blood got on it, she would moisten it with her saliva and then scrape it off with her saliva.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū ʿAbd Allāh, or Hishām ibn Ḥassān, from Ḥafṣah,
from Umm ʿAṭiyyah, who said: We were forbidden to mourn for a dead person for more than three days,
except for a husband, for whom it is four months and ten days.
We would not apply kohl, nor perfume, nor wear a dyed garment, except a ʿaṣb garment.
And we were permitted, at the time of purification, when one of us had bathed after her menses, to use a small piece of qusṭ and aẓfār incense.
And we were forbidden to follow funeral processions.
He said: Hishām ibn Ḥassān narrated it from Ḥafṣah, from Umm ʿAṭiyyah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He raised the narration [to the Prophet ﷺ], that he said:
"Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has appointed an angel over the womb, and he says: 'My Lord, a drop! My Lord, a clot! My Lord, a lump of flesh!'

When Allah wishes to decree its creation, the angel says: 'My Lord, male or female? Wretched or happy? What is its provision? What is its lifespan?' And so it is written while it is in its mother's womb."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [She was] a wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and she said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year of the Farewell Hajj. Some of us declared the intention for ʿUmrah and some for Hajj, until we came to Makkah. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever has entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah and has not brought a sacrificial animal should come out of iḥrām. Whoever has entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah and has brought a sacrificial animal should not come out of iḥrām until he slaughters his sacrificial animal. And whoever has declared intention for Hajj should complete his Hajj."

ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: Then I began menstruating and remained so until the day of ʿArafah, and I had declared the intention only for ʿUmrah. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered me to undo my hair, comb it, declare the intention for Hajj, and leave the ʿUmrah. She said: I did that, and when I had completed my Hajj, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr with me and ordered me to perform ʿUmrah from al-Tanʿīm in place of my ʿUmrah during which the Hajj overtook me and from which I had not come out of iḥrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to ʿUmar and said: I am in a state of major ritual impurity and I cannot find water.
He said: Do not pray.

ʿAmmār said: Do you not remember, Commander of the Faithful, when you and I were in a military detachment, and we became ritually impure and could not find water? As for you, you did not pray, but as for me, I rolled in the dust and prayed. Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"It would have been enough for you to strike the ground with your hands, then blow on them, then wipe your face and your hands with them."
ʿUmar said: Fear Allah, ʿAmmār!
He said: If you wish, I will not narrate it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We prayed Maghrib with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then we said, "If only we would stay until we pray ʿIshāʾ with him." He said: So we stayed, and he came out to us and said:
"You are still here?"
We said, "O Messenger of Allah, we prayed Maghrib with you, then we said we would stay until we pray ʿIshāʾ with you." He said:
"You have done well," or he said, "You have been right."
He said: Then he raised his head to the sky, and he would often raise his head to the sky, and he said:

"The stars are a source of security for the sky, so when the stars go, what the sky has been promised comes to it. And I am a source of security for my Companions, so when I go, what my Companions have been promised comes to them. And my Companions are a source of security for my nation, so when my Companions go, what my nation has been promised comes to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of you are my generation, then those who come after them, then those who come after them, then those who come after them."
ʿImrān said: I do not know whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, after mentioning his generation, two times or three times:

"Then after them there will be a people who bear witness without being asked to bear witness, who betray and are not trusted, who make vows and do not fulfil them, and obesity will appear among them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Through the chain of Maʿmar, like his narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of Kufah came as a delegation
to ʿUmar, and among them was a man who used to mock Uways. ʿUmar said, "Is there anyone here from the people of Qaran?" That man came, and ʿUmar said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

'A man will come to you from Yemen, called Uways. He will leave behind in Yemen only a mother of his. He had a white patch [of leprosy], and he prayed to Allah and He removed it from him except for a spot the size of a dinar or a dirham. Whoever among you meets him, let him ask him to seek forgiveness for you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The best of the Tābiʿūn is a man called Uways. He has a mother, and he had a white patch [of leprosy]. So ask him to seek forgiveness for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When reinforcements from the people of Yemen came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he would ask them, "Is Uways ibn ʿĀmir among you?" until he came upon Uways and said, "Are you Uways ibn ʿĀmir?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "From Murād, then from Qaran?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "You had leprosy and were cured of it except for a spot the size of a dirham?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "Do you have a mother?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Dharr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You will conquer Egypt, and it is a land in which the qīrāṭ is mentioned. When you conquer it, treat its people well, for they have a covenant of protection and ties of kinship," or he said:
"a covenant of protection and ties by marriage. If you see two men disputing there over the space of a brick, leave it."
He said: Then I saw ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shuraḥbīl ibn Ḥasanah and his brother Rabīʿah disputing over the space of a brick, so I left it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a man to one of the Arab tribes, and they insulted him and beat him. He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If you had come to the people of ʿUmān, they would not have insulted you or beaten you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A grandmother came to Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq asking for her inheritance. Abū Bakr said to her, "You have no share in the Book of Allah, and I do not know of anything for you in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So go back until I ask the people."

He asked the people, and al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah said, "I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he gave her a sixth." Abū Bakr said, "Is there anyone with you [who knows this]?" So Muḥammad ibn Maslamah al-Anṣārī stood up and said the same as al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah had said, and Abū Bakr carried it out for her.

Then the other grandmother, the paternal one, came to ʿUmar asking for her inheritance. He said, "You have no share in the Book of Allah, and the judgment that was given was only for someone other than you. I will not add anything to the fixed shares, but it is that sixth. If the two of you are together, it is shared between you, and whichever of you is alone with it, it is hers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
died and left no heir except a slave of his whom he had freed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Does he have anyone?"
They said, "No, except a slave of his whom he had freed."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave his inheritance to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The people of two different religions do not inherit from one another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "What is the Sunnah regarding a man from the polytheists who accepts Islam at the hands of a Muslim man?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He is the closest of people to him in his life and in his death."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb used to say, "The blood money is for the ʿāqilah [the paternal kin], and a woman does not inherit anything from the blood money of her husband," until aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Sufyān said to him, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to me that I should let the wife of Ashyam aḍ-Ḍibābī inherit from the blood money of her husband." So ʿUmar retracted.
Aḥmad ibn Ṣāliḥ said: ʿAbd ar-Razzāq narrated this hadith to us from Maʿmar, from az-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd, and he said in it: The Prophet ﷺ had appointed him over the Bedouin.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the news of the death of Jaʿfar came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Prepare food for the family of Jaʿfar,
for something has come to them that preoccupies them," or [he said], "a matter that preoccupies them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kissed ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn while he was dead, and it is as if I can see his tears flowing down his cheeks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a funeral was brought to him and those following it seemed few, he would arrange them in three rows, then pray over it, and say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No three rows of Muslims form over a deceased person except that it becomes obligatory [for him, i.e. Paradise]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ followed a funeral, he would not sit until the body was placed in the grave. A Jewish rabbi approached him and said, "This is how we do it, Muḥammad."
He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat down and said, "Do the opposite of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Uḥud, and we said,
"O Messenger of Allah, digging a grave for every person is difficult for us." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Dig, make [the graves] deep, and do it well,
and bury two or three in one grave." They said,
"Whom should we put first, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Put first the one who knows the most Qurʾān." He said:
So my father was the third of three in one grave.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever swears and says, 'I am free of Islam,' then if he is lying, he is as he said,
and if he is truthful, he will never return to Islam safe."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He
asked the Prophet ﷺ about a sister of his who had vowed to walk barefoot and without a head covering. The Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"Command her to cover her head, to ride, and to fast three days."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In Medina we used to sell and buy wasqs [of goods], and we called ourselves brokers (samāsirah), and the people called us that. One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and gave us a name better than the one we had called ourselves and the people had called us. He said:
"O assembly of merchants, oaths and lying attend your sales, so mix it with charity (ṣadaqah)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah in Tihāmah, the people got hold of some camels and sheep, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at the rear of the group. The first of them hurried, slaughtered, and set up the cooking pots. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came up to them and ordered the pots to be overturned, and they were upset. Then he distributed [the animals] among them, counting ten sheep as equal to one camel. While they were like that, a camel bolted, and there were only a few horses among the people. They went after it but it wore them out, so a man shot it with an arrow and Allah stopped it. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"These animals have wild traits like the wild traits of wild beasts. So whatever of them overpowers you, do this with it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about hunting, and he said:
"When you send your arrow or your dog, and you mention the name of Allah, and your arrow kills [the game], eat."
He said: What if it is gone from me for a night, Messenger of Allah? He said:
"If you find your arrow and do not find any trace of anything else on it, eat; but if it fell into the water, do not eat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: Messenger of Allah, I send my dog and it catches the game, and I do not find anything to slaughter it with, so I slaughter it with a sharp stone or a stick. He said:
