"Let the blood flow with whatever you wish, and mention the name of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Plundering is not lawful, nor is any predatory animal with a fang lawful, nor is the animal that is tied up and shot at [for sport] lawful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They

went on the expedition to Khaybar with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while the people were hungry. They found domestic donkeys there and the people slaughtered some of them. This was reported to the Prophet ﷺ, so he ordered ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who announced among the people:
"Beware! The meat of domestic donkeys is not lawful for whoever bears witness that I am the Messenger of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ through some of the mountain passes of al-Rawḥāʾ, and they were in the sacred state of iḥrām, there was a wild donkey that had been wounded. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Leave it, for its owner will soon come to it."
Then a man from Bahz came, who was the one who had wounded the donkey, and said: Messenger of Allah, it is yours to dispose of as you wish.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered Abū Bakr to divide it among the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He hunted a wild donkey and brought it to his companions, who were in the sacred state of iḥrām while he was not. We ate from it, and some of them said to others: If only we had asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it. So we asked him, and he said: "You have done well." Then he said to us:
"Do you have any of it with you?" We said: Yes. He said: "Then give it to us as a gift."
So we brought him some of it, and he ate from it while in the sacred state of iḥrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Mūsā
was brought a chicken, and a man among the people withdrew. He said: What is the matter with you? He said: I saw it eating something filthy, so I swore that I would not eat it.
Abū Mūsā said: Come near and eat, for I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eat it.
And he ordered him to make expiation for his oath.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent us with Abū ʿUbaydah on an expedition, and our provisions ran out. We passed by a fish that the sea had cast ashore, and we wanted to eat from it, but Abū ʿUbaydah forbade us. Then he said: We are the envoys of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and are in the cause of Allah, so eat.
We ate from it for days. When we came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we told him, and he said:
"If anything of it is left with you, send it to us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A physician
mentioned a frog in a medicine in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade killing it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ slaughtered by nahr on the day of the Aḍḥā in Madinah. He said: And when he did not slaughter by nahr, he would slaughter by dhabḥ at the prayer ground.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We offered the sacrifice with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a young ram of sheep.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were on a journey when the Aḍḥā came, and a man among us began buying a mature animal in exchange for two or three young ones. A man from Muzaynah said to us: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey when this day came, and a man began seeking a mature animal in exchange for two or three young ones. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The young ram suffices in what the mature animal suffices."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The last instruction the Prophet ﷺ gave me, when he appointed me over Ṭāʾif, was that he said to me:
"O ʿUthmān, be brief in prayer, and gauge the people by the weakest of them, for among them are the old and the young, the sick, the traveler from afar, and the one with a need."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed Allah and His angels send blessings upon those who join the rows, and whoever closes a gap, Allah raises him one degree because of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to ask forgiveness for the front row three times, and for the second row once.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were forbidden from forming rows
between the pillars during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we were driven away from them forcefully.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out until we came to the Prophet ﷺ, and we pledged allegiance to him and prayed behind him. Then we prayed another prayer behind him, and when he had finished the prayer he saw a man praying alone behind the row.
He said: So the Prophet of Allah ﷺ stood by him when he finished and said, "Repeat your prayer,
for there is no prayer for the one who prays alone behind the row."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ that the left side of the mosque had been left empty. So the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever fills the left side of the mosque will have written for him a double share of reward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished circling the House, he came to the Station of Ibrāhīm, and ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is the station of our father Ibrāhīm, about which Allah, Glorified is He, said: {And take the Station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer}."
Al-Walīd said: I said to Mālik, "Is this how he recited it: {And take the Station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer}?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ toward Bayt al-Maqdis for eighteen months, and the direction of prayer was changed to the Kaaba two months after he entered Medina. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis, he would often turn his face toward the sky, and Allah knew from the heart of His Prophet ﷺ that he longed for the Kaaba. Then Jibrīl ascended, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ followed him with his gaze as he ascended between the heaven and the earth, looking for what he would bring him. So Allah revealed: {We see the turning of your face toward the heaven} [to the end of] the verse. Then someone came to us and said that the direction of prayer had been changed to the Kaaba, while we had prayed two rakʿahs toward Bayt al-Maqdis and were bowing. So we turned and built upon what had passed of our prayer. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Jibrīl, what is the state of our prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis?"
So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {And Allah would never let your faith go to waste}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and the sky became cloudy and the direction of prayer was unclear to us. So we prayed and marked our positions. When the sun rose, we found that we had prayed in a direction other than the qiblah. We mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, so Allah revealed: {Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw Shabath ibn Ribʿī spit in front of him, and he said, "O Shabath, do not spit in front of you, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to forbid that, and he said:
'When a man stands to pray, Allah turns toward him with His Face until he turns away or commits some evil breach of his purity.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spat into his garment while he was in prayer, then rubbed it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed on a mat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray on his carpet.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to us and led us in prayer in the mosque of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal, and I saw him place his hands on his garment when he prostrated.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed among Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal wearing a cloak wrapped around himself, placing his hands on it to protect them from the coldness of the pebbles.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My grandfather Aws used to pray and would gesture to me while in prayer, and I would give him his sandals. He would say, "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray in his sandals."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We certainly saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray in sandals and in leather socks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in the gathering of Banū Salimah, and I was the youngest of them.
They said, "Who will ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for us about the Night of Qadr?" That was on the morning of the twenty-first of Ramadan.
So I went out and met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the Maghrib prayer. Then I stood at the door of his house, and he passed by me and said, "Come in."
So I entered, and his dinner was brought. He saw me holding back from it because of how little there was. When he had finished, he said, "Hand me my sandals."
Then he stood up and I stood with him, and he said,
"Do you have a need?"
I said, "Yes. A group from Banū Salimah sent me to you to ask you about the Night of Qadr." He said, "What night is it tonight?"
I said, "The twenty-second." He said, "It is tonight."
Then he turned back and said, "Or the next one."
He meant the night of the twenty-third.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have a desert dwelling where I stay, and I pray there, praise be to Allah. So command me to a night on which I should come down to this mosque." He said,
"Come down on the night of the twenty-third."

I said to his son, "How did your father act?" He said, "He would enter the mosque when he had prayed the ʿAṣr prayer and would not leave it for any need until he had prayed the Fajr prayer. When he had prayed Fajr, he would find his mount at the door of the mosque, sit on it, and return to his desert dwelling."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us,
"Seek it on the night of the seventeenth of Ramadan, and the night of the twenty-first, and the night of the twenty-third." Then he fell silent.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ concerning the Night of Qadr, he said,
"The Night of Qadr is the night of the twenty-seventh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the Night of Qadr while I was listening, and he said,
"It is in every Ramadan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me,
"Fast three days of every month, and recite the Qur'an in a month."
I tried to reduce it, and he reduced it for me, then he said,
"Fast one day and break the fast one day."
ʿAṭāʾ said: We differed concerning my father; some of us said seven days and some of us said five.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me,
"Recite the Qur'an in a month."
I said, "I have strength." He said,
"Recite it in three."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim asked me, "In how many days do you recite the Qur'an?" I said, "I do not divide it into portions."
Nāfiʿ said to me, "Do not say, 'I do not divide it into portions,' for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
'I recited a portion of the Qur'an.'"
He said: I think he mentioned it from al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and al-Aswad,
both said: A man came to Ibn Masʿūd and said, "I recite the Mufaṣṣal in one rakʿah."

He said, "Is it a rapid recitation like the reciting of poetry, and scattering like the scattering of bad dates? But the Prophet ﷺ used to recite pairs of similar surahs in one rakʿah: ar-Raḥmān and an-Najm in one rakʿah; Iqtarabat and al-Ḥāqqah in one rakʿah; aṭ-Ṭūr and adh-Dhāriyāt in one rakʿah; idhā waqaʿat and Nūn in one rakʿah; Saʾala sāʾil and an-Nāziʿāt in one rakʿah; Wayl lil-muṭaffifīn and ʿAbasa in one rakʿah; al-Muddaththir and al-Muzzammil in one rakʿah; Hal atā and Lā uqsimu bi-yawmil-qiyāmah in one rakʿah;
and ʿAmma yatasāʾalūn and al-Mursalāt in one rakʿah; and ad-Dukhān and idhash-shamsu kuwwirat in one rakʿah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Whoever stands in prayer with ten verses will not be recorded among the heedless; whoever stands with a hundred verses will be recorded among the devout; and whoever stands with a thousand verses will be recorded among those who receive great reward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "Teach me to recite, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"Recite three of those that begin with Alif Lām Rā."
The man said, "I have grown old, my heart is hardened, and my tongue is heavy." He said,
"Then recite three of those that begin with Ḥā Mīm."
He said the same as he had said before. So he said,
"Recite three of the Musabbiḥāt."
He said the same as he had said before, then the man said, "O Messenger of Allah, teach me a comprehensive surah."
So the Prophet ﷺ taught him {When the earth is shaken} until he finished it.
The man said, "By the One who sent you with the truth, I will never add to it." Then the man turned away, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "The little man has succeeded." He said it twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not perform prostration in any of the Mufaṣṣal since he moved to Medina.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The believers will gather on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be inspired in them—or they will be moved to think (Saʿīd was unsure)—and they will say, 'If only we would seek intercession with our Lord, so that He may relieve us from our place.' So they will come to Adam and say, 'You are Adam, the father of mankind. Allah created you with His Hand and made His angels prostrate to you. So intercede for us with your Lord, that He may relieve us from this place of ours.'

He will say, 'I am not in a position for that'—and he will mention to them the sin he committed and feel ashamed of it—'but go to Noah, for he was the first messenger Allah sent to the people of the earth.' So they will go to him, and he will say, 'I am not in a position for that'—and he will mention that he asked his Lord about something of which he had no knowledge, and feel ashamed of it—'but go to the Khalīl of the Most Merciful, Abraham.' So they will go to him, and he will say, 'I am not in a position for that, but go to Moses, a servant to whom Allah spoke and whom He gave the Torah.'

So they will go to him, and he will say, 'I am not in a position for that'—and he will mention his killing of a person other than in retribution for a life—'but go to Jesus, the servant of Allah and His Messenger, His Word and a spirit from Him.'
So they will go to him, and he will say, 'I am not in a position for that, but go to Muhammad, a servant whose past and future sins Allah has forgiven.'
He said: "So they will come to me and I will set out." He said: Then he mentioned this phrase from al-Ḥasan.
He said: "And I will walk between two rows of believers."
He said: Then he returned to the hadith of Anas and said:

"I will ask permission to come before my Lord, and I will be given permission. When I see Him, I will fall down in prostration, and He will leave me as long as Allah wills to leave me. Then it will be said, 'Raise your head, Muhammad. Speak and you will be heard; ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' So I will praise Him with a praise that He teaches me, then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return a second time, and when I see Him I will fall down in prostration, and He will leave me as long as Allah wills to leave me. Then it will be said to me, 'Raise your head, Muhammad. Speak and you will be heard; ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' So I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise that He teaches me, then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return a third time, and when I see my Lord I will fall down in prostration, and He will leave me as long as Allah wills to leave me. Then it will be said, 'Raise your head, Muhammad. Speak and you will be heard; ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' So I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise that He teaches me, then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return a fourth time and say, 'My Lord, no one is left except those whom the Qurʾān has confined [to the Fire].'"
Qatādah said, following this hadith: And Anas ibn Mālik told us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever said 'There is no god but Allah' and had in his heart goodness equal to the weight of a barley grain will be brought out of the Fire; and whoever said 'There is no god but Allah' and had in his heart goodness equal to the weight of a wheat grain will be brought out of the Fire; and whoever said 'There is no god but Allah' and had in his heart goodness equal to the weight of an atom will be brought out of the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My brother Wahb ibn Munabbih said: This is what Abū Hurayrah narrated to us from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Then he mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The prayer of any one of you is not accepted when he has broken his wudūʾ until he performs ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was not Abū ʿUbaydah who mentioned it, but ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from his father,
that he heard ʿAbd Allāh
say: The Prophet ﷺ went to relieve himself,
and he ordered me to bring him three stones. I found two stones,
and I looked for a third but could not find it, so I took a piece of dung and brought it to him.
He took the two stones and threw away the dung, saying, "This is unclean."
And Ibrāhīm ibn Yūsuf said, from his father, from Abū Isḥāq: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to me
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were in the mosque with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a Bedouin came and stood up to urinate in the mosque. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Stop! Stop!"
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not interrupt him; leave him alone."
So they left him until he had finished urinating.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him and said to him:
"These mosques are not suitable for any of this urine or filth. They are only for the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for prayer, and for the recitation of the Qurʾān."
Or as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said.
He said: Then he ordered a man from the people, who came with a bucket of water and poured it over it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, [said] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to be brought infants; he would pray for blessings upon them and rub their palates with chewed dates. Once an infant was brought to him and urinated on him, so he asked for water and poured it over the urine, and he did not wash it [thoroughly].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed, Allah has placed the truth upon the tongue and the heart of ʿUmar."

And Ibn ʿUmar said: Whenever a matter came upon the people and they gave their opinion on it, and ʿUmar gave his opinion on it—or he said, Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb—(Khārijah doubted which), the Qurʾān was revealed concerning it in line with what ʿUmar had said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"O Allah, strengthen Islam with Abū Jahl ibn Hishām or with ʿUmar."
He said: So the next morning ʿUmar went early to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and accepted Islam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar said to Abū Bakr: O best of people after the Messenger of Allah!
Abū Bakr said: As for you, if you say that, then I have indeed heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The sun has not risen upon a man better than ʿUmar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I do not think that a man who disparages Abū Bakr and ʿUmar loves the Prophet ﷺ.
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If there were to be a prophet after me, it would be ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith; we do not know it except through the narration of Mishrah ibn Hāʿān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"I entered Paradise and there I was at a palace of gold. I said, 'Whose palace is this?' They said, 'It belongs to a young man of Quraysh.' I thought that I was the one, so I said, 'And who is he?' They said, 'ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.'"
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose in the morning, called Bilāl, and said:

"O Bilāl, by what did you precede me to Paradise? I have never entered Paradise but that I heard your footsteps ahead of me. Last night I entered Paradise and heard your footsteps ahead of me. I came upon a square, lofty palace of gold and said, 'Whose palace is this?' They said, 'It belongs to a man of the Arabs.' I said, 'I am an Arab. Whose palace is this?' They said, 'It belongs to a man of Quraysh.' I said, 'I am a Qurashī. Whose palace is this?' They said, 'It belongs to a man of the nation of Muḥammad.' I said, 'I am Muḥammad. Whose palace is this?' They said, 'It belongs to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.'"

Bilāl said: O Messenger of Allah, I have never called the adhān without praying two rakʿahs afterward, and I have never broken my wuḍūʾ without performing ablution right then, and I considered that I owed Allah two rakʿahs.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By these two."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on one of his military expeditions. When he returned, a black slave girl came and said: O Messenger of Allah, I had vowed that if Allah brought you back safely, I would beat the tambourine and sing before you.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"If you vowed, then beat it; and if not, then do not."

So she began to beat it. Abū Bakr entered while she was beating it, then ʿAlī entered while she was beating it, then ʿUthmān entered while she was beating it, then ʿUmar entered, and she threw the tambourine beneath her and sat on it.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed, the Devil fears you, O ʿUmar. I was sitting while she was beating it, and Abū Bakr entered while she was beating it, then ʿAlī entered while she was beating it, then ʿUthmān entered while she was beating it. But when you entered, O ʿUmar, she threw down the tambourine."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting when we heard noise and the voices of boys. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, and there was an Abyssinian woman dancing with the boys around her. He said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, come and look."
So I came and rested my chin on the shoulder of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I began to look at her from between his shoulder and his head. He said to me:
"Have you not had enough? Have you not had enough?"
She said: I kept saying, "No," in order to see my standing with him, when ʿUmar appeared. She said: The people dispersed from around her. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I am looking at the devils of mankind and jinn; they have fled from ʿUmar." She said: So I went back.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I am the first for whom the earth will be split open, then Abū Bakr, then ʿUmar. Then I will come to the people of al-Baqīʿ, and they will be gathered with me. Then I will wait for the people of Makkah until I am gathered between the two sanctuaries."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"A man of the people of Paradise will appear before you."
Then Abū Bakr appeared. Then he said:
"A man of the people of Paradise will appear before you." Then ʿUmar appeared.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with my father at al-Qāʿ of Namirah when a group of riders passed by us and stopped at the side of the road. My father said to me, "Stay with the flock until I go to these people and ask them."

He said: He went out, and I came closer, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The time of prayer came, so I prayed with them, and I kept looking at the whiteness of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ armpits whenever he prostrated.
Ibn Mājah said: People say ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, while Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah said that people say ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked ʿĀʾishah about the fasting of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said: "He used to make a point of fasting on Mondays and Thursdays."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He combined Hajj and ʿUmrah and performed a single circumambulation, and he said: "This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned to him a woman I was seeking to marry, and he said:
"Go and look at her, for that is more likely to create harmony between the two of you."
So I went to a woman of the Anṣār and asked her parents for her hand, and I told them what the Prophet ﷺ had said.
It seemed that they disliked that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ conquered Makkah, he said in his sermon:
"For wounds that expose the bone, [the blood money is] five [camels] each."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he mentioned
a statement with the same meaning, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The blood money for the people of the covenant is half the blood money of the Muslims."
They are the Jews and the Christians.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ with some women of the Anṣār to pledge allegiance to him, and we said: "O Messenger of Allah, we pledge allegiance to you that we will not associate anything with Allah, we will not steal, we will not commit adultery, we will not bring a slander that we fabricate between our hands and our feet, and we will not disobey you in what is right." He said:
"In what you are able and capable of."
She said: We said, "Allah and His Messenger are more merciful to us. Come, let us pledge allegiance to you, O Messenger of Allah."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I do not shake hands with women. My word to a hundred women is like my word to one woman," or he said, "like my word to a single woman."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I bear witness about ʿImrān that he narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade wearing silk, wearing gold rings, and drinking from the green jars.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When Allah has saved the believers from the Fire and they are safe, none of you will argue more fiercely with his companion over a right he has in this world than the believers will argue with their Lord over their brothers who have been admitted to the Fire.
He said: They will say, 'Our Lord, our brothers used to pray with us, fast with us, and perform Hajj with us, yet You have admitted them to the Fire.'

He will say, 'Go and bring out whomever you recognize among them.' So they will come to them and recognize them by their features, for the Fire does not consume their features. Some of them the Fire will have seized up to the middle of their shins, and some up to their ankles. They will bring them out and say, 'Our Lord, we have brought out those You commanded us to.'

Then He will say, 'Bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of a dinar of faith,' then 'whoever has in his heart the weight of half a dinar,' then 'whoever has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed.'"

Abū Saʿīd said: Whoever does not believe this, let him recite: {Indeed, Allah does not wrong [anyone] even by the weight of an atom, and if it is a good deed He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade plucking gray hair and said:
"It is the light of the Muslim."
He said: This is a ḥasan hadith. It has been narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith and more than one other, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said — and [in another chain] Ibn Numayr narrated to us:
My father and Muḥammad ibn Bishr narrated to us,
both saying: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Qays,
who said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no envy except in two cases: a man whom Allah has given wealth and empowers him to spend it away in the cause of truth, and a man whom Allah has given wisdom, so he judges by it and teaches it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray in sheep pens,
then afterwards I heard him say: He used to pray in sheep pens before the mosque was built.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Idrīs and Abū Usāmah, all from Burayd,
from Abū Burdah,
from Abū Mūsā,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The believer to the believer is like a building, each part strengthening the other."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I sneezed, so I said: "Praise be to Allah, abundant, good and blessed praise, blessed upon him, as our Lord loves and is pleased with."
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished the prayer, he turned and said:
"Who was the one speaking during the prayer?"
No one spoke. Then he said it a second time:
"Who was the one speaking during the prayer?"
Again no one spoke. Then he said it a third time:
"Who was the one speaking during the prayer?"
Rifāʿah ibn Rāfiʿ ibn ʿAfrāʾ said: "It was I, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "What did you say?"
He said: I said: "Praise be to Allah, abundant, good and blessed praise, blessed upon him, as our Lord loves and is pleased with." Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, thirty-odd angels raced to it, [each wanting to be] the one to carry it up."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade buying and selling in the mosque, announcing a lost item in it, and reciting poetry in it. He also forbade sitting in gatherings [in circles] before the prayer on Friday.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṭalq ibn ʿAlī visited us one day in Ramadan and stayed with us until evening and broke his fast. Then he stood in prayer with us that night and prayed Witr with us. Then he went down to his own mosque and led his companions in prayer, until, when it was time for Witr, he put forward a man and said: "Lead your companions in Witr, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'There are not two Witr prayers in one night.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I performed Hajj with ʿUmar, and I heard him say at Jamʿ: "Indeed, the Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge from five things:

'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from miserliness and cowardice, and I seek refuge in You from an evil old age, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of the heart, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, with part of the beginning of this hadith, he said:

"If you have two hundred dirhams and a year passes over them, then five dirhams are due on them, and nothing is due from you—meaning on gold—until you have twenty dinars. When you have twenty dinars and a year passes over them, then half a dinar is due on them, and whatever exceeds that is calculated accordingly."
He said: I do not know whether ʿAlī said "is calculated accordingly"
or whether he attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ:
"There is no zakāh on wealth until a year has passed over it."
Except that Jarīr—Ibn Wahb said—added in the hadith from the Prophet ﷺ:
"There is no zakāh on wealth until a year has passed over it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet's ﷺ zakāh collector came to us, so I took his hand and read in his covenant: "Separate [animals] are not to be combined, nor combined ones separated, for fear of the charity (ṣadaqah)."

Then a man came to him with a large, well-formed she-camel, but he refused to take it. So he brought another, lesser than it, and he took it and said: "What earth will bear me and what sky will shade me when I come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ having taken the best camels of a Muslim man?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he was asked about fruit hanging [on the tree], and he said:

"Whoever takes some with his mouth out of need, without carrying any away in his garment, there is nothing upon him. But whoever leaves with some of it, he must pay a penalty of twice its value, and be punished. And whoever steals some of it after it has been brought into the drying-place and it reaches the price of a shield, the hand is to be cut."
He also mentioned stray camels and sheep, as others have mentioned. He said: And he was asked about lost property, and he said:

"What is found in a well-traveled road or a large inhabited town, announce it for a year. If its owner comes, hand it over to him; and if he does not come, it is yours. And what is found in ruins—meaning—on it and on buried treasure is the fifth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that his father, Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith, and al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Rabīʿah and to al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās: "Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and say to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, we have reached the age you see, and we wish to marry. And you, O Messenger of Allah, are the most righteous of people and the one who best maintains family ties. Our fathers do not have the means to pay the bridal gift on our behalf, so appoint us, O Messenger of Allah, over the charity collections, and we will deliver to you what the collectors deliver, and we will take whatever benefit there is in it.'"
He said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib came to us while we were in that state and said to us: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has said:
'No, by Allah, we will not appoint any of you over the charity.'"
Rabīʿah said to him: "This is of your doing. You have obtained a marriage tie with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we did not envy you for it."

So ʿAlī threw his cloak down, then lay down on it and said: "I am Abū Ḥasan, the seasoned one. By Allah, I will not leave until your two sons return to you with the answer to what you sent them to the Prophet ﷺ about."

ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said: So I and al-Faḍl set off to the door of the Prophet's ﷺ room, and we found the Ẓuhr prayer had already begun, so we prayed with the people. Then I and al-Faḍl hurried to the door of the Prophet's ﷺ room, and on that day he was with Zaynab bint Jaḥsh. We stood at the door until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came. He took hold of my ear and the ear of al-Faḍl, then said: "Bring out what you are hiding." Then he entered and gave permission to me and al-Faḍl, and we entered. We each waited for the other to speak for a little while, then I spoke to him, or al-Faḍl spoke to him (ʿAbdullāh was unsure which). He said: he spoke to him about the matter that our fathers had commanded us with. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent for a while and raised his gaze toward the ceiling of the house, until we thought it was taking long and that he would not reply to us at all, until we saw Zaynab gesturing from behind the screen with her hand, meaning that we should not rush and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was considering our matter. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lowered his head and said to us:
"This charity is only the impurities of people, and it is not lawful for Muḥammad nor for the family of Muḥammad. Call Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith for me."
So Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith was called for him, and he said:
"O Nawfal, marry off ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib."
So Nawfal married me off. Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Call Maḥmiyah ibn Jazʾ for me."
He was a man of Banū Zubayd whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had appointed over the fifths. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Maḥmiyah: "Marry off al-Faḍl."
So he married him off. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Get up and pay on their behalf from the fifth such and such an amount."
ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥārith did not specify it to me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "No fault is to be found with the one who fasts nor with the one who breaks his fast. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted while traveling and also broke his fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that a man

came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, how do you fast?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry at his words. When ʿUmar saw that, he said: "We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muḥammad as Prophet. We seek refuge in Allah from the anger of Allah and the anger of His Messenger."
ʿUmar kept repeating it until the anger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ subsided.
Then the man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about one who fasts all of time?" He said:
"He has neither fasted nor broken his fast." Musaddad said:
"He did not fast and did not break the fast, or: he has neither fasted nor broken the fast." Ghaylān was unsure.
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about one who fasts two days and breaks his fast one day?" He said:
"Is anyone able to do that?"
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about one who fasts one day and breaks his fast one day?" He said:
"That is the fast of Dāwūd."
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about one who fasts one day and breaks his fast two days?" He said:
"I would love to be given the strength for that."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Three days of every month, and Ramadan to Ramadan, that is fasting all of time. As for the fast of the Day of ʿArafah, I hope from Allah that it will expiate the year before it and the year after it. And as for the fast of the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, I hope from Allah that it will expiate the year before it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that they had sheep grazing at Salʿ,
and one of our slave girls saw that one of our sheep was dying,
so she broke a stone and slaughtered it with it.
He said to them, "Do not eat it until I ask the Prophet ﷺ,
or until I send someone to ask the Prophet ﷺ."
He asked the Prophet ﷺ about that, or he sent someone, and he commanded him to eat it.
ʿUbaydullāh said: It pleases me that she was a slave girl, and that she slaughtered [it].
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man had a claim against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he spoke harshly to him, so the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ wanted to deal with him. The Prophet ﷺ said: "
The one who is owed a right has the right to speak." Then he said to them: "Buy him a camel of the same age and give it to him."
They said: "We can only find one that is better than his camel in age." He said: "
Then buy it and give it to him, for among the best of you, or the best of you, are those who are best in repaying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ibn Shihāb [said]: ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr claimed that Marwān
and al-Miswar ibn Makhramah
informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up when the delegation of Hawāzin came to him as Muslims,
and they asked him to return to them their property and their captives.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "
You see who is with me,
and the most beloved speech to me is the most truthful.
So choose one of the two: either the captives or the property.
I had been waiting for you."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had delayed [the matter] for them for some ten nights or more,
when he returned from Ṭāʾif.
When it became clear to them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would return to them only one of the two, they said: "We choose our captives."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among the Muslims,
praised Allah as He deserves, and then said: "To proceed:
Your brothers have come to us repenting,
and I have decided to return their captives to them.
So whoever among you is willing to do that willingly, let him do so,
and whoever among you wishes to keep his share,
until we give it to him from the first spoils Allah grants us, let him do so."
The people said: "We have willingly agreed to that, O Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
We do not know which of you has permitted it and which of you has not, so go back until your representatives bring your decision to us."
So the people went back and their representatives spoke with them, then they returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him that they had willingly agreed and given permission.
This is what has reached me about the captives of Hawāzin.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led the dawn prayer,
then turned to the people and said: "
While a man was driving a cow, he mounted it and struck it, and it said: 'We were not created for this,
we were only created for plowing.'"
The people said: "Glory be to Allah! A cow speaking!" He said: "
I believe this, and so do Abū Bakr and ʿUmar," though they were not there. "And while a man was with his sheep, a wolf attacked and carried off a sheep from them,
so he pursued it until he seemed to have rescued it from the wolf.
The wolf said to him: 'You rescued it from me, but who will protect it on the day of the predators,
the day when it will have no shepherd but me?'"
The people said: "Glory be to Allah! A wolf speaking!" He said: "
I believe this, and so do Abū Bakr and ʿUmar."
And they were not there.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave Khaybar [to be cultivated] for half of what it produced of fruit or crops. He used to give his wives each year one hundred wasqs: eighty wasqs of dates and twenty wasqs of barley. When ʿUmar took charge and divided Khaybar, he gave the wives of the Prophet ﷺ the choice of having land and water allotted to them, or having the wasqs guaranteed to them every year. They differed: some of them chose the land and water, and some chose the wasqs each year. ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah were among those who chose the land and water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They used to cultivate it for a third, a quarter, or a half, so the Prophet ﷺ said: "
Whoever has land, let him cultivate it or lend it,
and if he does not do so, let him keep his land."
Al-Rabīʿ ibn Nāfiʿ Abū Tawbah said: Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from Yaḥyā,
from Abū Salamah,
from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Whoever has land, let him cultivate it or lend it to his brother,
and if he refuses, let him keep his land."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever says in the morning: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things,' will have the reward of freeing a slave from the descendants of Ishmael; ten good deeds will be recorded for him, ten sins will be erased from him, he will be raised ten degrees, and he will be protected from Satan until evening. And if he says it in the evening, he will have the like of that until morning."
He said in the hadith of Ḥammād: A man saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a dream and said, "O Messenger of Allah, Abū ʿAyyāsh narrates from you such and such." He said:
"Abū ʿAyyāsh has spoken the truth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever says in the morning: 'O Allah, we have entered the morning calling You to witness, and calling to witness the bearers of Your Throne, Your angels, and all Your creation, that You are Allah, there is no god but You alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger,'
Allah will forgive him whatever sin he commits that day. And if he says it in the evening, Allah will forgive him whatever sin he commits that night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out on a rainy night of intense darkness looking for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to lead us in prayer. We found him, and he said, "Have you prayed?"
I did not say anything, so he said, "Say it."
I did not say anything. Then he said, "Say it."
I still did not say anything. Then he said, "Say it."
So I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what should I say?" He said:
"'Say: He is Allah, the One' and the two sūrahs of refuge, three times when you enter the evening and three times when you enter the morning; they will suffice you against everything."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wind is from the mercy of Allah."
Salamah said: The mercy of Allah brings mercy and brings punishment. So when you see it, do not curse it; ask Allah for its good and seek refuge with Allah from its evil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ give the call to prayer in the ear of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī when Fāṭimah gave birth to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Let people stop boasting about their forefathers who have died; they are but coals of Hell. Otherwise they will surely be more insignificant to Allah than the dung beetle that rolls dung with its nose. Allah has removed from you the arrogance of the Jāhiliyyah. There are only a God-fearing believer and a wretched sinner. All people are children of Adam, and Adam was created from dust."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Uḥud. I struck a man of the polytheists and said, "Take that from me, I am the Persian boy!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to me and said:
"Why did you not say, 'Take that from me, I am the Anṣārī boy'?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Intercede and you will be rewarded, for I may want to do a matter and then delay it so that you intercede and are rewarded. For the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Intercede and you will be rewarded."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man from Banū Salimah came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, is there any kindness left that I can show my parents after their death?" He said:
"Yes: praying for them, seeking forgiveness for them, fulfilling their pledges after them, maintaining the ties of kinship that exist only through them, and honoring their friend."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say during the illness in which he died:
"Prayer, and those whom your right hands possess."
He kept repeating it until his tongue could no longer express it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, how many times should we forgive the servant?" He remained silent. The man repeated the question, and he remained silent. The third time, he said:
"Forgive him seventy times every day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah sent him with milk, young gazelle meat, and small cucumbers to the Prophet ﷺ, while the Prophet ﷺ was at the upper part of the valley. He said: I entered upon him without giving greetings of peace and without asking permission, so the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Go back and say: 'Peace be upon you, may I enter?'"
That was after Ṣafwān had become Muslim.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "Peace be upon you."
He returned the greeting, then the man sat down. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Ten."
Then another came and said, "Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah."
He returned the greeting, and the man sat down. He said, "Twenty."
Then another came and said, "Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings."
He returned the greeting, and the man sat down. He said, "Thirty."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
There is no contagion, no bird omen, no owl omen, and no Ṣafar omen,
and flee from the leper as you would flee from a lion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us and said: "
Nothing infects anything else."
A Bedouin said, "O Messenger of Allah, a camel with mange on its rump—we rub it with tar, yet it gives mange to all the camels."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Then who gave the first one the mange? There is no contagion and no Ṣafar. Allah created every soul and wrote its life, its provision, and its afflictions."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah about ruqyah (healing by recitation),
and she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted ruqyah for a family of the Anṣār for any poisonous sting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two women of Hudhayl fought, and one of them struck the other with a stone and killed her and what was in her womb. They brought their dispute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the blood-money for her fetus was a ghurrah, a male or female slave, and he ruled that the blood-money for the woman was to be paid by her ʿāqilah (paternal kin), and that her children and those with them would inherit from her.

Ḥamal ibn Mālik ibn al-Nābighah al-Hudhalī said, "O Messenger of Allah, how can I pay for one who did not drink, did not eat, did not speak, and did not cry out at birth? Such a case should be nullified." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
This man is one of the brothers of the soothsayers."
[He said this] because of the rhymed speech he had uttered.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
saw upon Umm Kulthūm, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a striped garment of sīrāʾ.
He said: Sīrāʾ is [cloth] striped with silk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Anas ibn Mālik, "How was the sandal of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "Each had two straps."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the gold ring.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a ring of gold, set its stone toward the inside of his palm, and had engraved on it: "
Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah."
Then people made gold rings, and when he saw that they had made them, he threw it away and said: "
I will never wear it."
Then he made a ring of silver, engraved on it: "
Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah."
Afterwards Abū Bakr wore the ring, then after Abū Bakr ʿUmar wore it, then after him ʿUthmān wore it, until it fell into the well of Arīs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw on the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a silver ring for one day.
Then people made rings of silver and wore them,
so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ threw away his ring,
and the people threw away their rings.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed men who imitate women,
and women who imitate men.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Zuhrī said: I memorized it as surely as you are here, from Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said: A man peered through a hole in the room of the Prophet ﷺ, while the Prophet ﷺ had a comb with which he was scratching his head. He said: "
If I knew that you were looking, I would poke it into your eye.
Seeking permission was only made obligatory because of the sight."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah,] the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The makers of these images will be punished on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to them: Bring to life what you have created."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever claims to have had a dream he did not see
will be charged with tying together two grains of barley, and he will never be able to do so.
Whoever listens to the conversation of people who dislike it or flee from it,
molten lead will be poured into his ears on the Day of Resurrection.
And whoever makes an image
will be punished and charged with blowing a soul into it, and he will not be able to blow."
Sufyān said: Ayyūb connected it for us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Among the greatest of major sins is for a man to curse his parents."
It was asked, "O Messenger of Allah, how can a man curse his parents?" He said: "
He curses another man's father, and that man curses his father; and he curses another man's mother, and that man curses his mother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim informed him that he
heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "
One who severs [family ties] will not enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kissed al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī while al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis al-Tamīmī was sitting with him.
Al-Aqraʿ said, "I have ten children and I have never kissed any of them."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at him and then said: "
One who shows no mercy will be shown no mercy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ once prayed two rak'ahs in her house after the afternoon prayer, and she mentioned that to him, so he said:
"They are two rak'ahs that I used to pray after the midday prayer, but I was kept busy from them until I had prayed the afternoon prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The call to prayer is nineteen phrases, and the iqāmah is seventeen phrases."
Then Abū Maḥdhūrah counted them out: nineteen, and seventeen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever gives the call to prayer for seven years, seeking reward from Allah, Allah will write for him freedom from the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with the Prophet ﷺ on his Hajj, and I prayed the dawn prayer with him in the Mosque of al-Khayf.
He said: When he finished his prayer and turned around, there were two men at the back of the people who had not prayed with him. He said, "Bring them to me."
They were brought, their shoulders trembling [with fear], and he said:
"What prevented you from praying with us?"
They said: O Messenger of Allah, we had already prayed in our saddles [at our camp].
He said: "Do not do that. If you have prayed in your camp and then come to a mosque where a congregation is [praying], pray with them, for it will count for you as a voluntary prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Anas and prayed with one of the governors. The people pushed us until we stood and prayed between two pillars. Anas began to step back and said: We used to avoid this in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say the takbīr at every rising and lowering, standing and sitting, and so did Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said to us: The knees have been made a sunnah for you, so take hold of the knees.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to lead us in prayer and then turn away to both sides, to his right and to his left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the last evening prayer (ʿishāʾ) "By the sun and its brightness" and similar surahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah bint al-Ḥusayn, from her grandmother,
Fāṭimah the Elder, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque, he would send blessings and peace upon Muḥammad and say:
"My Lord, forgive me my sins and open for me the doors of Your mercy."
And when he went out, he would send blessings and peace upon Muḥammad and say:
"My Lord, forgive me my sins and open for me the doors of Your bounty."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to sleep in the mosque in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when we were young men.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What is between the east and the west is a qiblah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade praying in seven places: the rubbish dump, the slaughterhouse, the graveyard, the middle of the road, the bathhouse, the resting places of camels, and on top of the House of Allah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The last prayer that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed with the people, he prayed wrapped in a single garment, behind Abū Bakr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to my father: O my father, you prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib here in Kufa for about five years. Did they recite the qunūt? He said: My son, it is an innovation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The poor came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, the rich pray as we pray and fast as we fast, and they have wealth with which they free slaves and give charity. He said:

"When you have prayed, say: Subḥān Allāh thirty-three times, al-ḥamdu lillāh thirty-three times, and Allāhu akbar thirty-four times, and lā ilāha illā Allāh ten times. By this you will overtake those who preceded you, and no one after you will overtake you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ missed the four rak'ahs before the midday prayer, he would pray them after the two rak'ahs following the midday prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever prays six rak'ahs after the sunset prayer without speaking any evil between them, they will be equal for him to twelve years of worship."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: The witr is not obligatory, nor is it like your prescribed prayers, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed witr. Then he said:
"O people of the Qur'an, pray witr.
For Allah is Odd (Witr) and loves the odd."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The witr is not obligatory like the prescribed prayer, but it is a sunnah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray two short rak'ahs after the witr, while sitting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over the martyrs of Uhud, then ascended the pulpit like one bidding farewell to the living and the dead, and said:

"I am your forerunner at the Pond, and its width is like the distance between Aylah and al-Juḥfah. I do not fear for you that you will associate partners with Allah after me, but I fear for you the world: that you will compete over it and fight one another, and so perish as those before you perished."
ʿUqbah said: That was the last time I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the pulpit.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the children of the polytheists who die while young, and he said:
"Allah knows best what they would have done."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Everyone who is born is born upon this natural disposition (fiṭrah), then his parents make him a Jew or a Christian, just as you breed camels: do you find any of them born with a cut ear, until you yourselves cut it?"
They said: O Messenger of Allah, what about one who dies young? He said:
"Allah knows best what they would have done."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Relaying it back to the Prophet ﷺ, he said:
"There is no man who does not pay the zakāh of his wealth except that on the Day of Resurrection Allah will place around his neck a bald-headed poisonous snake."
Then he recited to us the confirmation of that from the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
"And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think..." [to the end of] the verse.
And on another occasion he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited its confirmation:
"What they withheld will be placed around their necks like a collar on the Day of Resurrection."
"And whoever seizes the property of his Muslim brother by means of an oath will meet Allah while He is angry with him."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited its confirmation from the Book of Allah:
"Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah..." [to the end of] the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, which charity (ṣadaqah) is greatest in reward? He said:

"By your father, I will tell you: that you give charity while you are healthy and stingy, fearing poverty and hoping for wealth; and do not delay until, when [the soul] reaches the throat, you say: 'Give so-and-so such and such, and so-and-so such and such,' when it already belongs to so-and-so."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf said: Al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, al-Zuhrī narrated to us,
he said: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī narrated to me,
he said: Abū Saʿīd, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me, saying: A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about emigration (hijrah), and he said:
"Woe to you! The matter of emigration is serious.
Do you have any camels?" He said: Yes. He said: "Do you give their charity (ṣadaqah)?" He said: Yes. He said:
"Do you lend some of them for milking?" He said: Yes. He said:
"Do you milk them on the day they come to water?" He said: Yes. He said:
"Then work from beyond the seas,
for Allah will not diminish anything of your deeds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of ʿAbdullāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Give charity (ṣadaqah), O company of women, even from your jewelry."

She said: So I returned to ʿAbdullāh and said: You are a man of little means, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has commanded us to give charity. Go to him and ask him whether this suffices for me; otherwise I will give it to someone other than you.
She said: ʿAbdullāh said to me: No, you go to him yourself.

She said: So I set off, and there was a woman of the Anṣār at the door of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, her need the same as mine. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was a figure of awe. She said: Bilāl came out to us, and we said to him: Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and tell him that two women are at the door asking you whether charity suffices from them for their husbands and for orphans in their care, and do not tell him who we are. She said: Bilāl went in to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Who are they?"
He said: A woman of the Anṣār and Zaynab.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Which Zaynab?"
He said: The wife of ʿAbdullāh.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"They will have two rewards: the reward of kinship and the reward of charity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Maʿqil ibn ʿUbaydillāh, from ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid,
from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb,

who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me to recite a sūrah. While I was sitting in the mosque, I heard a man reciting it differently from my recitation. I said to him, "Who taught you this sūrah?" He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
I said, "Do not leave me until we go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." So I went to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, this man has differed from my recitation of the sūrah you taught me."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Recite, O Ubayy."
So I recited it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, "You have done well."
Then he said to the man, "Recite."
He recited, and differed from my recitation, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "You have done well."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"O Ubayy, the Qurʾān was revealed in seven modes, each of them sufficient and fully adequate."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nothing has troubled my heart since I became Muslim, except that I recited a verse and another man recited it differently from my recitation. I said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught it to me."
And the other said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught it to me."
So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Prophet of Allah, did you teach me such-and-such verse?" He said, "Yes."
And the other said, "Did you not teach me such-and-such verse?" He said,
"Yes. Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl, peace be upon them, came to me. Jibrīl sat on my right and Mīkāʾīl on my left. Jibrīl, peace be upon him, said, 'Recite the Qurʾān in one mode.'
Mīkāʾīl said, 'Ask for more, ask for more,' until it reached seven modes. Each mode is sufficient and fully adequate."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he led the dawn prayer and recited [Sūrat] ar-Rūm, and it became confused for him. When he finished the prayer, he said,
"What is the matter with people who pray with us but do not perform purification properly? It is only that the Qurʾān is made confusing for us [because of] those people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I only learned {Qāf. By the Glorious Qurʾān} from behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; he used to recite it in the dawn prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ recite in the dawn prayer {When the sun is wrapped up}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the two sūrahs of refuge.
ʿUqbah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer reciting them in the morning prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I followed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was riding, and I placed my hand on his foot and said, "O Messenger of Allah, teach me Sūrat Hūd and Sūrat Yūsuf." He said,
"You will never recite anything more excellent in the sight of Allah than {Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak} and {Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind}."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prostrated at {Ṣād} and said,
"Dāwūd prostrated at it in repentance, and we prostrate at it in gratitude."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited Sūrat an-Najm in Makkah and prostrated, and those near him prostrated. I raised my head and refused to prostrate; al-Muṭṭalib had not yet become Muslim at that time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were at aṭ-Ṭaff with Anas, and he led them in the noon prayer. When he finished he said, "I prayed the noon prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he recited for us these two sūrahs in the two rakʿahs: {Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High} and {Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming?}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to lead us in the noon prayer and recite in the first two rakʿahs, letting us hear the verse in this way. He would lengthen the first rakʿah of the noon prayer, and the first rakʿah, that is, in the dawn prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We visited Anas ibn Mālik, and he said, "Have you prayed?" We said, "Yes."
He said, "O girl, bring me water for ablution. I have not prayed behind any imām whose prayer resembled the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ more than this imām of yours."
Zayd said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz used to complete the bowing and prostration and keep the standing and sitting brief.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I have not prayed behind anyone whose prayer resembled the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ more than so-and-so.

So we prayed behind that person. He would lengthen the first two rakʿahs of the noon prayer and shorten the last two, and shorten the afternoon prayer. He would recite the short sūrahs of the mufaṣṣal in the sunset prayer, recite {By the sun and its brightness} and the like in the night prayer, and recite two long sūrahs in the dawn prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited {Ḥā Mīm} ad-Dukhān in the sunset prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zuhayr said: I think it was from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:

"Bring a quarter of a tenth: one dirham from every forty dirhams. You owe nothing until you reach two hundred dirhams. When you have two hundred dirhams, five dirhams are due on it, and whatever exceeds that is calculated accordingly. As for sheep, one sheep is due for every forty sheep; if you have only thirty-nine, nothing is due from you on them."
He then related the charity on sheep as al-Zuhrī did. He said:
"For cattle, a tabīʿ is due for every thirty, and a musinnah for forty, and nothing is due on working animals. And for camels..."
He then mentioned the charity due on them as al-Zuhrī mentioned. He said:

"For twenty-five, five sheep are due. If there is one more, a bint makhāḍ is due; if there is no bint makhāḍ, then a male ibn labūn, up to thirty-five. If there is one more, a bint labūn is due, up to forty-five. If there is one more, a ḥiqqah fit to be covered by the male camel is due, up to sixty."
Then he related it like the hadith of al-Zuhrī. He said:

"If there is one more, meaning ninety-one, two ḥiqqahs fit to be covered by the male camel are due, up to one hundred and twenty. If the camels exceed that, then a ḥiqqah is due for every fifty. Those that are together are not to be separated, nor those that are separate to be joined, out of fear of the charity. No old animal, defective animal, or male goat is to be taken in charity, unless the collector wishes. And for crops, a tenth is due on what is watered by rivers or rain, and a half of a tenth on what is watered by the bucket."
In the hadith of ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥārith:
"The charity is due every year."
Zuhayr said: I think he said, "once."
And in the hadith of ʿĀṣim:
"If among the camels there is neither a bint makhāḍ nor an ibn labūn, then ten dirhams or two sheep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ sent him to Yemen, he commanded him to take from cattle a tabīʿ or tabīʿah for every thirty, and a musinnah for every forty, and from every adult, meaning one who has reached puberty, a dinar or its equivalent in maʿāfir, which are garments found in Yemen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I traveled, or he said: One who traveled informed me,
with the collector of the Prophet ﷺ, and it was in the covenant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
"Do not take from a nursing animal, do not join together what is separate, and do not separate what is together."
He would only come to the watering places when the sheep came to drink, and he would say, "Pay the charities due on your wealth."

He said: A man among them went to a big-humped she-camel. He said: I said, "O Abū Ṣāliḥ, what is a kawmāʾ?" He said, "One with a large hump." He said: The collector refused to accept it. The man said, "I would like you to take the best of my camels."

He said: The collector refused to accept it. So the man led another to him, lesser than it, and he refused to accept it. Then he led another to him, lesser than it, and he accepted it, and said, "I am taking it, but I fear that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will be displeased with me and say to me, 'You went to a man and chose the best of his camels.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed a man over a military expedition, he would advise him personally to fear Allah, and to treat the Muslims who were with him well. Then he said:

"Fight in the name of Allah and in the cause of Allah. Fight those who disbelieve in Allah. Fight, but do not be treacherous, do not steal from the spoils, do not mutilate, and do not kill a child. When you meet your enemies from among the polytheists, invite them to one of three options or qualities. Whichever of them they accept, accept it from them and hold back from them. Invite them to Islam; if they accept, accept it from them and hold back from them. Then invite them to move from their land to the land of the emigrants, and inform them that if they do so, they will have what the emigrants have and owe what the emigrants owe. If they refuse, then inform them that they will be like the Bedouin Muslims: the ruling of Allah that applies to the believers will apply to them, but they will have no share in the war gains or the spoils unless they strive alongside the Muslims. If they refuse to enter Islam, then ask them to pay the jizyah; if they do, accept it from them and hold back from them. If they refuse, then seek help from Allah against them and fight them. If you besiege a fortress and they want you to grant them the protection of Allah and the protection of His Prophet, do not grant them the protection of Allah or the protection of His Prophet; rather grant them your own protection and the protection of your fathers and your companions, for if you break your own protection and the protection of your fathers, that is lighter for you than breaking the protection of Allah and the protection of His Messenger. If you besiege a fortress and they want you to let them surrender according to the judgment of Allah, do not let them surrender according to the judgment of Allah; rather let them surrender according to your judgment, for you do not know whether you will reach the judgment of Allah regarding them or not."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to say:

"Some jealousy is loved by Allah and some is hated by Allah. As for the jealousy that Allah loves, it is jealousy where there is cause for suspicion. As for the jealousy that Allah hates, it is jealousy where there is no cause for suspicion. And some pride is hated by Allah and some is loved by Allah. As for the pride that Allah loves, it is a man's pride in himself during fighting and his pride when giving charity. As for the pride that Allah hates, it is his pride in wrongdoing." Mūsā said: "and boasting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A woman gains three inheritances: [from] her freed slave, her foundling, and her child over whom she has made a oath of condemnation (liʿān)."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb; it is not known except through this route, from the hadith of Muḥammad ibn Ḥarb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ. Transfer of chain: and ʿAbdullāh ibn Saʿīd narrated to us,
Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar narrated to us, Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
who said: When the dead person was placed in the grave, the Prophet ﷺ would say:
"In the name of Allah and upon the creed of the Messenger of Allah."
Abū Khālid said on one occasion: When the dead person was placed in his niche, he would say:
"In the name of Allah and upon the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah."
And Hishām said in his narration:
"In the name of Allah, and in the cause of Allah, and upon the creed of the Messenger of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he
asked Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ about white wheat
in exchange for barley. Saʿd said to him: Which of the two is better? He said: The white wheat.
So he forbade him from that and said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being asked about buying dates with fresh dates, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do fresh dates diminish when they dry?"
They said: Yes. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She asked ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her: There is an orphan in my care; may I eat from his wealth? She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Among the best of what a man eats is that which is from his own earnings, and his child is from his earnings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin

gave a young she-camel as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he compensated him for it with six young camels, but the man was displeased with it. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, so he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said:

"So-and-so gave me a she-camel as a gift, and I compensated him for it with six young camels, yet he remained displeased. I had intended not to accept a gift except from a Qurashī, an Anṣārī, a Thaqafī, or a Dawsī."
There is more to the hadith than this.

This hadith has been narrated through more than one route from Abū Hurayrah. Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrates from Ayyūb Abū al-ʿAlāʾ, who is Ayyūb ibn Miskīn, also called Ibn Abī Miskīn. Perhaps this hadith that is narrated from Ayyūb from Saʿīd al-Maqburī is [from] Ayyūb Abū al-ʿAlāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Madinah, and while I was in

a circle in which there was a group of Quraysh, a man came in coarse clothes, with a coarse body and a coarse face. He stood over them and said, "Give glad tidings to those who hoard wealth of hot stones that will be heated in the Fire of Hell and placed on the nipple of one of them until it comes out from the soft part of his shoulder, and placed on the soft part of his shoulder until it comes out from the nipple of his breast, shaking about." He said: The people lowered their heads, and I did not see any of them give him any reply. He said: He turned away and I followed him until he sat by a pillar. I said, "I did not see these people except that they disliked what you said to them."
He said, "These people understand nothing. My beloved friend, Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ, called me and I answered him. He said, 'Do you see Uhud?'"
I looked at how much of the sun was left, thinking that he would send me on some errand of his, and I said, "I see it." He said, "
It would not please me to have gold the like of it that I would spend all of it, except for three dīnārs."
Then these people go on gathering the world, understanding nothing.
He said: I said, "What is the matter with you and your brothers from Quraysh? You do not go to them and take something from them."
He said, "No, by your Lord, I will not ask them for anything of the world, nor seek a religious ruling from them, until I meet Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was among a group of Quraysh when Abū Dharr passed by saying, "Give glad tidings to those who hoard wealth of a brand on their backs that will come out from their sides, and a brand on the backs of their necks that will come out from their foreheads."
He said: Then he moved aside and sat down.
He said: I said, "Who is this?" They said, "This is Abū Dharr."
He said: I got up and went to him and said, "What was it I heard you saying a moment ago?" He said, "I said only something I heard from their Prophet ﷺ."
He said: I said, "What do you say about this stipend?" He said, "Take it, for today it is a help. But if it becomes the price of your religion, then leave it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "

A dīnār you spend in the cause of Allah, a dīnār you spend to free a slave, a dīnār you give in charity to a poor person, and a dīnār you spend on your family: the greatest of them in reward is the one you spend on your family."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr when his steward came in to him and said, "Have you given the slaves their food?" He said, "No."
He said, "Go and give it to them."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
It is enough sin for a person that he withholds the food of those he is responsible for."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of ʿAbdullāh
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this chain of narration
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my mother died suddenly and did not make a bequest, and I think that if she had been able to speak she would have given charity. Will she have a reward if I give charity on her behalf?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Dharr [reported] that some people

from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said to the Prophet ﷺ, "O Messenger of Allah, the wealthy have gone off with the rewards. They pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, and they give charity from their surplus wealth." He said, "

Has Allah not given you something to give in charity?
