Every glorification (tasbīḥah) is a charity, every declaration of Allah's greatness (takbīrah) is a charity, every praise of Allah (taḥmīdah) is a charity, every declaration that there is no god but Allah (tahlīlah) is a charity, enjoining what is right is a charity, forbidding what is wrong is a charity, and in the private part of each of you is a charity."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, one of us fulfils his desire and he will have a reward for it?" He said, "
Do you not see that if he put it in what is forbidden, he would bear a sin for it? So likewise, when he puts it in what is lawful, he will have a reward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "

Every human being among the children of Adam was created with three hundred and sixty joints. Whoever declares Allah's greatness, praises Allah, declares that there is no god but Allah, glorifies Allah, seeks forgiveness from Allah, removes a stone from the people's path, or a thorn or a bone from the people's path, and enjoins what is right or forbids what is wrong, to the number of those three hundred and sixty joints, will walk that day having removed himself from the Fire."
Abū Tawbah said: Perhaps he said, "will spend the evening."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the early part of the day.
[He narrated] like the hadith of Ibn Jaʿfar. In the hadith of Ibn Muʿādh there is this addition: He said: Then he prayed the Zuhr prayer, then he delivered a sermon.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when some people came to him wearing striped woollen garments, and they related the hadith with its story. In it: He prayed the Zuhr prayer, then ascended a small pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said, "
To proceed: Allah has revealed in His Book: {O people, fear your Lord} [the verse]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah as-Sulamī said: In the time of ignorance I used to think that the people were misguided and had nothing sound, as they worshipped idols. Then I heard of a man in Makkah who was giving news, so I sat on my mount and went to him. There was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, hiding, while his people were bold against him. I dealt gently [with them] until I entered upon him in Makkah, and I said to him: "What are you?" He said: "I am a prophet."
I said: "And what is a prophet?" He said: "Allah has sent me."
I said: "And with what has He sent you?" He said:
"He sent me to maintain the ties of kinship, to break the idols, and that Allah be declared One, with nothing associated with Him."
I said to him: "Who is with you in this?" He said: "A free man and a slave."
He said: And with him that day were Abū Bakr and Bilāl, among those who had believed in him.
I said: "I will follow you." He said:
"You cannot do that today. Do you not see my condition and the condition of the people? But return to your family, and when you hear that I have become victorious, come to me."

He said: So I went to my family, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah while I was with my family. I began to seek news and to ask the people when he came to Madinah, until a group of the people of Yathrib, of the people of Madinah, came to me. I said: "What has this man who came to Madinah done?" They said: "The people are hastening to him, and his people wanted to kill him but were not able to do so."
So I came to Madinah and entered upon him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you know me?" He said:
"Yes, you are the one who met me in Makkah."
He said: I said: "Yes indeed."
Then I said: "O Prophet of Allah, tell me about what Allah has taught you and I do not know."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were in Madinah, and when the muʾadhdhin called the adhān for the Maghrib prayer, they would rush to the pillars and pray two units, two units, so that a stranger entering the mosque would think that the prayer had already been performed because of the many people praying them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he used to narrate about the prayer of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in times of fear, and he would say: "I prayed it with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," with this meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We fought with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a people from Juhaynah, and they fought us fiercely. When we had prayed Ẓuhr, the polytheists said: "If we were to charge them in one assault, we would cut them off."

Then Jibrīl informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of that, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ told us of it. He said: They also said: "A prayer will soon come to them that is dearer to them than their children." When the time of ʿAṣr came, he said: We formed two rows, with the polytheists between us and the qiblah. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the takbīr and we said the takbīr; he bowed and we bowed; then he prostrated and the first row prostrated with him. When they stood, the second row prostrated. Then the first row moved back and the second row moved forward, and they stood in the place of the first. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the takbīr and we said the takbīr; he bowed and we bowed; then he prostrated and the first row prostrated with him, while the second remained standing. When he prostrated, the second row prostrated. Then they all sat, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the salām to them.
Abū az-Zubayr said: Then Jābir specified that he said: "Just as these leaders of yours pray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My two sons, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ, with similar wording.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ said:
"Indeed, in Friday there is an hour which no Muslim happens upon while standing in prayer, asking Allah for good, except that He gives it to him."
And he gestured with his hand to show that it is short, making it seem small.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"We were guided to Friday, and Allah led astray from it those who were before us."
Then he mentioned [the rest] with the meaning of the hadith of Ibn Fuḍayl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Ḥarmalah,
and ʿAmr ibn Sawwād al-ʿĀmirī,
Abū aṭ-Ṭāhir said: "Ḥaddathanā," and the other two said:
"Akhbaranā Ibn Wahb; Yūnus informed me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
Abū ʿAbdillāh informed me,
al-Aghar, that he heard Abū Hurayrah
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When it is the day of Friday, at every door of the mosque there are angels recording the first, then the next. When the imam sits, they fold up the scrolls and come to listen to the remembrance. The likeness of one who comes early is that of one who offers a camel, then like one who offers a cow, then like one who offers a ram, then like one who offers a chicken, then like one who offers an egg."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever performs ghusl, then comes to Friday [prayer] and prays what has been decreed for him, then remains silent until the imam finishes his sermon, and then prays with him, will be forgiven for what is between that and the next Friday, and an additional three days."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day we were praying behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his head from bowing, he said:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him."
A man behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, our Lord, and to You belongs all praise, abundant, good and blessed praise." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he said:
"Who was the one who spoke those words just now?"
The man said: "I was, O Messenger of Allah."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I saw more than thirty angels racing to it, each of them wanting to be the first to record it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ concluded the prayer with the salām, he would stay in his place for a short while.
Ibn Shihāb said: "We think—and Allah knows best—that this was so that the women who were leaving could go out."
Ibn Abī Maryam said: Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd informed us,
he said: Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿah informed me,
that Ibn Shihāb
wrote to him, saying: Hind bint al-Ḥārith al-Firāsiyyah narrated to me,
from Umm Salamah,
the wife of the Prophet ﷺ—and Hind was one of her companions—she said: He would give the salām, and the women would leave,
and enter their homes before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left.
Ibn Wahb said, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb: Hind al-Firāsiyyah informed me.
ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar said: Yūnus informed us, from az-Zuhrī: Hind al-Firāsiyyah narrated to me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Raising the voice in remembrance of Allah when the people left after the obligatory prayer was done in the time of the Prophet ﷺ.
And he said that Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I would know that they had finished the prayer when I heard it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān,
from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUtbah,
from Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī, who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the dawn prayer at al-Ḥudaybiyah after rain that had fallen during the night. When he finished, he turned to the people and said:
"Do you know what your Lord has said?"
They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"He said: 'This morning some of My servants have become believers in Me and others disbelievers. As for the one who said, "We have been given rain by the grace of Allah and His mercy,"
he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the star. And as for the one who said, "We have been given rain by such and such a star,"
he is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the star.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAṭāʾ claimed that Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh
claimed that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever eats garlic or onions, let him keep away from us—or he said: let him keep away from our mosque—
and let him stay in his house."
And a pot was brought to the Prophet ﷺ containing cooked green vegetables,
and he found a smell in it. He asked, and was told what vegetables were in it, so he said: "Bring it near"
to one of his Companions who was with him.
When he saw it, he disliked eating it, and he said:
"Eat, for I converse with one with whom you do not converse."
Aḥmad ibn Ṣāliḥ said, from Ibn Wahb: A badr was brought.
Ibn Wahb said: meaning a dish containing green vegetables.
Al-Layth and Abū Ṣafwān, from Yūnus, did not mention the story of the pot,
so I do not know whether it is from the words of az-Zuhrī or part of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man asked Ibn ʿAbbās: "Did you attend the ʿĪd with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Yes, and had it not been for my standing with him, I would not have attended, because of my young age. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to the landmark near the house of Kathīr ibn aṣ-Ṣalt, and he prayed and then gave a sermon. He did not mention any adhān or iqāmah. Then he commanded charity." He said: "The women began to point to their ears and their throats." He said: "So he commanded Bilāl, who went to them, and then returned to the Prophet ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: "If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seen what the women have introduced, he would have prevented them from the mosque, as the women of the Children of Israel were prevented."
Yaḥyā said: I said to ʿAmrah: "Were the women of the Children of Israel prevented?" She said: "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"If your wife asks your permission to go to the mosque, do not prevent her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My brother Wahb ibn Munabbih said: This is what Abū Hurayrah narrated to us, from Muḥammad,
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"We are the last, yet the first on the Day of Resurrection, although they were given the Book before us and we were given it after them. This is their day which was made obligatory for them, but they differed about it, and Allah guided us to it. So in this they follow us: the Jews tomorrow, and the Christians the day after tomorrow."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh about riding the sacrificial animal,
and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Ride it in a reasonable manner when you need to, until you find another mount."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade that a woman be married together with her paternal aunt, or a paternal aunt with her brother's daughter, or a woman with her maternal aunt, or a maternal aunt with her sister's daughter. The younger is not to be married together with the older, nor the older with the younger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When any of you is invited to a wedding banquet, let him attend it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was recited to him while I was listening,
from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr, from ʿAmrah, from ʿĀʾishah,

who said: Among what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed—and al-Ḥārith said: among what was revealed of the Qurʾān—was: ten known breastfeedings make [marriage] unlawful. Then it was abrogated by five known breastfeedings. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away, and that was among what was still being recited of the Qurʾān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah bint Qays,

the sister of al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays, informed him that Abū Ḥafṣ ibn al-Mughīrah al-Makhzūmī divorced her three times and then set out for Yemen. His family said to her: You are not entitled to any maintenance from us.

So Khālid ibn al-Walīd went with a group of men and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the house of Maymūnah and said: Abū Ḥafṣ divorced his wife three times; is she entitled to maintenance? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"She has no maintenance, and she must observe the waiting period." And he sent word to her:
"Do not get ahead of me concerning yourself."
And he commanded her to move to Umm Sharīk. Then he sent word to her:
"The early Emigrants visit Umm Sharīk, so go to Ibn Umm Maktūm, the blind man, for if you take off your headscarf he will not see you."
So she went to him, and when her waiting period was over, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her to Usāmah ibn Zayd ibn Ḥārithah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to practice sharecropping in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He mentioned that one of his uncles came to him and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has forbidden something that was beneficial to us, but obedience to Allah and His Messenger is more beneficial to us.
He said: We asked: What is that? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has land, let him cultivate it or let him lend it to his brother to cultivate, and let him not rent it out for a third, or a quarter, or a specified amount of food."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If you sell fruit to your brother and it is struck by a blight, it is not lawful for you to take anything from him. For what reason would you take your brother's money without right?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A dinar for a dinar and a dirham for a dirham, with no excess between them. Whoever needs silver, let him exchange it for gold, and whoever needs gold, let him exchange it for silver, and exchange must be hand to hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father gave me a gift—Ismāʿīl ibn Sālim said, among the people, that it was a servant boy of his—and my mother ʿAmrah bint Rawāḥah said to him: Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and have him witness it. So he went to the Prophet ﷺ to have him witness it, and mentioned that to him, saying: I have given my son al-Nuʿmān a gift, and ʿAmrah asked me to have you witness it. He said: Then he said:
"Do you have any other child besides him?"
He said: I said: Yes. He said:
"Did you give each of them the like of what you gave al-Nuʿmān?"
He said: No. Then some of these narrators said: "This is injustice." And some of them said:
"This is a case of coercion, so have someone other than me witness it."
Mughīrah said in his narration:
"Would it not please you that they be equal toward you in dutifulness and kindness?" He said: Yes. He said:
"Then have someone other than me witness this."
And Mujālid mentioned in his narration:
"They have a right over you that you treat them justly, just as you have a right over them that they be dutiful to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the descendants of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: When ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) described the Prophet ﷺ, he would say: He was neither excessively tall nor short and stooping; he was of medium height among people. His hair was neither tightly curled nor completely straight; it was wavy. He was not plump, nor was his face fully round, but his face had some roundness. He was white with a reddish tinge, with very black eyes and long eyelashes. He had large joints and a broad upper back, with little body hair, and a thin line of hair running from his chest to his navel. His hands and feet were thick and strong. When he walked, he lifted his feet firmly, as though descending a slope; and when he turned, he turned with his whole body. Between his shoulders was the seal of prophethood, and he is the seal of the prophets. He was the most generous of people in hand, the most expansive in heart, the most truthful in speech, the gentlest in nature, and the noblest in companionship. Whoever saw him suddenly stood in awe of him, and whoever mixed with him and came to know him loved him. One who describes him would say: I have never seen anyone like him, before him or after him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not speak rapidly in a continuous flow as you do; rather, he spoke with clear, distinct words that anyone sitting with him could remember.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would repeat a statement three times so that it would be understood from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw anyone smile more than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Like this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The seal of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, meaning the one between his shoulders, was a reddish gland like a pigeon's egg.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had thin shins, and he would only laugh by smiling. When I looked at him, I would say he had kohl-darkened eyes, though he did not use kohl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw anything more beautiful than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; it was as though the sun were running across his face. And I never saw anyone walk faster than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; it was as though the earth was being folded up for him. We would exhaust ourselves, while he was unconcerned.
He said: This is a gharīb ḥadīth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr is our master, the best of us, and the most beloved of us to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr said: Am I not the most deserving of people of it? Am I not the first to accept Islam? Am I not the one who did such and such? Am I not the one who did such and such?
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would come out to his Companions, from the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār, while they were sitting, among them Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. None of them would raise his gaze to him except Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, for they would look at him and he would look at them, and they would smile at him and he would smile at them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abū Bakr:
"You are my companion at the Basin and my companion in the cave."
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb ḥadīth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw Abū Bakr and ʿUmar and said:
"These two are the hearing and the sight."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not fitting for a people among whom is Abū Bakr that anyone other than him should lead them in prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"While a man was riding a cow, it said: I was not created for this; I was only created for plowing."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I believe in that, as do Abū Bakr and ʿUmar."
Abū Salamah said: They were not among the people on that day, and Allah knows best.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ ordered that all the doors be closed except the door of Abū Bakr.
This ḥadīth is gharīb from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr
entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"You are Allah's freed one from the Fire."
So from that day he was named ʿAtīq.
This ḥadīth is gharīb.
Some of them narrated this ḥadīth from Maʿn and said: from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, from ʿĀʾishah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no prophet who does not have two ministers from the people of the heavens and two ministers from the people of the earth. As for my two ministers from the people of the heavens, they are Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl; and as for my two ministers from the people of the earth, they are Abū Bakr and ʿUmar."
This is a ḥasan gharīb ḥadīth.
Abū al-Jaḥḥāf's name is Dāwūd ibn Abī ʿAwf.
He also narrates from Sufyān al-Thawrī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, strengthen Islam with whichever of these two men is more beloved to You: Abū Jahl or ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb."
He said: And the more beloved of the two to Him was ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were discussing this with Abū aḍ-Ḍuḥā, and he said: Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to us,
He said: One morning we woke and the wives of the Prophet ﷺ were weeping,
with each of them having her family beside her.
So I went out to the mosque,
and it was full of people. Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb came and went up to the Prophet ﷺ, who was in an upper room of his,
He gave the greeting of peace, but no one answered him.
Then he gave the greeting again, but no one answered him.
Then he gave the greeting a third time, but no one answered him.
So he called out, and he was admitted to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: Have you divorced your wives? He said:
"No, but I have taken an oath to keep away from them for a month."
So he stayed away for twenty-nine days,
then he went in to his wives.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade plundering and mutilation [of bodies].
label: machine translation

segments_en: She had hung a curtain with images on it over a shelf of hers, and the Prophet ﷺ tore it down.
So she made two cushions out of it,
and they were kept in the house and used for sitting on.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out an expedition toward the coast,
and appointed Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ as their commander. They were three hundred, and I was among them.
We set out, and when we were part of the way along, the provisions ran out.
So Abū ʿUbaydah ordered that the provisions of the whole army be collected, and they came to two bags of dates.
He would give us our daily ration of them, a little at a time,
until they ran out, and we were getting only a single date each.
I said: What good is a single date? He said: We truly felt its loss when it was gone.
He said: Then we reached the sea, and there was a fish like a small hill.
The army ate from it for eighteen nights.
Then Abū ʿUbaydah ordered two of its ribs to be set up,
then ordered a riding camel to be saddled, and it passed beneath them without touching them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: O Messenger of Allah, accept his pledge. He said: "He is young."
So he wiped over his head and prayed for him.
And from Zuhrah ibn Maʿbad:

His grandfather ʿAbdullāh ibn Hishām used to take him out to the market, and he would buy food. Then Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn az-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them, would meet him and say to him: Take us in as partners,
for the Prophet ﷺ prayed for blessing for you. So he would take them in as partners,
and sometimes he would gain a whole camel-load just as it was,
and he would send it off to the house.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When I was coming to the Prophet ﷺ, I said on the way: "O what a long and wearisome night, yet it has saved me from the land of disbelief." He said: And a servant of mine ran away on the road. He said: When I came to the Prophet ﷺ, I pledged allegiance to him,
and while I was with him, the servant appeared.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"O Abū Hurayrah, this is your servant."
I said: He is free for the sake of Allah. And I set him free.
Abū Kurayb did not say "free" in his narration from Abū Usāmah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some men
from the Anṣār asked permission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, permit us to waive the ransom of our nephew ʿAbbās. He said:
"Do not leave out a single dirham of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went to ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and said: I was a slave of ʿUtbah ibn Abī Lahab,
and he died and his sons inherited me,
and they sold me to Ibn Abī ʿAmr,
and Ibn Abī ʿAmr set me free,
but the sons of ʿUtbah stipulated the right of walāʾ.
She said: Barīrah, who was a mukātabah, came to me and said: Buy me and free me. I said: Yes.
She said: They will not sell me unless they stipulate my walāʾ.
So I said: I have no need of that.
The Prophet ﷺ heard of this, or it reached him, and it was mentioned to ʿĀʾishah,
so ʿĀʾishah told him what Barīrah had said to her. He said: "Buy her and free her,
and let them stipulate whatever they wish."
So ʿĀʾishah bought her and freed her, and her former owners stipulated the walāʾ. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Walāʾ belongs to the one who frees,
even if they stipulate a hundred conditions."
label: machine translation

segments_en: to ʿUrwah, son of my sister:
We would watch for the new moon, then another new moon,
three new moons within two months,
and no fire was lit in the houses of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
I said: O aunt, what did you live on? She said: The two black things, dates and water,
except that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had neighbors among the Anṣār who had milch animals,
and they used to send the Messenger of Allah ﷺ some of their milk, and he would give it to us to drink.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prohibited shighār.
I asked Nāfiʿ, "What is shighār?" He said: A man marries another man's daughter and in exchange the other marries his daughter, without any dowry;
or a man marries another man's sister and in exchange the other marries his sister, without any dowry.
Some people said: If someone uses a ruse until he marries by way of shighār, it is valid and the condition is void.
And regarding temporary marriage (mutʿah), he said: The marriage is invalid and the condition is void.
And some of them said: Temporary marriage and shighār are valid, and the condition is void.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He heard him] on the pulpit saying that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The believer is the brother of the believer. So it is not lawful for a believer to outbid his brother's sale, nor to propose to a woman his brother has already proposed to, until he gives it up."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He] heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the pulpit saying:

"The family of Hishām ibn al-Mughīrah asked my permission to marry their daughter to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. I do not give permission, then I do not give permission, then I do not give permission, unless the son of Abū Ṭālib wishes to divorce my daughter and marry their daughter. For my daughter is a part of me; what troubles her troubles me, and what harms her harms me."
And the reports are in the narration of Aḥmad.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from the Aslam tribe came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in the mosque and called out to him, saying, "O Messenger of Allah, the other one has committed adultery," meaning himself. He turned away from him, so the man moved to the side of his face toward which he had turned away, and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the other one has committed adultery." He turned away from him, so he moved to the side of his face toward which he had turned away, and said the same to him. He turned away from him, so the man moved to face him a fourth time.
When he had testified against himself four times, he called him and said:
"Are you insane?" He said, "No." Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Take him away and stone him."
And he was a married man. And from az-Zuhrī,
who said: One who
heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Anṣārī informed me,
who said: I was among those who stoned him. We stoned him at the prayer ground in Medina.
When the stones hurt him badly, he fled until we caught up with him at al-Ḥarrah,
and we stoned him until he died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went on seven or six military expeditions with the Prophet ﷺ,
and we would eat locusts with him.
Sufyān, Abū ʿAwānah, and Isrāʾīl said, from Abū Yaʿfūr, from Ibn Abī Awfā: seven expeditions.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not make nabīdh from unripe dates and fresh ripe dates together, and do not make nabīdh from fresh dates and raisins together; rather, make nabīdh from each one separately."
And Yaḥyā claimed that he met ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Qatādah, who narrated to him from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, something similar to this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should wish for death because of a harm that has befallen him.
If he must wish for death, let him say: O Allah, keep me alive as long as life is better for me,
and take me when death is better for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ made a ring of silver and engraved on it "Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah." He said to the people:
"I have made a ring of silver and engraved on it 'Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah.'
So let no one engrave the like of its engraving."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to visit us, and I had a young brother who was called Abū ʿUmayr. He had a little bird (nughar) that he played with, and it died. One day the Prophet ﷺ came to him and saw him sad, and said, "What is the matter with him?"
They said, "His little bird died." So he said:
"O Abū ʿUmayr, what did the little bird do?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest. His special entitlement is a day and a night. Hospitality is three days, and it is not lawful for him [the guest] to stay with his host until he puts him in difficulty. Whatever is spent on him after three days is charity (ṣadaqah)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men sneezed in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said a supplication for one of them and left the other. It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, two men sneezed, and you made supplication for one of them and left the other." He said:
"This one praised Allah, and this one did not praise Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was walking with Thābit al-Bunānī, and he passed by some children and greeted them with salām.
Thābit narrated that he was walking with Anas, who passed by some children and greeted them with salām.
And Anas narrated that he was walking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who passed by some children and greeted them with salām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ about a debt that my father had owed, and I knocked on the door. He said, "Who is that?" I said, "It is I." He said, "I, I," as though he disliked it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some preachers

stood up in Syria, and among them were men from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The last of them to stand was a man called Murrah ibn Kaʿb. He said, "Were it not for a hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would not have stood up."

He mentioned the trials and said they were near. Then a man passed by, covering his head with his garment, and he said, "On that day, this man will be on guidance." So I went up to him, and it was ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān.
He said: I turned to him with his face and said, "This one?" He said, "Yes." This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the descendants of Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh, from al-Ṣalt ibn Dīnār,
from Abū Naḍrah,
who said: Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Whoever would be pleased to look at a martyr walking on the face of the earth, let him look at Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I would ask a man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ about verses of the Qurʾān that I knew better than he did; I only asked him so that he would feed me something. So whenever I asked Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib, he would not answer me until he took me to his house and said to his wife, "Asmāʾ, feed us something."

Once she had fed us, he would answer me. Jaʿfar loved the poor; he would sit with them, talk with them, and they would talk with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to call him "Abū al-Masākīn" (Father of the Poor).
label: machine translation

segments_en: My mother asked me, "When was the last time you were with the Prophet ﷺ?"
I said, "I have not been with him since such and such a time."
She reproached me, so I said to her, "Let me go to the Prophet ﷺ and pray the Maghrib prayer with him, and ask him to seek forgiveness for me and for you."
So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and prayed Maghrib with him. He kept praying until he had prayed ʿIshāʾ, then he turned to leave and I followed him. He heard my voice and said:
"Who is this? Ḥudhayfah?" I said, "Yes." He said:
"What do you need? May Allah forgive you and your mother." He said:

"This is an angel who had never descended to earth before this night. He asked his Lord's permission to greet me and to give me the glad tidings that Fāṭimah is the leader of the women of Paradise, and that al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn are the leaders of the youth of Paradise."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb from this route; we only know it from the narration of Isrāʾīl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They

went out with the Prophet ﷺ to a meal to which they had been invited, and there was Ḥusayn playing in the street. He said: The Prophet ﷺ went ahead of the people and spread out his hands, and the boy began to run this way and that, and the Prophet ﷺ made him laugh until he caught him. He placed one hand under his chin and the other on the back of his head, and kissed him, and said:
"Ḥusayn is from me and I am from Ḥusayn. May Allah love whoever loves Ḥusayn. Ḥusayn is a grandson among the grandsons."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is Simāk ibn al-Walīd al-Ḥanafī, from Mālik ibn Marthad, from his father,
from Abū Dharr,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The sky has not shaded nor the earth carried anyone more truthful in speech or more faithful than Abū Dharr; he resembles ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, peace be upon him."
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said, as if envious, "O Messenger of Allah, should we recognize that for him?" He said:
"Yes, so recognize it for him."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb from this route.
Some of them narrated this hadith and said:
"Abū Dharr walks upon the earth with the asceticism of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, peace be upon him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Use the siwāk, for the siwāk purifies the mouth and pleases the Lord. Jibrīl never came to me without advising me about the siwāk, until I feared it would be made obligatory upon me and upon my nation. And were it not that I fear burdening my nation, I would have made it obligatory for them. I use the siwāk so much that I feared I would wear away the front of my mouth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to sleep while in a state of major impurity, he would perform ablution; and when he wished to eat or drink, she said, he would wash his hands, then eat or drink.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said: While we were in the mosque, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and said:
"Let us go to the Jews."
So we went out with him until we came to them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and called out to them, saying:
"O assembly of Jews, accept Islam and you will be safe."
They said, "You have conveyed [the message], O Abū al-Qāsim."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them:
"That is what I want. Accept Islam and you will be safe."
They said, "You have conveyed [the message], O Abū al-Qāsim."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them, "That is what I want."
Then he said it to them a third time, and said:

"Know that the earth belongs to Allah and His Messenger, and I want to expel you from this land. So whoever among you finds that he has some property, let him sell it; otherwise, know that the earth belongs to Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ wrote to Heraclius:
"From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, the ruler of the Byzantines. Peace be upon whoever follows the guidance."

Ibn Yaḥyā reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that Abū Sufyān informed him, saying: We entered upon Heraclius and he seated us before him. Then he called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and in it was:
"In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, the ruler of the Byzantines. Peace be upon whoever follows the guidance. To proceed:"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"We have been favored over other people in three ways: our rows have been made like the rows of the angels; the whole earth has been made a place of prayer for us; and its soil has been made a means of purification for us when we cannot find water."
And he mentioned another characteristic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I have been favored over the prophets in six ways: I was given concise yet comprehensive speech; I was made victorious through terror [cast into the hearts of enemies]; the spoils of war were made lawful for me; the earth was made a means of purification and a place of prayer for me; I was sent to all of creation; and the prophets were sealed with me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [This is] like the hadith of Yūnus.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen months, until the verse in Sūrat al-Baqarah was revealed: "Wherever you may be, turn your faces toward it." It was revealed after the Prophet ﷺ had prayed. A man from the people set out and passed by some of the Anṣār while they were praying, and he told them, so they turned their faces toward the House [the Kaʿbah].
label: machine translation

segments_en: and al-Aswad,
that they entered upon ʿAbdullāh, and he said, "Do those behind you pray [with you]?" They said, "Yes."

So he stood between them, placing one on his right and the other on his left. Then we bowed, and we placed our hands on our knees, but he struck our hands. Then he joined his palms together and placed them between his thighs. When he finished the prayer, he said, "This is how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this chain of transmission; and in the hadith of Ibn Jaʿfar there is not the phrase "fa-dhaʿtuhu."
As for Ibn Abī Shaybah, he said in his narration "fa-daʿtuhu."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were sitting in the mosque, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us.
[This is] similar to their hadith, except that he did not mention that he led the people in that prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That some men
came to Sahl ibn Saʿd. [Another chain:] Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
and Ibn Abī ʿUmar,
they said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us,
from Abū Ḥāzim, who said:
They came to Sahl ibn Saʿd and asked him what the pulpit of the Prophet ﷺ was made of, and they related the hadith similar to the hadith of Ibn Abī Ḥāzim.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he saw phlegm on the qiblah wall of the mosque.
Except for al-Ḍaḥḥāk, for in his narration it says "phlegm in the direction of prayer."
[It is] similar in meaning to the hadith of Mālik.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade eating onions and leeks.
Then need overcame us and we ate some of them, so he said:
"Whoever eats from this foul-smelling plant should not come near our mosque, for the angels are harmed by what harms human beings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We had hardly stopped [waiting] before Khaybar was conquered,

and we, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, fell upon that plant, garlic, while the people were hungry, and we ate of it heartily. Then we went to the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ detected the smell, and he said:
"Whoever has eaten anything from this foul plant should not come near us in the mosque."
The people said, "It has been forbidden! It has been forbidden!"
That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"O people, it is not for me to forbid what Allah has made lawful for me, but it is a plant whose smell I dislike."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions passed by an onion field. Some of them dismounted and ate from it, while others did not eat. Then we went to him, and he called those who had not eaten the onions forward and kept the others back until the smell had gone.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin came after the Prophet ﷺ had prayed the dawn prayer.
He put his head through the door of the mosque, and then he related [the hadith] like their hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of transmission of these [narrators], and he said: "Let him seek what is correct."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat to supplicate, he would place his right hand on his right thigh and his left hand on his left thigh, and point with his index finger, placing his thumb on his middle finger, and he would cup his left palm over his knee.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a governor
in Mecca used to give the salām twice, so ʿAbdullāh said, "He has [truly] learned it." Al-Ḥakam said in his narration that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Warrād,

the freed slave of al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, said: Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah wrote to Muʿāwiyah—Warrād wrote that letter for him—"I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say when he concluded the prayer with the salām," [and he related it] like their two hadith, except for the words:
"and He has power over all things."
For he did not mention [this].
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He heard him] delivering a sermon on this pulpit, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say, when he concluded with the salām at the end of the prayer or prayers:
Then he related it like the hadith of Hishām ibn ʿUrwah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent some men of the Anṣār to Abū Rāfiʿ, the Jew,
and appointed ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAtīk over them.
Abū Rāfiʿ used to harm the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and to help others against him,
and he was in a fortress of his in the land of the Hijāz.
When they came near it,
after the sun had set
and the people had brought their livestock back [home], ʿAbdullāh said to his companions, "Sit where you are, for I am going on, and I will try to be gentle with the gatekeeper,
so that perhaps I may get in."
He advanced until he drew near the gate, then covered himself with his garment as if he were relieving himself,
while the people had gone in.
The gatekeeper called out to him, "O servant of Allah, if you want to come in, then come in,
for I want to close the gate." [ʿAbdullāh said:] So I entered and hid.
When the people had all come in, he closed the gate,
then hung the keys on a peg. He said: I got up and went to the keys,
took them, and opened the gate.
Abū Rāfiʿ used to have evening conversations in his company,
and he was in an upper chamber of his.
When the people of his evening company had left him, I climbed up to him,
and every time I opened a door, I locked it behind me from the inside.
I said, "If the people become aware of me, they will not be able to reach me until I have killed him." So I reached him,
and there he was in a dark house, in the midst of his family,
and I did not know where in the house he was. So I said, "O Abū Rāfiʿ!"
He said, "Who is this?" So I lunged toward the voice
and struck him a blow with the sword,
while I was bewildered, and it accomplished nothing.
He cried out, so I went out of the house
and waited a short while, then went back in to him and said, "What is this voice, O Abū Rāfiʿ?"
He said, "Woe to your mother!
A man is in the house who just struck me with a sword."
He said: So I struck him a blow that wounded him severely, but I did not kill him.
Then I placed the point of the sword on his belly until it came out through his back,
and I knew that I had killed him.
I began opening the doors one by one until I reached a staircase of his,
and I put down my foot, thinking that I had reached the ground, but I fell on a moonlit night and broke my leg. I bound it with a turban,

then went on until I sat at the gate and said, "I will not leave tonight until I know whether I have killed him." When the rooster crowed, the announcer of the death stood on the wall and said, "I announce the death of Abū Rāfiʿ, the merchant of the people of the Hijāz."
So I went to my companions and said, "Flee to safety,
for Allah has killed Abū Rāfiʿ."
I came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him, and he said, "Stretch out your leg." So I stretched out my leg, and he wiped over it,
and it was as if I had never been in pain from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said, "War is deception."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Uḥud the Prophet ﷺ appointed ʿAbdullāh ibn Jubayr over the foot soldiers, and they were fifty men, and he said,
"If you see us being snatched up by the birds,
do not leave this place of yours until I send for you.
And if you see that we have defeated the enemy and trampled them, do not leave until I send for you." Then they defeated them.
[Al-Barāʾ] said: By Allah, I saw the women running, their anklets showing and their legs, lifting up their garments.
The companions of ʿAbdullāh ibn Jubayr said, "The spoils, O people, the spoils!

Your companions have prevailed, so what are you waiting for?" ʿAbdullāh ibn Jubayr said, "Have you forgotten what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to you?" They said, "By Allah, we will go to the people and take some of the spoils."
But when they came to them, their faces were turned away, and they came back defeated.
That is when the Messenger was calling them from behind them,
and no more than twelve men were left with the Prophet ﷺ.
They inflicted seventy [casualties] on us,
whereas the Prophet ﷺ and his companions had inflicted on the polytheists on the day of Badr one hundred and forty: seventy captives and seventy killed.
Abū Sufyān said, "Is Muḥammad among the people?" three times.
The Prophet ﷺ forbade them to answer him. Then he said, "Is the son of Abū Quḥāfah among the people?" three times.
Then he said, "Is the son of al-Khaṭṭāb among the people?" three times.
Then he returned to his companions and said, "As for these, they have been killed."
ʿUmar could not restrain himself and said, "You lie, by Allah, O enemy of Allah!
Those whom you counted are all alive,
and what will grieve you remains for you."
[Abū Sufyān] said, "A day for the day of Badr, and war is [a matter of] turns.
You will find mutilation among your people, which I did not order, though it did not displease me."
Then he began chanting, "Exalted be Hubal, exalted be Hubal!" The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Will you not answer him?"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah,
what should we say?" He said,
"Say: Allah is Higher and more Majestic."
[Abū Sufyān] said, "We have al-ʿUzzā, and you have no ʿUzzā." The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Will you not answer him?"
They said,
"O Messenger of Allah, what should we say?" He said,
"Say: Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I performed the circumambulation with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, and when we had finished the seven rounds, we prayed two rakʿahs behind the Kaʿbah. I said, "Shall we not seek refuge in Allah from the Fire?"
He said, "I seek refuge in Allah from the Fire."

Then he went on and touched the corner, then stood between the Black Stone and the door, and pressed his chest, his hands, and his cheek against it. Then he said, "This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to lead Ibn ʿAbbās and make him stand at the third section, near the corner that is next to the Stone, the one by the door. Ibn ʿAbbās would say to him, "I was informed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray here." He would say, "Yes." Then [Ibn ʿAbbās] would stand and pray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to stop at ʿArafah in the valley of Namirah.
He said: When al-Ḥajjāj killed Ibn al-Zubayr, he sent a message to Ibn ʿUmar: "At what hour did the Prophet ﷺ set out on this day?" He replied, "When that time comes, we will set out."
So al-Ḥajjāj sent a man to watch for the time of departure.
When Ibn ʿUmar wanted to set out, he said, "Has the sun passed its zenith?" They said, "Not yet."
So he sat down, then said, "Has the sun passed its zenith?" They said, "Not yet."
So he sat down, then said, "Has the sun passed its zenith?" They said, "Not yet."
So he sat down, then said, "Has the sun passed its zenith?" They said, "Yes."
When they said it had passed its zenith, he set out.
Wakīʿ said: That is, he departed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressing the people on the day of ʿArafah on a camel, standing in the two stirrups.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to send ahead the weak members of his family in the darkness before dawn, and he would instruct them not to throw the pebbles at the Jamrah until the sun had risen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us while we were at Minā, and our ears were opened so that we could hear what he said while we were in our dwellings. He began teaching them the rites of Hajj until he reached the Jamarāt. He put his two index fingers in his ears and said, "With pebbles the size of those used for flicking."
Then he commanded the Muhājirūn, and they camped at the front of the mosque, and he commanded the Anṣār, and they camped behind the mosque. Then the rest of the people camped after that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to go to the Jamarāt on the three days after the Day of Sacrifice, walking both going and returning, and he would report that the Prophet ﷺ used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about something
concerning the matter of the Jamarāt. He said, "I do not know whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ threw six or seven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ did not walk briskly (ramal) in the seven rounds in which he performed the Ifāḍah circumambulation.
ʿAṭāʾ said: And there is no ramal in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed a certain place in the house of Yaʿlā (ʿUbaydullāh forgot which), he would face the House and make supplication.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man sent some dirhams with me as a gift to the House.
He said: I entered the House while Shaybah was sitting on a chair, and I handed them to him.
He said, "Are these yours?" I said, "No, and if they were mine I would not have brought them to you."

He said, "If you say that, then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb sat in this very seat of yours where you are sitting and said, 'I will not leave until I distribute the wealth of the Kaʿbah among the poor Muslims.'"
I said, "You will not do that." He said, "I certainly will."
He said, "Why is that?" I said, "Because the Prophet ﷺ saw its place,
and so did Abū Bakr, and they were in greater need of money than you, yet they did not disturb it."
So he got up just as he was and left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "My wife does not refuse the hand of anyone who touches her." He said:
"Divorce her if you wish."
He said, "I fear that I would still long for her." He said, "Then enjoy her company."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "I have found a woman of noble lineage and high standing, except that she does not bear children. Shall I marry her?" He forbade him. Then he came to him a second time, and he forbade him. Then he came to him a third time, and he forbade him. He said:
"Marry women who are loving and fertile, for I will boast of your great numbers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her while she was in the land of Abyssinia. The Negus married her to him, gave her a dowry of four thousand, and prepared her from his own means, and sent her with Shuraḥbīl ibn Ḥasanah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not send her anything. The dowry of his wives was four hundred dirhams.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A girl,
a virgin, came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned to him that her father had married her off while she was unwilling. So the Prophet ﷺ gave her the choice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik ibn Anas, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
that he said: The Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him that a man and a woman from among them had committed adultery. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them,
"What do you find in the Torah concerning adultery?"
They said, "We disgrace them and they are flogged."
ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām said, "You are lying; it contains stoning."

So they brought the Torah and spread it open, and one of them placed his hand over the verse of stoning, then began reading what came before it and what came after it. ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām said to him, "Raise your hand."
He raised it, and there was the verse of stoning. They said, "He has spoken the truth, O Muhammad; the verse of stoning is in it."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that the two be stoned, and they were stoned.
ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: I saw the man leaning over the woman, shielding her from the stones.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Minā, the moon split into two parts, one part behind the mountain and one part on this side of it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us, "Bear witness." That is, [referring to the verse:]
"The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split." He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to the Prophet ﷺ while we were in the cave, "If one of them were to look at his feet, he would see us beneath his feet." He said:
"O Abū Bakr!
What do you think of two, the third of whom is Allah?"
He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb. It is only known from the narration of Hammām, who was alone in narrating it.
This hadith has also been narrated by Ḥabbān ibn Hilāl and more than one other, from Hammām, similar to this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke with him about something,
and he instructed her to do something. She said, "What do you think, O Messenger of Allah, if I do not find you?" He said:
"If you do not find me, then go to Abū Bakr."
Al-Ḥumaydī added, from Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd: It was as if she meant death.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever drags his garment out of arrogance, Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection."
Abū Bakr said, "One side of my garment hangs down unless I take care of it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You are not doing that out of arrogance."
Mūsā said: I said to Sālim, "Did ʿAbdullāh mention 'whoever drags his lower garment'?" He said, "I did not hear him mention anything except 'his garment'."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ climbed Uḥud, and with him were Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān, and it shook with them. He struck it with his foot and said:
"Be still, Uḥud! There is upon you only a prophet, a ṣiddīq, and two martyrs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was laid on his bier, and the people gathered around him, supplicating, praising him and praying for him before he was lifted, and I was among them. [Ibn ʿAbbās] said: I was startled only by a man who took hold of my shoulder from behind. I turned to him and it was ʿAlī. He asked Allah's mercy for ʿUmar and said, "You have left behind no one whom I would love more to meet Allah with the like of his deeds than you. By Allah, I used to think that Allah would place you with your two companions, because I often heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'I came, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; I entered, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; I left, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.'
So I hoped, or I thought, that Allah would place you with them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I set out with the Prophet ﷺ and he entered an orchard belonging to the Anṣār and relieved himself. He said to me:
"O Abū Mūsā, guard the door for me, and let no one enter upon me except with permission."
A man came and knocked on the door. I said, "Who is this?" He said, "Abū Bakr."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is Abū Bakr asking permission." He said:
"Let him in and give him the good news of Paradise."
He entered, and I gave him the good news of Paradise. Another man came and knocked on the door. I said, "Who is this?" He said, "ʿUmar."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is ʿUmar asking permission." He said:
"Open for him and give him the good news of Paradise."
So I opened the door and he entered, and I gave him the good news of Paradise. Then another man came and knocked on the door. I said, "Who is this?" He said, "ʿUthmān."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is ʿUthmān asking permission." He said:
"Open for him and give him the good news of Paradise, along with a trial that will befall him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this report he said: Then dates were brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he gave them to him, about fifteen ṣāʿs, and said, "Give this in charity (ṣadaqah)."
He said: He said, "O Messenger of Allah, [is there anyone] poorer than me and my family?" So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Eat it, you and your family."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My brother ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit [reported] that the Prophet ﷺ gave him fifteen ṣāʿs of barley to feed sixty poor people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jamīlah

was married to Aws ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit, who was a man afflicted with a touch of madness. Whenever it grew severe, he would pronounce ẓihār against his wife, so Allah, the Exalted, revealed concerning him the expiation for ẓihār.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From ʿIkrimah. Abū Dāwūd said: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Ḥurayth wrote to me, saying: Al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā informed us, from Maʿmar,
from al-Ḥakam ibn Abān, from ʿIkrimah,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
with similar meaning, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥabībah bint Sahl

was married to Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās, and he struck her and broke part of her [body]. She came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after the dawn prayer and complained about him to him. So the Prophet ﷺ called Thābit and said,
"Take part of her property and separate from her."
He said, "Is that proper, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "I gave her two gardens as her dowry, and they are in her possession." The Prophet ﷺ said, "Take them and separate from her." So he did.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The waiting period of a woman who has obtained a khulʿ divorce is one menstrual cycle.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The husband of
Barīrah was a free man when she was emancipated, and she was given the choice. She said, "I do not like to be with him, and I would have such and such."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Barīrah
was emancipated while she was married to Mughīth, a slave of the family of Abū Aḥmad. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave her the choice and said to her,
"If he comes near you, you have no choice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She wished to emancipate
two slaves of hers who were husband and wife. He said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ about that, and he commanded her to begin with the man before the woman.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He embraced Islam, but his wife refused to embrace Islam. She came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "My daughter," and she was weaned or about that age. Rāfiʿ said, "My daughter."
The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "Sit on one side," and said to her, "Sit on one side."
He said: And he seated the little girl between them, then said, "Call her."
The girl inclined toward her mother, so the Prophet ﷺ said, "O Allah, guide her."
Then the girl inclined toward her father, and he took her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī,
"Keep the woman with you until she gives birth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present at their mutual imprecation (liʿān) before the Prophet ﷺ, when I was fifteen years old.
And he related the hadith, saying in it: Then she went out pregnant, and the child was called by his mother's name.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this report he said: He was called, meaning the child, by his mother's name.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In this report he said: So he divorced her three times in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ enforced it, and what he did in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ became the established practice.

Sahl said: I was present for this before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Thereafter the established practice regarding two who have exchanged imprecation was that they be separated and never come together again.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Musaddad said: I witnessed the two who exchanged imprecation in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when I was fifteen years old, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them when they had exchanged imprecation.
The hadith of Musaddad is complete.

The others said that he witnessed the Prophet ﷺ separate the two who had exchanged imprecation, and the man said, "I would be lying about her, O Messenger of Allah, if I kept her." Some of them did not say "about her." Abū Dāwūd said: No one corroborated Ibn ʿUyaynah in [saying] that he separated the two who had exchanged imprecation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever eats from this plant, garlic, let him not harm us with it in this mosque of ours."
Ibrāhīm said: My father would add to it leeks and onions, from the Prophet ﷺ.
He means that he added to the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, which mentions garlic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge from the jinn and from the evil eye of humans, until the two chapters of refuge were revealed. When they were revealed, he took to them and left everything else.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He looked down from above on the day of the siege of the house and said: "I ask you by Allah, do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'The blood of a Muslim is not lawful except for one of three [reasons]: adultery after being married, apostasy after Islam, or killing a person without right, for which he is killed.'

By Allah, I never committed adultery, neither in the Time of Ignorance nor in Islam, I have not apostatized since I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I have not killed the soul that Allah has forbidden. So for what [reason] do you kill me?" Abū ʿĪsā said: There are also narrations on this topic from Ibn Masʿūd, ʿĀʾishah, and Ibn ʿAbbās.
And this is a good (ḥasan) hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I stayed with Abū Hāshim ibn ʿUtbah while he was stricken with the plague. Muʿāwiyah came to visit him, and Abū Hāshim wept. Muʿāwiyah said: "What makes you weep, uncle? Is it a pain that distresses you, or is it grief over the world, whose best has already passed?" He said: "Neither of these. Rather, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a covenant with me, and I wish I had followed it." He said:
"Perhaps you will live to see wealth distributed among people, but all that will suffice you is a servant and a mount in the path of Allah." Yet I lived to see it, and I accumulated [wealth].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The covenant between us and them is the prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A believer has six rights over another believer: he visits him when he is ill, attends his funeral when he dies, answers him when he invites him, greets him with salām when he meets him, says 'May Allah have mercy on you' when he sneezes, and gives him sincere advice when he is absent or present."
He said: This is a good and authentic (ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ) hadith.
Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Makhzūmī al-Madanī is trustworthy; ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad and Ibn Abī Fudayk narrated from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'Say: He is Allah, [who is] One' is equal to a third of the Qur'an."
This is a good and authentic (ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ) hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a woman who prayed behind the Prophet ﷺ, one of the most beautiful of people. Some of the men would move forward to the first row so that they would not see her, while others would hang back until they were in the last row. When he bowed, one would look like this, from beneath his armpit. So Allah revealed: {And We certainly know the preceding ones among you, and We certainly know the later ones} concerning her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah has guaranteed for the one who goes out in His path, nothing bringing him out except striving in My path, belief in Me, and affirmation of My messengers: he is under My guarantee that I will admit him to Paradise, or return him to his home from which he went out, having gained whatever he gained of reward or spoils.

By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no wound is inflicted in the path of Allah except that it will come on the Day of Resurrection as it was when it was inflicted: its color the color of blood, and its scent that of musk. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, were it not that it would be hard on the Muslims, I would never stay behind any expedition that fights in the path of Allah. But I do not find the means to carry them, and they do not find the means, and it would be hard on them to stay behind me. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, I would love to fight in the path of Allah and be killed, then fight and be killed, then fight and be killed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were waiting for ʿAbdullāh when Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah came. We said: "Will you not sit?" He said: "No, but I will go in and bring your companion out to you,
and if not, I will come back."
So I sat. Then ʿAbdullāh came out, holding his hand, and stood before us and said: "I know that you are here,
but what keeps me from coming out to you is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to space out his admonitions to us over the days,
fearing that we would become bored."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent one of his Companions on some errand of his, he would say:
"Give glad tidings and do not repel; make things easy and do not make them difficult."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Abū Jaʿfar, I said to him: "It has been narrated to me from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh
that the Prophet ﷺ performed ablution once each." He said: "Yes."
I said: "And twice each, and three times each?" He said: "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us one day wearing a Roman woollen cloak with narrow sleeves, and he led us in prayer in it, wearing nothing else.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Banū Murrah ibn ʿUbayd sent me with the charities (ṣadaqāt) from their wealth to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I came to him in Medina and found him sitting between the Emigrants and the Helpers. Then he took me by the hand and went with me to the house of Umm Salamah, and he said:
"Is there any food?"

So a large bowl was brought to us with plenty of tharīd and wadhr [pieces of meat]. We began to eat from it, and I moved my hand around its sides, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ate from what was in front of him. He gripped my right hand with his left hand and then said:
"O ʿIkrāsh, eat from one place, for it is one kind of food."

Then a tray was brought to us containing various kinds of fresh dates or dried dates—ʿUbaydullāh was unsure which. He said: I began to eat from what was in front of me, while the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ moved around the tray, and he said:
"O ʿIkrāsh, eat from wherever you wish, for it is not one kind."
Then water was brought to us, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ washed his hands, and wiped his face, forearms and head with the moisture of his palms, and said:
"O ʿIkrāsh, this is the ablution [required] after what the fire has touched."
There is a story in the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ...who is called ʿAṭāʾ, from the people of Syria, from Abū Usayd, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Eat olive oil and anoint yourselves with it, for it comes from a blessed tree."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Worship the Most Merciful, feed others, and spread the greeting of peace; you will enter Paradise in peace."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The one who treats those under his authority badly will not enter Paradise."
They said: O Messenger of Allah, did you not tell us that this nation has more slaves and orphans than any other nation? He said:
"Yes. So honor them as you honor your own children, and feed them from what you eat."
They said: Then what will benefit us in this world? He said:
"A horse that you keep tethered and fight on in the cause of Allah. Your slave suffices you, and when he prays, he is your brother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to have cupping done on the two veins of the neck and between the shoulders, and he used to have it done on the seventeenth, nineteenth and twenty-first [of the month].
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
shot another man with an arrow and killed him, and he had no heir except a maternal uncle. Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ wrote about that to ʿUmar, and ʿUmar wrote back to him that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Allah and His Messenger are the protector of one who has no protector, and the maternal uncle is the heir of one who has no heir."
label: machine translation

segments_en: During the Farewell Pilgrimage, he said to the people:
"Which day is this?"
They said: The day of the greater Hajj. He said:

"Indeed your blood, your property and your honor are sacred among you, like the sanctity of this day of yours in this land of yours. Beware! No offender offends except against himself. Beware! No offender offends against his child, nor a child against his father. Beware! Satan has despaired of ever being worshipped in this land of yours, but he will be obeyed in what you regard as insignificant of your deeds, and he will be pleased with that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, and there was a dead sheep with its leg raised. He said:

"Do you see this as worthless to its owner? By the One in whose hand is my soul, this world is more worthless to Allah than this is to its owner. If this world weighed with Allah as much as the wing of a mosquito, He would never give a disbeliever a drop of water from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of my shoulder and said:
"Be in this world as if you were a stranger or a passer-by, and count yourself among the dwellers of the graves."

Ibn ʿUmar said to me: When you reach the morning, do not expect the evening, and when you reach the evening, do not expect the morning. Take from your health before your illness, and from your life before your death, for you do not know, O servant of Allah, what your name will be tomorrow.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever among you wakes up secure in his dwelling, healthy in his body, having his food for the day, it is as if the world has been gathered for him." Abū ʿĪsā said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith; we only know it from the narration of Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah. Ḥīzat means 'was gathered'. Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl narrated it to us, [saying] al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us, [saying] Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, similarly. And there is a report on this topic from Abū al-Dardāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Ḥamzah,
the two sons of ʿAbdullāh, from their father,
from the Prophet ﷺ. (Transfer of chain.) And Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā and ʿAmr al-Nāqid narrated to us,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb, from Sufyān, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father,
from the Prophet ﷺ. (Transfer of chain.) And ʿAmr al-Nāqid narrated to us,
Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ,
from Ibn Shihāb, from Sālim and Ḥamzah,
the two sons of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,
from the Prophet ﷺ. (Transfer of chain.) And ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth ibn Saʿd narrated to me: my father narrated to me, from my grandfather,
ʿUqayl ibn Khālid narrated to me,
(Transfer of chain.) And Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā narrated it to us,
Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal informed us,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn
Isḥāq. (Transfer of chain.) And ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Dārimī narrated to me,
Abū al-Yamān informed us: Shuʿayb informed us,
all of them from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father,
from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning ill omen.
Like the hadith of Mālik. None of them mentions, in the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, 'the ʿAdawī' and 'bird omens', except Yūnus ibn Yazīd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas ibn Mālik
informed them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted permission to al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf to wear two shirts of silk because of an itching ailment that afflicted them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that the Quraysh were concerned about the matter of the woman who had stolen during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, in the campaign of the Conquest. They said, "Who will speak to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about her?" They said, "Who would dare to do so except Usāmah ibn Zayd, the beloved of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?"
She was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Usāmah ibn Zayd spoke to him about her. The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed color, and he said:
"Do you intercede regarding one of the prescribed punishments of Allah?"
Usāmah said to him, "Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of Allah."
In the evening, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up and delivered a speech. He praised Allah as He deserves, then said:

"To proceed: Those before you were destroyed only because when a noble among them stole, they let him go, and when a weak person among them stole, they carried out the punishment on him. By the One in whose hand is my soul, if Fāṭimah, daughter of Muḥammad, were to steal, I would cut off her hand."
Then he gave the order concerning that woman who had stolen, and her hand was cut off.

Yūnus said: Ibn Shihāb said: ʿUrwah said: ʿĀʾishah said: Her repentance was good afterwards, and she married. She used to come to me after that, and I would present her need to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that a man
accused his wife of adultery and disowned her child during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered them both, and they performed mutual imprecation, as Allah said.
Then he ruled that the child belonged to the woman, and he separated the two who had performed the mutual imprecation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever among you swears and says in his oath, 'By al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā,'
let him say, 'There is no god but Allah.'
And whoever says to his companion, 'Come, let me gamble with you,' let him give charity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The example of the believer who recites the Qur'an is that of the citron: its fragrance is good and its taste is good. The example of the believer who does not recite the Qur'an is that of the date: its taste is good but it has no fragrance. The example of the wicked person who recites the Qur'an is that of basil: its fragrance is good but its taste is bitter. The example of the wicked person who does not recite the Qur'an is that of the colocynth: its taste is bitter and it has no fragrance. The example of the righteous companion is that of the seller of musk: if nothing of it reaches you, its fragrance still does. The example of the evil companion is that of the blacksmith's bellows: if his soot does not reach you, his smoke does."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When what happened between Abraham and his family had happened,
he went out with Ishmael and Ishmael's mother,
and they had with them a water skin containing water.
Ishmael's mother would drink from the water skin, and her milk would flow for her baby, until he came to Makkah.
He placed her under a large tree,
then Abraham returned to his family,
and Ishmael's mother followed him,
until, when they reached Kadā', she called out to him from behind him: "O Abraham, to whom are you leaving us?" He said: "To Allah."
She said: "I am content with Allah."
He said: So she went back and would drink from the water skin, and her milk would flow for her baby,
until, when the water ran out, she said: "If only I went and looked, perhaps I might sense someone."
He said: So she went and climbed aṣ-Ṣafā and looked and looked, [to see] whether she could sense anyone, but she sensed no one.
When she reached the valley, she ran, and came to al-Marwah, and she did that for several laps.
Then she said: "If only I went and looked at what has become of him," meaning the child. So she went and looked,
and there he was in his condition, as though he were gasping in death.
So she could not bear to stay,
and she said: "If only I went and looked, perhaps I might sense someone."
So she went and climbed aṣ-Ṣafā and looked and looked, but she sensed no one,
until she had completed seven [laps].
