Then she said: "If only I went and looked at what has become of him."
Then suddenly there was a voice, and she said: "Help me, if you have any good [to offer]!" And there was Gabriel.
He said: He struck with his heel like this,
and he pressed his heel into the ground.
He said: And the water gushed forth,
and Ishmael's mother was bewildered, and she began to hasten [to contain it].
He said: Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ said:
"If she had left it, the water would have flowed openly."
He said: So she began to drink from the water,
and her milk would flow for her baby. He said: Then some people of Jurhum passed by the bottom of the valley,
and there were birds,
as though they found that strange,
and they said: "Birds are only found over water." So they sent their messenger,
and he looked and found the water,
so he came to them and told them, and they came to her,
and they said: "O mother of Ishmael,
will you permit us to be with you, or to dwell with you?" Her son grew up and married a woman from among them.
He said: Then it occurred to Abraham, and he said to his family: "I am going to look in on what I left behind."
He said: So he came and greeted, and said: "Where is Ishmael?" His wife said: "He has gone hunting."
He said: "Tell him when he comes: change the threshold of your door."
When he came, she told him. He said: "That is you; go back to your family."
He said: Then it occurred to Abraham, and he said to his family: "I am going to look in on what I left behind."
He said: So he came and said: "Where is Ishmael?" His wife said: "He has gone hunting,
" and she said: "Will you not get down and eat and drink?" He said: "What is your food and what is your drink?" She said: "Our food is meat and our drink is water."
He said: "O Allah, bless them in their food and drink."
He said: Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ said:
"A blessing from the supplication of Abraham."
He said: Then it occurred to Abraham, and he said to his family: "I am going to look in on what I left behind."
So he came and found Ishmael behind Zamzam,
mending arrows of his.
He said: "O Ishmael,
your Lord has commanded me to build a house for Him."
He said: "Obey your Lord."
He said: "He has commanded me that you help me with it."
He said: "Then I will do so."
Or as he said.
He said: So they rose, and Abraham began to build
while Ishmael handed him the stones,
and they both said: {Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.} He said: until the building rose high and the old man grew too weak to carry the stones,
so he stood on the stone of the Station,
and Ishmael kept handing him the stones,
and they both said: {Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ
mention the one who hamstrung the she-camel. He said:
"A man of might and protection among his people, strong like Abū Zamʿah, rose up for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at al-Ḥijr during the expedition of Tabūk, he commanded them not to drink from its well
and not to draw water from it. They said: "We have already kneaded dough with it and drawn water."
So he commanded them to throw away that dough and pour out that water.
It is also narrated from Sabrah ibn Maʿbad and Abū ash-Shumūs that the Prophet ﷺ commanded that the food be thrown away.
Abū Dharr said, from the Prophet ﷺ:
"Whoever kneaded dough with its water..."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Umm Rūmān,
who is the mother of ʿĀʾishah,
about what was said concerning her. She said: While I was sitting with ʿĀʾishah,
a woman of the Anṣār came in to us,
saying: "May Allah do such and such to so-and-so!"
She said: I said: "Why?" She said: "He spread the story," and she mentioned the report.
ʿĀʾishah said: "Which report?" So I told her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy ibn Qamaʿah ibn Khindif is the father of Khuzāʿah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution, he would take a handful of water and do like this—Shuʿbah described it—and sprinkle his private part with it. I mentioned it to Ibrāhīm and he liked it. The Shaykh Ibn al-Sunnī said: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Al-Ḥakam is the son of Sufyān al-Thaqafī, may Allah be pleased with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, perform ablution washing three times each, then he stood and drank the remainder of his ablution water and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did as I have done.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ at al-Baṭḥāʾ, and Bilāl brought out the leftover water of his ablution, and the people rushed to it, and I obtained some of it. A short spear was planted for him, and he led the people in prayer while donkeys, dogs and women passed in front of him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not single us out with anything apart from the people except three things: he commanded us to perform ablution thoroughly, not to eat charity, and not to breed donkeys with horses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Perform ablution thoroughly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how is ablution performed?" He said:

"As for ablution, when you perform ablution and wash your hands and cleanse them, your sins leave from between your nails and fingertips. When you rinse your mouth, sniff water into your nostrils, wash your face and your arms up to the elbows, wipe your head and wash your feet up to the ankles, you have been cleansed of most of your sins. Then if you set your face toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, you come out of your sins like the day your mother bore you."

Abū Umāmah said: I said, "O ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah, consider what you are saying! Is all this given in a single sitting?" He said: "By Allah, my age has advanced and my time is near, and I am not in poverty that I would lie about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I heard it with my own ears and my heart retained it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Marwān, during his governorship of Madīnah, mentioned that one performs ablution after touching the private part when a man's hand reaches it. I rejected that and said: There is no ablution required for the one who touches it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray while I lay across in front of him like a funeral bier, until, when he wanted to pray the Witr, he would touch me with his foot.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Should I perform ablution because of food that I find in the Book of Allah to be lawful, merely because fire has touched it?" So Abū Hurayrah gathered some pebbles and said: "I bear witness, by the number of these pebbles, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Perform ablution after what fire has touched.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eat bread and meat, then stand for prayer without performing ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Thumāmah ibn Uthāl al-Ḥanafī went to a palm grove near the mosque and bathed, then entered the mosque and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger. O Muḥammad, by Allah, there was no face on earth more hateful to me than your face, and now your face has become the most beloved of all faces to me. Your horsemen seized me while I was intending ʿUmrah; what do you think?" So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him glad tidings and commanded him to perform ʿUmrah. [Abridged]
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He], may Allah be pleased with him, came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Abū Ṭālib has died." He said: "Go and bury him."
He said: "He died a polytheist." He said: "Go and bury him."
When I had buried him, I returned to him, and he said to me: "Bathe."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Water is from water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Ḥabībah bint Jaḥsh, who
was married to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, suffered from abnormal bleeding and did not become pure. Her case was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"This is not the menstrual period, but a kick from the womb. Let her observe the length of her usual menstrual period and leave prayer for it, then look at what follows and bathe for every prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿĀʾishah and asked her, saying: "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bathe at the beginning of the night or at the end of it?" She said: "He did both; sometimes he bathed at the beginning and sometimes at the end."
I said: "Praise be to Allah, who made allowance in the matter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A cup was brought to Mujāhid, which I estimated to hold eight raṭls. He said: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to bathe with the like of this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recall myself contending with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over the vessel, as he and I bathed from it together.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾidh Allāh reported that ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit, who was among those who fought at Badr with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and was one of his Companions on the Night of al-ʿAqabah, informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, while a group of his Companions was around him: "
Come and pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, that you will not steal, that you will not commit adultery,
that you will not kill your children,
that you will not bring a slander which you invent between your hands and your feet,
and that you will not disobey me in what is right.
Whoever among you fulfills this, his reward is with Allah.
Whoever commits any of these and is punished for it in this world, it is an expiation for him.
Whoever commits any of these and Allah conceals it, his matter is left to Allah:
if He wills, He will punish him,
and if He wills, He will pardon him."
He said: So I pledged allegiance to him on that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was narrated from] the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ that the Prophet ﷺ said: "

While I was asleep, I saw people being presented to me, wearing shirts; some reached only the chest, and some reached lower than that. Then ʿUmar was presented to me, wearing a shirt that he was dragging."
They said: "How did you interpret it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked which deeds are best, or which deeds are better. He said: "
Belief in Allah and His Messenger."
It was said: "Then what?" He said: "
Jihad, the peak of the deed."
It was said: "Then what, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "
Then an accepted Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥawlāʾ bint Tuwayt ibn Ḥabīb ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā passed by her while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with her. I said: "This is al-Ḥawlāʾ bint Tuwayt, and they claim that she does not sleep at night." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
She does not sleep at night? Take on only the deeds that you can bear, for by Allah, Allah does not grow weary until you grow weary."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from the Jews came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, there is a verse in your Book that you recite; if it had been revealed to us, the community of Jews, we would have taken that day as a festival." He said: "Which verse?" He said: "Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and approved Islam as your religion." ʿUmar said: "I know the place where it was revealed and the day on which it was revealed. It was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at ʿArafāt on a Friday."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from the people of Najd, with disheveled hair, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We could hear the buzz of his voice but could not understand what he was saying, until he came near, and it turned out he was asking about Islam. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Five prayers in the day and night."
He said: "Is there anything else I must do?" He said: "
No, unless you volunteer."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also mentioned to him fasting in the month of Ramadan. He said: "Is there anything else I must do?" He said: "
No, unless you volunteer."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also mentioned charity to him.
He said: "Is there anything else I must give?" He said: "
No, unless you volunteer."
The man turned away, saying: "By Allah, I will not add to this nor subtract from it."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
He will succeed if he is truthful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah died, [Jarīr] stood up, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said: "Hold fast to fear of Allah alone, who has no partner,
and to dignity and calm until a new governor comes to you,
for he will be coming to you soon."
Then he said: "Ask forgiveness for your governor,
for he used to love pardoning."
Then he said: "To proceed:
I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, 'I pledge allegiance to you on Islam.'
He made it a condition upon me to give sincere advice to every Muslim.
So I pledged allegiance to him on this,
and by the Lord of this mosque, I am indeed sincere toward you."
Then he asked forgiveness and came down.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That some people

from the people of Iraq came and said, "O Ibn ʿAbbās, do you consider the ritual bath on Friday to be obligatory?" He said, "No, but it is purer and better for whoever does it, and whoever does not bathe, it is not obligatory upon him. And I will tell you how the bathing began: the people were in hardship, wearing wool and working on their backs, and their mosque was cramped with a low ceiling; it was merely a shelter of branches. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out on a hot day, and the people had sweated in that wool until foul odors rose from them, and they were harming one another with it. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ noticed that odor, he said:
"O people, when this day comes, bathe, and let each of you apply the best of the oil and perfume that he has."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: Then Allah brought about prosperity, and they wore clothes other than wool, were spared from labor, their mosque was enlarged, and some of the harm they used to cause one another through sweat went away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "I have accepted Islam."
The Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"Shave off the hair of disbelief from yourself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, about a menstruating woman whose garment gets blood on it.
She said: She should wash it, and if its trace does not go away, she should change its color with a little yellow dye.
She said: I used to menstruate during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for three menstrual periods together, and I would not wash a garment of mine.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Umm Salamah, and a woman from Quraysh asked her about praying in the garment of a menstruating woman. Umm Salamah said: We used to menstruate during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and one of us would stay for the days of her menses, then become pure, and look at the garment in which she had been turning about. If blood had gotten on it, we would wash it and pray in it, and if nothing had gotten on it, we would leave it, and that did not stop us from praying in it. As for the woman with braided hair, one of us would have her hair braided, and when she bathed she would not undo it; rather she would pour three handfuls of water over her head, and when she saw that the roots of the hair were wet, she would rub them, then pour water over the rest of her body.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Khawlah bint Yasār
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have only one garment, and I menstruate in it. What should I do?" He said:
"When you become pure, wash it, then pray in it."
She said, "And if the blood does not come out?" He said:
"Washing away the blood is enough for you, and its trace will not harm you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to serve the Prophet ﷺ, and when he wanted to bathe he would say, "Turn your back to me."
So I would turn my back to him and screen him with it. Then al-Ḥasan or al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, was brought, and he urinated on his chest. I came to wash it, and he said:
"The urine of a girl is washed, and the urine of a boy is sprinkled."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That she saw Umm Salamah pouring water over the urine of a boy so long as he had not begun eating food; when he had begun eating food, she would wash it. And she would wash the urine of a girl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, with this story. He said in it that he, meaning the Prophet ﷺ, said:
"Take the soil on which he urinated and throw it away, and pour water over its place."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was informed that Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Maqburī
related from his father,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you treads on filth with his sandals, the soil is a purifier for them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That she asked ʿĀʾishah about menstrual blood that gets on a garment. She said: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we were wearing our undergarments, and we had thrown a cloak over them. When the morning came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the cloak and put it on, then went out and prayed the morning prayer, then sat. A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is a spot of blood."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gripped the part next to it and sent it to me, bundled up in the hand of the servant boy, and said:
"Wash this and dry it, then send it back to me."
So I called for my bowl, washed it, then dried it and sent it back to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came at midday, and it was upon him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spat in his garment and rubbed one part of it against another.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to pray the Ẓuhr prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I would take a handful of pebbles so that they would cool in my palm, and I would place them for my forehead to prostrate upon them because of the intensity of the heat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And al-ʿAwālī is two or three miles away.
He said: And I think he said, or four.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Its life is that you find its heat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ recited the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about Ibrāhīm: "My Lord, indeed they have led astray many of the people; so whoever follows me, then he is of me..." [Ibrāhīm 14:36], the verse.

And ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, said: "If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Almighty, the All-Wise." [al-Māʾidah 5:118] Then he raised his hands and said:
"O Allah, my Ummah, my Ummah!"

And he wept. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "O Jibrīl, go to Muhammad—and your Lord knows best—and ask him what makes him weep." So Jibrīl, peace and blessings be upon him, came to him and asked him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ told him what he had said, though He knows best.
Then Allah said: "O Jibrīl, go to Muhammad and say: We will please you concerning your Ummah, and We will not displease you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, something similar to this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When [the verse] "And warn your closest kinsmen" was revealed, he said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ set out to a rocky height on a mountain, climbed to the top of it on a stone, and then called out:

"O sons of ʿAbd Manāf! I am a warner. My likeness and yours is that of a man who saw the enemy, so he went off to scout for his family, fearing that the enemy would get ahead of him, and he began to cry out: 'O, the morning attack!'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, Ibn Judʿān in the Pre-Islamic Era used to maintain ties of kinship and feed the poor. Will that benefit him?" He said:
"It will not benefit him, for he never said one day: 'My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and he said: "Which of you saw the star that shot down last night?" I said: "I did."
Then I said: "I was not in prayer, but I had been stung."
He said: "What did you do?" I said: "I sought a ruqyah [cure by recitation]."
He said: "What made you do that?" I said: "A hadith that ash-Shaʿbī narrated to us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The nations were presented to me."
Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith, similar to the hadith of Hushaym, but he did not mention the beginning of his hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar entered upon Ibn ʿĀmir to visit him while he was ill, and [Ibn ʿĀmir] said: "Will you not supplicate to Allah for me, O Ibn ʿUmar?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr and Wakīʿ, from Isrāʾīl,
all of them from Simāk ibn Ḥarb,
with this chain of narration, from the Prophet ﷺ, the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with ʿUthmān when he called for water for ablution, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"There is no Muslim man whose obligatory prayer comes due, and he performs its ablution well, and its humility and its bowing well, except that it will be an expiation for the sins before it, as long as he does not commit a major sin. And that applies for all time."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿUthmān,
performed ablution at al-Maqāʿid and said: "Shall I not show you the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" Then he performed ablution, washing each part three times.
Qutaybah added in his narration: Sufyān said: Abū an-Naḍr said, from Abū Anas, who said: And with him were men from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to set out ablution water for ʿUthmān, and no day passed but that he would pour some of it over himself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān performed ablution one day, a fine ablution, then said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution and do it well, then he said:
"Whoever performs ablution like this, then goes out to the mosque with nothing driving him but the prayer, his previous sins will be forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the same chain as theirs, and he related the hadith, saying in it: He rinsed his mouth, sniffed water into his nose, and blew it out, using three handfuls.
He also said: Then he wiped his head, moving [his hands] forward and back, once.
Bahz said: Wuhayb dictated this hadith to me.
And Wuhayb said: ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā dictated this hadith to me twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He mentioned that he saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution: he rinsed his mouth, then blew out his nose, then washed his face three times, his right hand three times and the other three times, and wiped his head with water other than what was left over on his hands, and washed his feet until he had cleaned them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he,
entered upon ʿĀʾishah, and he related from her, from the Prophet ﷺ, the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever performs ablution and does it well, his sins will come out of his body, even from under his fingernails."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"My Ummah will come to me at the Basin, and I will drive people away from it as a man drives another man's camels away from his own camels."
They said: "O Prophet of Allah, will you recognize us?" He said:

"Yes. You will have a mark that no one else has: you will come to me with bright faces and limbs from the traces of ablution. And a group of you will be turned away from me and will not reach [it]. I will say: 'My Lord, these are my Companions.' Then an angel will answer me, saying: 'Do you know what they innovated after you?'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The people closest to Allah are those who are first to greet with salām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you meets his brother, let him greet him with salām. If a tree, a wall, or a stone comes between them and then he meets him again, let him greet him with salām again.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in an upper room of his, and said, "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you all. May ʿUmar enter?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us while I was a boy among the boys, and he greeted us with salām. Then he took me by the hand and sent me on an errand, and he sat in the shade of a wall—or he said, by a wall—until I returned to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him. Abū Dāwūd said: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī traced it back to the Prophet. He said:
"It suffices for a group,
when they pass by, that one of them
give the greeting, and it suffices for those sitting that one of them return it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When two Muslims meet and shake hands, and praise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and seek His forgiveness, they are forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the people of Yemen came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The people of Yemen have come to you, and they are the first to have introduced the handshake."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a man of ʿAnazah, that he said to Abū Dharr when he was sent away from Syria: "I want to ask you about a hadith from the sayings of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said, "I will tell you, unless it is a secret."

I said, "It is not a secret. Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shake hands with you when you met him?" He said, "I never met him but that he shook my hand. One day he sent for me when I was not with my family. When I came, I was told that he had sent for me, so I went to him while he was on his couch, and he embraced me. And that was better, and better still."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the people of
Qurayẓah surrendered to the judgment of Saʿd, the Prophet ﷺ sent for him, and he came on a pale white donkey. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Stand for your chief," or, "for the best among you."
Then he came and sat near the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿĀʾishah,
may Allah be pleased with her, said: Then he—meaning the Prophet ﷺ—said:
"Rejoice, O ʿĀʾishah, for Allah has revealed your innocence."
And he recited the Qurʾān to her. My parents said, "Get up and kiss the head of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
She said, "I praise Allah, not the two of you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ met Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib, embraced him, and kissed him between his eyes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Abū Naḍrah kiss the cheek of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, peace be upon them both.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A story. He said: Then we drew near—meaning—to the Prophet ﷺ and kissed his hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Let me retaliate." He said, "Retaliate."
He said, "You are wearing a shirt, and I was not wearing a shirt."
So the Prophet ﷺ lifted his shirt, and he embraced him and began kissing his side. He said, "This is all I wanted, O Messenger of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"O Abū Dharr."
I said, "At your service, and happy to serve you, O Messenger of Allah, and may I be your ransom."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the days of ignorance we used to say, "May Allah make your eye pleased with you, and good morning." When Islam came, we were forbidden from that.
ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar said, "It is disliked for a man to say, 'May Allah make you a joy to the eye,' but there is no harm in saying, 'May Allah make your eye pleased.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was on a journey and they became thirsty. The hasty ones among the people went ahead, but I stayed close to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that night, and he said:
"May Allah protect you as you have protected His Prophet."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah came out to Ibn al-Zubayr and Ibn ʿĀmir. Ibn ʿĀmir stood up and Ibn al-Zubayr remained seated. Muʿāwiyah said to Ibn ʿĀmir, "Sit down, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever loves for men to stand before him, let him take his seat in the Fire.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us leaning on a staff, and we stood up for him. He said:
"Do not stand as the non-Arabs stand, honoring one another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting at the door of al-Ḥasan when a man came and said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather, who said: My father sent me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "Go to him and convey my greetings of peace."
He said: I went to him and said, "My father conveys greetings of peace to you." He said:
"Upon you and upon your father be peace."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked, "Which deeds are best?" He said:
"Belief in Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We fasted Ramadan with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he did not lead us in any night prayer during it until seven nights remained. Then he led us in prayer on the seventh night [from the end] until about a third of the night had passed. Then came the sixth night after it, and he did not pray it with us. Then on the fifth night after it he led us until about half the night had passed. So I said, "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would lead us in voluntary prayer for the rest of this night of ours!" He said:
"Whoever prays with the imam until he finishes, it is counted for him as the prayer of a whole night."
Then came the fourth night after it, and he did not pray it with us, until the third night after it [came].
He said: He gathered his wives and his family, and the people gathered.
He said: He led us in prayer until we feared that we would miss al-falāḥ.
It was asked, "What is al-falāḥ?" He said, "The pre-dawn meal (suḥūr)."
He said: Then he did not lead us in any more prayer for the rest of the month.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray Witr with {Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High}, {Say: O disbelievers}, and {Say: He is Allah, [who is] One}. Ḥuṣayn differed from them, and narrated it from Dharr, from Ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abzā, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me words to say in Witr. Ibn Jawwās said: in the Qunūt of Witr:

"O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, grant me well-being among those You have granted well-being, take me into Your care among those You have taken into Your care, bless me in what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed. Indeed You decree, and none decrees over You. Indeed, he whom You take as an ally is not humiliated, and he whom You take as an enemy is not honored. Blessed are You, our Lord, and Exalted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a man was standing in prayer. When he had bowed, prostrated, and recited the tashahhud, he made supplication and said in his supplication: "O Allah, I ask You by [the fact] that to You belongs all praise; there is no god but You, the Bestower of favors, Originator of the heavens and the earth, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor, O Ever-Living, O Sustainer, I ask You."
The Prophet ﷺ said to his Companions:
"Do you know what he supplicated with?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, he has called upon Allah by His Greatest Name, which, when He is called upon by it, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I have exempted you from charity (ṣadaqah) on horses and slaves, so bring the charity on silver: one dirham out of every forty dirhams. There is nothing due on one hundred and ninety. When it reaches two hundred, then five dirhams are due on it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever begs while he has what suffices him will come on the Day of Resurrection with scratches, or lacerations, or wounds on his face."
It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is sufficiency?" He said:
"Fifty dirhams, or its value in gold."

Yaḥyā said: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUthmān said to Sufyān, "I remember that Shuʿbah did not narrate from Ḥakīm ibn Jubayr." Sufyān said, "But Zubayd narrated it to us from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Charity (ṣadaqah) is not permissible for a rich person, nor for one who is strong and able-bodied."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Jibrīl came to me and commanded me to order my Companions and those with me to raise their voices in the ihlāl"—or he said, "in the talbiyah." One of the two narrators meant [this]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever breaks a bone or becomes lame has come out of ihrām, and he owes another Hajj."
I asked Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Hurayrah, and they both said, "He has spoken the truth."
Shuʿayb said in his narration: "and he owes the Hajj in the following year."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Narrating it back to the Prophet ﷺ, he said:
"Do not prevent anyone from circumambulating this House and praying at any hour he wishes, by night or day."
al-Faḍl said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Banū ʿAbd Manāf, do not prevent anyone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

said to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, I see you walking while the people hurry." He said, "If I walk, I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ walk; and if I hurry, I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ hurry; and I am an old man."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I set out with Ḥuṣayn

ibn Sabrah and ʿUmar ibn Muslim to Zayd ibn Arqam. When we sat with him, Ḥuṣayn said to him, "O Zayd, you have received much good: you saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, heard his speech, fought alongside him, and prayed behind him. You have received much good, O Zayd. Narrate to us, O Zayd, what you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said, "O son of my brother, by Allah, I have grown old, my time has become distant, and I have forgotten some of what I used to retain from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So accept what I narrate to you, and what I do not, do not burden me with it."

Then he said: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us to deliver a sermon at a watering place called Khumm, between Makkah and Madinah. He praised Allah and extolled Him, admonished and reminded, and then said:

"To proceed: Beware, O people! I am only a human being. The messenger of my Lord is about to come and I will answer. I am leaving among you two weighty things. The first of them is the Book of Allah, in which there is guidance and light. So take the Book of Allah and hold fast to it."
He urged adherence to the Book of Allah and encouraged it. Then he said:

"And the people of my household. I remind you of Allah regarding the people of my household. I remind you of Allah regarding the people of my household. I remind you of Allah regarding the people of my household."

Ḥuṣayn said to him, "Who are the people of his household, O Zayd? Are his wives not among the people of his household?" He said, "His wives are among the people of his household, but the people of his household are those for whom charity is forbidden after him."
He said, "And who are they?" He said, "They are the family of ʿAlī, the family of ʿAqīl, the family of Jaʿfar, and the family of ʿAbbās."
He said, "Is charity forbidden to all of these?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We entered upon him and said to him, "You have indeed seen much good.
You accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and prayed behind him."
And he narrated the hadith similar to the hadith of Abū Ḥayyān, except that he said:

"Beware! I am leaving among you two weighty things. One of them is the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; it is the rope of Allah. Whoever follows it will be on guidance, and whoever leaves it will be in misguidance."

And in it: We said, "Who are the people of his household? Are they his wives?" He said, "No, by Allah. A woman may be with a man for a period of time, then he divorces her and she returns to her father and her people. The people of his household are his own origin and his paternal relatives, for whom charity was forbidden after him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from the family of Marwān was appointed over Madinah. He said: He summoned Sahl ibn Saʿd and ordered him to curse ʿAlī. He said: Sahl refused. So he said to him, "If you refuse, then say: May Allah curse Abū Turāb."
Sahl said, "ʿAlī had no name more beloved to him than Abū Turāb, and he would be delighted when called by it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I and ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah were

on the day of the Trench with the women in the fortress of Ḥassān. He would lower himself for me once so that I could look, and I would lower myself for him once so that he could look. And I recognized my father as he passed on his horse, in armor, heading toward Banū Qurayẓah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of the Trench, I and ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah were in the fortress where the women were, meaning the women of the Prophet ﷺ. And he narrated the hadith with the same meaning as the hadith of Ibn Mushir in this chain of transmission. He did not mention ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUrwah in the hadith, but he included the account in the hadith of Hishām, from his father, from Ibn al-Zubayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of Yemen
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "Send a man with us to teach us the Sunnah and Islam."
He said: So he took Abū ʿUbaydah by the hand and said:
"This is the trustworthy one of this nation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had me ride behind him, and he confided a matter to me which I will not tell to anyone among the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was never jealous of any of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ except Khadījah, though I never met her.
She said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ slaughtered a sheep, he would say:
"Send some of it to the friends of Khadījah."
She said: One day I made him angry and said, "Khadījah!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have been granted love for her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was never jealous on behalf of the Prophet ﷺ over any of his wives as I was jealous over Khadījah, because of how often he mentioned her, and I never saw her at all.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ did not marry anyone else in addition to Khadījah until she died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The quickest of you to join me will be the one with the longest hand."
She said: They used to measure their hands against one another to see which of them had the longest hand.
She said: The one with the longest hand among us was Zaynab, because she used to work with her hand and give in charity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men of Quraysh and one of Thaqīf, or two of Thaqīf and one of Quraysh, gathered near the House. Their bellies were fat and their hearts had little understanding. One of them said, "Do you think that Allah hears what we say?" Another said, "He hears if we speak aloud, but He does not hear if we speak quietly."

And the other said, "If He hears when we speak aloud, then He hears when we speak quietly." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {You did not conceal yourselves lest your hearing, your sight, and your skins testify against you} [Fuṣṣilat 41:22], to the end of the verse.
Sufyān used to narrate this to us and say: "Manṣūr, or Ibn Abī Najīḥ, or Ḥumayd narrated to us," one of them or two of them,
then he settled on Manṣūr,
and he abandoned the others on several occasions.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Abī ʿUmar [narrated] to us: Sufyān narrated to us, from az-Zuhrī,
from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū
Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: The son of Ādam harms Me by cursing time, while I am Time; in My hand is the command, and I alternate the night and the day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Two gardens of silver,
their vessels and all that is in them; and two gardens of gold, their vessels and all that is in them.
And there is nothing between the people and their looking at their Lord except the cloak of majesty over His face, in the Garden of ʿAdn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when Sūrat al-Jumuʿah was revealed, and he recited it. When he reached:
{And others among them who have not yet joined them}, a man said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, who are those who have not yet joined us?" But he did not answer him.
He said: Salmān al-Fārisī was among us.
He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed his hand on Salmān and said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, if faith were at the Pleiades, men from among these would reach it."
This is a ḥasan ḥadīth, and it has been narrated through more than one route from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
And Abū al-Ghayth's name is Sālim, the freed slave of ʿAbdullāh ibn Muṭīʿ, from Madīnah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with my uncle, and I heard ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse."
He also said, "If we return to Madīnah, the more honorable will surely drive out the more humble from it."
I mentioned that to my uncle, and my uncle mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy and his companions,
and they swore that they had not said it.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ believed them and did not believe me,
so I was struck by a grief the like of which had never struck me,
and I sat in my house.

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {When the hypocrites come to you} up to His words {They are the ones who say, 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah'} up to His words {the more honorable will surely drive out the more humble from it}. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for me, recited it to me, and then said:
"Allah has verified what you said."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about a woman who gave birth twenty nights after her husband's death: is it permissible for her to marry? He said, "No, not until the later of the two periods."
[Abū Salamah] said: I said, "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: {And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth}." He said, "That applies only in the case of divorce."
Then Abū Hurayrah said, "I am with my nephew,"
meaning Abū Salamah.

So he sent his servant Kurayb and said, "Go to Umm Salamah and ask her whether this was a sunnah from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He came back and said: She said, "Yes. Subayʿah al-Aslamiyyah gave birth twenty nights after her husband's death, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded her to marry. Abū as-Sanābil was among those who proposed to her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say about what is made unlawful [for oneself] that it is an oath, for which one must offer expiation.
And Ibn ʿAbbās said: {There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gesture with his two fingers like this, the middle finger and the one next to the thumb, and say:
"I was sent, and the Hour, like these two."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon in which he mentioned the she-camel and the one who hamstrung her, and said:
"{When the most wretched of them rose up}: a man rose up for it, mighty, fierce, and protected among his clan, like Abū Zamʿah."
Then he mentioned women and exhorted [the men] about them, and then said:
"Why does one of you flog his wife?"
In the narration of Abū Bakr: "like the flogging of a slave woman."
And in the narration of Abū Kurayb:
"like the flogging of a slave, and perhaps he will lie with her at the end of the day."
Then he admonished them about laughing at passing wind, and said:
"Why does one of you laugh at what he does himself?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw in a dream that I was emigrating from Makkah to a land with date palms. My mind went to it being al-Yamāmah or Hajar, but it was Madinah, Yathrib. And in this dream of mine I saw that I brandished a sword and its blade broke off; that was what befell the believers on the day of Uḥud. Then I brandished it again and it returned better than it had been; that was the conquest Allah brought and the gathering of the believers. I also saw cows in it, and Allah is the best; they were the group of believers on the day of Uḥud. And the good was what Allah brought afterward of good, and the reward of truthfulness that Allah gave us after the day of Badr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ were with him, not one of them absent, when Fāṭimah came walking, her gait not differing at all from the gait of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When he saw her, he welcomed her and said, "Welcome, my daughter."
Then he seated her on his right or on his left, and whispered to her, and she wept bitterly. When he saw her distress, he whispered to her a second time, and she laughed.

I said to her, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ singled you out from among his wives with a secret, and then you weep?" When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose, I asked her, "What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say to you?" She said, "I would not disclose the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

She said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, I said, "I charge you, by the right I have over you, to tell me what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to you." She said, "Now, yes. When he whispered to me the first time, he told me:

'Jibrīl used to review the Qur'an with him once every year, or twice, and this year he reviewed it with him twice; and I do not see but that my appointed time has drawn near. So fear Allah and be patient, for I am an excellent predecessor for you.'"
She said: "So I wept as you saw. When he saw my distress, he whispered to me a second time and said:
'O Fāṭimah, are you not pleased to be the leader of the women of the believers, or the leader of the women of this nation?'"
She said: "So I laughed as you saw."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"While I was at a well drawing water from it, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar came to me.
Abū Bakr took the bucket
and drew one bucket or two, and there was weakness in his drawing,
and Allah forgives him.
Then Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb took it from Abū Bakr's hand,
and in his hand it turned into a large bucket.
I never saw a mighty man among the people do work like his.
He drew until the people watered their camels and settled them at the watering place."
Wahb said: al-ʿaṭan is the place where camels are made to kneel;
he means: until the camels were satisfied and knelt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am ruined!" He said, "What has ruined you?"
He said, "I turned my mount around last night."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not reply to him at all. Then Allah revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ this verse:
"Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish" — front or back, but avoid the rear passage and menstruation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He married his sister to a man from among the Muslims during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she stayed with him for as long as she did. Then he divorced her with one divorce and did not take her back until her waiting period had ended. He came to love her and she loved him. Then he proposed to her along with other suitors. [Maʿqil] said to him, "You fool! I honored you with her and married her to you, and you divorced her! By Allah, she will never return to you, ever!" He said: Allah knew his need for her and her need for her husband, so Allah revealed: "And when you divorce women and they have reached the end of their term..." up to His saying: "...while you do not know." When Maʿqil heard it, he said, "I hear and obey my Lord." Then he called him and said, "I will marry her to you and honor you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The devil has a touch upon the son of Adam, and the angel has a touch. As for the devil's touch, it is a promise of evil and a denial of the truth. As for the angel's touch, it is a promise of good and a confirmation of the truth. Whoever finds the latter, let him know that it is from Allah and let him praise Allah. And whoever finds the other, let him seek refuge with Allah from the accursed devil." Then he recited:
"The devil threatens you with poverty and commands you to immorality."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this verse was revealed:

"Whether you reveal what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills," it grieved us. He said: We said, "One of us speaks to himself and is held to account for it, and we do not know what will be forgiven of it and what will not." Then this verse was revealed after it and abrogated it: "Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have what it has earned, and it will bear what it has earned."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She asked ʿĀʾishah about the saying of Allah, the Exalted:
"Whether you reveal what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it," and about His saying:
"Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it." She said, "No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:

'This is Allah's admonishing of the servant for what afflicts him of fever and misfortune, even the small sum he places in his shirt sleeve and then misses, and is alarmed about it, until the servant emerges from his sins just as red gold emerges from the furnace.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he is al-Kharrāz, and Yazīd ibn Ibrāhīm, both from Ibn Abī Mulaykah,
Yazīd said, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah,
from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀʾishah,
though Abū ʿĀmir did not mention al-Qāsim. She said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about His saying:
"As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow what is unclear of it, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation," he said:
"When you see them, recognize them."
And Yazīd said: "When you see them (plural), recognize them."
He said it two or three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every prophet has allies among the prophets, and my ally is my father and the intimate friend of my Lord." Then he recited:
"Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe. And Allah is the ally of the believers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of Uḥud:
"O Allah, curse Abū Sufyān. O Allah, curse al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām. O Allah, curse Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah." He said: Then was revealed:
"You have no part in the matter, whether He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them." So Allah turned to them in forgiveness and they accepted Islam, and their Islam was good.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to invoke against four men, so Allah revealed:
"You have no part in the matter, whether He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers." Then Allah guided them to Islam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I raised my head on the day of Uḥud and began to look, and there was none of them that day except that he was swaying under his shield from drowsiness. That is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic:
"Then He sent down upon you, after distress, security: drowsiness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Among the greatest of the major sins are associating partners with Allah, disobeying one's parents, and the false oath. No one swears a binding oath by Allah and inserts into it even the like of a gnat's wing, except that it becomes a stain on his heart until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever climbs the mountain pass, the pass of al-Murār, will have taken from him what was taken from the Children of Israel."
He said: The first to climb it were our horsemen, the horsemen of Banū al-Khazraj. Then the people followed one after another. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"All of you are forgiven, except the owner of the red camel."

So we went to him and said to him, "Come, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will ask forgiveness for you." He said, "By Allah, finding my lost animal is dearer to me than your companion asking forgiveness for me."
He said: And he was a man who was searching for a lost animal of his.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from a journey, and when he was near Madinah a violent wind arose that almost buried the rider. He claimed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"This wind has been sent for the death of a hypocrite."
When he arrived in Madinah, a prominent hypocrite among the hypocrites had died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We visited a man who had a fever along with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: I placed my hand on him and said, "By Allah, I have never seen a man as hot as he is today."
Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"Shall I not inform you of those who will be hotter than he on the Day of Resurrection? Those two riders who turned their backs and went away."
[He said this] about two men of his Companions at that time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took me by the hand and said:

"Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the earth on Saturday, and created the mountains on it on Sunday, and created the trees on Monday, and created the disliked things on Tuesday, and created light on Wednesday, and spread the beasts upon it on Thursday, and created Adam, peace be upon him, after the afternoon on Friday, at the end of creation, in the last hour of the hours of Friday, between the afternoon and the night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Jahl said, "Does Muhammad rub his face in the dust in front of you?" It was said, "Yes."

He said, "By al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, if I see him do that, I will surely trample on his neck, or I will surely rub his face in the dust." He said: So he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was praying, intending, he claimed, to trample on his neck. He said: Then they were suddenly startled to see him retreating on his heels and shielding himself with his hands. He said: It was said to him, "What is the matter with you?" He said, "Between me and him there is a trench of fire, and terror, and wings."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If he had come near me, the angels would have snatched him away limb by limb."

He said: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed—we do not know whether it is in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah or something that reached him—{No! Indeed, man transgresses * when he sees himself self-sufficient. * Indeed, to your Lord is the return. * Have you seen the one who forbids * a servant when he prays? * Have you seen if he is upon guidance * or enjoins righteousness? * Have you seen if he denies and turns away?}—meaning Abū Jahl—{Does he not know that Allah sees? * No! If he does not desist, We will surely seize him by the forelock, * a lying, sinful forelock. * Let him then call his associates. * We will call the guards of Hell. * No! Do not obey him.} ʿUbaydullāh added in his narration: He said, "And he commanded him with what he commanded him."
And Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā added: "Let him then call his associates," meaning his people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The calamities of this world are: the Romans, the severe seizure, or the smoke.
Shuʿbah was unsure whether it was the severe seizure or the smoke.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, similar to that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"On the Day of Resurrection, the person who lived the most comfortable life in the world, from among the people of the Fire, will be brought and dipped once in the Fire. Then it will be said, 'O son of Adam, have you ever seen any good? Has any comfort ever passed over you?' He will say, 'No, by Allah, O Lord.'

And the person who suffered the most hardship in the world, from among the people of Paradise, will be brought and dipped once in Paradise. Then it will be said to him, 'O son of Adam, have you ever seen any hardship? Has any distress ever passed over you?' He will say, 'No, by Allah, O Lord, no hardship has ever passed over me, and I have never seen any distress.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed, Allah does not wrong a believer in any good deed: he is given for it in this world and rewarded for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is given food in this world for the good deeds he did for Allah, until, when he reaches the Hereafter, he has no good deed left for which he could be rewarded."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the lack of rain. So he ordered a pulpit, and it was set up for him at the prayer ground, and he promised the people a day on which they would go out. ʿĀʾishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out when the edge of the sun appeared, and he sat on the pulpit. He ﷺ said the takbīr and praised Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then said:

"You have complained of the drought in your lands and of the rain being delayed beyond its usual season. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you to call upon Him, and He has promised to answer you." Then he said:

"{Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgment.} There is no god but Allah; He does what He wills. O Allah, You are Allah; there is no god but You, You are the Self-Sufficient and we are the needy. Send down rain upon us, and make what You send down a strength for us and a provision for a time."

Then he raised his hands, and he continued raising them until the whiteness of his armpits appeared. Then he turned his back to the people and turned over his cloak, while still holding his hands raised. Then he faced the people and came down and prayed two rak'ahs. Then Allah brought forth a cloud; it thundered and lightened, then it rained by Allah's permission. He had not even reached his mosque before the torrents were flowing. When he saw how quickly the people hurried to shelter, he ﷺ laughed until his molars showed, and said:
"I bear witness that Allah has power over all things, and that I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say— (and a second chain:) Sahl ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us: ʿAlī ibn Qādim narrated to us: Sufyān informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for rain, he would say:
"O Allah, give water to Your servants and Your animals, spread Your mercy, and bring to life Your dead land."
This is the wording of the hadith of Mālik.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ led them in prayer. He recited a long sūrah, bowed five times, and prostrated twice. Then he stood for the second rak'ah, recited a long sūrah, bowed five times, and prostrated twice. Then he sat, as he was, facing the qiblah, making supplication until the eclipse cleared.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and led the people in prayer. He stood, and I estimated his recitation and thought that he recited Sūrat al-Baqarah— and he related the rest of the hadith— then he prostrated twice, then stood and prolonged the recitation. I estimated his recitation and thought that he recited Sūrat Āl ʿImrān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed, and the people with him. He stood for a long time, about the length of Sūrat al-Baqarah, then bowed— and he related the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he began to pray two rak'ahs after two rak'ahs and to ask about it until it cleared.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and could hardly bow; then he bowed and could hardly rise; then he rose and could hardly prostrate; then he prostrated and could hardly rise; then he rose and could hardly prostrate; then he prostrated and could hardly rise; then he rose. He did the same in the other rak'ah. Then he blew at the end of his prostration and said, "Uff, uff." Then he said:
"My Lord, did You not promise me that You would not punish them while I am among them? Did You not promise me that You would not punish them while they seek forgiveness?"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer, and the sun had cleared— and he related the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a darkness in the time of Anas ibn Mālik. He said: I came to Anas and said, "O Abū Ḥamzah, did something like this happen to you in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "Allah forbid! When the wind became strong, we would hurry to the mosque, fearing the Hour."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Anas ibn Mālik: Narrate to us something you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said: When we were travelling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and we said, "The sun has passed its zenith," or "it has not," he would pray the Ẓuhr and then set out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ withdrew from his wives, [ʿUmar] said: I entered the mosque and found the people striking the ground with pebbles and saying, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has divorced his wives." This was before they were commanded to observe the veil. ʿUmar said: I said, "I will surely find out about this today." He said: So I went in to ʿĀʾishah and said, "O daughter of Abū Bakr, has it reached the point that you hurt the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" She said, "What do I have to do with you, O son of al-Khaṭṭāb? Look after your own daughter."

He said: Then I went in to Ḥafṣah bint ʿUmar and said to her, "O Ḥafṣah, has it reached the point that you hurt the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? By Allah, you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ does not love you.
And were it not for me, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have divorced you."
She wept bitterly. I said to her, "Where is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" She said, "He is in his storeroom in the upper chamber."

So I went in, and there was Rabāḥ, the servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, sitting on the threshold of the upper chamber with his legs dangling over a notched log of wood, which was a palm trunk the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to climb up and down. I called out, "O Rabāḥ, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
Rabāḥ looked at the room, then looked at me, and said nothing. Then I said, "O Rabāḥ, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

Rabāḥ looked at the room, then looked at me, and said nothing. Then I raised my voice and said, "O Rabāḥ, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I think the Messenger of Allah ﷺ believes I have come on account of Ḥafṣah. By Allah, if the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to strike her neck, I would strike her neck."

I raised my voice, and he gestured to me to climb up. I went in to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was lying on a mat. I sat down, and he pulled his lower garment over himself; he had nothing else on, and the mat had left marks on his side. I looked around in the storeroom of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and there was a handful of barley, about a ṣāʿ, and a similar amount of qaraẓ in a corner of the room, and a tanned hide hanging up. He said: My eyes filled with tears. He said:
"What makes you weep, O son of al-Khaṭṭāb?"

I said, "O Prophet of Allah, why should I not weep? This mat has left marks on your side, and this is your storeroom, in which I see nothing but what I see. Yet Caesar and Chosroes live among fruits and rivers, while you are the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and His chosen one, and this is your storeroom!" He said:
"O son of al-Khaṭṭāb, are you not content that the Hereafter be ours and this world theirs?"

I said, "Yes." He said: When I entered upon him, I saw anger in his face, so I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what troubles you about the women? If you have divorced them, then Allah is with you, and His angels, Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl, and I and Abū Bakr and the believers are with you." Seldom did I speak, praising Allah, without hoping that Allah would confirm the words I was saying. And the verse of the option was revealed: {Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you} {But if you support one another against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Jibrīl and the righteous among the believers, and the angels thereafter are his supporters.} ʿĀʾishah bint Abī Bakr and Ḥafṣah were the two who supported one another against the rest of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, have you divorced them?" He said, "No."

I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I entered the mosque while the Muslims were striking the ground with pebbles, saying, 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has divorced his wives.' Shall I go down and tell them that you have not divorced them?" He said:
"Yes, if you wish."

I kept talking to him until the anger lifted from his face and he smiled broadly and laughed, and he had the most beautiful teeth of all people. Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came down, and I came down, clutching at the trunk, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ descended as if walking on the ground, not touching it with his hand. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, you were in the room for only twenty-nine days." He said:
"The month can be twenty-nine days."
Then I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has not divorced his wives!"

And this verse was revealed: {And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it around. But if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, then those who can draw out its conclusion would have known it.} So I was the one who drew out that matter, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed the verse of the option.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Fāṭimah bint Qays, and she told me that her husband from the Makhzūm clan had divorced her and refused to provide maintenance for her. So she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You have no maintenance. So move and go to Ibn Umm Maktūm and stay with him, for he is a blind man; you may take off your garments at his place."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I wrote that down from her own mouth as a document. She said: "I was with a man of Banū Makhzūm, and he divorced me irrevocably. So I sent word to his family seeking maintenance."
And they narrated the hadith in the sense of the hadith of Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr from Abū Salamah,
except that in the hadith of Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr [it says]:
"Do not let yourself slip away from us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We visited Fāṭimah bint Qays, and she treated us to fresh dates, of the kind called Ibn Ṭāb dates, and gave us barley porridge to drink. Then I asked her about the woman divorced

three times: where should she spend her waiting period? She said: "My husband divorced me three times, and the Prophet ﷺ permitted me to spend my waiting period in my family's house." She said: "Then the call was made among the people: 'The prayer is being gathered!'" She said: "So I went out among those who went out. I was in the front row of the women, which is next to the last row of the men." She said: "Then I heard the Prophet ﷺ speaking from the pulpit, and he said:
'The cousins of Tamīm ad-Dārī sailed on the sea...'"
And he narrated the rest of the hadith and added in it: She said: "It is as though I can see the Prophet ﷺ pointing his staff toward the ground and saying: 'This is Ṭaybah,'" meaning Madinah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with al-Aswad ibn Yazīd in the great mosque, and ash-Shaʿbī was with us. Ash-Shaʿbī narrated the hadith of Fāṭimah bint Qays, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not grant her lodging or maintenance. Then al-Aswad took a handful of pebbles and threw them at him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān and I visited Fāṭimah bint Qays and asked her. She said: "I was married to Abū ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ ibn al-Mughīrah, and he went out on the expedition to Najrān."
And he narrated the hadith similar to the hadith of Ibn Mahdī and added: She said: "Then I married him, and Allah honored me through Ibn Zayd and dignified me through Ibn Zayd."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Salamah and I visited Fāṭimah bint Qays in the time of Ibn az-Zubayr, and she told us that her husband had divorced her with a final, irrevocable divorce.
Similar to the hadith of Sufyān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no good for Fāṭimah in mentioning this.
He said: She meant her statement, "There is no lodging or maintenance."
label: machine translation

label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A woman must not mourn for a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband, [for whom she mourns] four months and ten days. She must not wear dyed clothing, except ʿaṣb cloth, and she must not apply kohl or touch perfume, except when she is purified, a little qusṭ or aẓfār."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jubayr said: I was asked about a couple who had exchanged oaths of imprecation (liʿān),

in the governorship of Muṣʿab: are they to be separated? He said: "I did not know what to say, so I went to the house of Ibn ʿUmar in Makkah and said to the servant: 'Ask permission for me [to enter].'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of Muṣʿab ibn az-Zubayr, I did not know what to say, so I went to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar and said: "What do you think about a couple who have exchanged oaths of imprecation: are they to be separated?" Then he mentioned [the rest] like the hadith of Ibn Numayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿUmar about liʿān,
and he mentioned from the Prophet ﷺ something similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It has reached us that Abū Hurayrah
used to narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ something similar to their hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning a slave owned jointly by two men, one of whom frees him, he said: "He must pay compensation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is not lawful for a Muslim to take as his patron the freed slave of another Muslim without his permission."
Then I was informed that in his document [he wrote] that whoever does that is cursed.
label: machine translation

label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade meeting the goods [of incoming traders] before they reach the markets.
This is the wording of Ibn Numayr.
And the other two said that the Prophet ﷺ forbade meeting [the caravans].
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb on the Day of Sacrifice. He began with the prayer before the sermon, then said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid fasting on these two days: as for the Day of Fitr, it is the day you break your fast and a festival for the Muslims; and as for the Day of Aḍḥā, eat from the meat of your sacrifices."
He said: This is a ṣaḥīḥ hadith.

Abū ʿUbayd, the freed slave of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, is named Saʿd, and he is also called the freed slave of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar is the cousin of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he forbade two kinds of sales. As for the two sales, they are munābadhah and mulāmasah. He claimed that mulāmasah is when a man says to another, "I sell you my garment for your garment," and neither of them looks at the other's garment, but he merely touches it. And munābadhah is when he says, "I throw what I have and you throw what you have," so that each buys from the other, without either knowing how much the other has, or words to that effect.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Abū Usāmah: "Did ʿUbaydullāh narrate to you from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade meeting the caravans [to buy their goods] before they enter the market?" Abū Usāmah acknowledged it and said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A sheep was given in charity to a freed slave woman of Maymūnah, and it died. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by it and said:
"Why did you not take its hide, tan it, and benefit from it?"
They said, "It is carrion." He said:
"Only eating it has been forbidden."
Abū Bakr and Ibn Abī ʿUmar said in their narration: from Maymūnah, may Allah be pleased with her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from among the people of their locality, among them Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathmah, [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of fresh fruit for dried dates, and said:
"That is ribā; that is muzābanah."
Except that he permitted the sale of ʿarāyā, a palm tree or two, which a household takes at its estimated value in dried dates, to eat as fresh dates.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I am closer to every believer than his own self. So whoever leaves behind a debt or dependants, [they come] to me; and whoever leaves behind wealth, it is for his heirs. And I am the protector of one who has no protector: I inherit his wealth and free his captive. And the maternal uncle is the protector of one who has no protector: he inherits his wealth and frees his captive."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I passed by Hishām ibn Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām while he was reciting Sūrat al-Furqān during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I listened to his recitation, and he was reciting in many ways that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not taught me. I almost seized him during the prayer, but I waited until he had finished with the salām. When he finished, I grabbed him by his cloak and said, "Who taught you this sūrah that I heard you reciting?" He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught it to me."
I said to him, "You have lied! By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself taught me this sūrah that you are reciting."

So I went off leading him to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I heard this man reciting Sūrat al-Furqān in ways that you did not teach me, and you taught me Sūrat al-Furqān." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Let him go, ʿUmar. Recite, Hishām."
So he recited to him the recitation that I had heard from him. The Prophet ﷺ said, "It was revealed thus."
Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Recite, ʿUmar."
So I recited the recitation that the Prophet ﷺ had taught me. The Prophet ﷺ said, "It was revealed thus."
Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Indeed, this Qur'ān was revealed in seven modes, so recite whatever is easy for you of it."
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
Mālik ibn Anas also narrated it from al-Zuhrī with this chain, similarly, except that he did not mention al-Miswar ibn Makhramah in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ; and al-Ḥajjāj, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"A morning or an evening journey in the cause of Allah is better than the world and all that is in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The polytheists detained the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the ʿAṣr prayer until the sun turned red or yellow. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"They have kept us from the middle prayer, the ʿAṣr prayer. May Allah fill their bellies and their graves with fire." Or he said:
"May Allah stuff their bellies and their graves with fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created Adam in his image, sixty cubits tall. When He had created him, He said, 'Go and greet that group'—a group of angels sitting—'and listen to how they reply to you, for that will be your greeting and the greeting of your offspring.' So he went and said, 'Peace be upon you.' They replied, 'Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah.' So they added 'and the mercy of Allah.' Everyone who enters Paradise will be in the image of Adam, sixty cubits tall. Creation has continued to diminish after him until now."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, then when he witnesses a matter let him speak good or remain silent. And treat women well, for woman was created from a rib, and the most crooked part of the rib is its uppermost. If you try to straighten it, you will break it, and if you leave it, it will remain crooked. So treat women well."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah, the Exalted, will say to the one who has the lightest punishment among the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, 'If you had everything on earth, would you offer it as ransom for yourself?' He will say, 'Yes.'
Then He will say, 'I asked of you something easier than this when you were in the loins of Adam: that you not associate anything with Me. But you refused and insisted on associating others with Me.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Shall I not tell you a account about the Dajjāl that no prophet told his people? He is one-eyed,
and he will come with something like Paradise and the Fire,
