and what he says is Paradise is in fact the Fire,
and I warn you of him just as Noah warned his people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Today an opening has been made in the barrier of Gog and Magog like this."
And Wuhayb made a circle with his hand, indicating ninety.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say on the Day of Resurrection, 'O Adam.'
He will say, 'Here I am, our Lord, at Your service,'
and he will be called with a voice: 'Allah commands you to bring forth from your offspring a delegation for the Fire.'

He will say, 'My Lord, what is the delegation for the Fire?' He will say, 'From every thousand'—I think he said—'nine hundred and ninety-nine.' At that time a pregnant woman will deliver her burden and a child will turn grey-haired, {and you will see the people intoxicated, though they are not intoxicated, but the punishment of Allah is severe}."
That was distressing to the people until their faces changed, so the Prophet ﷺ said:
"From Gog and Magog will be nine hundred and ninety-nine, and from you one.
Then you among the people are like a black hair on the side of a white ox,
or like a white hair on the side of a black ox,
and I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise."
We said, "Allahu akbar!" Then he said:
"A third of the people of Paradise."
We said, "Allahu akbar!" Then he said:
"Half of the people of Paradise." And we said, "Allahu akbar!"
Abū Usāmah reported from al-Aʿmash: {you will see the people intoxicated, though they are not intoxicated}, and he said: from every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.
And Jarīr, ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus, and Abū Muʿāwiyah recited: {intoxicated, though they are not intoxicated}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was asked, "Who is the most honorable of people?" He said, "The most honorable of them is the most God-fearing of them."
They said, "O Prophet of Allah,
it is not about this that we ask you." He said:
"Then the most honorable of people is Joseph, the prophet of Allah, son of a prophet of Allah, son of a prophet of Allah, son of the Khalīl of Allah."
They said, "It is not about this that we ask you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Abraham was circumcised when he was eighty years old, and he was circumcised with an adze." [The word] is pronounced with a light d.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the Messiah, the Dajjāl, in the midst of the people and said:
"Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is not one-eyed. But the Messiah, the Dajjāl, is blind in the right eye, as though his eye were a floating grape."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also said:

"Last night I saw myself in a dream near the Kaʿbah, and there was a man of brown complexion, the finest you could see of brown-complexioned men, with hair reaching between his shoulders, combed straight, and his head dripping water.
He had placed his hands on the shoulders of two men and was circumambulating the House between them. I asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'The Messiah, son of Mary.'

Then I saw behind him a man with very curly hair, blind in the right eye, most resembling Ibn Qaṭan among the people I have seen, with his hands on the shoulders of two men, circumambulating the House. I asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'This is the Messiah, the Dajjāl.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey. One day I was close to him as we were traveling, and I said, "O Messenger of Allah, tell me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise and keep me away from the Fire." He said, "

You have asked about something momentous, yet it is easy for the one for whom Allah makes it easy: worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, establish the prayer, give the zakāh, fast Ramadan, and perform Hajj to the House." Then he said, "
Shall I not guide you to the gates of goodness? Fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire, and [so does] a man's prayer in the depths of the night."
He said: Then he recited:
"Their sides forsake their beds..." until he reached:
"...they used to do." Then he said, "
Shall I not tell you of the head of the matter, its pillar, and its highest peak?"
I said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "
The head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is prayer, and its highest peak is jihād." Then he said, "
Shall I not tell you of the foundation of all that?"
I said, "Yes, O Prophet of Allah." He took hold of his tongue and said, "
Restrain this."
I said, "O Prophet of Allah, will we be held accountable for what we say?" He said, "
May your mother lose you, Muʿādh! Does anything cast people into the Fire on their faces"—or he said, "on their noses—other than the harvests of their tongues?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died and Abū Bakr was made his successor after him,
and some of the Arabs disbelieved, ʿUmar said to Abū Bakr, "How can you fight the people,
when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
'I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no god but Allah.
So whoever says: There is no god but Allah,
his wealth and his life are protected from me, except by its right,
and his reckoning is with Allah.'"
He said, "By Allah, I will fight whoever separates prayer from zakāh,
for zakāh is the due right on wealth.
By Allah, if they withheld from me even a hobbling cord that they used to give to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would fight them for withholding it."
ʿUmar said, "By Allah, it was only that I saw that Allah had opened Abū Bakr's heart to fighting, and I knew that it was the truth."
Ibn Bukayr and ʿAbdullāh said, from al-Layth, "a young goat" instead, and that is more correct.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "

No one gives charity from what is good—and Allah accepts only what is good—except that the Most Merciful takes it in His right hand, even if it is a single date, and it grows in the palm of the Most Merciful until it becomes greater than a mountain, and He nurtures it for him as one of you nurtures his foal or his young camel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Prophet of Allah, I have nothing except what az-Zubayr brings in to me. Is there any blame on me if I give from what comes to me?" He said, "
Give as much as you can, and do not hoard, for then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would withhold from you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I know it only from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When [the verse] "You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love" was revealed, Abū Ṭalḥah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says in His Book: 'You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love,' and the dearest of my properties to me is Bayruḥāʾ." He said: It was a garden which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to enter, shade himself in, and drink from its water. "So it is for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger ﷺ; I hope for its reward and its store with Allah,
so place it, O Messenger of Allah, wherever Allah shows you."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Well done, Abū Ṭalḥah!
That is profitable wealth.
We accept it from you and return it to you,
so make it for your relatives."
So Abū Ṭalḥah gave it as charity to his kinsfolk.
He said: Among them were Ubayy and Ḥassān.
He said: Ḥassān sold his share of it to Muʿāwiyah,

and it was said to him, "Are you selling the charity of Abū Ṭalḥah?" He said, "Should I not sell a ṣāʿ of dates for a ṣāʿ of dirhams?" He said: That garden was at the site of the palace of Banū Ḥudaylah, which Muʿāwiyah built.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people of the Anṣār asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he gave each of them who asked until what he had was exhausted. Then, when everything he had spent with his own hands was gone, he said to them, "
Whatever good I have, I will not withhold it from you.
Whoever seeks to be chaste, Allah will make him chaste;
whoever strives to be patient, Allah will make him patient;
and whoever seeks to be self-sufficient, Allah will make him self-sufficient.
And you will never be given a gift better and more expansive than patience."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The last of those to enter Paradise will be a man who walks at times, stumbles at times, and is scorched by the Fire at times. When he has passed beyond it, he will turn to look back at it and say: 'Blessed is He who has saved me from you! Allah has given me something He has not given to anyone among the earlier or the later generations.'
Then a tree will be raised up for him, and he will say: 'My Lord, bring me closer to this tree so that I may take shade in its shade and drink from its water.'
Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'O son of Adam, perhaps if I give you that, you will ask Me for something else.'
He will say: 'No, my Lord.'

And he will make a pledge to Him that he will not ask Him for anything else, and his Lord will excuse him, because He sees what he cannot bear to be without. So He will bring him near it, and he will take shade in its shade and drink from its water. Then another tree, more beautiful than the first, will be raised up for him, and he will say: 'My Lord, bring me closer to this one so that I may drink from its water and take shade in its shade. I will not ask You for anything else.'
He will say: 'O son of Adam, did you not pledge to Me that you would not ask Me for anything else?' Then He will say: 'Perhaps if I bring you near it, you will ask Me for something else.'

So he will make a pledge to Him that he will not ask for anything else, and his Lord will excuse him, because He sees what he cannot bear to be without. So He will bring him near it, and he will take shade in its shade and drink from its water.
Then a tree will be raised up for him at the gate of Paradise, more beautiful than the first two.
He will say: 'My Lord, bring me closer to this one so that I may take shade in its shade and drink from its water. I will not ask You for anything else.'
He will say: 'O son of Adam, did you not pledge to Me that you would not ask Me for anything else?' He will say: 'Yes, my Lord, this one; I will not ask You for anything else.'

And his Lord will excuse him, because He sees what he cannot bear to be without. So He will bring him near it, and when He has brought him near it, he will hear the voices of the people of Paradise and say: 'My Lord, make me enter it.'

He will say: 'O son of Adam, what will put an end to your asking Me? Would it please you if I gave you the world and its like along with it?' He will say: 'My Lord, are You mocking me, when You are the Lord of the worlds?'"
Ibn Masʿūd laughed and said: "Will you not ask me why I am laughing?" They said: "Why are you laughing?" He said: "This is how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed."
They said: "Why are you laughing, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"At the laughter of the Lord of the worlds when he says: 'Are You mocking me, when You are the Lord of the worlds?' He will say: 'I am not mocking you, but I am able to do whatever I will.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is a man whose face Allah turned away from the Fire before Paradise, and a shady tree was shown to him. He said: 'My Lord, bring me forward to this tree so that I may be in its shade.'"
And he narrated the hadith like the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd, but did not mention:
"He will say: 'O son of Adam, what will put an end to your asking Me?'"
up to the end of the hadith, and he added in it:

"And Allah will remind him: 'Ask for such and such,' until, when his wishes run out, Allah will say: 'It is yours, and ten times its like.'" He said: "Then he will enter his house, and his two wives from among the ḥūr al-ʿīn will come in to him and say: 'Praise be to Allah, who has given you life for us and given us life for you.'" He said: "He will say: 'No one has been given the like of what I have been given.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the Day of Resurrection we will come on such and such,

[and he said:] Look which of that is above the people. He said: "Then the nations will be called with their idols and whatever they used to worship, one after another. Then after that our Lord will come to us and say: 'Whom are you waiting for?' They will say: 'We are waiting for our Lord.'
He will say: 'I am your Lord.'
They will say: 'Not until we look upon You.'

So He will reveal Himself to them, laughing." He said: "Then He will go with them, and they will follow Him, and each one of them, hypocrite or believer, will be given a light. Then they will follow Him. On the bridge over Hell there will be hooks and thorns that will seize whomever Allah wills. Then the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished, and the believers will be saved. The first group to be saved, their faces like the moon on the night of the full moon, will be seventy thousand who will not be brought to account. Then those who follow them, like the brightest star in the sky, and so on. Then intercession will be permitted and they will intercede, until whoever said 'There is no god but Allah' and had in his heart good equal to the weight of a barley grain is brought out of the Fire. They will be placed in the courtyard of Paradise, and the people of Paradise will sprinkle water over them until they sprout like plants sprout in the silt of a flood, and the burning will leave them. Then he will ask until the world and ten times its like are given to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ with my own ears say:
"Allah will bring some people out of the Fire and make them enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Some people will come out of the Fire after being burned in it, except for the circles of their faces, until they enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was a freed slave of the family of Ṭalḥah, [and he narrated] from Sulaymān ibn Yasār,
from al-Rubayyiʿ bint Muʿawwidh ibn ʿAfrāʾ,
that she obtained a khulʿ divorce in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ commanded her, or she was commanded, to observe a waiting period of one menstrual cycle.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the story of Barīrah, she said: Her husband was a slave, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave her the choice, and she chose herself. Had he been free, he would not have given her the choice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
came to the Prophet ﷺ and accepted Islam, and a man married her.
He said: Then her first husband came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I had accepted Islam along with her, and she knew of my conversion."
He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took her away from the other husband and returned her to her first husband.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I accepted Islam while I had eight wives. So I went to the Prophet ﷺ and told him that, and he said:
"Choose four of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ commanded the couple to swear the oaths of mutual imprecation (liʿān), he ordered a man to place his hand over the mouth of the swearer at the fifth oath, saying that it is the one that makes [the curse] binding.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Every child whose paternity is claimed after the death of his father, to whom he was attributed, [and] whom his heirs claim after him, he ruled: if the child is from a slave woman whom the father owned on the day he had relations with her, then the child is attached to the one who claimed him, but he has no share in any inheritance that was divided before that; whatever inheritance he finds not yet divided, he receives his share. He is not attached if the father to whom he was attributed had denied him. And if he is from a slave woman whom the father did not own, or from a free woman with whom he committed fornication, then he is not attached and does not inherit. And even if the one to whom he is attributed claimed him himself, he is a child of fornication, belonging to his mother's people, whether she was a free woman or a slave woman."
Muḥammad ibn Rāshid said: By this he means what was divided in the Jāhiliyyah, before Islam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah bint Qays said: My husband divorced me three times in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You have no right to lodging or maintenance."

Mughīrah said: I mentioned it to Ibrāhīm, and he said: ʿUmar said, "We do not abandon the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of our Prophet ﷺ on the word of a woman; we do not know whether she remembered or forgot."
And ʿUmar used to grant her lodging and maintenance.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning His words: {And those who are taken in death among you and leave wives behind, [let them make] a bequest for their wives, provision for a year without turning [them] out}: this was abrogated by the verse of inheritance, by what was prescribed for her of the fourth or the eighth, and the term of a year was abrogated by making her waiting period four months and ten [days].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ [narrated] from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "A woman whose husband has died should not wear garments dyed with safflower, nor those dyed with red clay, nor jewelry; she should not apply henna, nor kohl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Her husband

died, and she was suffering from her eyes, so she used to apply jalāʾ kohl. Aḥmad said: the correct wording is "kohl of jalāʾ." She sent a freed woman of hers to Umm Salamah, who asked her about jalāʾ kohl. She said: Do not apply it except in a case of necessity that becomes severe for you; then apply it at night and wipe it off in the daytime.
Then Umm Salamah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me when Abū Salamah died, and I had put aloe on my eyes. He said:
"What is this, Umm Salamah?"
I said: It is only aloe, O Messenger of Allah; it has no perfume. He said:
"It brightens the face, so do not use it except at night, and remove it in the daytime. And do not comb your hair with perfume or with henna, for it is a dye."
She said: I said, "With what shall I comb my hair, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"With lote-tree leaves (sidr), covering your head with it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: By Allah, whoever wishes, I am ready to swear a mutual oath of imprecation with him: the shorter Sūrat al-Nisāʾ was revealed after the four months and ten [days].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Do not confuse for us his Sunnah, Ibn al-Muthannā said: the Sunnah of our Prophet ﷺ: the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died is four months and ten [days].
He means the umm walad.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ [narrated] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not advance the month until you complete the count or see the crescent. Then fast, and do not break the fast until you see the crescent or complete the count of thirty."
Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh transmitted it as a mursal report.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called me to the pre-dawn meal (suḥūr) in Ramadan and said:
"Come to the blessed meal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to the door of ʿUmar and asked permission to enter. ʿUmar said, "One."
Then he asked permission a second time, and ʿUmar said, "Two."
Then he asked permission a third time, and ʿUmar said, "Three."

Then he left, and [ʿUmar] sent someone after him who brought him back. [ʿUmar] said, "If this is something you memorized from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then [bring proof], and if not, I will make an example of you."
Abū Saʿīd said: He came to us and said, "Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Seeking permission is three times'?"
He said: They began to laugh. He said: So I said, "Your Muslim brother has come to you terrified, and you laugh? Go, for I will share with you in this punishment."
So he went to [ʿUmar] and said, "This is Abū Saʿīd."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Mūsā came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and said, "Peace be upon you, this is ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays."
But [ʿUmar] did not give him permission. [Abū Mūsā] said, "Peace be upon you, this is Abū Mūsā. Peace be upon you, this is al-Ashʿarī."
Then he left, and [ʿUmar] said, "Bring him back to me, bring him back to me."
So he came, and [ʿUmar] said, "O Abū Mūsā, what made you turn back? We were occupied."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
and Ibn Abī ʿUmar,
they said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us,
(Transfer of chain) And Abū Kāmil al-Jaḥdarī narrated to us,
ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us,
both of them from al-Zuhrī,
from Sahl ibn Saʿd,
from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to the hadith of al-Layth and Yūnus.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ṭalḥah said: We were sitting in the courtyards talking, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and stood over us and said:
"What is with you and sitting in the pathways? Avoid sitting in the pathways."
We said, "We only sat for no harm; we sat discussing and talking." He said:
"If you must, then fulfil its right: lowering the gaze, returning the greeting, and good speech."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The right of a Muslim over a Muslim is six."
It was asked, "What are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:

"When you meet him, greet him with salām; when he invites you, accept; when he seeks your advice, advise him sincerely; when he sneezes and praises Allah, say 'may Allah have mercy on you'; when he is ill, visit him; and when he dies, follow [his funeral]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of Jews asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "Death be upon you."
ʿĀʾishah said, "Rather, upon you be death and the curse."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, Allah loves gentleness in all matters."
She said, "Did you not hear what they said?" He said:
"I said, 'And upon you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Beware! No man is to spend the night with a previously married woman unless he is her husband or a close relative [mahram]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of the Banū Hāshim entered upon Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays. Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, who was married to her at that time, entered and saw them, and disliked that. He mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "I saw nothing but good."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah has cleared her of that."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood on the pulpit and said:
"After this day of mine, no man may enter upon a woman whose husband is away unless he has with him one or two other men."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"None of you should make his brother get up and then sit in his place."
And whenever a man stood up from his seat for him, Ibn ʿUmar would not sit in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to serve al-Zubayr with the household chores. He had a horse, and I used to look after it. No chore was harder on me than looking after the horse: I would cut grass for it, tend to it, and care for it.
She said: Then she [Asmāʾ's mother's household] received a servant: captives were brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he gave her a servant.

She said: Caring for the horse was taken off me, as [the servant] relieved me of its burden. Then a man came to me and said, "O Umm ʿAbdillāh, I am a poor man and wish to sell in the shade of your house."

She said, "If I give you permission, al-Zubayr may refuse that, so come and ask me while al-Zubayr is present." So he came and said, "O Umm ʿAbdillāh, I am a poor man and wish to sell in the shade of your house."

She said, "You have nothing in Medina but my house." Al-Zubayr said to her, "What is it to you to prevent a poor man from selling?" So he used to sell until he earned [enough]. Then I sold him the servant girl, and al-Zubayr came in to me while her price was in my lap.
He said, "Give it to me."
She said, "I have given it away in charity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had a she-camel that was my share of the war booty,
and the Prophet ﷺ had given me another she-camel from the fifth [of the spoils].

So when I wished to consummate my marriage to Fāṭimah, may peace be upon her, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I arranged with a goldsmith from Banū Qaynuqāʿ that he would travel with me so that we could bring back idhkhir grass, which I intended to sell to the goldsmiths,
and use the proceeds to help pay for my wedding feast.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr said: There was a man here whose name was Nawwās,
and he had thirsty camels [suffering from an illness].
So Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, went and bought those camels from a partner of his.
Then his partner came to him and said: We have sold those camels.
He said: To whom did you sell them? He said: To an old man, of such and such description.
He said: Woe to you! By Allah, that was Ibn ʿUmar.
So he came to him and said: My partner sold you diseased camels and did not recognize you. He said: Then take them back.
He said: When he went to drive them away, [Ibn ʿUmar] said: Leave them.
We are content with the ruling of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: there is no contagion.
Sufyān heard this from ʿAmr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and I was riding a stubborn young camel belonging to ʿUmar.
It would overpower me and move ahead of the people,
and ʿUmar would rebuke it and pull it back.
Then it would move ahead again, and ʿUmar would rebuke it and pull it back. Then the Prophet ﷺ said to ʿUmar: "Sell it to me."
He said: It is yours, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Sell it to me."
So he sold it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"It is yours, O ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar; do with it as you wish."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I sold to the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUthmān, some property I had in the valley in exchange for property of his in Khaybar.
When we had concluded the sale, I walked backwards until I left his house,
fearing that he might ask me to revoke the sale,
for the established practice was that the two parties to a sale have the option [to cancel] until they separate.

ʿAbdullāh said: When my sale and his had become binding, I thought that I had cheated him, because I had driven him to the land of Thamūd, three nights away, while he had driven me to Madinah, three nights away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, may Allah be pleased with them both, and said: Tell me about the description of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Torah. He said: Yes,

by Allah, he is described in the Torah with some of his description in the Qurʾān: "O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good news, and a warner," and as a protection for the unlettered.
"You are My servant and My messenger; I have named you al-Mutawakkil [the one who relies on Allah].
He is not harsh or coarse, nor one who shouts in the markets.
He does not repay evil with evil, but pardons and forgives.
Allah will not take him until through him He sets straight the crooked community, so that they say: There is no god but Allah.
And through it He will open blind eyes, deaf ears, and sealed hearts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a man to sell food until he has taken full possession of it.
I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: How is that? He said: That is dirhams for dirhams, while the food is delayed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said:] Who has money to exchange? Ṭalḥah said: I do, until our treasurer comes from al-Ghābah.
Sufyān said: This is what we memorized from az-Zuhrī; there was no addition to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Rarely did a day pass on which the Prophet ﷺ did not come to the house of Abū Bakr at one end of the day.
When he was given permission to leave for Madinah, he came to us at midday, which startled us.
Abū Bakr was informed of it and said: The Prophet ﷺ has not come to us at this hour
except for some new matter.
When he entered, he said to Abū Bakr:
"Send away those who are with you."
He said: O Messenger of Allah, they are only my two daughters,
meaning ʿĀʾishah and Asmāʾ. He said:
"Do you know that I have been given permission to leave?"
He said: Companionship, O Messenger of Allah! He said: "Companionship."
He said: O Messenger of Allah, I have two she-camels that I have prepared for the departure; take one of them. He said:
"I have taken it for its price."
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar met him and said: O Abū Saʿīd,
what is this that you are narrating from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Abū Saʿīd said, concerning currency exchange: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Gold for gold, like for like; silver for silver, like for like."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not sell fruit until its fitness [for harvest] is evident,
and do not sell fresh fruit for dried dates."
Sālim said: ʿAbdullāh informed me
from Zayd ibn Thābit
that after that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted a concession regarding the sale of ʿarāyā for fresh dates or for dried dates,
and he did not grant a concession for anything other than that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) about Sūrat al-Anfāl. He said: It was revealed concerning Badr.
"Ash-shawkah" means the sharp edge. "Mturdifīn" means following one troop after another.
"Radafanī" and "ardafanī" mean: he came after me. "Dhūqū" means: engage in it, experience and try it, and this is not tasting with the mouth. "Fa-yarkumahu" means: he gathers it together.
"Sharrid" means: scatter. "Wa-in janaḥū" means: they sought. "Yuthkhin" means: to prevail.
Mujāhid said: "Mukāʾ" means putting their fingers into their mouths, and "taṣdiyah" means whistling. "Li-yuthbitūka" means: to imprison you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not use reason." He said: They are a group from Banū ʿAbd ad-Dār.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar came out to us, and we hoped that he would narrate to us

a good hadith. He said: A man hurried to him and said: O Abū ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, tell us about fighting during the fitnah, for Allah says: "And fight them until there is no fitnah." He said: Do you know what the fitnah is, may your mother lose you?
Muḥammad ﷺ used to fight the polytheists,
and entering into their religion was a fitnah,
and it was not like your fighting for the sake of rulership.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Ḥudhayfah, and he said: None are left of the people of this verse except three,
and none of the hypocrites except four.
A Bedouin said: You are the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, and you tell us things but we do not know; so what about those who break into our houses and steal our precious belongings?
He said: Those are the transgressors.
Yes, none of them is left except four,
one of whom is a very old man who, if he drank cold water, would not feel its coldness.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When something occurred between him and Ibn az-Zubayr. I said: His father was az-Zubayr, his mother was Asmāʾ, his maternal aunt was ʿĀʾishah,
his grandfather was Abū Bakr, and his grandmother was Ṣafiyyah.
Then I said to Sufyān about its chain of transmission...
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abī Mulaykah said: There was something between the two of them, so I went in the morning to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: Do you intend to fight Ibn az-Zubayr,
and so make lawful what Allah has made sacred?
He said: Allah forbid!
Allah has decreed that Ibn az-Zubayr and the Banū Umayyah would make it lawful,
and by Allah, I will never make it lawful.
He said: The people said: Pledge allegiance to Ibn az-Zubayr.
I said: How far is this matter from him! As for his father, he was the disciple of the Prophet ﷺ, meaning az-Zubayr;
as for his grandfather, he was the Companion of the Cave,
meaning Abū Bakr;
his mother was she of the two waist-belts, meaning Asmāʾ;
as for his maternal aunt, she was the Mother of the Believers, meaning ʿĀʾishah;
as for his paternal aunt, she was the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, meaning Khadījah;
as for the paternal aunt of the Prophet ﷺ, she was his grandmother, meaning Ṣafiyyah;
then he is chaste in Islam, a reciter of the Qurʾān.
By Allah, if they maintain ties with me, they do so as close kin,
and if they rule over me, those who rule over me are noble peers,
so he preferred the Tuwaytāt, the Usāmāt and the Ḥumaydāt,
meaning clans of Banū Asad: Banū Tuwayt, Banū Usāmah and Banū Asad.
The son of Abū al-ʿĀṣ has come forth walking proudly,
meaning ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān,
while he has twisted his tail,
meaning Ibn az-Zubayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: Do you not marvel at Ibn az-Zubayr, who has risen up in this affair of his? I said: I will hold myself to account for him as I did not hold myself to account for Abū Bakr or ʿUmar,
though they were more deserving of every good than he,
and I said: He is the son of the paternal aunt of the Prophet ﷺ, and the son of az-Zubayr,
and the son of Abū Bakr's daughter's household,
and the nephew of Khadījah,
and the son of ʿĀʾishah's sister. Yet he holds himself above me and does not want that. I said: I did not think that I would offer this of myself and he would refuse it,
and I do not see that he wants good.
But if it must be so, that my cousins rule over me is dearer to me than that others rule over me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Something was sent to the Prophet ﷺ,
and he divided it among four people and said: "I am winning their hearts."
A man said: You have not been just. He said:
"From the offspring of this man will come a people who pass through the religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: By Allah,

after Allah guided me to Islam, no blessing He has bestowed upon me is greater than my truthfulness to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in that I did not lie to him and so perish as those who lied perished, when revelation was sent down: "They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them" up to "the defiantly disobedient."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:
"Tonight two comers came to me and took me out,
and we arrived at a city built of bricks of gold and bricks of silver.
Men met us, half of whose bodies were as beautiful as the best you have ever seen,
and half as ugly as the ugliest you have ever seen. The two said to them: Go and throw yourselves into that river.
They plunged into it, then returned to us, and that ugliness had gone from them,
and they were in the finest form. The two said to me: This is the Garden of ʿAdn,
and that is your dwelling. They said: As for the people, half of whom were beautiful and half ugly, they mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil, and Allah has pardoned them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he,

came with some milch animals of his in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and stayed with Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh. [Ṭalḥah] said: "The Prophet ﷺ forbade a town-dweller to sell on behalf of a desert-dweller. Rather, go to the market and see who will deal with you, then consult me, until I either direct you or forbid you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no hoarding in dates.
Ibn al-Muthannā said: [He narrated] from al-Ḥasan. We said to him: "Do not say 'from al-Ḥasan.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sufyān disliked this interpretation of "He is not of us" [as meaning] "he is not like us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out on one of our expeditions and stopped at a halting place. A companion of ours sold a horse in exchange for a slave, and the two stayed for the rest of that day and night. When the next morning came and it was time to depart, [the seller] got up to saddle his horse, but regretted [the sale]. He came to the man and demanded that the sale be cancelled, but the man refused to hand it back to him. So he said: "Between you and me [shall judge] Abū Barzah, the Companion of the Prophet ﷺ." They came to Abū Barzah in a corner of the camp and told him this story.
He said: "Will you both be satisfied if I judge between you with the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'The two parties to a sale have the option [to cancel] as long as they have not separated.'"
Hishām ibn Ḥassān said: Jamīl narrated that he said: "I do not think you two have separated."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Abū Zurʿah made a sale to a man, he would give him the option. [The narrator] said: Then he would say: "Give me the option," and say: "I heard Abū Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Two people must not separate except by mutual consent.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When you deal in ʿīnah sales, take hold of the tails of cattle, are content with farming, and abandon jihad, Allah will impose upon you a humiliation that He will not remove until you return to your religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Shaddād and Abū Burdah disagreed about advance sales (salaf), so they sent me to Ibn Abī Awfā and I asked him. He said: "We used to make advance sales in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, in wheat, barley, dates and raisins" — Ibn Kathīr added: "with people who did not possess it [at the time]."
Then the two agreed. And I asked Ibn Abzā, and he said the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Calamities (jawāʾiḥ) are every evident destructive thing, such as rain, hail, locusts, wind, or fire.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no [allowance for] calamity in what is lost amounting to less than a third of the capital. Yaḥyā said: And that is the established practice of the Muslims.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed Allah has forbidden wine and its price, has forbidden carrion and its price, and has forbidden swine and its price."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Musaddad, in the hadith of Khālid ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Barakah Abū al-Walīd,
then the two agreed, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sitting by the corner [of the Kaʿbah]. He said: He raised his gaze to the sky and laughed, and said:
"May Allah curse the Jews," three times.
"Indeed Allah forbade them fat, so they sold it and ate its price. And indeed when Allah forbids a people to eat something, He forbids them its price."
In the hadith of Khālid ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Ṭaḥḥān, he did not say "I saw." And he said:
"May Allah fight the Jews."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever sells wine, let him [also] butcher swine."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I bought some oil in the market, and when I had made the purchase my own, a man met me and offered me a good profit on it. I wanted to strike hands with him, but a man grabbed my arm from behind. I turned around and it was Zayd ibn Thābit. He said: "Do not sell it where you bought it until you have taken it to your own lodging, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade selling goods where they are bought until the merchants have taken them to their own lodgings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I sold it, meaning his camel, to the Prophet ﷺ and stipulated that I be carried on it to my family. At the end [of the hadith] he said:
"Do you think I haggled with you only to take your camel? Take your camel and its price; both are yours."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The yield is [due] with liability."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a partnership between me and some other people in a slave. I employed him while some of us were absent, and he produced some earnings. [One of them] brought a case against me over his share before one of the judges, who ordered me to return the earnings. So I went to ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr and told him. ʿUrwah went to him and narrated to him from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The yield is [due] with liability."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, in a long narration, and he said: "
I became drowsy and fell into a heavy sleep, and I saw my Lord in the best form. He said: 'About what are the highest assembly disputing?'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this was revealed:

"Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, you will dispute before your Lord," az-Zubayr said: "O Messenger of Allah, will the dispute be repeated for us after what happened between us in the world?" He said: "Yes."
He said: "Then the matter is indeed severe."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite:
"O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins," and "He does not mind."
label: machine translation

segments_en: So the Prophet ﷺ laughed in amazement and in affirmation.
He said: This is a hasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jewish man passed by the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "
O Jew, tell us."
He said: "What do you say, O Abū al-Qāsim, when Allah places the heavens on this, the earths on this, the water on this, the mountains on this, and the rest of creation on this?"
Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn aṣ-Ṣalt pointed with his little finger first, then continued until he reached the thumb. Then Allah revealed:
"They have not appraised Allah with true appraisal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Do you know how vast Hell is?" I said: "No."
He said: "Indeed, by Allah, you do not know.
ʿĀʾishah told me that she asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about His saying:

"And the whole earth will be within His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand." She said: I said: "Then where will the people be on that day, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "
On the bridge over Hell."
There is a story in the hadith.
He said: This is a hasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb hadith from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: O Messenger of Allah,
"And the whole earth will be within His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand." Then where will the believers be on that day?" He said: "
On the Path, O ʿĀʾishah."
This is a hasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited:
"Indeed, those who say, 'Our Lord is Allah,' and then remain steadfast," and he said: "
People have said it, then most of them disbelieved. So whoever dies upon it is among those who remained steadfast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Banū Murrah said: I came to Kufa and was told about Bilāl ibn Abī Burdah,

so I said: "There is certainly a lesson in him." I went to him while he was imprisoned in the house he had built. Everything about him had changed from torture and beating, and he was in rags. I said: "Praise be to Allah, O Bilāl! I saw you passing by us holding your nose, though there was no dust, and you are in this state today." He said: "Where are you from?" I said: "From Banū Murrah ibn ʿUbād."
He said: "Shall I not tell you a hadith by which Allah may benefit you?" I said: "Go ahead."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

There is no believer except that he has two doors: a door through which his deeds ascend, and a door through which his provision descends. When he dies, they both weep for him. That is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: 'And neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them, nor were they given respite.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When they intended to kill ʿUthmān, ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām came, and ʿUthmān said to him: "What brings you?" He said: "I came to support you."
He said: "Go out to the people and drive them away from me, for you going out is better for me than you coming in."

So ʿAbdullāh went out to the people and said: "O people, my name in the Days of Ignorance was so-and-so, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named me ʿAbdullāh. Verses of the Book of Allah were revealed about me. It was revealed about me:

'And a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something similar, and he believed while you were arrogant. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.' And it was revealed about me:

'Say: Sufficient is Allah as witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture.' Indeed, Allah has a sheathed sword held back from you, and the angels have become neighbors to you in this town of yours, where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ settled. So fear Allah, fear Allah regarding this man; do not kill him. By Allah, if you kill him, you will drive away your neighbors, the angels, and you will draw Allah's sheathed sword against you, and it will not be sheathed against you until the Day of Resurrection."
They said: "Kill the Jew, and kill ʿUthmān!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was a friend of Umayyah ibn Khalaf.
Whenever Umayyah passed through Madinah, he would stay with Saʿd,
and whenever Saʿd passed through Makkah, he would stay with Umayyah.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, Saʿd set out to perform ʿUmrah
and stayed with Umayyah in Makkah.
He said to Umayyah, "Find me a time when it is quiet, so that perhaps I may circumambulate the House."
So Umayyah went out with him around midday, and Abū Jahl met them and said, "O Abū Ṣafwān,
who is this with you?" He said, "This is Saʿd."
Abū Jahl said to him, "I see you circumambulating in Makkah in safety,
when you have given shelter to the apostates,
and claimed that you would support and help them!
By Allah, were it not that you are with Abū Ṣafwān, you would not return to your family safe."
Saʿd said to him, raising his voice at him, "By Allah, if you stop me from this, I will stop you from something far harder for you than it: your route through Madinah."
Umayyah said to him, "Do not raise your voice, Saʿd, against Abū al-Ḥakam, the master of the people of the valley."
Saʿd said, "Leave us alone, Umayyah.
By Allah, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say that they will kill you."
He asked, "In Makkah?" He said, "I do not know."
Umayyah was seized with great fear because of that.
When Umayyah returned to his family, he said, "O Umm Ṣafwān,
did you not see what Saʿd said to me?" She asked, "What did he say to you?" He said, "He claims that Muḥammad told them that they will kill me.
I said to him, 'In Makkah?' He said, 'I do not know.'"
Umayyah said, "By Allah, I will not leave Makkah."
When the day of Badr came, Abū Jahl called the people to march out and said, "Go and intercept your caravan."
Umayyah disliked going out,
so Abū Jahl came to him and said, "O Abū Ṣafwān,
if the people see that you have stayed behind, and you are the master of the people of the valley, they will stay behind with you."
Abū Jahl kept on at him until he said, "Since you have overcome me,
by Allah, I will buy the best camel in Makkah." Then Umayyah said, "O Umm Ṣafwān, prepare me for the journey."
She said to him, "O Abū Ṣafwān, have you forgotten what your brother from Yathrib said to you?" He said, "No,
I only intend to go along with them a short distance."
When Umayyah set out, he would not stop at any halting place without hobbling his camel,
and he continued like that until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, caused him to be killed at Badr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir said, "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he had with him only five slaves, two women, and Abū Bakr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was an exchange between Abū Bakr and ʿUmar,
and Abū Bakr made ʿUmar angry.
ʿUmar turned away from him in anger,
and Abū Bakr followed him, asking him to seek forgiveness for him,
but he did not do so, until he shut his door in his face.
So Abū Bakr came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Abū al-Dardāʾ said: We were with him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"As for this companion of yours, he has surely been quarrelling."
He said: ʿUmar regretted what he had done, so he came, greeted with salām, and sat with the Prophet ﷺ, and told the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what had happened.
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry, and Abū Bakr kept saying, "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I was the one more in the wrong." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Will you not leave my companion to me? Will you not leave my companion to me? I said, 'O people, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all,' and you said, 'You are lying.'
But Abū Bakr said, 'You have spoken the truth.'" Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: "Ghāmara" means he took the lead in what is good.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The gaze of the Prophet ﷺ became fixed, and then he said,
"In the Highest Companionship," three times. And she related the hadith.
She said: There was no sermon of the two of them but that Allah benefited [people] by it.
ʿUmar frightened the people, and there was hypocrisy among them,
and Allah turned them back by that.

Then Abū Bakr gave the people insight into guidance and made them recognise the truth that was upon them, and they went out reciting it: {Muḥammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him} up to {the grateful}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman was escorted as a bride to a man from the Ansār, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, did you not have some entertainment with you? For the Ansār enjoy entertainment."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafiyyah bint Shaybah said: The Prophet ﷺ held a wedding banquet for some of his wives with two mudds of barley.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Free the captive, respond to the one who invites, and visit the sick."
label: machine translation

segments_en: None of you should flog his wife as a slave is flogged,
and then have intercourse with her at the end of the day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and he would draw near to one of them,
then he went in to Ḥafṣah,
and he stayed longer than he usually stayed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "My little daughter, do not be deceived by this one who is pleased with her own beauty, [thinking of] the love of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for her," meaning ʿĀʾishah. Then I recounted it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he smiled.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ heard.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was counted against me as one divorce.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Prophet ﷺ until we set off to an orchard called ash-Shawṭ,
until we reached two orchards and sat between them. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Sit here."
He went in, and the Jawniyyah woman had been brought,
and she had been lodged in a house among the palm trees, in the house of Umaymah bint an-Nuʿmān ibn Sharāḥīl, with her was her nurse who looked after her.
When the Prophet ﷺ entered upon her, he said:
"Give yourself to me."
She said: "Does a queen give herself to an ordinary person?"
He said: He reached out his hand to place it on her so that she would be calm, and she said: "I seek refuge in Allah from you." He said:
"You have sought refuge with One who is a [worthy] refuge."
Then he came out to us and said:
"O Abū Usayd, give her two linen garments and send her back to her family."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this [chain/wording].
label: machine translation

segments_en: If you had divorced once or twice—for the Prophet ﷺ commanded me with this—
but if you divorce her three times, she becomes unlawful for you until she marries a husband other than you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Jamīlah... and he mentioned the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Ibn ʿUmar,
when he was asked about marrying a Christian woman or a Jewish woman,
would say: "Allah has forbidden polytheistic women to the believers,
and I know of no polytheism greater than a woman saying that her lord is Jesus,
when he is [only] one of the servants of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The polytheists were in two positions with respect to the Prophet ﷺ and the believers:
polytheists at war, whom he fought and who fought him,
and polytheists under a treaty, whom he did not fight and who did not fight him.
When a woman from the people of war emigrated, she would not be proposed to until she had menstruated and become pure,
and when she became pure, marriage was lawful for her.
If her husband emigrated before she married, she was returned to him.
If a male or female slave of theirs emigrated, they were free and had what the emigrants had.

Then he mentioned, regarding the people of the treaty, [something] like the hadith of Mujāhid: if a male or female slave belonging to the polytheists under treaty emigrated, they were not returned, but their price was returned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qarībah bint Abī Umayyah was married to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he divorced her,
then Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān married her.
Umm al-Ḥakam, daughter of Abū Sufyān, was married to ʿIyāḍ ibn Ghanm al-Fihrī, and he divorced her,
then ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ath-Thaqafī married her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with them both. He used to say regarding the oath of abstention (īlāʾ) that Allah named: after the appointed term it is not lawful for anyone except to retain [his wife] with kindness,
or to resolve on divorce,
as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When four months have passed, he is made to stand [before the authorities] until he divorces,
and divorce does not take effect upon him until he divorces.
This is mentioned from ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Abū ad-Dardāʾ, ʿĀʾishah, and twelve men from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed tawāf on his camel,
and whenever he came to the corner, he pointed to it and said "Allāhu akbar."
Zaynab said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Today an opening has been made in the barrier of Yājūj and Mājūj like this," and he made a circle with his fingers [indicating] ninety.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Hilāl ibn Umayyah accused his wife [of adultery],
so he came and testified, while the Prophet ﷺ was saying:
"Allah knows that one of you two is lying,
so is either of you willing to repent?"
Then she stood up and testified.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān about the first
thing that was revealed of the Qur'an.

He said, "O you who are wrapped [in garments]" (al-Muddaththir). I said, "They say it was "Recite in the name of your Lord who created"?" Abū Salamah said: I asked Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh, may Allah be pleased with them both, about that, and I said to him what you have said. Jābir said: I will only tell you what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ told us. He said: "I stayed in seclusion at Ḥirāʾ.
When I had completed my stay, I descended, and I was called. I looked to my right and saw nothing,
and I looked to my left and saw nothing,
and I looked in front of me and saw nothing,
and I looked behind me and saw nothing.
Then I raised my head and saw something,

so I went to Khadījah and said, 'Wrap me up and pour cold water over me.'" He said: So they wrapped me up and poured cold water over me. He said: Then was revealed: "O you who are wrapped [in garments], arise and warn, and your Lord glorify."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Between the two blasts [of the trumpet] there are forty."
They said, "O Abū Hurayrah, forty days?" He said, "I refuse [to say]."
They said, "Forty months?" He said, "I refuse."
They said, "Forty years?" He said, "I refuse."
"Then Allah will send down water from the sky, and they will sprout like vegetables." He said:
"There is nothing of the human being that does not decay, except one bone, which is the tailbone. From it the creation will be reassembled on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Abū Jahl said, "If I see Muḥammad praying at the Kaʿbah, I will trample on his neck."
This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"If he did it, the angels would seize him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"While I was walking in Paradise, there appeared before me a river, whose banks were domes of pearl.

I said to the angel, 'What is this?' He said, 'This is al-Kawthar, which Allah has given you.' Then he struck his hand into the clay and brought out musk. Then the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary was shown to me, and I saw a great light by it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There was no prophet among the prophets except that he was given signs of the kind that people believed in because of them. What I was given was only revelation, which Allah revealed to me. So I hope that I will have the most followers among them on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "And whoever deceitfully takes [from the spoils] will come on the Day of Resurrection with what he took." Then he said: By which recitation do you order me to recite? I recited to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ more than seventy sūrahs, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ know that I am the most knowledgeable of them regarding the Book of Allah. If I knew that anyone was more knowledgeable than I, I would travel to him.
Shaqīq said: I sat in the circles of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, and I did not hear anyone reject that from him or find fault with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in Ḥimṣ, and some of the people said to me, "Recite to us."
So I recited Sūrat Yūsuf to them. He said: A man among the people said, "By Allah, it was not revealed like this."
I said, "Woe to you! By Allah, I recited it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he said to me, 'You have done well.'"

While I was speaking to him, I noticed the smell of wine on him. I said, "Do you drink wine and deny the Book? You will not leave until I flog you." He said: So I flogged him the prescribed punishment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh, may Allah be pleased with him, said: By Allah, other than Whom there is no god, no sūrah of the Book of Allah was revealed except that I know where it was revealed, and no verse of the Book of Allah was revealed except that I know about what it was revealed.
And if I knew anyone more knowledgeable than I of the Book of Allah, whom camels could reach, I would ride to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people
from among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were on a journey, and they passed by one of the Arab tribes and asked them for hospitality, but they did not host them.
Then [the tribe] said to them, "Is there anyone among you who can perform ruqyah? For the chief of the tribe has been stung or afflicted."
One of them said, "Yes." He went to him and recited ruqyah over him with Fātiḥat al-Kitāb, and the man recovered. He was given a flock of sheep, but he refused to accept it,
and said, "Not until I mention that to the Prophet ﷺ."
He came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him.
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I only performed ruqyah with Fātiḥat al-Kitāb." He smiled and said:
"What made you know that it is a ruqyah?" Then he said:
"Take it from them, and set aside a share for me with you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd was wounded on the day of the Trench. A man from Quraysh called Ibn al-ʿAriqah shot him.

He shot him in the ʿakḥal (the arm vein), so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pitched a tent for him in the mosque so that he could visit him from nearby. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from the Trench, he put down his weapons and washed. Then Jibrīl came to him, shaking the dust from his head, and said, "You have put down your weapons? By Allah, we have not put them down. Go out against them."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Where?"

Jibrīl pointed toward Banū Qurayẓah. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fought them, and they surrendered to the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who referred the judgment about them to Saʿd. He said, "I judge concerning them that the fighters be killed, that the children and women be taken captive, and that their wealth be divided."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he was at Khaybar, after they had conquered it,
and I said, "O Messenger of Allah, give me a share."
Some of the sons of Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ said, "Do not give him a share, O Messenger of Allah."
Abū Hurayrah said, "This is the killer of Ibn Qawqal."
The son of Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ said, "How strange, a badger that has come down to us from the peak of Ḍa'n,"
"reproaching me for the killing of a Muslim man whom Allah honored at my hands, and did not humiliate me at his hands!"
He said: I do not know whether he gave him a share or did not give him a share.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The martyrs are five: the one who dies of plague, the one who dies of a stomach illness,
the one who drowns, the one crushed by a collapsed building,
and the martyr in the cause of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā
wrote, and I read it, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you meet them, be patient."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Muhājirūn and the Anṣār were digging the trench around Madinah,
and carrying the earth on their backs, saying: "We are the ones who pledged allegiance to Muhammad to Islam for as long as we live." He said: The Prophet ﷺ was replying to them, saying:
"O Allah, there is no good except the good of the Hereafter,
so bless the Anṣār and the Muhājirah."
He said: They would be brought two handfuls of barley, and it would be cooked for them with rancid fat and placed before the people, while the people were hungry,
and it was foul in the throat and had a stinking smell.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When it was the day of the Confederates,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dug the trench, I saw him carrying earth from the trench until the dust covered the skin of his belly,
and he had much hair.
I heard him reciting verses of Ibn Rawāḥah in rhythm,

as he carried the earth, saying: "O Allah, were it not for You we would not have been guided, nor given charity, nor prayed. So send down tranquility upon us and make our feet firm if we meet [the enemy]. Those [people] have wronged us, and if they desire trial [against us], we refuse." He said: Then he would extend his voice at the end of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the expedition of Tabūk.
He then narrated the hadith, which includes: Then we came forward until we reached Wādī al-Qurā, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I am going to hurry; whoever of you wishes, let him hurry with me, and whoever wishes, let him stay."
So we set out until we came in view of Madinah, and he said:
"This is Ṭābah, and this is Uḥud, a mountain that loves us and we love it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would not enter upon any woman except his wives, except Umm Sulaym; he would enter upon her. He was asked about that, and he said:
"I have compassion for her; her brother was killed alongside me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever keeps a horse for the cause of Allah, out of faith in Allah and belief in His promise,
then its fullness, its drink, its dung, and its urine will be in his scale on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He went out with the Prophet ﷺ, and Abū Qatādah stayed behind with some of his companions, who were in iḥrām, while he was not in iḥrām.
They saw a wild donkey before he saw it.
When they saw it, they left it alone until Abū Qatādah saw it,
so he mounted a horse of his called al-Jarādah,
and asked them to hand him his whip, but they refused.
So he took it himself, charged, and hamstrung the animal.
Then he ate, and they ate.
Then they regretted it. When they caught up with him, he said:
"Do you have any of it with you?"
He said, "We have its leg."
So the Prophet ﷺ took it and ate it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Whoever frees a slave that he co-owns with another person is obliged to secure his full release."
This is the wording of Ibn Suwayd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, with the same meaning as the report of Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to sell the mothers of children during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and of Abū Bakr. Then when ʿUmar became ruler, he forbade us, and we stopped.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this [chain] he added, and he said, meaning the Prophet ﷺ:
"You have more right to its price, and Allah is independent of need of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

freed six slaves at the time of his death, and he had no property other than them. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he spoke harshly to him. Then he called them, divided them into three groups, and cast lots among them. He freed two and kept four in slavery.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The child of adultery is the worst of the three."
Abū Hurayrah said: To benefit someone with a whip in the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is dearer to me than freeing a child of adultery.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to Wāthilah ibn al-Asqaʿ and said to him, "Narrate to us a hadith
with no addition and no omission." He became angry and said, "One of you recites [the Qurʾān] while his copy hangs in his house, and he still adds and omits."
We said, "We only wanted a hadith that you heard from the Prophet ﷺ."
He said: We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a companion of ours who had made the Fire obligatory [for himself] through killing. He said:
"Free a slave on his behalf; Allah will free from the Fire a limb of his for every limb of the slave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We besieged the fortress of aṭ-Ṭāʾif with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Muʿādh said: I heard my father say "the castle of aṭ-Ṭāʾif" and "the stronghold of aṭ-Ṭāʾif," all of these. Then I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Whoever delivers an arrow in the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will have a rank [in Paradise]."
And he went on with the hadith. And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"Any Muslim man who frees a Muslim man, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will make every bone of the freed man a protection from the Fire for the corresponding bone of the one who freed him. And any woman who frees a Muslim woman, Allah will make every bone of hers a protection from the Fire for the corresponding bone of the one who freed her, on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Whoever frees a believing slave, it will be his ransom from the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him: that the Prophet ﷺ recited: {And take the station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from miserliness and from decrepit old age."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was the delegate of Banū al-Muntafiq, or I was among the delegation of Banū al-Muntafiq, to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he mentioned the hadith, and he said, meaning the Prophet ﷺ: "Do not think..."
And he did not say, "Do not think..."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ used to recite: {other than those who are disabled}. Saʿīd did not say, "he used to recite."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: {And We prescribed for them therein: a life for a life, an eye for an eye.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: {from weakness}
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: {In the bounty of Allah and His mercy, in that let them rejoice.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ recited: {In the bounty of Allah and His mercy, in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to play with dolls, and sometimes the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would come in while the girls were with me. When he entered they would leave, and when he left they would come back in.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah] may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from the expedition of Tabūk or Khaybar, and there was a curtain over her shelf. A wind blew and lifted a corner of the curtain, uncovering some dolls belonging to ʿĀʾishah. He said:
"What is this, ʿĀʾishah?" She said, "My dolls."
Among them he saw a horse with two wings made of scraps of cloth, and he said:
"What is this that I see in the middle of them?" She said, "A horse." He said:
"And what is this on it?" She said, "Two wings." He said:
"A horse with two wings?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], may Allah be pleased with her,

said: When we arrived in Medina, some women came to me while I was playing on a swing, with my hair cut short to my ears. They took me away, prepared me and adorned me, and then brought me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he consummated the marriage with me when I was nine years old.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: We arrived in Medina and stayed among the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj. She said: By Allah, I was on a swing between two palm branches when my mother came to me and brought me down, and I had short hair to my ears. And he narrated the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Reaching back to the Prophet ﷺ:
"The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One above the heavens will be merciful to you."
Musaddad did not say "the freed slave of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr," and he said: The Prophet ﷺ said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to hear and obey, and to give sincere advice to every Muslim. He said: When he sold something or bought something, he would say:
"What we have taken from you is dearer to us than what we have given you, so choose."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You will be called on the Day of Resurrection by your names and your fathers' names, so make your names good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man,
called Aṣram, was among the group who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "What is your name?"
He said, "I am Aṣram." He said:
"Rather, you are Zurʿah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "What is your name?" He said, "Ḥazn." He said, "You are Sahl."
He said, "No. Sahl [what is smooth] is trodden on and treated with contempt."
Saʿīd said: I thought that harshness would befall us after him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If I live, Allah willing, I will forbid my Ummah from naming [anyone] Nāfiʿ, Aflaḥ, and Barakah."
Al-Aʿmash said: I do not know whether he mentioned Nāfiʿ or not.
"For a man says, when someone arrives, 'Is Barakah there?' and they say, 'No.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb,

may Allah be pleased with him, struck a son of his who was called Abū ʿĪsā, and al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah was [also] called Abū ʿĪsā. ʿUmar said to him, "Is it not enough for you to be called Abū ʿAbdillāh?" He replied, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me that name." He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had all his past and future sins forgiven, while we are [still] in our wanderings." So he continued to be called Abū ʿAbdillāh until he died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "O my son."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever takes my name should not take my kunyah, and whoever takes my kunyah should not take my name."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafiyyah bint Shaybah, from ʿĀʾishah,

may Allah be pleased with her, said: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have given birth to a boy and named him Muḥammad and given him the kunyah Abū al-Qāsim, and it was mentioned to me that you dislike that." He said:
"What made my name permissible and my kunyah forbidden?" or:
"What made my kunyah forbidden and my name permissible?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], may Allah be pleased with her, said, "O Messenger of Allah, all my companions have kunyahs." He said:
"Then take the kunyah from your son ʿAbdullāh."
meaning her sister's son. Musaddad said: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr. She said: So she was called Umm ʿAbdillāh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is a grave betrayal that you tell your brother something and he believes you, while you are lying to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Masʿūd said to Abū ʿAbdillāh, or Abū ʿAbdillāh said to Abū Masʿūd: What did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say about "they claim"?
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ addressed them and said, "To proceed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The heart is like a feather that the winds turn over and over in an open desert."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No wealth has ever benefited me as much as the wealth of Abū Bakr has benefited me."
He said: Abū Bakr wept and said, "Am I and my wealth anything but for you, O Messenger of Allah?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿUmar accepted Islam, Jibrīl came down and said: "O Muḥammad, the people of the heavens have rejoiced at the news of ʿUmar's acceptance of Islam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The first whom the Truth will shake hands with is ʿUmar, and the first whom it will greet with salām, and the first whose hand it will take and then admit him into Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, strengthen Islam specifically through ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The best of people after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is Abū Bakr, and the best of people after Abū Bakr is ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ met ʿUthmān at the door of the mosque and said:
"O ʿUthmān, this is Jibrīl. He has informed me that Allah has married you to Umm Kulthūm with a dowry like that of Ruqayyah, and on the same terms of companionship as she had."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O ʿUthmān, if Allah one day entrusts you with this authority, and the hypocrites want you to take off your shirt that Allah has clothed you with, do not take it off."
He said that three times.
an-Nuʿmān said: I said to ʿĀʾishah, "What prevented you from teaching people this?" She said, "By Allah, I had forgotten it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said during his illness:
"I wish that some of my Companions were with me."
We said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall we call Abū Bakr for you?" He was silent. We said, "Shall we call ʿUmar for you?" He was silent. We said, "Shall we call ʿUthmān for you?" He said, "Yes."
So ʿUthmān came and he was alone with him, and the Prophet ﷺ began speaking to him while the face of ʿUthmān kept changing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We returned with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on his Hajj that he performed, and he stopped on the road and ordered the call, "Prayer is about to be held in congregation." Then he took ʿAlī by the hand and said:
"Am I not closer to the believers than they are to themselves?" They said, "Yes." He said:
"Am I not closer to every believer than he is to himself?" They said, "Yes." He said:
"So this is the protecting friend of whomever I am the protecting friend. O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him, and be an enemy to whoever is an enemy to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Laylā used to spend evenings in conversation with ʿAlī, who would wear summer clothes in winter and winter clothes in summer. We said, "If only you would ask him." So he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for me on the day of Khaybar while I had sore eyes. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have sore eyes."
So he spat in my eyes, then said:
"O Allah, remove from him the heat and the cold."
He said: After that day I never felt heat or cold. And he said:
"I will send a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love, who does not flee."
The people were eager for it, but he sent for ʿAlī and gave it to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī said: I am the servant of Allah and the brother of
His Messenger ﷺ, and I am the greatest truthful one;
no one says it after me except a liar. I prayed seven years before the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah came during one of his Hajj journeys, and Saʿd visited him. They mentioned ʿAlī, and he spoke ill of him. Saʿd became angry and said: "Do you say this about a man of whom I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever I am his protecting friend, ʿAlī is his protecting friend.' And I heard him say:
'You are to me in the position of Hārūn to Mūsā, except that there is no prophet after me.' And I heard him say:
'Today I will give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: And my maternal uncle,
Yaʿlā and Wakīʿ, from Ismāʿīl, from Qays,
said: I heard Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ
say: I was the first of the Arabs to shoot an arrow in the cause of Allah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the tenth of ten, and he said:
"Abū Bakr is in Paradise, ʿUmar is in Paradise, ʿUthmān is in Paradise, ʿAlī is in Paradise, Ṭalḥah is in Paradise, az-Zubayr is in Paradise, Saʿd is in Paradise, and ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān is in Paradise."
He was asked, "Who is the ninth?" He said, "I am."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar
gave him the good news that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever wishes to recite the Qurʾān fresh, as it was revealed, let him recite it according to the recitation of Ibn Umm ʿAbd."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whom do you count as a martyr among you?"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, whoever is killed in the cause of Allah is a martyr." He said:
