"Then the martyrs of my Ummah would be few."
They said, "Then who are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Whoever is killed in the cause of Allah is a martyr; whoever dies in the cause of Allah is a martyr; whoever dies of the plague is a martyr; and whoever dies of a stomach illness is a martyr."
Ibn Miqsam said: I bear witness concerning your father in this hadith that he said: "And the one who drowns is a martyr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying, "I send out my dog, and I find another dog with my dog that has caught [the game], and I do not know which of them caught it." He said:
"Do not eat it, for you only mentioned Allah's name over your dog and did not mention it over the other."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Qutaybah and Ibn
Ḥujr, from Ismāʿīl,
Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said: Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar informed us,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Dīnār,
that he heard Ibn ʿUmar
say: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about the ḍabb (spiny-tailed lizard), and he said:
"I will not eat it, nor do I declare it forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a ḍabb (spiny-tailed lizard). He began looking at it and turning it over, and he said:
"A nation was transformed [into animals], and it is not known what became of it. I do not know, perhaps this is from them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Jābir about the ḍabb (spiny-tailed lizard),
and he said, "Do not feed it [to people]."
And he found it distasteful. He said that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: The Prophet ﷺ did not forbid it.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, benefits more than one person by it, and it is the food of most herdsmen. Had I had any, I would have eaten it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was sitting, and beside him was a nephew of his, who threw a pebble with his fingers. He forbade him and said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it," and he said:
"It does not hunt any game and does not harm an enemy, but it breaks a tooth and puts out an eye."
He said: His nephew then went back to throwing pebbles, so he said, "I tell you that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it, and then you go back to throwing pebbles? I will never speak to you again."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade killing any animal by confining it and shooting at it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered a horned ram, which walks in black, lies down in black, and looks in black. It was brought to him to sacrifice, and he said to her:
"O ʿĀʾishah, bring the knife." Then he said, "Sharpen it with a stone."
She did so. Then he took it, took the ram, laid it down, and slaughtered it. Then he said:
"In the name of Allah. O Allah, accept this from Muhammad, the family of Muhammad, and the Ummah of Muhammad."
Then he sacrificed it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He attended the festival prayer with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. He said: Then I prayed with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. He said: He led us in prayer before the sermon, then addressed the people and said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade you to eat the meat of your sacrifices beyond three nights, so do not eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"None of you should eat from the meat of his sacrifice beyond three days."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Abū al-Zubayr,
from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh,
that he informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade eating the meat of sacrificial animals after three days, and then said:
"Eat, take provisions, and store [it]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a sacrifice, then said:
"O Thawbān, prepare for us the meat of this sheep."
He said: I kept feeding him from it until we reached Madinah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib when a man came to him and said, "What did the Prophet ﷺ confide to you in secret?" He became angry and said, "The Prophet ﷺ did not confide to me anything that he concealed from the people, except that he told me four statements."
The man said, "What are they, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: He said:

"Allah curses the one who curses his father; Allah curses the one who slaughters for other than Allah; Allah curses the one who shelters an innovator [or criminal]; and Allah curses the one who alters the boundary markers of the land."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about wine being made into vinegar, and he said, "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Who will take these words from me, and act upon them, or teach someone who will act upon them?"
Abū Hurayrah said: I said, "I will, O Messenger of Allah." So he took my hand and counted five [things], and said:

"Avoid what is forbidden and you will be the most devout of people; be content with what Allah has apportioned for you and you will be the richest of people; be good to your neighbor and you will be a believer; love for people what you love for yourself and you will be a Muslim; and do not laugh excessively, for excessive laughter deadens the heart."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿUthmān stood at a grave, he would weep until his beard was wet. It was said to him: "You remember Paradise and the Fire and do not weep, yet you weep over this?" He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The grave is the first of the stages of the Hereafter. If one is saved from it, what comes after is easier than it; and if one is not saved from it, what comes after is more severe than it."
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have never seen a sight except that the grave is more dreadful than it."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb ḥadīth; we only know it from the narration of Hishām ibn Yūsuf.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I see what you do not see and I hear what you do not hear. The heavens groan, and they have every right to groan. There is not a space of four fingers in them except that an angel has placed his forehead there, prostrating to Allah.
By Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, you would not take pleasure in women on your beds, and you would go out to the open roads, crying out to Allah."
[Abū Dharr said:] "By Allah, I wish I were a tree that is cut down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A man may speak a word, seeing no harm in it, and fall because of it seventy autumns into the Fire."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb ḥadīth from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was among a group of riders with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he came upon a discarded lamb. He said:
"Do you see how worthless this is to its owners?"
It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, it is because of its worthlessness that they threw it away."
Or as he said. He said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, the world is more worthless to Allah than this is to its owners."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The world is cursed, and cursed is what is in it, except the remembrance of Allah and what accompanies it, a scholar, or a student."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The lifespans of my Ummah are between sixty and seventy years, and few of them go beyond that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"This is the son of Adam, and this is his appointed term."
He placed his hand at the back of his neck, then stretched it out and said:
"And there is his hope, and there is his hope, and there is his hope."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by us while we were repairing a hut of ours, and he said: "What is this?"
I said: "A hut of ours that has become worn; we are mending it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I do not see the matter [of death] except as coming sooner than that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Detachment from the world is not in making the lawful unlawful, nor in wasting wealth. Rather, detachment from the world is that you are not more confident in what is in your own hands than in what is in the Hand of Allah, and that, when a calamity strikes you, you desire its reward more than you would desire to have it remain with you."
Hishām said: Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī used to say that this ḥadīth among the other ḥadīth is like pure gold among gold.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If you were to rely upon Allah as He should be relied upon, you would be provided for as the birds are provided for: they go out in the morning hungry and return in the evening full."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The poor among the Emigrants complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about how Allah had favored their rich over them, so he said:
"O company of the poor, shall I not give you glad tidings? The poor among the believers will enter Paradise before their rich by half a day, which is five hundred years."
Then Mūsā recited this verse: {And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would spend consecutive nights hungry, and his family would find no supper; and most of their bread was barley bread.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jewish woman came to me and said, "The punishment of the grave is from urine." I said, "You have lied."
She said, "Indeed it is so; we cut away the skin and the garment because of it."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the prayer while our voices were raised, and he said, "What is this?"
So I told him what she had said, and he said, "She has spoken the truth."
After that day he never prayed a prayer except that, at the end of the prayer, he would say:
"O Lord of Jibrīl, Mīkāʾīl and Isrāfīl, protect me from the heat of the Fire and the punishment of the grave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Kaʿb
swore to him by Allah, who split the sea for Moses: "Indeed we find in the Torah that Dāwūd, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, whenever he finished his prayer, would say:

'O Allah, set right for me my religion, which You have made a safeguard for me, and set right for me my worldly life, in which You have placed my livelihood. O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your displeasure, and I seek refuge in Your pardon from Your retribution, and I seek refuge in You from You. There is none who can withhold what You have given, and none who can give what You have withheld, and the fortune of the fortunate does not benefit him against You.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he heard his father
saying at the end of the prayer:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief, poverty, and the punishment of the grave."
So I began to supplicate with them, and he said, "My son, I taught you these words." I said, "Father, I heard you supplicating with them at the end of the prayer, so I learned them from you."
He said, "Then keep to them, my son, for the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate with them at the end of the prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever glorifies Allah a hundred times after the dawn prayer and says 'there is no god but Allah' a hundred times, his sins will be forgiven, even if they were like the foam of the sea."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drink standing and sitting, pray barefoot and wearing sandals, and turn away from the prayer to his right and to his left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ [reported] that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Going out to the Friday prayer is obligatory upon every person who has reached puberty."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They mentioned the Friday bath in the presence of ʿĀʾishah, and she said: "The people used to live in the outlying district and would attend the Friday prayer while dirty. When the wind blew on them, their odors spread and the people were bothered by them. That was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said, 'Why do they not bathe?'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: On Friday the angels sit at the doors of the mosque and record the people according to their ranks. The people in it are like one who offers a camel, like one who offers a cow, like one who offers a sheep, like one who offers a chicken, like one who offers a sparrow, and like one who offers an egg."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered the sermon, he would lean against the trunk of a palm tree, one of the pillars of the mosque. When the pulpit was made and he took his place on it, that pillar shook and moaned like a she-camel until the people of the mosque heard it, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came down to it and embraced it, and it became quiet.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:

"There is no man who purifies himself on Friday as he has been commanded, then goes out from his house until he comes to the Friday prayer and listens silently until he completes his prayer, except that it will be an expiation for what is between it and the previous Friday."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he asked Ibn Shihāb about the bath
on Friday, and he said, "It is a sunnah, and Sālim ibn ʿAbdillāh has related it to me
from his father,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke about it from the pulpit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to remember Allah often, engage in idle talk little, lengthen the prayer, and shorten the sermon. He did not disdain walking with a widow or a poor person and fulfilling their need.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed two units with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while traveling, two with Abū Bakr, and two with ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in Makkah for fifteen days, praying two units at a time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She performed ʿUmrah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Madīnah to Makkah, and when she arrived in Makkah she said, "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be ransomed for you, you shortened [the prayer] and I prayed in full, you broke the fast and I fasted." He said:
"You did well, ʿĀʾishah."
And he did not find fault with me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar would not add to two units when traveling, and would pray neither before them nor after them.
It was said to him, "What is this?" He said, "This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when the sun was eclipsed. He jumped up, dragging his garment, and prayed two units until it cleared.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed at an eclipse in the porch of Zamzam four units with four prostrations.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ delivering a sermon, saying:
"No man may be alone with a woman unless a mahram of hers is with her, and a woman may not travel except with a mahram."
A man stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my wife has set out for Hajj, and I have been enrolled for such and such an expedition." He said:
"Go and perform Hajj with your wife."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The site of the mosque was an enclosed garden belonging to Banū al-Najjār, in which there were crops, date palms, and the graves of polytheists. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Name your price for it."
They said, "We seek no price for it."
So the date palms were cut down, the ground was levelled, and the graves of the polytheists were dug up. He then narrated the hadith, and said "forgive" in place of "grant victory."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I was commanded to [migrate to] a town that devours [other] towns. They call it Yathrib, and it is Madinah.
It expels people as the bellows expel the impurities of iron."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They will leave Madinah in the best condition it has ever been,
and none will come to it except the 'awāfī," meaning beasts of prey and birds. "The last to be gathered will be two shepherds from Muzaynah,
who will head for Madinah, calling out to their sheep, and will find it a wilderness.
When they reach Thaniyyat al-Wadāʿ, they will fall on their faces."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yemen will be conquered, and a people will come who urge on their animals, and they will carry off their families and those who obey them, while Madinah is better for them, if only they knew. Then Syria will be conquered, and a people will come who urge on their animals, and they will carry off their families and those who obey them, while Madinah is better for them, if only they knew. Then Iraq will be conquered, and a people will come who urge on their animals, and they will carry off their families and those who obey them, while Madinah is better for them, if only they knew."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
Then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Ibn Numayr and added in the hadith:
"No one intends evil against the people of Madinah except that Allah will dissolve him in the Fire as lead dissolves, or as salt dissolves in water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no town that the Dajjāl will not trample,
except Makkah and Madinah.
There is no pass leading into them but the angels are standing in rows upon it, guarding them.
Then Madinah will shake with its people three times,
and Allah will drive out every disbeliever and hypocrite."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Dajjāl will emerge, and a man from among the believers will head toward him. The Dajjāl's armed patrols will meet him and say to him, 'Where are you headed?' He will say, 'I am headed to this one who has emerged.' They will say to him, 'Do you not believe in our Lord?' He will say, 'There is nothing hidden about our Lord.' They will say, 'Kill him.'

Some of them will say to others, 'Has your lord not forbidden you to kill anyone without his consent?' So they will take him to the Dajjāl. When the believer sees him, he will say, 'O people, this is the Dajjāl whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned.' The Dajjāl will order that he be stretched out, and will say, 'Seize him and wound his head.'

His back and belly will be flogged severely. Then he will say to him, 'Do you not believe in me?' He will say, 'You are the false Messiah.' Then he will be ordered, and he will be sawn with a saw from the parting of his hair until his legs are split apart. Then the Dajjāl will walk between the two pieces, then say to him, 'Rise.'

He will stand up straight. Then he will say to him, 'Do you believe in me?' He will say, 'I have only increased in insight about you.' Then he will say, 'O people, he will not do this to anyone after me.' The Dajjāl will take him to slaughter him, but the area between his neck and his collarbone will be turned to copper, so he will be unable to do anything to him. Then he will seize him by his hands and feet and throw him, and people will think he has thrown him into the Fire, whereas he has in fact been thrown into Paradise."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"This man will be the greatest of people in martyrdom before the Lord of the worlds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning this verse:
"Why are you two parties concerning the hypocrites?" he said: Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned back on the day of Uhud.
The people were divided about them into two groups: one group said, "Kill them."
And another group said, "No."
So this verse was revealed:
"Why are you two parties concerning the hypocrites?" And he said:
"It is Ṭayyibah," and he said, "It expels the impure as the fire expels the impurities of iron."
label: machine translation

segments_en: O Allah, grant Madinah twice the blessing that You have granted Makkah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with disheveled hair and said, "O Messenger of Allah, tell me what prayer Allah has made obligatory upon me." He said: "The five prayers,
unless you wish to volunteer something more."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he performed ablution in his house, then went out and said, "I will surely stay close to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and be with him this whole day."
He said: So he came to the mosque and asked about the Prophet ﷺ. They said, "He went out,

in this direction." He said: So I went out following his trail, asking about him, until he entered the well of Arīs. He said: I sat at the door, and its door was made of palm branches, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had relieved himself and performed ablution. Then I stood and went to him, and there he was, sitting on the well of Arīs, in the middle of its stone platform, with his shins uncovered and dangling them into the well. He said: I greeted him with salām, then went back and sat at the door, and I said, "I will be the doorkeeper of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ today."
Then Abū Bakr came and pushed the door. I said, "Who is this?" He said, "Abū Bakr."
I said, "Wait a moment." He said: Then I went and said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is Abū Bakr asking permission to enter." He said, "
Let him in, and give him the glad tidings of Paradise."

He said: So I went forward until I said to Abū Bakr, "Enter, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gives you the glad tidings of Paradise." He said: So Abū Bakr entered and sat on the right of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with him on the platform, and dangled his legs in the well as the Prophet ﷺ had done, and uncovered his shins. Then I went back and sat down, having left my brother performing ablution so that he would join me. I said, "If Allah wills good for so-and-so"—meaning his brother—"He will bring him."
Then someone was shaking the door. I said, "Who is this?" He said, "ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb."
I said, "Wait a moment."
Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, greeted him with salām, and said, "This is ʿUmar asking permission to enter." He said, "
Let him in, and give him the glad tidings of Paradise."

So I went to ʿUmar and said, "You are permitted, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gives you the glad tidings of Paradise." He said: So he entered and sat with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the platform, on his left, and dangled his legs in the well. Then I went back and sat down and said, "If Allah wills good for so-and-so"—meaning his brother—"He will bring him." Then someone came and shook the door. I said, "Who is this?" He said, "ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān."
I said, "Wait a moment." He said: I went to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and he said, "
Let him in, and give him the glad tidings of Paradise, along with a trial that will befall him."

He said: So I went and said, "Enter, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gives you the glad tidings of Paradise, along with a trial that will befall you." He said: So he entered and found the platform already full, so he sat opposite them on the other side.
Sharīk said: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said, "I interpreted that as [referring to] their graves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that a man
asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Hour,
saying, "When is the Hour?" He said, "
What have you prepared for it?"
He said, "Nothing, except that I love Allah and His Messenger ﷺ." He said, "
You will be with those whom you love."
Anas said: We were never as happy about anything as we were about the saying of the Prophet ﷺ, "
You will be with those whom you love."
Anas said: I love the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar,
and I hope to be with them because of my love for them,
even if I have not done deeds like theirs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū ʿUthmān claimed that on some of those days in which the Prophet ﷺ fought, no one remained with him except Ṭalḥah and Saʿd. [This is] from their account.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the hand of Ṭalḥah withered; he had shielded the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with it on the day of Uḥud.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ said: No one had accepted Islam on the day that I accepted Islam, and I remained for seven days while I was a third of Islam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "I have a slave woman who is our servant and who draws water for us, and I have relations with her, but I do not want her to become pregnant." He said, "
Practice withdrawal with her if you wish, for what has been decreed for her will come to her."
The man waited, then came to him and said, "The slave woman has become pregnant." He said, "
I told you that what has been decreed for her would come to her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A wife] of the Prophet ﷺ said to ʿĀʾishah, "By Allah, I am not comfortable with a boy seeing me after he has outgrown the age of nursing."
ʿĀʾishah said, "Why? Sahlah bint Suhayl came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I see in the face of Abū Ḥudhayfah [signs of displeasure] at Sālim's coming in.'"
She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Nurse him."
She said, "But he has a beard." He said, "
Nurse him, and what is in the face of Abū Ḥudhayfah will go away."
She said, "By Allah, I never again noticed anything of it in the face of Abū Ḥudhayfah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The rest of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ refused to allow anyone to enter upon them on the basis of that nursing, meaning the nursing of an adult, and they said to ʿĀʾishah, "By Allah, we do not consider what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Sahlah bint Suhayl to do to be anything but a special concession from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for Sālim alone. By Allah, no one will enter upon us on the basis of this nursing, nor see us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
The world is but [temporary] enjoyment, and nothing in the enjoyment of the world is better than a righteous woman."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He asked,] "What is your view about a man who divorced his wife while she was menstruating?" He said: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar divorced his wife while she was menstruating in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ʿUmar asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar divorced his wife while she was menstruating." ʿAbdullāh said: He returned her to me and did not count it as anything, and he said, "
When she is pure, let him either divorce her or keep her."
Ibn ʿUmar said: The Prophet ﷺ recited, {O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them} at the beginning of their waiting period.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to Ibn ʿAbbās and said, "O Ibn ʿAbbās, do you not know that the three [pronouncements of divorce]
in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, of Abū Bakr, and in the early part of the caliphate of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, were counted as one?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
and the wording is Muḥammad's, from Ibn al-Qāsim, from Mālik,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Yazīd,
from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
from Fāṭimah bint Qays,
that Abū ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ
divorced her with a final divorce while he was away. He sent his agent to her with some barley, but she was displeased with it.
He said, "By Allah, you have no claim on us at all."
So she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said, "
You have no maintenance."
He commanded her to spend her waiting period in the house of Umm Sharīk, then said, "

That is a woman whom my Companions frequently visit. Spend your waiting period with Ibn Umm Maktūm, for he is a blind man and you can take off your clothes. When your waiting period ends, let me know."
She said: When my waiting period ended, I mentioned to him that Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān and Abū Jahm had proposed to me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
As for Abū Jahm, he never lays his staff down from his shoulder; and as for Muʿāwiyah, he is a pauper with no wealth. But marry Usāmah ibn Zayd."
I disliked him, but then he said, "
Marry Usāmah ibn Zayd."
So I married him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed good in him, and I was envied because of him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She

was married to Abū Ḥafṣ ibn al-Mughīrah, and Abū Ḥafṣ ibn al-Mughīrah divorced her with the last of three pronouncements of divorce. She claimed that she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked for his ruling about her leaving her house, and he commanded her to move to Ibn Umm Maktūm, the blind man. Marwān refused to accept the report of Fāṭimah about a divorced woman leaving her house.
ʿUrwah said: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, disapproved of what Fāṭimah bint Qays [said].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah bint Qays said, "O Messenger of Allah, I fear that someone will break in upon me."
So he commanded her to move.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Ibn ʿUmar, "[What about] a man who accuses his wife [of adultery]?"
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated the two siblings of Banū al-ʿAjlān and said, "
Allah knows that one of you is lying.
Is either of you willing to repent?"
He repeated it three times, but they refused, so he separated them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people from ʿUkl and ʿUraynah came to the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah and professed Islam. They said, "O Prophet of Allah, we are people of livestock [and milk],
and we are not people of farmland." And they found Madinah unhealthy for them,
so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that they be given some camels and a herdsman,
and he ordered them to go out with them,
and to drink their milk and their urine.
They set out, and when they reached the area of al-Ḥarrah, they disbelieved after having embraced Islam,
and they killed the Prophet's ﷺ herdsman and drove off the camels.
The news reached the Prophet ﷺ, so he sent a search party after them, and he gave orders concerning them: their eyes were branded with heated nails, and their hands were cut off,
and they were left in the area of al-Ḥarrah until they died in that condition.
Qatādah said: It has reached us that after that the Prophet ﷺ used to urge charity (ṣadaqah),
and forbid mutilation.
Shuʿbah, Abān and Ḥammād reported from Qatādah that they were from ʿUraynah.
And Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr and Ayyūb reported from Abū Qilābah, from Anas: A group from ʿUkl came
label: machine translation

segments_en: By Allah, I certainly know who used to wash the wound of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who used to pour the water, and with what it was treated. He said: Fāṭimah, may peace be upon her, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, used to wash it, and ʿAlī used to pour the water from a shield.
When Fāṭimah saw that the water only made the bleeding greater, she took a piece of a woven mat,
burned it, and pressed it onto the wound, and the bleeding stopped.
On that day his front tooth was broken, his face was wounded,
and the helmet was smashed on his head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When you go to your bed, perform ablution as you would for prayer, then lie down on your right side and say: O Allah, I have submitted my face to You, entrusted my affair to You, and turned my back to You, out of fear of You and longing for You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You. I believe in Your Book which You have revealed and in Your Prophet whom You have sent.
If you die during your night, you will die upon the natural disposition (fiṭrah)."
He said: I repeated them in order to memorize them, and I said, "I believe in Your Messenger whom You have sent," and he said:
"Say: I believe in Your Prophet whom You have sent."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
It has been narrated through more than one route from al-Barāʾ, and we do not know of any narration that mentions ablution except in this hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to bathe from a large vessel, which is the faraq, and I used to bathe together with him from a single vessel.
In the narration of Sufyān: from one vessel.
Qutaybah said that Sufyān said: The faraq is three ṣāʿs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ and one of his wives used to bathe from a single vessel.
Muslim and Wahb added, from Shuʿbah: from ritual impurity (janābah).
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bathed after ritual impurity (janābah), he would call for something like a ḥilāb [vessel], take [water] in his hand, begin with the right side of his head, then the left, then take [water] with both hands and pour it over his head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The prayer was called, and the people had formed their rows. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out, and when he stood in his place, he remembered that he had not bathed, so he said to the people, "Stay in your places."
Then he returned to his house and came out to us with his head dripping, having bathed, while we were [still] in rows.
This is the wording of Ibn Ḥarb. ʿAyyāsh said in his narration: We remained standing, waiting for him, until he came out to us having bathed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ met him on one of the roads of Madinah while he was in a state of ritual impurity (janābah), so he slipped away and went and bathed. The Prophet ﷺ missed him, and when he came, he said:
"Where were you, Abū Hurayrah?"
He said: O Messenger of Allah, you met me while I was in a state of ritual impurity, and I disliked sitting with you until I had bathed.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Glory be to Allah! The believer does not become impure."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to rest his head in my lap while I was menstruating, and he would recite the Qurʾān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. When they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, face our qiblah, eat our slaughtered animals, and pray our prayer, then their blood and their wealth are forbidden to us, except by its right. They have what the Muslims have, and they owe what the Muslims owe."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was sitting with a group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and we mentioned the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ. Abū Ḥumayd as-Sāʿidī said: "I am the one among you who remembers best the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I saw him, when he said the takbīr, raise his hands level with his shoulders;
and when he bowed, he set his hands firmly on his knees,
then he straightened his back;
and when he raised his head, he stood upright until every vertebra returned to its place;
and when he prostrated, he placed his hands neither spread out nor clasped together,
and he turned the tips of the toes of his feet toward the qiblah;
when he sat after the two units of prayer, he sat on his left foot and set the right one upright;
and when he sat in the last unit, he brought his left foot forward, set the other upright, and sat on his seat."
Al-Layth heard from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, and Yazīd from Muḥammad ibn Ḥalḥalah, and Ibn Ḥalḥalah from Ibn ʿAṭāʾ.
Abū Ṣāliḥ said, from al-Layth: "every vertebra."
Ibn al-Mubārak said, from Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb: Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb told me that Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to him: "every vertebra."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, and we gave the salām when he gave the salām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ finished a prayer, he would turn his face toward us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar used to pray [voluntary prayer] in the same place where he had prayed the obligatory prayer, and al-Qāsim did the same.
It is mentioned from Abū Hurayrah, attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ: "The imam should not pray voluntary prayer in his place." But this is not authentic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ delayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer until late in the night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṭāwus said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: They claim that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Wash yourselves on Friday and wash your heads, even if you are not in a state of janābah,
and apply perfume."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: "As for washing, yes;
but as for perfume, I do not know."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr came in to the Prophet ﷺ while I was supporting him against my chest,
and ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān had a fresh siwāk with which he was cleaning his teeth.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fixed his gaze on it,
so I took the siwāk, chewed it, shook it out, and softened it,
then I handed it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he cleaned his teeth with it.
I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ clean his teeth better than that.
Hardly had the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished when he raised his hand or his finger and then said:
"In the Highest Companionship."
[He said it] three times, and then he passed away.
And she used to say: "He died between my chest and my throat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"We are the last, yet the foremost on the Day of Resurrection.
They were given the Book before us,
and we were given it after them.
This is the day about which they differed, and Allah guided us to it.
So tomorrow is for the Jews, and the day after tomorrow is for the Christians." Then he fell silent. Then he said:
"It is a duty upon every Muslim to bathe once every seven days, washing his head and his body on that day." Then he said:
"It is a duty upon every Muslim to bathe once every seven days, washing his head and his body on that day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A wife of ʿUmar used to attend the dawn prayer and the night prayer in congregation at the mosque.

It was said to her: "Why do you go out when you know that ʿUmar dislikes that and is jealous?" She said: "And what prevents him from forbidding me?" He said: "What prevents him is the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
'Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to pray the Friday prayer with the Prophet ﷺ, and then there would be the midday nap.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While he was sitting on the pulpit,
the muʾadhdhin gave the call to prayer and said: "Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar."
Muʿāwiyah said: "Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar."
[The muʾadhdhin] said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah."
Muʿāwiyah said: "And I."
[The muʾadhdhin] said: "I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah."
Muʿāwiyah said: "And I."
When the call to prayer was completed, he said: "O people, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in this very place, when the muʾadhdhin gave the call, say what you have heard me say."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a palm trunk that the Prophet ﷺ would stand beside [to deliver the sermon]. When the pulpit was made for him, we heard the trunk make a sound like that of pregnant she-camels, until the Prophet ﷺ came down and placed his hand on it.
Sulaymān said, from Yaḥyā: Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUbaydillāh ibn Anas informed me that he heard Jābir.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun set while I was with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, and we kept travelling. When we saw that evening had come, we said, "Prayer!"

He kept travelling until the twilight had faded and the stars had come out. Then he dismounted and prayed the two prayers together. Then he said, "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when the journey pressed on him, pray this prayer of mine," meaning he combined the two after nightfall.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never combined the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers while travelling, except once.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Between them is ten miles, meaning between Makkah and Sarif.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ travelled and wished to pray voluntarily, he would face the qiblah with his camel, say the takbīr, and then pray in whatever direction his mount faced.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, "Was permission given to women to pray on their mounts?" She said, "No permission was given to them in that, whether in hardship or in ease."
Muḥammad said: This refers to the obligatory prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went on a military expedition with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and witnessed the conquest of Makkah with him. He stayed in Makkah for eighteen nights, praying only two rakʿahs, and he would say:
"People of the city, pray four, for we are travellers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in Makkah for seventeen days, shortening the prayer.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Whoever stays seventeen days shortens the prayer, and whoever stays longer completes it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿAlī,

may Allah be pleased with him, when he travelled, would continue after the sun had set until it was nearly dark. Then he would dismount and pray Maghrib, then call for his supper and eat it, then pray ʿIshāʾ, then set out again. He would say, "This is what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do."

ʿUthmān said, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī: I heard Abū Dāwūd say: Usāmah ibn Zayd reported from Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUbaydillāh, meaning the son of Anas ibn Mālik, that Anas would combine the two prayers when the twilight disappeared, and he would say, "The Prophet ﷺ used to do this." And the narration of az-Zuhrī from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, is similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in Tabūk for twenty days, shortening the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The fear prayer is that the imam stands with one group of his Companions while another group faces the enemy. The imam bows one rakʿah and prostrates with those who are with him, then stands. When he is standing upright, he remains standing while they complete the remaining rakʿah for themselves, then give the salām and leave, while the imam remains standing. They then take position facing the enemy. Then the others, who have not prayed, come and say the takbīr behind the imam. He bows and prostrates with them, then gives the salām. They then stand and bow for themselves the remaining rakʿah, then give the salām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ towards Najd until, when we were at Dhāt ar-Riqāʿ in Nakhl, he met a gathering of Ghaṭafān. Then he mentioned the same meaning, with wording different from the wording of Ḥaywah, and said in it: when he had bowed and prostrated with those who were with him, he said, "When they stood, they walked backwards to the places of their companions' rows." And he did not mention turning their backs to the qiblah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the takbīr, and the group who had lined up with him said the takbīr. Then he bowed and they bowed, then he prostrated and they prostrated, then he rose and they rose. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained sitting, and they prostrated the second time by themselves. Then they stood and withdrew on their heels, walking backwards, until they stood behind them. The other group came and stood, said the takbīr, then bowed for themselves. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated and they prostrated with him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, and they prostrated the second time for themselves. Then both groups stood together and prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He bowed and they bowed, then he prostrated and they all prostrated. Then he returned and prostrated the second time, and they prostrated with him quickly, as fast as one can possibly hurry, sparing no effort in speed. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the salām and they gave the salām. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose, and the people had shared with him in the whole of the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the fear prayer. They stood in two rows: one row behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and one row facing the enemy. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed one rakʿah with them. Then the others came and took their place, while the first group turned to face the enemy. The Prophet ﷺ prayed one rakʿah with them, then gave the salām. Then this group stood and prayed one rakʿah for themselves, then gave the salām, then went and took the place of the others facing the enemy, while the others returned to their place. They prayed one rakʿah for themselves, then gave the salām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ṭālib set out for Syria, and the Prophet ﷺ went out with him among some elders of Quraysh. When they came in sight of the monk, they dismounted and unloaded their saddles. The monk came out to them, though before this they used to pass by him and he would neither come out to them nor pay them any attention.

He said: While they were unloading their saddles, the monk began moving among them until he came and took the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "This is the master of all the worlds. This is the Messenger of the Lord of all the worlds. Allah will send him as a mercy to all the worlds."

The elders of Quraysh said to him, "How do you know this?" He said, "When you came in sight from the mountain pass, there was no tree or stone that did not fall down in prostration, and they prostrate only for a prophet. And I recognize him by the seal of prophethood below the cartilage of his shoulder, like an apple."

Then he returned and prepared food for them. When he brought it to them, [the Prophet ﷺ] was out tending the camels. He said, "Send for him." So he came, with a cloud shading him. When he drew near the people, he found that they had beaten him to the shade of the tree. When he sat down, the shade of the tree inclined over him. He said, "Look at the shade of the tree, how it has inclined over him."

He said: While the monk was standing over them, urging them not to take him to the Romans, because if the Romans saw him they would recognize him by his description and kill him, he turned and there were seven men who had come from the Romans. He went to meet them and said, "What brings you here?" They said, "We have come because this Prophet is about to emerge during this month, and no road was left without people being sent to it. We were informed of news about him, so we were sent to this road of yours." He said, "Is there anyone behind you who is better than you?" They said, "We were only told of his news on this road of yours."
He said, "Do you see a matter that Allah intends to carry out, can anyone among the people turn it back?" They said, "No."

He said: So they pledged allegiance to him and stayed with him. He said, "I ask you by Allah, which of you is his guardian?" They said, "Abū Ṭālib." He kept appealing to him until Abū Ṭālib sent him back, and Abū Bakr sent Bilāl with him, and the monk provisioned him with cake and olive oil.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, taking turns eating from one large bowl from morning until night: ten would stand up and ten would sit down.
We said, "What was it that made it replenished?" He said, "What do you find surprising? It was replenished only from here," and he pointed with his hand to the sky.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah, and we went out to some of its outskirts. Every mountain and tree that faced him said, "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah."
He said: This is a gharīb hadith.
More than one person narrated it from al-Walīd ibn Abī Thawr, and they said it was from ʿAbbād Abū Yazīd, among them Farwah ibn Abī al-Maghrāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "By what can I know that you are a prophet?" He said,
"If I call this cluster of dates from this palm tree, will you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?"
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called it, and it began to come down from the palm tree until it fell before the Prophet ﷺ. Then he said, "Go back."
So it went back, and the Bedouin accepted Islam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiped his hand over my face and made supplication for me. ʿAzrah said: He lived one hundred and twenty years, and there was nothing on his head but a few white hairs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was begun in prophethood, when Allah wished to honor him and show mercy to His servants through him, was that he would see nothing but that it came true like the breaking of dawn. He remained like that for as long as Allah willed, and solitude was made beloved to him; nothing was dearer to him than to be alone.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was neither tall nor short. He had thick hands and feet, a large head, and large joints, and a long line of hair from the chest to the navel. When he walked, he leaned forward as if descending a slope. I never saw anyone like him, before or after.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the Time of Ignorance I saw a female monkey who had committed adultery, and a group of monkeys gathered around her,
and they stoned her, and I stoned her along with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are traits from the traits of the Time of Ignorance: slandering lineages and wailing over the dead. And he forgot the third.
Sufyān said: They say that it is seeking rain through the stars.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the mosque of Kūfah he said: By Allah, I saw myself bound by ʿUmar to Islam before ʿUmar became Muslim,
and if Uhud were to crumble because of what you did to ʿUthmān, it would be right for it to crumble.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While he was in his house, afraid,
al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil as-Sahmī, Abū ʿAmr, came to him,
wearing a robe of striped Yemeni cloth
and a shirt trimmed with silk.
He was from Banū Sahm, who were our allies in the Time of Ignorance. He said to him: What is the matter with you? He said: Your people claim they will kill me if I accept Islam.
He said: There is no way to you.
After he said it, I felt safe. Then al-ʿĀṣ went out
and met the people, with the valley flooded by them. He said: Where are you headed? They said: We want this son of al-Khaṭṭāb who has abandoned his religion.
He said: There is no way to him.
So the people turned back.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: When ʿUmar accepted Islam, the people gathered at his house and said: ʿUmar has abandoned his religion.
I was a boy then, on top of my house,
and a man came wearing a silk brocade cloak and said: ʿUmar has abandoned his religion.
He said: No matter, for I am his protector.
He said: Then I saw the people disperse from him. I said: Who is this? They said: al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The moon was split.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came from the land of Abyssinia while I was a young girl,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ clothed me in a patterned wool garment,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began wiping the patterns with his hand and saying: "Sanāh, sanāh."
al-Ḥumaydī said: That means: beautiful, beautiful.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Then we met Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib,
and we stayed with him until we arrived,
and we met the Prophet ﷺ when he conquered Khaybar. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"You, people of the ship, have two migrations."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, in the expedition of Tabūk, at length.
Ibn Bukayr said in his narration: I was present with the Prophet ﷺ on the night of al-ʿAqabah when we pledged ourselves to Islam,
and I would not wish to have been present at Badr in its place, even though Badr is more mentioned among the people.
It is remembered more among the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr used to say: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh say: My two maternal uncles were present with me at al-ʿAqabah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAṭāʾ said: Jābir said: I, my father, and my maternal uncle
were among the people of al-ʿAqabah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I visited ʿĀʾishah with ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr al-Laythī, and we asked her about the migration.
She said: There is no migration today.
A believer used to flee with his religion to Allah, the Exalted, and to His Messenger ﷺ, fearing he would be persecuted for it.
But today Allah has made Islam manifest,
and today a person worships his Lord wherever he wishes,
but there is jihad and intention.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We met Anas ibn Mālik when he came to Syria; we met him at ʿAyn al-Tamr. I saw him praying on a donkey, with his face turned toward that side—Hammām gestured to the left of the qiblah—so I said to him, "I saw you praying facing other than the qiblah."
He said, "Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do it, I would not have done it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I fell ill with a sickness, and Ibn ʿUmar came to visit me. He said: I asked him about the voluntary prayer

while traveling. He said, "I accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on journeys and I never saw him offer voluntary prayers. Had I been one to offer them, I would have completed the prayer. And Allah the Exalted has said: 'There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell ill and did not rise for the night prayer for two or three nights. A woman came to him and said, "O Muhammad, I hope that your devil has left you; I have not seen him near you for two or three nights." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: 'By the morning brightness, and by the night when it grows still, your Lord has not abandoned you, nor has He detested you.'
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was asked about the fasting of the Prophet

ﷺ. He said: He would fast during a month until we thought he did not intend to break the fast in it, and he would go without fasting until we thought he did not intend to fast any of it. And you would not wish to see him praying at night except that you would see him praying, nor sleeping except that you would see him sleeping.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Bilāl at the dawn prayer:
"O Bilāl, tell me of the deed you have done in Islam in which you have the most hope of benefit, for I heard last night the sound of your sandals before me in Paradise."

Bilāl said, "I have not done any deed in Islam in which I have more hope of benefit than this: I never perform purification completely at any hour of the night or day except that I pray with that purification as much as Allah has decreed for me to pray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer,
then he prayed eight rakʿahs standing,
and two rakʿahs between the two calls to prayer, and he never abandoned them.
Jaʿfar ibn Musāfir said in his narration:
and two rakʿahs sitting between the two calls to prayer. He added: sitting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ prayed the two rakʿahs of Fajr, he would lie down on his right side.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Pray two rakʿahs before Maghrib." Then he said:
"Pray two rakʿahs before Maghrib, for whoever wishes."
[He said this] fearing that people would take it as a established sunnah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Juray was worshipping in a hermitage when his mother came.

Humayd said: Abū Rāfiʿ described to us how Abū Hurayrah described, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had described, the mother when she called him: how she placed her palm above her eyebrows, then raised her head toward him calling him, and said, "O Juray, I am your mother, speak to me."
She found him praying, and he said, "O Allah, my mother and my prayer!"
He chose his prayer, so she went back. Then she returned a second time and said, "O Juray, I am your mother, speak to me."
He said, "O Allah, my mother and my prayer!"
He chose his prayer, so she said, "O Allah, this is Juray, and he is my son. I spoke to him and he refused to speak to me. O Allah, do not let him die until You show him the prostitutes."
He said: Had she prayed against him that he be put to trial, he would have been put to trial.

He said: There was a shepherd of sheep who took shelter at his monastery. He said: A woman from the village came out and the shepherd had relations with her; she became pregnant and bore a boy. It was said to her, "What is this?" She said, "From the man of this monastery."

He said: They came with their axes and spades and called out to him, and found him praying, and he did not speak to them. He said: They began to demolish his monastery. When he saw that, he came down to them. They said to him, "Ask this woman." He said: He smiled, then wiped the head of the boy and said, "Who is your father?" He said, "My father is the shepherd of sheep."
When they heard that from him, they said, "We will rebuild what we demolished of your monastery with gold and silver."
He said, "No, but restore it as dust as it was." Then he climbed up.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he prayed a prayer, then said:
"Satan appeared before me,
and rushed at me to cut off my prayer,
but Allah gave me power over him, and I choked him.

I had even intended to tie him to a pillar until morning so that you could all look at him, but I remembered the saying of Solomon, peace be upon him: 'My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone after me.'
So Allah sent him back humiliated."
Then al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: "fa-dhaʿtuhu" with dhāl means I choked him, whereas "fadaʿtuhu" is from the saying of Allah, 'the Day they will be driven' meaning pushed away. The correct form is
"fadaʿtuhu", except that he said it thus, with emphasis on the ʿayn and the tāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Saying subḥān Allāh is for men,"
meaning during the prayer,
"and clapping is for women. Whoever makes a gesture in his prayer that can be understood from him, let him repeat it." He meant the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ said: The sun was eclipsed during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the mosque, stood, and said the takbīr, and the people lined up behind him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited at length, then said the takbīr and bowed for a long time. Then he raised his head and said:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him; our Lord, and to You belongs all praise."
Then he stood and recited at length, but less than the first recitation. Then he said the takbīr and bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he said:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him; our Lord, and to You belongs all praise."

Then he prostrated (Abū al-Ṭāhir did not mention "then he prostrated"). Then he did the same in the other rakʿah, until he completed four rakʿahs and four prostrations, and the sun cleared before he finished. Then he stood and addressed the people, praising Allah as He deserves. Then he said:
"The sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah. They are not eclipsed for the death of anyone, nor for his life. So when you see them, hasten to prayer." He also said:
"Pray until Allah relieves you."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"In this place of mine I saw everything that you have been promised, until I saw myself wanting to take a bunch of fruit from Paradise when you saw me move forward" (al-Murādī said: "step forward"). "And I saw Hell, parts of it smashing into other parts, when you saw me step back. And I saw in it Ibn Luḥayy, who was the one who introduced the practice of setting animals free [for idols]."
The narration of Abū al-Ṭāhir ended at his words: "hasten to prayer."
He did not mention what comes after it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He is not one of us who strikes the cheeks, tears the garments, or calls with the calls of the Jāhiliyyah."
This is the narration of Yaḥyā. As for Ibn Numayr and Abū Bakr, they said "and tears" and "and calls" without the "or."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb, and Ibn
Numayr, they said: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father,
from ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you see a funeral procession, stand for it until it passes you or is set down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah,
may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: I used to perfume the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for his ihrām before he entered ihrām, and for his release from it before he circumambulated the House.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from Sālim,
ibn ʿAbd Allāh, that he heard his father,

may Allah be pleased with him, say: This desert of yours, about which you lie against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not begin the talbiyah except from beside the mosque, meaning Dhū al-Ḥulayfah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had cupping done on his head while in ihrām, because of a pain he had, at a water called Laḥy Jamal.
Muḥammad ibn Sawāʾ said: Hishām informed us, from ʿIkrimah,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had cupping done on his head while in ihrām, because of a migraine he had.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Numayr and Isḥāq al-Ḥanẓalī, both from Ibn ʿUyaynah,
Ibn Numayr said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us,
from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār,
from Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ, that Ibn
ʿAbbās informed him that the Prophet ﷺ married Maymūnah while in ihrām.
Ibn Numayr added: I related it to al-Zuhrī, and he said: Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm informed me that he married her when he was out of ihrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to observe iʿtikāf in the last ten days of Ramadan.
Nāfiʿ said: ʿAbd Allāh, may Allah be pleased with him, showed me the place in the mosque where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to observe iʿtikāf.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a man
from the Ansār came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a man who finds another man with his wife:
should he kill him, or what should he do?" So Allah revealed concerning him what is mentioned in the Qur'an about the matter of those who invoke curses (li'ān). The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Allah has decided concerning you and your wife."
He said: So they carried out the mutual invocation of curses in the mosque, while I was present.
When they had finished, he said, "I would have lied about her, O Messenger of Allah, if I were to keep her."
So he divorced her three times before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him, when they had finished the mutual cursing,
and he separated from her in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, who said,
"That is a separation between every couple who have invoked curses."
Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Shihāb said: The established practice after the two of them was that those who invoke curses are separated. She was pregnant,
and her son was called by his mother's name.
He said: Then the practice continued regarding her inheritance, that she inherits from him and he inherits from her what Allah has prescribed for him.
Ibn Jurayj said, from Ibn Shihāb, from Sahl ibn Saʿd as-Sāʿidī, in this hadith, that the Prophet ﷺ said,
"If she brings him forth reddish and short, like a wahrah (a small lizard),
then I think she has told the truth and he has lied about her.
But if she brings him forth dark, with large eyes and large buttocks,
then I think he has told the truth about her."
And she brought him forth in the form that was disliked of those.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ
label: machine translation

segments_en: What is wrong with Fāṭimah? Does she not fear Allah,
meaning in her saying that there is neither lodging nor maintenance [for a divorced woman]?
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah
denied that [claim] of Fāṭimah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade
"and she must not touch perfume, except a little when she becomes pure from her menses,
a small piece of qusṭ and aẓfār (types of incense)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Maʿmar said to me: Ath-Thawrī said to me, "Have you heard anything about a man who gathers for his family their provision for a year, or part of a year?" Maʿmar said: Nothing came to my mind at the time,
then I remembered a hadith that Ibn Shihāb az-Zuhrī narrated to us, from Mālik ibn Aws, from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: that the Prophet ﷺ used to sell the date palms of Banū an-Naḍīr,
and he would set aside for his family their provision for a year.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was afflicted with severe hardship, and I met ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb,
and asked him to recite to me a verse from the Book of Allah.
He entered his house and explained it to me,
and I walked a short distance,
then I fell on my face from hardship and hunger, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing over my head. He said,
"O Abū Hurayrah."
I said, "At your service, O Messenger of Allah, and at your pleasure."
He took my hand and made me stand up,
and he knew what was wrong with me,
and he took me to his dwelling,
and ordered a large cup of milk for me, and I drank from it. Then he said,
"Return, O Abū Hirr." So I returned and drank. Then he said, "Return."

So I returned and drank until my belly was full and became like an arrow-shaft. He said: Then I met ʿUmar and told him what had happened to me, and I said to him, "Allah put this in the charge of one more deserving of it than you, O ʿUmar.
By Allah, I asked you to recite the verse to me when I knew it better than you."
ʿUmar said, "By Allah, that I had let you in is dearer to me than having red camels."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Food was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and with him was his stepson ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah. He said, "Say the name of Allah,
and eat from what is in front of you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of Syria used to taunt Ibn az-Zubayr, saying, "O son of the woman of the two waist-belts!"
Asmāʾ said to him, "My son, they taunt you about the two waist-belts.
Do you know what the two waist-belts were? It was my waist-belt that I split in two,
and with one half I tied the waterskin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
and I put the other in his food bag."
He said: So whenever the people of Syria taunted him about the two waist-belts, he would say, "Yes, by God!
That is a reproach whose shame is far removed from you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"I do not eat while reclining."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to a man who was with him,
"I do not eat while I am reclining."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was a guest of Abū Hurayrah for seven days,
and he, his wife, and his servant would divide the night into three parts in turns: this one would pray,
then he would wake the next.
And I heard him say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ distributed dates among his Companions,
and I received seven dates, one of which was a dry, hard date.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw myself as the seventh of seven with the Prophet ﷺ; we had no food except leaves of the ḥublah tree (or the ḥublah), until one of us would pass dung like that of a sheep,
then the Banū Asad began to rebuke me over Islam,
then I would be a loser, and my effort would have been in vain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved sweets and honey. After performing the ʿAṣr prayer, he would go around to his wives and draw near to them. He went in to Ḥafṣah and stayed with her longer than he usually stayed, so I asked about it, and I was told: "A woman of her people gave her a skin of honey as a gift, and she gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a drink of it." I said: "By Allah, we will devise a plan against him."
So I mentioned that to Sawdah and said: "When he enters upon you, he will come close to you. Say to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, have you eaten maghāfīr?' He will say to you: 'No.'
Then say to him: 'What is this smell?' — and it was very hard on the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a smell to be found on him — and he will say to you: 'Ḥafṣah gave me a drink of honey.'

Then say to him: 'Its bees must have fed on ʿurfuṭ.' I will say that to him as well, and you say it too, O Ṣafiyyah." When he entered upon Sawdah, she said: "By the One besides Whom there is no god, I was about to say to him what you told me while he was still at the door, out of fear of you." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew near, she said: "O Messenger of Allah, have you eaten maghāfīr?" He said: "No."
She said: "Then what is this smell?" He said:
"Ḥafṣah gave me a drink of honey."
She said: "Its bees must have fed on ʿurfuṭ."

When he entered upon me, I said the same to him. Then he entered upon Ṣafiyyah, and she said the same. When he entered upon Ḥafṣah, she said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I not give you some of it to drink?" He said:
"I have no need of it."
She said: Sawdah said: "Glory be to Allah! By Allah, we have deprived him of it."
She said: I said to her: "Be quiet."
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ. [Another chain:] And Muḥammad ibn Rāfiʿ narrated to me,
and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd,
ʿAbd said: "He informed us," and Ibn Rāfiʿ said:
"ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī,
from Ibn al-Musayyib,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no faraʿ and no ʿatīrah."
Ibn Rāfiʿ added in his narration: The faraʿ was the first offspring of a livestock animal, which they would slaughter [as an offering].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ went in to a man of the Anṣār, who had a companion with him,
and the Prophet ﷺ and his companion greeted him with salām.
The man returned the greeting and said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom,
and it was a hot hour,
and he was channeling water in a garden of his," and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"If you have water that has spent the night in a waterskin, [give it to us]; otherwise we will drink directly [from the channel]."
The man was channeling water in the garden, and the man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have water that has spent the night in a waterskin."
So he went to the shelter and poured water into a cup,
then milked some of his tame goat's milk onto it,
and the Prophet ﷺ drank, then he handed it back,
and the man who had come with him drank.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We entered upon Khabbāb to visit him while he had been cauterized seven times. He said: "Our companions who passed on have gone, and the world did not diminish [their reward]. But we have obtained so much that we find no place for it except the soil. And had the Prophet ﷺ not forbidden us to pray for death, I would have prayed for it."
Then we came to him another time while he was building a wall of his, and he said: "Indeed, a Muslim is rewarded for everything he spends, except for what he puts into this soil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: No one will enter Paradise by his deeds alone."
They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I,
unless Allah envelops me in His favor and mercy. So be upright and strive for what is near to it, and let none of you wish for death. If he is a doer of good, perhaps he will increase in goodness,
and if he is an evildoer, perhaps he will seek to make amends."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from ʿAbd Allāh ibn
ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah, that ʿUmar
set out for Syria, and when he came to Sargh, news reached him that a plague had broken out in Syria.
Then ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you hear of it in a land, do not go to it.
And when it breaks out in a land while you are in it, do not leave to flee from it."
So ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb turned back from Sargh.
And from Ibn Shihāb, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh: ʿUmar turned the people back only because of the hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ heard a man praising another man and exaggerating in his praise, so he said:
"You have destroyed him," or, "You have broken the man's back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ presented me [for military service] on the day of Uhud, when I was fourteen years old, and he did not permit me. Then he presented me on the day of the Trench, when I was fifteen years old, and he permitted me.
Nāfiʿ said: I came to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who was caliph at that time, and told him this hadith. He said, "This is indeed the boundary between the young and the adult."
So he wrote to his governors to assign a stipend to whoever was fifteen years old, and to count whoever was younger than that among the dependents.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with them. He said: When the Prophet ﷺ died, some money came to Abū Bakr from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī,
and Abū Bakr said: Whoever is owed a debt by the Prophet ﷺ,
or was promised something by him, let him come to us.
Jābir said: I said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ promised me that he would give me like this, and like this, and like this,"
and he spread out his hands three times.
Jābir said: He counted out five hundred into my hand, then five hundred, then five hundred.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ, "If only you would go to ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy."
So the Prophet ﷺ went to him, riding a donkey,
and the Muslims went walking with him,
over land that was salty and barren.
When the Prophet ﷺ came to him, he said, "Keep away from me,
for by Allah, the stench of your donkey has harmed me."
A man from the Anṣār among them said, "By Allah, the donkey of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smells better than you."
A man from ʿAbdullāh's people became angry on his behalf, and the two men insulted each other,
and the companions of each of them became angry for him,
and there was fighting between them with palm branches, hands, and sandals.
It reached us that this verse was revealed: {And if two groups of the believers fight each other, make peace between them.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made peace with the people of al-Ḥudaybiyah, ʿAlī wrote a document between them. He wrote: "Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah."
The polytheists said, "Do not write 'Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah',
for if you were a messenger we would not have fought you." So he said to ʿAlī, "Erase it."
ʿAlī said, "I am not the one who will erase it."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ erased it with his own hand,
and he made peace with them on the condition that he and his companions would enter for three days,
and that they would not enter it except with the julubbān of weapons.
They asked him, "What is the julubbān of weapons?" He said, "The sheath with what is in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard the loud voices of two disputants at the door,
and one of them was asking the other to reduce his debt
and to be lenient with him in something, while the other said, "By Allah, I will not do it."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to them and said:
"Where is the one who swears by Allah that he will not do a good deed?"
He said, "I am he, O Messenger of Allah,
and he may have whichever of the two he prefers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Abū Hurayrah reported] from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, mentioning several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Every joint of the people must give charity each day the sun rises. Judging justly between two people is charity. Helping a man with his mount, lifting him onto it or lifting his belongings onto it, is charity. A good word is charity. Every step you take to prayer is charity. And removing harmful things from the road is charity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father died leaving a debt,
so I offered his creditors to take dates for what he owed,
but they refused, not thinking that it would cover it.
So I went to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said:
"When you have harvested it and placed it in the drying place, let the Messenger of Allah ﷺ know."
So he came, with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, and sat on it,
and prayed for blessing, then said, "Call your creditors and pay them in full."
I did not leave anyone to whom my father owed a debt except that I paid him,
and there remained thirteen wasqs, seven of ʿajwah
and six of lawn, or six of ʿajwah and seven of lawn.
Then I met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the Maghrib prayer and told him that, and he laughed and said:
"Go to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar and tell them."
They said, "We knew, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did what he did, that this would happen."
Hishām said, from Wahb, from Jābir: [it was] the ʿAṣr prayer.
He did not mention Abū Bakr, nor the laughing,
and he said: My father left a debt of thirty wasqs.
And Ibn Isḥāq said, from Wahb, from Jābir: [it was] the Ẓuhr prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should eat with his left hand, nor drink with it, for the Devil eats with his left hand and drinks with it."
He said: Nāfiʿ would add to it:
"and he should not take with it, nor give with it."
And in the narration of Abū al-Ṭāhir:
"None of you should eat"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Letting [the garment] hang down below the ankles applies to the lower garment, the shirt and the turban. Whoever drags anything out of arrogance, Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection."
Abū Bakr said: How strange it is!
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever kills a gecko with the first strike will have such and such a number of good deeds; whoever kills it with the second strike will have such and such a number of good deeds, fewer than the first; and if he kills it with the third strike, he will have such and such a number of good deeds, fewer than the second."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah bint Ṭalḥah, from ʿĀʾishah, the Mother of the Believers,
