said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was called to the funeral of a boy from the Ansar. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, glad tidings for this one, a sparrow from the sparrows of Paradise, who did no evil and did not reach it." He said:

"Or is it otherwise, O ʿĀʾishah? Allah created for Paradise its people, creating them for it while they were still in the loins of their fathers, and He created for the Fire its people, creating them for it while they were still in the loins of their fathers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward equal to the rewards of those who follow him, without that diminishing their rewards in the slightest. And whoever calls to misguidance will bear sin equal to the sins of those who follow him, without that diminishing their sins in the slightest."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ṣāliḥ used to instruct us, when one of us wished to sleep, to lie down on his right side and then say:

"O Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and the Lord of everything, Splitter of the grain and the date-stone, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Criterion, I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything whose forelock You hold. O Allah, You are the First, so there is nothing before You; You are the Last, so there is nothing after You; You are the Manifest, so there is nothing above You; and You are the Hidden, so there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debts for us and enrich us against poverty."
And he would narrate that from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he
asked ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ: What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ most often supplicate with before his death? She said: The supplication he made most often was:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done and from the evil of what I have not done."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah gathered the earth together for me." Or he said:

"My Lord gathered the earth together for me, and I saw its easts and its wests. The dominion of my Ummah will reach as far as was gathered together for me, and I was given the two treasures, the red and the white. I asked my Lord for my Ummah that He not destroy it with a general famine, and that He not set over them an enemy from outside themselves who would violate their sanctuary. My Lord said to me: O Muhammad, when I decree a decree it is not revoked. I will not destroy them with a general famine, and I will not set over them an enemy from outside themselves who would violate their sanctuary, even if those from all its regions, or he said from its regions, gather against them, until some of them destroy others and some of them take others captive. What I fear for my Ummah are misleading leaders. When the sword is placed among my Ummah, it will not be lifted from it until the Day of Resurrection. The Hour will not come until tribes of my Ummah join the polytheists and until tribes of my Ummah worship idols. There will be among my Ummah thirty liars, each claiming to be a prophet, but I am the Seal of the Prophets; there is no prophet after me. A group of my Ummah will not cease to adhere to the truth."
Ibn ʿĪsā said: "prevailing." Then both agreed:
"Those who oppose them will not harm them until the command of Allah comes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting talking in the shade of a room belonging to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we mentioned the Hour, and our voices rose. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Hour will not come, or will not be established, until ten signs come before it: the sun rising from its place of setting, the emergence of the Beast, the emergence of Gog and Magog, the Dajjāl, ʿĪsā son of Maryam, the smoke, and three landslides: a landslide in the west, a landslide in the east, and a landslide in the Arabian Peninsula. The last of that will be a fire coming out of Yemen, from the depths of Aden, driving the people to the place of gathering."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "This man killed my brother." He said,
"Go and kill him as he killed your brother."
The man said to him, "Fear Allah and pardon me, for that is greater for your reward and better for you and for your brother on the Day of Resurrection."
So he let him go. Then the Prophet ﷺ was informed, so he asked him, and he told him what he had said to him. He said, and he rebuked him:
"Indeed, that was better than what he would have done to you on the Day of Resurrection. He would say: My Lord, ask this one why he killed me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled retaliation for a tooth, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Book of Allah prescribes retaliation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever castrates his slave, we will castrate him, and whoever cuts off his slave's nose, we will cut off his nose."
The wording is that of Ibn Bashshār.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak, from Shuʿbah, from Qatādah, from ʿAṭāʾ,
from Ibn Yaʿlā, from his father,
similar to the case of the one who bit and his front tooth fell out, that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"You have no blood-money."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
insulted a father of his from the Pre-Islamic Era, so al-ʿAbbās slapped him. His people came and said, "We will surely slap him as he slapped him."
They put on their weapons. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, so he ascended the pulpit and said:
"O people, which people on earth do you know to be most honored with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?" They said, "You." He said:
"Indeed, al-ʿAbbās is from me and I am from him. Do not revile our dead, lest you harm our living."
Then the people came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we seek refuge in Allah from your anger. Ask forgiveness for us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ submit himself to retaliation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Children of Israel were bound by retaliation and had no blood-money. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed blood-money for them and made it for this nation as a relief compared with what was upon the Children of Israel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave a sermon on the day of the Conquest. (Mursal)
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The blood-money for a woman is the same as that for a man until it reaches a third of her full blood-money."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw a man throwing pebbles with his fingers and said, "Do not throw pebbles, for the Prophet of Allah ﷺ forbade throwing pebbles, or disliked it." Kahmas was unsure [which].
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar
consulted the people about the unborn child. Ḥamal ibn Mālik said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled a ghurrah for the unborn child."
Ṭāwūs said, "A horse is a ghurrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman of Banū Laḥyān struck her co-wife with a tent pole and killed her, and the slain woman was pregnant. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the blood-money be paid by the paternal relatives of the killer, and a ghurrah for what was in her womb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he take as his patron a Muslim without his permission.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"The fingers are equal: ten [camels each]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the document held by the family of ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm was found, which they said the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had written for them, they found in it:
"And for the fingers there, ten each."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The fingers: ten each.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote a letter to the people of Yemen containing the obligations, the practices, and the blood-money rulings, and sent it with ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm. It was read to the people of Yemen; this is its copy:
"From Muḥammad the Prophet ﷺ to Shuraḥbīl ibn ʿAbd Kulāl, Nuʿaym ibn ʿAbd Kulāl, and al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd Kulāl, [rulers] of Dhū Ruʿayn, Maʿāfir, and Hamdān. To proceed:"
And in his letter was:

"Whoever kills a believer unjustly, with clear proof, is subject to retaliation, unless the guardians of the slain person are satisfied. In a life the blood-money is one hundred camels. In the nose, when it is entirely cut off, the blood-money; in the tongue, the blood-money; in the two lips, the blood-money; in the two testicles, the blood-money; in the male organ, the blood-money; in the spine, the blood-money; in the two eyes, the blood-money; in one leg, half the blood-money; in a head wound reaching the membrane of the brain, a third of the blood-money; in a wound penetrating the body cavity, a third of the blood-money; in a wound that dislodges the bone, fifteen camels; in each finger of the hand and foot, ten camels; in a tooth, five camels; in a wound exposing the bone, five camels. A man is killed for a woman. And upon the people of gold, one thousand dinars."
Muḥammad ibn Bakkār ibn Bilāl differed from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah bint Qays said: Tamīm al-Dārī came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he had sailed on the sea and his ship had lost its way with him, so he was cast up on an island. He went out onto it looking for water and met a man dragging his hair.
He related the rest of the account, and in it [the man] said: Had I been given permission to leave, I would have trodden every land except Ṭaybah.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ brought him out to the people and he told them. [The Prophet ﷺ] said:
"This is Ṭaybah, and that is the Dajjāl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Seventy thousand of the Jews of Isfahan will follow the Dajjāl, wearing shawls (ṭayālisah)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among them were Abū al-Dahmāʾ and Abū Qatādah. They said: We used to pass by Hishām ibn ʿĀmir on our way to ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn. One day he said: You pass me by to go to men who were no more present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than I was, and who do not know his ḥadīth better than I do. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"From the creation of Adam until the Hour is established, there is no creation greater than the Dajjāl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, with this [report].
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
asked the Prophet ﷺ, "When will the Hour be established?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent for a short while, then looked at a young boy in front of him from the Azd of Shanūʾah and said:
"If this one lives, old age will not overtake him before the Hour is established."
He said: Anas said: That boy was one of my peers at that time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A servant boy of al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, who was one of my peers, passed by, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"If this one is granted a long life, old age will not overtake him before the Hour is established."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

"The Hour will be established while a man is milking his she-camel, and the vessel will not reach his mouth before it is established; while two men are trading a garment, and they will not complete the sale before it is established; and while a man is plastering his water trough, and he will not finish before it is established."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The servant says, 'My wealth, my wealth!' Yet he has of his wealth only three things: what he ate and used up, what he wore and wore out, or what he gave away and so stored up [for the Hereafter]. Whatever is besides that is going away, and he leaves it for the people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of Yūnus and the like of his ḥadīth, except that in the ḥadīth of Ṣāliḥ [it says]:
"And it will distract you as it distracted them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ was with his camels when his son ʿUmar came to him. When Saʿd saw him, he said: I seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this rider. [ʿUmar] dismounted and said to him: You have settled among your camels and sheep and left the people disputing over sovereignty among themselves! Saʿd struck him on the chest and said: Be quiet! I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Allah loves the servant who is God-fearing, self-sufficient, and unnoticed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He had lived in the Jāhiliyyah. He said: ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwān, who was governor of Basrah, delivered a sermon.
Then he mentioned something like the ḥadīth of Shaybān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he laughed and said:
"Do you know why I am laughing?"
We said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said:
"[I am laughing] at the servant's address to his Lord. He will say: 'My Lord, did You not protect me from wrongdoing?' He will say: 'Yes.'

Then he will say: 'I will permit no witness against myself except one from myself.' [Allah] will say: 'Today you yourself suffice as a witness against you, and the noble scribes as witnesses.' Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will be told: 'Speak.'
So they will speak of his deeds. Then he will be released to speak, and he will say: 'Away with you, and be gone! It was for your sake that I was fighting.'"
"It was on your behalf that I was arguing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While a man was in an open desert, he heard a voice in a cloud: 'Water the garden of so-and-so.'

That cloud moved away and poured out its water on a rocky tract, and one of the channels there took in all that water. The man followed the water and found a man standing in his garden, diverting the water with his spade. He said to him: 'Servant of Allah, what is your name?' He said: 'So-and-so,'

the very name he had heard in the cloud. He said to him: 'Servant of Allah, why do you ask me my name?' He said: 'I heard a voice in the cloud whose water this is, saying: "Water the garden of so-and-so," using your name. What do you do with it?' He said: 'Since you say this, I look at what comes out of it and give a third in charity, my family and I eat a third, and I return a third to it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿAbd al-Raḥmān came to us, the Prophet ﷺ made a pledge of brotherhood between him and Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ. Then the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"Hold a wedding feast, even if only with a sheep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A funeral bier was brought to the Prophet ﷺ so that he might pray over it, and he said:
"Does he owe any debt?" They said, "No." So he prayed over him.
Then another bier was brought, and he said:
"Does he owe any debt?" They said, "Yes." He said:
"Pray over your companion."
Abū Qatādah said, "His debt is upon me, O Messenger of Allah." So he prayed over him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: "I have known my parents only as following the religion [of Islam]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I wrote an agreement with Umayyah ibn Khalaf that he would protect my family and property in Makkah,
and I would protect his family and property in Madinah.
When I mentioned ar-Raḥmān, he said, "I do not know ar-Raḥmān.
Write to me with your name that you had in the time of ignorance."

So I wrote to him as ʿAbd ʿAmr. On the day of Badr, I went out to a mountain to protect him when the people were asleep, but Bilāl saw him, went out, and stood at a gathering of the Anṣār and said, "Umayyah ibn Khalaf!
May I not be saved if Umayyah is saved!"
So a group of the Anṣār went out with him, following our tracks.
When I feared that they would catch up with us, I left his son behind for them
to occupy them. They killed him, but they still refused to stop until they followed us.
He was a heavy man.
When they caught up with us, I said to him, "Kneel down." So he knelt,
and I threw myself over him to protect him,
but they thrust their swords through him from beneath me until they killed him,
and one of them struck my foot with his sword.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf used to show us that mark on the top of his foot.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have offered myself to you [in marriage]."
A man said, "Marry her to me." He ﷺ said:
"We have married her to you for what you have of the Qur'an."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed me to guard the zakāh of Ramadan,
and someone came to me and began scooping up handfuls of the food, so I seized him,
and I said, "By Allah, I will take you to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said, "I am needy, and I have a family to support,
and my need is severe."
He said: So I let him go. In the morning the Prophet ﷺ said:
"O Abū Hurayrah, what did your captive do last night?"
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, he complained of severe need and a family, so I took pity on him and let him go." He said:
"Indeed, he lied to you, and he will return."
So I knew he would return, because of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ saying that he would return.
I lay in wait for him, and he came scooping up handfuls of the food. I seized him and said, "I will take you to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said, "Leave me, for I am needy,
and I have a family to support. I will not return." So I took pity on him,
and I let him go. In the morning,
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"O Abū Hurayrah,
what did your captive do?"
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, he complained of severe need and a family,
so I took pity on him and let him go." He said:
"Indeed, he lied to you, and he will return."
So I lay in wait for him a third time, and he came scooping up handfuls of the food,
and I seized him and said, "I will take you to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
and this is the last of three times that you claim you will not return and then you return."
He said, "Leave me, and I will teach you words by which Allah will benefit you."
I said, "What are they?" He said, "When you go to your bed, recite Āyat al-Kursī, {Allah, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining}, until you finish the verse,
for a guardian from Allah will remain over you, and no devil will come near you until morning."
So I let him go. In the morning,
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"What did your captive do last night?"
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, he claimed that he would teach me words
by which Allah would benefit me, so I let him go." He said, "What are they?"

I said, "He said to me: When you go to your bed, recite Āyat al-Kursī from its beginning until you finish {Allah, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining}, and he said to me: A guardian from Allah will remain over you, and no devil will come near you until morning."
They were the keenest of people for what is good. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Indeed, he told you the truth, though he is a liar.
Do you know whom you have been speaking to for three nights, O Abū Hurayrah?" He said, "No." He said, "That was a devil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the charity (ṣadaqah) of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: "There is no blame on the one in charge of it if he eats from it and feeds a friend, without accumulating wealth [for himself]."
Ibn ʿUmar was the one in charge of the charity of ʿUmar, and he would give gifts to people of Makkah
with whom he used to stay.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among those of my friends whom I envy most is a believer who is light of burden, with a share of prayer, who worships his Lord well and obeys Him in secret, who is obscure among the people, not pointed out with fingers, whose provision is just sufficient, and who is patient with that."
Then he struck his hand [together] and said: "
His death comes quickly, his mourners are few, and his inheritance is small."
And by this chain of narration, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "

My Lord offered to turn the pebbly valley of Makkah into gold for me. I said: 'No, my Lord, but let me be full one day and hungry one day' – or he said three days, or words like this – 'so that when I am hungry I humble myself to You and remember You, and when I am full I thank You and praise You.'"
He said: This is a good (ḥasan) hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
O Allah, let me live poor, let me die poor, and gather me on the Day of Resurrection among the poor."
ʿĀʾishah said: "Why, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "

They will enter Paradise forty years before their rich. O ʿĀʾishah, do not turn away a poor person, even with half a date. O ʿĀʾishah, love the poor and bring them close, for Allah will bring you close on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

When Allah wants good for His servant, He hastens his punishment in this world; and when Allah wants evil for His servant, He withholds from him his sins until he is repaid in full for them on the Day of Resurrection."
And by this chain of narration, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "
Great reward comes with great trial. When Allah loves a people, He tests them. Whoever is pleased [with it] will have [Allah's] pleasure, and whoever is displeased will have [Allah's] displeasure."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with a group of people in Īliyā' (Jerusalem), and a man among them said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
More people than Banū Tamīm will enter Paradise through the intercession of one man from my Ummah."
It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, other than you?" He said: "Other than me."
When he stood up, I said: "Who is this?" They said: "This is Ibn Abī al-Jadhʿāʾ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The shrewd person is the one who holds himself to account and works for what comes after death, and the incapable is the one who follows his own desires and [yet] wishes upon Allah."
He said: This is a good (ḥasan) hadith.
He said: The meaning of his saying: "
He who holds himself to account"
is: he takes himself to account in this world before he is taken to account on the Day of Resurrection.

It is reported from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he said: Take yourselves to account before you are taken to account, and prepare yourselves for the greatest presentation. The reckoning on the Day of Resurrection will be lighter only for the one who took himself to account in this world.

It is reported from Maymūn ibn Mihrān that he said: A servant does not become God-fearing until he takes himself to account as he takes his business partner to account: where his food and his clothing come from.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Companion of the Prophet ﷺ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The one who eats and is grateful has a reward like that of the one who fasts and is patient."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī: "What have you memorized from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: I memorized from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "
Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt, for truthfulness is tranquillity and lying is doubt."
There is a story in the hadith.
He said: Abū al-Ḥawrā' as-Saʿdī's name is Rabīʿah ibn Shaybān.
He said: This is a good and sound (ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ) hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "
Say often: 'There is no power and no strength except with Allah,' for it is one of the treasures of Paradise."
Makḥūl said: Whoever says, 'There is no power and no strength except with Allah, and there is no refuge from Allah except in Him,'
seventy doors of harm will be removed from him, the least of which is poverty.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when Abū Bakr and ʿUmar appeared, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
These two are the masters of the middle-aged men of the people of Paradise, among the first and the last, except for the prophets and messengers. O ʿAlī, do not tell them."
This hadith is gharīb from this route.
Al-Walīd ibn Muḥammad al-Muwaqqarī is considered weak in hadith, and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn did not hear from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.
This hadith has also been narrated from ʿAlī by other routes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Banū Zuhrah, from al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abī Dhubāb,
from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh,
who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Every prophet has a companion, and my companion – meaning in Paradise – is ʿUthmān."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: When the verse in Sūrat al-Furqān was revealed, {And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden [to be killed] except by right}, the polytheists of Makkah said: We have killed the soul which Allah has forbidden, we have invoked another deity along with Allah, and we have committed indecencies.

So Allah revealed: {Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds; for those Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds}. So this [verse] is for those people. He said: As for the verse in Sūrat an-Nisāʾ, {And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell}, the verse—he said: [it refers to] a man who knows the laws of Islam and then kills a believer intentionally; his recompense is Hell, and there is no repentance for him.
I mentioned this to Mujāhid, and he said: Except for one who feels remorse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stayed in Makkah for thirteen years—meaning that revelation was coming to him—and he died at the age of sixty-three.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah and found the Jews fasting on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ. They were asked about that, and they said: This is the day on which Allah gave Moses and the Children of Israel victory over Pharaoh, so we fast it out of reverence for it. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"We have more right to Moses than you." So he commanded that it be fasted.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yazīd

went out to pray for rain for the people. He prayed two rakʿahs and then asked for rain. [Abū Isḥāq] said: On that day I met Zayd ibn Arqam—and he said: there was no one between him and me except one man, or [he said] between him and me was a man—I said to him: How many military expeditions did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ undertake? He said: Nineteen. I said: How many did you fight along with him? He said: Seventeen expeditions. I said: What was the first expedition he undertook? He said: Dhāt al-ʿUsayr, or al-ʿUshayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Companions of Muhammad ﷺ who were present at Badr [told us] that they were the same number as the companions of Ṭālūt who crossed the river with him,
a little over three hundred.
Al-Barāʾ said: No, by Allah, none crossed the river with him except a believer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He swore that these verses were revealed about these six men on the day of Badr: {These are two adversaries who disputed concerning their Lord}, up to His saying:

{Indeed, Allah does what He wills}—about Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith, ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah, and al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah. They disputed in [their] contest on the day of Badr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Umm Salamah], the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, [said] that Abū Ḥudhayfah ibn ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah ibn ʿAbd Shams had adopted Sālim and married him to his brother's daughter, Hind bint al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, and he was a freed slave of a woman of the Anṣār, just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had adopted Zayd. In the pre-Islamic period, whoever adopted a man, people would call him by [the adopter's] name, and he would inherit from him, until Allah, Glorified and Exalted, revealed concerning that: {Call them by [the names of] their fathers} up to His saying: {then they are your brothers in religion and your freed slaves}. So they were returned to their fathers, and whoever's father was not known was a freed slave and a brother in religion. Then Sahlah bint Suhayl ibn ʿAmr al-Qurashī al-ʿĀmirī—who was the wife of Abū Ḥudhayfah—came and said: O Messenger of Allah, we used to regard Sālim as a son. He would stay with me and Abū Ḥudhayfah in one house, and he would see me in my casual dress. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed concerning them what you know, so what do you see [we should do] about him? The Prophet ﷺ said to her: "Nurse him."

So she nursed him five times, and he became like her son by nursing. For this reason ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, would instruct her sisters' daughters and her brothers' daughters to nurse whomever ʿĀʾishah wished to see her and enter upon her, even if he was grown, five nursings, and then he would enter upon her. But Umm Salamah and all the other wives of the Prophet ﷺ refused to allow anyone to enter upon them by such nursing unless he had nursed in infancy. They said to ʿĀʾishah: By Allah, we do not know; perhaps it was a concession from the Prophet ﷺ for Sālim alone, not for other people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and entered upon me on the morning after my wedding was consummated, and sat on my bed as you are sitting [now] with me, while some of our young girls were beating their tambourines and lamenting those of my fathers who were killed on the day of Badr, until one of them said: "And among us is a prophet who knows what will be tomorrow."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"Leave off this, and say what you were saying before it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us to deliver a sermon of admonition and said:

"O people, you will be gathered to Allah barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised: 'Just as We began the first creation, We shall repeat it—a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We are ever doers [of what We promise].' Beware! The first of creation to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection will be Abraham, peace be upon him. Beware! Some men from my nation will be brought forward and taken to the left. I will say: 'My Lord, my Companions!'
It will be said: 'You do not know what they introduced after you.'

Then I will say as the righteous servant said: 'And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things. If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are indeed the Almighty, the All-Wise.'" He said: "Then it will be said to me: 'They have continued to turn back on their heels since you left them.'"
And in the narration of Wakīʿ and Muʿādh: "
'It will be said: You do not know what they introduced after you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"We are more deserving of doubt than Abraham when he said: 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.' He said: 'Do you not believe?' He said: 'Yes, but to put my heart at rest.' And may Allah have mercy on Lot; he used to take refuge in a strong support. And had I stayed in prison as long as Joseph stayed, I would have answered the summoner."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I met Moses, peace be upon him." And the Prophet ﷺ described him:
"He was a man—I think he said—lean, with hair neither curly nor straight, as if he were one of the men of Shanūʾah." He said: "And I met Jesus." And the Prophet ﷺ described him:
"He was of medium height, ruddy, as if he had just come out of a bathhouse."
—meaning a bath—He said:

"And I saw Abraham, blessings of Allah be upon him, and I am the one of his children most resembling him." He said: "Then two vessels were brought to me, in one of which was milk and in the other wine. It was said to me: 'Take whichever you wish.'
So I took the milk and drank it.
Then it was said: 'You have been guided to the natural way,' or 'You have attained the natural way. Had you taken the wine, your nation would have gone astray.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Khalīfah said to me: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah,
from Abū al-ʿĀliyah,
from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ, among what he narrates from his Lord, who said:
"It is not proper for any servant to say that he is better than Jonah son of Matta."
And he attributed him to his father.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While a Jew was offering his goods for sale, he was offered for them something he disliked.
So he said: "No, by the One who chose Moses above all mankind!"
A man of the Anṣār heard him, stood up, and slapped his face,
and said: "Do you say, 'By the One who chose Moses above all mankind,'
while the Prophet ﷺ is among us?" The Jew went to him
and said: "O Abū al-Qāsim,
I have a pledge of protection and a covenant,
so what is the matter with so-and-so that he slapped my face?" He said:
"Why did you slap his face?" The man told him,
and the Prophet ﷺ became angry until anger could be seen in his face. Then he said:
"Do not prefer one among the prophets of Allah over another,
for the Trumpet will be blown,
and those in the heavens and those on the earth will fall unconscious,
except whom Allah wills.
Then it will be blown a second time,
and I will be the first to be raised, and there will be Moses holding on to the Throne.
I do not know whether he was reckoned as having already had his unconsciousness on the day of Ṭūr, or whether he was raised before me. And I do not say that anyone is better than Jonah son of Matta."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The likeness of me and the people is like a man who kindled a fire,
and the moths and these creatures began to fall into the fire." And he said: "
Two women had their two sons with them. A wolf came and took away the son of one of them.
Her companion said: 'It only took your son.'
The other said: 'It only took your son.'
So they took their dispute to David,
and he ruled that the child belonged to the elder. They went out to Solomon son of David and told him.
He said: 'Bring me a knife so that I may split him between them.'
The younger said: 'Do not do so, may Allah have mercy on you; he is her son.'
So he ruled that the child belonged to the younger."
Abū Hurayrah said: "By Allah, I never heard the word 'sikkīn' [knife] except that day,
for we used to say only 'mudyah.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I am the closest of people to Jesus son of Mary, in this world and the Hereafter.
The prophets are brothers from different mothers: their mothers are various, but their religion is one."
And Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭahmān said, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah,
from Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym,
from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār,
from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"In the last days there will emerge men who seek worldly gain through religion. They will wear sheepskins before people to display softness; their tongues will be sweeter than sugar, but their hearts will be the hearts of wolves. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Are they deceived by My forbearance, or are they audacious against Me? By Myself I swear, I will send upon those people a trial that will leave even the forbearing among them bewildered.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is salvation?" He said:
"Hold your tongue, let your house suffice you, and weep over your sins."
label: machine translation

"Do not speak much without the remembrance of Allah, for much speech without the remembrance of Allah hardens the heart, and the person furthest from Allah is the hard-hearted."

segments_en: A man from the people of Madinah said: Muʿāwiyah wrote to ʿĀʾishah, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her: "Write me a letter in which you advise me, and do not make it long."
So ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, wrote to Muʿāwiyah: "Peace be upon you. To proceed: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'Whoever seeks the pleasure of Allah at the displeasure of the people, Allah will suffice him against the burden of the people. And whoever seeks the pleasure of the people at the displeasure of Allah, Allah will leave him to the people.'" And peace be upon you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The feet of a servant will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about his life and how he spent it, about his knowledge and what he did with it, about his wealth and where he earned it and how he spent it, and about his body and how he used it."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
Saʿīd ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Jurayj is from Basra and was a freed slave of Abū Barzah, and Abū Barzah's name was Naḍlah ibn ʿUbayd.

segments_en: The son of Adam will be brought on the Day of Resurrection like a lamb, and he will be made to stand before Allah. Allah will say to him: 'I gave you, I granted you authority, and I favored you. So what did you do?'
He will say: 'My Lord, I gathered it and increased it, and I left it greater than it was, so send me back and I will bring it all to You.'
He will say to him: 'Show Me what you sent ahead.'
He will say: 'My Lord, I gathered it and increased it, and I left it greater than it was, so send me back and I will bring it all to You.'
Then it will be a servant who sent ahead nothing good, and he will be taken away to the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will say to him: 'Did I not give you hearing and sight, wealth and children, and subject to you the livestock and the crops, and leave you to lead and to take a quarter [as a chief]? Did you think that you would meet this day of yours?' He will say: 'No.'
So He will say to him: 'Today I forget you as you forgot Me.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: "On that Day it will report its news," and said:
"Do you know what its news is?"
They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"Its news is that it will testify against every male or female servant about what they did on its surface, saying: 'He did such and such on such and such day.' That is its news."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"How can I be at ease when the one with the Horn has put the Horn to his mouth, bent his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting to be commanded to blow so that he may blow?"
The Muslims said: "Then what should we say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Say: 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs; in Allah, our Lord, we have put our trust.'"
Sufyān sometimes said: "In Allah we have put our trust."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The motto of the believer on the Bridge is: 'My Lord, grant safety, grant safety.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Prophet ﷺ to intercede for me on the Day of Resurrection, and he said: "I will do so."
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, where should I look for you?" He said:
"Look for me first at the Bridge."
I said: "And if I do not meet you at the Bridge?" He said:
"Then look for me at the Scale."
I said: "And if I do not meet you at the Scale?" He said:
"Then look for me at the Pond, for I will not miss these three places."

segments_en: The delegation of Thaqīf came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a gift, and he said, "

Is it a gift or charity? If it is a gift, then it is sought by it the favor of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the fulfilment of a need; and if it is charity, then it is sought by it the face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
They said, "No, it is a gift."
So he accepted it from them and sat with them, asking them and being asked by them, until he prayed the Ẓuhr together with the ʿAṣr.

came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "You set up rivals to Allah and you associate partners with Him; you say, 'What Allah wills and you will,' and you say, 'By the Kaʿbah.'"
So the Prophet ﷺ commanded them, when they wished to swear, to say, "By the Lord of the Kaʿbah," and to say, "
What Allah wills, then what you will."

"I was shown Laylat al-Qadr, then I was made to forget it. And I was shown that on its morning I would be prostrating in water and mud."
He said: It rained on the night of the twenty-third, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer. When he finished, the marks of water and mud were on his forehead and nose.
He said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Unays used to say, "The twenty-third."

segments_en: The polytheists used to say, "Labbayka, You have no partner." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say:
"Woe to you! Enough, enough!"
But they would say, "Except a partner who is Yours, whom You own and all that he owns."
They would say this while circling the House.

segments_en: I performed Hajj and ʿUmrah with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with them both, twelve times in all, and I said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, I have seen four things from you."

And he related the hadith with this meaning, except in the account of the declaration of ihrām, in which he differed from the narration of al-Maqburī, and he mentioned it with a meaning other than what the latter mentioned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from ʿUbaydullāh ibn
ʿAbdullāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
from al-Ṣaʿb ibn Jaththāmah al-Laythī,

that he gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a wild donkey as a gift while he was at al-Abwāʾ, or Waddān, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned it to him. He said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw what was on my face, he said:
"We did not return it to you except that we are in a state of iḥrām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until, when we were at al-Qāḥah, some of us were in iḥrām and some were not. Then I noticed my companions looking at something, and I looked, and there was a wild donkey.
I saddled my horse, took my spear, and mounted, but my whip fell from me. I said to my companions, who were in iḥrām, "Hand me the whip."
They said, "By Allah, we will not help you with anything against it."

So I dismounted, picked it up, and mounted again. I caught up with the donkey from behind, as it was behind a small hill, and I struck it with my spear and hamstrung it. I brought it to my companions, and some of them said, "Eat it."
And some of them said, "Do not eat it."
The Prophet ﷺ was ahead of us, so I urged my horse on and reached him, and he said:
"It is lawful, so eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, mentioning nothing but Hajj, until we came to Sarif, and I began to menstruate. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me while I was weeping and said, "What makes you weep?"
I said, "By Allah, I wish I had not gone out this year." He said:
"What is the matter with you? Perhaps you have begun your menses?" I said, "Yes." He said:
"This is something Allah has decreed for the daughters of Ādam. Do what the pilgrim does, except that you must not circle the House until you are pure."
She said: When I arrived in Makkah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions, "Make it an ʿUmrah."

So the people came out of iḥrām, except those who had brought sacrificial animals. She said: The sacrificial animals were with the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and men of means. Then they entered iḥrām for Hajj when they set out. She said: When the Day of Sacrifice came, I was pure, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me, and I performed the ṭawāf al-ifāḍah. She said: Beef was brought to us.
I said, "What is this?" They said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sacrificed cows on behalf of his wives."

When it was the night of al-Ḥaṣbah, I said, "O Messenger of Allah, the people are returning with a Hajj and an ʿUmrah, and I am returning with only a Hajj." She said: So he commanded ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr, and he seated me behind him on his camel. She said: I remember, as a young girl of tender age, dozing off, and the back of the saddle striking my face, until we came to al-Tanʿīm, and from there I entered iḥrām for an ʿUmrah, in compensation for the ʿUmrah that the people had performed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: What we memorized from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār is that he said: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us out, three hundred riders, with Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ as our commander, to watch for a caravan of Quraysh.
We stayed on the coast for half a month, and severe hunger struck us until we ate leaves (khabaṭ).
So that army was called the Army of the Leaves.
Then the sea cast up for us an animal called al-ʿAnbar.
We ate from it for half a month and rubbed ourselves with its fat until our bodies recovered.

Abū ʿUbaydah took one of its ribs and set it upright, then picked the tallest man with him (Sufyān once said: he took one of its bones and set it upright, and took a man and a camel) and had him pass beneath it. Jābir said: One of the men slaughtered three camels,
then he slaughtered three camels,
then he slaughtered three camels,
and then Abū ʿUbaydah forbade him.
ʿAmr used to say: Abū Ṣāliḥ informed us that Qays ibn Saʿd said to his father: I was in the army and they became hungry. He said: Slaughter. I said: I slaughtered.
He said: Then they became hungry. He said: Slaughter. I said: I slaughtered.
He said: Then they became hungry. He said: Slaughter.
I said: I slaughtered. Then they became hungry. He said: Slaughter. I said: I was forbidden.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The two best men, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, nearly perished: they raised their voices in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ when the riders of Banū Tamīm came to him.
One of them pointed to al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis, of Banū Mujāshiʿ,
and the other pointed to a different man (Nāfiʿ said: I do not remember his name). Abū Bakr said to ʿUmar: You only wanted to oppose me.
He said: I did not want to oppose you.
Their voices rose over that,
so Allah revealed: {O you who believe, do not raise your voices...} the verse.
Ibn al-Zubayr said: After this verse, ʿUmar would not speak to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ without asking him to repeat what he said so that he could understand.
He did not mention that about his father,
meaning Abū Bakr.
label: machine translation

"The people of Yemen have come to you. They are softer in heart and gentler in spirit. Understanding is Yemeni, and wisdom is Yemeni."

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the days of the Camel,

after I had almost joined the companions of the Camel and fought alongside them. He said: When the news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that the Persians had made the daughter of Khosrow their ruler, he said:
"A people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never prosper."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to hear that no prophet dies until he is given a choice between this world and the Hereafter. She said: Then I heard the Prophet ﷺ in his final illness, when his voice had become hoarse, saying: {...with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.} She said: So I thought he was being given the choice at that time.

"O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, and join me with the Highest Companion."

segments_en: I was praying in the mosque when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called me, but I did not answer him.
I said: O Messenger of Allah, I was praying. He said:
"Did Allah not say: {Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you}?" Then he said to me: "I will teach you a surah that is the greatest surah in the Qur'an before you leave the mosque."
Then he took me by the hand,
and when he was about to leave, I said to him: Did you not say:
"I will teach you a surah that is the greatest surah in the Qur'an"? He said:
"{Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds}. It is the Seven Oft-Repeated verses and the Great Qur'an that I have been given."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months, then we were turned toward the Kaʿbah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, a black boy has been born to me."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Then how did that come about?"
He said, "I do not know." He ﷺ said,
"Do you have any camels?" He said, "Yes." He said, "What colors are they?" He said, "Red." He said,
"Is there among them a grayish camel?"
He said, "There are grayish camels among them." He said,
"Then how did that come about?"
He said, "I do not know, O Messenger of Allah, except that perhaps a lineage [trait] drew it out." He said,
"And perhaps this too, a lineage [trait] drew it out."
For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that it is not permissible for a man to disown a child who was born on his bed, unless he claims that he saw an indecent act.
label: machine translation

segments_en: This is the hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Yūnus ibn Jubayr,
from Ḥiṭṭān ibn ʿAbdullāh,
from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us, explained our Sunnah to us and taught us our prayer. He said, "When you pray,
and you are at the sitting,
let the first thing any of you says be: 'All greetings, good words and prayers are for Allah.
Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.
Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah,
and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.'
These are seven phrases, which are the greeting of the prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us and said,

"By the One besides Whom there is no god, the blood of a Muslim man who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah is not lawful except in three cases: the one who abandons Islam and separates from the community, or the community—Aḥmad was unsure about it—and the married person who commits adultery, and a life for a life."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Hearing and obeying is a duty upon a Muslim person, in what he likes and dislikes, as long as he is not commanded to disobedience. If he is commanded to disobedience, then there is no hearing and no obedience."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to hear and obey, and then he would say, "As much as you are able." And he said, "As much as you [all] are able."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Numayr, Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm and Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAlāʾ—Isḥāq said "he informed us," and the others said,
"Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, from Abū

Mūsā, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about a man who fights out of courage, fights out of zeal, and fights to be seen: which of these is in the cause of Allah? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is the highest, he is in the cause of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man who feels something during prayer was mentioned in a complaint to the Prophet ﷺ.
[They asked,] "Should he break off the prayer?" He said, "No,
not until he hears a sound or smells an odor."
Ibn Abī Ḥafṣah said, from al-Zuhrī: There is no need for ablution except if you smell an odor or hear a sound.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ milked a sheep and drank some of its milk, then called for water, rinsed his mouth and said,
"It has fat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ held a race between the horses that had been trained, and he sent them off from al-Ḥafyāʾ,
and their finish line was Thaniyyat al-Wadāʿ.
I said to Mūsā, "How far was it between the two?" He said, "Six or seven miles."
And he held a race between the horses that had not been trained,
and he sent them off from Thaniyyat al-Wadāʿ,
and their finish line was the mosque of Banū Zurayq.
I said, "How far was it between the two?" He said, "A mile or about that."
And Ibn ʿUmar was among those who took part in racing them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ two days before the Eid al-Aḍḥā, and we were giving jadhaʿah sheep in place of thaniyyah ones. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The jadhaʿah suffices in the place of what the thaniyyah suffices."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Then he—it seems he meant the Prophet ﷺ—went, on the Day of Sacrifice, to two white-and-black rams and slaughtered them, and to a young sheep (jadhīʿah) and distributed it among us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to count ten sheep as equal to one camel in the distribution of the spoils of war.
Shuʿbah said: Most of what I know is that I heard it from Saʿīd ibn Masrūq, and Sufyān also narrated it to me from him. And Allah the Exalted knows best.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man of the Anṣār had a she-camel that was grazing in the area before Uḥud. Something befell it, so he slaughtered it with a peg.
I said to Zayd: Was the peg of wood or of iron? He said: No, of wood. Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him, and he commanded him to eat it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade [keeping] the meat of the sacrificial animals beyond three days. Then Qatādah ibn al-Nuʿmān arrived—he was the maternal half-brother of Abū Saʿīd and was one who had fought at Badr—and they served him [some of it]. He said: Has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not forbidden this? Abū Saʿīd said: A new ruling has come about concerning it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us to eat it beyond three days, then he permitted us to eat it and to store it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah about the meat of the sacrificial animals,
and she said: We used to store the trotters for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a month, and then he would eat them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade keeping the sacrificial meat beyond three days, then he said: "Eat and feed others."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The animal that has been confined and shot at (the mujaththamah) is not lawful [to eat]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by some people who were shooting arrows at a ram. He disliked that and said:
"Do not mutilate animals."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"Allah has cursed whoever mutilates an animal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"Whoever kills a sparrow needlessly, it will cry out to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection, saying: O my Lord, so-and-so killed me needlessly and did not kill me for any benefit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Among the signs of the Hour is that wealth will spread and increase, trade will spread, and knowledge will become widespread; a man will make a sale and say, 'No, not until I consult the merchant of the family of so-and-so,' and a skilled scribe will be sought in a neighborhood and will not be found."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you sells a sheep or a milch animal, he must not leave its milk held back in the udder [to give a false impression]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"Do not go out to meet the caravans [to buy from them], and do not tie up the udders of camels and sheep [to deceive buyers]. Whoever buys any of that has the better of the two options: if he wishes he may keep it, and if he wishes to return it he may return it along with a ṣāʿ of dates."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not go out to meet the caravans [to buy from them], and do not undercut one another's sales—and do not bid up prices deceitfully—and a city-dweller must not sell for a desert-dweller."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade going out to meet [trade caravans before they reach the market].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade deceitful bidding (najsh).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sold a drinking cup and a saddle-cloth to the highest bidder.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade two ways of dressing and two kinds of sale. As for the two sales, they are mulāmasah and munābadhah. Munābadhah is when he says: When you throw this garment [to me], the sale is binding. And mulāmasah is that he touches it with his hand without unfolding it or turning it over; once he touches it, the sale is binding.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ ordered the remission [of payment] for losses from natural disasters (jawāʾiḥ).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted a concession regarding ʿarāyā [the sale of fresh dates on the tree for dried dates].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"A heap of food must not be sold for a heap of food, nor a heap of food for a specified measure of food."
label: machine translation

segments_en: O Messenger of Allah, we cannot find [dates of the] Ṣayḥānī type, nor a cluster, to exchange for dates unless we give them more.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Sell it for silver, then buy with it [what you want]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought some fine, juicy dates—the dates of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were from rain-fed trees and somewhat dry—and he said:
"From where do you have this?"
They said: We bought a ṣāʿ of it for two ṣāʿs of our dates. He said:
"Do not do that, for this is not valid. Rather, sell your dates and buy what you need of these with the proceeds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was standing with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a rabbi from among the Jewish rabbis came and said, "Peace be upon you, O Muhammad."
I pushed him so hard that he nearly fell down. He said, "Why did you push me?" I said, "Will you not say, 'O Messenger of Allah'?"
The Jew said, "We only call him by his name, the name his family gave him."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"My name is Muhammad, the name my family gave me."
The Jew said, "I have come to ask you something."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him,
"Will anything benefit you if I tell you?"
He said, "I will listen with my ears." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to scratch the ground with a stick he had with him, and said, "Ask."
The Jew said, "Where will the people be on the Day when the earth is changed into another earth, and the heavens as well?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"They will be in the darkness, before the bridge."
He said, "And who will be the first of the people to cross?" He said, "The poor among the Emigrants."
The Jew said, "What will be their gift when they enter Paradise?" He said,
"The extra lobe of the liver of the fish."
He said, "And what will be their food after that?" He said,
"The ox of Paradise, which used to graze on its outskirts, will be slaughtered for them."
He said, "And what will be their drink with it?" He said,
"From a spring in it called Salsabīl." He said, "You have spoken the truth."
He said, "I have also come to ask you about something that no one on earth knows except a prophet, or a man, or two men." He said,
"Will it benefit you if I tell you?"
He said, "I will listen with my ears."
He said, "I have come to ask you about the child." He said,

"The man's fluid is white and the woman's fluid is yellow. When they meet, and the man's fluid prevails over the woman's fluid, it is a male, by Allah's permission; and when the woman's fluid prevails over the man's fluid, it is a female, by Allah's permission."
The Jew said, "You have spoken the truth, and you are indeed a prophet." Then he turned and left.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"He asked me about what he asked me, and I had no knowledge of any of it until Allah brought it to me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this chain of transmission; and in their narration there is no mention of washing the two feet.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ bathed after sexual impurity. He began by washing his hands three times. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abū Muʿāwiyah, but he did not mention washing the feet.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bathed after sexual impurity, he would begin by washing his hands before putting his hand into the vessel, then perform ablution like his ablution for prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to bathe after sexual impurity from a vessel called the faraq.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bathed, he would begin with his right hand, pouring water over it and washing it. Then he would pour water with his right hand over the impurity on him and wash it away with his left hand. When he had finished that, he would pour water over his head.
ʿĀʾishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I used to bathe from one vessel while we were both in a state of sexual impurity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: To the best of my knowledge, and what comes to my mind, is that Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ informed me that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to bathe with the water left over by Maymūnah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this chain of transmission; and in the hadith of ʿAbd al-Razzāq: "Shall I undo it for menstruation and sexual impurity?" He said, "No."
Then he mentioned it with the meaning of the hadith of Ibn ʿUyaynah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Asmāʾ bint Shakal came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, how should one of us bathe when she is purified from menstruation?" And he related the hadith, but did not mention in it bathing after sexual impurity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came carrying a heavy stone, wearing a light waist-wrapper. He said: My wrapper came undone while I had the stone with me, and I could not put it down until I had brought it to its place. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Go back to your garment and take it, and do not walk about naked."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ's statements would abrogate one another, just as the Qur'an abrogates itself in parts.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said about a man who has relations with his wife but does not ejaculate:
"He washes his private part and performs ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

segments_en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām heard of the arrival of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah, so he came to him
and said, "I am going to ask you about three things that none knows except a prophet:

what is the first sign of the Hour, what is the first food the people of Paradise will eat, and from what does a child resemble its father, and from what does it resemble its maternal uncles?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Jibrīl has just informed me of them."
ʿAbd Allāh said, "That is the enemy of the Jews among the angels."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather the people from the east to the west.
As for the first food that the people of Paradise will eat, it is the extra lobe of the liver of a fish.
As for resemblance in the child, when a man has relations with a woman and his fluid precedes hers, the child resembles him,
and when her fluid precedes, the child resembles her."
He said, "I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah."
Then he said, "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews are a people who slander.
If they learn of my Islam before you ask them, they will slander me before you."
The Jews came, and ʿAbd Allāh entered the house.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"What kind of man is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām among you?"
They said, "He is the most knowledgeable of us and the son of our most knowledgeable, and the best of us and the son of our best."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"What do you think if ʿAbd Allāh were to accept Islam?"
They said, "May Allah protect him from that."
Then ʿAbd Allāh came out to them and said, "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah,
and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."
They said, "He is the worst of us and the son of our worst," and they disparaged him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the Day of Resurrection Ibrāhīm will meet his father Āzar,
and Āzar's face will be covered with darkness and dust.
Ibrāhīm will say to him, 'Did I not tell you not to disobey me?' His father will say, 'Today I will not disobey you.'
Ibrāhīm will say, 'My Lord,
You promised me that You would not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected,
and what disgrace is worse than my father being far removed [from Your mercy]?' Allah the Exalted will say, 'I have forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers.'
Then it will be said, 'O Ibrāhīm, what is beneath your feet?' He will look, and there will be a hyena smeared [with filth],
and it will be seized by its legs and thrown into the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered the House [the Kaʿbah] and found in it an image of Ibrāhīm and an image of Maryam. He said, "What is wrong with them?
They have heard that the angels do not enter a house in which there is an image.
Here is Ibrāhīm depicted; why is he [shown] divining by arrows?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Tonight two [angels] came to me,
and we came upon a very tall man,
I could hardly see his head because of his height, and he was Ibrāhīm ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Ibrāhīm did not lie except three times."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the killing of the gecko and said,
"It used to blow [on the fire] against Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O best of creation!"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "That is Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Among the most righteous of deeds of piety is for a man to maintain ties with the loved ones of his father after he has gone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"The gates of Paradise are opened on Monday and Thursday, and every servant who does not associate anything with Allah is forgiven, except a man who has hatred between himself and his brother. It is said: 'Wait for these two until they reconcile; wait for these two until they reconcile; wait for these two until they reconcile.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"When two people abuse each other, what they say is upon the one who began, as long as the one who was wronged does not transgress."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was asked, "O Messenger of Allah, what is backbiting?" He said,
"Your mentioning your brother in a way he dislikes."
It was said, "What if what I say is true of my brother?" He said,
"If what you say is in him, then you have backbitten him; and if what you say is not in him, then you have slandered him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said,

"A man who had never done any good removed a thorny branch from the road, whether it was on a tree and he cut it and cast it aside, or it was lying there and he removed it. Allah appreciated that from him and admitted him to Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The polytheists of Quraysh came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to dispute about destiny, so this verse was revealed:
"On the Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces: 'Taste the touch of Saqar.' Indeed, We have created everything according to a decree."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The boy whom al-Khiḍr killed was destined from the outset to be a disbeliever, and had he lived, he would have burdened his parents with transgression and disbelief."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever says in the morning and in the evening, 'Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him,' one hundred times,
no one will come on the Day of Resurrection with anything better than what he brings, except someone who said the same as he said or more."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Whoever relieves a believer of a distress of this world, Allah will relieve him of a distress of the Day of Resurrection. Whoever eases the hardship of one in difficulty, Allah will ease matters for him in this world and the Hereafter. Whoever conceals the faults of a Muslim, Allah will conceal his faults in this world and the Hereafter. Allah is in the aid of the servant as long as the servant is in the aid of his brother. Whoever travels a path seeking knowledge therein, Allah will make easy for him thereby a path to Paradise. No people gather in one of the houses of Allah, reciting the Book of Allah and studying it among themselves, except that tranquility descends upon them, mercy covers them, the angels surround them, and Allah mentions them among those who are with Him. And whoever is slowed by his deeds, his lineage will not hasten him forward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He testified regarding Abū Hurayrah and Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that they both testified regarding the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said,
"No people remember Allah except that the angels surround them, mercy covers them, tranquility descends upon them, and Allah mentions them among those who are with Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah went out to a circle in the mosque and said, "What has made you sit?" They said, "We sat to remember Allah."
He said, "By Allah, did nothing make you sit except that?" They said, "By Allah, nothing made us sit except that."

He said, "I did not ask you to swear out of suspicion of you. No one who was in my position with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has narrated fewer hadith from him than I. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once went out to a circle of his Companions and said, 'What has made you sit?'"
They said, "We sat to remember Allah and praise Him for guiding us to Islam and for bestowing His favor upon us." He said,
"By Allah, did nothing make you sit except that?"
They said, "By Allah, nothing made us sit except that." He said,
"I did not ask you to swear out of suspicion of you, but Jibrīl came to me and informed me that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is boasting about you to the angels."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to his bed, he would say,
"Praise be to Allah who fed us, gave us drink, sufficed us and gave us shelter; for how many there are who have no one to suffice them or give them shelter."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to supplicate,
"O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity, and richness [self-sufficiency]."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to trim from his beard, from its width and its length.
label: machine translation

was sent by him to ʿAlī to ask his permission to enter upon Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays, and [ʿAlī] gave him permission. segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Three things are not to be refused: pillows, oil, and milk."
By oil he means perfume.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you is given sweet basil, he should not refuse it, for it has come out of Paradise."
He said: This is a gharīb hadith; we do not know it except through this chain.
And we do not know Ḥannān except in this hadith. Abū ʿUthmān an-Nahdī's name is ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Mull; he lived in the time of the Prophet ﷺ but did not see him and did not hear from him.

segments_en: Allah is Pure and loves purity; He is Clean and loves cleanliness; He is Generous and loves generosity; He is Bountiful and loves bounty. So clean—I think he said—your courtyards, and do not imitate the Jews.

He said: I mentioned that to Muhājir ibn Mismār, and he said: ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ narrated it to me from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it, except that he said: "Clean your courtyards."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Beware of going naked, for with you are those who do not leave you except when you relieve yourselves and when a man goes in to his wife. So be modest before them and honor them."

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a bright moonlit night, and I began looking at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and at the moon, and he was wearing a red garment. To me he was more beautiful than the moon.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafiyyah bint ʿUlaybah and Duḥaybah bint ʿUlaybah narrated it to him from Qaylah bint Makhramah, and they were

her stepdaughters, and Qaylah was the grandmother of their father, his mother's mother. She said: We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—then she mentioned the hadith at length—until a man came when the sun had risen and said: "Peace be upon you, Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"And upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah."
He—meaning the Prophet ﷺ—was wearing two worn-out garments dyed with saffron that had faded, and the Prophet ﷺ had a palm branch with him.

"Indeed Allah loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His servant."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The one who is consulted is trusted."
He said: This is a ḥasan hadith.
More than one person has narrated it from Shaybān ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān an-Naḥwī. Shaybān was a man of a book, and he is sound in hadith, and his kunyah is Abū Muʿāwiyah.

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, fair-skinned, with some gray hair, and al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī resembled him. He ordered thirteen young she-camels for us, and we went to receive them, but his death reached us, so they gave us nothing. When Abū Bakr took charge, he said: "Whoever has a promise from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, let him come."
So I went to him and informed him, and he ordered that they be given to us.

segments_en: I was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when a drink was brought. He drank from it, then handed it to me and I drank from it. Then I said, "I have committed a sin, so ask forgiveness for me." He said, "What is that?"
She said, "I was fasting and I broke my fast." He said,
"Was it for a make-up fast that you were making up?" She said, "No." He said, "Then it does not harm you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to hear Simāk ibn Ḥarb say, "One of the two sons of Umm Hāniʾ narrated to me." Then I met [them], and I am the better of the two. His name was

Jaʿdah, and Umm Hāniʾ was his grandmother. He narrated to me from his grandmother that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon her and asked for a drink. He drank, then handed it to her and she drank. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, I was fasting."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The one fasting voluntarily is the trustee of himself: if he wishes he fasts, and if he wishes he breaks his fast."
Shuʿbah said: I said to him, "Did you hear this from Umm Hāniʾ?" He said, "No. Abū Ṣāliḥ and our family informed me from Umm Hāniʾ."
Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated this hadith from Simāk ibn Ḥarb and said, "from Hārūn, the son of Umm Hāniʾ's daughter, from Umm Hāniʾ."
The narration of Shuʿbah is better.
Thus Maḥmūd ibn Ghaylān narrated to us from Abū Dāwūd, and he said, "the trustee of himself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I and Ḥafṣah were

fasting, and some food that we desired was presented to us, so we ate from it. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, and Ḥafṣah hurried to him before me, for she was her father's daughter, and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we were fasting and food that we desired was presented to us, so we ate from it." He said,
"Make up another day in its place."
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ to that effect.

It is narrated from Ibn al-Mubārak that he said about this hadith: It is permissible in the speech of the Arabs, when a person has fasted most of the month, to say, "He fasted the whole month," and to say, "So-and-so stood in prayer the entire night."
Perhaps he had dinner and was occupied with some of his affairs.
Ibn al-Mubārak saw both hadith as being in agreement, saying that the meaning of this hadith is only that he used to fast most of the month.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man asked him, saying, "Which month do you command me to fast after the month of Ramadan?" He said to him, "I have not heard anyone ask about this except a man whom I heard ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while I was sitting. He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, which month do you command me to fast after the month of Ramadan?' He said,

'If you are to fast after the month of Ramadan, then fast Muharram, for it is the month of Allah. In it is a day on which Allah accepted the repentance of a people, and in it He will accept the repentance of other people.'"

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast, in one month, Saturday, Sunday and Monday, and in the next month Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

Ibn ʿUmar said: By Allah, I think that if ʿĀʾishah heard this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then I think the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only left off touching the two corners because they are not on the foundations of the House, and the people only circled beyond the Hijr for that reason.

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ circling the House on his mount, touching the corner with his curved staff and then kissing it. Muḥammad ibn Rāfiʿ added: Then he went out to Ṣafā and Marwah and circled seven times on his mount.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions performed ʿUmrah from al-Jiʿrānah. They walked briskly around the House, having put their cloaks under their armpits and thrown them over their left shoulders.
