segments_en: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Your people claim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ walked briskly around the House and that this is a sunnah.
He said: They told the truth and they lied.

I said: What did they get right and what did they get wrong? He said: They were right that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ walked briskly, and they were wrong that it is a sunnah. At the time of al-Ḥudaybiyah, Quraysh said: Leave Muḥammad and his Companions until they die like the nughaf-worms.

When they made a treaty with him that they would come the following year and stay in Makkah for three days, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, while the polytheists were on the side of Qaʿīqiʿān, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions:
"Walk briskly around the House three times." And it is not a sunnah.
I said: Your people claim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ circled between Ṣafā and Marwah on his camel and that this is a sunnah. He said: They told the truth and they lied.

I said: What did they get right and what did they get wrong? He said: They were right that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went between Ṣafā and Marwah on his camel, and they were wrong that it is a sunnah. The people were not being pushed back or driven away from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he went around on a camel so that they could hear his words, see where he was, and so that their hands would not reach him.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ uncovered his right shoulder, touched the corner, and said the takbīr, then walked briskly for three circuits. When they reached the Yemeni corner and were out of sight of Quraysh, they walked normally, then they would appear before them walking briskly. Quraysh would say: They are like gazelles. Ibn ʿAbbās said: So it became a sunnah.

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became heavily ill and his pain grew severe,
he asked permission from his wives to be nursed in my house, and they permitted him.
So he went out between two men,
his feet dragging on the ground, between al-ʿAbbās and another man.
I informed Ibn ʿAbbās [of this], and he said: Do you know who the other man was, whom ʿĀʾishah did not name? I said: No.
He said: It was ʿAlī.
ʿĀʾishah said: The Prophet ﷺ said, after he had entered her house and his pain had grown severe:
"Pour over me seven water-skins whose ties have not been untied,
so that I may give instructions to the people."
She said: So we sat him down in a tub belonging to Ḥafṣah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and then we began pouring over him from those water-skins,
until he started to signal to us that we had done [enough].
She said: Then he went out to the people, led them in prayer, and addressed them.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ went out on one of his journeys with some of his Companions, and they set off walking.
The time for prayer came, and they could not find water to perform ablution.
So a man from among the people went off,
and came back with a cup containing a small amount of water. The Prophet ﷺ took it and performed ablution.
Then he spread his four fingers over the cup and said, "Get up and perform ablution." So
the people performed ablution until they had finished all the ablution they wanted,
and they were seventy or about that number.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he wiped over the two leather socks.
And ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar asked ʿUmar about that, and he said: Yes. If Saʿd tells you something from the Prophet ﷺ, do not ask anyone else about it.
And Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah said: Abū al-Naḍr informed me that Abū Salamah told him that Saʿd narrated to him, and ʿUmar said to ʿAbdullāh something similar.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to perform ablution for every prayer.
I said: And what did you all do? He said: We used to pray all the prayers with a single ablution as long as we did not break it.

segments_en: A Bedouin urinated in the mosque,
and the people rose against him to attack him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them, "Leave him alone,
and pour a bucket of water over his urine, or a large bucket of water. For you have been sent to make things easy,
and you have not been sent to make things difficult."

"I saw myself in a dream cleaning my teeth with a tooth-stick, and two men pulled at me, one of whom was older than the other. I handed the tooth-stick to the younger of the two, and it was said to me, 'Give precedence to the elder.'
So I gave it to the elder."

and some people were with him, and they asked him about the ritual bath.
He said: A ṣāʿ is enough for you.
A man said: It is not enough for me.
Jābir said: It was enough for one who had more hair than you, and was better than you,
and then he led us in prayer wearing a single garment.

perform his ablution as for prayer, and then bathe,
then he would run his hand through his hair,
until, when he thought that he had wetted his skin,
he would pour water over it three times,
then wash the rest of his body.
And she said: I used to bathe, I and the Messenger of Allah,
ﷺ, from a single vessel, scooping from it together.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"While Ayyūb, peace be upon him, was bathing naked, a swarm of golden locusts fell upon him, and he began scooping them into his garment. His Lord, Mighty and Majestic, called out to him: 'O Ayyūb, have I not made you free of need?' He said: 'Yes, my Lord, but I cannot do without Your blessings.'"

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a man who has relations with a woman but does not ejaculate. He said:
"He should wash whatever of the woman touched him, then perform ablution and pray."

segments_en: I entered the mosque with ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr,
and there was ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar sitting by the room of ʿĀʾishah, while people were performing the forenoon prayer in the mosque. We asked him about their prayer, and he said, "It is an innovation."
ʿUrwah said to him, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, how many ʿUmrahs did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform?" He said, "Four ʿUmrahs, one of them in Rajab."
We disliked to call him a liar or to contradict him, and we heard ʿĀʾishah brushing her teeth with the siwāk in the room.

ʿUrwah said, "Do you not hear, O Mother of the Believers, what Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān says?" She said, "What does he say?" He said, "He says that the Prophet ﷺ performed four ʿUmrahs, one of them in Rajab."
She said, "May Allah have mercy on Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never performed an ʿUmrah except that he was with him, and he never performed an ʿUmrah in Rajab at all."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and my heart retained it,
from Muhammad, peace be upon him, that he said:
"Whoever claims to be the son of someone other than his father, knowing that he is not his father, Paradise is forbidden to him."
He said: I met Abū Bakrah and mentioned that to him, and he said, "My two ears heard it and my heart retained it from Muhammad ﷺ."
ʿĀṣim said: I said, "O Abū ʿUthmān, two men have testified to this before you, and what men they are!"

He said, "As for one of them, he was the first to shoot an arrow in the cause of Allah, or in Islam," meaning Saʿd ibn Mālik, "and the other came from Ṭāʾif with some twenty men on foot," and he mentioned his merit.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Spend, and I will spend on you.' And he said: 'The Hand of Allah is full; spending does not diminish it,
pouring forth night and day.' And he said: 'Do you see what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? It has not diminished what is in His Hand,
and His Throne was upon the water,
and in His Hand is the balance; He lowers and raises.'"
{iʿtarāka}: it is of the form ifʿalta from "ʿarawtuhu," meaning I afflicted him,
and from it come yaʿrūhu and iʿtarānī. {Aakhidhun bi-nāṣiyatihā}: that is, within His dominion and authority.
ʿanīd, ʿanūd and ʿāndin are the same;
it is an emphasis of tyranny.
{istaʿmarakum}: He made you inhabitants who settle it;
aʿmartuhu al-dār, so it is a ʿumrā: I gave it to him.
{nakirahum}, ankarahum and istankarahum are the same. {Ḥamīdun majīd}: as if it is of the form faʿīl from mājid.
Maḥmūd is from ḥamida.
Sijjīl means severe and great.
Sijjīl and sijjīn: the lām and the nūn are sisters;
and Tamīm ibn Muqbil said: "And foot soldiers striking the white swords in the open, a striking by which the heroes urge one another, severe (sijjīnan)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Something about his Companions reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he gave a sermon and said:
"Paradise and the Fire were shown to me, and I have never seen the like of today in good and evil. If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much."

He said: No day was harder on the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than that. He said: They covered their heads and had muffled sobbing. He said: Then ʿUmar stood and said, "We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Prophet." He said: Then that man stood and said, "Who is my father?" He said, "Your father is so-and-so."
Then it was revealed: {O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if made plain to you, would trouble you.}

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about bitʿ, which is a honey drink,
and the people of Yemen used to drink it.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every drink that intoxicates is forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I brought a son of mine to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; I had treated his throat for uvula inflammation by pressing it, and he said:
"Why do you torment your children by pressing their throats? Use this Indian aloeswood,
for it has seven cures,
among them pleurisy: it is taken as snuff for throat inflammation,
and poured in the side of the mouth for pleurisy."
I heard al-Zuhrī say, "He explained two to us and did not explain five to us."
I said to Sufyān, "Maʿmar says 'aʿlaqtu ʿalayhi.'"
He said, "He did not memorize it; it is 'aʿlaqtu ʿanhu.'
I memorized it from the mouth of al-Zuhrī."
Sufyān described the boy's palate being rubbed with the finger, and Sufyān put his finger into his own palate,
meaning only that he lifted his palate with his finger,
and he did not say, "Treat anything for him by pressing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to assess the blood-money for accidental killing among the people of the towns at four hundred dinars, or its equivalent in silver. He would assess it according to the prices of camels: when they became expensive, he raised its value, and when they became cheap through abundance, he lowered its value. In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ it ranged between four hundred dinars and eight hundred dinars, or its equivalent in silver, eight thousand dirhams. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that among the owners of cattle it was two hundred cows, and for those whose blood-money was in sheep, two thousand sheep. He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The blood-money is an inheritance among the heirs of the slain person according to their kinship, and whatever remains goes to the male relatives on the father's side."

He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled concerning the nose, when it is cut off completely, the full blood-money; and if its tip is cut off, half the blood-money: fifty camels, or their equivalent in gold or silver, or one hundred cows or one thousand sheep. For the hand, when it is cut off, half the blood-money; for the foot, half the blood-money; for the wound reaching the membrane of the brain, a third of the blood-money: thirty-three and a third camels, or their value in gold, silver, cows or sheep. The wound penetrating the body cavity is the same. For the fingers, ten camels for each finger; for the teeth, five camels for each tooth. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the blood-money of a woman goes to her male relatives on the father's side, who inherit nothing from her except what remains after her heirs; and if she is killed, her blood-money is among her heirs, and they may put her killer to death. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The killer has nothing [of the inheritance]. If he has no other heir, then his heir is the person nearest to him, and the killer does not inherit anything."
Muḥammad said: All of this Sulaymān ibn Mūsā narrated to me, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The blood-money for a killing resembling intentional killing is made heavy, like the blood-money for intentional killing, but its perpetrator is not put to death."
He said: Khalīl added for us, from Ibn Rāshid:
"That is when Satan stirs up [trouble] among people so that blood is shed blindly, without enmity and without carrying weapons."

segments_en: "Every boy is held in pledge for his ʿaqīqah, which is slaughtered for him on the seventh day, and his head is shaved and [it] is smeared with blood."

Qatādah, when asked about the blood and how it should be done, would say: "When the ʿaqīqah is slaughtered, take a piece of wool from it and hold it to its jugular veins [to soak up the blood]. Then it is placed on the soft spot of the boy's head until it flows over his head like a thread. Afterwards his head is washed and shaved."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say: "Removing the harm is shaving the head."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ... And Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Anbārī narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Malik, meaning Ibn ʿAmr, narrated to us, from Dāwūd, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, [and] I think from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the ʿaqīqah, and he said:
"Allah does not love disobedience (ʿuqūq)."
It was as if he disliked the name. And he said:
"Whoever has a child born to him and wishes to offer a sacrifice for him, let him do so: for a boy, two equivalent sheep, and for a girl, one sheep."
And he was asked about the faraʿ, and he said:

"The faraʿ is right. But if you leave it until it becomes a strong young adult, a yearling she-camel or a two-year-old, then give it to a widow or mount someone on it in the cause of Allah, that is better than slaughtering it so that its flesh sticks to its fur, you spill your vessel and make your she-camel grieve."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the Pre-Islamic Era, when a boy was born to one of us, he would slaughter a sheep and smear the boy's head with its blood. When Allah brought Islam, we would slaughter a sheep, shave his head and smear it with saffron.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ said:

"If you shoot your arrow and mention the name of Allah, and you find the game the next day, and it has not fallen in water and there is no mark on it other than your arrow, then eat. But if a dog from another owner has mixed with your dogs, do not eat, for you do not know; perhaps the one that is not yours killed it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ said:
"If your shot falls into water and [the animal] drowns and dies, do not eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whatever you have trained, whether a dog or a hawk, and you send it out while mentioning the name of Allah, eat of what it catches for you."
I said: "Even if it kills?" He said:
"If it kills it and does not eat any of it, then it has only caught it for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said regarding game caught by a dog:
"If you send your dog and mention the name of Allah, then eat, even if it has eaten of it, and eat whatever your hands bring back to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a Bedouin,
called Abū Thaʿlabah, said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have trained hunting dogs, so give me a ruling about their catch." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"If you have trained dogs, then eat of what they catch for you."
He said: "Whether slaughtered or not slaughtered?" He said: "Yes."
He said: "Even if it has eaten of it?" He said:
"Even if it has eaten of it."
Then he said: "O Messenger of Allah, give me a ruling about my bow." He said:
"Eat whatever your bow brings back to you." He said:
"Whether slaughtered or not slaughtered?"
He said: "Even if it disappears from me?" He said:
"Even if it disappears from you, so long as it does not rot or you find no mark on it other than your arrow."
He said: "Give me a ruling about the vessels of the Magians, if we are forced to use them." He said:
"Wash them and eat from them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, similar to the narration of Musaddad, he said:
"Whoever keeps close to the ruler is put to trial." He added:
"And no servant draws nearer to the ruler except that he grows further from Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"For a person to give one dirham in charity during his lifetime is better for him than to give one hundred at the time of his death."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "If he leaves behind wealth, a bequest for parents and relatives." So the bequest was like that until the verse of inheritance abrogated it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, and from his maternal uncle ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Aḥmad, who said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: I memorized from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
"There is no orphanhood after puberty, and no silence for a whole day until night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a man
asked him, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, what are the major sins?" He said: "They are nine."
Then he mentioned the like of it, adding:
"And disobeying Muslim parents, and treating the Sacred House as lawful [to violate]; it is your qiblah, alive and dead."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr was killed on the day of Uḥud and had nothing but a single striped cloak. When we covered his head with it, his feet were exposed, and when we covered his feet, his head was exposed. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Cover his head with it, and put some idhkhir grass over his feet."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Healing is in three: a drink of honey, the cut of the cupper's blade, and cauterization with fire,
and I forbid my Ummah from cauterization."
The hadith was traced back to the Prophet ﷺ, and al-Qummī narrated it from Layth, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning honey and cupping.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh came to us at our home, where a man was complaining of a boil or a wound he had. He said, "What are you complaining of?" He said, "A boil on me, which has been hard on me."
He said, "Boy, bring me a cupper."
The man said to him, "What will you do with the cupper, Abū ʿAbdillāh?" He said, "I want to apply a cupping glass to it."
He said, "By Allah, a fly landing on me, or my garment touching me, pains me and is hard on me."
When Jābir saw his aversion to that, he said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'If there is any good in your remedies, it is in the cut of a cupper's blade, a drink of honey, or a burn of fire.'"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"But I do not like to be cauterized."
He said: So he brought a cupper, who made an incision, and what the man had been feeling went away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw a man dragging his lower garment and said, "Who are you from?" The man gave his lineage, and he was a man from Banū Layth, and Ibn ʿUmar recognized him. He said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with these two ears of mine say:
'Whoever drags his lower garment, intending by it nothing but arrogance, Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUthmān said: ʿUmar wrote to us while we were in Azerbaijan: "ʿUtbah ibn Farqad, this wealth is not from your own toil, nor from the toil of your father, nor from the toil of your mother. So feed the Muslims in their dwellings from what you fill yourself with in your own dwelling. And beware of luxury, the dress of the polytheists, and wearing silk, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade wearing silk, except thus."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised for us his two fingers, the middle finger and the index finger, and joined them together. Zuhayr said: ʿĀṣim said, "This is in the book."
He said: And Zuhayr raised his two fingers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They were discussing the Hour in the presence of Marwān, and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say..."
[He then narrated] like their two hadith, but did not mention the forenoon.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [One narrated] from the Prophet ﷺ and the other from himself, saying:
"The believer sees his sins as if he were sitting beneath a mountain, afraid it will fall on him,
while the wicked sees his sins like a fly that passes over his nose."
And he did so—Abū Shihāb [demonstrated] with his hand above his nose. Then he said:
"Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than a man who stops at a resting place where there is danger of destruction,
and with him is his mount carrying his food and drink.
He lays his head down and sleeps for a while,
then wakes up and his mount has gone,
until the heat and thirst grow severe on him, or as much as Allah willed.
He says, 'I will return to my place.'
So he returns and sleeps for a while,
then raises his head,
and there is his mount beside him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: O Allah, Muḥammad is only a human being; he becomes angry as human beings become angry. I have taken a covenant with You that You will not break: so any believer whom I have harmed, insulted, or lashed, make that an expiation for him and a means of nearness by which You bring him close to You on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"By Allah, if Allah wills, I never swear an oath and then see something else better than it, except that I make expiation for my oath
and do what is better." Or he said:
"Except that I do what is better and make expiation for my oath."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and al-Ḥasan al-Ḥulwānī,
and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd,
ʿAbd said: He informed me; and
the other two said: Yaʿqūb narrated to us,
—he is the son of Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd—my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn
Shihāb: Ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me,
and Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, that Abū Hurayrah
said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Trials will come in which the one sitting is better than the one standing, the one standing is better than the one walking, and the one walking is better than the one running. Whoever exposes himself to them, they will overtake him; and whoever finds a refuge in them, let him take refuge in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A silk cloak was given as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he wore it,
then prayed in it.
Then he turned away and took it off forcefully, as if he disliked it, and then said:
"This is not fitting for the God-fearing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Abū al-Naḍr,
from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾishah,

who said: I used to sleep in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with my legs in his qiblah. When he prostrated, he would nudge me and I would draw in my legs, and when he stood, I would stretch them out again. She said: And in those days the houses had no lamps.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jarīr urinated, then performed ablution and wiped over his leather socks. It was said to him, "Do you do this?"
He said, "Yes. I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ urinate, then perform ablution and wipe over his leather socks."
Al-Aʿmash said: Ibrāhīm said: This hadith used to please them because Jarīr's acceptance of Islam came after the revelation of Sūrat al-Māʾidah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ prostrated, he would spread his arms apart from his sides until we could see his armpits.
He said: And Ibn Bukayr said: Bakr narrated to us: the whiteness of his armpits.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the people were at Qubāʾ in the dawn prayer, someone came to them and said, "Qurʾān was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ tonight,
and he has been commanded to face the Kaaba, so face it."
Their faces were turned toward Syria,
so they turned around toward the Kaaba.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"Complete the bowing and the prostration. By Allah, I truly see you from behind my back when you bow and when you prostrate."
And in the narration of Saʿīd:
"When you bow and when you prostrate."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I presented to Mālik ibn Anas, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥah,
that he heard Anas ibn Mālik
say: Abū Ṭalḥah said to Umm Sulaym, "I have heard the voice of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, weak, and I can tell that he is hungry. Do you have anything?" She said, "Yes."

She brought out some barley loaves, then brought out a headscarf of hers and wrapped the bread in part of it, then tucked it into my hand and wrapped me with the rest of it, and sent me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: I took it to him and found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sitting in the mosque with people. I stood before them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Did Abū Ṭalḥah send you?" I said, "Yes." He said, "With food?" I said, "Yes."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to those with him, "Get up."

He said: They set off, and I walked ahead of them until I came to Abū Ṭalḥah and told him. Abū Ṭalḥah said, "Umm Sulaym, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has come with the people, and we do not have enough to feed them."
Umm Sulaym said, "Allah and His Messenger know best."
He said: Abū Ṭalḥah went out until he met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came forward with Abū Ṭalḥah until they both entered, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Bring what you have, Umm Sulaym."

She brought that bread, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that it be crumbled. Umm Sulaym squeezed out a small skin of ghee she had and seasoned it. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said over it whatever Allah willed him to say, and then said, "Admit ten."
He admitted them, and they ate until they were full, then left. Then he said, "Admit ten."
He admitted them, and they ate until they were full, then left. All the people ate and were satisfied, and the people numbered seventy or eighty men.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ fell ill, some of his wives mentioned a church they had seen in the land of Abyssinia,
called Māriyah.
Umm Salamah and Umm Ḥabībah, may Allah be pleased with them both, had gone to the land of Abyssinia,
and they mentioned its beauty and the images in it.
He raised his head and said:
"Those people, when a righteous man among them died, built a place of worship over his grave,
and then made those images in it.
Those are the worst of creation in the sight of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he would set his camel crosswise and pray facing it.
I said, "What if the camels are stirred up and move?"
He said, "He would take the saddle, set it upright, and pray toward its rear part," or he said, "its back." And Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to do this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said. (Transmission switches:) And ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me: my father narrated to us, from my grandfather,
ʿUqayl ibn
Khālid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb,
that he said: Ibn al-Musayyib said: Abū Hurayrah informed me
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Hour will not come until a fire emerges from the land of the Hijaz that illuminates the necks of the camels at Buṣrā."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he was asked about the Antichrist (the Dajjāl), and he said:
"Indeed, your Lord is not one-eyed. Indeed, he is blind in his right eye, as if it were a floating grape."
label: machine translation

segments_en: You will become eager for leadership,
and it will be a cause of regret on the Day of Resurrection,
for how excellent is the one who nurses, and how wretched is the one who weans."
Muḥammad ibn Bashshār said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥamrān narrated to us,
ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated to us,
from Saʿīd al-Maqburī,
from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḥakam,
from Abū Hurayrah, [as] his own statement.
label: machine translation

segments_en: So I was among those who stoned him. We stoned him at the prayer ground, and when the stones hurt him badly he fled, and we caught up with him at al-Ḥarrah and stoned him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy came to the Prophet ﷺ, and when she went back he set out with her.
Two men of the Anṣār passed by him, so he called them and said:
"She is only Ṣafiyyah."
They said: "Glory be to Allah!" He said:
"Indeed, Satan runs in the son of Adam like the flowing of blood."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr. Ibn Ayyūb said: Ismāʿīl ibn
Jaʿfar narrated to us: ʿAbdullāh ibn Dīnār informed me
that he heard ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar
saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to come to Qubāʾ riding and walking.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:

"O Allah, to You I have submitted, in You I have believed, upon You I have relied, to You I have turned in repentance, and by You I have disputed. O Allah, I seek refuge in Your might—there is no god but You—lest You lead me astray. You are the Ever-Living who does not die, while the jinn and mankind die."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh, from the account of

ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, when the people of the slander said about her what they said, and Allah cleared her of what they said. Each of them related to me a portion of the account, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: "But by Allah, I never thought that Allah would send down revelation about my innocence that would be recited,
and I considered myself too insignificant for Allah to speak about my affair in words that would be recited,

but I had hoped that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would see a dream in his sleep by which Allah would clear me." Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed: {Indeed, those who brought forth the slander...}, the ten verses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made me ride behind him one day, and he confided to me a matter that I will not tell to anyone among the people.
The place the Messenger of Allah ﷺ most loved to take cover behind when relieving himself was a mound or a cluster of palm trees. He said:
He entered the garden of a man from the Anṣār, and there was a camel. When it saw the Prophet ﷺ, it moaned and its eyes flowed with tears.
The Prophet ﷺ came to it and wiped behind its ears, and it became quiet. Then he said:
"Who is the owner of this camel?
To whom does this camel belong?"
A young man of the Anṣār came and said:
"It is mine, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"Do you not fear Allah regarding this animal that Allah has given you to own?
For it has complained to me that you keep it hungry and wear it out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm,
all from Sufyān,
— Abū Bakr said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us — from al-Zuhrī,
from Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ,
from ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit,
who traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ:
"There is no prayer for the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and they were
two companions who sat with Abū Hurayrah. They said: Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever performs a prayer in which he does not recite the Opening of the Book, it is deficient,"
saying it three times, similar to their narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If you knew—or: if they knew—what is in the front row, there would be a drawing of lots."
And Ibn Ḥarb said:
"The first row; it would only be by drawing lots."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥallim ibn Jaththāmah al-Laythī killed a man of Ashjaʿ in the time of Islam, and this was the first blood-money case the Messenger of Allah ﷺ decided upon. ʿUyaynah spoke up regarding the killing of the man of Ashjaʿ because he was from Ghaṭafān, and al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis spoke in defense of Muḥallim because he was from Khindif. Voices rose, and the dispute and uproar grew. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O ʿUyaynah, will you not accept the blood-money?"
ʿUyaynah said: "No, by Allah, not until I bring upon his women the war and grief that he brought upon my women."
He said: Then voices rose again, and the dispute and uproar grew. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O ʿUyaynah, will you not accept the blood-money?"

ʿUyaynah said the same thing again, until a man of Banū Layth called Mukaytil stood up, wearing his weapons and with a small leather shield in his hand. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I find no likeness for what this man did, at the dawn of Islam, except sheep that came to water: the first of them was struck with an arrow, so the last of them bolted. Set a precedent today and change it tomorrow." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Fifty now, in this very journey of ours, and fifty when we return to Madinah."

This was on one of his journeys. Muḥallim was a tall, dark man, and he was at the edge of the people. They kept on until he made his way through and sat before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his eyes streaming with tears. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I did what has reached you, and I repent to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. So ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to forgive me, O Messenger of Allah."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Did you kill him with your weapon at the dawn of Islam? O Allah, do not forgive Muḥallim!"

[He said it] in a loud voice. Abū Salamah added: So he got up, catching his tears with the edge of his cloak. Ibn Isḥāq said: His people claim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked forgiveness for him after that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came crying out for help to the Prophet ﷺ, about a slave girl of his, and said: "O Messenger of Allah!" He said:
"Woe to you, what is the matter with you?"
He said: "Something terrible. He saw his master with a slave girl of his, and became jealous, so he cut off his private parts."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bring me the man."
He was sought but could not be found. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Go, you are free."
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, who will help me?" He said:
"Every believer." Or he said: "Every Muslim."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was distributing a share, a man came forward and pressed upon him, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ poked him with a palm-stalk he had with him, and it scratched his face. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Come and take retaliation."
He said: "Rather, I pardon, O Messenger of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"Those who are fighting must withdraw from one another, the first and then the next, even if it is a woman."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The fingers are equal, and the teeth are equal: the incisor and the molar are equal; this one and that one are equal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The blood-money for the fingers of the hands and the feet is equal: ten camels for each finger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said in his sermon, while leaning his back against the Kaʿbah:
"For the fingers, ten each, ten each."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that for a blind eye that remains in its place, when it is destroyed, [the compensation is] a third of its blood-money; for a withered hand, when it is cut off, a third of its blood-money; and for a blackened tooth, when it is pulled out, a third of its blood-money.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There were two women, neighbors, between whom there was a quarrel. One of them threw a stone at the other and caused her to miscarry a boy whose hair had already grown, dead, and the woman herself died. So he ruled that the blood-money be paid by the ʿāqilah [the paternal relatives].
Her paternal uncle said: "O Messenger of Allah, she miscarried a boy whose hair had already grown."
The father of the killer said: "He is lying. By Allah, he did not cry out, nor drink, nor eat. Such a one is [to be] nullified." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"This is rhymed speech like the rhymed speech of the pre-Islamic days and their soothsaying! For the child there is a ghurrah."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: One of them was Mulaykah and the other was Umm Ghuṭayf.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar used to bring me in with the elders of Badr,
and some of them said, "Why do you bring this youth in with us,
when we have sons like him?" He said, "He is one of those whom you know."
[Ibn ʿAbbās] said: So one day he called them

and called me with them. He said: I did not think he had called me that day except to show them something of me. He said, "What do you say about {When the victory of Allah and the conquest come * and you see the people entering} until he finished the sūrah?"
Some of them said, "We were commanded to praise Allah and seek His forgiveness
when we are given victory and conquest."
And some of them said, "We do not know,"
or some of them said nothing.
Then he said to me, "O Ibn ʿAbbās, is that what you say?" I said, "No."

He said, "Then what do you say?" I said, "It is the appointed time of the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which Allah made known to him: {When the victory of Allah and the conquest come}, the conquest of Mecca,

and that is the sign of your appointed time: {Then glorify the praises of your Lord and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance}." ʿUmar said, "I know nothing about it except what you know."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "At your service [O Allah], with ʿUmrah and Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My dearest friend ﷺ advised me to do three things, which I do not abandon for anything: to fast three days of every month, not to sleep except after praying witr, and to pray the Ḍuḥā prayer, whether at home or while travelling.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Wakīʿ,
and Abū Usāmah, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid,
from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim,
from Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh,
who said: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon, the fourteenth night, and said:

"You will see your Lord just as you see this moon, without any crowding or harm in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in [performing] a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so."
Then he recited this verse: {So glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: Learn about your lineages enough to maintain your ties of kinship, for maintaining kinship ties brings love among family, increases wealth, and delays the end of one's life.
label: machine translation

segments_en: heard the Prophet ﷺ. (Another chain:) And Muḥammad narrated to me:
ʿAbdullāh ibn Rajāʾ narrated to us: Hammām informed us,
from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbdullāh,
who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAmrah informed me
that Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to him that he
heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Three men among the Children of Israel, a leper, a bald man, and a blind man, were such that Allah willed to test them,
so He sent an angel to them. The angel came to the leper
and said, 'What thing do you love most?' He said, 'A good complexion and good skin,
for people find me repulsive.' The angel wiped over him, and it went away from him,
and he was given a good complexion and good skin.
The angel said, 'Which property do you love most?' He said, 'Camels,' or he said, 'Cattle'; the narrator was unsure about that,
but the leper and the bald man,
one of them said camels,
and the other said cattle. So he was given a pregnant she-camel, ten months along.
The angel said, 'May Allah bless you in it.'
Then he came to the bald man and said, 'What thing do you love most?' He said, 'Good hair,
and that this be taken away from me,
for people find me repulsive.'
The angel wiped over him, and it went away,
and he was given good hair.
The angel said, 'Which property do you love most?' He said, 'Cattle.'
So the angel gave him a pregnant cow
and said, 'May Allah bless you in it.'
Then he came to the blind man and said, 'What thing do you love most?' He said, 'That Allah restore my sight to me,
so that I may see people with it.' The angel wiped over him,
and Allah restored his sight to him.
The angel said, 'Which property do you love most?' He said, 'Sheep.'
So he gave him a ewe about to give birth. Then the first two animals bred and this one gave birth,
so that one had a valley full of camels,
another had a valley full of cattle,
and the other had a valley full of sheep.
Then the angel came to the leper in his former form and appearance and said, 'I am a poor man;
the ropes [of my means] have been cut off for me on my journey,
and today there is no means of reaching my destination except through Allah and then through you.
I ask you, by the One who gave you the good complexion, good skin, and wealth, for a camel to carry me on my journey.'
The man said to him, 'The obligations are many.'
The angel said to him, 'It is as though I know you.
Were you not a leper whom people found repulsive, and poor, and then Allah gave you [wealth]?' He said, 'I inherited this from one great man after another.'
The angel said, 'If you are lying, may Allah return you to what you were.'
Then he came to the bald man in his former form and appearance
and said to him the same as he had said to the first,
and he replied to him just as the first had replied. So the angel said, 'If you are lying, may Allah return you to what you were.'
Then he came to the blind man in his former form and said, 'I am a poor man and a traveler, and the ropes [of my means] have been cut off for me on my journey,
and today there is no means of reaching my destination except through Allah,
and then through you. I ask you, by the One who restored your sight to you, for a sheep to carry me on my journey.'
The man said, 'I was blind and Allah restored my sight,
and I was poor and He enriched me,
so take whatever you wish.
By Allah, today I will not make it hard for you over anything that you take for the sake of Allah.'
The angel said, 'Keep your property, for you were only being tested,
and Allah is pleased with you and is displeased with your two companions.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever kills a sparrow or anything larger without its right, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will question him about it on the Day of Resurrection."
It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is its right?" He ﷺ said, "
Its right is that you slaughter it and eat it, and that you do not cut off its head and throw it away."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Sālim ibn ʿUbayd when a man among the people sneezed and said, "Peace be upon you."
Sālim said, "And upon you, and upon your mother."

Afterwards he said, "Perhaps you were upset by what I said to you." The man said, "I wish you had not mentioned my mother, whether for good or for ill." He said, "I only said to you what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said. While we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man among the people sneezed and said, 'Peace be upon you.' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
'And upon you, and upon your mother.' Then he said,
'When one of you sneezes, let him praise Allah.'"
He said: So he mentioned some words of praise. [The Prophet ﷺ said,]
'And let the one beside him say to him, "May Allah have mercy on you," and let him respond to them—meaning, to those who said it—"May Allah forgive us and you."'
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was talking with al-Qāsim in the presence of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

Al-Qāsim was a man who made mistakes in his speech, and he was the son of a concubine. ʿĀʾishah said to him, "What is the matter with you that you do not speak as this son of my brother speaks? I know where you went wrong.
This one was raised well by his mother, and you were raised by your mother." He said: Al-Qāsim became angry and resented her. Then, when he saw that ʿĀʾishah's food had been brought, he got up.
She said, "Where [are you going]?" He said, "To pray." She said, "Sit down."
He said, "I am going to pray."
She said, "Sit down, you disloyal one! I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'There is no prayer when the food is served, nor when one is pressed by the two filthy things [i.e., urine and stool].'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Dreams are of three kinds: some are terrifying visions from Satan, meant to grieve the son of Adam; some come from what a man is preoccupied with in his waking life, so he sees it in his sleep; and some are one part of forty-six parts of prophecy."

He said: I said to him, "Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "Yes, I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ saying openly, not secretly:
"Indeed, the family of Abū
" ʿAmr said: in the book of Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar there is a blank space "are not my allies.
My ally is only Allah and the righteous among the believers."
ʿAnbasah ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid added, from Bayān, from Qays, from ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
"But they have kinship, which I will maintain with its due moisture."
Meaning: I will join it with its due connection.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The best shroud is the ḥullah (a two-piece garment), and the best sacrificial animal is the horned ram."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The `Ishā' prayer was about to begin when a man stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have a need."
So he stood speaking privately with him until the people, or some of the people, grew drowsy. Then he led them in prayer. And he did not mention [anything about] ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a man enters the state of ihram for Hajj, then comes to Makkah and circles the House and [walks between] Ṣafā and Marwah, he has come out of ihram, and it is an ʿUmrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "There is no jalab and no janab."
Yaḥyā added in his narration: "in racing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Hour will not be established until my Ummah follows the ways of the generations before it,
handspan by handspan and forearm's length by forearm's length."
It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, like the Persians and the Romans?" He ﷺ said, "
And who else among the people [would it be] but those?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Dreams are of three kinds: a glad tiding from Allah, the talk of the soul, and a fright from Satan. So if one of you sees a dream that pleases him, let him relate it if he wishes; and if he sees something he dislikes, let him not relate it to anyone, and let him get up and pray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people used to depart in every direction, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should depart until his last act is [to be] at the House."
Zuhayr said: "They would depart in every direction."
And he did not say "in
label: machine translation

segments_en: Perform ablution after eating camel meat, and do not perform ablution after eating sheep meat. Perform ablution after drinking camel milk, and do not perform ablution after drinking sheep milk. Pray in the sheep pens, and do not pray in the camel pens."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The envoys of the disbelievers of Quraysh came to us, setting a blood-money for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and for Abū Bakr, for each one of them,
for whoever killed him or captured him.
While I was sitting in one of the gatherings of my people, Banū Mudlij, a man from them came forward until he stood over us as we sat,
and said, "O Surāqah,
I have just seen some dark shapes on the coast; I think they are Muhammad and his companions."
Surāqah said: I knew that it was them,
so I said to him, "They are not them,
but you saw so-and-so and so-and-so, who went off before our eyes."
Then I stayed in the gathering for a while,
then I got up and went in, and I ordered my slave girl to take my mare out, behind a hillock, and hold her for me, and I took my spear,
and went out with it from the back of the house,
and I lowered its tip to the ground
and held its upper end low until I reached my mare and mounted her,
and I urged her on, and she ran with me at a gallop until I drew near them,
then my mare stumbled with me,
and I fell off her and got up,
and I put my hand to my quiver and drew out the divining arrows,
and I cast lots with them to see whether I should harm them or not, and what I disliked came out. So I mounted my mare, disobeying the arrows,
and she ran with me until I heard the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was not looking around,
while Abū Bakr was turning around often, [then] my mare's forelegs sank into the ground up to the knees,
and I fell off her, then I scolded her and she rose,
but she could hardly pull her forelegs out.
When she stood upright,
there was, from the trace of her forelegs, a rising cloud of dust in the sky like smoke. I cast lots with the arrows again,
and what I disliked came out,
so I called out to them for safe-conduct, and they stopped.
I rode my mare until I came to them,
and when I met with what I met of being held back from them, it occurred to me that the cause of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would prevail. So I said to him, "Your people have set blood-money for you."
I told them the news of what people intended for them,
and I offered them provisions and goods,
but they took nothing from me and asked me for nothing, except that he said, "Keep us hidden."
So I asked him to write me a document of security,
and he ordered ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayrah,
who wrote it on a piece of leather,
then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿIkrimah,
the freed slave of Ibn ʿAbbās, [narrated] from Ibn ʿAbbās,

that he said: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib came to him and said, "May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! This Qur'an keeps slipping away from my chest, and I find that I am not able to hold on to it."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him,
"O Abū al-Ḥasan, shall I not teach you words by which Allah will benefit you and benefit those whom you teach, and by which what you have learned will be firmly fixed in your chest?"
He said, "Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah, teach me." He said,

"When it is the night of Friday, if you are able to rise in the last third of the night, do so, for it is an hour that is witnessed, and supplication in it is answered. My brother Jacob said to his sons:

'I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord'—meaning, until the night of Friday comes. If you are not able, then rise in the middle of it; if you are not able, then rise in the first part of it and pray four rakʿahs. In the first rakʿah recite the Opening of the Book and Sūrah Yā Sīn; in the second rakʿah the Opening of the Book and Ḥā Mīm ad-Dukhān; in the third rakʿah the Opening of the Book and Alif Lām Mīm Tanzīl as-Sajdah; and in the fourth rakʿah the Opening of the Book and Tabārak al-Mufaṣṣal. When you have finished the tashahhud, praise Allah and offer excellent praise to Allah, and send blessings upon me and do so well, and upon all the prophets, and ask forgiveness for the believing men and believing women and for your brothers who preceded you in faith. Then at the end of that say: O Allah, have mercy on me by my abandoning acts of disobedience for as long as You keep me alive, and have mercy on me that I not burden myself with what does not concern me, and grant me good insight into what pleases You with me. O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Possessor of Majesty and Honor, and of might that cannot be sought to be overcome, I ask You, O Allah, O Most Merciful, by Your majesty and the light of Your Face, that You make my heart cling to the memorization of Your Book as You have taught me, and grant me that I recite it in the manner that pleases You with me. O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Possessor of Majesty and Honor, and of might that cannot be sought to be overcome, I ask You, O Allah, O Most Merciful, by Your majesty and the light of Your Face, that You illuminate my sight with Your Book, that You loosen my tongue with it, that You relieve my heart with it, that You expand my chest with it, and that You wash my body with it; for none helps me toward the truth but You, and none grants it except You, and there is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Mighty. O Abū al-Ḥasan, do that for three Fridays, or five, or seven, and you will be answered, by the permission of Allah. By the One who sent me with the truth, it has never failed a believer."

ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās said: By Allah, ʿAlī waited only five or seven [Fridays] before he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the same sort of gathering and said, "O Messenger of Allah, in the past I would take in only four verses or so, and when I recited them to myself they would slip away. Today I learn forty verses or so, and when I recite them to myself it is as though the Book of Allah is between my eyes. And I used to hear a hadith, and when I repeated it, it would slip away; today I hear hadiths, and when I relate them I do not omit a single letter of them."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him at that point,
"A believer, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah, O Abū al-Ḥasan!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Those who love one another for the sake of My majesty will have pulpits of light, and the prophets and the martyrs will envy them.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was neither obscene nor given to obscenity, and he said:
"Among those dearest to me are those of you with the best character." And he said:
"Learn the Qur'an from four: from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd,
and Sālim, the freed slave of Abū Ḥudhayfah,
and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb,
and Muʿādh ibn Jabal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was begun of revelation was the true dream in sleep.
He would not see a dream except that it came true like the breaking of dawn.
Then he would go to Ḥirāʾ and engage in taḥannuth there, which is devotion, for a number of nights,
and he would take provisions for that. Then he would return to Khadījah and she would provision him for a similar period,
until the truth came upon him suddenly while he was in the cave of Ḥirāʾ. The angel came to him there and said, "Read!"
The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "
I said, 'I am not one who reads.' So he took hold of me and squeezed me until I could bear no more, then released me and said, 'Read!'
I said, 'I am not one who reads.'
So he took hold of me and squeezed me a second time until I could bear no more,
then released me and said, 'Read!'
I said, 'I am not one who reads.'
So he squeezed me a third time until I could bear no more,
then released me and said, 'Read in the name of your Lord who created.'"
[The angel recited] until he reached "what he did not know." Then he returned with it, his shoulder muscles trembling, until he entered upon Khadījah and said, "Cover me, cover me!"
So they covered him until the fear left him. Then he said, "
O Khadījah, what is wrong with me?"
And he told her what had happened, and said, "
I fear for myself."
She said to him, "Never! Rejoice,
for by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you.
You maintain family ties, you speak the truth, you bear the burdens of the weak, you honor the guest,
and you help those afflicted by calamities in the cause of truth."
Then Khadījah set out with him until she brought him to Waraqah ibn Nawfal ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Quṣayy, who was Khadījah's cousin, her father's brother's son.
He was a man who had converted to Christianity in the Jāhiliyyah,
and he used to write the Arabic script, and he would write from the Gospel in Arabic as much as Allah willed him to write.
He was a very old man who had gone blind. Khadījah said to him, "O my cousin, listen to your nephew."
Waraqah said, "O my nephew, what do you see?" The Prophet ﷺ told him what he had seen. Waraqah said, "This is the Nāmūs that was sent down upon Moses.
Would that I were a young man in it, would that I were alive
when your people drive you out."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Will they drive me out?"
Waraqah said, "Yes.
No man has ever come with what you have come with except that he was met with hostility,
and if I live to see your day, I will support you with strong support."
Soon after, Waraqah died,

and the revelation paused for a period, so that the Prophet ﷺ was grieved, as has reached us, with such grief that he went out several times in order to throw himself from the peaks of towering mountains.
Each time he reached the top of a mountain in order to throw himself down from it,
Jibrīl appeared to him and said, "O Muḥammad, you are truly the Messenger of Allah."
Thereupon his anxiety would calm and his soul would be at rest, and he would return.
Then when the pause in revelation grew long for him, he would go out for the same purpose,
and when he reached the top of a mountain, Jibrīl would appear to him and say the same to him.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Splitter of the daybreak" means the light of the sun by day,
and the light of the moon by night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And al-Layth,
and he mentioned another [chain] from Bukayr,
from Sulaymān ibn Yasār,
from Ḥamzah ibn ʿAmr al-Aslamī,
who said: "O Messenger of Allah, I find that I have the strength to fast while travelling." He said:
"If you wish, fast, and if you wish, break your fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by me at al-Abwāʾ or Waddān, and he was asked about the people of a household of the polytheists who are attacked at night,
and some of their women and children are hit. He said, "They are from them." And I heard him say,
"There is no protected pasture except for Allah and His Messenger ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The blood money for a person under covenant is half the blood money for a free [Muslim] man."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Love your beloved in moderation, for he may become someone you despise one day; and despise the one you despise in moderation, for he may become your beloved one day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: […] my brother from Banū Mujāshiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us one day to deliver a sermon and said:
"Indeed, Allah has commanded me […]"
And he narrated the hadith like the hadith of Hishām from Qatādah, and he added in it:
"And indeed, Allah has revealed to me that you should be humble, so that no one boasts over another and no one transgresses against another."
And he said in his narration:
"They will be followers among you, seeking neither family nor wealth."

So I said, "Will that really be, O Abū ʿAbd Allāh?" He said, "Yes, by Allah! I knew them in the Time of Ignorance, when a man would tend sheep for a tribe and have nothing with him but their slave girl, with whom he would have relations."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when a man from Yemen came and said, "Three men from the people of Yemen came to ʿAlī, disputing before him over a child. They had all had relations with one woman in a single period of purity." He said to two of them, "Be content to give the child to this one."
But they protested. Then he said to two [others], "Be content to give the child to this one."
But they protested. Then he said to two [others], "Be content to give the child to this one."

But they protested. So he said, "You are quarrelling partners. I will cast lots among you; whoever the lot falls to will have the child, and he must pay his two companions two-thirds of the blood-money."
So he cast lots among them and gave the child to the one on whom the lot fell. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed until his molars, or his back teeth, showed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever says after the dawn prayer: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise; in His hand is all good, and He has power over all things,' it is as if he had freed a slave from the descendants of Ismāʿīl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The baḥīrah is the she-camel whose milk was withheld for the idols (ṭawāghīt), so no one among the people would milk it.
The sāʾibah is the one they would let loose for their gods, so that nothing was loaded upon it.
He said: And Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I saw ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir al-Khuzāʿī dragging his intestines in the Fire;
he was the first to set loose the sāʾibah animals."
The waṣīlah is the young she-camel that gives birth first, in the first birth of the camels,
and then follows it with a second birth of a female.
They would let them loose for their idols if one of them was joined to the other with no male between them.
The ḥām is the stud camel that is allowed to mate a counted number of times;
when its mating was completed, they would dedicate it to the idols and exempt it from carrying loads, so nothing was loaded upon it, and they called it the ḥāmī.
And Abū al-Yamān said to me: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī: I heard Saʿīd
say, relating this to him: And Abū Hurayrah said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say something similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Beware of praising one another, for it is [like] slaughtering."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He never said] about anything, "I think it is such-and-such,"
except that it turned out as he thought.
While ʿUmar was sitting, a handsome man passed by him, and he said, "My assumption has surely been mistaken,
or this man is still upon his religion from the Jāhiliyyah,
or he was surely their soothsayer." The man was brought to him and called for,
and he said that to him.
The man said, "I have never seen a day like today, when a Muslim man is confronted with such [a thing]."
He said, "I adjure you to tell me."
He said, "I was their soothsayer in the Jāhiliyyah."
He said, "What is the most astonishing thing your female jinn brought you?" He said, "One day I was in the marketplace when she came to me, and I could recognize fear in her,

and she said, 'Have you not seen the jinn, their despair and their misery, after their being overturned, and their joining the young she-camels and their saddle-cloths?'" ʿUmar said, "He has spoken the truth.
"While I was beside their idols, a man came with a calf and slaughtered it,
and a crier cried out at it,
and I had never heard a crier with a louder voice than his, saying, 'O Jalīḥ!
The matter is one of success: a man of eloquent speech says, "There is no god but You."'
The people jumped up, [but] I said, 'I will not leave until I know what is behind this.' Then he called out, 'O Jalīḥ! The matter is one of success: a man of eloquent speech
saying, "There is no god but Allah."'
So I got up, and it was not long before it was said, 'This is a prophet.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: and others,
some of them adding to others,
and not all of them reported it in full; [rather,] one man among them [reported it] from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey,
and I was on a sluggish camel,
which was always at the back of the group.
The Prophet ﷺ passed by me and said, "Who is this?"
I said, "Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh." He said, "What is the matter with you?"
I said, "I am on a sluggish camel." He said, "Do you have a stick with you?" I said, "Yes." He said, "Give it to me."
I gave it to him, and he struck the camel and rebuked it,
and from that place it was at the front of the group. He said, "Sell it to me."
I said, "Rather, it is yours, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"Sell it to me. I have taken it for four dinars,
and you may have its back [to ride] until Medina."
When we drew near Medina, I began to set off. He said, "Where are you going?"
I said, "I have married a woman who was previously married." He said,
"Why not a young girl, whom you could play with and who could play with you?"
I said, "My father died and left behind daughters,
so I wanted to marry a woman who is experienced and previously married." He said, "That is it, then."
When we arrived in Medina, he said,
"O Bilāl, pay him and give him extra."
So he gave him four dinars and added one qīrāṭ.
Jābir said: The addition from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will never leave me.
And so the qīrāṭ never left the pouch of Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died while Abū Bakr was at as-Sunḥ (Ismāʿīl said: meaning in al-ʿĀliyah). ʿUmar stood up and began saying, "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has not died!"
She said: ʿUmar said, "By Allah, nothing came to my mind except that, and Allah will surely raise him, and he will surely cut off the hands and feet of men."
Then Abū Bakr came and uncovered the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and kissed him, saying, "May my father and mother be your ransom. You were good in life and in death.
By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, Allah will never make you taste death twice."
Then he went out and said, "O you who swear, take it easy."
When Abū Bakr spoke, ʿUmar sat down.
Abū Bakr praised Allah and extolled Him, and said, "Whoever used to worship Muhammad ﷺ, then Muhammad has died,
and whoever used to worship Allah, then Allah is Ever-Living and does not die."

And he recited: {Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die}, and: {Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If he were to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will never harm Allah at all, and Allah will reward the grateful.} He said: The people burst into sobbing and weeping. He said: The Anṣār gathered around Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah in the porch of Banū Sāʿidah and said, "From us a leader and from you a leader."
So Abū Bakr, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ went to them.
ʿUmar began to speak, but Abū Bakr silenced him.
ʿUmar used to say, "By Allah, I only did that because I had prepared a speech that pleased me, and I feared that Abū Bakr would not reach it."
Then Abū Bakr spoke, and he spoke most eloquently of all people. Among his words was: "We are the leaders and you are the ministers."
Ḥubāb ibn al-Mundhir said, "No, by Allah, we will not do that.
From us a leader and from you a leader."
Abū Bakr said, "No,
rather we are the leaders and you are the ministers. They [the Quraysh] are the best of the Arabs in homeland,
and the most noble of them in lineage. So pledge allegiance to ʿUmar or Abū ʿUbaydah."
ʿUmar said, "Rather, we pledge allegiance to you,
for you are our master, the best of us, and the most beloved of us to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
Then ʿUmar took his hand and pledged allegiance to him, and the people pledged allegiance too.
Someone said, "You have killed Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah."
ʿUmar said, "Allah has killed him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The group whom ʿUmar had appointed gathered and consulted one another.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said to them, "I am not the one who will compete with you for this matter,
but if you wish, I will choose [a leader] for you from among yourselves."
So they entrusted that to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
When they had given ʿAbd al-Raḥmān authority over their affair, the people turned to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
so much so that I did not see anyone from the people following that group or walking in their footsteps.
The people turned to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, consulting him during those nights, until it was the night after which we woke in the morning
and pledged allegiance to ʿUthmān. Al-Miswar said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān came knocking at my door after part of the night had passed, and he knocked until I woke up. He said, "I see you are sleeping.
By Allah, I have not had much sleep this night.
Go and call al-Zubayr and Saʿd."
So I called them for him, and he consulted them. Then he called me and said, "Call ʿAlī for me."
I called him, and [ʿAbd al-Raḥmān] spoke with him privately until a good part of the night had passed.
Then ʿAlī got up and left him,
hopeful [of being chosen],
and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān had been fearing something from ʿAlī.
Then he said, "Call ʿUthmān for me."
I called him, and he spoke with him privately until the muʾadhdhin for the dawn prayer separated them.
When he had led the people in the dawn prayer, and that group had gathered at the minbar,
he sent for those of the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār who were present,
and he sent for the commanders of the armies, who had come for that Hajj with ʿUmar.
When they had gathered, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān recited the testimony of faith and then said, "To proceed: O ʿAlī,
I have looked into the matter of the people, and I have not seen them regard anyone as equal to ʿUthmān,
so do not make a way [of blame] against yourself."
Then he said [to ʿUthmān], "I pledge allegiance to you on the Sunnah of Allah and His Messenger and of the two caliphs after him."
So ʿAbd al-Raḥmān pledged allegiance to him,
and the people pledged allegiance to him: the Muhājirūn, the Anṣār, the commanders of the armies, and the Muslims.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The collector of unjust taxes will not enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered the mosque when the sun had set, and the Prophet ﷺ was sitting. He said,
"O Abū Dharr, do you know where this goes?"
I said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said,
"It goes until it asks permission to prostrate, and it is given permission. It is as though it will be told: 'Rise from where you came,' and it will rise from its place of setting."
He said: Then he recited,
"And that is its place of rest."
He said: And that is the recitation of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Disputing about the Qurʾān is disbelief."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Whoever I take away his two beloved ones [his eyes], and he is patient and seeks reward from Allah, I will not accept for him any reward less than Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: O people,
listen to me [as I tell] you what I say,
and let me hear from you what you say,
and do not go away and say, "Ibn ʿAbbās said,
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Whoever circumambulates the House should circumambulate from behind the Ḥijr,"
and do not call it the Ḥaṭīm,
for in the Time of Ignorance a man would swear an oath and then throw down his whip, or his sandal, or his bow.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I memorized part of it,
and Maʿmar confirmed it for me from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr,
from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah
and Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam,
one of them adding to the other. They both said: The Prophet ﷺ set out in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyyah with a little over a thousand of his Companions.
When he reached Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, he garlanded the sacrificial animal and marked it,
and entered the state of iḥrām from there for ʿUmrah,
and he sent ahead a scout of his from the tribe of Khuzāʿah.
The Prophet ﷺ continued on until he was at Ghadīr al-Ashṭāṭ,
where his scout came to him and said: Quraysh have gathered forces against you,
and they have gathered the Aḥābīsh against you,
and they will fight you, turn you away from the House, and prevent you. So he said: "
Advise me, people.
Do you think I should move against the families and children of those who want to turn us away from the House?
If they come out to us, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will have cut off a scout of the polytheists,
and if not, we will have left them plundered and ruined."
Abū Bakr said: Messenger of Allah,
you set out intending only this House,
not wishing to kill anyone or fight anyone, so proceed toward it,
and whoever turns us away from it, we will fight him. He said: "
Go forward in the name of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had the best character of all people.
I had a brother called Abū ʿUmayr—I think [the narrator said] he had been weaned—and whenever the Prophet ﷺ came, he would say,
"O Abū ʿUmayr, what did the nughayr do?"
It was a small sparrow he used to play with.
Sometimes the time of prayer would arrive while he was in our house,
and he would order the mat beneath him to be swept and sprinkled with water.
Then he would stand, and we would stand behind him, and he would lead us in prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥamnah bint Jaḥsh said: "I used to suffer from very heavy, severe bleeding [outside my menstrual period]. So I went to the Prophet ﷺ to seek his ruling and to inform him, and I found him in the house of my sister Zaynab bint Jaḥsh. I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I suffer from very heavy, severe bleeding. What do you command me regarding it? It has prevented me from fasting and prayer.' He said: "
"I recommend that you use cotton, for it takes away the blood."
She said, "It is more than that." He said, "Then bind [it] tightly."
She said, "It is more than that." He said, "Then use a cloth."
She said, "It is more than that; it is simply a gushing flow." So the Prophet ﷺ said: "
"I will command you with two things; whichever of them you do will suffice you. But if you are able to do both, then you know best." Then he said: "

"This is only a kick from Satan. So count yourself as menstruating for six or seven days, in the knowledge of Allah, then wash. When you see that you are clean and purified, pray for twenty-four nights or twenty-three nights, along with their days, and fast and pray, for that will suffice you. And do likewise every month, as [other] women menstruate and as they become pure at the appointed time of their menstruation and their purity. If you are able to delay the Ẓuhr prayer and hasten the ʿAṣr prayer, then wash when you become pure and pray Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr together; then delay the Maghrib prayer and hasten the ʿIshāʾ prayer, then wash and combine the two prayers, do so. And wash with the dawn and pray. Do likewise, and fast if you are able to do that."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
"And this is the more pleasing of the two ways to me.""
label: machine translation

segments_en: In Mecca, and Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd al-Jawharī, both said: Al-Aḥwaṣ ibn Jawwāb narrated to us,
from Suʿayr ibn al-Khims,
from Sulaymān al-Taymī,
from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī,
from Usāmah ibn Zayd,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has a kindness done to him and says to the one who did it, 'Jazāka Allāhu khayran' (may Allah reward you with goodness), has indeed gone to the utmost in praise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: By the One in whose hand is my soul, were it not that some men among the believers would not be content to stay behind me,
and I cannot find the means to carry them,
I would never stay behind from any expedition that fights in the cause of Allah.
By the One in whose hand is my soul, I would love to be killed in the cause of Allah, then brought back to life,
then be killed, then brought back to life,
then be killed, then brought back to life, then be killed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If you are attacked at night, let your watchword be: Ḥā Mīm, they will not be helped."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I was sitting
with Sulaymān ibn Yasār, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jābir came and spoke to Sulaymān ibn Yasār.
Then Sulaymān ibn Yasār turned to us and said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jābir narrated to me that his father narrated to him that he
heard Abū Burdah al-Anṣārī say:
I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
"Do not flog more than ten lashes, except in one of the prescribed punishments (ḥudūd) of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am with My servant when he remembers Me and his lips move with Me.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The eye that stays awake in the cause of Allah is forbidden to the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah,] the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out before [the Battle of] Badr, and when he reached Harrat al-Wabarah, a man caught up with him who was known for his courage and valor. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were glad when they saw him. When he reached him, he said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "I have come to follow you and to share in [the spoils] with you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "
Do you believe in Allah and His Messenger?"
He said, "No." He said, "
Then go back, for I will not seek help from a polytheist."

She said: Then he proceeded until we were at the tree [of Dhul-Hulayfah], and the man caught up with him and said to him what he had said the first time, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him what he had said the first time. He said, "
Then go back, for I will not seek help from a polytheist."
She said: Then he went back, and he caught up with him at al-Baydāʾ and said to him what he had said the first time. [The Prophet ﷺ said,] "
Do you believe in Allah and His Messenger?" He said, "Yes."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Then come along."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Angels came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was asleep, and some of them said, "He is asleep."
Others said, "The eye sleeps, but the heart is awake."
Then they said, "This companion of yours has a parable, so give him a parable."
Some of them said, "He is asleep."
And others said, "The eye sleeps, but the heart is awake."
They said, "His example is that of a man who built a house,
and set up a banquet in it, and sent out a caller to invite people.
Whoever answered the caller entered the house and ate from the banquet,
and whoever did not answer the caller did not enter the house and did not eat from the banquet."
Then they said, "Interpret it for him so that he understands it." Some of them said, "He is asleep."
And others said, "The eye sleeps, but the heart is awake."
They said, "The house is Paradise,
and the caller is Muhammad ﷺ. Whoever obeys Muhammad ﷺ has obeyed Allah,
and whoever disobeys Muhammad ﷺ has disobeyed Allah,
and Muhammad ﷺ is a distinction between people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever is a worker for us, let him take a wife; if he has no servant, let him take a servant; and if he has no dwelling, let him acquire a dwelling."
He said: Abū Bakr said: I was informed that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever takes anything beyond that is a misappropriator or a thief."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hajj is a form of jihad, and ʿUmrah is voluntary."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A young slave woman
who was black and belonged to a clan of the Arabs, was set free by them,
and she stayed with them. She said: One of their little girls went out wearing a red leather-strap sash. She said: She put it down, or it fell from her,
and a kite passed by it while it was lying there,
