and mistook it for meat and snatched it up. She said: They searched for it but did not find it, and they accused me of taking it. She said: They began to search me, even searching her private parts. She said: By Allah, I was standing with them
when the kite passed by and dropped it. She said: It fell among them. I said: This is what you accused me of, as you claimed, while I was innocent of it,
and here it is. She said: Then she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and embraced Islam.

ʿĀʾishah said: She had a tent in the mosque, or a small room. She said: She used to come to me and talk with me. She said: She would never sit with me except that she said: "The day of the sash was one of the wonders of our Lord; indeed, it rescued me from the land of disbelief." ʿĀʾishah said: I asked her, "What is the matter with you? You never sit with me except that you say this." She said: Then she told me this account.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O people, give charity."
Then he passed by the women and said, "
O company of women, give charity,
for I have seen that you are the majority of the people of the Fire."
They said, "And why is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "
You curse frequently and are ungrateful to your husbands.
I have not seen anyone more deficient in intellect and religion who can overcome the mind of a firm man than one of you, O company of women."
Then he left. When he reached his house, Zaynab, the wife of Ibn Masʿūd, came asking permission to enter, and it was said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is Zaynab." He said, "Which Zaynab?"
It was said, "The wife of Ibn Masʿūd." He said, "
Yes, let her in."
So she was admitted. She said, "O Prophet of Allah, today you commanded charity,
and I have some jewelry of mine,
and I wanted to give it in charity,
but Ibn Masʿūd claimed that he and his children are more deserving of what I give in charity to them." The Prophet ﷺ said, "
Ibn Masʿūd spoke the truth.
Your husband and your children are the most deserving of those to whom you give charity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar delivered a sermon from the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "The prohibition of wine has been revealed,
and it is made from five things: grapes, dates, wheat, barley, and honey.
And wine is whatever clouds the intellect.
There are three things I wish the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not left us without giving us a clear instruction about: the grandfather, the kalālah, and some of the categories of ribā."
[The narrator] said: I said, "O Abū ʿAmr, what about something that is made in Sind from rice?"
He said, "That did not exist in the time of the Prophet ﷺ," or he said, "in the time of ʿUmar."
And Ḥajjāj said, on the authority of Ḥammād, on the authority of Abū Ḥayyān: "raisins" in place of "grapes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Beware of taking the backs of your riding animals as pulpits, for Allah has only subjected them to you so that they may carry you to a land you would not otherwise reach except with great hardship. And He has made the earth for you, so attend to your needs upon it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to the Prophet ﷺ,
"Your uncle, the misguided old man, has died,
so who will bury him?" He said: "
Go and bury your father, and do not do anything new until you come to me."
So I buried him, then I came, and he ordered me, so I bathed, and he supplicated for me,
and he mentioned a supplication that I did not memorize.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Three are all [people] whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is bound to help: the one who strives in the cause of Allah, the one who marries desiring chastity, and the contracted slave who desires to pay [his freedom price]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever washes him, let him perform the full bath; and whoever carries him, let him perform ablution." He means the deceased.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥarām died,
leaving a debt, so I asked the Prophet ﷺ for help with his creditors, that they might reduce something of his debt.
The Prophet ﷺ asked them, but they did not do so.
Then the Prophet ﷺ said to me,
"Go and sort your dates into their kinds,
the ʿAjwah on its own,
and the ʿidhq of Zayd on its own,
then send for me." So I did so.
Then I sent for the Prophet ﷺ, and he sat on top of it,
or in the middle of it, and then said, "Measure out for the people."
So I measured out for them until I had paid them in full what was owed to them, and my dates remained
as if nothing had been taken from them.
And Firās reported from ash-Shaʿbī: Jābir narrated to me from the Prophet ﷺ:
He kept measuring out for them until he had paid it off.
And Hishām said, from Wahb, from Jābir: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Pick his dates and pay him in full."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, on the authority of Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Zayd ibn Aslam,
from Abū Ṣāliḥ as-Sammān,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Horses are a reward for one man, a covering for another, and a burden for another. As for the one for whom they are a reward, he is a man who tethers them in the cause of Allah, giving them a long tether in a meadow or a garden. Whatever they eat within the length of that tether in the meadow or garden is counted as good deeds for him. And if the horse breaks its tether and runs over one or two hills, its footprints
And in the narration of al-Ḥārith: "

and its dung are good deeds for him. And if it passes by a river and drinks from it, though he did not intend to water it, that too is counted as good deeds. So it is a reward for him. Another man ties them up for self-sufficiency and to remain independent of others, and he does not forget Allah's due in their necks or their backs; so for him they are a covering. And another man ties them up out of pride, showing off, and hostility toward the people of Islam; so for him they are a burden."
The Prophet ﷺ was asked about donkeys, and he said: "
Nothing has been revealed to me about them except this comprehensive, unique verse: {So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever we appoint to a task and we provide him with a provision, then whatever he takes beyond that is misappropriation (ghulūl)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of them added to the other, and others besides them, I heard him narrating it from Saʿīd, who said: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās in his house,
when he said, "Ask me." I said, "O Abū ʿAbbās, may Allah make me your ransom! In Kūfah there is a storyteller called Nawf,
who claims that he [al-Khiḍr's companion] is not the Moses of the Children of Israel."
As for ʿAmr, he said to me that [Ibn ʿAbbās] said: "The enemy of Allah has lied."
As for Yaʿlā, he said to me that Ibn ʿAbbās said: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Moses, the messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, once reminded the people [with a sermon], until the eyes overflowed
and the hearts softened, and he turned to leave. Then a man caught up with him
and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you?' He said, 'No.'

So Allah rebuked him, for he did not attribute knowledge to Allah. It was said [to him], 'Yes, [there is].' He said, 'My Lord, where is he?' He said, 'At the meeting of the two seas.' He said, 'My Lord, give me a sign by which I will know that place.'"
Then ʿAmr said to me that he said:
"Where the fish leaves you."
And Yaʿlā said to me that he said:
"Take a dead fish [at the place] where the soul is breathed into it."
So he took a fish and put it in a basket, and said to his servant, "I only charge you with this: tell me when the fish leaves you."

He said, "That is not much to ask." That is the saying of Allah, mighty is His mention: {And [remember] when Moses said to his servant} — Joshua son of Nūn (this is not from Saʿīd). He said: While he was in the shade of a rock in a damp place,
the fish stirred while Moses was asleep.
His servant said, "I will not wake him," but when he awoke, he forgot to tell him. And the fish stirred
until it entered the sea. Allah held back the flow of the sea from it, so that its trace was like [a mark] in a rock. ʿAmr said to me: Its trace was like this, in a rock,

and he made a circle with his two thumbs and the fingers next to them. {We have certainly suffered fatigue from this journey of ours.} He said: "Allah has removed fatigue from you." (This part is not from Saʿīd.) He told him.
So they returned and found al-Khiḍr. ʿUthmān ibn Abī Sulaymān said to me: on a green carpet in the middle of the sea. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: wrapped in his garment, with one end of it under his feet
and the other end under his head.
Moses greeted him with salām,
and he uncovered his face
and said, "Is there [a greeting of] peace in my land? Who are you?" He said, "I am Moses."
He said, "Moses of the Children of Israel?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "What brings you?" He said, "I came so that you may teach me some of what you have been taught of right guidance."
He said, "Is it not enough for you that the Torah is in your hands
and that revelation comes to you?
O Moses, I have knowledge which it is not fitting for you to know, and you have knowledge which it is not fitting for me to know."

Then a bird took [water] from the sea with its beak, and he said, "By Allah, my knowledge and your knowledge, compared with the knowledge of Allah, are only like what this bird took from the sea with its beak."
Then they boarded a boat, and found small ferries carrying the people of this shore to the people of the other shore. They recognized him
and said, "The righteous servant of Allah." (We said to Saʿīd, "Al-Khiḍr?" He said, "Yes.") "We will not charge him a fare."
But he made a hole in it and drove a peg into it.

Moses said, {Have you made a hole in it to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing} (Mujāhid said: a awful thing). He said, {Did I not say that you would never be able to have patience with me?} The first was out of forgetfulness, the middle was a condition, and the third was deliberate. He said, {Do not hold me to account for what I forgot, and do not burden me with hardship in my affair.} [Then]
they met a boy and he killed him. Yaʿlā said: Saʿīd said: He found boys playing,
and he took a disbelieving, handsome boy and laid him down,
then slaughtered him with a knife.

He said, {Have you killed an innocent soul, [who had killed] no soul? You have done a terrible thing, though he had not committed a sin.} Ibn ʿAbbās used to read it "zakiyyah" or "zākiyah," meaning a Muslim, like your saying "a pure boy." {Then they set out,

and found a wall about to collapse, and he set it straight.} Saʿīd said: with his hand like this, and he raised his hand and it stood straight. Yaʿlā said: I think Saʿīd said: he wiped it with his hand and it stood straight.
{If you wished, you could have taken a payment for it.} Saʿīd said: a payment that we could eat. {For there was behind them}
{there was ahead of them} (Ibn ʿAbbās read it: ahead of them was a king.) They claim, from someone other than Saʿīd, that he was Hadad ibn Badad, and the boy who was killed,
they claim, was named Jaysūr. {A king who seizes every boat by force.}
{So I intended that, when it passed by him, he would leave it because of its defect,}
and when they had passed, they would repair it and benefit from it. Some say they sealed it with a bottle, and some say with tar.
{As for the boy, his parents were believers,
and he was a disbeliever, and we feared that he would burden them with transgression and disbelief,}

that his love would lead them to follow him in his religion. {So we wished that their Lord would give them in exchange one better than him in purity} — in response to his words, "Have you killed an innocent soul?" — {and closer in kinship}, meaning they would be more merciful to him than they were to the first.
The one who killed [him] was al-Khiḍr. Someone other than Saʿīd claimed that they were given a girl in exchange.
As for Dāwūd ibn Abī ʿĀṣim, he said, from more than one [source], that it was a girl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, the Corner (the Black Stone) and the Station (of Ibrāhīm) are two sapphires from the sapphires of Paradise. Allah effaced their light, and had He not effaced their light, they would have illuminated everything between the east and the west."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever is given his share of gentleness has been given his share of good, and whoever is deprived of his share of gentleness has been deprived of his share of good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting in the circle of ʿAbdullāh when Hudhayfah came and stood over us,
greeted us with salām, and then said, "Hypocrisy was sent down upon a people better than you."
Al-Aswad said, "Glory be to Allah!
Allah says: {Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire}." So ʿAbdullāh smiled,
and Hudhayfah sat down in a corner of the mosque.
Then ʿAbdullāh got up and his companions dispersed, and he threw pebbles at me.
So I came to him, and Hudhayfah said, "I was surprised at his laughing,
although he knew what I had said.
Hypocrisy was indeed sent down upon a people who were better than you,
then they repented, and Allah accepted their repentance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The one performing ʿUmrah recites the Talbiyah until he touches the Stone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Hamdānī,
that Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī
said: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as he was distributing some shares, Dhū al-Khuwayṣirah, a man from Banū Tamīm, came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, be just!"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Woe to you! Who will be just if I am not just? I would be ruined and a loser if I were not just."
Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to strike his neck."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Leave him, for he has companions such that one of you would regard his prayer as small beside their prayer, and his fasting beside their fasting. They recite the Qur'an, but it does not go beyond their collarbones. They pass through Islam as the arrow passes through the game. One looks at its blade and finds nothing on it; then he looks at its metal band and finds nothing on it; then he looks at its shaft, which is the wood, and finds nothing on it; then he looks at its feathers and finds nothing on them. It has passed ahead of the dung and the blood.
Their sign is a black man, one of whose arms is like a woman's breast, or like a piece of flesh that quivers. They will emerge at a time of division among the people."

Abū Saʿīd said: I bear witness that I heard this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I bear witness that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, fought them while I was with him. He ordered that man to be sought, and he was found and brought, until I looked at him and he matched the description that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had given.

segments_en: My uncle brought me [to Madinah] in the Pre-Islamic Period of Ignorance and sold me to al-Ḥubāb ibn ʿAmr, the brother of Abū al-Yasar ibn ʿAmr. I bore him ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥubāb, and then he died. His wife said, "By Allah, now you will be sold off to pay his debt." So I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am a woman from outside Qays ʿAylān. My uncle brought me to Madinah in the Pre-Islamic Period of Ignorance and sold me to al-Ḥubāb ibn ʿAmr, the brother of Abū al-Yasar ibn ʿAmr, and I bore him ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥubāb. Now his wife says, 'By Allah, now you will be sold off to pay his debt.'"
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Who is the heir of al-Ḥubāb?"
It was said, "His brother, Abū al-Yasar ibn ʿAmr." So he sent for him and said:
"Set her free. And when you hear that slaves have come to me, come to me and I will compensate you for her."
She said: So they set me free, and slaves came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he compensated them for me with a slave boy.

segments_en: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said: I heard Bushayr say,
I heard Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathmah say,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of fresh fruit for dried dates,
and he permitted the ʿarīyyah, that it be sold by estimate, so that its owners may eat it as fresh dates.
And on another occasion Sufyān said: Except that he permitted the ʿarīyyah, that its owners sell it by estimate and eat it as fresh dates.
He said: It is the same.
Sufyān said: I said to Yaḥyā, while I was a young boy, "The people of Makkah say that the Prophet ﷺ permitted the sale of the ʿarāyā."
He said, "What do the people of Makkah know?" I said, "They narrate it from Jābir." So he fell silent.
Sufyān said: I only meant that Jābir was from the people of Madīnah.
Sufyān was asked, "Does it not contain a prohibition on selling fruit until its goodness appears?" He said, "No."

segments_en: I saw ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, say, "O ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,
go to the Mother of the Believers, ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and say: 'ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb sends you greetings of peace.'
Then ask her whether I may be buried with my two companions."
She said, "I had wanted it for myself,
but today I will prefer him over myself."
When he [ʿAbdullāh] returned, [ʿUmar] said to him, "What do you have?" He said, "She has given you permission, O Commander of the Faithful."
He said, "Nothing was more important to me than that resting place.
So when I have died, carry me, then give greetings of peace, and say: 'ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb asks permission.'
If she permits me, bury me [there],
and if not, return me to the graveyards of the Muslims.
I know of no one more entitled to this matter than this group of men with whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pleased when he died.
Whomever they choose as successor after me is the caliph,
so listen to him and obey."
Then he named ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ṭalḥah, az-Zubayr, ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.
A young man from the Anṣār came in to him and said, "Rejoice, O Commander of the Faithful, in the glad tidings of Allah.
You had precedence in Islam, as you know,
then you were made caliph and you ruled with justice,
and then, after all this, martyrdom."
He said, "I wish, O son of my brother, that all of that would be even, neither against me nor for me. I advise the caliph after me to treat the first Emigrants well,
that he recognize their right,
and that he preserve their sanctity.
And I advise him to treat the Anṣār well, those who made their home in the city and [settled] in faith before them: that he accept from those among them who do good,
and pardon those among them who do wrong.
And I advise him regarding the covenant of Allah and the covenant of His Messenger ﷺ: that he fulfill their covenant with them,
that he fight on their behalf,
and that they not be burdened beyond their capacity."

but I was taken [as a captive] when I was a boy."

segments_en: I was with ʿĀʾishah, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, when an Iraqi man came to her and said, "Which shroud is best?" She said, "Woe to you! What harm does it do you?" He said, "Mother of the Believers, show me your copy of the Qurʾān."
She said, "Why?" He said, "So that I may arrange the Qurʾān according to it, for it is being recited without arrangement."
She said, "What harm does it do you which part you recite first?
The first thing to be revealed of it was a sura from the mufaṣṣal, in which Paradise and the Fire are mentioned, until, when people had turned to Islam, the lawful and the unlawful were revealed.
Had the first thing revealed been, 'Do not drink wine,'
they would have said, 'We will never give up wine.' And had it been, 'Do not commit adultery,'
they would have said, 'We will never give up adultery.'

Indeed, there was revealed in Makkah to Muhammad ﷺ, while I was a young girl playing, {Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more grievous and more bitter}. And Sūrat al-Baqarah and Sūrat an-Nisāʾ were not revealed except while I was with him."
He said: So she brought out the copy of the Qurʾān for him, and she dictated to him the order of the suras.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "While a man was tending his sheep, a wolf came and took a sheep. Its owner came and snatched it back from him. The wolf said, 'How will you do with it on the Day of the Predator, a day when it will have no shepherd but me?'"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I believe in that, and so do Abū Bakr and ʿUmar."
Abū Salamah said: Neither of them was present among the people on that day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting beside Ibn ʿUmar while we were waiting for the funeral of Umm Abān, the daughter of ʿUthmān, and ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān was with him. Then Ibn ʿAbbās came, being led by a guide, and I think he had been told where Ibn ʿUmar was.

He came until he sat beside me, so I was between the two of them. Then there was a sound of crying from the house, and Ibn ʿUmar said, as if urging ʿAmr to get up and forbid them, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'The dead person is punished because of the weeping of his family.'"
[The narrator] said: ʿAbdullāh [ibn ʿUmar] reported it without qualification.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: We were with the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, until, when we were at al-Baydāʾ, he saw a man resting beneath a tree. He said to me, "Go and find out for me who that man is."
So I went, and it was Ṣuhayb.
I returned to him and said, "You ordered me to find out who that was, and it is Ṣuhayb."
He said, "Tell him to join us."
I said, "His family is with him."

He said, "Even if his family is with him." Ayyūb sometimes said, "Tell him to join us." Then when we arrived, it was not long before the Commander of the Faithful was struck down. Ṣuhayb came saying, "Oh my brother! Oh my companion!"
ʿUmar said, "Do you not know, or have you not heard," and Ayyūb said, "or he said: Did you not know, or did you not hear, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'The dead person is punished because of some of the weeping of his family.'"
He said: ʿAbdullāh reported it without qualification, but ʿUmar said "some."
Then I got up and went in to ʿĀʾishah and told her what
Ibn ʿUmar had said. She said, "No, by Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never said:
'The dead person is punished because of the weeping of anyone.' Rather, he said:
'Allah increases the disbeliever in punishment because of the weeping of his family. And it is Allah who makes [people] laugh and weep, and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another.'"

Ayyūb said: Ibn Abī Mulaykah said: al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad told me: When the statement of ʿUmar and Ibn ʿUmar reached ʿĀʾishah, she said, "You are reporting to me from people who are neither liars nor accused of lying, but hearing can make mistakes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The one who works to collect charity (ṣadaqah) with honesty is like the fighter in the cause of Allah, until he returns to his home."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ observed iʿtikāf during the middle ten days of Ramadan, seeking Laylat al-Qadr before it was made known to him. When those days had passed, he ordered the tent to be taken down, and it was taken down. Then it was made clear to him that it was in the last ten days, so he ordered the tent to be set up again, and it was. Then he came out to the people and said:

"O people, Laylat al-Qadr was made clear to me, and I came out to inform you of it. But two men came disputing, and Satan was with them, so I forgot it. So seek it in the last ten days of Ramadan; seek it on the ninth, the seventh, and the fifth."
[The narrator] said: I said, "O Abū Saʿīd, you know the counting better than we do." He said, "Yes.
We have more right to that than you."

I said, "What are the ninth, the seventh, and the fifth?" He said, "When twenty-one has passed, the one following it, the twenty-second, is the ninth. When twenty-three has passed, the one following it is the seventh. When twenty-five has passed, the one following it is the fifth."
Ibn Khallād said, in place of "disputing" (yaḥtaqqān), "quarreling" (yakhtaṣimān).
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had long wanted to ask ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb about the two women among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ concerning whom Allah the Exalted said: {If you two repent to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined}, until he went on Hajj and I went on Hajj with him. He turned aside [from the road] and I turned aside with him, carrying a water container, and he relieved himself. Then he came back and I poured water over his hands from it, and he performed ablution. I said to him, "O Commander of the Faithful, who were the two women among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ concerning whom Allah the Exalted said: {If you two repent to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined}?" He said, "How astonishing of you, O Ibn ʿAbbās! They were ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah." Then ʿUmar took up the account and related it, saying: I and a neighbor of mine from the Anṣār, from Banū Umayyah ibn Zayd, who lived in the upper outskirts of Medina, used to take turns visiting the Prophet ﷺ. He would go down one day and I would go down one day. When I went down, I would bring him news of that day, of revelation or otherwise, and when he went down, he would do the same. We, the people of Quraysh, used to have the upper hand over women, but when we came to the Anṣār, we found a people whose women had the upper hand over them, and our women began to pick up the ways of the Anṣār women. I once shouted at my wife and she answered me back. I disliked that she should answer me back. She said, "Why do you dislike that I answer you back? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ answer him back, and one of them may stay away from him from morning until night." That alarmed me, and I said to her, "Whoever among them does that has failed and lost!" Then I put on my clothes and went down and entered upon Ḥafṣah and said to her, "O Ḥafṣah, does one of you make the Prophet ﷺ angry all day until night?" She said, "Yes." I said, "You have failed and lost! Do you not fear that Allah will be angry because of the anger of His Messenger ﷺ, and you will be destroyed? Do not make demands of the Prophet ﷺ, do not answer him back in anything, and do not stay away from him. Ask me for whatever you need, and do not be deceived if your neighbor is more beautiful than you and more beloved to the Prophet ﷺ," meaning ʿĀʾishah. ʿUmar said: We had been saying that Ghassān were shoeing their horses to attack us. My Anṣārī companion went down on the day of his turn, and returned to us in the evening and knocked on my door very hard and said, "Is he there?" I was alarmed and went out to him, and he said, "A great matter has happened today." I said, "What is it? Have Ghassān come?" He said, "No, rather it is greater and more terrible than that: the Prophet ﷺ has divorced his wives." I said, "Ḥafṣah has failed and lost! I had thought this was about to happen." So I put on my clothes and prayed the Fajr prayer with the Prophet ﷺ. Then the Prophet ﷺ entered an upper room of his and withdrew there, and I went in to Ḥafṣah and found her weeping. I said, "What makes you weep? Did I not warn you about this? Has the Prophet ﷺ divorced you?" She said, "I do not know. There he is, withdrawn in the upper room." I went out and came to the pulpit, and around it was a group, some of whom were weeping. I sat with them for a little while, then what I felt overcame me, so I went to the upper room where the Prophet ﷺ was and said to a black servant of his, "Ask permission for ʿUmar." The servant went in and spoke to the Prophet ﷺ, then came back and said, "I spoke to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned you to him, but he was silent." So I left and sat with the group by the pulpit, then what I felt overcame me again, so I came and said to the servant, "Ask permission for ʿUmar." He went in, then returned and said, "I mentioned you to him, but he was silent." So I went back and sat with the group by the pulpit, then what I felt overcame me again, so I came to the servant and said, "Ask permission for ʿUmar." He went in, then returned to me and said, "I mentioned you to him, but he was silent." As I was turning to leave, the servant called me and said, "The Prophet ﷺ has permitted you." So I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found him lying on a mat of woven palm fibers, with no bedding between him and it, and the weave had left marks on his side. He was leaning on a leather pillow stuffed with palm fiber. I greeted him with salām, then said while standing, "O Messenger of Allah, have you divorced your wives?" He raised his gaze to me and said, "No." I said, "Allahu akbar!" Then I said, while standing, seeking to put him at ease, "O Messenger of Allah, if only you had seen me: we, the people of Quraysh, used to have the upper hand over women, but when we came to Medina we found a people whose women had the upper hand over them." The Prophet ﷺ smiled. Then I said, "O Messenger of Allah, if only you had seen me when I entered upon Ḥafṣah and said to her, 'Do not be deceived if your neighbor is more beautiful than you and more beloved to the Prophet ﷺ,' meaning ʿĀʾishah." The Prophet ﷺ smiled again. So I sat down when I saw him smile, and I raised my gaze around his house. By Allah, I saw nothing in his house that would catch the eye except three pieces of tanned leather. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to give abundance to your community, for Persians and Romans have been given abundance and given the world, though they do not worship Allah." The Prophet ﷺ sat up, having been reclining, and said: "Are you in doubt about this, O son of al-Khaṭṭāb? Those are a people whose good things were hastened for them in the life of this world." I said, "O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me." The Prophet ﷺ had withdrawn from his wives for twenty-nine nights because of that matter, when Ḥafṣah disclosed it to ʿĀʾishah. He had said: "I will not go in to them for a month," because of his intense displeasure with them, when Allah admonished him. When twenty-nine nights had passed, he went in to ʿĀʾishah, beginning with her. ʿĀʾishah said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, you swore that you would not come in to us for a month, and it is only the morning of the twenty-ninth night; I have been counting them one by one." He said: "The month is twenty-nine." And that month was twenty-nine nights. ʿĀʾishah said: Then Allah the Exalted revealed the verse of choice, and he began with me, the first of his wives, and I chose him. Then he gave all his wives the choice, and they said what ʿĀʾishah had said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿAmr ibn Maymūn said:] I saw ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, a few days before he was stabbed, in Medina. He stood before Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān and ʿUthmān ibn Ḥunayf and said, "What have you done? Do you fear that you have burdened the land with more than it can bear?" They said, "We have burdened it with something it is able to bear; there is not much surplus in it." He said, "Consider whether you have burdened the land with more than it can bear." They said, "No." Then ʿUmar said, "If Allah keeps me safe, I will leave the widows of the people of Iraq in no need of any man after me, ever." [ʿAmr] said: Only four days passed after that before he was stabbed. He said: I was standing, with nothing between me and him but ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās, on the morning he was stabbed. Whenever he passed between the rows, he would say, "Stand straight." When he saw no gaps in them, he would step forward and say the opening takbīr. Perhaps he would recite Sūrat Yūsuf or al-Naḥl or the like in the first rakʿah, until the people had gathered. No sooner had he said the takbīr than I heard him say, "The dog has killed me," or "has eaten me," when [the man] stabbed him. Then the unbeliever fled with a double-edged knife, stabbing everyone he passed on his right or left, until he had stabbed thirteen men, seven of whom died. When one of the Muslims saw that, he threw a cloak over him. When the unbeliever thought he was caught, he killed himself. ʿUmar took ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf by the hand and put him forward [to lead]. Those close to ʿUmar saw what I saw, but as for the outer parts of the mosque, they did not know anything except that they had lost the sound of ʿUmar, and they were saying, "Glory be to Allah! Glory be to Allah!" ʿAbd al-Raḥmān led them in a short prayer. When they had finished, [ʿUmar] said, "O Ibn ʿAbbās, find out who struck me." He went around for a while, then came back and said, "The slave of al-Mughīrah." He said, "The craftsman?" He said, "Yes." He said, "May Allah fight him! I had commanded that he be treated well. Praise be to Allah, who did not make my death at the hand of a man who claims Islam. You and your father used to like having many non-Arab unbelievers in Medina," and al-ʿAbbās had the most slaves among them. [Ibn ʿAbbās] said, "If you wish, I will do it," meaning, "if you wish, we will kill them." He said, "You are wrong, after they have spoken your language, prayed toward your qiblah, and performed Hajj as you perform it." Then he was carried to his house and we went with him. It was as though the people had never suffered a calamity before that day. One would say, "There is no harm." Another would say, "I fear for him." Then date-wine was brought and he drank it, and it came out from his belly. Then milk was brought and he drank it, and it came out from his wound, so they knew that he would die. We went in to him, and the people came praising him. A young man came and said, "Receive good news, O Commander of the Faithful, of the glad tidings Allah has given you: your companionship with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and your early standing in Islam, as you know, then you were given authority and you ruled justly, and then martyrdom." He said, "I wish that that would be even—neither against me nor for me." When [the young man] turned away, his garment was touching the ground. [ʿUmar] said, "Bring the young man back to me." He said, "O son of my brother, raise your garment, for that is cleaner for your garment and more mindful of your Lord. O ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, see how much debt I owe." They calculated it and found it to be about eighty-six thousand or so. He said, "If the wealth of the family of ʿUmar suffices for it, then pay it from their wealth; otherwise ask the Banū ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb, and if their wealth is not enough, ask among Quraysh, and do not go beyond them to anyone else. Pay this debt on my behalf. Go to ʿĀʾishah, the Mother of the Believers, and say, 'ʿUmar sends you greetings of peace.' And do not say 'the Commander of the Faithful,' for today I am not the commander of the believers. And say, 'ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb asks permission to be buried with his two companions.'" [ʿAbdullāh] greeted her with salām and asked permission, then entered upon her and found her sitting, weeping. He said, "ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb sends you greetings of peace and asks permission to be buried with his two companions." She said, "I had wanted it for myself, but today I will certainly prefer him over myself." When [ʿAbdullāh] returned, it was said, "Here is ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar; he has come." [ʿUmar] said, "Lift me up," and a man supported him against himself. He said, "What do you have?" [ʿAbdullāh] said, "What you love, O Commander of the Faithful: she has given permission." He said, "Praise be to Allah. Nothing was more important to me than that. When I have died, carry me, then give greetings of peace and say, 'ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb asks permission.' If she permits me, bring me in, and if she refuses me, return me to the graveyard of the Muslims." The Mother of the Believers, Ḥafṣah, came, with women walking with her. When we saw her we stood up, and she went in to him and wept beside him for a while. Then the men asked permission, and she went inside, away from them, and we heard her weeping from within. They said, "Give a bequest, O Commander of the Faithful; appoint a successor." He said, "I find no one more entitled to this matter than this group, or these men, with whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pleased when he died." Then he named ʿAlī, ʿUthmān, al-Zubayr, Ṭalḥah, Saʿd, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and said, "ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar will be a witness with you, but he will have no share in the matter"—as a form of consolation for him—"If the leadership falls to Saʿd, then so be it; otherwise, whichever of you becomes leader should seek his help, for I did not remove him from office out of incapacity or betrayal." And he said, "I advise the caliph after me to be mindful of the first Emigrants: to recognize their right, and to safeguard their sanctity. And I advise him to treat the Anṣār well— those who had settled in the abode and in faith before them— to accept from those of them who do good, and to pardon those of them who do wrong. And I advise him to treat the people of the garrison towns well, for they are the support of Islam, the collectors of wealth, and a source of rage for the enemy, and that nothing be taken from them except their surplus, with their consent. And I advise him to treat the Bedouin well, for they are the root of the Arabs and the substance of Islam: that [zakāh] be taken from the edges of their wealth and given back to their poor. And I advise him regarding the covenant of Allah and the covenant of His Messenger ﷺ: that their agreement with them be fulfilled, that they be fought for from behind them, and that they not be burdened beyond their capacity." When he passed away, we took him out and went walking. ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar greeted her with salām and said, "ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb asks permission." She said, "Bring him in." So he was brought in and was laid there with his two companions. When the burial was finished, that group gathered, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said, "Place your affair in the hands of three of you." Al-Zubayr said, "I have placed my share in the hands of ʿAlī." Ṭalḥah said, "I have placed my share in the hands of ʿUthmān." And Saʿd said, "I have placed my share in the hands of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf." ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said, "Which of you two will withdraw from this matter so that we may entrust it to him? Allah and Islam are upon him [as witnesses]: he must look to the best of them in his own judgment." The two elders were silent, so ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said, "Will you entrust it to me, with Allah as my witness that I will not fall short in choosing the best of you?" They said, "Yes." Then he took one of them by the hand and said, "You have kinship to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and early standing in Islam, as you know. So I ask you by Allah: if I appoint you, will you surely act justly, and if I appoint ʿUthmān, will you surely listen and obey?" Then he took the other aside and said the same to him. When he had taken the pledge, he said, "Raise your hand, O ʿUthmān," and he gave him the pledge of allegiance. Then ʿAlī pledged allegiance to him, and the people of the house entered and pledged allegiance to him.

segments_en: Hishām was asked about a man who accuses his wife [of adultery]. So Hishām narrated to us, from Muḥammad, who said: I asked Anas ibn Mālik about that, thinking that he had knowledge of it. He said: Hilāl ibn Umayyah accused his wife of [adultery] with Sharīk ibn Saḥmāʾ—who was the maternal brother of al-Barāʾ ibn Mālik—and he was the first to take the oath of condemnation (liʿān). So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ held the oath of condemnation between them, then said: "Watch her. If she gives birth to a child who is fair, with straight hair and light, weak-looking eyes, then he belongs to Hilāl ibn Umayyah; and if she gives birth to a child with kohl-darkened eyes, curly hair, and thin calves, then he belongs to Sharīk ibn Saḥmāʾ." He said: Then I was informed that she gave birth to a child with kohl-darkened eyes, curly hair, and thin calves.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would often say to his Companions: " Has any of you seen a dream?" He said: Then whoever Allah willed would relate [his dream] to him. One morning he said: " Last night two [angels] came to me, and they roused me, and they said to me, 'Set out.' So I set out with them, and we came upon a man lying down, and another man was standing over him with a rock, and he would drop the rock on his head, crushing his head, and the stone would roll away over there, and he would follow the stone and take it, and he would not return to him until his head was whole again as it had been, then he would go back to him and do to him the same as he had done the first time. I said to them: 'Glory be to Allah! Who are these two?' They said to me: 'Go on, go on.' So we went on and came upon a man lying on his back, and another man was standing over him with an iron hook, and he would come to one side of his face and tear open his jaw to the back of his neck, and his nostril to the back of his neck, and his eye to the back of his neck." He said: Perhaps Abū Rajāʾ said: "he would slit." He said: "Then he would turn to the other side, and do to it the same as he had done to the first side, and he would not finish with that side until it was whole again as it had been, then he would return to it and do the same as he had done the first time." He said: "I said: 'Glory be to Allah! Who are these two?' They said to me: 'Go on, go on.' So we went on and came upon something like an oven." He said: I think he said: "In it there was clamor and voices." He said: "We looked into it, and in it were naked men and women, and a flame would come at them from beneath them, and when the flame reached them, they cried out." He said: "I said to them: 'Who are these?' They said to me: 'Go on, go on.' So we went on and came upon a river" — I think he said — "red like blood, and in the river was a man swimming, and on the bank of the river was a man who had gathered many stones beside him, and the swimmer would swim for as long as he swam, then come to the one who had gathered the stones, open his mouth for him, and he would feed him a stone, and he would go off swimming, then return to him, and each time he returned to him, he opened his mouth for him and fed him a stone." He said: "I said to them: 'Who are these two?' They said to me: 'Go on, go on.' We went on and came upon a man of hideous appearance, the most hideous you could see in a man, and beside him was a fire which he was stoking and running around." He said: "I said to them: 'What is this?' They said to me: 'Go on, go on.' So we went on and came upon a lush, dark-green garden, with every kind of spring blossom, and in the midst of the garden was a very tall man; I could hardly see his head, so high was it in the sky, and around the man were more children than I had ever seen." He said: "I said to them: 'What is this? Who are these?' They said to me: 'Go on, go on.' He said: "So we went on until we reached a great garden; I had never seen a garden greater or more beautiful than it. He said: They said to me: 'Go up into it.' So we went up into it and reached a city built of bricks of gold and bricks of silver, and we came to the gate of the city and asked for it to be opened, and it was opened for us, and we entered it, and there we were met by men, half of whose bodies were as beautiful as the best you could see, and half as ugly as the worst you could see." He said: "The two said to them: 'Go and throw yourselves into that river.' He said: There was a river flowing across, its water as pure white as milk, so they went and threw themselves into it, then they came back to us with that ugliness gone from them, and they had become of the most beautiful form." He said: "They said to me: 'This is the Garden of ʿAdn, and that is your abode.' He said: My sight rose upward, and there was a palace like a white cloud." He said: "They said: 'That is your abode.' I said to them: 'May Allah bless you both. Let me enter it.' They said: 'Not now, but you will enter it.' I said to them: 'Tonight I have seen wonders, so what is it that I have seen?' They said to me: 'We will tell you. As for the first man you came upon, whose head was being crushed with the rock, he is the man who takes up the Qurʾān and then rejects it, and sleeps through the obligatory prayer. As for the man you came upon whose jaw was being torn to the back of his neck, and his nostril to the back of his neck, and his eye to the back of his neck, he is the man who goes out from his house in the morning and tells a lie that reaches the horizons. As for the naked men and women in the structure like an oven, they are the adulterers, men and women. As for the man you came upon swimming in the river and being fed stones, he is the one who consumed ribā [usury]. As for the man of hideous appearance beside the fire, stoking it and running around it, he is Mālik, the keeper of Hell. As for the tall man in the garden, he is Ibrāhīm ﷺ, and as for the children around him, they are every child who died upon the natural disposition (fiṭrah)." He said: Some of the Muslims said: "O Messenger of Allah, and the children of the polytheists?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "And the children of the polytheists. As for the people, half of whom were beautiful and half ugly, they are people who mixed a righteous deed with another, evil one; Allah has overlooked their sins."

segments_en: [Al-Miqdād said:] My two companions and I came, and our hearing and our sight had been affected by hardship. We began presenting ourselves to the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but none of them would take us in. Then we went to the Prophet ﷺ, and he took us to his family, where there were three goats. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Milk these goats and share the milk among us." He said: So we would milk them, and each of us would drink his share, and we would set aside the Prophet's ﷺ share. He said: He would come at night and give a greeting that would not wake a sleeper but would be heard by one who was awake. Then he would go to the mosque and pray, then come to his drink and drink it. One night Satan came to me, after I had drunk my share, and said: "Muhammad goes to the Anṣār and they give him gifts, and he receives from them what he needs; he has no need of this little sip." So I went to it and drank it. When it had settled in my belly and I knew there was no way back, Satan made me regret it and said: "Woe to you, what have you done? You drank Muhammad's drink! He will come and not find it, and will pray against you, and you will be destroyed, and you will lose your world and your Hereafter." I had on me a cloak such that if I put it over my feet my head was uncovered, and if I put it over my head my feet were uncovered. Sleep would not come to me, whereas my two companions slept, and did not do what I had done. He said: The Prophet ﷺ came and gave the greeting as he used to, then went to the mosque and prayed, then came to his drink and uncovered it, but found nothing in it. He raised his head to the sky, and I said: "Now he will pray against me and I will perish." But he said: "O Allah, feed the one who has fed me, and give drink to the one who has given me drink." He said: So I took the cloak and tied it around myself, took the knife, and went to the goats to see which of them was the fattest, so that I could slaughter it for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. But behold, she was full of milk, and so were all of them. So I took a vessel belonging to the family of Muhammad ﷺ, which they had never hoped to milk into. He said: I milked into it until froth rose on top, and I brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Have you all drunk your drink tonight?" He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, drink." So he drank, then handed it to me, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, drink." He drank, then handed it to me. When I realized that the Prophet ﷺ had been satisfied and that I had obtained his supplication, I laughed until I fell to the ground. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "That is one of your mischiefs, Miqdād!" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, such and such happened with me, and I did such and such." The Prophet ﷺ said: "This is nothing but a mercy from Allah. Why did you not let me know, so that we could wake our two companions and they could receive some of it?" He said: I said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, I do not care, when you and I have received it, who else among the people receives it."

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, who used to lead Kaʿb among his sons when he went blind, said: I heard Kaʿb ibn Mālik relating, when he stayed behind, the account of Tabūk. Kaʿb said: I never stayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in any expedition he undertook except the expedition of Tabūk, though I did stay behind in the expedition of Badr, and no one who stayed behind from it was reproached. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had only gone out seeking the caravan of Quraysh, until Allah brought them and their enemy together without a prior appointment. And I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of al-ʿAqabah when we pledged ourselves to Islam, and I would not wish to have the occasion of Badr in its place, even though Badr is more widely mentioned among the people than it. As for my account: I had never been stronger or better off than when I stayed behind from him in that expedition. By Allah, I had never before had two riding animals together until I gathered them in that expedition. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never intended an expedition without concealing it by speaking of another, until that expedition. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ undertook it in intense heat, facing a long journey, a desert, and a great number of enemies, so he made the matter clear to the Muslims so that they could prepare fully for their expedition, and he informed them of the direction he intended. The Muslims with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were many, and no written register could contain them all—he meant the register. Kaʿb said: Any man who wished to be absent would think it would remain hidden from him so long as no revelation from Allah came down about it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ undertook that expedition when the fruits and the shade were pleasant, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims with him made preparations. I began going out in the morning to prepare with them, but I would return having accomplished nothing, and I would say to myself: I am able to do it. That kept dragging on with me until the people became serious and urgent, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out in the morning with the Muslims, while I had not prepared anything of my equipment. I said: I will prepare a day or two after him, then join them. So I went out in the morning after they had departed to prepare, but I returned having accomplished nothing. Then I went out again, then returned having accomplished nothing. It continued with me until they hurried on and the expedition had slipped far ahead, and I intended to set off and catch up with them—and I wish I had done so— but that was not decreed for me. After the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had left, whenever I went out among the people and walked among them, it grieved me that I saw only a man suspected of hypocrisy or a man among the weak whom Allah had excused. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not mention me until he reached Tabūk. While sitting among the people at Tabūk, he said: "What has Kaʿb done?" A man from Banū Salimah said: O Messenger of Allah, his two cloaks and his looking admiringly at his own sides have held him back. Muʿādh ibn Jabal said: What an evil thing you have said! By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing of him but good. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent. Kaʿb ibn Mālik said: When news reached me that he was heading back, anxiety overcame me, and I began to think of lying and to say: How will I escape his anger tomorrow? And I sought help in that from every person of sound opinion among my family. When it was said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was about to arrive, falsehood left me, and I knew that I would never escape from him with anything involving a lie, so I resolved to tell the truth. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in the morning, and whenever he returned from a journey he would begin with the mosque, pray two rakʿahs in it, then sit with the people. When he did that, those who had stayed behind came to him, and began making excuses to him and swearing oaths to him. They were some eighty-odd men. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted their outward statements, took their pledge, asked forgiveness for them, and left their inner secrets to Allah. Then I came to him, and when I greeted him he smiled the smile of one who is angry, then said: "Come." I came walking until I sat before him. He said to me: "What kept you back? Had you not bought your mount?" I said: Yes. By Allah, if I were sitting before anyone other than you from among the people of this world, I would see that I could escape his anger with an excuse, and I have been given skill in argument, but by Allah, I know that if I tell you a false account today to make you pleased with me, Allah would soon make you angry with me, and if I tell you a truthful account in which you find fault with me, I hope in it for Allah's pardon. No, by Allah, I had no excuse. By Allah, I was never stronger or better off than when I stayed behind from you. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for this man, he has told the truth. Get up until Allah decides your case." I got up, and some men of Banū Salimah rose and followed me, and they said to me: By Allah, we have not known you to have committed a sin before this. You were unable not to offer the Messenger of Allah ﷺ an excuse like the one those who stayed behind offered him. The forgiveness the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have asked for you would have sufficed for your sin. By Allah, they kept rebuking me until I wanted to go back and call myself a liar. Then I said to them: Has anyone else met the same as I have? They said: Yes, two men who said what you said, and the same was said to them as was said to you. I said: Who are they? They said: Murārah ibn ar-Rabīʿ al-ʿAmrī and Hilāl ibn Umayyah al-Wāqifī. They mentioned to me two righteous men who had been present at Badr, in whom there was an example. So I went on when they mentioned them to me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the Muslims to speak to us, the three, out of all those who had stayed behind from him, so the people avoided us and changed toward us until the earth itself seemed strange to me, not the one I knew. We remained in that state for fifty nights. As for my two companions, they gave in and stayed in their houses weeping, but as for me, I was the youngest of the people and the most robust, so I would go out and attend the prayer with the Muslims and walk about the markets, and no one would speak to me. I would come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and greet him while he was in his sitting place after the prayer, and I would say to myself: Did he move his lips in returning the greeting to me or not? Then I would pray near him and steal glances at him. When I turned to my prayer, he would turn toward me, and when I turned toward him, he would turn away from me, until, when that harshness of the people had gone on long for me, I walked until I climbed over the wall of Abū Qatādah's garden—he was my cousin and the dearest of people to me—and greeted him, but by Allah, he did not return my greeting. I said: O Abū Qatādah, I ask you by Allah, do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger? He was silent. I repeated it to him and asked him, and he was silent. I repeated it to him and asked him again. He said: Allah and His Messenger know best. My eyes overflowed, and I turned back until I climbed over the wall. He said: While I was walking in the market of Madinah, there was a Nabatean of the Nabateans of Syria, among those who had come with food to sell in Madinah, saying: Who will direct me to Kaʿb ibn Mālik? The people began pointing to me for him, until he came to me and handed me a letter from the king of Ghassān. In it was written: To proceed: it has reached me that your companion has treated you harshly, and Allah has not placed you in a place of humiliation or loss. So join us, and we will console you. When I read it, I said: This too is part of the trial. So I took it to the oven and burned it in it. When forty of the fifty nights had passed, there came a messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commands you to withdraw from your wife. I said: Should I divorce her, or what should I do? He said: No, rather withdraw from her and do not approach her. He sent the same message to my two companions. I said to my wife: Go to your family and stay with them until Allah decides this matter. Kaʿb said: The wife of Hilāl ibn Umayyah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, Hilāl ibn Umayyah is an old man with no one to look after him, and he has no servant. Do you dislike that I serve him? He said: "No, but he must not approach you." She said: By Allah, he has no movement toward anything. By Allah, he has not stopped weeping since his affair happened until this day. Some of my family said to me: If only you would ask permission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding your wife, as he gave permission to the wife of Hilāl ibn Umayyah to serve him. I said: By Allah, I will not ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission regarding her, for I do not know what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say if I asked permission about her, and I am a young man. Then I waited ten more nights after that, until fifty nights were complete for us from the time the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade speaking to us. When I had prayed the dawn prayer on the morning of the fiftieth night, while I was on the roof of one of our houses, as I was sitting in the condition Allah has described, my soul constricted for me, and the earth, vast as it is, constricted for me, I heard the voice of a crier who had climbed Mount Salʿ, calling at the top of his voice: O Kaʿb ibn Mālik, receive glad tidings! He said: I fell down in prostration, and I knew that relief had come. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had announced Allah's acceptance of our repentance when he prayed the dawn prayer, and people went to give us the glad tidings, and bearers of glad tidings went to my two companions, and a man spurred a horse toward me, and a man of Aslam ran and climbed the mountain, and the voice was faster than the horse. When the one whose voice I had heard came to me to give me glad tidings, I took off my two garments for him and clothed him with them for his good news. By Allah, I owned nothing else that day. I borrowed two garments and put them on, and went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The people met me in groups, congratulating me on the acceptance of my repentance, saying: May Allah's acceptance of your repentance bring you joy. Kaʿb said: Until I entered the mosque, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sitting with the people around him. Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh got up and hurried to me until he shook my hand and congratulated me. By Allah, no other man of the Muhājirūn stood up for me besides him, and I will never forget that of Ṭalḥah. Kaʿb said: When I greeted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, his face shining with joy: "Receive glad tidings of the best day that has passed over you since your mother bore you." He said: I said: Is it from you, O Messenger of Allah, or from Allah? He said: "No, rather it is from Allah." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was happy, his face would light up until it was like a piece of the moon, and we used to recognize that in him. When I sat before him, I said: O Messenger of Allah, part of my repentance is that I divest myself of my wealth as charity to Allah and to His Messenger. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Keep some of your wealth, for that is better for you." I said: Then I will keep my share at Khaybar. And I said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah has saved me only through truthfulness, and part of my repentance is that I will speak only the truth for as long as I live. By Allah, I do not know any of the Muslims whom Allah has tested in truthfulness of speech, since I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, better than He tested me. Since I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until this day of mine, I have not deliberately lied, and I hope that Allah will protect me in whatever remains. And Allah revealed to His Messenger ﷺ: {Allah has certainly accepted the repentance of the Prophet and the Muhājirūn} up to His saying {and be with the truthful}. By Allah, Allah has never bestowed on me a favor, after guiding me to Islam, greater in my soul than my truthfulness to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that I did not lie to him and so perish as those who lied perished, for Allah said about those who lied, when the revelation came down, the worst of what He said about anyone. He, Blessed and Exalted, said: {They will swear by Allah to you when you return} up to His saying {then indeed Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people}. Kaʿb said: We, the three, were left behind from the matter of those whose excuses the Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted when they swore to him, for he took their pledge and asked forgiveness for them, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ postponed our matter until Allah decided it. Concerning that Allah said: {And [He also accepted the repentance of] the three who were left behind}. What Allah mentioned is not our staying behind from the expedition; it is rather his leaving us behind and postponing our matter, as distinct from those who swore to him and made excuses to him, and he accepted it from them.

segments_en: And Muḥammad ibn Jubayr had mentioned to me part of that hadith. So I set out until I entered upon Mālik ibn Aws, and I asked him about that hadith. Mālik said: While I was sitting with my family when the day had grown long, the messenger of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb came to me and said, "Answer the Commander of the Faithful." So I went with him until I entered upon ʿUmar, and he was sitting on a bed woven of palm fronds, with no bedding between him and it, reclining on a leather cushion. I greeted him with salām and then sat down. He said: "O Mālik, a few families from your people have come to us, and I have ordered a small grant for them, so take it and distribute it among them." I said: "O Commander of the Faithful, if only you would order someone other than me to do it." He said: "Take it, man." While I was sitting with him, his doorkeeper Yarfāʾ came to him and said: "Would you receive ʿUthmān, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, al-Zubayr and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ? They are asking permission to enter." He said: "Yes." So he admitted them, and they entered, greeted him with salām, and sat down. Then Yarfāʾ sat for a short while and said: "Would you receive ʿAlī and al-ʿAbbās?" He said: "Yes." So he admitted them, and they entered, greeted him with salām, and sat down. Al-ʿAbbās said: "O Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this one." The two were disputing over what Allah had granted to His Messenger ﷺ from the property of Banū al-Naḍīr. The group, ʿUthmān and his companions, said: "O Commander of the Faithful, judge between them and relieve each of them of the other." ʿUmar said: "Be patient. I ask you by Allah, by whose permission the heaven and the earth stand, do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'We are not inherited from; whatever we leave is charity'?" By this the Messenger of Allah ﷺ meant himself. The group said: "He did say that." Then ʿUmar turned to ʿAlī and al-ʿAbbās and said: "I ask you both by Allah, do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that?" They said: "He did say that." ʿUmar said: "Then I will tell you about this matter. Allah singled out His Messenger ﷺ in this fayʾ with something He gave to no one else." Then he recited: {And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them} up to His words {Able [to do all things]}. "So this was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. By Allah, he did not take it for himself to the exclusion of you, nor did he prefer himself over you in it. He gave it to you and distributed it among you until this property remained from it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would spend from this property on his family their provision for the year, then take what remained and put it to the use of the property of Allah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted in this way throughout his life. I ask you by Allah, do you know that?" They said: "Yes." Then he said to ʿAlī and al-ʿAbbās: "I ask you both by Allah, do you know that?" ʿUmar said: "Then Allah took His Prophet ﷺ, and Abū Bakr said: 'I am the successor of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.' So Abū Bakr took charge of it and acted in it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had acted, and Allah knows that in it he was truthful, righteous, rightly guided, and a follower of the truth. Then Allah took Abū Bakr, and I became the successor of Abū Bakr. I took charge of it for two years of my rule, acting in it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had acted and as Abū Bakr had acted in it, and Allah knows that in it I am truthful, righteous, rightly guided, and a follower of the truth. Then you two came to me, speaking to me, and your word was one and your affair was one. You came to me, O ʿAbbās, asking for your share from your brother's son, and this one came to me, meaning ʿAlī, wanting the share of his wife from her father. I said to you both that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'We are not inherited from; whatever we leave is charity.' Then when it seemed right to me to hand it over to you, I said: 'If you wish, I will hand it over to you on condition that you bind yourselves by the covenant and pledge of Allah to act in it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted in it, and as Abū Bakr acted in it, and as I have acted in it since I took charge of it.' You both said: 'Hand it over to us.' On that basis I handed it over to you. So I ask you by Allah, did I hand it over to them on that basis?" The group said: "Yes." Then he turned to ʿAlī and al-ʿAbbās and said: "I ask you both by Allah, did I hand it over to you on that basis?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Are you then seeking from me a judgment other than that? By Allah, by whose permission the heaven and the earth stand, I will not give any judgment in it other than that. And if you are unable to manage it, then return it to me, and I will suffice you in it."

segments_en: On the night the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey from the mosque of the Kaʿbah, three people came to him before revelation was sent to him, while he was asleep in the Sacred Mosque. The first of them said, "Which one of them is he?" The middle one said, "He is the best of them." The last of them said, "Take the best of them." That was that night, and he did not see them again until they came to him another night, in what his heart perceived, for his eyes would sleep but his heart would not sleep; and so it is with the prophets: their eyes sleep but their hearts do not sleep. They did not speak to him, but carried him and placed him by the well of Zamzam. Gabriel took charge of him from among them, and Gabriel split open what lies between his throat and the hollow of his chest until he had finished with his chest and his belly, and he washed it with the water of Zamzam with his own hand, until he had cleansed his belly. Then a golden basin was brought, containing a golden vessel, filled with faith and wisdom, and with it he filled his chest and the fleshy parts of his throat, meaning the veins of his throat. Then he closed it up and ascended with him to the lowest heaven. He knocked on one of its doors, and the people of heaven called out, "Who is this?" He said, "Gabriel." They said, "And who is with you?" He said, "Muhammad is with me." They said, "Has he been sent for?" He said, "Yes." They said, "Welcome to him, and may he be at home." The people of heaven rejoiced at him, for the people of heaven do not know what Allah intends for him on earth until He informs them. In the lowest heaven he found Adam. Gabriel said to him, "This is your father; greet him." So he greeted him, and Adam returned the greeting and said, "Welcome and may you be at home, my son, what an excellent son you are."  Then in the lowest heaven he saw two rivers flowing. He said, "What are these two rivers, Gabriel?" He said, "This is the Nile and the Euphrates, their source." Then he went on with him through the heaven, and there was another river, on which stood a palace of pearl and chrysolite. He struck it with his hand and it was musk. He said, "What is this, Gabriel?" He said, "This is al-Kawthar, which your Lord has kept hidden for you." Then he ascended to the second heaven, and the angels said to him the same as the first had said: "Who is this?" Gabriel said, "Gabriel." They said, "And who is with you?" He said, "Muhammad ﷺ." They said, "Has he been sent for?" He said, "Yes." They said, "Welcome to him, and may he be at home." Then he ascended with him to the third heaven, and they said to him the same as the first and the second had said. Then he ascended with him to the fourth, and they said the same to him. Then he ascended with him to the fifth heaven, and they said the same. Then he ascended with him to the sixth heaven, and they said the same to him. Then he ascended with him to the seventh heaven, and they said the same to him. In every heaven there were prophets whom he named, and I retained among them Idrīs in the second, Hārūn in the fourth, another in the fifth whose name I did not memorize, Ibrāhīm in the sixth, and Mūsā in the seventh, because of the distinction of having been spoken to by Allah. Mūsā said, "My Lord, I did not think that anyone would be raised above me." Then he was taken up above that, to a height that none knows except Allah, until he came to the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary. The Almighty, the Lord of Might, drew near and came down until He was at a distance of two bow-lengths or nearer. Among what Allah revealed to him was: fifty prayers for your nation every day and night. Then he descended until he reached Mūsā, who detained him and said, "Muhammad, what did your Lord enjoin upon you?" He said, "He enjoined upon me fifty prayers every day and night." He said, "Your nation cannot bear that. Go back, and let your Lord lighten it for you and for them." So the Prophet ﷺ turned to Gabriel, as if consulting him about that, and Gabriel signaled to him: "Yes, if you wish." So he ascended with him to the Almighty, and he said, while remaining in his place, "My Lord, lighten it for us, for my nation cannot bear this." So He removed ten prayers from him. Then he returned to Mūsā, who detained him, and Mūsā kept sending him back to his Lord until it became five prayers. Then Mūsā detained him at the five and said, "Muhammad, by Allah, I tried to persuade the Children of Israel, my people, to accept less than this, but they were too weak and abandoned it. Your nation is weaker in bodies, hearts, physiques, sight and hearing. So go back, and let your Lord lighten it for you." Each time, the Prophet ﷺ turned to Gabriel to seek his advice, and Gabriel did not dislike that. So he took him up at the fifth, and he said, "My Lord, my nation are weak in their bodies, hearts, hearing and physiques, so lighten it for us." The Almighty said, "Muhammad." He said, "At Your service, and happy to obey." He said, "The word is not changed with Me, as I have decreed for you in the Mother of the Book." He said, "Every good deed is rewarded tenfold, so they are fifty in the Mother of the Book, and five for you." He returned to Mūsā, who said, "What did you do?" He said, "He lightened it for us: He gave us for every good deed ten like it." Mūsā said, "By Allah, I tried to persuade the Children of Israel to accept less than that, and they abandoned it. Go back to your Lord and let Him lighten it for you further." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Mūsā, by Allah, I am ashamed before my Lord of how often I have gone back to Him." He said, "Then descend in the name of Allah." He said: and he woke up while he was in the Sacred Mosque.

segments_en: We used to speak about the Farewell Hajj while the Prophet ﷺ was among us, and we did not know what the Farewell Hajj was. Then he praised Allah and extolled Him, and then mentioned the Antichrist (al-Masīḥ ad-Dajjāl) and spoke about him at length. He said: "Allah did not send any prophet except that he warned his nation. Nūḥ warned it, and so did the prophets after him. And indeed he will emerge among you. Whatever is hidden from you about his affair, it is not hidden from you that your Lord is not hidden from you [in His attributes]" — three times. "Indeed, your Lord is not one-eyed, but he is blind in the right eye, as if his eye were a floating grape." " Beware! Indeed, Allah has made your blood and your wealth sacred to you, like the sacredness of this day of yours, in this land of yours, in this month of yours. Have I conveyed [the message]?" They said, "Yes." He said, "O Allah, bear witness" — three times — "Woe to you," or he said, "Alas for you, beware, do not return after me as disbelievers, striking one another's necks."
label: machine translation
